docs.title: CCSDS File Delivery Protocol
docs.text: title: CCSDS File Delivery Protocol (CCSDS 727.0-B-5) description: CFDP in full, covering entities, transactions, the unacknowledged and acknowledged modes, every PDU with bit layouts, checksums, timers and faults, the MIB, user operations and the store-and-forward overlay, and how it relates to PUS ST[23], ST[13] and the draft ST[24], with Solar Orbiter's non-CFDP file transfer as a contrast. tags: [CCSDS, CFDP, Application layer, File transfer, PUS, ST[13], ST[23], Solar Orbiter] sources: [ccsds-727-0-727x0b5e1, ecss-e-st-70-41c-15april2016, ecss-e-st-70-41c-rev1-dir1, ecss-e-70-41a-30jan2003-pus, ecss-e-hb-50a-15november2008, ccsds-130-0-130x0g4e1, pecchioli-egs-cc-esoc, sol-s-astr-tn-00079-07, mib-20250916m25925pfms001-sol]

docs.title: CCSDS File Delivery Protocol (CCSDS 727.0-B-5)
docs.text:
Spacecraft used to store data on tape recorders that could only be dumped, and ground teams handled them with ad hoc, private protocols. Solid-state mass memory changed this. It gives random access to gigabytes, so data lost on the link can be sent again and delivery of critical information can be guaranteed. Much routine traffic can then become files.1 The CCSDS File Delivery Protocol (CFDP) is the CCSDS standard for moving files to and from that storage. It also offers simple file management on the remote file system. It is designed for noisy, bandwidth-limited, asymmetric and interrupted links with long light times, and for platforms with little computing power and memory.15

CFDP runs over almost any packet service. Examples are the CCSDS Space Packet over TM, TC or AOS frames, the Encapsulation Packet, DTN bundles, and ground networks.316 It can be started by the sender or by the receiver.3 This page describes CCSDS 727.0-B-5 (July 2020, Editorial Change 1 of September 2024) as held in the library. It ends by comparing CFDP with the PUS alternatives that ESA missions such as Solar Orbiter use instead.

At a glance

Property Value Layer Application layer120 Data unit PDU: 4-octet fixed header part + variable entity IDs and sequence number + data field74 PDU types File Directive (EOF, Finished, ACK, Metadata, NAK, Prompt, Keep Alive) and File Data78 Service classes Class 1 unreliable (unacknowledged), Class 2 reliable (acknowledged)103 Integrity optional CRC-16 per PDU (TC CRC); mandatory 32-bit file checksum (modular, CRC-32 variants or null)3334 File size 32-bit "small" or 64-bit "large" (Large File flag)7477 Underlying service UNITDATA.request/indication only, with in-sequence but possibly lossy and erroneous delivery16 Security none built in; must come from the layers below117 Relay Store and Forward Overlay (normative annex B)109

docs.title: History of the standard
docs.text:
Issue Date Notes 727.0-B-1 January 2002 original issue 727.0-B-2 October 2002 727.0-B-3 June 2005 727.0-B-4 January 2007 the issue cited in the PUS-C bibliography121 727.0-B-5 July 2020 moves SFO to annex B; removes the Extended Procedures (and so classes 3 and 4); adds large files, multi-segment records and per-segment metadata; adds a choice of checksum from a SANA registry EC 1 September 2024 heading numbering under 7.2.3; A4 page size

The issue list and change summary are from the document control page.23 The 2008 ECSS handbook still describes four classes. Classes 3 and 4 were unreliable and reliable transfer through waypoints using the Extended Procedures, which forwarded file data inside CFDP itself. The handbook also describes the SFO as an alternative that works file by file.134 Issue 5 keeps only the SFO.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  U["CFDP user<br/>(software task)"] <-->|"service primitives<br/>(Put.request, ...indication)"| E["CFDP protocol entity"]
  E <--> F["Filestore<br/>(virtual filestore)"]
  E <--> M["MIB<br/>(local and remote entity configuration)"]
  E <-->|"UNITDATA.request / .indication<br/>(UT_SDU, UT address)"| UT["Unitdata Transfer (UT) layer<br/>Space Packets, Encapsulation, DTN, TCP/UDP..."]

Redrawn after CCSDS 727.0-B-5 figure 2-1.6

  • User. A software task, which may be operated by a human. Each entity has at most one user.6
  • Protocol entity. An implementation of the core procedures, "roughly analogous" to an Internet host.64
  • Filestore. Each entity has exactly one filestore, described to the protocol as a virtual filestore that each implementation maps to real storage. The minimum capabilities are create, delete, rename, append and replace file, and create, remove and list directory. Optionally the filestore distinguishes record-structured files from octet streams.611
  • Unitdata Transfer (UT) layer. One conceptual service at one service access point. CFDP uses nothing from it except addressing and PDU delimitation. Multiplexing of transactions, sequence auditing and error detection all happen inside CFDP. That is why the PDU header carries its own length.7
  • Management Information Base (MIB). Mostly static tables of defaults, address mappings and timer settings. This is not the SCOS-2000 MIB. The name is the same, but the CFDP MIB is an entity configuration store.8

docs.title: Addressing
docs.text: Each entity has a name, its entity ID, that is unique within the CFDP network. Because an entity owns exactly one filestore, the entity ID also names the filestore. The MIB maps entity IDs to UT addresses. A UT address can be an Internet address, a radio buffer, an APID, a virtual channel number or any other local mechanism.10

docs.title: What CFDP expects from the layer below
docs.text: The UT service has two primitives, UNITDATA.request (UT_SDU, UT Address) and UNITDATA.indication (UT_SDU, UT Address). The assumed minimum quality of service is delivery with possible errors, possibly incomplete, but in sequence. In-sequence delivery is what the immediate, asynchronous and prompted lost-segment detection modes and Keep Alive rely on. CFDP tolerates loss and corruption, but it is not meant for networks where they are common: the standard warns of "severe performance reductions" in that case.16 Implementations may add non-mandatory primitives, such as a flow-control "ready" indication or a transmission-complete indication for starting acknowledgement timers.16

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text:
Term Meaning File Delivery Unit (FDU) a file plus its metadata (file names, messages to user, filestore requests). An FDU may be metadata only4 Transaction the end-to-end delivery of one FDU between two entities, identified by a transaction ID = source entity ID + transaction sequence number413 Source / destination the entity holding the file at the start of the task / the one holding a copy at the end4 Sender / receiver the two ends of one point-to-point copy operation. With relays, the source is the first sender and the destination the last receiver4 Offset the number of file octets that precede a given octet4 Progress for a File Data PDU, offset + length. Transmission and reception progress are the maxima over all PDUs sent or received4

A transaction ends when the file has been delivered, when either end has disallowed it, when a fault has cancelled it, or when a user has cancelled it.9

docs.title: User services and primitives
docs.text:
The user can start file transfers, start remote filestore operations, receive events, ask for status, exchange messages, and suspend, resume or cancel transactions. An entity must accept a new Put.request before earlier transactions have finished, so "virtually any number" of transactions can be in progress at once.12

Request Parameters (optional in brackets) Put.request destination entity ID, [source file name], [destination file name], [segmentation control], [fault handler overrides], [flow label], [transmission mode], [closure requested], [messages to user], [filestore requests]17 Cancel.request transaction ID18 Suspend.request transaction ID19 Resume.request transaction ID20 Report.request transaction ID21 Indication Parameters Notes Transaction.indication transaction ID issued on Put.request22 EOF-Sent.indication transaction ID optional; on first transmission of the EOF PDU23 Transaction-Finished.indication transaction ID, [filestore responses], [status report], condition code, file status, delivery code always at the source; optional at the destination24 Metadata-Recv.indication transaction ID, source entity ID, [file size], [source/destination file names], [messages to user] on receipt of the Metadata PDU25 File-Segment-Recv.indication transaction ID, offset, length, [record continuation state, segment metadata length, segment metadata] optional26 Suspended.indication transaction ID, condition code 27 Resumed.indication transaction ID, progress 28 Report.indication transaction ID, status report content implementation-specific29 Fault.indication transaction ID, condition code, progress fault handled by "ignore"30 Abandoned.indication transaction ID, condition code, progress fault handled by "abandon"31 EOF-Recv.indication transaction ID optional; at the destination32

The main parameters behave as follows:1415

  • Segmentation control says whether the file is cut as an array of octets or as an array of variable-length records.
  • Fault handler overrides pick, for a given fault type, one of four actions: cancel, suspend, ignore (with a Fault.indication) or abandon (with an Abandoned.indication). Where no override is given, the MIB default applies.
  • Transmission mode is acknowledged or unacknowledged. It overrides the MIB default.
  • Closure requested asks the receiver to confirm an unacknowledged transaction with a Finished PDU.
  • Filestore requests are actions (create, delete, rename, append or replace file, create or remove directory, "deny" file or directory) that the destination executes, in the order given, after the data transfer completes.
  • Messages to user are delivered to the destination user at the start of the transaction. They are the vehicle for the user operations.
  • Flow label is a hint for prioritisation and pre-emption. Its use is an implementation matter.
  • Segment metadata is 0 to 63 octets of per-segment data whose meaning is set by the implementation.

docs.title: PDU formats
docs.text: Every PDU is a fixed-format header followed by a data field of fixed or variable format. The data field holds data items in five possible formats: fixed, LV (length-value), TLV (type-length-value), raw file data, and FSS (file-size sensitive).7376

docs.title: Fixed PDU header
docs.text:
Field Bits Values Purpose Version 3 001 protocol version 274 PDU type 1 0 directive, 1 file data 74 Direction 1 0 toward receiver, 1 toward sender used for PDU forwarding74 Transmission mode 1 0 acknowledged, 1 unacknowledged 74 CRC flag 1 0 absent, 1 present 74 Large File flag 1 0 small, 1 large a file whose size does not fit in an unsigned 32-bit integer, and every file of unbounded size, is "large"74 PDU data field length 16 octets 74 Segmentation control 1 0 boundaries not preserved, 1 preserved 0 and ignored for directives74 Length of entity IDs 3 octets − 1 74 Segment metadata flag 1 0 absent, 1 present 0 and ignored for directives75 Length of transaction sequence number 3 octets − 1 75 Source entity ID variable unsigned integer entity that originated the transaction75 Transaction sequence number variable unsigned integer unique among that entity's transactions75 Destination entity ID variable unsigned integer final destination of the metadata and file data75

Entity IDs and sequence numbers of different lengths are compared as if the shorter one were padded with leading zeros. The length itself has no meaning.76 The sequence number is allocated in order by the entity that answers the Put.request.75 The header always names the source and destination of the transaction. The Direction bit tells relays and peers which way a given PDU is travelling.7439

Inference

Table 5-1 gives the PDU Data field length only as "in octets". Unlike the Space Packet, it does not specify a "minus one" convention, so the field is read here as the plain octet count of the data field. Clause 4.1.3.2, which says the CRC's length "shall be included in the PDU data field length", is consistent with that reading.33 With 1 to 8 octet entity IDs and sequence numbers, the header is 7 to 28 octets long.

docs.title: LV, TLV and FSS items
docs.text:
• LV: an 8-bit length (0 to 255) followed by that many octets. The position is fixed, the length variable.76
  • TLV: an 8-bit type, an 8-bit length and the value. Both position and length vary, so these are used for options.76
  • FSS: integers (file sizes and offsets) that are 32 bits when the Large File flag is 0 and 64 bits when it is 1.77

docs.title: File Directive PDUs
docs.text:
A directive's data field is a directive code octet followed by the directive parameters.78

Code Directive Code Directive 0x00-0x03 reserved 0x08 NAK PDU 0x04 EOF PDU 0x09 Prompt PDU 0x05 Finished PDU 0x0C Keep Alive PDU 0x06 ACK PDU 0x0D-0xFF reserved 0x07 Metadata PDU

The directive table lists no codes 0x0A and 0x0B.78 Several directives carry a 4-bit condition code:79

Code Condition Code Condition 0000 No error 1000 Inactivity detected 0001 Positive ACK limit reached 1001 Invalid file structure 0010 Keep alive limit reached 1010 Check limit reached 0011 Invalid transmission mode 1011 Unsupported checksum type 0100 Filestore rejection 1100-1101 reserved 0101 File checksum failure 1110 Suspend.request received 0110 File size error 1111 Cancel.request received 0111 NAK limit reached

docs.title: Metadata PDU (0x07)
docs.text: The Metadata PDU opens every copy operation. It carries the file size (if known), the source and destination path names as LVs (zero length when no file is involved, as in proxy messages), the closure flag, the checksum type and the option TLVs: filestore requests, messages to user, fault handler overrides and flow label.8340 Making all metadata fit in one Metadata PDU is the implementation's responsibility, and a repeated Metadata PDU is discarded.4043

docs.title: EOF PDU (0x04)
docs.text: The sender issues EOF (No error) when the Metadata PDU and all File Data PDUs have been sent. For an unbounded file this is when the session ends. EOF (No error) carries the file's checksum and length, which may not have been known when the Metadata PDU was sent.8042 On cancellation the sender sends EOF (cancel). Its file size field is the current transmission progress, its checksum covers the data sent so far, and a Fault Location TLV names the entity at which the cancellation began.8067

docs.title: Finished PDU (0x05)
docs.text: The destination sends a Finished PDU when delivery is complete. It is mandatory in acknowledged mode and sent in unacknowledged mode only if closure was requested. The condition code is "No error" if the checksums matched, or "Unsupported checksum type" if no real checksum could be verified.5047 A filestore response TLV accompanies every filestore request of the Metadata PDU.81

docs.title: ACK PDU (0x06)
docs.text: Only EOF and Finished PDUs are acknowledged. The transaction status reports what the acknowledging entity knows about the transaction. Undefined means it keeps no history. If it does keep history, the transaction is Active, Terminated (once active, now ended) or Unrecognized (never active at this entity).82 An ACK confirms receipt only. Entities must always send it, even for unknown transactions, so that the peer's retransmission timer stops.60

docs.title: NAK PDU (0x08)
docs.text:
Parameter Size Meaning Start of scope FSS first offset covered by this NAK End of scope FSS end of the range covered Segment requests (× N) 2 × FSS each start offset and end offset (first octet after the gap) of each missing extent. Missing metadata is requested as the pair 0, 0

The layout is from tables 5-10 and 5-11.84 For small files each segment request is 64 bits.

docs.title: Prompt PDU (0x09) and Keep Alive PDU (0x0C)
docs.text: The Prompt PDU is one parameter octet. Its first bit selects the response wanted (0 = NAK, 1 = Keep Alive) and seven spare bits follow.85 The Keep Alive PDU carries a single FSS progress value, the receiver's reception progress in octets.86

docs.title: File Data PDU
docs.text:
Field Bits Present when Record continuation state 2 segment metadata flag = 1 Segment metadata length 6 (0 to 63) segment metadata flag = 1 Segment metadata 0 to 504 flag = 1 and length > 0 Offset FSS always File data variable always

The table is from table 5-14.87 The record continuation state describes how the segment lines up with the file's records:87

Value Meaning 00 the segment holds neither the start nor the end of a record. This means "continuation" if the segmentation control flag is 1, and "no records" otherwise 01 the first octet starts a record whose end is not in this segment 10 the last octet ends a record whose start is not in this segment 11 the segment starts with the first octet of a record and ends with the last octet of that record or of a later one

Record continuation state must be present when record boundaries are to be respected (flag 1). It may be present otherwise, but then it is always 00. If boundaries are requested but the file has no visible record structure, an Invalid File Structure fault is declared.41

docs.title: TLV options
docs.text:
Type TLV Value 0x00 Filestore Request 4-bit action code, 4 spare bits, LV first file name, LV second file name (for rename, append, replace)88 0x01 Filestore Response action code, 4-bit status code, LV file names, LV filestore message89 0x02 Message to User undefined content. Messages beginning with the ASCII characters cfdp are reserved for the standard user operations90 0x04 Fault Handler Override 4-bit condition code + 4-bit handler: 0001 cancel, 0010 suspend, 0011 ignore, 0100 abandon91 0x05 Flow Label undefined content92 0x06 Entity ID an entity ID, used as the Fault Location93

The filestore action codes are 0000 Create File, 0001 Delete File, 0010 Rename File, 0011 Append File, 0100 Replace File, 0101 Create Directory, 0110 Remove Directory, 0111 Deny File (delete if present) and 1000 Deny Directory (remove if present).88 Response status 0000 means success and 1111 means "not performed". Codes in between give action-specific failures, such as "file does not exist" or "not allowed".89

docs.title: Integrity: CRC and file checksum
docs.text:
PDU CRC. When the CRC option is active, the sender sets the CRC flag and appends the standard CCSDS telecommand CRC to every PDU. The CRC covers everything from the first header octet to the last data octet before the CRC. Its length counts in the data field length. The receiver discards any PDU that fails the check.33 The algorithm is the one in clause 4.2.1.3 of the TC Space Data Link Protocol. See TC SDLP.33

File checksum. Every file is protected by a 32-bit checksum that the sender puts in EOF (No error) and the receiver recomputes.343536 The algorithm is identified by a 4-bit type from the SANA "Checksum Identifiers" registry:34118

Type Algorithm Requirement 0 Modular checksum mandatory 1 Proximity-1 CRC32 (CCSDS 211.2-B-3 annex C) optional 2 CRC-32C (RFC 4960 appendix B) optional 3 IEEE 802.3-2018 FCS optional 4-14 reserved for CFDP 15 Null checksum (value 0) mandatory

The sender uses the type configured in the MIB for the receiver. The receiver uses the type named in the Metadata PDU.3536 If the preferred algorithm is not available, an Unsupported Checksum Type fault is raised. The sender then falls back to the modular checksum and the receiver to the null checksum.34 With a null checksum the file is not protected. The standard recommends implementing one of the stronger algorithms for large files.34

The modular checksum adds 4-octet words modulo \(2^{32}\), with words aligned to file offsets that are multiples of 4 and carries out of the top octet discarded. Data at an offset Q that is not a multiple of 4 is aligned by inserting Q mod 4 zero octets in front. A final group shorter than 4 octets is padded with zeros after it. Because addition commutes, segments can be summed in any order of arrival.37119

Modular checksum (example from annex F)

A 15-octet file 00 01 … 0E is sent in segments of 6, 6 and 3 octets. The words are 00010203, 04050607, 08090A0B and 0C0D0E00 (the last one padded). When the segments arrive out of order, the segment at offset 6 is aligned to 00 00 06 07 08 09 0A 0B. The words are then 00010203, 04050000, 0C0D0E00, 00000607 and 08090A0B, and 04050000 + 00000607 gives the same contribution as 04050607.119 The sum, computed by this wiki, is 0x181C2015.

docs.title: Put and transaction start
docs.text: A Put.request starts a Transaction Start Notification (a new sequence number and a Transaction.indication) and a Copy File procedure. Missing file names mean metadata only. Transmission mode and closure come from the MIB unless the request overrides them.38 No two transactions with activity at the same time may share a transaction ID.38

docs.title: PDU forwarding
docs.text: Each PDU goes to the UT address that the MIB gives for its target entity. ACKs go to the entity that sent the acknowledged PDU. File Data, Metadata, EOF and Prompt PDUs go to the receiver. NAK, Finished and Keep Alive PDUs go to the sender. A PDU whose destination entity ID does not match the entity that receives it is discarded.39

docs.title: Copy File: common procedures
docs.text:
At the sender: Metadata PDU first, then the file data in File Data PDUs (each with its offset), then EOF (No error), and optionally an EOF-Sent.indication. The segmentation algorithm is not specified.404142

At the receiver:4344

  1. Store the transmission mode bit of the first PDU. Declare Invalid Transmission Mode if that mode is not supported.
  2. Store the fault handler overrides, file size, flow label and names from the Metadata PDU. Discard repeated Metadata PDUs. Declare Filestore Rejection if the filestore cannot accept the file.
  3. At the destination, issue Metadata-Recv.indication with any messages to user, and queue filestore requests until the data transfer completes.
  4. Assemble the file from offset and length. Discard duplicate data. Declare File Size Error if any data lies beyond the size given in EOF, or if reception progress already exceeds that size when EOF arrives.
  5. Once Metadata, all File Data and EOF (No error) are in, compute the checksum with the applicable algorithm. If it matches, or if the algorithm is null, delivery is Complete. Otherwise declare File Checksum Failure. The default handler may be "ignore", so the file can still be delivered with a Fault.indication.

docs.title: Unacknowledged mode (Class 1)
docs.text:
Class 1 works over simplex links. A duplex link is needed only if transaction closure is requested.45

  • Sender: sending EOF (No error) completes the transaction (Notice of Completion), unless closure was requested. In that case a Check timer runs. Receiving a Finished PDU stops it, and expiry declares Check Limit Reached.46
  • Receiver: on EOF (No error), if the file is complete it issues Notice of Completion, plus a Finished PDU if closure was requested. If the file is not complete it starts a Check timer and re-examines completeness each time the timer expires, up to an implementation-specific limit, then declares Check Limit Reached. The timer allows for PDUs that arrive after EOF over reordering networks.47

docs.title: Acknowledged mode (Class 2)
docs.text:
Acknowledged mode needs a duplex path.48 The receiver detects gaps: data not starting at offset 0, a hole between extents, or data ending short of the EOF file size. It detects lost metadata when a File Data or EOF PDU arrives before any Metadata PDU.50 Gaps are reported in NAK sequences. Each sequence covers a scope. It starts at the end of the previous sequence's scope, or at 0 for a timer-driven NAK. It ends at the file length if EOF has arrived, or at the current reception progress otherwise. The sequence is split over as many NAK PDUs as the UT_SDU size requires, though normally one is enough.50 The sender retransmits whatever is requested. Its new segments need not match the original segmentation or the NAK boundaries.49

When NAKs are sent depends on the lost-segment detection modes:515253

Mode Trigger Before or after EOF Immediate each gap or lost metadata as soon as it is detected before EOF (No error) only Prompted receipt of a Prompt (NAK) PDU; an empty NAK if nothing is missing before EOF Asynchronous an implementation-specific external event (for example a contact window opens) before EOF Deferred receipt of EOF (No error), then each expiry of the NAK timer while data is missing (scope 0 to end of file) after EOF; required for interoperability in Class 2

An implementation-specific measure of NAK activity, typically the number of NAK-timer expiries without new data, leads to NAK Limit Reached when it hits its limit.54 The receiver may also send periodic Keep Alive PDUs, and must send one in reply to a Prompt (Keep Alive). It stops once EOF arrives. The sender may declare Keep Alive Limit Reached if reported reception progress lags transmission progress by more than a preset amount.55

Positive acknowledgement applies to EOF (expected response ACK (EOF)) and Finished (expected response ACK (Finished)). The sender of the PDU keeps it, runs a timer, retransmits on expiry, counts retries, and declares Positive ACK Limit Reached when the count exceeds the limit.604950

sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Source entity
  participant D as Destination entity
  S->>D: Metadata PDU
  S->>D: File Data PDU (1 .. N)
  S--xD: File Data PDU (N+1) lost
  S->>D: File Data PDU (N+2 .. M)
  D->>S: NAK (N+1)  [immediate mode]
  S->>D: File Data PDU (N+1) retransmitted
  S->>D: EOF (No error, checksum, size)
  D->>S: ACK (EOF)
  Note over D: checksum verified, Notice of Completion
  D->>S: Finished (No error, Data Complete, retained)
  S->>D: ACK (Finished)
  Note over S: Notice of Completion, Transaction-Finished.indication

Redrawn after CCSDS 727.0-B-5 section 7.3.3, the Class 2 event diagram.106

docs.title: Cancel, suspend, resume, report
docs.text:
• Cancel. The sender issues EOF (cancel) and the receiver issues Finished (cancel), each carrying the reason (Cancel.request received, or the fault's condition code). In acknowledged mode they are positively acknowledged with a matching condition code. Any fault during that exchange abandons the transaction.676856
  • Suspend. Ignored if the transaction is already suspended, or if the receiver suspends an unacknowledged transaction. The sender stops Metadata, File Data, EOF and Prompts, freezes the inactivity timer and positive-ack timers, and saves status. The receiver stops NAKs, Keep Alives, the inactivity timer and Finished PDUs. Received EOF and Finished PDUs are still acknowledged, and File Data PDUs are still accepted, so a file can be completely received while suspended.6970
  • Resume reverses suspension and issues Resumed.indication. It is ignored for transactions that are not suspended.58 The standard recommends sending the peer a Remote Suspend or Remote Resume message whenever a transaction is suspended or resumed locally, so both ends stay in step.6957
  • Report. Report.request yields a Report.indication with no protocol exchange.59

docs.title: Faults, filestore actions, inactivity
docs.text: Each fault type has a default handler in the MIB. Overrides from the Metadata PDU replace it, but a receiver cannot know the overrides until the metadata has arrived. Handlers are Notice of Cancellation, Notice of Suspension (only in acknowledged mode, or at the source), ignore with Fault.indication, or abandon with Abandoned.indication. All faults are logged.61 Filestore requests run only if the copy completed without error. They run in order, and stop at the first failure, with later requests reported as "not performed". A filestore failure is never a fault.62 The inactivity monitor declares an Inactivity fault (default handler: cancel) after a period without PDUs. It does not run at the sender of an unacknowledged transaction.63

docs.title: Notices of completion
docs.text: When a transaction completes, the sender releases its retransmission buffer, stops sending and issues Transaction-Finished.indication. In acknowledged mode that indication carries the destination's filestore responses.65 The receiver stops NAKs and Keep Alives, executes the filestore requests if the transaction completed, and either keeps or discards incomplete data from a cancelled transaction, as the MIB says.66 A Notice of Completion (Canceled) can follow a Notice of Completion (Completed). This happens, for example, when the Finished PDU is never acknowledged and the receiver reaches its positive-ACK limit. By then the file has already been delivered.64

docs.title: Link state changes: freeze and thaw
docs.text:
CFDP expects the environment to signal the start and end of transmission and reception opportunities for each remote entity. These are typically pass boundaries shifted by the one-way light time. At the end of an opportunity, affected transactions are frozen. Freezing has the effects of suspension, but it issues no indication and does not count as a suspension. At the next opportunity they are thawed. Unacknowledged reception is never frozen, and thawing has no effect on a transaction that a user has suspended.7172 This is the mechanism that lets one transaction span several ground-station passes. The ECSS handbook calls it the "link lost" signal.135

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Active: Put.request
  state Active {
    [*] --> Running
    Running --> Suspended: Suspend.request or fault handler
    Suspended --> Running: Resume.request
    Running --> Frozen: end of opportunity
    Frozen --> Running: start of opportunity
  }
  Active --> Terminated: completed, cancelled or abandoned
  Terminated --> [*]

The Running, Suspended and Terminated states follow the PUS Rev.1 draft's summary of CFDP transaction statuses.130 The Frozen sub-state is this wiki's addition, based on clause 4.12.71

docs.title: Service classes
docs.text:
Class Purpose Key procedures Class 1, Unreliable Transfer bounded or unbounded files over simplex or duplex paths. Closure only on duplex paths CRC, checksum, Put, forwarding (Metadata, File Data, EOF only), Copy File, unacknowledged mode, resume, report, fault handling (cancel at source, abandon at destination), filestore, inactivity (destination), internal, transmission opportunity104 Class 2, Reliable Transfer bounded or unbounded files with guaranteed delivery all of Class 1, plus acknowledged mode, incremental and deferred lost-segment detection, Keep Alive, positive acknowledgement, cancel response with acknowledgement, and link state change procedures105

State transition diagrams and state tables for each class are in the CFDP implementers' Green Book, which the standard's annex D lists as CCSDS 720.2-G-4 "forthcoming". That book is not in this wiki's library.103113

docs.title: The CFDP MIB
docs.text:
Local entity configuration (one value per entity): local entity ID; whether EOF-Sent, EOF-Recv, File-Segment-Recv, Transaction-Finished (as receiver), Suspended (as receiver) and Resumed (as receiver) indications are required; and the default fault handler for each fault type.107

Remote entity configuration (one set per directly reachable remote entity):108

Item Item Remote entity ID CRCs required on transmission Protocol version number Maximum file segment length (octets) UT address Keep Alive discrepancy limit (octets) Positive ACK timer interval Positive ACK timer expiration limit NAK timer interval NAK timer expiration limit Keep Alive interval Transaction inactivity limit Immediate NAK mode enabled Start / end of transmission opportunity (signals) Default transmission mode Start / end of reception opportunity (signals) Transaction closure requested Disposition of incomplete file on cancellation (discard / retain) Check limit Default checksum type for files sent to this entity

Timer settings must reflect the link, especially the round-trip delay. The ECSS handbook stresses that reliable modes need the necessary return bandwidth and correctly set timers.135

docs.title: User operations
docs.text:
User operations let a user ask the remote user to start transactions. The request is carried in Reserved CFDP Messages, which are Message to User TLVs whose value starts with the 32-bit ASCII identifier cfdp, followed by an 8-bit message type.9495 An Originating Transaction ID message (type 0x0A) links a reply to the request that caused it. It holds the entity-ID length, the sequence-number length, the source entity ID and the sequence number.95

Operation Message types What happens Proxy put 0x00 Put Request, 0x01 Message to User, 0x02 Filestore Request, 0x03 Fault Handler Override, 0x04 Transmission Mode, 0x05 Flow Label, 0x06 Segmentation Control, 0x07 Put Response, 0x08 Filestore Response, 0x09 Put Cancel, 0x0B Closure Request the respondent issues its own Put.request on the originator's behalf. If the beneficiary is the originator, this is a "Get". The result returns in a third transaction with Put Response and Originating Transaction ID969798 Directory listing 0x10 Request (directory name, listing file name), 0x11 Response (1-bit success code) the remote user sends back a file containing the listing99 Remote status report 0x20 Request, 0x21 Response the remote user returns a status report file, a success code and the transaction status values of the ACK PDU100 Remote suspend 0x30 Request, 0x31 Response acknowledged mode only. The response reports whether the transaction is now suspended101 Remote resume 0x38 Request, 0x39 Response acknowledged mode only. Several suspension reasons can apply at once, so a resume may leave the transaction suspended102

The Proxy Put Request contains the beneficiary's entity ID (as an LV) and the source and destination file names (LVs, zero length if omitted). The respondent copies the other proxy options into its own Put.request.97 Proxy operations can invoke core CFDP transfers but not the Store and Forward Overlay.96

docs.title: Store and Forward Overlay (annex B)
docs.text:
The SFO carries files between users whose entities may never be in contact. Each hop is an ordinary CFDP transaction to the next waypoint user, until the agent, the user whose entity can reach the destination directly, performs an SFO final delivery transaction. Reports travel back the same way.109

flowchart LR
  SRC["Source user"] -->|"SFO transmission FDU<br/>(file + SFO Request)"| W1["Waypoint"]
  W1 -->|"relay transaction"| AG["Agent (last waypoint)"]
  AG ==>|"SFO final delivery<br/>(original metadata + SFO Request)"| DST["Destination user"]
  AG -.->|"SFO Report"| W1
  W1 -.->|"SFO Report"| SRC

Redrawn after CCSDS 727.0-B-5 figure B-1.109

  • Message types: 0x40 SFO Request, 0x41 SFO Message to User, 0x42 SFO Flow Label, 0x43 SFO Fault Handler Override, 0x44 SFO Filestore Request, 0x45 SFO Report, 0x46 SFO Filestore Response.110
  • Routing: each user keeps an information base of which entities can receive directly from which others, and computes the shortest route. An empty route fails at once. A route of only the local and destination entities is a plain Put.111
  • Intermediate file names follow the form SFOsourceEntityID_SFOrequestLabel.sfo, without a path. Waypoints should reserve filestore space for files in transit.111112
  • SFO Request fields: 2-bit trace control (0 none, 1 toward source, 2 toward destination, 3 both); transmission mode and segmentation control for the final hop (agent to destination); a closure request bit that controls closure notices at waypoints; 3 spare bits; an 8-bit prior waypoints count (incremented at each hop, with relaying refused at 255); then LV request label (printable ASCII), source entity ID, destination entity ID, and source and destination file names.114115
  • SFO Report report codes: 1 final delivery completed, 2 relay failed, 3 routing failed, 4 relay succeeded, 5 final delivery failed, 6 maximum waypoints exceeded, 7 invalid intermediate file name. The report also carries the condition code, direction, delivery code and file status.116

docs.title: Security
docs.text: CFDP was designed before CCSDS recognised that protocols need protection against attack. It has no security mechanisms. Confidentiality, integrity, authentication and availability must come from the UT-layer stack beneath it.11716 On a space link this usually means SDLS.

docs.title: Worked example: a Class 2 transfer on the wire
docs.text:
The bytes below are illustrative. They were constructed by this wiki from tables 5-1 to 5-9. A ground entity with ID 0x0001 sends a 1 024-octet file a.bin to an on-board entity 0x0017 as b.bin, in acknowledged mode, without CRC. The entity IDs are 2 octets and the sequence number is 4 octets (transaction 5).

Metadata PDU (30 octets):

Octets Value Meaning 0 20 version 001, directive, toward receiver, acknowledged, no CRC, small file 1-2 00 12 data field length 18 octets 3 13 seg. control 0, entity ID length 2 (001), no segment metadata, sequence number length 4 (011) 4-5 00 01 source entity ID 6-9 00 00 00 05 transaction sequence number 10-11 00 17 destination entity ID 12 07 directive code: Metadata 13 00 closure not requested (ignored in acknowledged mode), checksum type 0 (modular) 14-17 00 00 04 00 file size 1 024 18-23 05 61 2E 62 69 6E LV source file name a.bin 24-29 05 62 2E 62 69 6E LV destination file name b.bin

The data PDUs that follow use the same header with the PDU type bit set (first octet 0x30). Each data field is a 4-octet offset followed by file data. The exchange then ends with these directive data fields:

PDU Direction bit Data field Meaning EOF (No error) 0 04 00 <checksum:4> 00 00 04 00 condition 0, checksum, size 1 024 ACK (EOF) 1 06 40 01 acknowledges EOF (0100/0000), condition 0, status Active Finished 1 05 02 No error, Data Complete, file retained (10) ACK (Finished) 0 06 51 01 acknowledges Finished (0101/0001), condition 0, status Active

Inference

Section 4.5.3 sends the ACK of a Finished PDU to the entity that sent the Finished PDU. The source therefore sends it toward the file receiver, and Direction = 0 is used above. The standard does not show the transaction status the source reports in ACK (Finished). "Active" is assumed because the source has not yet issued its Notice of Completion.

docs.title: CFDP and PUS: three ways to move big data
docs.text: PUS does not use CFDP directly. It offers related services, and a newer draft adopts CFDP outright.

docs.title: ST[13] large packet transfer
docs.text:
ST[13] exists because ground-space links usually limit packet length below the CCSDS maximum. A sending entity splits a large packet into numbered parts. Each part travels in one packet, and the receiver rebuilds the original. The services that produce and consume large packets do not need to know this is happening.122 In PUS-C the downlink parts are TM[13,1] (first), TM[13,2] (intermediate) and TM[13,3] (last). Uplink parts are TC[13,9], TC[13,10] and TC[13,11], and a failed uplink is reported with TM[13,16]. A reception timeout bounds the gap between parts.124123 In this wiki's comparison, PUS-C ST[13] differs from CFDP in that it works on packets rather than files, and defines no file checksum, no NAK-based retransmission and no filestore.

PUS-A's ST[13] was a richer "large data transfer" service. It had acknowledgement and retransmission: (13,5) downlink reception acknowledgement, (13,6) repeat parts, (13,7)/(13,12) repeated parts, (13,14) uplink reception acknowledgement, (13,15) unsuccessfully received parts, and (13,4)/(13,8)/(13,13)/(13,16) aborts.128

docs.title: ST[23] file management
docs.text: ST[23] manages on-board files and directories: create, delete, lock, find, report attributes and so on. It also copies and moves files between file systems, including ground to space and space to ground, with TC[23,14] (copy) and TC[23,15] (move). Suspend, resume, abort and status reporting use messages [23,16] to [23,24], among them the TM[23,23] file copy status report. PUS-C explicitly assumes a dedicated file transfer layer such as CFDP below the copy service, but does not standardise that layer.125126127 ST[23]'s filestore operations overlap CFDP's filestore requests. A mission can command them either through PUS or inside CFDP metadata.

docs.title: ST[24]/ST[25] in the PUS Rev.1 draft
docs.text: The December 2024 draft ECSS-E-ST-70-41C Rev.1 introduces File Based Operations. Its new ST[24] file transfer service has a file transaction subservice that adopts CFDP (CCSDS 727.0-B-5) as its protocol, and a file downlink manager subservice that downlinks files from prioritised directories on its own. A new ST[25] service maps on-board data sources into files.129131 ST[24] defines TC[24,1] to TC[24,4] for the start and stop of transmission and reception opportunities, which are CFDP's link state signals. TC[24,5] to TC[24,7] suspend, resume and cancel a transaction. TC[24,8] and TM[24,9] report transaction status, TC[24,10] to TM[24,12] modify and report the remote CFDP entity configuration, and TC[24,13] to TC[24,20] manage downlink managers.133 The local CFDP entity, the on-board one, is linked to exactly one uplink and one downlink communication channel. Its remote entity configuration includes at least the default transmission mode and the positive ACK timer.132 See PUS-A vs PUS-C for the draft's status.

docs.title: Practical guidance from ECSS
docs.text:
The ECSS-E-ST-50 handbook (2008) suggests choosing the class from the link. The forward link is already well protected and may use COP-1 retransmission, so Class 1 with a report of the received file can be enough. The return link can suffer outages, for example on X-band in bad weather, so Class 2 may suit it better.135 CFDP PDUs need a packet service to carry them. For PUS missions the handbook notes that PUS is not strictly needed, because the APID already routes packets between the two entities, and multiplexing PDUs directly into CCSDS packets has the lowest overhead. PUS packets may be used as long as cross-support with another agency's CFDP is not required.135 CFDP retransmits automatically from receiver feedback. It does not support an operator manually requesting a missing segment by telecommand.135

At ESOC, the EGS-CC-based ground systems are to provide a CFDP extension. It wraps a generic ESA CFDP implementation, converts PDUs to and from TM/TC packets, connects them to the EGS-CC file store, and exposes the CFDP engine to monitoring and control.136 See Ancillary systems and EGS-CC.

docs.title: Solar Orbiter: file transfer without CFDP
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter predates the draft ST[24]. It moves files with PUS service 13. Uplinked files (OBCPs, TC files, profiles, ephemerides) are split into a first part with the data unit characteristics, intermediate parts, and a last part with a CRC. The parts go into on-board "partitions". Files from the SSMM, such as science files, come down the same way. Reception can be confirmed at the end, and failed data units can be requested again.137 The 2025 MIB shows two layers:140

Layer Commands (CCF, type 13) Reports (PID, type 13) OBC uplink, APID 172 / 170 (PUS-A subtypes) ZCD00D09 Accept First Uplink Part (13,9), ZCD00D0A intermediate (13,10), ZCD00D0B last (13,11), ZCD00D0D abort reception (13,13), ZCD00D80 change file transfer time-out (13,128) Uplink Reception Acknowledgement (13,14, SPID 14166), Unsuccessfully Received Parts (13,15), Reception Abort (13,16) SSMM downlink "FTS", APID 492 / 483 / 490 / 493 (private subtypes) ZSM00050 Start FTS (13,129), suspend/resume/terminate/abort FTS (13,131 to 13,134), append LLFT (13,135), change EOFT timeout, downlink VC and retransmit limit (13,136 to 13,138), request FTS parameters report (13,139), enable/disable LLFT (13,141), replace/suspend/resume/abort LLFT (13,142 to 13,145), repeat LLFT parts (13,146), confirm correct FDUs reception (13,147), request LLFT EOFT report (13,148), reset FTS queue (13,153) LLFT Start (13,130), FTS Parameters (13,140), LLFT EOFT (13,149), Retransmission OOL (13,150), EOFT timeout (13,151), FDU Layout (13,152)

Inference

The SSMM file transfer system uses CFDP-like terms ("FDU", end-of-file "EOFT", retransmission limit) and is controlled from the ground, which is how CFDP Class 2 would be operated. Its commands, however, are private PUS service 13 subtypes, and none of the Solar Orbiter sources in the library mention CFDP. The expansions of "FTS", "LLFT" and "EOFT" are not stated in the available sources. Solar Orbiter's TM/TC ICD also lists a private Service 133 "File Management".138

Solar Orbiter's on-board file management is the private service 133. This wiki compares it with PUS-C ST[23]; the ICD itself makes no such link. The ICD lists subtypes 6 to 12 (copy file, delete file, modify file, request report, report info, request mapping, report mapping) and 128 (verify file checksum).139 The 2025 MIB holds six service 133 commands on APID 172: ZCD08506 Copy File (133,6), ZCD08507 Delete File (133,7), ZCD08508 Modify File Attributes (133,8), ZCD08509 Request File Information (133,9), ZCD0850B Request Partition Mapping (133,11) and ZCD08580 Verify File Checksum (133,128). It also holds two reports on APID 163: SPID 14319 File Information Report (133,10) and SPID 14320 Partition Mapping Report (133,12).140

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL)
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID FROM ccf
  WHERE CCF_TYPE='13' ORDER BY CAST(CCF_STYPE AS INT);
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR FROM pid
  WHERE PID_TYPE IN ('13','23') ORDER BY CAST(PID_STYPE AS INT);   -- no type 23 packets
SELECT CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, COUNT(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE IN ('13','23') GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE='133';   -- 6 commands, APID 172
SELECT PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE='133';    -- SPIDs 14319, 14320, APID 163

docs.title: COP-1: FOP-1, FARM-1 and the CLCW (CCSDS 232.1-B-2)
docs.text:
The Communications Operation Procedure-1 (COP-1) is the closed-loop retransmission procedure of the CCSDS telecommand link. It runs inside the TC Space Data Link Protocol (and the Unified Space Data Link Protocol) on every virtual channel, and it uses an Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ) scheme of the go-back-n type: the receiver accepts Type-A frames only in strict sequence, and the sender, on any sign of a loss, sends again every frame that has not yet been acknowledged. The result is delivery of telecommands to the spacecraft without omission, duplication or reordering.1

COP-1 is a pair of synchronised state machines per virtual channel: the Frame Operation Procedure-1 (FOP-1) at the sending end, normally on the ground, and the Frame Acceptance and Reporting Mechanism-1 (FARM-1) at the receiving end, on board. The FARM-1 reports its state back in a 32-bit Communications Link Control Word (CLCW), which travels in the Operational Control Field of the telemetry frames.12 This page follows CCSDS 232.1-B-2 (Blue Book, September 2010, with Technical Corrigendum 1 of April 2019), the CLCW definition of CCSDS 232.0-B-4, the ECSS adoption notice ECSS-E-AS-50-26C, the superseded ECSS-E-ST-50-04C (31 July 2008) whose clause 7 was the European COP-1 text, and the real Solar Orbiter documentation and MIB.34106

COP-1 at a glance

Item Value ARQ type Go-back-n, with sliding windows at both ends Sequence numbers 8-bit Frame Sequence Number N(S), all arithmetic modulo 256 Services Sequence-Controlled (AD) and Expedited (BD) Frame types used Type-AD (data, checked), Type-BD (data, bypass), Type-BC (control commands Unlock and Set V(R)) FOP-1 states S1 Active, S2 Retransmit without Wait, S3 Retransmit with Wait, S4 Initialising without BC Frame, S5 Initialising with BC Frame, S6 Initial FARM-1 states S1 Open, S2 Wait, S3 Lockout Report CLCW, usually in the TM or AOS Operational Control Field FOP-1 revision Revision B (FOP-1B), introduced in issue 2 of the old Command Operation Procedures standard; ESA PSS-04-107 used the older COP-1A

Sources: CCSDS 232.1-B-2 §2, §5.1.2, §5.2.1, §5.3.1 and §6.1.2; ECSS-E-ST-50-04C annex B.15678124

docs.title: Why COP-1 exists
docs.text:
Space links are noisy. Correctness of what is delivered is guaranteed, within known probabilities, by the channel coding of the CLTU and by the Frame Validation Checks of the data link protocol. Completeness, order and absence of duplicates on a virtual channel need something else: a numbering scheme for frames and a feedback loop. That is the job of COP-1.9 ECSS-E-ST-50C turns this into a system requirement: a service shall guarantee in-sequence delivery of telecommands, and the space communication system shall support both commanding in the blind and the return of telecommand acknowledgements.10

COP-1 handles, strictly speaking, partial frames: FDUs plus the header fields that COP-1 generates (Bypass Flag, Control Command Flag, N(S)); the rest of the frame is completed by the frame generation procedure.1

docs.title: The two services
docs.text:
Sequence-Controlled Service (AD Service). With high probability no FDU is lost, duplicated or delivered out of sequence. Two frame types are used: Type-AD frames carry the FDUs, Type-BC frames carry the control commands that configure COP-1 (Unlock and Set V(R)). The service is started with one of four "Initiate AD Service" directives; once initialised, FDUs are sent in the order in which they are presented. The guarantee holds per virtual channel only. A Wait mechanism lets the receiver signal that it has no resources for more data.1516

Expedited Service (BD Service). Type-BD frames are sent once, with no retransmission and no guarantee of delivery. FOP-1 gives them immediate access as far as the lower layers allow, and FARM-1 passes their FDUs on immediately. The service is for exceptional situations such as spacecraft recovery, or for use under a higher layer that retransmits by itself. "Expedited" does not mean faster: if a reliable AD service is running, AD is recommended even for urgent data, and an inserted frame must not use the MAP of an unfinished multi-segment transfer.1718

Valid Type-B frames are always accepted by FARM-1 and only counted (in the FARM-B counter of the CLCW). Both frame types are protected by the coding sublayer and must pass the Frame Validation Checks, so accepted Type-B frames are very probably error-free, but their order is not controlled.1 ECSS-E-ST-50-04C put it differently: its expedited service delivers data in order and without duplication, but with possible omissions, and passes a BD FDU on even when FARM-1 is in Wait or Lockout. The two texts agree that nothing is retransmitted; only the CCSDS book declines to promise anything about order.10717

Shared buffers

Some FARM-1 implementations use one buffer for both Type-AD and Type-BD FDUs. A Type-BD frame then erases an FDU that is being delivered or is waiting, without any sign of it in the CLCW. With such receivers the sender should terminate the AD service before using the BD service on the same virtual channel.18

docs.title: Interfaces of COP-1
docs.text:
COP-1 is defined through abstract signals between procedures, not through an implementation.19

At the sending end, FOP-1 sits between the Higher Procedures (segmentation, blocking, conversion of service primitives) and the Lower Procedures (frame generation, multiplexing, coding):20

Signal Direction Parameters Purpose Directive Request Higher → FOP-1 Request Identifier, GVCID, Directive Type, Directive Qualifier From DIRECTIVE.request21 Directive Notification FOP-1 → Higher Request Identifier, GVCID, Notification Type To DIRECTIVE_Notify.indication Asynchronous Notification FOP-1 → Higher GVCID, Notification Type, Notification Qualifier To Async_Notify.indication22 Request to Transfer FDU Higher → FOP-1 Request Identifier, GVCID, FDU, Service Type One per FDU (one service data unit may become several FDUs)23 Transfer Notification FOP-1 → Higher Request Identifier, GVCID, Notification Type Accept, Reject, Positive or Negative Confirm23 Transmit Request for Frame FOP-1 → Lower GVCID, Bypass Flag, Control Command Flag, N(S), data field Hand a frame to the lower procedures24 Abort Request FOP-1 → Lower GVCID Cancel ongoing processing of AD and BC frames, to retransmit quickly24 Response Lower → FOP-1 GVCID, Response Type AD_Accept, AD_Reject, BC_Accept, BC_Reject, BD_Accept, BD_Reject: flow control per frame25

The CCSDS book has an Abort Request cancel only Type-AD and Type-BC processing, and lets it optionally reach into the coding sublayer. ECSS-E-ST-50-04C spells out three details: Type-BD frames are not deleted by an abort, a frame already being radiated as a CLTU is completed rather than cut, and the lower procedures return no response to the abort.24108

At the receiving end, the Lower Procedures validate and demultiplex frames and signal each valid frame with Valid Frame Arrived Indication (GVCID). FARM-1 places an accepted Type-AD FDU in a buffer only if one is free, otherwise the frame is discarded; a Type-BD FDU is placed in a buffer even if none is free, overwriting older data. Each new FDU is announced with FDU Arrived Indication (GVCID), and an optional Aborted Indication may report data erased in favour of a BD FDU. If the on-board flow control can ever set the Wait flag, it must also provide a Buffer Release Signal when space for at least one more maximum-size frame becomes available.262728

docs.title: Directives
docs.text:
An authorised user controls COP-1 of a virtual channel through directives passed with DIRECTIVE.request (in TC-SDLP terms, the COP Management Service). Table 4-1 defines eleven directive types in four groups: four Initiate AD Service directives, one Terminate, one Resume and five FOP-1 Setup directives (Set V(S) and the four Set directives for K, T1_Initial, Transmission_Limit and Timeout_Type). The standard's text calls them "twelve Directives" corresponding to events E23 to E40; the count in the categories and the table is eleven. Any other directive is rejected as invalid.2930

Directive Type Qualifier FOP-1 event Effect (from S6 Initial unless stated) Initiate AD Service (without CLCW check) none E23 Initialise, confirm at once, go to S1 Active Initiate AD Service (with CLCW check) none E24 Initialise, start the timer, go to S4; a clean CLCW with N(R) = V(S) confirms and leads to S1 Initiate AD Service (with Unlock) none E25, E26 If BC_Out_Flag is Ready: initialise, send an Unlock BC frame, go to S5 Initiate AD Service (with Set V(R)) V*(R), the new V(R) E27, E28 If BC_Out_Flag is Ready: initialise, set V(S) and NN(R) to V*(R), send a Set V(R) BC frame, go to S5 Terminate AD Service none E29 In S1 to S5: Alert [term] and go to S6; in S6: just confirm Resume AD Service none E30 to E34 In S6 with SS = 1 to 4: resume in S1 to S4 respectively; rejected if SS = 0 Set V(S) to V*(S) V*(S) E35 Only in S6 and only if SS = 0: set V(S) and NN(R) to V*(S) Set FOP_Sliding_Window_Width new K E36 Accepted in every state Set T1_Initial new T1_Initial E37 Accepted in every state Set Transmission_Limit new limit E38 Accepted in every state Set Timeout_Type new TT E39 Accepted in every state any other — E40 Rejected

Directive list from table 4-1; events and effects from the FOP-1 state table (parts 4 to 6).2911 The four Initiate directives differ in how much they rely on the receiving end. Two of them send a control command and wait for its effect to show in the CLCW, retrying on a timer up to a limit; the other two start without waiting for any receiving-end action, one of them after checking for a good CLCW.15

Notes in the standard: Terminate has no effect on a suspended AD service in S6 (it is accepted and confirmed, but the service stays suspended and the queues are not purged); resume it first, or re-initiate it. Set V(S) is meant for re-aligning FOP-1 with FARM-1 after a break in contact, with V*(S) taken from N(R) of the CLCW, and should not be used while suspended. Setup directives are allowed while AD is active but also affect frames already on the Sent_Queue.31

docs.title: Directive and transfer notifications
docs.text:
For every directive FOP-1 first returns Accept Response to Directive or Reject Response to Directive (if rejected, nothing else follows), then later Positive Confirm or Negative Confirm Response to Directive. A negative confirm carries no reason, but every condition that can cause one also raises an Alert.32

For each Request to Transfer FDU, FOP-1 returns Accept or Reject Response to Request to Transfer FDU; for AD FDUs it later returns Positive Confirm (the FDU was received and acknowledged by a CLCW) or Negative Confirm (COP-1 cannot guarantee the transfer). The user-level XXX_Notify.indication primitives carry the same four types. An AD FDU whose acceptance FOP-1 delays sits in the one-place Wait_Queue, and the Higher Procedures may not submit another until it is accepted or rejected; this is the flow control seen by the user.3334

Between acceptance and Positive Confirm an FDU is in a "gray area": nobody can know yet whether it reached the spacecraft. A Negative Confirm means a break in the sequence-controlled guarantee, and the FDU may or may not have arrived. BD FDUs are only accepted or rejected (there is no Wait_Queue for them, no copy is kept, and no confirmation is given).3435

ECSS-E-ST-50-04C names the span of the guarantee: a sequence-controlled session begins when the management entity receives the Positive Confirm of an Initiate AD Service directive and ends with the next Alert. It also lists cases in which the guarantee does not hold at all: FOP-1 and FARM-1 sequence numbers not synchronised at the start of a session, several FOP-1 instances sending to one FARM-1 at the same time, and CLCWs delivered to FOP-1 from the wrong spacecraft.110109

docs.title: Alert and Suspend
docs.text:
Two asynchronous notifications exist: Alert, with a Reason Code, and Suspend.36 An Alert means an unrecoverable condition and the end of the sequence-controlled guarantee; higher layers may need to recover. After an Alert no further Alert occurs until an Initiate AD directive is received, except Alert [LLIF], which can occur at any time.3738

Reason Code Condition Limit A CLCW negatively acknowledges a frame while Transmission_Limit = 1 T1 The timer expires with Transmission_Count at Transmission_Limit (only if TT = 0), or the transmission limit of a BC frame (Unlock, Set V(R)) is exhausted Lockout The CLCW shows Lockout Synch A CLCW with Retransmit = 0 and N(R) = NN(R) arrives after one with Retransmit = 1; or all frames are acknowledged but Retransmit = 1; or frames are acknowledged during the initialising phase S4 NN(R) A CLCW with an invalid N(R) arrives CLCW A CLCW with Wait = 1 and Retransmit = 0 arrives, or a CLCW with an invalid bit pattern LLIF Lower Layer Interface: FOP-1 and the lower procedures are out of step (a frame is rejected although the Out flag was Ready) Term A Terminate AD Service directive arrived

Restated from table 4-4.37

Alerts linked to the transmission count can be caused by a physical-layer break outside the data link layer. All others report a breakdown of the protocol itself: some part of the system does not work to specification, and earlier reports may have been wrong. Because the VCID in received data may then be corrupt, one failure can raise Alerts on several virtual channels.38 ECSS-E-ST-50-04C adds that after an Alert the management entity should take recovery actions so that no data is lost, duplicated or erroneous; that an implementation may report, with the Alert, the FOP-1 event number and state that caused it; and that FOP-1 should pass further, implementation-dependent status information to management for performance monitoring and diagnosis.111112

Suspend is the deep-space tool: with TT = 1 and a small T1_Initial, FOP-1 sends a sequence of AD frames a set number of times and then suspends itself without clearing its buffers; a later Resume directive continues in the same state.39

docs.title: FOP-1 variables
docs.text:
FOP-1 keeps fifteen variables per virtual channel. The state table and actions, not the variable descriptions, are the master definition.40

Variable Values Role State S1 to S6 Column of the state table V(S) 0–255 N(S) for the next new Type-AD frame Wait_Queue 0 or 1 FDU Holds one AD FDU until FOP-1 can accept it; primary user flow control41 Sent_Queue frames Master copies of all AD and BC frames between first transmission and the end of their processing (positive acknowledgement, or purge by an exception or Terminate)42 To_Be_Retransmitted_Flag per frame Marks frames on the Sent_Queue that still have to be retransmitted, so that CLCWs can be processed while a retransmission is in progress43 AD_Out_Flag, BC_Out_Flag, BD_Out_Flag Ready, Not_Ready Whether a Transmit Request for that frame type is still outstanding at the lower procedures44 NN(R) 0–255 Oldest unacknowledged AD frame; may lag V(R) by the loop delay45 T1_Initial duration Timer start value Transmission_Limit integer Maximum transmissions of the first frame on the Sent_Queue Transmission_Count integer Transmissions so far of the first frame on the Sent_Queue K 1–255 FOP sliding window width TT 0, 1 Timeout type SS 0–4 Suspend state

docs.title: FOP-1 states
docs.text:
State Name Meaning S1 Active Normal state: no recent errors, no flow-control incidents S2 Retransmit without Wait The CLCW shows Retransmit = 1, nothing else exceptional S3 Retransmit with Wait The CLCW shows Wait = 1 (and therefore also Retransmit = 1, because Wait is only set after a frame has been discarded) S4 Initialising without BC Frame After Initiate AD (with CLCW check), waiting for a clean CLCW S5 Initialising with BC Frame After Initiate AD (with Unlock or with Set V(R)), waiting for the BC frame to be sent and a clean CLCW S6 Initial AD service not running: at start-up, after Terminate, after any Alert, and while suspended; only BD frames can be sent

Restated from §5.1.2.5 The initial state must be re-enterable many times during a mission, because the link is interrupted and several sending ends may serve one receiver.5

docs.title: Timer, transmission limit and timeout type
docs.text:
Every transmission of an AD or BC frame starts (or restarts) the timer with T1_Initial; the timer is not used for BD frames. Without it, the loss of the last frame sent would never be noticed. If an acknowledgement arrives and nothing new has been sent, the timer is cancelled.46

For normal operation, T1_Initial must be at least the sum of eight delays:47

  1. processing below FOP-1 at the sending end;
  2. transmitting a maximum-length frame as a serial bit stream, including CLTU and coding overhead;
  3. one-way light time to the receiver (including any relay satellite);
  4. processing below FARM-1 at the receiving end;
  5. the worst-case time to sample FARM-1 status and encode it as a CLCW;
  6. the worst-case time to send the CLCW in the return-link data structure;
  7. one-way light time back;
  8. extracting the CLCW and delivering it to FOP-1.

The transmission limit applies only to the first frame on the Sent_Queue, and the count is reset whenever any frame is acknowledged. So the limit is in effect a property of the queue: each frame is sent at least Transmission_Limit times (unless the limit is 1, in which case nothing is ever retransmitted), and a frame that moves to the head of the queue may be sent more often. When the count reaches the limit, a negative acknowledgement raises Alert [Limit] (limit 1) and a timer expiry raises Alert [T1] if TT = 0 or suspends the AD service if TT = 1. BC frames are retransmitted only on timer expiry, with Alert [T1] when the limit is reached.4849

docs.title: The FOP sliding window
docs.text: The FOP sliding window limits how many frames may be sent ahead of the last acknowledged one, so that a new frame can never carry the same N(S) as a frame that the receiver rejected. A new AD frame is sent only while V(S) < NN(R) + K (modulo 256). K must satisfy 1 ≤ K ≤ PW and K < 256, where PW is the positive window of the FARM.5051 ECSS-E-ST-50-04C warns implementers that comparisons of V(S), N(R) and NN(R) must respect the valid ranges of the sequence number: with K greater than 127 a conventional modulo-256 comparison can give the wrong answer.113

docs.title: Variables and states
docs.text:
FARM-1 keeps nine variables per virtual channel: State, Lockout_Flag, Wait_Flag, Retransmit_Flag, V(R), FARM-B_Counter, and the window widths W, PW and NW.57

State Name Behaviour S1 Open Accepts in-sequence Type-AD frames and passes their FDUs on S2 Wait No buffer is free for another Type-A FDU; entered when an in-sequence frame cannot be stored, left when a buffer is released S3 Lockout Entered when a frame arrives with N(S) outside the range a correctly working FOP could produce; a safe state in which no Type-A FDU is accepted; left only by an Unlock command

Restated from §6.1.2.8

  • Lockout_Flag is 1 exactly in Lockout and Wait_Flag exactly in Wait; both are copied into the CLCW.58
  • Retransmit_Flag is 1 whenever FARM-1 knows a Type-AD frame was lost or discarded for lack of buffer space. At the sender it negatively acknowledges every frame with N(S) ≥ N(R). It is cleared by receiving the frame with N(S) = V(R), by Set V(R) (unless locked out) and by Unlock.58
  • FARM-B_Counter counts valid Type-BD and Type-BC frames. It is not used by either state machine; it gives higher layers a minimal error-control loop for the BD service. Only its two least significant bits go into the CLCW.59
  • V(R) is the N(S) expected in the next Type-AD frame.60

docs.title: The FARM sliding window
docs.text:
The windows protect FARM-1 against an uncontrolled sequence of frames whose N(S) runs at least 256 ahead of V(R), and more generally against a malfunctioning or wrongly set-up FOP-1. The window has a total width W, a positive part PW starting at V(R) and a negative part NW ending at V(R) − 1, the number of the last accepted frame. Everything else (256 − W values) is the lockout area.61

When retransmission is allowed (the normal case), W is an even integer from 2 to 254, fixed for the mission unless otherwise specified (there is no command to change it), and PW = NW = W/2. A received Type-AD frame then falls in one of four cases:6263

Case Condition (modulo 256) FARM-1 action Typical cause In sequence N(S) = V(R) Accept (if a buffer is free), V(R) := V(R) + 1, Retransmit := 0 Normal operation, or a retransmission after a loss Positive window V(R) < N(S) ≤ V(R) + PW − 1 Discard, Retransmit := 1 An earlier frame was lost; retransmission has not started Negative window V(R) − NW ≤ N(S) < V(R) Discard, nothing else Frames resent although already accepted: T1 too short, a link outage, or deliberate repetition in deep space Lockout area otherwise Discard, Lockout := 1, go to Lockout FOP and FARM out of step

If a mission sends each Type-AD frame only once per session (Transmission_Limit = 1), it may set PW > NW, down to NW = 0 and PW = W, with W from 1 to 256. K may never exceed 255 in any case.64 ECSS-E-ST-50-04C spells out one exception to the fixed window: a mission whose commanding performance depends on different window widths in different mission phases fixes W, PW and NW per phase rather than for the whole mission.115

Window arithmetic (illustrative)

With W = 10 (PW = NW = 5) and V(R) = 250: N(S) = 250 is accepted; 251 to 254 are in the positive window (discard and request retransmission); 245 to 249 are in the negative window (silently discarded duplicates); 255 and 0 to 244 are in the lockout area, 246 values = 256 − W. A FOP with K = 5 never has more than five frames outstanding, so none of its frames can land in the lockout area: a new frame falls at V(R) or in the positive window, and a repeat of an already accepted frame falls in the negative window. Constructed by this wiki from §6.1.8.3.1 and §5.1.12.6250

docs.title: FARM-1 actions and state table
docs.text:
The actions are Accept (place the FDU in a buffer and signal FDU Arrived, optionally Aborted for an overwritten BD buffer), Discard, Report (produce the CLCW values) and Ignore. Before the table is applied, FARM-1 checks that a Type-BC frame holds one of the two legal control commands; the table then looks at the Bypass Flag, the Control Command Flag and N(S).6566

Event Condition S1 Open S2 Wait S3 Lockout E1 Type-AD, N(S) = V(R), buffer available Accept, V(R) + 1, Retransmit := 0 N/A Discard E2 Type-AD, N(S) = V(R), no buffer Discard, Retransmit := 1, Wait := 1 → S2 Discard Discard E3 Type-AD, N(S) in positive window, ≠ V(R) Discard, Retransmit := 1 Discard Discard E4 Type-AD, N(S) in negative window Discard Discard Discard E5 Type-AD, N(S) outside window Discard, Lockout := 1 → S3 Discard, Lockout := 1 → S3 Discard E6 Valid Type-BD frame Accept, FARM-B + 1 same same E7 Valid Unlock (Type-BC) FARM-B + 1, Retransmit := 0 FARM-B + 1, Retransmit := 0, Wait := 0 → S1 FARM-B + 1, Retransmit := 0, Wait := 0, Lockout := 0 → S1 E8 Valid Set V(R) to V*(R) (Type-BC) FARM-B + 1, Retransmit := 0, V(R) := V*(R) FARM-B + 1, Retransmit := 0, Wait := 0, V(R) := V*(R) → S1 FARM-B + 1 only E9 Invalid frame Discard Discard Discard E10 Buffer release signal Ignore Wait := 0 → S1 Wait := 0 E11 CLCW report time Report V(R), Lockout, Wait, Retransmit, FARM-B same same
