docs.title: The CLCW
docs.text:
The CLCW is the only reporting mechanism of COP-1. It is defined in the TC Space Data Link Protocol as ten fields in 32 bits:269

Field Bits Values Meaning Control Word Type 1 (0) 0 Distinguishes the CLCW from another report that may share the same field (a TM Type-2 report)70 CLCW Version Number 2 (1–2) 0b00 Version 1, the only one defined71 Status Field 3 (3–5) mission-specific Local enhancements by agencies; not part of COP71 COP in Effect 2 (6–7) 0b01 COP-171 Virtual Channel Identification 6 (8–13) 0–63 VC of the report; each VC in use has its own CLCW71 Reserved Spare 2 (14–15) 0b00 Reserved71 No RF Available 1 (16) 0, 1 0: physical layer available; 1: not available, frames cannot get through without physical-layer action. Common to all VCs; mission defines which RF elements count (for example transponder and demodulator)72 No Bit Lock 1 (17) 0, 1 Optional: 0 bit lock achieved, 1 not; set to 0 if unused. A missing bit lock signals a physical layer working below nominal and a high frame rejection rate72 Lockout 1 (18) 0, 1 FARM-1 of this VC is in Lockout73 Wait 1 (19) 0, 1 The receiving end cannot accept more Type-A data on this VC (for example no storage or processing resources)73 Retransmit 1 (20) 0, 1 One or more Type-A frames were rejected or found missing; speeds up COP-1 by telling the FOP at once74 FARM-B Counter 2 (21–22) 0–3 Two least significant bits of the FARM-B counter of this VC; lets the sender verify that Type-B frames arrived74 Reserved Spare 1 (23) 0 Reserved75 Report Value 8 (24–31) 0–255 N(R) = V(R) of this VC75

Transport. In a TM Transfer Frame the CLCW is a Type-1 report in the 4-octet Operational Control Field (OCF), identified by a type flag of 0 in OCF bit 0; a type flag of 1 marks a Type-2 report, which may carry an SDLS Frame Security Report. The OCF can be associated with the master channel or a virtual channel, and the spacecraft designer must make sure that VCs carrying it are sent often enough that COP-1 does not time out.76 The CLCW reporting rate is a managed parameter; it need not match the uplink frame rate, but some minimum rate is necessary.277

Decoding a CLCW (illustrative)

0x0104002A = 0 00 000 01 | 000001 00 | 0 0 0 0 0 00 0 | 00101010: a CLCW, COP-1, VC 1, all flags clear, FARM-B 0, N(R) = 42. The same report with FARM-1 locked out is 0x0104202A (bit 18 set), and with only Retransmit set it is 0x0104082A (bit 20). Values constructed by this wiki from the field layout.69

ECSS rules and recommended practice. The ECSS adoption of TC-SDLP makes the No Bit Lock flag mandatory: 0 when at least one spacecraft demodulator of the physical channel has bit lock, 1 when none has, always reporting the real physical channel even in the CLCW of an inactive virtual channel.78 The ECSS handbook recommends choosing TC VCIDs with a large Hamming distance from each other, so that a corrupted CLCW is less likely to show another valid VCID, and avoiding the all-zeros and all-ones VCIDs, because a failed or unpowered decoder can produce such CLCWs.79 Both rules come from ECSS-E-ST-50-04C §6.3, which also sets the following:116117

  • the No RF Available flag to be 0 when the RF connection is available through at least one transponder and 1 when through none, and, like No Bit Lock, to report the true physical channel state in every CLCW;
  • the Status Field to be 000 unless the mission defines a use for it;
  • the CLCW to travel in the OCF of a TM (version 1) or AOS (version 2) frame, and to be given to FOP-1 only if it comes from an error-free frame (a successfully corrected frame counts as error-free) of the spacecraft to which the TC virtual channel belongs;
  • the width of the on-board FARM-B counter is left to the implementation: the CLCW carries its two least significant bits, and telemetry may report the full value.

It also notes that the TM virtual channel that carries a CLCW is unrelated to the TC virtual channel the CLCW reports on.116

Use by the ground station. The SLE Forward CLTU service consumes one OCF channel of the return link, extracts the CLCWs and uses their No RF Available and No Bit Lock flags to decide whether the physical channel is available. Its managed parameters clcw-global-VCID and clcw-physical-channel name where the CLCW comes from, and rf-available-required and bit-lock-required decide whether the flags must be clear before production status becomes operational. CLCW evaluation can be switched off by service management.8081

docs.title: Starting the AD service
docs.text:
The four Initiate directives fit different situations. The selection guidance below is this wiki's reading of the state table and directive notes.

Directive Needs from the spacecraft Typical use Without CLCW check (E23) Nothing V(S) already known to equal V(R), or no CLCW available (blind start); immediate S1 With CLCW check (E24) A clean CLCW with N(R) = V(S) before the timer runs out Resuming after a pass when the FARM state is unchanged With Unlock (E25) A clean CLCW after the Unlock frame FARM-1 was in Lockout or Wait; V(S) must already match V(R) With Set V(R) (E27) A clean CLCW after the Set V(R) frame Force both ends to a chosen sequence number V*(R); fails if FARM-1 is locked out 
sequenceDiagram
    participant Op as Operator / higher procedures
    participant FOP as FOP-1
    participant FARM as FARM-1
    Op->>FOP: Initiate AD Service (with Set V(R)), V*(R)=0
    FOP-->>Op: Accept Response to Directive
    Note over FOP: S6 to S5: initialise queues,<br/>V(S) := 0, NN(R) := 0, start timer
    FOP->>FARM: BC frame, data field 82 00 00
    Note over FARM: S1 Open: V(R) := 0, Retransmit := 0, FARM-B + 1
    FARM-->>FOP: CLCW Lockout 0, Retransmit 0, Wait 0, N(R) = 0
    Note over FOP: E1 in S5: confirm, release BC copy,<br/>cancel timer, S1 Active
    FOP-->>Op: Positive Confirm Response to Directive
    Op->>FOP: Request to Transfer FDU (AD)
    FOP->>FARM: AD frame N(S) = 0

Sequence constructed by this wiki from FOP-1 events E27 and E1 and FARM-1 event E8.1112

docs.title: Retransmission and flow control
docs.text: Retransmission starts either on a Retransmit flag in the CLCW or on timer expiry, and always resends all unacknowledged frames; the windows prevent a new frame from reusing the number of a missing one.1 A worked example is in the loop in one picture. If the spacecraft runs out of buffers, FARM-1 discards the in-sequence frame, sets Wait and Retransmit and enters Wait; FOP-1 moves to S3 and stops sending new frames, and when the buffer release signal clears Wait, the next CLCW shows Retransmit alone and FOP-1 resends from N(R).1211 A CLCW showing Wait without Retransmit is a protocol error (Alert [CLCW]), because Wait is only ever set after a frame has been discarded.537

docs.title: Lockout and its recovery
docs.text:
Lockout means that FARM-1 received a Type-AD frame with an N(S) that a correct FOP could not have produced: typically FOP and FARM lost step, for example after a break in contact, a reset of either end, or two sending ends commanding the same receiver, a case COP-1 cannot handle.856 FOP-1 sees the Lockout flag and raises Alert [lockout], ending the AD service.11

Inference: recovery recipe

Unlock clears Lockout, Wait and Retransmit but leaves V(R) unchanged, and a FOP that is initialising with a BC frame (S5) only confirms on a clean CLCW whose N(R) equals V(S). The usual recoveries are therefore either (1) Set V(S) to V*(S) with V*(S) taken from the N(R) of the latest CLCW, followed by Initiate AD Service (with Unlock); or (2) Initiate AD Service (with Unlock), then, once FARM-1 is open, Initiate AD Service (with Set V(R)) to realign both ends on a chosen number (Set V(R) alone does nothing in Lockout). In recipe (2), if V(S) differs from V(R), the first directive cannot get the confirming CLCW (event E1) and, once the BC frame has been sent Transmission_Limit times, ends with Alert [T1] (event E17), although the Unlock itself has reached FARM-1; the second directive then starts from S6. These recipes are this wiki's reading of the state tables and of the note on Set V(S); the operational procedure of a given mission is not stated in the available sources.121131

The SCOS-2000 database ICD strongly recommends defining the BC-frame commands with a global interlock on at least the second uplink verification stage, so that the ground releases no further commands until AD mode has been set up.103 In the Solar Orbiter MIB, UNLOCK and SETVR are defined without an interlock (CCF_ILSCOPE = N); see TC-SDLP control commands.98

docs.title: Deep-space options
docs.text:
On a long-delay link the normal T1 leaves the uplink idle for most of the round trip. COP-1 offers two remedies, which can be combined with the coding sublayer's systematic retransmission:8283

  • Early automatic retransmission. A small T1_Initial forces FOP-1 to resend the whole Sent_Queue several times before any acknowledgement arrives. With TT = 1 it then suspends instead of raising an alert, and is resumed to process the acknowledging CLCWs. The resulting pattern is ABCDEF ABCDEF …; it resists error bursts but loses the rest of a cycle after an early loss.8284
  • Set V(R) without verification. A small T1_Initial lets the Set V(R) command be sent a few times without waiting for its confirmation; the user is alerted when the transmissions are used up and can then issue Initiate AD Service (without CLCW check).82
  • Systematic retransmission in the coding sublayer repeats each CLTU (pattern AAABBBCCC…), which is good against sporadic losses. It is invisible to FOP-1: it changes neither its state nor its counters, and duplicate frames are simply rejected by FARM-1 in the negative window.8285

The CCSDS overview report confirms that the sequence-controlled service still delivers each FDU once and in order even when frames are transmitted several times.83 See the CLTU page for the coding-sublayer side.

docs.title: Blind commanding
docs.text: When no telemetry, and thus no CLCW, is available, the BD service can be used because it does not need the feedback loop. Data then arrives with high probability of being error-free but possibly with gaps. Alternatively the AD service can be combined with multiple transmissions; for deep space this can be more efficient than BD.86 The FARM-B counter in the CLCW lets the sender check afterwards that BD frames arrived.74 The ECSS handbook recommends that near-Earth missions use the sequence-controlled service and keep the expedited service for exceptional situations such as recovery.87

docs.title: Managed parameters
docs.text:
FOP-1 (per virtual channel):88

Managed parameter Allowed values T1_Initial Integer Transmission_Limit Integer FOP_Sliding_Window_Width (K) 1 to 255 (and 1 ≤ K ≤ PW) Timeout_Type 0 or 1

FARM-1 (per virtual channel):77

Managed parameter Allowed values FARM_Sliding_Window_Width (W) 1 to 256; an even number from 2 to 254 when retransmission is allowed FARM_Positive_Window_Width (PW) 1 to 256; W/2 when retransmission is allowed FARM_Negative_Window_Width (NW) 0 to 127; W/2 when retransmission is allowed CLCW reporting period Real number (seconds)

The TC-SDLP managed parameters "COP in Effect" (1), "CLCW Version Number" (1) and "CLCW Reporting Rate" complete the set.89 ECSS-E-ST-50-04C covered the same ground with informative mission configuration parameters of a virtual channel: the four FOP-1 values can be set with directives and may vary during a mission, as may the CLCW reporting rate; the use of the CLCW Status Field is a mission choice; W, PW and NW are fixed for the mission or a mission phase; and the CLCW version and COP in Effect are fixed by the standard. Its physical channel parameters add the operational circumstances in which the expedited service is used.118

docs.title: ECSS adoption (ECSS-E-AS-50-26C)
docs.text: ECSS adopts CCSDS 232.1-B-2 through ECSS-E-AS-50-26C (1 March 2021), which with ECSS-E-AS-50-24C and ECSS-E-AS-50-25C replaces ECSS-E-ST-50-04C, whose clause 7 specified COP-1. The 2019 corrigendum of the CCSDS book does not affect the adoption notice.9091 The notice changes one thing: when a Type-BD FDU is accepted with no free buffer, the buffered data is erased and the FDU Arrived Indication carries a mandatory FDU aborted indication parameter, set exactly in that case, which tells the higher procedures that data were overwritten.92 Its annex records that the special FARM-1 with a single back-end buffer, specified in ECSS-E-ST-50-04C, is not part of the CCSDS book.93 The ECSS handbook explains why: some European on-board hardware has a single back-end buffer per virtual channel, so a new frame can overwrite the previous FDU, and operators must understand the link between uplink and on-board flow control.94 The coding notice ECSS-E-AS-50-24C records the same three-way replacement in its change log.125

docs.title: COP-1 in ECSS-E-ST-50-04C
docs.text:
Clause 7 of ECSS-E-ST-50-04C (31 July 2008) was the ECSS text of COP-1, written against CCSDS 232.1-B-1 (2003). It covers the same ground: FOP-1 and FARM-1 with their variables, the eleven directive types, the eight Alert reasons and the two state tables (its tables 7-8 and 7-9), and it states that its FOP-1 is the updated revision B ("FOP-1B"), whose revision explains the non-sequential numbering of some events. This wiki compared the directive and Alert lists, which match the CCSDS tables above, but not the state tables entry by entry.106119126 Its annex C lists two differences from CCSDS 232.1-B-1, both on the receiving side, and both are what ECSS-E-AS-50-26C still records today:1209293

  • the FDU Arrived Indication always carries the FDU aborted indication, which CCSDS 232.1-B-1 left optional;
  • it specifies how a FARM-1 with only one back-end buffer per virtual channel behaves, a case the CCSDS book did not consider.

The single-buffer rules of §7.5.4 are short. FARM-1 needs at least one front-end buffer for one maximum-length frame and at least one back-end buffer for one maximum-length FDU. With a single back-end buffer a valid Type-BD frame always wins, in all three FARM-1 states: if the buffer is free the FDU is copied and announced normally; if not, the FDU overwrites the previous one, which may have come from a Type-AD or a Type-BD frame, and the FDU Arrived Indication is raised with the aborted indication set. The erasure is invisible in the CLCW, and if the lost FDU came from a Type-AD frame it has already been acknowledged, so the sequence-controlled guarantee is broken. Hence the companion rule of §7.4.4.2: with such a FARM-1 the sending-end management must terminate any ongoing AD service before starting the BD service on the same virtual channel. The standard sees the design's merit in reduced complexity and resource use, hence reliability.121122123

From COP-1A to COP-1B. Annex B of ECSS-E-ST-50-04C records that ESA's Packet Telecommand Standard PSS-04-107 (issue 2, April 1992) specified the older version, now called COP-1A, and that the changes affect only the sending end (FOP-1), not FARM-1. The PSS text also differed around the report: its CLCW Status Field was always zero, it fixed the CLCW sampling through two Standard Insertion Schemes, which ECSS-E-ST-50-04C replaced by project-specific rates, and it spoke of the Command Operation Procedure and the Command Link Control Word; one PSS CLCW field called Report Type became a Reserved Spare.124 The CCSDS book gives the same lineage from its side: FOP-1B was introduced in issue 2 of the old Command Operation Procedures-1 recommendation, FOP-1A being defined in issue 1.7 The history is told on From ESA PSS to CCSDS and ECSS.

docs.title: COP-1 on Solar Orbiter
docs.text:
Spacecraft side. The Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD addresses its two on-board telecommand decoders through two TC virtual channels, VC1 (0b000001) and VC2 (0b000010), and requires the same values in the CLCWs. Every TM frame has the OCF flag set and carries a CLCW (type flag 0) in its OCF. The frame sequence number is V(S) for AD frames and zero for BC and BD frames.959697 The ICD sentence that still calls the suggested VCIDs "Zero and One" appears, from its change record, to be a leftover of an earlier issue;99 see the Solar Orbiter profile of TC-SDLP. Choosing 1 and 2 also avoids the all-zeros VCID that the ECSS handbook advises against.79

In the MIB. The MIB defines the two control frames UNLOCK and SETVR (see TC-SDLP control commands), and decodes the CLCW in two places:100101

  • On board, each decoder's CLCW is reported in the "DMS OBC Status Slow" housekeeping packets TM(3,25) (SPID 19541 on APID 164 and SPID 19550 on APID 162). Decoder A's word sits at octets 29–32, both as the raw 32-bit parameter NCDD05J1 TC Decoder A.PdecCLCW and split into the CLCW fields NCD0Z021 (Type, bit 0) to NCD0Z02D (RepValue, octet 32), including NCD0Z029 LkOt, NCD0Z02A Wait and NCD0Z02B ReTx. Decoder B's word (NCDD05N1) sits at octets 153–156. The bit offsets reproduce the CLCW layout exactly; the 1-bit spare before the Report Value has no parameter. The 3-bit Status Field (NCD0Z023 PDEC_CLCW.A.Status, and NYGD0657 CLCW Status Field on the ground) carries no textual calibration, so the MIB gives it no mission-specific meaning; whether Solar Orbiter uses the field, as ECSS-E-ST-50-04C allowed, is not stated in the available sources.116100101
  • On the ground, the "Good", "Bad" and "Idle mini-transfer frame" packets (SPIDs 66980, 66981 and 66982, APID 1966, type 161, subtypes 5, 4 and 3) each decode a TM frame primary header (octets 0–5), the frame secondary header (octets 6–9), the OCF (octets 10–13) split into CLCW fields, and the FECF (octets 14–15); the Good packet adds the earth reception time. Each packet has its own parameter set: in the Good packet the OCF is NYGG0670 with CLCW fields NYGD0655 to NYGD0668, in the Bad packet NYGG0570 with NYGD0555 to NYGD0568, and in the Idle packet NYGG0770 with NYGD0755 to NYGD0768. Only the Good packet also carries per-VC copies, such as NYGDA663 VC1 Lockout and NYGDB663 VC2 Lockout, which are valid only when the CLCW VC Id parameter NYGD0659 equals 1 or 2; their textual calibrations read, for example, 0 = NO LOCKOUT, 1 = LOCKOUT. The Solar Orbiter data delivery ICD lists these packets as internally generated by the mission control system, to be filtered out by external users.101102

Inference

The mini-transfer-frame packets appear to be how the Solar Orbiter control system turns each received TM frame header and its CLCW into monitoring parameters, so that FOP-1 status and Lockout or Retransmit conditions can be displayed per TC virtual channel. Which ground element runs FOP-1 for Solar Orbiter (the SCOS-2000 telecommand chain or the station interface) is not stated in the available sources. The textual calibration of the on-board NoRF and NoBL fields maps raw 0 to "Asserted" and 1 to "Not_Asserted", which this wiki reads as "RF available asserted" in line with the CCSDS meaning of 0. The ground-side calibrations of the same flags support that reading: they map 0 to "RF" and 1 to "NO RF", and 0 to "BIT LOCK" and 1 to "NO BIT LOCK".100101

EGSE heritage. In the SCOS-2000-based EGSE described by the EMCS user manual, each TC packet sent to the TC front end carries the virtual channel number, the MAP ID and the service (AD = 0, BD = 2). For an AD command the uplink acknowledgement (UL_Ack) reports whether the packet was confirmed through the processing of the CLCW; for a BD command it only reports whether the packet was completely sent. The NCTRS simulator of that EGSE includes a CLCW simulator.105104

SQL used

All queries ran with sqlite3 -readonly on solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL); the 2020 release (solo-2020-04-16.sqlite) gave the same frame-level commands.

-- frame-level commands (BC frames and control segments)
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_CTYPE, CCF_PKTID, CCF_ILSCOPE, CCF_ILSTAGE, CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_CTYPE IN ('F','R');
SELECT * FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('SETVR','UNLOCK','RESET','TC_ONLY','REIN_TTR')
  ORDER BY CDF_CNAME, cast(CDF_BIT AS int);
SELECT * FROM tcp WHERE TCP_ID = 'NO_HDR';
-- high-priority (CPDU) commands
SELECT CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID, CCF_APID, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;
-- CLCW parameters and where they are
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_CURTX, PCF_VALID, PCF_VALPAR FROM pcf
  WHERE PCF_DESCR LIKE 'PDEC_CLCW%' OR PCF_DESCR LIKE '%PdecCLCW%' OR PCF_NAME LIKE 'NYGD%';
SELECT p.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, p.PLF_SPID, p.PLF_OFFBY, p.PLF_OFFBI
  FROM plf p JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = p.PLF_NAME
  WHERE p.PLF_NAME LIKE 'NCD0Z02%' OR p.PLF_NAME IN ('NCDD05J1','NCDD05N1')
  ORDER BY p.PLF_SPID, cast(p.PLF_OFFBY AS int), cast(p.PLF_OFFBI AS int);
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid
  WHERE PID_SPID IN (19541, 19550, 66980, 66981, 66982);
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR IN ('CBCTZ011TM','CYGT0659TM','CYGT0661TM','CYGT0662TM',
  'CYGT0663TM','CYGT0664TM','CYGT0665TM');
SELECT PLF_SPID, PLF_NAME, PLF_OFFBY, PLF_OFFBI FROM plf WHERE PLF_SPID IN (66980, 66981, 66982)
  ORDER BY PLF_SPID, cast(PLF_OFFBY AS int), cast(PLF_OFFBI AS int);
-- the CLCW Status Field parameters (no textual calibration: PCF_CURTX empty)
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_CURTX FROM pcf
  WHERE PCF_NAME IN ('NCD0Z023', 'NCD0Z053', 'NYGD0557', 'NYGD0657', 'NYGD0757');

docs.title: Encapsulation Packet Protocol (CCSDS 133.1-B-3)
docs.text:
The CCSDS Space Data Link Protocols carry only packets whose Packet Version Number (PVN) CCSDS has authorized. The Encapsulation Packet Protocol (EPP) is how anything else reaches a space link, such as an IP datagram, an LTP segment or a private protocol data unit. EPP wraps each such data unit, unchanged, in an Encapsulation Packet. This packet is "Version 8 CCSDS Packet", PVN 0b111. Its header is 1, 2, 4 or 8 octets long, so the overhead can be as small as the data unit allows.411 The 2023 Overview of Space Communications Protocols calls EPP a "shim". It is also the standard carrier of CCSDS-recognized IP datagrams over a space link, through IP over CCSDS.30

This page follows CCSDS 133.1-B-3 (May 2020, with Editorial Change 1 of November 2020), the issue in the library.1 For the fixed-header alternative, see the Space Packet Protocol.

At a glance

Property Value Packet Version Number 0b111 (Version 8 CCSDS Packet)11 Header length 1, 2, 4 or 8 octets, chosen by the Length of Length field10 Packet length 1 to 4 294 967 295 octets9 Encapsulated data 0 to 4 294 967 287 octets, one data unit per packet95 Addressing Encapsulation Protocol ID (3 bits), with a 4-bit extension when the ID is 0b11012 Idle packet Protocol ID 0b000. The shortest is one octet, 0xE0.1213 Length field meaning Total packet length including the header (unlike the Space Packet)17 Security None in EPP; use SDLS or the Bundle Security Protocol23

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
CCSDS first designed the Space Data Link Protocols to carry application-layer data put straight into their data fields. EPP is the shim that defines, without ambiguity, how they can also carry other protocol data units, such as internetworking, file transfer or message transfer protocols.2 A data unit that the data link protocols can carry directly has a CCSDS-authorized PVN, listed in a SANA registry. EPP exists mainly to move data units that have no such PVN.4 The overview of the data link protocols puts it this way. Packets with authorized PVNs go straight through the packet services, and packets without one can be carried by the encapsulation service.36

In 2008, the ECSS communications handbook gave a concrete reason. IPv4 datagrams could be carried directly as packets. The layout of the IPv6 version number, however, required an encapsulation service with low overhead. At that time the authorized PVNs included the Space Packet, the Encapsulation Packet and the IPv4 datagram.4847 The current content of the SANA PVN registry is not in the library, so this page does not list it.

Space Packet or Encapsulation Packet?

Earlier issues of this standard ("Encapsulation Service", 133.1-B-1 and B-2) could wrap a data unit in either a Space Packet or an Encapsulation Packet.3647 Issue 3 removes the Space Packet from the available formats and renames the standard.1 At the same time, Editorial Change 1 of CCSDS 133.0-B-2 made the reference-model figure show that the shim position holds either EPP or SPP.26 Carrying another protocol inside Space Packets is still possible, but it is now a mission-specific use of APIDs and no longer part of EPP.27

docs.title: Position in the protocol stack
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  X["Protocol X data unit<br/>(no authorized PVN)"] --> EPP
  Y["Protocol Y data unit<br/>(no authorized PVN)"] --> EPP
  EPP["Encapsulation Packet Protocol<br/>one data unit = one Encapsulation Packet"] --> PS
  subgraph DLL["Data Link Layer"]
    PS["VC / MAP / Proximity-1 Packet Service<br/>of a Space Data Link Protocol"] --> SCC["Synchronization and Channel Coding"]
  end
  SCC --> PHY["Physical Layer"]

Redrawn after CCSDS 133.1-B-3 figure 2-1.4

EPP is used together with one of the Space Data Link Protocols (TM, TC, AOS, Proximity-1 or USLP). It relies on their Virtual Channel Packet, MAP Packet or Proximity-1 Packet services, and management decides which data link protocol is used.4

docs.title: Service features
docs.text:
• A user of EPP is a protocol entity that sends or receives data units with no authorized PVN.5
  • Each data unit is wrapped unchanged in exactly one Encapsulation Packet. It may be any whole number of octets up to 4 294 967 287, within project limits.5
  • Data units given to one Service Access Point are processed in order. No order is kept between different SAPs. CCSDS recommends no flow-control scheme.5
  • Transfer is one-way, with no timing relationship to the data link mechanisms, and the sender gets no confirmation. The provider may signal gaps, and the sequence is kept, although it may have gaps.5

Inference

Clause 2.2 says an Encapsulation.indication "acknowledges the receipt of the Encapsulation.request". Clause 3 defines the indication as the primitive that delivers a data unit at the receiving end. That earlier sentence looks like a leftover from an earlier issue.58

docs.title: Addressing and service primitives
docs.text:
The user is identified by its Encapsulation Protocol ID (EPI), a value registered in SANA as a "defined Protocol ID". A SAP is identified by three things together: the PVN, the EPI and the SDLP channel that carries the data.6 The SDLP_Channel parameter depends on the underlying service:7

Underlying service SDLP_Channel contains Virtual Channel Packet (VCP) service of TM, TC or AOS Global Virtual Channel Identifier (GVCID) MAP Packet (MAPP) service of TC or USLP Global MAP ID (GMAP ID) Packet service of Proximity-1 Transfer Frame Version Number, SCID, Physical Channel ID, Data Field Construction ID and Port ID Primitive Parameters Generated ENCAPSULATION.request Data Unit, SDLP_Channel, EPI By the sending user, to have a data unit transferred through the data link protocol ENCAPSULATION.indication Data Unit, SDLP_Channel, EPI By the provider, to deliver a data unit to the receiving user. The effect on the user is undefined.

After CCSDS 133.1-B-3 clauses 3.2 and 3.3.78

Two expansions of EPI

The header specification (clause 4.1.2.3) and clause 3.2.3 call the 3-bit field the "Encapsulation Protocol ID" or "Encapsulation Protocol Identifier". The addressing clause 2.3 and Annex B expand the abbreviation EPI as "Encapsulated Protocol Identifier". Both refer to the same field.671225

docs.title: The Encapsulation Packet
docs.text:
An Encapsulation Packet is a Packet Header of 1 to 8 octets followed by an optional Encapsulated Data Field of 0 to 4 294 967 287 octets. The whole packet is 1 to 4 294 967 295 octets.9 The header has three, four, six or seven fields, depending on its length:10

Field Bits Present in header of Values and meaning Packet Version Number 3 (bits 0 to 2) all 0b111, the Encapsulation Packet (Version 8 CCSDS Packet)11 Encapsulation Protocol ID 3 (bits 3 to 5) all The protocol inside. 0b000 is idle, 0b110 means "see the extension", 0b111 is mission-specific private data. Other values are registered in SANA.12 Length of Length 2 (bits 6 and 7) all Length of the Packet Length field: 00 none, 01 1 octet, 10 2 octets, 11 4 octets13 User Defined Field 4 4- and 8-octet headers Mission-specific, privately defined header data14 Encapsulation Protocol ID Extension 4 4- and 8-octet headers Identifies the protocol when the EPI is 0b110; otherwise all zeros. Values are registered in SANA.15 CCSDS Defined Field 16 8-octet header Reserved for future CCSDS use, set to all zeros by convention16 Packet Length 8, 16 or 32 2-, 4- and 8-octet headers Total packet length in octets, header included17

The four header formats, as bit-field diagrams:10

docs.title: Packet Version Number
docs.text: Bits 0 to 2 are 0b111. Like the Space Packet's PVN, the field leaves room for other packet structures. This value identifies the Encapsulation Packet, which the standard calls "Version 8 CCSDS Packet".11 A receiver can therefore tell an Encapsulation Packet from a Space Packet (PVN 0b000) by the first three bits, even when both share one Virtual Channel.1138

docs.title: Encapsulation Protocol ID (EPI)
docs.text:
Bits 3 to 5 name the protocol whose data unit the packet carries. The values CCSDS recognizes are registered with SANA. The standard itself fixes three:12

EPI Meaning 0b000 Encapsulation Idle Packet. It may fill space in a fixed-length TM, AOS or USLP Transfer Frame. 0b110 The 4-bit Encapsulation Protocol ID Extension identifies the protocol. 0b111 Mission-specific, privately defined data others Registered in the SANA "Protocol Identifier" registry

The 2008 ECSS handbook says the registered values then included IPv6, IPv4 and CFDP.47 The present registry content is not in the library.

Inference

The extension field exists only in 4- and 8-octet headers. An EPI of 0b110 is therefore meaningful only with Length of Length 10 or 11. The standard does not state this restriction in so many words.1015

docs.title: Length of Length
docs.text:
Bits 6 and 7 give the size of the Packet Length field:13

Length of Length Packet Length field Header length 00 absent 1 octet 01 1 octet 2 octets 10 2 octets 4 octets 11 4 octets 8 octets

When the value is 00, the EPI must be 0b000. Such a packet is an Encapsulation Idle Packet of exactly one octet, with neither a length nor a data field.13 Receivers must accept both fixed and variable header lengths. A sender may keep one header size, or change the size packet by packet to match the payload and reduce overhead.10

docs.title: User Defined Field, Protocol ID Extension and CCSDS Defined Field
docs.text: These fields exist only in the longer headers. The User Defined Field (4 bits) carries mission-specific header data.14 The Encapsulation Protocol ID Extension (4 bits) identifies the protocol when the EPI is 0b110. Otherwise it is all zeros, and its values are registered in a separate SANA registry.15 The CCSDS Defined Field (2 octets, 8-octet header only) is reserved and set to zeros by convention.16

docs.title: Packet Length
docs.text:
When present, the Packet Length is the last header field. It holds the total length of the packet in octets, header included.17 This differs from the Space Packet, whose length field counts only the data field and subtracts one.29 A 4-octet length field can represent IPv6 "jumbograms" of up to 4 294 967 287 octets (\(2^{32}-5\)), although that use is unlikely in space.17

Header length Packet Length field Packet length Encapsulated Data Field 1 octet absent 1 absent 2 octets 1 octet 2 to 255 0 to 253 4 octets 2 octets 4 to 65 535 0 to 65 531 8 octets 4 octets 8 to 4 294 967 295 0 to 4 294 967 287

All lengths in octets, after CCSDS 133.1-B-3 table 4-2. An implementation may set a lower maximum for the data field.17

docs.title: Encapsulated Data Field
docs.text: The data field follows the Packet Length field with no gap. It is a whole number of octets and contains the data of the protocol named by the EPI (and the extension, if used). With EPI 0b000 it contains idle data. It is absent when the Length of Length is 00, or when the Packet Length equals the header length. Whenever it is absent, the EPI must be 0b000.18 So an Encapsulation Packet with no data is always an idle packet.

docs.title: Encapsulation Idle Packets
docs.text:
An Encapsulation Idle Packet has EPI 0b000 and holds idle data. CCSDS does not specify the idle bit pattern.318 Its value lies in the one-octet minimum. The TM and AOS protocols may fill a frame that must go out at its release time with either an SPP Idle Packet or an Encapsulation Idle Packet. An SPP Idle Packet is at least 7 octets, so in a gap of fewer than 7 octets it spills into the next frame. An Encapsulation Idle Packet can fill a gap of a single octet.3942 USLP goes further. When there are not enough packets at release time, it shall insert one Encapsulation Idle Packet of the right length to complete the frame's data zone.43

flowchart LR
  A["Frame data field<br/>at release time"] --> B{"Space left<br/>after last packet?"}
  B -->|"0 octets"| C["Release frame"]
  B -->|"1 octet"| D["Insert 0xE0<br/>(1-octet idle)"]
  B -->|"2 to 255 octets"| E["Insert 2-octet-header idle:<br/>0xE1, total length"]
  B -->|"256 to 65 535 octets"| F["Insert 4-octet-header idle:<br/>0xE2, 0x00, 16-bit length"]
  D --> C
  E --> C
  F --> C

This wiki's illustration of the fill rules. The header byte values follow from clause 4.1.2. The flow itself is not taken from a CCSDS figure.1043

ECSS took up the option early. ECSS-E-ST-50-03C (2008) already allowed a TM idle packet to be either an idle Space Packet or a "fill encapsulation packet" of 133.1-B-1, and noted that this second option was still being evaluated.45 The 2008 handbook explained that the Fill Encapsulation Packet (the old name) can be one octet long. It also warned that implementations would probably be few for some time.49

docs.title: Procedures
docs.text:
At the sending end, the Encapsulation Function takes data units from users and rejects any that break the size limits. It wraps each valid unit in an Encapsulation Packet and passes it to the packet service of the data link protocol underneath.19 At the receiving end, the De-encapsulation Function takes Encapsulation Packets from that packet service, strips the headers, and delivers each data unit to the user named by the EPI or extended EPI.20

sequenceDiagram
  participant U as Protocol user (sender)
  participant E as Encapsulation Function
  participant L as SDLP Packet Service (VC or MAP)
  participant D as De-encapsulation Function
  participant R as Protocol user (receiver)
  U->>E: ENCAPSULATION.request(Data Unit, SDLP_Channel, EPI)
  alt size outside min/max managed limits
    E-->>U: rejected
  else valid
    E->>L: Encapsulation Packet (PVN 111, EPI, length)
    L->>D: Encapsulation Packet (extracted from Transfer Frames)
    D->>R: ENCAPSULATION.indication(Data Unit, SDLP_Channel, EPI)
  end

Sequence drawn by this wiki from clauses 3.3, 4.2 and 4.3.81920

A data link receiver extracting packets from a frame needs to know where each packet ends. The rule below follows directly from the header definition. It is not a numbered CCSDS procedure.

Parsing an Encapsulation Packet (derived from clause 4.1)

  1. Read octet 0. Bits 0 to 2 must be 111, otherwise the packet is not an Encapsulation Packet. Take the EPI from bits 3 to 5 and the Length of Length (LoL) from bits 6 and 7.
  2. If LoL = 00, the packet is a 1-octet idle packet, so continue at the next octet.
  3. Otherwise the header is 2, 4 or 8 octets for LoL 01, 10 or 11. Read the Packet Length from the last 1, 2 or 4 octets of the header.
  4. The packet occupies Packet Length octets from octet 0. The data unit is Packet Length − header length octets. If the EPI is 000, discard the packet as idle. If the EPI is 110, read the extension from the low 4 bits of octet 1.

This procedure is this wiki's summary of clauses 4.1.2 to 4.1.3.10131718

docs.title: Managed parameters
docs.text:
Managed parameter (table 5-1) Allowed values Defined in Minimum Data Unit Length (octets) Integer §4.1 Maximum Data Unit Length (octets) Integer §4.1 Valid Encapsulation Protocol Identifiers Set of integers Reference [9], the SANA registry "Protocol Identifier for Encapsulation Service" Valid Extended Encapsulation Protocol Identifiers Set of integers Reference [10], the SANA registry "Extended Protocol Identifiers"

After CCSDS 133.1-B-3 table 5-1 and the normative references of §1.7. Annex A2.3 asks SANA to rename both registries (see Edition history).212224

As with other CCSDS protocols, these are long-lived settings, conveyed by a management system rather than in the packets, so that space-link bandwidth is saved.21 The data link protocol also needs to know which PVNs to accept on each Virtual Channel. For TM, "Valid Packet Version Numbers" is a managed parameter of packet transfer.41

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
All byte values below are illustrative, built by this wiki from the header rules.101317

Case Header bytes Explanation 1-octet idle packet E0 111 PVN · 000 EPI (idle) · 00 LoL. Packet length 1. 5-octet idle packet E1 05 + 3 idle octets 111 000 01, then a length of 5 that includes the 2-octet header 10 octets of private data FD 0C + 10 data octets 111 111 01 (EPI 111, mission-specific), total length 12 1000-octet unit, protocol in extension FA, then 0 and the extension nibble, then 03 EC, + 1000 octets 111 110 10, then user-defined 0000 and the 4-bit extension (a SANA value, not shown), then total length 1004 = 0x03EC 100 000-octet unit FF 00 00 00 00 01 86 A8 + data 111 111 11 (private, 8-octet header), user-defined 0000, extension 0000 (required because the EPI is not 110), CCSDS Defined Field 0x0000, total length 100 008 = 0x000186A8

Header size and overhead

For a data unit of n octets, the smallest legal header is 2 octets when \(n \le 253\), 4 octets when \(n \le 65\,531\), and 8 octets beyond that.17 Wrapping the same unit in a Space Packet costs 6 octets of header, and SPP data fields stop at 65 536 octets.28 The 2023 overview gives this lower overhead as the reason the Encapsulation Packet is the more bandwidth-efficient carrier for LTP segments.31

docs.title: Comparison with the Space Packet
docs.text:
Aspect Space Packet Encapsulation Packet PVN 0b000 0b111 Header Fixed 6 octets 1, 2, 4 or 8 octets What is addressed Managed data path (11-bit APID) Carried protocol (3-bit EPI plus 4-bit extension) Length field Data field octets minus 1 Total packet octets, header included Size limits 7 to 65 542 octets 1 to 4 294 967 295 octets Sequence count 14-bit count or name per APID None Extra header space Optional secondary header 4-bit user-defined field in 4- and 8-octet headers Idle form APID 2047, at least 7 octets EPI 000, at least 1 octet Typical payload Application data such as PUS reports and commands, CFDP PDUs IP datagrams, LTP segments, bundles, private PDUs

Compiled from CCSDS 133.0-B-2 clause 4.1 and CCSDS 133.1-B-3 clause 4.1. The "typical payload" row draws on the 2023 overview.28299103431

docs.title: EPP as the carrier for network protocols
IP over CCSDS
docs.text:
CCSDS recognizes two network-layer standards: CCSDS-recognized IP datagrams and the DTN Bundle Protocol.32 Over a space link, the data link protocols can carry IP data units, multiplexed or not, inside Encapsulation Packets. The separate standard IP over CCSDS Space Links (CCSDS 702.1-B-1) specifies how this is done. That standard is not in the library.30 The overview of the data link protocols states it directly: IP over CCSDS uses the Encapsulation Packet as the data structure that holds the IP datagram.37

flowchart TB
  APP["Application-specific protocols"] --> TCPUDP["TCP / UDP"]
  TCPUDP --> IPOC["IP over CCSDS (CCSDS 702.1-B)"]
  IPOC --> EP["Encapsulation Packet (CCSDS 133.1-B)"]
  EP --> SDLP["CCSDS Space Data Link Protocols"]
  SDLP --> RF["RF and Modulation Systems"]

Redrawn after CCSDS 130.0-G-4 figure 4-4.35

In that configuration the Internet is extended into the space segment. Each IP router makes its routing decisions from the destination address, and EPP provides the shim that puts the datagrams into the CCSDS link and takes them out at the other end.35 The overview says this suits missions that need their space segment integrated into the Internet, where connectivity and round-trip light time allow it.35

docs.title: LTP, the Bundle Protocol and CFDP
docs.text:
• LTP usually carries each segment in one link-layer data unit, an Encapsulation Packet. Space Packets are also possible. The overview prefers EPP because its overhead is lower.31
  • The Bundle Protocol reaches links through convergence layer adapters, one of which runs over EPP or SPP (ENCAPCLA in the reference model).33
  • CFDP needs only a simple unitdata service from below. One option given in CCSDS 727.0-B-5 is the Encapsulation service, with the CFDP PDU as the data field of an Encapsulation Packet. The CFDP standard also refers to a Magenta Book, Operation of CFDP over Encapsulation Service (CCSDS 722.1-M-1), which is not in the library.44 See CFDP.

docs.title: Where an ESA ground-segment engineer may meet it
docs.text:
Inference

This section joins sourced facts to show where EPP appears in practice. The assessment is this wiki's own.

  • Telemetry frames from newer spacecraft. A TM or AOS on-board encoder may fill frames with Encapsulation Idle Packets, and a USLP encoder must.394243 Ground packet extraction (in the station, in NCTRS/NIS or in the control system) then has to recognize PVN 0b111 and discard idle packets, as TM receiving ends already do with SPP idle packets.40
  • Not on Solar Orbiter. The Solar Orbiter packet ICD fills frames with idle Space Packets (APID all ones, random data), not Encapsulation Idle Packets.52 Its TM and TC traffic is PUS packets, which are Space Packets (see Space Packet: Solar Orbiter case study).
  • SCOS-2000 and the MIB. The SCOS-2000 import ICD identifies telemetry packets by APID, type, subtype and extra identification fields in the pid table. It has no key for packet version.51 So the MIB has nowhere to describe Encapsulation Packets, and the library sources do not say how SCOS-2000 would handle them.
  • IP, DTN and file-transfer experiments. EPP is the standard way to carry IP datagrams, LTP segments, bundles or CFDP PDUs that should not be wrapped in mission APIDs.303144
  • ECSS context. ECSS-E-ST-50C Rev.1 (2021) shows the "Encapsulation Service" and the "Encapsulation Packet" (CCSDS 133.1-B) under IP over CCSDS in its protocol figure.46 The 2008 handbook listed CCSDS 133.1-B as "support to IPv6 for all ECSS space links". It recommended the Space Packet as the encapsulating packet unless very long data units had to be carried, because few implementations then supported Encapsulation Packets.5047

docs.title: Edition history
docs.text:
Edition Date Main points CCSDS 133.1-B-1 June 2006 "Encapsulation Service", Issue 1, superseded1 CCSDS 133.1-B-2 October 2009 "Encapsulation Service", Issue 2, superseded1 CCSDS 133.1-B-3 May 2020 Removes the Space Packet from the encapsulation formats, renames the standard "Encapsulation Packet Protocol" and adds USLP to the supported data link protocols1 EC 1 November 2020 Updates obsolete page-header text1

Issue 3 also asked SANA to rename two registries, without changing their contents. They are now "Protocol Identifier for Encapsulation Packet Protocol" and "Extended Protocol Identifier for Encapsulation Packet Protocol". The old names referred to the "Encapsulation Service".24 EPP offers no security functions of its own. Authentication, confidentiality and integrity come from SDLS at the data link layer or from the Bundle Security Protocol at the network layer.23
