docs.title: Proximity-1 Space Link Protocol (CCSDS 211.0-B-6)
docs.text:
Proximity-1 is the CCSDS link protocol for proximity space links: short-range, two-way radio links, fixed or mobile, between probes, landers, rovers, orbiting constellations and orbiting relays. Such links have short delays, moderate (not weak) signals and short, independent sessions.1 The ECSS handbook calls it a departure from earlier CCSDS link protocols such as TM and TC: contacts are brief and mission control is remote, with long delays, so the two spacecraft set up the link locally by a handshake (hailing), without precise scheduling, and can renegotiate data rates during the contact.194 Proximity-1 then exchanges data reliably and ends the session itself.6 The Blue Book specifies the data link layer. It covers the Frame, Medium Access Control (MAC), Data Services and Input/Output (I/O) sublayers, the protocol data units, the sequence-controlled and expedited transfer, timing services and the procedures that start and end a session between a caller and a responder.2

This page follows issue 6 of the Blue Book (July 2020, with Editorial Change 1 of September 2024). It adds the USLP annex that maps Proximity-1 onto Version-4 frames, the CCSDS overview Green Book, the ECSS communications handbook and the CCSDS security report.3183193

Issue Date Notes from the document control page 211.0-B-1 October 2002 Original issue, titled "Proximity-1 Space Link Protocol" 211.0-B-2 April 2003 Retitled "...Data Link Layer" 211.0-B-3 May 2004 Superseded 211.0-B-4 July 2006 Superseded 211.0-B-5 December 2013 Superseded 211.0-B-6 July 2020 Current issue: adds text on using the CCSDS Version-4 (USLP) Transfer Frame EC 1 September 2024 Corrects heading numbering in section 2 and paragraph numbering in section 6; A4 page size

Restated from the document control page.3

Proximity-1 at a glance

Item Value Layer Data link layer, in five sublayers: Coding and Synchronization (C&S), Frame, MAC, Data Services, I/O Companion standards CCSDS 211.2 (C&S sublayer) and CCSDS 211.1 (physical layer). Neither is in this wiki's library Protocol data units Version-3 Transfer Frame (or the USLP Version-4 frame), carried in a PLTU PLTU 24-bit ASM 0xFAF320 + frame + CRC-32 Frame length 5 to 2048 octets, with a 5-octet header and a data field of up to 2043 octets Addressing 10-bit SCID with a source-or-destination flag, 1-bit PCID, 3-bit Port ID Frame types U-frame (user data) and P-frame (supervisory PDUs: directives, reports, PLCW) Reliability Sequence Controlled (go-back-n ARQ by COP-P) or Expedited (no retransmission) Report 16-bit Proximity Link Control Word (PLCW) Directionality Full duplex (mandatory), half duplex and simplex (optional) Security None in the protocol; SDLS does not apply to Version-3 frames

Sources: scope, frame structure, PLTU, PICS and security sections of CCSDS 211.0-B-6; the CCSDS security report.222182138198

docs.title: Where Proximity-1 sits
docs.text:
The Proximity-1 model has a physical layer and a data link layer. Work is split into a send side, which radiates the transmitted physical channel and acquires the received one, and a receive side, which processes the received bit stream. The transmitter is driven by states. The receiver, once it is on, has no modes: it accepts every valid local and remote directive and delivers the received data units to the users.10 The physical layer takes control variables and PLTUs from the layers above and performs the requested channel coding. On reception it reports two status signals, CARRIER_ACQUIRED and SYMBOL_INLOCK_STATUS, and outputs the coded symbol stream.11

flowchart TB
    VC["Vehicle controller<br/>(e.g. spacecraft C&DH)"] -- "local directives,<br/>notifications" --- MAC
    U["User data (SDUs)<br/>+ QoS, Port ID, PCID"] --> IO["I/O Sublayer<br/>queues, segmentation,<br/>reassembly, delivery per Port ID"]
    IO --> DS["Data Services Sublayer<br/>COP-P = FOP-P + FARM-P"]
    DS --> FR["Frame Sublayer<br/>build and validate Version-3 frames,<br/>choose next frame to send"]
    MAC["MAC Sublayer<br/>session set-up and end, persistence,<br/>directive decoder, MIB"] --> FR
    FR --> CS["C&S Sublayer (CCSDS 211.2)<br/>PLTU = ASM + frame + CRC-32,<br/>idle, coding, time tags"]
    CS --> PL["Physical Layer (CCSDS 211.1)<br/>transceiver"]
    PL -. "CARRIER_ACQUIRED,<br/>SYMBOL_INLOCK_STATUS" .-> MAC

Sublayers and their main jobs, after section 2.1.4 and figure 2-1 of the Blue Book.1210

The five sublayers divide the work as follows:12

Sublayer Send side Receive side Coding and Synchronization (C&S), CCSDS 211.2 Builds a PLTU around each Version-3 or Version-4 frame, inserts idle data, codes the bit stream Delimits PLTUs, checks them (including decoding), passes valid frames up; time-tags data on request Frame Builds frames and fills in header fields, decides the order of transmission Checks the version, SCID and source-or-destination flag, routes U-frames to Data Services and P-frames to MAC Medium Access Control (MAC) Starts, maintains and ends sessions; changes data rates and other link settings; holds the MIB parameters Accepts directives from the local controller and across the link; sets MODE, TRANSMIT and DUPLEX Data Services Runs FOP-P for Sequence Controlled and Expedited service Runs FARM-P Input/Output (I/O) Accepts SDUs and routing information from on-board users Delivers SDUs to users through the Port ID given in the frame

The CCSDS overview counts Proximity-1 among the Space Data Link Protocols. It notes that Proximity-1, like TC and USLP, uses variable-length frames to suit variable-length messages with different latency needs. Like TC, it has a retransmission procedure, COP-P, which the Green Book calls similar to COP-1.189 The Green Book also expects that future missions may use USLP instead of TM, TC, AOS and Proximity-1. Both Proximity-1 and USLP can run over the Proximity-1 C&S sublayer and physical layer.189190 ECSS-E-ST-50C shows the Proximity-1 suite in its protocol architecture figure, but describes it as only one possible choice for proximity links.207 The Space Packet Protocol Blue Book likewise draws Prox-1 beside USLP, TM, TC and AOS as a data link protocol that can carry Space Packets or Encapsulation Packets.206

docs.title: Terms used throughout
docs.text:
Term Meaning in Proximity-1 Caller / responder The caller starts link establishment and manages any negotiation. The responder usually receives the link parameters from the caller. The caller calls on a prearranged channel with predefined parameters.4 Forward / return link The forward link carries data from caller to responder (typically commands). The return link carries data from responder to caller (typically telemetry).46 Hailing The persistent activity that a caller uses to set up a link to a responder, in full or half duplex. It does not apply to simplex.4 Hailing channel The pair of forward and return frequencies used to set up physical communication.4 Session A dialogue in three phases: establishment, data services (which may include resynchronization and reconnect) and termination. Termination is either coordinated, by exchanging "no more data" directives, or each side decides on its own after communication is lost.6 Reconnect The caller hails the responder again during a session because no progress is being made. FOP-P and FARM-P variables, including the frame counters, are kept.6 Resynchronization The caller sees a sequence count anomaly and forces the responder's counter with the SET V(R) activity.6 U-frame / P-frame A frame carrying user data, or a frame carrying only supervisory protocol data units (SPDUs).57 Vehicle controller The on-board entity (e.g. the spacecraft computer) that receives the notifications of annex D.7 Asynchronous data link A sequence of variable-length PLTUs that are not necessarily back to back. Proximity-1 is currently defined only for asynchronous links.477

Rates have their own names. Rd is the data rate of the PLTU-plus-idle bit stream at the encoder input. Rcs is the coded symbol rate between the C&S sublayer and the physical layer. Rchs is the channel symbol rate at the transmitter output, after optional Bi-Phase-L encoding.9 Bits are numbered as in all CCSDS standards: bit 0 is transmitted first and is the most significant bit, and all spare bits are zero.8

docs.title: Addressing: SCID, PCID and Port ID
docs.text:
Proximity-1 uses a triad of identifiers:15191

  • Spacecraft Identifier (SCID). The SCID names the spacecraft that is either the source or the destination of the frame. A separate bit, the Source-or-Destination Identifier, says which.
  • Physical Channel Identifier (PCID). The PCID can select one of two redundant receivers at the receiving end. Either receiver supports both services.
  • Port ID. The Port ID routes user data inside the receiving spacecraft. A port can be logical, such as an application or a transport process. It can also be physical, such as an on-board bus or a hardware command decoder.

SCIDs for Version-3 frames are assigned by the procedures of CCSDS 320.0. These procedures keep a separate SCID table for each Transfer Frame Version Number. Version 3 ('10') has a 10-bit SCID range of 0 to 1023.28201 See space link identifiers for how SANA assigns them. CCSDS has registered three Port ID uses (bitstream, hardware commands, packets). They are listed on that page.200

docs.title: The Proximity Link Transmission Unit (PLTU)
docs.text:
The PLTU is the data unit of the C&S sublayer. It is sized to fit what it carries: a variable-length frame that holds variable-length packets.14 It consists of:22182

Part Size Content Attached Synchronization Marker (ASM) 3 octets 0xFAF320. The 24-bit marker suits short-delay, moderate-signal links and sets the bit error tolerance for synchronization Transfer Frame up to 2048 octets Version-3 frame (5-octet header + up to 2043 octets of data field) or a Version-4 frame CRC 4 octets CRC-32 for detecting transmission errors

An idle sequence between PLTUs keeps symbol synchronization. PLTUs are inserted only after a physical connection exists.14 The PLTU itself is specified in CCSDS 211.2, which is not in this wiki's library. Because the CRC-32 is outside the frame, frame validation for COP-P is done by the C&S sublayer, not by a frame error control field.14188

docs.title: The Version-3 Transfer Frame
docs.text:
A Version-3 Transfer Frame is a mandatory 5-octet header followed by a data field of up to 2043 octets. A particular implementation may allow less on a given physical channel.23

Field Bits Values Meaning Transfer Frame Version Number 2 (0–1) 0b10 Marks a Version-3 frame. Other values belong to other CCSDS frames.24 Quality of Service (QoS) Indicator 1 (2) 0 / 1 0 = Sequence Controlled service, 1 = Expedited service. At the receiver, COP-P checks the sequence number of Sequence Controlled frames only. Expedited frames bypass the check.2425 PDU Type ID 1 (3) 0 / 1 0 = U-frame with user data, 1 = P-frame with SPDUs.26 Data Field Construction ID (DFC ID) 2 (4–5) 00–11 Says how user data is arranged in a U-frame (table below). Not used in P-frames, where it must be 00.27 Spacecraft Identifier (SCID) 10 (6–15) 0–1023 Spacecraft that is the source or the destination of the data in the frame.28 Physical Channel Identifier (PCID) 1 (16) 0 / 1 Selects which of two concurrently operating receivers processes the frame.29 Port ID 3 (17–19) 0–7 Output port to which the I/O sublayer delivers the SDUs. Must be 0 in P-frames.30 Source-or-Destination Identifier 1 (20) 0 / 1 0: the SCID is the sender (Local_Spacecraft_ID). 1: the SCID is the intended receiver (Remote_Spacecraft_ID).31 Frame Length 11 (21–31) 4–2047 Total octets in the frame minus one, from the first header octet to the last data field octet. The maximum frame is 2048 octets.33 Frame Sequence Number (FSN) 8 (32–39) 0–255 Counts Sequence Controlled frames (SEQ_CTRL_FSN) or Expedited frames (EXP_FSN) separately, per PCID.34

Ranges as listed in the PICS requirements list.134

docs.title: Notes on the header fields
docs.text:
PCID. The PCID is meant for a receiving system with two transceivers working at the same time, for example a primary and a backup. An implementation may also ignore the PCID and accept both values with one set of MIB parameters and one set of state machines, including COP-P. If it does distinguish the two values, each PCID must have its own complete set of MIB parameters and state machines. If only one transponder is powered at a time, the standard advises against using the PCID to select it.29

Port ID. There are eight ports. They are independent of the physical channel, so all SDUs for the same Port ID reach the same port whatever PCID carried them. CCSDS-reserved values are kept in the SANA registries.30

Source-or-Destination and SCID checking. The sender fills the SCID field from its MIB: with Local_Spacecraft_ID when the flag is 0 (source), and with Remote_Spacecraft_ID when it is 1 (destination).31 The receiver validates frames as follows:32118

S/D flag Test_Source SCID compared with Behaviour 1 (destination) true or false Local_Spacecraft_ID A mismatch rejects the frame 0 (source) true RECEIVING_SCID_BUFFER (the remote SCID) A mismatch is a session violation and the vehicle controller is notified. If the buffer is still zero, it is loaded from the first source-flagged frame and used for the rest of the session 0 (source) false (no test) Accepted

Frame Sequence Number. The FSN increases monotonically and separately for the Sequence Controlled and the Expedited frames of each PCID. The SET INITIALIZE MODE directive resets both counters to 0. SEQ_CTRL_FSN drives the sequence check. EXP_FSN plays no part in frame validation but is needed to correlate time tags in the timing services.34

docs.title: Frame Data Field
docs.text:
The data field follows the header without a gap. It holds from zero octets up to the lesser of 2043 octets and Maximum_Frame_Length minus 5.35 In a U-frame the DFC ID says what it holds:27

DFC ID Content of a U-frame data field Rules 00 An integer number of complete, unsegmented packets All for the same Port ID and PCID. The first bit of the data field is the first bit of a packet header.36 01 One segment data unit: an 8-bit segment header and a piece of one packet See below.37 10 Reserved for future CCSDS definition Must not be used.39 11 User-defined data (an octet stream) The user may even send frames with an empty data field.39

In a P-frame the data field holds only SPDUs.39 The packets carried must have a Packet Version Number authorised by CCSDS, such as Space Packets or Encapsulation Packets.18 For the Proximity-1 packet service, the Encapsulation Packet Protocol identifies its channel by TFVN, SCID, PCID, DFC ID and Port ID.202

The segment header holds two Sequence Flags (01 first, 00 continuing, 10 last, 11 whole packet) and a 6-bit pseudo packet identifier. The pseudo packet ID is a temporary label that the protocol assigns to a user packet during segmentation. Segments of one packet must travel in frames with the same PCID and Port ID. Segments of another packet may be interleaved only in frames with a different PCID or Port ID.376 The receiver reassembles by Routing ID, the combination of PCID, Port ID and pseudo packet ID, and delivers only complete packets. It discards the packet being assembled, and logs the event in the session accountability report, in three cases: the packet length field disagrees with the octets received; the first segment for a Routing ID is not a start segment; or a new packet starts before the last segment of the previous one has arrived.38

Same flags as TC

The four sequence flag values are the same as those of the TC segment header (01 first, 00 continuing, 10 last, 11 no segmentation).38203

docs.title: Worked example: a U-frame header
docs.text:
The bytes below are illustrative, built for this page from the field definitions. They are not taken from a real link. Take a Sequence Controlled U-frame that carries whole packets to Port ID 2, which the CCSDS port assignment reserves for packets.200 It is addressed (S/D = 1) to an illustrative spacecraft with SCID 42 on PCID 0. The frame is 205 octets long, so C = 204, and its sequence number is 7:2433

Octet Bits Hex Fields 0–1 10 0 0 00 0000101010 80 2A TFVN 10, QoS 0, PDU Type 0, DFC 00, SCID 42 2–3 0 010 1 00011001100 28 CC PCID 0, Port ID 2, S/D 1, Frame Length 204 4 00000111 07 FSN 7 (a SEQ_CTRL_FSN, because QoS = 0)

The receiver checks that the first two bits are 10, a Version-3 frame (11 would mean Version-4, and 00 or 01 are rejected). With S/D = 1 it compares SCID 42 with its own Local_Spacecraft_ID. It then hands the U-frame to FARM-P, which accepts it only if 7 equals its V(R).118129

docs.title: Supervisory protocol data units (SPDUs)
docs.text: SPDUs carry protocol directives and reports. Directives configure and control the protocol processor at the receiving node, set up, maintain and end sessions, and carry time correlation and synchronization data. Reports describe the configuration and status of the sending node.13 An SPDU is either fixed-length or variable-length, depending on its SPDU Format ID bit. SPDUs identify and delimit themselves, and they are sent only with Expedited QoS.40

docs.title: Fixed-length SPDU: the Proximity Link Control Word (PLCW)
docs.text:
A 1 in the Format ID marks a 16-bit fixed-length SPDU: a 2-bit SPDU header and 14 bits of data. Type 0 is the PLCW. Type 1 is reserved for future CCSDS use.4142 The PLCW reports the progress of the Sequence Controlled service from the receiver back to the sender. It is sent with Expedited QoS.4243

Field Bits Values Meaning SPDU Format ID 1 (0) 1 Fixed-length SPDU.42 SPDU Type Identifier 1 (1) 0 PLCW (1 reserved).42 PLCW Retransmit Flag 1 (2) 0 / 1 0: no outstanding rejections, nothing to resend. 1: a received frame left a gap in the sequence numbers and the expected frame must be retransmitted.46 PCID 1 (3) 0 / 1 The physical channel the report belongs to (from RECEIVING_PCID_BUFFER). Each PCID in use has its own PLCW reporting.45 Reserved Spare 1 (4) 0 Always 0.44 Expedited Frame Counter 3 (5–7) 0–7 Modulo-8 counter showing that Expedited frames have arrived.44 Report Value 8 (8–15) 0–255 The FARM-P variable V(R), reported separately for each physical channel and independently of the I/O port.44

For comparison, the TC CLCW of COP-1 is a 32-bit report carried in the 4-octet Operational Control Field of TM frames.204205 The PLCW fits in 16 bits and is sent inside a P-frame.42

Illustrative example. A responder has accepted frames 0 to 7 (V(R) = 8) on PCID 0 and has counted three Expedited frames. Its PLCW is 1 0 0 0 0 011 00001000 = 0x8308. In a second case, the responder has accepted only frame 0 (V(R) = 1) when frame 1 is lost and frame 2 arrives. V(R) stays at 1 and the Retransmit flag is set: 1 0 1 0 0 011 00000001 = 0xA301 (with the same Expedited count). These values are built for this page from the field definitions.4644129

docs.title: Variable-length SPDUs
docs.text:
A 0 in the Format ID marks a variable-length SPDU. Its 1-octet header carries a 3-bit Type Identifier and a 4-bit Data Field Length. This is the actual number of data octets (0 to 15), not length minus one. The data field holds one or more directives or reports of the same SPDU type.4147

SPDU type Type bits Data field Use Type 1 000 0 to 7 concatenated 16-bit directives or reports Link control (annex B1).4748 Type 2 001 1 to 15 octets: directive type octet + time value TIME DISTRIBUTION (annex B2).4749 Type 3 010 0 to 15 octets Status reports. Their format is enterprise-specific and left to the implementation.50 Types 4–8 011–111 — Reserved for CCSDS.47

docs.title: Type 1 directives and reports
docs.text:
Each Type 1 protocol object is 16 bits long and identifies itself by a 3-bit Directive Type in bits 13–15. Objects are concatenated without gaps. The Directive Type sits at the end of the word so that the format stays compatible with the NASA Mars Odyssey orbiter.14348

Directive Type Object Purpose PICS 000 SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS Sets the partner's transmit frequency, encoding, modulation, data rate and mode M 001 SET CONTROL PARAMETERS Token pass, Remote No More Data, duplex change, time sampling M 010 SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS Sets the partner's receive frequency, decoding, modulation, data rate and mode M 011 SET V(R) Forces the partner's FARM-P V(R) (resynchronization) M 100 REPORT REQUEST Asks for a status report, a time-tag exchange or a PLCW per PCID O 101 Reserved — — 110 SET PL EXTENSIONS Enables physical-layer options outside the core standard M 111 REPORT SOURCE SPACECRAFT ID Reports the sender's own SCID O

Directive types from figure B-1; status from the PICS (M = mandatory, O = optional).144139

docs.title: SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS and SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS
docs.text:
These two directives share one layout. Seen from the forward link, SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS sets the responder's transmit (return) channel and SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS sets its receive (forward) channel. Actual frequencies are defined in the physical layer standard.145154

Field Bits Values Mode 0–2 001 Proximity-1 protocol; 000, 010–101 mission-specific; 110, 111 reserved by CCSDS.150 Data Rate 3–6 Rate before encoding (transmitter) or after decoding (receiver); see the table below.148 Modulation 7 0 coherent PSK, 1 non-coherent PSK.147 Data Encoding / Decoding 8–9 00 LDPC (2048,1024) rate ½; 01 convolutional code (7,½) with inverted G2 and an attached CRC-32; 10 bypass all codes; 11 concatenated R-S(204,188) and CC(7,½). The last option is an ETSI standard and is not needed for cross support.146 Frequency 10–12 Channels 0 to 7: Ch0R–Ch7R for the transmitter, Ch0F–Ch7F for the receiver.145154 Directive Type 13–15 000 (transmitter) or 010 (receiver).145154

Because of the Odyssey implementation, the 8, 32, 128 and 256 kb/s codes also depend on the modulation (NC = non-coherent, C = coherent). Rates of 1, 512, 1024 and 2048 kb/s can only be chosen with SET PL EXTENSIONS:148

Bits Rate (kb/s) Bits Rate (kb/s) Bits Rate (kb/s) Bits Rate (kb/s) 0000 8 NC 0100 128 NC 1000 2 1100 16 0001 8 C 0101 128 C 1001 4 1101 64 0010 32 NC 0110 256 NC 1010 reserved (R1) 1110 reserved (R3) 0011 32 C 0111 256 C 1011 reserved (R2) 1111 reserved (R4)

The data rate follows from the coded symbol rate: Rd = Rcs uncoded, Rd = 0.5 × Rcs with the convolutional code, and Rd = 0.48484 × Rcs with LDPC. The tabulated coded symbol rates run from 1000 to 4 096 000 symbols per second. For example, Rcs = 16 000 gives 16 000, 8000 or about 7757.6 b/s.149

docs.title: SET CONTROL PARAMETERS
docs.text: SET CONTROL PARAMETERS changes zero to four control parameters at once.151 Token (bit 12): 1 passes the half-duplex send token, so the recipient switches to transmit. Remote No More Data (bit 11): 1 tells the recipient that the sender has nothing more to send, so the session can end once the recipient has nothing either. Duplex (bits 6–8): 000 no change, 001 full, 010 half, 011 simplex transmit, 100 simplex receive, 101–111 reserved. Time Sample (bits 0–5): a non-zero value n tells the recipient to capture time and frame sequence numbers for the next n frames. Bits 9–10 are zero.151152153 The illustrative word for "no more data" alone is 0x0011.

docs.title: SET V(R), REPORT REQUEST and REPORT SOURCE SPACECRAFT ID
docs.text: SET V(R) carries, in bits 0–7, the Sequence Controlled FSN to which the partner's receiver must be set. Bits 8–12 are spare.155 REPORT REQUEST asks the remote node for a PLCW for PCID 1 (bit 12) or PCID 0 (bit 11), sent on the PCID the request arrived on. It can also ask for a time-tag exchange (bits 8–10 non-zero) or a status report (bits 3–7). All status report types are still reserved for CCSDS.156157 REPORT SOURCE SPACECRAFT ID lets a transceiver tell its partner its own SCID in bits 0–9.166

docs.title: SET PL EXTENSIONS
docs.text:
SET PL EXTENSIONS turns on or off physical-layer options that are outside the core standard. It exists so that transceivers with extra physical-layer and C&S capabilities can work together.158159

Field Bits Values and cross-support status Direction 0 0 transmit side, 1 receive side.159 Frequency Table 1 0 channels 0–7 of the core directives; 1 extended channels 8–15 (Ch8F–Ch15F forward, Ch8R–Ch15R return).165 Rate Table 2 0 default rate set (required for cross support). 1 extended set: 0000 1000 b/s, doubling up to 1011 2 048 000 b/s, with 1100–1111 reserved. The extended set is required for cross support below 2000 b/s and above 256 000 b/s.164 Carrier Modulation 3–4 00 none, 01 PSK, 10 FSK, 11 QPSK. FSK and QPSK are not needed for cross support.163 Data Modulation 5–6 00 NRZ-L, 01 Bi-Phase-L (Manchester), others reserved. NRZ-L is needed only to work with NASA MRO.163 Mode Select 7–8 00 suppressed carrier (needs a 90° modulation index and differential mark encoding/decoding), 01 residual carrier, others reserved. Suppressed carrier is needed only to work with MRO.162 Scrambler 9–10 00 and 10 bypass, 01 CCITT, 11 IESS. None of these is needed for cross support.161 Differential Mark Encoding 11 1: each output bit is the XOR of the data bit and the previous output bit. Needed only to work with MRO.161 R-S Code 12 0 R-S(204,188), 1 R-S(255,239). Neither code is specified elsewhere by CCSDS, so neither is needed for cross support.160

docs.title: Type 2: the TIME DISTRIBUTION SPDU
docs.text:
A TIME DISTRIBUTION SPDU holds exactly one TIME DISTRIBUTION directive in a 15-octet data field. All time fields use the CCSDS Unsegmented Time Code (see time codes).167

Field Octets Content when the type is TIME TRANSFER (otherwise zero) Directive Type 0 0x00 NULL, 0x01 TIME TRANSFER, all others reserved.167 Transceiver Clock 1–8 Clock value when the trailing edge of the last ASM bit of the transmitted PLTU crosses the clock capture point. 5 octets of coarse time and 3 of fine time.168 Send Side Delay 9–11 Delay between the internal clock capture point and the time reference point. 1 coarse octet and 2 fine octets.168 One-Way Light Time 12–14 Light time between the two reference points, used if the mission decides so. 1 coarse octet and 2 fine octets.168

docs.title: Worked example: a hail P-frame
docs.text:
Illustrative bytes, built for this page. A caller hails SCID 42 and asks it to use the Proximity-1 protocol mode at 8 kb/s coherent with the convolutional code on channel 0 in both directions. The hail directives go in one frame, in this order: SET PL EXTENSIONS (TX) if present, SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS, SET PL EXTENSIONS (RX) if present, SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS. Here no extensions are used.7980104

Octets Hex Meaning 0–4 B0 2A 08 09 00 Header: TFVN 10, QoS 1 (Expedited), PDU Type 1 (P-frame), DFC 00, SCID 42, PCID 0, Port 0, S/D 1, length C = 9 (10 octets), EXP_FSN 0 5 04 Variable-length SPDU header: Format 0, Type 000, 4 data octets 6–7 22 40 SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS: mode 001, rate 0001 (8 kb/s C), modulation 0, coding 01, channel 000, type 000 8–9 22 42 SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS: the same settings, type 010

The P-frame uses Expedited QoS, as every SPDU must. The DFC ID and the Port ID are zero, as required in P-frames.402730 On the wire the C&S sublayer adds the ASM FA F3 20 in front and a CRC-32 behind.182

docs.title: Services and qualities of service
docs.text:
When a user, for example the vehicle controller, hands over an SDU, it also gives the PCID, the quality of service and the destination Port ID.16 There are two data transfer services and a timing service:1718

  • Packet delivery service. Carries packets whose Packet Version Number is authorised by CCSDS. A packet larger than the frame data field is segmented and reassembled. Smaller packets can share a frame. The Port ID selects the output port.
  • User-defined data delivery service. Carries one user's octet-aligned data unit, whose format the service does not know or use. A large SDU is spread over several frames and delivered frame by frame, without reassembly.
  • Timing services. Time-tag frames for time correlation, and transfer time to a remote asset (see timing services).

Each transfer has one of two qualities of service, controlled by COP-P:192021

Sequence Controlled Expedited QoS Indicator 0 1 Mechanism Go-back-n ARQ with sequence numbers at both ends and the PLCW report Sent without ARQ, independently of the Sequence Controlled frames waiting on the same channel Guarantee Within one session without COP-P resynchronization: no SDU lost, duplicated or out of order, with high probability None. SDUs may be sent once or several times, but never again because of a retransmission request. Any such request is handled outside the protocol Segmented packets Reassembled; only complete packets are delivered Reassembled; only complete packets are delivered. User-defined data units larger than a frame are delivered in pieces Typical use Normal reliable transfer Upper layers with their own retransmission, or exceptional cases such as spacecraft recovery Supervisory traffic Not allowed All SPDUs, including PLCWs

The Sequence Controlled guarantee does not cover sessions with a COP-P resynchronization, which may lose or duplicate data. It also does not remove duplicates at the boundary between two sessions; that is left to the controlling data system.62 The ECSS handbook sums up the two grades: in order and without gaps or duplicates, or in order without duplicates but possibly with gaps.196

docs.title: Frame Sublayer: building, validating and choosing frames
docs.text:
At the sending end the Frame Sublayer takes frames from Data Services and MAC, adjusts field values, builds PLCWs and status reports into P-frames, decides the order of transmission and passes frames to C&S. At the receiving end it checks that a frame is Version-3 or Version-4 and that the SCID and S/D flag allow local acceptance. It routes valid U-frames to Data Services, the SPDUs of valid P-frames to MAC, and PLCWs to Data Services.52 Frames are sent only while TRANSMIT is on. When NEED_PLCW or NEED_STATUS_REPORT is true, the report goes into a P-frame.53

Each time a frame is needed, the source is chosen by a fixed priority:54

  1. a frame from the MAC queue;
  2. a PLCW or status report, if the last frame sent was a U-frame (U-frame_last_sent true);
  3. an Expedited frame from the I/O sublayer's Expedited queue;
  4. a Sequence Controlled frame, first from the Sent queue if a retransmission is needed, then from the Sequence Controlled queue;
  5. a PLCW or status report, if U-frame_last_sent is false.

U-frame_last_sent is set true at session start and after any frame other than a report, and false after a PLCW or status report. Steps 2 and 5 therefore alternate reports with user data. While PERSISTENCE is true, only supervisory frames from the MAC queue are sent.54

docs.title: MAC Sublayer: persistence
docs.text:
The MAC Sublayer sets up and ends each session and makes any physical-layer change during data services. Many of these operations are a handshake based on the physical-layer signals. Because a control message may be corrupted on the link, each MAC activity uses a persistence process: the expected result must be confirmed before the next activity starts.5556 A persistent activity uses Expedited QoS and the MAC queue. It consists of one or more actions, such as sending directives, followed by a waiting period for a response. Only one activity runs at a time, but activities can be chained. Three are defined: hailing, COMM_CHANGE and resynchronization (SET V(R)).56

Persistence parameter Meaning ACTIVITY Name of the activity WAITING_PERIOD Time allowed for the RESPONSE before the activity is repeated or aborted RESPONSE The responder's acknowledgement that the activity was accepted NOTIFICATION Success or failure message to the local vehicle controller LIFETIME How long, or how many times, the activity is repeated before it is aborted

Per-activity values are MIB parameters (for hailing: Hail_Wait_Duration, Hail_Response, Hail_Notification, Hail_Lifetime).5790 When an activity starts, PERSISTENCE is set true and the Frame Sublayer sends only from the MAC queue. The activity succeeds if the RESPONSE arrives within the LIFETIME and fails otherwise. In both cases the vehicle controller is notified and PERSISTENCE returns to false.58 MAC_FRAME_PENDING tells the Frame Sublayer that a whole frame is in the MAC queue. A Directive Decoder applies received directives to the configuration of both layers. Two buffers hold the egress and ingress clock times, sequence numbers and QoS for the timing service.5960

docs.title: Data Services Sublayer and I/O Sublayer
docs.text:
Data Services orders the transfer of user data within the session and provides both qualities of service. On the send side it runs FOP-P, processes received PLCWs, confirms complete SDUs to the I/O Sublayer and accepts frames from it. On the receive side it runs FARM-P on received U-frames.6162 FOP-P reports frame-level accounting, V(S) and VE(S), to the I/O Sublayer for every frame it numbers.65

The I/O Sublayer is the interface to on-board data systems. For a Version-3 frame its I/O Port ID is the PCID followed by the Port ID. For a Version-4 frame it is the VCID followed by the MAP ID.66 At the sending end the user gives, for each data unit, the QoS, output Port ID, PDU type, DFC ID, Remote_Spacecraft_ID, PCID and S/D flag. The I/O Sublayer then builds the frame data unit and the header (with the FSN still empty) within Maximum_Packet_Size and Maximum_Frame_Length, segmenting packets if needed.67 All data units in one frame must have the same destination, PDU type, PCID, Port ID, QoS and DFC ID.132 The user is told when an Expedited SDU has been radiated, and when a Sequence Controlled SDU has been acknowledged. For the latter, the I/O Sublayer associates each SDU with the FSN of the frame that holds its last octet and checks it against NN(R).6768 Two queues, Expedited and Sequence Controlled, raise EXPEDITED_FRAME_AVAILABLE and SEQUENCE_CONTROLLED_FRAME_AVAILABLE while they hold frames. A frame taken by Data Services leaves its queue for good. The local directive CLEAR QUEUE can empty a queue.6869 At the receiving end the I/O Sublayer reassembles segments and delivers only complete data units to the port named in the frame. With Version-4 frames these functions pass to the USLP service users.133132

docs.title: Operations: states, variables and events
docs.text: Section 6 of the Blue Book describes operations with state tables and diagrams for full duplex, half duplex and simplex. It applies to both Version-3 and Version-4 frames.76

docs.title: State and operational variables
docs.text:
Four state control variables define each state:778283

Variable Values Meaning MODE inactive, connecting-T, connecting-L, active inactive: transmitter and receiver off. connecting-T: hailing (transmit-connecting). connecting-L: receiver on, transmitter off (listening). active: data services DUPLEX full, half, simplex transmit, simplex receive Set with the local SET DUPLEX directive TRANSMIT (T) on, off Turns the transmitter on or off when MODE is not inactive SS (sub-state) 0–7 Tracks the sequence through the states and selects what goes into the output FIFO

Further operational control variables steer sub-processes:84858687

Variable Values Use X (session termination) 0–5 0 data flowing both ways; 1 local "no more data" received (half duplex); 2 sending RNMD after a local LNMD; 3 local data still pending but RNMD received (half duplex); 4 RNMD received, RNMD to be sent once local data is done; 5 neither side has data, so the session ends after RNMD and X returns to 0 Y (COMM_CHANGE) 0–5 0 none; 1 local request; 2 sending the COMM_CHANGE directive; 3 waiting for acknowledgement; 4 remote COMM_CHANGE directive (RCCD) received; 5 acting on the RCCD (4 and 5 in full duplex only) Z (SYMBOL_INLOCK_STATUS) 0 / 1 Whether symbol lock has dropped during a COMM_CHANGE (state S48) MODULATION on / off Modulates the carrier with coded symbols, or radiates carrier only PERSISTENCE true / false A persistent activity is in progress NEED_PLCW, NEED_STATUS_REPORT true / false Set at initialization, by state transitions, by the PLCW timer and by COP-P. Cleared when the report is selected for output REMOTE_SCID_BUFFER SCID Used to test frames whose S/D flag is destination COMMUNICATION_VALUE_BUFFER link settings Staging area for the HAIL and COMM_CHANGE parameters RECEIVING_SCID_BUFFER SCID Expected remote SCID. Loaded by the vehicle controller or from the first valid frame RECEIVING_PCID_BUFFER 0 / 1 Loaded with the PCID of the first valid received frame

Setting MODE to inactive (also through SET INITIALIZE MODE) resets TRANSMIT, MODULATION and PERSISTENCE to off, off and false. It resets SS, X, Y, Z, the wait timer, the carrier loss timer, the PLCW timer and both FSN counters to 0. SET INITIALIZE MODE also triggers the COP-P initialization events SE0 and RE0.97

docs.text:

In S80 the caller turns its transmitter off for Drop_Carrier_Duration so that the responder loses carrier lock and falls back to S2, while all COP-P variables are kept.78798081

The hailing sequence, as a timeline between the two transceivers:

Events E1 to E11 of table 6-7. The responder may treat SYMBOL_INLOCK_STATUS = true as the Hail response instead of a valid frame; this is an implementation option.10490

The caller starts a session by setting its local transmitter and receiver parameters, loading Test_Source if needed, and issuing SET MODE (connecting-T).113 Each transmission starts with Carrier_Only_Duration of unmodulated carrier, then Acquisition_Idle_Duration of idle pattern for symbol and decoder lock. It ends with Tail_Idle_Duration of idle to flush the receiver's decoders. The same idle generator fills gaps when no frame is ready.88114 Reconnect handles loss of carrier during data services. When the caller's CARRIER_LOSS_TIMER expires (E80), it turns its transmitter off for Reconnect_Wait_Duration, returns to the initial hail settings and hails again (E81). (Table 6-2 calls the carrier-off time Drop_Carrier_Duration, and only that name appears in annex C and in the PICS, item DLL-172. Reconnect_Wait_Duration is not defined as a MIB parameter.)78171141 FOP-P and FARM-P variables are kept. Implementations may use other durations for re-hailing. When the responder's timer expires (E82), it returns to S2 and waits for the hail.105 The carrier loss timer avoids dropping the session on a short fade from multipath or obstruction. When it runs out, the vehicle controller decides whether to end the session or to reconnect.94

docs.title: COMM_CHANGE
docs.text: A COMM_CHANGE changes data rate, frequency or other link parameters during a session. Locally it uses SET TRANSMITTER PARAMETERS and SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS, and possibly SET PL EXTENSIONS. Sent across the link, the same directives form the Remote COMM_CHANGE Directive (RCCD).98 In full duplex (table 6-8) a local request (E12) moves S40 to S48 with Y = 1 and PERSISTENCE true. When no frames are pending, the RCCD is sent (E14, Y = 2). After it has left the FIFO, the caller waits Persistence_Wait_Time (E15, Y = 3) and resends if no answer comes (E18).106 When symbol lock drops (E16) the caller applies its new receiver parameters and sets Z = 1. The first valid frame on the new settings (E17) applies the new transmitter parameters and returns to S41 for re-acquisition. A responder that receives the RCCD (E13) sends its tail idle (E19, E20) and then switches both directions. It sets NEED_PLCW, so that a fresh PLCW confirms the link.106 The response, lifetime, notification and waiting period are the Comm_Change_* MIB parameters.89

docs.title: Session termination
docs.text:
Termination is coordinated through the X variable and the "no more data" signals. LNMD is the local LOCAL_NO_MORE_DATA directive from the vehicle controller. RNMD is the Remote No More Data bit of SET CONTROL PARAMETERS sent across the link.107101

Event (full duplex) From To Action E21 LNMD received S40, X = 0 S40, X = 2 Put an RNMD into the MAC queue and send it E22 RNMD received S40, X = 0 S40, X = 4 Wait for the local side to finish E23 RNMD received S40, X = 2 S40, X = 5 Both done: start terminating E24 LNMD received S40, X = 4 S40, X = 5 Send RNMD E25 no frames pending S40, X = 5 S45 Start Tail_Idle_Duration E26 tail time-out S45 S1 SET MODE inactive; report end of session and the number of octets received E28 local SET MODE inactive or SET INITIALIZE MODE any S1 Same, from any state

Table 6-9.107

docs.title: Half duplex and token passing
docs.text:
In half duplex only one side transmits at a time, and the right to transmit passes back and forth as a token in SET CONTROL PARAMETERS.80151 The sender stays in S50 for at most Send_Duration. When that runs out (E38) it sets PERSISTENCE so that only MAC frames are sent. Once nothing is pending and no PLCW is needed (E39), it puts the token into the MAC queue (S56), sends the tail (E42, S58) and turns around to receive (E43, S62, wait for carrier).10891 The receiver expects transmissions for up to Receive_Duration. It moves from S62 to S61 on carrier lock (E47), from S61 to S60 on the first valid frame (E46), and from S60 or S61 back to transmitting (S51) on receiving the token (E49).108 If the token is missed, the receive timer and loss of carrier lock send it to transmit anyway (E48). The vehicle controller is told about "sender exceeded prescribed transmission interval" (E44), "no data transferred" (E45, E50) and "no carrier received" (E50).108173 After Maximum_Failed_Token_Passes cycles through S50, S56, S58, S62, S51 and S52 without success, E83 puts the caller into S80 to reconnect.109172

Termination and COMM_CHANGE work as in full duplex, but also use X values 1 and 3. Termination passes through the transmit states S54 (Terminate Reply) and S55 (Tail before Quit), and COMM_CHANGE through S56 and S58. If both nodes are out of data, receiving RNMD with X = 2 ends the session at once (E58).111110 PICS lists full duplex as mandatory and half duplex and simplex as optional.138

docs.title: Simplex
docs.text: Simplex is entered from S1 by a "transmit simplex" or "receive simplex" directive (E71 to S71, E72 to S72). Either sets DUPLEX and TRANSMIT and then SET MODE active. A local SET MODE inactive returns to S1 with an end-of-session notification (E73).81112 There is no feedback in simplex, so receipt without gaps cannot be confirmed.195

docs.title: Timers, the output FIFO and what gets transmitted
docs.text:
All timers count down at the MIB frequency Interval_Clock, for example 100 Hz. The event fires when a timer reaches 1, and a timer at 0 is inactive. The wait timer (WT) is loaded from whichever MIB duration the state tables call for. The CARRIER_LOSS_TIMER is loaded with Carrier_Loss_Timer_Duration when carrier is lost in mode active (in full duplex, or in half duplex while receiving), and is cleared when carrier returns. The PLCW timer is reloaded with PLCW_Repeat_Interval after each PLCW and sets NEED_PLCW when it fires. A zero interval means "never".939592 When the output FIFO is empty, the next content is chosen by sub-state and flags:115

SS SPDU pending PERSISTENCE NEED_PLCW SDU pending Loaded into the output FIFO 2, 4 or 7 any any any any Idle (acquisition or tail) 0, 3 or 6 true any any any ASM + P-frame (SPDU) + CRC 0, 3 or 6 false true any any Idle 0, 3 or 6 false false true any ASM + PLCW / status report + CRC 0, 3 or 6 false false false true ASM + U-frame (SDU) + CRC 0, 3 or 6 false false false false Idle

SS = 1 means carrier only, and SS = 5 means transmitter off and receiver waiting for a response. Choosing an SDU asks FOP-P to supply the next frame. No_Frames_Pending fires when the FIFO is empty and nothing is selectable.11596 Running several PCIDs at once is possible but needs concurrent COP-P instances with per-PCID reporting. How their output is prioritised is outside the standard.116

docs.title: Local and remote directives
docs.text: Local directives come from the local controller and never cross the link: SET MODE, SET INITIALIZE MODE, LOCAL COMM_CHANGE (LCCD), LOAD COMMUNICATIONS VALUE BUFFER, LOCAL_NO_MORE_DATA, SET DUPLEX, SET RECEIVING SCID BUFFER and READ STATUS. In the PICS, LNMD and READ STATUS are optional.99100137 Remote directives are sent to the partner. SET TRANSMITTER and SET RECEIVER PARAMETERS put the recipient's MODE into active. Together with SET PL EXTENSIONS they serve both for hailing and for COMM_CHANGE. SET CONTROL PARAMETERS swaps transmit and receive in half duplex, ends the session, changes duplex and sets up the timing service.102103

docs.title: Frame reception and validation
docs.text: Receiving is set up by SET MODE (connecting-L) or (connecting-T). The Frame Sublayer gets its frames from the C&S ChannelAccess.indication primitive. C&S has already delimited them using the frame length field and rejected any with a CRC-32 error.117 Validation then checks the version (10 for Version-3, 11 for Version-4, 00 or 01 rejected) and the SCID rules shown earlier. Each validated Expedited frame increments the Expedited Frame Counter.118 Validated U-frames go to COP-P. In validated P-frames the SPDUs are delimited, PLCWs go to COP-P and all other directives and reports are executed.119

docs.title: COP-P: the Communication Operations Procedure for Proximity links
docs.text:
COP-P works between one sender and one receiver on a direct link. The receiver accepts every valid Expedited frame, and valid Sequence Controlled frames only if they arrive in sequence. It reports its state in PLCWs, and the sender uses them to retransmit Sequence Controlled frames. Expedited frames are never retransmitted. Data can flow both ways at once, so each node runs both a FOP-P (sending) and a FARM-P (receiving).6364

flowchart LR
    subgraph A["Node A (caller)"]
      FA["FOP-P<br/>V(S), VE(S)"]
      RA["FARM-P<br/>V(R)"]
    end
    subgraph B["Node B (responder)"]
      RB["FARM-P<br/>V(R)"]
      FB["FOP-P<br/>V(S), VE(S)"]
    end
    FA -- "forward U-frames, N(S)F" --> RB
    RB -. "PLCW N(R)F in return P-frames" .-> FA
    FB -- "return U-frames, N(S)R" --> RA
    RA -. "PLCW N(R)R in forward P-frames" .-> FB

After figure 4-1. The PLCWs about forward-link progress travel on the return link, and the other way round.64

The FOP-P orders and multiplexes user data, keeps in step with the FARM-P and starts retransmissions. If no valid PLCW arrives within Synch_Timeout, it tells the local controller that it is out of step. If Resync_Local is false, the controller decides how to recover. Otherwise FOP-P forces a resynchronization with SET V(R). The FARM-P is purely data-driven: it reacts to what it receives and relies on C&S (error-free frame) and the Frame Sublayer (valid frame for this node). With Version-4 frames, the use of FOP-P and FARM-P is specified in USLP.64 The ECSS handbook calls the scheme a simplified version of the COP-1 retransmission protocol that uses little bandwidth for acknowledgements.196

docs.title: Modulo-256 arithmetic
docs.text: All COP-P counters are single octets that count modulo 256. A − B is the number of increments that take B to A. B < A means that A − B is between 1 and 127, B > A that it is between 128 and 255, and B = A that it is 0.120

docs.title: FOP-P variables
docs.text:
Variable Type Meaning VE(S) 8-bit Sequence number of the next Expedited frame V(S) 8-bit Sequence number of the next new Sequence Controlled frame VV(S) 8-bit Number for the next Sequence Controlled frame to send. Equals V(S) unless a retransmission is in progress N(R) 8-bit Report Value of the current PLCW: last acknowledged frame + 1 NN(R) 8-bit Report Value of the previous valid PLCW R(R) Boolean Retransmit Flag of the current PLCW RR(R) Boolean Retransmit Flag of the previous valid PLCW NEED_PLCW / NEED_STATUS_REPORT Boolean A new PLCW or status report must be sent (a PLCW whenever its content changes) SYNCH_TIMER countdown Wait for a valid PLCW, loaded from Synch_Timeout (0 = never expires) RESYNC Boolean True while the SET V(R) activity runs

FOP-P keeps one output queue, the Sent queue of frames sent but not yet acknowledged.121122123 Transmission_Window caps the number of unacknowledged frames at 127 or fewer. With a window of 10, the sender must wait for an acknowledgement after 10 frames. Designers should consider the latency added when Sent-queue frames must be resent before new ones.128

docs.title: FOP-P procedures and state table
docs.text:
The procedures used by the state table:124125

  • Initialize: V(S) = VE(S) = VV(S) = NN(R) = N(R) = 0; R(R) = RR(R) = RESYNC = false; NEED_PLCW = NEED_STATUS_REPORT = true; clear the Sent and SEQ queues.
  • Remove acknowledged frames: drop N(R) − NN(R) frames from the Sent queue.
  • Start / Clear SYNCH_TIMER: load Synch_Timeout if the timer is 0, or set it to 0 (clearing does not trigger a resynchronization).
  • Store this PLCW: NN(R) = N(R), RR(R) = R(R).
  • Send EXP frame: take a frame from the EXP queue, number it VE(S), increment VE(S), report VE(S) to I/O and pass the frame down.
  • Resend SEQ frame: copy frame VV(S) from the Sent queue, increment VV(S), pass it down.
  • Send new SEQ frame: take a frame from the SEQ queue, number it V(S), append a copy to the Sent queue, increment V(S) and VV(S), report V(S) to I/O and pass it down.

FOP-P has two states, S1 Active and S2 Resync:127128

Event In S1 Active In S2 Resync SE0 session start-up Initialize (or keep variables when reconnecting) — SE1 Frame Sublayer needs a frame Expedited frame available → send it. Else VV(S) < V(S) → resend (continue a retransmission). Else a new SEQ frame is available and V(S) − NN(R) < Transmission_Window → send it. Else NN(R) < V(S) → start a progressive retransmission: VV(S) = NN(R), resend. Else nothing to send — SE2 valid PLCW If N(R) > NN(R), remove acknowledged frames. If R(R) or N(R) > VV(S), set VV(S) = N(R). Store the PLCW and clear SYNCH_TIMER If R(R) = false and N(R) = NN(R): RESYNC = false, PERSISTENCE = false, go to S1 SE3 invalid PLCW Start SYNCH_TIMER; VV(S) = NN(R) Ignore SE4 SYNCH_TIMER expired Notify the vehicle controller. If Resync_Local: RR(R) = false, RESYNC = true, go to S2 — SE5 / SE6 set Transmission_Window / Synch_Timeout Accept and set Accept and set SE7 reset request Initialize Initialize, go to S1 SE8 invalid request Reject Reject

A PLCW is invalid if it does not match the PLCW format, if N(R) < NN(R) (too small), if N(R) > V(S) (too large), if R(R) is set while N(R) = V(S) (retransmit requested although everything is acknowledged), or if the retransmit flag clears without any new acknowledgement (R(R) false, RR(R) true, N(R) = NN(R)).128

Resynchronization (SET V(R) persistent activity). The activity uses the MIB parameters Resync_Waiting_Period, Resync_Response, Resync_Notification and Resync_Lifetime, with Resync_Local true. FOP-P sets RESYNC. The MAC Sublayer then builds a SET V(R) directive with NN(R) as the FSN and the PCID of this FOP-P, queues it in the MAC queue and sets PERSISTENCE. The activity ends when a valid PLCW shows N(R) = NN(R) with R(R) false, or when Resync_Lifetime expires.126127

Inconsistencies in the source

The text of 7.2.2 and the state table do not agree on event numbers. Clause 7.2.2 i) says that SYNCH_TIMER expiry triggers "SE6", and 7.2.2 j) that RESYNC is reset by "SE7". In the state table SE4 is the timer expiry, SE6 sets Synch_Timeout and SE7 is the reset request, while RESYNC is cleared under SE2 in state S2. Likewise 4.2.2.3 points to tables 6-8 and 6-11 for hailing and to 6-9 and 6-12 for COMM_CHANGE, but hailing is in tables 6-7 and 6-10 and COMM_CHANGE in 6-8 and 6-11. This page follows the tables.1231275676

docs.title: FARM-P
docs.text:
The receiver keeps four variables: V(R), the last acknowledged Sequence Controlled frame + 1; R(S), the retransmit flag copied into the PLCW; N(S), the FSN of the arriving frame; and the 3-bit Expedited Frame Counter.130 Its state table has one state:129

Event Action RE0 session start R(S) = false, V(R) = 0, Expedited Frame Counter = 0, NEED_PLCW and NEED_STATUS_REPORT = true RE1 invalid frame Discard RE2 valid SET V(R) R(S) = false, V(R) = the FSN in the directive, NEED_PLCW = true RE3 valid Expedited frame Pass to I/O, increment the Expedited Frame Counter RE4 valid Sequence Controlled frame, N(S) = V(R) Pass to I/O, R(S) = false, increment V(R), NEED_PLCW = true RE5 N(S) > V(R) (gap) Discard, R(S) = true, NEED_PLCW = true RE6 N(S) < V(R) (already received) Discard RE7 Frame Sublayer asks for PLCW content Report R(S), V(R) and the Expedited Frame Counter

FARM-P passes valid Expedited and in-sequence U-frames to the I/O Sublayer, which buffers and reassembles them and delivers the result through the output port.131

docs.title: Worked example: a lost frame
docs.text:
The trace below is illustrative. It applies the FOP-P and FARM-P tables to a link where Sequence Controlled frame 1 is lost and the window is 10:127129128

sequenceDiagram
    participant F as FOP-P (sender)
    participant R as FARM-P (receiver)
    F->>R: U-frame N(S)=0 (V(S) becomes 1)
    Note over R: RE4 in sequence, V(R)=1
    F--xR: U-frame N(S)=1 lost (V(S)=2)
    F->>R: U-frame N(S)=2 (V(S)=3)
    Note over R: RE5 gap: discard, R(S)=true
    R->>F: PLCW Report Value 1, Retransmit 1
    Note over F: SE2 valid: N(R)=1 > NN(R)=0, remove frame 0.<br/>R(R) true, so VV(S)=1. Store: NN(R)=1
    F->>R: resend N(S)=1 (VV(S) becomes 2)
    Note over R: RE4, V(R)=2, R(S)=false
    F->>R: resend N(S)=2 (VV(S)=3=V(S))
    Note over R: RE4, V(R)=3
    R->>F: PLCW Report Value 3, Retransmit 0
    Note over F: SE2: remove frames 1 and 2, NN(R)=3

This is the go-back-n behaviour: after a gap, FARM-P discards everything until the missing frame arrives, and FOP-P resends from the first unacknowledged frame.20129

docs.title: Timing services
docs.text:
Proximity-1 defines two timing services for Version-3 or Version-4 frames. They provide information for a time correlation function that is outside the standard. Implementations may offer further parameters.70

Time tag recording. When time tagging is active, a transceiver records the time at which the trailing edge of the last ASM bit of every incoming and outgoing frame crosses its clock capture point. All tags must be correlatable to the enterprise-defined time reference point. MODE must be active, in full or half duplex or in simplex, and tagging may run alongside data transfer. The vehicle controller asks its initiator to send SET CONTROL PARAMETERS with a Time Sample value n. Both MAC sublayers then capture local time, frame sequence number, direction and QoS for n frames and package them for time correlation.7172 The correlation process needs both data sets, the relation of one clock to UTC, all path delays (the spacecraft builder measures those from antenna to radio port, the radio builder those inside the radio, which depend on coding, symbol rate and mode) and the time code formats. Collecting tags in both directions at once improves accuracy.73

Time transfer to a remote asset. Every transceiver must be able to distribute time. The initiator's vehicle controller may first add the one-way light time to the enterprise time at the planned instant, formatted as a CCSDS Unsegmented Time Code. It then commands a TIME DISTRIBUTION directive with that time, the sender path delay and the OWLT, if used. The responder sets its clock and may add the delays according to its accuracy needs. Accuracy depends on the initiator's own time error, the latency up to transmission, the OWLT accuracy and the delay until the remote master clock is loaded.7475 The ECSS handbook adds that timing services provide time correlation data among units and time-derived ranging measurements.196

docs.title: Management Information Base (MIB) parameters
docs.text:
Proximity-1 uses the word MIB for its own configuration parameters. They have nothing to do with the SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base. The parameters are fixed for a session ("session static") unless noted. Layers: P physical, C C&S, F frame, M MAC, D data services, I I/O, U USLP.169

Parameter Status Layer Use Acquisition_Idle_Duration M P, M Idle pattern after carrier only, for symbol and decoder lock Carrier_Loss_Timer_Duration M D Grace period after carrier loss (full and half duplex) Carrier_Only_Duration M P, M Unmodulated carrier at the start of each transmission Comm_Change_Lifetime M M Duration or repetitions of the COMM_CHANGE activity Comm_Change_Notification M M Success or failure notice to the vehicle controller Comm_Change_Response M M The responder's acknowledgement (events E17, E20, E68) Comm_Change_Waiting_Period M M Time the caller waits for the response Drop_Carrier_Duration M D Carrier-off time that forces the responder back to S2 (reconnect) Frame Version in use — F, U 3 (Proximity-1) or 4 (USLP) Hail_Lifetime M M Duration or repetitions of the hailing activity Hail_Notification M M Hailing success or failure notice Hail_Response M M A valid frame, or (implementation option) symbol lock Hail_Wait_Duration M M Time the caller waits for a response to each hail Hailing_Channel M P, M Enterprise-specific forward/return frequency pair for establishment Hailing_Data_Rate M P, M Data rate during hailing Interval_Clock M C Frequency used by all timers (e.g. 100 Hz) Local_PCID O M PCID of the local receiver Local_Spacecraft_ID M M Own SCID, checked on destination-flagged frames Maximum_Failed_Token_Passes O D Half-duplex token cycles before reconnect (E83) Maximum_Frame_Length M F, U Largest frame between the nodes; its maximum depends on the frame version Maximum_Packet_Size M if packets I Largest packet, used in segmentation Persistence_Wait_Time M M Wait for the COMM_CHANGE acknowledgement PLCW_Repeat_Interval M D Maximum time between PLCWs (0 = infinite) Receive_Duration M D Longest expected transmission from the half-duplex partner Remote_PCID M M Powered receiver of the remote transceiver Remote_Spacecraft_ID M F, M, D, I Partner SCID (session dynamic) Resync_Lifetime, Resync_Notification, Resync_Response, Resync_Waiting_Period M M, D SET V(R) persistent activity Resync_Local M D True: FOP-P resynchronizes by itself. False: the local controller decides Send_Duration M D Longest half-duplex transmission before passing the token Source_Destination_ID M M 0 = source SCID, 1 = destination SCID Synch_Timeout M D Initial value of SYNCH_TIMER Tail_Idle_Duration M P, M Idle at the end of a transmission to flush the decoders Test_Source M F Whether source-flagged SCIDs are checked Transmission_Window M D COP-P window, at most 127

Restated from annex C.169170171

Status mismatches

Annex C lists Local_PCID as optional, but item DLL-164 of the PICS marks it as mandatory. Conversely, annex C calls Send_Duration and Receive_Duration mandatory, while the PICS (DLL-171, DLL-180) marks them optional; both serve only half duplex, itself optional.170171140141 Annex C also describes Local_Spacecraft_ID as a validation check when the Source-or-Destination ID equals source, while table 3-3 and clause 6.7.2 b) use it for frames flagged destination. The table above follows table 3-3 and 6.7.2.17032118

Annex D. Event E27 is cited there, but tables 6-7 to 6-9 contain no E27. Full duplex carrier loss is handled by E80 and E82.173107105

docs.title: Conformance (PICS)
docs.text: Annex A is a Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement proforma with 196 items (DLL-1 to DLL-196). The allowed values it lists match the field ranges above: TFVN 2, SCID 0–1023, Port ID 0–7, Frame Length 4–2047, data field 0–2043 octets, SS 0–7, X and Y 0–5.134136 At least one of the four DFC ID options must be supported.134 The other optional items are: Type 2 (time distribution) and Type 3 (status report) SPDUs; the time correlation process; computing the enterprise time (with the OWLT) before a time transfer (DLL-61); LNMD and READ STATUS; half duplex and simplex operation; REPORT REQUEST and REPORT SOURCE SPACECRAFT ID; Maximum_Failed_Token_Passes, Send_Duration and Receive_Duration; and the three half-duplex notifications (5 to 7). Everything else is mandatory, including full duplex, all COP-P variables and procedures, SET PL EXTENSIONS, time tag recording and the time distribution steps DLL-60 and DLL-62 to DLL-64. The PICS thus makes the Type 2 SPDU (DLL-23) optional, although the TIME DISTRIBUTION directive it carries is part of the mandatory time distribution.134135137138139140142

docs.title: Version-4 (USLP) frames over Proximity-1
docs.text:
Since issue 6 a USLP Version-4 frame may replace the Version-3 frame over the Proximity-1 C&S sublayer. USLP then takes over the Frame Sublayer functions, and its users take over the I/O Sublayer functions.51132 USLP annex C maps the fields:183185

Version-3 field (bits) Version-4 equivalent (bits) TFVN 10 (0–1) TFVN 1100 (0–3): the last 2-bit value 11 extended with 00 QoS Indicator (2) Bypass/Sequence Control Flag (48) PDU Type ID (3) Protocol Control Command Flag (49) DFC ID (4–5) and segment header flags TFDZ Construction Rules (the first 3 bits of the TFDF header; annex C calls them bits 1–3, §4.1.4.2.2.1.2 bits 0–2, see USLP)184 Pseudo Packet ID 5-bit USLP Protocol Identifier (UPID) field, for segmented data SCID, 10 bits (6–15) SCID, 16 bits (4–19) PCID (16) Most significant VCID bit (21) (no Version-3 field) Remaining VCID bits 22–26, giving 32 VCIDs for proximity operations Port ID (17–19) MAP ID, bits 28–30 only Source-or-Destination (20) Source-or-Destination (20) Frame Length, 11 bits (21–31) Frame Length, 16 bits (32–47); frames up to 65 536 octets Frame Sequence Number (32–39) VC Frame Count (56–63), with the VCF Count Length set to 001 (1 octet)

Data field contents map as follows:185186

Version-3 DFC ID Segment flags Version-4 construction rule 00 whole packets — 111 no segmentation 01 segment 01 first 100 starting segment 01 segment 00 continuing 101 continuing segment 01 segment 10 last 110 last segment 01 segment 11 none 111 no segmentation 11 user-defined — 011 octet stream

Segment flag values in USLP table C-2

USLP table C-2 prints the Version-3 sequence flags as 00 → 100 starting segment and 01 → 101 continuing segment. In CCSDS 211.0-B-6 table 3-4, however, 01 is the first segment and 00 a continuing one. The table above pairs the rules by meaning, following 211.0-B-6. Neither document comments on the difference.18538

In Proximity operations the TFDF header is reduced to the construction rule and the UPID. Proximity-1 uses only variable-length USLP frames, so the First Header/Last Valid Octet Pointer is dropped. The Insert Zone is not allowed, and the UPID values 00001 and 11111 do not apply. The PLCW, or an SDLS Frame Security Report, can go in a separate P-frame or in the OCF, even in a frame with no data field. The FECF is optional, because the PLTU's CRC-32 already protects the frame.186187 Because one VCID bit stands in for the PCID, only 32 VCIDs remain for proximity links. Different spacecraft can be given different VCIDs and so use different SDLS security associations.187 For COP-P over Proximity-1 coding, frame validation is done by the C&S sublayer, since the CRC-32 lies outside the frame.188

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The Proximity-1 data link layer has no security services. Annex E assumes that a layer above or below provides them as needed: authentication where commands must be authentic, integrity against altered commands, software or telemetry, and confidentiality against eavesdropping. It lists the consequences of leaving any of these out.174 The CCSDS security report states that SDLS cannot be used with the Proximity-1 data link protocol. It recommends applying security above the I/O sublayer, to the user data, with all Proximity-1 handling unchanged, which it compares to Transport Layer Security.198 The SDLS Blue Book itself excludes Proximity-1, and the overview Green Book notes that no Proximity-1 security requirements have been set so far.199192 With Version-4 frames, SDLS can be used through the USLP Security Header and Trailer, chosen per VCID.187 See SDLS and security in CCSDS space links. The current issue required no SANA action, and the existing Proximity-1 registries continue.175

docs.title: Where Proximity-1 is used: Mars relay
docs.text: Proximity-1 was partly a response to the need for interoperable Mars spacecraft. The ECSS handbook gives typical scenarios: a base station and a roving vehicle, such as Pathfinder, or an orbiter and a lander, such as NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) talking to ESA's ExoMars rover or NASA's MER rovers.193 It explains the design choices. Contacts are short because of orbiter motion and planetary rotation, and mission control is far away. Proximity-1 therefore sets up links locally by handshake, without precise scheduling, and can renegotiate data rates during a contact as the link budget changes. Frequency-agile transceivers can use a separate hailing channel and working channel, which reduces interference when several landed and orbiting elements are in view.194 The protocol is symmetric, so the same equipment can serve both ends. In practice, however, return rates are often much higher than forward rates: often 256 to 1, and up to 2000 to 1. Overflight geometry, signal strength and light time also vary, so session parameters must be tuned.195

docs.title: NASA Mars Odyssey (annex F)
docs.text:
Annex F records capabilities of the Mars Odyssey orbiter (Mars Surveyor Project 2001). They are given for information only:176177178

  • Tone Beacon Mode. A CW tone that tells microprobes to send their data. Four orbiter beacon frequencies (437.1000, 440.7425, 444.3850 and 448.0275 MHz) address several microprobes, and the lander beacon frequency is 401.585625 MHz. A 437.1 MHz tone coherently transponded at 401.585625 MHz supports Doppler measurements.
  • Transmit Standby Mode. This is the default when several landed elements are in view of a hailing orbiter. It stops them all answering at once.
  • Convolutional code. Odyssey's rate ½, constraint-length 7 code does not invert G2, so the encoding field must be set to match.
  • Directive values. Channel 000 is 401.585625 MHz for the responder's return transmissions and 437.1 MHz for its forward reception. The coding options are scrambler, convolutional (no G2 inversion, CRC-32 attached) and bypass. Only 8, 32, 128 and 256 kb/s are available. The mode values are standby, sequence controlled, expedited, unreliable bitstream, tone beacon and (transmitter only) canister.
  • PLCW. Odyssey sets the Expedited Frame Counter to zero (unused), always uses PCID 0, and never sets the Retransmit Flag. A Report Value that fails to increase signals a rejected frame. Odyssey called the PCID field "VCID".

docs.title: NASA MRO Electra (annex G)
docs.text:
Annex G explains the options needed to work with MRO's Electra radio:179180181

Topic Residual carrier Suppressed carrier Symbols Bi-Phase-L (Manchester): spectral null at the centre, where the carrier tone sits NRZ-L, with all power in the data Modulation index Typically 60°, giving 25 % of power in the carrier and 75 % in the data 90° Carrier tracking Standard carrier loop, practical loop SNR threshold 7 dB Costas loop with a 180° ambiguity, about 16 dB loop SNR needed; differential encoding resolves the ambiguity When to use Low rates, low or uncertain signals, critical events such as entry, descent and landing; partners that only support it, such as Odyssey's CE-505 radio When loop SNR allows: about 1.25 dB more power in the data

Projects that want to work with MRO above 512 ks/s should consider NRZ-L instead of Bi-Phase-L, unless Bi-Phase-L performs well enough. Manchester coding uses about twice the bandwidth of NRZ-L at the same symbol rate, and NRZ-L is usually combined with a scrambler.179180 Electra's Viterbi decoder chip follows a commercial convention without G2 inversion. The extra bit handling it needs creates a sign ambiguity, so differential encoding is recommended with the CCSDS G2-inverted code. Differential decoding turns each channel bit error into two output errors. FSK and QPSK are not implemented on Electra.181

docs.title: Recommended practice for UHF orbiter-lander links
docs.text:
The ECSS handbook gives intra-agency best practice for orbiter-lander links in the UHF band. Its table 4-5 is headed "CFDP best practice", but its rows are Proximity-1 parameters:197

Item Recommendation Hailing frequency UHF Channel 1 Channels implemented Channel 1 mandatory; channels 0 and 2 to 7 optional Polarization Right-hand circular Data rates 8 kb/s mandatory, others optional Quality of service Sequence Controlled and Expedited both mandatory Service Packet service Communication modes Full duplex and half duplex both mandatory Carrier_Only_Duration 5 s / 1 s Acquisition_Idle_Duration, Tail_Idle_Duration 4096 bits each

For cross-agency work the handbook points to mission-to-mission negotiation and to CCSDS protocol profiles, the first of them for Mars missions.197 Apart from the handbook's ExoMars rover example, no document in this wiki's library describes an ESA spacecraft's Proximity-1 implementation.

Inference

For the ESA ground segment documented elsewhere in this wiki (SCOS-2000, NCTRS), Proximity-1 is invisible. It runs between two spacecraft, and relayed lander data reaches the ground over the orbiter's own space-to-ground link. None of the ESA ground segment documents in the library mentions Proximity-1.
