docs.title: Radio frequency, modulation and ranging
docs.text:
Everything else on this wiki, from Space Packets to CLTUs and CADUs, eventually becomes a modulated radio carrier. The physical layer decides on which frequency that carrier sits, how the coded symbols are impressed on it, how much spectrum and power the emission may use, how the ground station and spacecraft find and lock onto each other, and how the same carrier is used to measure the spacecraft's distance and velocity. CCSDS covers this in one omnibus Blue Book, CCSDS 401.0-B, Radio Frequency and Modulation Systems, Part 1: Earth Stations and Spacecraft; ECSS covers it in ECSS-E-ST-50-05C (Radio frequency and modulation) and ECSS-E-ST-50-02C (Ranging and Doppler tracking).199148175 This page is a structured overview of all three, not a reprint of every recommendation; it links to the TM coding and TC coding pages for the sublayer immediately above.

At a glance

Item Value CCSDS document CCSDS 401.0-B-32, October 2021; a collection of individual recommendations, first issued January 19872 ECSS documents ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Rev. 2 (4 October 2011), with many clauses derived from CCSDS 401.0-B-20; ECSS-E-ST-50-02C (31 July 2008)98106147 Mission categories Category A: less than 2 × 10⁶ km from Earth; Category B (deep space): 2 × 10⁶ km or more6 Residual-carrier formats PCM/PSK/PM on a subcarrier (8 or 16 kHz for TC, 2–300 kHz for TM) and PCM/PM with SP-L (bi-phase-L) directly on the carrier119118 Suppressed-carrier formats BPSK, QPSK, UQPSK, OQPSK, filtered OQPSK, GMSK, 4D-8PSK TCM (ECSS); CCSDS adds SRRC-QPSK/OQPSK/8PSK and 16/32/64-APSK for Earth-exploration bands12756 Coherent turnaround ratios 221/240 (2 GHz up, 2 GHz down), 749/880 (7 GHz up, 8 GHz down), 221/880, 749/240, 749/3344, 3599/3344 and others10106 Tracking techniques ESA tone-plus-code ranging and integrated Doppler (ECSS-E-ST-50-02C), PN ranging and GMSK+PN, telemetry ranging, Delta-DOR (CCSDS 401)154606372

docs.title: Where the physical layer sits
docs.text:
The CCSDS layered architecture places these recommendations in the physical layer, which the Foreword itself subdivides into technical characteristics, policy constraints and procedures.1 The ECSS communications handbook draws the same boundary: its protocol map puts ECSS-E-ST-50-05 and ECSS-E-ST-50-02 at the bottom, under the TM and TC synchronization and channel coding standards, with CCSDS 211.1-B as the physical layer of Proximity-1 beside them; it also warns that the choice of TC and TM modulation must take into account whether a ranging service compatible with ECSS-E-ST-50-02 is needed.174176 The figure below shows the chain in both directions; the boxes in the middle are the subject of this page.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Ground["Earth station"]
      direction TB
      CLTU["CLTUs + idle sequence<br/>(TC coding sublayer)"] --> TCMOD["TC modulation<br/>PCM/PSK/PM, PCM/PM/SP-L or BPSK"]
      RNG["Ranging signal<br/>tone + code, or PN"] --> TCMOD
      TCMOD --> UP["Up-conversion, HPA<br/>EIRP, sweep, Doppler compensation"]
      DEM["Receiver: carrier PLL,<br/>demodulator, Doppler + ranging"] --> CADU["CADUs<br/>(TM coding sublayer)"]
    end
    subgraph Space["Spacecraft"]
      direction TB
      RX["Transponder receiver<br/>carrier lock, TC demod,<br/>ranging channel"] --> TX["Transmitter<br/>coherent or non-coherent"]
      TMSYM["TM channel symbols"] --> TX
    end
    UP -- "Earth-to-space carrier" --> RX
    TX -- "space-to-Earth carrier<br/>(turnaround ratio if coherent)" --> DEM

The diagram is this wiki's synthesis of the functional descriptions in ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §4.1 and the modulation clauses of ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §6.151117127 For the data link layer above, see TM synchronization and channel coding, TC synchronization and channel coding and the ECSS overview in ECSS-E-ST-50C communications. The overall flows are described in Downlink and Uplink.

docs.title: How CCSDS 401.0-B is organised
docs.text:
CCSDS 401.0-B is unusual among CCSDS Blue Books: it is a loose-leaf collection of short recommendations, each written in the ITU-style "considering ... recommends" form, so that agencies can add, update or delete recommendations independently.4 They are grouped into three sections: technical (section 2), policy (section 3) and procedural (section 4), plus terminology and a glossary (section 5).4

Section Subsections Character 2 Technical 2.1 Earth-to-space RF, 2.2 Telecommand, 2.3 Space-to-Earth RF, 2.4 Telemetry, 2.5 Radio metric, 2.6 Spacecraft quantitative characteristics of equipment and signals 3 Policy 3.1 Frequency utilization, 3.2 Power limitations, 3.3 Modulation methods, 3.4 Operational procedures, 3.5 Testing, 3.6 Spacecraft systems directive rules for sharing the spectrum 4 Procedural 4.1 Design tools, 4.2 Computational algorithms link design control table, modulation-loss and bandwidth formulas 5 5.1 Terminology, 5.2 Glossary definitions

Each recommendation has a self-describing number. Page 2.5.3A-1, for example, is the first page of a technical recommendation (2) in the radio metric subsection (5), third in that subsection (3), and applicable to Category A only (A); a number without a letter applies to both categories.47 The terms "Telecommand" and "Telemetry" are kept for historical reasons but cover any data sent to or from the spacecraft, including science and file transfers.5

Issue 32 (October 2021) updated recommendations 2.4.18 and 2.4.23 and added 2.6.13 and 2.6.15; the document control table records 32 issues since January 1987, each adding, updating or deleting individual recommendations (for example the deletion of 2.1.8A/B by resolution CMC-R-2018-02-001).23

docs.title: Mission categories and radio services
docs.text:
Four ITU radiocommunication services matter to CCSDS: Space Research, Space Operation, Earth Exploration-Satellite and Meteorological-Satellite.6 Within Space Research, some bands are reserved for deep space. WARC ORB-88 moved the ITU deep-space boundary from lunar distance to 2.0 × 10⁶ km with effect from 16 March 1990; because the ITU has no name for the nearer region, CCSDS defines Category A (altitude below 2.0 × 10⁶ km) and Category B (2.0 × 10⁶ km or more).6 The same split appears in the terminology of §5.1, while the glossary of §5.2 places the boundary case the other way (Category A "less than or equal to", Category B "greater than"); the difference only matters for a spacecraft exactly at 2 × 10⁶ km.8 ECSS-E-ST-50-05C and ECSS-E-ST-50-02C adopt the same two categories, and ECSS adds that bands allocated to Space Research (deep space) shall only be used by Category B spacecraft.100149102

ECSS-E-ST-50-05C defines the services by reference to the ITU Radio Regulations (ITU/RR): the Space Operation service (SO) is concerned exclusively with operating spacecraft (tracking, telemetry and telecommand, TTC); Space Research (SR) uses spacecraft for scientific and technological research; Earth Exploration-Satellite (EES) obtains information about the Earth from orbiting sensors, and, for this standard, includes the Meteorological-Satellite service.10099 A service with a primary allocation coordinates only with co-primary services and need not protect secondary users; a secondary service must not cause harmful interference to, and cannot claim protection from, primary services.102

docs.title: Frequency bands
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Table 4-1 lists the recommended bands. All are primary allocations.101

Band (MHz) Service Direction Conditions 2 025 – 2 110 SR, SO, EES Earth-space EIRP chosen for a 3 dB link margin; power adjustable in steps of 3 dB or less; no uplink when no tracking or telecommand operations take place103 2 110 – 2 120 SR (deep space) Earth-space part of the IMT-2000/UMTS core band; new assignments only with the frequency coordinator's agreement and formally discouraged103176 2 200 – 2 290 SR, SO, EES space-Earth occupied bandwidth at most 6 MHz; no downlink when no station is in view; reliable switch-off devices103 2 290 – 2 300 SR (deep space) space-Earth no special requirement, but usefulness limited by its paired 2 110–2 120 MHz band103 7 145 – 7 190 SR (deep space) Earth-space Category B only101102 7 190 – 7 235 SR Earth-space not deep space; paired with Category A downlinks in Table 5-1101106 8 025 – 8 400 EES space-Earth same RFI mitigation as 2 200–2 290 MHz; the only EES direct-data band below 20 GHz104 8 400 – 8 450 SR (deep space) space-Earth maximum bandwidth B25 as a function of symbol rate (below)104 8 450 – 8 500 SR space-Earth occupied bandwidth at most 10 MHz; priority to Lagrangian-point missions104 25 500 – 27 000 SR, EES space-Earth use as agreed with the frequency coordinator104 31 800 – 32 300 SR (deep space) space-Earth EHF; Category B only, like every deep-space band101102 34 200 – 34 700 SR (deep space) Earth-space EHF; Category B only101102 37 000 – 38 000 SR space-Earth use as agreed with the frequency coordinator104 40 000 – 40 500 SR Earth-space use as agreed with the frequency coordinator104

CCSDS adds policy recommendations on top of the ITU rules. Recommendation 3.1.1 asks geostationary satellites of non-science services that use the shared 2 GHz bands for TTC to limit themselves to one frequency pair and to launch, orbit insertion and emergency operations; 3.1.2A reserves 8 450–8 500 MHz for Category A missions needing up to 10 MHz each (in particular libration-point missions) and says Category B missions should not use it; 3.1.4A constrains the 14–17 GHz bands; 3.1.6B gives a channel plan for Category B; 3.1.7 covers several spacecraft in one antenna beam.97980

docs.title: The B25 mask in the 8 400–8 450 MHz deep-space band
docs.text:
Mars-region spacecraft cannot be separated spatially, and a single unrestricted high-rate mission could occupy the whole 50 MHz allocation. CCSDS 3.1.2B therefore limits each mission's B25 bandwidth, the width outside which the power spectral density is at least 25 dB below its peak (discrete lines such as a residual carrier do not count), as a function of symbol rate.81 In the transition region the limit is

\[B_{25}\,[\text{MHz}] = \frac{k\,R_s}{0.41 + R_s},\qquad k = 8.53 \text{ (all missions)},\ k = 12.5 \text{ (non-Mars missions, non-interference basis)}\]

with \(R_s\) in Msps; the curves flatten at 8.0 MHz and 12.0 MHz. Outside B25 the spectral power flux density at the Earth's surface is limited to −266 dB(W/Hz/m²).81 ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §4.2.3 imposes the same mask using the equivalent symbol rate \(R_{ES}\), which is twice the NRZ symbol rate for SP-L and equal to it otherwise.104 With GMSK (BTs = 0.5), the 12 MHz and 8 MHz caps correspond to maximum coded symbol rates of 9.3 and 6.2 Msps respectively; missions needing more must move to 31.8–32.3 GHz.55

docs.title: Frequency assignment procedure
docs.text: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C makes the frequency coordinator the exclusive authority for assignments. The project requests its frequencies before the design phase, marking preliminary data as such, and must supply final data for the ITU advance publication, coordination and notification procedures (ITU/RR articles 9 and 11) no later than three years before launch.105 Annex E adds that the ITU Radio Regulations cannot be tailored.146

docs.title: Category B channel frequency plan
docs.text:
CCSDS 3.1.6B asks agencies to choose Category B frequencies from a single channel plan, coordinated through the SFCG, so that up- and downlink pairs automatically respect the turnaround ratios.82 Each channel derives from a 2 GHz downlink reference \(F_{2DN} = N \cdot 10/27 + 2295\) MHz, with channel number \(N + 14\); the 7 GHz uplink is computed from \(F_{2DN}\) and the other bands are derived from the 7 GHz value through the frequency factors 221, 240, 749, 880, 3328, 3344, 3360 and 3599, each result rounded to the nearest Hz.83

Worked example: channel 14 (values from Table 3.1.6B-1)

For channel 14, \(N = 0\) and \(F_{2DN}\) = 2 295.000000 MHz. The table then gives 2 113.312500 MHz (2 GHz up, factor 221), 7 162.312500 MHz (7 GHz up, 749), 8 415.000000 MHz (8 GHz down, 880), 31 977.000000 MHz (32 GHz down, 3344) and 34 415.437500 MHz (34 GHz up, 3599).83 Multiplying the 2 295 MHz reference by 221/240, 749/240 and 880/240 reproduces 2 113.3125, 7 162.3125 and 8 415 MHz exactly, which shows how the plan embeds the turnaround ratios (this wiki's arithmetic).

docs.title: Coherent transponders and turnaround ratios
docs.text:
For coherent Doppler tracking the spacecraft transponder derives its transmitted carrier from the received one by phase-lock techniques, multiplying it by a fixed transponder turnaround frequency ratio (TTFR).10674 A defined ratio is only needed for missions that require both cross-support from other agencies' stations and up/down coherency, and on-board implementations may deviate from the nominal value and add a significant downlink delay that orbit determination must account for.74

flowchart LR
    FT["Station transmits F_T"] -- "one-way Doppler D" --> FRX["Spacecraft receives<br/>F_rx = D·F_T"]
    FRX -- "turnaround ratio q" --> FTX["Spacecraft transmits<br/>F_tx = q·D·F_T"]
    FTX -- "one-way Doppler D" --> FR["Station receives<br/>F_R = q·D²·F_T"]
    FT -- "× q locally" --> FL["Reference F_L = q·F_T"]
    FR --> DF["Δf = F_R − F_L ≈ −q·F_T·2v/c"]
    FL --> DF

The relations are those of ECSS-E-ST-50-02C Annex C, where \(D = \sqrt{(1-v/c)/(1+v/c)} \approx 1 - v/c\) is the one-way Doppler coefficient and \(v\) the radial velocity.173

Ratio (up/down) Bands (MHz) Category Recommendation 221/240 2 025–2 120 / 2 200–2 300 A and B CCSDS 2.6.1; ECSS Table 5-1 749/880 7 145–7 235 / 8 400–8 500 A and B CCSDS 2.6.2; ECSS Table 5-1 221/900 2 025–2 110 / 8 450–8 500 A CCSDS 2.6.3A; ECSS Table 5-2 (alternative) 765/240 7 190–7 235 / 2 200–2 290 A CCSDS 2.6.4A; ECSS Table 5-2 (alternative) 221/880 2 110–2 120 / 8 400–8 450 B CCSDS 2.6.5B; ECSS Table 5-1 749/240 7 145–7 190 / 2 290–2 300 B CCSDS 2.6.6B; ECSS Table 5-1 749/3328, 749/3344, 749/3360 7 145–7 190 / 31 800–32 300 B CCSDS 2.6.7B; ECSS Table 5-1 3599/3344, 3599/3360 (ECSS adds 3599/3328) 34 200–34 700 / 31 800–32 300 B CCSDS 2.6.8B; ECSS Table 5-1 3599/880 34 200–34 700 / 8 400–8 450 B ECSS Table 5-1 only 221/3344; 3599/240 2 110–2 120 / 31 800–32 300; 34 200–34 700 / 2 290–2 300 B ECSS Table 5-2 only (alternatives) 749/2652 … 749/2800 7 190–7 235 / 25 500–27 000 A CCSDS 2.6.9A; ECSS Table 5-1 221/2772, 221/2850 2 025–2 110 / 25 500–27 000 A CCSDS 2.6.10A; ECSS Table 5-1 749/836 … 749/864 7 190–7 250 / 8 025–8 400 A CCSDS 2.6.11A 749/876 … 749/884 7 145–7 235 / 8 400–8 500 A and B CCSDS 2.6.13 (flexible ratios for MSPA) 2407/2720, 2407/2760, 2407/2816 22 550–23 150 / 25 500–27 000 A CCSDS 2.6.14 2407/2800, 2407/2816 23 150–23 550 / 27 000–27 500 inter-satellite CCSDS 2.6.15

Sources for the table: the CCSDS spacecraft recommendation summary and recommendations 2.6.7B, 2.6.8B and 2.6.13–2.6.15, and ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Tables 5-1 and 5-2, which also give the exact usable sub-bands (for example 7 192.102 273–7 234.659 091 MHz up for 8 450–8 500 MHz down at 749/880).1075767778106 ECSS says band pairs should be taken from its Table 5-1 and, if not, shall come from Table 5-2.106

The flexible 749/876–884 ratios exist for one particular way of serving several spacecraft from one antenna: a common uplink frequency, with each spacecraft turning it around to a different downlink. All keep 749 in the numerator for compatibility with existing receivers; 749/877, 749/881 and 749/883 may not suit analog multiplier designs because of large prime factors, and 749/882 needs care against self-interference.76

docs.title: Frequency stability
docs.text:
Item Requirement Source Spacecraft transmitter, 2 200–2 300, 8 025–8 500, 25 500–27 000 MHz ±2 × 10⁻⁵ under all conditions and over lifetime ECSS Table 5-3 Spacecraft transmitter, 31 800–32 300 MHz ±1.5 × 10⁻⁶ at one temperature (+10 to +40 °C, 15 h after 4 h warm-up); ±0.2 × 10⁻⁶/°C; ageing ±2.5 × 10⁻⁶ per year ECSS Table 5-3 Category B short-term stability phase error below 10° peak in a second-order PLL of the mission's 2BL, high SNR, non-coherent mode ECSS 5.2.1b Spacecraft receiver, 2 025–2 110 and 7 190–7 235 MHz ±2 × 10⁻⁵ including ±4.8 × 10⁻⁶ initial setting; ageing over seven years ±7.1 × 10⁻⁶ ECSS Table 5-4 Spacecraft receiver, 34 200–34 700 MHz ±1.7 × 10⁻⁵ at one temperature; ±2.4 × 10⁻⁷/°C; ageing ±2.5 × 10⁻⁶ per year ECSS Table 5-4 Earth station carriers phase locked to a reference of at least ±5 × 10⁻⁹ accuracy ECSS 5.2.3 Earth station reference (Allan deviation) curve A for Category A except lunar missions (range rate 1 mm/s), curve B for Category B and lunar missions (0.1 mm/s); clock drift at most 10 µs per month CCSDS 2.3.7

Sources: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §5.2 and CCSDS 2.3.7.10737 The deeper Allan-variance requirements used for Doppler tracking are in ECSS-E-ST-50-02C (see below).

docs.title: Polarization, bandwidth and emissions
docs.text:
Polarization. Both CCSDS and ECSS require circular polarization. Linear polarization would vary with aspect angle on near-omnidirectional antennas and suffer Faraday rotation at low frequencies; CCSDS asks Earth stations to switch between LCP and RCP with a carrier interruption of no more than 5 seconds, and ECSS requires stations to transmit either sense at the user's choice.1436108

Occupied bandwidth. Occupied bandwidth is the band holding all but 0.5 % of the mean power on each side (ITU/RR 1.153); spurious emissions are those beyond ±2.5 times that bandwidth.100 ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Table 5-5 gives the maxima, where \(f_t\) is the ranging tone and \(R_s\) the symbol rate:109

Band (MHz) Function Category Maximum occupied bandwidth 2 025–2 120, 7 145–7 235 TC, 8 kHz subcarrier A and B 50 kHz 2 025–2 120, 7 145–7 235 TC, 16 kHz subcarrier A and B 100 kHz 2 025–2 120, 7 145–7 235 TC, direct modulation A and B 12 × Rs 2 025–2 120, 7 145–7 235 ranging A and B 2.5 × ft (deep space may exceed with approval) 2 200–2 290, 8 450–8 500 TM, Rs < 10 ksps A 300 kHz 2 200–2 290, 8 450–8 500 TM, 10–60 ksps A 1 200 kHz or 30 × Rs, whichever is smaller 2 200–2 290, 8 450–8 500 TM, 60 ksps–2 Msps A 1 200 kHz or 12 × Rs, whichever is larger, up to 6 MHz (2 GHz) or 10 MHz (8 GHz) 2 200–2 290, 8 450–8 500 TM, ≥ 2 Msps A 1.1 × Rs, same caps 2 200–2 290, 8 450–8 500 ranging A 2.5 × ft 2 290–2 300 TM, ≥ 2 Msps B 1.2 × Rs 8 025–8 400 (EES band) TM – (none given) 1.1 × Rs 2 290–2 300, 8 400–8 450 ranging B 2.5 × ft 8 400–8 450 TM B B25 mask; at ≥ 2 Msps also 1.2 × Rs

CCSDS 4.2 gives approximations for the 99 % bandwidth of unfiltered signals: for PCM/PM, \(BW = 2(26.2m - 5.16)R_{CS}\) with bi-phase-L and \(2(8.93m - 1.75)R_{CS}\) with NRZ (0.4 ≤ m ≤ 1.4 rad, coded symbol rate before bi-phase-L encoding); for PCM/PSK/PM with a sine-wave subcarrier, \(B = 4nR_{CS}\) for 0.8 < m < 1.35 and n > 7, where n is the subcarrier-to-symbol-rate ratio; and a cubic expression in m for square-wave subcarriers.959697

Spurious emissions. Any single spurious emission is limited to −60 dBc (relative to the unmodulated carrier) by CCSDS 2.4.16; ECSS measures the same −60 dBc in a 4 kHz reference bandwidth for all transmitters from 100 MHz to 40.5 GHz, and limits carrier harmonics of Category B transmitters to −30 dBc. ECSS applies the limit even to deep-space missions, which ITU would exempt, because they spend long periods closer than 2 × 10⁶ km.53110 Unwanted emissions must also protect radio astronomy (with GSO satellites 15 dB and single non-GSO satellites 13 dB below the terrestrial thresholds of ITU-R RA.769-2), deep-space antenna sites (for example −255.1 dBW/m²/Hz in 8 400–8 450 MHz) and the launcher's RF system.111112

Power flux density. ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Table 5-10 limits the PFD at the Earth's surface in all mission phases, for example −154 dBW/m² in 4 kHz at low elevation for 1 525–2 300 MHz, rising to −144 above 25°; −150 to −140 dBW/m²/4 kHz for 8 025–8 500 MHz; and per-MHz limits for 25.5–27, 31.8–32.3 and 37–38 GHz.114 CCSDS 2.3.2 makes exceeding these limits with a residual carrier one of the reasons to switch to suppressed-carrier modulation, and 3.6.1A recommends coding and suppressed carriers to lower power spectral density in the 2 GHz band.3190

Earth station power and elevation. CCSDS 3.2.1A asks agencies to keep uplink EIRP to what safe operation needs, prefer adjustable transmitters, and use antennas with a diameter-to-wavelength ratio of at least 70.85 ECSS caps EIRP towards the horizon (for 1–15 GHz, +40 dBW in any 4 kHz for a horizon elevation of 0° or below, +55 dBW for deep space), and forbids transmission below 3° (SO and EES), 5° (SR Category A) or 10° (SR Category B) antenna elevation; because host administrations may impose tighter limits, the actual minimum is agreed with the frequency coordinator.115 Both directions may only radiate during actual operations, and every spacecraft must be able to stop its emissions by telecommand (ITU/RR 22.1).113116

docs.title: Residual-carrier modulation
docs.text: A residual-carrier system phase-modulates the carrier with a peak deviation (the modulation index, in radians) small enough that a discrete carrier line remains for a conventional phase-locked loop (PLL) receiver to track. CCSDS recommends residual-carrier phase modulation for the uplink and retains residual-carrier receivers on the ground for low-rate telemetry because most receivers and autotrack systems need that line.1330 ECSS requires phase modulation for telecommand and ranging in the 2, 7 and 34 GHz uplink bands, for ranging in the 2, 8 and 32 GHz downlink bands, and for telemetry in those downlink bands unless suppressed-carrier modulation is adopted.117

docs.title: PCM waveforms
docs.text:
Waveform Definition (ECSS Figure 6-1) Where allowed NRZ-L level A for "1", level B for "0" only on a subcarrier (ECSS 6.1.3d)118 NRZ-M a level change for "1", no change for "0" TC on a subcarrier; prevented for Category B TC by ECSS118 SP-L (split-phase-level, also called bi-phase-L or Manchester) "1" = level A then B within the symbol; "0" = B then A only directly on the carrier, without subcarrier; not for TM below 10 ksps118

Sources: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §6.1.3 and Figure 6-1.118 CCSDS gives the reasoning: NRZ relies entirely on data transitions for clock recovery, bi-phase-L has a mid-symbol transition in every symbol, and both a PSK subcarrier with an integer frequency-to-symbol-rate ratio and bi-phase-L have zero spectral density at the carrier, so the data does not disturb the carrier loop; NRZ-M and NRZ-S cause errors in pairs.42

docs.title: Telecommand
docs.text:

docs.text:
Parameter CCSDS 401 ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Use of subcarriers only when technically justified (low bit rate, radio science); PSK; sine for Category A, square for Category B (2.4.3) 2–300 kHz; sine for Category A, square for Category B; NRZ-L (Table 6-2) Subcarrier ratio integer; 4 (Category A) or 5 (Category B) above 60 kHz unless overlaps force a higher integer for ≤ 0.3 dB / ≤ 0.1 dB degradation; Category B subcarrier ≤ 300 kHz (2.4.14A/B) same rule, maximum 300 kHz (6.1.4.1.3b–c) Above 60 ksps no explicit rule; 2.4.15A/B instead bound bi-phase-L at low rates relative to the carrier loop bandwidth no subcarriers; SP-L directly up to 1 Msps in 2 and 8 GHz, or suppressed carrier (6.1.4.1.3a) Subcarrier offset and stability ±200 ppm; ±1 × 10⁻⁶ short term; ±2 × 10⁻⁵ over 5 min (2.4.6) within ±1 × 10⁻⁴; ±1 × 10⁻⁵ over 5 min; ±1 × 10⁻⁶ short term (6.1.4.2.2) Symbol asymmetry ≤ 0.2 % at the modulator input (2.4.8) ≤ 1 % (6.1.3b) Transition density runs ≤ 64 symbols; ≥ 125 (A) or ≥ 275 (B) transitions per 1000 symbols; follow CCSDS 131.0 on the use of the pseudo-randomizer (2.4.9) same values; randomizer of ECSS-E-ST-50-01 clause 9 if not ensured otherwise (6.1.5)

Sources: CCSDS 2.4.3–2.4.15 and ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §6.1.3–6.1.5.404950414344119121123 The CCSDS reasoning for the subcarrier ratio is that integer ratios leave a spectral minimum around the carrier, and the smallest practical integer keeps the spectrum compact while holding data interference in the carrier loop (C/I above 20 dB for Category A, 25 dB for Category B with concatenated coding) negligible.4950 Subcarrier modulation itself must be PSK with the subcarrier an integer multiple of the symbol rate, PCM transitions within ±2.5 % of a subcarrier period of a zero crossing, and phase within ±5° of an ideal PSK signal after 25 % of a period.122 For spacecraft subcarrier modulators, CCSDS 2.4.13B limits phase and amplitude imbalance to 2° and 0.2 dB (Category B).48

docs.title: Modulation index, carrier suppression and other signal quality
docs.text:
Function Minimum (rad peak) Maximum (rad peak) Telecommand, NRZ-L/NRZ-M on subcarrier 0.2 1.4 Telecommand, SP-L 0.2 1.0 Telemetry, sine-wave subcarrier – 1.5 Telemetry, square-wave subcarrier or SP-L – 1.25 (1.39 if the carrier-loop SNR stays above 15 dB) Ranging, Earth-space 0.1 1.4 Ranging, space-Earth (effective, after uplink-noise power sharing) 0.01 0.7

Source: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Table 6-3; the combined uplink index (linear sum of peak indices) should not exceed 1.75 rad, and worst-case tolerances apply.124 CCSDS sets the carrier-suppression rules that frame these numbers: the reduction of carrier power by all modulating signals should not exceed 10 dB on the uplink (2.1.6), nor 10 dB for sine-wave modulation on the downlink, while square-wave modulation may exceed 10 dB if the carrier tracking loop SNR stays above 15 dB (2.3.8).2038 ECSS words this as residual carrier power above −15 dBc (space-Earth) and −10 dBc (Earth-space).126

The power split follows from the modulation-loss formulas of CCSDS 4.1.5: for a sine-wave subcarrier the carrier keeps \(J_0^2(m)\) of the total power and the data channel \(2J_1^2(m)\); for a square wave (or SP-L) the shares are \(\cos^2 m\) and \(\sin^2 m\). These are the single-channel cases of the CCSDS tables, which multiply such factors for every simultaneous signal.93

Inference

With \(\cos^2(1.25) \approx 0.099\) (−10.0 dB) and \(\cos^2(1.39) \approx 0.032\) (−14.9 dB), the ECSS limits of 1.25 rad and 1.39 rad for square-wave telemetry correspond almost exactly to a 10 dB carrier suppression (the CCSDS 2.3.8 limit, which square-wave modulation may exceed while the carrier loop SNR stays above 15 dB) and to the −15 dBc residual-carrier floor of ECSS 6.1.11a. The standards do not state this derivation; it is this wiki's arithmetic from the CCSDS 4.1.5 formulas.9338124126

Further ECSS signal-quality requirements: a positive-going video voltage advances the carrier phase (also CCSDS 2.1.5/2.3.6), and a directly modulated SP-L "1" starts with a phase advance; phase deviation linear within ±3 % up to 1.5 rad; residual amplitude modulation below 2 %; integrated phase noise of the unmodulated carrier below 2° rms at UHF and 4° at SHF (10 Hz–100 kHz) in the non-deep-space bands, 1° rms (0.1 Hz–1 kHz) in the 2 GHz deep-space bands, and 4° (SHF) or 10° (EHF) between 1 Hz and 10 kHz in the other deep-space bands; discrete lines below −45 dBc, modulation products below −30 dBc in the occupied bandwidth and within ±60 kHz (UHF), ±220 kHz (SHF) or ±850 kHz (EHF) of the carrier.12519126

CCSDS 2.4.15A/B add charts of where PCM/PM/bi-phase-L is not permitted: at low symbol rates the data spectrum falls into the carrier loop bandwidth, so the ratio of loop bandwidth to symbol rate and the index determine whether the carrier-to-interference ratio stays above 15–25 dB.5152 CCSDS 4.1.1 recommends a graphical procedure for choosing the indices of simultaneous ranging, telecommand and telemetry, and 2.1.7B adds Category B constraints: telecommand index at least 0.2 rad, uplink ranging index at most 1.4 rad, telecommand subcarrier period an integer subdivision of the bit period, and low-frequency ranging tones chopped by the highest tone.9121

docs.title: Suppressed-carrier modulation
docs.text:
When all the power goes into the data, the carrier line disappears and the receiver recovers the carrier with a suppressed-carrier tracking loop such as the Costas loop, which still supports Doppler measurement.29 CCSDS notes that a suppressed-carrier loop frequently has more than 10 dB better carrier SNR than a residual-carrier loop, at least as good symbol-error performance, and makes PFD limits easier to meet; short periodic data patterns can however leave zero power at the carrier frequency, and the CCSDS randomizer is required.31

When to use it. CCSDS 2.3.2 requires (filtered) BPSK, (filtered) QPSK, filtered OQPSK or GMSK when a residual carrier would exceed the PFD limits, up to 2 Msps in the 2 and 8 GHz bands, 10 Msps at 26 GHz and 20 Msps at 32 GHz, recommends them whenever practicable at lower rates, prefers filtered OQPSK or GMSK, and requires the CCSDS 131.0 randomizer.31 ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §6.2.1 requires suppressed carrier for telemetry in the 2 200–2 300, 8 025–8 400 and 8 400–8 500 MHz bands when PFD limits would be exceeded and in any case above 1 Msps; above 2 Msps (below 8.5 GHz) or 20 Msps (31.8–32.3 GHz) only TCM 8PSK (8 025–8 400 MHz only), filtered OQPSK (below 8 400 MHz and in 8 450–8 500 MHz) or GMSK (all bands) may be used, and new projects may use BPSK, QPSK, UQPSK and OQPSK only below those rates.127 ECSS-E-ST-50-02C ranging cannot be combined with these modulations.127155

Scheme (ECSS 6.2.3) Key ECSS requirements BPSK carrier reversed at each transition; constellation points 180 ± 2° apart QPSK equal-rate I and Q channels; quadrature 90 ± 5°; amplitude imbalance < 0.5 dB; cross-channel suppression > 21 dB; symbol clocks aligned within ±2 % or 1 ns; Q-DNRZ differential coding equations if used UQPSK two channels with different rates and amplitudes; rate imbalance (Rs1 − Rs2)/(Rs1 + Rs2) > 0.05; power imbalance 4–10 dB OQPSK / filtered OQPSK Q delayed by half a channel symbol; same balance limits; filtering by SRRC (α = 0.5) before the modulator, or a 4-pole/2-zero elliptic post-amplifier filter for very high rates at 8 025–8 400 MHz; matched SRRC receive filter; FIR at least 16 bits GMSK precoded; BTs = 0.25 for Category A and 8 025–8 400 MHz, BTs = 0.5 for Category B; FIR at least 5 bits (A) or 4 bits (B), coefficients at least 12 bits 4D-8PSK TCM adjacent phase states 45 ± 1.5°; amplitude imbalance < 0.3 dB; carrier and sideband rejection ≥ 30 dB

Sources: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §6.2.3.1–6.2.3.6.129130131

Phase ambiguity. A suppressed-carrier receiver can lock in any of 2 (BPSK) or 4 (QPSK) phases. CCSDS and ECSS prefer resolving this with the frame synchronization marker where the ground network can, synchronizing before convolutional decoding; otherwise differential coding (NRZ-M, or Q-DNRZ for quadrature schemes) is applied before the convolutional encoder and removed after the Viterbi decoder, which limits error propagation; with differential coding the I and Q channels are encoded independently.3946128 ECSS Table 6-4 maps each scheme to its waveform: NRZ-L without differential encoding; NRZ-M (BPSK, UQPSK) or Q-DNRZ (QPSK, OQPSK, filtered OQPSK) with it; GMSK uses precoding and TCM its own differential encoder.128

QPSK bit mapping. CCSDS 2.4.10 sends even-numbered bits (bit 0 first, the MSB) on I and odd bits on Q, and maps the (I, Q) pairs "00", "10", "11" and "01" to carrier phases of 45°, 135°, 225° and 315°, so that a 90° phase error corrupts at most one bit.45

docs.title: GMSK
docs.text: GMSK is a constant-envelope continuous-phase modulation whose phase is the integral of Gaussian-filtered frequency pulses. ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §9.1 defines the carrier as \(x(t) = \sqrt{2P}\cos(2\pi f t + \varphi(t) + \varphi_0)\) with \(\varphi(t) = \sum_k a_k \frac{\pi}{2}\int_{-\infty}^{t-kT_s} g(\tau)\,d\tau\). The frequency pulse \(g\) is a rectangle of one symbol duration convolved with a Gaussian of standard deviation \(\sigma T_s\), \(\sigma = \sqrt{\ln 2}/(2\pi BT_s)\), B being the one-sided 3 dB bandwidth; the transmitted symbols are precoded as \(a_k = (-1)^k d_k d_{k-1}\) from the information symbols \(d_k = \pm 1\).141 Because GMSK is inherently differential, the precoder removes the need for differential decoding and improves receiver performance.14154 GMSK and baseband-filtered OQPSK can both be received with a conventional OQPSK receiver, at the price of extra losses if the receiver is not matched.54

docs.text:

Sources: the respective CCSDS recommendations.545556585962 For the higher-order schemes CCSDS also specifies the RF chain: modulator phase imbalance at most 5° (3° for 32APSK and 64APSK) and amplitude imbalance 0.5 dB, AM/PM slope below 5°/dB unless the receiver equalizes, phase-noise masks, and linearization or equalization at least from 16APSK; it regards as acceptable, even without equalization, a channel with up to 0.1 dB ripple, at least 30 dB out-of-band rejection and group-delay variation up to 10 % of the symbol duration.5662 For BPSK, (O)QPSK, GMSK and 8PSK in general, 2.4.12A/B set 5° and 0.5 dB.47

Spectral roll-off and stability. Above 60 ksps, telemetry in 2 200–2 290, 8 025–8 400 and 8 450–8 500 MHz must fit the spectral masks of ECSS Figure 6-5, measured against \(R_{ES}\) (2 × Rs for SP-L; including the trellis overhead for 8PSK TCM).133 Carrier suppression must exceed 30 dBc, discrete lines stay below −45 dBc, and the symbol rate must be within ±1 × 10⁻⁴ of nominal, stable to ±1 × 10⁻⁵ over 5 minutes and ±1 × 10⁻⁶ over 100 symbols (CCSDS 2.4.19 asks for ±100 ppm, ±1 × 10⁻⁶ and ±1 × 10⁻⁵).13257

docs.title: 4D-8PSK trellis-coded modulation
docs.text: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §9.2 specifies the European 4-dimensional 8PSK TCM used for Earth-exploration downlinks: a serial-to-parallel converter, a differential encoder (removing the 22.5° ambiguity), a 64-state, constraint length 7, rate-¾ systematic trellis encoder with the octal polynomials h3 = 050, h2 = 024, h1 = 006, h0 = 103, a constellation mapper delivering four 3-bit symbols with natural mapping, and an 8PSK modulator.142 Two spectral efficiency factors are allowed: SEF = 2 (b = 8 input lines) and SEF = 2.5 (b = 10), giving \(R_{ES} = 1.5\,R_S\) and \(1.2\,R_S\) respectively; shaping is SRRC with α = 0.35 or 0.5 before a linear modulator, or an elliptic filter after a nonlinear amplifier.142143 CCSDS 2.4.18 allows four efficiencies (2.0, 2.25, 2.5 and 2.75 b/s/Hz) where ECSS keeps two; the handbook records that only European agencies had declared an intention to use the scheme.56177

docs.title: Link acquisition
docs.text:
Acquisition is where the physical layer interacts most directly with operations.

Space-to-Earth. Normally on-board automation switches the transmitter on at the scheduled start of a pass, modulated with at least housekeeping telemetry, and the ground allows time for a triangular frequency search at worst-case margin. As a secondary mode the transmitter can be switched on by telecommand after the uplink sweep. Coherent mode is activated automatically or by telecommand once the uplink is confirmed locked; if the coherent/non-coherent switch causes a frequency step that loses telemetry, the downlink must be re-acquired.134

Earth-to-space. The ECSS procedure for the 2 025–2 110 MHz Category A band is the template for the others.135

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unmodulated: carrier on, no data or subcarrier
    Unmodulated --> Sweep: symmetrical triangular sweep,<br/>phase continuous, constant rate
    Sweep --> Centre: single sweep ends at centre frequency
    Centre --> Locked: lock status in spacecraft TM<br/>(standard location: CLCW)
    Locked --> Assigned: Cat A - carrier brought back<br/>to the assigned value
    Locked --> Compensated: Cat B - Doppler-compensated,<br/>kept within ±5 kHz of best lock
    Assigned --> Commanding: idle sequence, then CLTUs<br/>(subcarrier and bit lock from preamble)
    Compensated --> Commanding
    Commanding --> [*]

The states paraphrase ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §7.2.1–7.2.2; the on-board demodulators must not rely on a frequency sweep for subcarrier or bit acquisition but on the preamble that precedes uplink messages, and outside acquisition the idle sequence is transmitted to limit uplink power spectral density.135 The lock flags of the CLCW and the PLOP carrier modulation modes are the data-link counterparts of this procedure.135181

Sources: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §7.2 and the CCSDS recommendations cited.1351361516171832333435 CCSDS explains the Category A uplink numbers: Doppler up to ±80 kHz at 2 GHz and ±300 kHz at 7 GHz, receiver rest-frequency uncertainty of ±50 kHz and ±200 kHz, but Doppler predictable to ±1 kHz.15

The ECSS handbook describes a failure mode on the receive side, the transponder dual lock condition: one transponder receiver operates very close to its telecommand threshold (for example about −122 dBm), and so at an inadequate bit error rate, while the other receiver is well above its threshold, which can cause telecommands to be rejected. Recent near-Earth and Lagrange-point designs such as Cryosat-2 combine both low-gain antennas through a 3 dB hybrid so that both receivers see the best uplink signal, a configuration the handbook says avoids this situation. It names the COP-1 sequence-controlled (AD) service as the best operational remedy for the resulting frame rejections, recommends it for all near-Earth missions, and strongly recommends a realistic pre-launch compatibility test.179

docs.title: Ranging and Doppler tracking (ECSS-E-ST-50-02C)
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-50-02C applies to projects needing unprocessed ranging accuracies of 2.5–30 ns and Doppler accuracies of 0.1–1 mm/s; less demanding projects may follow CCSDS 401.0-B.148180 Measurements use an active transponder that re-transmits the uplink signal; ranging signals are generated and measured in the Earth station, and the same transponder normally also carries telecommand and telemetry.151 The standard divides the system into five functions:151

flowchart TB
    ES["Earth-to-space link function<br/>ranging signal generation (tone + code),<br/>source selection RNG / TC / RNG+TC, PM, up-conversion"]
    TR["Transponder function<br/>carrier tracking, TC and ranging demodulation,<br/>independent carrier and baseband AGC,<br/>coherent / non-coherent, source selection"]
    SE["Space-to-Earth link function<br/>carrier tracking, integrated Doppler,<br/>ranging replica, correlation"]
    LC["Link control function<br/>tone → tone + codes → final code"]
    DA["Data acquisition function<br/>Doppler, ranging and meteo data<br/>to the control centre"]
    CAL["Ground calibration transponder<br/>station delay calibration"]
    ES --> TR --> SE --> DA
    LC -.-> ES
    LC -.-> SE
    ES --> CAL --> SE

docs.title: The tone-plus-code ranging signal
docs.text:
The baseband ranging signal is a sine-wave tone of frequency \(f_t\) that is phase-modulated by a series of codes used to resolve the ambiguity of the tone phase. The n-th code is \(C_n = Q_1 \oplus Q_2 \oplus \dots \oplus Q_n\), where \(Q_i\) is a square wave at \(2^{-i} f_t\) (the outputs of a divide-by-two chain driven by the tone), and code transitions occur when the unmodulated tone phase is 90°. Each code is sent for a fixed time so that the ground can correlate and align its replica; a simple implementation sends \(C_{n-1}\) followed by its complement.154 The link-control sequence is tone alone, tone with the sequence of codes, then tone with the final code; deep-space missions may restart the sequence continuously, trading accuracy for faster re-acquisition.152

As codes are added, the spectrum evolves from discrete lines at multiples of \(f_t\) to a quasi-continuous spectrum between \(2^{-N}f_t\) and \((2-2^{-N})f_t\), N being the longest code.157 On the Earth-to-space link the tone is selectable from 100 kHz to 1.5 MHz, the code period is \(2^n/f_t\) with n = 0 … 20, the modulation is PCM/PSK/PM, and the tone-to-code modulation index is 45° during ambiguity resolution and 22.5° during measurement.161

Illustrative arithmetic: ambiguity of a 698.26 kHz tone

The tone period of \(f_t\) = 698 260 Hz (the Herschel/Planck tone, see the worked example below) is 1.432 µs, which repeats every 214.7 m of one-way range. A code with n = 20 has a period of \(2^{20}/f_t\) = 1.502 s, so the ambiguity grows to about 225 000 km one way. These figures are this wiki's arithmetic from the code-period definition, not values stated in the standard.161

docs.title: Choosing the tone
docs.text:
ECSS selects the lowest tone compatible with TC, TM and ranging to minimise bandwidth, keeps \(f_t\) (plus or minus Doppler) within 100 kHz–1.5 MHz in a region of stable transponder group delay, and gives spacing rules against the telemetry and telecommand spectra:153158

  • against telemetry with subcarrier \(f_{sc}\) and symbol rate \(f_{symb}\), with \(D\) the one-way Doppler factor: \(|Df_t - f_{sc}| \ge 2.5 f_{symb}\), \(|Df_t - 3f_{sc}| \ge f_{symb}\) and \(|k f_{symb} - Df_t| \ge 5\) Hz; for SP-L telemetry take \(f_{sc} = f_{symb}\), and if no compatible tone results, place \(f_t\) near an SP-L spectral null but more than the Doppler shift plus 5 Hz away;158
  • against PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM telecommand with subcarrier \(f_{TC}\) and bit rate \(f_b\): \(|2m f_{TC} - f_t| \ge 5\) Hz and \(|(2n-1) f_{TC} - f_t| \ge 2f_b\); for PCM(SP-L)/PM telecommand, \(|f_t - f_b| \ge 2.5 f_b\), \(|f_t - 3f_b| \ge f_b\) and \(|k f_b - f_t| \ge 5\) Hz.159

Simultaneous ranging and telecommand should be used to avoid scheduling conflicts, with time sharing if the link budget does not allow it; slow on-board baseband AGC can transiently over-modulate the downlink when TC or ranging starts, which ramping the uplink modulation can mitigate.156 Suppressed-carrier telemetry is not compatible with simultaneous tone ranging, so orbit determination must then use integrated Doppler on the regenerated carrier, time sharing between telemetry and ranging, or a separate ranging transponder.155

docs.title: Performance and ancillary measurements
docs.text:
Integrated Doppler is not a series of independent velocity measurements but the continuous phase of the received carrier relative to its reference: \(\varphi(t) - \varphi_0 = 2\pi\int\Delta f\,d\tau \approx -(2\pi q F_T \cdot 2/c)\int v\,d\tau\), a high-resolution measurement of the change in range up to an unknown constant ("non-destructive range-rate measurement"). One-way Doppler is also possible with the transponder non-coherent, relative to the downlink carrier.173 Its error budget distinguishes bias (station reference drift, digital synthesis offsets, acceleration effects) from jitter (reference, converters, transponder stability, thermal and phase noise, quantization below 1/1000 of a carrier period).167 For ranging, the quantization must be at most 1/65 536 of the tone period and the station's measurement accuracy 1 ns or 1/1000 of the tone period, whichever is larger; station calibration before and after a pass is required when group-delay drift would exceed the mission need.168

Propagation corrections need meteorological data at the station (pressure ±1 hPa, temperature ±1 °C, relative humidity ±1 %), multiple-frequency ranging or Doppler, or differenced range versus integrated Doppler (DRVID), and the antenna phase centre known to 0.5 m.169 CCSDS 3.4.2 tabulates which charged-particle calibration methods (Faraday rotation, DRVID, dual frequency) apply to which tracking modes.88 At ESA's ESTRACK stations the IF and modem system (IFMS) makes these measurements available to data clients such as the NCTRS as Doppler, AGC, meteorological, open-loop and ranging data sets; see NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface.197

docs.title: Compatibility with CCSDS networks
docs.text: ECSS Annex A explains that CCSDS assumes different ranging systems: for Category A a 100 kHz major tone with minor tones down to 4 kHz (hence the 3–110 kHz transponder passband of CCSDS 2.5.4A), for Category B a 1 MHz tone with code components down to 1 Hz (3 kHz–1.1 MHz, noise bandwidth ≤ 3.5 MHz, CCSDS 2.5.4B). ECSS-compliant transponders do not automatically meet those low-frequency requirements, but no major incompatibility is expected, at some cost in performance.1716970 The handbook adds that other techniques, Differential One-way Ranging and regenerative ranging, are not included in the ECSS standard (it names ECSS-E-ST-50-05) and that CCSDS was working on recommendations for them. CCSDS 401.0-B-32 addresses both: regenerative PN ranging in 2.5.5A and 2.4.22A/B, and Delta-DOR in 2.5.6B (see below).180716072

docs.title: Compatibility testing
docs.text: ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §5 requires tests with engineering qualification models (often in a portable "suitcase") of: non-coherent downlink frequency versus time after switch-on; spectrum (spurious and modulation indices); transmitter power; downlink phase jitter; ranging group delay and jitter versus tone, levels, Doppler, index and presence of TC/TM; correct ambiguity resolution; coherent phase stability (Allan variance); and turnaround ratio versus input frequency.170 CCSDS 3.5.1 lists a wider minimum set covering spacecraft RF, telemetry, telecommand, ranging, Doppler and antenna tracking, performed from maximum power down to threshold.89

docs.title: CCSDS radio-metric and advanced ranging recommendations
Group delay and ranging channel
docs.text:
Rec. Requirement 2.5.1A / 2.5.1B station group delay calibrated to ≤ 10 ns (A) or ≤ 7 ns 1σ (B, 7 145–7 190 / 8 400–8 450 MHz, consistent with 2 m range accuracy) 2.5.2A / 2.5.2B station ranging group delay variation ≤ 20 ns (A) or ≤ 2 ns (B) over any 12 h; Category B delay rate within ±0.1 mm/s 2.5.3A / 2.5.3B spacecraft ranging-channel delay variation ≤ ±50 ns (A) or ±30 ns (B); calibration to ±5 ns or ±2.5 ns at any time; Category B differential delay between channels < ±2 ns 2.5.4A / 2.5.4B transponder ranging passband flat to ±0.5 dB over 3–110 kHz (A) or 3 kHz–1.1 MHz (B); phase linear within ±6° 2.5.5A PN code delay through a regenerative transponder within 20 ns of its pre-launch calibration

Sources: CCSDS 2.5.1A–2.5.5A.11666768697071 The rationale is a 10 m accuracy budget for Category A orbit determination (station share 30 %, transponder 15 %) and 3 m for Category B.6768

Policy recommendation 3.4.1 asks all agencies to design spacecraft for simultaneous telecommand, telemetry and ranging, because station time is expensive and telemetry interruptions lose data.87 3.3.1 requires sine-wave ranging on Category A uplinks when combined with telecommand (either waveform for Category B) and recommends sine-wave ranging on all downlinks shared with telemetry.86

docs.title: PN ranging with GMSK telemetry
docs.text:
GMSK and filtered OQPSK cannot carry a conventional residual-carrier ranging signal, yet some missions need both high-rate telemetry and precise ranging. CCSDS 2.4.22A (Category A, 8.45–8.50 GHz) and 2.4.22B (Category B, 8.40–8.45 and 31.8–32.3 GHz) combine GMSK with an on-board regenerated PN ranging signal through a phase modulator, which keeps a constant envelope and allows an always-on ranging capability.6061

Parameter Value Ranging chip shaping half-sine: \(h(t) = \sin(\pi t/T_C)\) for \(0 \le t \le T_C\), with \(T_C = 1/R_{RG}\) Peak ranging index \(m_{RG}\) 0.2–0.45 rad without ranging cancellation; 0.2–0.7 rad with cancellation PN code T4B when accuracy matters most; T2B when acquisition time matters most Chip-rate to telemetry symbol-rate ratio without cancellation, a non-integer above 1 (performance figures valid for 1–3; slightly below 1 allowed if margins permit); with cancellation, a non-integer (performance figures valid for ⅓–10); chip and symbol rates not coherent Telemetry symbol error rate better than 0.1 at the receiver Typical losses telemetry 0.2–1.0 dB (below 0.1 dB with cancellation); ranging SNR 0.3–3.0 dB; ranging jitter variance +0.3–1.5 dB; carrier jitter variance +0.2–1.0 dB

Sources: CCSDS 2.4.22A and 2.4.22B.6061 The PN ranging codes themselves are defined in CCSDS 414.1-B-2, which is not in this wiki's library; their structure is not stated in the available sources. The Solar Orbiter MIB nevertheless exposes the T2B/T4B choice (see below).

docs.title: Telemetry ranging
docs.text:
CCSDS 2.4.24 (added in Issue 30, February 2020) goes one step further and removes the downlink ranging signal altogether.2 The spacecraft tracks an uplink PN ranging signal (per CCSDS 414.1-B-2) and latches the range code phase, on a signal triggered by the transmission of the leading edge of a frame's synchronization marker, together with that frame's frame counter (FC). The pairs are sent to the ground as ordinary telemetry, and the ground computes range from the uplink tuning history, the time-tagged uplink PN phase, the on-board phase and the frame's Earth-received time.6364

sequenceDiagram
    participant G as Ground (uplink range assembly)
    participant S as Spacecraft transponder
    participant T as Telemetry encoder
    participant R as Ground TM receiver
    G->>S: uplink PN ranging signal (phase time-tagged on ground)
    S->>S: acquire and track range code phase ψ(t)
    T-->>S: start of frame (leading edge of sync marker), FC = n
    S->>S: latch ψ at start of frame, pair (ψ, FC)
    S->>T: insert (ψ, FC) pair into a later TM frame (mission-specific format)
    T->>R: TM frames, no downlink PN signal
    R->>R: measure Earth-received time of frame FC = n
    R->>G: range = f(tuning history, uplink phase, ψ, ERT)
Item Requirement or value Bands space-to-Earth 8.40–8.50 GHz (Categories A and B) and 31.8–32.3 GHz (Category B) Range code phase format 40-bit number = chips × 2²⁰, rounded, in 5 octets, bit 0 = MSB, bit 39 = LSB Range code period L = 1 009 479 chips Resolution 1 ps for a 2 Mchip/s sequence (40 bits) Accuracy 1 m standard deviation at ≥ 200 ksps coded symbol rate, total timing error below 6 ns Cost up to 4 % of telemetry throughput Restriction no punctured convolutional or punctured concatenated codes Compatibility GMSK or filtered OQPSK above 2 Msps; other CCSDS modulations at lower rates Frames TM or AOS Transfer Frames; FC type, position and size depend on the frame type

Sources: CCSDS 2.4.24 and its Appendices A and B.636465

Inference

CCSDS 2.4.24 specifies only a single 40-bit value (chips × 2²⁰). The split into 20 integer and 20 fractional bits shown above follows arithmetically from L = 1 009 479 < 2²⁰ = 1 048 576 and is this wiki's presentation. Illustrative encoding (constructed, not from a source): a phase of 123 456.75 chips gives 123 456.75 × 2²⁰ = 0x1E240C0000, sent as octets 1E 24 0C 00 00. One 2²⁰ step at 2 Mchip/s is about 0.48 ps, consistent with the stated 1 ps resolution, and the full code period at that rate is 0.505 s.6364

docs.title: Delta-DOR
docs.text:
Differential One-way Ranging measures the angular position of a Category B spacecraft by VLBI: two widely separated stations record sine-wave DOR tones phase-modulated on the downlink, and the difference of their arrival times, corrected by observing an angularly nearby quasar (ΔDOR), gives a geometric delay. The delay precision is \(\varepsilon_\tau = 1/(\pi f_{BW}\sqrt{2 (P_{DOR}/N_0) T_{obs}})\), where \(f_{BW}\) is the spanned bandwidth (usually twice the tone frequency).72

Item CCSDS 2.5.6B Waveform sine-wave tones, phase-modulated on the RF carrier; coherent with the carrier if carrier-aided detection is used Number of tones 1 at 2 GHz, 2 at 8 GHz, 3 at 32 and 37 GHz Tone frequencies ±1 or ±4 MHz; plus ±20 MHz at 8 GHz; plus ±20 and ±76 MHz at 32/37 GHz (a 250 kHz–1 MHz telemetry subcarrier can replace the 1 MHz tone) Detection threshold PDOR/N₀ ≈ 13 dBHz direct, 1 dBHz carrier-aided (carrier SNR > 13 dB) Oscillator stability (one-way) Δf/f ≤ 4 × 10⁻¹⁰ (2 GHz), 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ (8 GHz), 0.3 × 10⁻¹⁰ (32/37 GHz) over 1 s Power enough in the outermost tone for the orbit-determination need, but PDOR/N₀ ≤ 30 dBHz; in-flight index reduction capability Protection PFD outside the deep-space band ≤ −211 dBW/m² (8 GHz) and −204 dBW/m² (32 GHz); no tones in 31.3–31.8 GHz Example 38.25 MHz spanned bandwidth, 600 s observation: 1.0 dBHz for ετSC = 0.21 ns, 24.1 dBHz for 0.015 ns

Source: CCSDS 2.5.6B and Table 2.5.6B-2.7273

docs.title: Multiple spacecraft per aperture
docs.text: CCSDS 3.1.7 lists four ways to serve several spacecraft in one Earth station beam (MSPA): time-multiplexed uplinks (short term), a flexible turnaround ratio with one common uplink frequency and commands separated by spacecraft identifier (intermediate, see 2.6.13), multiple uplink carriers through one HPA (intermediate, see 2.1.9) and CDMA (long term).84 Table 3.1.7-1 was written while the related recommendations were "under development" and points the flexible-ratio method to 2.1.9 and the multiple-carrier method to 2.6.13, the reverse of what those two recommendations now contain.842276 Recommendation 2.1.9 asks stations using multiple uplink carriers to dimension linearizers and HPA back-off so that intermodulation stays at the ITU spurious limit of −60 dBc.22 Separation by spacecraft identifier is where this physical-layer option meets the data link layer.

docs.title: Link budgets and RF interface control
docs.text:
CCSDS Design Control Table. Recommendation 4.1.2 defines a standard telecommunications link Design Control Table (DCT) so agencies can exchange link performance: every parameter has a design value and favourable and adverse tolerances, with 3-sigma tolerances for telecommand and 2-sigma for other links.92 Recommendation 4.1.4 assigns default probability density functions, and 4.1.5 provides algorithms for the mean and variance of the modulation losses ("the fraction of the total transmitted power allotted to a designated channel"), avoiding the 512 tolerance combinations that a coherent ranging channel with TC and TM would otherwise require.1294

ECSS link budget tables. ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §8.3 uses the DCT terminology with its own layout: separate budgets per parameter combination at the maximum planned distance; for each parameter a design value D, adverse tolerance A and favourable tolerance F; a mean and variance computed from the uniform, triangular or Gaussian density assigned to that parameter (Table 8-1); and margins on the design values above 3 dB and on the mean minus 3σ and the RSS worst case above 0 dB.138139

Density (ECSS Table 8-1) Example parameters Uniform Earth-station antenna gain and losses, polarization loss, phase jitter loss, waveform distortion Triangular spacecraft antenna gain and pointing loss, transmit power and EIRP, demodulator and ranging losses, loop bandwidths Gaussian atmospheric attenuation, ionospheric loss, system noise temperature

Interface control. A spacecraft-Earth station interface control document, drafted in Phase B and controlled by the project manager, records stations and usage profile, station and spacecraft configurations and performance with tolerances, applicable TTC standards and waivers, the selected parameter subsets (PCM types, bit rates, subcarriers, indices) and the TTC subsystem operational modes; it feeds the link budget tables. Compatibility is demonstrated by tests per ECSS-E-ST-10-03 using at least an engineering model, with a test plan before and a test report after.137144140 The Herschel/Planck SGICD below is a real example of such a document.

docs.title: ECSS versus CCSDS
docs.text:
Topic ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Rev. 2 CCSDS 401.0-B Category B telecommand waveform NRZ-L only, for its better performance NRZ-L or NRZ-M (2.2.3) Filtered OQPSK at Category A high rate specific filters and roll-off only any filter with equivalent BTs ≤ 0.5 meeting the SFCG mask; all quaternary offset types interoperate EES 8 GHz 4D-8PSK TCM at 2.0 and 2.5 b/s/Hz, GMSK, restricted filtered OQPSK 4D-8PSK TCM at 2.0–2.75 b/s/Hz, SRRC QPSK/OQPSK/8PSK/APSK and filtered OQPSK (Issue 32); GMSK, which 401.0-B-20 still listed for this band, is no longer among the options FQPSK-B, shaped OQPSK not included; Rev. 2 aligned Annex D with their suppression in 401.0-B-20 listed in earlier issues (the 2008 handbook still compares against them), since removed Filtered OQPSK in 8 400–8 450 MHz removed in Rev. 2, to align with 401.0-B-20 GMSK for Category B (2.4.17B) Scope Earth stations and spacecraft, no data relay; normative requirements recommendations; Part 2 (data relay) foreseen

Sources: ECSS-E-ST-50-05C change log, scope and Annex D, the handbook's difference analysis, and the CCSDS Foreword and Rec. 2.4.18.9899145177178156

Inference

ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Rev. 2 compares itself against CCSDS 401.0-B-20 (April 2009). Recommendations that CCSDS added or rewrote later, such as the APSK options of 2.4.18 and 2.4.23, GMSK+PN ranging (2.4.22A/B, 2015), telemetry ranging (2.4.24, 2020), MSPA (3.1.7, 2.1.9, 2.6.13) and the 2.6.14/2.6.15 ratios, therefore have no ECSS counterpart in the documents available here. This is deduced from the dates in both documents, not stated by either.982

docs.title: Worked example: the Herschel/Planck X-band link (real values)
docs.text:
The Herschel/Planck Space/Ground Interface Control Document (SCI-PT-ICD-07418, issue 3.2, December 2004) shows how a real mission picks values inside these standards. Both spacecraft were Category A X-band missions with redundant transponders.182

Item Herschel / Planck (SGICD) Standard it satisfies Downlink 8 468.5 MHz / 8 455.0 MHz, 8 450–8 500 MHz band, RHC 8 450–8 500 MHz Category A band; circular polarization Uplink 7 207.8483 MHz / 7 196.3580 MHz, 7 190–7 235 MHz, 3 MHz emission bandwidth 7 190–7 235 MHz Category A Turnaround 749/880 CCSDS 2.6.2, ECSS Table 5-1 TC PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM, 16 kHz sine subcarrier, 125 bps and 4 kbps, index 1 rad 8/16 kHz sine; 4000/2⁵ and 4000/2⁰; 4 kbps with 16 kHz TM low rates 500 bps and 5 kbps, PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM, 45 884 Hz sine subcarrier, ratios N = 40 and 4 sine subcarrier for Category A; integer ratio TM medium rate 150 kbps, PCM(SP-L)/PM, with a pre-modulation filter SP-L direct modulation above 60 ksps TM high rate 1.5 Mbps, GMSK BTb = 0.25; no ranging at this rate (Doppler only) GMSK BTs 0.25 for Category A Coding RS(255,223), I = 5, plus convolutional rate ½, k = 7; ASM 0x1ACFFC1D; randomizer TM coding Ranging tone 698 260 Hz, 10 kHz from an SP-L null ECSS-E-ST-50-02C tone selection Uplink sweep ±130 kHz at 500 Hz/s, discontinuity ≤ 1 Hz, within 3 min (TBC) ECSS 7.2.4 (100 Hz/s–50 kHz/s, ≤ ±500 kHz, 1 Hz) Modes uplink: carrier, command, ranging, both; downlink: carrier, TM, ranging, both; coherent/non-coherent settable by TC ECSS-E-ST-50-02C 4.5.2

Sources: SGICD §2.1–2.2 and §3.1; standards as cited above.184185186187188189190

The numbers check out. \(7\,207.8483 \times 880/749 = 8\,468.500\) MHz and \(7\,196.3580 \times 880/749 = 8\,455.000\) MHz, the published downlinks. The ratio column of the rate table gives \(45\,884/1\,147.1 = 40\) and \(45\,884/11\,471 = 4\), and the medium-rate transmitted symbol rate is 344 130 sps.186 The change record says the tone was set at 1 kHz from the SP-L null in issue 3.0 and corrected in issue 3.1 to give a 10 kHz offset.183

Inference

An SP-L spectrum at 344 130 sps has a null at twice the symbol rate, 688 260 Hz; the tone of 698 260 Hz is exactly 10 kHz above it (and the earlier 687 260 Hz exactly 1 kHz below). That placement is the fallback that ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §4.2.3.2.2c prescribes when the general spacing rules give no tone compatible with the mission. With \(f_{sc} = f_{symb}\) = 344 130 Hz those rules only leave tones above about 1.38 MHz, whose ECSS occupied bandwidth of 2.5 × ft would exceed the SGICD's 2.0 MHz ranging emission bandwidth. The SGICD does not show this calculation.188186184158109

Some illustrative arithmetic (this wiki's, with the formulas of CCSDS 4.1.5, 4.2 and ECSS Annex C):

  • Uplink power split. With a 1 rad index on a sine subcarrier, the carrier keeps \(J_0^2(1) = 0.586\) (−2.3 dB) of the power and the telecommand sidebands \(2J_1^2(1) = 0.387\) (−4.1 dB).93191
  • Downlink power split. A 1.2 rad SP-L telemetry index leaves \(\cos^2(1.2) = 0.131\) (−8.8 dB) in the carrier; adding 0.7 rad of sine-wave ranging multiplies by \(J_0^2(0.7) = 0.777\), giving about −9.9 dB. The SGICD sets these nominal indices (±10 %) and, as printed, also requires the combined telemetry and ranging indices to give "carrier suppressions of more than or equal to 15 dB"; how this squares with the −9.9 dB above and with the ECSS rule of a residual carrier above −15 dBc is not explained in the available sources.93192126
  • Bandwidth. CCSDS 4.2.1 estimates the unfiltered 99 % bandwidth of the 150 kbps SP-L signal as \(2(26.2 \times 1.2 - 5.16) \times 344\,130 \approx 18\) MHz, far above the 6.2 MHz medium-rate emission bandwidth, which is consistent with the SGICD's demand for a pre-modulation filter. For the 500 bps mode (n = 40), CCSDS 4.2.2 gives \(4 \times 40 \times 1\,147.1 \approx 184\) kHz against an allotted 340 kHz.9596184185
  • Doppler. At 1 km/s receding radial velocity, the two-way shift measured on the 8 468.5 MHz coherent downlink is \(-q F_T \cdot 2v/c \approx -56.5\) kHz, while the one-way shift seen by the spacecraft receiver at 7 207.8 MHz is about −24 kHz, well inside the ±130 kHz uplink sweep that the SGICD sizes for the maximum Doppler.173189

docs.title: Solar Orbiter's deep-space transponder in the MIB
docs.text: The library has no Solar Orbiter RF interface document. The early Experiment Interface Document assumed an X-band uplink, parallel X- and Ka-band downlinks and support for state-of-the-art ΔDOR, and the E-FECS planning ICD shows that each pass event carries the downlink rate, the modulation, whether ranging is on, and a "MIB code" for the transponder configuration.193195 The Solar Orbiter MIB, however, defines the deep space transponder (DST) telemetry and commands in detail, and they line up closely with the requirements above. The actual Solar Orbiter frequencies and turnaround ratio are not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: The DST housekeeping packet
docs.text:
The 2025 MIB has 428 parameters whose description starts with "DST" (case-insensitive match; 416 in 2020). The main report is SPID 33793 "PLF DST HK", a ST[03] TM(3,25) report on APID 212 with SID 93 and 165 parameter placements in both releases. It carries the two transponders (DST-A from octet 17, DST-B from octet 49), four supply voltages from octet 81, and from octet 97 the configuration selections held on board (output power, DOR, coherence, ranging type and scheme, TM rate, index and scheme).198199 Offsets below are PLF octet and bit offsets, counted from the start of the source packet with bit 0 the most significant.198

Fields shown as "(none)" or "(no individual parameter)" are covered only by the 16-bit word parameters (NDSG0001 to NDSG0005); the MIB does not name them. The analog part of each block (from octet 29 for DST-A) holds the non-coherent and coherent AGC in dBm, the "SPE" in Hz, subcarrier, ESA-ranging and PN-ranging AGCs, the measured RF output power, three internal temperatures and the software version; octets 81–96 carry four receiver and transmitter voltages.198 ECSS-E-ST-50-02C expands SPE as static phase error, and CCSDS 2.5.3A/B list static phase error, with voltage and temperature, among the telemetered data used to calculate the transponder's ranging group delay.15068

This maps almost one to one onto ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §4.5.5, which requires telemetry on the mode, the receiver input level, the offset from best lock frequency, the lock status, and the temperature and supply voltage:165198

ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §4.5.5 item Solar Orbiter MIB parameter(s), DST-A chosen mode of operation NDSD0063 coherent on/off, NDSD0043 ranging on/off, NDSD0022 ranging type, NDSD0053 DOR on/off, NDSD0033 TM modulation on/off receiver input level NDS00009 non-coherent AGC and NDS00010 coherent AGC, dBm offset from best lock frequency NDS00011 "DST-A SPE", Hz, calibrated by curves named "DstLoopStress" lock status NDSD0021 carrier, NDSD0031 subcarrier, NDSD0041 bit sync, NDSD0071 PN tracking temperature and supply voltage NDS00027, NDS00017, NDS00018 (Tx, Rx, digital, °C); NCFT1Y10, NCFT1Y20 (DST1 Rx and Tx voltages)

docs.title: Calibrations and enumerations
docs.text:
The textual calibrations record the transponder's options:198

Calibration Values Compared with the standards CDST0003TM TC bit rate 7.8125, 15.625, 250, 1000, 2000, 4000 bps all of the form 4000/2ⁿ (n = 9, 8, 4, 2, 1, 0), the CCSDS 2.2.4 / ECSS Table 6-1 set CDST0005TM TM modulation index 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25 rad-pk the top value equals the ECSS maximum for SP-L or square-wave telemetry CDST0009TM TM modulation scheme GMSK, SPL two of the options ECSS allows above 60 ksps: SP-L directly on the carrier, or a suppressed-carrier scheme such as GMSK (BTs 0.5 for Category B) CDST0006TM TM symbol rate 67 rates, 21.3333 sps to 3 333 333.33 sps the top rates exceed 2 Msps, where Category B requires GMSK CDST0001TM / CCDT0234TX ranging PN, STD (command side: PN, STDESA) PN ranging (CCSDS 414.1) or ESA standard tone ranging (ECSS-E-ST-50-02C) CDST0002TM / CCDT0233TX PN scheme T2B, T4B the two PN codes named by CCSDS 2.4.22A/B CDST0008TM DOR index (high and low) 0.0, 0.1, 0.2 rad-pk two DOR tones at 8 GHz in CCSDS 2.5.6B, whose recommends (9) asks for in-flight index flexibility CDST0010TM receiver state POR_Init, Sig_Det, C_Acq_WB, C_Track_WB, SC_Track_WB, C_Acq_IB, C_Track_IB, SC_Track_IB, C_Acq_NB, C_Track_NB, SC_Track_NB acquisition and tracking of carrier and subcarrier CCDT0313TX TM rate mode ("Dst TM symbol rate modulation id") 147 modes from BPSK_2_21 to GMSK_2_2000000, plus SPL_… and GMSK_4_… combined rate, scheme and coding settings

Numerical calibrations show the physics behind the raw counts. The SPE calibration CDSP0055TM "DST DstLoopStress_EM" maps raw 0 … 2³¹ − 1 to 0 … +86 187 499.5 Hz and raw 2³¹ … 2³² − 1 to −86 187 499.5 … 0 Hz, a two's-complement reading of the unsigned 32-bit field; the coherent AGC curve CDSP0044TM "DST_CAGCPwrPFM_WB" is a 16-point table (for example raw 28 → −95 dBm, 243 → −120 dBm, 936 → −132 dBm); and the CUR table selects among twelve such curves for NDS00010 by flight unit (EM, PFM, FM1, FM2) and by WB, IB or NB, and between two curves for the ranging index NDSD0044 by ranging type (STD or PN).198

Inference

Several readings above are this wiki's, not documented in the MIB: that WB, IB and NB denote wide, intermediate and narrow carrier-loop bandwidths (supported by the AGC curves being selected per bandwidth); that "SPE" (static phase error) is the loop-stress measurement ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §7.2.2c requires for estimating best lock frequency; that the "High" and "Low" DOR indices drive the two 8 GHz DOR tones of CCSDS 2.5.6B; and that in rate-mode names such as GMSK_4_2000000 the middle digit is the turbo code-rate denominator (2 or 4, matching TURBO_1_2 and TURBO_1_4 of NCFT1YN0, see TM coding) and the last number the symbol rate (the calibration's own description, "Dst TM symbol rate modulation id", and pairs such as BPSK_2_21/BPSK_4_42, whose symbol rates differ by exactly the factor of two between rate ½ and rate ¼ coding, support this). The BPSK_… modes stop at 52 428 sps and the SPL_…/GMSK_… modes start at 60 787 sps, which matches the ECSS rule that subcarriers are not used above 60 ksps, so "BPSK" plausibly means PSK on a subcarrier; the transponder's own scheme parameter only offers GMSK and SPL. How the 6-bit ranging-index field relates to the 0–1023 domain of its calibration and of the 12-bit command parameter is not stated in the available sources.198121136

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> POR_Init
    POR_Init --> Sig_Det: signal detected
    Sig_Det --> C_Acq_WB
    C_Acq_WB --> C_Track_WB: carrier acquired
    C_Track_WB --> SC_Track_WB: subcarrier tracked
    SC_Track_WB --> C_Acq_IB: narrow the loop
    C_Acq_IB --> C_Track_IB
    C_Track_IB --> SC_Track_IB
    SC_Track_IB --> C_Acq_NB

Inference

The diagram only orders the eleven enumerated values of CDST0010TM; the MIB defines no transitions, and the sequence (wide to narrow, carrier before subcarrier) is this wiki's reading of the names.198

docs.title: DST commands
docs.text:
The transponder is commanded with TC(131,1) "Perform Functions" of Solar Orbiter's private service 131, Private Function Management, which controls on-board software functions that are not standard services, for example equipment management functions that switch units on or off. Its application data is a 2-octet Function ID followed by function-specific parameters (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS).196 In the MIB every DST command goes to APID 236 and starts with that 16-bit Function ID, followed by an 8-bit unit identifier (transmitter: DST_TX_CTR_A, DST_TX_CTR_B, DST_TX_INUSE, DST_TX_NOTUSE; receiver: DST_RX_CTR_A, DST_RX_CTR_B) and an 8-bit or 16-bit setting; 143 commands mention "DST" (case-insensitive match) in both MIB releases.198199

Command Description Function ID (fixed area) Setting parameter ZCSD3409 DST-TX Coherence ON-OFF 0x3409 PCSB0054 OFF/ON ZCSD3502 DST Set Ranging Type 0x340F PCSB00DC PN or STDESA ZCSD3503 DST Set PN Ranging Schm 0x3410 PCSB00DB T2B or T4B ZCSD3504 DST Set Ranging ON-OFF 0x3411 PCSB00DE "XBAND ranging on/off", OFF/ON ZCSD3401 Dst-TX Set RF ON-OFF 0x3401 PCSB0058 DST_TX_OFF_SEL / DST_TX_ON_SEL ZCSD340D DST-Tx Set DOR ON-OFF 0x340C PCSB0057 OFF/ON ZCSD3505 DST Set Ranging Mod idx 0x3412 PCSB00DD, 12-bit, range 0–1023 ZCSD3402 Dst Set TC Bit Rate 0x3402 PCSB004E, six rates from 7.8125 to 4000 bps ZCSD3406 DST-Tx Set TM Mod index 0x3406 PCSB0050, 0.25–1.25 rad-pk ZCSD3408 Set TLM Bitrate-Mod Schm 0x3408 PCSB0101, one of the 147 rate modes ZCSD340E DST-Tx Set Low DOR Tone 0x340D PCSB0056 "DST-TX DOR Tone Idx", DORMOD_RADPK00 to DORMOD_RADPK02

The coherence and ranging on/off commands are exactly the two independent telecommand-selectable modes that ECSS-E-ST-50-02C §4.5.2d requires of a coherent ranging transponder, and the selectable ranging index corresponds to §4.5.9b; the RF on/off command corresponds to the telecommanded cessation of emissions that ECSS-E-ST-50-05C §5.5.2 requires.164166113198

Inference

The MIB stores the first 16 bits of each command as a fixed area (CDF_ELTYPE = A, element description "Identification number of", truncated in the MIB) whose values (3409, 340F, ...) contain hexadecimal digits. Matching this field to the 2-octet Function ID of TC(131,1) follows the packet layout in the TM/TC ICD; the list of Function IDs itself is in a document the ICD references but which is not in the library. That Solar Orbiter is a Category B mission is likewise deduced, not stated as such: from its "deep space transponder", from the E-FECS reference to ESA's three deep-space stations, and from the EID-A's planned approach to 0.22 AU from the Sun, which puts the spacecraft at least about 0.78 AU (roughly 1.2 × 10⁸ km) from Earth, far beyond 2 × 10⁶ km.198195196194

SQL used 

-- DST parameters, by description (solo-2025-09-16.sqlite; 2020 release for comparison)
-- (LIKE is case-insensitive in SQLite; GLOB 'DST*' gives 426 / 414)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_DESCR LIKE 'DST%';
-- DST HK packet header and layout
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_SPID = '33793';
SELECT l.PLF_OFFBY, l.PLF_OFFBI, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC, l.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, c.PCF_CURTX, c.PCF_UNIT
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID = '33793'
 ORDER BY CAST(l.PLF_OFFBY AS INT), CAST(l.PLF_OFFBI AS INT);
-- textual calibrations
SELECT TXF_NUMBR, TXF_DESCR FROM txf WHERE TXF_NUMBR IN ('CDST0006TM','CCDT0313TX');
SELECT TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM, TXP_ALTXT FROM txp
 WHERE TXP_NUMBR IN ('CDST0001TM','CDST0002TM','CDST0003TM','CDST0005TM','CDST0006TM','CDST0008TM',
                     'CDST0009TM','CDST0010TM','CCDT0313TX','CCDT0233TX','CCDT0234TX')
 ORDER BY TXP_NUMBR, CAST(TXP_FROM AS INT);
-- numerical calibrations and curve selection
SELECT * FROM caf WHERE CAF_NUMBR IN ('CDSP0055TM','CDSP0044TM','CDSP0021TM','CDSP0022TM');
SELECT * FROM cap WHERE CAP_NUMBR IN ('CDSP0055TM','CDSP0044TM');
SELECT * FROM cur WHERE CUR_PNAME IN ('NDS00010','NDS00011','NDSD0044');
SELECT CAF_NUMBR, CAF_DESCR FROM caf WHERE CAF_NUMBR BETWEEN 'CDSP0039TM' AND 'CDSP0058TM';
-- commands and their parameters
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID FROM ccf WHERE CCF_DESCR LIKE '%DST%';
SELECT d.CDF_CNAME, d.CDF_BIT, d.CDF_ELTYPE, d.CDF_ELLEN, d.CDF_PNAME, d.CDF_VALUE,
       p.CPC_DESCR, p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_PAFREF, p.CPC_PRFREF
  FROM cdf d LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = d.CDF_PNAME
 WHERE d.CDF_CNAME IN ('ZCSD3401','ZCSD3402','ZCSD3406','ZCSD3408','ZCSD3409','ZCSD340D',
                       'ZCSD340E','ZCSD3502','ZCSD3503','ZCSD3504','ZCSD3505')
 ORDER BY d.CDF_CNAME, CAST(d.CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALVAL, PAS_ALTXT FROM pas
 WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CCDT0258TX','CCDT0020TC','CCDT0299TX','CCDT0222TC','CCDT0232TX','CCDT0234TX');
SELECT * FROM prv WHERE PRV_NUMBR = 'VCD00314';
