docs.text:
Question Where it is answered Should data link security be used at all, or another layer? 350.0-G-3, on this page What the Security Header and Trailer look like and how frames are processed SDLS (355.0-B-2) Why COP-1 frames, the OCF and the Insert Zone are unprotected 350.5-G-2, on this page; also SDLS Which algorithms and key sizes 352.0-B-2, on this page How keys reach the spacecraft and change state 355.1-B-1 Key Management, on this page How SAs are created, keyed, started and stopped in flight 355.1-B-1 SA Management, on this page How the ground learns of rejected frames The FSR, on this page; the CLCW on COP-1 Where ECSS points to SDLS for European missions ECSS-E-ST-50C and the adoption notices

The SDLS protocol standard specifies only the parameters of the SA data base. It leaves the services that manage them, and the initialization and maintenance of the data bases, to the Extended Procedures.221222 The Null, Unkeyed, Keyed and Operational states, and the directives that move between them, therefore come from 355.1-B-1, described above.

docs.title: In the Solar Orbiter MIB
docs.text:
The public Solar Orbiter MIB (release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL, and the April 2020 release) does not mention SDLS. Searches of parameter, command and textual-calibration descriptions for "SDLS", "crypt", "anti-replay", "Security Assoc" and "Frame Security" return nothing. "OTAR" matches only unrelated substrings such as "BootArea".226 Three items still relate to this page.

  1. "AU Mode" status. Four parameters in pcf report the mode of an "AU": NCDD05G1 OBCHP_TTRA_AU A Mode, NCDD05G2 OBCHP_TTRA_AU B Mode, and their TTRB counterparts NCDD05L1 and NCDD05L2. Each is a 1-bit enumerated parameter (PTC 2, PFC 1; see parameter types). Its textual calibration CCDT0046TM, "AU Mode" (tables txf and txp), maps 0 to CLEAR and 1 to SECURE. The four parameters appear in seven PUS TM(3,25) housekeeping packets on APIDs 162, 164 and 165, for example SPID 19500 "DMS OBC Status Fast" and SPID 19578 "DMS Safe Mode Slow". The 2020 release has the same parameters and calibration.227228
  2. MAP 0 for high-priority commands. 125 commands have CCF_MAPID = 0, and all of them have CCF_HIPRI = 'Y', for example ZBC04001 "Select PM A EEPROM Image 1" on APID 44. 128 commands use MAP 1 and 77 use MAP 54, and the remaining 5,124 have no MAP ID (see ccf). This matches 350.5-G-2's description of MAPs that route high-priority commands, and the URD note that direct commands on MAP 0 go to the CPDU of the ESA TC decoder. COP-1 on Solar Orbiter covers these commands.22995126
  3. The OCF type bit. The CLCW decomposition includes NCD0Z021 PDEC_CLCW.A.Type, a 1-bit parameter (PTC 1) placed at the first bit of the decoded CLCW. This is the Control Word Type bit that would tell a CLCW (0) from an FSR (1) in the OCF.230188

Inference

The MIB does not expand "AU". In ESA's Telecommand Decoder Specification (PSS-04-151, see From ESA PSS to CCSDS and ECSS), "AU" is the Authentication Unit, the on-board authentication part of the TC decoder.231 The parameters' placement next to the TC decoder registers (NCDD05J1 TC Decoder A.PdecCLCW and its neighbours) and their CLEAR/SECURE states, which match the Clear Mode and Secure Mode terms of the SDLS user requirements, suggest such an authentication unit in the Solar Orbiter telecommand chain. Whether that unit implements SDLS or an earlier ESA scheme, and how it is configured or operated, is not stated in the available sources.227120

SQL used

All queries ran with sqlite3 -readonly on solo-2025-09-16.sqlite. The same queries on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite gave the same AU parameters, calibration and MAP 0 count (MAP 1: 115 commands in 2020).

-- absence of SDLS vocabulary (repeated for each term)
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_DESCR LIKE '%SDLS%' OR PCF_DESCR2 LIKE '%SDLS%';
SELECT count(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_DESCR LIKE '%SDLS%' OR CCF_DESCR2 LIKE '%SDLS%';
SELECT count(*) FROM txp WHERE TXP_ALTXT LIKE '%SDLS%';
-- AU mode parameters, calibration and packets
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_CATEG, PCF_CURTX FROM pcf
  WHERE PCF_CURTX = 'CCDT0046TM';
SELECT * FROM txf WHERE TXF_NUMBR = 'CCDT0046TM';
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CCDT0046TM';
SELECT p.PLF_SPID, d.PID_TYPE, d.PID_STYPE, d.PID_APID, d.PID_DESCR, count(*)
  FROM plf p JOIN pid d ON d.PID_SPID = p.PLF_SPID
  WHERE p.PLF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf WHERE PCF_CURTX = 'CCDT0046TM')
  GROUP BY p.PLF_SPID;
-- MAP usage and high-priority flag
SELECT CCF_MAPID, CCF_HIPRI, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_APID FROM ccf WHERE CCF_MAPID = '0' LIMIT 6;

docs.title: Points to watch in the sources
docs.text:
The documents disagree in a few places. These are noted here rather than resolved.

  • Security Header maximum. 350.5-G-2 table 3-4 says the Security Header can reach 42 octets. SDLS §4.1.1.1.4 allows up to 64 octets.93223
  • TM baseline sequence number. 350.5-G-2 §4.4.2 lists a 32-bit in-line anti-replay sequence number for the TM baseline. Its annex A3.4 and SDLS annex E1 say that the 96-bit IV takes that role and the Sequence Number field is empty.106225
  • SA count. 350.5-G-2 §3.2.2 gives a maximum of \(2^{16}\) simultaneous SAs per physical channel. §3.4.2.2 gives 65,534 per Master Channel, since two SPI values are reserved.7783
  • Reserved SPIs. SDLS reserves 0 and 65535 "for future use". The Extended Procedures allow them for EP PDUs, and their baseline uses them, while their own managed parameter table gives the SPI range as 1–65534.224194210206
  • Create SA PDU. The clause text gives the authentication bit mask length field as 8 bits. Figure 5-16 draws it as 16 bits. The PICS lists encryption and authentication Key IDs as mandatory Create SA fields, but the PDU definition has none.204155
  • Switching SAs. 350.5-G-2 §3.2.2 places the mechanism for switching between active SAs in the Extended Procedures. §4.1 calls it an application layer function.77101
  • Editorial leftovers in 350.0-G-3. §6.5.1 mentions an "Option B as described in 5.3", but §5.3 of Issue 3 defines no such option.44 §3.1 first speaks of four security implementation points and then lists five, and §5.1 considers four layers.922 §5.5 cites reference [9], the Cross Support Reference Model, for the space packet layer, while the Space Packet Protocol is reference [8].335
  • Overhead budget. 350.5-G-2 §2.4 limits the SDLS overhead to 32 octets per transfer frame, while its table 3-4 allows a 42-octet Security Header and a 64-octet Security Trailer. The baselines use 6 + 16 = 22 octets (TC) and 14 + 16 = 30 octets (TM, AOS, USLP); these sums are this wiki's arithmetic.5993225
  • Length units. The EP Length field counts bits. The baseline Key Verification lengths (\(N \times 18\) and \(N \times 46\)) match the field sizes only when counted in octets.199215

docs.title: Space link identifiers: SCIDs, VCIDs, APIDs and SANA
docs.text:
Every CCSDS space link protocol labels its data units with identifiers. These are small numeric fields that say which kind of frame or packet this is, which spacecraft it belongs to, and which channel or application it is for. Some values are defined by CCSDS in the protocol standards. Some are assigned by CCSDS when an agency asks for one. Others are left to each project.25 This page lists all of them, gives their sizes and reserved values, explains the procedure by which the Space Assigned Numbers Authority (SANA) assigns spacecraft identifiers, and shows what the identifiers look like in a real mission database, the Solar Orbiter MIB.

Status of the sources

CCSDS 135.0-B-4 Space Link Identifiers (October 2009) collected the identifiers in one Blue Book. The copy in this wiki's library is stamped CCSDS Historical Document: it is no longer current. The CCSDS overview Green Book (2023) states that SANA replaces the retired Space Link Identifiers Blue Book: the identifier names and values now live in SANA registries. SCID assignment follows the Magenta Book CCSDS 320.0-M-7.140 This page therefore uses 135.0-B-4 for structure and history and the current protocol Blue Books for values, and says where they differ.

docs.title: Three ways of managing an identifier
docs.text:
CCSDS manages each identifier in one of three ways, so that values can be added or changed without editing the protocol standards:54

Method Who sets the values Examples Defined by CCSDS Fixed in the protocol specification Transfer Frame Version Number, Packet Version Number, Proximity-1 Port IDs, Encapsulation Protocol IDs Assigned by CCSDS Given out on request by agencies, under a separate procedure Spacecraft Identifier (SCID) Managed by projects Each project, independently. CCSDS may reserve a few values for cross-agency use VCID, MAP ID, APID, CFDP Entity ID

Lossless data compression, SCPS-FP and the TM and TC synchronization and channel coding standards use no identifiers and are left out.5

docs.title: The identifier hierarchy
docs.text:
The data link protocols nest their identifiers. A Physical Channel, one stream of bits in one direction, is named only by management and never appears in a frame. Frames with the same Master Channel Identifier (MCID) form a Master Channel. Usually that is the whole Physical Channel, but several spacecraft can share one Physical Channel as several Master Channels with the same TFVN. Frames with the same Global Virtual Channel Identifier (GVCID) form a Virtual Channel. In TC and USLP, frames that also share a MAP ID form a MAP Channel.41454953

\[\begin{aligned} \text{MCID} &= \text{TFVN} + \text{SCID}\\ \text{GVCID} &= \text{MCID} + \text{VCID}\\ \text{GMAP ID} &= \text{GVCID} + \text{MAP ID} \quad\text{(TC and USLP)} \end{aligned}\] 
flowchart TB
    PC["Physical Channel<br/>(name set by management)"] --> MC["Master Channel<br/>MCID = TFVN + SCID"]
    MC --> VC["Virtual Channel<br/>GVCID = MCID + VCID"]
    VC --> MAP["MAP Channel (TC, USLP)<br/>GMAP ID = GVCID + MAP ID"]
    VC --> PKT["Packets in the data field<br/>PVN, then APID (Space Packet)<br/>or Protocol ID (Encapsulation)"]
    MAP --> PKT
    PX["Proximity-1 link"] --> PXI["SCID + Source-or-Destination flag<br/>PCID (one of two receivers)<br/>Port ID (output port)"]

Channel nesting of TM, TC, AOS and USLP, and the Proximity-1 triad.4142

Packets add their own naming level. The APID of a Space Packet is unique only inside one naming domain, which usually corresponds to one spacecraft or one element of a constellation. Each project allocates the APIDs of its own domain.67

docs.title: Identifier fields by protocol
docs.text:
Identifier TM (132.0) TC (232.0) AOS (732.0) Proximity-1 (211.0) USLP (732.1) TFVN bits 0–1 = 00 bits 0–1 = 00 bits 0–1 = 01 bits 0–1 = 10 bits 0–3 = 1100 SCID bits 2–11 (10 bits) bits 6–15 (10 bits) bits 2–9 (8 bits) bits 6–15 (10 bits) bits 4–19 (16 bits) VCID bits 12–14 (3 bits, 0–7) bits 16–21 (6 bits, 0–63) bits 10–15 (6 bits, 0–63) — bits 21–26 (6 bits, 0–63) MAP ID — segment header bits 2–7 (6 bits, 0–63) — — bits 27–30 (4 bits, 0–15) Source-or-Destination — — — bit 20 bit 20 PCID — — — bit 16 (0–1) — Port ID — — — bits 17–19 (0–7) — Reserved VCID none none 63 = OID frames — 63 = OID frames

Bit positions from the frame header clauses of each Blue Book. Ranges agree with table 3-1 of the overview Green Book.4650515261545743

The TM and TC identification prefixes are drawn on the CCSDS overview and on the TM and TC pages.

docs.title: Transfer Frame Version Numbers
docs.text:
The TFVN tells receivers which frame format follows. It is defined by CCSDS. A Physical Channel must not mix frames of different versions.1141

Version Binary Frame Defined in 1 00 TM Transfer Frame CCSDS 132.0 1 00 TC Transfer Frame CCSDS 232.0 2 01 AOS Transfer Frame CCSDS 732.0 3 10 Proximity-1 (Version-3) Transfer Frame CCSDS 211.0 4 1100 USLP (Version-4) Transfer Frame CCSDS 732.1

The first four rows come from 135.0-B-4. TM and TC share version 1 and are told apart by the TM Attached Sync Marker or the TC Start Sequence.1146 USLP took the last free 2-bit value, 11, and appended 00 to form a 4-bit TFVN, 1100. This leaves room for future versions.55 A Proximity-1 receiver uses the same two bits to accept Version-3 (10) or Version-4 (11) frames and rejects 00 and 01.63

docs.title: Spacecraft identifiers per frame version
docs.text:
The SCID field size depends on the frame version, so CCSDS 320.0-M-7 keeps a separate SCID table for each TFVN:24

Version TFVN SCID range Bits Protocols 1 00 0–1023 10 TC and TM 2 01 0–255 8 AOS 3 10 0–1023 10 Proximity-1 4 1100 0–65 535 16 USLP

Linking a spacecraft to a TFVN is a managed parameter. A spacecraft that uses protocols with different TFVNs may need two or more distinct SCIDs.24 In USLP the 20-bit global SCID (TFVN.SCID, the same thing as the MCID) runs from 0xC0000 to 0xCFFFF.59

The SCID is static throughout all mission phases in TM and TC.4650 The TM Blue Book adds that SCIDs are unique only within the spacecraft's frequency band. The same value may be given to another spacecraft in another band.46 In TM, TC and AOS the SCID names the spacecraft associated with the data. Proximity-1 and USLP add a Source-or-Destination Identifier: 0 means the SCID is the sender, 1 means it is the intended receiver.6256 ECSS-E-ST-50C requires that all telecommands carry an identifier of the destination spacecraft. All telemetry must carry an identifier of the source spacecraft, which ground systems normally keep as an annotation. Frames must identify the spacecraft and link, and the frame version number can identify the link.747576

docs.title: Assigning SCIDs: CCSDS 320.0-M-7
docs.text:
The CCSDS Spacecraft Identification Field Code Assignment Control Procedures govern how SCIDs are requested, assigned and given back. They also define who may take part and how SCIDs may be used. Issue 7 (November 2017, with Technical Corrigendum 1 of July 2019) applies to TC, TM, AOS, Proximity-1 and USLP. All organisations that need a SCID for CCSDS space communication must follow it.22

Issue Date Change from the document control page 320.0-B-1 to -B-6 1993 to 2013 "CCSDS Global Spacecraft Identification Field" Blue Books 320.0-M-7 November 2017 Adds the frequency band as a qualifier (Q-SCID); replaces the paper request form by the SANA web form; becomes a Recommended Practice (Magenta Book) Cor. 1 July 2019 Adds USLP (version 4) frames; frequency bins now use ITU ranges; editorial updates

Restated from the document control pages.2021

docs.title: Why SCIDs are qualified
docs.text:
The SCID fields of version 1 to 3 frames are only 8 or 10 bits long, and they must tell apart all the spacecraft that are operating at the same time. The SCID therefore cannot be a permanent identifier, and SCIDs must be reused. The procedures are meant to ensure that data from one spacecraft is never mistaken for another's, and that commands are never acted on by the wrong spacecraft.25 Missions with different frequency bands are already isolated, so each band can be treated as a separate namespace. Hence:2523

  • GSCID (global spacecraft identifier) = TFVN . SCID, where "." means concatenation.
  • Q-SCID (qualified spacecraft identifier) = FB . TFVN . SCID, where FB is the frequency band.
  • Each TFVN has its own assignment table, and each frequency band within a TFVN has its own table.
  • A spacecraft that uses more than one protocol or band may receive several Q-SCIDs. SANA tries, but does not guarantee, to give the same number in each domain.
  • Every registered spacecraft also receives a permanent ISO object identifier. The SCID is valid only during operations, but the object identifier is permanent.

The frequency bands follow ITU usage for Earth exploration-satellite (EESS), space research (SRS) and space operation (SOS) services. SANA uses frequency band designators for them:27

Range Band Near-Earth downlink allocation (SANA designator) Deep-space downlink allocation (designator) 300–1000 MHz UHF UHF UHF 1–2 GHz L 1.525–1.535 GHz SOS (L) L 2–3 GHz S 2.200–2.290 GHz EESS, SRS, SOS (S-NE) 2.290–2.300 GHz SRS-DS (S-DS) 6–10 GHz X 8.025–8.400 GHz EESS and 8.450–8.500 GHz SRS (X-NE) 8.400–8.450 GHz SRS-DS (X-DS) 22–32.5 GHz Ka 25.250–27.500 GHz Inter-Satellite Service (restricted to space research and Earth exploration data) and 25.500–27.000 GHz EESS, SRS (Ka-NE) 31.800–32.300 GHz SRS-DS (Ka-DS) 32.5–40.5 GHz Ka 37.000–38.000 GHz SRS and 37.500–40.500 GHz EESS, secondary (Ka-S) 37.000–38.000 GHz SRS (Ka-S) Optical 1064 nm, 1550 nm to be supplied (O1, O2) to be supplied (O1, O2)

Abridged from table 2-1, which also lists HF, VHF, C, Ku, K, V, W and millimetre bands. Only downlink frequencies are shown. A request states the uplink and downlink bands separately, and only one SCID is needed if both use the same TFVN and band.272833

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Duties CCSDS Secretariat Resolves issues the procedures do not cover; finds an Agency Representative for requests from organisations without a CCSDS agency; keeps the lists of agencies and Heads of Delegation Agency Head of Delegation (HoD) Appoints the agency's Agency Representative (AR) and keeps the AR's contact data up to date in SANA Agency Representative Submits Q-SCID requests, deals with SANA on them, watches the agency's missions, and relinquishes their Q-SCIDs no later than two months after the end of the operational phase SANA Keeps the agency, HoD and AR lists; reviews, logs and assigns Q-SCIDs per band; assigns object identifiers; keeps separate Q-SCID registries per band and TFVN; recovers Q-SCIDs of finished missions for reuse

Section 3.1.293031

docs.title: Request, assignment, use and relinquishment
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Agency Representative<br/>fills the SANA web form:<br/>TFVN, uplink and downlink bands"] --> S["SANA reviews and logs<br/>the request"]
    S --> Q["Assigns Q-SCID(s) by availability<br/>(same number in each band if possible)<br/>+ spacecraft object identifier"]
    Q --> U["Used through the active phases:<br/>pre-launch tests, launch, operations"]
    U --> E["End of operations<br/>(AR and mission manager decide)"]
    E --> R["AR relinquishes via the form<br/>within two months"]
    R --> B["SANA puts the number at the<br/>bottom of the free stack"]

Sections 3.2 to 3.5.33343236

  • Requests. Only the designated AR may request, using the online form at the SANA site, one form per request. Organisations without a CCSDS agency go through the Secretariat. The form gives the TFVN and the uplink and downlink bands, not exact frequencies. E-mail is accepted only in exceptional cases.33
  • Assignment. SANA alone assigns, based on availability. Each Q-SCID is unique within its TFVN and band while assigned, and assignments are made spacecraft by spacecraft. Requests to reserve blocks for unspecified spacecraft are refused, but a multi-spacecraft mission may receive several Q-SCIDs. A specific number is honoured only in exceptional cases and only if free, so requesters should check the registry first.3435
  • Simulators. SANA no longer assigns SCIDs for simulation, test or ground assemblies, because they never radiate. Missions may manage such SCIDs internally. Protoflight models and simulators may receive their own object identifier, treated as a "non-radiating" Q-SCID, but no separate SCID.2635
  • Lifetime. A Q-SCID may be used through all active phases. Soon after telemetry is received, the SCID should be replaced by the permanent object identifier or another agency identifier, because SCIDs are reused and identifying archived data by SCID is problematic.32
  • Relinquishment. The AR and the mission manager decide when operations are complete. The AR marks "RELINQUISH current GSCID" on the form. SANA puts the number at the bottom of the stack of free SCIDs, so that it is reused as late as possible.36

docs.title: The SANA spacecraft identifier registry
docs.text:
Annex A describes the registry: one table per Q-SCID version, with these columns:3738

Column Content Spacecraft Name Up to 64 characters, assigned by the agency Channel TC, TLM, AOS or Other Version Number(s) From table 1-1; may be extended for new protocols SCID Hex, from 001 to the maximum for the version GSCID Hex, per frequency band Object ID ISO object identifier under 1.3.112.4.7 Requestor Name, Affiliation, Affiliation Country Must match the AR, Organization and ISO country registries Last Request Date, Registered by, Status Status: Assigned, Returned, object identifier only, or null Spacecraft Name Abbreviation and Alias(es) Agency abbreviation, pre- and post-launch names S/C Transmitting and Receiving Frequency Band(s) Band designators from table 2-1 Expected Launch Date, Expected Mission End Date, Note Dates in yyyy-mm-dd; the end date can be extended on request

The registration rules allow a request for an object identifier only, which helps organisations that do not use CCSDS link protocols but want a registered designator. If a request names a band that has no bin yet, SANA creates bins for it in all TFVNs. Requests are accepted only from organisations of type member agency, observer agency or affiliate, and only from persons with the AR role.3839

Who assigns, in the Blue Books

The TM, AOS and USLP Blue Books say that SANA assigns SCIDs under CCSDS 320.0-M. The TC Blue Book (issue 4, 2021) still says the CCSDS Secretariat assigns them. Under 320.0-M-7, all Q-SCID assignments are made by SANA.4652545034

docs.title: Virtual channel and MAP identifiers
docs.text:
VCIDs and MAP IDs are managed by projects. They need not be numbered consecutively.10475051

  • TM: 3 bits, VCIDs 0 to 7, none reserved. A frame with only idle data is marked by the First Header Pointer value 11111111110, not by a VCID.4748
  • TC: 6 bits, none reserved. The MAP ID is in the segment header (bits 2–7). If MAPs are not used but a segment header is present, the MAP ID is a constant.5051
  • AOS: 6 bits. All zeros if only one VC is used. VCID 63 (all ones) is reserved for Only Idle Data (OID) frames. This was the only VCID that 135.0-B-4 reserved.5212
  • USLP: 6 bits. VCIDs 0 to 62 are free, and VCID 63 is reserved for OID frames, which also use MAP ID
  • MAP IDs are 4 bits (1 to 16 MAP channels). Each SDU is on one MAP at a time and must be finished before another MAP's SDU starts on the same VC. SANA lists USLP VCIDs as unmanaged.575859
  • Proximity-1 has no VCID. With Version-4 frames over Proximity-1, the most significant VCID bit stands for the PCID, which leaves 32 VCIDs.60

docs.title: Proximity-1 identifiers
docs.text:
Proximity-1 uses a triad: the SCID with its source-or-destination flag, a PCID that selects one of two receivers, and a Port ID that routes user data to a logical or physical port inside the receiving spacecraft.4264 Port IDs are defined by CCSDS. 135.0-B-2 (2005) added them, and 135.0-B-3 clarified the meaning of the packets port.310 The last published assignment is:16

Port ID Forward link (both PCIDs) Return link (both PCIDs) 000 Bitstream Bitstream 001 Hardware commands Reserved by CCSDS 010 Packets (Space Packet, SCPS-NP, Encapsulation, IPv4) Packets 011–111 Reserved by CCSDS Reserved by CCSDS

The current Proximity-1 Blue Book refers to the SANA registry for the reserved Port IDs. Its issue 6 required no SANA action and keeps the existing registries.6566

docs.title: Packet Version Numbers
docs.text:
Every packet carried by a Space Data Link Protocol starts with a 3-bit Packet Version Number. Its values are defined by CCSDS and held in SANA. Receivers use the PVN to find each packet's length field:141944

PVN Binary Packet Length field (bits from packet start) Meaning of the length 1 000 Space Packet 32–47 Data field octets minus 1 (add 7 for the whole packet) 2 001 SCPS-NP 3–16 Total octets including the header (minimum 4) 8 111 Encapsulation Packet 8–15, 16–31 or 32–63 Total octets including the header

docs.title: Application Process Identifier (APID)
docs.text:
The APID is bits 5–15 of the Space Packet primary header: 11 bits, 0 to 2047. It names the managed data path and may identify the sending or receiving application on a spacecraft. Missions decide whether it means source, destination or packet type.6968 APIDs are managed by projects, need not be consecutive, and are unique only within their naming domain. A mission with several processors or spacecraft must sub-allocate the single domain or extend it through its own secondary header fields.69688

Reserved APIDs have shrunk over time:871

Source Reserved APIDs CCSDS 135.0-B-4 (2009), table 5-2 2040–2044 possible future use; 2045 CFDP; 2046 ISO 8473; 2047 idle packet CCSDS 133.0-B-2 (2020) and the SANA policy it set 0–2046 unmanaged; 2047 idle packet (11111111111) only

Issue 1 of the Space Packet Protocol reserved APIDs for carrying PDUs of other protocols such as CFDP and LTP. Issue 2 made that coupling mission-specific and removed those reservations from the SANA registry.86971

docs.title: Encapsulation and other protocol identifiers
docs.text: The Encapsulation Packet names its payload with a 3-bit Encapsulation Protocol ID (bits 3–5). The value 000 marks an Encapsulation Idle Packet, 110 means the 4-bit extension field identifies the protocol, and 111 means mission-specific private data. The recognised values are held in SANA.7273 135.0-B-4 listed 010 IPE, 011 CFDP, and 001, 100 and 101 reserved. All extended IDs 0000–1111 were reserved at the time.15 Its annex A defined the Internet Protocol Extension (IPE): a header of one or more octets after the Encapsulation header. The least significant bit of each octet is 0 if another octet follows and 1 in the last octet, so only odd values are valid (33 IPv4, 87 IPv6, 97–113 header-compression formats).1718 USLP adds a 5-bit USLP Protocol Identifier (UPID) in its data field header. SANA manages the values 00000–11111.59

docs.title: Other identifiers in 135.0-B-4
docs.text:
Protocol Identifier Method CFDP Entity ID Managed by projects, no value reserved SCPS-TP Connection Identifier Managed by projects, no value reserved SCPS-NP Domain Identifier Assigned by CCSDS (no procedure defined) SCPS-NP End System Identifier, Path Identifier Managed by projects SCPS-NP Transport Protocol Identifier Defined by CCSDS TM Frame Secondary Header Version Number Defined by CCSDS: 00 = version 1 TC CLCW Version Number Defined by CCSDS: 00 = version 1

Tables 3-1, 4-1, 6-1, 7-1, 7-4 and 7-5.791013 The CFDP and COP-1 pages describe these fields in their protocols.

docs.title: Security aspects
docs.text: 135.0-B-4 defines no confidentiality, integrity, authentication, access control, availability or auditing measures for the identifiers. It refers to the individual protocols for these.6 See security in CCSDS space links.

docs.title: Identifiers in the Solar Orbiter database
docs.text: Solar Orbiter is the mission whose real database is published with this wiki (see the Solar Orbiter MIB). Its TM/TC interface control document fixes the link identifiers, and the MIB shows how SCOS-2000 uses them.7892

docs.title: Spacecraft, virtual channels and MAP IDs
docs.text:
Identifier Solar Orbiter value Source SCID 0x28A = 650 for both TM and TC; the same ID for the flight model, the ETB and the OBC-DM ICD §3.4, §4.3 TC VCIDs 1 (000001) for TC decoder 1, 2 (000010) for decoder 2, used the same way in the CLCWs ICD §3.4 TC MAP IDs 0 for CPDU (high-priority) commands, 1 for all other commands; MAP IDs never address the active CSW processor ICD §3.3.1 TM VCIDs 0 real-time, 1 OBC playback, 2 and 3 SSMM playback, 4 real-time high priority, 5 critical event log, 7 idle frames only ICD §4.3 TM idle frames VC 7, First Header Pointer 11111111110 ICD §4.3

Sources: Solar Orbiter TM/TC and packet structure ICD.77787980

A small inconsistency in the ICD

The ICD says the suggested TC VCID values are "Zero and One", but the two values it lists are 000001 and 000010, that is 1 and 2.78 The MIB uses 1 and 2 (below).

None of the MIB tables queried for this page holds the SCID or the VCIDs as a configuration value. The MIB does, however, decode them where they appear in telemetry. The packet "Good mini-transfer frame" (SPID 66980, TM(161,5) on APID 1966: process ID 122, in the ICD's EGSE range 112–127, and packet category 14, "Reserved OCC/EGSE") lays out the TM frame header: a 2-bit TF version number at bit 0, a 10-bit "Spacecraft Id." at byte 0 bit 2 (PCF_PTC 3, PCF_PFC 6), a 3-bit "VC Id." at byte 1 bit 4, then the frame counts, data field status, secondary header and the CLCW. Bad and idle frames have their own SPIDs, 66981 and 66982.92838182 These positions are exactly bits 0–1, 2–11 and 12–14 of the TM primary header.46 In the CLCW part, 18 parameters are split per TC virtual channel ("VC1 ..." and "VC2 ..."). Each is valid only when the CLCW's 6-bit VC Id (NYGD0659) equals 1 or 2, through PCF_VALID and PCF_VALPAR. A textual calibration shows the value as "VC 1" or "VC 2".9284 The OBC's own housekeeping, TM(3,25) "DMS OBC Status Slow", reports the VCIDs of both decoders' CLCWs (PDEC_CLCW.A.VCID, PDEC_CLCW.B.VCID).92 Ground-generated packets carry a 16-bit "GS Spacecraft ID" (TM(165,1), APID 1966), matching the NCTRS packet headers described on NCTRS and NIS.92

See the packets in the explorer: good mini-transfer frame, NYGD0659 and NYGDA659.

Inference

The "mini-transfer frame" packet has fields for the frame header (6 octets), a 4-octet secondary header (8-bit ID at octet 6 and 24-bit data at octet 7), the CLCW at octet 10, the frame error control field at octet 14 and the earth reception time from octet 16. These are exactly the header and trailer fields that the ICD puts in every Solar Orbiter TM frame: a secondary header with an 8-bit ID and a 24-bit extension of the VC frame count, a CLCW in the Operational Control Field and a Frame Error Control Word.80 The packet apparently carries a TM frame without its data field, so that the control system can monitor frame-level identifiers and the CLCW of every frame. The MIB also defines "Good", "Bad" and "Idle complete transfer frame" packets (SPIDs 1000006, 1000002 and 1000003, type 0, APID 1), which fits this reading of "mini".92 This is deduced from the parameter offsets and descriptions. The packets are not described in the documents in this wiki's library.

On the telecommand side the MIB does carry the MAP ID. The ICD defines CCF_HIPRI as marking a high-priority command whose MAP ID is forced to the value in CCF_MAPID (0–63), and which cannot be time-tagged on board or aggregated with others. CCF_MAPID is irrelevant unless CCF_HIPRI is Y.89 In the September 2025 release:92

CCF_PKTID (header) CCF_HIPRI CCF_MAPID Commands APID What they are HPC1_TC (HPC_TC_Packet_Header) Y 0 125 44 CPDU high-priority (HPC-1) commands, e.g. ZBC04001 "Select PM A EEPROM Image 1" NO_HDR (TCP Header for CF/CS) Y (empty) 5 none Frame-level directives: UNLOCK and SETVR (control frames, CCF_CTYPE F), RESET, TC_ONLY and REIN_TTR (control segments, R) NOM_TC (NOM_DH_TC_Packet_Header) N empty, 1 or 54 5 318 30 APIDs Ordinary PUS commands NOS2KHDR (NIS Throw Events) N (empty) 6 1964 NIS throw events (CCF_CTYPE N), type 251, never uplinked

MAP ID 0 for the 125 CPDU commands matches the ICD (process ID 2 is "High Priority TC Functions to CPDU (MAP ID = 0)").7782 The NO_HDR entries have no APID because they are not packets. The ICD defines CCF_CTYPE F as a BC frame (Unlock and Set V(R)) and R as a control segment, whose PCDF/CDF entries describe a frame data field, not a packet.87 These are the COP-1 control commands. 128 ordinary commands carry CCF_MAPID 1 and 77 carry 54, all with CCF_HIPRI = N.92

Inference

The values 1 and 54 in non-high-priority commands have no effect under the ICD rule above. The value 1 is the MAP ID that the Solar Orbiter ICD assigns to all normal (non-CPDU) commands, so those 128 entries merely restate the MAP ID the commands use anyway.77 The 77 commands with 54 are all on APID 876, whose process ID is 54 (an EPD process). This suggests that an instrument team's tool copied the process ID into the field. The 2020 release already has the same pattern (115 commands with 1, 77 with 54).93

docs.title: APIDs in the MIB
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 extends the APID beyond 11 bits for its own purposes. PID_APID and CCF_APID are 0–2047 for spacecraft packets and commands, and 2048–65 535 for anything else, such as packets generated by SCOS-2000 or by SCOE equipment.8588 When a command is encoded, its packet header comes from the tcp/pcdf tables. A pcdf element of type A takes its value from CCF_APID, and the source sequence counter is kept per APID.86 In the Solar Orbiter headers NOM_TC and HPC1_TC, that element is the 11-bit field at bit 5, after a fixed version 000 and type bit 1. The secondary header flag is 1 for PUS commands and 0 for CPDU commands, and the sequence flags are fixed at 11.92 CCF_RAPID may name a redundant APID for redundant units. Solar Orbiter uses none.9092 The optional dst table routes commands per APID and sends everything else to the NCTRS. Its only Solar Orbiter row sends APID 1372 (SPICE) to EGSE.TC.0x8800, discussed on SCOS-2000 as EGSE.9192

Solar Orbiter divides the 11-bit APID into a 7-bit process ID and a 4-bit packet category. All telecommands use category 12.8182

The MIB follows this exactly. Every command with an APID uses category 12, on 32 distinct APIDs:92

TC APID Process Owner (ICD annex 8) Commands TM APIDs of the same process 44 2 OBC hardware, CPDU 125 1 172 10 CSW data management 1 971 9 188 11 CSW AOCS 454 7 204, 220, 236, 268 12, 13, 14, 16 CSW payload, platform and system control; OBC software thermal control 78, 118, 966, 84 7 each 492, 508, 524 30–32 SSMM (operational, debug A, debug B) 182, 14, 14 8, 5, 5 652, 668 40, 41 Star trackers A, B 49, 49 6, 6 796 49 Payload broadcast 5 0 812, 876 50, 54 EPD 40, 78 5, 6 924 57 EUI 122 6 1020 63 MAG 126 2 1084 67 METIS 126 7 1164 72 PHI 199 5 1212–1308 (step 16) 75–81 RPW 67, 22, 20, 19, 5, 2, 3 2 to 6 1324 82 SOLOHI 102 8 1372 85 SPICE 91 4 1452 90 STIX 98 6 1532 95 SWA 200 2 1948, 1964 121, 122 EGSE range 14, 6 2, 15

Process 15 (OBCP) has no command APID. Fourteen of the 32 command APIDs also appear as telemetry APIDs. These are category-12 science packets of instruments and the EGSE APID 1964 (process 122). This is legal, because the Packet Type bit tells a telecommand (1) from telemetry (0) with the same APID.9270

On the telemetry side, the 2025 release defines 11 150 packets on 293 APIDs (0 to 2065), with 287 of them below 2048. The 2020 release has 9 027 packets on 268 APIDs (0 to 2047). Neither release uses the APIDs 2040–2046 that 135.0-B-4 once reserved. Both use only 2047, for the idle packet, and APID 0 for the time report TM(9,2).92938 Six packets above 2047 (2048–2065) are ground-generated LMS_... packets, analysed on the Solar Orbiter MIB page, which also breaks down all TM APIDs by component. The command APID set is identical in the 2020 and 2025 releases.9293

The instrument databases follow the same plan (see SWA, STIX and the instrument interface documents). The SWA database (v6.5.0) has 613 TM packets on 15 APIDs (1525–1596, processes 95–99) and 201 commands, all on APID 1532. STIX (v2.26.38) has 246 TM packets on 9 APIDs (1441–1509) and 100 commands on APIDs 1452 (process 90) and 796, the payload broadcast APID.949582 Explorer links: APID 1532 (SWA), APID 1452 (STIX), APID 44 (CPDU), SETVR.

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB 20250916M25925PFMS001)
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_APID), min(CAST(PID_APID AS INT)), max(CAST(PID_APID AS INT)),
       count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(PID_APID AS INT) < 2048 THEN PID_APID END) FROM pid;
                                               -- 11150 | 293 | 0 | 2065 | 287
SELECT PID_APID, count(*) FROM pid
 WHERE CAST(PID_APID AS INT) BETWEEN 2040 AND 2046;               -- (no rows)
SELECT CAST(CCF_APID AS INT) & 15, count(*), count(DISTINCT CCF_APID)
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_APID <> '' GROUP BY 1;                       -- 12 | 5449 | 32
SELECT CCF_PKTID, CCF_APID, CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID, count(*) FROM ccf
 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 ORDER BY CAST(CCF_APID AS INT);
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_CTYPE, CCF_DESCR FROM ccf WHERE CCF_PKTID = 'NO_HDR';
SELECT * FROM tcp;  SELECT * FROM pcdf ORDER BY PCDF_TCNAME, CAST(PCDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT count(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_RAPID <> '';                   -- 0
SELECT * FROM dst;                                                -- 1372|EGSE.TC.0x8800
-- TC APIDs with the TM APIDs of the same process
WITH tc AS (SELECT CAST(CCF_APID AS INT) a, count(*) n FROM ccf WHERE CCF_APID <> '' GROUP BY 1),
     tm AS (SELECT CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 p, count(DISTINCT PID_APID) na FROM pid GROUP BY 1)
SELECT tc.a, tc.a >> 4, tc.n, tm.na FROM tc LEFT JOIN tm ON tm.p = tc.a >> 4 ORDER BY tc.a;
SELECT count(DISTINCT CCF_APID) FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_APID <> '' AND CCF_APID IN (SELECT PID_APID FROM pid);  -- 14
-- frame-level identifiers decoded in telemetry
SELECT p.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, p.PLF_OFFBY, p.PLF_OFFBI, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC
  FROM plf p JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = p.PLF_NAME
 WHERE p.PLF_SPID = '66980' ORDER BY CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS INT), CAST(PLF_OFFBI AS INT);
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_VALID, PCF_VALPAR, PCF_CURTX FROM pcf
 WHERE PCF_VALID = 'NYGD0659';                                    -- 18 rows
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CYGT0659TM';                 -- 1 VC 1 / 2 VC 2
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_DESCR FROM pid
 WHERE PID_DESCR LIKE '%transfer frame%';      -- 3 complete (APID 1) + 3 mini (APID 1966)
-- solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_APID), max(CAST(PID_APID AS INT)) FROM pid;  -- 9027 | 268 | 2047
SELECT CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2;
-- swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite and stix-idb-2.26.38.sqlite
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_APID), min(CAST(PID_APID AS INT)), max(CAST(PID_APID AS INT)) FROM pid;
SELECT count(*), group_concat(DISTINCT CCF_APID) FROM ccf;
