docs.text:
Parameter Result tag ParameterName Value and meaning acquisition-sequence-length [0] 201 Octets of acquisition pattern bit-lock-required [1] 3 yes (0) / no (1): CLCW 'No Bit Lock' must be false for 'operational' clcw-global-VCID [2] 202 GVCID carrying the CLCW, or 'not configured' clcw-physical-channel [3] 203 Return RF channel carrying the CLCW (VisibleString 1–32), or 'not configured'; implies the frame version delivery-mode [4] 6 'fwd online' expected-cltu-identification [5] 10 (expectedSlduIdentification) Next expected cltu-identification; 0 before any START expected-event-invocation-identification [6] 9 Next expected THROW-EVENT number; initially 0 maximum-cltu-length [7] 21 (maximumSlduLength) 12 to 4,096 octets minimum-delay-time [8] 204 Minimum guard time between CLTUs modulation-frequency [9] 22 Subcarrier frequency, or bit rate for direct modulation, in 0.1 Hz modulation-index [10] 23 Peak phase deviation in milliradians notification-mode [11] 205 deferred (0) / immediate (1) plop-1-idle-sequence-length [12] 206 Octets; 0 = no idle plop-in-effect [13] 25 plop1 (0) / plop2 (1) protocol-abort-mode [14] 207 abort (0) / continue (1) reporting-cycle [15] 26 Off, or seconds return-timeout-period [16] 29 1 to 600 s rf-available-required [17] 31 yes (0) / no (1): CLCW 'No RF Available' must be false for 'operational' subcarrier-to-bit-rate-ratio [18] 34 Subcarrier divisor; 1 = direct carrier modulation minimum-reporting-cycle [19] 301 1 to 600 s

Sources: table 3-11,32 ASN.1 CltuGetParameter and ParameterName.202662 Table 3-1 records which of these only service management can set. The user sets the reporting cycle through SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT, and selected production parameters may be changed through THROW-EVENT, which is allowed but not mandated.63

docs.title: CLTU-THROW-EVENT
docs.text:
THROW-EVENT asks the provider to pass an event to SLE complex management. The standard's example is changing the uplink bit rate. The mission first sends a telecommand that reconfigures the spacecraft receiver. When that has executed, the user throws the event that changes the ground bit rate. The event happens when the invocation arrives, so it is asynchronous with CLTU radiation. Keeping it in step with specific CLTUs (for example by controlling their radiation times) is the user's job.42

Parameter Inv. Ret. Meaning invoke-ID M M Echoed event-invocation-identification M M Starts at 0 after the first BIND, increments per accepted event, survives re-binding; the return holds the next expected value event-identifier M Event to forward (IntPosShort) event-qualifier M 1 to 1,024 octets of event-specific data, checked only for type and length by the provider result, diagnostic M, C Diagnostic Code duplicate invoke-ID common 100 operation not supported specific 0 out of sequence specific 1 (eventInvocIdOutOfSequence) no such event specific 2 other reason common 127

Sources: parameters and diagnostics,64 ASN.1.6546 A positive return only means "forwarded". The outcome arrives later as 'action list completed', 'action list not completed' or 'event condition evaluated to false'.4266 Event identifiers and qualifiers must be agreed in advance between complex and utilization management. THROW-EVENT is optional for conforming providers.6645

The standard gives informative examples, which assume a 16 kHz subcarrier and therefore a maximum of 4,000 bit/s:67

Name ID event-qualifier Range Precondition Set Mod 1 on or off — 'on' requires production 'operational' Change Rate 2 br <BR> 7.8125 to 4000.0 bit/s No CLTU radiating, buffer empty Change Index 3 mi <MI> 1 to 1570 mrad No CLTU radiating, buffer empty Change Rate/Index 4 br <BR> mi <MI> as above No CLTU radiating, buffer empty

docs.title: Buffering, termination and protocol abort
docs.text:
The service package states the provider's CLTU buffer size in octets, and only complete CLTUs are buffered.68 The conforming minimum is 4,194,304 octets, equivalent to 1,024 CLTUs of 4,096 octets each.37

When an association ends, production stops at once, except for a CLTU that is being radiated, and all buffered CLTUs are discarded. The one exception is a protocol abort (loss of the communications link) when protocol-abort-mode is 'continue'. Buffered CLTUs are then kept and radiated as if nothing had happened. Notifications produced meanwhile are not delivered or queued (logging them is recommended). After re-binding, the user can rebuild the picture from a status report, and must choose a first-cltu-identification above any CLTU still in the buffer.6061 Sequence numbers that relate notifications to operations are not reset by a protocol abort.61

Inconsistent naming in the standard

§4.1.5.3 and the conformance matrix call the discarding value of protocol-abort-mode 'flush' (the default behaviour if the parameter is not supported). Table 3-11 and the ASN.1 call it 'abort' (abort (0)).61373220 This wiki treats them as the same value.

docs.title: State machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unbound: instance created
    Unbound --> Ready: CLTU-BIND (user) positive
    Ready --> Active: CLTU-START positive
    Active --> Ready: CLTU-STOP positive<br/>(unradiated CLTUs discarded)
    Ready --> Unbound: UNBIND / PEER-ABORT / protocol abort
    Active --> Unbound: PEER-ABORT / protocol abort<br/>(buffer kept only if 'continue')
    state Active {
        [*] --> Accepting
        Accepting --> Blocked: 'sldu expired' /<br/>'production interrupted' /<br/>'production halted'
        Blocked --> Blocked: TRANSFER-DATA →<br/>'unable to process'
    }

Diagram based on figure 2-4 and §3.7.3 of the FCLTU specification.1055 Getting out of 'Blocked' needs a STOP, which returns the provider to 'ready'. The normative behaviour is the state table in §4.2, and conformance to it is mandatory.37

docs.title: FCLTU and the other forward TC services
Three functional groups, four services
docs.text:
The reference model stacks three forward telecommand functional groups. Each higher group adds one layer of telecommand processing, and each layer has its own transfer service:9798

Service The user supplies Provider functional groups involved What the extra group does Recommended Standard Forward CLTU (FCLTU) CLTUs Forward TC Space Link Processing PLOP sequences, modulation, radiation, CLCW checks of the physical channel 912.1-B-5 (this page) Forward TC Frame (FTCF) TC frames, in blocks of one or more frames per CLTU + Forward CLTU Generation Optional randomisation, BCH encoding, start and tail sequences none yet (as stated in 2016)87 Forward TC Virtual Channel Access (TC-VCA) Frame Data Units with the GVCID to use + Forward TC VC Data Insertion Builds TC frames; for sequence-controlled frames sets the frame sequence count, keeps a copy and retransmits or deletes it according to the CLCW not in this library Forward Space Packet (FSP) Space Packets + Forward TC VC Data Insertion Blocks or segments packets into frames (segmented packets only with sequence control), with the same frame sequence numbering, copy keeping and CLCW-driven retransmission 912.3-B-3 (page)

Sources: §4.3.2.3 and §5.6.2 of the reference model, and the FSP specification.979887 If TC-VCA and FSP are both active on one virtual channel, only one of them may be sequence-controlled.97 Because no FTCF standard exists, FSP requires the CLTU Generation and the TC VC Data Insertion groups to sit in the same complex, while the radiation group may still be in another complex, reached through an FCLTU service instance.8784 The FSP page compares the user's and the provider's tasks under FCLTU and FSP in detail.

Attribute FCLTU (912.1-B-5) FSP (912.3-B-3) ApplicationIdentifier fwdCltu (16) fwdTcSpacePkt (13) BIND version-number in the library issue 6 5 Data unit per TRANSFER-DATA one CLTU one Space Packet Release-time control earliest and latest radiation time earliest and latest production time COP-1 (FOP-1) runs at the user the provider; the user may send COP-1 directives (FSP-INVOKE-DIRECTIVE) Production status values configured, operational, interrupted, halted configured, operational (sub-states 'BD', 'AD and BD', 'AD suspended'), interrupted, halted

Sources: the BIND, TRANSFER-DATA and production status clauses of both specifications.89884089901191

docs.title: The FCLTU radiation function inside FSP production
docs.text:
FSP reuses the FCLTU production rules for its radiation group. Annex D of the FSP specification states that most of the Forward TC Space Link Processing production is already described in the FCLTU specification, and defines how that group handles each CLTU Transfer Data SLE-SDU coming from the CLTU Generation group in the same complex. The differences from a real FCLTU CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA are these:84

Aspect FCLTU service (CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA from a user) Inside FSP production (CLTU Transfer Data SLE-SDU) Credentials and invoke-ID carried and checked none passed or authenticated; they matter only when the groups are in different complexes and a real FCLTU instance connects them cltu-identification sequencing enforced ('out of sequence') not enforced; the CLTU identifier only labels acceptance, rejection and radiation reports Earliest and latest radiation time supported, with 'sldu expired' none; each CLTU is radiated as soon as possible after those already queued, and eventually radiated as long as production is operational Delay time per invocation, at least minimum-delay-time taken from the SDU; acceptance or rejection reported on the same minimum Radiation report report parameter, CLTU-ASYNC-NOTIFY flag in the SDU; radiation reported to the CLTU Generation group CLTU content any octet-aligned bit pattern exactly one TC frame per CLTU, although the coding standard allows more

Sources: annex D1.1 and D1.2 of 912.3-B-3.8485 Service management configures the same eleven production parameters as for FCLTU: acquisition-sequence-length, bit-lock-required, clcw-physical-channel, clcw-global-VCID, minimum-delay-time, modulation-frequency, modulation-index, plop-1-idle-sequence-length, plop-in-effect, rf-available-required and subcarrier-to-bit-rate-ratio. The CLTU Generation group adds two of its own: the maximum CLTU length and whether the randomiser is used.8485

sequenceDiagram
    participant VCDI as TC VC Data Insertion FG (FSP)
    participant CG as CLTU Generation FG
    participant FSLP as Forward TC Space Link Processing FG
    VCDI->>CG: TC Frame Transfer Data SLE-SDU<br/>(frame, delay, frame id, report flag)
    CG->>CG: randomise (option), BCH, start + tail;<br/>map frame id to CLTU id
    CG->>FSLP: CLTU Transfer Data SLE-SDU<br/>(CLTU, delay, CLTU id, report flag)
    alt delay at least minimum-delay-time
        FSLP-->>CG: accepted (CLTU id)
        CG-->>VCDI: frame accepted (frame id)
    else delay too short
        FSLP-->>CG: rejected (CLTU id)
        CG-->>VCDI: frame rejected (frame id)
    end
    FSLP-->>CG: radiated (CLTU id), if requested
    CG-->>VCDI: frame radiated (frame id)
    Note over VCDI: maps frame id to packet-identification<br/>and reports radiation per FSP instance

Diagram based on annex D1.1 to D1.3 of the FSP specification.848586

Each group passes its production status up the chain, combined with its own. The CLTU Generation group combines the radiation group's status (the FCLTU values) with its own as follows:85

Space link processing status ↓ / CLTU Generation status → configured operational interrupted halted configured configured configured interrupted halted operational configured operational interrupted halted interrupted interrupted interrupted interrupted halted halted halted halted halted halted

Source: table D-1.85 The TC VC Data Insertion group applies the same combination to the result and its own status (table D-2), and an 'operational' aggregate then also carries the FSP sub-states.86 In words: 'halted' anywhere wins, then 'interrupted', and the chain is 'operational' only if every group is.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Commanding is the most sensitive SLE service. FCLTU adds one integrity mechanism of its own: the monotonically increasing cltu-identification. A CLTU without the expected number is rejected, which constrains a third party's ability to inject extra commands. The strict operation sequence of the state table constrains a third party's ability to take over an instance without being detected.69 Everything else (authentication of BIND or of every PDU, confidentiality, denial-of-service protection, auditing) relies on the common SLE mechanisms, the underlying network and bilateral agreements. The standard warns that a hijacked forward service could be used to subvert or destroy a spacecraft.6970 See SDLS for protection of the TC frames themselves, which the FCLTU service carries transparently.49

docs.title: SCOS-2000, the NIS and throw events
Throw events in the MIB
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 has supported throw events as commands since release 5.0. The import ICD defines two special values of the command type CCF_CTYPE.7172

  • 'T' (SLE throw event): sent to the SLE service provider (the ground station equipment) and not uplinked. Its CDF entries define the Event ID and the following fields according to the NIS/NCTRS MCS interface ICD.
  • 'N' (NIS throw event): executed by the NIS itself and not forwarded to the station. Its CDF entries follow the NIS Throw Events ICD.

The referenced documents are EGOS-NIS-NCTR-ICD-0002 "ICD NIS/NCTRS Volume 2 – MCS I/F" issue 4.0.2 and EGOS-NIS-NIS-ICD-0003 "NIS Throw Events ICD" issue 1.3. Neither is in this library.73 Throw events cannot be blocked with other commands in a sequence or command source.71

The Solar Orbiter MIB (release 25925PFM, 2025-09-16) has no 'T' commands and six 'N' commands. All six use the packet header NOS2KHDR ("NIS Throw Events"), type 251, subtype 1 and APID 1964. That header has no PCDF fields.74

CCF_CNAME Description Event ID (CNISX205TC) Further content ESESIONO OPEN SESSION OPEN_SESSION 10 unnamed fixed octet (0), 16-bit "Polling Frequency" (ENISTE01), fixed octet described as "Spare" ESESIONC CLOSE SESSION CLOSE_SESSION 11 unnamed fixed octet (0) EGENRTCO GENERIC OPEN TC LINK OPEN_LINK 20 service type FCLTU, First CLTU ID, service instance identifier EGENRTCC GENERIC CLOSE TC LINK CLOSE_LINK 21 service type FCLTU, service instance identifier EGENRTMO GENERIC OPEN TM LINK OPEN_LINK 20 RCF, GVCID fields, times, identifier (see return services) EGENRTMC GENERIC CLOSE TM LINK CLOSE_LINK 21 RCF, identifier

The Event ID calibration also defines HEARTBEAT_MSG (12), ABORT_LINK (22) and CHANGE_MODE (23), which no Solar Orbiter command uses. The SLE service type calibration CNISX207TC lists RAF 1, RCF 2, ROCF 3, FCLTU 4 and FSP 5.74 The interface therefore knows FSP, but both Solar Orbiter TC-link commands fix the service type to FCLTU (CDF_ELTYPE 'F'), and the TM-link commands carry RCF as the default of an editable element (CDF_ELTYPE 'E'), in the 2025 and the 2020 releases alike.7476 As far as these commands show, the TC link is opened as FCLTU, so the frames, COP-1 and the CLTUs are produced on the user side of the SLE interface, as the FCLTU division of work implies.3

The last element, ENISTE37 "Service_Instance_End", is a variable-length ASCII string (PTC 8, PFC 0) with the default "g=1.cltu=cltu01". The three parts together form sagr=144.spack=NN11-PERM.fsl-fg=1.cltu=cltu01, a valid FCLTU service instance identifier.7475 The 2020-04-16 release contains the same six commands with the same values.76

Inference

The "First CLTU ID" field corresponds to FCLTU's first-cltu-identification. This suggests that the NIS performs CLTU-BIND and CLTU-START towards the station when it receives OPEN_LINK. Likewise, "OPEN SESSION" with a polling frequency suggests a session between SCOS-2000 and the NIS, inside which links are opened. The ICD that would confirm these semantics is not in the library.

SQL used 
-- Solar Orbiter MIB, release 25925PFM (VDF: 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33)
SELECT CCF_CTYPE, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY CCF_CTYPE;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_PKTID, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_CTYPE = 'N';
SELECT * FROM tcp WHERE TCP_ID = 'NOS2KHDR';
SELECT count(*) FROM pcdf WHERE PCDF_TCNAME = 'NOS2KHDR';   -- 0

SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_ELTYPE, CDF_DESCR, CDF_ELLEN, CDF_BIT,
       CDF_PNAME, CDF_INTER, CDF_VALUE
  FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('EGENRTCO','EGENRTCC','ESESIONO','ESESIONC')
 ORDER BY CDF_CNAME, CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);

SELECT CPC_NAME, CPC_DESCR, CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC, CPC_PAFREF, CPC_DEFVAL
  FROM cpc WHERE CPC_NAME LIKE 'ENISTE%';
SELECT PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALTXT, PAS_ALVAL FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR LIKE 'CNISX2%';

-- Which SLE service type each command fixes (same result in solo-2020-04-16)
SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_ELTYPE, CDF_VALUE FROM cdf WHERE CDF_PNAME = 'ENISTE03' ORDER BY CDF_CNAME;
-- -> EGENRTCC F FCLTU, EGENRTCO F FCLTU, EGENRTMC E RCF, EGENRTMO E RCF

The relevant MIB tables are CCF, CDF, CPC, PAS, TCP and PCDF; command definition in general is explained in commanding.

docs.title: Bit-rate changes: on board and on the ground
docs.text:
The FCLTU example of a bit-rate change (first reconfigure the spacecraft, then throw an event) has a visible on-board half in the Solar Orbiter MIB. The "Set TC bit rate" commands include the following. The MIB has five more TC bit-rate commands: ZCS2Z05J and ZCS2Z05K ("Set DST-RX Antenna A/B TC Bitrate SDP") and ZCD2Z086 to ZCD2Z088 ("Set SGM ... TC Bitrate").77

Command Description Type/Subtype APID ZCSD3402 Dst Set TC Bit Rate 131/1 236 ZDSG0009 DST-RX A Set TC bitrate 2/128 172 ZDSG1009 DST-RX B Set TC bitrate 2/128 172 ZYP66991 PSS Set TC Bit Rate 170/7 1948

Inference

These are on-board commands. The matching ground-side change would be an SLE throw event ('T'), of which this MIB has none, or a station reconfiguration made by other means. How ESA actually sequences a Solar Orbiter uplink rate change is not stated in the available sources.

SQL used 
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_CNAME IN ('ZCSD3402','ZDSG0009','ZDSG1009','ZYP66991');
-- all TC bit-rate commands
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_DESCR LIKE '%TC Bit%Rate%' OR CCF_DESCR LIKE '%TC bitrate%';

docs.title: Ground responses and verification stages
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 tracks every telecommand through verification stages. The EDDS external user ICD defines the first three as follows:78

Stage Meaning R Release from SCOS-2000 to "the SLE User (NCTRS/NIS)". It fails if the PTV check fails, if there is no TCP/IP connection to the NCTRS, or if the NCTRS rejects the command (for example because the station connection is not available) G Ground station reception (first uplink verification stage) T Uplink, also called radiation (second stage). For a throw event command this is the execution stage

The Solar Orbiter MIB defines an internal ground packet "TM Packet used by the Releaser G/S response" (SPID 66850, type 165/1, APID 1966). Its fields are listed below.79

Octet Parameter Description PTC/PFC, calibration 0 NYG02201 GS Packet Size 3/14 4 NYG02202 GS Packet Type 2/16, CYGT2202TM 6 NYG02203 GS Spacecraft ID 3/12 8 NYG02204 GS Acceptance Time 9/2 19 NYG02206 GS CLTU ID 3/14 23 NYG02207 GS Acknowledgement 2/8, CYGT2207TM 24 NYG02208 GS Acknowledgement ¾ 26 NYG02210 GS Next TC ID 3/14

The "GS Packet Type" calibration lists BDseq (0), BDseq_response (1), LinkStatus_PCM (3), COP1directive (4), ThrowEvnt (5), ThrowEvnt_Resp (6), CLTU (7), CLTU_Resp (8), SDID_MKII_RQM (9), SDID_MKII_TRM (10), FSPPkt (20), FSPPkt_Resp (21), FSPdirective (22) and FSPdir_Resp (23). The acknowledgement calibration lists Confirm_Accept (0), ConfirmTrnsmit (1), Failure_accept (3), FailureTrnsmit (4) and Nis_Rejected (9).79 The four FSP values (identical in the 2020 release) suggest message types for packets and COP-1 directives sent to an FSP provider; they are discussed on the FSP page.76

Inference

"GS CLTU ID" and "GS Next TC ID" mirror the FCLTU cltu-identification in the TRANSFER-DATA invocation and the next expected value in its return. The accept and transmit confirmations and failures look like the positive or negative TRANSFER-DATA return (stage G) and the 'cltu radiated' or failure notification (stage T). This mapping is not stated in the available sources.

SQL used 
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, p.PCF_DESCR, l.PLF_OFFBY, p.PCF_PTC, p.PCF_PFC, p.PCF_CURTX
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID = 66850 ORDER BY CAST(l.PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
SELECT TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM, TXP_ALTXT FROM txp
 WHERE TXP_NUMBR IN ('CYGT2202TM','CYGT2207TM') ORDER BY TXP_NUMBR, CAST(TXP_FROM AS INT);

See command verification and the TXP table.

docs.title: Routing and CLTU size limits
docs.text:
Commands normally go to the NCTRS. The MIB's DST table can route an APID elsewhere. Solar Orbiter has a single entry, which sends APID 1372 (91 commands, ZIC00000 to ZICCMS65) to EGSE.TC.0x8800.8081 The import ICD also explains that the mission specific maximum CLTU size limits commands. The variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (default 248 octets) must be set to the maximum CLTU size minus the time-tag wrapper, so that time-tagged commands still fit.82

SQL used 
SELECT * FROM dst;                                   -- 1372 | EGSE.TC.0x8800
SELECT count(*), min(CCF_CNAME), max(CCF_CNAME) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_APID = '1372';

The page on NCTRS and the NIS describes the ESA side of the interface, and uplink follows a command end to end.

docs.title: SLE forward service: Forward Space Packet (FSP)
docs.text:
The Forward Space Packet (FSP) service lets a mission send telecommand Space Packets to a spacecraft through someone else's ground system. The packets can go in sequence-controlled mode or in expedited mode.1 Of the forward SLE services for conventional telecommand (FCLTU, FSP and Enhanced FCLTU), it is the one that works at packet level.3 The user hands over whole packets. The provider does the rest: it blocks or segments the packets into TC Transfer Frames, runs the sending end of COP-1, encodes each frame into a CLTU and radiates it.2 Several users, each with its own service instance, can share one Virtual Channel (VC) and one uplink. The provider multiplexes their packets by fixed rules, so the users do not have to coordinate with each other.23

Compare this with FCLTU, where the user builds the frames and CLTUs and runs COP-1 itself. The SLE overview explains the concepts that FSP shares with the other services (BIND, states, authentication). The architecture behind it is on the cross support reference model and service management.

At a glance

Item Value Specification CCSDS 912.3-B-3, August 2016 ("adds clarifications and corrections"); earlier issues B-1 November 2004 and B-2 July 20104 Status The library copy carries the CCSDS "Historical Document" banner.5 The 2023 overview lists it as 912.3-B-3-S, made historical in September 2022.6 Data unit One telecommand Space Packet per FSP-TRANSFER-DATA (1 to 65,536 octets as an ASN.1 SpaceLinkDataUnit)78 Space link stack TC only: TC SDLP, COP-1, TC coding. The AOS profile named in the reference model is out of scope.9 Produced by Forward TC VC Data Insertion SLE-FG, fed into CLTU Generation and Forward TC Space Link Processing10 Instance One instance per pair of TC VC and Mission User Entity (MUE)2 Delivery mode Forward online only (fwdOnline (3)); offline is "the subject of further study"118 Transmission modes Sequence-controlled (AD) and expedited (BD)11 Binding User-initiated; ApplicationIdentifier fwdTcSpacePkt (13)1213 BIND version-number 5 in this issue14 Provider states 1 'unbound', 2 'ready', 3 'active'15 Production status configured, operational (BD / AD and BD / AD suspended), interrupted, halted16 Time UTC as CDS (1958 epoch, 16-bit day), microsecond or picosecond resolution, 0.1 s precision and accuracy17 Service instance attribute fsp, OID {iso 3 112 4 3 1 2 10}; value "fsp" plus an instance number18

docs.title: What FSP does
docs.text:
The user sends packets wrapped in SLE-SDUs with FSP-TRANSFER-DATA. The provider reads the Packet Primary Header to check, for example, that the APID is one the user may use. It does not otherwise look at, interpret or change the packet. A telecommand packet with a valid header is sent bit for bit as received.2 Through the operations of the service the user can bind, send annotated packets, get notifications and status reports, stop and restart sending, change some parameters, invoke COP-1 directives, throw events at complex management, and unbind.212

FSP was conceived for packet structures in general. This issue handles only CCSDS Space Packets, and only on the TC protocol stack (TC SDLP, COP-1, TC synchronization and channel coding).9 The FSP version of the TC VC Data Insertion function does not apply Space Data Link Security. The reason given is that a user would not want to tell a third party (the FSP provider) how its SDLS is configured.19

docs.text:
Task With FCLTU With FSP Build the Space Packet User User Block or segment packets into TC frames, choose MAP User Provider (TC VC Data Insertion FG)19 Run FOP-1: frame sequence numbers, retransmission from CLCWs User Provider; the user can only send COP-1 directives1920 Multiplex MAPs and VCs User Provider, using the algorithms of annex B21 Randomize, BCH-encode, add start and tail sequences User Provider (CLTU Generation FG); one TC frame per CLTU2223 Radiate under PLOP-1 or PLOP-2, watch RF and bit lock in the CLCW Provider Provider (Forward TC Space Link Processing FG)24 Release-time control Earliest and latest radiation time per CLTU25 Earliest and latest production time per packet; no radiation-time limits inside the provider2627 Unit the provider reports on CLTU Packet: processing started, radiated, acknowledged28

Sources: functional groups and production requirements of FSP, CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA of FCLTU.

docs.title: Where FSP sits: the forward TC functional groups
docs.text:
Three SLE Functional Groups (SLE-FGs) produce FSP. The data channel between two FGs is carried by an SLE transfer service if the FGs are in different SLE Complexes, and by local means if they are in the same complex.10 No Recommended Standard exists for the Forward TC Frame (FTCF) service. So, until CCSDS publishes one, the CLTU Generation FG and the TC VC Data Insertion FG must be in the same complex.10

flowchart LR
    U1["MUE 1<br/>(FSP user)"] -- "FSP-TRANSFER-DATA<br/>(Space Packet + annotation)" --> VCDI
    U2["MUE 2<br/>(FSP user)"] -- "FSP" --> VCDI
    subgraph CX["SLE Complex"]
        VCDI["Forward TC VC Data Insertion FG<br/>blocking / segmentation,<br/>MAP mux, FOP-1, VC mux"]
        CG["Forward CLTU Generation FG<br/>randomize (option), BCH,<br/>start + tail sequence"]
        FSLP["Forward TC Space Link Processing FG<br/>PLOP-1/PLOP-2, modulation,<br/>radiation"]
        VCDI -- "TC Frame Transfer Data SLE-SDU<br/>(frame, delay, frame id,<br/>report flag)" --> CG
        CG -- "CLTU Transfer Data SLE-SDU<br/>(CLTU, delay, CLTU id,<br/>report flag)" --> FSLP
    end
    FSLP --> SC(("Spacecraft"))
    OCF["Return frame processing<br/>(OCF data channel,<br/>Control Word Type 0)"] -. "CLCW: retransmit / acknowledge" .-> VCDI
    OCF -. "CLCW: No RF Available,<br/>No Bit Lock" .-> FSLP

Diagram based on the forward TC functional groups and the production requirements of annex D.10192923

  • Forward TC VC Data Insertion FG. For each FSP instance it takes the packets out of the SLE-SDUs and blocks or segments them into TC frames. For sequence-controlled frames it sets the Frame Sequence Number and keeps a copy. It reads the CLCWs from Operational Control Field channels (Control Word Type 0 only) and retransmits or deletes the kept frames.19 It also provides the TC VC Access (TC VCA) service, but only one of the two service types is allowed on a given VC.30
  • Forward CLTU Generation FG. It optionally randomizes the frames, BCH-encodes them and adds the start and tail sequences.22 For FSP a CLTU carries exactly one TC frame, even though the coding standard allows more.23
  • Forward TC Space Link Processing FG. It checks from the CLCW that the physical channel is available, generates the acquisition and idle sequences of the PLOP in effect, and modulates and radiates the CLTUs.24 This is the same function that provides FCLTU, and annex D reuses the FCLTU rules for it.27

The reference model gives FSP two production profiles. The AOS profile runs through the Forward AOS VC Data Insertion and AOS Space Link Processing FGs. The TC profile runs through the three FGs above.31 FSP 912.3-B-3 specifies only the TC profile.9 The reference model adds two rules for TC. Segmented packets can only be sent with sequence control. If FSP and TC-VCA are both active on one VC, only one of them can be sequence-controlled.32

When the FGs are in different complexes, FSP depends on the FTCF and/or Forward CLTU services underneath it. The FSP schedule must then fit the schedules of those underlying services.33

docs.title: What the provider checks in each packet
docs.text:
The provider looks only at the 6-octet Space Packet primary header, and only to enforce what service management has set up.234

Field layout from the Space Packet Protocol. Version '000' and Type '1' for telecommand are its values.3536 The checks and diagnostic codes come from FSP-TRANSFER-DATA.3439

The apid-list parameter is either any or an ascending list of up to 2,048 APIDs (0 to 2047).3934 The ASN.1 allows maximum-packet-length values from 7 to 65,542 octets.40 That is the length range of a complete Space Packet.37 The data parameter of FSP-TRANSFER-DATA, however, is an ASN.1 SpaceLinkDataUnit of 1 to 65,536 octets (see Notes on the specification text).8 The provider buffers only complete packets.41

docs.title: Production, provision and the managed parameters
docs.text:
FSP separates service provision, which makes the operations available to one user, from service production, which turns the FSP channel into the RF channel. Provision parameters, such as the status-report frequency, affect one instance. Service management sets them when it creates the instance, and the user may change them through operations. Production parameters, such as maximum packet length or the VC multiplexing scheme, can affect several instances and the complex's resources, so only service management may change them. There is one exception: COP-1 directives. For each VC, one service instance may invoke them. Some directives act on the spacecraft, so FSP treats them as part of the telecommand service rather than of its management.42 One production instance may serve several FSP instances. Production extracts the packets from the concurrent streams and multiplexes them onto the space link, independently of any single instance.43

Service packages, agreed between SLE Utilization Management and SLE Complex Management, define which instances exist, when, and their initial parameters. Production parameters include the VC, the multiplexing schemes, the maximum packet and frame lengths, and the CLTU-generation and space-link configuration. Provision parameters include the instance's start and stop times.44 The service package also sets the provider's buffer size in octets.41

docs.text:

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operation Invoked by Confirmed Valid in states Invocation / return PDU tag FSP-BIND User (initiator) Yes 1 100 / 101 FSP-UNBIND User (initiator) Yes 2 102 / 103 FSP-START User Yes 2 0 / 1 FSP-STOP User Yes 3 2 / 3 FSP-TRANSFER-DATA User Yes 3 10 / 11 FSP-ASYNC-NOTIFY Provider No 2, 3 12 FSP-SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT User Yes 2, 3 4 / 5 FSP-STATUS-REPORT Provider No 2, 3 13 FSP-GET-PARAMETER User Yes 2, 3 6 / 7 FSP-THROW-EVENT User Yes 2, 3 8 / 9 FSP-INVOKE-DIRECTIVE User Yes 3 14 / 15 FSP-PEER-ABORT User or provider No 2, 3 104

Sources: table 2-1, the "valid only in state" clause of each operation, and the FspUserToProviderPdu and FspProviderToUserPdu CHOICE tags.124748

The conformance matrix (annex E) makes every operation mandatory except FSP-THROW-EVENT, which is optional. Version negotiation in FSP-BIND is optional, and so are the credentials parameters and stop-production-time. Buffering is mandatory, with a minimum size of 1,024 maximum-length FSP-TRANSFER-DATA invocations.85

The rules common to all operations are the usual SLE ones. Every confirmed operation returns a result, plus a diagnostic when the result is negative. 'Other reason' may be used only when no specific value fits. Checks should be made in the order the diagnostics are listed, and an implementation that uses another order must document it.49 Access control is two-level: initiator and responder must be registered with each other, and both must be authorised for the instance.50 Authentication can be 'all' (every invocation and return except PEER-ABORT), 'bind' or 'none'.51 Every confirmed operation except BIND and UNBIND carries an invoke-ID (0 to 65,535). Such operations are non-blocking, and a duplicate outstanding ID is rejected with 'duplicate invoke-ID' (common diagnostic 100).528

docs.title: FSP-BIND, FSP-UNBIND and FSP-PEER-ABORT
docs.text:
FSP-BIND carries the usual parameters. The service-type is redundant because its only valid value is fwdTcSpacePkt, but it is kept for a future generic SLE-BIND.53 A responder that does not negotiate versions accepts the version configured in service-version-number. One that does negotiate may answer with a lower version.14 The BIND diagnostics are 'access denied' (0), 'service type not supported' (1), 'version not supported' (2), 'no such service instance' (3), 'already bound' (4), 'service instance not accessible to this initiator' (5), 'inconsistent service type' (6), 'invalid time' (7), 'out of service' (8, production halted) and 'other reason' (127).5413 A successful BIND moves the provider from state 1 to state 2.55

FSP-UNBIND is valid only in 'ready', so the user must stop first. Its unbind-reason is 'end' (0), after which the provider may delete the instance, 'suspend' (1), 'version not supported' (2) or 'other' (127). The only possible result is 'positive result'.5613 FSP-PEER-ABORT carries one diagnostic: 'access denied' (0), 'unexpected responder ID' (1), 'operational requirement' (2), 'protocol error' (3), 'communications failure' (4, gateways only), 'encoding error' (5), 'return timeout' (6), 'end of service instance provision period' (7), 'unsolicited invoke-ID' (8) or 'other reason' (127). Values 128 to 255 are reserved for the communications technology. PEER-ABORT carries no credentials.5713

What survives the end of an association matters for commanding. The provider discards the packets it holds for the instance. Packets already turned into Frame Data Units and placed in the segment queues are still sent. Three things persist across associations: accounting information, the identifiers that link notifications to the operations that caused them, and the COP parameters set by directives. Other provision parameters return to the values set by service management.5859

docs.title: FSP-START and FSP-STOP
docs.text:
Parameter In Return Meaning first-packet-identification M packet-identification expected in the first TRANSFER-DATA after this START start-production-time C Before 'operational': estimated time the provider can start processing, allowing for the uplink acquisition sequence. Otherwise: the most recent time production became 'operational'. Positive result only. stop-production-time C Estimated time production stops (may be later than the provision period ends), or null result, diagnostic M, C 'duplicate invoke-ID' (100), 'out of service' (0, halted), 'unable to comply' (1, interrupted), 'production time expired' (2), 'other reason' (127)

Sources: FSP-START parameters and diagnostics.6039

After 'unable to comply' the user may try again later. If complex management decides the problem is more than transient, the provider may abort.60 FSP-STOP discards the instance's packets that have not yet reached the segment queues. Packets already in the segment queues are completed, and any radiation or acknowledgement notifications that were asked for are still sent. STOP also clears the 'service instance blocked' and 'AD blocked' flags.6162 This is how a user recovers after 'sldu expired', 'production interrupted' or 'production halted': STOP, then a new START with a fresh first-packet-identification. The new identifiers should be chosen so that packets still being processed from before can be told apart.6364

docs.title: FSP-TRANSFER-DATA
docs.text:
Parameter ASN.1 type Meaning packet-identification 0 to 2³²−1 Sequence number: the START value, then +1 for each accepted packet. The return holds the next expected value. earliest-production-time null or Time Earliest time processing of the packet may start latest-production-time null or Time Latest time processing may start; if passed before the packet leaves the packets queue: 'sldu expired' delay-time microseconds (0 to 2³²−1) Minimum gap between the last CLTU carrying this packet and the next CLTU transmission-mode sequence-controlled (0), expedited (1), sequence-controlled and unblock AD (2) AD, BD, or AD with unblocking MAP-identifier none, or MAP 0–63 MAP to use; must be none if no Segment Headers are generated blocking permitted (0) / not permitted (1) May this packet share a frame with others? (written as yes/no in the text) processing-started-notification produce (0) / do not produce (1) Notify when the packet moves to a segments queue radiated-notification produce (0) / do not produce (1) Notify when radiation completes acknowledged-notification produce (0) / do not produce (1) Notify when all segments are acknowledged by CLCW (AD only) data 1 to 65,536 octets The Space Packet packet-buffer-available (return) 7 to 66,560 octets Free space left in this instance's request queue

Sources: table 3-6 and parameter clauses; ASN.1 FspTransferDataInvocation and FspTransferDataReturn.7266566674748

The time window. Times may not go backwards from one packet to the next. If the earliest time is null, processing starts at once, provided production is operational and the required transmission mode is available, or the latest time is also null.26 If the latest time is null, the packet waits as long as the instance is 'active' and production is not halted. If a latest time is given, the provider holds the packet back while production is 'interrupted' or the transmission mode is unavailable, until recovery or expiry.26 Two notes in the standard matter in practice. First, the processing steps (for example blocking) take a non-negligible time. Setting the latest time equal to the earliest time therefore usually produces 'late sldu'. Second, once a packet is inside a TC frame, its latest time no longer applies. Multiplexing may then radiate it later than that time.26

Delay time. The delay runs from the trailing edge of the last radiated bit of the last CLTU that carries part of the packet to the leading edge of the first bit of the next CLTU. Zero means no delay. The delay also applies when a frame is retransmitted under COP-1, and whatever VC the next frame is on. When several packets are blocked into one frame, the largest of their delay times is used. An unacceptable value is caught by the space link processing FG, and the rejection travels back up so that the TRANSFER-DATA return is negative.65

Transmission mode and AD blocking. After a 'packet transmission mode mismatch', the AD mode of the instance is blocked. Every later AD request is rejected with 'invalid transmission mode' until the user sends a packet with mode 'sequence-controlled and unblock AD mode'. That mode is accepted only while AD is blocked. If the unblocking packet has to start before the AD service is back, a new mismatch occurs and AD is blocked again.66

MAP and blocking. With a polling-vector MAP scheme, a packet on a permitted MAP that is not in the vector is queued but not processed until the vector changes. Segment Headers are needed when packets can exceed the frame's data field, or when MAPs are used on the VC.67 If blocking-usage is 'not permitted', the per-packet blocking flag is ignored, and each frame carries at most one packet.68

docs.title: Diagnostics of FSP-TRANSFER-DATA
docs.text:
Code Diagnostic Cause 100 duplicate invoke-ID invoke-ID already outstanding 0 unable to process Production not operational (already notified), provider still blocked after a fault and recovery, instance blocked after 'sldu expired', or production paused to process a THROW-EVENT 1 unable to store Not enough space left in the request queue 2 out of sequence packet-identification is not the expected value 3 duplicate packet identification Same identifier as a packet still buffered or in process (possible only after STOP/START) 4 inconsistent time range Earliest time later than latest time 5 invalid time Window does not overlap the scheduled production period or the provision period 6 conflicting production time intervals Window starts or ends earlier than that of an already accepted packet 7 late sldu Latest time already past when the invocation arrives 8 invalid delay time Outside the range supported by the space link processing configuration 9 invalid transmission mode Mode not permitted, AD requested while blocked, or unblock requested while not blocked 10 invalid MAP MAP not in map-list, or a MAP given when no Segment Headers are generated 11 invalid notification request Acknowledgement notification requested for an expedited packet 12 packet too long Over the maximum packet length 13 unsupported packet version Version not supported by CCSDS or by this instance 14 incorrect packet type Packet Type is not telecommand 15 invalid packet apid APID not allowed for this instance 127 other reason

Sources: diagnostic list in the order of the standard (check order); codes from DiagnosticFspTransferData and Diagnostics.34398

Rejecting 'conflicting production time intervals' up front is deliberate. Such a packet need not cause 'sldu expired', but it could. Rejecting it lets the user correct the time window, instead of losing the packets already buffered when the earlier packet expires during production.34

Worked example (illustrative values): sequence numbers

The user starts with first-packet-identification = 1000. TRANSFER-DATA with id 1000 is accepted, and the return carries 1001. The user then sends id 1002 by mistake. It is rejected with 'out of sequence', and the return again carries 1001, the value the provider still expects. A correct id 1001 is then accepted, and the return carries 1002.7

docs.title: FSP-ASYNC-NOTIFY
docs.text:
Every notification carries notification-type, packet-identification-last-processed, packet-identification-last-ok and production-status. When the last-processed identifier is not null, it also carries production-start-time and packet-status. When the last-ok identifier is not null, it also carries production-stop-time.6970 The identifiers survive release or abort of the association.70

Tag Notification Sent to Extra content 0 packet processing started Submitting user, if asked The packet's id 1 packet radiated Submitting user, if asked Id + frame-sequence-number (0–255) of the frame with the last segment 2 packet acknowledged Submitting user, if asked (AD only) Id 3 sldu expired Submitting user Expired id first, then ids of all its other discarded packets; instance blocked 4 packet transmission mode mismatch Users whose AD packets were discarded Discarded ids; AD blocked 5 transmission mode capability change All users of the VC (see conditions) fop-alert 6 buffer empty User of the instance None (not sent after STOP or after a discard event) 7 no invoke directive capability on this VC All other users of the VC None 17 invoke directive capability established on this VC All other users of the VC None 8 positive confirm response to directive Directive invoker directive-executed-identification 9 negative confirm response to directive Directive invoker Directive id + fop-alert 10 VC aborted All users of the VC Discarded ids (including frames already built) 11 production interrupted Users with packets in process Discarded ids (including frames already built); instance blocked 12 production halted All connected users Discarded ids; instance blocked 13 production operational Users not yet told, or told something else None; sub-state starts at 'BD' 14 action list completed Event thrower event-thrown-identification 15 action list not completed Event thrower event-thrown-identification 16 event condition evaluated to false Event thrower event-thrown-identification

Sources: notification-type definitions, conditional parameters and the FspNotification CHOICE.717273

A 'packet acknowledged' notification means the spacecraft received every frame carrying parts of the packet. It does not mean that the packet was reassembled or executed correctly. Only telemetry can show that.7471 On the telemetry side, see command verification in the MIB and ST[01] request verification.

FOP alerts. The fop-alert parameter reports why the sequence-controlled guarantee ended. Its values follow the COP-1 alert reason codes:

Code FSP value COP-1 cause 0 no FOP alert Capability changed without ending the guarantee 1 FOP alert-limit Transmissions exhausted for an AD frame, or for a BC frame from an 'Unlock' or 'Set V(R)' directive 2 FOP alert-lockout Lockout detected 3 FOP alert-synch Retransmit flag cleared with N(R) = NN(R) after it was set; all frames acknowledged but Retransmit = 1; or acknowledgement attempted in state S4 4 FOP alert-NN(R) CLCW with invalid N(R) 5 FOP alert-CLCW Wait = 1 with Retransmit = 0, or an invalid CLCW bit pattern 6 FOP alert-LLIF FOP-1 and the lower layer out of synchronisation 7 FOP alert-term 'Terminate AD Service' directive received

Sources: FSP fop-alert, ASN.1 FopAlert, COP-1 table 4-4.753976

COP-1 itself reports exhausted transmissions under two reason codes: 'Limit' or 'T1' for an AD frame, and 'T1' for a BC frame. FSP has the single value 'FOP alert-limit' for both cases.7675

Packet status. The status of the last processed packet uses the shared ForwardDuStatus type: 'radiated' (0), 'expired' (1), 'interrupted' (2), 'acknowledged' (3), 'production started' (4), 'production not started' (5) and 'unsupported transmission mode' (6). 'Expired' and 'unsupported transmission mode' guarantee that the packet was not radiated. 'Interrupted' means processing began and was aborted, because production became 'interrupted' or 'halted' or because 'Abort VC' was executed. Earlier packets may also be affected, and an AD packet may already have completed radiation before its status changed to 'interrupted'.778 production-stop-time is the end of radiation for a BD packet, and the time of the last acknowledging CLCW for an AD packet.78

Losing telemetry during commanding. The frame-sequence-number in 'packet radiated' exists for one case. Telemetry is lost before commanding finishes, and commanding must continue through another station and therefore another FSP provider. The new provider does not know which packet went in which frame. With GET-PARAMETER the user reads its transmitter-frame-sequence-number. From the frame numbers it already received, the user can then work out which packets arrived on board, and resume without sending any packet twice or missing one.79

docs.title: Status reports
docs.text: FSP-SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT asks for one report now ('immediately'), periodic reports ('periodically', with a 2 to 600 s cycle), or no more reports ('stop'). Periodic reporting is off after every BIND. Its diagnostics are 'duplicate invoke-ID', 'already stopped' (1), 'invalid reporting cycle' (2) and 'other reason'.8081 Each FSP-STATUS-REPORT contains the last-processed and last-ok groups and the production status. It also contains AD and BD counts of packets received, processed and radiated, the count of AD packets acknowledged, and the free buffer space.8248 Only packets that passed the checks count as received. "Processed" includes packets that aborted or are still in process. A packet counts as radiated once, however many times COP-1 retransmits it. The counts run over the whole provision period and survive new associations.8283

docs.title: FSP-THROW-EVENT
docs.text:
THROW-EVENT asks the provider to pass an event to SLE Complex Management, typically a change of production parameters. The standard's examples are an uplink bit-rate change after a telecommand has reconfigured the on-board receiver, and releasing the bit pattern that resets a Packet Assembly Controller.84 The event happens when it is thrown, not in step with any radiation. If the user needs it synchronised with a particular packet, the user must arrange that with production times or notifications.84 The operation is optional. It must be enabled per instance, and several instances (for example one per VC) may be allowed to throw events.8485

Parameter Type Meaning event-identifier 1 to 65,535 Event agreed between Complex Management and Utilization Management event-qualifier 1 to 1,024 octets Event-specific data; the provider checks only type and length, and complex management checks the content event-invocation-identification 0 to 2³²−1 0 after the first BIND, +1 per accepted event; return carries the next expected value; kept across re-binding

Sources: THROW-EVENT parameters and FspThrowEventInvocation.8647

The return only says whether the request was accepted: 'duplicate invoke-ID', 'operation not supported' (0), 'out of sequence' (1), 'no such event' (2) or 'other reason'. The outcome arrives later as 'action list completed', 'action list not completed' or 'event condition evaluated to false'.8739 If space link processing is in another complex, the FSP provider throws the matching FTCF or CLTU THROW-EVENT there, and translates the notifications that come back.8488

Annex H gives example events. They are not binding. Qualifier fields are separated by white space.89

Event ID Qualifier Action and preconditions Set Mod 1 on or off Switch command modulation of the carrier; 'on' needs production at least 'configured' Change Rate 2 br <BR>, 7.8125 to 4000.0 bit/s New bit rate (range assumes a subcarrier; up to 256 kb/s with direct modulation) Change Index 3 mi <MI>, 1 to 1570 mrad New modulation index Change Rate/Index 4 br <BR> mi <MI> Both

For events 2 to 4, no radiation may be in progress, and all packet, segment and directive queues must be empty. Otherwise the provider answers 'event condition evaluated to false'.89 A worked example with illustrative values: the user throws event 2 with the qualifier br 2000. The return is positive. Once the station has switched, an 'action list completed' notification follows, quoting the same event-invocation-identification.8986 SCOS-2000 and the NIS model station-side events with their own throw-event commands (see below).

docs.title: FSP-INVOKE-DIRECTIVE
docs.text:
This operation lets the user drive the provider's FOP-1. At most one FSP instance per VC may be configured to invoke directives. The operation is valid only in 'active'.20

Tag FSP directive COP-1 directive Qualifier 0 Initiate AD Service (without CLCW check) same none 1 Initiate AD Service (with CLCW check) same none 2 Initiate AD Service (with Unlock) same; sends a BC segment none 3 Initiate AD Service (with Set V(R)) same; sends a BC segment V*(R), 0–255 4 Terminate AD Service same; deletes queued AD packets of the VC, keeps BD packets none 5 Resume AD Service same none 6 Set V(S) to V*(S) same V*(S), 0–255 7 Set FOP_Sliding_Window_Width same 1–255 8 Set T1_Initial same µs, 1 to 2³²−1 9 Set Transmission_Limit same 1 to 65,535 10 Set Timeout_Type same terminate AD (0) / suspend AD (1) 11 Abort VC FSP only none: implies Terminate AD, deletes all queued frames and packets of the VC, BD included 12 Modify map-multiplexing-control FSP only priority list or polling vector

Sources: FSP directive list, ASN.1 FspInvokeDirectiveInvocation, COP-1 table 4-1.204790

directive-identification is numbered like event-invocation-identification: it starts at 0 after the first BIND and is kept across re-binding. The diagnostics are 'duplicate invoke-ID', 'directive invocation not allowed' (0), 'directive identification out of sequence' (1), 'directive error' (2) and 'other reason'.2039 A positive return only means that the directive was passed to FOP-1. Completion is reported as 'positive confirm response to directive', or as 'negative confirm response to directive' with a FOP alert, because the negative confirmation itself carries no reason.917192 After 'Abort VC', only BD packets can be sent until one of the four Initiate directives restarts the AD service.20

docs.title: Inside the provider: queues and multiplexing
docs.text:
Annex B is normative. It describes the provider with a logical model, and an implementation conforms if its external behaviour matches that model.30

flowchart TB
    subgraph SI1["Service instance 1 (VC X)"]
        RQ1["Requests queue<br/>(time-stamped on arrival)"] --> PQ1a["Packets queue<br/>MAP 1"]
        RQ1 --> PQ1b["Packets queue<br/>MAP 2"]
        PQ1a -->|"segment / block"| SQ1a["Segments queue<br/>MAP 1"]
        PQ1b -->|"segment / block"| SQ1b["Segments queue<br/>MAP 2"]
        DQ["Directives queue<br/>(only the instance allowed<br/>to invoke directives)"]
    end
    subgraph SI2["Service instance 2 (VC X)"]
        RQ2["Requests queue"] --> PQ2["Packets queue<br/>MAP 4"] --> SQ2["Segments queue<br/>MAP 4"]
    end
    SQ1a --> MM["MAP multiplexing<br/>(FIFO / absolute priority /<br/>polling vector)"]
    SQ1b --> MM
    SQ2 --> MM
    MM --> FOP["FOP-1 of VC X"]
    DQ --> FOP
    FOP --> VM["VC multiplexing<br/>(FIFO / absolute priority /<br/>polling vector)"]
    FOPY["FOP-1 of other VCs<br/>(FSP or TC VCA)"] --> VM
    VM --> CG["Forward CLTU Generation FG<br/>(AD x sequence-controlled-frames-repetition,<br/>BC x cop-control-frames-repetition,<br/>BD once)"]

Diagram based on figures B-1 to B-3 and clauses B3 to B5.30939596

The queue rules, in order:

  1. Each instance has one requests queue. It has one packets queue, or one per permitted MAP if MAPs are used. Each packets queue has one segments queue. The instance allowed to invoke directives also has a directives queue, so a VC has at most one.93
  2. A packet is stamped with its arrival time when it enters the requests queue. It moves to its MAP's packets queue when that queue has room and one of these holds. Production is operational with the needed mode available (sub-state 'AD and BD' for AD packets) and the earliest time is null. Or the same, with the earliest time reached. Or both times are null. Or the latest time, minus an implementation guard period, has been reached. The guard period makes sure the user gets the right notification ('packet transmission mode mismatch' or 'production interrupted') rather than 'late sldu'. Only the packet at the head of the requests queue is examined.93
  3. When a segments queue is empty, the head packet of its packets queue is segmented if needed and moved. If blocking is permitted and the packet allows it, the provider starts a blocking timer (blocking-timeout-period). It adds same-mode packets until the Frame Data Unit is full, a no-blocking packet comes next, or the timer expires.9394
  4. The latest-time check is made when a packet leaves the packets queue, and never again afterwards.94
  5. A Frame Data Unit takes the time stamp of its (first) packet. MAP multiplexing then picks Frame Data Units for the FOP. FIFO takes the earliest time stamp. Absolute priority always searches from the highest-priority MAP, and all priorities must be different. A polling vector visits MAPs in vector order and wraps round. VC multiplexing between FOPs works the same way, and the chosen frame goes to CLTU Generation.9596 The MAP schemes of different VCs and the VC scheme are independent.21
  6. Directives go into the directives queue for immediate execution.95
  7. Discards. STOP, PEER-ABORT, 'sldu expired' and protocol abort discard packets not yet in a segments queue and keep the built Frame Data Units. A transmission mode mismatch discards the built AD Frame Data Units, plus all AD packets of every instance that lost one. 'Abort VC' clears every queue of the VC. 'Interrupted' clears all queues of the instances that had Frame Data Units in progress. 'Halted' clears all queues.95
  8. When the FOP sliding window is full of unacknowledged AD and BC frames, BD Frame Data Units still pass to the FOP.96
  9. Frame repetition (optional). AD frames go to CLTU Generation sequence-controlled-frames-repetition times, and BC frames cop-control-frames-repetition times. Neither may exceed repetition-limit. BD frames go once. Repetition is meant for links with long light-time delay, where it raises the chance that a sequence of frames gets through in a short session. A provider that does not support repetition sets both parameters to 1.96

Worked example (illustrative numbers): one large packet and three small ones

Assume maximum-frame-length = 256 octets, a Frame Error Control Field and Segment Headers on the VC. A TC frame has a 5-octet header and an optional 2-octet FECF.97 That leaves 256 − 5 − 2 = 249 octets of frame data field, and after the 1-octet Segment Header, 248 octets of packet per frame. A 1,000-octet AD packet on MAP 2 therefore needs five segments (4 × 248 = 992, plus 8). Their Sequence Flags are 0b01, 0b00, 0b00, 0b00 and 0b10.98 It must be sent sequence-controlled, because segmented packets cannot go without sequence control.32 FSP puts each frame in its own CLTU, so this means five CLTUs. The packet's delay-time applies after the fifth.2365

Next, three 40-octet AD packets with blocking allowed, on the same MAP, with delay times 0, 20,000 and 5,000 µs. They fit in one frame (120 + 1 octets ≤ 249), carry Sequence Flags 0b11, and the CLTU that carries them gets the largest delay, 20,000 µs.6598

Segment Header layout and Sequence Flags from TC SDLP; MAP range from the FSP ASN.1.9839

This annex is also why the CCSDS link-protocol overview makes an exception to its rule that the project chooses the multiplexing algorithm. If FSP is used on the ground with TC SDLP, the FSP algorithms must be used for VC and MAP multiplexing.99 The ECSS communications handbook adds that the one-octet PAC control segment used in European TC could affect interoperability, for example with SLE FSP.100 See TC SDLP.

docs.title: Production status
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> configured
    configured --> operational: management makes production operational<br/>(sweep / acquisition done, CLCW lock flags OK)
    state operational {
        [*] --> BD
        BD --> ADandBD: Initiate AD Service<br/>completes
        ADandBD --> BD: FOP alert /<br/>Terminate AD
        ADandBD --> ADsuspended: transmission limit reached,<br/>timeout type 'suspend'
        ADsuspended --> ADandBD: Resume AD Service
    }
    operational --> interrupted: production fault
    interrupted --> operational: fault corrected
    configured --> halted: management action
    operational --> halted: management action
    interrupted --> halted: management action
    halted --> configured: configuration restored<br/>(no notification)

Diagram based on figure C-1, table C-1 and the definitions of the sub-states. CCSDS leaves the sub-state transitions to COP-1.10116

The ASN.1 encodes the status as configured (0), operational-BD (1), operational-AD-and-BD (2), operational-AD-suspended (3), interrupted (4) and halted (5).39 The initial status is 'configured'. The uplink is switched on with the nominal sweep (carrier modulation mode CMM-1) when the supported agency asks for it, by schedule or by voice.102 The step to 'operational' depends on the PLOP and on the two CLCW checks:102

plop-in-effect rf-available-required bit-lock-required Production becomes 'operational' PLOP-1 no n/a when the uplink sweep completes PLOP-1 yes n/a when the sweep completes and the CLCW shows RF available PLOP-2 no no when the acquisition sequence has been radiated PLOP-2 yes no after acquisition, and the CLCW shows RF available PLOP-2 no yes after acquisition, and the CLCW shows bit lock PLOP-2 yes yes after acquisition, and the CLCW shows both

Production becomes 'interrupted' when a lock check is required and the uplink status no longer has the required value.102 PLOP handling is formally part of the Forward TC Space Link Processing FG. FSP specifies it because that FG may be visible to the user only through FSP.102 The PLOPs themselves are described on the FCLTU page.

Production status BIND START TRANSFER-DATA Others halted rejected, 'out of service' rejected, 'out of service' rejected, 'unable to process' no effect configured accepted accepted accepted accepted operational accepted accepted accepted accepted interrupted accepted rejected, 'unable to comply' rejected, 'unable to process', once this instance has been notified accepted

Source: table C-2.103 INVOKE-DIRECTIVE and THROW-EVENT are accepted in any production status. If the resources are missing, the failure shows up in the notification.102

Aggregation across complexes. Each FG combines its own status with the status of the FG below it, and the worse one wins. Halted beats interrupted, interrupted beats configured, and configured beats operational. Only "operational and operational" gives 'operational'. The TC VC Data Insertion result carries the operational sub-states.104

docs.title: Provider state machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    state "1 unbound" as S1
    state "2 ready" as S2
    state "3 active" as S3
    [*] --> S1
    S1 --> S2: FSP-BIND accepted<br/>(notify 'production operational' later)
    S2 --> S3: FSP-START accepted
    S3 --> S2: FSP-STOP accepted<br/>(clear queues, unblock)
    S2 --> S1: FSP-UNBIND
    S2 --> S1: PEER-ABORT / protocol abort /<br/>end of provision period
    S3 --> S1: PEER-ABORT / protocol abort /<br/>end of provision period
    S3 --> S1: UNBIND or BIND in 'active'<br/>→ peer abort 'protocol error'

Diagram based on figure 2-4 and table 4-1.15105

Table 4-1 is normative. The behaviour of an instance depends on its state and on four Boolean flags, all initially false: "AD blocked", "notify production operational", "notify production interrupted" and "service instance blocked".105106 Some rules worth knowing:

  • In 'ready', a TRANSFER-DATA, STOP or INVOKE-DIRECTIVE is a protocol error, and the provider aborts. In 'unbound', all incoming PDUs except BIND are ignored.105
  • When production is interrupted, the provider notifies 'production interrupted' and blocks only those active instances with packets in process. For any other instance, it sets "notify production interrupted" and sends the notification (and blocks) when that instance's next packet is about to start processing.105106
  • A START rejected for 'out of service' or 'unable to comply' sets the flag, so that the user gets 'production operational' once production recovers.62
  • Incoming events are queued first-in first-out and never lost. A BIND for an instance that is already bound gets 'already bound' and does not disturb the existing association.107
  • If the invoker of a confirmed operation gets no return within return-timeout-period, it aborts with 'return timeout'. A return whose invoke-ID matches no pending invocation causes an abort with 'unsolicited invoke-ID'. A PDU that cannot be decoded causes 'encoding error'.108105

docs.title: A typical session
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant UM as SLE Utilization Mgmt
    participant CM as SLE Complex Mgmt
    participant U as FSP user (MUE)
    participant P as FSP provider
    participant SC as Spacecraft
    UM->>CM: agree service package (instance, times, VC, MAPs, APIDs)
    CM->>P: create service instance (state 1 'unbound')
    U->>P: FSP-BIND
    P-->>U: +BIND return (state 2 'ready')
    P->>SC: uplink sweep / acquisition (production 'configured' → 'operational')
    P-->>U: FSP-ASYNC-NOTIFY 'production operational' (sub-state BD)
    U->>P: FSP-SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT periodically
    U->>P: FSP-START (first-packet-identification n)
    P-->>U: +START return (state 3 'active')
    U->>P: FSP-INVOKE-DIRECTIVE Initiate AD Service (with Unlock)
    P->>SC: BC frame (Unlock)
    SC-->>P: CLCW (via return link)
    P-->>U: ASYNC-NOTIFY 'positive confirm response to directive'
    P-->>U: ASYNC-NOTIFY 'transmission mode capability change' (AD and BD)
    U->>P: FSP-TRANSFER-DATA id n (AD, MAP m)
    P-->>U: +return (expects n+1, buffer left)
    P->>SC: TC frame(s) in CLTU(s)
    P-->>U: ASYNC-NOTIFY 'packet radiated' (id n, frame sequence number)
    SC-->>P: CLCW acknowledges
    P-->>U: ASYNC-NOTIFY 'packet acknowledged' (id n)
    P-->>U: ASYNC-NOTIFY 'buffer empty'
    U->>P: FSP-STOP
    U->>P: FSP-UNBIND (end)

Diagram based on the operational scenario of 2.7, the directive and notification clauses, and the COP-1 Initiate directives.109207190

Service management creates the instance some time before its start. The provision period usually starts a little before the space link session, so that the user can bind in time.109 At the end of the session, the user uses the notifications or status reports to check that every packet was radiated or acknowledged. It then stops, and either starts again with another batch or unbinds.109

docs.title: Security
docs.text: FSP provides authentication (three levels) and access control. Everything else is left to the communications service or to the mission. It specifies no confidentiality, no denial-of-service protection and no auditing.110 For integrity it has the monotonically increasing packet-identification, which makes it harder to inject extra packets, and the strict operation sequence of the state table. Neither prevents a third party from replacing the data of a PDU in transit. Protection against that has to come from above (for example encrypted packets), from below (the network), or from bilateral additions.110 The standard states that the consequences of not applying security can include losing the ability to command the spacecraft, and losing the spacecraft.110 This page describes the protections only. See also security in CCSDS space links.

docs.title: The FSP API (CCSDS 916.3-M-2)
docs.text:
The SLE API core (914.0-M) defines a C++ API for SLE transfer services. The FSP Recommended Practice adds what FSP needs: FSP-specific behaviour of the components, the interfaces, and their visible behaviour. Issue 2 is from September 2015 and issue 1 from October 2008. Issue 2 updated the text to the then-current service specification and split provisions by generation.111112 It supports two generations of FSP:113

Generation BIND version-number Service specification referenced G2 1 912.3-B-1-S (historical) G3 4 912.3-B-2 (July 2010)

Version mismatch with the service book in this library

The API references FSP issue 2 (912.3-B-2), whose BIND version is 4.114113 The service book in this library is issue 3, which defines version 5.14 Whether an API issue covers version 5 is not stated in the available sources. Generation 1 is not valid for FSP, because FSP was first issued as part of generation 2.113

A comparison of the two parameter lists shows the same gap. The API's FSP_ParameterName enumeration lacks codes 202, 203, 300, 301, 303 and 304, which the 2016 FSP ASN.1 defines.1158

Inference

The missing codes (clcwGlobalVcId, clcwPhysicalChannel, copCntrFramesRepetition, minReportingCycle, sequCntrFramesRepetition, throwEventOperation) are probably additions of issue 3, so a 2015 API implementation could not report them. The issue 2 book is not in the library to confirm this.

docs.title: Components and interfaces
docs.text:
The package FSP Service Instances adds two service-instance classes. FSP SI User adds nothing to the base user class. FSP SI Provider exports three interfaces. The core's conceptual I<SRV>_SIAdmin is split in two because FSP has so many parameters.116

Interface Used by the application to Contents IFSP_SIAdmin configure the instance before ConfigCompleted() apid-list, [G3:] bit-lock-required, blocking-timeout-period, blocking-usage, directive-invocation-enabled, map-list, maximum-frame-length, maximum-packet-length, [G3:] rf-available-required, segment-header, vc-multiplexing-control, vc-multiplexing-scheme, virtual-channel (all may be changed later); plus maximum packet buffer size, initial production status and, for an instance not enabled for directives, the initial directive-invocation-online (these three are fixed after configuration) IFSP_FOPMonitor initialise and keep updated the FOP parameters fop-sliding-window, timeout-type, timer-initial, transmission-limit, transmitter-frame-sequence-number, fop-state, and the MAP multiplexing scheme and control (because a directive can change MAP control) IFSP_SIUpdate report production events for the whole lifetime of the instance, bound or not methods below

Sources: 2.2.3, tables 2-2 and 2-3, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3.116117118119

IFSP_SIUpdate method Event Notification the API can send PacketStarted() Processing of a packet started packet processing started PacketRadiated() Radiation completed packet radiated PacketAcknowledged() All segments acknowledged by CLCW packet acknowledged BufferEmpty() Packet buffer empty buffer empty PacketNotStarted() Could not start: latest time expired, production interrupted, or mode unavailable (FSP_Failure expired 0, interrupted 1, mode mismatch 2) sldu expired / production interrupted / transmission mode mismatch ProductionStatusChange() Production status changed production operational / interrupted / halted / transmission mode capability change / mismatch VCAborted() 'Abort VC' executed VC aborted NoDirectiveCapability() Directive-capable instance unbound no invoke directive capability on this VC DirectiveCapabilityOnline() Directive-capable instance bound invoke directive capability established DirectiveCompleted() Directive finished positive / negative confirm response EventProcCompleted() Thrown event finished (FSP_EventResult 0, 1, 2) action list completed / not completed / condition false

Sources: table 2-1 and the A2 type definitions.120115

The provider-side service instance answers GET-PARAMETER by itself, generates the STATUS-REPORT invocations by itself (the application never creates that operation object), and can send the notifications on the application's behalf.121122 It also keeps the status counters. For example, packet-buffer-available is reset to the maximum after STOP, 'buffer empty', PEER-ABORT and protocol abort. expected-sldu-identification is set from the first-packet-identification of a START that the application confirms positively, and then from the packet-identification of each TRANSFER-DATA return.123124 The initial values after configuration are zero or null for all counters and identifiers, 'invalid' for packet status, and the configured values for production status, buffer size and directive-invocation-online.125

docs.title: What the API does not check, and why
docs.text:
The API deliberately leaves several checks to the application. Production status can change between the moment the service element looks at a PDU and the moment the application sees it. So the API need not check production status for BIND and START, the 'blocked' and 'AD blocked' states, time windows against the current time, or the production period. The API treats packets as opaque, so it does not check APID, packet version or packet type either.126 For TRANSFER-DATA, THROW-EVENT and INVOKE-DIRECTIVE, it may pass an invocation that failed its own checks to the application with the diagnostic already set. The application then fills in the next expected identifier (and, for TRANSFER-DATA, the free buffer space) before the return goes out. This departs from the core API's handling of confirmed operations. Applications that want substitutable API products must expect it.127128

The checks the service element does make on TRANSFER-DATA, in its own order, are: time range consistent, window overlaps the provision period, MAP valid for the Segment Header setting, mode matches the permitted mode, no acknowledgement request for expedited packets, and packet not too long.129 As a result, the documented order of diagnostics is split.130

Set by the API service element Set by the application (standard order kept) duplicate invoke id; inconsistent time range; invalid time; invalid MAP; invalid notification request; packet too long unable to process; unable to store; out of sequence; duplicate packet identification; invalid time; conflicting production time intervals; late sldu; invalid delay time; invalid transmission mode; unsupported packet version; incorrect packet type; invalid packet apid; other reason

The API's C++ enumerations mirror the ASN.1. Examples are FSP_Directive (fspDV_initiateADwithoutCLCW = 0 to fspDV_modifyMapMuxControl = 12), FSP_NotificationType (0 to 17, with fspNT_invokeDirectiveCapabilityOnThisVC = 17), FSP_ProductionStatus (0 to 5) and FSP_FopAlert (0 to 7). The annex says every enumeration has an invalid value, and most define it as −1, but FSP_Failure and FSP_EventResult are printed without one.115 The operation objects are IFSP_Start, IFSP_TransferData, IFSP_AsyncNotify, IFSP_StatusReport, IFSP_GetParameter, IFSP_ThrowEvent and IFSP_InvokeDirective. BIND, UNBIND, PEER-ABORT, STOP and SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT use the core objects.131132 See ISP1 and the SLE API for the core components.

docs.title: FSP in ESA's ground segment and the Solar Orbiter MIB
docs.text:
The public Solar Orbiter MIB shows that the ESOC ground interface knows about FSP but that the mission's TC links are opened as FCLTU. The NIS throw-event command parameter ENISTE03 "SLE Service Type" is calibrated by the textual calibration CNISX207TC. It lists RAF (1), RCF (2), ROCF (3), FCLTU (4) and FSP (5). Yet both TC-link commands, EGENRTCO "GENERIC OPEN TC LINK" and EGENRTCC, fix it to FCLTU. The TM-link commands fix it to RCF. The 2020-04-16 release has the same values.133134 The NIS throw events are described on NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface.

The MIB's "Releaser G/S response" telemetry parameter NYG02202 "GS Packet Type" (in SPID 66850) has textual calibration CYGT2202TM. Beside CLTU, COP-1 directive and throw-event values, it defines FSPPkt (20), FSPPkt_Resp (21), FSPdirective (22) and FSPdir_Resp (23).133

Inference

The GS packet types suggest that the NCTRS/NIS ground interface has message types for forwarding packets and COP-1 directives to an FSP provider. The two Solar Orbiter TC-link commands use FCLTU, so on this mission frames and COP-1 appear to be produced on the ground side of the SLE interface and FSP appears unused. The NIS interface document that would confirm this is not public.

The MIB also shows a real SLE service instance identifier, split across the elements of EGENRTCO. The values sagr=144.spack=, NN11-PERM.fsl-f and g=1.cltu=cltu01 join up as sagr=144.spack=NN11-PERM.fsl-fg=1.cltu=cltu01.133 That is exactly the attribute syntax that the FSP ASN.1 defines. It names the service agreement (sagr), the service package (spack), the forward functional group (fsl-fg) and the service (cltu plus an instance number), separated by dots. An FSP instance would end in fsp=fsp<n>.18 The meaning of agreements and packages is on service management.

SQL used 

-- SLE service type enumeration of the NIS throw-event parameter (2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16)
SELECT PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALTXT, PAS_ALVAL FROM pas
 WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CNISX205TC','CNISX207TC') ORDER BY PAS_NUMBR, CAST(PAS_ALVAL AS INT);
-- -> CNISX207TC: RAF 1, RCF 2, ROCF 3, FCLTU 4, FSP 5

-- Which commands fix the SLE service type, and to what
SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_VALUE FROM cdf WHERE CDF_PNAME = 'ENISTE03' ORDER BY CDF_CNAME;
-- -> EGENRTCC FCLTU, EGENRTCO FCLTU, EGENRTMC RCF, EGENRTMO RCF (same in 2020)

-- Service instance identifier pieces of the TC link opening command
SELECT CDF_ELTYPE, CDF_ELLEN, CDF_BIT, CDF_PNAME, CDF_VALUE FROM cdf
 WHERE CDF_CNAME = 'EGENRTCO' ORDER BY CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);

-- GS packet types of the releaser ground-station response
SELECT TXP_FROM, TXP_ALTXT FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CYGT2202TM' ORDER BY CAST(TXP_FROM AS INT);
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR FROM pcf WHERE PCF_CURTX = 'CYGT2202TM';
Tables: ccf, cdf, cpc, pas, pcf, txp.

The extensible service management concept uses a telecommand mission as an example. Its service agreement allows each SLS service package either up to five FSP instances or one FCLTU instance, never both in one package, together with RAF, RCF, ROCF, tracking data and monitored data. That mirrors the FSP-or-FCLTU choice above.135

docs.title: Notes on the specification text
docs.text:
Some inconsistencies appear in the library copy of 912.3-B-3. They are recorded here so that implementers can check them against the current CCSDS text:

  • In FspGetParameter, context tag [27] is used for both parBitLockRequired and parClcwGlobalVcId, and tag [28] for both parClcwPhysicalChannel and parRfAvailableRequired.40
  • 3.9.2.12.2 says the acknowledged count is set to zero "if Space Packets have been acknowledged". The parallel clauses read "if no Space Packets…".82
  • One reason for 'unable to process' (3.6.2.18.1 b 2) refers to CLTU-ASYNC-NOTIFY, which is an FCLTU operation.34
  • The text calls the THROW-EVENT diagnostic 'out of sequence'. The ASN.1 names it eventIdentificationOutOfSequence.8739
  • transmission-limit is reported as 1 to 255 by GET-PARAMETER. The 'Set Transmission_Limit' directive accepts 1 to 65,535.4047
  • The text disagrees with itself on when a packet "starts to be processed". The processing-started-notification parameter (3.6.2.12) and the note in 3.7.2.9 place it at the move from a packets queue to a segments queue. The 'packet processing started' notification (3.7.2.3 a), the 'production started' packet status (3.7.2.11 c) and the note in 3.9.2.3.1 place it at the move from the requests queue to a packets queue.28717082
  • maximum-packet-length is described as the maximum "Packet Data Length" (table 3-11 and diagnostic 'packet too long'). Its ASN.1 range, 7 to 65,542 octets, is that of a whole Space Packet, while the data parameter (SpaceLinkDataUnit) stops at 65,536 octets.463440837

The API book has its own slips:

  • The header of A3.7 (Invoke Directive) names the file IFSP_ThrowEvent.H.131
  • 3.1.5.1.1 d) has the service element check the transmission mode against the permitted mode. Yet 3.4.2 lists 'invalid transmission mode' among the diagnostics set by the application, not by the service element.129130
  • 1.1 calls the API core specification "reference [5]", but [5] in 1.7 is the C++ language standard and the core (914.0-M-2) is [4].111114
  • It dates the generation 2 book, 912.3-B-1, to December 2004. The FSP book's document control gives November 2004.1144
