docs.text:
TM[3,25] and TM[3,26] contain the structure ID (the figure gives it as unsigned integer) followed by a "deduced" sequence of parameter values: their number, order and types follow from the structure definition.36

docs.title: 7. PUS-A: the housekeeping and diagnostic data reporting service
docs.text: PUS-A's service 3 has two independent subservices (housekeeping, periodic and filtered, and diagnostic) and is designed around the needs of the time: report content and frequency must be changeable in flight because initial designs turn out suboptimal, sensors age and failures happen.5368 Its minimum housekeeping implementation is the periodic reporting of predefined packets.68

docs.title: 7.1 Requests and reports
docs.text:
Subtype PUS-A name Data (in order) (3,1), (3,2) Define New Housekeeping / Diagnostic Parameter Report SID; collection interval (optional); NPAR1; NPAR1 × parameter#; NFA; NFA × [NREP; NPAR2; NPAR2 × parameter#] (3,3), (3,4) Clear Housekeeping / Diagnostic Parameter Report Definitions NSID (optional); NSID × SID (3,5) to (3,8) Enable / Disable Housekeeping / Diagnostic Parameter Report Generation NSID (optional); NSID × SID (3,9), (3,11) Report Housekeeping / Diagnostic Parameter Report Definitions NSID (optional); NSID × SID (3,10), (3,12) ... Report Definitions Report NSID (optional); NSID × [SID; collection interval (optional); NPAR1; parameters; NFA; arrays] (3,13), (3,14) Report ... Parameter Sampling-Time Offsets SID (3,15), (3,16) ... Sampling-Time Offset Report SID; one relative time per parameter (3,17), (3,18) Select Periodic ... Generation Mode SID (3,19), (3,20) Select Filtered ... Generation Mode SID; timeout (optional); N (optional); N × [parameter#; threshold type (optional); threshold (optional)] (3,21), (3,22) Report Unfiltered ... Parameters SID (3,23), (3,24) Unfiltered ... Parameters Report SID; N; N × [parameter#; threshold type; threshold] (3,25), (3,26) Housekeeping / Diagnostic Parameter Report SID; mode (optional); parameters

5960616263646566

PUS-A details worth knowing:

  • The parameter# is an on-board number used for optimisation, with a one-to-one correspondence to the ground's parameter ID.59 SCOS-2000 stores it as PCF_PID (section 9.3).
  • The collection interval is expressed in units of the mission constant <DIAG_MIN_INTERV>, the minimum sampling interval of diagnostic mode (typically 10 to 30 ms), and is omitted when the service uses a default.5969
  • NFA counts the fixed-length arrays, NREP the samples per parameter in an array, and NPAR2 the parameters of the array.59 This is the PUS-A form of the super commutated set.
  • A new definition starts with its "Report Generation Flag" disabled and in periodic mode.59
  • Requests that can only handle one SID at a time omit NSID.6061
  • Forwarding of reports to the ground is not part of service 3 but of the packet forwarding control service (PUS-C ST[14]).55

docs.title: 7.2 Filtered mode
docs.text: PUS-A's second generation mode, the filtered mode, produces a report at the end of a collection interval only if at least one unfiltered parameter changed by more than its threshold since the previous interval; for parameters sampled several times, any change of a sample counts.55 The threshold of each parameter is either a percentage (threshold type 0) or an absolute delta (type 1), and a timeout, a multiple of the collection interval, forces a one-shot report when nothing has changed for too long.6455 The optional mode field of (3,25) and (3,26) tells the ground why the report exists: 0 periodic, 1 filtered and a threshold was exceeded, 2 filtered but generated by the timeout.66 Filtered mode was intended mainly for status parameters, so that a report is only sent when something changes, with noisy analogue values filtered out of the comparison.6855 Selecting a mode that is already active generates an error report.64

docs.title: 7.3 Sampling-time offsets
docs.text: PUS-A requires that absolute and relative sampling times of housekeeping parameters can be determined on the ground to accuracies set by mission constants, and allows three methods: knowledge of the on-board sampling mechanism, explicit time-stamping of parameters, or offsets measured on board and reported with (3,15)/(3,16). In the third case the report is also generated automatically when a new SID is defined, before its first report, and only the first sample of each array is given an offset.5663 The static time offsets of SCOS-2000 (section 9.1) suit the first method, or the third once the measured offsets have been entered in the database; this pairing is this wiki's reading, not a statement of either source.7056

The general comparison of the two issues is on PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: 8. The Rev.1 draft: one subservice, six categories
docs.text:
The December 2024 draft for public review restructures the service. It defines only two subservice types, housekeeping reporting and parameter functional reporting configuration; the diagnostic subservice disappears.48 Instead, every housekeeping structure has one of six categories, statically deduced from its structure identifier, and the category selects the message type of the report: TM[3,25] for category 1, TM[3,26] for category 2 and the new TM[3,50] to TM[3,53] for categories 3 to 6.5051 The draft's example of a tailoring is category 1 for nominal reports, 2 for diagnostic reports, 3 for essential reports used at low bit rate and 4 for troubleshooting reports stored only on board.50 The diagnostic requests disappear from the interface clause, and the housekeeping periodic generation properties report is printed as TM[3,34] instead of TM[3,35], consistently in clause 6.3.3.11, in clause 8.3.2.11 and in Annex C, so it is not a single misprint; the reason is not stated in the available sources.52

Comparison with Solar Orbiter

Solar Orbiter separates kinds of housekeeping with the packet category field of its APIDs (section 9.4) rather than with the message type.89 The parallel with the Rev.1 categories is this wiki's comparison; neither document draws it.

docs.title: 9. SCOS-2000 and the Solar Orbiter MIB
9.1 What SCOS-2000 does (and does not do) with service 3
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 import ICD says that there is no service-specific processing of service 3 packets, and lists the consequences:70

  • every TM packet must be recognised from the MIB, so a new housekeeping or diagnostic packet created with service 3 commands must first be added to the database; the efficient approach, typical of ESA missions, is to define the packet in the database first and generate the service 3 commands from it, in the mission's database manager rather than in the SCOS-2000 kernel;
  • the time stamp of each parameter sample is the packet time plus a time offset statically defined in the database, so the offsets must be known in advance and identical for every instance of the packet;
  • the collection interval of periodic packets is also static in the database and is not updated when a service 3 command changes it on board.

docs.title: 9.2 How a housekeeping packet is recognised
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 telemetry packetiser identifies a packet from its APID, type and subtype and, for some type/subtype combinations, up to two additional identification fields defined in pic by byte offset and bit width. The full key (type, subtype, APID, PI1, PI2) is then looked up in pid to find the SCOS-2000 packet ID (SPID) and, for variable packets, the structure definition (TPSD).7173 For housekeeping this first additional field is naturally the SID.

flowchart LR
  P["TM packet"] --> H["APID, type, subtype<br/>(fixed positions)"]
  H --> C{"pic entry for<br/>type/subtype?"}
  C -- "yes (3,25), (3,26)" --> X["PI1 = SID<br/>offset 16, 8 bits"]
  C -- no --> Z["PI1 = PI2 = 0"]
  X --> K["pid lookup:<br/>type, subtype, APID, PI1, PI2"]
  Z --> K
  K --> S["SPID (fixed) via plf<br/>or TPSD (variable) via vpd"]
  S --> V["Parameter samples<br/>time = packet time + PLF_TIME"]
  V --> M["Calibration, limits,<br/>displays (pcf and related)"]

The offsets in the diagram are those of the Solar Orbiter MIB; the flow is the ICD's description of the packetiser.717392

In plf, each parameter of a fixed packet has a byte offset PLF_OFFBY counted from the start of the TM source packet, a bit offset PLF_OFFBI, and four fields for super commutation and timing: PLF_NBOCC (number of occurrences, 1 for a simply commutated parameter), PLF_LGOCC (bits between consecutive occurrences), PLF_TIME (offset of the first occurrence from the packet time, in ms) and PLF_TDOCC (ms between occurrences). A super commutated parameter is a single record.74 Overlapping records and gaps are allowed.74 Variable packets such as the structure reports TM(3,10) and TM(3,12) are described in vpd instead, and PID_INTER gives the expected interval of periodic packets, after which their samples expire.7572

docs.title: 9.3 How a definition command is built
docs.text: A create command contains parameter identifiers. SCOS-2000 supports a special command parameter type, "Parameter ID" (CPC_CATEG = P, PTC 3), that accepts the name of a monitoring parameter and encodes its on-board identifier PCF_PID, which corresponds one to one to the PUS parameter#.767778 This is how a generic "Define New Housekeeping Parameter Report" can be filled from the database.

docs.title: 9.4 Solar Orbiter's tailoring
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter's TM/TC ICD uses PUS-A service 3 with private subtypes. It describes housekeeping for nominal operations, configurable per mission phase, and diagnostic reports for error investigation, with SIDs unique within a process ID (the note under TC(3,1) adds: unique across housekeeping and diagnostic definitions of one process ID).7981 In the mission's service list only TM(3,25) is marked "M" (minimum capability for every user); all other service 3 subtypes are optional ("O").87 For the central software, the predefined definitions can be modified, deleted or extended by the ground, but the defaults are reloaded after a software reset.80

Subtype Solar Orbiter name Notes TC(3,1) Define New HK Parameter Report SID (1 octet), collection interval (2 octets), NPAR (1 octet), parameter IDs (4 octets); no arrays TC(3,2) Define New diagnostic Parameter Report as (3,1) plus NFA (0 or 1), NREP, NPAR2 (1 octet each) and parameter IDs TC(3,3), (3,4) Clear HK / Diag Parameter Report Definition one SID; only after disabling TC(3,5) to (3,8) Enable / Disable HK / Diag Parameter Report Generation one SID TC(3,9), TM(3,10), TC(3,11), TM(3,12) Report definitions layouts as (3,1) and (3,2) TM(3,25), TM(3,26) HK / Diag Parameter Report SID (1 octet) then parameters; SSMM reports put the SSMM mode in the first octet after the SID TC(3,128), TM(3,134) HK/Diag definitions in summary form per SID: status (0 disabled, 1 enabled) and collection interval TC(3,129) Update HK Report Generation Period SSMM only; collection interval in 8 Hz cycles, minimum 1 s, default 16 s TC(3,130), (3,131) Define HK / Diagnostic Report Collection Interval diagnostic: only while disabled, interval divisible by NREP TC(3,136) Request HK/Diagnostic Parameter Report one-shot report TC(3,138) Append Parameters to a HK Parameter Report SID, NPAR, parameter IDs TC(3,139) Request Snapshot HK Parameter Anomaly Report EID (2 octets), SID: one TM(5,x) event carrying the HK packet's parameters

818283848586

The collection interval is counted in cycles of the application's scheduling: the ICD's example is an application scheduled at 10 Hz that needs a value of 10 for one report per second.81 The SID ranges of Annex 10 are 1-127 for TM(3,25) (with sub-ranges for status, mode, equipment, specific requests, ESOC and ancillary data) and 128-255 for TM(3,26), the last block (232-255) being "diagnostic to packet store only".88 The packet category in the low 4 bits of the APID separates the kinds of report: 2 for high-priority telemetry (HPTM) housekeeping of the platform, 4 for routine housekeeping, 5 for "functional cyclic" housekeeping produced on ground request, and 8 for diagnostics.89

Inference

By function, TC(3,130)/(3,131) correspond to PUS-C TC[3,31]/[3,32], TC(3,136) to TC[3,27]/[3,28], TC(3,138) to TC[3,29], and TC(3,128)/TM(3,134) to TC[3,33]/TM[3,35] combined for both kinds of report. Solar Orbiter thus implemented as private subtypes several capabilities that PUS-C later standardised. This mapping is this wiki's comparison; the ICD does not state it.

docs.title: 9.5 The numbers in the MIB
docs.text:
The September 2025 release defines 397 service 3 packets and 345 service 3 commands:91

Packet Count APIDs Packet category Structure TM(3,25) 288 62 2 (68), 4 (169), 5 (51) fixed, plf TM(3,26) 89 14 8 (89) fixed, plf TM(3,10) 7 7 3 variable, vpd TM(3,12) 6 6 3 variable, vpd TM(3,134) 7 7 3 variable, vpd

91

The pic table identifies TM(3,25) and TM(3,26) by a first additional field at byte offset 16, 8 bits wide, for all APIDs: the 1-octet SID right after the 16 octets of headers. The three definition and summary reports have no additional identification.92 Every one of the 377 HK and diagnostic packets starts its plf layout at byte 16, i.e. the SID is itself decoded as a parameter (for the platform software, NCD030A1 "OBCHP_HK SID" and NCD030C1 "OBCHP_DIAG SID", PTC 3, PFC 4).93 No process ID uses the same SID for two report packets, which is consistent with the ICD rule that SIDs are unique per process ID across both kinds.9181 PID_INTER is empty for all 11,150 packets of the release, so no packet has an expiry interval.91

plf statistic TM(3,25) TM(3,26) packets / records 288 / 65,567 89 / 17,578 distinct parameters 31,581 17,437 super commutated records (PLF_NBOCC > 1) 0 99 in 10 packets (up to 257 occurrences) records with a non-zero PLF_TIME 0 91

93

The ICD's layouts predict this: its TC(3,1) has no array fields, and it expects diagnostic reports to contain "a predominance of fixed-length arrays". In the data, super commutation and sample timing appear only in diagnostic packets.938180

The central software's SID allocation in the MIB is denser than Annex 10. For the six CSW applications (process IDs 10 to 14 and 16) the routine housekeeping SIDs on category 4 run from 77 to 102, the functional cyclic ones on category 5 from 153 to 192 and the HPTM ones on category 2 from 1 to 21, while the diagnostics use 193 to 255.91 The CSW category 5 housekeeping SIDs thus lie in the range that Annex 10 gives to TM(3,26).88 For the DMS application the 15 HPTM packets on APID 162 (SIDs 1 to 16, without 15) have the same descriptions as the routine packets with SIDs 77 to 92 on APID 164, and 14 of the 15 pairs have identical plf layouts; the exception is "DMS Overview Fast", whose HPTM version (SID 11, SPID 19539) has two more records (NCDX0001 and NCDX0002 at bytes 17 and 25) than its routine version (SID 87, SPID 19559).94

Inference

The CSW appears to generate nearly the same report contents under two SIDs, one routed as high-priority telemetry and one as routine housekeeping, with SID = HPTM SID + 76. The MIB shows the duplication; the reason (for example HPTM availability when the software is degraded) is not stated in the available sources.

The April 2020 release had 269 TM(3,25), 86 TM(3,26) and 331 service 3 commands; the 2025 release adds 19, 3 and 14 respectively. The SWA instrument database defines 12 TM(3,25) and 9 TM(3,26) packets with the same pic convention.99100

Command Commands in 2025 Of which fully predefined TC(3,1) define HK 82 (on 7 APIDs) 75 TC(3,2) define diagnostic 77 71 TC(3,138) append 40 34 TC(3,5), TC(3,6) enable, disable HK 24 each (24 APIDs) - TC(3,129) update HK period 19 (13 APIDs, used by several instruments as well as the SSMM) - TC(3,130) define HK interval 14 - others (3,3), (3,4), (3,7), (3,8), (3,9), (3,11), (3,128), (3,131), (3,136), (3,139) 6 to 8 each -

95

"Fully predefined" means that no element in cdf is editable: every element is a fixed area or a fixed (non-editable) parameter, so the command creates one specific report (for TC(3,1) 72 commands use fixed areas only and 3 use fixed parameters; for TC(3,2) 66 and 5); the others are generic commands with editable parameters. This is the ICD's recommended practice in action: the packet exists in the database and the command that creates it on board is generated alongside.9570

docs.title: 9.6 Worked example 1: from TC(3,1) to TM(3,25)
docs.text:
The command ZCA2Z05B "Define HK: AOCS Dynamics FAST" is a TC(3,1) to APID 188 (process ID 11, AOCS, category 12). Its application data is entirely made of fixed areas, so its bytes are real data from the MIB:96

4D | 00 30 | 08 | 0B201C1C 0B201950 0B201C1B 0B20143B 0B201459 0B201477 0B201495 0B201C29
SID   CI     NPAR  eight 32-bit on-board parameter IDs (PCF_PID)

Each parameter ID matches exactly one pcf entry through PCF_PID, and the resulting packet is TM(3,25) SID 77 on APID 180 (process ID 11, category 4), SPID 29530 "AOCS Dynamics FAST":96

Order Parameter ID (hex) Parameter Type (PTC/PFC) Byte offset in SPID 29530 - - NCD030A1 OBCHP_HK SID ¾ 16 1 0B201C1C NCAG6VN0 GyrStarOutputEstRateEst 7/24 17 2 0B201950 NCAG4NP0 ErrGenErrAngErr 7/24 41 3 0B201C1B NCAG6VL0 GyrStarOutputEstQuat 7/32 65 4 0B20143B NCAT1AG0 RW1_RATE 5/1 97 5 0B201459 NCAT1B10 RW2_RATE 5/1 101 6 0B201477 NCAT1BK0 RW3_RATE 5/1 105 7 0B201495 NCAT1C40 RW4_RATE 5/1 109 8 0B201C29 NCAG6VZ0 WsEstTrqFricEST 7/16 113

96

The offsets follow from the sizes: 16 header octets, the SID, then 24 + 24 + 32 + 4 × 4 + 16 octets, so the last parameter occupies bytes 113 to 128.96 The octet strings (PTC 7) are additionally decoded by overlapping plf records into their components: for example NCAD6VN1, NCAD6VN2 and NCAD6VN3 (GSE_EST_RATE-X, -Y, -Z, PTC 5/PFC 2, 64-bit reals) at offsets 17, 25 and 33 inside NCAG6VN0.96 This is the ICD's allowance for overlapping records used to show both the raw block and its engineering components.74

The parameter identifiers themselves follow the 32-bit layout that Annex 11 of the Solar Orbiter ICD defines for the central software's data pool: a 1-bit filler (0), the 7-bit process ID, a read/write flag (0 = read and write, 1 = read only) and a 23-bit local ID made of a 3-bit filler 0b010, an 8-bit unit ID and a 12-bit counter (for CSW-generated parameters its last 4 bits give the functional type of the parameter).90 Decoded this way, 0x0B201C1C is filler 0, process ID 11 (AOCS), read/write flag 0, filler 0b010, unit ID 1 and counter 0xC1C; the process ID matches the AOCS APIDs 180 and 188 of the example.9096

Inference

The cdf description of the collection interval fixed area is "Interval=6000 ms (cycl)" for these 48 cycles, and "Interval=2000 ms (cycl)" for the 16 cycles of the next example; both imply a 125 ms (8 Hz) AOCS application cycle.9697 The ICD does not state the AOCS cycle; it only says that the interval counts cycles of the application's scheduling.81

docs.title: 9.7 Worked example 2: a super commutated diagnostic report
docs.text:
ZCA2Z06V "Define Diag: AOCS OCM 8Hz Diag" is a TC(3,2) whose fixed areas, with the descriptions stored in cdf, are: SID 0xE5 (229), collection interval 0x0010 described as "Interval=2000 ms (cycl)", NPAR1 = 1 (OCMT_AUTO_TRANS_ENABLED), one fixed length array (NFA = 1), "NoOfSamples=16" (NREP = 16) and NPAR2 = 16 parameters (accelerometer measurement, estimated quaternion and rate, nine durations AOCS_NC_FCV_1_DUR to AOCS_NC_FCV_9_DUR and four wheel rates).97 Sixteen cycles for 2,000 ms means a 125 ms cycle, i.e. 8 Hz, as the name says.

The matching TM(3,26) is SPID 29540 on APID 184 (process ID 11, category 8). Its plf has the SID at byte 16, the simply commutated flag at byte 17, and from byte 18 the 16-parameter record repeated 16 times: PLF_NBOCC = 16, PLF_LGOCC = 744 bits (93 octets per record), PLF_TDOCC = 125 ms and PLF_TIME = -1,875 ms.97

Sample 1 2 3 ... 15 16 Byte offset of the record 18 111 204 ... 1,320 1,413 Time relative to packet time -1,875 ms -1,750 ms -1,625 ms ... -125 ms 0 ms

The table is computed from the four plf fields. The 16 samples are spaced by the collection interval divided by the repetition number (2,000 / 16 = 125 ms), exactly the PUS-C sub-period rule, and the last sample carries the packet time.976 Because SCOS-2000 applies these offsets statically, the on-board sampling must always follow this pattern.70

docs.title: 9.8 The structure reports as variable packets
docs.text:
The definition reports are decoded as variable packets. For the DMS application, TM(3,10) (TPSD 14164) is SID (8 bits), collection interval (16 bits), a counter of parameters and then one 32-bit parameter ID per entry; TM(3,12) (TPSD 14163) adds the array counter, the number of samples, the number of super commutated parameters and their IDs; TM(3,134) (TPSD 14165) is a counter of SIDs followed by SID, report generation status (8 bits) and collection interval for each.98 These are the ICD layouts of section 9.4 expressed as vpd repeat groups.9882

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL)
SELECT PID_STYPE, COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT PID_APID), SUM(PID_TPSD != '-1')
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PID_STYPE, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) % 16 AS cat, COUNT(*) FROM pid
 WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' AND PID_STYPE IN ('25','26') GROUP BY 1, 2;

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pid WHERE PID_INTER IS NOT NULL AND PID_INTER != '';
-- SID ranges per APID, and uniqueness of SIDs per process ID

  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' AND PID_STYPE IN ('25','26') GROUP BY 1, 2;

 WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' AND PID_STYPE IN ('25','26') GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING n > 1;  -- empty
-- plf statistics
SELECT d.PID_STYPE, COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT p.PLF_SPID), SUM(CAST(p.PLF_NBOCC AS INT) > 1),
       MAX(CAST(p.PLF_NBOCC AS INT)), SUM(CAST(p.PLF_TIME AS INT) != 0), COUNT(DISTINCT p.PLF_NAME)
  FROM plf p JOIN pid d ON d.PID_SPID = p.PLF_SPID
 WHERE d.PID_TYPE = '3' AND d.PID_STYPE IN ('25','26') GROUP BY 1;
-- worked examples
SELECT * FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('ZCA2Z05B','ZCA2Z06V') ORDER BY CDF_CNAME, CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT PCF_PID, PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC FROM pcf WHERE PCF_PID = '186653724';
SELECT p.*, c.PCF_DESCR FROM plf p JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = p.PLF_NAME
 WHERE p.PLF_SPID IN ('29530','29540') ORDER BY p.PLF_SPID, CAST(p.PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
SELECT * FROM vpd WHERE VPD_TPSD IN ('14163','14164','14165') ORDER BY VPD_TPSD, CAST(VPD_POS AS INT);
-- service 3 commands
SELECT CCF_STYPE, COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT CCF_APID) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '3' GROUP BY 1;
-- "fully predefined" = no editable cdf element
SELECT c.CCF_STYPE, COUNT(*), SUM(NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdf d
       WHERE d.CDF_CNAME = c.CCF_CNAME AND d.CDF_ELTYPE = 'E'))
  FROM ccf c WHERE c.CCF_TYPE = '3' AND c.CCF_STYPE IN ('1','2','138') GROUP BY 1;
-- HPTM versus routine DMS packets (APIDs 162 and 164)
SELECT PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' AND PID_APID IN ('162','164');

docs.title: 10. Design notes
docs.text:
• One packet type, many structures. All housekeeping reports share TM[3,25]; the SID is what makes them different. Ground systems therefore need an identification rule that looks inside the packet, which SCOS-2000 provides with pic, and an on-board design that puts the SID at a fixed position.71
  • Ground and board must agree. Because SCOS-2000 decodes packets only from the database, a service 3 change on board without a matching MIB change produces undecodable telemetry; changing an interval on board does not change the expected interval or the sample time offsets on the ground.70
  • Delete and append need a disabled report. Both are rejected while periodic generation is enabled, so a change to a running report is a disable, change, enable sequence.912 Solar Orbiter applies the same rule to its clear and diagnostic interval commands.8385
  • Diagnostics are temporary by design. PUS-A asks the ground to weigh carefully how much of the downlink diagnostic packets may take; PUS-C makes their enabling and disabling a minimum capability.6947

docs.title: ST[04] Parameter statistics reporting
docs.text:
The parameter statistics reporting service, service type 4 of the Packet Utilization Standard, lets an on-board application process watch a list of on-board parameters and compute, for each of them, the maximum, minimum, mean and (optionally) standard deviation of the values it samples during a time interval. Instead of downlinking every sample, the spacecraft sends a single parameter statistics report TM[4,2] that summarises the interval.1 The standard names the typical use: missions with limited ground coverage, such as low Earth orbiters, can read one report after acquisition of signal and learn how parameters behaved during the previous period of "no contact".134

This page describes the service as defined by ECSS-E-ST-70-41C ("PUS-C", clause 6.4 for the system requirements and clause 8.4 for the packet layouts), compares it with ECSS-E-70-41A ("PUS-A", clause 9), lists the tailoring data required by ECSS-E-ST-70-31C, summarises the changes in the 2024 Rev.1 draft, and explains how ground systems such as SCOS-2000 handle it - including the finding that the real Solar Orbiter MIB contains no service 4 packet at all.

At a glance

Item Value Service type 4, "parameter statistics reporting"17 Subservice types exactly one: the parameter statistics reporting subservice1 Providers per application process at most one2 Message types (PUS-C) 7 requests TC[4,1], [4,3]-[4,8]; 2 reports TM[4,2], TM[4,9]27 Minimum capability TC[4,1], TM[4,2], TC[4,3]27 Always evaluated maximum, minimum, mean; standard deviation by declaration4 Subservice observables none in PUS-C; one in the 2024 draft1649 PUS-A equivalent clause 9, subtypes 1-10 (10 = clear the list)45 Solar Orbiter "Service 4: Not Used"; no type 4 packet or command in the MIB6062

docs.title: 1.1 Why evaluate statistics on board
docs.text: PUS-A presents "statistical data reporting" as a second mechanism, next to housekeeping reporting, for reducing the quantity of engineering data sent to ground: evaluate mean, minimum, maximum and standard deviation on board and report only the results. In its minimum form the parameter set and the evaluated attributes are predefined and evaluation is continuous; optional extensions let the ground change the parameters and the evaluation intervals.34 PUS-A also suggests the service as an alternative to housekeeping reporting during non-coverage when on-board storage capacity is limited.35 PUS-C keeps that rationale - the service is "especially appropriate" for missions with limited ground coverage - and adds that it can reduce the engineering data that is systematically reported.1

docs.title: 1.2 The model
docs.text:
Each parameter statistics definition names one parameter and its sampling interval. The subservice keeps a list of such definitions (the "list of evaluated parameters"), at most one definition per parameter, and the maximum number of definitions it can evaluate at the same time is a declared constant of the subservice.3 For each listed parameter it evaluates all the supported statistic types at any time: maximum, minimum and mean always; standard deviation only if the subservice declares that it supports it.4 A default sampling interval is declared per parameter.5

Evaluation is continuous. What varies is when results are reported and when the accumulators are cleared:

flowchart TB
  S["Every sampling interval<br/>(per parameter)"] --> U["Update accumulators:<br/>number of samples, max + time first attained,<br/>min + time first attained, mean, (std. deviation)"]
  U --> S
  R1["TC[4,1] report the parameter statistics"] --> G["Generate one TM[4,2]<br/>(one notification per parameter<br/>sampled at least once since last reset)"]
  P["End of periodic reporting interval<br/>(if periodic reporting enabled)"] --> G
  G --> D{"Reset?"}
  D -- "periodic report: always" --> Z["Clear accumulators,<br/>restart evaluation"]
  D -- "TC[4,1]: if reset flag set,<br/>or subservice auto-resets" --> Z
  D -- "otherwise" --> S
  R3["TC[4,3] reset the parameter statistics"] --> Z
  Z --> S

Sources for the diagram: the sampling and notification rules of clause 6.4.5.3, the reset rules of clauses 6.4.4, 6.4.5.1-6.4.5.2 and 6.4.6.2h.967811

The PUS-A version of the concept is the same: statistics are evaluated continuously from successive samples, reports are generated on request or periodically, the evaluation is systematically reset when a periodic report is generated and can be reset on request at any time.36 PUS-A gives the operational recipe for covering a non-coverage period: reset the evaluation just before loss of signal (LOS) and request the report shortly after acquisition of signal (AOS).36

Which time is in the packet header?

Because the interval between reports can be long, PUS-A recommends that the time field of the packet header indicates the report generation time, not the beginning of the evaluation interval.36 PUS-C sidesteps the ambiguity by putting both the start time and the end time of the evaluation interval in the report itself.9

docs.title: 1.3 Statistics: what is and is not defined
docs.text: Quantity Defined by PUS-C Notes Number of samples yes, per parameter, in each notification<sup>9</sup> new in PUS-C; PUS-A has no such field<sup>37</sup> Maximum and its time the maximum sampled value and the time it was first attained<sup>9</sup> Minimum and its time the minimum sampled value and the time it was first attained<sup>9</sup> Mean mean of the sampled values during the interval<sup>9</sup> Standard deviation of the sampled values, only if supported<sup>9</sup><sup>4</sup> population or sample formula: not stated in the available sources Value format specific to the parameter identified by the parameter ID (deduced)<sup>19</sup> the format of a mean or standard deviation of an integer parameter is not stated in the available sources

docs.title: 2. Declarations a mission must make
docs.text:
PUS-C leaves most choices to the mission and records them as declarations "when specifying that subservice". The full list for ST[04]:

Declaration Clause Maximum number of parameter statistics definitions evaluated at the same time 6.4.3.1a3 Whether the standard deviation is evaluated 6.4.3.2b4 Default sampling interval of each parameter 6.4.3.3a5 Exactly one of: reset flag carried in TC[4,1], or automatic reset after every TC[4,1] 6.4.5.1a-c7 Whether periodic reporting is supported 6.4.6.1a10 Periodic reporting interval implicitly known (and its value), or carried in TC[4,4] 6.4.6.1b-d10 Whether definitions can be added or updated (TC[4,6]) 6.4.7.1a13 Whether TC[4,6] can set the sampling interval 6.4.7.1b13 Whether the definitions can be reported (TC[4,8]/TM[4,9]) 6.4.7.3a15

Sampling intervals are expressed against the spacecraft's on-board parameter minimum sampling interval: each on-board parameter is associated to exactly one such interval, all parameters accessed by an application process share the same one, and the standard gives the example of a platform at 125 ms and a payload at 500 ms.29 The 2024 draft adds an explicit note to the ST[04] sampling interval clause pointing to that requirement.46

docs.title: 3. Message types and capability sets
docs.text:
PUS-C Annex C lists the ST[04] message types with their applicability constraint. "Minimum" means every subservice provides the capability; "by declaration" means the mission decides; "implied by" means the capability comes automatically with another one; "requires" means it can only be chosen if the other is present.2827

Message type Name Requirement / interface clause Applicability TC[4,1] report the parameter statistics 6.4.5.2 / 8.4.2.1 minimum TM[4,2] parameter statistics report 6.4.5.3 / 8.4.2.2 response to TC[4,1] (also periodic) TC[4,3] reset the parameter statistics 6.4.4 / 8.4.2.3 minimum - support for periodic reporting 6.4.6.1a by declaration TC[4,4] enable the periodic parameter statistics reporting 6.4.6.2 / 8.4.2.4 implied by 6.4.6.1a TC[4,5] disable the periodic parameter statistics reporting 6.4.6.3 / 8.4.2.5 implied by 6.4.6.1a TC[4,6] add or update parameter statistics definitions 6.4.7.1 / 8.4.2.6 by declaration TC[4,7] delete parameter statistics definitions 6.4.7.2 / 8.4.2.7 implied by TC[4,6] TC[4,8] report the parameter statistics definitions 6.4.7.3 / 8.4.2.8 requires TC[4,6] TM[4,9] parameter statistics definition report 6.4.7.3 / 8.4.2.9 response to TC[4,8]

Source: Table C-8.27 Every ST[04] packet has service type 4.17 The notation and the full catalogue across services are on PUS message types.

docs.title: 4. The messages field by field
docs.text: Field types below are the PUS types of clause 7.3: enumerated (PTC 2), unsigned integer (PTC 3), Boolean (PTC 1), absolute time (PTC 9), relative time (PTC 10) and deduced (PTC 11, format deduced from a preceding field).30313233 Their sizes (PFCs) are mission choices, so the byte layouts depend on the mission.

docs.title: 4.1 TC[4,1] report the parameter statistics
docs.text:
Field Type Presence Meaning reset flag Boolean optional Present only if the subservice uses the "explicit reset flag" option; asks for a reset after the report is generated.188

Each request contains exactly one instruction (which itself has no argument) and produces exactly one TM[4,2]. After the report is generated, the statistics are reset if the request asked for it or if the subservice is configured to reset automatically after every request.8 A Boolean value greater than zero means TRUE.30

docs.title: 4.2 TM[4,2] parameter statistics report
docs.text:
Field Type Presence Meaning start time absolute time always Start of the evaluation interval.199 end time absolute time always End of the evaluation interval.199 N unsigned integer always Number of parameter statistic notifications that follow.19 repeated N times: parameter ID enumerated always The sampled parameter.19 number of samples unsigned integer always Samples used to produce the statistics.199 max value deduced always Maximum sampled value.19 max time absolute time always Time the maximum was first attained.199 min value deduced always Minimum sampled value.19 min time absolute time always Time the minimum was first attained.199 mean value deduced always Mean of the sampled values.19 standard deviation value deduced optional Present only if the subservice evaluates the standard deviation.194

The subservice emits one notification for each parameter that has been sampled at least once since the last reset; parameters never sampled are left out.9 The deduced fields take the format of the parameter named by the preceding parameter ID.19

The field order follows Figure 8-54;19 the bit widths in the diagram are an illustrative mission choice (they are the sizes used in the worked example of section 7), not values set by the standard.

docs.title: 4.3 TC[4,3] reset the parameter statistics
docs.text: No application data.20 The subservice stops the evaluation, clears every accumulated result and restarts the evaluation. The reset is independent of report generation.6

docs.title: 4.4 TC[4,4] enable the periodic parameter statistics reporting
docs.text:
Field Type Presence Meaning reporting interval relative time optional Present only if the subservice lets TC[4,4] set the periodic reporting interval.2111

The subservice keeps a periodic parameter statistics reporting status (enabled or disabled).10 TC[4,4] is rejected - with a failed start of execution notification, see ST[01] - if it specifies a reporting interval shorter than the sampling interval of any evaluated parameter.11 Otherwise the status becomes "enabled" and the interval, if given, is stored. While enabled, the subservice generates exactly one TM[4,2] at the end of each reporting interval and systematically resets the statistics each time.11

docs.title: 4.5 TC[4,5] disable the periodic parameter statistics reporting
docs.text: No application data. It sets the status to "disabled".2212 Evaluation itself goes on: in PUS-A terms, periodic reporting and resetting stop "and the parameter statistics evaluation shall continue".39

docs.title: 4.6 TC[4,6] add or update parameter statistics definitions
docs.text:
Field Type Presence Meaning N unsigned integer always Number of instructions.23 repeated N times: parameter ID enumerated always Parameter to add or update.23 sampling interval relative time optional Present only if TC[4,6] may set sampling intervals.2313

Each instruction is checked on its own and rejected (failed start of execution for that instruction) if the parameter is unknown, if its sampling interval is greater than the reporting interval, or if it would add a definition when the maximum is already reached; the valid instructions are executed regardless of faulty ones.13 A new parameter is added and its evaluation starts immediately; an existing one gets the new sampling interval and its evaluation restarts.13

Partial intervals and duplicates

Because evaluation of a newly added parameter starts at once, independently of the reporting interval, the next report (and only that report) covers that parameter over a shorter interval than the others. If one request contains two instructions for the same parameter, the second overrides the first.13

docs.title: 4.7 TC[4,7] delete parameter statistics definitions
docs.text:
Field Type Presence Meaning N unsigned integer always Number of parameter IDs; N = 0 deletes all definitions.24 parameter ID enumerated repeated N times Parameter whose definition is removed.24

An instruction naming a parameter that is not in the list is rejected; valid instructions are executed anyway. If the list is empty after the request, the periodic reporting status is set to "disabled".14

docs.title: 4.8 TC[4,8] report the parameter statistics definitions and TM[4,9]
docs.text:
TC[4,8] has no application data.25 Its response TM[4,9] has the following source data:

Field Type Presence Meaning reporting interval relative time optional Present if the subservice lets TC[4,4] change the interval; set to 0 s when periodic reporting is not enabled.2615 N unsigned integer always Number of definitions.26 parameter ID enumerated repeated N times Parameter.26 sampling interval relative time repeated, optional Present if sampling intervals can be set.2615

docs.title: 4.9 Observables
docs.text: PUS-C defines no observables for this subservice.16 The 2024 draft defines one: the number of parameter statistics definitions currently defined on board.49

docs.title: 5. State model
docs.text:
The only persistent state, besides the accumulators and the list itself, is the periodic reporting status. Its initial value after start-up is not stated in the available sources.

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  state "Periodic reporting DISABLED" as D
  state "Periodic reporting ENABLED" as E
  D --> E: TC[4,4] accepted (interval stored if present)
  E --> D: TC[4,5]
  E --> D: TC[4,7] leaves the list empty
  E --> E: end of reporting interval / TM[4,2] then reset
  E --> E: TC[4,1] / TM[4,2] (reset if requested or automatic)
  D --> D: TC[4,1] / TM[4,2] (reset if requested or automatic)
  D --> D: TC[4,3] / reset
  E --> E: TC[4,3] / reset

Transitions from clauses 6.4.4, 6.4.5.2, 6.4.6.2, 6.4.6.3 and 6.4.7.2i.68111214

docs.title: 6. A typical exchange
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant G as Ground (MCS)
  participant P as On-board AP (ST[04] provider)
  G->>P: TC[4,6] add PARAM_A (120 s), PARAM_B (10 s)
  P-->>G: TM[1,1] / TM[1,7] (if requested by the ack flags)
  G->>P: TC[4,4] reporting interval 600 s
  Note over P: periodic status ENABLED
  loop every 600 s
    P-->>G: TM[4,2] start, end, N=2, statistics
    Note over P: automatic reset
  end
  Note over G,P: LOS ... AOS
  G->>P: TC[4,8]
  P-->>G: TM[4,9] interval 600 s, 2 definitions
  G->>P: TC[4,5]
  Note over P: periodic status DISABLED, evaluation continues

The behaviour follows clauses 6.4.6 and 6.4.7;11121315 request verification reports are those of ST[01], and whether successful stages are reported depends on the acknowledgement flags in the TC secondary header.

docs.title: 7. Worked example (illustrative bytes)
docs.text:
Illustrative TM[4,2] source data

All values below are constructed for explanation; they are not from any mission. The assumed mission choices are: absolute times in CUC with 4 octets of coarse and 2 of fine time (PTC 9, PFC 17, since (17 + 1) / 4 = 4 rem 231), N as an 8-bit unsigned integer, parameter ID and number of samples as 16-bit fields, and a parameter 0x0102 whose format is an IEEE 754 32-bit real. Five samples of a temperature are taken every 120 s from coarse time 1 000 000 000 (0x3B9ACA00): 21.50, 21.75, 22.00, 21.25, 21.50 degC.

Offset (octets) Bytes Field Value 0 3B 9A CA 00 00 00 start time 1 000 000 000 s 6 3B 9A CC 58 00 00 end time start + 600 s 12 01 N 1 13 01 02 parameter ID 0x0102 15 00 05 number of samples 5 17 41 B0 00 00 max value 22.0 21 3B 9A CA F0 00 00 max time start + 240 s (third sample) 27 41 AA 00 00 min value 21.25 31 3B 9A CB 68 00 00 min time start + 360 s 37 41 AC CC CD mean value 21.6 41 3E 82 88 EF standard deviation 0.2550 (population formula)

The source data is 45 octets. With the sample (n - 1) formula the standard deviation would be 0.2850 - PUS-C does not say which one applies, so a mission specification must.

docs.title: 8. PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A) differences
docs.text:
PUS-A clause 9 defines the same service with ten subtypes.45

Aspect PUS-A (2003) PUS-C (2016) Instances any number of application processes may each provide a single instance35 at most one provider per application process2 Name of the list parameter statistics list, maximum <PSLIST_MAX_PARAMS>36 list of evaluated parameters made of parameter statistics definitions3 TC 4,1 reset flag Enumerated, "No" = 0, "Yes" = 1, omitted if the service always resets37 Boolean, optional18 TM 4,2 header fields tstart (last reset time) and NPAR only37 start time, end time and N19 TM 4,2 per parameter Parameter#, Maxval, tmax, Minval, tmin, Meanval, optional Stddevval3738 adds the number of samples; max/min times are "first attained"199 Reporting interval rule must be greater than the sampling interval of every listed parameter39 rejected only if smaller than a sampling interval11 Sampling interval rule must be smaller than the reporting interval when periodic40 rejected if greater than the reporting interval13 Subtype 6 "Add Parameters to Parameter Statistics List"; NPAR omitted if one parameter at a time40 "add or update ... definitions"; N always present; update restarts evaluation2313 Subtype 7 delete; evaluation stops immediately and the parameters are not reported in the next report41 delete; N = 0 means delete all24 Subtypes 8/9 "Report Parameter Statistics List" / "Parameter Statistics List Report"; reporting interval 0 s if not periodic; omitted if no periodic concept or a default is used42 "report the parameter statistics definitions" / "definition report"; 0 s if not enabled26 Subtype 10 "Clear Parameter Statistics List"43 removed (use TC[4,7] with N = 0)2724

PUS-A capability sets:44

Set Subtypes Dependencies Minimum 1, 2, 3 - Additional: standard deviation Stddevval in subtype 2 - Additional: periodic reporting 4 and 5 each requires the other Additional: list maintenance 6 requires 7 and/or 10 7 requires 6 8 and 9 each requires the other 10 requires 6

More PUS-A-to-PUS-C changes are summarised on PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: 9. Tailoring data in ECSS-E-ST-70-31C
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-70-31C, the standard for ground-segment monitoring and control data, defines the data a mission database must hold to describe its tailoring of service 4. Its model follows the PUS-A subtype numbering.53

Tailoring item (Boolean) Meaning Condition S4 ST4 and ST5 Provider periodic reporting supported - S4 Default Reporting Interval a default reporting interval is used if periodic supported S4 Add Parameters parameters can be added - S4 Default Sampling Interval a default sampling interval is used if add supported S4 Multiple Parameters several parameters per request if add supported S4 ST6 and ST7 Provider parameters can be deleted if add supported S4 ST6 and ST10 Provider the list can be cleared if delete supported; forced TRUE if add is TRUE and delete is FALSE S4 ST8 and ST9 Provider the list can be reported - S4 Always Reset evaluation always reset on report - S4 Standard Deviation standard deviation evaluated -

Source: Table 6-27.51 Table 6-28 then asks for the PFCs of the reset flag (PTC 2, only if not "always reset"), the time fields (PTC 9), NPAR (PTC 3), the parameter number (PTC 2) and the relative time fields (PTC 10); Table 6-29 asks for the maximum number of parameters (the PUS mission constant <PSLIST_MAX_PARAMS>), the default reporting interval and the default sampling interval.52 The decision tree of Figure A-5 walks through the same questions in order.53

docs.title: 10. Changes in the 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-70-41C Rev.1 DIR1 (11 December 2024) keeps the nine message types and their layouts (only the figures are renumbered, 8.4-1 to 8.4-6)50 but changes the error semantics of list maintenance:4748

  • TC[4,6] and TC[4,7] now carry an ordered list of instructions, and the whole request is rejected if any instruction is invalid (unknown parameter, sampling interval greater than the reporting interval, list full, parameter not in the list). A request with only valid instructions is executed in order. In PUS-C each faulty instruction was rejected on its own and the others were executed.1314
  • TC[4,7]'s "delete all" becomes "a single instruction".48
  • A subservice observable is added: the number of definitions currently on board.49

docs.title: 11.1 SCOS-2000
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD states that there is no specific processing of service 4 in SCOS-2000 and no specific limitation, except that all service 4 reports are variable packets and therefore inherit the general variable-packet limitation.54 That limitation is important: parameter values extracted from variable packets cannot take part in full telemetry processing - validity, monitoring checks, verification checks, synthetic parameters - because their parameters and time references are only known once the packet is opened.55 On the command side SCOS-2000 offers command parameters of type "Parameter ID", which take the name of a telemetry parameter and encode its on-board identifier; the ICD names TC(4,6) as an example.56

Inference: how a MIB would describe TM[4,2]

The ICD does not give a service 4 example. In the SCOS-2000 MIB a TM[4,2] would be identified by PID (type 4, subtype 2, APID), given a TPSD and described in the VPD table: N as a repeat counter (VPD_GRPSIZE), the parameter ID with VPD_PIDREF = 'Y' so that its value is matched against PCF_PID in PCF, followed by the deduced value fields.58 Because of the variable-packet limitation, statistics delivered this way could be displayed and archived, but not limit-checked like ordinary telemetry.

docs.title: 11.2 Not to be confused with ground-side statistics
docs.text: ESA's ground archive services compute their own statistics. For example the EDDS "Parameter Statistics" request returns statistics records with start time, storage time, minimum, maximum, average, standard deviation and the number of valid and invalid samples.59 These are evaluated on ground from archived samples; they are unrelated to the on-board ST[04] service.

docs.title: 12.1 Solar Orbiter: not used
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter space-to-ground ICD, whose applicable PUS is ECSS-E-70-41A, lists the service simply as "Service 4: Not Used".6160 The public MIB agrees: neither the April 2020 nor the September 2025 release contains a single TM packet (PID), packet identification rule (PIC) or telecommand (CCF) of service type 4, and neither does the SWA instrument database.626364 The only packet with "statistic" in its description is a housekeeping report, TM(3,25) "DAS Housekeeping Parameter Report (failure statistics)" on APID 1204.62

SQL used 
-- run on solo-2025-09-16.sqlite, solo-2020-04-16.sqlite and swa-idb.sqlite
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '4';        -- 0 in all three
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pic WHERE PIC_TYPE = '4';        -- 0 in all three
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '4';        -- 0 in all three
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_DESCR
  FROM pid WHERE PID_DESCR LIKE '%statistic%';        -- one TM(3,25) packet
-- infrastructure that ST[04] would need on the ground side:
SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(PCF_PID IS NOT NULL AND PCF_PID <> '') FROM pcf;  -- 126745, 19803
SELECT CPC_CATEG, COUNT(*) FROM cpc GROUP BY 1;       -- 152 'P' (Parameter ID) parameters

The ground infrastructure that ST[04] would rely on does exist in the database: 19 803 of the 126 745 monitoring parameters carry an on-board parameter identifier (PCF_PID), and 152 command parameters are of the "Parameter ID" category (CPC_CATEG = P), the SCOS-2000 type that encodes a telemetry parameter name as its on-board identifier.625657

docs.title: 12.2 Herschel and Planck: no requirement
docs.text:
The Herschel/Planck Operations Interface Requirements Document (2003) keeps a section "Statistics Reporting (Service 4)" only as a placeholder: no requirement had been identified for such a service.65 See Herschel and Planck.

Inference: why ST[04] is rare in ESA science missions

Both missions documented in this wiki's library chose not to use ST[04]. A plausible reason, not stated in the sources, is that deep-space and L2 missions store all housekeeping on board and dump it at each pass, so a statistical summary adds little; the standard itself targets missions with limited ground coverage.1 The service drew only 8 of the 664 discrepancy review reports raised on the PUS-C draft, against 44 for ST[06].66
