docs.title: 7. PUS-A: the on-board operations scheduling service
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's on-board software implements the 2003 version of service 11: its applicable PUS document is ECSS-E-70-41A.8486 SCOS-2000's built-in service 11 support also predates PUS-C: it assumes the Rosetta packet structure, and its section references match the clause numbers of PUS-A (see the inference on ST[08]).70 The PUS-A service is therefore described here in detail.

docs.title: 7.1 Concept
docs.text:
PUS-A motivates on-board scheduling by two scenarios: missions out of ground contact for long periods (low Earth orbit, deep space), and missions that want to minimise their dependency on the ground even when permanently in view, such as geostationary telecommunication or meteorological spacecraft. The simplest form stores time-tagged commands and releases them when their on-board time is reached, open-loop. Optional extensions are:43

  • sub-schedules, logical partitions without their own size limit, to group commands per destination or per sequence;
  • interlocks: a command's release can depend on the success, or the failure, of one earlier command of the same sub-schedule, giving simple preconditions and even IF-THEN-ELSE branches;
  • time-shift "en bloc" by a delta time, instead of deleting and reloading;
  • relative times, counted from a scheduling event such as the start of the schedule or of a sub-schedule, or the execution of the interlocking command.

docs.title: 7.2 The command schedule
docs.text:
Each telecommand in the PUS-A command schedule has these scheduling attributes: its sub-schedule, the interlock it sets (if any), the interlock it depends on (if any), whether it depends on the success or the failure of that interlock, and an absolute or relative release time, all in CUC.46 Its release status is "enabled" only if release is enabled at three independent levels, the whole schedule, its sub-schedule and its destination application process:47

Schedule Sub-schedule Destination APID Release status enabled enabled enabled enabled any other combination disabled

This collapses PUS-A Table 22, whose eight rows give "enabled" only in the all-enabled case.47

docs.title: 7.3 Interlocks and scheduling events
docs.text:
When a command that sets an interlock is due: if its release status is disabled or its own interlock status is "locked", it is not released and its execution result becomes "failure"; otherwise it is released, the destination is told to report its completion back to the scheduler, and the result becomes "success" or "failure" on that report, or "failure" if no report arrives within the command's execution timeout. A dependent command is locked if it waits for success and the interlock result is failure, or waits for failure and the result is success.48

sequenceDiagram
  participant SCH as PUS-A scheduler
  participant AP as Destination process
  Note over SCH: TC A sets interlock 1, timeout 60 s
  SCH->>AP: release TC A (interlock flagged)
  AP-->>SCH: completion report: success (within 60 s)
  Note over SCH: interlock 1 = success
  Note over SCH: TC B depends on 1+ (success): clear to go
  SCH->>AP: release TC B
  Note over SCH: TC C depends on 1- (failure): locked, not released

The example mirrors PUS-A Figure 5 ("1+" means the release depends on the success of the command setting interlock 1, "1-" the opposite).48 Scheduling events give relative times an absolute anchor: the on-board CUC time at which the schedule was enabled, at which a sub-schedule was enabled, or at which an interlocking command's completion report (or timeout) arrived. Once an event has occurred, the absolute times of the dependent commands are known; a repeat of the event does not change them. Insertions and time-shifts that would put an interlock-dependent command before the end of its interlocking command's execution window are refused.49

docs.title: 7.4 Auxiliary information and the scheduling activity
docs.text: The PUS-A service also needs the maximum size of the schedule, the maximum numbers of sub-schedules and interlocks, the list of sources it accepts commands from and the list of destination processes, which it uses for error detection.50 A command whose release time is due is always processed, even if the schedule is disabled: if its release status is disabled or its interlock status locked, it is not released, its execution result becomes "failure" if it sets an interlock, and the time of the scheduling event it defines (if any) becomes the current time; otherwise it is released. The service must also detect and report on-board CUC time jumps, and on a jump suspend itself once it has processed the commands interlocked with commands already released.51 Requests that would make the schedule inconsistent are refused as a whole.45

docs.title: 7.5 PUS-A messages
docs.text:
Subtype PUS-A name Application / source data (11,1) / (11,2) Enable / Disable Release of Telecommands N1 (optional), N1 × [sub-schedule ID (0 = all), N2 (optional), N2 × APID] (11,3) Reset Command Schedule none (11,4) Insert Telecommands in Command Schedule sub-schedule ID (optional, not 0), N (optional), N × [interlock set ID, interlock assessed ID, assessment type, scheduling event (all optional), absolute or relative time tag, execution timeout (optional), telecommand packet] (11,5) Delete Telecommands N (optional), N × [APID, sequence count, number of telecommands] (11,6) Delete Telecommands over Time Period range, time tag 1, time tag 2, N1, N1 × [sub-schedule ID, N2, N2 × APID] (11,7) Time-Shift Selected Telecommands time offset, N, N × [APID, sequence count, number of telecommands] (11,8) Time-Shift Selected Telecommands over Time Period range, time tag 1, time tag 2, time offset, N1 × [sub-schedule ID, N2 × APID] (11,9) Report Subset of Command Schedule in Detailed Form as (11,5) (11,10) Detailed Schedule Report N × [sub-schedule ID, interlock set ID, interlock assessed ID, assessment type, scheduling event, time tag, execution timeout, telecommand packet] (11,11) Report Subset of Command Schedule in Detailed Form over Time Period as (11,6) (11,12) Report Subset of Command Schedule in Summary Form as (11,5) (11,13) Summary Schedule Report N × [sub-schedule ID, scheduling event, time tag, APID, sequence count] (11,14) Report Subset of Command Schedule in Summary Form over Time Period as (11,6) (11,15) Time-Shift All Telecommands time offset (11,16) / (11,17) Report Command Schedule in Detailed / Summary Form none (11,18) Report Status of Command Schedule none (11,19) Command Schedule Status Report N1 × [sub-schedule ID, status, N2 × (APID, status)]

The table condenses PUS-A clauses 14.3.1 to 14.3.6.525354555657 Selected details:

  • (11,1)/(11,2): N1 = 0 acts on the whole schedule (and an enable sets the schedule's scheduling event time); N1 > 0 with N2 = 0 acts on the listed sub-schedules; N1 > 0 with N2 > 0 acts on the listed APIDs within the listed sub-schedules. An error in one part does not stop the rest.52
  • (11,3): clears all entries, disables the schedule and all sub-schedules, enables commanding to all APIDs, and resets interlocks and scheduling event times.52
  • (11,4) assessment type: 1 = "Success", 0 = "Failure"; scheduling event: 0 = absolute, 1 = schedule, 2 = sub-schedule, 3 = interlock, other values mission-specific. Errors include a full schedule, an invalid destination, a time in the past or inside the execution window of the interlocking command, and equal interlock IDs.53
  • Deletion refuses to delete an interlocking command whose dependants survive; any error means nothing is deleted. (11,5) deletes a run of successive commands to one APID starting at a sequence count; commands with not-yet-known relative release times can only be deleted this way.54
  • Time-shift: refused if a command would move into the past, before the end of its interlocking command's window, or to a negative relative time; any error means nothing is shifted; commands whose absolute time is still unknown are not shifted.55
  • Reports cover all sources, are ordered by predicted release time, include only commands not yet released, and must reflect a consistent view at the report packet time.56

The PUS-A "Range" field of (11,6), (11,8), (11,11) and (11,14) has values 0 = "All", 1 = "Between" (time tag 1 to 2 inclusive), 2 = "Before" (at or before time tag 1) and 3 = "After" (at or after time tag 1).54

Range values 2 and 3 swapped between editions

PUS-A value 2 means "Before" and 3 "After". PUS-C Table 8-5 assigns 2 to "from time tag" (at and after) and 3 to "to time tag" (before and at), the opposite meanings.5433 A ground system or database that mixes the editions would delete or shift the wrong half of the schedule. Solar Orbiter follows PUS-A here (section 11.3).

docs.title: 7.6 PUS-A capability sets
docs.text: The minimum capability set is (11,1) to (11,4). Additional capabilities are sub-schedules, relative times, interlocking, "scatter" delete, time-shift and report (the N arrays), selection at sub-schedule and at APID level, and subtypes 5 to 19 with dependencies; for example (11,8) requires (11,7) and (11,15), and (11,18) and (11,19) require each other.58

docs.title: 8. PUS-A to PUS-C: what changed
docs.text:
Aspect PUS-A (2003) PUS-C (2016) Name on-board operations scheduling time-based scheduling Interlocks, execution timeout, assessment type yes (optional) removed; releases are independent Relative times and scheduling events yes (optional) removed; release times are absolute Enable/disable granularity schedule, sub-schedule, destination APID within sub-schedule execution function, sub-schedule, group Sub-schedule creation not specified; an insert names a non-zero sub-schedule ID, and ID 0 means "all" in the other requests created on first insert (disabled), deleted when empty; N = 0 means "all" Groups - yes (optional), explicit create/delete Identification of a command (APID, sequence count, number of successive telecommands) request identifier: (source ID, APID, sequence count) Reset disables schedule and sub-schedules, enables APIDs, clears interlocks disables function, deletes activities and sub-schedules, enables groups Failed instructions insert: processed one by one; delete/time-shift: all or nothing most instructions rejected individually; time-shift offset checks per request (11,19) command schedule status (sub-schedules and APIDs) sub-schedule status only; groups via TM[11,27] Time margin, release accuracy not specified declared parameters

The comparison is assembled from the clauses cited in sections 4 to 7.46525491122 The PUS-C working group replaced the PUS-A service by three service types: ST[11], ST[21] request sequencing (called telecommand sequencing at ADCSS 2015) and ST[22] position-based scheduling (then called orbit-based scheduling).6942 See also PUS-A vs PUS-C.

Inference

No PUS-C service keeps the PUS-A interlocks as such. Missions that need a release to depend on the outcome of an earlier command would, in PUS-C terms, use ST[21] request sequences or ST[18] on-board control procedures; the standard does not state this mapping.

docs.title: 9. The 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-70-41C Rev.1 DIR1 keeps the 27 message types (its Table C-17 lists the same interface clauses 8.11.2.1 to 8.11.2.27) and changes the model in several places:66596061626364

  • each time-based scheduling subservice is associated with exactly one event reporting subservice that issues its events (new 6.11.3.2);
  • the declarations gain the time resolution, a maximum activity release time (how late a due activity may still be released; it takes the place of PUS-C's maximum delta between specified and real release time, 6.11.4.2e) and a configuration policy for start and restart, covering for example whether emptied sub-schedules or groups are automatically disabled and loading an alternative content after a safe mode;
  • the execution function status at start-up becomes a declaration instead of always "disabled";
  • reset enables all sub-schedules (PUS-C deletes them);
  • an insert instruction naming an unknown sub-schedule is rejected, and a request whose instructions are all valid executes them in order;
  • activities with the same release time are released in insertion order;
  • a due activity that cannot be released within the maximum activity release time is deleted and an event report is generated;
  • releasing requests must not block the processing of other requests to the subservice, so a report request is accepted even while a sub-schedule is executing.

The draft is not yet a standard.65

docs.title: 10. Ground side: SCOS-2000 and time-tagged commands
10.1 What SCOS-2000 does
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD lists service 11 among the services with specific ground support:70

  • commands with an execution time-tag are automatically encapsulated in (11,4) commands;
  • a ground image of the on-board schedule is maintained by modelling the effect of service 11 commands, and (from SCOS-2000 R5.2) also built from the reports received from the spacecraft;
  • delayed verification of execution time-tagged commands works with live and playback telemetry; playback data must be in chronological order for parameter-based verification;
  • service 11 commands implementing an action selected in the ground image (for example deleting a range of commands) are generated automatically.

The limitations are equally explicit: the structure of the service 11 packets cannot be configured; the Rosetta spacecraft structure is the reference, and other structures need mission-specific modifications; each (11,4) contains one TC packet, several time-tagged commands blocked together become several (11,4) packets aggregated in one TC segment; only absolute time tags are supported; interlocks and the time-shift commands are not modelled; (11,19) reports are not used to update the ground image.70 The model is the On-Board Queue Model (OBQM), listed among the SCOS-2000 TC servers with the multiplexer, releaser and verifier, and shown on the On-Board Queue Display (OBQD).8283

flowchart LR
  OP["Operator / planning file<br/>command with execution time"] --> ST["Manual stack or<br/>command sequence"]
  ST --> REL["Releaser: wrap in TC(11,4)<br/>(MISC CMD_LOAD_TT*)"]
  REL --> NC["NCTRS / ground station"]
  NC --> SC["Spacecraft schedule"]
  REL --> OBQM["OBQM: ground image<br/>of the on-board queue"]
  SC -. "TM(11,10) / (11,13)<br/>reports" .-> OBQM
  SC -. "TM(1,x) at execution" .-> VER["Verifier: windows relative<br/>to execution time"]

The diagram combines the ICD statements of this section; the component names are those of the GSAW 2003 SCOS-2000 presentation.707183 The ICD does not say which component performs the TC(11,4) encapsulation: placing it in the releaser is this wiki's assumption.

docs.title: 10.2 What the MIB says about time tags
docs.text:
The MIB has no time-tag field in its command definition table ccf: a time tag is attached when a command is loaded onto a stack or through a sequence. Several fields prepare that use:727173747576

Table, field Role for time-tagged commands ccf CCF_HIPRI Y for high-priority commands (typically CPDU commands): fixed MAP ID, cannot be execution time-tagged, cannot be blocked ccf CCF_SUBSCHEDID default on-board sub-schedule (1 to 65535) when loaded as execution time-tagged; if null, CCF_SUBSYS is used csf CSF_IFTT Y: the sequence has execution time-tagged commands, the user gives a reference time at load; B: the user chooses at load to treat it as on-board time-tagged (execution times only) or ground time-tagged (release times only); N: none csf CSF_SUBSCHEDID default sub-schedule for all execution time-tagged commands of the sequence; overrides CCF_SUBSCHEDID css CSS_EXTIME delta execution time-tag of an element, [+][ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] or negative; relative to the previous execution time-tagged command (CSS_PREVREL = R) or to the sequence execution start (A); null means immediate execution css CSS_RELTIME delta release (ground) time-tag, hh.mm.ss; a separate concept cvs CVS_START verification window opens this many seconds after release, or after execution for time-tagged commands cdf CDF_VALUE fixed areas must not be used for service 11 elements that the OBQM has to process

The (11,4) command itself must exist in the MIB (ccf and cdf); its name, type, subtype and parameters are configured in SCOS-2000 through the MISCconfig variables CMD_LOAD_TT*.71 From SCOS-2000 5.5.4, (11,4) is encoded according to its cdf definition.78 In the Solar Orbiter MIB, 3 354 of the 3 404 sequences have CSF_IFTT = B and 50 have N; none uses Y. Of the 13 879 sequence elements, 13 784 carry a CSS_EXTIME delta, most often 00.00.01 (6 635 elements) or 00.00.00 (3 159).101 CPDU commands can be defined so that they cannot be put into a TC(11,4) or aggregated with other commands.77

docs.title: 10.3 The size budget
docs.text:
The maximum size of a command is the MISC variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (default 248 octets). The space for parameters shrinks by the header, the CRC (CMD_CRC_SIZE, default 2 octets) and, for time-tagged commands, the size of the time-tag wrapper named by CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME (20 octets if that command is not found). With a 10-octet header, a command can then carry at most 238 octets of parameters without time tag or CRC, or 216 with both. The final encoded time-tagged command is larger than CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE by the wrapper, so the variable must be set to the maximum CLTU size minus the length of the wrapper parameters.71

Solar Orbiter's numbers match

On Solar Orbiter a TC data field is at most 242 octets (4 header, 236 data, 2 CRC), so a TC packet is at most 248 octets. A command for the MTL is limited to 228 octets (216 of application data), so that its TC(11,4) stays within 248.9688 The TC(11,4) overhead is 6 (primary header) + 4 (data field header) + 1 (sub-schedule) + 1 (N) + 6 (time tag) + 2 (CRC) = 20 octets, exactly the ICD's default wrapper size, and 248 - 10 - 2 - 20 = 216 is the ICD's own example.7188 The arithmetic is this wiki's.

docs.title: 11.1 The service on board
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter's central software implements service 11 following PUS-A: the ICD reproduces the PUS-A objective and activity list, and the summary table lists all PUS-A subtypes 1 to 19 for the CSW.8485 The schedule is the MTL. A Back-Up Timeline is a file of service 11 time-tagged TCs kept in the safeguard memory (SGM); at software initialisation the TC sequencer service 134 executes the selected file and so loads the backup TCs into the MTL queue, after which all service 11 functions apply to them. At least two file placeholders exist, so the ground can update one while the other is selected.84 Service 134 executes TC files uploaded with service 13; a file marked "Immediate" runs as soon as its upload completes, which is "the intended mechanism for MTL uploading".98

The ICD reserves ground source IDs 110 for the Mission TimeLine and 113 for the Back-Up Mission TimeLine, next to 111 (TC sequences), 112 (event-action recovery commands) and 120 (direct commands).97

Inference

The ICD lists these as "ground sources (set by ground)", so a TC destined for the MTL presumably carries source ID 110 in its own data field header, and its verification reports can then be told apart from those of direct commands. The available sources do not show an example.97

docs.title: 11.2 Message layouts
docs.text:
The mission fixes the PUS-A fields as follows:8788899091929394

Message Solar Orbiter layout and rules TC(11,1) / (11,2) N1, sub-schedule IDs (0 to 255, 0 = all), N2, PIDs. N1 = 0: whole MTL; N1 > 0, N2 = 0: the listed sub-schedules; N1 = 1, N2 > 0, sub-schedule 0: the listed PIDs. PID and sub-schedule statuses are independent: a disabled PID releases nothing, whatever the sub-schedule TC(11,3) no application data; clears all entries TC(11,4) sub-schedule ID (1 octet, 1 to 255), N (1 octet), then N × [time tag (6 octets, absolute release time), complete TC packet (at most 228 octets)] TC(11,5) N, then N × [filler (1 bit), PID (7 bits), filler (2 bits), sequence count (14 bits), number of TCs (1 octet)]; successive TCs are counted by time tag, not by sequence count TC(11,6) range (1 octet: 0 complete, 1 between, 2 before time tag 1, 3 after time tag 1), time tags 1 and 2 (6 octets each), N1, sub-schedule IDs, N2, PIDs (1 filler bit + 7 bits) TC(11,7) time offset, N (1 to 57), PID, sequence count, number of TCs TC(11,8) range, time tags, time offset, N1 (0 = all sub-schedules, 1 = select by PID, 2 or more = by sub-schedule), sub-schedule IDs, N2, PIDs TC(11,9) / (11,12) N (1 to 58), PID, sequence count, number of TCs TM(11,10) N × [sub-schedule ID, sub-schedule status, PID status, time tag, TC packet] TC(11,11) / (11,14) as TC(11,8) without the offset TM(11,13) N × [sub-schedule ID, sub-schedule status, PID status, time tag, TC packet header, TC data field header] TC(11,15) time offset, CUC, 6 octets TC(11,16), (11,17), (11,18) no application data TM(11,19) N1 × [sub-schedule ID (0 = global status), status, N2 (number of registered PIDs for ID 0, else 0), N2 × (PID, status)]

The 57 and 58 limits follow from the 236-octet maximum application data field and the wish to avoid nesting service 11 commands in the MTL.9091 The arithmetic works out if each entry takes 4 octets: 6 (offset) + 1 (N) + 57 × 4 = 235 for TC(11,7), and 1 + 58 × 4 = 233 for TC(11,9) (this wiki's check). TC(11,15) fails at completion if the new time tag is in the past, with the note "Time Tags later than OBT + 5secs are considered as past".93

Inference

Read literally, the note would treat almost every future time as "past". It most likely means time tags earlier than OBT + 5 s, that is, a 5-second time margin in the sense of PUS-C's time-based schedule time margin.936

The two diagrams follow the ICD tables; the embedded TC packet is variable and drawn with a nominal width.8889 In TC(11,5) the 1-bit filler pads the 7-bit process ID to an octet and the 2-bit filler pads the 14-bit sequence count to 16 bits.

docs.title: 11.3 Service 11 in the 2025 MIB
docs.text:
All service 11 telecommands in release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL go to APID 172 and all service 11 reports come from APID 163; both belong to process ID 10, the CSW Data Management System application, which handles the PUS services.10199

Subtype MIB command Parameters (PTC/PFC) Explorer 1 ZCD00B01 Enable Release of Telecommands PCD0B011 N1 (¾, 0 to 78), PCD0B012 sub-schedule (¾), PCD0B013 N2 (¾), PCD0B014 PID (¾) ZCD00B01 2 ZCD00B02 Disable Release of Telecommands, and 14 fixed variants ZCSX0021 to ZCSX0030 and ZCSX0043 to ZCSX0046 as subtype 1 ZCD00B02 3 ZCD00B03 Reset Command Schedule ("resets the MTL to its default state") none ZCD00B03 4 ZCD00B04 and INSERTTT Insert Telecommands in Command Schedule PCD0B041 sub-schedule (¾, range 1 to 254), PCD0B042 N (¾, 1 to 13, default 1), PCD0B043 time tag (9/17), TC packet (7/0) ZCD00B04 5 ZCD00B05 Delete Telecommands N (1 to 58), PID, SSC (3/12), number of TCs ZCD00B05 6 ZCD00B06 Delete Telecommands over Time Period time span (2/8, calibration CCDT0022TC), time tags 1 and 2 (9/17), N1, sub-schedule, N2, PID ZCD00B06 7 ZCD00B07 Time-Shift Selected Telecommands relative time (10/17), N (1 to 57), PID, SSC, number of TCs ZCD00B07 8 ZCD00B08 TimeShift Selected TCs over Time Period time span, time tags, relative time, N1, sub-schedule, N2, PID ZCD00B08 9, 11, 12, 14 ZCD00B09, ZCD00B0B, ZCD00B0C, ZCD00B0E (reports of subsets) as 5 and 6 ZCD00B09 15 ZCD00B0F Time-Shift all Time-Tagged Telecommands relative time (10/17) ZCD00B0F 16, 17, 18 ZCD00B10, ZCD00B11, ZCD00B12 none ZCD00B12 132 (private) ZCD00B84 and INSERTBU Insert Backup MTL Telecommands in Command Schedule same as subtype 4 ZCD00B84

The values come from this wiki's queries of ccf, cdf, cpc, prf and prv.101 Three details:

  • The textual calibration CCDT0022TC of the "Time Span" field is COMPLETE = 0, BETWEEN_TTAGS = 1, BEFORE_TTAG_1 = 2, AFTER_TTAG_1 = 3: the PUS-A meaning of the range values.10154
  • The range set VCD00269 of the sub-schedule ID is described as "Integer between 1 and 25" but allows 1 to 254; the description field is 24 characters wide, so the text is truncated.10179
  • The two TC(11,4) commands differ only in the TC packet parameter: in ZCD00B04 it is PCD0B044 with CPC_CATEG = A, a "Command ID" parameter (PTC 7, PFC 0) whose value is another MIB command, while INSERTTT and INSERTBU use PCDXB044 with category N, a plain octet string.10180

Inference

The name INSERTTT ("insert time-tagged") and its plain octet-string packet field suggest that it is the command SCOS-2000 uses as CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME to wrap execution time-tagged commands, while ZCD00B04 lets an operator compose a TC(11,4) by naming the command to insert. The MISC configuration is not part of the MIB, so this cannot be confirmed from the available sources.71101

The reports are variable packets (vpd), all with PID_DFHSIZE = 16:10181

SPID Report Decoding in the vpd 14174 TM(11,19) Command Schedule Status Report NCD0B131 count, group of 5: sub-schedule ID, its status (CCDT0003TX), NCD0B134 count of registered PIDs, group of 2: PID (CCDT0018TX), PID status 14175 TM(11,10) Detailed Schedule Report NCD0B0A1 count (16 bits), group of 9: sub-schedule ID, sub-schedule status, PID status, release time (9/17), TC packet ID, TC sequence control, packet length (a repeat counter for one data byte), data bytes, last data byte 14176 TM(11,13) Summary Schedule Report NCD0B0A1 count, group of 17: sub-schedule ID, statuses, release time, TC packet ID, sequence control, length, the 32-bit data field header, then its fields (secondary header flag, PUS version, four ack bits, service type, subtype, source ID)

Inference: two decoding tricks

In SPID 14175 the TC packet length C is used as the repeat counter of a one-octet data field, followed by a "last byte": C repetitions plus one octet equals the C + 1 octets of the packet data field, so the embedded TC is unpacked octet by octet. In SPID 14176 the first data field header sub-field has VPD_OFFSET = -32, so the 32 bits just read as "Data field header" are read again field by field.10181

docs.title: 11.4 How the sub-schedules are organised
docs.text:
Every command definition with a value has CCF_SUBSCHEDID equal to CCF_SUBSYS, so the default sub-schedule is the subsystem number. Platform commands use 1, 2 and 4 to 8; the ten instruments use 101 to 110.101

Sub-schedule Instrument (command prefix) Commands Further sub-schedules seen 101 MAG (ZIM) 127 121, 141, 161 102 EUI (ZIU) 122 122, 142, 162 103 EPD (ZID) 119 123, 143, 163 104 PHI (ZIP) 200 124, 144, 164 105 STIX (ZIX) 100 125, 145, 165 106 RPW (ZIW) 138 126, 146, 166 107 SoloHI (ZIH) 102 127, 147, 167 108 SPICE (ZIC) 91 128, 148, 168 109 SWA (ZIA) 200 129, 149, 169, and 111 to 114 for EAS1, EAS2, PAS, HIS 110 METIS (ZIT) 126 130, 150, 170

The "further sub-schedules" are the ones the MIB's own commands and sequences address:101

  • 141 to 150 are each instrument's iVSTP sub-schedule: sequences ADMF740A to ADMF740U "Enable iVSTP instrument" and "Disable iVSTP instrument" send TC(11,1) or TC(11,2) with exactly that sub-schedule.
  • 161 to 170 are the default sub-schedules of each instrument's recovery sequences, for example AIMC805A "Recover MAG OFF" and AIMC805B "Rcvr MTL P_OFF MAG".
  • 121 to 130 appear only where an instrument's whole set of sub-schedules is disabled or re-enabled: the protection and recovery commands below, the emergency-configuration sequences ASYC602C to ASYC602K, and the EPD and RPW pre-action sequences AIDC060A, AIWC060A and AIWC060B.
  • Sequences default mostly to sub-schedule 1 (780 of 3 404), 2 (404) and the instrument numbers; 56 sequences use 254, the top of the allowed range.

Inference

"iVSTP" is not expanded in the available sources; given Solar Orbiter's planning cycles it probably denotes an instrument very-short-term-planning product. The meaning of the 101-110 and 121-130 bands, beyond being per-instrument, is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: 11.5 Protecting the MTL when an instrument switches off
docs.text:
The MIB shows a complete on-board protection loop built from events, event-action definitions and the MTL:101

  1. Sequence ADMF730A "Define P_OFF S12 S19" loads on-board monitoring and event-action definitions. Each TC(19,1), for example ZCSX0031 "Define P_OFF_EPD S19", ties an event such as "EPD scvTM OFF" (a fixed event ID parameter) to a TC to send (a fixed "Command ID" parameter).
  2. That TC is a fixed TC(11,2), for example ZCSX0023 "P_OFF_EPD SSID", whose four fixed octet pairs disable sub-schedules 0x67, 0x7B, 0x8F, 0xA3, that is 103, 123, 143 and 163, with N2 = 0 each (raw cdf values 4 67 0 7B 0 8F 0 A3 0).
  3. When the instrument is recovered, a sequence such as AIDC805B "EPD_Enable_MTL" sends TC(11,1) with sub-schedules 103, 123 and 163.
Instrument Event-action TC(19,1) Embedded TC(11,2) Sub-schedules disabled Re-enabled by MAG ZCSX0033 (defined, but not loaded by ADMF730A in 2025, see below) ZCSX0021 101, 121, 141, 161 AIMC805B: 101, 121, 161 EUI ZCSX0032 ZCSX0022 102, 122, 142, 162 AIUC805D: 102, 122, 162 EPD ZCSX0031 ZCSX0023 103, 123, 143, 163 AIDC805B: 103, 123, 163 PHI ZCSX0035 ZCSX0024 104, 124, 144, 164 AIPC805A: 104, 124, 164 STIX ZCSX0039 ZCSX0025 105, 125, 145, 165 AIXC805B: 105, 125, 165 RPW ZCSX0036 ZCSX0026 106, 126, 146, 166 AIWC805B: 106, 126, 166 SoloHI ZCSX0037 ZCSX0027 107, 127, 147, 167 AIHC805B: 107, 127, 167 SPICE ZCSX0038 ZCSX0028 108, 128, 148, 168 AICC805A: 108, 128, 168 SWA ZCSX0040 ZCSX0029 109, 129, 149, 169, 111 to 114 AIAC805G: 109, 129, 169 METIS ZCSX0034 ZCSX0030 110, 130, 150, 170 AITC805D: 110, 130, 170

The SWA sensors have their own events and fixed commands: the event-action definitions ZCSX0047 to ZCSX0054 release ZCSX0043 to ZCSX0046, which disable 111 (EAS1), 112 (EAS2), 113 (PAS) and 114 (HIS), on events such as Eas1OffEvent or PasDetOffErOFF. For MAG, the 2025 ADMF730A loads a different definition, ZCSX0042, instead of ZCSX0033: it reacts to "MAG scvTM OFF" by loading and starting an OBCP (TC(18,140) ZCPX0009 "Load and start OBCP (MAG2)"). No sequence of the 2025 release loads ZCSX0033 or uses ZCSX0021; the 2020 release loaded ZCSX0033.101102

sequenceDiagram
  participant INS as EPD (off)
  participant EV as ST05 event
  participant EA as ST19 event-action
  participant MTL as ST11 MTL
  participant OPS as Ground
  INS->>EV: "EPD scvTM OFF"
  EV->>EA: event matches ZCSX0031
  EA->>MTL: release ZCSX0023 = TC(11,2) disable 103, 123, 143, 163
  Note over MTL: EPD activities falling due are dropped, not released
  OPS->>MTL: later: AIDC805B = TC(11,1) enable 103, 123, 163

The note in the diagram applies the PUS-A rule that a due command whose release is disabled is not released; the rest of the chain is MIB data.51101

Inference

The recovery sequences re-enable three of the four sub-schedules and leave the iVSTP sub-schedule (14x) disabled; enabling it is a separate operation (ADMF740x). The reason is not stated in the available sources. Note also that these TC(11,2) commands are built entirely from fixed areas, which the ICD says should not be used for service 11 elements the OBQM must process: the ground model presumably cannot reflect them, which matters little since they are released on board.76101

Between the April 2020 and September 2025 releases the protection loop changed:101102

  • the four SWA sensor commands ZCSX0043 to ZCSX0046 and their event-action definitions ZCSX0047 to ZCSX0054 were added, as was the MAG OBCP definition ZCSX0042;
  • the ten fixed TC(11,2) commands ZCSX0021 to ZCSX0030 disabled three sub-schedules in 2020 (raw cdf values 3 67 0 7B 0 8F 0 for EPD: 103, 123 and 143). In 2025 they disable four, with the 16x band added, and the SWA command also disables 111 to 114;
  • the 2020 release has none of the recovery sequences AI?C805x, iVSTP sequences ADMF740x or emergency sequences ASYC602x, and no sequence defaults to sub-schedules 161 to 170.

docs.title: 11.6 Verification
docs.text: Every service 11 command in the MIB has two report-based verification stages, acceptance and completion: stages 14001 and 14007 for the 17 ZCD00Bxx commands, stages 11 and 17 for INSERTTT, INSERTBU and the 14 ZCSX commands; all four stages open at 0 s with a 20 s interval.101 This matches the ICD, which has each of these TCs generate TM(1,2) on a failed static check and TM(1,8) on a completion failure.87 See Command verification in the MIB.

docs.title: 11.7 Worked example: a TC(9,1) inserted in the MTL
docs.text:
The bytes below insert TC(9,1) "Change Time Report Generation Rate" (MIB command ZCD00901, rate code 5) into sub-schedule 1, its default CCF_SUBSCHEDID, for release at OBT 811 339 200.0 s. The layouts are real (MIB cdf of ZCD00B04 and ZCD00901, ICD field sizes); the sequence counts, source IDs, time and therefore CRCs are illustrative.1018895

18 AC C0 02 00 1A | 19 0B 04 78 | 01 01 | 30 5C 0D C0 00 00 | 18 AC C0 01 00 06 19 09 01 6E 05 23 43 | AF 55
 primary header     DFH (11,4)    SS N    time tag (CUC 4+2)  embedded TC(9,1), 13 octets               CRC
Octets Field Value 18 AC TC, data field header present, APID 172 (process 10, category 12) C0 02 stand-alone packet, sequence count 2 illustrative 00 1A data length C = 26: 4 + 1 + 1 + 6 + 13 + 2 = 27 octets 19 0B 04 78 PUS version 1, ack acceptance + completion (CCF_ACK 9), service 11, subtype 4, source 120 (direct command) source illustrative 01 sub-schedule 1 (PCD0B041) CCF_SUBSCHEDID of ZCD00901 01 N = 1 (PCD0B042) 30 5C 0D C0 00 00 time tag (PCD0B043, PTC 9 PFC 17): 811 339 200 s, fine 0 nominally 2025-09-16 12:00:00 OBT 18 AC C0 01 00 06 embedded TC primary header: APID 172, count 1, C = 6 illustrative count 19 09 01 6E embedded data field header: service 9, subtype 1, source 110 (Mission TimeLine) source per section 11.1 inference 05 rate exponent 5 (PCD09011, EVERY_32_TMFR) 23 43 embedded TC CRC computed AF 55 CRC of the TC(11,4) over its first 31 octets computed

The CRC is the CCITT CRC-16 with all-ones preset of the Solar Orbiter ICD; the routine used here reproduces the PUS-C Annex B test vectors.10041 The embedded TC is 13 octets, far below the 228-octet MTL limit; the outer TC is 33 octets, of which 20 are the wrapper overhead.

docs.title: SQL used
ST[12] On-board monitoring
docs.text:
The on-board monitoring service type, ST[12] of the Packet Utilization Standard, moves part of the limit checking that a mission control system does on the ground into the spacecraft. An on-board application process samples its own parameters, compares them with checks loaded by the ground, records every change of check result ("check transition"), reports those transitions to the ground and, when a monitoring condition is violated, raises an event. The event can go to the ground through ST[05] event reporting and can be caught on board, for example by ST[19] event-action, to start an autonomous recovery.1 PUS-A explained the purpose plainly: monitoring on board removes the need to downlink all low-level housekeeping and to have the ground permanently watching it.64 Abbreviations such as PMON and FMON are expanded in the glossary.

At a glance

Item Value Service type 122 Subservices (PUS-C) parameter monitoring (exactly one), functional monitoring (at most one)3 Check types limit-check and expected-value-check (minimum), delta-check (optional)8 Message types (PUS-C) 22 requests and 6 reports: TC[12,1]-[12,8], [12,10], [12,13], [12,15]-[12,25], [12,27]; TM[12,9], [12,11], [12,12], [12,14], [12,26], [12,28]58 Minimum capability TC[12,1], [12,2], [12,15], [12,16], TM[12,12]; plus TC[12,17]-[12,20] if functional monitoring exists58 Depends on one ST[05] event reporting subservice per monitoring service45 PUS-A (2003) clause 15 "On-board monitoring service", subtypes 1-1265 Solar Orbiter PUS-A based service 12 in six Central Software applications plus METIS; functional monitoring in private service 1427994

docs.title: Where it sits
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P["On-board parameter<br/>(sampled every monitoring interval)"] --> V{"Check validity<br/>condition"}
  V -- false --> I["PMON checking status = invalid"]
  V -- true --> C["Check: limit / expected value / delta"]
  C --> R{"'repetition number'<br/>consistent results?"}
  R -- yes, new status --> T["Check transition list"]
  T --> TM12["TM[12,12] check transition report<br/>(to ground)"]
  R -- yes, violation --> E["Raise event<br/>(event definition ID)"]
  E --> S5["ST[05] event report<br/>to ground"]
  E --> S19["ST[19] event-action<br/>(on board)"]
  C -.->|PMON checking statuses| F["Functional monitoring<br/>(FMON)"]
  F -->|minimum PMON failing number reached| E

The figure summarises clauses 6.12.3 and 6.12.4 of ECSS-E-ST-70-41C: the parameter monitoring process, the check transition list and its report, the events raised by violations and the functional monitoring layer built on top of the parameter checks.171935 Ground-side limit checking in SCOS-2000 is a separate mechanism, defined in the MIB monitoring check tables; SCOS-2000 applies no specific processing to service 12 packets, which it decodes as ordinary variable packets.106

docs.title: Service layout
docs.text:
• Each on-board monitoring service contains exactly one parameter monitoring subservice and at most one functional monitoring subservice; when both exist they are hosted by the same application process.3
  • Each service is associated with exactly one event reporting subservice, declared in the service specification. That subservice catches the events raised by the monitoring service and issues the event notifications; an event is identified by the application process that hosts the event reporting subservice plus an event definition identifier.4
  • The foundation model lists this dependency among the few cross-service rules: the on-board monitoring and event-action services require an event reporting service.5
  • The parameter monitoring subservice can monitor every on-board parameter accessible to its hosting application process.6 On-board parameters are identified by a spacecraft-unique parameter identifier, and each belongs to an "on-board parameter minimum sampling interval", the time unit used by monitoring and housekeeping (the standard's example: 125 ms for a platform, 500 ms for a payload).7

docs.title: Check types
docs.text:
Check type What is compared Success condition Capability Limit-check the parameter value with a low and a high limit low limit <= value <= high limit minimum Expected-value-check the parameter value after a bitwise AND with a mask, with an expected value masked value = expected value minimum Delta-check the difference between two consecutive values with a low and a high threshold low threshold <= delta <= high threshold optional, declared

Sources: requirements 6.12.3.2.1 and 6.12.3.2.2.8 The standard notes that the applicable check depends on the nature of the parameter: analogue values are limit or delta checked, status values are expected-value checked.11 There is no limit on how many checks one parameter may have: one definition can hold warning limits and another danger limits for the same parameter, and a parameter can be limit-checked and delta-checked at the same time through two definitions.1

docs.title: The parameter monitoring definition
docs.text:
Each check is a separate parameter monitoring definition, kept in the PMON list. Its maximum size is declared for the subservice, which must accept several definitions for the same parameter, for example to adapt the monitoring plan to spacecraft modes through different validity conditions.9

Element Content Present PMON identifier identifier of the definition always Monitored parameter ID on-board parameter to monitor always Check validity condition validity parameter ID, bit-mask, expected value; the check runs only when (sample AND mask) = expected value if conditional checking is declared Monitoring interval time between two evaluations, in minimum-sampling-interval units if definition-specific intervals are declared (otherwise one subservice-wide interval) Check definition repetition number, check type and type-dependent criteria (below) always

Sources: requirements 6.12.3.3d-i.910

Check type Type-dependent criteria Limit-check low limit, event definition ID for "below low limit", high limit, event definition ID for "above high limit" Expected-value-check expected value, mask applied to the sample, event definition ID for "unexpected value" Delta-check number of consecutive delta values averaged, low delta threshold, event ID for "below low threshold", high delta threshold, event ID for "above high threshold"

Every event ID is optional in the sense that the value 0 means "no event report to generate".1049

The repetition number is the count of successive, consistent check results needed before a new checking status is established; it filters out single noisy samples. For a delta check, the averaged delta is

\[\overline{\Delta} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(x_k - x_{k-1}\right),\]

where \(n\) is the "number of consecutive delta values" and \(x_k\) are consecutive samples; the standard defines the delta as the difference of two consecutive values and compares the average of \(n\) such deltas with the thresholds.810 (Arithmetically the sum telescopes to \((x_n - x_0)/n\).)

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
Status Scope Values PMON function status whole subservice enabled, disabled; "enabled" when the subservice starts PMON status each definition enabled (1), disabled (0) PMON checking status each definition depends on the check type (table below)

The checking status is the established result. "Unchecked" and "invalid" mean that no checking status is currently established.12

Raw value Expected-value-check Limit-check Delta-check 0 expected value within limits within thresholds 1 unchecked unchecked unchecked 2 invalid invalid invalid 3 unexpected value below low limit below low threshold 4 - above high limit above high threshold

Sources: Tables 8-7 to 8-9 and 8-10 of the interface specification.56

docs.title: The monitoring process
docs.text:
At the end of each monitoring interval, for each enabled definition (and only while the PMON function is enabled), the subservice:

  1. computes the check validity condition, if conditional checking is supported;
  2. if it is false, sets the checking status to "invalid" and resets the repetition counter;
  3. otherwise performs the check with a newly sampled value and, if the last "repetition number" checks all produced the same result, establishes a new checking status;
  4. if the newly established status differs from the previous one, records a check transition in the check transition list and, if an event definition is attached to that transition, raises the event.17

For a limit-check, "above high limit" is established only when every one of the repeated checks was above the high limit, "below low limit" only when every one was below the low limit, and "within limits" when all passed; the delta-check works the same way with thresholds, and the expected-value-check distinguishes only "expected" and "unexpected".18

stateDiagram-v2
  state "unchecked (1)" as U
  state "invalid (2)" as I
  state "within limits (0)" as W
  state "below low limit (3)" as B
  state "above high limit (4)" as A
  [*] --> U : TC[12,5] add (PMON status disabled)
  U --> I : validity condition false
  W --> I : validity condition false
  B --> I : validity condition false
  A --> I : validity condition false
  U --> W : N consecutive passes
  I --> W : N consecutive passes
  U --> B : N consecutive below low
  I --> B : N consecutive below low
  U --> A : N consecutive above high
  I --> A : N consecutive above high
  W --> B : N consecutive below low
  W --> A : N consecutive above high
  B --> A : N consecutive above high
  A --> B : N consecutive below low
  B --> W : N consecutive passes
  A --> W : N consecutive passes
  W --> U : TC[12,2] disable, TC[12,7] modify, TC[12,15]
  B --> U : TC[12,2] disable, TC[12,7] modify, TC[12,15]
  A --> U : TC[12,2] disable, TC[12,7] modify, TC[12,15]

The diagram assembles requirements 6.12.3.5.1c (enabling the function resets enabled definitions to "unchecked"), 6.12.3.6.2g (disabling a definition), 6.12.3.6.3 (validity and repetition), 6.12.3.9.1h (a new definition starts "unchecked" and disabled) and 6.12.3.9.4g (a modification resets the definition) for a limit-check; N is the repetition number.1316172124

Inference

The standard does not say explicitly whether entering "invalid" because the validity condition is false is itself a recorded check transition, since requirement 6.12.3.6.3c.2 sets the status directly rather than "establishing" it. The out-of-limits rules (6.12.3.12) do treat "invalid" as a valid previous status.

Worked example (illustrative values)

A limit-check with low limit 10, high limit 50 and repetition number 3, starting "unchecked". Samples arrive at t1, t2, ...

Sample Value Result Established status Recorded transition t1-t3 30, 31, 29 pass x3 within limits unchecked -> within limits (time t1) t4-t6 55, 56, 48 above, above, pass (unchanged) none: the three results differ t7-t9 57, 58, 60 above x3 above high limit within limits -> above high limit (time t7); event raised if its ID is not 0 t10-t12 5, 4, 6 below x3 below low limit above high limit -> below low limit (time t10)

The transition time is the sampling time of the first of the samples that established the new status, and the reported value is the last sample used.19

docs.title: Reporting the check transitions: TM[12,12]
docs.text: The subservice reports the check transition list in a TM[12,12] check transition report, then removes the reported transitions from the list. A report is issued when either the declared maximum number of transitions is reached or the maximum transition reporting delay has elapsed since the first transition in the list. The delay is expressed in minimum-sampling-interval units; its default is declared, and if the capability exists TC[12,3] changes it.1920 Each notification carries: PMON ID, monitored parameter ID, check type, the expected-value mask (expected-value checks only), the parameter value that caused the transition, the limit crossed, the previous and new checking statuses and the transition time.19

docs.title: Out-of-limits: TC[12,10] and TM[12,11]
docs.text:
On request, TM[12,11] lists only the transitions that represent a violation:28

Check type Reported transitions Expected-value unchecked, invalid or expected value -> unexpected value Limit unchecked, invalid or within limits -> below low limit / above high limit; below low <-> above high Delta unchecked, invalid or within threshold -> below low / above high threshold; below low <-> above high threshold

Generating an out-of-limits report does not clear the check transition list; only a check transition report does.29

Printed typo

Requirement 6.12.3.12e.5 prints "within threshold" to "below high threshold"; from the structure of the list it is evidently meant to read "below low threshold". Figure 8-122 is also captioned "limit-checking" although it shows the delta-checking fields.2850

docs.title: Managing definitions: requests and rejection rules
docs.text:
All multi-instruction requests follow the PUS rule that valid instructions are executed even if others in the same request are rejected; each rejected instruction gives a failed start of execution notification through ST[01].1521

Request Effect Rejected when TC[12,15] enable the PMON function function enabled; every enabled definition reset to "unchecked" with its repetition counter; process starts (PMON statuses unchanged) - TC[12,16] disable the PMON function function disabled; process stops (statuses kept) a functional monitoring subservice has its FMON function enabled TC[12,1] enable definitions PMON status enabled, repetition counter reset (checking status unchanged) ID not in PMON list; used by a protected FMON TC[12,2] disable definitions PMON status disabled, checking status "unchecked" ID not in PMON list; used by a protected FMON TC[12,3] change max reporting delay new delay (capability by declaration) TC[12,5] add definitions added as "unchecked" and disabled list full; ID already used; parameter or validity parameter not accessible; high limit < low limit; high threshold < low threshold TC[12,4] delete all PMON list and check transition list emptied any definition used by functional monitoring; PMON function enabled TC[12,6] delete definitions removed ID unknown; definition enabled; used by an FMON TC[12,7] modify definitions repetition number, limits/mask/expected value/thresholds and event IDs replaced; status "unchecked"; counter reset ID unknown; monitored parameter differs; inconsistent limits or thresholds; used by a protected FMON; check type differs TC[12,8] report definitions TM[12,9] with each definition and its PMON status (N = 0 means all) ID unknown TC[12,13] report status of each definition TM[12,14] with ID and PMON status of every definition - TC[12,10] report the out-of-limits TM[12,11] -

Sources: clauses 6.12.3.5 to 6.12.3.12 and 8.12.2.7c.13141516202122232425262728 To change anything else in a definition, such as the check type, the standard recommends deleting it and adding a new one.24 If a subservice can add definitions it must also be able to delete them (TC[12,4] or TC[12,6]).21

The subservice exposes three observables: the number of free PMON list entries, the number of enabled definitions and the PMON function status.30

docs.title: Functional monitoring subservice
docs.text:
Functional monitoring watches the health of an on-board element (a software application, a hardware unit) by combining parameter monitoring definitions. A functional monitoring definition (in the FMON list) names a set of PMON definitions; when at least a "minimum PMON failing number" of them are in violation at the same time, the functional definition fails and its event is raised. A minimum of 1 behaves as a logical OR; a minimum equal to the number of members behaves as a logical AND. If the subservice does not support the parameter, 1 is used.3132

Element Present FMON identifier always Check validity condition (validity parameter ID, mask, expected value) if conditional checking is declared Event definition ID of the event to raise always Minimum PMON failing number if declared List of one or more PMON identifiers (maximum count declared) always

Sources: requirement 6.12.4.2.1.32

The subservice keeps an FMON function status, a per-definition FMON status (enabled/disabled), an FMON checking status ("unchecked" 0, "running" 1, "invalid" 2, "failed" 3) and, if protection is supported, an FMON protection status (unprotected 0, protected 1).3357 Whenever a member PMON definition establishes a new checking status, an enabled FMON that is not "failed" first evaluates its validity condition ("invalid" if false) and, if not invalid, counts its members in violation: reaching the minimum sets "failed" and raises the event, otherwise the status becomes "running".35

stateDiagram-v2
  state "unchecked (0)" as FU
  state "running (1)" as FR
  state "invalid (2)" as FI
  state "failed (3)" as FF
  [*] --> FU : TC[12,23] add (disabled, protected if supported)
  FU --> FR : member PMON status change, count below minimum
  FU --> FF : count reaches minimum, raise event
  FU --> FI : validity condition false
  FR --> FF : count reaches minimum, raise event
  FR --> FI : validity condition false
  FI --> FR : later evaluation, validity true, count below minimum
  FF --> FU : TC[12,20] disable (or TC[12,17] re-enable function)
  FR --> FU : TC[12,20] disable
  FI --> FU : TC[12,20] disable

The transitions follow requirements 6.12.4.4.1e, 6.12.4.5.1, 6.12.4.5.3g and 6.12.4.7.1i.34353639 A "failed" definition stays failed: the evaluation is skipped while the status is "failed".35

Inference

Requirement 6.12.4.5.1 evaluates the validity condition only when the status is not "failed", and counts violations only when it is neither "failed" nor "invalid". Read literally, nothing moves an "invalid" definition back to "running" when its validity condition becomes true again, except disabling and re-enabling it. The arrow FI to FR above is this wiki's assumption; it matches the rule Solar Orbiter's service 142 states explicitly (see below).92

Protection freezes a functional monitoring definition and its members: a protected FMON cannot be deleted, and the PMON definitions it uses cannot be enabled, disabled or modified.3337 The standard gives no rationale; guarding FDIR monitoring against accidental changes is the obvious use (this wiki's reading).

Request Effect Rejected when Capability TC[12,17] enable FMON function enabled; enabled definitions set "unchecked"; monitoring starts PMON function disabled minimum TC[12,18] disable FMON function disabled; monitoring stops (statuses kept) - minimum TC[12,19] / TC[12,20] enable / disable definitions FMON status set; disabling also sets "unchecked" ID unknown minimum TC[12,21] / TC[12,22] protect / unprotect protection status set ID unknown by declaration / implied by TC[12,21] TC[12,23] add definitions added "unchecked", disabled, protected (if supported) whole request: an ID already exists or appears twice; instruction: list full, unknown PMON ID, validity parameter not accessible by declaration TC[12,24] delete definitions removed ID unknown; enabled; protected implied by TC[12,23] TC[12,25] report definitions TM[12,26] with contents, protection and FMON status (N = 0 means all) ID unknown requires TC[12,23] TC[12,27] report status of each TM[12,28] with protection, FMON status and checking status - by declaration

Sources: clauses 6.12.4.4 to 6.12.4.9 and Annex C Table C-19.3436373839404158 The observables are the free FMON entries, the enabled definitions and the FMON function status.42

docs.text: PUS-C gives field types but leaves most widths to the mission ("enumerated", "unsigned integer"); "deduced" fields take the format of the monitored or validity parameter.49 The tables below restate the interface figures; the Solar Orbiter section draws real layouts with sizes. Type names follow the PUS parameter types.

docs.text: TC[12,1], [12,2], [12,6] and [12,8] carry N (unsigned integer) followed by N PMON IDs (enumerated); TC[12,8] uses N = 0 for "all". TC[12,19]-[12,22], [12,24] and [12,25] carry N and N FMON IDs; TC[12,25] uses N = 0 for "all". TC[12,3] carries one unsigned integer, the maximum reporting delay. TC[12,4], [12,10], [12,13], [12,15]-[12,18] and [12,27] have no application data.434445464748

docs.title: The 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text: The ECSS-E-ST-70-41C Rev.1 DIR1 draft (public review until 28 February 2025) keeps the service structure and adds two requests, TC[12,29] and TC[12,30], to start and stop logging check transitions in the check transition list (stopping also empties the list).59 It renames TC[12,10]/TM[12,11] "report the current out-of-limits", drops the separate mask from the check transition notification (the value is reported after the mask is applied), and changes the add request so that a faulty instruction rejects the whole ordered request.626061 The draft also proposes 2-byte PMON and FMON identifiers in its key element size table.63 Until published, these remain proposals; see PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A, 2003)
docs.text:
PUS-A organised the service around a monitoring list of parameters, each carrying a set of check definitions, instead of one definition per check.66 Per parameter it stored: whether its monitoring is enabled, an optional Boolean validity parameter, a monitoring interval in units of the mission constant <DIAG_MIN_INTERV>, and the check definitions.67 Each check definition held its type, its limits/thresholds/expected value, an optional Boolean check selection parameter (the check applies only while it is TRUE), a number of repetitions #REP and the report identifier (RID) of the event to generate.67 For delta checks #REP was the number of deltas averaged, not a repetition filter.67

A check definition was used only if monitoring was enabled at service level and for the parameter, the validity parameter was TRUE and the selection parameter was TRUE. Otherwise its status became "unchecked", "invalid" or "unselected" respectively - a status PUS-C dropped.68 Violations generated an event report TM(5,4) "high severity" containing the RID and no auxiliary data.69 One behaviour differs from PUS-C: from "within limits", samples alternating below and above the limits counted towards the repetition, and the new status was the result of the current sample.69 PUS-C requires all repeated results to be the same.18

Subtype PUS-A request or report Data (12,1) / (12,2) Enable / Disable Monitoring of Parameters N, N x Parameter#; N = 0 means service level (12,3) Change Maximum Reporting Delay delay in <DIAG_MIN_INTERV> units (12,4) Clear Monitoring List none; also disables monitoring at service level (12,5) Add Parameters to Monitoring List optional interval, Value #REP, Delta #REP, N; per parameter: Parameter#, optional Validity Parameter#, then NOL limit checks (selection parameter, low limit, RID, high limit, RID), NOD delta checks (same with thresholds), NOE expected-value checks (selection parameter, expected value, RID) (12,6) Delete Parameters from Monitoring List N, N x Parameter# (12,7) Modify Parameter Checking Information per check a signed Check Position: > 0 replace, < 0 delete, 0 add (12,8) / (12,9) Report Current Monitoring List / Current Monitoring List Report monitoring status, maximum reporting delay, the list (12,10) / (12,11) Report Current Parameters Out-of-limit List / report N; Parameter#, value, limit crossed, previous and current status, transition time (12,12) Check Transition Report same entry layout; transition time optional

Sources: clauses 15.3.1 to 15.3.9.7071727374757677 The minimum capability set was (12,1), (12,2) and (12,12); everything else, including support for validity parameters, several checks of a type per parameter and each check type, was an additional capability.78

Encoding PUS-A checking status value PUS-C raw value within limits / thresholds, expected value 0 0 unchecked 1 1 invalid 2 2 unselected 3 (removed) below low limit / threshold, unexpected value 4 3 above high limit / threshold 5 4

Sources: PUS-A §15.3.8 and PUS-C Tables 8-7 to 8-9.7656 The violation codes moved down by one, so the two issues are not wire-compatible here.

docs.title: Solar Orbiter
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's spacecraft interface follows PUS-A tailored by Airbus (see also How Solar Orbiter uses PUS and The Solar Orbiter MIB). In the service table of the TM/TC and packet structure ICD, service 12 is optional for payload software, with TC(12,1), TC(12,2) and TM(12,12) mandatory if implemented; all subtypes 1-12 are provided by the Central Software (CSW) of the on-board computer.79 Each CSW application hosts its own instance: a request applies only to the service 12 instance of the application addressed by the packet's APID. In TC(12,1) and TC(12,2), N = 0 enables or disables monitoring at service level and leaves each entry in its current state; N > 0 acts on the listed monitoring IDs (1 byte each).80

docs.title: Data structures
docs.text:
The ICD fixes the field sizes. Monitoring IDs are 1 byte (1-255), parameter IDs 4 bytes, and limits and expected values occupy fixed 8-byte and 4-byte fields, right-aligned and padded with zeros on the left when the parameter is shorter.8384

Unlike PUS-A's separate add and modify, Solar Orbiter's TC(12,5) adds or replaces: an existing monitoring ID is overwritten. Each entry has either a limit check (NOL = 1) or an expected-value check (NOE = 1); there is no delta check and no check selection parameter.8384 TC(12,7) modifies only the criteria (N, monitoring ID, NOL, 20-byte limit criteria, NOE, 10-byte expected-value criteria).85 The ICD recommends not using TC(12,4) "Clear Monitoring List" in flight.82 TC(12,3) carries a 1-byte delay counted in 8 Hz cycles (125 ms), where 0 means no transition report is generated.81

TM(12,11) has the same entry layout, and TM(12,9) echoes TC(12,5) preceded by the global monitoring status (1 byte) and the maximum reporting delay (1 byte).878688 The checking status uses the PUS-A codes: 0 valid (within limits or expected), 1 unchecked, 2 invalid, 4 unexpected or below low, 5 above high; 3 (unselected) is not used.8788 When a monitor triggers, the event report carries the monitoring ID, parameter ID, mask, value, limit crossed, both statuses and the transition time (CUC, 4 + 2 bytes).89

docs.title: Solar Orbiter in the MIB
docs.text:
The 2025 MIB release defines 254 service 12 commands and 32 service 12 packet definitions (the April 2020 release: 247 and 19).9497 The commands are addressed to seven APIDs. Decoding APID = 16 x PID + category with the ICD's allocation, 172/188/204/220/236/268 are the DMS, AOCS, payload, platform, system control and thermal control applications of the CSW (PID 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, category 12) and 1084 is METIS (PID 67).9094

Subtype Commands Applications (APID) 1 / 2 enable / disable 13 each 6 CSW applications (one each) + 7 METIS variants 3 change delay 7 6 CSW + METIS 4 clear, 6 delete, 8 report list, 10 report OOL 6 each 6 CSW 5 add 114 6 CSW (15-36 per application) 7 modify 83 6 CSW (13-18 per application)

Data: ccf grouped by type and subtype.94 Explore APID 172 or the generic add command ZCD00C05.

The MIB (see commanding in the MIB) shows how operators fill the "deduced" limit fields. Besides one generic command per application whose limits are 8-byte octet strings, there are typed variants such as ZCD2Z08A "Add param monitor high/low (uint8)": fixed areas zero-fill the leading bytes and an 8-bit editable limit sits at bit 200, the last byte of the 8-byte low-limit field - the right alignment the ICD asks for.95 Variants exist for uint8/16/32, sint16/32 and float4/8 limits and for uint/sint expected values. The thermal application adds sensor-specific modify commands such as ZTC2X02F "Mod Hi/Lo ANY PT-1000", whose limits are entered in degrees Celsius and converted to raw values by the 31-point command calibration CTC4Z102TC (cca).9596 The parameter identifiers use command parameters of category P in cpc: the operator types a telemetry parameter name and SCOS-2000 encodes its on-board identifier.95110 The system control application also carries predefined monitors such as "Define SWA_A_OFF S12" (ZCSX0019).94

Inference: repetition field width

In every MIB definition of the DMS add command (ZCD00C05, bits 96-127) and of the monitoring list reports, "Repetition Interval" is a 32-bit unsigned integer (PTC 3, PFC 14), making each entry 48 octets, while the ICD prints "Rep" as 1 byte (45-octet entry). The fixed-layout reports confirm 48-octet entries (consecutive monitoring IDs at byte offsets 19 and 67).9510183 The MIB reflects what the ground actually sends, so the ICD table is probably out of date on this point; the available sources do not say.

On the telemetry side the 2025 MIB defines TM(12,9), TM(12,11) and TM(12,12) for each of the six CSW applications at category 3 ("table generation") APIDs 163, 179, 195, 211, 227 and 259, and a TM(12,12) for METIS at APID 1075.9790 They are variable packets: for example SPID 14171 decodes a 16-bit count, then per entry the monitoring ID, the monitored parameter ID NCD0C095 flagged VPD_PIDREF = Y, the mask, the value and limit as deduced parameters (PTC 11), both statuses through the text calibration CCDT0011TX and a CUC time (PTC 9, PFC 17).98 VPD_PIDREF = Y tells SCOS-2000 to look the value up among the PCF_PID values to find the parameter.107108 Each deduced field names NCD0C095 in PCF_RELATED, which identifies the parameter whose value gives the on-board parameter ID, and carries a PCF_WIDTH of 64 bits (32 for the expected value); for a deduced parameter with a PCF_WIDTH the import ICD says the value is extracted from a fixed-width field rather than one sized by the parameter type. This matches the ICD's fixed 8-byte (4-byte) slots.98105 CCDT0011TX maps 0 VALID, 1 UNCHECKED, 2 INVALID, 4 BELOW_LOW, 5 ABOVE_HIGH and 6 OUT_OF_LIMIT; the identifier calibration PARAMIDTM has 19 803 entries.99 The value 6 is not a service 12 checking status in the ICD. It does appear there as the "check state type" "Out of Limit" (below low or above high) that a service 142 FMON can trigger on (TC(142,5)).8793

Inference: two ways to decode the monitoring list

The MIB also holds fixed-layout definitions of TM(12,9) at APIDs 1986-1990 (PID 124, inside the EGSE range 112-127 of the ICD), one set per application, keyed by the first monitoring ID at byte 19 (PIC PI1) and holding up to 85 entries each: AOCS 189 entries, payload 129, platform 228, system 47 or 49, thermal 216.10010190 The parameter names (PID11_S001_...) suggest ground-side decoders for the fixed 8-byte limit fields; the available sources do not explain these APIDs. The per-monitor S12 event definitions described below sit on APIDs 1954-1979 (PIDs 122 and 123), also inside that EGSE range.10290 The SCOS-2000 import ICD does not say where, inside a 64-bit PCF_WIDTH slot, a shorter deduced value is taken from. The Solar Orbiter ICD right-aligns it.10584

Monitoring violations reach the operators as ST[05] events. The MIB defines TM(5,3) event packets with event IDs 33537 "S12_Higher_Limit_Exceeded", 33538 "S12_Lower_Limit_Exceeded" and 33539 "S12_Unexpected_Value", each with the SCOS-2000 event severity A (alarm), and TM(5,2) warning variants 32512 (unexpected value), 32513 (lower limit) and 32514 (higher limit) with severity W.102109 In the ICD, TM(5,2) is a low-criticality (warning) and TM(5,3) a medium-criticality anomaly report, which needs a ground recovery action. PUS-A §15.2.3 instead prescribes a TM(5,4) high-severity report for monitoring violations.10369 In hexadecimal, 33537-33539 are 0x8301-0x8303, inside the ICD's TM(5,3) range for general application software events. 32512-32514 are 0x7F00-0x7F02, inside the TM(5,2) range that Annex 9 allocates to ESOC (this conversion is this wiki's).104 Besides one generic definition per CSW application (for example SPID 14425 for the DMS), 573 high-limit, 573 low-limit and 220 unexpected-value definitions distinguish individual monitors through PI2 at byte 18 (the monitoring ID), for example "S_DST1A_A DST TX-A Temp_HI".102

docs.title: Functional monitoring as service 142
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's service set is tailored from PUS-A (its capability sets refer to ECSS-E-70-41A), which has no functional monitoring, so this function is the private service 142.7965 It groups service 12 monitors into an FMON with OR or AND logic, can be protected, and is used for FDIR.91 Rules from the ICD: a disabled FMON becomes "unchecked"; enabling it makes it "running"; a false validity condition makes it "invalid"; after triggering it stays enabled in a failed state until disabled and re-enabled; and new FMONs start disabled and protected.92 Each FMON also has a timeout, in cycles, before it is re-enabled if the triggered event-action sequence has not done so.93 The MIB carries 59 service 142 commands (58 in April 2020): subtypes 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 for the six CSW applications and the SSMM (APID 492), 10, 12 and 13 for the CSW applications only, and 3, 4 and 14 only for the SSMM, whose own service 142 manages redundancy. It also carries the FMON event 45718 (a TM(5,3) on the system control application, alias "FMON_TRIGGERED" in the event-ID set CCDT0004TX).9410291

docs.title: The Herschel/Planck precedent
docs.text:
The Herschel/Planck Operations Interface Requirements Document required a single centralised on-board monitoring function in the CDMS, active by default, able to monitor any housekeeping parameter, with unique monitoring identifiers, partial modification of entries, and an event when an item changes state in either direction after the repetition count.111

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL); same counts on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, COUNT(*), GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CCF_APID)
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE IN ('12','142') GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT CCF_TYPE, COUNT(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE IN ('12','13','14','142') GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR, PID_TPSD
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE IN ('12','142');
SELECT c.CDF_ELTYPE, c.CDF_DESCR, c.CDF_ELLEN, c.CDF_BIT, c.CDF_GRPSIZE, c.CDF_PNAME,
       p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_CATEG, p.CPC_CCAREF
  FROM cdf c LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = c.CDF_PNAME
 WHERE c.CDF_CNAME IN ('ZCD00C05','ZCD2Z08A','ZTC2X02F') ORDER BY c.CDF_CNAME, CAST(c.CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT * FROM cca WHERE CCA_NUMBR = 'CTC4Z102TC';
SELECT v.VPD_POS, v.VPD_NAME, v.VPD_GRPSIZE, v.VPD_PIDREF, p.PCF_PTC, p.PCF_PFC, p.PCF_CURTX
  FROM vpd v JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = v.VPD_NAME WHERE VPD_TPSD IN ('14171','14172','14173');
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_WIDTH, PCF_RELATED FROM pcf
 WHERE PCF_NAME IN ('NCD0C095','NCD0C09B','NCD0C09D','NCD0C09H','NCD0C0B5','NCD0C0B6');
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR = 'CCDT0004TX'
   AND PAS_ALVAL IN ('32512','32513','32514','33537','33538','33539','45718');
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CCDT0011TX';
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'PARAMIDTM';
SELECT * FROM pic WHERE PIC_TYPE IN ('12','142');
SELECT l.PLF_SPID, COUNT(*), SUM(p.PCF_DESCR LIKE '%\_ID' ESCAPE '\')
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE CAST(l.PLF_SPID AS INT) BETWEEN 65909 AND 65925 OR l.PLF_SPID = '65954' GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PID_STYPE, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_EVENT, COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT PID_APID)
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '5'
   AND PID_PI1_VAL IN ('32512','32513','32514','33537','33538','33539','45718') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;
