docs.title: 9. PUS-A (2003): a different service under the same number
docs.text:
PUS-A's service 15 shares the subtypes 1 to 6 and the storage-selection idea with PUS-C, but the retrieval part is built differently.626364

  • Downlink options. Retrieved packets could be sent either in the same virtual channel as real-time data, wrapped in a "real-time" envelope of service 15 (the report (15,8)), or in a virtual channel dedicated to retrieval, "exactly as originally received by the packet store". A given service implements only one of the two.60 When wrapped, the service could use the large data transfer service (ST[13]) to send a long (15,8).60
  • Ordering. Packets are ordered by their time of arrival at the store; downlink can cover the whole store or a subset, for example a packet range.60
  • Store management - creation, deletion and attributes - was outside the standard.63
PUS-A subtype Name Application/source data (15,1) / (15,2) Enable / Disable Storage in Packet Stores N; Store ID x N (N = 0: all stores; N omitted if only one store) (15,3) / (15,4) Add / Remove Packets to/from Storage Selection Definition Store ID; N1 x {APID; N2 x {Type; N3 x Subtype}} (15,5) / (15,6) Report Storage Selection Definition / Storage Selection Definition Report Store ID / same layout as (15,3) (15,7) Downlink Packet Store Contents for Packet Range Store ID; Packet Set (0 All, 1 Between, 2 Before, 3 After); APID 1, Source Sequence Count 1; APID 2, Source Sequence Count 2 (15,8) Packet Store Contents Report N; N x any TM packet (the retrieved packets in storage order) (15,9) Downlink Packet Store Contents for Time Period Store ID; Time Span (0 All, 1 Between, 2 Before, 3 After); Storage Time 1; Storage Time 2 (15,10) Delete Packet Stores Contents up to Specified Packets Deletion Set (0 All, 1 Before); N; N x (15,11) Delete Packet Stores Contents up to Specified Storage Time End Time; N; Store ID x N (15,12) / (15,13) Report Catalogues for Selected Packet Stores / Packet Store Catalogue Report N; Store ID x N / see below

6263646566676869

Some rules worth knowing:

  • In (15,7), the boundaries are packets identified by APID and source sequence count, matched against the stored packets. If a lower boundary packet is missing, retrieval starts with the last earlier packet of the same APID (or the oldest packet); if an upper boundary is missing, it ends with the first later packet of that APID (or the end of the store). Whatever the criterion, retrieval ends at the latest with the last packet stored when the request arrived.65
  • (15,9) uses storage times: between (inclusive), at or before Storage Time 1, at or after Storage Time 1. Their format is fixed per destination application process.66
  • (15,10) and (15,11) delete up to a packet or up to a storage time; while deletion is running, new packets may already be written into the freed space.6768
  • The (15,13) catalogue gives, per store, the header fields (APID, source sequence count, service type and subtype, packet sub-counter) and storage time of the oldest and of the newest packet, the percentage filled and the percentage downlinked, the number of packets stored and the number downlinked.69

The capability sets: packet selection minimum = (15,1) and (15,2); storage and retrieval minimum = one downlink option (a dedicated VC or the (15,8) report) with (15,7) and/or (15,9); additional capabilities = (15,3)-(15,6), circular and bounded stores, time-stamping, (15,7), (15,9), (15,10), (15,11), (15,12)-(15,13).70 ECSS-E-ST-70-31C models the same service as a decision tree of tailoring choices, for example whether packets go down "in the same VC as real-time packets" (which enables (15,8)).7879

The general differences between the two issues are on PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: 10. The 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text:
The December 2024 draft ECSS-E-ST-70-41C Rev.1 DIR1 keeps the architecture but tightens the storage and retrieval subservice. It is a draft for review, not an approved standard.

  • A new clause on configuration asks each mission to declare the policy applied when the subservice starts or restarts, and requires storage, routing configuration and retrieval pointers to survive spacecraft mode transitions, such as safe mode or a processor reboot.71
  • Queuing of pending retrieval requests becomes mandatory, with a declared maximum queue length; if priorities are supported, each store gets a default retrieval priority, and the subservice may not limit how many retrievals share one priority level.72
  • Each store gets an open retrieval policy that says whether an open retrieval stays open after the last packet stored before the request has been sent, or suspends.72 Its raw values are 0 "suspend" and 1 "stay open"; TC[15,15] gains an open retrieval policy field, and a retrieval priority of 0 selects the store's default priority.7674
  • New requests: TC[15,10] "abort all requests to copy the packets contained in a packet store selected by time window" (no application data) and TC[15,41] "change the default retrieval priority of a packet store" (store ID, default retrieval priority).7375
  • Storage control per diagnostic parameter report structure is gone: the draft's packet selection subservice defines only the application process, housekeeping and event-blocking configurations, and TC[15,31], TC[15,32], TC[15,37] and TM[15,38] do not appear in its list of service 15 messages.10477

docs.title: 11. Playback telemetry and virtual channels
docs.text:
PUS-C has no separate playback packet: a retrieved packet is the original packet, routed to the virtual channel associated with its store.106 Virtual channels are system objects declared in the space-to-ground interface specification,56 and PUS-C names "separating real-time data from playback data" as one of their uses.57 The operability standard adds the rules that make this work on the ground: the assignment of VCs to data classes (real-time TM, playback, high-priority TM, critical event log) is agreed with the operator and not changed during the mission; real-time and deferred telemetry must be transmittable at the same time;81 packets of one APID arrive in generation order within a VC, except across separate retrievals from storage, where the original order is not always kept;82 the ground must be able to verify completeness whatever the route; and idle data must not be interleaved while there is real data to send, "e.g. during packet store dumps".83

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant G as Ground (MCS)
  participant S as Spacecraft ST[15]
  Note over S: between passes, reports are stored<br/>in packet stores (storage enabled)
  G->>S: TC[15,15] resume open retrieval (store P)
  S-->>G: TM[1,1] / TM[1,7] verification (real-time VC)
  S-->>G: stored packets of P, oldest first (playback VC)
  Note over G: end of pass approaching
  G->>S: TC[15,16] suspend open retrieval (store P)
  Note over S: next pass resumes with no gap or overlap
  G->>S: TC[15,9] start by-time-range retrieval [t1, t2]
  S-->>G: re-sent packets with storage time in [t1, t2]
  Note over S: by-time-range status back to disabled at t2

The sequence is an illustration composed by this wiki from the PUS-C rules quoted above, not a procedure taken from a mission document.

On the ground, the SCOS-2000 database import ICD says that SCOS-2000 has no specific processing for service 15 and no ground model of the on-board storage status or configuration. It cannot unpack packets encapsulated in (15,8) reports, but needs nothing special when stored packets arrive as they were stored.98 Its command verifier can use playback telemetry too, for example for delayed verification of time-tagged commands, as long as playback data arrive in chronological order.99 In the binary delivery format of the EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS) each TM packet record carries a virtual channel field, and each TC record holds separate acceptance and execution verification states for the real-time (VC0) and playback (VC1) streams.105 Solar Orbiter's data delivery ICD maps SCOS-2000 stream IDs to virtual channels: 1000 = VC0 real-time non-science, 1001 = VC1 playback non-science, 1002 = VC2 science and 1003 = VC3 file transfer, with 2000-2003 for the offline streams.97

docs.title: 12. Solar Orbiter: two implementations of service 15
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's TM/TC and packet structure ICD (SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079, issue 7) tailors PUS-A. Service 15 is implemented twice: in the central software (CSW) of the on-board computer, which manages the OBC mass memory (OMM), and in the software of the solid state mass memory (SSMM). The two implementations differ, and the ICD documents the CSW structures in detail while referring to an SSMM document for most SSMM structures. Both have packet selection, downlink ("playback") and storage maintenance functions; the CSW selects packets by process ID, type and subtype, the SSMM by APID.86

docs.title: 12.1 Who is who
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter splits the 11-bit APID into a 7-bit process ID (PID) and a 4-bit packet category.95 The service 15 traffic in the 2025 MIB uses:10696

APID PID / category Role 172 10 (OBC CSW, data management) / 12 (telecommand) CSW service 15 commands 163 10 / 3 (table generation) CSW service 15 reports 161 10 / 1 (TC verification) CSW failure reports TM[1,8] 167 10 / 7 (event generation) CSW events about stores and downlinks 162, 164 10 / 2 (high priority TM) and 4 (routine HK) "DMS OMM Packet Stores" housekeeping 492 30 (operational SSMM memory controller) / 12 SSMM service 15 commands 483, 484 30 / 3 and 4 SSMM reports and "SSMM PS Status TM"

The CSW stores are an enumerated 1-byte identifier, not a character string. The textual calibration CCDT0021TX names nine: 1 PS_HK, 2 PS_ACK, 3 PS_EVENT, 4 PS_DIAG, 5 PS_DUMP, 6 PS_REPORTS, 7 PS_PASS_HK, 8 PS_PASS_ACK and 9 PS_PASS_EVT.106 The SSMM stores are numbered 0-63.88106

docs.title: 12.2 The commands and reports in the MIB
docs.text:
The 2025 release defines 47 service 15 commands (17 for the CSW, 30 for the SSMM) and 7 service 15 report packets; the April 2020 release has the same subtypes and counts.106

Subtype CSW (APID 172) SSMM (APID 492) 1 / 2 ZCD00F01 / ZCD00F02 enable / disable storage ZSM00145 / ZSM00150 3 / 4 ZCD00F03 / ZCD00F04 add / remove packets to/from storage selection ZSM00155 / ZSM00160 5 / TM 6 - ZSM00165 report storage selection definition; TM(15,6) SPID 80019 9 ZCD00F09 downlink packet store contents for time period ZSM00170 10 ZCD00F0A delete packet store contents (complete) ZSM00175 delete up to specified packet 11 ZCD00F0B delete up to specified time ZSM00180 12 / TM 13 - ZSM00185 report catalogues; TM(15,13) SPID 80020 128 ZCD00F80 stop playback - 129 ZCD00F81 start playback of packet store contents ZSM00190 create file (packet store) 130-133, TM 134 - resize, delete, rename, list files; TM(15,134) SPID 80021 135-139 - stop downlink, set cyclic / non-cyclic, change default VC, change default priority 140 ZCD00F8C add SIDs to storage selection ZSM00240 / ZSM00241 find packet in PS (by time / by APID); TM(15,141) SPID 80022 142 ZCD00F8E report SID storage selection ZSM00245-ZSM00247 copy file, modes 0-2 143 / 144 - abort copy; reset copy TC queue 145 ZCD00F91 report storage routing definition table ZSM00256 unbounded downlink 146 - ZSM00257 delete content of non-cyclic PS 147 ZCD00F8D remove SIDs from storage selection ZSM00258 "Move Packet Store RP Position" 148 - ZSM00259 "Resynchronise Packet Store RP Position" 150 / 151 ZCD00F96 format PS memory on OMM / ZCD00F97 get format - 153 / 154 ZCD00F99 set PS playback pointer / ZCD00F9A change PS attributes - TM 152, 155, 156 Packet Store Format Report (SPID 14354), SID Storage Selection Definition Report (14180), Storage Routing Definition Table Report (14179), all on APID 163 -

10694

The CSW playback model uses two playback pointers per store: TC(15,129) "start playback" names a store and a pointer (0 = pointer 1, 1 = pointer 2) and downlinks from that pointer until stopped or until all data are read; TC(15,128) stops the current TC(15,129) or TC(15,9) and keeps the pointers for the next playback; TC(15,153) moves a pointer to a packet found by coarse time, APID and source sequence count.9093 Why two pointers exist is not stated in the available sources. TC(15,150) re-partitions the OMM in flight; the old contents are lost, packets routed to the memory during the operation are discarded, and newly created stores start disabled.93

The SSMM implementation has several features that PUS-C also standardises: stores created as "files" with a size in 1 MB sectors, a default virtual channel (0 = OBC VC3, 1 = OBC VC2) and a default downlink priority 0-15; read operations identified by a read ID; bounded and unbounded downlinks; copies between stores with a copy queue.909192106

Inference: TN issue 7 and the 2025 MIB disagree on a few subtypes

The ICD is not consistent about the subtypes of the two CSW configuration reports. The request sections announce TM(15,143) (SID storage selection) and TM(15,146) (storage routing table), and the TC(15,5)/TM(15,6) section also points to TC(15,145)/TM(15,146); the report sections and Table 5.1-1 call them TM(15,148) "SID Storage Selection Definition Report" and TM(15,149) "Storage Routing Definition Table Report"; both MIB releases define them as TM(15,155) and TM(15,156).889294106 Likewise, "remove SIDs from storage selection" is TC(15,147) in its section title but subtype 141 in its structure and in Table 5.1-1; the MIB uses 147.9294106 Finally, the ICD's general notes say that, unlike the SSMM, the CSW has no per-store virtual channel,86 while its CSW TC(15,154) and TM(15,152) structures list a VC field (value "VC1");93 the MIB definitions of these two (ZCD00F9A and SPID 14354) have no VC field, which matches the general note.106 The MIB is the database actually used for operations, so this wiki treats it as authoritative where they differ.

docs.title: 12.3 Real layouts from the MIB
docs.text:
The CSW TC(15,9) ZCD00F09 has a counter "Nb Packet Stores" (range 0-9) whose repeated group has four elements, so the time window is given per store:106101

This is the PUS-A (15,9) with the PUS-A "Time Span" codes, extended to several stores at once. In SCOS-2000 terms PTC 9 PFC 17 is a 6-octet CUC time (4 octets coarse, 2 octets fine) and PTC 9 PFC 15 a 4-octet coarse-only CUC time.102 The ICD adds that the storage times are coarse seconds with the sub-second field set to zero.89

The SSMM TC(15,9) ZSM00170 is a different structure that carries two ideas PUS-C also has - a virtual channel and a priority per retrieval:10689

Mode 1 "retrieve all packets since end of the last retrieval" is, in effect, an open retrieval, and the ICD notes that an unbounded read is mode 1 with the end time set to 0xFFFFFFFF.89

docs.title: 12.4 Which virtual channel carries the playback
docs.text:
The ICD allocates a fixed virtual channel (VC) to each class of downlink data and fixes the order in which the telemetry encoder serves them: VC4 real-time high-priority TM first, then VC5 critical event log (playback), VC0 real-time TM, VC1 playback from the OBC mass memory, VC2 and VC3 playback from the SSMM, and VC7 idle frames; VC2 and VC3 may carry compressed packets, VC0, VC1, VC4 and VC5 never do.103 The service 15 definitions follow this split:

  • The CSW stores, which live in the OBC mass memory, are played back on VC1:103 the ICD's TC(15,154) and TM(15,152) give "VC1" as the only VC value,93 and the MIB versions of both carry no VC field at all.106
  • The SSMM chooses between its two downlink channels per store (default VC in TC(15,129) "create file" and TC(15,138)) and per retrieval (TC(15,9)): 0 = VC3, 1 = VC2, calibrated in the MIB as CSMT0104TC "SM VCA OBC VC3" / "SM VCB OBC VC2".899091106
  • On the ground, the SCOS-2000 stream IDs of the mission keep the channels apart: 1000 = VC0 real-time non-science, 1001 = VC1 playback non-science, 1002 = VC2 science, 1003 = VC3 file transfer.97

Inference

Read together, these sources suggest that VC1 carries the platform playback from the nine CSW stores (housekeeping, acknowledgements, events, diagnostics, dumps and reports), while VC2 and VC3 carry what the SSMM stores. No single source states this end-to-end mapping.

docs.title: 12.5 Monitoring the stores
docs.text:
All service 15 reports of both implementations except the SSMM TM(15,141) are variable packets (they have a vpd definition). SCOS-2000 cannot use values extracted from variable packets in full telemetry processing (validity, limit checks, synthetic parameters), so such packets should carry special reports rather than regular housekeeping.100 Solar Orbiter accordingly monitors its stores through fixed housekeeping packets:106

  • "DMS OMM Packet Stores" - SPID 19565 (TM(3,25) SID 9 on APID 162) and SPID 19549 (SID 85 on APID 164) - with one enable/disable bit per CSW store and, for each of the nine stores, its ID, type (circular, bounded, undef), available space and size in bytes, start address, both playback pointer addresses, write pointer, first and last valid packet pointers, last downlinked packet pointer, two fields named ARPS1/ARPS2 and an on-board time named nextDwlTmPktObt.
  • "SSMM PS Status TM" - SPID 80246 (TM(3,25) SID 4 on APID 484) - with the number of created and active stores and, for each of 64 stores, flags named "PS Created", "S15 Bounded Active", "S15 Unbounded Act", "S13 Active" and "ST Enabled", the fill level (for example NSM00808 "PS0 Filled"), accumulated data and the bounded and unbounded read IDs.

Events and failure reports complete the picture: TM(5,1) EIDs 960 "Packet_Store_Down-link_Started" and 961 "Packet_store_Down-link_Ended"; TM(5,3) EIDs 33730-33732 for a full bounded store, an unknown store and a failed mass-memory write; TM(5,2) EID 17344 for an invalid checksum read from the downlink partition; and on APID 161 a block of TM(1,8) failure codes 3841-3900 such as 3842 "Selected store ID does not exist", 3871 "A downlink transfer is already in progress", 3879 "Playback pointer packet not found" and 3900 "packet store is enabled".106

Inference

The 38xx failure codes appear to be the CSW's service 15 error space: every description in that range concerns stores, storage control or downlinks. The ICD refers to a separate document ([RD8]) for the failure cases, which is not in this wiki's library.87 The MIB also defines 40 packets on APID 1985 that repeat CSW events with an extra identifier - for example EID 960 with the store ID as second key ("PS_HK Down-link Started" ... "PS_REPORTS Down-link Started"). APID 1985 (process ID 124, packet category 1) lies in the process-ID range 112-127 that the ICD reserves for EGSE, and category 1 is the one reserved for service 1 reports, not the event category 7,96 so these look like ground-side specialisations for display, not spacecraft packets.

SQL used (Solar Orbiter service 15) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL); same queries on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT CCF_TYPE, CCF_APID, COUNT(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '15' GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID, CCF_NPARS FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_TYPE = '15' ORDER BY CAST(CCF_STYPE AS INT), CCF_APID;
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR, PID_TPSD FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '15';
-- command layouts
SELECT c.CDF_CNAME, c.CDF_BIT, c.CDF_ELTYPE, c.CDF_ELLEN, c.CDF_GRPSIZE, c.CDF_PNAME,
       p.CPC_DESCR, p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_PRFREF, p.CPC_PAFREF
  FROM cdf c LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = c.CDF_PNAME
 WHERE c.CDF_CNAME IN ('ZCD00F09', 'ZSM00170', 'ZCD00F81') ORDER BY 1, CAST(c.CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CCDT0021TX', 'CCDT0022TC', 'CCDT0100TC', 'CSMT0104TC', 'CSMT0105TC');
SELECT * FROM prv WHERE PRV_NUMBR IN ('VCD00165', 'VSM00011');
-- housekeeping, events and failure codes
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid
 WHERE PID_DESCR LIKE '%store%' OR PID_DESCR LIKE '%playback%' OR PID_DESCR LIKE '%Down-link%';
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, l.PLF_OFFBY, l.PLF_OFFBI, p.PCF_DESCR, p.PCF_PTC, p.PCF_PFC, p.PCF_CURTX
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME WHERE l.PLF_SPID IN ('19565', '80246');
SELECT PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' AND PID_STYPE = '8'
   AND PID_APID = '161' AND CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) BETWEEN 3840 AND 3910;

docs.title: ST[17] Test
docs.text:
The simplest question an operator can ask a spacecraft is "are you there?". Service type 17 of the Packet Utilization Standard answers it. Its core is the are-you-alive connection test: the ground sends TC[17,1] to an application process, and if the process is alive and both the uplink and downlink routes to it work, a TM[17,2] report comes back. PUS-C adds an on-board connection test, in which one on-board process checks that another one responds, and the 2024 draft adds a variable-size version of the are-you-alive test for checking long telecommands.13516 The service type is meant to hold the test functions of a mission, most of which are mission specific.12 This page covers every message of the service in ECSS-E-ST-70-41C ("PUS-C", 2016), compares it with ECSS-E-70-41A ("PUS-A", 2003) and the Rev.1 draft, and shows how the real Solar Orbiter MIB defines connection tests for its central software, mass memory, star trackers and ten science instruments.

Where this page sits

The test reports travel like any other telemetry, and the test commands are verified like any other telecommand: see ST[01] request verification and PUS packet structures. On the ground, the expected reports are configured as verification stages, described in Command verification in the MIB.

docs.text: Item Value Service type 17<sup>7</sup> PUS-C name ST[17] test<sup>1</sup> PUS-A name Test service (clause 19)<sup>11</sup> Subservice type test (at least one per service; at most one provider per application process)<sup>2</sup> PUS-C message types TC[17,1], TM[17,2], TC[17,3], TM[17,4]<sup>8</sup> PUS-C minimum capability (Annex C) TC[17,1] and TC[17,3], each with its response TM[17,2] / TM[17,4]<sup>8</sup> PUS-A message types (17,1) Perform Connection Test, (17,2) report; both minimum, no additional capabilities<sup>13</sup><sup>14</sup> Rev.1 draft additions TC[17,5] / TM[17,6] variable size are-you-alive connection test<sup>16</sup><sup>17</sup> Observables none<sup>6</sup>

docs.title: 2. Why a test service
docs.text:
PUS-A placed the service under the concept of off-line testing: for troubleshooting or validation before use, an on-board unit or process can be run "off-line", outside any active control loop but with its normal outputs in telemetry, and each application process should offer a set of mission-specific end-to-end test functions under ground control. As a minimum, a standard "are you alive" function tests the end-to-end connection between the ground and an application process.15 ECSS-E-ST-70-31C describes the generic test in the same terms: a ground request makes the on-board test service generate a standard report, which confirms that the uplink and downlink routes work and that the process can do basic work, including telecommand processing and telemetry packet generation.19

The 2025 operability standard ECSS-E-ST-70-11C makes the capability a requirement under testability: the space segment must provide end-to-end tests of any on-board application process, exercisable under ground control, with an "are you alive" function as the example. The same clause asks for off-line operation of redundant equipment for testing, health checks of unused units before use, and test modes that neither disable fault management nor trigger it with off-line data.20

Mission requirements say the same. The Herschel/Planck operations interface requirements ask for an "are you alive" function between the ground and the data management system or any other on-board intelligent user, implemented as an "I am alive" response; the test between the data management system and an intelligent user is performed by the data management system itself, and the ground can ask it to start one.21 That last requirement resembles what PUS-C standardises as the on-board connection test TC[17,3] (section 4).

docs.title: 3. The are-you-alive connection test: TC[17,1] and TM[17,2]
docs.text:
Every test subservice provides it. A request TC[17,1] "perform an are-you-alive connection test" contains exactly one instruction, with no argument; the subservice answers with exactly one TM[17,2] "are-you-alive connection test report", which says only that the hosting application process is alive and has received the request.3 Both packets have an empty data field: the TC has no application data and the TM no source data.7

What the report proves is spelled out in two notes. The end-to-end connection is achieved "when the application process is alive and the communication to the application process is active"; and its reception on the ground confirms that the uplink and downlink routes between the ground and the process work and that the process performs a minimum set of functions.3

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant G as Ground (MCS)
  participant AP as Application process (APID n)
  G->>AP: TC[17,1] perform an are-you-alive connection test
  AP-->>G: TM[1,1] successful acceptance (if acceptance acknowledgement requested)
  AP-->>G: TM[17,2] are-you-alive connection test report (no source data)
  AP-->>G: TM[1,7] successful completion (if completion acknowledgement requested)
  Note over G: TM[17,2] received = uplink route, downlink route<br/>and the process itself are working

The verification reports in this diagram come from ST[01] and depend on the acknowledgement flags of the TC; PUS-C does not prescribe their order relative to TM[17,2], so the order shown is this wiki's illustration.

Inference: what a connection test does not prove

A TM[17,2] shows that a TC reached the process, was decoded and dispatched to the test subservice, and that the process could build and send a report. It says nothing about the process's other functions, and since the report has no data it cannot carry a test pattern. The variable-size test of the 2024 draft (section 6) fills that gap for the uplink path.

docs.title: 4. The on-board connection test: TC[17,3] and TM[17,4]
docs.text:
The second PUS-C test is between two on-board application processes: the one that hosts the test subservice and executes the request, and the one named in the request.5 The mission declares which application processes can be tested this way (the host itself is not in that list) and, for each of them, what counts as a successful test.4

  • TC[17,3] "perform an on-board connection test" carries exactly one instruction holding the identifier of the application process to test.5
  • A request naming a process outside the declared list is rejected with a failed start of execution notification.5
  • Otherwise the subservice tests the connection. If the declared criteria are met, it generates one notification carrying the tested process's identifier, sent as one TM[17,4] "on-board connection test report"; if not, it generates a failed completion of execution verification report instead.5
Message Data field Type TC[17,3] application process ID enumerated TM[17,4] application process ID enumerated

7

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant G as Ground
  participant H as Host process (test subservice)
  participant T as Target process (APID t)
  G->>H: TC[17,3] perform an on-board connection test (APID t)
  alt t not in the declared list
    H-->>G: TM[1,4] failed start of execution
  else t in the list
    H->>T: connection test (mission-defined mechanism and criteria)
    alt criteria satisfied
      H-->>G: TM[17,4] on-board connection test report (APID t)
    else criteria not satisfied
      H-->>G: TM[1,8] failed completion of execution
    end
  end

How the host actually tests the target is left to the mission: PUS-C only asks for the list and the success criteria to be declared.4 The diagram's mapping of the notifications to TM[1,4] and TM[1,8] follows the PUS-C report types of ST[01].

A discrepancy in PUS-C

Clause 6.17.4.2a says the capability to perform an on-board connection test "shall be declared", i.e. it is optional, while Annex C, Table C-25, marks TC[17,3] as "minimum".58 A mission tailoring PUS-C has to decide which reading applies. The 2024 Rev.1 draft aligns the annex with the clause: its Table C-25 marks TC[17,3] "by declaration".18

docs.title: 5. Message type catalogue
docs.text:
Type Name (PUS-C) Clauses Data field Applicability (Annex C) TC[17,1] perform an are-you-alive connection test 6.17.3 / 8.17.2.1 omitted minimum TM[17,2] are-you-alive connection test report 6.17.3 / 8.17.2.2 omitted response to TC[17,1] TC[17,3] perform an on-board connection test 6.17.4.2 / 8.17.2.3 application process ID (enumerated) minimum TM[17,4] on-board connection test report 6.17.4.2 / 8.17.2.4 application process ID (enumerated) response to TC[17,3]

87

The standard defines no observables for the test subservice.6 ESA's 2015 status presentation, which counts per clause and service type the discrepancy reports (DRRs) processed after the 2014 public review of the draft, gives ST[17] 2 DRRs, the fewest of any service type.22 The service is listed with all others in the PUS message type catalogue.

docs.title: 6. PUS-A and the 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text:
PUS-A defined only the end-to-end connection test: (17,1) "Perform Connection Test" with no application data, and (17,2) "Link Connection Report" with no source data; its capability table calls the report "Connection Test Report". Both are the minimum capability set, and no additional capability was defined.1314 PUS-A requires the report to be a one-shot report generated by the application process, and its reception to confirm that the routes work and that the process performs a minimum set of functions, which includes telecommand processing.12 ECSS-E-ST-70-31C lists no tailoring choices for this service.19

Topic PUS-A (2003) PUS-C (2016) Rev.1 draft (2024) Ground-to-process test (17,1) / (17,2) TC[17,1] / TM[17,2] (renamed "are-you-alive") unchanged Process-to-process test - TC[17,3] / TM[17,4] unchanged Variable-size test - - TC[17,5] / TM[17,6] Failure path not defined TC[17,3]: failed start (unknown APID) or failed completion (criteria not met) unchanged

The draft's variable size are-you-alive connection test (clause 6.17.5) is a declared capability. TC[17,5] carries an arbitrary connection test data string of variable length, up to the maximum telecommand length; the subservice returns the same string in TM[17,6]. The draft notes that this allows a test command of arbitrary length, in particular of the maximum telecommand length.16 Both data fields are a variable octet-string ("test data").17

The structure of a variable-length octet-string - a length field followed by that many octets, with the length PFC declared per application process - is defined in PUS-C clause 7.3.8.9 The draft is not an approved standard; Solar Orbiter solved the same problem with a private subtype (section 8.4).

docs.title: 7. Ground support in SCOS-2000
docs.text: The SCOS-2000 database import ICD says there is no specific processing of service 17 packets in SCOS-2000 and no specific limitation.23 In practice a connection test is an ordinary command whose expected TM[17,2] is not modelled by the service: the ground configures the acknowledgement flags and verification stages of the command like any other (see Command verification in the MIB), and the TM[17,2] report is an ordinary packet definition in pid.24

docs.title: 8.1 The tailoring
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter's TM/TC and packet structure ICD (SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079, issue 7) tailors PUS-A and calls service 17 "Connection Test". Its objective and description repeat the PUS-A text. The service is mandatory for all users: (17,1) and (17,2) are marked as implemented by the central software (CSW), the solid state mass memory (SSMM) software and the star tracker (STR) software, and as mandatory for payload software.2625 It defines four subtypes:25

Subtype Name (ICD) Data Notes TC(17,1) Perform Connection Test none test between the ground and an on-board application process; result in TM(17,2) and the TM(1,x) reports; a TM(1,8) only applies to the CSW, not the SSMM TM(17,2) Connection Test Report none sent when the test succeeds TC(17,3) Request Connection Test PID (enumerated, 1 octet); time-out (unsigned, 1 octet, seconds, > 0) asks the CSW to perform a connection test by TC(17,1) to the given process ID, with a time-out TC(17,128) Test Command of Maximum Length filler (TBD in the ICD) on reception a TM(17,2) is generated; filler parameters build a maximum-size packet; described as SSMM only

TC(17,3), which Table 5.1-1 marks for the CSW only, is Solar Orbiter's private counterpart of the PUS-C on-board connection test: the CSW tests another process by sending it a real TC(17,1).2625 Solar Orbiter's packet category table reserves category 7, "event generation", for service 5 events and TM(17,2), which is why every Solar Orbiter TM(17,2) has an APID ending in category 7.27

docs.title: 8.2 What the MIB contains
docs.text:
The 2025 MIB defines 27 service 17 commands and 17 TM(17,2) packets; the April 2020 release has the same counts.33 Solar Orbiter splits each APID into a 7-bit process ID (PID) and a 4-bit packet category, 12 for telecommands.28 The connection tests line up as follows:3327

Unit (process ID) TC(17,1) command TC APID TM(17,2) SPID - name TM APID (PID) Verification stages: CVS_INTERVAL (s) acceptance / completion OBC CSW (10) ZCD01101 Perform Connection Test 172 14178 Connection Test Response Report 167 (10) 14001 / 14007: 20 / 20 SSMM operational (30) ZSM00260 SSMM Perform Connection Test 492 80023 SSMM Connection Test Report 487 (30) 10001 / 10007: 20 / 20 SSMM controller A, debug (31) ZSM00261 508 80024 SSMA Connection Test Report 503 (31) 20 / 20 SSMM controller B, debug (32) ZSM00262 524 80025 SSMB Connection Test Report 519 (32) 20 / 20 Star tracker A (40) ZST17001 STR1 Connection Test 652 91172 STR1 Connection Test 647 (40) 20 / 20 Star tracker B (41) ZST27001 STR2 Connection Test 668 92172 STR2 Connection Test 663 (41) 20 / 20 EPD (50) ZID52505 TC 17,1 connection test 812 52006 TM 17,2 Connect test resp 807 (50) 60 / 60 EPD (54) ZID52307 17,1 SIS_PUS_CON_TST 876 52855 17,2 Connection Test Report 871 (54) 60 / 60 EUI (57) ZIU51001 EUI_TestCommand 924 51100 EUI_TstReport 919 (57) 4 / 4 MAG (63) ZIM01701 MAG Perform Connection Test 1020 50172 MAG Connection Test Report 1031 (64) 60 / 60 METIS (67) ZIT01701 Connection Test 1084 59450 TM(17,2) - Connection Test Report 1079 (67) 16 / 32 PHI (72) ZIP11010 performConnectionTest 1164 53072 PHI_connectionTestReport 1159 (72) 10 / 60 RPW (75) ZIW00012 DPU_TEST_CONNECTION 1212 55058 "Contains a connection test report." 1207 (75) 20 / 20 SoloHI (82) ZIHWTEST SWCONNTEST 1324 56335 OBC SoloHI Test Report Pkt 1335 (83) 60 / 180 SPICE (85) ZIC0C000 CONNECTION_TEST 1372 57300 SPICE Connection Test Report 1383 (86) 60 / 60 STIX (90) ZIX17001 STIX Perform Connection Test 1452 54330 STIX Connection Test Report 1447 (90) 20 / 60 SWA (95) ZIA58001 SWA_TC_CONN_TEST 1532 58061 SWA_TM_CT_REP 1591 (99) 20 / 20 EGSE range (121) ZYP66999 PSS Test TC 1948 - - 20 / 20

All verification stages open at release (CVS_START 0) and are report-based (CVS_SOURCE R); every service 17 command has CCF_ACK 9, i.e. acceptance and completion reports requested.3324 The SWA instrument's own database contains the same pair, ZIA58001 and SWA_TM_CT_REP (see the SWA explorer).32

Observations from the table:

  • For MAG, SoloHI, SPICE and SWA the TM(17,2) comes from a different process ID than the one the TC(17,1) was sent to (for example SWA: TC to PID 95, report from PID 99). The ICD allocates several process IDs to each instrument, so both are the same instrument.27
  • Only one TM(17,2) has any content: EPD's SPID 52006 defines a 16-bit parameter NID00048 "CRC" at byte offset 16, right after the 16-octet headers; all other TM(17,2) definitions are header-only.33
  • ZYP66999 "PSS Test TC" targets APID 1948, process ID 121, inside the 112-127 range that the ICD reserves for EGSE; the meaning of "PSS" is not stated in the available sources.2733

Inference

The differences in verification intervals (4 s for EUI, up to 180 s for SoloHI completion) presumably reflect how long each instrument's software needs to answer through the OBC, but the MIB records only the values, not the reasons.

docs.title: 8.3 TC(17,3) "Request Connection Test"
docs.text:
The CSW command ZCD01103 has two parameters:3325

The calibration CCDT0126TX "Process IDentifier reach" lists exactly the process IDs the CSW can reach for this test: the three SSMM processes (30-32), the two star trackers (40, 41) and the payload process IDs 50-104 - but not the CSW itself, matching the PUS-C rule that the host process is not in the list of testable processes.334 The MIB also defines a TM(5,2) event, EID 17472 "TM_Timed_Out_Connection_Request_Received_(TM_17-2)", on APID 167.33 Its exact trigger is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: 8.4 TC(17,128) "Test Command of Maximum Length"
docs.text: The SSMM variants ZSM00265, ZSM00266 and ZSM00267 consist of 59 fixed 32-bit areas, all 0xDEADDEAD: 1 888 bits, or 236 octets of application data.33 That is exactly the largest Solar Orbiter application data field: a TC packet data field holds at most 242 octets, made of the 4-octet data field header, 236 octets of application data and the 2-octet packet error control.29 With the 6-octet primary header the packet is 248 octets long, the maximum uplink length the ICD mentions elsewhere.30 The PSS variant ZYP66998 has the same length filled with 0xAAAAAAAA; the star tracker variants (ZST17128, ZSTX7128, ZST27128, ZSTX7228) are 14 elements, 416 bits (52 octets), with the values 0x5A, 0xFFFFFFFF and 0xFFFFFF.33 Although the ICD text describes TC(17,128) as SSMM-only, its service table marks the subtype "X" (implemented) for the SSMM and STR software and "O" (optional) for payload software, with no mark for the CSW, and the MIB defines both SSMM and STR variants.252633

docs.title: 8.5 Worked example: a TC(17,1) to the CSW, byte by byte
docs.text:
The bytes below are illustrative: the APID, service type, subtype, acknowledgement flags and header layout are real (from the MIB and the ICD), while the sequence count (0) and the source ID (120, the ICD's "direct commands" ground source) were chosen for the example. The CRC was computed by this wiki with the PUS CRC (polynomial \(x^{16}+x^{12}+x^5+1\), register preset to all ones).103133

Octets Hex Meaning 0-1 18 AC version 0, TC, secondary header present, APID 172 2-3 C0 00 stand-alone packet, sequence count 0 4-5 00 05 packet data field of 6 octets 6 19 PUS version 1, ack 1001 7-8 11 01 service 17, subtype 1 9 78 source ID 120 10-11 EA 91 CRC over octets 0-9

The whole packet is 12 octets, the minimum for a Solar Orbiter PUS telecommand, because it has no application data. For comparison, the same packet sent to the SSMM (APID 492) would be 19 EC C0 00 00 05 19 11 01 78 DA 0D, and a TC(17,3) asking the CSW to test process 30 (OP_SSMM) with a 10-second time-out, sequence count 1, would be 18 AC C0 01 00 07 19 11 03 78 1E 0A 8B 7F (all illustrative, CRCs computed by this wiki).33 The header fields are explained on PUS packet structures and a complete real command is built step by step in the TC worked example.

SQL used (Solar Orbiter service 17) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL); counts also on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID, CCF_NPARS, CCF_ACK FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_TYPE = '17' ORDER BY CAST(CCF_STYPE AS INT), CAST(CCF_APID AS INT);
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_DESCR, PID_DFHSIZE FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '17'
 ORDER BY CAST(PID_APID AS INT);
SELECT l.*, p.PCF_DESCR FROM plf l LEFT JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '17');
-- verification stages per command (cvp/cvs use generic COLn names: cvp COL1 = task, COL3 = stage;
-- cvs COL1 = CVS_ID, COL2 = type, COL3 = source, COL4 = start, COL5 = interval)
SELECT c.CCF_CNAME, s.COL2, s.COL1, s.COL4, s.COL5 FROM ccf c
  JOIN cvp v ON v.COL1 = c.CCF_CNAME JOIN cvs s ON s.COL1 = v.COL3 WHERE c.CCF_TYPE = '17';
SELECT c.CDF_CNAME, c.CDF_BIT, c.CDF_ELLEN, c.CDF_PNAME, p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_PRFREF, p.CPC_PAFREF
  FROM cdf c LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = c.CDF_PNAME WHERE c.CDF_CNAME = 'ZCD01103';
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR = 'CCDT0126TX' ORDER BY CAST(PAS_ALVAL AS INT);
SELECT CDF_CNAME, COUNT(*), SUM(CDF_ELLEN), GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CDF_VALUE) FROM cdf
 WHERE CDF_CNAME IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '17' AND CCF_STYPE = '128') GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_PI1_VAL = '17472';
-- swa-idb.sqlite
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_APID FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '17';

docs.title: ST[18] On-board operations procedure
docs.text:
An on-board control procedure (OBCP) is a small program that runs on the spacecraft itself: it sends telecommands, reads telemetry parameters, waits, tests and branches, much as a ground operator's procedure would, but without waiting for the ground. Service type 18 of the Packet Utilization Standard is the ground's handle on these programs. It loads them into an interpreter called the OBCP engine, starts and stops them, holds and resumes them step by step, passes them values while they run, and reports their state.12 ECSS-E-70-41A ("PUS-A", 2003) called it the on-board operations procedure service; ECSS-E-ST-70-41C ("PUS-C", 2016) calls it "on-board control procedure" in clause 6.18 and "on-board operations procedure" in its Annex C.4138 This page covers the PUS-C service completely - both subservices, the execution state machine, the observability levels, every message type and its data fields, the rejection rules - then the PUS-A service, the 2024 Rev.1 draft, SCOS-2000 support, and the OBCP commands and reports of the real Solar Orbiter MIB.

Where this page sits

OBCPs are one of several on-board automation tools. Commands released at a given time come from ST[11] time-based scheduling, commands triggered by an event from ST[19] event-action (which can itself start an OBCP), and fixed command lists from ST[21] request sequencing. OBCP files can be uploaded with ST[23] file management or, on PUS-A missions, ST[13] large packet transfer. Every request an OBCP releases is verified through ST[01].

docs.title: 1. At a glance
docs.text: Item Value Service type 18<sup>30</sup> PUS-C name ST[18] on-board control procedure (Annex C: on-board operations procedure)<sup>1</sup><sup>38</sup> PUS-A name On-board operations procedure service (clause 20)<sup>41</sup> Companion standard ECSS-E-ST-70-01, spacecraft on-board control procedures; see ECSS-E-ST-70-01C<sup>1</sup> Subservice types OBCP management (exactly one); OBCP engine management (at most one)<sup>4</sup> OBCP execution status inactive (0), active and running (1), active and held (2)<sup>9</sup><sup>37</sup> Observability levels no-observability (0), at-procedure-level (1), at-step-level (2), at-detailed-level (3)<sup>37</sup> PUS-C message types 18 requests and 2 reports, subtypes 1-9 and 12-22<sup>38</sup> PUS-C minimum capability one load request (TC[18,1], TC[18,13] or TC[18,19]), TC[18,3], TC[18,4], TC[18,12], TC[18,8]/TM[18,9], TC[18,21], TC[18,22]<sup>38</sup> PUS-A minimum capability (18,1) to (18,6) and (18,12)<sup>48</sup>

docs.title: 2. Why OBCPs exist
docs.text:
PUS-A explains the idea: besides standard services, a mission may have a set of procedures, loaded from the ground, that resemble the stepwise procedures executed on the ground. They can in principle also be started autonomously on board, for example when an event is detected. The language they are written in is out of scope, but each procedure must be built from logical steps so that it can be suspended and resumed at step level, and it can receive run-time parameters when started or while running.39 An event-action definition can start a procedure, which is how OBCPs become part of on-board fault management.40

The 2025 operability standard ECSS-E-ST-70-11C defines an on-board operations procedure as a monitoring and control procedure stored on board whose activation is under ground control.51 It requires that the spacecraft can execute ground-loaded and ground-controlled OBCPs, more than one at a time; that an OBCP can send any command available to the ground and read any engineering telemetry parameter available to the ground; and that OBCP execution can be prioritised, for example to favour fault management procedures when they conflict.52

Mission documents show what this buys in practice. For Herschel/Planck a "principle mode of operation" was the execution of pre-defined OBCPs started from the mission timeline, written in a Spacecraft Control Language and able to send commands, test parameters and branch; the document's example powers on an instrument, checks its current, waits for its boot, checks its housekeeping, sends it a time update and logs success with an event.53 The same document requires load, start, stop, suspend, resume, delete and dump of OBCPs, passing parameters without first suspending, inspecting OBCP data at any time, listing the stored OBCPs and managing multiple triggering of the same OBCP.54

docs.title: 3.1 Subservices, engine and host
docs.text:
PUS-C defines two subservice types. The OBCP management subservice is the interface to the engine and lets the ground control the on-board execution of OBCPs; the OBCP engine management subservice starts and stops the engine itself.23 A service has exactly one of the first and at most one of the second; if both are present they live in the same application process, and an application process hosts at most one provider of each.4 Each service is tied to exactly one OBCP engine and keeps an OBCP engine status ("running" or not), which exists even when there is no engine management subservice to change it.4

flowchart LR
  G["Ground"] -- "TC[18,x]" --> M["OBCP management<br/>subservice"]
  G -- "TC[18,21] / TC[18,22]" --> EM["OBCP engine management<br/>subservice"]
  F[("on-board files<br/>(ST[23])")] -. "load by reference" .-> E
  M --> E["OBCP engine<br/>(loaded OBCPs, status, traces)"]
  EM --> E
  E -- "requests released by OBCPs" --> X["executing services<br/>(any addressable APID)"]
  X -- "ST[01] verification reports" --> M
  E -- "observability events" --> EV["ST[05] event reporting"]
  P["on-board parameters"] -. "read" .-> E

The diagram is this wiki's summary of clauses 6.18.1-6.18.4. The mission declares which application processes the service may address; the host process is always among them, and all requests of the addressable processes may be used. When an OBCP releases a request, the service type and APID in the request decide who executes it; that executing service generates the verification reports, and sends them to the process hosting the OBCP service.5 The service must be able to read every on-board parameter accessible to the addressable processes.6

docs.title: 3.2 Code, arguments, parameters and steps
docs.text: The OBCP code is the form of a procedure that the engine can load and execute. An OBCP can declare arguments, values it expects when its execution starts, and parameters, values it expects to receive while executing; PUS-C refers to ECSS-E-ST-70-31 (see ECSS-E-ST-70-31C) for both. The OBCP itself, not the management subservice, checks that the values it receives are valid.2 Following ECSS-E-ST-70-01, a procedure can contain steps - sequences of source statements that are its smallest operational units - and each step is represented in the OBCP code by exactly one step identifier.2

docs.title: 3.3 What a mission must declare
docs.text:
Declaration Clause Maximum number of OBCPs the subservice can process at the same time 6.18.4.1.1a7 Total resources available to the engine for storing OBCPs 6.18.4.1.1b7 Whether the OBCP code checksum is verified at load time (algorithm per clause 5.4.4) 6.18.4.1.2a728 Which load capabilities exist (direct load, load by reference, load by reference and activate) and whether the ECSS-E-ST-70-01 loading policy is supported 6.18.4.4.110 Which observability levels are supported, or the fixed level if it cannot be configured 6.18.4.2.1a-b8 The event reporting subservice that issues observability events 6.18.4.2.2a8 The OBCP engine initialisation procedure 6.18.5.1.1f27 Addressable application processes 6.18.3.1a5

Each OBCP has a unique OBCP identifier; when an OBCP is loaded from a file, the identifier can drive the loading policy.7 PUS-C's general checksum clause 5.4.4 uses OBCPs as its example: a mission declares which subservice providers use each checksum algorithm, so that an OBCP file checksummed both by the OBCP service and by a memory service is checksummed the same way by both.28

docs.title: 4. Execution status and its state machine
docs.text:
For every OBCP loaded in the engine, the management subservice keeps an execution status: inactive, active and running or active and held. "Held" means suspended; an OBCP that is waiting for an event is still "running"; "active" covers both running and held.9 Raw values are 0, 1 and 2.37 The diagram, drawn by this wiki from the requirements of clause 6.18.4, shows which request moves an OBCP between states:

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Inactive: TC[18,1] direct-load / TC[18,13] load by reference
  [*] --> Running: TC[18,19] load by reference and activate
  Inactive --> Running: TC[18,3] activate
  Inactive --> Held: TC[18,14] activate and execute one step
  Running --> Held: TC[18,5] suspend (end of step)
  Held --> Running: TC[18,6] resume
  Held --> Held: TC[18,15] resume and execute one step
  Running --> Inactive: end of execution / TC[18,4] stop / TC[18,12] abort / TC[18,17] abort all
  Held --> Inactive: TC[18,4] stop / TC[18,12] abort / TC[18,17] abort all
  Inactive --> [*]: TC[18,2] unload / TC[18,20] / TC[18,22]
  Running --> [*]: TC[18,20] stop and unload / end of a TC[18,19] OBCP / TC[18,22] stop engine
  Held --> [*]: TC[18,20] stop and unload / TC[18,22] stop engine
  • An OBCP activated by TC[18,3] stays loaded (inactive) after it ends; one started by TC[18,19] is removed from the engine when it ends.1415
  • "Execute one step" runs the OBCP until the next step identifier is raised and then freezes it in "active and held".23
  • Stop and suspend act at the end of a step - the current one, or a named one - while abort freezes execution immediately.161821
  • Stopping the engine aborts every OBCP, unloads all of them and sets the engine status to "not running".27

docs.title: 5. Observability levels
docs.text:
How much the ground sees of a running OBCP is set by its execution observability level. Each mission declares which of the four levels it supports:8

Level (raw) Events raised no-observability (0) none at-procedure-level (1) one event each time the status changes to running (activation, resume), to held (suspend, completion of execution of a step) or to inactive (successful or failed completion, abort, stop) at-step-level (2) the procedure-level events plus one event for every step reached at-detailed-level (3) the step-level events plus mission-declared events, for example the start of an activity, a branch (an IF or a loop) or a statement

837

The events are issued as ST[05] event reports by a declared event reporting subservice; their auxiliary data include the OBCP identifier and the condition that caused the event. PUS-C notes that ground-initiated activations, suspensions, resumptions, stops and aborts can also be seen in the verification reports of the requests, and that procedure-level observability is especially useful for OBCPs started autonomously from within an OBCP.8 The level is chosen in the activation request (if selectable) and can be changed for active OBCPs with TC[18,16] "set the observability level of OBCPs", which takes effect immediately: the events of the new level are enabled and those of the old level disabled.1425 Its application data are N followed by N pairs of OBCP ID (fixed character-string) and observability level (enumerated).35

docs.title: 6. The requests in detail
docs.text:
Almost every ST[18] request contains exactly one instruction, and a faulty request is rejected as a whole with a failed start of execution notification (reported through ST[01]). The exception is TC[18,16], which can carry several instructions that are checked one by one.1125 Nearly every request is rejected if the engine is not running.1127

Request Engine running OBCP loaded OBCP state required Other rejection causes TC[18,1] direct-load yes must not be loaded - checksum fails; no resources11 TC[18,13] load by reference yes must not be loaded - file missing, not an OBCP file, policy file missing, checksum fails, no resources12 TC[18,19] load by reference and activate yes must not be loaded - as TC[18,13]; invalid observability level; resources to load and activate15 TC[18,2] unload yes yes inactive -13 TC[18,3] activate yes yes inactive invalid observability level; no resources14 TC[18,14] activate and execute one step yes yes inactive invalid observability level23 TC[18,4] stop / TC[18,20] stop and unload yes yes any -1617 TC[18,12] abort yes yes any -18 TC[18,17] abort all and report yes - - -19 TC[18,5] suspend yes yes active -21 TC[18,6] resume yes yes active -22 TC[18,15] resume and execute one step yes yes held -23 TC[18,7] communicate parameters yes yes active -24 TC[18,16] set observability level yes (whole request) yes (per instruction) active invalid level (per instruction)25 TC[18,8] report execution status yes - - -20 TC[18,21] start engine must not be running - - -27 TC[18,22] stop engine yes - - -27

docs.title: 6.1 Loading: TC[18,1], TC[18,13] and TC[18,19]
docs.text:
The service must offer at least one way to load an OBCP into the engine: direct load, where the request carries the code, or load by reference, where the code is already in an on-board file and the request names that file (or lets the ECSS-E-ST-70-01 loading policy pick the file).10

  • TC[18,1] direct-load an OBCP carries the OBCP identifier, the code and - if checksums are verified - the checksum, which the subservice checks before loading. The OBCP is then inactive, and the engine stores its identifier and checksum.11
  • TC[18,13] load an OBCP by reference carries the identifier and, unless the loading policy is used, the file path (repository path and file name). If checksums are verified, the code in the file is checksummed before loading (the checksum is in the file or a file attribute).127
  • TC[18,19] load by reference and activate an OBCP combines loading with activation; the OBCP is removed from the engine and its identifier freed when it ends.15

The field order and the 16-bit checksum are from Figure 8-196; the PFC of the length field is declared per application process, as for every variable-length octet-string.3029

Message Fields (in order) TC[18,1] direct-load an OBCP OBCP ID (fixed character-string); OBCP code (variable octet-string); checksum (bit-string, 16 bits, optional) TC[18,13] load an OBCP by reference OBCP ID (fixed character-string); file path = repository path (variable character-string) + file name (variable character-string), optional TC[18,19] load by reference and activate an OBCP OBCP ID; file path (optional); observability level (enumerated, optional); argument values (deduced, deduced presence) TC[18,2] unload an OBCP OBCP ID

303436

docs.title: 6.2 Unloading: TC[18,2]
docs.text: TC[18,2] "unload an OBCP" is mandatory whenever direct load or load by reference exists. It removes an inactive OBCP from the engine and cleans all information about it, so that its identifier can be reused.13

docs.title: 6.3 Activating: TC[18,3]
docs.text:
TC[18,3] "activate an OBCP" carries the identifier, the observability level (if selectable) and the argument values (if the OBCP has arguments). The subservice removes the execution trace of any previous run, enables the observability events of the chosen level, sets the status to "active and running" and starts the OBCP with its arguments.14

The presence and structure of the argument values follow from the definition of the OBCP named by the identifier - a "deduced" field in PUS terms.31 See PUS parameter types for deduced fields.

docs.title: 6.4 Stopping and aborting: TC[18,4], TC[18,20], TC[18,12] and TC[18,17]
docs.text:
• TC[18,4] stop an OBCP carries the identifier and a step ID; step ID 0 means "at the end of the current step". If the OBCP is running, the subservice waits until it finishes that step (or reaches the named step), freezes the remaining statements, clears pending "stop at step" settings and sets it inactive. When several stop requests are pending, the OBCP stops at the first of the steps reached.1631
  • TC[18,20] stop and unload an OBCP does the same and then unloads the OBCP and cleans the engine.1736
  • TC[18,12] abort an OBCP freezes the remaining statements immediately and sets the OBCP inactive.18
  • TC[18,17] abort all OBCPs and report freezes every OBCP, sets every active one inactive and answers with TM[18,18] aborted OBCP report: N followed by the N identifiers of the aborted OBCPs.1935

docs.title: 6.5 Suspending and resuming: TC[18,5], TC[18,6], TC[18,14] and TC[18,15]
docs.text:
TC[18,5] suspend an OBCP (identifier and step ID, 0 = end of current step) waits for the end of the step, freezes execution and sets "active and held"; several pending suspends act at the first step reached. TC[18,6] resume an OBCP (identifier only) unfreezes a held OBCP where it was frozen and sets it running; it must exist whenever suspend exists.21223132

TC[18,14] activate and execute one OBCP step activates an inactive OBCP exactly like TC[18,3] (same fields) but freezes it again as soon as the first step identifier event is raised. TC[18,15] resume and execute one OBCP step then advances a held OBCP to the next step identifier event and freezes it again.2334 Together they let the ground run an OBCP one step at a time.

Message Fields TC[18,4] stop / TC[18,5] suspend / TC[18,20] stop and unload OBCP ID (fixed character-string); step ID (enumerated; 0 = end of current step) TC[18,6] resume / TC[18,12] abort / TC[18,15] resume and execute one step OBCP ID TC[18,14] activate and execute one step OBCP ID; observability level (optional); argument values (deduced)

3132333436

docs.title: 6.6 Passing parameters: TC[18,7]
docs.text: TC[18,7] "communicate parameters to an OBCP" passes parameter values to an active OBCP: an identifier followed by the values, whose structure is driven by the OBCP's definition.2432 This is the PUS-C form of the PUS-A ability to change a running procedure's parameters.

docs.title: 6.7 Reporting: TC[18,8] and TM[18,9]
docs.text:
TC[18,8] "report the execution status of each OBCP" has no application data. TM[18,9] "OBCP execution status report" lists, for each loaded OBCP, its identifier, its checksum (if checksums are verified) and its execution status.2033

The required observables are the engine running status and, for each loaded OBCP, its identifier, its execution status and - when it is running or suspended - its current step.26

docs.title: 6.8 The engine: TC[18,21] and TC[18,22]
docs.text: TC[18,21] "start the OBCP engine" and TC[18,22] "stop the OBCP engine" have no application data. Starting runs the declared engine initialisation procedure and is refused if the engine is already running; stopping aborts all OBCPs, unloads them all and sets the status to "not running".2736 The engine management subservice has no observables.27

Subtypes 10 and 11 are not used in PUS-C (they were the PUS-A "active procedures" list).47 Clause 6.18.4.5.1a makes TC[18,8] a declared capability, whereas Annex C lists it as minimum; the 2024 Rev.1 draft keeps both readings.20386368 The engine requests are "minimum" in Table C-27, which applies only to a service that includes the optional engine management subservice.384 The PUS message type catalogue lists the service with all others. ESA's 2015 status presentation, which counts per clause and service type the discrepancy reports (DRRs) processed after the 2014 public review, gives ST[18] 41 DRRs, the fourth-highest count of any service type,55 and the 2014 status presentation lists "load an OBCP by reference" among the standard requests that operate with files, next to ST[23] file management.56

docs.title: 8. PUS-A (2003)
docs.text:
PUS-A identifies a procedure by a Procedure ID (a character string of mission-defined length) and its steps by Step IDs. Its statuses are "inactive", "running" and "held", the last two together being "active". The service keeps lists of the loaded and of the active procedures; progress can be reported with telecommand verification reports or with event reports.42

stateDiagram-v2

  Inactive --> Running: Start (18,3)
  Running --> Held: Suspend (18,5)
  Held --> Running: Resume (18,6)
  Running --> Inactive: Completion / Stop (18,4) / Abort (18,12)
  Held --> Inactive: Stop (18,4) / Abort (18,12)
  Inactive --> [*]: Delete (18,2)

This diagram redraws the states and transitions of PUS-A Figure 9.42

docs.title: 9. The 2024 Rev.1 draft
docs.text:
The December 2024 draft keeps the same subtypes, 18 requests and 2 reports,57 but changes several of them:

  • It adds that the service starts the OBCP engine automatically at initialisation; that the mission declares the list of event reporting subservices whose event reports the OBCP service can catch; and that it declares the configuration policy applied when the engine management subservice starts or restarts.585960
  • TC[18,2] becomes "unload OBCPs": N followed by N OBCP IDs, with N = 0 unloading all OBCPs. The whole request is rejected if any instruction names an OBCP that is not loaded or is active, and the instructions are executed in order.6162
  • TM[18,9] gains a step ID per OBCP: the step being executed for a running OBCP, the next step to execute for a held one. The subservice observables are redefined the same way.636466
  • TC[18,16] is now rejected as a whole if any of its instructions is faulty, and its instructions are executed in order.65
  • The engine management subservice gets observables, to be declared by the mission.67

It is a draft for review, not an approved standard.

docs.title: 10. Ground support in SCOS-2000
docs.text: The SCOS-2000 database import ICD states that SCOS-2000 has no specific processing of service 18 packets and no specific limitation for them.69 The generic PUS support covers what the service needs: variable-length octet strings (the OBCP code of a direct load) can be encoded in telecommands, although they are not decoded natively in telemetry; and deduced parameter fields - argument and parameter values - are supported, while a deduced data structure is not.7071 A command parameter of category P ("Parameter ID") lets an operator give an on-board parameter by its telemetry name, which SCOS-2000 encodes as the parameter's on-board identifier PCF_PID.7273

docs.title: 11.1 The tailoring
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter's TM/TC and packet structure ICD tailors PUS-A. An OBCP there is "an interpretable program" compiled on the ground with a dedicated compiler and uploaded with service 13 into one of the file partitions; the ground controls OBCPs mainly through service 18, but they can also start autonomously, for example on an event. Each OBCP has an "OBCP ID", an execution status inactive, running or held, and optional "Step ID" markers placed by the designer to report progress. OBCPs run in the OBCP interpreter in a dedicated RAM area: an OBCP is copied from its storage area (for example the OBC mass memory) into one of a limited number of execution slots, which is why the service offers an "auto-delete" option at the end of execution. An OBCP runs with "normal" or "emergency" priority, and only one emergency OBCP can run at a time.76

The service is implemented in the central software only (CSW, APID 172). It keeps the PUS-A subtypes 5-9 and replaces load, start, stop and delete by private subtypes (the last column is this wiki's mapping to PUS-C):8285

Subtype Name (ICD) Commands in the 2025 MIB Closest PUS-C equivalent TC(18,5) Suspend OBCP ZCD01205 TC[18,5] TC(18,6) Resume OBCP ZCD01206 TC[18,6] TC(18,7) Communicate parameters to OBCP ZCD2Z00F, ZCD2Z00G, ZCD2Z00H (1-, 2- and 4-byte values) TC[18,7] TC(18,8) / TM(18,9) Report List of OBCP / OBCP List Report ZCD01208 / SPID 14405 on APID 163 TC[18,8] / TM[18,9] TC(18,140) Load and Start an OBCP 38 commands: 3 generic (ZCD2Z00R/S/T) and 35 for named OBCPs TC[18,19] TC(18,141) Stop and Delete an OBCP ZCD0128D TC[18,20] TC(18,142) / TM(18,144) Set OBCP HKTM / OBCP TM ZCD0128E / SPID 14406 on APID 165 none

In the 2025 release there are 46 service 18 commands, against 32 in April 2020: the 14 new ones (ZCPX0001 to ZCPX0015, no ZCPX0013) are all TC(18,140) variants for specific OBCPs.85 For commands generated on board, the ICD reserves the TC source ID 15 for "OBCP" (set by the CSW).83

docs.title: 11.2 Real layouts
docs.text:
The generic ZCD2Z00R "Load and start OBCP (1-byte parameters)" shows the TC(18,140) structure as the MIB encodes it:8579

The named variants fix all or most of these fields. For example ZCD2Z01E "Load and start OBCP (SWA1)" is built only from fixed areas (CDF_VALUE in hexadecimal):8574

Bits Element Fixed value Meaning (from the ICD field definitions) 0-31 OBCP ID 61940010 OBCP 0x61940010 32 Emergency 0 normal priority 33 Auto-delete 1 delete from RAM when it ends 34-39 spare 0 40-55 NL 0002 two load-parameter bytes follow 56-63 load parameter 1 01 retry protocol 64-71 load parameter 2 02 two retries 72-87 NS 0000 no start parameters

The application data are therefore the 11 octets 61 94 00 10 40 00 02 01 02 00 00 (real values from the MIB, assembled by this wiki).8579 Per the ICD, with the retry protocol a load failure is reported only after the load has failed "number of retry + 1" times; and because auto-delete is set, the OBCP is deleted from RAM both when the start fails and when it completes.79

Inference: structured OBCP identifiers

The 35 named load-and-start commands use OBCP IDs whose upper 16 bits match the owner named in the command: 0x6022 DMS, 0x6032/0x6034 SSMM, 0x6042 STR, 0x6081 TTC, 0x6114 EUI, 0x6124 MAG, 0x6132/0x6134 METIS, 0x6142/0x6144 PHI, 0x6154 RPW, 0x6164 SOL(OHI), 0x6174 SPICE, 0x6184 STI(X) and 0x6192/0x6194 SWA, with the low bits numbering the procedures (for example SWA1, SWA2, SWA3, SWA5, SWA6 and SWA7 = 0x61940010, 0x61940020, 0x61940030, 0x61940050, 0x61940060 and 0x61940070). The ICD does not document an OBCP ID numbering scheme; this pattern is deduced from the MIB values.85

Some named OBCPs take start parameters. ZCPX0003 "Load and start OBCP (TTC2)" has 44 elements (8 fixed areas, 18 fixed and 18 editable parameters). Its fixed parameters of category P (the ICD's "Parameter ID" type; MIB description "Datapool parameter ID") hold telemetry parameter names such as NCPTT000 "TTC2_HPTM_RATE", which SCOS-2000 encodes as the parameter's on-board ID PCF_PID; each is followed by an editable value.857273

The other Solar Orbiter service 18 layouts are short:85778081

Command Elements (bits) TC(18,5) suspend, ZCD01205 / TC(18,141) stop and delete, ZCD0128D OBCP ID (32); Step ID (16, PTC 4 signed, range -1..32767: -1 immediate, 0 end of current step, other values OBCP-specific) TC(18,6) resume, ZCD01206 OBCP ID (32) TC(18,7) communicate parameters, ZCD2Z00H OBCP ID (32); N (16, range 0..45, group of 2); N x TC(18,142) set OBCP HKTM, ZCD0128E OBCP ID (32); TM status (1: 0 disabled, 1 enabled); TM period (15, number of 8 Hz cycles between two TM(18,144))

Note that Solar Orbiter's step ID -1 ("immediate") has no PUS-C counterpart in TC[18,4]/[18,5], where immediate termination is the separate abort request. The ICD adds that a suspend or stop is acknowledged when the target step is set, followed by an event report when it actually takes effect, and that "immediate" may wait for a running library call to end cleanly.7780

docs.title: 11.3 Reports and monitoring
docs.text:
TM(18,9) "OBCP List Report" (SPID 14405) is a variable packet repeating, for N OBCPs (16 bits), the OBCP ID (32), checksum (16), state (8), instruction pointer (16) and current step ID (16).8578 The state calibration CCDT0124TM reads 0 FREE, 1 LOADING, 2 INACTIVE, 3 RUNNING, 4 HELD; the ICD lists only values 1-4.8578 TM(18,144) "OBCP telemetry" (SPID 14406), produced cyclically when enabled by TC(18,142), carries the OBCP ID, checksum, N and N pairs of OBCP parameter ID (32 bits) and current value, the value being a deduced parameter (PTC 11) whose type follows from the parameter ID.8581 The housekeeping packets "DMS OBCP Details" (TM(3,25) SID 10 on APID 162, SPID 19566, and SID 86 on APID 164) show, among 847 parameter positions, the emergency queue entries with their OBCP ID and "IsStart&Load", "IsAutoDelete" and "IsUsed" flags.85

Events and failures (APIDs 167 and 161):85

Packet Key Name in the MIB TM(5,1) EID 1156 / 1158 / 1160 LOAD_OBCP_TC_Successful / START_OBCP_TC_Successful / LOAD_AND_START_OBCP_TC_Successful TM(5,1) EID 1152 / 1153 OBCP_Stopped_(OBCP_STOP) / OBCP_Suspended_(Suspend_Requested) TM(5,1) EID 1162 Request_To_Start_Emergency_OBCP_Is_Queued_in_Emergency_List TM(5,3) EID 33925 / 33929 LOAD_OBCP_TC_failure / LOAD_AND_START_OBCP_TC_failure TM(5,4) EID 50306 / 50311 OBCP_Stopped_(OBCP_ERROR) / START_OBCP_TC_failure TM(1,8) failure codes 4609-4646 e.g. 4611 checksum not coherent with OBCP file, 4612 OBCP ID invalid, 4614 no more free space in OBCP list, 4616 no more free space in OBCP storage area, 4622 no more free space in emergency queue, 4629 OBCP stop already set, 4646 OBCP load wrong protocol

The emergency queue explains a remark in the ICD: when an emergency load-and-start is queued because the emergency slot is busy, the execution acknowledgement is only sent when the start takes effect, and an event announces the delay (EID 1162).7985 The TC(18,140) commands are verified on acceptance and completion, all with stages that open at release and have a 20-second interval: stages 14001 and 14007 for the 24 commands that already existed in April 2020, stages 11 and 17 for the 14 ZCPX commands added since.8575 The MIB further defines events on APID 1985 that duplicate EIDs 1152 and 1160 with the OBCP ID as a second key (for example "OBCP SWA6 Started", key 0x61940060), and eight events on APID 183 (process ID 11, AOCS) whose names start with OBCP_STR1:.85

Inference

APID 1985 belongs to process ID 124, which the ICD reserves for EGSE, and has packet category 1 (reserved for service 1 reports) rather than the event category 7, so the per-OBCP "Started/Ended" packets look like ground-side display specialisations of the generic CSW events, not separate spacecraft packets.84 The MIB does not say so explicitly.

SQL used (Solar Orbiter service 18) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL); counts also on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID, CCF_NPARS FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_TYPE = '18' ORDER BY CAST(CCF_STYPE AS INT), CCF_CNAME;
SELECT c.CDF_CNAME, c.CDF_BIT, c.CDF_ELTYPE, c.CDF_ELLEN, c.CDF_GRPSIZE, c.CDF_VALUE, c.CDF_PNAME,
       p.CPC_DESCR, p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_CATEG, p.CPC_PRFREF, p.CPC_PAFREF
  FROM cdf c LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = c.CDF_PNAME
 WHERE c.CDF_CNAME IN ('ZCD2Z00R', 'ZCD2Z01E', 'ZCD0128D', 'ZCD0128E', 'ZCD01205', 'ZCD2Z00H', 'ZCPX0003')
 ORDER BY 1, CAST(c.CDF_BIT AS INT);
-- OBCP IDs of the named load-and-start commands
SELECT c.CCF_CNAME, c.CCF_DESCR, d.CDF_VALUE FROM ccf c JOIN cdf d
    ON d.CDF_CNAME = c.CCF_CNAME AND d.CDF_BIT = '0'
 WHERE c.CCF_TYPE = '18' AND c.CCF_STYPE = '140' ORDER BY d.CDF_VALUE;
SELECT * FROM prv WHERE PRV_NUMBR IN ('VCD00173', 'VCD00251', 'VCD00159', 'VCD00238');
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CCDT0124TM';
SELECT v.*, p.PCF_PTC, p.PCF_PFC FROM vpd v JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = v.VPD_NAME
 WHERE v.VPD_TPSD IN ('14405', '14406') ORDER BY 1, CAST(v.VPD_POS AS INT);
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid
 WHERE PID_DESCR LIKE '%OBCP%' ORDER BY 1, 2, CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT);

docs.title: ST[19] Event-action
docs.text:
The event-action service (service type 19) lets the ground attach an action to an on-board event. The ground loads a list of event-action definitions, each pairing an event with a telecommand request. When an associated event reporting subservice raises that event and the definition is enabled, the event-action subservice releases the stored request at once. The request can, for example, reconfigure hardware directly, start an on-board control procedure or start a request sequence.1 PUS-C calls the subservice "an extension of the ground monitoring and control".1 Together with on-board monitoring, whose events "can be sent to ground and caught on-board, e.g. by an event-action subservice", it is the standard building block of on-board failure detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR).2

This page covers the ECSS-E-ST-70-41C ("PUS-C", 2016) service clause by clause, compares it with ECSS-E-70-41A ("PUS-A", 2003) and the 2024 Rev.1 public-review draft, explains how the SCOS-2000 MIB models the embedded telecommand, and documents the real event-action definitions in the Solar Orbiter database.

Where this page sits

The packet headers that carry these messages are on PUS packet structures. The field types (enumerated, unsigned integer, TC packet) are on PUS parameter types. Event definitions themselves belong to ST[05] Event reporting. Version differences across the whole standard are summarised on PUS-A vs PUS-C, and all message types on the message type catalogue.

docs.title: 1. The service at a glance
docs.text:
PUS-C defines a single subservice type for ST[19], the event-action subservice.1 Annex C lists its eleven message types and their capability class: minimum (always present), by declaration (present if the mission declares it), implied by or requires another capability, or response to a request.3

Message type Name Capability System clause / interface clause TC[19,1] add event-action definitions minimum 6.19.8.1 / 8.19.2.1 TC[19,2] delete event-action definitions by declaration 6.19.8.3 / 8.19.2.2 TC[19,3] delete all event-action definitions by declaration 6.19.8.4 / 8.19.2.3 TC[19,4] enable event-action definitions minimum 6.19.7.1 / 8.19.2.4 TC[19,5] disable event-action definitions minimum 6.19.7.2 / 8.19.2.5 TC[19,6] report the status of each event-action definition by declaration 6.19.8.5 / 8.19.2.6 TM[19,7] event-action status report response to TC[19,6] 6.19.8.5 / 8.19.2.7 TC[19,8] enable the event-action function minimum 6.19.6.1 / 8.19.2.8 TC[19,9] disable the event-action function minimum 6.19.6.2 / 8.19.2.9 TC[19,10] report event-action definitions requires TC[19,1] 6.19.8.6 / 8.19.2.10 TM[19,11] event-action definition report response to TC[19,10] 6.19.8.6 / 8.19.2.11

In addition, clause 6.19.8.2a requires at least one of TC[19,2] and TC[19,3], and Annex C marks this rule as "implied by" TC[19,1].34

    E1["event occurrence<br/>(APID, event definition ID)"]
  end
  subgraph EA["ST[19] event-action subservice"]
