docs.title: Command verification in the MIB
docs.text: Releasing a telecommand is only the start. The flight control team needs to know, for every command, whether the ground station received it, whether it was radiated, whether the spacecraft received the frame, whether the addressed application accepted the packet, and whether the action actually took effect. SCOS-2000 tracks each command through these verification stages and shows their status in the command history. The ground stages are driven by the NCTRS and the COP-1 protocol. The on-board stages, called command execution verification, are defined per command in three MIB tables: cvs (what a stage is), cve (which telemetry values prove it) and cvp (which stages a command has).12 This page explains those tables, how SCOS-2000 combines them with the reports of PUS ST[01] request verification, and how the Solar Orbiter MIB uses them. The command definitions themselves are on Commanding in the MIB.

docs.title: Two kinds of check
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 supports two kinds of verification check:1

  • Report-based checks rely on dedicated telemetry packets that report the success or failure of an execution stage, that is the PUS Service 1 reports.
  • Parameter-based checks compare the value of one or more monitoring parameters with a criterion, for example "the converter status reads ON".

A stage is defined once in cvs and can be shared by many commands; the many-to-many relationship with commands is resolved by cvp. A parameter-based stage owns one or more expressions in cve, which are ANDed. cve has a second job: it names the parameters that a command is expected to change, so their status consistency checking can be suspended while the command executes.2 Verification of sequences is foreseen by the table design but not supported by SCOS-2000 at issue 7.0.1

erDiagram
    CCF ||--o{ CVP : "CVP_TASK"
    CVS ||--o{ CVP : "CVP_CVSID"
    CVS ||--o{ CVE : "CVE_CVSID (source V only)"
    PCF ||--o{ CVE : "CVE_PARNAM"
    CDF ||--o{ CVE : "echo value (CVE_INTER C)"
    PID }o--o| CVS : "CVS_SPID"

The relationships follow the field definitions of the three tables in ICD 7.0.61113

docs.title: The stages of a command's life
docs.text:
The ICD names five stages that an interlock can wait for: reception at the ground station (R), uplink, also called radiation or transmission (U), on-board reception, also called transfer and the final uplink verification (O), application acceptance (A) and completion (C). When commanding in BD mode O is automatically handled as U; the Rosetta/Mars Express command history likewise marks on-board reception as applicable only in AD mode.336 The on-board side adds start of execution and up to ten progress steps.6

Stage Name in TC history Evidence (summary) Defined in Release R Command passed PTV and was handed to the NCTRS (or SLE user) SCOS-2000 itself Ground station reception (1st uplink stage) G (CRV) Station TC front-end reports the command received NCTRS Uplink / radiation (2nd uplink stage) T (CSV) Station TC front-end reports the command sent NCTRS On-board reception / transfer (3rd uplink stage, AD only) O (CUV) CLCW verification of the transfer frame COP-1 via NCTRS Application acceptance A (CAV) TM(1,1)/(1,2) or parameter check cvs type A Start of execution SS TM(1,3)/(1,4) or parameter check cvs type S Progress step 0–9 1122… TM(1,5)/(1,6) (step 0 only) or parameter check cvs type 0–9 Completion of execution C (CEV), CC TM(1,7)/(1,8) or parameter check cvs type C

The history letters and abbreviations come from the command history descriptions of the Rosetta/Mars Express control system and of the EDDS external user ICD (version 24.0), which also shows that the execution stages are tracked twice, once from real-time and once from playback telemetry.3637 The SCOS-2000 EGSE manual describes the three uplink acknowledgements as returned by the ground station or SCOE TC front-end on reception, on sending in BD mode, and on the spacecraft's confirmation in AD mode.9 CRV, CSV, CUV, CAV and CEV are the stage abbreviations of the Rosetta/Mars Express document (the EDDS ICD uses only the letters); CUV is described there as the CLCW verification of the transfer frame.3436

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as SCOS-2000<br/>(releaser, verifier)
    participant N as NCTRS / station
    participant SC as Spacecraft
    S->>S: static and dynamic PTV
    S->>N: release (stage R)
    N-->>S: station reception (G)
    N->>SC: CLTU radiated
    N-->>S: uplink (T)
    SC-->>N: CLCW in TM (AD mode)
    N-->>S: on-board reception (O)
    SC-->>S: TM(1,1) or (1,2): acceptance (A)
    SC-->>S: TM(1,7) or (1,8): completion (C)
    SC-->>S: housekeeping: parameter-based check (C)

The diagram is this wiki's summary of the stages listed above; which reports a command really produces depends on its acknowledgement flags and on the on-board software.522

docs.title: Background: PUS Service 1
docs.text:
ECSS-E-ST-70-41C defines ST[01] request verification with three subservices: routing and reporting, acceptance and reporting, and execution reporting. The acceptance subservice checks a request before it is passed to the service that executes it; the execution reporting subservice issues reports on behalf of that service when it notifies start, progress or completion of execution.21 Each request carries four flags that ask for the successful acceptance, start, progress and completion reports; a failure is always reported.2223

Report PUS-C name Generated when TM[1,1] successful acceptance verification report acceptance passed and the acceptance flag is set TM[1,2] failed acceptance verification report acceptance failed (always) TM[1,3] / TM[1,4] successful / failed start of execution flag set / always TM[1,5] / TM[1,6] successful / failed progress of execution flag set / if configured for the request type TM[1,7] / TM[1,8] successful / failed completion of execution flag set / always TM[1,10] failed routing verification report a routing check failed (PUS-C only)

232425

In ECSS-E-ST-70-41C the flags occupy the 4-bit acknowledgement field of the TC secondary header: bit 3 for acceptance, bit 2 for start, bit 1 for progress and bit 0 for completion.26 PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A), which Solar Orbiter follows, uses the same assignment and states that the Ack field also tells the ground which stages to expect, so it can show "packets uplinked but not yet verified".28 In the MIB the default value of the field is CCF_ACK, a decimal number from 0 to 15; 9 means acceptance plus completion.5

Every report starts with a copy of the request's packet ID and packet sequence control, which together identify the request. Failure reports add a failure code and optional data; progress reports add a step number.2729

The Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD defines these reports with 2-byte packet ID, 2-byte sequence control and, for failures, a 2-byte failure ID followed by optional parameters.32 PUS-A defines six standard acceptance failure codes: 0 illegal APID, 1 incomplete or invalid length, 2 incorrect checksum, 3 illegal packet type, 4 illegal packet subtype, 5 illegal or inconsistent application data.29 The service in general is covered on ST[01] Request verification.

docs.title: How SCOS-2000 uses Service 1 reports
docs.text:
Appendix C of the ICD states how the SCOS-2000 verifier handles Service 1:16

  • It extracts the four bytes that echo the TC packet header (packet ID and sequence control) from each Service 1 packet and uses them to find the command instance. The four bytes must be at the same position in all type 1 packets.
  • The mapping of subtypes to stages is static configuration (subtype 1 is typically success of the acceptance stage) and is the same for every command of the mission.
  • Progress reports (subtypes 5 and 6) can only feed progress step 0; further steps must be parameter-based.
  • The failure code of negative reports is ignored; only the subtype tells the verifier that a stage failed.
flowchart TD
    A["TM packet of service type 1 arrives"] --> B["Read 4 echo bytes:<br/>TC packet ID + sequence control"]
    B --> C{"Released command<br/>with this ID?"}
    C -- no --> X["Not used for verification"]
    C -- yes --> D["Map subtype to stage<br/>(mission-wide static table)"]
    D --> E{"Stage in the command's<br/>verification profile (cvp)?"}
    E -- no --> X
    E -- yes --> F{"Success or failure<br/>subtype?"}
    F -- "1, 3, 5, 7" --> P["Stage PASSED"]
    F -- "2, 4, 6, 8" --> Q["Stage FAILED<br/>(failure code ignored)"]

The flowchart restates the Appendix C rules; the exact matching order inside the verifier is not stated in the available sources.16

Inference

Because the request ID in a report does not contain the source of the request, PUS-C notes that the destination ID of the report's secondary header is needed to identify the request uniquely.27 SCOS-2000 as described in ICD 7.0 matches only on the 4 echo bytes. A ground system that runs several command sources with independent sequence counters for the same APID could therefore see ambiguous matches; how SCOS-2000 avoids this is not stated in the available sources. The Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD asks for the TC sequence count to be maintained per APID and Source ID, which makes such duplicates possible in principle on that mission.30

docs.title: cvs: verification stages
docs.text:
cvs has one record per stage; the same stage may be used by many commands.6

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* CVS_ID Number(5), M Unique stage identifier, 0–32767 2 CVS_TYPE Char(1), M Stage in the execution profile: A application acceptance, S start of execution, 0–9 progress step n, C completion 3 CVS_SOURCE Char(1), M R based on TM report packets; V based on monitoring parameter values checked against cve 4 CVS_START Number(5), M Seconds after release (after execution for time-tagged commands) before the verification window opens 5 CVS_INTERVAL Number(5), M Seconds; length of the sampling interval used to compute the overall verification window 6 CVS_SPID Number(10) SPID of the TM packet whose arrival closes the stage after the window (future extension; source V only) 7 CVS_UNCERTAINTY Number(5) Seconds; stage-specific window replacing the default window of the TC SPACON; -1 keeps the default -1

67

Two constraints shape every profile. The verifier processes TM(1,5) progress reports only for stage 0, so a report-based progress stage can only have CVS_TYPE = 0; this is a limitation of the SCOS-2000 Service 1 implementation.6 And a command may have at most one stage of each CVS_TYPE, so only one acceptance stage and one completion stage.13

Without CVS_SPID, a parameter-based stage closes as soon as any valid sample of any of its parameters arrives with a time stamp during or after the window closure time. That is why the ICD recommends taking all parameters of one stage from the same TM packet.710

The window formula is not in the ICD

The ICD says that CVS_INTERVAL is used to calculate the overall verification window "as specified in [AD-2]", the SCOS-2000 Commanding SRD (SRD-0002). That document is not among the available sources, so the exact formula is not stated here.718

docs.title: cve: verification expressions
docs.text:
cve has one record per check. All checks of one stage are ANDed, and only stages with CVS_SOURCE = V may have checks.1011

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* CVE_CVSID Number(5), M Stage (CVS_ID, source V) 2* CVE_PARNAM Char(8), M Monitoring parameter with a numerical raw value, processed by the TM model (in plf or synthetic) 3 CVE_INTER Char(1) R raw values (for synthetics, the OL output); E engineering values (calibrated parameters only); C CVE_VAL names a command parameter whose value is echoed, CVE_TOL raw R 4 CVE_VAL Char(17) Expected value, decimal if raw; for C, the command parameter name (first instance if it repeats). Only used if CVE_CHECK = B 5 CVE_TOL Char(17) Tolerance: the check passes if the parameter lies within CVE_VAL ± CVE_TOL. Must be null for engineering checks of status parameters 6 CVE_CHECK Char(1) B used for verification and for status consistency checking (the value becomes the new expected value at the end of the window); S only suspends status consistency checking, and only alongside a B check of the same stage B

1112

The ICD adds several consistency rules:101112

  • The validity of the parameter is part of the check: a check passes only if the parameter is valid and satisfies the criterion.
  • For a parameter subject to status consistency checking (PCF_USCON = Y) the representation in CVE_INTER must match that of its out-of-limits checks (OCF_INTER); echo checks then require raw OOL checks.
  • A parameter must use the same representation in every cve record; engineering is allowed only if all its records use it.

Echo verification (CVE_INTER = C) compares telemetry with the value the operator actually gave to a command parameter, for example a commanded set point, so one stage definition can serve every value of the command.11 Status consistency checking compares the valid value of a parameter, typically a status affected by commanding, with a reference value that SCOS-2000 maintains from the predicted or detected effect of commands.8 The cve records of a command tell SCOS-2000 which parameters to leave alone during the window and, with CVE_CHECK = B, what the new reference is afterwards. See Monitoring checks.1012

docs.title: cvp: verification profiles
docs.text:
cvp attaches stages to commands, one record per stage of a command.13

# Field Type Meaning Default 1* CVP_TASK Char(8), M Command (CCF_CNAME) or sequence (CSF_NAME) 2* CVP_TYPE Char(1) C command; S sequence (not supported) C 3* CVP_CVSID Number(5), M Stage (CVS_ID); at most one per CVS_TYPE

Since SCOS-2000 R4.0 an operator can disable a report-based stage when loading a command, by clearing the corresponding acknowledgement flag. The mechanism can only switch off stages that are already in the profile; it cannot add one. Every command for which the receiving application generates a Service 1 report must therefore have the matching stage in cvp.13

The interlock stage of a command (CCF_ILSTAGE, overridable per sequence element with CSS_ILSTAGE) is checked against the profile on import: if it asks for an execution stage the profile does not have, the importer replaces it with the highest stage that applies.3

docs.title: Stage status and the verification window
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 reports each stage with a status. The Rosetta/Mars Express data delivery ICD encodes it in a 16-bit word per stage with exactly one bit set (bit 0 is the least significant bit); an all-zero word means the stage did not apply, because it was not in the database or was disabled before release.35

Only PASSED, FAILED and UNVERIFIED are final; a command is complete when all its stages are final.35

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> IDLE: command released
    IDLE --> PENDING: window opens (CVS_START)
    PENDING --> PASSED: report or parameter check succeeds
    PENDING --> FAILED: failure report or check fails
    PENDING --> UNKNOWN: window closes, no applicable TM
    UNKNOWN --> UNVERIFIED: consolidated by controllers
    PENDING --> TIMEDOUT: CUV only, no CLCW in time
    PENDING --> ASSUMED: CUV only, later CAV or CEV passes
    TIMEDOUT --> ASSUMED: later CAV or CEV passes
    PASSED --> [*]
    FAILED --> [*]
    UNVERIFIED --> [*]

The state diagram is this wiki's rendering of the status definitions; the source defines the statuses, not the transitions.35 The EDDS TC report, whose ASCII layout follows the Command History application of SCOS-2000 5.⅗.4, lists more statuses: Fail, Unverified, Unknown, Pending, Time-out, Success, Idle, Assumed Passed, Affected, Uncertain Successful, Uncertain Failed and Superseded, plus "D" for execution stages of a time-tagged command disabled at execution and "DELETED" for a time-tagged command deleted before execution.37

For time-tagged commands CVS_START counts from the execution time instead of the release time.6 SCOS-2000 supports this delayed verification from live and from playback telemetry, but playback data must arrive in chronological order for parameter-based verification to work.17

Verification data stays with the command

The command history must remain readable after the MIB has changed. In the Solar Orbiter control system each released command is archived as a SCOS-2000 TC packet that holds the static MIB information (mnemonic, parameters, verification details) and the dynamic status of the verification checks. A separate packet with SPID 200 stores the PTV/CEV details of each command, such as the expected values of parameter-based checks.38 See Mission archives and EDDS.

docs.title: Interlocks
docs.text:
An interlock holds back further commanding, within its scope, until the chosen stage of the interlocking command has been verified; the ICD calls this the WAIT state. Its scope is CCF_ILSCOPE (or CSS_ILSCOPE in a sequence) and its stage CCF_ILSTAGE (or CSS_ILSTAGE):314

Scope Effect (ICD 7.0) EDDS TC report label G Interlocks the whole system Wait-Fail Global L Interlocks only the local command source Wait-Fail Local S Interlocks local commanding of the command's subsystem Wait-Fail Subsystem Local B Interlocks global commanding of the command's subsystem (not listed) F Local source, only on verification failure (no WAIT state) Fail-Only Local T Subsystem-local, only on verification failure Fail-Only Subsystem Local N No interlock

337

The ICD's recommendation for BC frames illustrates the use: a global interlock at the uplink stage ensures that no further command leaves before the AD set-up directives have gone through.4 Within a group or block of a sequence, the scopes G and L are allowed only on the last command.14 Group and block semantics are on Command sequences and parameter sets.

docs.title: Solar Orbiter: the verification set-up
docs.text:
The September 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB has 206 stages, 171 expressions and 10,697 profile records, the same number of stages and expressions as the April 2020 release (which had 10,277 profile records).4142

Kind CVS_TYPE / CVS_SOURCE Stages Acceptance by report A / R 16 Completion by report C / R 23 Completion by parameter check C / V 167

41

No start or progress stage exists, which matches the Solar Orbiter rule that the start and progress acknowledgement bits are always zero.4131 The same ICD describes 0001 as "acceptance success or failure" with no TM(1,7) or TM(1,8), and 1000 as execution success or failure with no TM(1,1) or TM(1,2), so on Solar Orbiter the two remaining bits select which report stages exist at all, not only whether success is reported.31 Every stage opens its window immediately (CVS_START = 0) and no stage overrides the default window (CVS_UNCERTAINTY is never set). All 167 parameter-based stages use CVS_INTERVAL = 60 s and each is used by exactly one command.41

docs.title: Profiles agree with the acknowledgement flags
docs.text:
Grouping the 5,454 commands by the shape of their profile and by their default Ack value shows a consistent design:41

Profile Commands CCF_ACK Typical commands Acceptance report + completion report 5,225 9 (1001) almost all PUS commands Acceptance report + completion by parameters 78 1 (0001) TC(2,128) power commands such as ZPW04604 Completion by parameters only 89 null 88 CPDU (HPC1_TC) commands and REIN_TTR No verification 62 0 (21) or null (41) 6 NIS throw events, 7 FDIR TC-file executions, 8 instrument commands (7 EUI ZID…, ZIM02028), 37 CPDU commands, RESET, SETVR, TC_ONLY, UNLOCK

Two more cvp records point at a command, ZCSD2005, that does not exist in ccf.41 The CPDU commands have no data field header and hence no Ack field, so they cannot ask for Service 1 reports; they can only be verified through telemetry.4130

docs.title: Report-based stages
docs.text:
The report-based stages come in pairs, one for acceptance and one for completion, mostly per instrument or unit. In seven pairs (11/17, 10001/10007, 14001/14007, 51901/51907, 58901/58907, 60001/60007, 70001/70007) the last digit mirrors the PUS subtype of the success report, 1 or 7; the others are numbered consecutively.41 Units are identified from the command APIDs with the Solar Orbiter process ID allocation.33

Stages (A / C) Interval A / C (s) cvp users Command APIDs (process ID: unit) 11 / 17 20 / 20 2,263 / 2,185 172, 188, 220, 236, … (platform CSW), 1532 (SWA), 1948, … 14001 / 14007 20 / 20 1,524 172, 188, 204, 220, 236, 268 (platform CSW) 10001 / 10007 20 / 20 112 492, 508, 524 (30–32: SSMM) 50001 / 50002 60 / 60 126 1020 (63: MAG) 51901 / 51907, 51917, 51927 4 / 4, 60, 36,000 122 / 99, 4, 19 924 (57: EUI) 52000 / 52001 60 / 60 39 812 (50: EPD) 52700 / 52701 60 / 60 73 876 (54: EPD) 53001 / 53002, 53003, 53004 10 / 60, 120, 180 200 / 193, 5, 2 1164 (72: PHI), 796 54001 / 54002, 54003, 54004 20 / 60, 1,800, 9,999 99 / 81, 2, 16 1452 (90: STIX), 796 55000 / 55001 20 / 20 138 1212–1308 (75–81: RPW) 56000 / 56001 60 / 180 102 1324 (82: SoloHI) 57490 / 57491 60 / 60 91 1372 (85: SPICE) 58901 / 58907 20 / 20 199 1532 (95: SWA) 59001 / 59003, 59004 16 / 32, 4,561 126 / 125, 1 1084 (67: METIS) 60001 / 60007 and 70001 / 70007 20 / 20 45 each 652 and 668 (40, 41: star trackers A and B)

4133

Several instruments have more than one completion stage, differing only in the interval, so that long-running commands get a longer window: EUI's 51927 allows 36,000 s (10 hours) for 19 commands, STIX's 54004 allows 9,999 s for 16.41

CVS_SPID on report-based stages

The ICD says CVS_SPID may only be given for parameter-based stages and is irrelevant for report stages.7 In the Solar Orbiter MIB it is empty on every parameter-based stage, but set on 20 report-based ones. Some values point at the instrument's own TM(1,1) and TM(1,7) packets (MAG 50001/50010, STIX 54001/54013), others at SPID 20000, which is an unrelated TM(5,1) event packet "CPS_Activation_Ended", and stages 14001/14007 carry 0.41 The SWA instrument database gives its two stages 58901/58907 the same value 20000.45 The Herschel/Planck System database (HPSDB) forced the field to null on output.39

Inference

Since the ICD calls CVS_SPID a future extension and the values found are inconsistent, the field is most likely ignored by the Solar Orbiter control system for report-based stages. This is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: How failure reports are identified
docs.text:
The verifier only looks at the subtype of a failure report, but the MIB still describes each failure code separately. The packet identification criteria (pic) give TM(1,2) and TM(1,8) an additional identification field at byte 20 of the packet, 16 bits wide, while TM(1,1) and TM(1,7) need none. Across 29 report APIDs the MIB defines 29 TM(1,1), 274 TM(1,2), 29 TM(1,7) and 1,477 TM(1,8) packets.44 For example the platform report APID 161 (process ID 10, category 1) has TM(1,2) SPID 14068 "Illegal CCSDS packet version number" for code 256 and SPID 14064 "Illegal packet type" for code 257.4433 See Monitoring in the MIB for pid and pic.

Inference

Byte 20 is where the failure ID follows the 4 echo bytes in the Solar Orbiter report layout, so each failure code becomes its own packet type with a readable description. Operators therefore see why a command failed even though the verifier itself ignores the code. This reading combines the pic data with the report layout; neither source states it.

docs.title: Parameter-based examples
docs.text:
ZPW04604 "PCDU A BDR1_C1 SwitchON" (the worked example on Commanding in the MIB) has stages 11 (acceptance report) and 32. Stage 32 is a completion check with one expression: NPWD0753 "IFA_BDR1_Conv1_ST" must equal raw 1 with tolerance 0, within a 60 s window.43 Its CCF_ACK is 1, so the spacecraft sends only the acceptance report and the completion is proven by telemetry.43

ZBC04001 "Select PM A EEPROM Image 1", a CPDU command, has a single stage 9000: parameter NCDD05GE "PM A Image select status" must read IMAGE_1 in engineering form.43

Stage 9082, used by ZBC06011 "RIU Ctrl-A On", has two expressions, ANDed: NCD2Z003 "OBCA RIU A Status A" and NCD2Z00U "OBCA RIU A Status B" must both read On. Four stages of the MIB have two expressions; the other 163 have one.4341

Stage 84, for ZPW04300 "PCDU A EOC 25.200 V Set", checks the synthetic parameter NPWSX001 for raw 1. Its OL source returns 1 when at least two of three voltage readings (NPWD5012, NPWD5013, NPWD5014, engineering values) lie strictly between 25.1 and 25.3, a two-out-of-three vote that a single cve comparison could not express.43 Of the 171 expressions, 25 use dynamic synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = D) and 146 use status parameters acquired from telemetry (PCF_NATUR = R, PCF_CATEG = S); 90 are engineering and 81 raw; all use CVE_CHECK = B, none uses echo verification, and none of the parameters is status-consistency checked.41 See Synthetic parameters and the OL language.

docs.title: Turning verification off in sequences
docs.text:
Sequence elements can disable the CEV checks of a command with CSS_CEV = Y.15 Solar Orbiter does this for 17 elements, all in two sequences that define on-board TC files: AACC362D "Define SNAFU TCF v02" and ATTC810F "Def LossOfUL REC TCF v02".41

Inference

Commands written into an on-board TC file are stored for later execution, not executed at once, so their normal execution checks would fail or time out. Disabling CEV for exactly these elements fits that explanation, which is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: A verification timeline (illustrative)
docs.text:
The sequence below shows how ZPW04604 would be tracked when released at time T in AD mode. The stage definitions are real; the times of the replies are invented for the illustration, and the exact window lengths depend on the Commanding SRD formula and TC SPACON settings, which are not in the available sources.437

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as SCOS-2000
    participant N as NCTRS
    participant SC as Solar Orbiter
    Note over S: T: release (R) after PTV
    S->>N: TC request
    N-->>S: T+1 s: station reception (G)
    N-->>S: T+2 s: radiated (T)
    Note over S: stage 11 (A) and stage 32 (C)<br/>windows open at T (CVS_START = 0)
    SC-->>N: CLCW reports frame accepted
    N-->>S: on-board reception (O)
    SC-->>S: TM(1,1) on APID 161, echoing 0x18AC + sequence control
    Note over S: stage 11 PASSED<br/>(20 s interval)
    SC-->>S: HK packet with NPWD0753 = 1
    Note over S: stage 32 PASSED<br/>(60 s interval)

Because CCF_ACK = 1, no TM(1,7) is expected. The report APID 161 in the diagram is derived from the Solar Orbiter rule that Service 1 reports use packet category 1 of the commanded process ID (10), and the MIB indeed defines TM(1,1) on APID 161 as SPID 14181 "Telecommand Acceptance Report - Success".3344 Setting the completion flag on the stack would not add a report-based completion stage, because the acknowledgement mechanism can only disable stages that are already in the profile.1343

docs.title: Commanding in the MIB: commands and their parameters
docs.text: A telecommand in SCOS-2000 is never typed bit by bit. The operator picks a mnemonic such as ZPW04604 from a command stack. The system looks the mnemonic up in the Mission Information Base (MIB) and builds the packet from three kinds of definition: a reusable packet header template, the command's own structure (an ordered list of fixed areas and parameters), and the characteristics of each parameter (type, calibration, allowed range, default value). This page goes through every commanding table of the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001, issue 7.0) field by field, explains why each field exists, and shows how the real Solar Orbiter MIB uses it. Verification of executed commands is covered in Command verification in the MIB. Command sequences and parameter sets are covered in Command sequences and parameter sets.137

docs.title: The commanding tables at a glance
docs.text:
The ICD groups the commanding data into packet headers, commands, sequences, verification, parameter sets, (de-)calibrations and range checks. The command definition (ccf) is the central entity, and many-to-many relationships are resolved with mapping tables (cdf maps commands to parameters, cvp maps commands to verification stages, psm maps commands to parameter sets).12

Table One record per Key fields Role ICD clause tcp TC packet header TCP_ID Names a header template §3.3.3.1.1 pcpc Header parameter PCPC_PNAME Named variable header field and its value format §3.3.3.1.2 pcdf Element of a header PCDF_TCNAME, PCDF_BIT Bit layout of each header template §3.3.3.1.3 ccf Command CCF_CNAME Identity, routing, header values and default behaviour of a command §3.3.3.2.1 dst APID (optional) DST_APID Destination of commands of one APID (EGSE use) §3.3.3.2.1.1 cpc Command parameter CPC_PNAME Type, display, calibration, range set and default of a parameter §3.3.3.2.2 cdf Element of a command CDF_CNAME, CDF_BIT, CDF_GRPSIZE Ordered structure of the application data field §3.3.3.2.3 ptv Static PTV check PTV_CNAME, PTV_PARNAM Telemetry condition that must hold before release §3.3.3.2.4 cca / ccs Curve / point CCA_NUMBR; CCS_NUMBR, CCS_YVALS Numerical (de-)calibration of command parameters §3.3.3.6.1–2 paf / pas Alias set / alias PAF_NUMBR; PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALVAL Textual (de-)calibration §3.3.3.6.3–4 prf / prv Range set / range PRF_NUMBR; PRV_NUMBR, PRV_MINVAL Allowed values or ranges §3.3.3.7.1–2

Fields marked as keys in the ICD (a * after the field number) may appear in only one record per combination of values, and an "M" marks a mandatory field that may not be left null.3

erDiagram
    TCP ||--o{ PCDF : "defines layout"
    PCPC ||--o{ PCDF : "names header field"
    TCP ||--o{ CCF : "CCF_PKTID"
    CCF ||--o{ CDF : "has elements"
    CPC ||--o{ CDF : "CDF_PNAME"
    CCF ||--o{ PTV : "static PTV"
    PCF ||--o{ PTV : "PTV_PARNAM"
    PCF ||--o{ CDF : "CDF_TMID dynamic default"
    CCF }o--o| DST : "by APID"
    CPC }o--o| CCA : "CPC_CCAREF"
    CCA ||--|{ CCS : "value pairs"
    CPC }o--o| PAF : "CPC_PAFREF"
    PAF ||--|{ PAS : "aliases"
    CPC }o--o| PRF : "CPC_PRFREF"
    PRF ||--|{ PRV : "ranges"
    CCF ||--o{ CVP : "verification profile"
    CCF ||--o{ PSM : "parameter sets"

The diagram restates the relationships described in the ICD: one command references one header and many PTV expressions; command parameters are shared between commands through cdf; each parameter references at most one numerical curve, one alias set and one range set, each of which can be shared by many parameters.1 The monitoring side of the same database (pcf, plf, and so on) is described in Monitoring in the MIB, and the whole model in MIB data model.

docs.title: From mnemonic to packet
docs.text:
The packet header is the first portion of the encoded TC packet and is followed by the application data field defined through cpc and cdf. Header fields are not edited by the operator: the command source or command handler fills them in, taking APID, type and subtype from ccf, computing the packet length (including repeated groups), and maintaining the source sequence counter per APID.4 Only command parameter values, not fixed areas, appear in the command history; fixed areas survive only in the hex dump of the packet.5

flowchart LR
    A["Operator / procedure<br/>loads CCF_CNAME"] --> B["ccf: header template,<br/>APID, type, subtype, ack"]
    B --> C["pcdf: header bit layout"]
    B --> D["cdf: ordered elements<br/>(fixed areas, parameters,<br/>group repeaters)"]
    D --> E["cpc: type PTC/PFC,<br/>calibration, range,<br/>default"]
    E --> F["De-calibration<br/>cca/ccs or paf/pas"]
    F --> G["Range check prf/prv"]
    G --> H["Static PTV (ptv)<br/>+ dynamic PTV"]
    H --> I["Encode, append CRC,<br/>optionally wrap in TC(11,4)"]
    I --> J{"Destination"}
    J -->|"default"| K["NCTRS"]
    J -->|"dst entry"| L["EGSE / SCOE"]
    J -->|"CTYPE N"| M["NIS throw event"]

The order of the boxes follows the processing described in the ICD; the split into separate steps is this wiki's presentation.524 The ground-side layers below the packet (segment, frame, CLTU, COP-1) and the route through NCTRS and NIS are explained in Uplink.

docs.title: Maximum command size
docs.text:
The size of a command is capped by the configuration variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE, which defaults to 248 bytes. Parameters must share what is left after the header (the sum of its PCDF_LEN values), the CRC (CMD_CRC_SIZE, default 2 bytes) and, for execution time-tagged commands, the parameters of the TC(11,4) wrapper named in CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME (default 20 bytes if that command is not found). The ICD's own example: with a 10-byte header and no CRC or time tag, a single parameter can be up to 238 bytes; with default time tagging and CRC it shrinks to 216 bytes.6 Because the wrapper is added on top of CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE, the ICD advises setting that variable to the mission's maximum CLTU size minus the length of the wrapper parameters.6

For Solar Orbiter the spacecraft TM/TC ICD caps the TC packet data field at 242 octets: 4 octets of data field header, 236 octets of application data and 2 octets of packet error control.50 With the 6-octet primary header that is a 248-octet packet, the same figure as the SCOS-2000 default.

Inference

The match between the Solar Orbiter maximum packet (6 + 242 = 248 octets) and the SCOS-2000 default CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE of 248 bytes is arithmetic done by this wiki. The value actually configured in the Solar Orbiter mission control system is not stated in the available sources.

docs.text:

tcp has one record per TC packet header.4

docs.text:
# Field Type Meaning 1* PCPC_PNAME Char(8), M Unique name of the header parameter 2 PCPC_DESC Char(24), M Description 3 PCPC_CODE Char(1), default U Format of the value in PCDF_VALUE: I signed integer, U unsigned integer

docs.title: pcdf: header layout
docs.text:
pcdf has one record per element of a header.4

# Field Type Meaning and values 1* PCDF_TCNAME Char(8), M Header (TCP_ID) the element belongs to 2 PCDF_DESC Char(24) Description, used for fixed areas only 3 PCDF_TYPE Char(1), M F fixed area (value from PCDF_VALUE); A APID from CCF_APID; T service type from CCF_TYPE; S subtype from CCF_STYPE; K acknowledgement flags from CCF_ACK; P other parameter set automatically by the command subsystem (packet length, source sequence counter) 4 PCDF_LEN Number(4), M Element length in bits. The same PCDF_PNAME must always have the same length, in every header 5* PCDF_BIT Number(4), M Bit offset from the start of the whole packet 6 PCDF_PNAME Char(8) Header parameter (PCPC_PNAME); for types A, T, S, K, P only, null for F 7 PCDF_VALUE Char(10), M Fixed value in hex for F; otherwise the default value (decimal for signed, PCDF_RADIX for unsigned) 8 PCDF_RADIX Char(1), default H D, H or O for unsigned values

4

docs.title: The Solar Orbiter headers
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter MIB (release 25925PFM, comment 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33) defines four headers. NOM_TC is used by 5,318 commands, HPC1_TC by 125, NOS2KHDR ("NIS Throw Events") by 6 and NO_HDR ("TCP Header for CF/CS") by 5. Only NOM_TC (13 rows) and HPC1_TC (7 rows) have a layout in pcdf; NO_HDR and NOS2KHDR have no pcdf rows at all. Of the seven pcpc parameters, PH_APID, PH_SSC and PH_LEN are used by both of those headers, while DFH_ACK, DFH_TYPE, DFH_STPE and DFH_SRC are used by NOM_TC only.40

The diagram is drawn from the 13 pcdf rows of NOM_TC.40 It matches the Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD: version 000, type 1, data field header present on every command except CPDU commands, the APID split into a 7-bit process ID and a 4-bit packet category fixed to 12, sequence flags 11 (stand-alone), and a 4-octet data field header with the secondary header flag set to 0, PUS version 1, the Ack field, the service type and the subtype. The remaining octet holds the Source ID, which the TN defines in its Annex 8.4955 The 1-bit secondary header flag and 3-bit PUS version follow the PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A) layout; ECSS-E-ST-70-41C uses a 4-bit version field set to 2 and a 16-bit source ID instead.5657 See PUS packet structures and PUS-A vs PUS-C.

HPC1_TC carries only the 6-octet primary header, with the data field header flag fixed to 0. All 125 commands that use it have APID 44, which is process ID 2, the OBC hardware function that receives high-priority commands for the Command Pulse Distribution Unit (CPDU) on MAP ID 0.405452

A header type the ICD does not define

In NOM_TC the Source ID element has PCDF_TYPE = O, a value not among the six types listed in ICD 7.0 (F, A, T, S, K, P), nor in issues 6.7 and 6.9.440 The Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database instead defines the same 8-bit field as a fixed area (F) with value 0x78 (120).41 The April 2020 release of the Solar Orbiter MIB also had the Source ID as a fixed area (F, value 0) and no DFH_SRC parameter in pcpc, so type O and DFH_SRC were introduced between the two releases.38 The Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD reserves Source ID 120 for "Direct commands" from ground, and 110 to 113 for the mission timeline, TC sequences, recovery actions and the back-up timeline.55

Inference

PCDF_TYPE = O is most likely a mission-specific extension that lets the Solar Orbiter control system set the Source ID according to the origin of each command (manual stack, timeline, sequence), instead of using one fixed value. This is not documented in the available sources.

docs.title: Commands: ccf
docs.text:
ccf has one record per command. Commands may be destined for the spacecraft or for other control domains such as ground equipment.7

# Field Type Meaning and allowed values Import default 1* CCF_CNAME Char(8), M Unique command name (mnemonic) 2 CCF_DESCR Char(24), M Short description 3 CCF_DESCR2 Char(64) Detailed description 4 CCF_CTYPE Char(8) Command type; special values R, F, S, T, N (below); anything else is mission-specific 5 CCF_CRITICAL Char(1) Y critical (hazardous), N not critical. The extra protection is mission-specific N 6 CCF_PKTID Char(8), M Header template (TCP_ID) 7 CCF_TYPE Number(3) Service type 0–255; may be null if the header has no T element 8 CCF_STYPE Number(3) Service subtype 0–255; may be null if no S element 9 CCF_APID Number(5) 0–2047 for spacecraft commands, 2048–65535 for non-spacecraft commands; may be null if no A element 10 CCF_NPARS Number(3) Number of elements (parameters and fixed areas), for consistency checking against cdf 11 CCF_PLAN Char(1) Which sources may put the command directly in a planning file: A all, F flight dynamics only, S SOC only, N none N 12 CCF_EXEC Char(1) Y may be loaded stand-alone on a manual stack; N only inside sequences Y 13 CCF_ILSCOPE Char(1) Default interlock: G global, L local source, S local for the subsystem, B global for the subsystem, F local and only on verification failure, T subsystem-local and only on failure, N none N 14 CCF_ILSTAGE Char(1) Stage the interlock waits for: R ground station reception, U uplink, O on-board reception, A application acceptance, C completion C 15 CCF_SUBSYS Number(3) Subsystem identifier 1–255 16 CCF_HIPRI Char(1) Y high priority on board: MAP ID forced to CCF_MAPID, cannot be execution time-tagged or blocked (typically CPDU commands) N 17 CCF_MAPID Number(2) MAP ID 0–63 for high-priority commands; irrelevant unless CCF_HIPRI = Y 18 CCF_DEFSET Char(8) Default parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) 19 CCF_RAPID Number(5) Redundant APID (1–2047 or 2048–65535); requires CCF_APID; all commands with one prime APID must share one redundant APID 20 CCF_ACK Number(2) Default acknowledgement flags: the decimal value 0–15 of the whole Ack field; may be null if no K element 21 CCF_SUBSCHEDID Number(5) Default on-board sub-schedule (1–65535) when loaded as execution time-tagged; falls back to CCF_SUBSYS

89101112

docs.title: Special command types (CCF_CTYPE)
docs.text:
For missions that follow the ESA Packet Telecommand Standard, five values of CCF_CTYPE mark special commands:9

Value Meaning What pcdf/cdf describe R Control segment, also called "Reset Map Command" The frame data field, not a packet F Control frame (BC frame, for example Unlock and Set V(R)) The frame data field S Command packet without the Packet Error Control field; the releaser does not append the 16-bit CRC. Typically used by EGSE for non-spacecraft commands Header and application data T SLE throw event, sent to the SLE service provider but not uplinked Event ID and following fields of the SLE forward service ICD N NIS throw event, executed by the NIS and not forwarded to the station Event ID and following fields of the NIS throw events ICD

The ICD strongly recommends that BC frames (F) carry a global interlock (CCF_ILSCOPE = G) waiting at least for the uplink stage (U), so that no further command is released before the AD mode set-up is complete.9 Throw events cannot be blocked with other entries of a sequence or command source.7 Frame-level directives are explained in COP-1; throw events in SLE FCLTU and NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface.

Solar Orbiter uses all of these mechanisms except S and T. Its five NO_HDR commands are UNLOCK and SETVR (CCF_CTYPE = F, FARM directives) and RESET, REIN_TTR and TC_ONLY (R). Its six NIS throw events (N, header NOS2KHDR, type 251, subtype 1, APID 1964) open and close the session, the TC link and the TM link, for example ESESIONO "OPEN SESSION".42 The cdf rows of the two FARM directives hold the frame data field exactly as CCSDS defines the control commands: UNLOCK is one fixed octet 0x00, and SETVR is the fixed area 0x8200 followed by an editable 8-bit VR parameter.4439

docs.title: How the Solar Orbiter MIB fills ccf
docs.text:
The 5,454 commands of the September 2025 release use the fields as follows.42

Field Values found (number of commands) CCF_PKTID NOM_TC 5,318; HPC1_TC 125; NOS2KHDR 6; NO_HDR 5 CCF_CTYPE null 5,443; N 6; R 3; F 2 CCF_CRITICAL N 5,448; null 6 (throw events). No command is flagged critical CCF_PLAN N 5,448; A 6 (the throw events) CCF_EXEC Y 5,448; null 6 CCF_ILSCOPE / CCF_ILSTAGE N / C 5,443; N / null 6; N / N 5 (directives) CCF_HIPRI / CCF_MAPID Y / 0: 125 (HPC1); Y / null: 5 (directives); N / null 5,119; N / 1: 128; N / 54: 77 CCF_ACK 9: 5,225; 1: 78; 0: 21; null 130 CCF_DEFSET, CCF_RAPID never used CCF_SUBSCHEDID equal to CCF_SUBSYS in every record (17 distinct values, null in 150 records) CCF_APID 32 distinct values; the largest groups are 172 (1,971 commands), 236 (966), 188 (454) CCF_TYPE 78 distinct service types; the largest are 2 (1,363), 131 (875), 3 (345), 12 (254)

The APIDs decode with the Solar Orbiter allocation (APID = 16 × process ID + category 12): 172 is process ID 10 (OBC central software, data management), 236 is 14 (system control), 188 is 11 (AOCS), and 1532 is 95 (SWA).5442 No command declares a default interlock, so any interlock must be chosen on the stack. 205 normal-priority commands still carry a MAP ID (1 or 54), which the ICD says is ignored when CCF_HIPRI is not Y.1142

Observed oddities

  • CCF_ILSTAGE = N on the five frame directives is not one of the ICD values (R, U, O, A, C).1042
  • The NIS throw events use APID 1964, which lies in the spacecraft range 0–2047 although they are never uplinked; 1964 is process ID 122, inside the EGSE range 112–127 of the Solar Orbiter allocation.85442

docs.title: The acknowledgement field (CCF_ACK)
docs.text:
CCF_ACK is the decimal value of the complete 4-bit Ack field of the data field header. Since SCOS-2000 R4.0 the operator can change the flags when loading the command.12 In ECSS-E-ST-70-41C, bit 3 of the field (the last transmitted) requests successful acceptance reports, bit 2 start of execution, bit 1 progress and bit 0 (the first transmitted) completion; PUS-A assigns the bits the same way.5756

Solar Orbiter restricts the field to 0000, 0001 (acceptance), 1000 (execution) and 1001 (both); the start and progress bits must be zero.51 In the MIB, 5,225 commands default to 9 (1001), 78 to 1 (acceptance only) and 21 to 0.42 In the PUS, failure reports are generated whatever the flags say; the flags only request the success reports.5658 The Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD words its four settings differently: 0001 asks for the acceptance report (success or failure) and no TM(1,7) or TM(1,8) is generated, 1000 asks for the execution report (success or failure) and no TM(1,1) or TM(1,2) is generated, and only for 0000 does it state that failures are still reported.51 How these reports are matched to verification stages is the subject of Command verification in the MIB and ST[01] Request verification.

docs.title: Command routing: dst
docs.text:
dst is optional and was, at issue 7.0, only used by SCOS-2000 based EGSE. It has at most one record per APID; commands whose APID is absent go to the default destination, the NCTRS.13

# Field Type Meaning 1* DST_APID Number(5), M Command APID, 0–65535 2 DST_ROUTE Char(30), M "Destination ID": up to three dot-separated fields. First: NCTRS (spacecraft commands only, the default) or EGSE. Second (EGSE only): SCOE for non-spacecraft or TC for spacecraft commands. Third (spacecraft commands not via NCTRS): address of the ground equipment

The ICD gives NCTRS, EGSE.SCOE and EGSE.TC.0x8800 (via the SCOE and TC front-end 0x8800) as valid examples.13 The EGSE user manual of the same era shows the same routing being chosen per command in test procedures, with the dst table as the default.59

The Solar Orbiter MIB has exactly one dst record, in both the 2020 and the 2025 release: APID 1372 is routed to EGSE.TC.0x8800. APID 1372 is process ID 85, which belongs to the SPICE instrument, and 91 commands use it.4354

Inference

A single dst entry pointing to an EGSE TC front-end looks like a leftover from instrument-level testing. Whether the operational control system honours it is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Command structure: cdf
docs.text:
cdf lists the elements of every command in order, one record per element. The elements are encoded with no gaps between them, so every bit of the application data field, padding included, must be covered by an element.18

# Field Type Meaning and values Import default 1* CDF_CNAME Char(8), M Command (CCF_CNAME) 2 CDF_ELTYPE Char(1), M A fixed area; F fixed (non-editable) parameter; E editable parameter. Only E parameters may appear in sdf 3 CDF_DESCR Char(24) Description, for fixed areas only 4 CDF_ELLEN Number(4), M Length in bits. Used for fixed areas; for parameters the length comes from PTC/PFC and this field is only a consistency check; 0 for variable-length parameters 5* CDF_BIT Number(4), M Bit offset from the start of the unexpanded application data field (after the header and data field header), computed as if every counter were 1. Only used to sort the elements 6* CDF_GRPSIZE Number(2) For a group repeater: number of following elements in the repeated group; otherwise 0 or null. Part of the key when non-zero 0 7 CDF_PNAME Char(8) Parameter (CPC_PNAME), mandatory for F and E 8 CDF_INTER Char(1) How CDF_VALUE is expressed: R raw; E engineering (calibrated parameters only); D take CPC_DEFVAL; T dynamic default from the monitoring parameter CDF_TMID (editable parameters only, static raw default still required) R 9 CDF_VALUE Char Fixed or default value. Fixed areas: raw unsigned hex, at most 32 bits (FFFF FFFF). Command ID parameters: a fully defined command name. Parameter ID parameters: a PCF_NAME with an on-board ID. Null on an editable parameter means the operator must enter a value 10 CDF_TMID Char(8) Monitoring parameter for dynamic defaults; same PTC/PFC as the command parameter; must be processed by the TM model (in plf or synthetic)

2223

The ICD adds that fixed areas must not be used for Service 11 command elements that the ground model of the on-board queue has to interpret.23 It also notes that the size limit of CDF_VALUE follows from the maximum command size.23

docs.title: Repeated groups
docs.text:
PUS requests often contain a counter N followed by N repetitions of a group of fields, sometimes nested. SCOS-2000 models this with one number per element: if CDF_GRPSIZE is greater than zero, the element is a counter and the value says how many following elements form the group.19 The ICD's own examples are the PUS-A Distribute On/Off command (2,1), where an address repeats N times (counter with group size 1), and the Disable Transmission of Telemetry Source Packets request (14,2), where N1, TYPE, N2, SUB-TYPE has N1 with group size 3 and N2 with group size 1.19

flowchart LR
    N1["N1<br/>GRPSIZE 3<br/>bit 0"] --> T["TYPE<br/>bit 8"] --> N2["N2<br/>GRPSIZE 1<br/>bit 16"] --> ST["SUB-TYPE<br/>bit 24"]
    ST -.->|"repeated N2 times"| ST
    N2 -.->|"TYPE..SUB-TYPE block repeated N1 times"| T

At load time the command is expanded from left to right: the operator is asked for N1 (unless it is fixed), the next three elements are generated N1 times, then each N2 is asked for and its subtype repeated.19 A counter can also be fixed in the database: with group size 0 it is just a fixed value and the repeated elements must be defined explicitly; with a fixed value and a group size above 0 the expansion happens without prompting. Since R4.2 commands with repeaters may be used in sequences, but only if every repeated value is fixed in the database.20

In the Solar Orbiter MIB, 569 elements in 512 commands are group repeaters.44 A typical case is ZCA00C05, TC(12,5) "Add parameters to Monitoring list": its first element PCD0C051 "Nb PMONs to add" (unsigned 8 bits) has CDF_GRPSIZE = 15, so the following 15 elements (monitoring ID, two Parameter ID parameters, intervals, limits, event IDs, mask and expected value) repeat once per monitor.48 On-board monitoring itself is described in ST[12].

docs.title: Default values and dynamic defaults
docs.text:
A parameter can receive a default at three levels: the parameter (CPC_DEFVAL), the command (CDF_VALUE) and the sequence element (SDF_VALUE). Option D (CDF_INTER, SDF_VTYPE) makes a level inherit the value of the level below, so a value maintained once in cpc propagates to every command and sequence. Conversely CDF_ELTYPE = F or SDF_FTYPE = F freezes the value at that level.14

flowchart LR
    A["cpc<br/>CPC_DEFVAL"] -->|"CDF_INTER = D"| B["cdf<br/>CDF_VALUE"]
    B -->|"SDF_VTYPE = D"| C["sdf<br/>SDF_VALUE"]
    T["Telemetry<br/>CDF_TMID"] -.->|"CDF_INTER = T<br/>after loading"| B
    C --> S["Value on the stack<br/>(editable unless F)"]

A dynamic default replaces the static default with the current value of a monitoring parameter, for example to initialise part of a command from the on-board state, or to steer a routing parameter used by many commands centrally through a User Defined Constant. The static raw default is still needed so the command can be loaded; the telemetry value takes over only after loading, and stops being tracked as soon as the operator types an explicit value.21

The Solar Orbiter MIB never uses dynamic defaults: CDF_TMID is empty in all 47,609 cdf records.44

CDF_ELTYPE CDF_INTER Records A (fixed area) R / null 15,292 / 1,614 F (fixed parameter) R / E / D 14,730 / 2,019 / 932 E (editable parameter) R / D / E 5,876 / 4,863 / 2,283

The elements belong to 5,011 commands; the remaining 443 commands have no application data, such as ZCD01101 TC(17,1) "Perform Connection Test". For every command with a value in CCF_NPARS, that value equals its number of cdf records.44

docs.title: Command parameters: cpc
docs.text:
cpc has one record per command parameter and describes how the parameter is typed, entered, displayed, calibrated and checked.14

# Field Type Meaning and values Import default 1* CPC_PNAME Char(8), M Unique parameter name 2 CPC_DESCR Char(24) Description 3 CPC_PTC Number(2), M Parameter Type Code (Appendix A); 11 for Deduced parameters since R5 4 CPC_PFC Number(5), M Parameter Format Code; for Deduced (PTC 11), 0 means "width of the TM parameter", a value above 0 forces the width in bits 5 CPC_DISPFMT Char(1) Input/display format of engineering values: A ASCII (textual calibration), I/U/R per CCA_ENGFMT (numerical calibration), T absolute time (PTC 9), D relative time (PTC 10) R 6 CPC_RADIX Char(1) Default radix of unsigned raw values: D, H, O D 7 CPC_UNIT Char(4) Engineering unit shown next to values 8 CPC_CATEG Char(1) C numerical calibration (needs CPC_CCAREF); T textual (needs CPC_PAFREF); B both (not supported); A Command ID (PTC 7, PFC 0); P Parameter ID (PTC 3); N none N 9 CPC_PRFREF Char(10) Range set (PRF_NUMBR); its PRF_DSPFMT must suit the parameter 10 CPC_CCAREF Char(10) Numerical curve (CCA_NUMBR); null unless category C or B 11 CPC_PAFREF Char(10) Alias set (PAF_NUMBR); null unless category T or B 12 CPC_INTER Char(1) Representation of CPC_DEFVAL: R raw, E engineering (calibrated parameters only) R 13 CPC_DEFVAL Char Default used when CDF_INTER = D. Command ID: a fully defined command; Parameter ID: a PCF_NAME with on-board ID 14 CPC_CORR Char(1) Y apply time correlation to absolute times, N do not; must be N for relative times Y 15 CPC_OBTID Number(5) Which on-board clock (1..N) defines correlation or epoch; default from TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID 0 16 CPC_ENDIAN Char(1) Future extension: B big endian, L little endian, for whole-byte types B

151617

Column names in this wiki's SQLite copy

The SQLite database used for this page follows the pyscos2000 schema, which names the first column CPC_NAME (ICD: CPC_PNAME) and the fifteenth CPC_OBTIP (ICD: CPC_OBTID), and adds a CPC_DESCR2 column before CPC_ENDIAN. The Solar Orbiter cpc.dat file has 15 fields per record, so CPC_DESCR2 and CPC_ENDIAN are always empty.45

docs.title: Special PUS parameter kinds
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 offers three special kinds of command parameter to make PUS requests easier to build:1431

  • Command ID (CPC_CATEG = A, PTC 7, PFC 0): the operator gives a command name and SCOS-2000 encodes the raw packet of that command as a variable octet string. This serves requests that carry other requests, such as TC(19,1). The referenced command must be fully encodable without input.
  • Parameter ID (CPC_CATEG = P, PTC 3): the operator gives a monitoring parameter name and SCOS-2000 encodes its on-board identifier (PCF_PID). This serves requests such as TC(4,6) or TC(12,1).
  • Deduced (PTC 11, since R5): the type, width and calibration come from the TM parameter named by the first Parameter ID parameter within the same (repeated) array of the command; PFC above 0 forces the width.

Appendix C of the ICD adds a caveat for Service 19: the packet embedded through a Command ID parameter is encoded with fixed header values, for example for the sequence counter.34

The Solar Orbiter MIB has two Command ID parameters and 152 Parameter ID parameters, and no Deduced parameter.45 ZCSX0031 "Define P_OFF_EPD S19" is a TC(19,1) whose last element PCD13013 "TC to send upon event" is a fixed Command ID with value ZCSX0023, the TC(11,2) "P_OFF_EPD SSID". The Parameter ID parameters appear in TC(3,1), (3,2), (3,138), (12,5), (18,140) and several private services (130, 131, 139, 142), for example PCD03014 "Datapool parameter ID" (unsigned 32 bits) in ZCA00C05.48 See ST[19] Event-action and ST[11] Time-based scheduling.

docs.title: Parameter types
docs.text:
The PTC/PFC pairs follow Appendix A of the ICD, which in turn follows the PUS. Unsigned and signed integers are limited to 32 bits (PFC 15 and 16, 48 and 64 bits, are not supported); PTC 5 PFC 4, the 48-bit MIL-STD-1750A real, is supported for command parameters only; variable-length octet strings (PTC 7, PFC 0) and character strings (PTC 8, PFC 0) exist only on the commanding side; absolute time with a p-field (PTC 9, PFC 0) is not supported; CDS time without microseconds (9,1) is supported from R5.0, and (9,30) is a Unix-style time not defined in PUS.3031 For variable strings the command source derives the length from the value it is given, and since R4.0 SCOS-2000 can be configured to insert the PUS length field automatically.30 Details are on MIB parameter types and PUS parameter types.

In the Solar Orbiter MIB the 7,155 command parameters are dominated by unsigned integers of 16 bits (PTC 3, PFC 12: 1,540), 8 bits (3,4: 1,120) and 32 bits (3,14: 984), IEEE single-precision reals (5,1: 630), and 1-bit and 8-bit enumerations (2,1: 598; 2,8: 364).45

Field Values found (number of parameters) CPC_CATEG N 4,991; T 1,624; C 327; P 152; null 59; A 2 CPC_DISPFMT R 5,468; A 1,624; T 58; U 4; D 1 CPC_RADIX D 3,155; H 2,195; null 1,805 CPC_INTER R 6,839; E 316 References range set 694; numerical curve 327; alias set 1,624; default value 1,230; unit 458 Times 35 parameters (9,15) and 23 (9,17), CUC with 4 coarse and 0 or 2 fine octets; one (10,17) relative time; CPC_CORR set in 13 records

45

docs.title: De-calibration of command parameters
docs.text: Command calibrations work in both directions: engineering to raw for encoding, raw to engineering for display. Only parameters whose raw representation is numerical (no strings or times) can be calibrated, and the ICD warns that every command curve must be one-to-one, otherwise an engineering value would map to more than one raw value.26 Monitoring calibrations, which only go from raw to engineering, are described in Calibration in the MIB.

docs.title: Numerical curves: cca and ccs
docs.text:
Table # Field Type Meaning Default cca 1* CCA_NUMBR Char(10), M Curve name 2 CCA_DESCR Char(24) Description 3 CCA_ENGFMT Char(1) Engineering format I, U or R R 4 CCA_RAWFMT Char(1) Raw format I, U or R U 5 CCA_RADIX Char(1) Radix of unsigned raw values D, H, O (may differ from the parameter's) D 6 CCA_UNIT Char(4) Unit, for consistency checks 7 CCA_NCURVE Number(3) Number of ccs records ccs 1* CCS_NUMBR Char(10), M Curve 2 CCS_XVALS Char, M Engineering value, always decimal 3* CCS_YVALS Char, M Raw value, in the curve's radix

27

Note the swap compared with monitoring curves: in ccs the engineering value is the X column and the raw value the Y column, the reverse of cap.27

Solar Orbiter has 99 command curves; 80 of them are two-point straight lines, and 80 map unsigned raw values to real engineering values.46 Curve CAHP0000TC "Periodic TC angular rate" (unit dg/s, raw format I) has two points: engineering −0.5 at raw −1024, and 0.49951 at raw 1023. It is shared by six parameters, among them PCS2Z007 "H-APME El Rate", a 16-bit signed parameter of ZCS2Z050 "Set HGA-APME Go To Az-El".46

Inference: worked de-calibration (illustrative)

The two points of CAHP0000TC lie on the line raw = 2048 × engineering, that is 1/2048 dg/s per least significant bit. If the curve is interpolated linearly, an operator entry of 0.25 dg/s gives raw 512 (0x0200) and −0.1 dg/s gives raw −204.8, which then needs rounding. ICD 7.0 does not state the interpolation or rounding rule for cca curves; linear interpolation is this wiki's assumption, based on how numerical calibration curves work for monitoring parameters.

docs.title: Textual de-calibrations: paf and pas
docs.text:
Table # Field Type Meaning Default paf 1* PAF_NUMBR Char(10), M Alias set name 2 PAF_DESCR Char(24) Description 3 PAF_RAWFMT Char(1) Raw format I, U or R U 4 PAF_NALIAS Number(3) Number of pas records pas 1* PAS_NUMBR Char(10), M Alias set 2 PAS_ALTXT Char, M Text shown and typed by the operator 3* PAS_ALVAL Char, M Raw value, decimal

28

The aliases can be used as default values, so a command definition can say BUS_1 instead of 0. Solar Orbiter has 624 alias sets with 11,834 aliases.2846 Set CCDT0126TX "Process IDentifier reach" maps 60 process IDs to names (30 OP_SSMM … 50 EPD_0 … 95 SWA_0 … 104 SPICE_8); it is the textual calibration of PCD11031 "Process IDentifier" in ZCD01103 TC(17,3) "Request Connection Test", so the operator chooses an instrument by name.46

docs.title: Range checks: prf and prv
docs.text:
Range sets restrict the values an operator may enter. They apply to command and sequence parameters whose raw representation is numerical or a time; strings cannot be range checked. When a sequence is loaded only its formal parameters are checked against their range sets, unless SCOS-2000 is configured to check every value.29

Table # Field Type Meaning Default prf 1* PRF_NUMBR Char(10), M Range set name 2 PRF_DESCR Char(24) Description 3 PRF_INTER Char(1) R raw limits; E engineering limits (all users calibrated) R 4 PRF_DSPFMT Char(1) Value format: A, I, U, R, T (absolute time), D (relative time) U 5 PRF_RADIX Char(1) Radix for unsigned values D, H, O D 6 PRF_NRANGE Number(3) Number of prv records 7 PRF_UNIT Char(4) Unit, for consistency checks prv 1* PRV_NUMBR Char(10), M Range set 2* PRV_MINVAL Char, M Low limit, or the single allowed value if PRV_MAXVAL is null 3 PRV_MAXVAL Char High limit (inclusive)

A set may combine discrete values and ranges, one prv record each; a value passes if it lies within, or equals, the limits of any record.29

Solar Orbiter defines 565 range sets with 1,072 values.46 They expose a practical pitfall of the 24-character description field: set VCD00176 is described as "Integer between 1 and 25" but its single prv record allows 1 to 255, and VCD00269 (same description) allows 1 to 254. Both descriptions read like "…255" and "…254" cut at 24 characters.46 The ICD says over-long fields are truncated on import with only a warning.35

docs.title: Pre-transmission validation: ptv
docs.text:
Static pre-transmission validation (PTV) blocks the release of a command unless telemetry shows the right state. Each ptv record is one check; all checks of a command are ANDed. An expression belongs to exactly one command and must be repeated for every other command that needs it.124

# Field Type Meaning Default 1* PTV_CNAME Char(8), M Command 2* PTV_PARNAM Char(8), M Monitoring parameter: numerical raw value, processed by the TM model (in plf or synthetic) 3 PTV_INTER Char(1) R raw (for synthetics, the OL output); E engineering, only for parameters with a single calibration (PCF_CURTX) R 4 PTV_VAL Char(17), M Value the parameter must equal, decimal if raw

24

The validity of the monitoring parameter is taken into account implicitly: a check passes only if the parameter is valid and has the required value.24 Besides this static, telemetry-based PTV, SCOS-2000 runs dynamic PTV (feasibility and time checks, interlocks); a sequence element can override either kind through CSS_DYNPTV and CSS_STAPTV, and EGSE test procedures could switch static PTV, dynamic PTV and CEV off per command.255960

Solar Orbiter's MIB had no PTV check in April 2020 and has five in September 2025.47

Command Description PUS type Parameter Required raw value ZCD00D09 Accept First Uplink Part (13,9) NCDXS005 "Nb Immediate TCF" 0 ZSM00120 SSMM Abort LLFT (13,145) NMAXS005 "SSMM FTS COMMANDING PTV" 0 ZSM00125 SSMM Repeat LLFT Parts (13,146) NMAXS005 0 ZSM00130 SSMM Confirm Correct FDUs Reception (13,147) NMAXS005 0 ZSM00135 SSMM Request LLFT EOFT Report (13,148) NMAXS005 0

47

Both parameters are dynamic synthetic parameters. The OL source of NMAXS005 wraps another parameter, NMAXU005, so that the result is always valid: it returns 0 ("NO WAIT") unless NMAXU005 is valid, in which case it returns that parameter's raw value.47

Inference

Wrapping the real telemetry in a synthetic that defaults to the permissive value means that the PTV check never blocks a command merely because the underlying packet is missing or stale. That design intent is this wiki's reading of the OL source; it is not documented in the available sources. See Synthetic parameters and the OL language.

docs.title: Worked example: ZPW04604, a real Solar Orbiter command
docs.text:
ZPW04604 "PCDU A BDR1_C1 SwitchON" uses the NOM_TC header, PUS type 2 subtype 128, APID 172, six elements, Ack 1 (acceptance report only), no interlock and sub-schedule 1.48 TC(2,128) "Distribute MilBus 1553 Commands" sends low-level MIL-STD-1553 commands on a selected bus; its fields are the bus, the bus coupler, the number of command words, the 1553 command word, the number of data words and the data words.53

CDF_BIT Bits CDF_ELTYPE Element CDF_INTER / CDF_VALUE Raw value 0 8 F PCD02801 "Bus ID" (PTC 2, PFC 8, alias set CCDT0031TX) E / BUS_1 0 8 8 E PCD02802 "Bus Coupler ID" (alias set CCDT0030TX) E / BUSCPLR_DEF 0 16 8 A "Number of bus commands" R / 0001 0x01 24 16 A "CMDWORD of RPW04604" 2201 0x2201 40 8 A "Length of RPW04604" 1 0x01 48 16 F RPW04604 "BDR1_BDR1_ON" (PTC 3, PFC 12, radix H) D → CPC_DEFVAL 0181 0x0181

48

The aliases come from pas: BUS_1 = 0 and BUS_2 = 1; BUSCPLR_DEF = 0, BUSCPLR_A = 1, BUSCPLR_B = 2. These match the TM/TC ICD, which defines bus 0 as "Bus 1" and bus coupler 0 as the default.4853 Only the bus coupler is editable; everything else is frozen by the database.

Putting the header, data field header and application data together gives the packet below. The application data bytes follow directly from the MIB; the sequence count, the Source ID and the CRC are assigned at release, so the values shown for them are illustrative.

Octets Field Value Origin 0–1 Packet ID 0x18AC version 0, type 1, DFH 1, APID 172 2–3 Sequence control 0xC000 flags 11, count 0 (illustrative) 4–5 Packet length 0x000D 4 + 8 + 2 octets of data field, minus 1 6 Sec. header flag, PUS version, Ack 0x11 0, 001, 0001 (CCF_ACK = 1) 7 Service type 0x02 CCF_TYPE 8 Service subtype 0x80 CCF_STYPE = 128 9 Source ID 0x78 120, "Direct commands" (illustrative) 10–17 Application data 00 00 01 22 01 01 01 81 cdf, cpc, pas 18–19 Packet error control CRC computed by the releaser

48495550

The same command is verified by its acceptance report and a parameter check of the converter status, as shown in Command verification in the MIB. A full byte-level walk-through including the CRC is on Worked example: building a real Solar Orbiter telecommand.

docs.title: A time-tag wrapper: TC(11,4)
docs.text:
To load execution time-tagged commands, the command used as wrapper ("Insert Telecommands in the Command Schedule", (11,4)) must itself exist in ccf and cdf; its name, type, subtype and parameters are set by the CMD_LOAD_TT* configuration variables. SCOS-2000 then encapsulates each time-tagged command in one (11,4) packet; several blocked time-tagged commands become several (11,4) packets aggregated in one TC segment, never one (11,4) with several commands.533

The Solar Orbiter wrapper candidates INSERTTT and ZCD00B04 (both TC(11,4), APID 172) have the same four elements:48

CDF_BIT Bits Element Type Notes 0 8 PCD0B041 "Sub_schedule Identifier" (3,4) range set VCD00269 (1–254) 8 8 PCD0B042 "Nb TCs to add in Sub-Sch" (3,4) group repeater, CDF_GRPSIZE = 2, default 1, range 1–13 16 48 PCD0B043 "Time Tag" (9,17) absolute CUC time, 4 + 2 octets 64 variable PCD0B044 "Complete TC packet" (ZCD00B04) or PCDXB044 (INSERTTT) (7,0) Command ID in ZCD00B04; plain variable octet string in INSERTTT

48

The time tag and embedded packet form the repeated group. Appendix C lists what SCOS-2000 does around Service 11: automatic encapsulation, a ground model of the on-board schedule, delayed verification of time-tagged commands from live and playback telemetry, and automatic generation of Service 11 commands; relative time tags, interlock modelling and the time-shift command are not modelled.33 The service itself is described in ST[11] Time-based scheduling.

docs.title: High-priority commands and CPDU
docs.text: The CPDU in the Solar Orbiter on-board computer can generate command pulses directly from ground commands, without the central software, so vital units can be switched even when the software is down. These ground commands are called HPC-1 and travel on MAP ID 0; normal commands use MAP ID 1.52 In the MIB the 125 HPC1_TC commands all have CCF_HIPRI = Y, CCF_MAPID = 0 and no Ack field, and their application data is two fixed areas: an HPC line ID and a pulse length. For example ZBC04001 "Select PM A EEPROM Image 1" has line ID 2 and pulse length 1.48 The ICD notes that SCOS-2000 can prevent CPDU commands from being included in TC(11,4) commands or aggregated with other commands in one segment, and that aggregation in general happens only at segment level, never inside one packet.3211

docs.title: Import-time checks and pitfalls
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 importer only catches the most dangerous inconsistencies; the ICD leaves full consistency to the off-line database system. On import:35

  • every field is checked against its declared characteristics; too-long fields are truncated with a warning, which matters for anything but descriptions;
  • a null mandatory field produces a warning and becomes 0 or an empty string;
  • a record that breaks relational integrity (for example a reference to a missing parameter) is not imported;
  • command and sequence parameter values are syntax-checked against Appendix A; a bad value becomes 0, an empty string, or 1970.001.00.00.00 for absolute times.

Names must be unique without regard to case, and the importer gives no warning when two names differ only in case.3 The ICD also checks CCF_ILSTAGE against the verification profile: if it asks for an execution stage (A or C) that the command's cvp/cvs definition does not have, the importer lowers it to the highest applicable level.10

docs.title: How the commanding tables evolved
docs.text:
The change annexes of ICD 7.0 record the evolution relevant to this page:36

Issue Change 6.0 (R4.0) Command ID and Parameter ID parameter types (repatriated from CryoSat); default sub-schedule ID fields in ccf and csf; acknowledgement flags editable when loading a command, which allows report-based verification stages to be disabled dynamically 6.4 (R5.0) Throw events added to CCF_CTYPE; Deduced command parameters; time type (9,1); clarification that only TM-model parameters may be used in CDF_TMID, PTV_PARNAM and similar fields 6.5 (R4.2) Commands with group repeaters allowed in sequences (SDF_REPPOS) 6.7 (R5.2) CPC_CORR and CPC_OBTID; time type (9,30) 7.0 Maximum sizes of CPC_DEFVAL, CDF_VALUE, CCS_*, PAS_*, PRV_* and others tied to the maximum command size; CCF_ILSCOPE values F and T documented; CPC_ENDIAN added as future extension; TC(11,4) encoding according to the cdf definition

The issue history as a whole is on History of the Database Import ICD. Projects that generate MIB files from their own databases sometimes impose extra rules; for example the Herschel/Planck System database (HPSDB) recomputed CCF_NPARS, CCF_HIPRI and CCF_SUBSYS itself and did not load the dst table.61 More on that in Mission tailoring of the MIB.

docs.title: MIB data model: how the tables relate
docs.text:
The MIB is a relational database spread over 53 tab-separated files. No file declares its relationships. Instead, the Database Import ICD says, in the description of each field, which field of which other table its value must match. This page collects those statements into one model. It lists the key of every table, draws the references as entity-relationship diagrams for each area (monitoring, packets, displays, commanding, verification and sequences, parameter sets), walks the main join paths with real records from the Solar Orbiter MIB, and reports how well that MIB respects the model.

Appendix B of the ICD contains six relationship figures: monitoring, display, command, command sequence, parameter set, and command and sequence parameter tables.1 In the 7.0 PDF they are images only. The extracted text of issue 5.1 still carries the field labels of the same figures.2 The diagrams on this page are therefore rebuilt from the field definitions of issue 7.0, cross-checked against the 5.1 figure labels, and then tested against the data.

docs.title: Modelling principles
docs.text:
Normalised tables. All tables are normalised: each field holds a single item, never a variable-length list. Many-to-many relationships are resolved through mapping tables.3 For example, a parameter can appear in many packets and a packet holds many parameters, so plf sits between pcf and pid. Likewise, cvp sits between commands and verification stages, and psm between commands or sequences and parameter sets.45

Keys. In the ICD's field tables, an asterisk after the field number (1*) marks a key field. A table may contain only one record for each combination of key values.6 The key is therefore the natural primary key of the file. Key fields are always mandatory.7

Names and identifiers. References use the referenced item's name (an alphanumeric ID, typically up to 8 characters) or identifier (a number).8 There are no surrogate keys. Renaming a parameter in the off-line database means rewriting every row that mentions it.

Integrity at import. The importer checks relational integrity. A record that refers to something missing, such as an unknown parameter, is not imported and a warning is logged.9 A reference error does not stop the import. The offending row is simply missing from the run-time database, and only the import log records why.

Cardinality as stated by the ICD. The overview sections spell out the cardinalities of the main relationships:45

Relationship Cardinality stated in the ICD Parameter → validity parameter (PCF_VALID) many-to-1. One validity parameter can serve many parameters. Parameter ↔ calibrations via cur many-to-many Parameter → numerical curve (caf) / textual calibration (txf) many-to-1. Curves are shareable. Each has 1 or more points. Parameter → monitoring check set (ocf) 1-to-1. One set holds up to 16 checks. Check → applicability parameter (OCP_RLCHK) Each check may reference 1 parameter. One parameter can serve many checks. Parameter ↔ TM packets via plf / vpd many-to-many Parameter ↔ groups (grpa), parameter ↔ displays (dpc, gpc, spc) many-to-many, possibly with repetitions Command → PTV expressions (ptv) 1-to-many. Expressions are ANDed and not shared between commands. Command ↔ verification stages via cvp many-to-many. Each stage has 1 or more ANDed cve expressions. Command ↔ parameter sets via psm many-to-many Command ↔ command parameters via cdf many-to-many. cdf gives each parameter's position. Command parameter → cca / paf / prf many-to-1. Each is shareable and has 1 or more points or entries. Sequence → elements (css) → element parameters (sdf) 1-to-many, and 1-to-many Sequence → formal parameters (csp) 1-to-many Packet header (tcp) ↔ header parameters (pcpc) via pcdf many-to-many Packet header (tcp) → commands (ccf) 1-to-many. Each command references exactly one header.

docs.title: Keys of every table
docs.text:
The keys below are exactly as marked in ICD 7.0. "Page" is the PDF page of the field table.10

Table Key fields (ICD 7.0) Page Remarks vdf none 38 The last record imported wins.11 pcf PCF_NAME 41 cur CUR_PNAME, CUR_POS 64 CUR_POS gives the evaluation order. caf CAF_NUMBR 65 Char(10) since ICD 6.0 (was Number(4)). cap CAP_NUMBR, CAP_XVALS 68 Each raw value occurs at most once per curve. txf TXF_NUMBR 69 txp TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM 70 mcf MCF_IDENT 71 lgf LGF_IDENT 72 ocf OCF_NAME 73 Same value as the parameter's PCF_NAME. ocp OCP_NAME, OCP_POS 78 pid PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL, PID_SPID 84–86 The packetiser's lookup key is the first five. Since R5.0 each SPID should map to one key.12 pic PIC_TYPE, PIC_STYPE, PIC_APID 92–93 PIC_APID became a key in issue 7.0 (S2K-8528).13 Issue 6.7 had explicitly dropped it from the key because it may be null (S2K-DCR-5502).17 tpcf TPCF_SPID 93 plf PLF_NAME, PLF_SPID 97 A super-commutated parameter has one row per packet. vpd VPD_TPSD, VPD_POS 100 grp GRP_NAME 108 grpa GRPA_GNAME, GRPA_PANAME 109 grpk GRPK_GNAME, GRPK_PKSPID 109–110 dpf DPF_NUMBE 111 dpc DPC_NUMBE, DPC_FLDN 111–112 gpf GPF_NUMBE 114 gpc GPC_NUMBE, GPC_POS 117 spf SPF_NUMBE 120 spc SPC_NUMBE, SPC_POS 121 ppf PPF_NUMBE 124 ppc PPC_NUMBE, PPC_POS 124–125 tcp TCP_ID 128 pcpc PCPC_PNAME 128 pcdf PCDF_TCNAME, PCDF_BIT 129–130 ccf CCF_CNAME 133 dst DST_APID 141 cpc CPC_PNAME 143 cdf CDF_CNAME, CDF_BIT, CDF_GRPSIZE 154–156 CDF_GRPSIZE is not a key in issue 5.1.14 ptv PTV_CNAME, PTV_PARNAM 160 csf CSF_NAME 165 css CSS_SQNAME, CSS_ENTRY 169 Entries must be consecutive (no gaps). sdf SDF_SQNAME, SDF_ENTRY, SDF_POS, SDF_PNAME 180–181 SDF_PNAME is part of the key when the command has group repeaters. csp CSP_SQNAME, CSP_FPNAME 184 cvs CVS_ID 192 Range 0 to 32,767 cve CVE_CVSID, CVE_PARNAM 195–196 cvp CVP_TASK, CVP_TYPE, CVP_CVSID 200 pst PST_NAME 201 psv PSV_PVSID 201 PSV_NAME (the owning set) is not part of the key. cps CPS_NAME, CPS_BIT 202 pvs PVS_ID, PVS_BIT 202–204 psm PSM_NAME, PSM_TYPE, PSM_PARSET 205 cca CCA_NUMBR 206 ccs CCS_NUMBR, CCS_YVALS 207–208 In ccs, CCS_YVALS is the raw value and CCS_XVALS the engineering value, the reverse of cap.15 paf PAF_NUMBR 209 pas PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALVAL 210 prf PRF_NUMBR 211 prv PRV_NUMBR, PRV_MINVAL 213

Raw and engineering columns in cap and ccs

In the monitoring curve table cap, CAP_XVALS holds the raw value. In the command curve table ccs the columns are swapped: the ICD remarks that the engineering values are in CCS_XVALS, and CCS_YVALS holds the raw value.15 Both tables are therefore keyed on the raw value (CAP_XVALS, CCS_YVALS). The Solar Orbiter data agrees: in curve CAHP0000TC the CCS_XVALS are reals such as −0.5 and the CCS_YVALS are integers such as −1024, matching CCA_ENGFMT = R and CCA_RAWFMT = I.66 Command curves must also map raw and engineering values one to one, because they are used in both directions.16
