docs.text:
erDiagram
    PCF ||--o{ PCF : "PCF_VALID, PCF_RELATED"
    PCF ||--o| OCF : "OCF_NAME = PCF_NAME"
    OCF ||--|{ OCP : "OCP_NAME"
    PCF |o--o{ OCP : "OCP_RLCHK (applicability)"
    PCF ||--o{ CUR : "CUR_PNAME"
    PCF |o--o{ CUR : "CUR_RLCHK (applicability)"
    CAF ||--|{ CAP : "CAP_NUMBR"
    TXF ||--|{ TXP : "TXP_NUMBR"
    CAF |o--o{ PCF : "PCF_CURTX (CATEG N)"
    MCF |o--o{ PCF : "PCF_CURTX (CATEG N)"
    LGF |o--o{ PCF : "PCF_CURTX (CATEG N)"
    TXF |o--o{ PCF : "PCF_CURTX (CATEG S)"
    CAF |o--o{ CUR : "CUR_SELECT"
    MCF |o--o{ CUR : "CUR_SELECT"
    LGF |o--o{ CUR : "CUR_SELECT"
    TXF |o--o{ CUR : "CUR_SELECT"
    PCF {
        char PCF_NAME PK
        char PCF_VALID FK
        char PCF_RELATED FK
        char PCF_CURTX FK
    }
    CUR {
        char CUR_PNAME PK
        num CUR_POS PK
        char CUR_RLCHK FK
        char CUR_SELECT FK
    }
    OCF {
        char OCF_NAME PK
    }
    OCP {
        char OCP_NAME PK
        num OCP_POS PK
        char OCP_RLCHK FK
    }

Validity and related parameters. PCF_VALID names a parameter whose raw value is compared with PCF_VALPAR to decide whether this parameter is valid. The validity parameter must be an integer parameter that the TM model processes, and circular validity chains are forbidden.26 PCF_RELATED has two uses. For a saved synthetic parameter it names the synthetic parameter whose value is stored. For a parameter of type deduced (PTC 11) it names the parameter that carries the on-board parameter ID used to interpret it.27

Calibration. A parameter has either one calibration or several.2829

  • One calibration: PCF_CURTX holds its name. The target table depends on PCF_CATEG. With category S (status) the name must be a TXF_NUMBR. With category N (numerical) it must be a CAF_NUMBR, an MCF_IDENT or an LGF_IDENT. The field carries no indication of which of the three it is.
  • Several calibrations: PCF_CURTX stays empty and cur lists the candidates. For each parameter, the cur rows are evaluated in increasing CUR_POS. The first whose applicability expression CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR holds selects the calibration named in CUR_SELECT.

PCF_CURTX must be empty for text parameters, for string and time parameters (PTC 7, 8, 9 and 10), and for every parameter that appears in cur.28 The calibration tables themselves are described on Calibration in the MIB.

Monitoring checks. ocf holds one record per checked parameter, keyed by the parameter's own name. It contains the number of checks and whether limits are expressed in raw or engineering form. ocp holds the individual checks, up to 16 per parameter. Each check may carry an applicability expression OCP_RLCHK = OCP_VALPAR. That expression is ignored for status-consistency checks (OCP_TYPE = C).430 See Monitoring checks.

docs.title: Packets: identification, layout and groups
docs.text:
erDiagram
    PIC |o--o{ PID : "PIC_TYPE, PIC_STYPE, PIC_APID (lookup rule)"
    PID ||--|| TPCF : "TPCF_SPID = PID_SPID"
    PID ||--o{ PLF : "PLF_SPID = PID_SPID"
    PCF ||--o{ PLF : "PLF_NAME"
    PID }o--o{ VPD : "VPD_TPSD = PID_TPSD"
    PCF ||--o{ VPD : "VPD_NAME"
    GRP ||--o{ GRPA : "GRPA_GNAME (GTYPE PA)"
    GRP ||--o{ GRPK : "GRPK_GNAME (GTYPE PK)"
    PCF ||--o{ GRPA : "GRPA_PANAME"
    PID ||--o{ GRPK : "GRPK_PKSPID = PID_SPID"
    PID {
        num PID_TYPE PK
        num PID_STYPE PK
        num PID_APID PK
        num PID_PI1_VAL PK
        num PID_PI2_VAL PK
        num PID_SPID PK
        num PID_TPSD
    }
    PIC {
        num PIC_TYPE PK
        num PIC_STYPE PK
        num PIC_APID PK
        num PIC_PI1_OFF
        num PIC_PI1_WID
        num PIC_PI2_OFF
        num PIC_PI2_WID
    }
    PLF {
        char PLF_NAME PK
        num PLF_SPID PK
        num PLF_OFFBY
        num PLF_OFFBI
    }
    VPD {
        num VPD_TPSD PK
        num VPD_POS PK
        char VPD_NAME FK
    }

Two numbers identify every SCOS-2000 TM packet:3132

  • the SPID (SCOS-2000 Packet ID), which keys the fixed layout in plf and the characteristics in tpcf;
  • the TPSD (Telemetry Packet Structure Definition), which keys the variable layout in vpd. It is −1 for packets that have no variable definition.

Identification. The packetiser recognises an incoming source packet in three steps:3118

  1. It reads the APID, type and subtype at fixed, MISCconfig-defined positions.
  2. It looks up pic, first for the type/subtype/APID combination and then for the type/subtype alone. The APID-specific lookup exists from issue 6.5, through PIC_APID.19 The pic record says where up to two further identification fields (PI1, PI2) sit and how wide they are.
  3. It looks up pid with APID, type, subtype, PI1 and PI2 to obtain the SPID and TPSD.

The pic→pid relationship is therefore a lookup rule, not a stored foreign key. A packet type with no pic entry is looked up with PI1 = PI2 = 0.3318

Layout. plf places a parameter at PLF_OFFBY bytes plus PLF_OFFBI bits. For the SCOS-2000 packetiser, the reference is the start of the source packet header.3435 vpd lists the parameters of a variable structure in VPD_POS order, with repeat counters (VPD_GRPSIZE, VPD_FIXREP) and parameter-ID fields (VPD_PIDREF).36 The data model allows a packet to be both fixed and variable.31 In the Solar Orbiter release none is (see integrity).

Groups. grp defines a named group of type PA (parameters) or PK (packets). grpa and grpk list the members. Groups exist so that their members can be enabled or inhibited together.37

docs.title: Displays and printouts
docs.text:
erDiagram
    DPF ||--|{ DPC : "DPC_NUMBE"
    GPF ||--|{ GPC : "GPC_NUMBE"
    SPF ||--|{ SPC : "SPC_NUMBE"
    PPF ||--|{ PPC : "PPC_NUMBE"
    PCF |o--o{ DPC : "DPC_NAME (null = free text)"
    PCF ||--o{ GPC : "GPC_NAME"

Each display or printout is a header table (*pf) with one row per display and a content table (*pc) with one row per field. Every content row names a monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME).38394041 An empty DPC_NAME marks a free-text entry, whose text is in DPC_TEXT. Free entries were added in ICD 6.0.3842 Only parameters that the TM model processes may appear in displays. Values from variable packets can only be displayed with the Variable Packet Display, which vpd itself drives.43 See Display definitions in the MIB.

docs.title: Commanding: packet headers, commands and command parameters
docs.text:
erDiagram
    TCP ||--|{ PCDF : "PCDF_TCNAME"
    PCPC |o--o{ PCDF : "PCDF_PNAME"
    TCP ||--o{ CCF : "CCF_PKTID"
    DST |o--o{ CCF : "DST_APID = CCF_APID"
    CCF ||--o{ CDF : "CDF_CNAME"
    CPC |o--o{ CDF : "CDF_PNAME"
    PCF |o--o{ CDF : "CDF_TMID (dynamic default)"
    CCF ||--o{ PTV : "PTV_CNAME"
    PCF ||--o{ PTV : "PTV_PARNAM"
    CCA |o--o{ CPC : "CPC_CCAREF"
    PAF |o--o{ CPC : "CPC_PAFREF"
    PRF |o--o{ CPC : "CPC_PRFREF"
    CCA ||--|{ CCS : "CCS_NUMBR"
    PAF ||--|{ PAS : "PAS_NUMBR"
    PRF ||--|{ PRV : "PRV_NUMBR"
    PSV |o--o{ CCF : "CCF_DEFSET"
    CCF {
        char CCF_CNAME PK
        char CCF_PKTID FK
        num CCF_TYPE
        num CCF_STYPE
        num CCF_APID
        char CCF_DEFSET FK
    }
    CDF {
        char CDF_CNAME PK
        num CDF_BIT PK
        num CDF_GRPSIZE PK
        char CDF_ELTYPE
        char CDF_PNAME FK
        char CDF_TMID FK
    }
    CPC {
        char CPC_PNAME PK
        num CPC_PTC
        num CPC_PFC
        char CPC_CATEG
        char CPC_PRFREF FK
        char CPC_CCAREF FK
        char CPC_PAFREF FK
    }

A command definition is built in three layers:544

  1. The packet header. CCF_PKTID selects a header layout in tcp, whose elements are listed bit by bit in pcdf. Each element is either a fixed area (F, with a value in PCDF_VALUE) or a named header parameter from pcpc. A named parameter takes its value from the command (A APID, T type, S subtype, K acknowledgement flags) or from the command subsystem (P, for example packet length and sequence count).45
  2. The application data field. cdf lists the command's elements in bit order. Each element is a fixed area (A), an editable parameter (E) or a fixed, non-editable parameter (F), and parameter elements name a cpc parameter. Only editable parameters can be given values in sequences (sdf). Elements are encoded with no gaps, so padding must be defined explicitly.46
  3. The parameter definitions. cpc gives each parameter's type (PTC/PFC; see parameter types), display format, and optional references. A numerical (de-)calibration goes to cca/ccs, a textual one to paf/pas, and a range check to prf/prv. CPC_CATEG decides which references are allowed. C requires CPC_CCAREF. T requires CPC_PAFREF. A, P and N forbid both.49

ptv attaches static pre-transmission validation expressions (parameter = value) to a command. These are ANDed and never shared.5 CDF_TMID names a monitoring parameter whose current value becomes a dynamic default. The PTC/PFC of that parameter must equal those of the command parameter.50 dst (optional, mainly for EGSE) maps an APID to a routing string such as NCTRS or EGSE.TC.0x8800. APIDs not listed go to NCTRS.51 The single Solar Orbiter dst record routes APID 1372 to EGSE.TC.0x8800.66 More on these tables: Commanding in the MIB.

docs.title: TC packet headers: tcp, pcpc, pcdf
docs.text:
The real Solar Orbiter header layout NOM_TC ("NOM_DH_TC_Packet_Header") is used by 5,318 of the 5,454 commands. Its 13 pcdf records describe this 80-bit structure. The values and bit positions below are real, taken from the pcdf table:66

The field names above are the PCDF_DESC texts, and the codes are the PCDF_TYPE values. The first seven fields (bits 0 to 47) follow the CCSDS Space Packet primary header. The last six (bits 48 to 79) form the PUS TC data field header (see PUS packet structures). The other three Solar Orbiter headers are HPC1_TC (125 commands, 7 pcdf records covering only the 48-bit primary header), NOS2KHDR ("NIS Throw Events", 6 commands) and NO_HDR ("TCP Header for CF/CS", 5 commands). The last two have no pcdf records at all.66

The "Source ID" element changed between releases. In the 2020 release it was a fixed area (F, value 0) with no header parameter. In 2025 it has type O and the new header parameter DFH_SRC ("Source ID") in pcpc.6625

Inference

ICD 7.0 lists the PCDF_TYPE values F, A, T, S, K and P.45 The O used for "Source ID" is not among them. It is presumably a Solar Orbiter or newer SCOS-2000 extension, for example a value supplied by the ground. How SCOS-2000 populates it is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Verification and sequences
docs.text:
erDiagram
    CCF ||--o{ CVP : "CVP_TASK (CVP_TYPE C)"
    CSF ||--o{ CVP : "CVP_TASK (CVP_TYPE S, not supported)"
    CVS ||--o{ CVP : "CVP_CVSID"
    CVS ||--o{ CVE : "CVE_CVSID (CVS_SOURCE V only)"
    PCF ||--o{ CVE : "CVE_PARNAM"
    PID |o--o{ CVS : "CVS_SPID (future extension)"
    CSF ||--|{ CSS : "CSS_SQNAME"
    CCF |o--o{ CSS : "CSS_ELEMID (CSS_TYPE C)"
    CSF |o--o{ CSS : "CSS_ELEMID (CSS_TYPE S)"
    CSF ||--o{ CSP : "CSP_SQNAME"
    CSS ||--o{ SDF : "SDF_SQNAME, SDF_ENTRY, SDF_ELEMID"
    CDF |o--o{ SDF : "SDF_PNAME, SDF_POS = CDF_BIT"
    CSP |o--o{ SDF : "SDF_PNAME, SDF_POS = CSP_FPNUM"
    CVS {
        num CVS_ID PK
        char CVS_TYPE
        char CVS_SOURCE
        num CVS_START
        num CVS_INTERVAL
        num CVS_SPID FK
    }
    CVP {
        char CVP_TASK PK
        char CVP_TYPE PK
        num CVP_CVSID PK
    }
    CSS {
        char CSS_SQNAME PK
        num CSS_ENTRY PK
        char CSS_TYPE
        char CSS_ELEMID FK
    }
    SDF {
        char SDF_SQNAME PK
        num SDF_ENTRY PK
        num SDF_POS PK
        char SDF_PNAME PK
        char SDF_VTYPE
        char SDF_VALUE
    }

Verification. A verification stage (cvs) is defined once and shared. It has a stage type, which is acceptance A, start S, progress 0–9 or completion C. It also has a source: report-based R (PUS service 1 reports) or parameter-based V, plus a time window.52 cvp links stages to commands (CVP_TYPE = C). The option S for sequences is defined, but the ICD states that SCOS-2000 supports verification for commands only, and a command may have at most one stage of each CVS_TYPE. cve holds the parameter/value expressions of parameter-based stages only.5354 An expression with CVE_INTER = C is an echo check. In that case CVE_VAL names a command parameter (CDF_PNAME), not a value.55 See Command verification.

Sequences. A sequence (csf) holds numbered elements (css) without gaps. Each element is a command (CSS_TYPE = C, a ccf name) or a nested sequence (S, a csf name). Comments (T) and formal-parameter elements (F, P) are defined in the ICD but marked as unsupported or future.56 The CSS_ELEMID description still says that a command element must not contain group repeaters, while the cdf section allows them from R4.2 when all repeated values are fixed in the database.5646 Solar Orbiter uses this: 2,467 command elements (234 distinct commands) contain a group repeater.66 Each element's parameter values are in sdf. A row there is keyed to the element by sequence name and entry number. For a command element, SDF_POS is the parameter's bit offset (CDF_BIT). For a nested sequence, it is the formal parameter number (CSP_FPNUM). With group repeaters, SDF_POS is the offset after expansion and SDF_REPPOS gives the original CDF_BIT.57 csp declares the sequence's formal parameters. An sdf value can refer to one of them (SDF_VTYPE = F). See Command sequences and parameter sets.

docs.title: Parameter sets
docs.text:
erDiagram
    PST ||--o{ PSV : "PSV_NAME"
    PST ||--o{ CPS : "CPS_NAME"
    PSV ||--|{ PVS : "PVS_ID"
    PST ||--o{ PVS : "PVS_PSID"
    PST ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_PARSET"
    CCF ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_NAME (PSM_TYPE C)"
    CSF ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_NAME (PSM_TYPE S)"
    PSV |o--o{ CCF : "CCF_DEFSET"
    PSV |o--o{ CSF : "CSF_DEFSET"
    PSV |o--o{ SDF : "SDF_VALSET (SDF_VTYPE P)"

A parameter set (pst) is a named collection of command or sequence parameters. A parameter value set (psv) is a named combination of values for those parameters, and its values are in pvs. psm attaches sets to commands and sequences. A command or sequence may name a default value set (CCF_DEFSET, CSF_DEFSET), and a sequence element may take its values from a set (SDF_VALSET).585960 The membership table cps is not used by SCOS-2000.61 In cps and pvs, the parameter is identified the same way as in sdf. That is CDF_PNAME plus CDF_BIT for commands, or CSP_FPNAME plus CSP_FPNUM for sequences.6162 Solar Orbiter defines no parameter sets: all five tables are empty.66

docs.title: Polymorphic references
docs.text:
Several fields point to one of several tables, and a type flag in the same or another record tells which. A generic schema tool cannot enforce these references. They are also the usual source of import warnings:

  • PCF_CURTX and CUR_SELECT share one namespace across caf, mcf, lgf and txf, disambiguated by PCF_CATEG (and, for N, by whichever table actually contains the name).2829 In 2001 the HIFI editor evaluation reported the rule then used, with numeric IDs: check caf first, then mcf, and keep the two number ranges disjoint.65
  • CVP_TASK and PSM_NAME hold a command or a sequence name, with CVP_TYPE or PSM_TYPE saying which.5363
  • CSS_ELEMID holds a command, a sequence or a formal parameter, according to CSS_TYPE.56
  • SDF_POS/SDF_PNAME, CPS_PAR/CPS_BIT and PVS_PNAME/PVS_BIT hold a command parameter (name plus bit offset) or a sequence formal parameter (name plus number).576162
  • CPC_DEFVAL and CSP_DEFVAL normally hold a value. For "Command ID" parameters (CATEG = A) they hold a command name, and for "Parameter ID" parameters (P) a parameter name.64
  • CVE_VAL normally holds a value, but a command parameter name when CVE_INTER = C.55

docs.title: Walking the main join paths with real data
docs.text: The examples below come from the 2025-09-16 Solar Orbiter MIB. The names link to the MIB explorer.66

docs.title: Packet → PID → PLF → PCF → calibration
docs.text:
The housekeeping packet TM(3,25) - SID 103 - Analog HK VLDA arrives with APID 1092, type 3 and subtype 25.

  1. pic for type 3 / subtype 25 (no APID given) says that PI1 is 8 bits wide at byte offset 16. There is no PI2 (offset −1).
  2. pid for (3, 25, 1092, PI1 = 103, PI2 = 0) gives SPID 59203, TPSD −1 (fixed layout) and PID_DFHSIZE = 16. The ICD declares PID_DFHSIZE irrelevant for fixed packets.20
  3. tpcf for SPID 59203 gives the mnemonic YIT59203 and TPCF_SIZE = 39. That size field is not imported and serves only mission-specific tools.47
  4. plf for SPID 59203 places 12 parameters, at byte offsets 16, 17, 19, …, 37. All are 16-bit unsigned integers (PTC 3, PFC 12), except the 8-bit SID field at offset 16.
  5. pcf for NIT0E028 ("V_Pix") gives category N and PCF_CURTX = CIT01053TM. The parameter NIT83001 ("HK_SID", PTC 2 PFC 8) is category S with PCF_CURTX = CITT1120TM.
  6. Calibration. CIT01053TM is not in caf. It is in mcf (poly/CIT01053TM, "Vpix_Abs_Bias"), a polynomial with coefficients 0 and 0.001033884, so eng = 0.001033884 × raw. CITT1120TM is in txf (txt/CITT1120TM, 18 aliases). Its txp maps raw 103 to HK_SID_103.

The SID field (NIT83001) is placed by plf at byte 16, exactly where pic tells the packetiser to read PI1. The identification field and the parameter that displays it are one and the same bits, defined twice: once as an identification rule and once as a parameter.

SQL used 
SELECT * FROM pic WHERE PIC_TYPE='3' AND PIC_STYPE='25';
SELECT * FROM pid WHERE PID_SPID='59203';
SELECT * FROM tpcf WHERE TPCF_SPID='59203';
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC, l.PLF_OFFBY, l.PLF_OFFBI,
       c.PCF_CATEG, c.PCF_CURTX
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID='59203' ORDER BY CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS int);
SELECT * FROM caf WHERE CAF_NUMBR='CIT01053TM';     -- no row
SELECT * FROM mcf WHERE MCF_IDENT IN ('CIT01053TM','CIT01063TM','CIT01064TM');
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR='CITT1120TM';

docs.title: Parameter → CUR → CAF/CAP, and parameter → OCF → OCP
docs.text:
The parameter NCFT2X70 ("BattDischarge_I1 (PCDUA)", PTC 3 / PFC 12, unit A) shows the two remaining monitoring paths. It is carried in SPID 30552, "SYS Safe Mode ULGA", at byte 182.66

  1. pcf gives category N and an empty PCF_CURTX, because the parameter has several calibrations.
  2. cur has two rows. Position 1 selects the numerical curve CPWP4752TM when NPWZ0000 = 10. Position 2 selects CPWP9752TM when NPWZ0000 = 11.
  3. The applicability parameter NPWZ0000 ("PCDU_MODEL", PTC 2 / PFC 8) is a dynamic user-defined constant: PCF_NATUR = R, located in SPID 66830 "Dynamic UDCs". Its textual calibration AYMODELE labels raw 10 as EM and raw 11 as FM.
  4. caf/cap. Both curves have two points. CPWP4752TM maps raw 0 and 4095 to −8.8449 and 29.8655. CPWP9752TM maps them to −8.9764 and 28.93.
  5. ocf for NCFT2X70 declares 2 checks (OCF_NBOOL) on calibrated values (OCF_INTER = C, real limits OCF_CODIN = R). An out-of-limit state needs 2 consecutive violating samples (OCF_NBCHCK).
  6. ocp holds the two checks: position 1 is a soft limit (S) from −8.9764 to 0.14, position 2 a hard limit (H) from −8.9764 to 0.15. Neither has an applicability parameter.

The calibration of this parameter therefore depends on a value that operators set on the ground through TM SPACON (see the MIB). The field semantics are those of the ICD.292324

SQL used 
SELECT * FROM cur WHERE CUR_PNAME='NCFT2X70';
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_CATEG, PCF_CURTX, PCF_NATUR FROM pcf
 WHERE PCF_NAME IN ('NCFT2X70','NPWZ0000');
SELECT PLF_NAME, PLF_SPID, PLF_OFFBY FROM plf WHERE PLF_NAME IN ('NCFT2X70','NPWZ0000');
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR='AYMODELE' AND TXP_FROM IN ('10','11');
SELECT * FROM cap WHERE CAP_NUMBR IN ('CPWP4752TM','CPWP9752TM');
SELECT * FROM ocf WHERE OCF_NAME='NCFT2X70';
SELECT * FROM ocp WHERE OCP_NAME='NCFT2X70';

docs.title: Command → CCF → CDF → CPC → PRF, and CVP → CVS
docs.text:
The command ZCD00382 ("Define HK Para Rpt Collection Interval", TC(3,130), APID 172) walks the commanding chain:

  1. ccf gives CCF_PKTID = NOM_TC, so the header is the 80-bit layout shown above.
  2. cdf has two elements, both editable (E) and both taking their default from the parameter definition (CDF_INTER = D): PCD03011 (8 bits at bit 0) and PCD03012 (16 bits at bit 8).
  3. cpc gives PCD03011 ("HK SID") the type PTC 3 / PFC 4, an 8-bit unsigned integer, with range set VCD00353. PCD03012 ("generation period report") gets PTC 3 / PFC 12, 16 bits, with range set VCD00187.
  4. prf/prv. VCD00353 allows 1 to 192 and VCD00187 allows 1 to 65535. Their descriptions read "Integer between 1 and 19" and "Integer between 1 and 65". Both are exactly 24 characters long, the Char(24) limit of PRF_DESCR, so they appear to be the real ranges cut off at that limit (84 prf descriptions are exactly 24 characters).6622
  5. cvp attaches stages 14001 and 14007. In cvs, 14001 is acceptance (A) and 14007 is completion (C). Both are report-based (R), open 0 s after release and use a 20 s interval. Report-based stages have no cve rows.
SQL used 
SELECT * FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME='ZCD00382';
SELECT CPC_NAME, CPC_DESCR, CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC, CPC_CATEG, CPC_PRFREF FROM cpc  -- CPC_PNAME is CPC_NAME in the SQLite copy
 WHERE CPC_NAME IN (SELECT CDF_PNAME FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME='ZCD00382');
SELECT * FROM prv WHERE PRV_NUMBR IN ('VCD00353','VCD00187');
SELECT * FROM cvp WHERE COL1='ZCD00382';        -- cvp/cvs are stored as COL1..COLn
SELECT * FROM cvs WHERE COL1 IN ('14001','14007');
SELECT * FROM pcdf WHERE PCDF_TCNAME='NOM_TC';

docs.title: Sequence → CSF → CSS → SDF / CSP
docs.text:
The sequence AACC309A ("STR A time update v06") has one formal parameter and two elements:

css entry Element Release sdf rows (SDF_POS, SDF_PNAME, SDF_VTYPE, SDF_VALUE) 1 command ZST15401 "STR1 Select ASP Channel", TC(154,1) A (relative to sequence start), 00.00.00 8, PST05054, F (formal parameter), XC309A01 2 command ZCD00982 "Start Time Synchronisation to User", TC(9,130) R, 00.00.01, with CSS_MANDISP = Y 0, PCD09821, E (engineering), STAR_TRACKER_A; and 8, PCD09822, R (raw), 0

The formal parameter XC309A01 ("ASP CHANNEL") is declared in csp with PTC 2 / PFC 8 and category T (textual calibration). When the sequence is loaded, the operator's value for XC309A01 flows into the PST05054 parameter of the first command.66 In the release column, CSS_RELTYPE = A counts CSS_RELTIME from the start of the sequence, and R counts it from the release of the previous command. For a command that needs its own manual dispatch (CSS_MANDISP = Y, as both elements here do), R counts from that command's dispatch time instead.48 More on release timing: Command sequences.

SQL used 
SELECT * FROM csf WHERE CSF_NAME='AACC309A';
SELECT CSS_ENTRY, CSS_TYPE, CSS_ELEMID, CSS_RELTYPE, CSS_RELTIME, CSS_MANDISP FROM css WHERE CSS_SQNAME='AACC309A';
SELECT * FROM sdf WHERE SDF_SQNAME='AACC309A';
SELECT CSP_FPNAME, CSP_FPNUM, CSP_DESCR, CSP_PTC, CSP_PFC, CSP_CATEG FROM csp WHERE CSP_SQNAME='AACC309A';

docs.title: How well the Solar Orbiter MIB respects the model
docs.text:
This wiki tested every main reference in the 2025-09-16 release:66

Reference Rows Resolved Notes plf.PLF_SPID → pid 400,792 400,792 plf.PLF_NAME → pcf 400,792 400,791 NYM0796V in SPID 66028 is missing from pcf. tpcf.TPCF_SPID ↔ pid.PID_SPID 11,150 11,150 Exactly one tpcf per pid. vpd.VPD_TPSD → pid.PID_TPSD, vpd.VPD_NAME → pcf 19,863 19,863 2,063 distinct TPSDs pcf.PCF_CURTX → calibration 30,936 30,936 26,533 txf, 3,433 caf, 970 mcf, 0 lgf cur → pcf / calibration 1,974 1,974 907 parameters. 1,944 select a caf, 30 a txf. None also has PCF_CURTX. ocf → pcf, ocp → ocf 5,338 / 7,369 all 859 checks have an applicability parameter, all resolved. cap → caf, txp → txf 7,830 / 35,032 all ccf.CCF_PKTID → tcp 5,454 5,454 4 header layouts cdf.CDF_CNAME → ccf, CDF_PNAME → cpc 47,609 / 30,703 all The other 16,906 elements are fixed areas (A). cpc → prf / cca / paf 694 / 327 / 1,624 all cvp.CVP_TASK → ccf 10,697 10,695 Two rows reference ZCSD2005, which is not in ccf. All CVP_TYPE values are C. cvp.CVP_CVSID → cvs 10,697 10,697 All 206 stages are used. cve → cvs (source V) 171 171 All 167 V stages have expressions. No R stage has any. css.CSS_ELEMID → ccf / csf 12,629 / 1,250 all Only types C and S occur. sdf → css 50,014 50,014 sdf (command elements) → cdf by name and bit 48,356 48,356 36,460 match SDF_POS = CDF_BIT. The other 11,896 match only through SDF_REPPOS = CDF_BIT (group repeaters). sdf (sequence elements) → csp by name and number 1,658 1,658 sdf with SDF_VTYPE = F → csp of the same sequence 11,575 11,575

By the ICD's import rule, the three orphan rows (one plf row and two cvp rows) would simply not be imported.9 The references agree with the model everywhere else, including the subtle SDF_REPPOS rule for commands with repeated groups.57

This wiki also tested the key of every populated table against the 2025 data. All keys are unique except in two tables:66

  • txp. Calibration CYCT0002TM contains the row raw 1 → "Active" twice, so the key TXP_NUMBR + TXP_FROM is duplicated once. The 2020 release has no such duplicate.25
  • ccs. The key CCS_NUMBR + CCS_YVALS (raw) is unique, which confirms the reading of the columns above. On the engineering side, curve CPWP8010TM maps engineering 0 to both raw 0 and raw 430. This conflicts with the ICD's requirement that command curves be one to one.16

The pid key, which includes PID_SPID, is unique. The packetiser's lookup key (the first five fields) is not: the three ground-frame packets 1000002, 1000003 and 1000006 ("Bad", "Idle" and "Good complete transfer frame") all use type 0, subtype 0, APID 1, PI1 0, PI2 0, and all three have PID_VALID = Y. The ICD allows several records with one lookup key, but only one may be valid, and at import only the last one with Y stays valid.1221

SQL used (key checks) 
-- repeat for each table with its ICD key
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM FROM txp GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 1);   -- 1
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT CCS_NUMBR, CCS_YVALS FROM ccs GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 1);  -- 0
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT CCS_NUMBR, CCS_XVALS FROM ccs GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 1);  -- 1
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL, count(*) FROM pid
 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 HAVING count(*) > 1;                                                       -- 0|0|1|0|0|3
SQL used (integrity checks) 
SELECT count(*), sum(PLF_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM pid)),
       sum(PLF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf)) FROM plf;
SELECT count(*), sum(PCF_CURTX<>''), sum(PCF_CURTX IN (SELECT CAF_NUMBR FROM caf)),
       sum(PCF_CURTX IN (SELECT TXF_NUMBR FROM txf)), sum(PCF_CURTX IN (SELECT MCF_IDENT FROM mcf))
  FROM pcf;
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_NAME IN (SELECT CUR_PNAME FROM cur) AND PCF_CURTX<>'';  -- 0
SELECT * FROM cvp WHERE COL1 NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM ccf);
SELECT COL3, count(*), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT COL1 FROM cve)) FROM cvs GROUP BY 1;
-- sdf -> cdf (temporary indexed copy, because the database is opened read-only)
CREATE TEMP TABLE tcdf AS SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_PNAME, CDF_BIT FROM cdf;
CREATE INDEX temp.i1 ON tcdf(CDF_CNAME, CDF_PNAME, CDF_BIT);
SELECT count(*), sum(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM tcdf d WHERE d.CDF_CNAME=s.SDF_ELEMID
                            AND d.CDF_PNAME=s.SDF_PNAME AND d.CDF_BIT=s.SDF_POS))
  FROM sdf s WHERE s.SDF_ELEMID IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM ccf);

docs.title: Display definitions in the MIB
docs.text:
A SCOS-2000 operator rarely looks at raw packets. They look at displays: pages of named parameter values, plots against time, or scrolling lists of samples. The Mission Information Base (MIB) can define three kinds of telemetry display and one kind of printed report. Each has a pair of tables, a header table and a content table: DPF/DPC for alphanumeric displays (ANDs), GPF/GPC for graphic displays (GRDs), SPF/SPC for scrolling displays (SCDs) and PPF/PPC for printout proformas.1 Three more tables, GRP, GRPA and GRPK, group parameters and packets so that their processing or monitoring can be switched on and off together.2

This page describes every field of these eleven tables, following the Database Import ICD issue 7.0 (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001, 2017-08-11), and notes where older issues differ. It then looks at how projects handled the tables and at what the public Solar Orbiter MIB release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL actually contains. All Solar Orbiter numbers come from this wiki's own SQL queries.62

docs.title: Where displays fit
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 monitoring chain turns packets into parameter samples (see Monitoring in the MIB), applies calibrations and limit checks, and finally shows the results. A 2003 ESA overview lists the monitoring displays of the system: alphanumeric displays of 32 or 64 parameters, graphic displays of 1 to 8 parameters against time or against another parameter (also as a strip chart), mimic displays, scrolling displays, the Telemetry Query Display (TQD), out-of-limits displays, packet displays (the Variable Packet Display and the Telemetry Packet History Display) and the On-Board Event History Display.43 The same overview lists alphanumeric and graphic definitions among the items that can be changed on line.44

Only the first three display kinds, plus printouts, have MIB tables:

Display kind Header table Content table One content record per Solar Orbiter 2025 (header / content rows) Alphanumeric display (AND) DPF DPC displayed parameter or free-text entry 33 / 626 Graphic display (GRD) GPF GPC plotted parameter 0 / 0 Scrolling display (SCD) SPF SPC parameter column 1 / 5 Printout proforma PPF PPC printed parameter 0 / 0 Monitoring group GRP GRPA (parameters), GRPK (packets) group member 2 / 0 + 4

Roles from the ICD;56 counts from the Solar Orbiter MIB.60

The ICD's summary of display data adds two limits. The DPF/DPC pair does not define the Telemetry Query Display or the detailed out-of-limits display. And the VPD table, which describes variable packets, carries its own display attributes.5 The ICD defines no table for mimic displays.

flowchart LR
    PLF["PLF<br/>fixed-packet parameters"] --> TMM["Telemetry model<br/>(validity, calibration,<br/>limit checks)"]
    SYN["Synthetic parameters<br/>(OL / hard-coded / saved)"] --> TMM
    TMM --> AND["AND<br/>DPF + DPC"]
    TMM --> GRD["GRD<br/>GPF + GPC"]
    TMM --> SCD["SCD<br/>SPF + SPC"]
    TMM --> PRT["Printout<br/>PPF + PPC"]
    VPD["VPD<br/>variable packets"] --> VPDAPP["Variable Packet Display<br/>(own display attributes)"]
    GRP["GRP + GRPA / GRPK"] -. "enable / disable<br/>processing or monitoring" .-> TMM

Diagram drawn from the ICD's description of displays, groups and variable packets.127

docs.title: Which parameters can appear on a display
docs.text: Only parameters processed by the telemetry model library can be put on an AND, GRD, SCD or printout. That means telemetry parameters located through the PLF, and synthetic parameters of any kind. Values extracted from variable packets can only be shown by the VPD application.1 Issue 5.1 of the ICD (2001) was stricter: it allowed only values extracted from fixed packets with the PLF, and did not mention synthetic parameters.36 Issue 6.4 added the wider rule as a clarification valid for all SCOS-2000 releases. The same restriction applies to the fields CDF_TMID, CUR_RLCHK, PCF_VALID, OCP_RLCHK, PTV_PARNAM and CVE_PARNAM.10 Elsewhere the ICD explains why: values extracted from variable packets do not take part in full telemetry processing, because their parameters and time references are only known once the packet is opened (see Monitoring in the MIB),11 while synthetic parameters are handled like telemetry parameters once computed (see Synthetic parameters).12

docs.title: From ASCII tables to XML in the FARC
docs.text:
From SCOS-2000 release 5.0 (ICD issue 6.4, March 2007), display and command sequence definitions are kept outside the run-time ("POST") MIB database, where earlier releases held them (the GPF and GPC were already read directly by the applications rather than imported, even in issue 5.1).54 Each AND, GRD and SCD is stored as an XML file in the FARC (File Archive), and the applications, such as the TM Desktop, load the definitions from there.1516

The ASCII tables are still accepted for backward compatibility. On user request, the importer converts them into XML files. The conversion works as a delta: only the displays present in the delivered ASCII files are replaced, and existing definitions, including displays drawn interactively with the TM Desktop display editor, are kept.116 The ICD gives two consequences of the change. A display can be updated without importing a new TM/TC database, and importing displays never deletes the ones already there.16 The XML format itself is defined in a separate document, AD-5, ICD-5001 "SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD".17 That document is not in this wiki's library, so the XML schema is not described here.

sequenceDiagram
    participant DB as Off-line database<br/>(mission)
    participant IMP as SCOS-2000 importer
    participant POST as Run-time MIB (POST)
    participant FARC as FARC (File Archive)
    participant TMD as TM Desktop
    DB->>IMP: pcf.dat, plf.dat, ... + dpf/dpc, gpf/gpc, spf/spc
    IMP->>POST: monitoring and commanding tables
    Note over IMP,FARC: Display tables are not loaded into POST (R5.0 onwards)
    IMP->>FARC: one XML file per AND / GRD / SCD,<br/>delta: only delivered displays are replaced
    TMD->>FARC: load display definition
    TMD-->>FARC: displays edited on line are stored too

Sequence drawn from ICD §2.5 and §3.3.2.7.161

Inference

Because the run-time system keeps its displays in the FARC, a mission's delivered dpf.dat and dpc.dat need not hold the full set of displays used in operations. Displays created with the TM Desktop editor exist only as XML files. A small or empty display table in a public MIB release therefore says little about how many displays the control team uses.

docs.title: Alphanumeric displays: DPF and DPC
docs.text: An alphanumeric display (AND) is a page of parameter names and current values. The DPF holds one record per display, and the DPC one record per displayed parameter or free comment.1920

docs.title: DPF fields
docs.text:
# Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) DPF_NUMBE Char(8) M Name of the AND, unique. 2 DPF_TYPE Char(1) M 1: 32-parameter display that also shows information about the packet that carried the last displayed sample. 3: 64-parameter display. 3 DPF_HEAD Char(32) Header text on the top line of the display.

Fields from the ICD.19 No value 2 is defined: the ICD lists only 1 and 3, in issue 5.1 as in issue 7.0.1938

docs.title: DPC fields
docs.text:
# Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) DPC_NUMBE Char(8) M AND name, matching DPF_NUMBE. 2 DPC_NAME Char(8) Parameter to display (a PCF_NAME), or null for a free-text entry. When null, DPC_COMM, DPC_MODE and DPC_FORM are irrelevant. When not null, DPC_TEXT is irrelevant. 3 (key) DPC_FLDN Number(2) M Position on the display, 0 to 63. Positions 0–31 are in the left column, 32–63 in the right column. 4 DPC_COMM Number(4) 0 Which sample of a super-commutated parameter (PLF_NBOCC > 1) to show, 0 to 9999. 0 selects all samples, shown in turn if super-commutated processing is enabled in the TM Desktop. 5 DPC_MODE Char(1) Y Y: invalid values are shown only if the TM Desktop option "Display invalid values" is set. N: invalid values are always shown. 6 DPC_FORM Char(1) N Value format: B binary, O octal, D decimal, H hexadecimal, N normal. B, O and H apply only to raw values of unsigned integers. N shows the engineering value of a calibrated parameter, and the raw value in decimal otherwise. 7 DPC_TEXT Char(32) Free comment, used only when DPC_NAME is null. Optional, for backward compatibility.

Fields from the ICD.202122 The key is DPC_NUMBE plus DPC_FLDN: one record per position. The 64 positions map onto the display like this:

Left column Right column position 0 position 32 position 1 position 33 … … position 31 position 63

Layout rule from DPC_FLDN.21 A type 1 display holds 32 parameters and also shows information about the packet of the last displayed sample.19

Inference

The ICD does not say in so many words that a type 1 AND is restricted to positions 0–31. It follows from "32-parameter display" combined with the left/right split of DPC_FLDN, and the Solar Orbiter data agree: none of the 404 DPC records of its type 1 displays uses a position above 31, while 93 of the 222 records of its type 3 displays do.63

docs.title: How the DPC changed between ICD issues
docs.text:
The DPC is one of the few display tables that changed noticeably after 2001:

Field Issue 5.1 (2001) Issue 7.0 (2017) DPC_NAME mandatory may be null (free-text entry) DPC_COMM default 1, range 1–9999 default 0, range 0–9999, 0 = all samples DPC_FORM = N engineering value "for parameters associated to a calibration curve" engineering value for parameters with "one or more calibration definitions" DPC_TEXT absent (6 fields) field 7, free comment

Comparison from the two issues.382122 The change log of issue 7.0 dates the free-text entries: they came with SCOS-2000 release 4.0, in ICD issue 6.0 ("It is now possible to insert free entries in ANDs display").53

Inference

The new DPC_FORM wording plausibly follows the addition of multiple, conditional calibrations through the CUR table (see Calibration in the MIB); the change log does not link the two.

docs.title: Generated ANDs: the System Control tool
docs.text: Not every AND is written by hand. The ICD describes a tool, SCTLgenerateMIB, that reads the configuration file of the System Control application (SCTL, which starts, stops and monitors the SCOS-2000 server families) and adds default records to the MIB ASCII files: PLF, PID, TPCF, OCF, OCP, TXP and a table printed "TXT" (presumably TXF) for the system control parameters, and DPF and DPC records for their ANDs. It must be run before System Control is first launched, followed by an import of the domain's database.52

docs.title: Worked example: a real Solar Orbiter AND record
docs.text:
The real line below (bytes from the Solar Orbiter file dpc.dat, with each tab shown as ⇥) puts the parameter NIC00M00 at position 0 of the AND DICAMCK0:64

DICAMCK0⇥NIC00M00⇥0⇥1⇥N⇥N⇥

Read against the field table: display DICAMCK0, parameter NIC00M00, position 0, sample 1, invalid values always shown (N), normal format (N), and an empty seventh field (DPC_TEXT). The trailing tab is required: the ICD asks for the separator of every field to be present even when the value is null.18 The four records of this display, joined with the PCF, give the whole page:64

Pos. Parameter PCF_DESCR PTC/PFC Calibration DPC_FORM 0 NIC00M00 Memory ID 2/16 CICT0205TM N 1 NIC00M05 Start Address 3/14 – H 2 NIC00M10 NSAUs 3/14 – H 3 NIC00M20 Memory CRC 3/12 – H

The display header in dpf.dat is DICAMCK0⇥1⇥Memory Check Report: a type 1 display.64 The memory identifier is an enumerated value (PTC 2) shown as text through its textual calibration. The start address, the size and the CRC are unsigned integers (PTC 3; see parameter types) shown in hexadecimal, which is exactly the case the ICD allows for format H.22 In the PLF these parameters sit in the packet (6,10) "SPICE Memory Check Report" of APID 1385, a PUS service 6 memory check report, so the display puts the result of a memory check on one page.64

docs.title: Graphic displays: GPF and GPC
docs.text: A graphic display (GRD) plots up to eight parameters against time, or against another parameter. The ICD remarks that the GPF and the GPC are not imported into the SCOS-2000 database but read directly by the SCOS-2000 applications.23

docs.title: GPF fields
docs.text:
# Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) GPF_NUMBE Char(8) M Name of the GRD, unique. 2 GPF_TYPE Char(1) M Layout: F full screen, 8 plots against time or another parameter. H half screen, 2 × 4 plots. Q quarter screen, 4 × 2 plots. S sliced screen, 8 × 1 plot. The plot count per area is a maximum, at present 8. 3 GPF_HEAD Char(32) Header text on the top line. 4 GPF_SCROL Char(1) N Y: scroll the display when the plot reaches the end of the area. Meaningless for plots against spin phase or another parameter. 5 GPF_HCOPY Char(1) N Y: automatic hard copy at the end of the plot area. 6 GPF_DAYS Number(2) M Days in the X-axis time span, 0–99. For parameter-against-parameter plots it sets the display duration. 7 GPF_HOURS Number(2) M Hours in the time span, 0–23. Same note. 8 GPF_MINUT Number(2) M Minutes in the time span, 0–59. Same note. 9 GPF_AXCLR Char(1) M Colour of axes, ticks and grids (colour codes below). 10 GPF_XTICK Number(2) M Intervals between ticks on the X axis, 1–99. 11 GPF_YTICK Number(2) M Intervals between ticks on the Y axis, 1–99. 12 GPF_XGRID Number(2) M Intervals between grid lines on the X axis, 1–99. 13 GPF_YGRID Number(2) M Intervals between grid lines on the Y axis, 1–99. 14 GPF_UPUN Number(2) Update rate in seconds, 1–99, for external applications that read the database. Not used by SCOS-2000.

Fields from the ICD.232425 Issue 5.1 differs on two points. GPF_MINUT was a decimal number from 0.0 to 59.9, so that 0.1 with no days and hours gave a 6-second axis. GPF_UPUN was expressed in milliseconds.39 Issue 6.7 corrected the GPF_MINUT description to an integer from 0 to 59 as an editorial fix (S2K-DCR-5502), applicable to all releases.13

docs.title: GPC fields
docs.text:
The GPC holds one record per plotted parameter and is expected to be sorted by GPC_NUMBE and GPC_POS.26

# Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) GPC_NUMBE Char(8) M GRD name, matching GPF_NUMBE. 2 (key) GPC_POS Number(1) M Order of the entry in the GRD. 3 GPC_WHERE Char(1) M Plot area (see the layout table below). 4 GPC_NAME Char(8) M Parameter to plot (PCF_NAME). 5 GPC_RAW Char(1) U C or space: plot the calibrated value. U: plot the raw value. 6 GPC_MINIM Char(14) M Value at the start of the axis, raw or engineering according to GPC_RAW, in a format compatible with the parameter type. 7 GPC_MAXIM Char(14) M Value at the end of the axis, same rules. 8 GPC_PRCLR Char(1) M Colour of the symbols and connecting lines. 9 GPC_SYMB0 Char(1) 0 Symbol per sample: 0 none, 1 X, 2 +, 3 0, 4 *, 5 <>, 6 []. 10 GPC_LINE Char(1) 0 Line between samples: 0 none, 1 solid, 2 long dash, 3 dash, 4 short dash, 5 dash alternated with short dash. 11 GPC_DOMAIN Number(5) Domain of the parameter, 0 to 2^16−1, for displays that mix parameters of several domains. Optional, for backward compatibility.

Fields from the ICD.26272829 The symbol field really is spelled GPC_SYMB0, with a zero, in both issue 5.1 and issue 7.0.2840 GPC_DOMAIN is the only new GPC field since issue 5.1. It lets one GRD mix parameters of several SCOS-2000 domains (see SCOS-2000 architecture).2940 It was added for SCOS-2000 release 4.0 (ICD issue 6.0). The change log adds that the equivalent for ANDs and SCDs would only be supported from release 5.0, and indeed the DPC and SPC have no domain field.14

GPC_WHERE depends on the GRD type:

GPF_TYPE Plot areas GPC_WHERE values F full screen 1 1 parameter to plot, P the X-axis parameter (for a parameter-against-parameter plot) H half screen 2 1 top graph, 2 bottom graph Q quarter screen 4 1–4, numbered clockwise from the top-left area S sliced screen 8 1–8, numbered top-down from the top-most area

Mapping from the ICD.26

flowchart TB
    subgraph Q["GPF_TYPE = Q (quarter screen): GPC_WHERE clockwise from top left"]
        direction LR
        q1["1 (top left)"] --- q2["2 (top right)"]
        q4["4 (bottom left)"] --- q3["3 (bottom right)"]
    end

Area numbering for type Q as stated by the ICD.26

docs.title: Colour codes
docs.text:
GRDs and SCDs share one eight-colour code:

Code 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 Colour Black (SPC only) Green Blue Cyan Red Yellow Magenta White

GPF_AXCLR and GPC_PRCLR accept codes 1 to 7. SPC_BACK and SPC_FORE also accept 0, black.252733

docs.title: Scrolling displays: SPF and SPC
docs.text: A scrolling display (SCD) shows up to five parameters. For each parameter, a new sample either opens a new line, so that the display becomes a running log, or overwrites the previous value.3031

docs.title: SPF fields
docs.text: # Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) SPF_NUMBE Char(8) M Name of the SCD, unique. 2 SPF_HEAD Char(32) Header text on the top line. 3 SPF_NPAR Number(1) M Number of parameters, 1–5. Must equal the number of SPC records of this SCD. 4 SPF_UPUN Number(2) Update rate in seconds, 1–99, for external applications. Not used by SCOS-2000.

docs.title: SPC fields
docs.text:
The SPC is expected to be sorted by SPC_NUMBE and SPC_POS.31

# Field Type M/Def Meaning 1 (key) SPC_NUMBE Char(8) M SCD name, matching SPF_NUMBE. 2 (key) SPC_POS Number(1) M Order of the entry in the SCD. 3 SPC_NAME Char(8) M Parameter (PCF_NAME). 4 SPC_UPDT Char(1) space Space or null: update by scrolling onto a new line. N: overwrite the old value (no scrolling). 5 SPC_MODE Char(1) space Space or null: invalid values shown only if the TM Desktop option is set. N: invalid values always shown. 6 SPC_FORM Char(1) N Value format, same codes as DPC_FORM. 7 SPC_BACK Char(1) 0 Background colour of the field. 8 SPC_FORE Char(1) M Foreground colour of the field.

Fields from the ICD.30313233 Note the asymmetry with the DPC: on an AND the default DPC_MODE is Y, while on an SCD the "respect the TM Desktop option" setting is a space.2232 As with the GRD, issue 5.1 expressed SPF_UPUN in milliseconds.41

docs.title: Printouts: PPF and PPC
docs.text:
A printout proforma lists up to 32 parameters to be printed. The ICD says that the PPF and PPC need not be imported into the run-time database and may be read directly by the relevant application as initialisation files. It also warns that, at present, printout proformas can only be defined with the SCOS-2000 editor: importing them as specified would need changes to the underlying data structures.34

Table # Field Type M/Def Meaning PPF 1 (key) PPF_NUMBE Char(4) M Name of the proforma, unique. Note the 4-character limit. PPF 2 PPF_HEAD Char(32) Header printed on the top line of each page. PPF 3 PPF_NBPR Number(2) Number of parameters, 1–32, consistent with the PPC records. PPC 1 (key) PPC_NUMBE Char(4) M Proforma name, matching PPF_NUMBE. PPC 2 (key) PPC_POS Number(2) M Position of the parameter in the printout. PPC 3 PPC_NAME Char(8) M Parameter (PCF_NAME). PPC 4 PPC_FORM Char(1) N Print format, same codes as DPC_FORM.

Fields from the ICD.3435 Issue 5.1 spells the third PPF field PPF_NBPR0.42

docs.title: Value formats shared by all displays
docs.text:
The format code is the same in DPC, SPC and PPC (and, for variable packets, VPD_FORM):

Code Shows Allowed for B binary raw values of unsigned integer parameters O octal raw values of unsigned integer parameters D decimal no restriction stated H hexadecimal raw values of unsigned integer parameters N "normal": the engineering value if the parameter is calibrated, otherwise the raw value in decimal any

Codes from the ICD.223235 For VPD_FORM, "normal" means the engineering value only when the parameter has a single calibration in PCF_CURTX.8 The calibration section of the ICD gives the reason: the Variable Packets Display, like the Packet History Display, cannot show the calibrated value of a parameter with conditional calibrations and shows the raw value instead.51

docs.title: Display attributes of variable packets
docs.text:
Variable packets have no DPF/GPF/SPF entries. The ICD says explicitly that the VPD has no relation to the DPF, GPF, SPF or PLF tables. The VPD carries its own display attributes, and a fixed packet can also be described in the VPD just to view it with the Variable Packet Display.7

Field Meaning for the display VPD_DISDESC Char(16) Text used to build the header line. VPD_WIDTH Number(2) 0: value not shown. Greater than 0: value shown in full. VPD_JUSTIFY Char(1) L left (default), R right, C centred. VPD_NEWLINE Char(1) Y: show this parameter on a new line. Only for packets without repeated groups; repeated groups are aligned one repetition per row automatically. VPD_DCHAR Number(1) 0 value only, 1 name and value, 2 name, PCF_DESCR and value. In variable packets, 2 only for parameters with VPD_PIDREF = Y. VPD_FORM Char(1) Value format, codes as above.

Fields from the ICD.89 The full VPD, including how repeated groups and choice fields are decoded, is on Monitoring in the MIB.

docs.title: Monitoring groups: GRP, GRPA and GRPK
docs.text:
Groups are not displays, but the ICD files them next to the display tables and they serve the same operator. A group lets the control system enable or disable the processing or the monitoring of a set of parameters or packets with one action.2

Table # Field Type M Meaning GRP 1 (key) GRP_NAME Char(14) M Group name, unique. GRP 2 GRP_DESCR Char(24) M Description. GRP 3 GRP_GTYPE Char(2) M PA parameter group, PK packet group. GRPA 1 (key) GRPA_GNAME Char(14) M Group (GRP_NAME of a PA group). GRPA 2 (key) GRPA_PANAME Char(8) M Member parameter (PCF_NAME); only PLF parameters or synthetic parameters. GRPK 1 (key) GRPK_GNAME Char(14) M Group (GRP_NAME of a PK group). GRPK 2 (key) GRPK_PKSPID Number(10) M Member packet (PID_SPID).

Fields from the ICD.234 Note that group names may be 14 characters long, longer than the 8 characters of parameter and display names. The three tables are absent from ICD issue 5.1 and present in issue 6.7 Draft A (see History of the Database Import ICD).3637

docs.title: How projects treated the display tables
docs.text:
Several Herschel/Planck documents show how projects and tools handled the display tables.

HPSDB, the Herschel/Planck system database. The Alcatel technical note on MIB processing by HPSDB lists, field by field, how each table is loaded and regenerated:45

  • DPF and DPC fields are copied. Names follow the project naming convention, and display headers must avoid the characters reserved by XML (<, >, quote, double quote and &).4546
  • GPF_MINUT must be an integer from 00 to 59; real values are forbidden. This matches the later ICD rule, but not issue 5.1, which allowed tenths of a minute.4739
  • GPF_UPUN and SPF_UPUN are not loaded and not generated, and must be set to null. A non-conformance report was open to support them.47
  • GPC_POS must be in the range 0–7. A non-conformance report asked for 0–9, and the note finds it odd that a key field could be null. For SPC_POS an NCR was to be written to enforce the range 1–9 with at most 5 records. SPF_NPAR is recalculated rather than copied.47
  • PPF and PPC are not loaded at all and "shall not be present".48
  • GRP, GRPA and GRPK are treated as Central Checkout System (CCS) data. Members of a parameter group must all be of the same type.49

HIFI. The HIFI requirements for a MIB editor (2000) group the six display tables as "Operator" data and ask for a form showing the layout of alphanumeric, graphic and scrolling displays.5055 HIFI's evaluation of ESOC's MS-Access database editor found that gpf_upun and spf_upun were wrongly enforced as mandatory.56

SPIRE. The SPIRE MIB naming convention gives each display kind its own name pattern: SAiiippp for numerical (alphanumeric) displays, SGiiippp for graphical displays and SLiiippp for scrolling displays. Here iii is a theoretical parameter identifier and ppp a position identifier.57 The details are on Mission tailoring of the MIB.

EGSE. ESA's SCOS-2000 based EGSE (EMCS; the copy in the library comes from the SPIRE archive) came with a minimum data set, MIN_EGSE (directory MIN_EGSE_v2), whose dpc.dat holds AND definitions. A mission had to update the ZREJTM and ZVERIFT6 definitions in dpc.dat to match its own TM packet header.58 See SCOS-2000 as EGSE.

The Herschel/Planck Operations Interface Requirements Document lists AND as "Alphanumerical Display", GRD as "Graphical Display" and MDD as "Mimic Display Diagrams" among its acronyms.59

docs.title: What the Solar Orbiter MIB contains
docs.text: The September 2025 Solar Orbiter release contains all eleven display and group tables. Four of them (gpf.dat, gpc.dat, ppf.dat, ppc.dat) are empty files, and grpa.dat is empty too.61

docs.title: Alphanumeric displays
docs.text:
There are 33 ANDs: 28 of type 1 (32 parameters) and 5 of type 3 (64 parameters), with 626 DPC records in total.62 Every DPC record names a parameter. There are no free-text entries, so the optional seventh field DPC_TEXT is filled only in a single test record, where it is irrelevant (see below). Every displayed parameter exists in the PCF. 621 of them are located by the PLF, and the other 5 are dynamic OL synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = D), which the ICD allows.63

The display names show who supplied them. Thirty-one of the 33 ANDs begin with DICA, and 608 of the 626 records display parameters whose names begin with NIC. Their headers and parameter descriptions point to the SPICE instrument: "SPICE Temperatures", "SPICE Instrument Params", "Focus_Derived_Posn".6263 One AND, DIPA0001 "Status Overview", shows 17 NIP parameters such as NIPS0000 "PHI_TMTCDB_version".63

AND Type Header Records DICA0000 3 SEB/DPM Params 61 DICA1100 3 SPICE Temperatures 33 DICA1200 3 RT HK Params 63 DICA2000 3 SPICE Instrument Params 64 DICA0100–DICA1500 (12 displays) 1 SDM, Detector Assembly, Slit Change Mechanism, Scan Stage, Focus Stage, FEE, HVPS, LVPS, PDS, TCS, Mechanisms, Static HK 10–27 each DICA5100–DICA5400 1 Nominal Progress / Low / Medium / High Severity Event Report 8 each DICARHK0–DICARHK3 1 RTHK Heaters & Temperatures, HV Parameters, Mechanism Parameters, Miscellaneous Parameters 14–24 each DICADHK0, DICAFHK0, DICAUHK0 1 Diagnostic HK, IPF HK, CPU HK Display 6–21 each DICAMCK0, DICATM12, DICATM18, DICA3000 1 Memory Check Report, TM Acceptance Failure Report, TM Execution Failure Report, SPICE SpW and Safety Params 4–23 each DIPA0001 1 Status Overview 17 DQQA1234 3 This is a test 1

All rows from dpf joined with dpc.6263

The field values are strikingly uniform. 625 records set DPC_COMM = 1 (show the first sample) and DPC_MODE = N (always show invalid values). Formats are N for 578 records, H for 41 and D for 7. All 48 records with H or D are unsigned integers (PTC 3), as the ICD requires for H.63

The event-report displays show a typical use of format H. DICA5400 "High Severity Event Report" shows an event identifier with its textual calibration (N), followed by a time stamp, five event parameters and a checksum, all in hexadecimal:64

Pos. Parameter PCF_DESCR PTC/PFC DPC_FORM 0 NIC05400 TM_54_EventID 2/16 N 1 NIC05405 TM_54_TimeStamp ¾ H 2–6 NIC05410–NIC05430 TM_54_Par1 … TM_54_Par5 ¾ H 7 NIC05435 TM_54_Cksum 3/12 H

In the PLF these parameters sit in packets of type (5,4), APID 1367, a high-severity event report, and the display is a simple decoder for them.64

docs.title: The scrolling display
docs.text: The single SCD, DICSP000 "SPICE SFM Positions", declares SPF_NPAR = 5 with an update rate of 10 s, and has exactly five SPC records, as the ICD requires.65 All five scroll (SPC_UPDT empty), always show invalid values (N), and use black background (0) with blue foreground (2). Four unsigned parameters, NIC0P015 Scan_LVDT_Cmd, NIC0P005 Scan_Position, NIC0P020 Focus_LVDT_Cmd and NIC0P010 Focus_Position, are shown in hexadecimal. The fifth, NICDF014 Scan_Loop_Mode, is an enumeration shown in normal format.65

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Two groups are defined: GRPHK "Packet for HK monitoring" (PK) and GRPPAR "Example for Parameters" (PA). GRPPAR has no members. GRPHK holds four packets, all of them SWA housekeeping packets of type (3,25): SPIDs 58200 SWA_TM_DPU_HK, 58201 SWA_TM_EAS1_HK and 58202 SWA_TM_EAS2_HK from APID 1540, and 58907 SWA_TM_II_INFO from APID 1525.66

docs.title: Traces of an instrument template
docs.text:
The test display DQQA1234 "This is a test" holds one record. It shows the SWA parameter NIA00510 (PLUS_12V_HT_OUT) at position 2, with DPC_COMM = 0, DPC_MODE = Y and the text "Comment" in DPC_TEXT, which the ICD ignores when a parameter is named.63 Exactly the same DPF and DPC rows, and the same two groups, appear in the separately published SWA instrument database.68 In the April 2020 release, the DPF, DPC, SPF, SPC and GRPK tables are identical to those of 2025, while GRPPAR is not yet defined.67

Inference

The display content of the public Solar Orbiter MIB looks like a merge of instrument contributions (SPICE, PHI and SWA) rather than the display set of the mission control team: no platform subsystem has an AND, and the only test display and both groups match the SWA instrument database one for one. Since SCOS-2000 release 5 keeps displays as XML files in the FARC, it is likely that the operational displays are maintained there and not delivered in the ASCII MIB. The MIB release itself does not say how its display tables are used.

SQL used

Run against solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (and solo-2020-04-16.sqlite, swa-idb.sqlite for the comparisons). The display and group tables are not in the pyscos2000 schema, so their columns are named COL1…COLn in ICD order: for dpc, COL1 = DPC_NUMBE, COL2 = DPC_NAME, COL3 = DPC_FLDN, COL4 = DPC_COMM, COL5 = DPC_MODE, COL6 = DPC_FORM, COL7 = DPC_TEXT.

-- row counts
SELECT count(*) FROM dpf;   -- 33   (likewise dpc 626, gpf 0, gpc 0, spf 1, spc 5,
                            --       ppf 0, ppc 0, grp 2, grpa 0, grpk 4)
SELECT COL2, count(*) FROM dpf GROUP BY 1;            -- type 1: 28, type 3: 5

-- records per AND and position range
SELECT COL1, count(*), min(CAST(COL3 AS int)), max(CAST(COL3 AS int)) FROM dpc GROUP BY 1;
SELECT f.COL2, count(*), sum(CAST(d.COL3 AS int) >= 32)
  FROM dpc d JOIN dpf f ON f.COL1 = d.COL1 GROUP BY 1; -- type 1: 404/0, type 3: 222/93

-- field value distributions
SELECT COL4, count(*) FROM dpc GROUP BY 1;   -- DPC_COMM
SELECT COL5, count(*) FROM dpc GROUP BY 1;   -- DPC_MODE
SELECT d.COL6, p.PCF_PTC, count(*) FROM dpc d JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = d.COL2 GROUP BY 1, 2;

-- integrity and nature of displayed parameters
SELECT count(*), sum(p.PCF_NAME IS NULL),
       sum(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM plf l WHERE l.PLF_NAME = d.COL2))
  FROM dpc d LEFT JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = d.COL2;   -- 626, 0, 621
SELECT p.PCF_NATUR, count(*) FROM dpc d JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = d.COL2 GROUP BY 1;
SELECT substr(COL2, 1, 3), count(*) FROM dpc GROUP BY 1;   -- NIC 608, NIP 17, NIA 1

-- scrolling display, groups
SELECT * FROM spf;  SELECT * FROM spc;
SELECT * FROM grp;
SELECT k.COL2, t.TPCF_NAME, p.PID_TYPE, p.PID_STYPE, p.PID_APID, p.PID_DESCR
  FROM grpk k JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = k.COL2 LEFT JOIN tpcf t ON t.TPCF_SPID = k.COL2;

The 2020 comparison compares the sorted contents of each table between the two databases; the SWA comparison reads dpf, dpc, grp and grpk of swa-idb.sqlite.

docs.title: History of the Database Import ICD (issues 5.1 to 7.2)
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD defines the ASCII tables of the MIB. It has changed together with SCOS-2000 itself, from the first official issue 3.2 in March 1999 to issue 7.0 in August 2017, and to an issue 7.2 of December 2019 that is known only indirectly. Each new issue documented a new SCOS-2000 release, merged functions developed for particular missions (the Herschel/Planck checkout system and Cryosat), or clarified how the importer actually behaved.1921 Compatibility is a stated goal. Issue 6.0 preserved compatibility with databases built for S2K-R3.1. Issue 7.0 states that all its changes are backwards compatible: new tables and fields may be omitted, so a MIB written to the previous issue can still be imported.12

This page reconstructs that history from the four issues in the wiki's library, using the change logs, the two annexes of implemented changes in issue 7.0, and a field-by-field comparison of the table definitions in each issue.

Issue in the library Date Document reference Issued by Library page 5.1 2001-10-26 S2K-MCS-ICD-0001-TOS-GCI ESA/TOS-GCI, "SCOS-2000 Team" icd-5-1-tos-gci 6.7 Draft A 2009-12-01 EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 ESA/OPS-GIC, "SCOS-2000 R5.2 Team" icd-6-7-drafta 6.9 2010-07-06 EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 ESA/OPS-GIC, "SCOS-2000 Team" icd-6-9-archive-org 7.0 FINAL 2017-08-11 EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 ESA/OPS-GIC, "SCOS-2000 GIMUS Team" icd-7-0-final

The title pages give the dates, references and preparing teams.3456 Between 5.1 and 6.x, the document reference changed from the "TOS-GCI" form to the "EGOS" form, and the issuing unit appears as ESA/OPS-GIC instead of ESA/TOS-GCI. The library page of each source records where and when this wiki copied it. The 6.9 copy is a third-party copy held by the Internet Archive (a "manualzilla" item), not a download from ESA.

Issues 3.2 to 7.0 and their dates come from the 7.0 change log.2 Issue 6.6 appears in that log without a date, and no library document dates it. The 7.2 entry is discussed below.

SLE throw-event command type. 6.5 2007-12-14 R4.2, R5.0.1 Updates for those releases 6.6 not in the change log (2008-08-25 per a web page outside the library) – See Annex 1 6.7 Draft A 2009-12-01 R4.5, R5.2.0i1 Includes NCR-5711 and SPR-4911 6.7 Draft B 2010-02-20 R4.5, R5.2 SCR-3774 (from DCR-6008) 6.7 Draft C 2010-05-24 R5.3.1 SPR-5504 (dynamic changes to TPSD) 6.9 2010-07-06 S2K 5.3, 5.3.1, 5.4 Consolidated version merging the parallel branches s2k52, s2k53, s2k531 and s2k4.51 7.0 FINAL 2017-08-11 5.5.x and 6.0.x (per Annex 2) 17 change requests and document updates (Annex 2) 7.2 FINAL 2019-12-13 not stated in the available sources Not in the library (see below)

The release mapping for 3.2 to 6.9 is taken from the change log.2 For 7.0 it comes from the "Applicable SCOS release" column of Annex 2.7 Issue 5.1 carries the same log up to its own entry.8 Two parallel SCOS-2000 lines can be seen in the table. The R4.x line (4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 4.5) and the R5.x line (5.0 to 5.4) were maintained side by side, which is why 6.5 serves both R4.2 and R5.0.1, and why 6.9 had to merge branches.

docs.title: The issues seen through their users
docs.text:
The library shows which issue real projects worked against:

  • The Herschel/Planck instrument EGSE "S2K", version 2.3eP5 based on SCOS-2000 2.3e, used ICD 5.1. The HPSDB technical note of 2006 takes it as its applicable document.9
  • The EGSE and Mission Control System (EMCS) user manual, issue 4.0, cites ICD 5.1 for the MIB.10
  • The HIFI MIB editor requirements of August 2000 cite the ICD as "S2K-MCS-ICD-1-TOS-GCI" without an issue number.11
  • The Thales Alenia Space/Intecs SRDB Translator was compliant with ICD 6.1 (its paper is undated in the PDF and cites issue 6.1 as "February 2006", while the 7.0 change log dates 6.1 to 10 January 2006). It could not import BepiColombo databases written to an earlier issue until the missing columns were added.122
  • The 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB has the pcf (23 fields) and cvs (7 fields) layout of issues 6.9 and 7.0. Its cpc stops after CPC_OBTID (15 fields), which is the 6.7/6.9 layout without the 7.0 future-extension field CPC_ENDIAN. The Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database writes pcf with 19 fields, cpc with 13, cvs with 6, caf with 7 and pic with 6, which are the 5.1 lengths, but vdf with 5, ccf with 21 and dpc with 7, which are the lengths introduced with 6.0.1315
  • The STIX instrument database v2.26.38 has the same mixture: pcf with 19 fields, cpc with 13, pic and cvs with 6 and caf with 7 (the 5.1 lengths), but vdf with 5 and ccf with 21 (see the STIX page).14

docs.title: Up to issue 5.1 (1999–2001)
docs.text:
Issue 5.1 already has 48 of the 53 tables of issue 7.0. It lacks only cur, lgf, grp, grpa and grpk (see the field comparison). Its Annex 1 lists the document changes that led to it:16

  • DCR-237. PTC 5 / PFC 4 was added, so that 48-bit MIL-STD reals are supported.
  • DCR-251. User-defined constants were aligned with the consolidated ICD 4.3. One UDC can no longer belong to both the static and the dynamic view.
  • DCR-253. The mapping from identification fields to SPIDs must not change, and SPIDs used during a mission phase must not be deleted. Data retrieval functions such as GDDS rely on this (see GDDS).
  • DCR-260. Only one valid SPID/TPSD/APID/type/subtype combination is allowed, for filtering in the packet history display.
  • DCR-261. Parameter names may not start with $.
  • DCR-262. VPD_OFFSET was added, so that variable packet definitions can contain gaps and overlaps.
  • DCR-263. The applicability fields OCP_RLCHK/OCP_VALPAR are not used for status consistency checks. The start reference of pic positions became the start of the source packet header.
  • DCR-255. CSF_ELEMS was widened from 3 to 5 digits.
  • DCR-188. High-priority commands may not be blocked. Blocking means aggregation into one segment.
  • DCR-241. A new command category S was introduced, for which no CRC is appended. The annex writes the field as CCF_TYPE, while the 5.1 and 7.0 field tables carry the option in CCF_CTYPE.17
  • DCR-242. A new, optional routing table was added (dst, for EGSE systems).
  • DCR-266. CCF_APID, CCF_RAPID and PID_APID were widened from Number(4) to Number(5). Values 0–2047 identify on-board APIDs and 2048–65535 ground processes.

docs.title: Issue 6.0 (2005): SCOS-2000 R4.0 and the checkout repatriations
docs.text:
Issue 6.0 is the largest single change in the library record. Its content is listed in the 7.0 Annex 1 under several headings.18

R4.0 change requests. DCR-2421 extended PCF_PID and PID_SPID from 2^31−1 to 2^32−1. DCR-2422 allowed super-commutated parameters in alphanumeric displays.18

Functions repatriated from the Herschel/Planck Central Checkout System:19

Function MIB impact Curve selection New table cur. A parameter can have several calibrations, selected by another parameter's value. Delta limits New monitoring check type: the change between successive samples must stay within a threshold. Enable/inhibit parameter or packet Processing can be stopped per parameter or per packet. Parameter and packet groups New tables grp, grpa and grpk, for enabling or inhibiting by group Curve ID Calibration identifiers changed from Number(4) to Char(10) Verification stage ID CVS_ID widened from Number(5) to Number(8) (later restricted again, see 6.7). The CVS_ID field itself is printed as Number(5) in all four library issues. Range set ID Command parameter range set identifiers changed from Number(4) to Char(10) Logarithmic curve New table lgf, Y = 1 / (A0 + A1·ln X + A2·ln² X + A3·ln³ X + A4·ln⁴ X), for platinum thermistors String parameters Octet and character strings editable on manual stacks Variable strings Optional automatic insertion of the PUS length field n

The Herschel/Planck HPSDB note of 2006 still lists cur, grp, grpa, grpk and lgf as "Specific CCS data" next to the ICD 5.1 tables. It confirms that these tables began as checkout-system extensions.20

Functions repatriated from Cryosat: "Command ID" and "Parameter ID" command parameters, and a default sub-schedule ID for execution-time-tagged commands. The sub-schedule ID added one field each to ccf and csf, namely CCF_SUBSCHEDID and CSF_SUBSCHEDID.21

R4.0 table changes: vdf gained the domain, release and issue fields. gpc gained GPC_DOMAIN, for multi-domain graphic displays (the same for ANDs and SCDs only from R5.0). Status parameters can have several OOL check sets with different applicability. dpc allows free-text entries (DPC_TEXT). Report-based verification can be disabled dynamically, through CCF_ACK.22

EGSE delivery only: PCF_NATUR = P, for SPEL-based derived parameters.23

docs.title: Issues 6.1 to 6.3 (2006–2007): R4.1 and clarifications
docs.text: Issue 6.1 restricted 48-bit reals (5/4) to command parameters (S2K-40-DCR-808). It stated that progress verification stages from spacecraft reports must be at stage 0 (DCR-0821). It corrected the PLF_TDOCC default from 0 to 1 (DCR-847). It also integrated DCRs from SCOS-2000 3.1 maintenance releases and clarified group repeaters and delta limits.24 Issues 6.2 and 6.3 (R4.1) changed the field types of the calibration and verification identifiers (CAF_NUMBR, CAP_NUMBR, TXF_NUMBR, TXP_NUMBR, CVS_ID, CVP_CVSID, CCA_NUMBR). They also removed the mandatory flag from PCF_NATUR and updated many field descriptions.25

docs.title: Issue 6.4 (2007): SCOS-2000 R5 and the FARC
docs.text:
With R5.0, command sequences and display definitions left the run-time database. They are converted into XML files in the FARC and imported as deltas, so they can be changed without re-importing the TM/TC database (see The MIB). Issue 6.4 also added:26

  • a new command type for SLE throw events, CCF_CTYPE = T;
  • command parameters of type Deduced;
  • the absolute time format 9/1 (CDS without µs);
  • the rule that only parameters processed by the TM model may be used in CDF_TMID, CUR_RLCHK, PCF_VALID, OCP_RLCHK, PTV_PARNAM, CVE_PARNAM and in displays.

docs.title: Issues 6.5 and 6.6: R4.2 and R5.0.1
docs.text:
Issue 6.5 added the following:27

  • PIC_APID (SPR-3071, DCR-4535), so that the position of the extra identification fields can depend on the APID as well as on type/subtype;
  • SDF_REPPOS (SPR-2904), so that commands with group repeaters can be used in sequences;
  • NIS throw events (CCF_CTYPE = N), beside SLE throw events (see NCTRS and NIS);
  • CSP_FPNUM extended to 65,535 formal parameters;
  • the deprecation of several packets sharing one SPID, since R5.0 stores packets in a database.

Issue 6.6 only clarified OCP_TYPE, CCF_HIPRI (high-priority commands cannot be blocked) and the CDF_ELTYPE/SDF_FTYPE combinations.29

docs.title: Issue 6.7 (2009–2010): R5.2, time correlation and the DARC
docs.text:
Issue 6.7 brought the pcf record to its final length of 23 fields. Draft A already has all four new fields:3031

  • PCF_DARC (S2K-DCR-5146, S2K-SPR-5711) flags parameters for the parameter archive (DARC). The importer itself ignores it.
  • PCF_CORR and PCF_OBTID, with CPC_CORR and CPC_OBTID (S2K-SCR-4917), encode time parameters according to on-board clock and correlation. The Unix time format 9/30 came with them.
  • PCF_ENDIAN (S2K-DCR-5192) is meant for little-endian telemetry. Draft A and 6.9 still describe it as a field that "can be used in the future". Issue 7.0 removes that wording (S2K-8353, applicable from SCOS-2000 6.0.1).317
  • PCF_DESCR was widened from 16 to 24 characters (S2K-SPR-3797).

Issue 6.7 also restricted CVS_ID to a signed short (S2K-DCR-3909). It documented CAF_INTER, present since R4 but never described (S2K-SPR-4911). And it added Appendix C, on PUS support in SCOS-2000 (S2K-DCR-5303).30 Draft B added CVS_UNCERTAINTY (S2K-SCR-3774), a per-stage verification window that overrides the TC SPACON default. Draft A does not yet have this field. Issue 6.9 has it.323334

docs.title: Issue 6.9 (2010): the consolidated R5.3/R5.4 baseline
docs.text: Issue 6.9 merged the parallel R5.2, R5.3, R5.3.1 and R4.5.1 work into one document. It set CVE_CVSID and CVP_CVSID to Number(5), in line with CVS_ID. It made PCF_OBTID and CPC_OBTID applicable from s2k52. It added §3.3.2.1.5 on system control parameters (SCTL and the SCTLgenerateMIB tool).32

docs.title: Issue 7.0 (2017): 17 changes for 5.5.x and 6.0.x
docs.text:
Annex 2 of issue 7.0 lists every change, with the SCOS-2000 release from which it applies:7

ID Type Change Applicable release S2K-6680 Change request New usage of CSF_SUBSCHEDID 5.5.2+, 6.0.0+ S2K-8073 Change request Value fields (CPC_DEFVAL, CDF_VALUE, CSP_DEFVAL, SDF_VALUE, CCS_XVALS, CCS_YVALS, PAS_ALVAL, PAS_ALTXT, PVS_VALS, PRV_MINVAL, PRV_MAXVAL) limited only by the maximum command size. Importer warnings removed. 5.5.3+, 6.0.0+ S2K-8325 Change request PCF_INTER and CAF_INTER descriptions aligned with the implementation 5.5.4+, 6.0.0+ S2K-8137 Document update ORACLE reference removed from §1.1 all S2K-8353 Change request PCF_ENDIAN description updated 6.0.1+ S2K-8560 Document update CCF_ILSCOPE values F and T documented (already supported) all S2K-8528 Document update PIC_APID made part of the key 4.2+ S2K-7551 Document update Files are in Unix format all S2K-7749 Document update New field CPC_ENDIAN as a future extension none S2K-7750 Document update VPD_FIXREP = −1 (repeat the group until the end of the packet) as a future extension none S2K-6884 Change request Reserved ground-station parameter names listed under PCF_NAME all S2K-8572 Document update PCF_CORR must be N for relative times all S2K-8063 Document update Blocking problem with the maximum time-tag encoding length explained all S2K-8681 Document update TMPH does not handle conditional calibration: the Packet History display shows raw values for such parameters (§3.3.2.2.1) all S2K-8782 Document update CDF_VALUE description updated all S2K-8226 Change request TC(11,4) encoded according to its cdf definition (MISCconfig variables) 5.5.4+ S2K-8778 Document update CPC_CORR cannot be Y for relative times all

docs.title: Issue 7.2 (2019)
docs.text:
Not in the library

No copy of issue 7.2 is in this wiki's library, and nothing on this page about 7.2 has been checked against the document itself. Two web pages outside the library report it, and this wiki has not re-opened either of them:

  • The Solar Orbiter operations wiki is reported to list the MIB ICD "iss 7.2, Final version, Dec 2019" among the MOC applicable documents: https://issues.cosmos.esa.int/solarorbiterwiki/display/SOSP/MOC+Applicable+Documents.
  • The documentation of the Python library pyscos2000 (IRF) is reported to state that its table schemas are based on EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 issue 7.2-FINAL of 2019-12-13: https://irf.developer.irf.se/pyscos2000/.

This wiki builds its SQLite copies of the MIB with column names taken from the pyscos2000 schema (see MIB tooling). Comparing those column lists with ICD 7.0 shows what pyscos2000 expects:

Table ICD 7.0 pyscos2000 ("7.2") Difference pcf 23 fields, ending PCF_ENDIAN 24 columns An extra last column, PCF_DESCR2 cpc 16 fields, ending CPC_ENDIAN 17 columns CPC_DESCR2 inserted before CPC_ENDIAN vdf, cpc, css VDF_DOMAINID, CPC_PNAME, CPC_OBTID, CSS_STAPTV VDF_DOMAIN, CPC_NAME, CPC_OBTIP, CSS_STATPTV Spelling only all others among its 36 tables – same names and order –

pyscos2000 has no schema for 17 of the 53 ICD 7.0 tables: grp, grpa, grpk, the eight display tables, cvs, cve, cvp, cps, pvs and psm.

Inference

The two "DESCR2" columns suggest that issue 7.2 added a long second description to monitoring and command parameters, like the existing CCF_DESCR2 and CSF_DESC2. The spelling differences may be pyscos2000's own choices or real 7.2 renamings, and the available sources cannot tell which. The Solar Orbiter files, which follow the 7.2 baseline according to the operations wiki above, use neither PCF_DESCR2 (23 fields per pcf line) nor CPC_ENDIAN (15 fields per cpc line).13

docs.title: Field-level comparison of the library issues
docs.text:
The table below compares the field tables of the four issues in the library. Fields were extracted from the text of each PDF, with their position, key flag and declared type, and compared table by table, then checked by hand against the PDF text. Only differences are listed. Two apparent differences are typing errors in issue 5.1 and are not listed: it numbers both PID_EVENT and PID_EVID as field 15, and prints PPF_NBPR as PPF_NBPR0. Issue 6.9 prints the CVE_CVSID and CVP_CVSID types as "Number(105", read here as the Number(5) that its Annex 1 entry states.3635

Table 5.1 → 6.7 Draft A 6.7 Draft A → 6.9 6.9 → 7.0 vdf +VDF_DOMAINID, VDF_RELEASE, VDF_ISSUE (2 → 5 fields) – – pcf +PCF_CORR, PCF_OBTID, PCF_DARC, PCF_ENDIAN (19 → 23). PCF_DESCR Char(16) → Char(24). PCF_CURTX Number(4) → Char(10). – – cur, lgf, grp, grpa, grpk new tables – – caf, cap, txf, txp, mcf, cca, ccs, paf, pas, prf, prv Identifier Number(4) → Char(10). +CAF_INTER. – Value fields of ccs, pas and prv lose their length limit pic +PIC_APID (6 → 7) – PIC_APID becomes a key dpc, gpc +DPC_TEXT, +GPC_DOMAIN – – ccf +CCF_SUBSCHEDID (20 → 21) – – cpc +CPC_CORR, CPC_OBTID (13 → 15). Reference fields Number(4) → Char(10). – +CPC_ENDIAN (15 → 16). CPC_DEFVAL unlimited. cdf CDF_GRPSIZE becomes a key – CDF_VALUE unlimited csf +CSF_SUBSCHEDID (15 → 16) – – css CSS_EXTIME Char(16) → Char(17) – – sdf +SDF_REPPOS (9 → 10). SDF_PNAME becomes a key. – SDF_VALUE unlimited csp CSP_FPNUM Number(3) → Number(5). Reference fields → Char(10). – CSP_DEFVAL unlimited cvs – +CVS_UNCERTAINTY (6 → 7) – cve, cvp *_CVSID Number(5) → Number(10) → Number(5) (per Annex 1) – pvs – – PVS_VALS unlimited

The rows above are this wiki's comparison of §3.3 in each issue.36313437 Each change matches an Annex 1 or Annex 2 entry described above. The table count rose from 48 (5.1) to 53 (6.7 Draft A onwards) and has not changed since, as far as the library issues show.

How to read 'unlimited'

In issue 7.0, the value fields are typed Char without a length. §3.3 explains that a field without a length is limited by another limit, here the maximum size of a command.38

docs.title: Practical consequences for MIB producers and consumers
docs.text:
• Readers must accept several record lengths. The 7.0 importer reads pcf records with 19 to 23 fields, and the backward-compatibility rule covers the other tables too.391 Real deliveries differ: 23 fields for the Solar Orbiter pcf, 19 for the SWA IDB.1315 A tool that hard-codes one issue's field count will reject valid MIBs. This is the failure the SRDB Translator ran into with BepiColombo databases.12
  • Identifiers changed type. Calibration and range-set identifiers changed from numbers to strings in 6.0 (verification-stage identifiers stayed numeric). A 5.1-era tool that stores them as integers loses leading zeros and cannot represent names such as CIT01053TM.1913
  • Sequences and displays are delta-imported from R5.0. Removing a definition from the ASCII files does not remove it from the FARC.40
  • Future-extension fields exist. CPC_ENDIAN, VPD_FIXREP = −1 and CVS_SPID are documented but not implemented (the first two are "No SCOS version" in Annex 2). A MIB may fill them in, but SCOS-2000 will not act on them.741
SQL and commands used for the Solar Orbiter field counts 

# fields per line in the raw .dat files (2025 and 2020 releases, SWA IDB)
awk -F'\t' '{print NF}' pcf.dat | sort | uniq -c    # 2025: 126745 x 23; SWA: 2885 x 19
awk -F'\t' '{print NF}' cpc.dat | sort | uniq -c    # 2025: 7155 x 15;   SWA: 531 x 13
awk -F'\t' '{print NF}' cvs.dat | sort | uniq -c    # 2025: 206 x 7;     SWA: 2 x 6

-- the SQLite copy uses the pyscos2000 column names; the extra columns stay empty
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_DESCR2 <> '';    -- 0
SELECT count(*) FROM cpc WHERE CPC_ENDIAN <> '';    -- 0
