docs.title: Monitoring checks: limits and out-of-limits
docs.text:
Calibration turns a telemetry sample into an engineering value. Monitoring checks decide whether that value is acceptable. In the SCOS-2000 MIB, two tables define every check the ground applies. The OCF holds one record per checked parameter. The OCP holds the checks themselves: soft and hard limits, expected statuses, deltas between samples, status consistency with commanding, and event triggers. Each check can be guarded by an applicability condition.16 When a valid sample violates an applicable check often enough, SCOS-2000 declares the parameter out of limits (OOL). It then shows the parameter on the OOL display. OOL records also end up in the packet archive, from which the EDDS delivers them to users.1923

Spacecraft can also check their own parameters, with the PUS on-board monitoring service ST[12]. The last section compares the two and shows how the Solar Orbiter MIB decodes the on-board reports. All Solar Orbiter numbers come from this wiki's SQL queries on release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL.40 Parameters and calibrations used here are introduced on Monitoring in the MIB and Calibration in the MIB.

docs.title: OCF: one record per checked parameter
docs.text:
The OCF holds at most one record per parameter. It says how many checks the parameter has, how many consecutive violations make it OOL, and in which representation the limits are written.4

# Field Type M Meaning 1* OCF_NAME Char(8) M checked parameter (PCF_NAME) 2 OCF_NBCHCK Number(2) M number of consecutive valid samples violating a check that are needed to declare the parameter OOL 3 OCF_NBOOL Number(2) M number of OCP records for this parameter, 1 to 16 4 OCF_INTER Char(1) M U uncalibrated: limits are raw values; C calibrated: limits are engineering values (only for calibrated parameters) 5 OCF_CODIN Char(1) M format of the limit values: R real, I integer, A ASCII

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.3.1.4 OCF_CODIN must match the representation chosen by OCF_INTER:4

OCF_CODIN Allowed when R real raw values of real parameters (OCF_INTER = U, PTC 5), or engineering values of parameters with a real numerical curve, a polynomial or a logarithmic calibration I integer raw values of integer parameters (OCF_INTER = U, PTC < 5), or engineering values of integer-valued numerical curves A ASCII engineering values of status parameters (PCF_CATEG = S, OCF_INTER = C), compared with alias texts

If the parameter is also used in a command verification expression, OCF_CODIN must be compatible with CVE_INTER.4

A configuration coupling

SCOS-2000's Behaviour Limit Checker can skip consecutive samples of periodic parameters whose value and validity are unchanged. If this optimisation is on (BEHV_ENABLE_OPTIMIZATION = 1), the configuration variable MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR must exceed the largest OCF_NBCHCK in the MIB.5

docs.title: OCP: the checks
docs.text:
The OCP holds one record per check. SCOS-2000 applies the checks of a parameter in the order of the table, which must be sorted by OCP_NAME and OCP_POS.68

# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* OCP_NAME Char(8) M checked parameter (OCF_NAME) 2* OCP_POS Number(2) M order of the check; soft/hard pairs ordered soft first 3 OCP_TYPE Char(1) M S soft limit check; H "hard limit or soft status check" (wording of ICD 6.7 to 7.0); D delta check; C status consistency (needs PCF_USCON = Y); E event generation only, no OOL 4 OCP_LVALU Char(14) low limit (numerical S, H, E checks; mandatory); or one expected status value (status parameters, S/H; mandatory); or minimum delta (D; optional, positive or empty) 5 OCP_HVALU Char(14) high limit (numerical S, H, E; mandatory); or maximum delta (D; optional, positive or empty); irrelevant for status parameters and C 6 OCP_RLCHK Char(8) applicability parameter; not used for C 7 OCP_VALPAR Number(5) 1 raw value of OCP_RLCHK that makes the check applicable; not used for C

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.3.2.8 Like validity and calibration-selection parameters, an applicability parameter must have an integer raw representation and be processed by the telemetry model (extracted through the PLF, or synthetic). SCOS-2000 also requires the applicability parameter to be valid.8

Inference

ICD issues 6.7, 6.9 and 7.0 all describe OCP_TYPE = H as "Hard limit or soft status check".813 Issue 5.1 simply has S soft OOL and H hard OOL,14 and the 7.0 rules say status checks, like limit checks, "can be associated to a check severity (Soft or Hard)".6 This wiki therefore reads S and H as soft and hard severity for both limit and status checks. The "soft status" wording looks like an editorial slip. In the Solar Orbiter MIB, status checks use both letters: 1,360 S and 696 H records.41

docs.title: Limit checks (soft and hard)
docs.text:
A limit check compares the valid value with a low/high pair. Limit checks are always given in pairs: a low limit alone is not possible. They apply only to numerical parameters (PCF_CATEG = N).7 Each check has a severity, soft (S) or hard (H). A soft/hard pair must share the same applicability condition (or have none) and follow each other in the order soft, then hard. Soft and hard checks may use the same low or high value. Either severity can also stand alone: a soft check does not need a hard partner.7

A value exactly equal to a limit is not out of limits.7 The Herschel clarification note puts it the other way round: OOL is raised only if the value is below the low limit or above the high limit, for both soft and hard limits.15 A parameter that violates several checks at once, such as a soft and a hard one, is displayed according to the more critical violation.7

docs.title: Status checks
docs.text: A status check compares a status parameter's value with a set of allowed values. Each allowed value takes one OCP record, with the value in OCP_LVALU. With OCF_CODIN = A the values are alias texts, which requires OCF_INTER = C.84 All records with the same applicability condition and the same type form one set of allowed values. Several sets, under different applicability conditions, let the expected status depend on the configuration.7

docs.title: Delta checks
docs.text: A delta check compares the difference between the current valid value and the last valid value with a minimum and maximum. OCP_LVALU is the minimum delta and OCP_HVALU the maximum. Either may be left empty to skip that side. Both must be positive, because the check applies to positive and negative deltas alike.87 Delta checks are allowed on numerical representations: PCF_CATEG = N, or the raw value of any parameter with PTC < 6.7 The ICD's compatibility note lists delta checks among the options introduced in recent issues. Issue 5.1 had no D type.214

docs.title: Status consistency checks
docs.text:
A status consistency check (SCC) compares a parameter, typically a status affected by commanding, with a reference value that SCOS-2000 maintains from the predicted or detected effect of commands.6 Several rules apply:739

  • The parameter needs PCF_USCON = Y.
  • The applicability condition is forced to true.
  • C checks (and E checks) must precede all other checks of the same parameter.
  • The CVE table, besides defining verification, identifies the parameters that a command affects. Their SCC is disabled during that command's verification window. For such parameters, the verification value (CVE_INTER) must use the same raw or engineering representation as the OOL checks (OCF_INTER).
  • CVE_CHECK says what a CVE record does for SCC. With B (the default), the record verifies the command and drives the SCC: its CVE_VAL becomes the new expected value of the parameter at the end of the verification stage window. With S, the record only disables the SCC during the window, and it must be combined with at least one B record of the same stage.9
  • The number of SCC parameters has a hard ceiling, set by the size of the SCOS-2000 packet that holds the snapshot of all SCC states. The ICD contradicts itself on whether the ceiling can be configured. The PCF_USCON description says it can be modified from release 4.1 through MAX_SCC_MESSAGE_LENGTH; the OCP rules say it "cannot be modified by configuration".37

The operator can reset SCC states from TM SPACON.20 The EGSE test language reports SCC states as SCC_UNINIT, SCC_INIT, SCC_DISABLE and SCC_OFF.16 ECSS-E-ST-70-31C defines the same idea in neutral terms. The reference is either the last uplinked value of a command argument, with the check suspended during the command's execution window, or an expression for autonomous on-board changes.33

docs.title: Event checks
docs.text: An E check is not a monitoring check in the usual sense. When the parameter leaves the given range (and the check is applicable), SCOS-2000 generates an event with the full ID BEHV::<OCP_NAME>. Such events can trigger configured actions such as sending an e-mail, setting a configuration variable or running a script. A parameter that triggers an E check does not appear on the OOL display.6 This differs from the packet-level PID_EVENT mechanism, which raises an event when a packet arrives (PID fields).10

docs.title: How SCOS-2000 selects and applies checks
docs.text:
For each new valid sample, SCOS-2000 runs through the parameter's OCP records in table order:7

  1. A check is applicable when it has no applicability parameter, or when its applicability parameter is valid and equals OCP_VALPAR. For C checks applicability is always true.
  2. The search stops at the first applicable check or soft/hard pair. Later sets are ignored, including after C or E checks. A global configuration variable, BEHV_STOP_FIRST_SET, can make SCOS-2000 apply all applicable checks instead, but only for the whole system, not per parameter.
  3. The selected checks are evaluated. A violation that persists for OCF_NBCHCK consecutive valid samples declares the parameter OOL.4

Inference

C and E checks must come first, and the search stops at the first applicable check, which for C is always the case. Read together, the two rules imply that a parameter with a status consistency check gets no further limit or status checks unless the global all-applicable option is set. The ICD does not spell this consequence out.

flowchart TD
    A["New valid sample of P"] --> B["Next OCP record of P<br/>(OCP_POS order)"]
    B --> C{"Type C?"}
    C -- yes --> APP["applicable (forced)"]
    C -- no --> D{"RLCHK empty, or<br/>RLCHK valid and = VALPAR?"}
    D -- no --> B
    D -- yes --> APP
    APP --> E{"Soft record followed by<br/>Hard record with same condition?"}
    E -- yes --> F["Use the soft/hard pair"]
    E -- no --> G["Use this check<br/>(or the set of status values<br/>sharing its condition and type)"]
    F --> H{"Global option<br/>BEHV_STOP_FIRST_SET"}
    G --> H
    H -- "standard rule: stop" --> I["Evaluate selected checks<br/>count consecutive violations<br/>OOL after OCF_NBCHCK"]
    H -- "option: apply all applicable" --> B

Logic from the OCP processing rules.7 Invalid samples are not limit checked, because the checks compare the valid value.6

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Nominal
    Nominal --> Violating: valid sample violates selected check
    Violating --> Violating: violation, count below OCF_NBCHCK
    Violating --> Nominal: valid sample within limits
    Violating --> OOL_soft: count = OCF_NBCHCK, soft check violated
    Violating --> OOL_hard: count = OCF_NBCHCK, hard check violated
    OOL_soft --> OOL_hard: hard check also violated
    OOL_hard --> OOL_soft: only soft check violated
    OOL_soft --> Nominal: sample back within limits
    OOL_hard --> Nominal: sample back within limits

Inference

The state diagram is this wiki's reading of the ICD. The ICD defines when a parameter becomes OOL (OCF_NBCHCK consecutive valid violating samples) and that the more critical violation is displayed. It does not state whether a return to nominal also needs OCF_NBCHCK samples, or what happens to the counter on invalid samples. The TDRS output, which includes a state VIOL for "not in limits, but its number of violations is not equal to the maximum number of violations", suggests the intermediate "violating" state exists in the implementation.22 PUS ST[12], by contrast, applies its repetition number in both directions (below).

docs.title: What the operator and the archive see
docs.text:
Displays and logs. The OOL display lists the telemetry parameters that are currently out of limits. The message display (event logger) scrolls SCOS-2000 log messages.19 Parameters carry an OOL state next to their value and validity. The SCOS-2000 EGSE test language, for example, returns an OOL state of NOMINAL, WARNING, ALARM or SCC for a parameter.16 It also lets a test procedure subscribe to a parameter so that it is notified when a limit applicability parameter or a calibration selection parameter changes, not only the value.17 Limit values, like calibration points and OL expressions, can be changed on line.20

Packets and files. The Herschel/Planck EGSE configuration of SCOS-2000 stores OOL event packets under a system SPID, OOL_PACKET_APID, default 3000.18 Herschel's science ground segment pulled OOL data out of SCOS-2000 as "Out-of-Limits files" (ORF). A file retriever asks SCOS-2000 for a time period and receives the name of the written file, and an ingestor links each OOL packet to the observation building block closest in time. In routine phase the same ingestor read OOL files from the MOC's Data Disposition System, recognised by the extensions .OOL or .TLM.21 See Herschel/Planck ground segment.

Retrieval services. The TDRS complete result file gives an OOL code for every sample.22 The EDDS delivers OOL records from the packet archive (PARC) with a typed state model. EDDS stream clients store them in OolRecording_… files.23

Source OOL vocabulary EGSE test language (getoolstate) NOMINAL, WARNING, ALARM, SCC TDRS result file (OOL column) NOM, L low, LL low-low, H high, HH high-high, SCC_UNIT (SCC initialised), SCC_F (SCC failure), UDEF, delta codes (MIN_D_LOW, MIN_D_HIGH, MAX_D_LOW, D_EQUAL and a second MIN_D_HIGH described as the high limit for positive deltas), VIOL EDDS OOL record (OOLRecordType) LIMIT, STATE, STATUS_CONSISTENCY, SOFT_HARD_LIMIT, LIMIT_MO, DELTA EDDS OOLParameterState NOMINAL, WARNING, OUT_OF_LIMITS, SCC, SCC_DISABLE, SCC_OFF, SCC_UNINIT, VIOLATION, NO_VALUE EDDS limit / status / delta / SCC states LIMIT_HIGH, LIMIT_HIGH_HIGH, LIMIT_LOW, LIMIT_LOW_LOW, LIMIT_WITHIN_RANGE; STATUS_ALLOWED, STATUS_UNEXPECTED; DELTA_ALLOWED, DELTA_EQUAL, MAX_DELTA_HIGH, MAX_DELTA_LOW, MIN_DELTA_HIGH, MIN_DELTA_LOW; B_SCC_ENABLE, B_SCC_DISABLE, B_SCC_FAIL, B_SCC_OFF, B_SCC_UNINIT

Vocabularies as printed in the sources.162223 An EDDS OOL record also carries the value, the lower and upper limits, the allowed values, the SCC reference value, the delta and last values, and hard and soft violation counts.23

Inference

The sources do not give a mapping from MIB check types to these vocabularies. A natural reading: a soft limit violation shows as WARNING / L or H / LIMIT_LOW or LIMIT_HIGH; a hard violation as ALARM (EGSE) or OUT_OF_LIMITS (EDDS) / LL or HH / LIMIT_LOW_LOW or LIMIT_HIGH_HIGH; a status check failure as STATUS_UNEXPECTED; an SCC failure as SCC / SCC_F / B_SCC_FAIL. Treat this as a hypothesis to verify against real EDDS output.

docs.title: Solar Orbiter: checks in numbers
docs.text:
Quantity 2020-04-16 2025-09-16 OCF records (checked parameters) 3,304 5,338 OCP records 4,686 7,369 hard (H) / soft (S) 2,306 / 2,265 4,153 / 3,096 delta (D) 102 105 status consistency (C) / PCF_USCON = Y 13 / 13 15 / 15 event (E) 0 0 OCP records with an applicability condition 703 859

Counts from both releases.4046

More detail on the 2025 release:4041

  • Representation. 2,029 parameters are checked on raw integers (U/I) and 110 on raw reals (U/R). 1,558 are checked on calibrated reals (C/R), 8 on calibrated integers (C/I) and 1,633 on alias texts (C/A).
  • Number of checks. 3,649 parameters have one OCP record, 1,453 have two, 185 three, 31 four, 1 five, 17 six, and 2 have fifteen.
  • Persistence. 3,989 parameters go OOL on the first violating sample (OCF_NBCHCK = 1), 1,116 need 2 samples and 203 need 3. A handful need 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15 or 24.
  • Pairs. Among numerical limit sets, 1,534 are soft/hard pairs. 1,921 are hard checks alone and 202 soft checks alone. Every pair is ordered soft before hard, and no limit set has its low limit above its high limit.
  • Applicability. 859 OCP records use 180 distinct applicability parameters. The most frequent is NSM00002 "Current SSMM Mode act" (120 records), followed by the heater status parameters NPWSX053 "EUI OU DEC HEATER Sts" (54) and NPWSX051 "SPICE CE DEC HEATER Sts" (42).
  • Synthetic parameters. 242 of the checked parameters are dynamic OL synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = D).

docs.title: Example: soft and hard limits on an IMU temperature
docs.text:
NMUD1113 "IMU11 SIA temperature" has OCF_NBCHCK = 1, OCF_NBOOL = 2, OCF_INTER = C and OCF_CODIN = R: two checks on calibrated real values, OOL at the first violation. Its OCP records (real MIB data):42

OCP_POS Type Low High Applicability 1 S soft −16 48 NCSD0P43 = 2 (IMUA Gyr1 SCV status ON) 2 H hard −18 54 NCSD0P43 = 2

The applicability parameter is the same one that makes the parameter valid (PCF_VALID = NCSD0P43, PCF_VALPAR = 2). Combined with the 11-point calibration curve CMUT0013TM (calibration page), these illustrative raw values give:

Raw (12-bit) Engineering (degC) Outcome 400 (0x190) invalid (below the curve, CAF_INTER = F) not checked: only valid values are checked 850 (0x352) 54.898 hard OOL (above 54) 1000 (0x3E8) 48.047 soft OOL (above 48, below 54) 1100 (0x44C) 44.343 nominal 2850 (0xB22) −13.837 nominal 2900 (0xB54) −16.032 soft OOL (below −16) 3150 (0xC4E) −34.426 hard OOL (below −18)

The outcomes apply the ICD rules to real MIB definitions; the raw values are illustrative.742 Its neighbour NMUD1112 "IMU11 ORG temperature" uses the same curve, the same validity criterion and the same high limits (48 and 54), but its low limits are 2 (soft) and 1 (hard), and both checks are conditioned on NCSD0P73 ("IMUA Gyr4 SCV Stat.Tm") while its validity uses NCSD0P43.42 This may be deliberate or a copy slip; the MIB does not say.

docs.title: Example: limits that depend on a heater
docs.text:
NRU02712 "ANP_1_1_12 SPICE CE" (16-bit raw, calibrated through the 51-point curve COMB000000 to DegC, OCF_NBCHCK = 2) has six checks. The heater status NPWSX051 "SPICE CE DEC HEATER Sts" (0 NOMINAL OFF, 1 NOMINAL ON, 2 INCORRECT CONF) selects one of three soft/hard pairs (real MIB data):43

OCP_POS Type Low High Applies when NPWSX051 = 1 S −44.5 −38.5 0 (NOMINAL OFF) 2 H −47.5 −35.5 0 3 S −44.5 57 1 (NOMINAL ON) 4 H −47.5 60 1 5 S −44.5 −38.5 2 (INCORRECT CONF) 6 H −47.5 −35.5 2

With the heater off, or incorrectly configured, the nominal band is −44.5 to −38.5 degC and the hard band −47.5 to −35.5 degC. With the heater on, the high limits rise to 57 and 60 degC. Under the standard "stop at first applicable set" rule, only the pair whose condition is true is evaluated, and two consecutive violating samples are needed.7 The parameter is located in three packets, YCF1Z079, YCF2Z003 and YCS2X188, all TM(3,25).43 The same pattern exists for other SPICE and EUI temperatures with six checks, keyed on NPWSX051 or on NPWSX053 "EUI OU DEC HEATER Sts" (for example NRU02730, NTCD50D6, NTCD50L6).41

docs.title: Example: a 15-value status check
docs.text: NCDT09N0 "OMMA_State" (32-bit enumerated, alias set CCDT0098TM with 16 states) has OCF_INTER = C, OCF_CODIN = A, and fifteen S records listing allowed texts: OFF, POWER_ON, POWER_OFF, FILLING, CHECKING, PREOPERATIONAL, OPERATIONAL, INIT, SYNCHRONISING, NOT_SYNC, ABORT_FILLING, ABORT_CHECKING, POWER_ON_END, POWER_OFF_END, INIT_END. The only state of the alias set that is missing is FAILED (raw 8). In effect, the soft status check flags that single state. NCDT09X0 (OMMB) is defined the same way (real MIB data).44

docs.title: Example: delta checks on error counters
docs.text:
All 105 delta checks in the Solar Orbiter MIB belong to 105 different NIU… counters, such as NIU01008 "TC_Bad", NIU0100A "TM_Bad", NIU0101C "SpWwriteErr" and NIU0202C "EUV_HSL_CommandsBad". Every one has OCF_NBCHCK = 1, OCF_INTER = U, OCF_CODIN = I, a single D check and no other check. In 102 of them the minimum and maximum delta are both 0. The other three, NIU0700B "FSI_HSL_Timeout", NIU0800B "Lya_HSL_Timeout" and NIU0900B "EUV_HSL_Timeout" (16-bit unsigned), have both thresholds set to 2048 (real MIB data).44

Inference

With a maximum delta of 0, any change of the counter between two valid samples exceeds the maximum, so each new error raises an OOL. The minimum delta of 0 can never be undercut by an absolute difference. For the three timeout parameters with both thresholds at 2048, any delta other than exactly 2048 lies below the minimum or above the maximum. The ICD does not say whether a delta exactly equal to a threshold counts as a violation. EDDS and TDRS both have a separate "delta equal" state (DELTA_EQUAL, D_EQUAL),2322 which suggests the implementation distinguishes it. Why these three checks use 2048 is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Example: status consistency checks
docs.text:
All 15 SCC parameters are counters of numerical category (13 unsigned integers and 2 enumerated parameters), each with one C check, OCF_INTER = U and OCF_CODIN = I; five use OCF_NBCHCK = 3 and ten use 1. Examples are NCDT02A0 "OBCHP_TTRMA_VC0_NB_Err" (OCF_NBCHCK = 3), NCDT07K0 "OBCHP_Nb_Reject_TcBuff", NDSD0046 "DST-A WD Reset Counter" and NSM01800 "PS0 Stored PKT counter". None of them appears in the CVE table, so no command verification disables their SCC (real MIB data).44

Inference

The ICD documents one way to set the SCC reference value: the CVE_VAL of a CVE_CHECK = B record at the end of a verification window. Because no CVE record names these counters, their reference value can only come from SCOS-2000's internal handling (for example initialisation from the first sample, or an operator reset in TM SPACON). The check then works like a latching "the counter has changed" alarm. The ICD does not describe how the reference value is initialised.

docs.title: Data-quality observations
docs.text:
The following points come from simple consistency queries. They are reported as observations, not as errors of the mission's MIB:41

  • NCDX9308 has an OCF record with OCF_NBOOL = 2 but no OCP records. The ICD requires the count to match the OCP table.4
  • 349 status parameters (PCF_CATEG = S) carry raw integer limit pairs (OCF_INTER = U, OCF_CODIN = I, OCP_HVALU filled). For example, NCDX9000 "E_SCV_OBC_TTR_CPDU_A" has a soft pair 2…2 and a hard pair 1…2. The ICD restricts limit checks to PCF_CATEG = N and calls OCP_HVALU irrelevant for status parameters.78 How SCOS-2000 treats these records is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Ground checks and on-board monitoring (PUS ST[12])
docs.text: Ground checks run in the control centre on every valid sample that reaches it. On-board monitoring runs on the spacecraft itself, and its events can trigger on-board reactions. The PUS-C standard defines it as ST[12]. Its parameter monitoring subservice checks on-board parameters against definitions loaded by the ground, reports check transitions to the ground and raises events when conditions are violated. Those events can be caught on board, for example by the event-action service ST[19].24

docs.title: ST[12] parameter monitoring in brief
docs.text:
• Check types. Limit checks and expected-value checks are mandatory; delta checks are optional. A limit check succeeds when low ≤ value ≤ high. An expected-value check masks the value and compares it with the expected value. A delta check compares the difference between consecutive values with two thresholds; its definition includes the number of consecutive deltas that are averaged.2526
  • Definitions. Each parameter monitoring definition (PMON) contains its own ID, the monitored parameter, an optional check validity condition, an optional definition-specific monitoring interval and a check definition. The check definition holds a repetition number, the check type, the limits or expected value and mask, and an optional event ID for each kind of violation. Several definitions may watch the same parameter, one with warning limits and one with danger limits, for example.2426
  • Check validity condition. A validity parameter, a bit mask and an expected value. The condition is true when (validity parameter AND mask) equals the expected value.26
  • Statuses. For a limit check the checking status is "unchecked", "invalid", "within limits", "below low limit" or "above high limit". A new status is established only after "repetition number" consecutive checks agree, in either direction.2728
  • Reporting. Each status change is recorded in a check transition list, reported in TM[12,12] check transition reports when a declared maximum number of transitions is reached or at the maximum transition reporting delay after the first recorded transition. TC[12,10] requests a TM[12,11] out-of-limits report.3031
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> unchecked: definition enabled
    unchecked --> invalid: check validity condition false
    invalid --> within_limits: condition true, N consecutive successes
    invalid --> below_low_limit: condition true, N values below low
    invalid --> above_high_limit: condition true, N values above high
    unchecked --> within_limits: N consecutive successes
    unchecked --> below_low_limit: N consecutive values below low
    unchecked --> above_high_limit: N consecutive values above high
    within_limits --> below_low_limit: N consecutive values below low
    within_limits --> above_high_limit: N consecutive values above high
    below_low_limit --> within_limits: N consecutive successes
    above_high_limit --> within_limits: N consecutive successes
    below_low_limit --> above_high_limit: N consecutive values above high
    above_high_limit --> below_low_limit: N consecutive values below low
    within_limits --> invalid: check validity condition false
    below_low_limit --> invalid: check validity condition false
    above_high_limit --> invalid: check validity condition false

Limit-check status model of ECSS-E-ST-70-41C, with N the repetition number. Every new status different from the previous one is recorded as a check transition.272829 While the check validity condition is false, the status is "invalid" and the repetition counter is reset.28

docs.title: Solar Orbiter's on-board monitoring and how the MIB decodes it
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter implements its own tailoring of service 12.34 Each monitoring entry added with TC(12,5) contains a monitoring ID, the parameter ID, a validity parameter ID (0 means "always check"; the validity parameter is a Boolean), a monitoring interval in application cycles, a repetition count Rep (1–255, the number of successive samples needed both to declare a parameter out of limits and to declare it back within limits), an enable status, and either a limit definition (low limit with EID, high limit with EID) or an expected-value definition (mask, expected value, EID).35 The checking statuses are coded 0 (within limits or expected value), 1 unchecked, 2 invalid, 3 unselected (not used), 4 unexpected value or below low limit, and 5 above high limit. The maximum reporting delay is counted in 8 Hz cycles, and 0 disables transition reports.3836

The reports reach the ground as variable packets. The MIB defines TM(12,9) monitoring list, TM(12,11) out-of-limit list and TM(12,12) check transition reports as variable packets for the six APIDs 163, 179, 195, 211, 227 and 259, each with its own TPSD, plus one more TM(12,12) on APID 1075. The TM(12,11) of APID 163 is TPSD 14173.45 Its VPD layout is drawn here (real MIB definitions; field sizes also printed in the Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure ICD):4538

The status fields use the alias set CCDT0011TX (0 VALID, 1 UNCHECKED, 2 INVALID, 4 BELOW_LOW, 5 ABOVE_HIGH, 6 OUT_OF_LIMIT). That set matches the codes of the TM-TC and Packet Structure ICD and adds a value 6 that the ICD does not list.4538 The Database Import ICD notes that all service 12 reports are variable packets. Their values therefore do not take part in validity, monitoring checks or synthetic parameters on the ground. The ICD recommends variable packets only for special reports that need no such cross-processing with other telemetry.1112 The MIB also contains fixed-layout TM(12,9) definitions on APIDs 1986 to 1990 ("AOCS", "PAYLOAD", "PLATFORM", "SYSTEM" and "THERMAL" monitoring list reports, numbered #1 to #3). They are distinguished by two 8-bit identification fields: PI1 at octet 19 and PI2 at an APID-specific offset (octet 883 for AOCS, 2083 for PAYLOAD, 2755 for PLATFORM, 2227 for SYSTEM and 2179 for THERMAL). The PLF names what sits there: the monitoring-ID fields of fixed entry slots. In SPID 65909 (AOCS #1), for example, octet 19 holds NXAS001A "PID11_S001_ID" and octet 883 holds NXAS041A "PID11_S041_ID". The three AOCS reports have PI1/PI2 values 1/41, 122/142 and 220/242. Two SYSTEM definitions (SPIDs 65917 and 65954) share PI1 = 1 and differ only in PI2 (255 and 253).45 This matches the TM-TC ICD, where the monitoring status, the maximum reporting delay and the count N precede the first monitoring ID of the report.37

Inference

The fixed (12,9) definitions look like a way to decode the expected content of the on-board monitoring list, split over several report packets, with the full PLF machinery rather than the VPD. The monitoring IDs of two entry slots then tell the packets apart. The source documents do not explain these definitions.

docs.title: Monitoring in the MIB: parameters and packets
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base (MIB) is split into a static part, usually called the database, and a dynamic part, the packet archive.1 The static part tells the control system everything it needs to turn downlinked telemetry packets into named, typed and validated parameter samples. On the monitoring side, nine ASCII tables do this work. The PCF defines every monitoring parameter. PID, PIC and TPCF tell the telemetry packetiser how to recognise an incoming packet and which processing keys to give it. PLF and VPD describe where parameter values sit inside fixed and variable packets. GRP, GRPA and GRPK group parameters and packets.4 Calibration and limit checking hang off the PCF and have their own pages: Calibration in the MIB and Monitoring checks.

This page follows the Database Import ICD issue 7.0 (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001, 2017-08-11). The library copy comes from the Solar Orbiter MOC document server, where the file name begins with "MOC-applicable MIB".7 Every Solar Orbiter number below comes from this wiki's own SQL queries on the public release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (database version 25925PFM, comment 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33).53 You can browse every object mentioned here in the MIB explorer.

docs.title: The monitoring tables at a glance
docs.text:
Each table is a tab-separated ASCII file named after the table in lower case (for example pcf.dat), with one record per line. An empty optional field still carries its separator.2 Fields marked with * in the ICD form the table key. Fields marked M are mandatory. An optional field left empty takes the import default given in the ICD.3

Table One record per Role Solar Orbiter rows (2025) PCF monitoring parameter name, type, validity, nature, calibration link, display and archive flags 126,745 PID packet identification key maps APID/type/subtype/PI1/PI2 to the processing keys SPID and TPSD 11,150 PIC type/subtype (optionally APID) where to find the extra identification fields PI1 and PI2 256 TPCF SPID packet mnemonic and (informative) size 11,150 PLF parameter occurrence in a fixed packet byte and bit offset, super-commutation, time offsets 400,792 VPD element of a variable packet structure ordered layout, repeat counters, display attributes 19,863 GRP monitoring group group name, description and type (parameters or packets) 2 GRPA parameter in a parameter group membership 0 GRPK packet in a packet group membership 4

Sources for the table: roles from the ICD,45 row counts from the Solar Orbiter MIB.54

The PCF sits at the centre of the data model. Each parameter can reference one validity parameter (many-to-one onto the PCF itself), one or several calibrations, at most one set of up to 16 monitoring checks, and any number of packets, groups and displays.6 The diagram shows the monitoring relationships described on this page. The data model page gives the full picture, including commanding.

erDiagram
    PCF ||--o| PCF : "PCF_VALID (validity)"
    PCF ||--o{ PLF : "located in fixed packets"
    PCF ||--o{ VPD : "appears in variable packets"
    PID ||--|| TPCF : "PID_SPID = TPCF_SPID"
    PID ||--o{ PLF : "PID_SPID = PLF_SPID"
    PID ||--o{ VPD : "PID_TPSD = VPD_TPSD"
    PIC ||--o{ PID : "explains PI1/PI2 of type/subtype"
    GRP ||--o{ GRPA : "parameter groups (PA)"
    GRP ||--o{ GRPK : "packet groups (PK)"
    GRPA }o--|| PCF : "GRPA_PANAME"
    GRPK }o--|| PID : "GRPK_PKSPID"
    PCF ||--o| OCF : "monitoring checks"
    PCF ||--o{ CUR : "conditional calibration"

Diagram based on the ICD's description of the monitoring data organisation.6

docs.title: From packet to parameter sample
docs.text:
The processing chain explains why the tables look the way they do. The SCOS-2000 telemetry packetiser receives a telemetry source packet. It reads the APID from its fixed place in the packet header, and the PUS service type and subtype from a position set by configuration variables. If the PIC says that this type/subtype needs more identification data, it extracts up to two further fields (PI1, PI2) from the packet data field. It then looks up the PID table with the full key and files and distributes a SCOS-2000 packet under the processing keys found there: the SPID for fixed packets and the TPSD for variable packets.28 PLF (fixed) or VPD (variable) definitions then govern parameter extraction.28

flowchart LR
    A[TM source packet] --> B["Read APID<br/>(fixed header position)"]
    B --> C["Read type / subtype<br/>(position set by MISCconfig)"]
    C --> D{"PIC record for<br/>type/subtype/APID<br/>or type/subtype?"}
    D -- yes --> E["Extract PI1 / PI2<br/>(PIC offsets, widths)"]
    D -- no --> F["PI1 = PI2 = 0"]
    E --> G["PID lookup:<br/>TYPE, STYPE, APID, PI1, PI2"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["SCOS-2000 packet<br/>filed with SPID (+TPSD)"]
    H --> I["PLF: fixed layout<br/>(per SPID)"]
    H --> J["VPD: variable layout<br/>(per TPSD)"]
    I --> K["PCF: decode PTC/PFC,<br/>validity, calibration,<br/>checks, displays"]
    J --> L["Variable Packets Display<br/>(limited processing)"]

Flow drawn from the packetiser description in the ICD.2832 The SCOS-2000 packet body holds the complete TM source packet. For missions that use the standard packetiser, PLF offsets therefore count from the first octet of the source packet header, and VPD processing starts PID_DFHSIZE octets later.34

Two design constraints for the on-board software

The ICD warns that the packetiser assumes two things. First, the type and subtype fields, when present, sit at the same position in every packet the spacecraft generates. Second, every packet with a given type/subtype carries its additional identification fields at the same position and with the same width.28 The ICD flags both as constraints that the on-board design must respect.

docs.title: PCF: monitoring parameter characteristics
docs.text: The PCF holds one record per monitoring parameter. The word "monitoring parameter" covers three things: telemetry parameters extracted from packets, user defined constants and synthetic parameters computed on the ground.8 Fields 20 to 23 are optional, for backward compatibility, and the importer accepts PCF records with 19 to 23 fields.8 The Solar Orbiter pcf.dat has 23 fields in every record.54

docs.title: Field reference
docs.text:
# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* PCF_NAME Char(8) M Unique parameter name. It must not start with VAR, GVAR or $ (reserved by the Operations Language), and the patterns NNOiiii, CEBiiii, KRUiiii, MSPiiii, VL2iiii, PERiiii, REDiiii, MLGiiii are reserved for ground-station telemetry.9 2 PCF_DESCR Char(24) Free-text description.9 3 PCF_PID Number(10) On-board parameter identifier ("Parameter#" of the PUS), range 0 to 2^32−1. It identifies the parameter in PUS variable packets. It must be unique; it is left empty for ground-only parameters.10 4 PCF_UNIT Char(4) Engineering unit shown next to the calibrated value, or next to the raw value when there is no calibration.10 5 PCF_PTC Number(2) M Parameter Type Code, 1 to 13. Needed even for synthetic parameters; saved synthetic parameters must use PTC 13.11 6 PCF_PFC Number(5) M Parameter Format Code. With the PTC it fixes the length of values extracted from packets.11 7 PCF_WIDTH Number(6) Padded width in bits. Used only for VPD extraction, to find where the next parameter starts; also controls fixed-width extraction of deduced parameters (PTC 11).12 8 PCF_VALID Char(8) Name of the validity parameter.13 9 PCF_RELATED Char(8) For saved synthetic parameters: the synthetic parameter that is computed. For deduced parameters: the parameter that carries the on-board parameter ID.14 10 PCF_CATEG Char(1) M Calibration category: N numerical, S status (textual calibration), T text (character strings).15 11 PCF_NATUR Char(1) M Nature: R raw TM, D dynamic OL synthetic, P SPEL synthetic, H hard-coded synthetic, S saved synthetic, C constant.16 12 PCF_CURTX Char(10) Name of the single calibration (numerical, polynomial, logarithmic or textual). Empty when the CUR table selects among several calibrations.17 13 PCF_INTER Char(1) F Extrapolation flag (P extrapolate, F invalid). Ignored by SCOS-2000, which uses CAF_INTER instead.18 14 PCF_USCON Char(1) N Y if the parameter is status-consistency checked. Must be Y when OCP holds a status consistency check.19 15 PCF_DECIM Number(3) Number of decimal places for displaying real values.19 16 PCF_PARVAL Char(14) Default raw value of a static user defined constant (PCF_NATUR = C, then mandatory).19 17 PCF_SUBSYS Char(8) Group the parameter belongs to; reserved for future filtering.20 18 PCF_VALPAR Number(5) 1 Raw value of the validity parameter that makes this parameter valid.20 19 PCF_SPTYPE Char(1) Output view of a synthetic parameter (E engineering, R raw). Not imported; used by the off-line consistency checker.20 20 PCF_CORR Char(1) Y Apply time correlation to absolute time parameters (Y/N); must be N for relative times (PTC 10).21 21 PCF_OBTID Number(5) On-board clock identifier (1..N) used for time correlation or for the time epoch; default from TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID.21 22 PCF_DARC Char(1) 0 1 adds the parameter to the parameter archive (DARC) recording list; 0 leaves it unchanged. Not imported by SCOS-2000.22 23 PCF_ENDIAN Char(1) B Byte order (B big endian, L little endian) for whole-octet integers, strings, octet strings and times.22

Names must be unique regardless of letter case (A1000 and a1000 clash), but the importer does not warn about such clashes.3

docs.title: Type and width: PTC, PFC and PCF_WIDTH
docs.text:
The PTC/PFC pair is the parameter's encoding. SCOS-2000 uses it to decode values of parameters whose nature is R or C.11 The meaning of each pair is listed in Appendix A of the ICD, which follows the nomenclature of the Packet Utilisation Standard (PUS). The MIB parameter types page covers it in full, and PUS parameter types gives the PUS side. Values are always handled in three forms. The encoded value is the bits in the packet. The raw value is the decoded number before calibration. The engineering value is the result of calibration. Raw and encoded values only coincide for unsigned integers; a 16-bit signed raw value of −1, for example, is encoded as 0xFFFF.1

The Solar Orbiter PCF uses these type codes:

PTC Appendix A meaning Solar Orbiter parameters 1 Boolean, 1 bit (PFC 0) 4,380 2 Enumerated, PFC bits (1–32) 29,443 3 Unsigned integer (PFC 0–12 → 4 to 16 bits, PFC 13 → 24 bits, PFC 14 → 32 bits; 48 and 64 bits not supported) 50,341 4 Signed integer (same PFC scheme as PTC 3) 1,950 5 Real (PFC 1 IEEE single, 2 IEEE double, 3 MIL-STD-1750A 32-bit) 29,718 6 Bit string, handled as unsigned integer of PFC bits (monitoring only) 950 7 Octet string (PFC > 0: fixed length in octets) 5,990 8 ASCII string (PFC > 0: fixed length in octets) 120 9 Absolute time (CDS or CUC variants; PFC 30 Unix time) 3,796 10 Relative time (CUC variants) 47 11 Deduced (type taken from the parameter ID in the packet) 8 13 Saved synthetic parameter 2

Type meanings from Appendix A and the PCF field descriptions;271112 counts from the Solar Orbiter PCF.55

PCF_WIDTH matters only for variable packets. It gives the slot width when it differs from the length implied by PTC/PFC, for example when padding bits byte-align the next field; padding bits always precede the value. For a deduced parameter (PTC 11), a width means "extract from a fixed-width slot"; no width means "use the length of the actual type, padded as defined for that type".1236 Only seven Solar Orbiter parameters set it. Five are deduced parameters of the on-board monitoring reports, each with a 64- or 32-bit slot. Two are saved synthetic parameters with a 104-bit (13-octet) slot.55 Thirteen octets is exactly the size the ICD prescribes for a saved synthetic parameter: 8 octets of value, 1 octet of value type and 4 octets of validity flags.23

docs.title: Validity: PCF_VALID, PCF_VALPAR and expiry
docs.text:
A parameter value is only meaningful in some on-board states. A heater current means nothing while the heater's power line is off. The MIB expresses this with a validity criterion: the parameter is valid when the parameter named in PCF_VALID has the raw value PCF_VALPAR (default 1). SCOS-2000 also requires the validity parameter itself to be valid. The validity parameter must have an integer raw representation and must be processed by the telemetry model (it appears in the PLF or it is synthetic). Circular validity chains are not allowed.13 For a synthetic parameter, the overall validity is the logical AND of the validity derived from its inputs and its own explicit criterion.13

A second mechanism needs no MIB entry. When no instance of a periodic packet arrives within its generation interval (PID_INTER) plus a globally configured margin, every parameter in it is flagged invalid ("expired"). The ICD notes that this removes the need to encode in validity criteria all the on-board conditions under which a packet is generated.8 Behind the single word "invalid" sits a bit set of reasons. The SCOS-2000 EGSE test language, for example, exposes flags such as VAL_STATE_OFF (state validity evaluates to 0), VAL_EXPIRED (packet not arrived), VAL_CALIBRATION (calibration failed) and VAL_UNKNOWN_STATE (state parameter invalid).51

In the Solar Orbiter MIB, 20,692 parameters have a validity parameter, drawn from 2,933 distinct validity parameters, all of them integer types (PTC 1 to 4). The most used validity parameters are the …SCV Status.scvTm enumerations of the two PCDU and two RIU sides: NCSD0PC3 (PCDU A, 1,369 dependants), NCSD0PD3 (PCDU B, 1,357), NCSD0PE3 (RIU A, 1,210) and NCSD0PF3 (RIU B, 1,210). Their textual calibration CCDT0065TM maps 0, 1 and 2 to NOT_APPLICABLE, OFF and ON. Dependent parameters therefore use PCF_VALPAR = 2, which means "valid when ON". Of the 20,692 records, 9,775 use the value 1, 8,216 use 2 and 2,436 leave the field empty and inherit the default 1. The remaining 265 use 0 (243 records), 80 (12), 32 (8) or 64 (2).55 No Solar Orbiter PID record sets PID_INTER, so, as far as the MIB is concerned, no packet is declared periodic for expiry purposes.5930

docs.title: Category and nature
docs.text:
PCF_CATEG tells SCOS-2000 which family of calibration applies. N covers numerical parameters, with or without a numerical, polynomial or logarithmic calibration, and all non-numerical types except character strings. S (status) is for parameters with a textual calibration. T (text) is for character strings (PTC 8).15 Solar Orbiter has 100,087 N, 26,538 S and 120 T parameters. The 120 T parameters match its 120 PTC 8 parameters exactly.55

PCF_NATUR tells SCOS-2000 where the value comes from:162325

Nature Name Source of the value Solar Orbiter 2025 Solar Orbiter 2020 R Raw telemetry extracted from TM packets (also dynamic UDCs and MISC variables, from internal packets) 125,161 101,714 D Dynamic OL synthetic Operations Language expression in a file named after the parameter, interpreted, not stored 1,582 354 P SPEL synthetic Synthetic Parameter Expression Language file; EGSE deliveries only 0 0 H Hard-coded synthetic C++ (written directly or compiled from OL) 0 36 S Saved synthetic value of the synthetic named in PCF_RELATED, computed centrally and stored in synthetic packets 2 0 C Constant (static UDC) value in PCF_PARVAL 0 0

Counts from both public releases.5566

Synthetic parameters behave like telemetry parameters once computed. They can be displayed, calibrated (the computed source value is treated as the raw value) and limit checked.24 Dynamic OL parameters are recomputed whenever a contributing sample changes in value or validity, also during retrieval. Saved synthetic parameters are computed by the Synthetic Parameters Packet Generator (SPPG) and written into synthetic packets, so retrieval shows exactly what was computed in real time. The price is that only the values present when a triggering packet arrives are stored.23 The synthetic parameters page covers the languages and the 1,582 Solar Orbiter definition files. Solar Orbiter's two saved synthetic parameters are NTTSS030 and NTTSS031 ("Last C_Lock DST-½"). They save the synthetic parameters NTTSX030 and NTTSX031, use PTC 13 and have the 104-bit width noted above. Their PLF entries place them at octets 0 and 13 of SPID 66838 "Saved Synthetics" (type 251, subtype 2, APID 1966), one 13-octet slot each.5561

User defined constants (UDCs) come in two kinds. A static UDC has PCF_NATUR = C and a database default in PCF_PARVAL, which can only be changed through the OL editor. A dynamic UDC has PCF_NATUR = R and a PLF entry in an internally generated "constants TM packet", whose values operators set through TM SPACON or the parameter injection interface.25 Solar Orbiter uses only dynamic UDCs. Its constants packet is SPID 66830 "Dynamic UDCs" (APID 1966, type 160, subtype 3). Among its 13 parameters are NCFZ0001 "TC Link Time Out", NDSZX003 "DST Uplink Path" and NPWZ0000 "PCDU_MODEL".56 The last one selects calibration curves at run time; see conditional calibration. The same pattern serves the MISC packet, which carries selected configuration variables as pseudo-telemetry. Those variables must be 32-bit signed integers (PTC 4, PFC 14), IEEE doubles (PTC 5, PFC 2) or character strings (PTC 8).26 Solar Orbiter's MISC packet is SPID 66832 "MISC_PACKET: Config variables packet MISCdynamic server" (APID 1966, type 160, subtype 5), with 21 parameters. Two of them use types outside that list: NYG01921 "TCO_DEFAULT_ENCOD_SCHEME" is PTC 5, PFC 1 (IEEE single) and NYG01923 "CMD VC ID" is PTC 4, PFC 12 (16-bit signed).56

docs.title: Calibration, checks and display fields
docs.text:
PCF_CURTX names the single calibration of a parameter. It must match a TXF_NUMBR for status parameters, or a CAF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT for numerical ones. It is mandatory for status parameters. It must be empty for text, string (PTC 7, 8) and time (PTC 9, 10) parameters, and for parameters calibrated through the CUR table.17 In Solar Orbiter, 30,936 parameters name a calibration: 26,533 textual, 3,433 numerical and 970 polynomial. Another 907 parameters use conditional selection through CUR.57 PCF_INTER is a leftover. The ICD states that SCOS-2000 ignores it and takes extrapolation behaviour from the calibration curve.18 The calibration page gives the details.

PCF_USCON = Y enables status consistency checking. The number of such parameters has a hard upper limit, set by the size of the packet that holds the snapshot of all status consistency checks; the PCF_USCON description says that from release 4.1 it can be changed with the configuration variable MAX_SCC_MESSAGE_LENGTH.19 The OCP rules elsewhere in the same ICD say it cannot be changed by configuration; see monitoring checks. Solar Orbiter flags 15 parameters, all with one OCP check of type C (monitoring checks).55

PCF_UNIT and PCF_DECIM are pure display attributes. Solar Orbiter gives a unit to 5,124 parameters. Where PCF_DECIM is set, the most common values are 3 (23,081 parameters) and 2 (13,434).55

docs.title: Time parameters, archiving and byte order
docs.text:
For absolute times, PCF_CORR = Y converts the on-board time to UTC with the time correlation of the clock named by PCF_OBTID. With N, the value is extracted unchanged and the clock's time format defines the epoch, or TCO_ESA_EPOCH when no clock is given.21 See time correlation in SCOS-2000 and CCSDS time codes. Solar Orbiter sets N for all 47 relative-time parameters, as the ICD requires, and for 3 absolute-time parameters. It never sets PCF_OBTID, so the mission default clock applies.55

PCF_DARC = 1 asks the parameter archive (DARC) to record the parameter. Solar Orbiter sets it on 49,330 parameters.5522 PCF_ENDIAN = L declares a little-endian parameter. Exactly one Solar Orbiter parameter uses it: NYG02201 "GS Packet Size", a 32-bit unsigned integer.55

docs.title: Worked example: NMUD1113, an IMU temperature
docs.text:
NMUD1113 ("IMU11 SIA temperature") shows most PCF features at once (real MIB values).58

Field Value Reading PCF_NAME / PCF_DESCR NMUD1113 / IMU11 SIA temperature PCF_PTC / PCF_PFC 3 / 8 12-bit unsigned integer PCF_UNIT degC shown next to the calibrated value PCF_CATEG / PCF_NATUR N / R numerical, extracted from telemetry PCF_CURTX CMUT0013TM 11-point numerical curve "FOG 200E temperature" PCF_VALID / PCF_VALPAR NCSD0P43 / 2 valid only while "IMUA Gyr1 SCV Stat.Tm" reads 2 (ON) PCF_DECIM 3 three decimals on displays PCF_DARC 1 recorded in the parameter archive PCF_PID, PCF_WIDTH, PCF_OBTID empty no on-board ID, not used in variable packets

The PLF places it in two packets, SPID 29534 (YCA2Z011) and SPID 29517 (YCA1Z087), both "AOCS IMU RAW" TM(3,25) packets. In both it sits at octet 69, bit 4.58 The calibration page converts one of its raw values, and the checks page evaluates it against its limits.

docs.title: Recognising packets: PID, PIC and TPCF
PID: packet identification
docs.text:
The PID maps packet identification values to SCOS-2000 packet IDs. The SPID identifies the structure of a fixed packet, as defined in the PLF. The TPSD identifies the structure of a variable packet, as defined in the VPD. One telemetry packet can be processed both ways.29

# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* PID_TYPE Number(3) M PUS service type, 0–255; 0 means no data field header 2* PID_STYPE Number(3) M PUS service subtype, 0–255; 0 as above 3* PID_APID Number(5) M APID: 0–2047 for spacecraft packets, 2048–65535 for packets generated by SCOS-2000 applications or other domains such as SCOEs 4* PID_PI1_VAL Number(10) 0 value of the first additional identification field (for example a structure ID), 0 to 2^31−1 5* PID_PI2_VAL Number(10) 0 value of the second additional identification field (for example a function ID) 6* PID_SPID Number(10) M SCOS-2000 packet ID, 1 to 2^32−1 (0 not allowed); up to S2K-R5 it also chose the history file 7 PID_DESCR Char(64) description; also the message text of the event raised when PID_EVENT is set 8 PID_UNIT Char(8) on-board subsystem (future filtering) 9 PID_TPSD Number(10) -1 structure ID for the Variable Packets Display; −1 if the packet is not in the VPD 10 PID_DFHSIZE Number(2) M octets from the start of the source packet to where VPD processing begins (0–99), typically primary header plus data field header 11 PID_TIME Char(1) N Y if the packet carries a generation time field 12 PID_INTER Number(8) generation interval of a periodic packet in ms, used for expiry; empty for non-periodic packets 13 PID_VALID Char(1) Y which of several records with the same key is valid 14 PID_CHECK Number(1) 0 1 to check the Packet Error Control CRC, 0 not to 15 PID_EVENT Char(1) N raise a SCOS-2000 event on reception: N none, I info, W warning, A alarm 16 PID_EVID Char(17) event number; the full event ID becomes TPKT_OBE::nnnn; 1–9999 suggested

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.4.1.30

The ICD attaches rules to the PID that protect the archive. These rules matter for anyone who maintains a MIB over a long mission:31

  • The packetiser key is the first five fields. Associating several keys with one SPID is deprecated from release 5.0: each distinct packet must have its own SPID.
  • Packets identified by APID alone, without a data field header, get 0 in all other key fields.
  • Once mission telemetry is being archived, the mapping from identification fields to SPID must not change. PID entries whose SPIDs exist in the archive must not be deleted, or advanced retrieval services such as the GDDS break. The TPSD of archived packets must not change either.
  • Internally generated packets (UDC, MISC, synthetic and system control packets) should also have PID entries, with a type/subtype/APID combination that no other source uses, plus a TPCF entry for the mnemonic.

docs.title: PIC: where the extra identification fields are
docs.text:
Many PUS packets share a type/subtype and differ only in the first field of their data. A housekeeping report TM(3,25) carries a structure ID; an event report TM(5,x) carries an event ID. The PIC tells the packetiser, for each type/subtype (and optionally APID), where the extra identification fields are. Offsets count in octets from the start of the source packet. Widths count in bits. An offset of −1 means "no such field".32

# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* PIC_TYPE Number(3) M service type 2* PIC_STYPE Number(3) M service subtype 3 PIC_PI1_OFF Number(5) M octet offset of PI1 from the start of the source packet, or −1 4 PIC_PI1_WID Number(3) M width of PI1 in bits 5 PIC_PI2_OFF Number(5) M octet offset of PI2, or −1 6 PIC_PI2_WID Number(3) M width of PI2 in bits 7* PIC_APID Number(5) 99999 APID the record applies to; empty means all APIDs

Precedence: a record matching type/subtype/APID wins. Otherwise a record matching type/subtype applies. Otherwise PI1 and PI2 are taken as 0. The packetiser reads the PIC directly; it is not imported into the run-time database.32 The Herschel ground segment added a sanity rule: a PID entry must not carry a non-zero PI1 when the matching PIC says PI1 is not used.41

On Solar Orbiter every telemetry packet except the standard spacecraft time packet has a data field header. The primary header is 6 octets and the data field header 10 octets, so source data starts at octet 16.42434445 This matches PID_DFHSIZE = 16 on 11,138 of the 11,150 PID records.59 The diagram shows the first 17 octets of a Solar Orbiter housekeeping report, the part the packetiser needs.

Inference

The positions of type and subtype inside the 10-octet data field header (octets 7 and 8 from the packet start) follow from the field order printed in SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 §4.2.2.1 (spares, PUS version, service type, subtype, spacecraft time), assuming the spares and the version share the first octet. The TN also defines an 8-bit destination ID in the TM data field header (§13.3), and the time field is CUC with 4 coarse and 2 fine octets. One octet each for version/spares, type, subtype and destination ID plus 6 time octets gives the 10 octets, but the order of the destination ID and the time is not stated in the text.4546 The figure with exact offsets was not available as text. The positions are a SCOS-2000 configuration item (MISCconfig), not part of the MIB.28

The Solar Orbiter PIC shows the pattern clearly:60

Type/subtype PI1 offset / width PI2 offset / width What PI1 is (from the packet definitions) (3,25), (3,26) 16 / 8 −1 1-octet SID of the housekeeping or diagnostic report48 (5,1) to (5,4), all APIDs 16 / 16 −1 event ID (5,1), (5,2), (5,3): 25 APID-specific records 16 / 16 18 / 8, 18 / 16, 18 / 32 or 19 / 8 event ID plus a second field defined per APID (1,2), (1,8) 20 / 16 −1 failure code after the 4-octet TC packet ID and sequence control echo (1,1), (1,7), (12,11), (12,12) and others (183 records in all) −1 −1 no extra identification

183 of the 256 PIC records declare no extra fields at all.60

docs.title: TPCF: packet characteristics
docs.text: The TPCF holds one record per SPID with the packet mnemonic, shown on displays to identify where a value came from (None when missing), and TPCF_SIZE. TPCF_SIZE is not imported. It exists for missions that generate history-file configuration and should then hold the full SCOS-2000 packet size: the source packet plus the SCOS-2000 packet header of 64 octets (header versions 0 to 3) or 76 octets (version 4), or 0 for truly variable packets.33 Solar Orbiter has a TPCF record for every PID SPID. 2,325 of them have size 0 and 8,825 give a non-zero size, from 6 to 4,136 octets. 7,484 of the non-zero sizes are below 64 octets, the size of the SCOS-2000 packet header alone, so the mission does not fill this field according to the ICD guideline (it is not imported, so this has no run-time effect).5933

docs.title: Solar Orbiter packets in numbers
docs.text:
The 11,150 PID records use 293 distinct APIDs. Event reporting and request verification account for most of them, because every event ID and every failure code gets its own SPID. The table lists the largest groups and the housekeeping and diagnostic reports; other groups, such as (21,6) with 151 records, are left out:59

Type/subtype Records PID_EVENT Meaning on Solar Orbiter (5,3) 2,911 A error/anomaly report, medium severity49 (5,4) 1,698 A error/anomaly report, high severity (1,8) 1,477 A TC completion report failure, one SPID per failure code (5,1) 1,374 I nominal/progress report (5,2) 1,159 W error/anomaly report, low severity (131,128) 460 empty "OBDB Dump" reports (from PID_DESCR); service 131 is the private function management service47 (6,6) 289 N memory dump report (3,25) 288 empty or N housekeeping parameter report (1,2) 274 A TC acceptance report failure (131,2) 232 empty "PCDU Snapshot" reports (from PID_DESCR) (3,26) 89 empty or N diagnostic parameter report

Because PID_DESCR becomes the event text, an operator who receives, for example, the TM(1,8) with failure code 264 from APID 161 (SPID 14088) sees an alarm saying "The actual TC length is different from the expected TC length". No record sets PID_EVID, so no custom event IDs are used.5930

Other features of the Solar Orbiter PID table:59

  • PID_TIME = Y for 11,141 records. The 9 exceptions are the 3 transfer-frame pseudo-packets and the 6 ground-station packets described below.
  • PID_DFHSIZE is 16 except for 12 records. Six have 0: the three transfer-frame pseudo-packets (APID 1, type 0) and the three MATIS packets of type 166. Six have 6, that is the primary header only: the time report SPID 9999 and five internal packets of types 160 and 161. The time report is keyed as type 9, subtype 2 on APID 0, the APID that Solar Orbiter reserves for its time packet, which has no data field header.43 The TM-TC ICD itself calls this packet "TM (9,2)" while stating that it has no data field header.46 The Database Import ICD's general rule would key a packet without data field header with type and subtype 0;31 how the Solar Orbiter packetiser reconciles the two is not stated in the available sources.
  • PID_CHECK = 1 (verify the packet error control) appears on only 6 records: the three "complete transfer frame" pseudo-packets CTFBAD, CTFIDLE, CTFGOOD (APID 1, type 0) and three MATIS packets. Every spacecraft packet has PID_CHECK = 0.
  • Six records use APIDs above 2047, as the ICD reserves for non-spacecraft sources. They are ground-station packets LMS_NNO, LMS_CEB and LMS_MLG, each at low and high frequency, on APIDs 2048–2065, with parameter descriptions such as "LMS_NNO WSDS1 Temp", "WSDS1 Wind Speed" and "FEC1 AZ act Pos". Their parameters are named NYN…, NYC… and NYM… rather than the reserved NNOiiii-style names.
  • Eighteen SCOS-internal and ground-generated packets share APID 1966 and use the private types 160 to 166 and 251. Examples are "Dynamic UDCs" (160,3), the MISC packet (160,5), "TC Spacon Packet" (160,6), the mini-transfer-frame packets (161,3–5), "Bad Telemetry Packets" (162,1), the time correlation packets (164,1–3), the three MATIS status packets (166,1–3) and "Saved Synthetics" (251,2). APID 1966 lies inside the range 0–2047 that the ICD assigns to spacecraft packets; the ICD only asks that internal packets use a type/subtype/APID combination that no other source produces.3031
  • 2,063 records have a TPSD. In every one of them the TPSD equals the SPID (for example 14173), and 2,063 distinct TPSDs are defined in the VPD.

The APID itself has structure on Solar Orbiter: 7 bits of process ID and 4 bits of packet category.43 APID 178 of YCA2Z011 is binary 0001011 0010, process ID 11 and category 2 (simple arithmetic on the rule; the APID allocation itself is in Annex 8 of the TN). See the APID 178 explorer page.

docs.title: Fixed packets: the PLF
docs.text:
The PLF describes packets whose layout is fixed, identified by SPID. A parameter can appear in many packets. Overlapping entries (two parameters from the same bits) and gaps are both allowed, but a parameter may have only one record per packet. A super-commutated parameter is therefore described by one record with a repetition count.35 All standard monitoring displays (alphanumeric, graphic, scrolling) extract values through the PLF.35

# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* PLF_NAME Char(8) M parameter (PCF_NAME) 2* PLF_SPID Number(10) M packet (PID_SPID) 3 PLF_OFFBY Number(5) M octet offset of the first occurrence, from the end of the SCOS-2000 header, which is the first octet of the source packet with the standard packetiser 4 PLF_OFFBI Number(1) M bit (0–7) of the first bit within that octet; bit 0 is the leftmost, most significant bit 5 PLF_NBOCC Number(4) 1 number of occurrences (1–9999); 1 for normal parameters 6 PLF_LGOCC Number(5) 0 bits between the starts of two consecutive occurrences (0–32767) 7 PLF_TIME Number(9) 0 time offset of the first occurrence from the packet time, in ms (±4,080,000) 8 PLF_TDOCC Number(9) 1 time between consecutive occurrences in ms (1–4,080,000)

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.5.1.35 The Herschel clarification note confirms that bit 0 is the most significant bit, and that offsets coincide with the source packet start only with the generic packetiser.40 The value length is not in the PLF: it follows from PTC/PFC.12 PLF_TIME and PLF_TDOCC time-stamp each sample. Graphic displays use them to plot super-commutated values, and scrolling displays and printouts use them to show times.35

The ICD's housekeeping note explains why these offsets have to be static. SCOS-2000 time-stamps each sample from the packet time plus the fixed MIB offset, so the offsets must be known in advance and be the same in every instance of the packet. Likewise, the collection interval of a periodic packet is fixed in the database; SCOS-2000 does not update it when a ST[03] command changes it on board.39 New ST[03] housekeeping structures must also be defined in the MIB before the spacecraft starts sending them; ESA missions usually generate the ST[03] definition commands from the database.39

In the Solar Orbiter MIB the PLF holds 400,792 records for 107,792 distinct parameters in 9,056 packets. 725 records are super-commutated, and 91 have a non-zero PLF_TIME.61

docs.title: Example: bit-level layout in an IMU housekeeping packet
docs.text:
Octets 65 to 70 of YCA2Z011 (SPID 29534, TM(3,25), APID 178, SID 11) hold status bits and two 12-bit temperatures of gyro IMU11 (real PLF data).62

Three PLF features show here. Single-bit flags are located by PLF_OFFBI alone (NMUD1104…NMUD1111 at bits 0–7 of octet 66). A 12-bit value starts in the middle of an octet (PLF_OFFBI = 4). The same bits are also exposed as whole 8- and 16-bit raw words (NMU0Z000: PTC 3, PFC 4 at octet 65; NMU0Z002: PTC 3, PFC 12 at octet 67), which is allowed because overlaps are legal.3562

docs.title: Example: super-commutation at 8 Hz
docs.text:
YCA2Z229 (SPID 29540, TM(3,26) "AOCS OCM 8Hz Diag", APID 184, SID 229) carries 16 samples of an AOCS state block. Every block parameter has PLF_NBOCC = 16, PLF_LGOCC = 744 bits (93 octets), PLF_TIME = −1875 ms and PLF_TDOCC = 125 ms. The n-th sample (n = 0…15) of a parameter first located at octet o therefore sits at bit \(8o + 744n\) and is time-stamped \(t_{pkt} - 1875 + 125n\) ms. The last sample carries the packet time itself, and the first is 1.875 s older (real PLF data; the formula restates the ICD field definitions).6235

The block adds up to 744 bits, exactly the PLF_LGOCC step, so consecutive samples are packed with no gap. Before the block sit the SID (NCD030C1, octet 16, 8 bits) and an enable flag (NCA3Z03A, octet 17).62 The largest repetition count in the Solar Orbiter MIB is 2,046: NIH0XCPI "Data from CPIO file", a 2-octet string repeated every 16 bits from octet 20 of SPID 56333 "SSMM XF Engineering Files".61 The ICD warns that a synthetic parameter fed by a super-commutated parameter is recomputed for every sample, which can be costly, and that saved synthetic parameters cannot be super-commutated.23

docs.title: Variable packets: the VPD
docs.text:
Some PUS reports have no fixed layout. A repeat counter N precedes N groups, or a parameter ID decides how the following value is interpreted. The VPD describes such packets, element by element, for packets whose PID gives a TPSD. It has no relation to the PLF or the display tables.36 Each element starts where the previous one ended, shifted by VPD_OFFSET bits: a positive offset makes a gap, a negative one an overlap.36 The table must be sorted by VPD_TPSD and VPD_POS.36

# Field Type M / default Meaning 1* VPD_TPSD Number(10) M structure ID (PID_TPSD) 2* VPD_POS Number(4) M ordinal position of the element 3 VPD_NAME Char(8) M parameter (PCF_NAME) 4 VPD_GRPSIZE Number(3) 0 for a repeat counter (or a dummy fixed-repeat element): number of following elements in the repeated group; nesting is allowed 5 VPD_FIXREP Number(3) 0 0 no repeat; > 0 fixed number of repetitions (the counter element is then a dummy, defined in the PCF but absent from the packet); −1 repeat to end of packet (future extension) 6 VPD_CHOICE Char(1) N Y: the value is a TPSD that defines the rest of the packet; must be the last element of its structure (choice is not supported by the VPD application) 7 VPD_PIDREF Char(1) N Y: the value is an on-board parameter ID, looked up in PCF_PID to name a following deduced value 8 VPD_DISDESC Char(16) column header text on displays 9 VPD_WIDTH Number(2) M 0 hides the value; > 0 displays it in full 10 VPD_JUSTIFY Char(1) L L, R or C justification 11 VPD_NEWLINE Char(1) N Y starts a new line; not allowed inside repeated groups 12 VPD_DCHAR Number(1) 0 0 value only, 1 name and value, 2 name, PCF_DESCR and value 13 VPD_FORM Char(1) N B, O, D, H or N (normal: engineering value if a single calibration exists) 14 VPD_OFFSET Number(6) 0 bits between the end of the previous element and this one (−32768…32767)

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.5.2.36

Limitations of variable packets

Appendix C of the ICD states that values extracted from variable packets do not take part in full telemetry processing: no validity, no monitoring checks, no validation or verification checks and no synthetic parameter evaluation. Their parameters and time references are only known once the packet is opened. The ICD therefore advises against delivering regular housekeeping in variable packets.38 Only parameters of packets defined in the VPD are shown in the full mode of the Packets History Display.34

Solar Orbiter defines 2,063 variable structures in 19,863 VPD rows. 711 rows are repeat counters (VPD_GRPSIZE > 0) and 1,449 rows carry parameter IDs (VPD_PIDREF = Y). No row uses VPD_FIXREP or VPD_CHOICE. 404 rows have a non-zero offset, 389 of them negative (overlaps).63

docs.title: Example: the out-of-limit list report TM(12,11)
docs.text:
The on-board monitoring report TM(12,11) on APID 163 (SPID and TPSD 14173, "Parameters Out-of-limit List Report") is a textbook variable packet. A 2-octet counter N is followed by N repetitions of eight fields, whose value fields take their type from the monitored parameter (real VPD data).6450

POS VPD_NAME Description PTC/PFC VPD attributes 1 NCD0C0B1 OBCHP_Nb Mon in 12,11 3/12 (16-bit unsigned) GRPSIZE = 8: repeat the next 8 elements N times 2 NCD0C094 OBCHP_S12_Mon_ID ¾ (8-bit) 3 NCD0C095 OBCHP_Monitored Par ID 2/32 (32-bit enumerated) PIDREF = Y 4 NCD0C0B4 OBCHP_S12_Bit Mask 3/14 (32-bit) 5 NCD0C0B5 OBCHP_S12_Par value 11/0 deduced, PCF_WIDTH = 64, PCF_RELATED = NCD0C095 6 NCD0C0B6 OBCHP_S12_Crossed Limit 11/0 deduced, width 64, related NCD0C095 7 NCD0C0B7 OBCHP_S12_Prev Status 2/8 8 NCD0C0C8 OBCHP_S12_Curr Status 2/8 9 NCD0C0B9 OBCHP_S12_Trans time 9/17 (CUC, 4 + 2 octets)

The VPD reproduces the structure printed in the Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure ICD. The document gives the counter as 2 octets, the monitoring ID as 1, the parameter ID as 4, the mask as 4, parameter value and limit crossed as 8 octets each ("deduced"), the two statuses as 1 octet each and the transition time as 6 octets.50 The deduced value fields show how PCF_RELATED, PCF_WIDTH and VPD_PIDREF work together. NCD0C095 delivers an on-board parameter ID, which SCOS-2000 matches against PCF_PID to find the monitored parameter and its type. The following 64-bit slots are decoded with that type.1412 The same nine-element structure is reused for the TM(12,12) check transition report (TPSD 14171), with counter NCAB0021 "Nb of PMONs in TM(12,12)".64 The monitoring checks page compares these on-board reports with ground checking. The ECSS-E-ST-70-31C data model describes the same idea in neutral terms: arrays with a repetition-number format, and deduced structures selected by conditions.52

docs.title: Monitoring groups: GRP, GRPA, GRPK
docs.text:
Groups let SCOS-2000 enable or disable the processing or monitoring of sets of parameters or packets in one action.37

Table Fields Notes GRP GRP_NAME Char(14) key; GRP_DESCR Char(24); GRP_GTYPE Char(2): PA parameter group, PK packet group all three mandatory GRPA GRPA_GNAME Char(14), GRPA_PANAME Char(8), both keys members must be processed by the telemetry model (in the PLF, or synthetic) GRPK GRPK_GNAME Char(14), GRPK_PKSPID Number(10), both keys members are SPIDs

Field definitions from ICD §3.3.2.6.37 Solar Orbiter barely uses groups. GRPHK ("Packet for HK monitoring", type PK) holds four SWA instrument packets: SPIDs 58200 SWA_TM_DPU_HK, 58201 SWA_TM_EAS1_HK, 58202 SWA_TM_EAS2_HK and 58907 SWA_TM_II_INFO. GRPPAR ("Example for Parameters", type PA) has no members, and GRPA is empty.65 See the SWA instrument database page for the instrument's own MIB.
