docs.title: MIB parameter types: PTC/PFC in SCOS-2000
docs.text:
Every value that SCOS-2000 extracts from telemetry or puts into a telecommand has a type, written as a pair of small integers: the Parameter Type Code (PTC) and the Parameter Format Code (PFC). The PTC names the abstract type, for example unsigned integer, real or absolute time. The PFC selects the concrete encoding and, through it, the width in bits. The pair comes from the ESA Packet Utilisation Standard. The Database Import ICD defines which pairs the SCOS-2000 MIB accepts, how wide each one is, and the text syntax in which values of each type are written in the ASCII tables.1

This page covers the full SCOS-2000 type table, the value syntax, the related fields (width, endianness, time correlation, calibration category) and the differences from PUS-A (2003) and PUS-C (2016). It ends with the frequency of each PTC/PFC pair in the real Solar Orbiter MIB. The PUS definitions themselves are on PUS parameter types.

docs.title: Where types appear in the MIB
docs.text:
Field Table Type Role PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC pcf Number(2), Number(5) Type of a monitoring parameter. Mandatory. PTC in the range 1 to 13.3 CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC cpc Number(2), Number(5) Type of a command parameter. Mandatory.4 CSP_PTC, CSP_PFC csp Number(2), Number(5) Type of a sequence formal parameter5 PCF_WIDTH pcf Number(6) "Padded" width in bits, used only when extracting through vpd6 PCF_ENDIAN pcf Char(1) Byte order of whole-byte types: B (default) or L7 PCF_CORR, PCF_OBTID pcf Char(1), Number(5) Whether time correlation is applied to time values, and which on-board clock8 CPC_CORR, CPC_OBTID, CPC_ENDIAN cpc as above The same for command parameters. CPC_ENDIAN is a future extension.910 PCF_CATEG, CPC_CATEG pcf, cpc Char(1) Calibration category. It must be consistent with the type.1112

For telemetry, the type controls decoding. SCOS-2000 uses PCF_PTC/PCF_PFC to decode parameters extracted from packets (PCF_NATUR = R or C). A synthetic parameter must still carry a valid pair that matches the format of its computed value, otherwise it is rejected at import. A saved synthetic parameter must have PTC 13.3 For commands, the type both drives encoding and constrains the raw values that are accepted in the MIB and on the stack. The importer syntax-checks every command and sequence parameter value against its type, and replaces bad values with 0, an empty string or 1970.001.00.00.00.13

Remember the distinction made in §1.3.1 of the ICD. The raw value is the value before calibration. The encoded value is the bit pattern on the link. The two coincide only for unsigned integers. A 16-bit signed integer with raw value −1 is encoded as 0xFFFF.14

docs.title: The SCOS-2000 type table
docs.text: Appendix A of the ICD (Table 4) lists every supported pair, together with the internal type and the width the importer assumes. It refers to the PUS nomenclature of ESA PSS-07-101 (Packet Utilisation Standard, issue 1, May 1994). Pairs that SCOS-2000 supports beyond that document are printed in bold, and pairs listed there but unsupported are printed in italics.12 The bold and italic marking does not survive in the text extraction used by this wiki, so the support status below is taken from the comment column and from Appendix C.

docs.title: PTC 1 Boolean and PTC 2 enumerated
docs.text:
PTC PFC SCOS-2000 internal type Width Notes 1 0 unsigned integer 1 bit Boolean 2 1 … 32 unsigned integer PFC bits Enumerated. PUS permits only some PFCs. SCOS-2000 only limits the width to 32 bits.1

An enumerated value has discrete, unordered values, each meaning a text. An error code is the classic example.15 In the MIB, those texts come from a textual calibration (PCF_CATEG = S, see Calibration).11 In the Solar Orbiter MIB, 25,081 of the 29,443 enumerated parameters have one.39

docs.title: PTC 3 unsigned and PTC 4 signed integers
docs.text:
PFC Width (PTC 3 and 4) Unsigned range Signed range SCOS-2000 0 … 12 PFC + 4 bits (4 … 16) 0 to 2^(PFC+4) − 1 −2^(PFC+3) to 2^(PFC+3) − 1 supported 13 24 bits 0 to 16,777,215 −8,388,608 to 8,388,607 supported 14 32 bits 0 to 2^32 − 1 −2^31 to 2^31 − 1 supported 15 48 bits 0 to 2^48 − 1 −2^47 to 2^47 − 1 not supported 16 64 bits 0 to 2^64 − 1 −2^63 to 2^63 − 1 not supported

The widths are those of ICD Table 4.1 The ranges follow the PUS definitions.16 Unsigned integers are most-significant-bit first. Signed integers use two's complement, with bit 0 as the sign.16 Appendix C confirms the 32-bit limit: PFC 15 and 16 are not supported.17 In practice, PTC 3 PFC 12 is the familiar 16-bit word and PFC 14 the 32-bit one.

docs.title: PTC 5 real
docs.text:
PFC Format Width SCOS-2000 1 IEEE 754 single precision 32 bits TM and TC 2 IEEE 754 double precision 64 bits TM and TC 3 MIL-STD-1750A single precision 32 bits TM and TC. ESA missions often call it "PTC=5, PFC=2". 4 MIL-STD-1750A extended precision 48 bits commands only (from R3.0), not telemetry

All four rows come from ICD Table 4.1 The command-only restriction for 5/4 was clarified in ICD 6.1 (S2K-40-DCR-808), and Appendix C repeats it.1817 The remark about "PTC=5, PFC=2" means that older ESA mission documents, such as the Rosetta Space/Ground ICD cited by Table 5, number the MIL single-precision format as PFC 2. SCOS-2000 numbers it PFC 3, so a translation is needed when such documents feed a MIB.19

The bit layouts below follow PUS-A, which reproduces both standards:20

The extended layout is derived from the PUS-A examples, which print each value as "Mantissa (MS) Exp Mantissa (LS)" with 6, 2 and 4 hexadecimal digits.21 As an example taken from PUS-A, 0.5 × 2^1 in MIL single precision is 0x40000001. The mantissa is 0x400000 (0.5) and the exponent is 0x01.20

docs.title: PTC 6 bit string
docs.text:
PFC Meaning Width SCOS-2000 0 variable-length bit string variable not supported 1 … 32 fixed-length bit string, handled as an unsigned integer PFC bits monitoring only

SCOS-2000 treats fixed bit strings as unsigned integers of PFC bits, at most 32, and only on the monitoring side.1 PUS-C also uses fixed-length PTC 6 for spare fields, whose bits must all be zero.22

docs.title: PTC 7 octet string and PTC 8 character string
docs.text:
PTC PFC Meaning Width SCOS-2000 7 0 variable-length octet string variable commands and sequences only 7 n > 0 fixed octet string n octets TM and TC 8 0 variable-length character string variable commands and sequences only 8 n > 0 fixed character string n characters (octets) TM and TC

Variable-length strings can be given values from a Stack Import file or on a manual stack. To receive values from stack files, they must be editable elements of the command (CDF_ELTYPE = E).23 In PUS, a variable-length string is preceded by an unsigned length field n. SCOS-2000 command sources work out the length by counting the octets or characters in the value, and they do not read n. Before R4.0, n had to be part of the value or a separate parameter. From R4.0, SCOS-2000 can be configured to insert n automatically.1924

The width of n is not fixed by PUS-C. It is declared per application process.25 Octet and character strings cannot be calibrated.19 On the telemetry side, variable-length strings are not decoded natively. Memory dumps and similar data need special processing.17

docs.title: PTC 9 absolute time
docs.text:
PFC Format Coarse octets Fine octets Total SCOS-2000 0 CUC or CDS with explicit P-field – – variable not supported 1 CDS without µs – – 6 supported from R5.0 2 CDS with µs – – 8 commands only 3 … 6 CUC 1 0 … 3 1 … 4 supported 7 … 10 CUC 2 0 … 3 2 … 5 supported 11 … 14 CUC 3 0 … 3 3 … 6 supported 15 … 18 CUC 4 0 … 3 4 … 7 supported 30 Unix time: 4 octets seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00, then 4 octets of µs within the second – – 8 SCOS-2000 specific, "not defined in PUS". Added in ICD 6.7.

All rows come from ICD Table 4.2627 For PFC 3 to 18, the number of coarse octets is ⌊(PFC + 1) / 4⌋ and the number of fine octets is (PFC + 1) mod 4. That is exactly the PUS rule.28 SCOS-2000 cannot recognise a time format from a P-field: the format must be known implicitly from the MIB.17 Absolute time values are converted between raw and encoded form by a mission-specific time correlation routine, and they cannot be calibrated.19 The CUC and CDS codes themselves are explained on Time code formats.

The CDS layout follows PUS-C Table 7-10 note 2, and the CUC value is t = C1·256³ + C2·256² + C3·256 + C4 + F1·256⁻¹ + F2·256⁻² (+ F3·256⁻³).28 The Unix layout is the one given in ICD Table 4.26

Worked example (illustrative bytes). Take a PTC 9 / PFC 17 field with bytes 0x2A 0x3B 0x4C 0x5D 0x80 0x00. The coarse time is 0x2A3B4C5D = 708,529,245 s and the fine time is 0x8000 / 65,536 = 0.5 s, so t = 708,529,245.5 s after the epoch. Which epoch, and whether on-board time correlation applies, depend on PCF_CORR and PCF_OBTID (see below). The bytes are constructed for this explanation. They are not taken from a real packet.

docs.title: PTC 10 relative time
docs.text:
PFC Format Coarse octets Fine octets SCOS-2000 3 … 18 CUC (same numbering as PTC 9) 1 … 4 0 … 3 supported

The rows come from ICD Table 4.29 A relative time is a positive or negative offset, negative values being two's complement.30 It cannot be calibrated. PCF_CORR and CPC_CORR must be N for relative times (clarified in issue 7.0, changes S2K-8572 and S2K-8778).831

Relative-time PFC numbering differs between PUS-A and SCOS-2000

PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A, 2003) numbers relative CUC times from PFC 1 to 16, with ⌊(PFC + 3) / 4⌋ coarse and (PFC + 3) mod 4 fine octets.32 SCOS-2000, like PUS-C, uses PFC 3 to 18 with the absolute-time rule.2930 The same four-coarse, two-fine relative time is therefore PFC 15 in PUS-A and PFC 17 in SCOS-2000. A mission whose packet ICD follows PUS-A must translate relative-time PFCs when building its MIB.

Inference

The translation rule is this wiki's arithmetic from the two formulas. The ICD refers to PSS-07-101 (1994) rather than to PUS-A, and that document is not in the library, so which numbering PSS-07-101 used is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: PTC 11 deduced
docs.text:
PFC Meaning SCOS-2000 0 Deduced. Type and width come from another, earlier field of the same packet. TM (through vpd) and TC n > 0 Deduced with a forced width of n bits commands only

These rows are from ICD Table 4.33 PUS defines a deduced field as one whose actual type and encoding are deduced from preceding fields of the same packet, from mission constants, or both.34 The typical case in the ICD is a parameter value whose type follows from a preceding on-board parameter identifier (PUS "Parameter#").35 SCOS-2000 implements this as follows:

  • Telemetry. A deduced parameter is decoded only in variable packets (vpd). Its PCF_RELATED names the parameter that carries the on-board parameter ID. That ID is matched against PCF_PID to find the real parameter, whose PTC/PFC is then used. PCF_WIDTH either forces a fixed slot width or, if empty, lets the slot follow the width of the identified parameter, padded by that parameter's own PCF_WIDTH.356
  • Commands. A deduced command parameter (CPC_PTC = 11) inherits type, width and calibration from the TM parameter named by the first "Parameter ID" command parameter in the same (repeated) array. CPC_PFC = 0 keeps that width, and a value above 0 forces the width in bits. Deduced command parameters were introduced with SCOS-2000 R5 (ICD 6.4).36437

A deduced data structure, as opposed to a deduced field, is not supported.38

Real example. In the Solar Orbiter MIB, variable structure TPSD 14406 ("OBCP telemetry", TM(18,144)) contains a repeated group of two fields. The group counter is NCD12091 with VPD_GRPSIZE = 2. The first field, NCD12904, is the parameter ID: PTC 3, PFC 14, flagged VPD_PIDREF = Y. The second, NCD12905 "OBCHP_S18_Param Value", is deduced: PTC 11, PFC 0, with PCF_RELATED = NCD12904.39

docs.title: PTC 13 saved synthetic
docs.text:
PTC PFC Meaning 13 0 Saved synthetic parameter. Its value characteristics come from the related synthetic parameter (PCF_RELATED).40

PTC 13 is specific to SCOS-2000: the PUS-C list of type codes ends at PTC 12.57 Each saved synthetic value occupies a 13-byte slot in its synthetic packet: 8 bytes of value, 1 byte of value type and 4 bytes of validity flags. The order of these parts within the slot is not stated in the available sources.41 Solar Orbiter's two saved synthetics, NTTSS030 and NTTSS031, carry PCF_WIDTH = 104 bits (13 bytes) and sit at byte offsets 0 and 13 of packet 66838.39

docs.title: Special command parameter types
docs.text:
The ICD defines three "special PUS command parameter types". Command ID and Parameter ID are expressed through CPC_CATEG on top of an ordinary PTC. Deduced command parameters use PTC 11, the same code as deduced telemetry fields:361217

Kind How it is declared What SCOS-2000 encodes Typical use Command ID CPC_CATEG = A, PTC 7, PFC 0 The complete raw packet of the named command (CCF_CNAME), with configurable header fields Commands that embed a TC, such as TC(19,1) Parameter ID CPC_CATEG = P, PTC 3 (any width) The on-board ID (PCF_PID) of the named TM parameter Commands that list TM parameter IDs, such as TC(4,6) and TC(12,1) Deduced CPC_PTC = 11 See PTC 11 Parameter-value lists

Command ID and Parameter ID came from Cryosat and were integrated into the ICD with release 4.0 (issue 6.0).42 Deduced command parameters came later, with R5 (issue 6.4).37 Solar Orbiter has 2 Command ID parameters, both PTC 7 / PFC 0 ("Complete TC packet" and "TC to send upon event"). It has 152 Parameter ID parameters, all PTC 3 / PFC 14.39

docs.title: Raw value syntax
docs.text:
Wherever the MIB holds a value, for example a default (CPC_DEFVAL, CDF_VALUE, SDF_VALUE), a limit (OCP_LVALU), a calibration point or a constant (PCF_PARVAL), the value is text in the raw format of its type (ICD Table 5):19

Type Encoding on the link Raw format in the MIB Examples from the ICD Unsigned integer unsigned integer Digits in the selected radix. Decimal is the default. Binary, octal or hexadecimal are possible. 15, 1111, 17, F Signed integer two's complement Decimal only 127, -1, -127 Real (IEEE single or double) IEEE 754 Scientific or fixed-point notation 23.13, -1.2E3, 2.5E38 (single), 1.6E308 (double) Real (MIL single) MIL-STD-1750A Scientific or fixed-point notation 23.13, -1.2E3, 1.6E38 Octet string unsigned integer Hex digits, two per octet, no spaces 0AAFBB Character string ASCII ASCII characters ANY-STRING Absolute time per PUS yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss 2001.159.23.59.59 Relative time per PUS +/-[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] -00.01.00, +251.23.59.59.010

Engineering (calibrated) values of unsigned integers are always input and displayed in decimal, even when the calibration's engineering format is unsigned. The engineering format of command parameters is dictated by the associated calibration.19 For integer fields of the tables, as opposed to parameter values, the C++ prefixes 0x and 0 select hexadecimal and octal.43 When a command or sequence parameter value does not match its type, the importer substitutes 0 (integers, reals, relative times), an empty string or 1970.001.00.00.00 (absolute times). A mandatory field left null becomes 0 or an empty string.13

docs.title: Width and padding
docs.text: PCF_WIDTH is the "padded" width of a parameter in bits. It is used only by the variable packet (vpd) extraction, to find where the next field starts when a slot is wider than the PTC/PFC implies. Padding bits always precede the value (they are its most significant bits). For fixed packets (plf) the width is always implied by PTC/PFC, and PCF_WIDTH is ignored.644 On the commanding side, CDF_ELLEN gives each element's length in bits.45

docs.title: Endianness
docs.text: PCF_ENDIAN (added in ICD 6.7, S2K-DCR-5192) declares the byte order of types whose length is a whole number of bytes. Issues 6.7 Draft A and 6.9 describe it as a field that "can be used in the future". Issue 7.0 drops "in the future" (S2K-8353, applicable from SCOS-2000 6.0.1).5831 B means big endian, most significant byte first, and is the default. L means little endian. The conversion applies to signed and unsigned integers, strings, octet strings, absolute times and relative times.72731 CPC_ENDIAN has the same values but is marked as a future extension (S2K-7749): issue 7.0 assigns it to "No SCOS version".1031 PUS itself always transmits the most significant bit first.16

docs.title: Time correlation flags
docs.text: PCF_CORR = Y (the default) applies time correlation to an absolute time parameter when it is decoded. N extracts the time without correlation. PCF_OBTID selects which on-board clock's format and correlation to use. The value is 1 to N for N clocks, and when it is left empty the MISCconfig default TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID applies. With N and no OBT ID, the epoch is the MISCconfig variable TCO_ESA_EPOCH. The command-side fields CPC_CORR and CPC_OBTID mirror these.89 All four fields arrived with SCOS-2000 R5.2 (ICD 6.7, S2K-SCR-4917), together with PFC 30.27 See Time correlation in SCOS-2000.

docs.title: Calibration category and type
docs.text:
The category must agree with the type:114612

  • PCF_CATEG = N (numerical) covers numerical parameters, with or without a numerical, polynomial or logarithmic calibration. It also covers PTC 6, 7, 9 and 10.
  • S (status) is for parameters with a textual calibration.
  • T (text) is for PTC 8 character strings only.
  • PCF_CURTX must be empty for PTC 7, 8, 9 and 10. Strings and times are never calibrated.
  • CPC_CATEG must be null or N for strings and times, unless the parameter is a Command ID (A) or a Parameter ID (P).

docs.title: SCOS-2000 compared with PUS-A and PUS-C
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 implements most of the PUS type system. The differences are listed below, because each one either limits what a mission's packets may contain or calls for a translation when the MIB is generated.

Topic PUS-A (2003) PUS-C (2016) SCOS-2000 MIB (ICD 7.0) Boolean PFC 0 (1 bit)47 PFC 0, or n > 1 bits48 PFC 0 only Enumerated widths 1–16, 24, 32 bits15 1–64 bits49 1–32 bits Unsigned/signed integers PFC 0–16 (up to 64 bits)50 PFC 0–16, plus unsigned 17–19 = 1, 2, 3 bits16 PFC 0–14 (up to 32 bits) Real PFC 1–420 PFC 1–451 PFC 1–3. PFC 4 for commands only. Bit string PFC 0 variable, n fixed52 same22 Only n ≤ 32, monitoring only, as unsigned Variable octet/character string supported53 supported25 Commands and sequences only. Length n counted, optionally inserted (R4.0). Absolute time PFC 0–1854 PFC 0–46 (19–46: CUC with 4 to 10 fine octets)28 PFC 1–18 (2 for TC only) and 30 (Unix). No P-field. Relative time PFC 0–16, (PFC + 3) / 4 rule32 PFC 2 (CDS) and 3–1830 PFC 3–18 Deduced PFC 034 PFC 055 PFC 0. PFC > 0 (forced width) for TC only. No deduced structures. Packet (PTC 12) – PFC 0 TM, PFC 1 TC56 Not in Table 4. Command ID parameters (7/0) carry TC packets instead. Saved synthetic (PTC 13) – – SCOS-2000 specific

The SCOS-2000 column summarises ICD Table 4 and Appendix C.117 The PUS migration itself is covered in PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: Types in the Solar Orbiter MIB
docs.text: The tables below count the PTC/PFC pairs in the 2025-09-16 Solar Orbiter MIB.39

docs.title: What the numbers show
docs.text:
• Within the SCOS-2000 limits. No parameter uses an integer wider than 32 bits, a MIL-STD real, a variable bit string or an explicit P-field.391 The time types are the 4-octet coarse CUC formats 9/15 and 9/17, plus three ground-side oddities (next point).
  • Two SCOS-specific time formats. The Unix-time format 9/30 appears exactly twice, NYG02101 "Period From" and NYG02102 "Period To", both in the "Time Correlation Report" packet (SPID 66840, APID 1966). The CDS-with-µs format 9/2 appears once, in telemetry: NYG02204 "GS Acceptance Time" in SPID 66850, "TM Packet used by the Releaser G/S response". ICD Table 4 says that 9/2 is supported for command parameters only.3926 The same packet holds the only little-endian parameter in the MIB, NYG02201 "GS Packet Size" (PTC 3, PFC 14, PCF_ENDIAN = L).39
  • Enumerated widths beyond PUS-A. 242 enumerated parameters use widths that PUS-A does not list (17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 25, 28, 30 and 31 bits). SCOS-2000 (up to 32 bits) and PUS-C (up to 64 bits) both allow them.391549
  • Small fields. Fields of 1 to 3 bits are encoded as Booleans (1/0, 4,380 parameters), enumerated (2/1–⅔, 13,306) or bit strings (6/1–6/3, 878), never as the PUS-C unsigned PFCs 17–19, which SCOS-2000 does not list.3916
  • Time correlation. All 50 parameters with PCF_CORR = N are relative times (47) or the three ground-side times above. No parameter sets PCF_OBTID.398
  • Consistency with the category rules. Category T occurs only with PTC 8 (120 parameters). No string or time parameter has a PCF_CURTX.3911

Inference

The parameters NYG021xx and NYG022xx are on APID 1966, in packets with mission-specific types (164 and 165) that describe ground functions. Unix-time, CDS-with-µs and little-endian encodings therefore most likely describe data produced by ground software rather than by the spacecraft. Whether SCOS-2000 decodes a 9/2 monitoring parameter despite the Table 4 restriction is not stated in the available sources.

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (command parameter name column is CPC_NAME in the SQLite copy)
SELECT PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1,2
 ORDER BY CAST(PCF_PTC AS int), CAST(PCF_PFC AS int);
SELECT PCF_PTC, count(*), count(DISTINCT PCF_PFC) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC, count(*) FROM cpc GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT CSP_PTC, CSP_PFC, count(*) FROM csp GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT CPC_CATEG, CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC, count(*) FROM cpc WHERE CPC_CATEG IN ('A','P') GROUP BY 1,2,3;
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_ENDIAN, PCF_CORR FROM pcf
 WHERE PCF_ENDIAN='L' OR (PCF_PTC='9' AND PCF_PFC IN ('2','30'));
SELECT PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_CORR, count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_PTC IN ('9','10') GROUP BY 1,2,3;
SELECT PCF_CATEG, PCF_PTC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_PTC IN ('7','8','9','10') AND PCF_CURTX <> '';  -- 0
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, PCF_WIDTH, PCF_RELATED FROM pcf WHERE PCF_WIDTH <> '';
SELECT VPD_POS, VPD_NAME, VPD_GRPSIZE, VPD_PIDREF FROM vpd WHERE VPD_TPSD='14406';

docs.title: Command sequences and parameter sets
docs.text: A spacecraft procedure rarely consists of one telecommand. Switching on an instrument, changing an on-board mode or dumping a packet store takes a fixed series of commands, released at set intervals and sharing a few values that the operator supplies. In SCOS-2000 such a series is a command sequence: an ordered list of commands and nested sequences, stored in the MIB as a template with place-holders called formal parameters. When the operator loads the sequence on a command stack, SCOS-2000 asks for the formal parameter values, expands nested sequences like macros, computes release and execution times, and turns the result into individual command requests.13 The MIB describes a sequence in four tables: csf (the sequence), css (its elements), sdf (the values of element parameters) and csp (its formal parameters). Five more tables define parameter sets, named collections of preset values for commands and sequences. This page covers all nine tables field by field and shows how the Solar Orbiter MIB uses them. Individual commands are described on Commanding in the MIB and their verification on Command verification in the MIB.

docs.title: Concepts and terminology
docs.text:
The ICD uses three terms that are easy to confuse:4

  • An element is one entry of a sequence: a command, a nested sequence, or (in principle) a formal parameter standing for a command or sequence name that is given later.
  • An element parameter is a parameter of an element: a command parameter if the element is a command, or a parameter of the nested sequence if the element is a sequence.
  • A formal parameter is an argument of the sequence being defined. Seen from a parent sequence, the formal parameters of a nested sequence are called sequence parameters.

An element parameter gets its value in one of three ways: explicitly in sdf, from the default of the original definition (cdf for commands, csp for nested sequences), or by mapping it to a formal parameter of the current sequence. Several element parameters may share one formal parameter if they have the same raw and engineering formats.4 A sequence can contain sequences to any depth, provided it never contains itself.3

The ICD illustrates the tables with two sequences. SQ1 has three elements: command CMD1, sequence SQ2 and a formal parameter element FP3. SQ2 has two commands, CMD3 and CMD6. SQ1's formal parameters are FP1 (a command parameter), FP2 (a sequence parameter) and FP3 (a command or sequence name); SQ2's are FP4 and FP5.5

flowchart LR
    subgraph SQ1["SQ1 (formal parameters FP1, FP2, FP3)"]
        C1["CMD1"]
        S2["SQ2"]
        E3["element given by FP3"]
    end
    subgraph SQ2d["SQ2 (formal parameters FP4, FP5)"]
        C3["CMD3"]
        C6["CMD6"]
    end
    FP1(["FP1"]) -.-> C1
    FP2(["FP2"]) -.->|"value of SQ2's FP5"| S2
    S2 --> SQ2d
    FP5(["FP5"]) -.->|"2nd parameter of CMD6"| C6

In the ICD's example the tables hold 2 csf, 5 css, 10 sdf and 5 csp records, and a value given for FP2 at load time travels through FP5 into the second parameter of CMD6. The element defined by FP3 has no parameters of its own; its parameters come from the defaults of whatever command or sequence is named, so only fully defined commands and sequences may be used that way.5 Formal parameter names need only be unique within one sequence.5

erDiagram
    CSF ||--|{ CSS : "CSS_SQNAME"
    CSF ||--o{ CSP : "CSP_SQNAME"
    CSS ||--o{ SDF : "SDF_SQNAME + SDF_ENTRY"
    CSS }o--o| CCF : "CSS_ELEMID (type C)"
    CSS }o--o| CSF : "CSS_ELEMID (type S)"
    SDF }o--o| CDF : "SDF_PNAME + SDF_POS (command element)"
    SDF }o--o| CSP : "SDF_VALUE (type F) or nested CSP"
    SDF }o--o| PSV : "SDF_VALSET (type P)"
    CSF ||--o{ PSM : "parameter sets"
    CSP }o--o| PRF : "CSP_PRFREF"
    CSP }o--o| CCA : "CSP_CCAREF"
    CSP }o--o| PAF : "CSP_PAFREF"

The relationships restate the ICD overview of the commanding data and the field definitions below.2

docs.title: Where sequences live: from the run-time database to the FARC
docs.text:
In SCOS-2000 releases before R5, sequence tables were imported with all other ASCII tables into the run-time database; ICD issue 5.1 describes csf, css, sdf and csp without any special handling, and issue 7.0 dates the separate storage of sequences from R5.0.323 ICD issue 6.4, written for SCOS-2000 R5, moved TC sequence and TM display definitions out of the run-time (POST) MIB database into the FARC as XML files.29 FARC is the SCOS-2000 File Archive.33 From R5 the command sources load sequence definitions from the FARC; the XML format is specified in a separate document, ICD-0051 "SCOS-2000 TC Sequences definitions ICD", which is not among the available sources.67

The ASCII tables remain the import format, for full backward compatibility. On request their content is converted into XML files and imported into the FARC with a "delta" approach: only the sequences in the delivered files are replaced, and previously imported sequences stay available.36 The ICD lists two consequences: sequences and displays are imported independently of the TM/TC database, so a sequence can be updated without importing a new database; and the delta import never removes old definitions.6

flowchart LR
    A["Off-line database<br/>(mission MIB editor)"] --> B["ASCII files<br/>csf.dat css.dat sdf.dat csp.dat"]
    B -->|"SCOS-2000 before R5"| C["Run-time database<br/>(imported with all tables)"]
    B -->|"SCOS-2000 R5 and later:<br/>convert on request, delta import"| D["XML sequence files<br/>in the FARC"]
    D --> E["Command sources<br/>(manual stacks, schedulers)"]
    C --> E

The diagram summarises ICD issues 5.1, 6.9 and 7.0; it is this wiki's drawing.32630 The same text appears in ICD issues 6.9 and 7.0, so the arrangement is unchanged since R5.303 The archives of SCOS-2000 are described on Mission archives: PARC, DARC and FARC, and the release history of the ICD on History of the Database Import ICD.

docs.title: csf: sequence header
docs.text:
csf has one record per sequence.8

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* CSF_NAME Char(8), M Unique sequence name 2 CSF_DESC Char(24), M Description 3 CSF_DESC2 Char(64) Detailed description 4 CSF_IFTT Char(1) Execution time-tags: Y the sequence (or a nested one) contains execution time-tagged commands and the operator gives an absolute reference time at load time, for commands with both a release and an execution time-tag; B the operator chooses at load time between on-board time-tagged (execution tags only) and ground time-tagged (release tags only, immediate execution); N no execution time-tags N 5 CSF_NFPARS Number(3) Number of formal parameters, for consistency checks against csp 6 CSF_ELEMS Number(5) Number of elements, for consistency checks against css 7 CSF_CRITICAL Char(1) Y critical (hazardous), N not; extra protection is mission-specific N 8 CSF_PLAN Char(1) Which sources may use the sequence in a planning file: A all, F flight dynamics, S SOC, N none N 9 CSF_EXEC Char(1) Y may be loaded stand-alone; N only as a nested sequence Y 10 CSF_SUBSYS Number(3) Subsystem 1–255 11 CSF_GENTIME Char(17) Time the sequence was generated 12 CSF_DOCNAME Char(32) Document it was generated from 13 CSF_ISSUE Char(10) Issue of that document 14 CSF_DATE Char(17) Issue date of that document 15 CSF_DEFSET Char(8) Default parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) 16 CSF_SUBSCHEDID Number(5) Default on-board sub-schedule (1–65535) for execution time-tagged loading

89

The meaning of CSF_SUBSCHEDID changed in ICD 7.0 (change request S2K-6680, SCOS 5.5.2 and later). In issue 6.9 it gave all time-tagged commands of the sequence the same sub-schedule and fell back to CSF_SUBSYS when empty; in issue 7.0 a non-null value still forces one sub-schedule for the whole sequence, but when it is null each command keeps its own CCF_SUBSCHEDID.31928

docs.title: css: sequence elements
docs.text:
css has one record per element. Everything it says about a command is a default: after loading, the command requests can still be edited on the manual stack.10

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* CSS_SQNAME Char(8), M Sequence the element belongs to 2 CSS_COMM Char(32) Comment; for a textual comment element it is shown in command sources 3* CSS_ENTRY Number(5), M Position of the element; consecutive, no gaps 4 CSS_TYPE Char(1), M C command; S sequence; T textual comment (not supported by SCOS-2000); F formal parameter standing for a command, P for a sequence (future extensions) 5 CSS_ELEMID Char(8) CCF_CNAME for C, CSF_NAME for S, CSP_FPNAME for F/P, null for T. The field text still says a command element must not contain group repeaters, although sdf allows them since R4.2 (see below) 6 CSS_NPARS Number(3) Number of editable parameters (records in sdf) 7 CSS_MANDISP Char(1) Y the command needs its own manual dispatch (ARM and GO); N it is dispatched with the previous command. Null for non-first commands of a group or block N 8 CSS_RELTYPE Char(1) R release time relative to the previous command (or to its own dispatch if manually dispatched); A relative to the start of the sequence R 9 CSS_RELTIME Char(8) Delta release time hh.mm.ss (up to 23.59.59, other separators allowed). Null for a command means release as soon as possible; for a sequence, zero offset 10 CSS_EXTIME Char(17) Delta execution time [+][ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] or negative -[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm]. Null means not execution time-tagged (command) or zero offset (sequence) 11 CSS_PREVREL Char(1) R execution time relative to the previous time-tagged command; A relative to the sequence's execution start R 12 CSS_GROUP Char(1) S, M, E: start, middle, end of a group released as a batch, not interleaved with other sources 13 CSS_BLOCK Char(1) S, M, E: start, middle, end of a block aggregated into one TC segment 14 CSS_ILSCOPE Char(1) Interlock scope G, L, S, B, F, T, N; null takes CCF_ILSCOPE 15 CSS_ILSTAGE Char(1) Interlock stage R, U, O, A, C; null takes CCF_ILSTAGE 16 CSS_DYNPTV Char(1) Y override dynamic PTV (feasibility and time checks, interlocks) N 17 CSS_STAPTV Char(1) Y override static (telemetry-based) PTV N 18 CSS_CEV Char(1) Y disable command execution verification checks N

111213

Column names in this wiki's SQLite copy

The pyscos2000 schema used by this wiki's SQLite database calls field 17 CSS_STATPTV; ICD 7.0 calls it CSS_STAPTV.1335

docs.title: Release times, execution times and manual dispatch
docs.text:
Release times and execution times are computed by two parallel sets of rules. For release (CSS_RELTYPE, CSS_RELTIME):12

  • a command with R and manual dispatch is released CSS_RELTIME after the operator dispatches it;
  • a command with R and no manual dispatch is released CSS_RELTIME after the release of the previous command of the expanded top-level sequence. If the previous element is a nested sequence, that means its last command;
  • a command with A is released CSS_RELTIME after the release start time of its own sequence;
  • a nested sequence with R starts CSS_RELTIME after the last command before it; with A, after the start of the containing sequence. The start of the top-level sequence is given by the operator at load time.

Execution times (CSS_PREVREL, CSS_EXTIME) follow the same pattern relative to the previous execution time-tagged command (R) or to the execution start of the sequence (A).12 Whether the release or the execution tags are used is decided by CSF_IFTT at load time; on-board time-tagged commands are wrapped in TC(11,4) as explained on Commanding in the MIB.8

flowchart TD
    Q{"Element type"} -->|"command"| C{"CSS_RELTYPE"}
    Q -->|"nested sequence"| S{"CSS_RELTYPE"}
    C -->|"A"| CA["release = sequence start + RELTIME"]
    C -->|"R"| M{"CSS_MANDISP"}
    M -->|"Y"| CY["release = own dispatch + RELTIME"]
    M -->|"N"| CN["release = previous command's release + RELTIME<br/>(previous command of the expanded sequence)"]
    S -->|"A"| SA["start = containing sequence start + RELTIME"]
    S -->|"R"| SR["start = last command before it + RELTIME"]

The flowchart restates the field description of CSS_RELTIME.12

docs.title: Groups and blocks
docs.text: A group is released as a batch that other command sources cannot interleave. A block goes further: its commands are aggregated into a single TC segment data field.13 Appendix C of the ICD adds that such an aggregated segment is transmitted to the spacecraft as a single frame and CLTU.27 Both need at least one S and one E entry, with a configurable maximum number of M entries between them, and only the first command may carry the manual dispatch flag or a release time-tag. A block may sit inside a group but not the reverse; a block must not exceed a mission limit on its length and must not contain high-priority commands (CCF_HIPRI = Y). Inside a group or block the interlock scopes G and L are allowed only on the last command.13 Segments and frames are described in TC Space Data Link Protocol.

docs.title: sdf: values of element parameters
docs.text:
sdf has one record per editable parameter of an element and says where its value comes from when the sequence is loaded.14

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* SDF_SQNAME Char(8), M Sequence 2* SDF_ENTRY Number(5), M Element (CSS_ENTRY), of type C or S 3 SDF_ELEMID Char(8), M Element name (CSS_ELEMID) 4* SDF_POS Number(4), M For a command: bit offset of the parameter (CDF_BIT), after expansion of repeated groups. For a nested sequence: position of the sequence parameter (CSP_FPNUM) 5* SDF_PNAME Char(8), M Editable command parameter (CDF_PNAME with CDF_ELTYPE = E) or sequence parameter (CSP_FPNAME) 6 SDF_FTYPE Char(1) F fixed once loaded; E editable on the stack E 7 SDF_VTYPE Char(1), M Source of the value: R raw from SDF_VALUE; E engineering from SDF_VALUE (calibrated parameters); F from the formal parameter named in SDF_VALUE (not for group repeaters); P from the value set in SDF_VALSET; S from the nested sequence's CSP_DEFVAL; D from the command's CDF_VALUE (or CPC_DEFVAL, or telemetry for a dynamic default) 8 SDF_VALUE Char The value, or the formal parameter name for F. Command ID parameters take a fully defined command, Parameter ID parameters a PCF_NAME with on-board ID. May be null only for D, P or S 9 SDF_VALSET Char(8) Parameter value set (PSV_PVSID); mandatory for SDF_VTYPE = P 10 SDF_REPPOS Number(4) Original CDF_BIT of a parameter shifted by group expansion; mandatory when SDF_POS differs from CDF_BIT

151617

Only parameters that are editable in the command definition may appear in sdf, and the importer rejects the invalid combinations:14

CDF_ELTYPE SDF_FTYPE Result F F or E not allowed E F valid; parameter not editable in the sequence E E valid; parameter editable in the sequence F no sdf record valid; parameter not editable

Since R4.2, commands with group repeaters can be sequence elements, provided every repeater value and every repeated parameter is defined in the database. One sdf record is needed per repeated instance; with a repeater value of 3, each repeated parameter needs three records, and SDF_REPPOS maps each shifted instance back to its CDF_BIT.1415

docs.title: csp: formal parameters
docs.text:
csp has one record per formal parameter. Formal parameters are declared much like command parameters and use the same calibration and range tables; they can also be of the special kinds Command ID and Parameter ID.418

# Field Type Meaning and values Default 1* CSP_SQNAME Char(8), M Sequence 2* CSP_FPNAME Char(8), M Name, unique within the sequence 3 CSP_FPNUM Number(5), M Position, consecutive; 0–65535 since R5.0 (0–999 before) 4 CSP_DESCR Char(24) Description 5 CSP_PTC Number(2), M Parameter Type Code; must equal that of every element parameter mapped to it 6 CSP_PFC Number(5), M Parameter Format Code; same rule 7 CSP_DISPFMT Char(1) Engineering format A, I, U, R, T, D; same rule R 8 CSP_RADIX Char(1) Default radix D, H, O; may differ from the element parameters D 9 CSP_TYPE Char(1), M C command name, S sequence name (future extensions); P mapped to one or more element parameters 10 CSP_VTYPE Char(1) Representation of the default: R raw, E engineering; required for type P with a default, null for C/S 11 CSP_DEFVAL Char Default value; null means the operator must enter a value before loading 12 CSP_CATEG Char(1) C numerical, T textual calibration, A Command ID, P Parameter ID, B both (future), N none; A/P only if every mapped element parameter is of the same kind N 13 CSP_PRFREF Char(10) Range set; may differ from the element parameters, but should only be more restrictive 14 CSP_CCAREF Char(10) Numerical curve; must be the same as that of the mapped element parameters 15 CSP_PAFREF Char(10) Alias set; must be the same as that of the mapped element parameters 16 CSP_UNIT Char(4) Unit, consistent with the element parameters

181920

At issue 7.0, formal parameters standing for a command or sequence name were still not supported by SCOS-2000.4 When a sequence is loaded, only the formal parameter values are checked against their range sets, unless SCOS-2000 is configured to check every parameter of every contained command.21 Range sets, calibrations and the PTC/PFC codes are described on Commanding in the MIB and MIB parameter types.

docs.title: What happens at load time
docs.text:
Putting the rules together, loading a sequence on a manual stack goes roughly as follows.

flowchart TD
    A["Operator selects CSF_NAME<br/>(CSF_EXEC = Y)"] --> B{"CSF_IFTT"}
    B -->|"B"| B1["choose on-board or ground time-tagging"]
    B -->|"Y"| B2["enter absolute reference time"]
    B -->|"N"| C
    B1 --> C["Enter formal parameter values<br/>(CSP defaults offered, null = mandatory)"]
    B2 --> C
    C --> D["Range-check formal parameters (prf/prv)"]
    D --> E["Expand css in CSS_ENTRY order,<br/>nested sequences expanded recursively"]
    E --> F["Resolve each sdf value:<br/>R / E / F / S / D / P"]
    F --> G["Compute release and execution times,<br/>apply groups, blocks, interlocks, PTV/CEV overrides"]
    G --> H["Individual command requests on the stack<br/>(still editable, subject to FTYPE)"]

Inference

The order of the steps in this flowchart is this wiki's reconstruction from the field descriptions of csf, css, sdf, csp and prf. The ICD describes what each field means, not the algorithm of the command sources, which is specified in documents that are not among the available sources.17

docs.title: Parameter sets: pst, psv, cps, pvs, psm
docs.text:
A parameter set is a named collection of command or sequence parameters. A parameter value set is a named combination of values for the parameters of one set. Applying a value set in real time fills all its parameters at once under one high-level mnemonic. Sets and value sets can be defined for commands and for sequences.22

Table # Field Type Meaning Default pst 1* PST_NAME Char(8), M Unique name of the parameter set 2 PST_DESCR Char(24) Description psv 1 PSV_NAME Char(8), M Parameter set (PST_NAME) 2* PSV_PVSID Char(8), M Unique name of the value set 3 PSV_DESCR Char(24) Description cps 1* CPS_NAME Char(8), M Parameter set 2 CPS_PAR Char(8), M Command parameter (CDF_PNAME) or formal parameter (CSP_FPNAME) in the set 3* CPS_BIT Number(4), M CDF_BIT of a command parameter, or CSP_FPNUM of a sequence parameter pvs 1* PVS_ID Char(8), M Value set (PSV_PVSID) 2 PVS_PSID Char(8), M Parameter set (PST_NAME) 3 PVS_PNAME Char(8), M Parameter given a value 4 PVS_INTER Char(1) R raw, E engineering (calibrated parameters only) R 5 PVS_VALS Char The value; null leaves the current value unchanged 6* PVS_BIT Number(4), M CDF_BIT or CSP_FPNUM, for unique identification psm 1* PSM_NAME Char(8), M Command (CCF_CNAME) or sequence (CSF_NAME) 2* PSM_TYPE Char(1), M C command, S sequence 3* PSM_PARSET Char(8), M Parameter set (PST_NAME)

222324

A few rules tie the tables together:2324

  • cps is not used by SCOS-2000, which takes set membership from pst; the off-line database can use it to check that value sets are complete.
  • If a command parameter and a sequence parameter with the same name are both used in parameter sets, they must share PTC and display format.
  • One parameter set cannot serve both a command and a sequence, because PVS_BIT would have to be a bit offset for one and a parameter position for the other.

Commands and sequences reference a default value set through CCF_DEFSET and CSF_DEFSET, and a sequence element can take its values from a set with SDF_VTYPE = P and SDF_VALSET.917

erDiagram
    PST ||--o{ PSV : "value sets of the set"
    PST ||--o{ CPS : "members (off-line check)"
    PSV ||--|{ PVS : "values"
    PST ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_PARSET"
    CCF ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_NAME, type C"
    CSF ||--o{ PSM : "PSM_NAME, type S"
    PSV ||--o{ SDF : "SDF_VALSET"

docs.title: Overall numbers
docs.text:
The September 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB holds 3,404 sequences with 13,879 elements, 50,014 element parameter values and 10,981 formal parameters. The April 2020 release had 2,701 sequences, 9,089 elements, 30,985 values and 5,598 formal parameters.3536

Field Values found CSS_TYPE C 12,629; S 1,250; no comments or formal-parameter elements Elements per sequence 1 element: 1,773 sequences; 2: 533; 3: 263; up to 312 (AIPF981A "PHI copy cal data v06") CSF_IFTT B 3,354; N 50 CSF_PLAN N 2,029; S (SOC) 1,177; F (flight dynamics) 195; A 3 CSF_CRITICAL, CSF_EXEC N and Y in every record CSF_SUBSCHEDID set in every record (33 distinct values); CSF_SUBSYS null in 2,633 CSF_DEFSET never used CSF_DOCNAME every sequence names its source document: xx-FCP-nnn 2,243, xx-CRP-nnn 1,091, xx-SEQ-nnn 70 CSF_DATE issue dates from 2016 to 2025; 1,481 sequences carry a 2019 date Formal parameters 1,575 sequences declare at least one (CSF_NFPARS > 0) and 1,573 have csp records; maximum 217; CSF_NFPARS disagrees with csp for 3 sequences (APWC508A, APWC508B, ATCC011C)

35

Nesting is used but shallow: 467 sequences contain nested sequences, 321 distinct sequences are used as elements, and the deepest chain has three levels, for example ATCC010A "DUP_TCL_RAM_P1 v02" → ATCC007A → ATCC008A → ADMF013F.35

Inference: naming convention

Every Solar Orbiter sequence name starts with A, followed by a two-letter subsystem code, a letter for the kind of procedure (F, C or S) matching FCP, CRP or SEQ in CSF_DOCNAME, a three-digit procedure number and a variant letter: ADMF521B comes from DM-FCP-521. The only exception is ADUMMYSQ (document SY-CRP-501). 1,072 of the 1,177 SOC-plannable sequences have a second letter I, which appears to denote the instruments, and 138 of the 195 flight-dynamics-plannable sequences belong to the AC subsystem, apparently AOCS. The convention is deduced from the data; it is not documented in the available sources.35 Naming conventions in general are discussed on Mission tailoring of the MIB.

docs.title: Timing, dispatch and overrides
docs.text:
Field Values found (elements) CSS_MANDISP Y for 12,199 of the 12,629 command elements; N for 430 and for all nested sequences CSS_RELTYPE / CSS_PREVREL always equal: R 10,475; A 3,404 CSS_RELTIME most common 00.00.01 (6,658), 00.00.00 (3,181), 00.00.01.000 (962), 00.00.02 (927), 00.00.05 (714) CSS_EXTIME same pattern; null in 95 CSS_ILSCOPE / CSS_ILSTAGE N / C for 12,494 commands; N / null for 6; null (taken from ccf) for 129 commands and all sequences CSS_DYNPTV, CSS_STAPTV never overridden CSS_CEV Y in 17 elements of two TC-file definition sequences

35

The 3,404 elements with A are exactly the first entries of the 3,404 sequences: every Solar Orbiter sequence anchors its first element to the sequence start and times all others relative to the previous command.35 1,107 release times (962 of them 00.00.01.000) are written with milliseconds, always .000 and always in the same elements as a millisecond execution time; this is a 12-character form that the ICD gives for CSS_EXTIME but not for CSS_RELTIME, whose documented format is hh.mm.ss in a Char(8) field; 44 release times are null.3512 The ICD says that a field longer than its declared length is truncated on import, with a warning.25

Inference

Truncating 00.00.01.000 to 8 characters gives 00.00.01, so these values would most likely still import as the intended whole-second offsets. Whether the Solar Orbiter importer or the XML conversion for the FARC truncates them, accepts them or rejects them is not stated in the available sources.

The elements with CSS_CEV = Y are discussed on Command verification in the MIB.

docs.title: Groups and blocks
docs.text:
Blocks appear in 29 sequences and groups in 23, covering 76 elements in total.35 ADMC403A "Set RM A Program Set v11" blocks four TC(6,2) memory loads (entries 2 to 5) between two high-priority CPDU commands, ZBC04010 "RM A Disable" and ZBC04009 "RM A Enable", which stay outside the block as the ICD requires for high-priority commands.3513 ATTF100A "DST full Power mode v08" puts all six of its commands in one group that contains three blocks of two commands, the "block inside a group" case the ICD allows.3513

Entry Command Description CSS_GROUP CSS_BLOCK CSS_MANDISP 1 ZCS2Z05L Set DST Output Pwr Clamp Status SDP S S Y 2 ZCSD3403 Dst-Tx Set Clamp ON-OFF M E N 3 ZCS2Z0AF Set DST TX A Output Pwr Sel PFM M S N 4 ZCS2Z07T Dst Set Tx output power (A:PFM) M E N 5 ZCS2Z0AL Set DST TX B Output Pwr Sel FM1 M S N 6 ZCS2Z07U Dst Set Tx output power (B:FM1) E E N

35

The ICD asks for CSS_MANDISP and CSS_RELTIME to be null on every command of a group or block except the first; in the Solar Orbiter data all 46 such commands instead carry N and 00.00.00.111235

docs.title: Values of element parameters
docs.text:
Element SDF_VTYPE R E F D S Command (48,356 values) 25,071 9,529 11,428 2,328 — Nested sequence (1,658 values) 612 849 147 — 50

35

Every command parameter in sdf is editable in its cdf definition (CDF_ELTYPE = E), as the ICD requires; 44,596 stay editable after loading (SDF_FTYPE = E) and 3,760 are frozen (F).3514 No value comes from a parameter value set (P). SDF_REPPOS is filled in every record, also where it equals SDF_POS; for nested sequence elements it is 0. For command elements it differs from SDF_POS in 11,896 values of 103 commands, all but two of them instances shifted by group expansion; 234 distinct commands with group repeaters appear in 2,467 sequence elements.35

docs.title: Worked example: ADMF521B, a sequence with nesting and formal parameters
docs.text:
ADMF521B "SSMM ChngPsPrioDump v05" comes from procedure DM-FCP-521, issue 5 of 04/10/2024. It has four elements, three formal parameters, CSF_IFTT = B, is not plannable and defaults to sub-schedule 1.38

CSS_ENTRY Type Element Comment CSS_MANDISP Release Execution 1 S ADMF517A SSMM Stop PS read v02 N A 00.00.00 A 00.00.00 2 C ZSM00235 SSMM Change PS Default Priority, TC(15,139) Y R 00.00.01 R 00.00.01 3 C ZSM00185 SSMM Rep Catalogues Select Pkt Store, TC(15,12) Y R 00.00.01 R 00.00.01 4 S ADMF525A SSMM unbound PS dump v01 N R 00.00.01 R 00.00.01

38

CSP_FPNUM CSP_FPNAME Description Type Range set Default 1 XF521B01 PS Read ID (PS ID + 200) (3,4) none none 2 XF521B02 Sto PS id (3,4) VSM00011 (0–63) none 3 XF521B03 Sto priority (3,4) VSM00018 (0–15) none

38

Because no formal parameter has a default, the operator must enter all three before loading. The sdf records then distribute them:3819

Entry Element SDF_POS Parameter SDF_FTYPE / SDF_VTYPE Value 1 ADMF517A 1 XF517A01 E / F ← XF521B01 2 ZSM00235 0 PSM00230 "Sto PS id" E / F ← XF521B02 2 ZSM00235 8 PSM00268 "Sto priority" E / F ← XF521B03 3 ZSM00185 8 PSM00226 (group repeater, CDF_GRPSIZE = 2) F / R 1 3 ZSM00185 24 PSM00230 E / F ← XF521B02 4 ADMF525A 1, 2 XF525A01, XF525A02 E / F ← XF521B01, XF521B02 4 ADMF525A 3–6 XF525A03 … XF525A06 E / S defaults of ADMF525A: 1, SM VCA OBC VC3, 0, 0

38

flowchart LR
    F1(["XF521B01<br/>PS Read ID"]) --> A1["ADMF517A.XF517A01"] --> P1["ZSM00215.PSM00245"]
    F1 --> B1["ADMF525A.XF525A01"] --> Q1["ZSM00256.PSM00245"]
    F2(["XF521B02<br/>Sto PS id"]) --> P2["ZSM00235.PSM00230"]
    F2 --> P3["ZSM00185.PSM00230"]
    F2 --> B2["ADMF525A.XF525A02"] --> Q2["ZSM00256.PSM00230"]
    F3(["XF521B03<br/>Sto priority"]) --> P4["ZSM00235.PSM00268"]

The nested sequences each contain one command: ADMF517A releases ZSM00215 "SSMM Stop Downln Pkt Store" TC(15,135) and ADMF525A releases ZSM00256 "SSMM Unbounded DWL PS" TC(15,145), both with their own sdf mapping to their formal parameters.38 One value typed for XF521B02 thus lands in two command parameters directly and in a third through the nested sequence, which is the mechanism of the ICD's SQ1/SQ2 example applied to real procedures.5

ZSM00185 contains a group repeater: PSM00226 at bit 8 repeats the next two elements. Because the sequence fixes it to 1, the command can be a sequence element, and no position shifts, so SDF_POS equals CDF_BIT.3814

With CSF_IFTT = B, the operator decides at load time whether the four commands are released with the ground release offsets (the first command at the sequence start, each later one 1 s after the previous command or after its own manual dispatch) or executed on board at times derived from the execution offsets.81238

Expanded result (illustrative values)

With XF521B01 = 205, XF521B02 = 5 and XF521B03 = 2, chosen by this wiki for illustration and within the range sets, loading produces four command requests: ZSM00215 (PSM00245 = 205), ZSM00235 (PSM00230 = 5, PSM00268 = 2), ZSM00185 (PSM00226 = 1, PSM00230 = 5) and ZSM00256 (PSM00245 = 205, PSM00230 = 5, plus the fixed and default values of ADMF525A). Element parameters marked E in SDF_FTYPE remain editable on the stack; PSM00226 does not.38

docs.title: Worked example: repeated groups inside a sequence
docs.text:
AACC250B "Exit OCM after RWMai v05" uses ZCA08E01 "Enable Functional Monitoring", TC(142,1), at entry 2. In cdf, ZCA08E01 has a 16-bit counter PCD8E011 "Nb FMONs to process" at bit 0 with group size 1, followed by the 32-bit PCD8E012 "FMON Id to process" at bit 16.38

SDF_POS SDF_PNAME SDF_FTYPE / SDF_VTYPE SDF_VALUE SDF_REPPOS 0 PCD8E011 F / R 4 0 16 PCD8E012 E / R 161 16 48 PCD8E012 E / R 162 16 80 PCD8E012 E / R 163 16 112 PCD8E012 E / R 164 16

38

The counter is fixed to 4 and there is one sdf record per repeated FMON ID, at the expanded bit offsets 16, 48, 80 and 112; SDF_REPPOS = 16 maps each instance back to the single cdf definition, exactly the rule of the ICD.141538 Functional monitoring is Service 142, a Solar Orbiter private service, and TC(142,1) "Enable Functional Monitoring" is defined in the Solar Orbiter TM/TC ICD;26 see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS.

docs.title: Parameter sets on Solar Orbiter and elsewhere
docs.text:
All five parameter set tables are empty in the 2020 and 2025 Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA instrument database, and no command or sequence names a default value set.353637 The SWA database also has no sequences at all.37 The Herschel/Planck System database (HPSDB), which ingested and generated MIB files both for the SCOS-2000 based instrument EGSE and for the Central Checkout System (CCS), marked csf, css, sdf and all parameter set tables as not supported by CCS ("do not use") and left csp "to be written", while HPSDB itself could still load them, for the sequence tables "in order to interface with MOIS for operations".34 MOIS itself, the procedure preparation tool, is described on operations preparation.

Inference

Parameter sets solve a problem that Solar Orbiter's large sequence library handles differently: preset combinations are expressed as separate sequences (variant letters such as ADMC403A/ADMC403B) or as formal parameters with defaults. That this is a deliberate design choice is this wiki's reading of the data, not a statement of the sources.

SQL used

Queries ran with sqlite3 -readonly on this wiki's SQLite copy of the Solar Orbiter MIB (solo-2025-09-16.sqlite; solo-2020-04-16.sqlite and swa-idb.sqlite for comparisons). All columns are stored as text, so counts and comparisons use cast(... as int).

SELECT count(*) FROM csf; SELECT count(*) FROM css; SELECT count(*) FROM sdf; SELECT count(*) FROM csp;
SELECT CSF_IFTT, count(*) FROM csf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT CSF_PLAN, substr(CSF_NAME, 2, 2), count(*) FROM csf GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT substr(CSF_DOCNAME, 4, 3), count(*) FROM csf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT n, count(*) FROM (SELECT CSS_SQNAME, count(*) AS n FROM css GROUP BY 1) GROUP BY n;
-- consistency of the counters
SELECT sum(cast(CSF_ELEMS AS int) <> (SELECT count(*) FROM css WHERE CSS_SQNAME = CSF_NAME)),
       sum(cast(CSF_NFPARS AS int) <> (SELECT count(*) FROM csp WHERE CSP_SQNAME = CSF_NAME)) FROM csf;
-- nesting depth
WITH RECURSIVE r(top, cur, depth) AS (
  SELECT CSF_NAME, CSF_NAME, 0 FROM csf
  UNION ALL SELECT r.top, s.CSS_ELEMID, r.depth + 1 FROM r
    JOIN css s ON s.CSS_SQNAME = r.cur AND s.CSS_TYPE = 'S' WHERE r.depth < 10)
SELECT max(depth) FROM r;
-- timing, groups, blocks, overrides
SELECT CSS_MANDISP, CSS_RELTYPE, CSS_PREVREL, count(*) FROM css GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;
SELECT CSS_RELTIME, count(*) FROM css GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT CSS_GROUP, CSS_BLOCK, count(*) FROM css GROUP BY 1, 2;
-- value sources by element type
SELECT s.SDF_VTYPE, e.CSS_TYPE, count(*) FROM sdf s
  JOIN css e ON e.CSS_SQNAME = s.SDF_SQNAME AND e.CSS_ENTRY = s.SDF_ENTRY GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT d.CDF_ELTYPE, s.SDF_FTYPE, count(*) FROM sdf s
  JOIN css e ON e.CSS_SQNAME = s.SDF_SQNAME AND e.CSS_ENTRY = s.SDF_ENTRY AND e.CSS_TYPE = 'C'
  JOIN cdf d ON d.CDF_CNAME = s.SDF_ELEMID AND d.CDF_PNAME = s.SDF_PNAME AND d.CDF_BIT = s.SDF_REPPOS
 GROUP BY 1, 2;
-- worked examples
SELECT * FROM css WHERE CSS_SQNAME = 'ADMF521B' ORDER BY cast(CSS_ENTRY AS int);
SELECT * FROM sdf WHERE SDF_SQNAME = 'ADMF521B' ORDER BY cast(SDF_ENTRY AS int), cast(SDF_POS AS int);
SELECT * FROM csp WHERE CSP_SQNAME IN ('ADMF521B', 'ADMF525A') ORDER BY 1, cast(CSP_FPNUM AS int);
SELECT * FROM sdf WHERE SDF_SQNAME = 'AACC250B' AND SDF_ELEMID = 'ZCA08E01';
-- parameter sets
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM pst), (SELECT count(*) FROM psv), (SELECT count(*) FROM cps),
       (SELECT count(*) FROM pvs), (SELECT count(*) FROM psm);
