docs.title: The project requirement: one common satellite database
docs.text: The Herschel/Planck Operations Interface Requirements Document (OIRD) sets the frame. The prime contractor and the instrument developers deliver a Satellite Database (SDB) that defines all telemetry, telecommands, command sequences and software parameters, the instrument parts being provided by the principal investigators. It must be a single common database for system engineering, AIV and operations, comply with the SCOS-2000 Import ICD issue 5.1 (the OIRD's AD-8),4 be internally consistent and consistent with the flight dynamics database and on-board software, contain no irrelevant data and no duplications, and record every update down to field level.1213 Deliveries are scheduled from version 0 (instrument AVM) to a pre-launch update one month before launch, as Oracle data files, each with a configuration control file and the on-board software versions it matches.13 For naming, the OIRD defers to the project naming convention H-P-1-ASPI-SP-0141.14

docs.title: The packet rules: the PS-ICD narrows the parameter types
docs.text:
Before any MIB rule, the Packet Structure ICD (SCI-PT-ICD-07527, issue 6.0 of January 2008) fixes what may appear in a packet at all: the space and ground segments support "all and only" the structures and services it defines, and packets may use only the parameter types of its Appendix 6.6768 That appendix is a subset of what the SCOS-2000 import ICD accepts, so every packet field described in a Herschel/Planck MIB had to use a PTC/PFC pair from this list (field meanings as on MIB parameter types):6869

PTC Type PFC allowed by the PS-ICD Restriction compared with the MIB 1 Boolean 0 - 2 Enumerated 1 to 8, 12, 16, 32 bits Other widths up to 32 bits excluded 3, 4 Unsigned, signed integer 0 to 14 (4 to 15 bits, 2, 3 or 4 octets) No 48- or 64-bit integers 5 Real 1 (IEEE single), 2 (IEEE double) MIL-STD-1750A formats excluded; PFC 3 was removed in issue 6.0 6 Bit string 1, 2, 4, 8 bits Other widths excluded 7 Octet string 0 (variable) or n octets Not editable by the operator when used in a TC 8 Character string 0 or n characters On board only for the PROM software version identifier (allowed since issue 6.draftA); free for SCOE/EGSE 9 Absolute time 17 (CUC, 4 octets coarse, 2 fine) Only one time format 10 Relative time - Not used 11 Deduced 0 Used for OBCP parameters in TM(18,13)

The right-hand column is this wiki's comparison with the MIB ICD; the PS-ICD values are from Appendix 6 and its change record.6869707174 The PS-ICD also reserves the APIDs 2016 to 2046 for SCOE and EGSE messages and 2047 for idle packets, and gives every instrument a base APID whose four low bits separate packet categories and prime from redundant units (HIFI: 1024 prime, 1025 redundant, 1026/1027 non-essential HK, 1028-1031 science).7273 By this wiki's reading, a MIB built for these rules therefore has many pid rows per instrument that differ only in the low bits of PID_APID; the PS-ICD does not discuss the MIB.

The PS-ICD type set against a later mission (real data, Solar Orbiter 2025)

Applied to the Solar Orbiter MIB of 16 September 2025, the Herschel/Planck type set would accept 124 203 of the 126 745 monitoring parameters. The other 2 542 use enumerations of other widths (250, for example 224 of 18 bits), bit strings of 3, 5, 6, 7, 11 or more bits (124), absolute times other than PFC 17 (2 119, of which 2 116 are PTC 9 PFC 15), relative times (47) and PTC 13 (2). All its reals are IEEE (PFC 1 or 2), and 120 parameters are character strings, among them software version strings such as NIC0A000 (FSW_VERSION_STR). Of the 7 155 command parameters, 40 fall outside the set (4 enumerated, 35 absolute time, 1 relative time).116

Inference

This is a comparison, not a judgement: Solar Orbiter has its own packet rules, and its choice of other PFC values is not an error. The comparison only shows how much narrower the Herschel/Planck packet rules were than the import ICD, and therefore than what a generic MIB tool must support.

docs.title: Alcatel faxes of 2003: identifier limits and reserved ranges
docs.text:
The Herschel Planck project office of Alcatel Space Industries (Cannes) sent two faxes to the five instrument teams, copied to ESTEC and ESOC, under the subject "SCOS – Limitation to naming convention". Their stated aim is to support a "smooth transition" from instrument-level to module-level testing.1518

H-P-ASP-LT-2607, 27 January 2003 sets five requirements:1617

# Requirement Justification given 1 Calibration curve identifiers limited to Number(3) the ICD (issue 5.1) allows Number(4); the naming convention defines a curve identifier at theoretical element level as "IDIN03F" 2 Range set identifiers limited to Number(3) same reasoning 3 Command verification stage identifiers limited to Number(4) the ICD allows Number(5); the convention defines "IDIN04F" 4 Dynamic UDCs allocated in fixed ranges of the single "constant packet" in the PLF the constant packet is unique, so allocations would overlap at integration 5 The SPID of the constant packet must support 1,024 octets every level produces the same archive format, at the cost of disk space at instrument level

The UDC allocation of requirement 4 partitions the constant packet as follows:17

Range Herschel Planck 0000–0099 System System 0100–0199 SVM SVM 0200–0299 PLM PLM 0300–0399 HIFI HFI 0400–0499 PACS LFI 0500–0599 HIFI (sic; SPIRE expected) not used ("Sorbtion cooler ?") 0600–1023 spare, allocated by ASP spare, allocated by ASP

A typo in the source

The fax's text layer really assigns 0500–0599 on Herschel to "HIFI" a second time (PDF p. 2).17 Since HIFI already holds 0300–0399 and SPIRE is the only Herschel instrument without a range, the second entry probably means SPIRE. This is this wiki's reading; no corrected version of the fax is in the library.

H-P-ASP-LT-2905, 27 March 2003 adds two requirements to those of the January fax. This fax is a scan without a text layer; its content here is summarised from the manual reading recorded in this wiki's library entry, which this review re-checked against the scanned page images. It numbers its requirements 5 and 6, so both faxes have a requirement 5.18

  • Requirement 5: in the pid table, PID_SPID must equal PID_TPSD. The justification is "only to facilitate the mapping" between the Herschel/Planck System Database (HPSDB) and the SCOS "bridge" files: different SCOS packets will no longer be able to address the same variable packet structure definition.18
  • Requirement 6: in the pcf table, the field printed "PCF-WIDTH" "shall not be set to 'Null'". The justification (where the field is printed "PCF_WIDFT") is that it is "(indirectly) redundant with VPD_OFFSET" and that HPSDB will only support VPD_OFFSET.18

Inference

The scan does say "shall not be set to 'Null'"; the manual reading did not invert it. The rule nevertheless sits oddly with its own justification and with the HPSDB processing note of 2006, which ignores PCF_WIDTH on input, forces it to null on output and says only VPD_OFFSET is used.45 Either the fax itself contains a slip (a rule that the field "shall be set to Null" would match its justification), or the project reversed the rule between 2003 and 2006. The available sources do not say which.

docs.title: SPIRE's MIB naming convention
docs.text:
SPIRE's technical note SPIRE-RAL-NOT-001155 (issue 1.2, 11 March 2002) applies the project naming convention to the SPIRE MIB, including the parameters of the SPIRE EGSE and test equipment, which are not delivered with the instrument. It calls the MIB the "Mission Implementation Base".19

Item ICD fields Pattern Convention ref. Command CCF_CNAME, CDF_CNAME, PTV_CNAME SCiiippp 4580 Command parameter CPC_PNAME, CDF_PNAME SPiiippp 5130 Command numerical / textual calibration CCA_NUMBR, CCS_NUMBR / PAF_NUMBR, PAS_NUMBR tttnnnrrr (alternative sss) 5370 Monitor packet PID_SPID, TPCF_SPID, PLF_SPID tttnnnnppp 4380 Monitor parameter PCF_NAME, OCF_NAME, OCP_NAME, PLF_NAME, PTV_PARNAM SMiiippp 5130 Numerical, textual, polynomial calibration CAF_NUMBR, TXF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT (and detail tables) tttnnnrrr (sss) 5370 Alphanumeric, graphical, scrolling display DPF_NUMBE, GPF_NUMBE, SPF_NUMBE SAiiippp, SGiiippp, SLiiippp 6100, 6110, 6130

Patterns from the note.20 The components are:21

  • iii, the theoretical parameter identifier: first character the subsystem ID, third character the parameter unit ID.
  • nnn/nnnn, running numbers from zero; ttt, the system element number; rrr, the real element number; ppp, the position identifier; sss, an alternative identifier for calibration curves in case SCOS-2000 cannot handle 8-character names.
  • System element numbers: OBS 480, DPU 490, DCU 500, MCU 510, SCU 520, EGSE 528, test facility (TFCS) 529, each with its subsystem letters (for example SCU: C calibrator, H heater, K sub-K, T temperature).21
  • Real element numbers start at 100 (AVM), 300 (QM), 500 (FM) and 700 (FS) and increase by one for each new configuration, so a data set records which hardware build it describes.22
  • Unit IDs: A current, B limit, E error, F status flag, H frequency, K temperature, L lower limit, M mode, N count, P position, R phase, S speed, T time, U upper limit, V voltage, W power.2223

Note that the leading S identifies SPIRE. The HCSS comments explain that instrument-related mnemonics start with H, P and S, and during instrument-level tests with I, O and Q.35

docs.title: The HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note
docs.text:
The Herschel Common Science System (HCSS) used the MIB to build instrument commands and to interpret downlinked data for quick-look and interactive analysis. The HSC note HSC/DOC/0300 (issue 1.5, 21 December 2004), approved by the HSC and the three Herschel instrument teams, specifies the MIB interface into the HCSS. It clarifies the ICD (issue 5.2) and the naming convention (issue 2.1), adds Herschel constraints, and lists the checks of the HCSS MIB ingestion software.242527

Clarifications of the ICD. Three of them (4.1.4, 4.1.6 and 4.1.7) correspond to Document Change Requests that ESOC raised against the ICD (DCR 286, 309 and 308):2837

Point Clarification 4.1.1 A line is one record, ended by LF (Unix) or CR LF (Windows). A record has N−1 tabs for N fields. Trailing fields that SCOS-2000 ignores (grey in the ICD) may be left out. 4.1.2 Mandatory fields must hold a value of the right type, and numeric fields must not be empty or blank. 4.1.3 A non-mandatory field without a stated default defaults to 0, 0.0 or the empty string. 4.1.4 The separator must always be present even when the value is empty (DCR-286). 4.1.5 An out-of-limits condition is raised only strictly below the low or above the high limit, for hard and soft limits. 4.1.6 PLF_OFFBY/PLF_OFFBI count from the end of the SCOS-2000 packet header, which equals the start of the TM source packet header with the generic packetiser (DCR-309). 4.1.7 Bit 0 of PLF_OFFBI is the most significant bit (DCR-308). 4.1.8 Real numbers use the decimal point, not a comma.

Naming clarifications. Of the naming convention, only NMCVT-0100-C (identifiers) and NMCVT-7600-C (descriptions) affect ingestion. NMCVT-0100-C forbids I, O and Q as leading characters. NMCVT-7600-C limits descriptions to letters, digits, space, +, - and _, asks for meaningful text and understandable abbreviations, and forbids an empty short description.29 For the HCSS the short description must match [a-zA-Z0-9_]+, because the scripting language of the Common Uplink System (CUS) cannot use + or -. The combination of the first character of the name and the full description must be unique for commands, command parameters and monitoring parameters, and PID_APID with PID_DESCR must be unique for packets.3236

Constraints for the final interface:3031

Point Herschel constraint 5.1 All ICD tables in one directory; synthetic definitions accepted in subdirectory synthetic; everything else ignored. An extra two-field table gives each command's duration for the CUS. 5.2.3 VDF ignored. 5.2.4 Constants (PCF_NATUR = C) ignored; all other natures accepted. 5.2.5 The SPID is the only key to a parameter's location; a packet is identified by type, subtype, APID and, where relevant, SID; one SPID per packet type is assumed. 5.2.6 A PID row may not give a SID value greater than 0 when the matching PIC row says no SID (PIC_PI1_OFF = -1). 5.2.7 Except pseudo commands starting with Z, every CCF_PKTID must have at least 4 PCDF rows (version, type, data field header flag, APID). The note observes that this contradicts the ICD's statement that PCDF_TCNAME is unique. 5.2.9 CDF_CNAME + CDF_PNAME unique; repeated groups instead of repeated parameters. 5.2.10–11 Command sequences (CSF, CSS, SDF, CSP) and parameter sets (PST, PSV, CPS, PVS) ignored. 5.2.12–13 TXP_FROM ≤ TXP_TO, and textual calibration ranges must not overlap.

Software version 0.2 was stricter: only R parameters, so no synthetics; only OCF_CODIN values R and I; no variable packets; and for engineering command parameters no raw default value.33

Checks. Section 7 numbers the checks of the ingestion software from 7.0.1 to 7.0.34 (7.0.6 is marked "check removed"), and marks those not yet in version 0.2 as "To be implemented", for example the validation of synthetic and variable packet definitions. Examples: input file names, field counts per line, field types (with a null value assigned on mismatch), non-R natures flagged with an assumed length of −1, missing calibrations, uniqueness of PCF_NAME, OCF_NAME, CPC_PNAME and CCF_CNAME, the description rules above, TXP range order and overlap, consistency of numerical and textual de-calibrations, CPC_RADIX limited to D, H and O, and PID_INTER allowed only for periodic (3,25) packets.34

SPID uniqueness. Section 10 records an e-mail exchange of September 2002. PACS reported that all its TC verification packets shared SPID 10006, because the SCOS-2000 version of the time did not allow a range of SPIDs for packet type 1. ESOC confirmed that all TM packets of type 1 with a given subtype had to share one SPID, because the Verifier listened only to a predefined list of SPIDs. Rosetta had implemented a change allowing any SPID for service 1 and CryoSat one allowing a range of SPIDs, and these were to be merged into release 3.1 by a function that reads all type-1 SPIDs from pid.dat.38 See Command verification in the MIB.

docs.title: HPSDB: how the system database processed MIB files
docs.text:
Alcatel Alenia Space's note H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060 (issue 1, February 2006) documents how HPSDB ingests SCOS-2000 (instrument EGSE, ICD 5.1) and CCS MIB files and regenerates them as "bridge files". Constraints in bold in the note cannot be checked by HPSDB and are the user's responsibility. The note warns that 100% round-trip compatibility cannot always be reached. For example, HPSDB allows an N-to-1 relation between TM packets and SPIDs, while the ICD allows N-to-N.40

Rule Content G1 object data model MIB data is wrapped in objects identified by identifier and position; every (object, generic object) pair must be consistent. G2 naming First letter of a character identifier gives the item type; curves are Number(6) (3 digits theoretical element + 3 free); subsystem letter prefixed and 3-digit position appended at instantiation; generic items use subsystem G, number 07, position 000. G3–G5 short S2K identifiers S2K curves Number(3) for specific and 1xxx for generic curves (G000xxx000); verification stages Number(4)/1xxxx; range sets Number(3)/1xxx. G6 enumerations Enumerated values limited to the HPSDB sets, possibly narrower than the ICD (e.g. type/subtype pairs from the packet structure ICD, no octal radix). G7 commutation HPSDB models packets as structures with repetition and super-commutation attributes; a packet can be fixed (PLF), variable (VPD) or both; SPID-to-variable-packet must be one to one. G8 defaults Defaults are always forced, sometimes with HPSDB values instead of ICD ones (e.g. PID_CHECK). G9 commonality Curves may be shared by TM and TC inside HPSDB; do not use the same identifier for a TM and a TC curve. G10 category flag 8-bit user-category flag per item (AIT, operations, software, flight dynamics); set to "all except FDD" on loading. G11 common fields 64-character mnemonic, 256-character long description and configuration data (user, date, reason, source, site, validation dates) per item, not supported by S2K and CCS. G12 TC header TC packet headers are generic; TCP, PCPC and PCDF are ignored on loading. G13 reserved characters <, >, quote, double quote and & never used (XML); restricted character set for short descriptions. G14 radix No octal radix for unsigned integers. G15 ranges Respect the range allocations of the naming convention (PID numbers, UDC location). G16 instantiation Last character of the short description, APID, PID, UDC and MISC positions computed from the element's position; keep one character of description spare. G17 descriptions All descriptions mandatory; an empty one is replaced by the identifier. G18 orphans Orphan items are not loaded. G19 sorting Output sorted by the ICD primary key; inputs must be sorted too. G20 derived parameters Expression files delivered with the MIB files.

Rules from §4 of the note.424344 The field-by-field part (§5) adds, among others: PCF_WIDTH ignored and forced to null; PID_TPSD forced to the SPID for variable packets and to −1 otherwise; PID_VALID and PID_TIME forced to Y; the PIC table taken from generic data, identical on every Herschel/Planck SCOS and CCS system; VPD choice fields forced to N; printout tables not allowed; command sequences and parameter sets "not supported by CCS"; and CCS-only tables for conditional curves (CUR), groups (GRP, GRPA, GRPK), SCOE definitions (SCO) and TC/TM distribution (TCD, TMD).4546474849

docs.title: Loading MIB files into HPSDB: the configuration files
docs.text:
GMV's HPSDB Software User Manual (version 2.6, September 2005) shows how a plain SCOS-2000 MIB was fitted into that object model. The user zips the bridge files with six configuration files, which supply what the import ICD has no field for:101102

File Fields What it adds to the MIB S2K_EL.txt Real element identifier (Char(14)), theoretical element number (Number(3)), SW or HW, description, product tree identifier Which physical units the data belong to; two redundant real elements share one theoretical element S2K_SUB.txt First line: subsystem identifier (Char(7)), description, pseudo position, pseudo element number; then per position: ACC and CDMU bus-controller flags, real element, SCOE host and port Where each element sits in the subsystem S2K_TM.txt A naming-convention TM packet identifier (Char(20)) followed by the 16 fields of pid.dat A project name for every packet; HPSDB reads packets from this file instead of pid.dat S2K_CUR.txt, S2K_CVS.txt, S2K_PRF.txt SCOS number and naming-convention identifier Maps short SCOS curve, verification stage and range set numbers (limited to 999, 9999 and 9999) to generic HPSDB items

The manual's example lines map three HIFI elements to positions 190, 191 and 194 and two SPIRE elements to positions 196 and 197 of subsystem H001001 (pseudo position 289), and the curves 900, 901 and 905 to the generic curves 000900, 000901 and 000905.103 The loader creates neither box types nor generic items, requires the OL expression files of derived parameters, and is explicitly "not a SCOS bridge file validator".101 Each user has one category flag code (Operations, OB for on-board software, AIT, or All), and bridge files can be generated for one category; the 2008 Herschel delivery to ASED for the Herschel IRR was generated with the "AIT User" filter.100104106

Two descriptions of the generic items

The processing note of 2006 codes a generic S2K curve as 1xxx, standing for the HPSDB curve G000xxx000 (rule G3), while the user manual of 2005 maps generic curves through S2K_CUR.txt, with SCOS numbers below 1000. The user manual also lists four category codes without flight dynamics, where rule G10 of the note names AIT, operations, software and flight dynamics.42102100 Which variant the deliveries used is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: The CCS External ICD: extending ICD 5.1 for checkout
docs.text:
The Herschel/Planck Central Checkout System read HPSDB "bridge files" in the format of the SCOS-2000 import ICD issue 5.1, which Terma's CCS External ICD (H-P-4-TE-ID-8020, issue 1.8 of 18 January 2006) declares fully applicable "with the explicit exceptions and additions" listed in its chapter 9.8182 Unlike the documents above, it extends the MIB rather than narrowing it:

Change (CCS ICD section) Tables Content Danger actions (§9.1) none A parameter beyond its danger limits starts the test sequence danger_<parname> (case sensitive) Delta limits (§9.2) ocp New OCP_TYPE 'D', with the delta in OCP_LVALU; the type list is S soft, H hard, D delta, C status consistency (needs PCF_USCON 'Y'), E event generation only Calibration selection (§9.3) pcf, new cur PCF_CURTX must be null when a selection exists; cur (CUR_PNAME, CUR_POS, CUR_RLCHK, CUR_VALPAR, CUR_SELECT), sorted by name and position, first match wins; only integer parameters may select Groups (§9.4) new grp, grpa, grpk Named parameter groups ('PA') or packet groups ('PK') built from existing parameters or SPIDs System parameters (§9.5) pcf, pid No parameter name may start with VAR, GVAR or $ (OL syntax) or with YZ; SPIDs 100 to 999 reserved for internal EGSE use EGSE and SCOEs (§9.6-9.8) new sco, tcd, tmd Equipment name, host and port; TC distribution to equipment by APID; TM distribution by SPID Extrapolation (§9.3.1, §9.9) pcf, caf PCF_INTER ignored by the HPCCS; new CAF_INTER 'P' (extrapolate from the two end points) or 'F' (invalid value, default) ECP 1 (§9.10) calibration, range set and verification tables Curve and range set identifiers from Number(4) to Char(10); CVS_ID from Number(5) to Number(10), range 0 to 2147483647 ECP 3 (§9.10.19) new lgf Logarithmic curve, \(Y = 1/(A_0 + A_1 \ln X + A_2 \ln^2 X + A_3 \ln^3 X + A_4 \ln^4 X)\) ECP 9 to 12 (§9.11) ccf, csf CCF_SUBSCHEDID and CSF_SUBSCHEDID: default on-board sub-schedule, 1 to 65535 "although the full range is not permitted" (see the PS-ICD)

Sources: §8-9.13 and the change record.848586878889919280 Issue 1.4 (May 2003) moved the extrapolation flag from pcf to caf; the note kept under PCF_INTER describes the problem with a per-parameter flag (the ICD does not say that it was the reason for the move): SCOS-2000 attaches the flag to the calibration curve, so parameters sharing a curve would all display with the flag of the last one imported.8085 It also overrules the ICD rule that calibrated limits (OCF_INTER 'C') need a PCF_CURTX: with a calibration selection that field may stay null.85

Inconsistencies as printed

Two details of the CCS ICD do not agree with themselves. The text of ECP 3 gives a second-order formula, \(T(R) = 1/[a_0 + a_1 \ln R + a_2 (\ln R)^2]\), while the lgf table has five coefficients up to the fourth power. And ECP 1 widens range set identifiers to Char(10), but the modified prf, prv and cpc/csp reference fields are printed as Char(8).8990

Most of these extensions returned to the standard import ICD as the Herschel/Planck "Check Out System functionalities repatriation" of ICD version 6.0 (the default sub-schedule ID came into the same version through the Cryosat repatriation, and CAF_INTER was documented only later, under S2K-SPR-4911), while sco, tcd and tmd do not (see History of the Database Import ICD).781181 The checkout system also returns a file to the HPSDB: an update file with one tab-separated line per telecommand (c) or parameter (p) validated by a test sequence, giving time, name, sequence name and issue and host, to be read together with the MIB issue in vdf.dat.83 The tcd configuration printed in a Herschel release note of 2008 sends APID 0 and the CDMS, ACMS and instrument APIDs (16, 512, 1024, 1152, 1280) to the TM/TC front end and ten EGSE APIDs between 2017 and 2044 to their own equipment.107

The CCS rules against a later mission (real data, Solar Orbiter 2025)

In the Solar Orbiter MIB of September 2025 no parameter name starts with VAR, GVAR, $ or YZ. Its 1 974 cur rows use 52 different selector parameters (CUR_RLCHK): 40 Booleans (PTC 1, 112 rows), 8 enumerations (PTC 2, 1 834 rows) and 4 unsigned integers (PTC 3, 28 rows), all unsigned integers in SCOS-2000's internal representation, so the CCS rule that only integer parameters select a calibration, which ICD 7.0 also states, holds. CUR_POS goes up to 12 and the largest CUR_VALPAR is 420.1177574 Its dst table, the standard ICD's own command routing, has a single row (see SCOS-2000 as EGSE).117

docs.title: One identifier, several widths
docs.text:
The same identifiers were given different widths by each layer of the Herschel/Planck chain:

Identifier ICD 5.1 (2001) Alcatel fax (Jan 2003), instrument S2K files HPSDB note (2006), S2K files CCS External ICD (ECP 1, 2003) ICD 7.0 (2017) Calibration curves (CAF_NUMBR, TXF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT, ...) Number(4) Number(3) Number(3) specific, 1xxx generic Char(10) Char(10) Parameter range sets (PRF_NUMBR) Number(4) Number(3) Number(3) specific, 1xxx generic Char(10) (but Char(8) in the field tables) Char(10) Verification stages (CVS_ID) Number(5) Number(4) Number(4) specific, 1xxxx generic Number(10) Number(5), 0 to 32767

Sources per column.7916428976 ICD 7.0's change history explains its last column: version 6.0 widened CVS_ID from NUM(5) to NUM(8) with the Herschel/Planck repatriation, and a later change request, S2K-DCR-3909 (listed among the clarifications of ICD 6.7, with the matching Number(5) length of CVE_CVSID and CVP_CVSID in ICD 6.9), restricted it to a signed short integer.7877 Inside HPSDB a curve was a Number(6), three digits of theoretical element number and three free digits.42 The HIFI MIB of 2008 shows the instrument side: its textual calibrations, numerical calibrations and command calibrations are numbered with three digits (for example 249, 293 and 134).112

Inference

The widths fit together if the short numbers belong to the instrument S2K files and the character identifiers to the CCS files that HPSDB generated from its own Number(6) and naming-convention identifiers. No source states this division of labour explicitly.

docs.title: Naming the EGSE, and real names decoded
docs.text:
The EGSE Interface Requirement Specification (H-P-1-ASPI-IS-0121, issue 4.1, December 2004) applies the naming convention to the test equipment, so that SCOE commands and monitoring can live in the same database as the spacecraft. Its rules:969795

  • the EGSE subsystem letter is Y, written as the number 25 (Y being the 25th letter) in remote monitoring packet names;
  • each EGSE item owns a range of positions: ACMS SCOE 920-939, CCS 940-941, PLM SCOE 942-943, CDMU DFE 944-945, TM/TC DFE 946-947, CDMU SCOE 948-949, TT&C SCOE 950-951, LPS 952-953, SAS 954-955, BATSIM 956-957, cryo SCOE 958-959, cryo COTE 960-961, HIFI 962-963, PACS 964-965, SPIRE 966-967, HFI 968-969, LFI 970-971;
  • remote command names are YC + three-character function + position, their parameters YP + function + position, remote monitoring parameters YM + function + position; remote monitoring packet identifiers combine the subsystem number 25, the position allocation and a four-digit element packet number whose first three digits repeat the position (this last rule does not apply to the cryo SCOE);
  • identifiers may use only the digits, the underscore and the upper-case letters except I, O and Q;
  • every SCOE subcontractor supplies its remote command and monitoring definitions (mnemonic, PTC, PFC, position in the packet, descriptions, calibration) in tables that can be loaded into the HPSDB.

The rule against I, O and Q is stricter than NMCVT-0100-C as the HCSS note reports it (those letters forbidden only as the first character, because the instrument centres used them for their EGSE-ILT parameters).2935 The Herschel release note of 2008 shows the EGSE subsystem as delivered: Y104 EGSE at model position 989, with elements such as 940 CCS, 946 TMTCDFE, 948 CDMUSCOE and 962, 964 and 966 for the instrument EGSEs.108

The same note gives the positions of the instrument elements, which explain the endings of the names in the printed HIFI MIB (issue 139, July 2008):108109

Name in the HIFI MIB Mnemonic Ending Element at that position in model HERSCH_FM9 HM009190 HI_Prime_red 190 HIFI_ICU_N HP056191 HIF_ch1_mxbias0_V 191 HIFI_FCU_N HM001193 HI_WBSV_S 193 HIFI_WBS_N HM000194 HI_LCU_S 194 HIFI_LCU_N HP001197 HIFI_BB_ID 197 HIFI_OBS_N

The names come from the annex's parameter lists and packet layouts.111110114113

Inference

Reading the names as subsystem letter (H), item-type letter (M monitoring parameter, P command parameter, D for names such as HD111190 HIFI_ptv_input), three free characters and the element position is this wiki's application of HPSDB rule G2 and of the EGSE pattern above; the HIFI documents do not explain their names. Thales Alenia Space's 2015 slides on the successor database list A TM packet, C curve, D synthetic parameter, G group, K constant and M TM parameter as item letters.42115 The SPIRE convention (SMiiippp, SPiiippp, SCiiippp) follows the same shape with the instrument letter S.

docs.title: The minimum EGSE data set
docs.text: The SCOS-2000 EGSE delivered to the instrument teams shipped with a minimum MIB, MIN_EGSE, that every mission had to adapt: its own TC packet header in tcp.dat, pcdf.dat and pcpc.dat, the ZLOADTT and ZBINTC commands, and the TM header related displays and parameters. All names in MIN_EGSE start with Z, and SPIDs 1 to 100 are reserved for the generic EGSE setup. A mergeDATA facility merges MIN_EGSE with instrument data sets into a new MIB directory.5051 See SCOS-2000 as EGSE.

docs.title: Configuration control at SPIRE
docs.text:
SPIRE's note on database management and CUS configuration control (issue 1.0, February 2007) shows the other half of tailoring, namely how a validated MIB is kept traceable in tests. The rationale is to know, at any later time, which version of which script produced a given set of telemetry.53 The steps for a new test database are: create a Versant database, create a mission configuration (config1), ingest the MIB with ingestmib under a user label, load calibration tables, import the CUS definitions, set the initial observation ID and create an instrument model for the configuration.54 Ingestion runs semantic checks and writes mibchecker.log. Serious problems stop the ingestion, while minor ones are only logged.55

Scripts are tagged in CVS as LABEL_CONFIGN, for example AVM_TEST_CONFIG6. During a test, changes are tracked only by the database's automatic versions (a CVS version 1.2 becomes 1.2.1 on ingestion), and the results are checked back into CVS afterwards. A new configuration freezes a snapshot of definitions and calibration tables.56 A calibration table TestSetup.txt with the keys configuration, environment (moc, ilt, hsc, ist, par), test type, prime or redundant instrument, thermal condition and debug level lets the same CUS definitions serve every test environment.57

docs.title: Solar Orbiter: tables beyond the ICD
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter MIB releases contain the 53 ICD tables plus extra files that the ICD does not define. The September 2025 release has six, ASW_sw_para.dat, pcf_glob_det.dat, dup.dat, s13a.dat, s13p.dat and s13t.dat, and the April 2020 release has the first three. The SWA instrument database has pcf_glob_det.dat, sw_para.dat and an empty ssy.dat.585960 No document in the library describes these files, so everything below is deduced from their contents.

File 2020 rows 2025 rows Columns Deduced role ASW_sw_para.dat 85,430 105,222 3 long software names and descriptions for MIB identifiers pcf_glob_det.dat 52,417 56,631 3 bit position of each "detail" parameter inside a "global" parameter dup.dat 36 69 2 packets to be re-identified under a second APID s13a.dat – 7 6 file attribute (content type) codes s13p.dat – 11 6 on-board file partitions s13t.dat – 12 7 file types, linking an attribute and a default partition

Counts from this wiki's queries.5859

Inference

All interpretations in this section are deduced from column contents and cross-table matches. The ICD does not define these files, and the Solar Orbiter documents in the library do not mention them. They may be consumed by mission-specific tools rather than by the SCOS-2000 importer.

docs.title: ASW_sw_para: software names and long descriptions
docs.text:
Each row holds an identifier, a software-level name and a description of up to 255 characters. The identifiers are unique and cover every kind of MIB object: 77,565 are monitoring parameters (PCF_NAME), 3,676 command parameters (CPC_PNAME), 2,221 commands (CCF_CNAME), 7,665 TM packet mnemonics (TPCF_NAME), 208 textual calibrations, 130 command textual calibrations and 77 range sets. 13,727 identifiers starting with B match no ICD table.61

Identifier Second column Third column (truncated) Matches NAH7Z002 NAH7Z002 "[Clone of NAHD0000] HGA-APME A Mode" PCF_NAME PCA8B021 PTC_GET_N_PARAM "Maximum value is (-1)/4" CPC_PNAME ZAHG0000 ZAHG0000 "This TC sends one 1553 command to the HGA-APME A …" CCF_CNAME YCA00101 TMA_TCACK_ACC_SUCCESS "This telemetry is the report generated when a TC is successfully received …" TPCF_NAME CCDT0001TX AOCS_PROFILE_ID "AOCS profiles" TXF_NUMBR VCD00147 Z_IDINT0TO1 "Integer between 0 and 1" PRF_NUMBR BCAY0002 AOCSCORE_STRUNITA_QUAT_LSB (empty) none

Real rows from the release.61

Inference

The file looks like the place where Solar Orbiter keeps what the ICD has no field for: the long, software-level mnemonic of each item (up to 122 characters in the second column) and a long description (up to 255 characters), much like the 64-character mnemonic and 256-character long description that HPSDB stored for every item but could not export to SCOS-2000.42 The B identifiers, with names such as AOCSCORE_STRUNITA_QUAT_LSB, look like on-board software constants that have no MIB table. The SWA database's sw_para.dat holds 2,841 identifiers in a differently filled layout (empty second column).60

docs.title: pcf_glob_det: detail parameters inside global parameters
docs.text:
Each of the 56,631 rows names a global parameter, a detail parameter and a number. All names are PCF parameters, each detail belongs to exactly one global, and there are 8,704 globals with up to 1,024 details each. A typical example is the 8-bit NAH0Z000 "APMHA_TM_1 [000]", split into the 3-bit NAHD0000 "APMHA_Mode" at offset 0 and five 1-bit flags at offsets 3 to 7.62

Global Detail Offset Detail description Detail type NAH0Z000 (PTC 3, PFC 4) NAHD0000 0 APMHA_Mode ⅔ NAHD0001 3 APMHA_Mode trans 2/1 NAHD0002 4 APMHA_SafePos achieved 2/1 NAHD0003–NAHD0005 5–7 APMHA_Survnce_ Stat, APMHA_Vind_Elev_Stat, APMHA_Va_Elev_Stat 2/1

The number is a bit offset. In every packet where both a global and one of its details are located by the PLF (215,859 such pairs), the detail starts exactly that many bits after the global: in SPID 33500, for instance, NAH0Z000 and NAHD0000 both start at octet 67, bit 0, and NAHD0001 at octet 67, bit 3.62 12,074 rows have a global with no PLF entry. Of the 8,704 globals, 5,124 are octet strings (PTC 7; 1,913 of them 8 octets long) and 3,580 are unsigned integers (PTC 3), mostly of 8 bits (1,607) or 16 bits (1,464).62

Inference

The table records, as data, the structure that the PLF expresses only implicitly through overlapping entries: a raw word is located once as a global parameter, and its fields are located again as overlapping detail parameters. Tools can use it to show a word together with its decoded fields, or to check that the overlaps are consistent. The ICD allows overlapping PLF entries,8 but has no table that ties a field to its container.

docs.title: dup: duplicating packets under a pseudo-APID
docs.text:
The 69 rows of dup.dat map a SPID to an APID. Every SPID exists in the PID, and every target APID is one of 41 APIDs between 1953 and 1996 that appear in the PID with their own packet definitions. The duplicated packets are generic reports: event reports (5,1), (5,2) and (5,3), memory dumps (6,6), monitoring list reports (12,9), functional monitoring reports (142,11) and some private services.63

The ICD offers one piece of the mechanism. Since issue 6.5 (release 4.2) the PIC table has an optional field PIC_APID, so the position and width of the extra identification fields PI1 and PI2 can be defined per APID and type/subtype instead of per type/subtype only.910 In the 2025 release 47 PIC rows set PIC_APID, and their APIDs are exactly the 41 dup targets.63

The chain for the AOCS monitoring list report shows how the pieces fit together:63

  1. The spacecraft sends a (12,9) monitoring list report from APID 179. The MIB defines it as SPID 20129 "Monitoring List Report", a variable packet (PID_TPSD = 20129), with no PI1/PI2.
  2. dup.dat maps SPID 20129 to APID 1986.
  3. For type 12, subtype 9 and APID 1986, the PIC places PI1 at octet 19 (8 bits) and PI2 at octet 883 (8 bits).
  4. The PID has three (12,9) packets on APID 1986: SPID 65909 "AOCS - Monitoring List Report #1" (PI1 = 1, PI2 = 41), SPID 65910 "#2" (122, 142) and SPID 65911 "#3" (220, 242). All are fixed packets (PID_TPSD = -1).
  5. SPID 65909 has 1,275 PLF entries, one fixed slot per expected monitor. PI1 is the ID field of the first slot (NXAS001A, octet 19), and PI2 the ID field of a later slot (NXAS041A, octet 883).
  6. Synthetic "consistency" parameters check every slot's ID and act as validity parameters for the slot's fields (see Synthetic parameters).
flowchart LR
    TM["(12,9) report<br/>APID 179"] --> V["SPID 20129<br/>variable packet (VPD)"]
    TM -. "dup.dat: 20129 -> 1986" .-> D["copy identified<br/>under APID 1986"]
    D --> PIC["PIC (12,9, APID 1986):<br/>PI1 @ octet 19, PI2 @ octet 883"]
    PIC --> P1["SPID 65909 #1<br/>PI1=1, PI2=41"]
    PIC --> P2["SPID 65910 #2<br/>PI1=122, PI2=142"]
    PIC --> P3["SPID 65911 #3<br/>PI1=220, PI2=242"]
    P1 --> PLF["fixed PLF slots +<br/>consistency synthetics"]

Chain reconstructed from dup, pic, pid and plf.63

Inference

The likely purpose is to get full telemetry processing for data that the spacecraft sends in variable packets. The ICD warns that parameters extracted from variable packets get no validity, limit checking or synthetic evaluation.11 By having a ground process re-identify a copy of each report under a pseudo-APID, the mission can describe the same bytes a second time as fixed packets, chosen by monitor IDs, whose parameters are fully processed. The release does not say which process makes the copy. The number of mapped packets grew from 36 (27 APIDs) in 2020 to 69 (41 APIDs) in 2025.6359

docs.title: s13a, s13p and s13t: file transfer definitions
docs.text:
The three s13 files are new in 2025. s13p lists 11 partitions with numeric identifiers 161 to 195, such as 161 "OMM TC Files (A)", 162 "OMM OBCPs (A)", 163 "OMM System Files (A)", 177 "OMM TC Files (B)" and 193 "SGM-EEPROM CSW TC Files (A)". s13a lists 7 codes 0 to 6: PLAIN, OBCP, DELAYED TC, IMMEDIATE TC, PAYLOAD CONTEXT, INVALID and OTHER. s13t lists 12 file types with codes −2 to 9, such as "TC sequence (CSF type 1)", "Time tagged TC sequence (CSF type 2)", "Backup MTL (CSF type 3)", "SCOS stack file" and "OBCP". Its sixth column refers to an s13a entry, and its seventh to a default s13p partition (TCFA, SYSA, OBCA).64

The partition numbers match the commanding side of the MIB. The command ZCD00D09 "Accept First Uplink Part", a PUS service 13 telecommand (13,9), has the parameters FTS Id, Partition Id, File IDentifier, File size, File Attribute and the file content. Its Partition Id is decalibrated by CCDT0192TX "Partition", whose 11 values are the same numbers 161 to 195 as in s13p (for example 161 OMM_TC_FILES_A, 193 SGMA_TC_FILES). Its File Attribute uses CCDT0082TX "File types": 0 FT_INVALID, 1 FT_OBCP, 2 FT_DEL_TCSEQ, 3 FT_IMM_TCSEQ, 4 FT_PL_CTX, 5 FT_PS, 6 FT_PLAIN, 7 FT_FAT.65

Inference

The s13 tables appear to configure a ground tool that uploads files to the on-board mass memory with service 13: s13p names the target partitions, s13a the attribute values, and s13t the kinds of file to upload with their default attribute and partition. Codes 1 to 4 of s13a match the File Attribute calibration, but codes 0, 5 and 6 do not (s13a has 0 PLAIN, 5 INVALID, 6 OTHER, while the calibration has 0 FT_INVALID, 5 FT_PS, 6 FT_PLAIN), and the s13p description of 164/180 ("OMM Spare") differs from the calibration (OMM_PAYLOAD_A/_B). The meaning of the one-letter flags in the second column (M, B, N in s13p; C, W in s13t) is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Patterns across projects
docs.text:
Pattern Herschel/Planck Solar Orbiter Narrower identifiers curve, range set and stage identifiers shortened by one digit in instrument files (faxes, HPSDB G3–G5) – Narrower packet types PTC/PFC limited to the PS-ICD Appendix 6 set; PUS version 0 only 2,542 of 126,745 parameters use pairs outside that set Wider identifiers and new tables CCS files: Char(10) curves and range sets, Number(10) stages; cur, grp, grpa, grpk, lgf, sco, tcd, tmd, delta limits, CAF_INTER, default sub-schedule uses the repatriated features: 1,974 cur rows, 105 delta checks, 2 groups, CCF_SUBSCHEDID Naming conventions project NMCVT, SPIRE and HIFI names ending in element positions, Z pseudo items, I/O/Q reserved, EGSE items Y with positions 920–971 consistent prefixes visible in the data: N… monitoring parameters, Y… packet mnemonics, Z… commands, P… command parameters, A… sequences, D… displays Reserved ranges UDC packet partitioned per subsystem; SPIDs 1–100 in the instrument EGSE and 100–999 in the CCS; APIDs 2016–2046 for SCOE/EGSE; parameter names YZ… for CCS system parameters pseudo-APIDs 1953–1996 for re-identified packets; only SPIDs 101–103 (MATIS packets on APID 1966) below 1000 Forbidden features constants, sequences, parameter sets, printouts, octal radix – Extra information command durations table (HCSS); HPSDB long mnemonics and descriptions ASW_sw_para, pcf_glob_det, dup, s13* Configuration control field-level change records (OIRD); HPSDB working, reference and archive areas with validation by the manager; release notes with change records, NCR status and MD5 checksums; CCS update files naming validated items; CVS tags and database configurations (SPIRE) release names and vdf comments (e.g. 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33)

Herschel/Planck entries from the documents above; Solar Orbiter entries from the release data (the naming prefixes are this wiki's observation).5866116117

SQL used

Run against solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (and solo-2020-04-16.sqlite, swa-idb.sqlite). The non-ICD tables have generic column names COL1…COLn in file order. The pcf_glob_det offset check was done in Python over the same data because the join is slow in SQLite without indexes.

-- sizes
SELECT count(*) FROM asw_sw_para;  SELECT count(*) FROM pcf_glob_det;  SELECT count(*) FROM dup;
SELECT * FROM s13a;  SELECT * FROM s13p;  SELECT * FROM s13t;

-- ASW_sw_para: what the identifiers are
SELECT count(*), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf)), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT CPC_NAME FROM cpc)),
       sum(COL1 IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM ccf)), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT TPCF_NAME FROM tpcf)),
       sum(COL1 IN (SELECT PRF_NUMBR FROM prf)), count(DISTINCT COL1)
  FROM asw_sw_para;
SELECT max(length(COL2)), max(length(COL3)) FROM asw_sw_para;

-- pcf_glob_det: example and integrity
SELECT g.COL1, g.COL2, g.COL3, pd.PCF_DESCR, pd.PCF_PTC, pd.PCF_PFC
  FROM pcf_glob_det g JOIN pcf pd ON pd.PCF_NAME = g.COL2 WHERE g.COL1 = 'NAH0Z000';
SELECT PLF_NAME, PLF_SPID, PLF_OFFBY, PLF_OFFBI FROM plf
 WHERE PLF_NAME IN ('NAH0Z000', 'NAHD0000', 'NAHD0001') AND PLF_SPID = '33500';
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT COL1), count(DISTINCT COL2) FROM pcf_glob_det;

-- dup and APID-specific PIC rows
SELECT d.COL1, d.COL2, p.PID_TYPE, p.PID_STYPE, p.PID_APID, p.PID_DESCR
  FROM dup d JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = d.COL1;
SELECT count(*) FROM pic WHERE PIC_APID <> '';                          -- 47
SELECT count(DISTINCT d.COL2) FROM dup d
 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pic WHERE PIC_APID = d.COL2);              -- 41
SELECT * FROM pic WHERE PIC_APID = '1986';
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL, PID_DESCR, PID_TPSD FROM pid
 WHERE PID_APID IN ('1986', '179') AND PID_TYPE = '12';

-- s13 tables against the ST[13] uplink command
SELECT c.CDF_ELTYPE, c.CDF_BIT, c.CDF_PNAME, p.CPC_DESCR, p.CPC_PAFREF
  FROM cdf c LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = c.CDF_PNAME WHERE c.CDF_CNAME = 'ZCD00D09';
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CCDT0192TX', 'CCDT0082TX');

-- PTC/PFC pairs against the Herschel/Planck PS-ICD Appendix 6 set
WITH t AS (SELECT CAST(PCF_PTC AS INT) ptc, CAST(PCF_PFC AS INT) pfc FROM pcf)
SELECT ptc, count(*), sum(CASE
    WHEN ptc = 1 THEN pfc = 0
    WHEN ptc = 2 THEN pfc IN (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,12,16,32)
    WHEN ptc IN (3,4) THEN pfc BETWEEN 0 AND 14
    WHEN ptc = 5 THEN pfc IN (1,2)
    WHEN ptc = 6 THEN pfc IN (1,2,4,8)
    WHEN ptc IN (7,8) THEN 1
    WHEN ptc = 9 THEN pfc = 17
    WHEN ptc = 11 THEN pfc = 0
    ELSE 0 END) AS inside
  FROM t GROUP BY ptc;            -- total 126745, inside 124203 (same query on cpc: 7155, 7115)
SELECT PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1, 2;   -- e.g. 2|18|224, 9|15|2116

-- CCS External ICD rules
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_NAME LIKE 'VAR%' OR PCF_NAME LIKE 'GVAR%'
    OR PCF_NAME LIKE '$%' OR PCF_NAME LIKE 'YZ%';                        -- 0
SELECT p.PCF_PTC, count(*), count(DISTINCT c.CUR_RLCHK)
  FROM cur c JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = c.CUR_RLCHK GROUP BY 1;          -- 1|112|40, 2|1834|8, 3|28|4
SELECT max(CAST(CUR_POS AS INT)), max(CAST(CUR_VALPAR AS INT)) FROM cur; -- 12 | 420
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_DESCR FROM pid
 WHERE CAST(PID_SPID AS INT) BETWEEN 100 AND 999;                        -- 101-103, APID 1966, type 166
SELECT count(*), sum(coalesce(CCF_SUBSCHEDID, '') <> '') FROM ccf;       -- 5454 | 5304
SELECT OCP_TYPE, count(*) FROM ocp GROUP BY 1;  SELECT count(*) FROM grp; -- D 105; 2
SELECT count(*) FROM dst;                                                -- 1
