docs.title: MIB tooling and open-source libraries
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base (MIB) is exchanged as plain ASCII tables, but nobody maintains 100,000 parameters in a text editor. Around the interface defined by the Database Import ICD has grown a family of tools: off-line databases and editors that produce the tables, importers and ingestion programs that check and load them, translators that feed other control systems, and, more recently, open-source software: a complete mission control framework (Yamcs) that can load a MIB through a plug-in, and small libraries that read MIBs and the packets they describe. This page surveys the tools documented in this wiki's library, the open-source packages published on PyPI and GitHub, and ends with the scripts that build this site. For how these tools fit into the wider preparation of operations data, see Operations preparation.

flowchart LR
    subgraph prep["Preparation (off-line)"]
        ED["Editors / off-line DBs<br/>ESOC MS-Access editor (Integral),<br/>HPSDB, SRDB"]
        GEN["Generators<br/>mib-generator (C headers)"]
    end
    MIB[("MIB ASCII tables<br/>+ synthetic files")]
    subgraph use["Consumers"]
        IMP["SCOS-2000 importer<br/>+ consistency checker"]
        HCSS["HCSS ingestmib<br/>(Herschel science ground segment)"]
        ECHO["SRDB Translator -> ECHO<br/>(TAS-I checkout)"]
        TERMA["Terma CCS5 / SCS5 / TSC<br/>(+ DYNHK, run-time additions)"]
        YAMCS["Yamcs + yamcs-scos2k<br/>(open-source M&C)"]
        PY["pyscos2000, scospus,<br/>SpacePyLibrary (Python)"]
        SPOT["Request editors<br/>(e.g. SPOT Cruise)"]
        SITE["This site:<br/>SQLite copies + MIB explorer"]
    end
    ED --> MIB
    GEN --> MIB
    MIB --> IMP
    MIB --> HCSS
    MIB --> ECHO
    MIB --> TERMA
    MIB --> YAMCS
    MIB --> PY
    MIB --> SPOT
    MIB --> SITE

Landscape drawn from the sources cited in each section below.

docs.title: What the ICD expects of tools
docs.text:
The ICD sets the division of labour. It places no constraint on how the ASCII files are produced, and expects that a relational database such as MS Access will usually be used.1 The off-line database is responsible for consistency. The SCOS-2000 importer checks only the most dangerous problems, and from release 4.0 an off-line database consistency checker is delivered with the main SCOS-2000 releases.2

The importer's own behaviour is precise:34

  • Every field is checked against its declared type and length. A field that is too long is truncated with a warning. A mandatory field left null is set to 0 or the empty string, with a warning.
  • Relational integrity is checked. A record that refers to something missing, such as an unknown parameter, is not imported.
  • Command and sequence parameter values are checked against their format. Invalid values become 0, the empty string or 1970.001.00.00.00 for absolute times.
  • All messages go to a log file that is overwritten at each import (/home/sops1/Import.log).
  • Import options are a full import (optionally per domain) and a "check only" run that reports without changing any data. From release 5.0, sequences and displays are converted to XML files in the FARC instead (see Display definitions).

The ICD also warns that the import default of a field is not the same thing as the default an off-line editor may propose.5 And it gives one example of logic that belongs in the off-line "TM/TC database manager", not in SCOS-2000: for housekeeping packets defined on board with PUS service 3, ESA missions typically define the packet in the database first and generate the service 3 commands from it automatically.6

docs.title: ESOC's MS-Access database editor and the HIFI evaluation
docs.text:
In April 2000, an ESA presentation of SCOS-2000 to the FIRST/Planck projects listed the elements on offer: SCOS-2000, a router and a Tcl/Tk procedure automation tool reused from PROBA, and, as additional elements, "Database Editors" based on MS Access from INTEGRAL.7

Requirements. HIFI wrote down what an instrument team needed from such an editor (SRON-U/HIFI-SP-2000-2, August 2000). The MIB, "a set of more than 30 ASCII files", configures SCOS-2000 and must evolve with the instrument during integration.8 The requirements group into five areas:9

Area Requirements (summary) Data content All data needed to configure SCOS-2000; one table per SCOS-2000 file. User interface A datasheet per table with ICD field names and tip texts; complete records visible without scrolling; forms that follow the MIB structure (PCF with checks and calibrations, CPC with range sets and de-calibrations, PID with VPD and PLF, CCF with CDF, PTV and verification, CSF with its sub-tables, packet headers, parameter sets, and display layouts); pull-down menus for foreign keys. Data checking Unique keys enforced; update cascades so keys can be edited; no unintended delete cascades; validation rules for enumerated fields; mandatory fields enforced; ICD defaults used and never exported blank; a configurable whole-data-set checker; counters maintained or regenerated. Groups of data Data organised per instrument subsystem, enterable by subsystem engineers without SCOS-2000 knowledge, reportable per subsystem, and swappable when a subsystem model (QM, FM) changes. Tools Import, append, export and delete sets of SCOS-2000 files; an intuitive entry tool for parameter value sets.

Its §3.4 names four groups of tables (parameter data, packet data, parameter sets and operator data), while the table of its Annex A uses five: Operator (the six display tables), Packet, Packet header, Parameter and Parameter set.910

Evaluation. HIFI's evaluation report (SRON-U/HIFI/RP/2001-1 issue 2, April 2001) assessed version 2.0 of the "SCOS-2000 Database Editing Subsystem", which the report also calls the "Integral MS Access editor", and includes the replies of the editor's author.11 The key findings:

Topic Finding Author's reply or status Polynomial calibrations (MCF) No form at first; later a form, but the PCF/PLF form still could not select an MCF curve, and MCF had no primary key. Not used by INTEGRAL; SCOS-2000 looks up PCF_CURTX first in CAF, then in MCF, so MCF numbers must not clash with CAF numbers. Version table (VDF) Filled automatically at export, but the new record was not exported; order of export and record creation reversed. Populated at export; requires the PC date format DD/MM/YY. Datasheets Requirements 3.2.1–3.2.4 not implemented: only forms. Tables now selectable in table view, considered dangerous for bulk maintenance. Primary key of PID Built from the first six fields instead of the first five. Needed for INTEGRAL's satellite database. Validation rules Initially missing (e.g. RAWFMT accepted any value), later enforced. – Defaults Empty fields with defaults exported empty. To be investigated. Consistency checks Delivered as a separate consistency checker, "an impressive tool". INTEGRAL database exceeded 870,000 populated fields; checking inside the editor would be too slow. Counters Maintaining master-detail counts is error-prone; the report questions why they exist. Mostly useless for SCOS-2000, which uses none of them. Surprises (PTC, PFC) = (5, 2) exported as (5, 3). INTEGRAL-specific processing, to be removed. Import Imports replace rather than append; failing records not identified. Single tables, sets or the whole database can be imported. ICD conformance OCP_RLCHK 6 characters instead of 8; limit values 10 instead of 14; several SPID-type fields cannot hold 10 digits; css_mandisp, gpf_upun, spf_upun wrongly mandatory. –

Findings from the report.12131415 The author's view of who may edit a database is telling: at ESOC only fully qualified database administrators with control-system and spacecraft experience edit satellite databases.14 The report concludes that version 2 had improved greatly and was "a good tool to work with".16

docs.title: Project databases: HPSDB and the satellite database
docs.text:
For Herschel/Planck, the Operations Interface Requirements Document required a single common Satellite Database, delivered as Oracle data files with field-level change records.17 The Herschel/Planck System Database (HPSDB), documented by Alcatel Alenia Space, loaded instrument and CCS MIB files and regenerated SCOS-2000 and CCS "bridge files". Its object model, naming, default values and per-field processing rules are summarised on Mission tailoring.18 Two of its design choices show what an engineering database adds to the bare ICD. Every item carries a 64-character mnemonic, a 256-character long description and configuration data (user, date, reason, source, validation dates), none of which SCOS-2000 can import. And an 8-bit category flag per item selects which users (AIT, operations, software, flight dynamics) see it when bridge files are generated.19

ESA's SCOS-2000 based EGSE (EMCS, user manual issue 4.0 of 2004) worked the other way round. ESA had started an Oracle-based repository for its space system model, but it was not available, so users populated mission data directly in the ASCII files. SCOS-2000 loaded them into its internal MIB database, and the mergeDATA and setSCOSdata facilities merged data sets and switched between them.2021

docs.title: Ingestion into a science ground segment: HCSS
docs.text: The Herschel Common Science System read MIBs with its own ingestion software, whose interface and checks are defined by the HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note.22 In practice (SPIRE, 2007), ingestmib reads the directory named by the property hcss.mib.datadir, runs semantic checks, writes mibchecker.log, and stores the MIB definitions in a Versant object database under a user label. Afterwards cusgui loads the labelled MIB for the Common Uplink System.23 The checks it performs are listed on Mission tailoring.

docs.title: SRDB Translator: from SCOS-2000 to ECHO
docs.text:
An undated paper by Intecs and Thales Alenia Space Italia describes the SRDB Translator, which imports a Satellite Reference Database (SRDB) in SCOS-2000 MIB form into ECHO, the TAS-I central checkout (EGSE) system. The motivation is that SCOS-2000 had become the standard for ESA mission control and often for EGSE, so the SRDB is "almost always" based on the SCOS-2000 run-time database, while unit tests and AIV at TAS-I used ECHO and its own database.24 The paper carries no date. Its most recent reference is ICD issue 6.1 of February 2006,37 and the copy in the library is hosted on the same ESA Indico event (number 109) as the Terma paper cited below, which is headed "SESP 2010".38

Analysis. The two databases cover similar entities (parameters, calibrations, checks, packets, commands, verification), both built on PUS, but a one-to-one table mapping is "almost inapplicable". For every item the authors distinguish data present in both, data present only in the SRDB (adopted by extending ECHO, or ignored) and data that only ECHO needs (supplied separately).25 Two of their conversion tables:26

Topic SCOS-2000 ECHO Rule Verification checks vs telecommands separate entities with a mapping table checks as a detail table of each TC duplicated for every linked TC Verification stage any stage of the execution profile not applicable stage not imported Verification window start time and interval in s maximum time from TC emission in ms (start + interval) × 1000 Expected value raw or engineering engineering only raw checks discarded Numerical curve identifier Char(10) integer 1–9999 mapping algorithm; original name kept in the description Radix of raw values decimal, octal, hex decimal only converted Points per curve unlimited 2 to 1,000 others not imported or truncated Polynomial curve boundaries not held mandatory ECHO relaxed Logarithmic curves supported not handled ECHO extended Curves per parameter unlimited 4 extended to 99

Implementation. The translator is a utility of the ECHO Database Manager (MTGP) on MS SQL Server, compliant with SCOS-2000 ICD issue 6.1. In a first step it loads the SCOS-2000 tables unchanged into dedicated tables. In a second step stored procedures transform them into ECHO tables, either directly or as a file for later import, and it can merge the result with EGSE-local objects. A log lists the outcome per object.27

Use and limits. It was first built for Galileo GIOVE-B (an SRDB delivered as a single MS Access 2000 file), extended for Sentinel-1, and used for BepiColombo on-board computer and SSMM databases of about 10,000 records each.28 Because the first step expects exactly the columns of its ICD issue, BepiColombo databases made to an earlier ICD issue had to be adjusted to add the missing columns before import, and every project's customisations require new analysis. The authors call for a standard XML-based exchange language.2930 CCSDS defines such a language, XTCE; the paper does not mention it.

docs.title: Terma CCS5, SCS5 and TSC
docs.text:
Terma's checkout and control products read SCOS-2000 MIBs natively. A 2010 paper explains the choice: building a new monitoring and control system from scratch was attractive only if users kept their test language and database interfaces. The MIB interface, it says, "while not perfectly normalized, and not always perfectly designed, is nevertheless well known, relatively well described, and well understood".31

The 2024 presentation and the data sheet list the MIB-related features:3234

  • the SCOS-2000 MIB data model "6.9+…7.2" (data sheet: "ICD 6.9 extended"), with unlimited field lengths;
  • variable packets and parameters supported globally, deduced parameters in TM and TC, configurable length fields, both endianities, VPD_CHOICE and dynamic housekeeping definitions;
  • different synthetic (derived parameter) languages;
  • dropping and loading several databases without restart, with a clean separation of data from different suppliers (platform, payloads, instruments, EGSE), and an online MIB browser with search, filter and patch features;33
  • all tables accessible from the TOPE procedure language; TC sequence tables not supported (TOPE or command stack files are used instead).

docs.title: Dynamic housekeeping definitions (DYNHK)
docs.text:
The "dynamic housekeeping definitions" in that list are described in a Terma B.V. paper by P. Kazmirchuk, "Managing Telemetry Definitions on the Fly". The paper shows what a checkout system can do with a MIB at run time.46 An on-board data pool can hold tens or even hundreds of thousands of parameters. During integration, engineers use telecommands of PUS service 3 to make the on-board computer generate new housekeeping or diagnostic packets that no one defined in advance. A central checkout system (CCS) identifies packets only through its reference database, so without help these packets arrive as unknown. Until then, engineers had to write static TM definitions by hand.47 DYNHK closes that gap. It watches the uplinked service 3 requests and writes the matching MIB rows itself.

What CCS5 provides. CCS5 uses the MIB as its reference-database format and TOPE, a Tcl-based language, for automated procedures. The paper says both are backward compatible with SCOS-2000. When a test session starts, CCS5 loads the MIB tables into memory. TOPE can then read every table and write some tables and columns. CCS5 can also merge several MIBs, for example from different equipment suppliers, and adds a field "Source" that records which MIB each row came from.49

The PUS requests it reads. The paper uses the PUS-A names (its reference is ECSS-E-70-41A): TC(3,1) and TC(3,2) define a new housekeeping or diagnostic report, TC(3,3) and TC(3,4) clear definitions, TC(3,5) enables generation, and TM(3,25) and TM(3,26) are the reports. PUS-C keeps these subtype numbers, under names such as "create a housekeeping parameter report structure" for TC[3,1].100 The application data of TC(3,1) and TC(3,2) carries the structure identifier (SID), a collection interval in units of the default housekeeping scheduling rate, and the list of on-board parameter IDs with their counters. The SID, together with the APID and the subtype, identifies a TM packet definition uniquely. The requests therefore carry enough information to build the definition.48

sequenceDiagram
    participant Op as Test operator
    participant CCS as CCS5 (server, clients, IFMGR)
    participant Dyn as DynHkMonitor.tcl (DYNHK)
    participant OBC as On-board computer
    Op->>OBC: TC(3,1) or TC(3,2): SID, interval, parameter IDs
    OBC-->>CCS: completion report (e.g. PUS service 1)
    CCS->>Dyn: verified TC and its parameters
    Dyn->>Dyn: derive PID and VPD rows, allocate a new SPID
    Dyn->>CCS: CCS5::remote: add rows to every in-memory MIB (one atomic call)
    Op->>OBC: TC(3,5) enable report generation
    OBC-->>CCS: TM(3,25) or TM(3,26), processed like a static packet
    Op->>OBC: later TC(3,3) or TC(3,4): clear SID
    Dyn->>CCS: set PID_VALID false; later packets of that SID are archived as unknown

This wiki's drawing of the paper's Fig. 1 workflow and the text around it.50

The component is a TOPE script running on the CCS server console. Its authors had to change the core C++ modules so that TM packets can be defined without disturbing ongoing monitoring and control, generate MIB rows from PUS request parameters, and distribute the new definitions to all workstations in time.49 A redefinition of a SID that already exists disables the old definition, adds one with a new SPID and logs a message. As a result, SPID and TPSD values are never reused within a session.50

Mapping to the MIB tables. CCS5 identifies TM packets in the same steps as SCOS-2000: APID, then service type and subtype, then the PIC entry that locates the extra identification fields PI1 and PI2, then the PID entry that yields the SPID, and finally the PLF and/or VPD rows that list the parameters.52 (See Monitoring in the MIB for the full procedure.) DYNHK writes VPD rather than PLF rows. The service 3 request lists parameter IDs but no offsets, and VPD normally packs parameters back to back, which matches the request. VPD also allows variable-length strings, and CCS5 archives every VPD sample of a packet, so retrieval does not depend on when the packet was (re)defined.52

PID field Value written by DynHkMonitor PID_TYPE 3 PID_STYPE 25 (housekeeping) or 26 (diagnostic) PID_APID from a configured mapping of TC APID to TM APID PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL derived from the SID, as the PIC entry dictates PID_SPID allocated from a configurable offset clear of the static definitions, incremented for each new request PID_DESCR generated text, for example "Dyn HK" followed by the SID PID_TPSD equal to the SPID PID_DFHSIZE derived from PIC: the start reference for variable parameters PID_TIME Y (on-board time assumed in the packet header) PID_INTER computed from the collection interval PID_CHECK 1 (packet error control assumed present) other fields blank, so the ICD defaults apply PID_VALID set to false when TC(3,3) or TC(3,4) clears the SID

Fields from the paper's "PID Table" section.54

In the simple case every parameter is sampled once. Each one gets a VPD row with VPD_TPSD = PID_TPSD, VPD_POS = 1 to NPAR, and VPD_NAME = the PCF name whose PCF_PID equals the on-board parameter ID in the request. When the request's NFA indicator is 1, super-commutated parameters follow. DYNHK then adds a group-repeater row with VPD_NAME "REPEATER", VPD_GRPSIZE = NPAR2 (parameters in the group) and VPD_FIXREP = NREP (samples).55

Three gaps between the PUS request and the MIB need configuration. The collection interval comes in scheduling-rate units, but CCS5 needs milliseconds to expire stale parameters, so a setting schedulingRate supplies the conversion. The TM APID cannot be derived from the TC APID, so a mapping is configured. And because the MIB ICD does not refer to the SID directly, PIC rows for the new packets must exist beforehand. CCS5 uses them to split the SID into PI1 and PI2 (or use it as PI1 alone) and to compute PID_DFHSIZE.5253

Persistence. The added rows live only in memory and are lost when the MIB is reloaded. They carry the Source value "DYNHK", so they can be saved as separate MIB files and merged into the next session. Whether that is wise depends on whether the on-board software keeps its dynamic definitions over a reboot, for example in EEPROM, so both saving and reloading are optional.51 The paper ends by noting that PUS-C (2016) has standardised many service 3 subservices that the implementation then handled under mission-specific numbers.56

Inference: date of the paper

The paper carries no date. It calls ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (2016) "published last year" and cites ICD issue 6.9 (2010), which suggests 2017. It is hosted on ESA Indico event 180, which also hosts a paper by F. Trifin and A. Walsh whose header names the Workshop on Simulation and EGSE for Space Programmes (SESP), 28–30 March 2017, at ESA-ESTEC.565758 That the Kazmirchuk paper was presented at SESP 2017 is this wiki's inference from the shared event; the paper itself does not say so.

The Solar Orbiter MIB for comparison. The public 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB takes the static route that DYNHK is meant to complement. It defines 288 TM(3,25) and 89 TM(3,26) packets on 76 APIDs. All 377 are fixed packets (PID_TPSD = −1, so their parameters are located through PLF), with PID_DFHSIZE 16, PID_TIME Y and PID_CHECK 0. Their PIC entries place PI1, the SID, at octet 16 with a width of 8 bits. On the command side the MIB holds 82 TC(3,1) and 77 TC(3,2) definitions. Thirteen are generic commands whose SID is an editable element: twelve "Define New … Parameter Report" commands, six per subtype, and the instrument command ZIT00301 "Def New HK Par. Rep.". The other 146 are predefined report definitions such as "Define HK: AOCS Dynamics FAST", each with a fixed SID that equals the PI1 value of a TM(3,25) or TM(3,26) packet already in PID. Example: command ZCA2Z05B (APID 188) fixes SID 77, and SPID 29530 "AOCS Dynamics FAST" is TM(3,25) with PI1 = 77 on APID 180.64

Inference

A DYNHK-style tool on this MIB would need its SPID offset above the existing range (the PID table's SPIDs run from 101 to 1,000,006) and could reuse the existing PIC rows for (3,25) and (3,26). In ICD terms, PID_CHECK 0 means that the packetiser does not check the packet error control field, either because the packet has none or because the check is disabled. The paper's choice of 1 enables the CRC check. Which of the two applies to Solar Orbiter housekeeping packets is not stated in the available sources.59

SQL used 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite
SELECT PID_STYPE, COUNT(*), SUM(PID_TPSD <> '-1') FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE='3' GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PID_DFHSIZE, PID_TIME, PID_CHECK, COUNT(*) FROM pid
  WHERE PID_TYPE='3' AND PID_STYPE IN ('25','26') GROUP BY 1,2,3;
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PID_APID) FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE='3' AND PID_STYPE IN ('25','26');
SELECT * FROM pic WHERE PIC_TYPE='3';
SELECT MIN(CAST(PID_SPID AS INT)), MAX(CAST(PID_SPID AS INT)) FROM pid;
SELECT CASE WHEN CCF_DESCR LIKE 'Define New%' THEN 'generic' ELSE 'predefined' END,
       CCF_STYPE, COUNT(*)
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE='3' AND CCF_STYPE IN ('1','2') GROUP BY 1,2;
-- element at bit 0 (the SID) of each TC(3,1)/TC(3,2): E = editable, A/F = fixed
SELECT d.CDF_ELTYPE, COUNT(*) FROM ccf f JOIN cdf d ON d.CDF_CNAME=f.CCF_CNAME
 WHERE f.CCF_TYPE='3' AND f.CCF_STYPE IN ('1','2') AND CAST(d.CDF_BIT AS INT)=0 GROUP BY 1;
-- each fixed SID (CDF_VALUE, hexadecimal for A, decimal for F) was then looked up in
-- pid.PID_PI1_VAL with PID_STYPE 25 (for TC(3,1)) or 26 (for TC(3,2)): 146 of 146 found
SELECT * FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE='3' AND PID_STYPE='25' AND PID_PI1_VAL='77';

Terma Data Base Manager

A separate Terma product called "Data Base Manager" (DBM) is not described in any document of this wiki's library. Its features, licence and version are therefore not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Yamcs and the yamcs-scos2k MIB loader
docs.text: Yamcs is an open-source mission control framework. Its server manual (release 5.14.1-SNAPSHOT, copyright 2026) is published by Space Applications Services NV/SA, Belgium, with Aerospace Applications North America in Houston.69 GitHub shows the yamcs/yamcs repository under the AGPL-3.0 licence.92 Yamcs follows a traditional monitoring and control model. Parameters arrive in groups, usually binary packets, and are checked against limits that can depend on context. Commands consist of a name and arguments, are gated by transmission constraints and significance, and pass through verification stages.70 The server is a single Java process. Data links connect to the target system, preprocessors and postprocessors handle packet details that the database does not describe (such as checksums), and processors apply the Mission Database (MDB) to turn packets into parameters and commands into packets.71

docs.title: The Mission Database and its loaders
docs.text:
The MDB uses terminology "very close" to XTCE: space systems, containers, parameters, commands and algorithms, with space systems named by UNIX-like paths such as /BogusSAT/SC001.72 Yamcs builds the MDB at start-up from a configurable loader tree in the instance configuration. Each loader fills one space system and can have sub-loaders for its children, and loaders of different types can be mixed as long as their content maps onto Yamcs' internal, XTCE-based model. The result is cached on disk.76 The manual documents three built-in loaders:747576

Loader type Input Notes xtce XTCE XML file(s) (file or fileset) tolerant reader: unknown tags ignored, and it "strives to be backward compatible" with XTCE 1.0 and 1.1; the unsupported XTCE features are listed on the XTCE page sheet Excel 97-2003 .xls workbook (.xlsx not supported) sheets General, ChangeLog, DataTypes, Parameters, DerivedParameters, LocalParameters, Containers, Algorithms, Alarms, Commands, CommandOptions, CommandVerification and Calibration; format versions 5.3 to 7.1 emptyNode none creates an empty space-system node to hang sub-loaders on

Two details matter for anyone coming from the MIB. First, in Yamcs a calibrator works in opposite directions for the two kinds of type: raw to engineering for parameters, engineering to raw for arguments. A parameter's calibration cannot simply be reused for a command argument, just as the MIB keeps CAF and CCA separate.73 Second, the MDB is normally read-only. Since version 5.8.8, sub-trees can be declared writable, so that parameters and parameter types can be added at run time and persisted in XTCE form.72 A note at the end of the same chapter still says that Yamcs "does not persist TM/TC definitions" and has no import function. The manual does not reconcile the two statements.76

docs.title: yamcs-scos2k
docs.text:
The SCOS-2000 loader is a separate plug-in, yamcs-scos2k. It is not described in the server manual beyond one mention, so the facts below come from its GitHub page, retrieved on 2026-11-12.93 The repository shows the AGPL-3.0 licence and 96 commits, no published releases and no description line. The README states that the test MIB comes from another project and cannot be published, so the tests live in a private repository. It names no ICD issue.

Item What the README says Installation a Maven dependency added to the Yamcs project's pom.xml MIB loader MDB loader type org.yamcs.scos2k.MibLoader path directory of the ASCII MIB files epoch time epoch, for example 1970-01-01T00:00:00 TC.vblParamLengthBytes size in bytes of the length tag in front of variable-length strings and octet strings in commands; default 0 TM.vblParamLengthBytes the same for telemetry (example value 1) TM.typeOffset, TM.subTypeOffset byte offsets of the PUS service type and subtype in TM packets (example values 7 and 8) Displays a service org.yamcs.scos2k.MibDisplayLoader, with Yamcs' ParameterListService, loads the MIB's alphanumeric displays as Yamcs parameter lists. These can be edited at run time but are lost at restart Not supported delta checks (OCP_TYPE = D), event generation (OCP_TYPE = E), status consistency checks (OCP_TYPE = C with PCF_USCON = Y), command-ID arguments (CPC_CATEG = A, loaded as a binary argument instead), command stacks Renaming duplicate command argument names become arg_<n>, because neither Yamcs nor XTCE allows duplicates

The server manual adds one detail. Yamcs' PUS command postprocessor can treat a binary argument as an embedded TC packet. It fills in the packet's length and sequence count and optionally appends a checksum, as needed for TC(11,4) schedule insertions or TC(22,4) activities. The manual says yamcs-scos2k marks command parameters of (PTC, PFC) = (12, 1) this way.78 PTC 12 is the PUS-C "packet" type, PFC 1 being a TC packet.63 It is not in the ICD 7.0 type list, which jumps from PTC 11 to PTC 13.101 There, TC packets are carried instead by command-ID parameters of type (7, 0), which SCOS-2000 encodes from the raw data of a specified command.61 See MIB parameter types.

Inference: the variable-length options

Two sources explain the two vblParamLengthBytes options. The ICD says that from SCOS-2000 R4.0 the PUS length field in front of variable-length octet and character strings in commands can be switched on or off by configuration.62 The Yamcs manual says that for command arguments only it accepts a length tag of 0 bits, which XTCE forbids, "for compatibility with other systems (e.g. SCOS-2k)".77 SCOS-2000 itself does not decode variable-length strings in telemetry,62 so the TM option serves packets that SCOS-2000 would need special processing for. A default of 0 bytes in the loader therefore matches a SCOS-2000 configuration without the length prefix. The example values 7 and 8 for the type and subtype offsets match the PUS TM layout: a 6-octet primary header followed by one secondary-header octet before the service type.

What the unsupported features would skip in the public databases. The counts below show how much of each public MIB copy falls into the README's unsupported categories:

Database OCP rows OCP_TYPE D OCP_TYPE E OCP_TYPE C PCF_USCON = Y CPC rows CPC_CATEG A CSF rows Solar Orbiter 2025 7,369 105 0 15 15 7,155 2 3,404 Solar Orbiter 2020 4,686 102 0 13 13 6,947 2 2,701 SWA (2021 ASCII set) 326 0 0 0 0 531 0 0 SWA v6.5.0 325 0 0 0 0 538 0 0 STIX 2.26.38 32 0 0 0 0 669 0 0

Row counts from this wiki's queries.6465666768

In the 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB the two command-ID arguments are PCD0B044 "Complete TC packet" and PCD13013 "TC to send upon event". They are used by 24 commands: one TC(11,4) (ZCD00B04, "Insert Telecommands in Command Schedule"), one TC(11,132) and 22 TC(19,1) event-action definitions. Both are of type (7, 0), as the ICD requires.6461 The README says yamcs-scos2k loads such arguments as binary arguments.93 The loader's source settles how this relates to the embedded-TC marker: a CPC_CATEG A parameter becomes a plain BinaryArgumentType, and only a parameter of PTC 12 with PFC 1 receives the embedded-TC ancillary data.94 No command in that MIB has two editable or fixed elements with the same parameter name, so the arg_<n> renaming would not occur.64

Inference

Loaded with yamcs-scos2k, these 24 Solar Orbiter commands would therefore take their nested telecommand as raw bytes, without the automatic length, sequence count and checksum that the PUS postprocessor applies to embedded TC packets, and without SCOS-2000's encoding of a named command into the argument.

The 15 status consistency checks belong to parameters such as NCDT02A0. The instrument databases (SWA, STIX) use none of the unsupported features.

SQL used 
-- run on solo-2025-09-16, solo-2020-04-16, swa-idb, swa-idb-v6.5.0, stix-idb-2.26.38
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ocp),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ocp WHERE OCP_TYPE='D'),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ocp WHERE OCP_TYPE='E'),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ocp WHERE OCP_TYPE='C'),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_USCON='Y'),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cpc),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cpc WHERE CPC_CATEG='A'),
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM csf);
-- solo-2025-09-16 only
SELECT CPC_NAME, CPC_DESCR, CPC_PTC, CPC_PFC FROM cpc WHERE CPC_CATEG='A';
SELECT f.CCF_TYPE||','||f.CCF_STYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT c.CDF_CNAME)
  FROM cdf c JOIN ccf f ON f.CCF_CNAME=c.CDF_CNAME
 WHERE c.CDF_PNAME IN (SELECT CPC_NAME FROM cpc WHERE CPC_CATEG='A') GROUP BY 1;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_PNAME, COUNT(*) n FROM cdf
 WHERE CDF_ELTYPE IN ('E','F') AND CDF_PNAME<>'' GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING n>1);
SELECT OCP_NAME FROM ocp WHERE OCP_TYPE='C';

docs.title: PUS support in Yamcs
docs.text:
The data links that carry MIB-described packets need Yamcs' PUS preprocessor and postprocessor. They are configured separately from the MDB:7980

Component Function Main options (defaults) PusPacketPreprocessor (TM) checks and identifies PUS packets per ECSS-E-ST-70-41C and sets the generation time errorDetection (16-SUM, CRC-16-CCIIT with initial value 0xFFFF, ISO-16 or NONE); timeEncoding (default CUC from the GPS epoch); pktTimeOffset (13); timePktTimeOffset for time packets without secondary header (7); tcoService and performTimeCorrelation for ground-side time correlation PusCommandPostprocessor (TC) sets the CCSDS length and per-APID sequence count, optionally appends a checksum errorDetection; seqCounterName for counters shared between links; pus11 options that wrap a command into TC(11,4) for time-tagged release, with sub-schedule and group IDs; embedded-TC handling

For time, the manual names three strategies. The third, maintaining a correlation on the ground, is the one it attributes to the ESA PUS; it is done with Yamcs' time correlation service (see Time correlation in SCOS-2000).81

docs.title: Request editors: SPOT Cruise
docs.text: MIBs are also read by tools that prepare operations requests. Starion's web-based SPOT Cruise framework at ESAC, built for BepiColombo and adapted for JUICE, edits payload operations requests (POR/PDOR) in the ESOC command request file (CRF) XML format. It manages MIB updates and checks every request against the applicable MIB, which the paper expands as "Mission Information Database".35

docs.title: Open-source libraries
docs.text:
Five small open-source packages on the Python Package Index (PyPI) deal with SCOS-2000 data. Of these, only mib-generator has documentation in this wiki's library (its Read the Docs manual, added in round 2). The facts in the table come from each package's PyPI JSON record (https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json), retrieved by this wiki on 2026-11-12, and are flagged as such. A sixth SCOS-2000 library, SpacePyLibrary, is not on PyPI and is described below, followed by generic CCSDS and XTCE packages.

Package Purpose (PyPI summary) Latest version (date) First release on PyPI Licence Python Organisation (from metadata) Source pyscos2000 "Python SCOS-2000 parsing and checking" 0.3.0 (2023-05-04) 0.1.0 (2023-02-23) MIT ≥ 3.6 IRF (irf.se) gitlab.irf.se/irf/pyscos2000 scospus "PUS packet parsing with SCOS backing" 0.2.0 (2023-06-13) 0.1.0 (2023-02-23) MIT ≥ 3.6 IRF (irf.se) gitlab.irf.se/irf/scospus SCOSpy "Python library to read the SCOS-2000 header" 0.5.0 (2025-11-20) 0.2.1 (2020-07-09) GNU GPL v3 ≥ 3.11 INAF (inaf.it) github.com/RomoloPoliti-INAF/SCOSpy mib-generator "Generator of SCOS 2000 MIB databases." 0.1.3 (2023-09-11) 0.1.1 (2023-09-03) MIT ≥ 3.10 individual author github.com/vachaj11/MIB-generator edds_process "Package to process data from the EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS) of ESA" 0.11.0 (2026-10-01) 0.9.1 (2022-11-23) CeCILL-2.1 ≥ 3.9, < 4 Observatoire de Paris (obspm.fr) gitlab.obspm.fr/ROC_PUBLIC/edds_process

All values from the PyPI JSON API.40 Dates are the upload times of the first file of each release. For SCOSpy the licence field reads "GNU GPL ver3" and the classifier "GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3)". For edds_process the licence is given only as the SPDX expression CECILL-2.1, the French CeCILL free-software licence, not MIT.40

docs.title: pyscos2000
docs.text:
pyscos2000 parses and checks the ASCII tables of a SCOS-2000 MIB. Its README shows the basic use: pyscos2000.SCOS('./ASCII') loads a MIB directory of .dat files, every table becomes an attribute (for example scos.plf), and its records are in rows. The README names no ICD issue and documents no writer.40 The library's API documentation (outside the library, retrieved 2026-11-12) adds the rest:39

  • Its scos2000 module defines the table schemas, "Based on EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 issue 7.2-FINAL (2019-12-13)" (see ICD history), with one class per table for 36 tables (CAFTable … VPDTable, including CURTable, LGFTable and DSTTable) and a ZipArchiveTextReader for reading the files from a zip archive.
  • The same module provides consistency checkers: bit offsets in the range 0–7, field lengths, forbidden characters in key columns, CAF entries without the right number of CAP rows, CAP rows without a CAF entry, unused CAF, TXF and MCF definitions, the PLF time delay range, constants (PCF_NATUR = C) without PCF_PARVAL, and validity parameter definitions. The checker module is a framework for writing further checkers.
  • A synthetic module has classes for synthetic parameter definitions and instances, including a DynamicSyntheticParameter for PCF_NATUR = D.
  • A browser module is described as a "very simple tool to browse a SCOS-2000 database", with main() and parse_args() entry points.

This wiki takes its SQLite column names from pyscos2000's table schemas, which were introspected into the file tools/pyscos2000_schema_icd72.json. For each of 36 tables the file records the schema class, its docstring, and per column the name, type, key flag, optionality and default.42 The 17 ICD 7.0 tables that pyscos2000 does not model are the three group tables, the eight display tables, the verification tables CVS, CVE and CVP, and CPS, PVS and PSM. Four column names are spelled differently from ICD 7.0, and one column is inserted:4341

Table Position pyscos2000 ICD 7.0 cpc 1 CPC_NAME CPC_PNAME cpc 15 CPC_OBTIP CPC_OBTID cpc 16 CPC_DESCR2 (new; CPC_ENDIAN moves to 17) CPC_ENDIAN css 17 CSS_STATPTV CSS_STAPTV vdf 3 VDF_DOMAIN VDF_DOMAINID

The project file also lists ccf field 21 (CCF_SUBSCHEDID against "CCF_SUBSCHED"), but that is a text-extraction artefact: the ICD 7.0 field table wraps the name over two lines as "CCF_SUBSCHED ID", and the ICD's own csf description calls the field CCF_SUBSCHEDID, the spelling pyscos2000 also uses.41

docs.title: scospus
docs.text: scospus parses PUS packets using a SCOS-2000 MIB as its packet description, and depends on pyscos2000. Its PyPI record carries no README text, so which services it decodes and how it applies the PLF and VPD are not stated in the sources consulted.40

docs.title: SCOSpy
docs.text:
SCOSpy decodes the SCOS-2000 packet header, the internal header that SCOS-2000 puts in front of each stored TM or TC packet in its archive (see Mission archives), not the CCSDS header. From a hexadecimal string, SCOS(packet) returns the common packet header, a TM or TC packet header and the data. According to the README:40

  • Common header fields include CTree, AccessF, SimFlag, FilingTime, CreationTime, CreateID, SCID, GSID, PSize, PType, Version, FilingFlag, DistFlag, TSPolicy, TQ, StreamID, SeqCounter, SPID and MissionID.
  • TM packet header fields: TPSD, RouteID, PUSAPID, PUSSSC, PUSService, PUSSubService.
  • TC packet header fields include UplinkTime, ExecTime, LUTime, RequestID, the PUS APID, sequence count, service, subservice and acknowledgement flags, and source host and type.
  • The event packet header is not implemented. Only packet types 1 (TM) and 2 (TC) are supported.
  • Lookup tables are built in for BepiColombo (mission ID 816, spacecraft IDs 816 and 817). The README shows how to add JUICE (ID 844) by extending two dictionaries.

The presence of SPID and TPSD in the TM header is what ties archived packets to the MIB: they are the processing keys from the PID table (see Monitoring in the MIB).

docs.title: mib-generator
docs.text:
mib-generator builds SCOS-2000 MIB databases from C header files. Its README describes "basic abilities" for parsing C syntax, interpreting declarations that follow an expected structure of TM and TC packets, and creating the corresponding MIB. It names neither a mission nor the tables it writes, and refers to separate online documentation.40 That documentation ("MIB Generator, Release 0.1", Josef Vácha, 15 September 2023) fills in the detail. It describes the tool as a set of Python scripts, run mainly from the terminal as mib-gen (with a PySide6 GUI, mib-gen-gui), that assumes one specific formatting of the input C files, and as "under active development".8284

Inputs. Four C files are expected:83

File Expected content TM .h structure of the TM packets, their entries and calibrations TM .c the list of TM packet types: an apidNum array mapping APID names to numbers, and a tmProperties array giving each packet type its APID, service type and subtype TC .h structure of the commands and of the TC packet headers, decalibrations and verifications TcTm .h definitions shared by TM and TC, such as common identifier structures and enums

Annotations. The generator evaluates #define macros and enum constants into one dictionary, then reads C comments of the form /*{ … }*/ as json5 dictionaries. A comment in front of a struct declares a packet: pack_type links it to the type, subtype and APID in the .c file, spid and text_id give its SPID and MIB name, and base_par_index with prefix names its parameters. In the documentation's example, prefix "LWT" and base index 59200 give the third entry the name LWT59202. Comments on the fields mark the SID (sid, with const_value), the SCOS type (type, for example CUCTIME4_3), a variable-packet role (vpd: fixed, count or data) and a calibration (cal). Bit-field widths such as uint8_t compression:5 are honoured, and nested structs are expanded in place.85 Calibrations are declared in comments keyed mcf (polynomial coefficients), lgf (logarithmic), text_cal or an annotated enum (textual) and num_cal (point pairs). Commands use service and sub, cdf: count|data for repeated groups, min/max for range checks, default, const_value for fixed areas, enum for a decalibration, and cvs for verification stages. Stages are declared in stand-alone comments (cvs_def, cvs_type, cvs_interval, default), and the sample code notes that CVS_SOURCE is always R (report-based) and the start time 0.86

Outputs. The construction classes documented in the API chapters produce rows for 25 tables:87

Object MIB tables TM packet pid, pic, tpcf, pcf, plf, cur, vpd TC header tcp, pcpc, pcdf TC command ccf, cpc, cdf, prf, prv, cvp Calibrations caf/cap, mcf, lgf, txf/txp Decalibrations paf/pas Verifications cvs

Before saving the tables as .dat files, the generation package checks every value against the type, length, uniqueness and mandatory flags recorded per column in its longdata module. Repeated rows in unique columns are deleted with a warning. One further check, mnemon_check, enforces unique, non-empty mnemonics in description fields, following "additional mib specifications by OHB Italia", the only user organisation the documentation names.89 A dedicated filter reduces the packet list to one PIC row per type and subtype, and warns when packets of the same type and subtype declare their identification fields at different positions.90 This is the constraint that the ICD itself places on PIC: all packets of one type and subtype must carry their extra identification fields at the same position and with the same length.60 Two simplifications are documented: only one calibration per parameter (through PCF_CURTX, not several CUR rows), and fixed repetitions in VPD, which need a counter, get an extra "virtual" PCF entry that no packet contains.88 Optionally, a .docx document lists the entries of every TM and TC packet in a layout that follows a usual ICD.89

Inference

Generating the MIB from the on-board software's own C structures is the reverse of the "database first" approach that the ICD describes for ESA missions,6 and suits small projects whose flight software is the single source of truth. The documented table set has no monitoring checks (ocf/ocp), no version record (vdf), no sequences and no displays, so those would have to come from elsewhere. The documentation states no ICD issue.

docs.title: edds_process
docs.text: edds_process handles data from the EGOS Data Dissemination System. Its edds_process.response module parses and creates EDDS XML files of the TmRaw and TcReport kinds. It depends on xmltodict.40 The corresponding XML types appear in the EDDS user ICD (for example the complex type PktTmRaw); see EDDS request and data formats.36 Its contact addresses belong to the Observatoire de Paris domain obspm.fr.40

docs.title: SpacePyLibrary
docs.text:
SpacePyLibrary, by Stefan Korner, describes itself as a "Python library for AeroSpace applications". GitHub shows it under the MIT licence with 364 commits and no published releases. The master branch is for Python 3 and a python2 branch keeps the Python 2 version. The README says nothing more, so the description below comes from the directory listing and one source file, retrieved on 2026-11-12.95

  • SCOS/MIB.py is headed "SCOS - Mission Database (MIB) handling". It says it partly implements egos-mcs-s2k-icd-0001-version69_signed.pdf, that is, ICD issue 6.9 (see ICD history). It reads nine tables, pid, pic, tpcf, pcf, plf, vpd, ccf, cpc and cdf, one record class per table, parsing only selected fields. It accepts PIC files both with and without the PIC_APID column. Its copyright line reads 2018.96
  • Other directories carry ground-segment protocol modules whose names match interfaces described on this wiki: GRND/NCTRS.py and NCTRSDU.py (NCTRS), EGSE/EDEN.py and EGSE/CNC.py (EGSE interfaces), next to CCSDS, PUS, SIM (simulator) and SCOE packages.95

Inference

The module names suggest a test environment that can act as an NCTRS or EDEN/CnC peer and use the MIB to build and decode packets. The repository's documentation (a .doc/.pdf manual in doc/) was not read for this page, so these roles are not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Generic CCSDS and XTCE packages
docs.text:
Several open-source tools handle the same packets without a MIB. They describe packets in code, in CSV or in XTCE. CCSDS 660.2-G-2 notes only that "many compliant vendor products and open source tools" exist and advises searching the internet for current listings.91 The table below records what each project's own pages said on 2026-11-12:979899

Tool What it does Version (date) Licence Language Maintainer (from metadata) Yamcs mission control framework; MDB from XTCE, spreadsheets or plug-in loaders such as yamcs-scos2k manual 5.14.1-SNAPSHOT AGPL-3.0 Java Space Applications Services yamcs-scos2k SCOS-2000 MIB loader and MIB display loader for Yamcs no releases (96 commits) AGPL-3.0 Java (Maven) Yamcs project OpenC3 COSMOS command and control system; imports XTCE 1.0–1.2 and exports XTCE 1.2 through xtce_converter not shown OpenC3 Builder's License V2 ("based on the Elastic License 2.0, modified by OpenC3, Inc.") Ruby and Python (repository topics) OpenC3, Inc. Space Packet Parser decodes CCSDS telemetry packets from an XTCE definition 6.2.0 (2026-09-13) BSD-3-Clause Python ≥ 3.10 LASP, University of Colorado CCSDSPy reads fixed- and variable-length CCSDS packets described in code or CSV 2.1.0 (2026-10-28) BSD Python ≥ 3.10 Daniel da Silva and Steven Christe (author e-mails); the documentation credits "CCSDSPy Developers" spacepackets implements Space Packets (133.0-B-2), CDS short time codes, PUS-C TC/TM with PUS-A legacy support, CFDP packets and USLP frames 0.32.0 (2026-05-03) Apache-2.0 Python ≥ 3.9 Robin Mueller (us-irs on GitHub) xtcetools software for the OMG Space Domain Task Force's XTCE specification, recommended by the Yamcs manual for validating XTCE files 1 tag, 357 commits Apache-2.0 not stated individual author

The Yamcs row also draws on the server manual.69 For the PyPI packages the dates are upload dates of the latest release. The earliest releases on PyPI are 0.0.7 (2017-06-29) for CCSDSPy, 4.0.1 (2023-03-10) for Space Packet Parser and 0.1.0 (2021-10-01) for spacepackets.97 The GitHub page of COSMOS shows a "License" link without a name. The README names the OpenC3 Builder's License, and LICENSE.md describes it as a modified Elastic License 2.0 that forbids offering the software as a hosted service to third parties and developing competing products.98

Inference

None of these packages reads a MIB directly. A MIB reaches them only through a conversion to XTCE, along the lines of the mapping on the XTCE page. Which XTCE features each consumer supports then matters. For example, the COSMOS converter does not yet support SplineCalibrator, which is the natural target of the MIB's CAF/CAP curves (see XTCE implementations).

docs.title: This site's own build scripts
docs.text:
The pages and explorer of this wiki are built from the same public data with a few scripts in the repository's tools/ directory:44

File What it does tools/srcgrep.py Lists the source registry and searches the extracted text of each library document, printing PDF page indexes (counted from the form feeds of pdftotext) for citations. tools/check_page.py Lints a wiki page: front matter keys, registered source slugs, relative links to planned or known pages, footnote definitions, bit-field JSON, balanced code fences and length. tools/build_explorer.py Reads a directory of MIB ASCII tables (plus the synthetic folder and the extra Solar Orbiter tables) and writes the JSON data of the MIB explorer: indexes of parameters, packets, commands, sequences and calibrations, detail records bucketed by an FNV hash, verification stages, and optionally a diff against an older release. tools/mib_columns.json Column order for all 53 tables: 36 in pyscos2000 order with ICD 7.0 names, 17 from the ICD 7.0 text, plus the list of name differences above. tools/pyscos2000_schema_icd72.json The introspected pyscos2000 schema. tools/build_pages.py Generates the data-driven pages: the library pages, the reference catalogue, the MIB table reference pages, the sources-and-copies page, the glossary and its abbreviation tooltips, and the field descriptions used by the explorer. tools/build_nav.py Writes the explicit navigation into mkdocs.yml, taking page titles from the front matter. tools/plan.json The page plan of the wiki.

The read-only SQLite copies of the Solar Orbiter MIBs used for every query on these pages name each table after its .dat file. They use the pyscos2000 column names where available and COL1…COLn in file order for the other tables, and hold the synthetic definitions in a table synthetic(NAME, SOURCE).45 The script that produced the SQLite files is not among the repository's tools.

docs.title: Choosing a tool
docs.text:
Need Tool in the sources Edit a mission MIB with forms and referential integrity an off-line relational database or editor (ESOC's MS-Access editor in the 2000s; mission databases such as HPSDB) Check a MIB before import the SCOS-2000 importer's "check only" option and the off-line consistency checker; in Python, pyscos2000's checkers Load a MIB into a non-SCOS checkout system the SRDB Translator (ECHO), Terma CCS5/TSC Recognise housekeeping packets defined on board during a test Terma CCS5 DYNHK Run an open-source control system on a MIB Yamcs with the yamcs-scos2k loader (no delta, event or status-consistency checks, no command stacks) Read a MIB in Python pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2 schemas); SpacePyLibrary (nine tables, ICD 6.9) Decode PUS packets with a MIB scospus Decode archived SCOS-2000 packet headers SCOSpy Create a MIB from flight-software C headers mib-generator Parse EDDS XML deliveries edds_process Decode CCSDS packets from an XTCE file Yamcs, OpenC3 COSMOS, Space Packet Parser Decode or build CCSDS/PUS packets described in code CCSDSPy, spacepackets Browse the public Solar Orbiter MIB this site's MIB explorer

Rows summarise the sections above.

Each page lists every field in ICD order, with its type, whether it is mandatory, its meaning and allowed values, foreign keys, history across ICD issues, and how it is filled in the real Solar Orbiter MIB. Field definitions come from the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 7.0, cross-checked against the open-source pyscos2000 schema (based on issue 7.2) and the data. For concepts, start with The MIB and the data model.

docs.title: asw_sw_para.dat: Flight-software names of MIB items (inferred title)
docs.text:
not defined in the ICD105,222 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Inference

This table is not defined by the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD. Its column meanings below were inferred from the data and are this wiki's interpretation.

Inferred from the data; not documented in any available ICD. Solar Orbiter's MIB delivers this extra file next to the ICD tables, as the ICD allows mission-specific extensions. Each record maps one MIB item name (column 1) to the symbolic name the item has in the on-board application software or instrument software (column 2) and to a longer free-text description (column 3). Most names in column 1 are monitoring parameters (pcf.PCF_NAME, 77,565 of 105,222 rows in the 2025 release); others are command parameters (cpc), commands (ccf), textual calibrations (txf, paf) and range sets (prf). About 21,400 names match no table of the same release; their prefixes (e.g. BCAY, YIU5, YTCV) suggest items of software or instrument databases not delivered in the public MIB. Column 2 holds names such as AOCSCORE_STRUNITA_QUAT_LSB or HKD_TTRCPLR_TTRA_PIO_REGISTER__WATCHDOGASTATUS; when no software name exists, column 1 is repeated. SCOS-2000 itself does not read this file (it is outside the ICD); it is most likely used by mission tools to trace MIB items to software documentation. That last point is an inference.

Key: COL1
tags: Solar Orbiter mission-specific tables (not in the ICD)

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1COL1Char (max 10 characters observed)MInferred: name of the MIB item described by the record. Unique in every release (105,222 distinct values in 105,222 rows of the 2025 release). Matches pcf.PCF_NAME (77,565 rows), cpc.CPC_PNAME (3,676), ccf.CCF_CNAME (2,221), txf.TXF_NUMBR (208), prf.PRF_NUMBR (77) and paf.PAF_NUMBR (52); 21,423 names match none of these tables in the same release.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME | cpc.CPC_PNAME | ccf.CCF_CNAME | txf.TXF_NUMBR | paf.PAF_NUMBR | prf.PRF_NUMBR (polymorphic, inferred). Solar Orbiter: filled in 105,222 of 105,222 rows; e.g. BCAY0000, BCAY0001, BCAY0002, BCAY0004, BCAY0007 2COL2Char (max 122 characters observed)OInferred: symbolic name of the item in the flight or instrument software (e.g. data-pool or ICD mnemonic). docs.title: caf.dat: Numerical calibrations
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.2679 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

caf defines numerical calibration curves, i.e. piecewise-linear point-pair calibrations that convert a parameter's raw value into an engineering value. It holds one record per curve; the raw/engineering point pairs themselves are in cap. A curve can be shared by any number of monitoring parameters, which reference it through PCF_CURTX (single calibration) or CUR_SELECT (conditional calibration). The record declares the numeric formats of the engineering and raw values stored in cap, the radix used to write unsigned raw values, an optional unit for consistency checks against PCF_UNIT, the number of points and the extrapolation behaviour. SCOS-2000 attaches the extrapolation behaviour to the curve (CAF_INTER), not to the parameter, so every parameter using a curve extrapolates in the same way; a copy of the curve with a different flag is needed if two parameters need different behaviour. Calibration applies only to parameters whose raw representation is numerical (no strings or times), including user defined constants and synthetic parameters, whose computed value is treated as raw (section 3.3.2.2, p. 62).1

Key: CAF_NUMBR

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 ('Numerical calibration curves: caf', p. 32) has seven fields with CAF_NUMBR as Number(4). ICD 6.0 changed calibration identifiers from Number(4) to Char(10) (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247; also listed under 6.2/6.3, p. 253). CAF_INTER existed in SCOS-2000 since R4 but was first documented in ICD 6.7 (S2K-SPR-4911, p. 259); ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 63) and 6.9 (p. 66) describe it as an interpolation/extrapolation switch ('P' interpolate/extrapolate, 'F' disabled) with default F. ICD 7.0 rewrote the description to make clear that the curve's flag, not PCF_INTER, governs extrapolation (S2K-8325, p. 261). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same eight fields, key and defaults (CAF_INTER default 'F').

Notes from the extraction

No structural discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 679 curves, all with real engineering format (CAF_ENGFMT 'R'); raw formats U (612, all with radix 'D'), I (66) and R (1). CAF_INTER is empty in every record, so the import default 'F' (no extrapolation) applies to all curves. CAF_NCURVE matches the actual number of cap points for all 679 curves (2 to 1,024 points). No CAF_NUMBR collides with an MCF_IDENT. 76 curves are referenced neither by PCF_CURTX nor by CUR_SELECT. Where both units are given, CAF_UNIT always equals the PCF_UNIT of the parameters that reference the curve through PCF_CURTX. Identifiers follow a 10-character pattern such as CAHP0000TM (the naming convention itself is not documented in the ICD).

docs.title: cap.dat: Numerical calibrations definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.37,830 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

cap holds the points of the numerical calibration curves declared in caf: one record per raw/engineering value pair. SCOS-2000 calibrates a raw value by locating it between two consecutive points of the curve and interpolating linearly between them (as the CAF_INTER description of ICD 6.7/6.9 explains). Outside the range covered by the points it either extrapolates from the first or last two points or returns an invalid value, depending on the curve's CAF_INTER flag. Raw values are written in the format declared by CAF_RAWFMT and, for unsigned integers, in the radix given by CAF_RADIX. Engineering values follow CAF_ENGFMT and are always decimal, even when they are unsigned integers. Because the key is the pair (CAP_NUMBR, CAP_XVALS), a curve cannot contain two points with the same raw value. The number of records per curve should agree with CAF_NCURVE.1

Key: CAP_NUMBR, CAP_XVALS

Unsigned integer raw values (CAF_RAWFMT = 'U') must be written in the radix of the curve (CAF_RADIX).Solar Orbiter: filled in 7,830 of 7,830 rows; e.g. 0, 4095, 255, -32768, 32767 ICD PDF p. 68 3CAP_YVALSChar(14)MEngineering value of the calibration point, written in a format compatible with CAF_ENGFMT. All engineering values, including unsigned integers, are written in decimal whatever the curve's CAF_RADIX.Solar Orbiter: filled in 7,830 of 7,830 rows; e.g. 0, 0.0201, 0.1001, 0.05, 1.002 ICD PDF p. 68

docs.title: cca.dat: Numerical (de-)calibration curves
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.6.199 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cca table defines the numerical (de-)calibration curves used for command and sequence parameters, one record per curve; the points of each curve are in CCS. A parameter with calibration category C (CPC_CATEG or CSP_CATEG) references one curve through CPC_CCAREF or CSP_CCAREF, and a curve may be shared by many parameters (many-to-one). Unlike the monitoring calibrations (CAF/CAP, TXF/TXP), the commanding (de-)calibrations work in both directions: engineering to raw, for display and for encoding, and raw to engineering, for display. They can be attached to command parameters (CPC) and to sequence formal parameters (CSP) alike, but only to parameters whose raw value is numerical (not strings or times). The record states the numeric format of the engineering values (signed, unsigned or real) and of the raw values, which must be compatible with the engineering display format and the type of the parameters using the curve, and the radix in which unsigned raw values are written in CCS. To avoid ambiguity when an operator types an engineering value, the ICD requires curves to give a one-to-one correspondence between raw and engineering values. The unit and the number of points are informative, for off-line consistency checks.1

Key: CCA_NUMBR

docs.title: ccf.dat: Command characteristics
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.2.15,454 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The ccf table is the master list of telecommands, one record per command, and is the central entity of the SCOS-2000 commanding data. A command may target the spacecraft or another control domain such as ground equipment, and since SCOS-2000 R5.0 it may also be an SLE or NIS throw event. The record gives the command name and descriptions, the packet header to use (CCF_PKTID), the values that fill the header placeholders (service type and subtype, APID, acknowledgement flags), special command types such as control frames, control segments or packets without error control, and the default operational attributes applied when the command is loaded on a command source: criticality, plannability by external sources, stand-alone loading, interlock scope and stage, high priority with forced MAP ID, default parameter value set, redundant APID and default on-board sub-schedule. The layout of the application data is given by CDF (elements) and CPC (parameters); static pre-transmission validation by PTV; verification stages through CVP/CVS/CVE; parameter sets through PSM. Only parameter values, not fixed areas, appear in the command history. Encoded commands are limited by the MISCconfig variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (default 248 bytes), from which the header, the CRC (CMD_CRC_SIZE, default 2 bytes) and, for time-tagged commands, the TC(11,4) wrapper defined by CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME (default 20 bytes) are deducted; that wrapper command must itself be defined in CCF and CDF.1

Key: CCF_CNAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CCF_CNAMEChar(8)MUnique name (mnemonic) of the command. It is the key referenced by CDF_CNAME (command structure), PTV_CNAME (pre-transmission validation), CVP_TASK (verification profile), PSM_NAME (parameter sets), CSS_ELEMID (use of the command in a sequence) and by the default values of command or sequence parameters of type 'Command ID'.Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,454 of 5,454 rows; e.g. EGENRTCC, EGENRTCO, EGENRTMC, EGENRTMO, ESESIONC ICD PDF p. 133 2CCF_DESCRChar(24)MShort textual description of the command, up to 24 characters, shown alongside the command name in SCOS-2000 displays.Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,454 of 5,454 rows; e.g. Dummy commands, Add Func Mon to the Mon List, Add HK Paras to Existing HK Def, Add param monitor exp.value (sint16), Add param monitor exp.value (sint32) ICD PDF p. 133 3CCF_DESCR2Char(64)ODetailed description of the command, up to 64 characters. Printed with a grey background in ICD 7.0, meaning that SCOS-2000 does not use the field for any processing.Solar Orbiter: filled in 2,554 of 5,454 rows; e.g. Defined by user, This telecommand clears the Monitoring List contents. ICD PDF p. 133 4CCF_CTYPEChar(8)OCommand type. For missions following the Packet Telecommand Standard it flags special commands that are not ordinary TC packets. For control segments (R) and control frames (F) the PCDF/CDF entries of the command describe the frame data field instead of a packet header plus application data; the ICD strongly recommends giving BC frames (Unlock, Set V(R)) a global interlock (CCF_ILSCOPE='G') waiting at least on the uplink stage (CCF_ILSTAGE='U'), so that no further command is released before the releaser has completed the AD-mode set-up. Type S marks a command packet without Packet Error Control field, whereas for normal commands the releaser appends a 16-bit CRC; this is typically used by EGSE systems for non-spacecraft commands. Types T and N are throw events (since R5.0): they are never uplinked, and their PCDF/CDF entries define the event identifier and following fields of the throw-event data unit described in the SLE and NIS interface documents; throw events cannot be blocked with other entries in a sequence or command source. For any other command the field may be empty or contain any mission-specific string that does not match R, F, S, T or N.

  • F Control Frame (BC frame, e.g. Unlock or Set V(R)); PCDF/CDF define the frame data field.
  • S Command packet without Packet Error Control field (no CRC appended by the releaser); typical for EGSE non-spacecraft commands.

  • N NIS Throw Event: executed by the NIS and not forwarded to the ground station; PCDF/CDF define the Event ID and following fields (Table 3.2 of the NIS reference).

  • L Only the local commanding source is interlocked.
  • S Local commanding is interlocked for the subsystem the command belongs to.
  • B Global commanding is interlocked only for the subsystem the command belongs to (printed in italics in ICD 7.0, i.e. not currently supported by SCOS-2000).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.2.1, PDF p.62-66) defines the first 20 fields with the same names, sizes and defaults, but CCF_CTYPE only has the special values R, F and S and CCF_ILSCOPE only G, L, S, B, N. CCF_SUBSCHEDID (field 21) was added in ICD 6.0 together with CSF_SUBSCHEDID (Annex 1 of ICD 7.0, PDF p.249) and is present in ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.124-131) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.129-135). The throw-event types were added to CCF_CTYPE for R5.0: SLE throw events in ICD 6.4 and NIS throw events in ICD 6.5 (Annex 1, PDF p.254 and p.256). ICD 6.0 also documented that acknowledgement flags can be changed to disable report-based verification (PDF p.250); ICD 6.6 added that high-priority commands cannot be blocked (S2K-50-DCR-1023, PDF p.257). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.132-140) added options F and T to CCF_ILSCOPE, which the software already supported (S2K-8560, PDF p.262), and added the explanations of the maximum command size and of the TC(11,4) time-tag wrapper MISC variables (S2K-8063, S2K-8226, PDF p.262-263). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same 21 columns in the same order, names the last one CCF_SUBSCHEDID, marks CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR and CCF_PKTID as mandatory and keeps the defaults N, N, Y, N, C and N for CCF_CRITICAL, CCF_PLAN, CCF_EXEC, CCF_ILSCOPE, CCF_ILSTAGE and CCF_HIPRI.

Notes from the extraction

Columns of ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 (7.2) and the Solar Orbiter ccf.dat (21 tab-separated columns in all 5454 lines) match one to one; the only naming difference is that the ICD 7.0 PDF text splits the last name as 'CCF_SUBSCHED ID'. Observations on the 2025-09-16 Solar Orbiter data: (1) CCF_DESCR exceeds the ICD 7.0 size of 24 characters in 2876 records (up to 40 characters); according to ICD 7.0 section 2.4 (PDF p.23) the importer truncates over-long fields with a warning, so either the target system accepts longer descriptions or the text is truncated on import (not stated in the available sources). (2) CCF_ILSTAGE='N' appears in the 5 NO_HDR directives (UNLOCK, SETVR, RESET, REIN_TTR, TC_ONLY); 'N' is not an ICD 7.0 option for this field. (3) CCF_CTYPE is used only for 2 control frames ('F': UNLOCK, SETVR), 3 control segments ('R': RESET, REIN_TTR, TC_ONLY) and 6 NIS throw events ('N': link and session open/close, APID 1964, type 251 subtype 1, header NOS2KHDR); these 6 throw events leave CCF_CRITICAL, CCF_EXEC and CCF_ILSTAGE empty and are the only commands with CCF_PLAN='A'. (4) CCF_MAPID is filled in 205 records with CCF_HIPRI='N' (values 1 and 54), where the ICD says it is irrelevant; the 125 HPC1_TC commands are high priority with MAP ID 0 and have no type, subtype or ack (their header has no T/S/K elements). (5) CCF_SUBSCHEDID equals CCF_SUBSYS in every record. (6) CCF_DEFSET and CCF_RAPID are never used (PST/PSV are empty). (7) 443 commands have no CDF record, consistent with CCF_NPARS=0. In the 2020-04-16 release ccf has 5238 records.

docs.title: ccs.dat: Numerical (de-)calibration curves definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.6.21,226 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The ccs table holds the points of the commanding numerical (de-)calibration curves declared in CCA, one record per engineering/raw value pair. Each pair links an engineering value to the raw value that is encoded in the command; SCOS-2000 uses the set of pairs of a curve to convert an engineering value entered by the user into the raw value to be encoded, and raw values back to engineering values for display. Contrary to the monitoring calibration tables (CAP), where the raw value comes first, here the engineering value is in the X column (CCS_XVALS) and the raw value in the Y column (CCS_YVALS). Engineering values are always written in decimal, whereas unsigned raw values use the radix declared for the curve (CCA_RADIX). Because the curve must be invertible without ambiguity, each engineering value should correspond to exactly one raw value and vice versa; the key (curve name plus raw value) prevents the same raw value from appearing twice in a curve. The value fields have no fixed size: their maximum length follows from the maximum command size.1

Key: CCS_NUMBR, CCS_YVALS

All values, unsigned integers included, are written in decimal whatever the curve radix (CCA_RADIX). Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,226 of 1,226 rows; e.g. 0, 1, 4, 0.25, 0.999984741 ICD PDF p. 208 3CCS_YVALSCharMRaw value of the point, in a format compatible with CCA_RAWFMT; unsigned integer raw values (CCA_RAWFMT=U) are written in the radix CCA_RADIX. Part of the key. Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,226 of 1,226 rows; e.g. 0, 255, 65535, -32768, 32767 ICD PDF p. 208

docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.6.2, PDF p.100-101): CCS_NUMBR Number(4), CCS_XVALS and CCS_YVALS Char(17), key CCS_NUMBR + CCS_YVALS. docs.title: cdf.dat: Commands definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.2.347,609 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cdf table defines the structure of each command's application data field, one record per command element. An element is either a fixed area (constant bits, possibly padding or unused bits) or an instance of a command parameter from CPC, which may be fixed (non-editable) or editable. Elements are encoded back to back with no gaps, in the order of their bit offsets, so every bit of the raw command after the packet header must be covered. The table supports PUS variable-length commands through repeated groups: a counter parameter (e.g. N) with a non-zero group size precedes a group of following elements that is repeated N times when the command is loaded, nested groups being expanded left to right; a fixed counter with a non-zero group size forces the expansion without prompting the user. Each editable element may carry a static default and, optionally, a dynamic default taken from a monitoring parameter (for instance a User Defined Constant controlled from TM SPACON), which replaces the static value after loading until an explicit value is entered. Default values can also be inherited from CPC_DEFVAL. Since R4.2 commands with group repeaters can be used in sequences only if all repeated values are fixed in the database. The structure also serves on-board control directives and throw events (see CCF_CTYPE).1

Key: CDF_CNAME, CDF_BIT, CDF_GRPSIZE

For fixed or editable parameters SCOS-2000 ignores it, because the length follows from the PTC/PFC of the referenced parameter, but it should still be filled correctly so that the consistency of command and parameter definitions can be checked. docs.text:

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.2.3, PDF p.70-73) has the same ten fields, but the key is only CDF_CNAME + CDF_BIT, CDF_VALUE is Char(17), and fixed areas and group repeaters both had to be hexadecimal. In ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.141-148) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.145-153) CDF_GRPSIZE is a key field (when non-zero). ICD 6.1 clarified that fixed areas must not be used for Service 11 elements processed for ground modelling and that 0 is allowed for group repeaters (Annex 1, PDF p.251); ICD 6.4 restricted dynamic defaults to parameters processed by the TM model (PDF p.254); ICD 6.6 defined the allowed CDF_ELTYPE/SDF_FTYPE combinations (S2K-SPR-3400, PDF p.257). In ICD 6.9 the 32-bit maximum (FFFF FFFF) was stated for CDF_VALUE as a whole; ICD 7.0 (PDF p.151-159) restricts it to fixed areas (S2K-8782, PDF p.263) and makes CDF_VALUE variable-length, bounded by the command size (S2K-8073, PDF p.261). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same ten columns in the same order, mandatory CDF_CNAME, CDF_ELTYPE, CDF_ELLEN and CDF_BIT, and defaults 0 for CDF_GRPSIZE and R for CDF_INTER, but marks only CDF_CNAME as key.

Notes from the extraction

Columns match between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter cdf.dat (10 columns in all 47609 lines). Key discrepancy: ICD 7.0 keys on CDF_CNAME + CDF_BIT (+ CDF_GRPSIZE when non-zero), while pyscos2000 flags only CDF_CNAME as key (necessarily incomplete, since a command has many elements). The Herschel HCSS tailoring note (point 5.2.9, PDF p.13 of hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note) further assumed that CDF_CNAME + CDF_PNAME is unique, repeated groups being the way to repeat a parameter. Solar Orbiter 2025: no duplicate (CDF_CNAME, CDF_BIT, CDF_GRPSIZE); element types F 17681, A 16906, E 13022; 569 group repeaters (CDF_GRPSIZE from 1 to 48); 48 variable-length parameter instances (PTC 7 or 8 with PFC 0) all with CDF_ELLEN=0 as required. CDF_INTER is empty for 1614 fixed areas and 'R' for the other 15292 (irrelevant for fixed areas). Editable parameters: 4863 take the CPC default (D), 5876 raw, 2283 engineering; 4959 editable raw entries have no value, i.e. the operator must supply it. Dynamic defaults are never used (CDF_TMID always empty, no CDF_INTER='T'). CDF_GRPSIZE is empty in 33 records (import default 0). All CDF_CNAME and CDF_PNAME values resolve to CCF and CPC records. 44944 records in 2020.

docs.title: cpc.dat: Command parameters
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.2.27,155 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cpc table defines the command parameters, one record per parameter. A command parameter is any part of a command's application data whose value has to be edited, calibrated or checked; it can be reused in any number of command definitions, where CDF places each instance. The record gives the parameter type and length (PTC/PFC pair, see Appendix A of the ICD), how engineering values are entered and displayed, the default radix for unsigned raw values, the engineering unit, the kind of calibration or special processing (numeric, textual, 'Command ID' or 'Parameter ID'), references to a range-check set (PRF), a numeric (de-)calibration curve (CCA) or a textual (de-)calibration (PAF), and a default value with its representation. Default values can be given at three levels - parameter (CPC_DEFVAL), command definition (CDF_VALUE) and sequence (SDF_VALUE) - and the 'D' options of CDF_INTER and SDF_VTYPE propagate the lower-level default upwards, so a value can be maintained centrally. Special PUS-oriented types are supported: 'Command ID' parameters encode the raw packet of another command as a variable octet string; 'Parameter ID' parameters encode the on-board identifier of a telemetry parameter; and, since R5, 'Deduced' parameters (PTC=11) inherit type, width and calibration from a TM parameter named by a preceding 'Parameter ID' parameter in the same (repeated) group. Time parameters can be time-correlated using a selected on-board clock.1

Key: CPC_PNAME

As from SCOS-2000 R5 the value 11 denotes a 'Deduced' parameter whose characteristics (type, calibration) are inherited from a TM parameter specified in the same command definition.Solar Orbiter: filled in 7,155 of 7,155 rows; e.g. 3, 2, 5, 1, 4 ICD PDF p. 144 4CPC_PFCNumber(5)MParameter Format Code: together with CPC_PTC it determines the length of the parameter, and its range must be compatible with the PTC as listed in Appendix A.
