Default D. Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,350 of 7,155 rows; e.g. D, H ICD PDF p. 145 7CPC_UNITChar(4)OEngineering unit mnemonic (for example VOLT) displayed next to the parameter value. CCA_UNIT and PRF_UNIT are checked against it for consistency in the off-line database.Solar Orbiter: filled in 458 of 7,155 rows; e.g. mA, ms, s, degC, deg ICD PDF p. 146 8CPC_CATEGChar(1)OKind of calibration or special processing applied to the parameter. It must be empty or N for parameters whose raw value is not numeric (strings, times) unless they are 'Command ID' or 'Parameter ID' parameters, and it is not used for 'Deduced' parameters, whose calibration comes from the associated TM parameter. It determines which of CPC_CCAREF and CPC_PAFREF must be filled and whether engineering representations (option E of CPC_INTER, CDF_INTER, SDF_VTYPE, PRF_INTER) may be used.
  • C Numeric (de-)calibration: CPC_CCAREF must be filled.
  • T Textual (de-)calibration: CPC_PAFREF must be filled.
  • B Both calibrations (not yet supported by SCOS-2000; italic in ICD 7.0).
  • A 'Command ID' parameter: value encoded as the raw data of a named command; requires PTC=7 and PFC=0.
  • P 'Parameter ID' parameter: value encoded as the on-board identifier (PCF_PID) of a named TM parameter; requires PTC=3.
  • N No calibration and no special processing (import default).
Default N. Solar Orbiter: filled in 7,096 of 7,155 rows; e.g. N, T, C, P, A ICD PDF p. 146 9CPC_PRFREFChar(10)OName of the parameter range set (PRF_NUMBR) that restricts the allowed values of the parameter. The representation of the range set (PRF_DSPFMT) must be compatible with the parameter type: with CPC_PTC if the ranges are raw (PRF_INTER=R), or with CPC_DISPFMT if they are engineering. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.Refers to prf.PRF_NUMBR. Solar Orbiter: filled in 694 of 7,155 rows; e.g. VIPDID00, VSM00006, VCD00176, VCD00186, VCD00187 ICD PDF p. 147 10CPC_CCAREFChar(10)OName of the numeric (de-)calibration curve (CCA_NUMBR) used to convert between engineering and raw values. The raw and engineering formats of the curve (CCA_RAWFMT, CCA_ENGFMT) must be compatible with CPC_PTC and CPC_DISPFMT. It must be empty if CPC_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or T, and must be filled if CPC_CATEG is C or B. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.Refers to cca.CCA_NUMBR. Solar Orbiter: filled in 327 of 7,155 rows; e.g. CAHP0003TC, CIWP0033TC, CAHP0007TC, CAMP0003TC, CAMP0007TC ICD PDF p. 147 11CPC_PAFREFChar(10)OName of the textual (de-)calibration, i.e. alias set (PAF_NUMBR), associated with the parameter; its aliases may also serve as default values. The raw format of the alias set (PAF_RAWFMT) must be compatible with CPC_PTC. It must be empty if CPC_CATEG is empty, A, P, N or C, and must be filled if CPC_CATEG is T or B. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.Refers to paf.PAF_NUMBR. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,624 of 7,155 rows; e.g. CIWT0006TC, CRUT0010TC, CAAT0031TC, CAHT0000TC, CAMT0000TC ICD PDF p. 148 12CPC_INTERChar(1)ORepresentation in which CPC_DEFVAL is written. Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.
  • R Default value is a raw value (import default).
  • E Default value is an engineering value; allowed only for calibrated parameters (CPC_CATEG T or C).
Default R. Solar Orbiter: filled in 7,155 of 7,155 rows; e.g. R, E ICD PDF p. 148 13CPC_DEFVALCharOParameter-level default value, used whenever a CDF entry asks for it (CDF_INTER='D'); useful when the same default must apply to every instance of the parameter in every command. Its maximum length is not fixed but depends on the maximum command size (section 3.3.3.2). It must be written in the representation chosen by CPC_INTER: raw values in a format compatible with CPC_PTC (and CPC_RADIX for unsigned integers), engineering values in a format compatible with CPC_DISPFMT. For a 'Command ID' parameter it must name a command (CCF_CNAME) whose parameters all have default values, so that it can be encoded without user input; for a 'Parameter ID' parameter it must name a monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) that has an on-board identifier (PCF_PID not empty). Not used for 'Deduced' parameters.Refers to ccf.CCF_CNAME / pcf.PCF_NAME (for CATEG A / P). Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,230 of 7,155 rows; e.g. 0, Not_Set, Set, 00, Disabled ICD PDF p. 149 14CPC_CORRChar(1)OStates whether an absolute time parameter is time-correlated, using the applicable time correlation coefficients, when its raw value is interpreted. For relative time parameters (PTC=10) it must be set explicitly to N. CPC_OBTID selects which on-board clock format and correlation apply; without correlation, the on-board time format must still be known to establish the time reference (the absolute time corresponding to zero), and if no OBT ID is given and correlation is off, the epoch is defined by the MISCconfig variable TCO_ESA_EPOCH. (The ICD text refers to PCF_PTC and PCF_CORR in this description, an evident copy from the PCF table.)
  • Y Apply time correlation (import default).
  • N Extract the time value without time correlation; mandatory for relative times.
Default Y. Solar Orbiter: filled in 13 of 7,155 rows; e.g. Y, N ICD PDF p. 150 15CPC_OBTIDNumber(5)OIdentifier of the on-board time (OBT) used to encode/interpret time parameters, either to apply the time correlation or to define the time format and in particular its epoch. The OBT ID is a SCOS-2000 configuration identifier for each on-board clock of the mission; with N clocks it takes values 1 to N. If not given, the mission default OBT ID set by the MISCconfig variable TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID is used.Default 0. ICD PDF p. 150 16CPC_ENDIANChar(1)OFuture extension (grey and italic in ICD 7.0, so not used by any SCOS-2000 version, as also stated by change S2K-7749). It is meant to give the byte order of parameters whose length is a whole number of octets; the conversion would be possible for signed and unsigned integers, strings, octet strings, absolute and relative times.
  • B Big endian, most significant byte first (import default).
  • L Little endian, least significant byte first.
Default B. Solar Orbiter: filled in 0 of 7,155 rows ICD PDF p. 151

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CPC_PNAME → cdf.CDF_PNAME: Instances of the parameter in command definitions (many-to-many between CCF and CPC through CDF).
  • CPC_PRFREF → prf.PRF_NUMBR: Range set used to check values (many parameters may share a set).
  • CPC_CCAREF → cca.CCA_NUMBR: Numeric (de-)calibration curve, required when CPC_CATEG=C.
  • CPC_PAFREF → paf.PAF_NUMBR: Textual (de-)calibration (alias set), required when CPC_CATEG=T.
  • CPC_DEFVAL → ccf.CCF_CNAME / pcf.PCF_NAME: For 'Command ID' (CATEG=A) the default names a fully defaulted command; for 'Parameter ID' (CATEG=P) a monitoring parameter with PCF_PID.
  • CPC_UNIT → cca.CCA_UNIT / prf.PRF_UNIT: Units of the referenced curve or range set are checked for consistency.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.2.2, PDF p.67-70) has 13 fields: CPC_PRFREF, CPC_CCAREF and CPC_PAFREF are Number(4), CPC_DEFVAL is Char(17), and CPC_CATEG offers only C, T, B and N. ICD 6.0 introduced the 'Command ID' and 'Parameter ID' categories A and P (Annex 1, PDF p.249) and later changed the calibration and range identifiers to Char(10) (PDF p.247 and p.253); 'Deduced' parameters (PTC=11) came with ICD 6.4 for R5.0 (PDF p.254). CPC_CORR and CPC_OBTID were added in ICD 6.7 for R5.2 (S2K-SCR-4917, PDF p.258) and the CPC_OBTID description updated in 6.9 (S2K-DCR-5743, PDF p.260); ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.133-140) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.137-145) therefore have 15 fields. ICD 7.0 (PDF p.142-151) made CPC_DEFVAL variable-length, bounded by the maximum command size (S2K-8073, PDF p.261), stated that CPC_CORR must be N for relative times (S2K-8778, PDF p.263; ICD 6.9 had spoken of absolute or relative times), and added CPC_ENDIAN as field 16 for future use (S2K-7749, PDF p.262). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) lists 17 columns: it names the key CPC_NAME, field 15 CPC_OBTIP, inserts CPC_DESCR2 (default empty string) as field 16 and moves CPC_ENDIAN (default B) to field 17.

Notes from the extraction

Several discrepancies. (1) Names: ICD 7.0 (and 5.1, 6.7, 6.9) call the key CPC_PNAME, whereas pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter SQLite use CPC_NAME; ICD 7.0 field 15 is CPC_OBTID, whereas pyscos2000 and the SQLite use CPC_OBTIP (apparently a misspelling). (2) Order/content: ICD 7.0 has 16 fields ending with CPC_ENDIAN; pyscos2000 (7.2) has CPC_DESCR2 at position 16 and CPC_ENDIAN at 17. A 16-column cpc.dat would therefore be read differently by the two schemas. (3) The Solar Orbiter cpc.dat files (2020 and 2025) have only 15 columns, i.e. the ICD 6.7/6.9 layout; CPC_DESCR2 and CPC_ENDIAN exist in the SQLite only because of the pyscos2000 schema and are empty in every record, and CPC_OBTIP (CPC_OBTID) is also never filled. (4) No record uses PTC=11 ('Deduced'). Time parameters are PTC=9 with PFC 15 or 17 (58 records) and one PTC=10/PFC=17 relative time (PCD0B071, CPC_CORR='N', as ICD 7.0 requires); these 59 time parameters leave CPC_CATEG empty, as allowed. (5) CPC_CORR='Y' is set on 12 non-time parameters (ENISTE*, PTC 2, 3 or 8) used only by the 6 NIS throw-event commands, where the ICD gives the flag no meaning. (6) Category usage in 2025: N 4991, T 1624 (all with CPC_DISPFMT='A'), C 327, P 152 (all PTC=3/PFC=14, i.e. 32-bit parameter IDs), A 2 (PCD0B044 and PCD13013, PTC=7/PFC=0, as required). (7) 316 records use CPC_INTER='E' (311 textual, 5 numeric), consistent with the rule that E needs a calibration. (8) All CPC_PRFREF, CPC_CCAREF and CPC_PAFREF values resolve to existing PRF, CCA and PAF records; every CPC_UNIT of a numerically calibrated parameter equals the unit of its curve. 7155 records in 2025, 6947 in 2020.

docs.title: cps.dat: Parameter sets definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5.30 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Parameter sets are named collections of command or sequence parameters for which predefined combinations of values, called parameter value sets, can be stored in the database and then applied in the real-time environment to give a value to every contained parameter with one high-level mnemonic (ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5, PDF p.200-201). The cps table can list explicitly the parameters contained in each parameter set: one record per member parameter, naming the set, the command parameter or sequence formal parameter, and the parameter's bit offset (commands) or position (sequences), which identifies it uniquely within the set. SCOS-2000 itself does not use this table, because parameter sets are defined by pst and populated through pvs. It is meant for the off-line database system, where it can be used to check that the associated parameter value sets are complete, that is, that every value set supplies the expected parameters.1

Key: CPS_NAME, CPS_BIT

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CPS_NAMEChar(8)MName of a parameter set (PST_NAME). Part of the key.Refers to pst.PST_NAME. ICD PDF p. 202 2CPS_PARChar(8)MName of a command parameter (CDF_PNAME) or of a sequence formal parameter (CSP_FPNAME) that belongs to the set given in CPS_NAME.Refers to cdf.CDF_PNAME / csp.CSP_FPNAME. ICD PDF p. 202 3CPS_BITNumber(4)MUnique identification of the parameter within the set: for command parameters, its bit offset in the command (CDF_BIT); for sequence parameters, its position (CSP_FPNUM). Part of the key.Refers to cdf.CDF_BIT / csp.CSP_FPNUM. ICD PDF p. 202

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CPS_NAME → pst.PST_NAME: Owning parameter set.
  • CPS_PAR → cdf.CDF_PNAME / csp.CSP_FPNAME: Member parameter; with CPS_BIT it identifies a specific occurrence.
  • CPS_BIT → cdf.CDF_BIT / csp.CSP_FPNUM: Same convention as pvs.PVS_BIT.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
The parameter-set tables appear with the same section numbers (§3.3.3.5.x) in ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.97-99), ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.188-192), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.193-197) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.200-205). In ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.97-98) none of the three cps fields is marked mandatory, not even the key fields. ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.189), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.194) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.202) mark all three 'M'. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

The database stores only a placeholder COL1 (no rows), because the file is empty. The file is empty (0 bytes) in the 2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16 Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB. Consistently, CCF_DEFSET is empty in all 5454 ccf rows of the 2025 release and SDF_VALSET is empty in all sdf rows, so Solar Orbiter does not use parameter sets in its MIB. The HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note says the HCSS (Herschel) ingestion ignores PST, PSV, CPS and PVS (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note, §5.2.11, PDF p.14), and the HPSDB note marks all five parameter-set tables 'not supported by CCS, do not use' (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, §5.3.16-5.3.20, PDF p.39-40). pyscos2000 has no cps model, consistent with the ICD statement that SCOS-2000 does not use the table.

docs.title: csf.dat: Command sequence characteristics
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.3.13,404 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The csf table is the top level of the command sequence definitions: one record per sequence, giving its name, descriptions and global attributes. A sequence is an ordered list of elements (commands or other sequences, nested to any depth but never containing itself) whose release and execution times, grouping and interlocks are defined in CSS; the values of the element parameters are given in SDF and the sequence's own 'formal parameters' (placeholders that let one definition serve as a template) in CSP. CSF says whether the sequence carries execution time-tagged commands and how the user loads it, its criticality, which external sources may plan it, whether it may be loaded stand-alone, its subsystem, provenance information (generation time, source document, issue and date), a default parameter value set and a default on-board sub-schedule. A nested sequence is expanded like a macro-command when the parent is loaded on a command source. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 these tables are converted on request into XML sequence definitions held in the FARC rather than the run-time MIB, imported as a delta without re-importing the TM/TC database.1

Key: CSF_NAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CSF_NAMEChar(8)MUnique name of the command sequence. Referenced by CSS_SQNAME, SDF_SQNAME and CSP_SQNAME (content of the sequence), by CSS_ELEMID when the sequence is nested in another one (CSS_TYPE=S), and by PSM_NAME and CVP_TASK.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. AACC160A, AACC160B, AACC161A, AACC161B, AACC250A ICD PDF p. 165 2CSF_DESCChar(24)MShort textual description of the sequence.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. Calibrate Slit Mech v07, EPD SIS Stop Macro v01, EUI HTRs Off Config v01, EUI Prep to Safe v01, EUI to Config v01 ICD PDF p. 165 3CSF_DESC2Char(64)ODetailed description of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.Solar Orbiter: filled in 726 of 3,404 rows; e.g. Execute Emergency TCM-3d, Average multiple datasets, Configuration of UVDA Analog, EUI: Change Mode to Config, EUI: Preparation to transition to Safe ICD PDF p. 165 4CSF_IFTTChar(1)OStates whether the sequence (or any nested sequence) contains execution time-tagged commands, and therefore how the user is asked for times when loading it.
  • Y The sequence contains execution time-tagged commands; at load time the user gives an absolute reference time from which all execution time tags are computed. Use this when commands are to be loaded on a manual stack with both a release time and an execution time tag.
  • B At load time the user chooses between loading the sequence as on-board time-tagged (only the execution time tags are used) or as ground time-tagged (only the release time tags are used and the commands execute immediately on board). Not to be used when commands need both a release and an execution time tag.
  • N Neither the sequence nor its nested sequences contain execution time-tagged commands (import default).
Default N. Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. B, N ICD PDF p. 166 5CSF_NFPARSNumber(3)ONumber of formal parameters of the sequence, for consistency checking against the number of CSP records of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 ICD PDF p. 166 6CSF_ELEMSNumber(5)ONumber of elements of the sequence, for consistency checking against the number of CSS records of the sequence. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ICD PDF p. 167 7CSF_CRITICALChar(1)OCriticality flag of the sequence; the additional protections for critical (hazardous) sequences are mission specific.
  • Y Critical (hazardous) sequence.
  • N Non-critical (import default).
Default N. Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. N ICD PDF p. 167 8CSF_PLANChar(1)OIdentifies which external sources may reference the sequence directly in a planning file.
  • A Plannable by all sources.
  • F Plannable by flight dynamics only.
  • S Plannable by the SOC only.
  • N Not plannable (import default).
Default N. Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. N, S, F, A ICD PDF p. 167 9CSF_EXECChar(1)OControls whether the sequence may be loaded stand-alone on SCOS-2000 manual stacks or only as a nested sequence inside another sequence.
  • N Cannot be loaded stand-alone (only nested).
  • Y No restriction (import default).
Default Y. Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. Y ICD PDF p. 167 10CSF_SUBSYSNumber(3)OIdentifier of the subsystem the sequence belongs to, 1 to 255.Solar Orbiter: filled in 771 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 109, 106, 4, 104, 110 ICD PDF p. 167 11CSF_GENTIMEChar(17)OTime at which the sequence was generated. Grey: informative only.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 13:25:42, 14:23:31, 08:56:09, 08:56:11, 13:25:41 ICD PDF p. 168 12CSF_DOCNAMEChar(32)OName of the document (procedure) from which the sequence was generated. Grey: informative only.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. DM-FCP-740, IW-FCP-052, IW-FCP-053, IW-FCP-033, SY-SEQ-001 ICD PDF p. 168 13CSF_ISSUEChar(10)OIssue of that document. Grey: informative only.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ICD PDF p. 168 14CSF_DATEChar(17)OIssue date of that document. Grey: informative only.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 29/03/2019, 24/10/2019, 27/03/2019, 13/12/2019, 08/05/2020 ICD PDF p. 168 15CSF_DEFSETChar(8)OName of the default parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) for the sequence.Refers to psv.PSV_PVSID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 0 of 3,404 rows ICD PDF p. 168 16CSF_SUBSCHEDIDNumber(5)ODefault on-board sub-schedule identifier (1 to 65535) used when the sequence is loaded as execution time-tagged. If set, every execution time-tagged command of the sequence is assigned this sub-schedule; if empty, each command keeps the default given by its own CCF_SUBSCHEDID.Solar Orbiter: filled in 3,404 of 3,404 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 103, 108, 3 ICD PDF p. 168

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CSF_NAME → css.CSS_SQNAME: Elements of the sequence (one-to-many); CSF_ELEMS should equal their number.
  • CSF_NAME → csp.CSP_SQNAME: Formal parameters of the sequence; CSF_NFPARS should equal their number.
  • CSF_NAME → sdf.SDF_SQNAME: Values of the element parameters of the sequence.
  • CSF_NAME → css.CSS_ELEMID: Use of this sequence as a nested element (CSS_TYPE=S) of other sequences.
  • CSF_NAME → psm.PSM_NAME: Parameter sets associated with the sequence (PSM_TYPE=S).
  • CSF_DEFSET → psv.PSV_PVSID: Default parameter value set.
  • CSF_SUBSCHEDID → ccf.CCF_SUBSCHEDID: If empty, each command uses its own CCF_SUBSCHEDID default.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.3.1, PDF p.77-78) has fields 1 to 15 with the same names, sizes and defaults. CSF_SUBSCHEDID was added in ICD 6.0 together with CCF_SUBSCHEDID (Annex 1 of ICD 7.0, PDF p.249) and appears in ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.154-157) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.158-161). In ICD 6.9 an empty CSF_SUBSCHEDID fell back to CSF_SUBSYS; ICD 7.0 (PDF p.165-168, change S2K-6680, PDF p.261) changed the fallback to each command's CCF_SUBSCHEDID. ICD 6.1 deleted the last sentence of option B of CSF_IFTT (PDF p.251). The move of sequences to XML files in the FARC dates from ICD 6.4 for R5.0 (PDF p.254). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same 16 columns, mandatory CSF_NAME and CSF_DESC, defaults N (CSF_IFTT, CSF_CRITICAL, CSF_PLAN) and Y (CSF_EXEC).

Notes from the extraction

No column discrepancy (16 columns in every line of the Solar Orbiter csf.dat). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16 has 3404 sequences (2701 in 2020-04-16). CSF_IFTT is 'B' for 3354 and 'N' for 50; CSF_PLAN is N 2029, S 1177 (SOC), F 195 (flight dynamics) and A 3; CSF_CRITICAL is always N and CSF_EXEC always Y. CSF_GENTIME holds only a clock time such as '13:25:42' and CSF_DATE a date in dd/mm/yyyy form, while CSF_DOCNAME holds procedure identifiers such as 'DM-FCP-740'. CSF_SUBSCHEDID is filled in every record although CSF_SUBSYS is filled in only 771, and the two differ in 183 records. CSF_DEFSET is never used. CSF_ELEMS always equals the number of CSS records, but CSF_NFPARS disagrees with the CSP count for 3 sequences (APWC508A and APWC508B declare 1 formal parameter but have none; ATCC011C declares 11 but has 10).

docs.title: csp.dat: Command sequence formal parameters
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.3.410,981 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The csp table defines the formal parameters of command sequences, one record per formal parameter. A formal parameter is an argument of the sequence: a placeholder whose value the user provides (or accepts as default) when loading the sequence, and which is propagated to every element parameter mapped to it in SDF (SDF_VTYPE=F) - a command parameter or a parameter of a nested sequence. In this way one sequence works as a template, and fewer sequences need to be defined. Several element parameters may share one formal parameter if they have the same raw and engineering formats. The definition mirrors that of command parameters: type and length (PTC/PFC), display format and radix, calibration category with references to numeric (CCA) or textual (PAF) (de-)calibrations, a range set (PRF), unit and a default value with its representation; 'Command ID' and 'Parameter ID' types are supported. Formal parameters representing a command or sequence name are foreseen (CSP_TYPE C/S) but not supported by current SCOS-2000 versions. Formal parameter names need only be unique within their sequence. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 these tables are converted on request into XML sequence definitions held in the FARC rather than the run-time MIB, imported as a delta without re-importing the TM/TC database.1

Key: CSP_SQNAME, CSP_FPNAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CSP_SQNAMEChar(8)MName of the sequence (CSF_NAME) owning the formal parameter.Refers to csf.CSF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 10,981 of 10,981 rows; e.g. AACF046A, AACF046B, AIXF429A, AIXF429D, AIAF149G ICD PDF p. 184 2CSP_FPNAMEChar(8)MName of the formal parameter; unique within the sequence but not necessarily across sequences. Referenced by SDF_VALUE (VTYPE=F) of the same sequence, by SDF_PNAME when the sequence is nested, and by CSS_ELEMID for formal-parameter elements.Solar Orbiter: filled in 10,981 of 10,981 rows; e.g. XF230A01, XF400A01, XF040A01, XF051A03, XF401A01 ICD PDF p. 184 3CSP_FPNUMNumber(5)MNumber of the formal parameter within the sequence, used to order the parameters (and, for a nested sequence, quoted in SDF_POS). Numbers must be consecutive without gaps. docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.3.4, PDF p.89-92) has the same 16 fields, but CSP_FPNUM is Number(3), CSP_PRFREF, CSP_CCAREF and CSP_PAFREF are Number(4), CSP_DEFVAL is Char(17), and the special categories A and P are absent. ICD 6.0 added the 'Command ID'/'Parameter ID' types (Annex 1, PDF p.249) and the identifiers became Char(10) (PDF p.247); ICD 6.5 extended CSP_FPNUM to 65535 for R5.0 (PDF p.256). ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.173-179) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.177-183) have CSP_FPNUM Number(5) and Char(10) references. ICD 7.0 (PDF p.184-191) makes CSP_DEFVAL variable-length (S2K-8073, PDF p.261). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same 16 columns, keys (CSP_SQNAME, CSP_FPNAME), mandatory fields and defaults (R, D, N).

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in columns, order, keys or optionality between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter csp.dat (16 columns; 10981 records in 2025, 5598 in 2020). All formal parameters are of CSP_TYPE P; CSP_FPNUM runs consecutively from 1 (maximum 217) in every sequence, i.e. the value 0 is never used. CSP_VTYPE is filled in every record (R 9124, E 1857), including the 4515 records without default value where the ICD makes it optional. Categories: N 8864, T 1765 (all with DISPFMT A), C 312, P 38, A 2. CSP_DEFVAL reaches 40 characters. One reference does not resolve: CSP_PRFREF 'VSM00001' of formal parameter XC534C01 of sequence ADMC534C has no PRF record; all CSP_CCAREF and CSP_PAFREF values resolve.

docs.title: css.dat: Command sequences definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.3.213,879 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The css table lists the elements of each command sequence, one record per element, in the order given by CSS_ENTRY (consecutive, without gaps). An element is a command, a nested sequence or (future extension) a formal parameter standing for a command or sequence chosen later. For each element the table defines the release timing - a delta release time relative either to the previous command of the expanded sequence (or to its manual dispatch time) or to the start of the sequence - and the execution time tag, relative either to the previous time-tagged command or to the execution start of the sequence; whether a command needs its own manual dispatch (ARM and GO) on the stack; grouping (commands released as an uninterrupted batch) and blocking (commands aggregated into a single segment); the interlock scope and stage, overriding the command defaults; and flags to override dynamic PTV, static PTV and CEV checks for individual commands. All these attributes are defaults: the command requests can still be edited on a manual stack after the sequence is loaded. CSS_NPARS gives the number of SDF entries holding the element's parameter values. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 these tables are converted on request into XML sequence definitions held in the FARC rather than the run-time MIB, imported as a delta without re-importing the TM/TC database.1

Key: CSS_SQNAME, CSS_ENTRY

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.3.2, PDF p.78-86) already defines the 18 fields with the same names and defaults (CSS_ILSCOPE including F and T), except that CSS_EXTIME is Char(16). ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.157-168), ICD 6.9 (PDF p.161-171) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.168-179) have CSS_EXTIME as Char(17). ICD 6.5 split the long CSS_RELTIME and CSS_EXTIME descriptions over two pages (Annex 1, PDF p.256) and the evolution-line changes clarified their input formats (Annex 1 item 8, PDF p.244). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has 18 columns in the same order but names field 17 CSS_STATPTV, marks only CSS_SQNAME as key (not CSS_ENTRY), and treats CSS_NPARS as mandatory; defaults N, R, R, N, N, N for CSS_MANDISP, CSS_RELTYPE, CSS_PREVREL, CSS_DYNPTV, CSS_STATPTV and CSS_CEV match the ICD.

Notes from the extraction

Name discrepancy: ICD 7.0 (and 5.⅙.7/6.9) field 17 is CSS_STAPTV, pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter SQLite use CSS_STATPTV. Optionality: CSS_NPARS carries no M in ICD 7.0 but is mandatory in pyscos2000. Key: pyscos2000 omits CSS_ENTRY from the key. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16 (18 columns, 13879 records; 9089 in 2020): only types C (12629) and S (1250) are used; every sequence starts with entry 1 having CSS_RELTYPE='A' and CSS_PREVREL='A' and all other entries 'R'; entries are consecutive from 1 in every sequence and CSS_NPARS always matches the SDF count. CSS_RELTIME exceeds the declared Char(8) and the hh.mm.ss format in 1107 records, which carry milliseconds (e.g. '00.00.01.000'); CSS_EXTIME values use the same style and are never negative. CSS_COMM is filled in every record although the ICD marks it unsupported. 234 distinct commands containing group repeaters are used in 2467 sequence elements, which ICD 7.0 allows since R4.2 only for fully defined repeated groups although its CSS_ELEMID description still forbids them. In the 46 group/block members that are not the first (M or E), CSS_MANDISP is 'N' instead of empty and CSS_RELTIME is filled, contrary to the ICD rule. Groups (24) and blocks (34) never contain high-priority commands. CSS_ILSCOPE is 'N' or empty and CSS_ILSTAGE 'C' or empty; CSS_DYNPTV and CSS_STATPTV are always N, CSS_CEV is Y for 17 elements.

docs.title: cur.dat: Calibration conditional selection
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.11,974 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

cur associates monitoring parameters with several calibration definitions and says which one applies at any moment. It holds one record per parameter/calibration pair. For each parameter the records are evaluated in increasing CUR_POS order and the first one whose applicability expression CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR is true selects the calibration (CUR_SELECT) to use; all later entries for that parameter are ignored. This conditional or multiple calibration lets one telemetry parameter be calibrated according to the value of another telemetry parameter (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246). A parameter listed here must leave PCF_CURTX empty. ICD 7.0 lists three limitations. Static pre-transmission validation (PTV) checks may not use the engineering value (PTV_INTER = 'E') of parameters with multiple calibrations. The Variable Packets Display cannot show calibrated values of conditionally calibrated parameters and shows raw values instead. The same applies to the Packet History display. All calibrations attached to one parameter must produce engineering values of the same format.1

Key: CUR_PNAME, CUR_POS

docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CUR_PNAMEChar(8)MName of the parameter to be calibrated; must match the PCF_NAME of an existing monitoring parameter (whose PCF_CURTX must then be left null).Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,974 of 1,974 rows; e.g. NDS00010, NDS01010, NDS3Z002, NDS3Z01X, NCF7Z021 ICD PDF p. 64 2CUR_POSNumber(2)MEvaluation order of the applicability criteria of the calibrations attached to the parameter, starting with the lowest value. Only the first calibration whose criterion CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR is true is activated; the other entries of the same parameter are ignored.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,974 of 1,974 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ICD PDF p. 64 3CUR_RLCHKChar(8)MName of the parameter whose value decides whether this calibration applies; CUR_VALPAR gives the value it is compared with. Only parameters with a signed or unsigned integer raw representation that are processed by the telemetry model library (TM parameters with a plf entry, or synthetic parameters of any kind) may be used.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,974 of 1,974 rows; e.g. NPWZ0000, NDSZ0001, NDSZ0002, NIMD6605, NIMD6609 ICD PDF p. 64 4CUR_VALPARNumber(5)MRaw value of the applicability parameter CUR_RLCHK for which this calibration applies; the applicability expression is CUR_RLCHK = CUR_VALPAR.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,974 of 1,974 rows; e.g. 10, 11, 1, 0, 2 ICD PDF p. 64 5CUR_SELECTChar(10)MIdentifier of the calibration to apply when the applicability expression is true. It must match TXF_NUMBR if CUR_PNAME is a status parameter (PCF_CATEG = 'S'), or CAF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT if it is numerical (PCF_CATEG = 'N'). All calibrations attached to the same parameter must give the same engineering format: ASCII for textual calibrations; real for polynomial, logarithmic and numerical curves with CAF_ENGFMT = 'R'; signed integer for numerical curves with CAF_ENGFMT = 'I'; unsigned integer for CAF_ENGFMT = 'U'. docs.text:
• CUR_PNAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: Parameter being calibrated; many-to-many link between parameters and calibrations (section 3.3.2, p. 38-39).
  • CUR_RLCHK → pcf.PCF_NAME: Applicability (selector) parameter; one parameter can drive many criteria.
  • CUR_SELECT → caf.CAF_NUMBR / mcf.MCF_IDENT / lgf.LGF_IDENT / txf.TXF_NUMBR: Calibration selected; the target table depends on PCF_CATEG of CUR_PNAME.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Not present in ICD 5.1 (2001), which allowed only one calibration per parameter through PCF_CURTX. Conditional calibration ('Curve Selection') was introduced in ICD 6.0 with the repatriation of Herschel/Planck CCS functions (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246). The five-field layout is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 58-60), 6.9 (p. 62-63) and 7.0 (p. 63-65). ICD 6.4 restricted CUR_RLCHK to parameters processed by the TM model (p. 254). ICD 6.9 lists only the PTV and Variable Packets Display limitations (icd-6-9 p. 62); ICD 7.0 adds the Packet History display limitation and speaks of 'conditional' calibration (S2K-8681, p. 263). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same five fields, keys and optionality.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 1,974 records for 907 parameters (902 numerical, 5 status), driven by 52 different selector parameters and pointing to 382 distinct calibrations (1,944 entries resolve to caf, 30 to txf, none to mcf or lgf). Every parameter has CUR_POS 1 and 2; up to 12 positions are used (e.g. NDS00010 has 12 entries selected by NDSS0783 to NDSS0794). All CUR_PNAME, CUR_RLCHK and CUR_SELECT values resolve, and no parameter in cur also has PCF_CURTX. The most used selector is NPWZ0000 ('PCDU_MODEL', 1,718 entries), a dynamic user defined constant in the 'Dynamic UDCs' packet (SPID 66830); together with NDSZ0001/NDSZ0002 this suggests (inference) that Solar Orbiter uses cur mainly to switch between unit-specific calibration models.

docs.title: cve.dat: Verification expressions
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.4.2171 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cve table holds the checks that make up the criteria of parameter-based verification stages: one record per check, naming a monitoring parameter, the expected value, a tolerance and the representation (raw, engineering, or echo of a command parameter value). All checks of the same stage are ANDed. The ICD recommends taking all verification parameters of a stage from the same telemetry packet (see CVS_SPID). Parameter validity is taken into account automatically: a check passes only if the parameter is valid and its value meets the criterion. The table has a second role: it identifies the monitoring parameters affected by a command, so that their status consistency checking (PCF_USCON) is suspended during the verification window and, at the end, the expected value is updated. For status-consistency-checked parameters the check must use the same raw or engineering form (CVE_INTER) as the parameter's out-of-limits checks (OCF_INTER), and all cve records for the same parameter must use the same representation, across all stages.1

Key: CVE_CVSID, CVE_PARNAM

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CVE_CVSIDNumber(5)MIdentifier (CVS_ID) of the verification stage this check belongs to. Only parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE = 'V') are allowed. Part of the key.Refers to cvs.CVS_ID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 171 of 171 rows; e.g. 20, 21, 22, 23, 28 ICD PDF p. 195 2CVE_PARNAMChar(8)MName of an existing monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) used for the check. Restrictions: its raw representation must be numerical (no strings or times), and it must be processed by the telemetry model, that is, a TM parameter in plf or a synthetic parameter of any type. If the parameter is subject to status consistency checking (PCF_USCON = 'Y'), the representation of the verification value (CVE_INTER) must match that of its OOL checks (OCF_INTER). Part of the key, so a parameter can appear only once per stage.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 171 of 171 rows; e.g. NPWD0757, NPWD0756, NPWD0759, NPWD0758, NPWD0753 ICD PDF p. 196 3CVE_INTERChar(1)ORepresentation of the expected value CVE_VAL and tolerance CVE_TOL. If one monitoring parameter appears in several parameter-based stages, 'E' is only allowed if every one of its cve records uses 'E': records with 'R' or 'C' and records with 'E' cannot be mixed for the same parameter.
  • R Raw values. For synthetic parameters the raw value is the source value produced by the OL or hard-coded definition
  • E Engineering (calibrated) values. Only for parameters with one or more calibration definitions (see PCF_CURTX)
  • C Echo check: CVE_VAL is the name of a command parameter; CVE_TOL is then always raw, so a status-consistency-checked verification parameter must be checked raw (OCF_INTER = 'U')
Default R. Solar Orbiter: filled in 171 of 171 rows; e.g. R, E ICD PDF p. 197 4CVE_VALChar(17)OValue the verification parameter is compared with. It uses raw form unless CVE_INTER = 'E'. Raw values are decimal, in a format compatible with the parameter type (PCF_PTC). Engineering values follow the parameter's engineering representation: ASCII text for status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S') or the CAF_ENGFMT of the numerical calibration. For echo verification (CVE_INTER = 'C'), the field holds the name of a command parameter (CDF_PNAME) whose value at command instantiation is the reference. That parameter should appear only once in the command; if it appears more than once, the first instance is used. The field is only applicable, and then cannot be Null, when CVE_CHECK = 'B'; it is not used when CVE_CHECK = 'S'.Refers to cdf.CDF_PNAME (only when CVE_INTER = 'C'). Solar Orbiter: filled in 171 of 171 rows; e.g. 0, 1, IMAGE_1, IMAGE_0, ENABLED ICD PDF p. 198 5CVE_TOLChar(17)OAllowed tolerance: the check passes when CVE_PARNAM lies within CVE_VAL plus or minus CVE_TOL. It is expressed in the same representation and format rules as CVE_VAL. It must be Null when an engineering representation (CVE_INTER = 'E') is used for a status parameter (PCF_CATEG = 'S').Solar Orbiter: filled in 78 of 171 rows; e.g. 0 ICD PDF p. 199 6CVE_CHECKChar(1)OControls whether the check drives only the status consistency checking of the verification parameter or also the actual command verification.
  • B Both: used for verification and to disable and then re-enable status consistency checking of CVE_PARNAM (if it is status-consistency checked); CVE_VAL becomes the new expected value at the end of the stage window
  • S Status consistency only: used just to disable status consistency checking of CVE_PARNAM. Allowed only together with at least one other check with CVE_CHECK = 'B' in the same stage
Default B. Solar Orbiter: filled in 171 of 171 rows; e.g. B ICD PDF p. 199

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CVE_CVSID → cvs.CVS_ID: Stage must have CVS_SOURCE = 'V'.
  • CVE_PARNAM → pcf.PCF_NAME: Numeric-raw, TM-model parameter. Its PCF_USCON, PCF_CATEG, PCF_CURTX and PCF_PTC constrain CVE_INTER, CVE_VAL and CVE_TOL.
  • CVE_INTER → ocf.OCF_INTER / ocf.OCF_CODIN: For status-consistency-checked parameters CVE_INTER must match OCF_INTER. ocf says OCF_CODIN must be compatible with CVE_INTER when the parameter is used in cve (§3.3.2.3.1, PDF p.74).
  • CVE_VAL → cdf.CDF_PNAME: Echo verification (CVE_INTER = 'C'): command parameter whose instantiated value is the reference.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.3.4.2 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.94-96) has the same 6 fields, with CVE_CVSID Number(5). The differences are in the text. In 5.1 any TM or synthetic parameter with a numerical raw value is allowed, 'E' requires PCF_CURTX not Null (a single calibration curve), and the introduction requires OCF_INTER = 'C' when CVE_INTER = 'E' and advises against status consistency checking of echo-verified parameters. ICD 6.0 added 'describe constraint in the use of parameter views in the CVE table' (Annex 1 item 6, PDF p.244), giving the same-representation rules. ICD 6.4 restricted CVE_PARNAM, like other TM references, to parameters processed by the TM model (PDF p.254). ICD 6.7 Draft A prints CVE_CVSID as Number(10) (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.182). ICD 6.9 changed it back to Number(5) to match CVS_ID (S2K-DCR-3909, PDF p.260; tracked change visible in icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.187). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.194-199) keeps Number(5). Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: COL1..COL6 = CVE_CVSID, CVE_PARNAM, CVE_INTER, CVE_VAL, CVE_TOL, CVE_CHECK; all 171 lines of the 2025 cve.dat have 6 fields. Consistency with ICD 7.0: every CVE_CVSID refers to a cvs stage with CVS_SOURCE = 'V', every 'V' stage has at least one check (167 stages, 171 checks; stages 9082-9085 have two ANDed checks each), and every CVE_PARNAM exists in pcf. CVE_INTER is 'R' in 81 rows and 'E' in 90. There is no echo verification ('C'), and CVE_CHECK is always 'B'. All 90 'E' checks use status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S', textual calibration) with text values such as ENABLED/DISABLED, On/Off, IMAGE_0/IMAGE_1, and CVE_TOL empty, as the ICD requires. No parameter used in cve has PCF_USCON = 'Y'. Release difference: in 2025, 78 'R' rows have CVE_TOL = '0', whereas the same rows have an empty tolerance in the 2020-04-16 release. This is the only change in cve between the releases. The SWA IDB cve.dat is empty. pyscos2000 has no cve model.

docs.title: cvp.dat: Verification profiles
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.4.310,697 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cvp table is the mapping table that gives each command its verification profile: which verification stages (cvs) apply to which task. There is one record per stage attached to a command or sequence, though current SCOS-2000 releases only support verification for commands. A command can have several stages, but at most one of each CVS_TYPE (for example only one acceptance stage). Since SCOS-2000 R4.0 a report-based stage can be disabled dynamically by clearing the corresponding acknowledgement flag when loading the command. This only disables a stage that cvs defines and cvp attaches to the command; it cannot add a new report-based stage at run time. Every command for which the receiving on-board application generates PUS service 1 reports must therefore be linked here to the matching stage. Together with cvs and cve, this table is the 'CEV' part of the commanding database (Table 3, PDF p.29).1

Key: CVP_TASK, CVP_TYPE, CVP_CVSID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CVP_TASKChar(8)MName of the command (CCF_CNAME) or sequence (CSF_NAME) that uses the stage given in CVP_CVSID. Part of the key.Refers to ccf.CCF_CNAME / csf.CSF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 10,697 of 10,697 rows; e.g. INSERTBU, INSERTTT, REIN_TTR, ZACX0001, ZAHG0000 ICD PDF p. 200 2CVP_TYPEChar(1)OType of task the verification stage is attached to. Part of the key, but printed with the import default 'C' instead of 'M' in the Ma/Def column.
  • C The task is a command
  • S The task is a sequence (not supported by SCOS-2000)
Default C. Solar Orbiter: filled in 10,697 of 10,697 rows; e.g. C ICD PDF p. 200 3CVP_CVSIDNumber(5)MIdentifier (CVS_ID) of the stage attached to the task. At most one stage of a given type (for example CVS_TYPE = 'A' or 'C') may be attached to each command. Part of the key.Refers to cvs.CVS_ID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 10,697 of 10,697 rows; e.g. 11, 17, 9088, 9000, 9001 ICD PDF p. 200

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CVP_TASK → ccf.CCF_CNAME / csf.CSF_NAME: In practice commands only (CVP_TYPE = 'C').
  • CVP_CVSID → cvs.CVS_ID: Many-to-many relationship between commands and stages (§3.3.3, PDF p.126).
  • CVP_TASK → ccf.CCF_ILSTAGE / ccf.CCF_ACK: The importer checks CCF_ILSTAGE against the stages attached here (PDF p.138). CCF_ACK flags can disable attached report-based stages at load time (PDF p.140, p.200).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.3.4.3 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.96-97) defines the same three key fields, with CVP_CVSID Number(5) and CVP_TYPE default 'C'. It says the first SCOS-2000 release supports only command verification and has no paragraph on dynamic disabling. That paragraph comes from the R4.0 change to the command ACK flags (ICD 6.0, Annex 1 PDF p.250) and is in ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.187). ICD 6.2/6.3 record 'CVP_CVSID Field Type changed' (PDF p.253). ICD 6.7 Draft A prints CVP_CVSID as Number(10) (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.187), and ICD 6.9 restored Number(5) to match CVS_ID (S2K-DCR-3909, PDF p.260; icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.192). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.199-200) keeps Number(5). Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: COL1..COL3 = CVP_TASK, CVP_TYPE, CVP_CVSID; all 10697 lines of the 2025 cvp.dat have 3 fields (10277 rows in the 2020-04-16 release). All rows have CVP_TYPE = 'C'. There are 5393 distinct tasks: 5304 commands have two stages (one acceptance 'A/R' and one completion, either 'C/R' or 'C/V'), and 89 have a single completion stage. No command has two stages of the same CVS_TYPE, as ICD 7.0 requires, and every CVP_CVSID exists in cvs. The most used stages are 11 (2263 commands), 17 (2185), and 14001 and 14007 (1524 each). Discrepancy: two rows attach stages 14001/14007 to ZCSD2005, which is in neither ccf nor csf. ICD 7.0 §2.4 says the importer rejects records that break relational integrity, with a warning (PDF p.23). 62 of the 5454 ccf commands have no cvp entry. The key printed in ICD 7.0 is all three fields; CVP_TYPE carries a default rather than 'M', although §3.3 says key fields are marked mandatory (PDF p.36). pyscos2000 has no cvp model. The HPSDB note generates CVP from the command's verification list and forces CVP_TYPE to 'C' (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb PDF p.38-39).

docs.title: cvs.dat: Verification stages file
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.4.1206 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The cvs table defines the command execution verification (CEV) stages used by SCOS-2000, one record per stage. SCOS-2000 supports two kinds of verification check: report based, which relies on dedicated telemetry packets (PUS service 1 verification reports) announcing the success or failure of an execution stage, and parameter based, which compares the values of one or more monitoring parameters with criteria held in cve. Each stage record says which step of the command execution profile it covers (application acceptance, start, a numbered progress step or completion), which kind of check it uses, when the verification window opens after release (or execution, for time-tagged commands), the sampling interval used to compute the window, optionally the packet that closes a parameter-based stage, and optionally a stage-specific window that overrides the TC Spacon default. Stages are defined once and shared: cvp attaches them to commands. The ICD notes that only verification of commands, not of sequences, is supported by current SCOS-2000 versions.1

Key: CVS_ID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1CVS_IDNumber(5)MUnique identifier of the verification stage, integer 0 to 32767 (a signed short). Referenced by cve.CVE_CVSID and cvp.CVP_CVSID.Solar Orbiter: filled in 206 of 206 rows; e.g. 11, 17, 20, 21, 22 ICD PDF p. 192 2CVS_TYPEChar(1)MStep of the command execution profile verified by this stage. Limitation of the SCOS-2000 service 1 implementation: the verifier processes progress reports (TM(1,5) packets) only for a stage of type '0'; reports for any other progress step are not processed. Per cvp, a command can have at most one stage of each type.
  • A Application acceptance
  • S Start of execution
  • 0 Progress step 0; the only progress step whose TM(1,5) reports the SCOS-2000 verifier processes
  • 1-9 Progress step n of execution
  • C Completion of execution
Solar Orbiter: filled in 206 of 206 rows; e.g. A, C ICD PDF p. 192 3CVS_SOURCEChar(1)MType of verification check used for this stage. Progress verification stages of the report type can only be stage 0. The ICD words this as 'R' being possible only for CVS_TYPE = '0'; in context this applies to progress stages, since acceptance and completion stages can also be report based. The ICD points to [RD-2] for the report packets.
  • R Report based: uses telemetry verification report packets
  • V Parameter based: monitoring parameter values are checked against the criteria in cve for this stage
Solar Orbiter: filled in 206 of 206 rows; e.g. R, V ICD PDF p. 193 4CVS_STARTNumber(5)MDelay, in seconds (positive integer), between release of the command (or its execution, for time-tagged commands) and the opening of the verification window.Solar Orbiter: filled in 206 of 206 rows; e.g. 0 ICD PDF p. 193 5CVS_INTERVALNumber(5)MLength, in seconds (positive integer), of the sampling interval used to calculate the overall verification window, as specified in the SCOS-2000 Commanding SRD [AD-2] (not in the library).Solar Orbiter: filled in 206 of 206 rows; e.g. 20, 60, 4, 36000, 10 ICD PDF p. 193 6CVS_SPIDNumber(10)OSCOS-2000 packet ID (PID_SPID) of the TM packet that marks when to close a stage once its verification window has elapsed; flagged as a future extension. It may only be given for parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE = 'V'), where it helps when the verification parameters come from several different packets. If it is not given, the stage closes as soon as a valid sample of any associated verification parameter arrives with a time stamp at or after the window closure time. It is irrelevant for report-based stages, because their packets are known implicitly from type and subtype. The extracted text prints the type as 'Number(10' (closing parenthesis lost at a line break; earlier issues print Number(10)).Refers to pid.PID_SPID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 20 of 206 rows; e.g. 0, 50001, 50010, 20000, 52000 ICD PDF p. 194 7CVS_UNCERTAINTYNumber(5)OStage-specific verification window in seconds (positive integer). When present it is used instead of the default window configured in the Spacon (the ICD says 'TM Spacon' in one sentence and 'TCspacon' in the next). If the field is empty, the importer sets -1, meaning that the standard TC Spacon verification window applies. The field name is split over two lines in the ICD table ('CVS_' / 'UNCERTAINTY').Default -1. Solar Orbiter: filled in 0 of 206 rows ICD PDF p. 194

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• CVS_ID → cve.CVE_CVSID: Parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE='V') have one or more cve checks, logically ANDed.
  • CVS_ID → cvp.CVP_CVSID: Many-to-many relationship between commands and stages, resolved by the mapping table cvp (§3.3.3, PDF p.126).
  • CVS_SPID → pid.PID_SPID: Packet that closes a 'V' stage.
  • CVS_TYPE → ccf.CCF_ILSTAGE: The importer checks that a command's default interlock stage ('A' or 'C') is foreseen in its cvp/cvs definition, and otherwise replaces CCF_ILSTAGE with the highest applicable level ('A' or 'O') (§3.3.3.2.1, PDF p.138).
  • CVS_SOURCE → ccf.CCF_ACK: Since R4.0 report-based stages attached to a command can be disabled at load time by clearing the corresponding acknowledgement flag (PDF p.140, p.200).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.3.4.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.93-94) has 6 fields (no CVS_UNCERTAINTY). CVS_ID is already Number(5), 0-32767, and there is no stage-0 note. ICD 6.0 brought in the Herschel/Planck CCS functions, including a CVS identifier range raised 'from NUM(5) to NUM(8)' (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, PDF p.247). ICD 6.1 (S2K-40-DCR-0821) updated CVS_TYPE and CVS_SOURCE to say that progress reports are only handled for stage 0 (PDF p.251). ICD 6.2/6.3 record 'CVS_ID Field Type changed' (PDF p.253). ICD 6.7 S2K-DCR-3909 restricted CVS_ID to signed short values (PDF p.259): ICD 6.7 Draft A prints Number(5), 0-32767, with 6 fields (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.180-181). CVS_UNCERTAINTY was added for R5.2 by S2K-SCR-3774 (override of the TcSpacon verification window, PDF p.260; it arrived in ICD 6.7 Draft B per the change log, PDF p.5). It is printed in ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.186), whose S2K-NCR-5531 updated its description (PDF p.260). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.192-194) is unchanged from 6.9. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: COL1..COL7 = CVS_ID, CVS_TYPE, CVS_SOURCE, CVS_START, CVS_INTERVAL, CVS_SPID, CVS_UNCERTAINTY. All 206 lines of the 2025 cvs.dat have 7 fields (ICD 6.9/7.0 layout), but CVS_UNCERTAINTY is empty in every row, so the importer default -1 (TC Spacon window) applies everywhere. The SWA IDB cvs.dat has only 6 fields per line (pre-R5.2 layout without CVS_UNCERTAINTY) and holds 2 stages, 58901 and 58907, which have the same values as the stages with those IDs in the Solar Orbiter MIB. Content: only types 'A' and 'C' are used, with no start or progress stages: A/R 16, C/R 23, C/V 167. CVS_START is 0 everywhere (the ICD describes it as a positive integer). CVS_INTERVAL ranges from 4 to 36000 s; stage 51927 changed from 8000 to 36000 between the 2020-04-16 and 2025-09-16 releases, the only cvs difference. Discrepancy 1: 33 CVS_ID values exceed the ICD 7.0 range 0-32767 (IDs run from 11 to 70007, for example 50001, 54004, 70007), which conflicts with the signed-short restriction of S2K-DCR-3909. Discrepancy 2: CVS_SPID is filled in 20 rows, all report-based (CVS_SOURCE='R'), although ICD 7.0 allows it only for 'V' stages and calls it irrelevant for 'R'. The values are 0 (stages 14001/14007), SPIDs of TM(1,1) or TM(1,7) success-report packets (for example 52000 'TM 1,1 accept report ok', 54013 'STIX TC EXEC SUCCESS'), or 20000, which in pid is a TM(5,1) event packet. Inference, not stated in the sources: the mission control system may use CVS_SPID to tell the verifier which report packet to expect. The 2002 e-mail reproduced in the HCSS note explains that the SCOS-2000 verifier then listened to a predefined list of SPIDs for report-based verification (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note PDF p.29). ICD 7.0 cites [RD-2] for report packets, but its reference list gives RD-2 as the SCOS-2000 Operations Language ADD and the PUS as RD-6 (PDF p.19), so the citation looks stale. pyscos2000 has no cvs model, so no 7.2 cross-check is possible. The HPSDB note forces CVS_SPID to Null (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb PDF p.38).

docs.title: dpc.dat: Alphanumeric displays definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.2626 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The dpc table defines the content of each Alphanumeric Display (AND) declared in dpf: one record per displayed monitoring parameter or per free-text comment, together with its position on the page. An AND has 64 positions (0 to 63); positions 0 to 31 are drawn in the left column and 32 to 63 in the right column. For each displayed parameter the record selects which sample of a super-commutated parameter is shown, whether the Telemetry Desktop setting for showing invalid values applies, and the number format (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal or the normal engineering/raw form). A record whose parameter name is empty is a free entry that displays a fixed text comment instead of a value. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model (plf-located TM parameters or synthetic parameters) can be displayed. As with dpf, from SCOS-2000 R5.0 these definitions are converted into XML display files in the FARC rather than imported into the run-time database.1

Key: DPC_NUMBE, DPC_FLDN

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1DPC_NUMBEChar(8)MName of the AND this record belongs to; must match DPF_NUMBE of an existing dpf record. Part of the table key together with DPC_FLDN.Refers to dpf.DPF_NUMBE. Solar Orbiter: filled in 626 of 626 rows; e.g. DICA0000, DICA0100, DICA0200, DICA0300, DICA0400 ICD PDF p. 111 2DPC_NAMEChar(8)OName of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) shown at this position, or Null. When Null the record is a free entry: the text in DPC_TEXT is shown and DPC_COMM, DPC_MODE and DPC_FORM are not relevant. When a parameter name is given, DPC_TEXT is ignored. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model (TM parameters appearing in plf or synthetic parameters) may be used (§3.3.2.7, PDF p.110). The ICD text misspells the cross-references as DCP_TEXT and DCP_NAME.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 626 of 626 rows; e.g. NIC0SN00, NIC0N080, NIC0F010, NIC0F015, NIC0N000 ICD PDF p. 112 3DPC_FLDNNumber(2)MPosition of the parameter on the display, 0 to 63. Positions 0-31 are shown on the left side and 32-63 on the right side. Part of the key: a display position can hold only one entry.Solar Orbiter: filled in 626 of 626 rows; e.g. 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 ICD PDF p. 112 4DPC_COMMNumber(4)OCommutation selector. For super-commutated parameters (PLF_NBOCC greater than 1, see plf, §3.3.2.5.1) it selects which sample within the packet is displayed. The value 0 selects all samples; they are then shown in turn when super-commutated processing is enabled in the Telemetry Desktop. Numeric value 0 to 9999, left justified.Default 0. B, O and H only apply to raw values of unsigned integer parameters; N shows the calibrated (engineering) value when the parameter has one or more calibration definitions, otherwise the raw value in decimal.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• DPC_NUMBE → dpf.DPF_NUMBE: Many dpc records per AND.
  • DPC_NAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: Parameter must be processed by the TM model (plf entry or synthetic). Null for free-text entries.
  • DPC_COMM → plf.PLF_NBOCC: Sample selection is meaningful for parameters with more than one occurrence in a packet (super-commutation).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.2 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.51-52) has only 6 fields: DPC_NAME is mandatory (no free entries), DPC_COMM has default '1' and range 1-9999 without the super-commutation explanation, and DPC_TEXT does not exist. ICD 6.0 (SCOS-2000 R4.0) introduced DCR-2422, display of super-commutated parameters in ANDs (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, PDF p.246), and the DPC change that allows free entries (PDF p.250); this gives the 7-field layout with optional DPC_NAME, DPC_TEXT and DPC_COMM default '0' already printed in ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.104-106) and ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.108-110), and unchanged in ICD 7.0 (PDF p.111-113). ICD 6.0 also said that a multi-domain field for ANDs and SCDs, like GPC_DOMAIN, would only be supported from S2K R5.0 (PDF p.249), but no such field appears in dpc in ICD 7.0. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: COL1..COL7 = DPC_NUMBE, DPC_NAME, DPC_FLDN, DPC_COMM, DPC_MODE, DPC_FORM, DPC_TEXT. All 626 lines of the 2025 dpc.dat have 7 fields, so the optional DPC_TEXT column is present (empty in 625 rows). Every DPC_NAME is filled and exists in pcf, so the file has no free-text entries; the only DPC_TEXT value ('Comment') is on the DQQA1234 test display, in a row that also names a parameter (NIA00510), so ICD 7.0 says the text is ignored. DPC_COMM is '1' in 625 rows and '0' in 1: the mission writes the ICD 5.1 default explicitly, whereas under ICD 7.0 a non-zero value selects one specific sample and '0' selects all samples. No displayed parameter has PLF_NBOCC > 1 in plf, so the choice has no effect here. DPC_MODE is 'N' in 625 rows ('Y' once), so invalid values are forced visible. DPC_FORM is N 578, H 41, D 7. DPC_FLDN covers 0-63. Content is identical in the 2020-04-16 release. pyscos2000 has no dpc model. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.28) maps only 6 fields (no DPC_TEXT) and uses a DPC_COMM default of '1', as in ICD 5.1.

docs.title: dpf.dat: Alphanumeric displays
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.133 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The dpf table lists the Alphanumeric Displays (ANDs) of the SCOS-2000 monitoring system, one record per display proforma. An AND is a tabular page of telemetry values: either a 32-parameter display that also shows information about the packet which carried the most recently displayed sample, or a 64-parameter display. dpf only gives the identity, layout type and header line of each display; the parameters shown and their positions are listed in the companion table dpc, keyed on the same display name. Only monitoring parameters processed by the telemetry model (parameters located in fixed packets through plf, or synthetic parameters of any type) can appear on ANDs; values extracted from variable packets can only be shown with the VPD application. ICD section 3.1 adds that dpf/dpc do not define the TM query display or the detailed out-of-limits display. From SCOS-2000 R5.0 the definitions are converted into XML files in the FARC instead of being imported into the run-time database; the ASCII format remains supported for backward compatibility and is imported in a delta fashion, so existing displays, including ones built at run time with the TM Desktop display editor, are kept.1

Key: DPF_NUMBE

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1DPF_NUMBEChar(8)MName of the Alphanumeric Display (AND): an alphanumeric string that uniquely identifies the display. It is the table key and is referenced by every dpc record (DPC_NUMBE) that places a parameter or a comment on this display.Solar Orbiter: filled in 33 of 33 rows; e.g. DICA0000, DICA0100, DICA0200, DICA0300, DICA0400 ICD PDF p. 111 2DPF_TYPEChar(1)MLayout type of the alphanumeric display. Two values are defined: a 32-parameter display that also shows information about the packet containing the last displayed parameter sample, or a 64-parameter display. No other code (for example '2') is defined in ICD 7.0.
  • 1 32-parameter display, with information about the packet that contained the last displayed parameter sample
  • 3 64-parameter display
Solar Orbiter: filled in 33 of 33 rows; e.g. 3, 1 ICD PDF p. 111 3DPF_HEADChar(32)OAlphanumeric header text shown on the top line of the display. Optional; no import default is given.Solar Orbiter: filled in 33 of 33 rows; e.g. SEB/DPM Params, SDM Params, Detector Assembly Params, Slit Change Mechanism Params, Scan Stage Params ICD PDF p. 111

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• DPF_NUMBE → dpc.DPC_NUMBE: One AND has many dpc records (one per displayed parameter or free-text entry). ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.2, PDF p.111.
  • DPF_NUMBE → pcf.PCF_NAME (through dpc.DPC_NAME): Many-to-many relationship between monitoring parameters and monitoring displays; the content of displays is defined in dpc, gpc and spc. ICD 7.0 §3.3.2, PDF p.39.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.50-51) defines the same three fields with the same types, keys and values. The table moved to §3.3.2.7.1 when monitoring groups were inserted as §3.3.2.6 (ICD 6.7 Draft A, icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.104; ICD 6.9, icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.108; ICD 7.0 PDF p.110-111). Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. The table is not modelled in pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2-based schema), so the 7.2 definition could not be compared.

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: the Solar Orbiter database stores this table as COL1..COL3, mapped here to DPF_NUMBE, DPF_TYPE, DPF_HEAD; every line of dpf.dat in MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL has exactly 3 tab-separated fields, matching ICD 7.0. Content: 33 ANDs (unchanged from the 2020-04-16 release), 28 of type '1' and 5 of type '3'. Thirty-one are named DICA* and show only NIC* parameters (608 dpc rows), with headers such as 'SPICE Temperatures' and 'SPICE Instrument Params'. DIPA0001 'Status Overview' shows 17 NIP* parameters whose PCF descriptions all start with 'PHI_'. DQQA1234 ('This is a test') is a one-entry test display that also appears, identically, in the SWA instrument database. pyscos2000 has no dpf model, so no 7.2 cross-check is possible. The H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060 note (Herschel/Planck HPSDB) copies all three fields unchanged (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.28).

docs.title: dst.dat: Command routing
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.2.1.11 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The optional dst table defines where the SCOS-2000 releaser delivers commands, keyed by command APID: at most one record per APID, applying to all commands whose CCF_APID has that value. Commands whose APID is not listed are sent to the default destination, the NCTRS. ICD 7.0 states that the table is currently used only by SCOS-2000 based EGSE systems, where commands may have to be delivered to ground equipment rather than to the NCTRS: either non-spacecraft commands addressed to a SCOE, or spacecraft commands issued to the spacecraft through a TC front end of the EGSE. The routing is written as a destination identifier string of up to three dot-separated fields: the receiving system (NCTRS or EGSE), then for EGSE the request type (SCOE for non-spacecraft commands or TC for spacecraft commands), then for spacecraft commands routed to EGSE the address of the ground equipment that uplinks the command.1

Key: DST_APID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1DST_APIDNumber(5)MCommand APID to which the routing applies, an integer 0 to 65535 (so it covers both spacecraft APIDs 0 to 2047 and non-spacecraft APIDs 2048 to 65535). All commands with this CCF_APID use the route.Refers to ccf.CCF_APID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 1372 ICD PDF p. 141 2DST_ROUTEChar(30)MDestination identifier: a string of up to three fields separated by dots. The first field is the system to which the SCOS-2000 releaser delivers the command: NCTRS (spacecraft commands only; the default for APIDs absent from the table) or EGSE (spacecraft or non-spacecraft commands). The second and third fields apply only to EGSE routing. The second gives the request type and layout: SCOE for non-spacecraft commands or TC for spacecraft commands. The third applies only to spacecraft commands not routed via the NCTRS and is the address of the ground equipment that sends the command to the spacecraft. Examples given by the ICD: NCTRS, EGSE.SCOE and EGSE.TC.0x8800 (spacecraft command routed via the SCOE and the TC front end 0x8800).
  • NCTRS Spacecraft command routed via the NCTRS (default).
  • EGSE.SCOE Non-spacecraft command delivered to the EGSE as a SCOE request.
  • EGSE.TC.<address> Spacecraft command delivered to the EGSE and uplinked by the ground equipment with the given address, e.g. 0x8800.
Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. EGSE.TC.0x8800 ICD PDF p. 141

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • DST_APID → ccf.CCF_APID: Routing applies to every command with this APID; commands whose APID is not in DST go to the NCTRS.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
The table has the same two fields (DST_APID Number(5) key, DST_ROUTE Char(30), both mandatory) in ICD 5.1 (section 3.3.3.2.1.1, PDF p.66-67), ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.132), ICD 6.9 (PDF p.136) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.141-142). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same two mandatory columns with DST_APID as key.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in columns between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter dst.dat (2 columns). Both Solar Orbiter releases (2020-04-16 and 2025-09-16) contain a single record routing APID 1372 to 'EGSE.TC.0x8800', which is literally the ICD example route. In the 2025-09-16 ccf, 91 commands use APID 1372 (92 in 2020), all with header NOM_TC and subsystem 108 and mnemonics starting with ZIC (for example ZIC0C000 'CONNECTION_TEST', service types 3, 6, 17, 21 and 255); all other APIDs fall back to the NCTRS default. Why this APID is routed to an EGSE front end in a flight-operations MIB is not stated in the available sources. Note also that ICD 7.0 calls the table 'DST' in upper case in its heading, while the file is dst.dat.

docs.title: dup.dat: Packet duplication to secondary APIDs (inferred title)
docs.text:
not defined in the ICD69 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Inference

This table is not defined by the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD. Its column meanings below were inferred from the data and are this wiki's interpretation.

Inferred from the data; not documented in any available ICD. Each record links one SCOS-2000 TM packet definition (column 1, a PID_SPID) to a second APID (column 2) in the range 1953-1996. These APIDs do not belong to on-board applications in this MIB: for each of the 41 distinct values the pid table holds many finer packet definitions with the same type/subtype, and the pic table holds a record keyed by that APID (PIC_APID) that places the second identification field PI2 (or PI1) deeper inside the packet. Example: SPID 14177 'On-board Parameters Value Report' (TM(139,3) from APID 163, no extra identification field) maps to APID 1953, where PIC defines a 32-bit PI1 at byte 17 and pid defines 20 specific reports (e.g. 'FSS Thresholds Value Report'). This suggests a ground mechanism that copies (duplicates) generic packets such as event reports (5,x), memory dumps (6,6), monitoring reports (12,9) or parameter reports under a ground-only APID, so that SCOS-2000 can identify and decommutate each variant with its own SPID and layout. The mechanism itself is not described in the available sources.

Key: COL1
tags: Solar Orbiter mission-specific tables (not in the ICD)

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1COL1Number (up to 5 digits observed)MInferred: SCOS-2000 packet ID (SPID) of the original packet definition. All 69 values (2025 release) exist in pid.PID_SPID and are unique. The referenced packets are mostly PUS event reports (5,1), (5,2), (5,3) (38 rows), memory dumps (6,6) (11), and mission-specific report types 12/9, 131/2, 131/128, 132/2, 139/3, 141/3 and 142/11.Refers to pid.PID_SPID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 69 of 69 rows; e.g. 10095, 10103, 10153, 10168, 10169 2COL2Number (4 digits observed, 1953-1996)MInferred: the secondary (ground) APID under which the duplicated packet is identified again. 41 distinct values in 2025; several SPIDs can share one APID (e.g. 1961 for six memory-dump SPIDs). Every value has pid records (PID_APID) and pic records (PIC_APID) with the same type/subtype as the source packet but different PI1/PI2 offsets.Refers to pid.PID_APID; pic.PIC_APID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 69 of 69 rows; e.g. 1995, 1989, 1975, 1969, 1960
tags: Solar Orbiter mission-specific tables (not in the ICD)

docs.text:
• COL1 → pid.PID_SPID: All 69 values match (inferred foreign key).
  • COL2 → pic.PIC_APID: All 41 APIDs have APID-specific PIC records defining the secondary identification fields (inferred).
  • COL2 → pid.PID_APID: All APIDs have packet definitions; APIDs 1950-1999 carry 2,421 pid records in 2025.

docs.text:
Not part of any ICD issue (5.1, 6.7 Draft A, 6.9, 7.0) nor of the pyscos2000 (7.2) schema. 36 rows in MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL, 69 rows in MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL. Not present in the SWA instrument database.

Notes from the extraction

Meanings inferred from joins against pid and pic (2025 release). The pic precedence rules of ICD 7.0 section 3.3.2.4.2 (type/subtype/APID first, then type/subtype; PDF p.91-92) explain how an APID-specific PIC record changes the identification of a packet; how and where the duplication is performed is not stated in the available sources. The name 'dup' presumably abbreviates 'duplicate' (inference).

docs.title: gpc.dat: Graphic displays definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.40 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The gpc table defines the parameters plotted on each Graphic Display (GRD) declared in gpf: one record per plotted parameter. Each record gives the entry's order in the display, the plot area where the parameter is drawn (or, for full-screen displays, whether it is the X-axis parameter of a parameter-against-parameter plot), the monitoring parameter name, whether raw or calibrated values are plotted, the minimum and maximum values mapped to the ends of the axis, and the colour, symbol and line style of the trace. An optional domain identifier allows a single graphic display to combine parameters from different SCOS-2000 domains. The file is expected to be sorted by display name and then by position. Like gpf, the ICD says this file is read directly by SCOS-2000 applications rather than imported, and from R5.0 display definitions are converted into XML files in the FARC.1

Key: GPC_NUMBE, GPC_POS

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1GPC_NUMBEChar(8)MName of the GRD; must match GPF_NUMBE of the corresponding display. Part of the key.Refers to gpf.GPF_NUMBE. ICD PDF p. 117 2GPC_POSNumber(1)MOrder of the parameter entry within the GRD (single digit). Part of the key; the file is expected to be sorted by GPC_NUMBE then GPC_POS (the ICD remark misspells the first as 'GCP_NUMBE'). ICD PDF p. 117 3GPC_WHEREChar(1)MPlot area where the parameter is drawn. The valid codes depend on the display type GPF_TYPE: for 'F' (full screen) '1' marks a plotted parameter and 'P' the X-axis parameter; for 'H' (half screen) '1' is the top graph and '2' the bottom graph; for 'Q' (quarter screen) areas are numbered 1-4 clockwise starting top-left; for 'S' (sliced screen) areas are numbered 1-8 from the top.
  • 1 F: parameter to be plotted; H: top graph; Q/S: area 1
  • P F only: X-axis parameter (parameter-against-parameter plot)
  • 2 H: bottom graph; Q/S: area 2
  • 3-4 Q/S: areas 3-4 (Q clockwise from top-left, S top-down)
  • 5-8 S only: areas 5-8 top-down
Refers to gpf.GPF_TYPE. ICD PDF p. 117 4GPC_NAMEChar(8)MName of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) plotted. Must be processed by the TM model (plf parameter or synthetic parameter, §3.3.2.7).Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. ICD PDF p. 117 5GPC_RAWChar(1)OSelects whether calibrated or raw values are plotted. It also fixes the representation used for GPC_MINIM and GPC_MAXIM.
  • C Calibrated (engineering) value plotted; a space has the same meaning
  • U Uncalibrated (raw) value plotted
Default U. ICD PDF p. 118 6GPC_MINIMChar(14)MMinimum value of the parameter, mapped to the start of the axis on which the value is projected. Expressed in raw or engineering form according to GPC_RAW, in a format compatible with the parameter type (Appendix A). ICD PDF p. 118 7GPC_MAXIMChar(14)MMaximum value of the parameter, mapped to the end of the axis. Raw or engineering form according to GPC_RAW, format per Appendix A. ICD PDF p. 118 8GPC_PRCLRChar(1)MColour of the plot symbol and of the connecting lines.
  • 1 Green
  • 2 Blue
  • 3 Cyan
  • 4 Red
  • 5 Yellow
  • 6 Magenta
  • 7 White
ICD PDF p. 118 9GPC_SYMB0Char(1)OSymbol drawn at each parameter value. The field name is printed with a final digit zero ('SYMB0') in the ICD text; the HPSDB note writes 'SYMBO'.
  • 0 No symbol
  • 1 X
  • 2 +
  • 3 0
  • 4 *
  • 5 <>
  • 6 []
Default 0. ICD PDF p. 119 10GPC_LINEChar(1)OLine style connecting two consecutive values (two symbols).
  • 0 No line
  • 1 Solid line
  • 2 Long dash
  • 3 Dash
  • 4 Short dash
  • 5 Dash alternating with short dash
Default 0. ICD PDF p. 119 11GPC_DOMAINNumber(5)OIdentifier of the SCOS-2000 domain to which the plotted parameter (GPC_NAME) belongs, unsigned integer 0 to 2^16-1. It lets one graphic display combine parameters from different domains. To stay compatible with single-domain definitions the field is optional and the column may be omitted. ICD PDF p. 120

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• GPC_NUMBE → gpf.GPF_NUMBE: Many gpc records per GRD.
  • GPC_NAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: TM-model parameters only (plf or synthetic).
  • GPC_DOMAIN → vdf.VDF_DOMAINID: Inference: the ICD does not name a target table; the domain identifier has the same range as the database domain identifier VDF_DOMAINID (§3.3.1.1, PDF p.38).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.4 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.54-55) has 10 fields: there is no GPC_DOMAIN and GPC_POS, although a key field, is not marked mandatory. ICD 6.0 (S2K R4.0) added the optional GPC_DOMAIN so that graphic displays can mix parameters from several domains (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, PDF p.249). ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.109-113) and ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.113-117) already show the 11-field layout, which ICD 7.0 keeps (PDF p.116-120). Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

gpc.dat is empty (0 bytes) in both Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB; the database has only a placeholder COL1 and no rows. pyscos2000 has no gpc model. GPC_POS is Number(1), so at most 10 entries (0-9) per display are possible, although a GRD holds at most 8 plots plus, for type F, an X-axis parameter. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.29-30) constrains GPC_POS to 0-7, with an NCR to allow 0-9, and writes GPC_PRCLR as 'GPC_PLCLR'.
