docs.title: gpf.dat: Graphic displays
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.30 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The gpf table lists the Graphic Displays (GRDs), the SCOS-2000 telemetry plots, one record per graphical display. Each record gives the screen layout (full, half, quarter or sliced screen, with at most 8 plots), the header line, whether the plot scrolls when it reaches the end of the plot area, whether a hardcopy is produced automatically at the end of the plot area, the time span of the X axis (days, hours, minutes; for parameter-against-parameter plots this sets the display duration), the colour of axes, ticks and grids, and the number of tick and grid intervals on each axis. The parameters plotted and their scaling are defined in gpc. The ICD remarks that gpf and gpc are not imported into the SCOS-2000 database but are read directly by SCOS-2000 applications, and from R5.0 display definitions are converted into XML files in the FARC. The update-rate field exists only for external applications and is not used by SCOS-2000.1

Key: GPF_NUMBE

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1GPF_NUMBEChar(8)MName of the Graphical Display (GRD): alphanumeric string that uniquely identifies it; referenced by gpc.GPC_NUMBE. ICD PDF p. 114 2GPF_TYPEChar(1)MScreen layout of the graphic display. The number of plots per screen portion is a maximum, currently 8 in total. The type also determines the allowed plot-area codes in GPC_WHERE.
  • F Full screen: up to 8 plots against time or against another parameter
  • H Half screen: 2 areas of 4 plots
  • Q Quarter screen: 4 areas of 2 plots
  • S Sliced screen: 8 areas of 1 plot
ICD PDF p. 114 3GPF_HEADChar(32)OAlphanumeric header shown on the top line of the display. ICD PDF p. 114 4GPF_SCROLChar(1)OControls whether the display scrolls when the plot reaches the end of the plot area(s). docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.3 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.52-53) has the same 14 fields, but GPF_MINUT is a fractional number 0.0-59.9 (0.1 meaning a 6-second X axis when days and hours are 0) and GPF_UPUN is an update rate in milliseconds with no range. ICD 6.7 DCR S2K-DCR-5502 made GPF_MINUT an integer 0-59 and asked to clarify the unit and size of GPF_UPUN/SPF_UPUN (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, PDF p.258-259; the annex misspells the field as 'GFP_UPUN'). ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.107-109), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.111-113) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.114-116) all print the integer GPF_MINUT and UPUN in seconds, range 1-99. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

gpf.dat is present but empty (0 bytes) in the 2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16 Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB, so the database holds only a placeholder column COL1 and no rows. pyscos2000 has no gpf model. ICD 7.0 lists GPF_DAYS/HOURS/MINUT, axis colour and the tick/grid counts as mandatory even though most display tools could supply defaults. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.29) forbids real values in GPF_MINUT (range 00-59), ignores GPF_UPUN, and lists the header as 'DPF_HEAD' (a copy error).

docs.title: grp.dat: Monitoring groups definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.6.12 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

grp defines named monitoring groups, one record per group. A group is either a parameter group (members listed in grpa) or a packet group (members listed in grpk). SCOS-2000 uses monitoring groups to enable or inhibit the processing or monitoring of many parameters or packets with a single command. According to the ICD change annex, inhibiting a parameter stops its processing: no calibration, no limit checking and no distribution of updates. Inhibiting a packet means it is still stored but neither distributed nor used for parameter extraction, while parameters also carried by other packets keep updating from those. Enabling or inhibiting a group simply repeats the operation on each member; membership of several groups gets no special treatment, and there is no dedicated user interface for the feature. A parameter is enabled by default at system start. The ICD declares all three fields mandatory, including the description.1

Key: GRP_NAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1GRP_NAMEChar(14)MUnique identification name of the monitoring group; referenced by GRPA_GNAME and GRPK_GNAME.Solar Orbiter: filled in 2 of 2 rows; e.g. GRPHK, GRPPAR ICD PDF p. 108 2GRP_DESCRChar(24)MTextual description of the monitoring group (the ICD prints 'Textural'). Mandatory.Solar Orbiter: filled in 2 of 2 rows; e.g. Example for Parameters, Packet for HK monitoring ICD PDF p. 108 3GRP_GTYPEChar(2)MType of the monitoring group, which decides whether its members are listed in grpa or grpk.
  • PA Parameters group (members in grpa)
  • PK Packets group (members in grpk)
Solar Orbiter: filled in 2 of 2 rows; e.g. PA, PK ICD PDF p. 108

docs.text:
• GRP_NAME → grpa.GRPA_GNAME: Members of parameter groups (GRP_GTYPE = 'PA').
  • GRP_NAME → grpk.GRPK_GNAME: Members of packet groups (GRP_GTYPE = 'PK').

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Not present in ICD 5.1. Parameter groups, packet groups and group enable/inhibit were introduced in ICD 6.0 with the repatriation of Herschel/Planck CCS functions (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246-247). ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 102), 6.9 (p. 106) and 7.0 (p. 108) give the same three mandatory fields. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) does not model grp, so no 7.2 comparison is possible from that source.

Notes from the extraction

grp is not part of the pyscos2000 schema, so the Solar Orbiter SQLite table uses generic columns COL1..COL3, mapped here in ICD order to GRP_NAME, GRP_DESCR, GRP_GTYPE. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 2 groups, 'GRPHK' ('Packet for HK monitoring', type PK) and 'GRPPAR' ('Example for Parameters', type PA). GRPPAR has no members because grpa.dat is empty, so both appear to be examples or templates rather than operational groups (inference). The 2020 release had a single group.

docs.title: grpa.dat: Parameters groups
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.6.20 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

grpa lists the members of parameter groups, one record per monitoring parameter included in a group. A parameter may belong to any number of groups, and a group contains many parameters. The section 3.3.2 overview even mentions the same parameter appearing several times, although the key GRPA_GNAME + GRPA_PANAME allows a given parameter only once per group. The group itself must be declared in grp with GRP_GTYPE = 'PA'. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model library may be members, i.e. TM parameters that have a plf entry or synthetic parameters of any kind. Enabling or inhibiting the group then enables or inhibits each member parameter in turn. An inhibited parameter is not calibrated or limit checked and its updates are not distributed (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246-247). There is no specific user interface for group enable/inhibit, and parameters in several groups receive no special handling.1

Key: GRPA_GNAME, GRPA_PANAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1GRPA_GNAMEChar(14)MName of the monitoring group to which the parameter belongs; must match GRP_NAME of a group with GRP_GTYPE = 'PA'.Refers to grp.GRP_NAME. ICD PDF p. 109 2GRPA_PANAMEChar(8)MName of the parameter belonging to the group; must match PCF_NAME. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model library (TM parameters in plf, or synthetic parameters of any type) may be used.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. ICD PDF p. 109

docs.text:
• GRPA_GNAME → grp.GRP_NAME: Group must have GRP_GTYPE = 'PA'.
  • GRPA_PANAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: Many-to-many link between parameters and parameter groups (section 3.3.2, p. 39).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Not present in ICD 5.1; introduced in ICD 6.0 together with grp and grpk (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247). ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 102), 6.9 (p. 106) and 7.0 (p. 109) give the same two mandatory key fields. Not modelled by pyscos2000, so no ICD 7.2 comparison is available.

Notes from the extraction

grpa is not in the pyscos2000 schema; because the Solar Orbiter grpa.dat files (2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16 releases, and the SWA database) are empty, the SQLite table has a single placeholder column COL1 and no rows, so the field mapping cannot be checked against data. The overview's 'possibly many times the same parameter' (p. 39) conflicts with the two-field key, which allows a parameter only once per group; the intended meaning is probably that one parameter can appear in many groups (inference).

docs.title: grpk.dat: Telemetry packets groups
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.6.34 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

grpk lists the members of packet groups, one record per telemetry packet (identified by its SCOS-2000 Packet ID) included in a group declared in grp with GRP_GTYPE = 'PK'. A packet may belong to several groups. Enabling or inhibiting the group enables or inhibits every member packet. An inhibited packet is still stored in the archive, but it is neither distributed nor used for parameter extraction. A parameter that is also carried in another, non-inhibited packet keeps being updated from that packet, and the telemetry query display highlights the inhibited packet in red (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246-247). Group enable/inhibit is simply the repetition of the packet operation over the group content; there is no special handling of packets that belong to several groups and no specific user interface.1

docs.title: lgf.dat: Logarithmic calibrations definitions
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.70 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

lgf defines logarithmic calibrations, one record per definition, by giving up to five coefficients. SCOS-2000 computes the engineering value Y of a raw value X as Y = 1 / [A0 + A1ln(X) + A2ln^2(X) + A3ln^3(X) + A4ln^4(X)], where A0 is LGF_POL1 and A4 is LGF_POL5. Unspecified coefficients default to 0. According to the ICD change annex, this curve type was introduced to compute temperatures from resistance readings of platinum thermistors. It was built to resemble the polynomial mcf calibrations, which is why it also accepts up to five coefficients. Parameters use a logarithmic calibration by naming it in PCF_CURTX or CUR_SELECT (numerical parameters); the result is real. Logarithmic identifiers share the name space of the other non-textual calibrations, so an LGF_IDENT may not equal any CAF_NUMBR or MCF_IDENT.1

Key: LGF_IDENT

docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1LGF_IDENTChar(10)MAlphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the logarithmic calibration; used in PCF_CURTX and CUR_SELECT. It must not overlap with CAF_NUMBR or MCF_IDENT values. ICD PDF p. 72 2LGF_DESCRChar(32)OFree textual description of the logarithmic calibration. ICD PDF p. 72 3LGF_POL1Char(14)MCoefficient A0, a numerical value in real format (Appendix A). ICD PDF p. 72 4LGF_POL2Char(14)OCoefficient A1 of the first-order logarithmic term ln(X), in real format; defaults to 0.Default 0. ICD PDF p. 72 5LGF_POL3Char(14)OCoefficient A2 of the second-order term ln^2(X), in real format; defaults to 0.Default 0. ICD PDF p. 72 6LGF_POL4Char(14)OCoefficient A3 of the third-order term ln^3(X), in real format; defaults to 0.Default 0. ICD PDF p. 72 7LGF_POL5Char(14)OCoefficient A4 of the fourth-order term ln^4(X), in real format; defaults to 0.Default 0. ICD PDF p. 72

docs.text: • LGF_IDENT → pcf.PCF_CURTX, cur.CUR_SELECT: Shareable among parameters; must be unique across caf.CAF_NUMBR and mcf.MCF_IDENT.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Not present in ICD 5.1. The logarithmic curve type was added in ICD 6.0 with the repatriation of Herschel/Planck CCS functions (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 248), which also notes that the H-P CCS project explicitly excluded patching of the curve definition. ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 67-68), 6.9 (p. 70-71) and 7.0 (p. 71-72) give the same seven fields. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches, including the '0' defaults for LGF_POL2 to LGF_POL5.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. ICD 7.0 p. 72 prints 'Logarithmic Logarithmic coefficient' for LGF_POL4 (editorial duplication). The formula takes ln(X), so it is only defined for positive raw values; the ICD does not say what SCOS-2000 returns for X <= 0 (not stated in the available sources). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: lgf.dat is present but empty (0 records), so Solar Orbiter uses no logarithmic calibrations; the 2020 release and the SWA instrument database are also empty.

docs.title: mcf.dat: Polynomial calibrations definitions
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.6229 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

mcf defines polynomial calibrations, one record per definition, by giving up to five coefficients. SCOS-2000 computes the engineering value Y of a raw value X as Y = A0 + A1X + A2X^2 + A3X^3 + A4X^4, where A0 is MCF_POL1 and A4 is MCF_POL5. Unspecified higher-order coefficients default to 0, so a linear calibration needs only MCF_POL1 and MCF_POL2. Parameters use a polynomial calibration by naming it in PCF_CURTX or CUR_SELECT (numerical parameters, PCF_CATEG = 'N'). The engineering result is always real, which matters when several calibrations are attached to one parameter through cur, because they must all share the same engineering format. Polynomial identifiers share a name space with the other non-textual calibrations: an MCF_IDENT may not equal any CAF_NUMBR or LGF_IDENT. The ICD suggests a naming convention or a reserved range of names to guarantee this.1

Key: MCF_IDENT

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 calls the table 'Polynomial calibration curves: mcf' (p. 34-35); it has the same seven fields with MCF_IDENT as Number(4) and default '0' for MCF_POL2 to MCF_POL5. MCF_IDENT became Char(10) with the other calibration identifiers in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247). Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 229 polynomial calibrations. Every record fills all five coefficients explicitly; 226 are linear (only A0 and A1 non-zero) and 3 use higher orders, e.g. CIAP0081TM 'DPU_TMP' (A0 = 180.65, A1 = -0.4018, A2 = 0.0003508, A3 = -0.0000001434, A4 = 0.000000000021, real data). Coefficients are written in fixed or scientific notation (e.g. 7.35043E-4). No MCF_IDENT collides with a CAF_NUMBR; 3 definitions are not referenced by any parameter.

docs.title: ocf.dat: Monitoring checks
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.3.15,338 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

ocf declares, for each monitoring parameter that is checked, the general characteristics of its monitoring checks (out-of-limit, status, delta, status-consistency and event checks); there is at most one record per parameter and the individual checks are listed in ocp. The record states how many consecutive valid samples must violate a check before the parameter is declared out of limits (OOL), how many ocp checks exist for the parameter (1 to 16), and how the limit values in ocp are to be interpreted: as raw or calibrated values, and as real, integer or ASCII values. These checks are run by the SCOS-2000 Behaviour Limit Checker. If its optimised processing of unchanged periodic samples is enabled (MISCconfig BEHV_ENABLE_OPTIMIZATION = 1), the MISCconfig variable MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR must be larger than the largest OCF_NBCHCK in the table. The relationship between pcf and ocf is one-to-one: each parameter references only one set of checks, which can contain up to 16 checks with their own types and applicability criteria.1

Key: OCF_NAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1OCF_NAMEChar(8)MName of the parameter to be checked; must match PCF_NAME of an existing monitoring parameter.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,338 of 5,338 rows; e.g. NAHD0004, NAHD0005, NAHD0006, NAHD0007, NAHD0008 ICD PDF p. 73 2OCF_NBCHCKNumber(2)MNumber of consecutive valid samples of the parameter that must violate a check before the parameter is declared out of limits (OOL). It filters out isolated glitches. When the Behaviour Limit Checker optimisation is enabled, MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR must exceed the largest value used here (warning at the start of section 3.3.2.3.1, p. 73, which spells the field 'OCF_NBCHK').Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,338 of 5,338 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 14, 5 ICD PDF p. 73 3OCF_NBOOLNumber(2)MNumber of checks defined for this parameter in ocp, an integer from 1 to 16. It must be consistent with the number of ocp records for the parameter.Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,338 of 5,338 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 ICD PDF p. 73 4OCF_INTERChar(1)MWhether the limit values OCP_LVALU and OCP_HVALU of this parameter are raw or engineering values. Option 'C' is allowed only for parameters with one or more calibrations (see PCF_CURTX and cur). OCF_CODIN must be compatible with the data type of the view chosen here, and if the parameter is used in a command verification expression (cve) OCF_CODIN must also be compatible with CVE_INTER.
  • U Uncalibrated: limits are raw values
  • C Calibrated: limits are engineering values
Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,338 of 5,338 rows; e.g. C, U ICD PDF p. 74 5OCF_CODINChar(1)MData type in which the limit values OCP_LVALU and OCP_HVALU are written.
  • R Real values: only for raw values of real parameters (OCF_INTER = 'U' and PCF_PTC = 5), for engineering values of parameters with numerical curves of real engineering format (PCF_CATEG = 'N', CAF_ENGFMT = 'R'), or for engineering values of parameters with polynomial or logarithmic calibrations
  • A ASCII strings: only for status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S') whose expected values are given in engineering (calibrated text) form, i.e. OCF_INTER = 'C'
  • I Integer values: only for raw values of integer parameters (OCF_INTER = 'U' and PCF_PTC < 5) or for engineering values of parameters with numerical curves of integer engineering format (PCF_CATEG = 'N', CAF_ENGFMT not 'R')
Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,338 of 5,338 rows; e.g. I, R, A ICD PDF p. 75

docs.text:

  • OCF_NAME → ocp.OCP_NAME: One ocf record owns OCF_NBOOL (1-16) ocp check records.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 35-36) has the same five fields, all mandatory. Its OCF_INTER 'C' option required 'a calibration curve (PCF_CURTX not null)', and its OCF_CODIN 'A' option was tied to OCF_INTER = 'U'; ICD 7.0 allows 'C' for any calibrated parameter (including via cur) and ties 'A' to OCF_INTER = 'C' (p. 74-75). ICD 6.0 added delta checks and multiple sets of status checks (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246 and 249). ICD 6.5 added the warning about BEHV_ENABLE_OPTIMIZATION and MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR (p. 256). The field layout is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 68-70), 6.9 (p. 71-73) and 7.0. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: five mandatory fields, key OCF_NAME.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. ICD inconsistency: the field is named OCF_NBCHCK in the table but OCF_NBCHK in the warning text and change annex. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 5,338 checked parameters. OCF_INTER/OCF_CODIN combinations: C/A 1,633 (status parameters checked against text), C/R 1,558, U/I 2,029, U/R 110, C/I 8. OCF_NBCHCK ranges from 1 (3,989 parameters) to 24; values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15 and 24 occur. OCF_NBOOL matches the number of ocp records for every parameter except NCDX9308, which declares 2 checks but has no ocp record (the ICD requires consistency; the importer behaviour in that case is not stated).

docs.title: ocp.dat: Monitoring checks definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.3.27,369 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

ocp lists the individual monitoring checks of each parameter declared in ocf, in the order SCOS-2000 applies them. Each check has a type, limit or expected values and an applicability criterion OCP_RLCHK = OCP_VALPAR that enables it. Supported types are soft and hard limit checks on a valid value's range, soft and hard status checks against lists of allowed discrete values, delta checks on the change between consecutive valid samples, and status-consistency checks against a reference value maintained from the predicted or detected effect of commands. Event checks ('E') raise no OOL; they generate a SCOS-2000 event with full ID 'BEHV::<OCP_NAME>' when the value leaves the range, which can trigger system actions. Search stops at the first applicable check or soft/hard pair unless MISCconfig BEHV_STOP_FIRST_SET says otherwise. Status-consistency and event checks must precede the others. Limit checks need numerical parameters and always come in low/high pairs; soft/hard pairs share one criterion, soft first. Several records of one type and criterion form one set of allowed status values. A value equal to a limit is not OOL, and the most critical violation is shown. The table must be sorted by OCP_NAME and OCP_POS.1

Key: OCP_NAME, OCP_POS

  • H Hard limit check, or soft status check per the ICD wording (see notes)

docs.text:
• OCP_NAME → ocf.OCF_NAME: Up to 16 checks per ocf record (OCF_NBOOL).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 36-38) has the same seven fields; OCP_POS is not marked mandatory there, OCP_TYPE has only 'S' Soft OOL, 'H' Hard OOL, 'C' and 'E', and the applicability parameter is described only as 'of type integer'. Delta checks ('D') and multiple sets of status checks with different applicability criteria were added in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246 and 249). ICD 6.1 clarified that delta limits must be positive and apply in both directions (p. 251). ICD 6.4 restricted OCP_RLCHK to TM-model parameters, stated that limit checks always come in pairs and that checks of any severity may stand alone (p. 254-255). ICD 6.6 updated the OCP_TYPE description (S2K-50-DCR-755, p. 257). Field layout is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 70-76), 6.9 (p. 73-79) and 7.0 (p. 75-81). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: OCP_NAME, OCP_POS, OCP_TYPE mandatory, the rest optional, OCP_VALPAR default '1'.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. The ICD 7.0 value list for OCP_TYPE prints 'H' as 'Hard limit or soft status check' (p. 78), while the soft value 'S' is described only as 'Soft limit check'; the rules text (p. 77) describes soft and hard checks for both limit and status checks, so 'soft status' under 'H' is probably an editorial slip for 'hard status' (inference). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 7,369 checks on 5,337 parameters: H 4,153, S 3,096, D 105, C 15; no event ('E') checks. OCP_POS values run from 0 to 15; 204 records use OCP_POS 0. All 15 'C' checks belong to parameters with PCF_USCON = 'Y' and leave OCP_LVALU empty, as required. Of the 105 delta checks, 102 use OCP_LVALU = OCP_HVALU = 0 (e.g. NIU01008) and 3 use 2048/2048; the effect of a 0/0 delta range is not explained in the ICD. Status checks give text values such as 'OK', 'TRUE' or 'DIS_UNCHECK'. 859 checks have an applicability parameter; 6 records give OCP_VALPAR without OCP_RLCHK (e.g. NCST5840), which the ICD does not discuss. A parameter has at most 15 checks (ICD limit 16).

docs.title: paf.dat: Textual (de-)calibrations
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.6.3624 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The paf table defines the textual (de-)calibrations of command and sequence parameters, also called parameter alias sets, one record per alias set; the alias/raw value pairs of each set are in PAS. A parameter with calibration category T (CPC_CATEG or CSP_CATEG) references one alias set through CPC_PAFREF or CSP_PAFREF, and an alias set may be shared by many parameters. The operator can then enter or read the parameter as a text string (an engineering value such as ENABLED) instead of a number, and the aliases may also serve as default values; parameters using textual calibration display and accept engineering values in ASCII (DISPFMT=A). Unlike the monitoring calibrations (CAF/CAP, TXF/TXP), the commanding (de-)calibrations work in both directions: engineering to raw, for display and for encoding, and raw to engineering, for display. They can be attached to command parameters (CPC) and to sequence formal parameters (CSP) alike, but only to parameters whose raw value is numerical (not strings or times). The record gives the numeric format of the raw values of the set, which must be compatible with the type of the parameters that use it, and, for off-line checking only, the number of aliases.1

Key: PAF_NUMBR

  • R Real

docs.text:

No column discrepancy (4 columns in paf.dat). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 624 alias sets (605 in 2020); PAF_RAWFMT U 622, I 2. PAF_NALIAS matches the PAS count wherever filled; it is empty for four sets (CNISX205TC, CNISX207TC, CNISX211TC, CNISX214TC) and set CCDT0004TX ('Event ID list') declares 1419 aliases, a four-digit value exceeding the declared Number(3). 30 alias sets are not referenced by any CPC or CSP record. Names end in 'TC' (547), 'TX' (58) or 'TM' (19), a mission naming convention not explained in the ICD.

docs.title: pas.dat: Textual (de-)calibrations definitions
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.6.411,834 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The pas table holds the entries of the commanding textual (de-)calibrations declared in PAF, one record per alias/raw value pair. Each record associates a text string - the engineering interpretation shown to and typed by the operator - with the raw numerical value encoded in the command. When a command or sequence parameter with textual calibration (category T) is entered in engineering form, SCOS-2000 looks the text up in the alias set to obtain the raw value to encode; when a raw value is displayed, the alias text is shown. Raw values are always written in decimal and must match the raw format of the set (PAF_RAWFMT). The key (set name plus raw value) makes each raw value appear only once in a set. The text and value fields have no fixed length in ICD 7.0: their maximum length follows from the maximum command size. Aliases can also be used as default values of the parameters that reference the set (CPC_DEFVAL, CDF_VALUE, SDF_VALUE or CSP_DEFVAL written with an engineering representation).1

Key: PAS_NUMBR, PAS_ALVAL

docs.title: pcdf.dat: Packet headers definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.1.320 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The pcdf table describes the bit-level structure of each TC packet header defined in TCP, with one record per element of the header. An element is either a fixed area, whose constant value is written in the record, or a header parameter (named in PCPC) whose value SCOS-2000 fills in when the command is encoded: APID, service type, service subtype and acknowledgement flags are copied from the corresponding CCF fields of the command being encoded, while other parameters such as the packet length (computed from the actual length, including expanded repeated groups) and the source sequence counter (maintained by the multiplexer per APID) are set automatically by the command subsystem. Each record gives the length in bits and the bit offset from the start of the packet, so the table fully describes the header that precedes the application data defined by CDF. The header length (sum of PCDF_LEN) is part of the overhead deducted from the maximum command size. Header parameters cannot be edited by operators on a SCOS-2000 manual stack. For special command types (CCF_CTYPE R or F) the PCDF/CDF entries describe the frame data field instead of a packet.1

Key: PCDF_TCNAME, PCDF_BIT

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PCDF_TCNAMEChar(8)MName of the packet header (TCP_ID) that this element belongs to. Together with PCDF_BIT it forms the key, so a header can have many elements but only one element starting at a given bit offset.Refers to tcp.TCP_ID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 20 of 20 rows; e.g. NOM_TC, HPC1_TC ICD PDF p. 129 2PCDF_DESCChar(24)OTextual description of the element. The ICD states that it is used for fixed areas only (header parameters are described by PCPC_DESC).Solar Orbiter: filled in 20 of 20 rows; e.g. APID, DataFieldHeaderFlag, Packet Length, Sequence Count, Type ICD PDF p. 129 3PCDF_TYPEChar(1)MType of the header element, which determines where its value comes from at encoding time. A fixed area takes its value from PCDF_VALUE. The A, T, S and K types are placeholders filled from the command definition (CCF_APID, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE and CCF_ACK respectively); a command whose header lacks one of these element types may leave the corresponding CCF field empty. Type P covers any other header parameter whose value the SCOS-2000 command subsystem sets automatically, for example the packet length or the source sequence count.
  • F Fixed area; value taken from PCDF_VALUE (hexadecimal).
  • A APID parameter; value taken from CCF_APID of the command.
  • T Service type parameter; value taken from CCF_TYPE.
  • S Service subtype parameter; value taken from CCF_STYPE.
  • K Acknowledgement flags parameter; value taken from CCF_ACK (which can be changed when the command is loaded, as from R4.0).
  • P Other packet parameter set automatically by the SCOS-2000 command subsystem (e.g. packet length, source sequence counter).
Solar Orbiter: filled in 20 of 20 rows; e.g. F, P, A, K, O ICD PDF p. 130 4PCDF_LENNumber(4)MLength of the header element in bits, given as an unsigned decimal integer. docs.text:
• PCDF_TCNAME → tcp.TCP_ID: Header to which the element belongs.
  • PCDF_PNAME → pcpc.PCPC_PNAME: Header parameter for elements of type A, T, S, K or P; PCPC_CODE decides how PCDF_VALUE is read.
  • PCDF_TYPE → ccf.CCF_APID / ccf.CCF_TYPE / ccf.CCF_STYPE / ccf.CCF_ACK: Elements of type A, T, S and K are filled from these fields of the command being encoded; a CCF field may be empty only if its header has no element of the corresponding type.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Structure unchanged from ICD 5.1 (section 3.3.3.1.3, PDF p.61-62) through ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.122), ICD 6.9 (PDF p.126-128) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.129-131): eight fields with key PCDF_TCNAME + PCDF_BIT, PCDF_VALUE Char(10) mandatory and PCDF_RADIX defaulting to 'H'. The PCDF_TYPE options F, A, T, S, K and P are the same in ICD 5.1 and ICD 7.0. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same eight columns in the same order, the same keys (PCDF_TCNAME, PCDF_BIT), the same mandatory fields and the default 'H' for PCDF_RADIX.

Notes from the extraction

Columns match ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000 one to one (8 columns in every line of the Solar Orbiter pcdf.dat). Discrepancy with ICD 7.0: in the 2025-09-16 Solar Orbiter MIB the NOM_TC element 'Source ID' (8 bits at bit 72, parameter DFH_SRC) has PCDF_TYPE='O', a value that is not among the options listed in ICD 7.0 (F, A, T, S, K, P); in the 2020-04-16 release the same element was a fixed area (type F, value 0). The meaning of 'O' is not stated in the available sources (the pyscos2000 schema dump does not list the allowed enumeration values). Solar Orbiter NOM_TC layout (real data, bit offsets from packet start): version 3 bits at 0 (F=0), type 1 bit at 3 (F=1), data field header flag 1 bit at 4 (F=1), APID 11 bits at 5 (A), sequence flags 2 bits at 16 (F=3), sequence count 14 bits at 18 (P), packet length 16 bits at 32 (P), secondary header flag 1 bit at 48 (F=0), PUS version 3 bits at 49 (F=1), ack 4 bits at 52 (K), service type 8 bits at 56 (T), subtype 8 bits at 64 (S), source ID 8 bits at 72 (O), i.e. an 80-bit (10-octet) header. HPC1_TC has only the 48-bit primary header with data field header flag 0. All Solar Orbiter PCDF_VALUE entries are 0, 1 or 3 and PCDF_RADIX is 'H' everywhere. Related tailoring: the Herschel HCSS MIB note (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note, point 5.2.7, PDF p.13) requires at least four PCDF rows per packet header ID and remarks that its reference ICD then described PCDF_TCNAME as unique; in ICD 7.0 PCDF_TCNAME is only part of a composite key with PCDF_BIT, so that conflict does not arise.

docs.title: pcf.dat: Monitoring parameters characteristics
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.1.1126,745 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

pcf is the central monitoring table: it holds one record for every monitoring parameter known to SCOS-2000, whether it is a raw telemetry parameter extracted from TM packets, a user defined constant, or a synthetic parameter computed on ground (OL, SPEL, hard-coded or saved synthetic). Each record gives the parameter's name, description, on-board identifier, unit, PUS type and format codes (PTC/PFC), calibration category and calibration link, validity condition, nature, display hints and time/endianness handling. Most other monitoring tables hang off it: cur, caf, txf, mcf and lgf for calibration, ocf/ocp for limit and status checks, plf and vpd for the location of the parameter inside fixed and variable packets, grpa for parameter groups and the display tables for ANDs, graphics and scrolling displays. SCOS-2000 evaluates a parameter's state validity as TRUE only when its validity criterion holds and the validity parameter is itself valid. In addition, parameters carried in periodic packets are automatically flagged 'expired' when no new packet arrives within the packet period (PID_INTER) plus a global margin set in MISCconfig and adjustable through TM SPACON. Fields 20 to 23 are optional for backwards compatibility, so the importer accepts records with 19, 20, 21, 22 or 23 fields.1

Key: PCF_NAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PCF_NAMEChar(8)MAlphanumeric name that uniquely identifies the monitoring parameter; it is the key used by every other table that refers to a monitoring parameter. Because the Operations Language (OL) recognises the nature of a component from its leading characters, no parameter name may start with 'VAR', 'GVAR' or '$'. The names NNOiiii, CEBiiii, KRUiiii, MSPiiii, VL2iiii, PERiiii, REDiiii and MLGiiii (iiii being four digits from 0000 to 9999) are reserved for ground-station telemetry and must not be used for spacecraft parameters. For dynamic synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR 'D' or 'P') the expression file must carry exactly this name. As for all ICD names, uniqueness is case-insensitive (A1000 and a1000 may not coexist, section 3.3, p. 35).Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. DUMMYVAL, NACSXN12, NACSXN13, NACSXN14, NACSXNE2 ICD PDF p. 41 2PCF_DESCRChar(24)OFree textual description of the parameter (up to 24 characters). It is displayed alongside the parameter name, for example in the Variable Packets Display when VPD_DCHAR = 2.Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. PADDING 32 bit, Spare, SPARE, Reserved, timeStep ICD PDF p. 41 3PCF_PIDNumber(10)OOn-board identifier of the telemetry parameter, i.e. the PUS 'Parameter#'. It creates a one-to-one mapping between the ground name and the on-board ID, and is used to recognise which parameter a value belongs to when values are delivered in a PUS variable packet (for example a parameter-ID field flagged with VPD_PIDREF = 'Y', or the ID field that drives a deduced parameter). On-board IDs must be unique; if two parameters share a PCF_PID, SCOS-2000 uses the last one imported. Leave it null when no on-board identifier exists, e.g. for ground-only parameters defined by the user. Unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^32-1.Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,803 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 0, 167776256, 167776257, 167776258, 167776259 ICD PDF p. 42 4PCF_UNITChar(4)OEngineering unit mnemonic, for example 'VOLT'. Monitoring displays show it next to the calibrated value for parameters that have a calibration (see PCF_CURTX), or next to the raw value for parameters that have none.Solar Orbiter: filled in 5,124 of 126,745 rows; e.g. DegC, A, V, degC, ms ICD PDF p. 42 5PCF_PTCNumber(2)MParameter Type Code: the PUS encoding format of the parameter. SCOS-2000 uses it to decode values extracted from TM packets (PCF_NATUR 'R' or 'C'). Synthetic parameters must also be given a valid PTC that matches the format in which their value is computed (integer, real, string, ...), otherwise the import rejects them; saved synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = 'S') must use PTC 13. Integer in the range 1 to 13; the supported PTC/PFC combinations are listed in Appendix A, Table 4 (PDF p. 214-224), which has no row for PTC 12.
  • 1 Boolean: unsigned integer of 1 bit (PFC 0)
  • 2 Enumerated: unsigned integer of PFC bits (PFC 1 to 32)
  • 3 Unsigned integer; PFC 0-12 give 4-16 bits, 13 = 24 bits, 14 = 32 bits (48/64-bit PFC 15/16 not supported)
  • 4 Signed integer (two's complement); same PFC-to-length mapping as PTC 3
  • 5 Real: PFC 1 IEEE single (32 bits), 2 IEEE double (64 bits), 3 MIL-STD-1750A 32-bit, 4 MIL-STD-1750A 48-bit (commands only)
  • 6 Bit string: handled by SCOS-2000 as an unsigned integer of PFC bits (1-32), monitoring side only; PFC 0 (variable) not supported
  • 7 Octet string: PFC = fixed length in octets; PFC 0 (variable length) only for command/sequence parameters
  • 8 ASCII character string: PFC = fixed length in octets; PFC 0 (variable length) only for command/sequence parameters
  • 9 Absolute time: PFC 1 CDS without microseconds, 2 CDS with microseconds (commands only), 3-18 CUC with 1-4 coarse and 0-3 fine octets, 30 Unix time (seconds + microseconds); PFC 0 (with p-field) not supported
  • 10 Relative time in CUC format (PFC 3-18)
  • 11 Deduced: the actual type is taken from the parameter whose on-board ID is given by the PCF_RELATED parameter
  • 13 Saved synthetic parameter: value characteristics derived from the related synthetic parameter (PCF_RELATED)
Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 3, 5, 2, 7, 1 ICD PDF p. 43 6PCF_PFCNumber(5)MParameter Format Code. Together with PCF_PTC it fixes the length (and sub-format) of the parameter. SCOS-2000 only uses it for parameters extracted from TM packets (PCF_NATUR 'R' or 'C'), but a valid PFC must still be given for synthetic parameters or the import rejects them. The allowed range depends on the PTC as specified in Appendix A.Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 1, 12, 4, 14, 8 ICD PDF p. 43 7PCF_WIDTHNumber(6)O'Padded' width of the parameter in bits. It is used only when samples are extracted with the VPD definition (variable packets): if set, the SCOS-2000 VPD application uses it to find the bit where the next parameter starts. This matters when the slot reserved for a parameter is wider than the length implied by its PTC/PFC, for example when padding bits byte-align the next field. For deduced parameters (PTC 11) it can be used in two ways: (a) if a width is given, the value is always extracted from a field of that fixed width; (b) if no width is given, the width follows the type of the parameter actually being downlinked, padded according to that parameter's own width if it has one. It is not used for fixed packets described in plf, where the length always follows from PTC/PFC.Solar Orbiter: filled in 7 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 64, 104, 32 ICD PDF p. 44 8PCF_VALIDChar(8)OName of the parameter that determines this parameter's state validity; PCF_VALPAR gives the value it is compared with, and SCOS-2000 also requires the validity parameter itself to be valid. Only parameters whose raw value is a signed or unsigned integer and that are processed by the telemetry model library (TM parameters with a plf entry, or synthetic parameters of any kind) may be used. For a synthetic parameter (PCF_NATUR other than 'R') the overall validity is the logical AND of the validity derived from its contributing parameters and this explicit criterion. Circular dependencies are forbidden: a parameter must not be, or feed a synthetic parameter that is, its own validity parameter, directly or through a chain of validity parameters.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 20,692 of 126,745 rows; e.g. NCSD0PC3, NCSD0PD3, NCSD0PE3, NCSD0PF3, NCSD0PC4 ICD PDF p. 45 9PCF_RELATEDChar(8)OName of another monitoring parameter, used for one of two purposes. For saved synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = 'S') it names the synthetic parameter whose computed value is stored in the synthetic parameter packets: a saved synthetic parameter has no expression of its own, it borrows the expression of this parameter. For deduced telemetry parameters (PCF_PTC = 11) it names the telemetry parameter (the PUS 'Parameter#') whose value gives the on-board parameter ID that tells SCOS-2000 how to interpret the deduced value in variable TM packets.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 10 of 126,745 rows; e.g. NCD0C095, NCAB0NU0, NCD12904, NTTSX030, NTTSX031 ICD PDF p. 46 10PCF_CATEGChar(1)MCalibration category of the parameter, which decides what kind of calibration PCF_CURTX or cur may point to and how checks are interpreted.
  • N Numerical: numerical parameters with one or more numerical, polynomial or logarithmic calibrations or with none, and also parameters with PTC 6, 7, 9 or 10 (all non-numerical types except character strings)
  • S Status: only for parameters associated with a textual calibration
  • T Text: only for character-string parameters (PTC 8)
Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. N, S, T ICD PDF p. 47 11PCF_NATURChar(1)MNature of the parameter, i.e. where its source value comes from. Dynamic OL and SPEL parameters need an ASCII expression file named after the parameter (directories IMPT_EXPR_DIR and IMPT_SPEL_DIR); saved synthetic parameters are computed centrally by the SPPG process and need a plf entry in a synthetic packet; static constants take their value from PCF_PARVAL. The description continues on PDF p. 49.
  • R Raw telemetry parameter whose value is extracted from TM packets (also used for 'dynamic' user defined constants carried in the constants TM packet)
  • D Dynamic OL synthetic parameter: Operations Language expression, not compiled, evaluated locally on demand
  • P SPEL-based dynamic synthetic parameter (Synthetic Parameters Expression Language); per section 3.3.2.1.2 supported only by the EGSE delivery of SCOS-2000
  • H Hard-coded synthetic parameter: written in C++ or compiled from OL and linked into the relevant library
  • S Saved synthetic parameter: computed from the expression of the PCF_RELATED parameter and stored in synthetic packets
  • C Constant ('static' user defined constant) whose value is PCF_PARVAL; must not also have a plf entry in the constants TM packet
Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. R, D, S ICD PDF p. 48 12PCF_CURTXChar(10)OIdentifier of the calibration to apply when the parameter has exactly one calibration definition. A monitoring parameter may have zero, one or several calibrations; several (conditional) calibrations are defined in cur instead. Depending on the category the value must match TXF_NUMBR (PCF_CATEG = 'S') or CAF_NUMBR, MCF_IDENT or LGF_IDENT (PCF_CATEG = 'N') of an existing textual, numerical, polynomial or logarithmic calibration. It cannot be null for status parameters, and it must be null for textual parameters ('T'), string parameters (PTC 7 or 8), time parameters (PTC 9 or 10) and any parameter that appears as CUR_PNAME in cur.Refers to txf.TXF_NUMBR | caf.CAF_NUMBR | mcf.MCF_IDENT | lgf.LGF_IDENT. Solar Orbiter: filled in 30,936 of 126,745 rows; e.g. CCDT0006TM, CCDT0004TX, PARAMIDTM, CCDT0078TM, CCDT0003TX ICD PDF p. 49 13PCF_INTERChar(1)OExtrapolation flag for parameters calibrated with a numerical curve: what to do with a raw value outside the curve. Only relevant with a numerical calibration; for textual calibrations a raw value with no text yields an invalid engineering value shown as '****'. ICD 7.0 states that SCOS-2000 ignores PCF_INTER and uses CAF_INTER of the calibration curve instead, so all parameters sharing a curve extrapolate the same way, while different curves of one parameter may differ. The row is shaded grey in the ICD (not used by SCOS-2000).
  • P Extrapolate a valid engineering value from the first two (below range) or last two (above range) calibration points
  • F Return an invalid engineering value for raw values outside the curve
Default F. Solar Orbiter: filled in 126,745 of 126,745 rows; e.g. F ICD PDF p. 50 14PCF_USCONChar(1)OEnables status consistency checking of the parameter (comparison of the telemetry value with a reference value maintained from the expected effect of commands). It must be 'Y' when ocp contains a status-consistency check (OCP_TYPE = 'C') for the parameter. The number of parameters that can be status-consistency checked is limited by the maximum size of the SCOS-2000 packet holding the snapshot of all status consistency checks; from release 4.1 the limit can be changed with the MISCconfig variable MAX_SCC_MESSAGE_LENGTH (a 4-byte integer).

  • N Parameter is not status-consistency checked

It applies only to 'static' user defined constants (PCF_NATUR = 'C'), for which it is mandatory. The value must be written in a format compatible with the parameter type (PTC/PFC, Appendix A). Static constants are initialised from this value unless a permanent change has been made with the OL editor since the last import (section 3.3.2.1.3, p. 59).Solar Orbiter: filled in 4 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 0, 10, 11 ICD PDF p. 51 17PCF_SUBSYSChar(8)OName of the group (subsystem) to which the parameter belongs, intended for organising and filtering parameters in a future extension. The row is shaded grey and in italics in the ICD: not used and not currently supported by SCOS-2000.Solar Orbiter: filled in 108,135 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 2, 1, 6, 4, 101 ICD PDF p. 52 18PCF_VALPARNumber(5)ORaw value of the validity parameter (PCF_VALID) for which this parameter is valid; the validity expression is PCF_VALID = PCF_VALPAR. Defaults to 1 when left null.Default 1. Solar Orbiter: filled in 18,256 of 126,745 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 0, 80, 32 ICD PDF p. 52 19PCF_SPTYPEChar(1)OOutput view of a synthetic parameter's calculation. If a synthetic parameter has a calibration, the value returned by its expression is treated as the raw value and the engineering view is obtained through the calibration. SCOS-2000 does not import this field (grey row); it exists so that the off-line consistency checker can verify that synthetic parameters which already return an engineering value are not wrongly given a calibration.
  • E Engineering
  • R Raw
Solar Orbiter: filled in 6 of 126,745 rows; e.g. R ICD PDF p. 52 20PCF_CORRChar(1)OWhether absolute time parameters are time-correlated (on-board time converted to ground time with the applicable time correlation coefficients) when the raw data are interpreted. It must be set explicitly to 'N' for relative time parameters (PTC 10). PCF_OBTID selects which on-board time format and correlation coefficients apply. Without correlation the OBT format is still needed to know the time reference (the absolute time that corresponds to zero); if no OBT ID is given and PCF_CORR = 'N', the epoch is defined by the MISC variable TCO_ESA_EPOCH.   • N Extract the time value without time correlation

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PCF_NAME → plf.PLF_NAME, vpd.VPD_NAME, cur.CUR_PNAME, ocf.OCF_NAME, grpa.GRPA_PANAME, dpc/gpc/spc display contents: Referenced by the packet-location, calibration-selection, monitoring-check, group and display tables (section 3.3.2, p. 38-39).
  • PCF_VALID → pcf.PCF_NAME: Many-to-one self-relationship: each parameter has at most one validity parameter, which may be shared by many parameters (p. 38).
  • PCF_RELATED → pcf.PCF_NAME: Saved synthetic parameter -> source synthetic parameter, or deduced parameter -> on-board parameter-ID parameter.
  • PCF_CURTX → caf.CAF_NUMBR / mcf.MCF_IDENT / lgf.LGF_IDENT (PCF_CATEG 'N') or txf.TXF_NUMBR (PCF_CATEG 'S'): Single calibration. Many-to-one: each parameter references one curve, a curve can be shared (p. 39). Conditional/multiple calibrations go through cur instead.
  • PCF_PID → values of parameter-ID fields in variable packets (vpd.VPD_PIDREF = 'Y') and of deduced-parameter ID fields: Maps the PUS on-board Parameter# to the ground parameter name.
  • PCF_NAME → synthetic expression file named PCF_NAME (OL or SPEL): Required for PCF_NATUR 'D' (directory IMPT_EXPR_DIR) and 'P' (directory IMPT_SPEL_DIR) (section 3.3.2.1.2, p. 55-56). In the wiki's SQLite copy these files are in table synthetic(NAME, SOURCE).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, p. 23-28) defines 19 fields; differences from 7.0: PCF_DESCR is Char(16), PCF_CURTX is Number(4) and refers only to textual, numerical or polynomial calibrations, PCF_NATUR has no 'P' option, and PCF_INTER has no import default. ICD 6.0 (SCOS-2000 R4.0, Annex 1 of ICD 7.0, p. 246-250) widened the PCF_PID range from 2^31-1 to 2^32-1 (DCR-2421), changed calibration identifiers from Number(4) to Char(10), introduced multiple/conditional calibrations (cur) and logarithmic curves, and added the SPEL option 'P' for the EGSE delivery. ICD 6.2/6.3 (R4.1) updated the descriptions of PCF_USCON, PCF_VALID, PCF_INTER and PCF_SPTYPE and removed the mandatory flag of PCF_NATUR (p. 253); ICD 6.7 restored the 'M' (S2K-SPR-4787, p. 258). ICD 6.4 limited PCF_VALID to parameters processed by the TM model and clarified PCF_WIDTH for deduced parameters (p. 254-255). ICD 6.7 (R5.2) widened PCF_DESCR to 24 characters (S2K-SPR-3797) and added fields 20-23: PCF_CORR and PCF_OBTID (S2K-SCR-4917), PCF_DARC (S2K-DCR-5146, S2K-SPR-5711) and PCF_ENDIAN (S2K-DCR-5192) (p. 258-259). ICD 6.9 updated PCF_OBTID (S2K-DCR-5743, p. 260) and printed an import default '0' for it (icd-6-9 p. 53), which ICD 7.0 no longer shows (p. 54). ICD 7.0 (2017, Annex 2, p. 261-263) states that PCF_INTER is ignored in favour of CAF_INTER (S2K-8325), rewrites PCF_ENDIAN (S2K-8353; in 6.9 it was a 'future extension' for integers longer than 16 bits, icd-6-9 p. 54), lists the reserved ground-station names in PCF_NAME (S2K-6884) and requires PCF_CORR = 'N' for relative times (S2K-8572). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) adds a 24th optional field PCF_DESCR2 (default empty string).

Notes from the extraction

ICD 7.0 vs pyscos2000 (7.2): names, order, optionality, keys and defaults of fields 1-23 agree; pyscos2000 adds PCF_DESCR2 as field 24, which ICD 7.0 does not define (its size and meaning are not stated in the available sources). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: all 126,745 records have exactly 23 fields, so PCF_DESCR2 is empty everywhere (the SQLite column exists only because the loader follows pyscos2000). PCF_NATUR values are R (125,161), D (1,582) and S (2); no H, P or C parameters. The 1,582 'D' parameters match the 1,582 expression files in table synthetic. PCF_CATEG: N 100,087, S 26,538, T 120 (all T parameters have PTC 8). PCF_PARVAL is filled for 4 parameters (NDSZ0001, NDSZ0002, NPWZ0000, NRUZ0000) whose PCF_NATUR is 'R', although the ICD defines PCF_PARVAL only for PCF_NATUR 'C'. Three of them (NDSZ0001 'DST1_MODEL', NDSZ0002, NPWZ0000 'PCDU_MODEL') are dynamic user defined constants located in SPID 66830 (TM(160,3), APID 1966, 'Dynamic UDCs') and serve as CUR_RLCHK model selectors in cur; NRUZ0000 has no plf entry. Inference: Solar Orbiter uses PCF_PARVAL to document an initial value of dynamic UDCs, which the ICD does not describe. PCF_INTER is 'F' in every record (ignored by SCOS-2000 anyway); PCF_OBTID is never filled (mission default OBT ID); PCF_DARC is '1' for 49,330 parameters and empty (default '0') otherwise; PCF_ENDIAN is 'L' for a single parameter (NYG02201 'GS Packet Size') and empty (default 'B') elsewhere. PCF_SUBSYS holds small numeric codes ('2', '1', '6', '4', '101', ...) rather than subsystem names. PCF_WIDTH is set for 7 parameters: 5 deduced parameters (PTC 11, 32 or 64 bits) and the 2 saved synthetic parameters NTTSS030/NTTSS031 (PTC 13, PFC 0, width 104 bits = the 13-byte slot required by section 3.3.2.1.2, related to NTTSX030/NTTSX031 and located at offsets 0 and 13 of SPID 66838, TM(251,2) APID 1966 'Saved Synthetics'). All 47 relative-time parameters (PTC 10) have PCF_CORR = 'N' as ICD 7.0 requires; 3 absolute-time parameters also have 'N'. Parameter NYG02204 uses PTC 9 / PFC 2 (CDS with microseconds), which Appendix A (p. 219) lists as supported for command parameters only, and NYG02101/NYG02102 use Unix time (9, 30). PCF_PID is filled for 19,803 parameters with no duplicates (DUMMYVAL 'ALWAYS_VALID' has PCF_PID 0). 2,436 parameters have PCF_VALID but no PCF_VALPAR (import default 1 applies); all validity parameters exist and have PTC 1, 2 or 3. No parameter has both PCF_CURTX and cur entries; the 5 status parameters without PCF_CURTX all use cur, consistent with the ICD. No names start with VAR, GVAR or $, and none match the reserved ground-station patterns. 15,067 raw parameters (PCF_NATUR 'R') have neither a plf nor a vpd entry (1,192 of them have a PCF_PID). ICD typo: the PCF_WIDTH description (p. 44) says 'PCD_WIDTH' where PCF_WIDTH of the downlinked parameter is meant.

docs.title: pcf_glob_det.dat: Global-to-detailed parameter decomposition (inferred title)
docs.text:
not defined in the ICD56,631 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Inference

This table is not defined by the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD. Its column meanings below were inferred from the data and are this wiki's interpretation.

Inferred from the data; not documented in any available ICD. Each record states that a 'detailed' monitoring parameter (column 2) is a bit field inside a 'global' monitoring parameter (column 1), starting column 3 bits after the start of the global parameter. Typical global parameters are whole words or octet strings that the spacecraft reports as one item (for example NAH0Z000 'APMHA_TM_1 [000]', an 8-bit unsigned integer with an on-board parameter ID); the detailed parameters are the flags and small enumerations inside them (NAHD0000 'APMHA_Mode', 3 bits at offset 0; NAHD0001, 1 bit at offset 3; and so on). The relation is consistent with the packet layouts: in all 215,859 cases (2025 release) where both parameters appear in the same packet, PLF bit position of the detailed parameter equals that of the global parameter plus column 3. SCOS-2000 extracts each parameter independently from PLF, so this table is probably used by mission tools, for example to generate PLF entries, to decode on-board parameter reports that carry only the global parameter, or to relate data-pool items to their fields. That use is an inference.

Key: COL2
tags: Solar Orbiter mission-specific tables (not in the ICD)

docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1COL1Char(8) observedMInferred: name of the global (container) parameter. Always a pcf.PCF_NAME. 8,704 distinct globals in 2025; they are unsigned integers (3/4, 3/12, 3/13, 3/14) or fixed octet strings (PTC 7, up to 6,448 octets), and 14,016 rows refer to globals that have an on-board parameter ID (PCF_PID).Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 56,631 of 56,631 rows; e.g. NAH0Z000, NAH0Z001, NAH0Z002, NAH0Z003, NAH0Z004 2COL2Char(8) observedMInferred: name of the detailed parameter contained in the global one. Always a pcf.PCF_NAME and unique in the table (each detailed parameter belongs to exactly one global parameter). Mostly booleans, enumerations, unsigned integers and reals (e.g. 1/0, 2/n, 3/4, 3/12, 5/1).Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 56,631 of 56,631 rows; e.g. NAHD0000, NAHD0001, NAHD0002, NAHD0003, NAHD0004 3COL3Number (0 to 50752 observed)MInferred: bit offset of the detailed parameter from the first (most significant) bit of the global parameter. Verified against PLF: detailed position = global position + offset in every co-located case (215,859 of 215,859 in 2025; 194,375 of 194,375 in 2020). No bit-field detail extends beyond the width of its integer or octet-string global.Solar Orbiter: filled in 56,631 of 56,631 rows; e.g. 0, 3, 4, 5, 6

docs.title: pcpc.dat: Packet headers parameters
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.1.27 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The pcpc table defines the named TC packet header parameters, one record per parameter. A header parameter is a header element whose value is not a constant fixed area but is filled in by SCOS-2000 at encoding time, for example the APID, the PUS service type and subtype, the acknowledgement flags, the packet length or the packet sequence count. PCDF records of type A, T, S, K or P point to a PCPC record through PCDF_PNAME to give such an element a name, and the same header parameter can be used at different positions or in several packet headers (with the constraint stated under PCDF_LEN that every use of a given parameter must have the same length). The only behavioural attribute held here is PCPC_CODE, which states whether the default value written in PCDF_VALUE for this parameter is a signed or an unsigned integer, and therefore whether PCDF_RADIX applies. Operators cannot edit these values on a manual stack: they come from the CCF record of each command or are computed by the command subsystem (packet length, source sequence counter per APID).1

Key: PCPC_PNAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PCPC_PNAMEChar(8)MUnique name of the packet header parameter. PCDF records of type A, T, S, K or P quote this name in PCDF_PNAME to identify which header parameter occupies a given position in a packet header.Solar Orbiter: filled in 7 of 7 rows; e.g. DFH_ACK, DFH_SRC, DFH_STPE, DFH_TYPE, PH_APID ICD PDF p. 128 2PCPC_DESCChar(24)MTextual description of the header parameter (up to 24 characters). Mandatory in the ICD, although it is descriptive only.Solar Orbiter: filled in 7 of 7 rows; e.g. APID, Ack, Packet Length, Sequence Count, Service Subtype ICD PDF p. 128 3PCPC_CODEChar(1)OFormat flag telling SCOS-2000 how the value given for this parameter in PCDF_VALUE is written: as a signed integer (then expressed in decimal) or as an unsigned integer (then expressed in the radix given by PCDF_RADIX). If left empty, unsigned is assumed.
  • I Signed integer: PCDF_VALUE is decimal and PCDF_RADIX is irrelevant.
  • U Unsigned integer (import default): PCDF_VALUE is expressed in the radix given by PCDF_RADIX.
Default U. Solar Orbiter: filled in 7 of 7 rows; e.g. U ICD PDF p. 129

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • PCPC_PNAME → pcdf.PCDF_PNAME: Each PCDF element of type A, T, S, K or P names a header parameter; one parameter may appear in several headers.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Unchanged in structure in ICD 5.1 (section 3.3.3.1.2, PDF p.60-61), ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.121), ICD 6.9 (PDF p.125-126) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.128-129): PCPC_PNAME Char(8) key, PCPC_DESC Char(24) mandatory and PCPC_CODE Char(1) with import default 'U' and values I/U. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same three columns, with PCPC_DESC mandatory and PCPC_CODE defaulting to 'U'.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in names, order or optionality between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 (7.2) and the Solar Orbiter pcpc.dat (3 columns). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16 defines 7 header parameters, all unsigned: PH_APID, PH_SSC, PH_LEN (primary header) and DFH_ACK, DFH_TYPE, DFH_STPE, DFH_SRC (data field header). DFH_SRC ('Source ID') is new compared with the 2020-04-16 release (6 records), where the source identifier was still a fixed area in PCDF.

docs.title: pic.dat: Packets identification criteria
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.4.2256 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

pic tells the SCOS-2000 telemetry packetiser which additional identification fields (PI1, PI2) to read from an incoming TM packet to identify it uniquely, and where to find them. A record covers one PUS type/subtype combination, optionally limited to one APID, and gives the byte offset and bit width of each field. If no extra field is needed, both offsets are set to -1. Lookup precedence: a record matching type, subtype and APID is used first; otherwise a record matching type and subtype only (APID left blank); if neither exists, pid is searched with PI1 = PI2 = 0. The packetiser then searches pid with type/subtype/APID/PI1/PI2 to find the SPID and TPSD. The section 3.3.2.4 overview warns that this assumes all packets of one type/subtype carry their identification fields at the same position and with the same length, a constraint on the on-board design that PIC_APID (ICD 6.5) relaxes per APID. pic is loaded directly by the packetiser and is not imported into the run-time database.1

Key: PIC_TYPE, PIC_STYPE, PIC_APID

Set to -1 when the second field is not relevant.Solar Orbiter: filled in 256 of 256 rows; e.g. -1, 18, 17, 19, 114 ICD PDF p. 93 6PIC_PI2_WIDNumber(3)MWidth of the second additional identification field in bits.Solar Orbiter: filled in 256 of 256 rows; e.g. 0, 8, 32, 16, 40 ICD PDF p. 93 7PIC_APIDNumber(5)OAPID of the TM source packet to which this record is restricted. If the field is omitted or blank, no APID is specified and the record applies to all APIDs of this type/subtype; the import default 99999 stands for 'any APID'. docs.text: • PIC_TYPE, PIC_STYPE, PIC_APID → pid.PID_TYPE, pid.PID_STYPE, pid.PID_APID: The extracted PI1/PI2 values are matched against pid.PID_PI1_VAL and pid.PID_PI2_VAL.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 42-43) has six fields keyed on type and subtype; PIC_PI2_OFF and PIC_PI2_WID are not mandatory there, and the second offset is described as counted from the 'end' of the SCOS-2000 packet body. ICD 6.5 (R4.2) added the optional PIC_APID so that PI1/PI2 position and width can be defined for a specific APID/type/subtype (SPR-3071, DCR-4535; ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 255). ICD 6.7 corrected PIC_PI2_OFF to count from the start of the body and stated that PIC_APID cannot be a key because it may be null or omitted (S2K-DCR-5502 items 3 and 7, p. 258-259). ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 86-87) and 6.9 (p. 90-91) show PIC_APID as field 7 without key mark or default. ICD 7.0 made PIC_APID part of the key (S2K-8528, applicable to SCOS-2000 4.2 or higher, p. 262) and prints the import default 99999 (p. 93). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches ICD 7.0: key PIC_TYPE + PIC_STYPE + PIC_APID, PIC_APID optional with default '99999'.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 256 records; 183 need no extra identification (PIC_PI1_OFF = -1 with width 0); PI1 is mostly at byte offset 16 (just after a 16-byte primary plus data field header), 8, 16 or 32 bits wide, and PI2 offsets reach byte 114. PIC_APID is filled in 47 records (41 distinct APIDs, e.g. TM(5,1) defined per APID 1974, 1975, 1985, 1991 with different PI2 widths); the others apply to all APIDs.

docs.title: pid.dat: Packets identification
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.4.111,150 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

pid maps the source packets produced by the spacecraft, or by ground systems, to SCOS-2000 telemetry packet identifiers. The telemetry packetiser recognises a packet by its APID, PUS type and subtype and up to two extra identification fields (PI1, PI2) whose position pic gives. It looks up pid with that 5-field key and then files and distributes the packet under the processing keys found there: the SPID, which selects the fixed layout in plf, and the TPSD, which selects the variable layout in vpd. One packet may be processed both ways. Packets identified by APID alone use 0 for the other key fields. Since R5.0 each distinct packet must have its own SPID. Duplicate keys are allowed only with PID_VALID selecting one valid record. Once archiving has started, the key-to-SPID allocation and the TPSD should not change and archived SPIDs must not be deleted, or retrieval services such as GDDS break. Internally generated packets (UDC, MISC, synthetic, system control) should also have pid and tpcf entries, with an unused type/subtype/APID combination. The table also sets the event packets raised on reception, the presence of a time field and of a checksum, and the period used for parameter expiry.1

Key: PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_PI2_VAL, PID_SPID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PID_TYPENumber(3)MPUS service type of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. Zero means that the packet has no specific type, e.g. it has no PUS data field header.Solar Orbiter: filled in 11,150 of 11,150 rows; e.g. 5, 1, 131, 3, 21 ICD PDF p. 84 2PID_STYPENumber(3)MPUS service subtype of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PID_SPID → plf.PLF_SPID, tpcf.TPCF_SPID, grpk.GRPK_PKSPID: SPID identifies the fixed packet layout (plf), its characteristics (tpcf) and packet-group membership.
  • PID_TPSD → vpd.VPD_TPSD: Variable packet structure used by the Variable Packets Display.
  • PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID → pic.PIC_TYPE, pic.PIC_STYPE, pic.PIC_APID: pic tells the packetiser where to read PI1/PI2 before searching pid.
  • PID_INTER → pcf (parameter expiry): Parameters in periodic packets expire after PID_INTER plus a global margin.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 38-42) already has the 16 fields in this order (its table misnumbers PID_EVID as 15). It allowed several keys to map to the same SPID, and PID_SPID also selected the history file. ICD 6.0 widened the PID_SPID range from 2^31-1 to 2^32-1 (DCR-2421, ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246). ICD 6.1 updated the PID_PI1_VAL/PID_PI2_VAL descriptions (CRY-OG-655 / DCR 3398, p. 251). ICD 6.4 stated that packets without a data field header can be recognised by APID alone (p. 255). ICD 6.5 (R5.0) deprecated mapping different packets to the same SPID and clarified the use of pid fields (DCR-3398, p. 256-257). The layout is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 77-85), 6.9 (p. 80-89) and 7.0 (p. 82-91). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: the same 16 fields and defaults, with the 6 key fields PID_TYPE to PID_SPID.

Notes from the extraction

No structural discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. ICD 7.0 marks PID_SPID with '*' (key) although the text says the packetiser key is the first five fields, so the import key is effectively type/subtype/APID/PI1/PI2 plus SPID. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 11,150 packets, SPID range 101 to 1,000,006, all SPIDs unique. PID_UNIT, PID_INTER and PID_EVID are never filled, so Solar Orbiter relies on no periodic-packet expiry and on default event IDs. PID_TIME is 'Y' for 11,141 packets. PID_CHECK is 1 for only 6 packets. PID_VALID is 'Y' or empty (default 'Y'). PID_EVENT: A 6,360, I 1,374, W 1,159, N 1,095, empty 1,162. 2,063 packets have a TPSD (each TPSD used by exactly one packet, all present in vpd) and DFHSIZE 16; packets with TPSD -1 have DFHSIZE 16, 6 or 0. A 16-byte DFHSIZE matches the 6-byte packet primary header plus a 10-byte PUS data field header (inference from the values; the header layout is not in this table). No packet is described in both plf and vpd, and 31 fixed packets have no plf entry. Eleven packets have type and subtype 0, including three ground frame-quality pseudo-packets 'Bad/Idle/Good complete transfer frame' (APID 1, SPIDs 1000002/3/6), all with the same key 0/0/1/0/0 and PID_VALID 'Y'. Per the ICD only the last imported of these would stay valid. APIDs 2048-2065 are used for internally generated 'LMS_NNO/CEB/MLG' packets (ground station telemetry, consistent with the reserved NNO/CEB/MLG names in pcf).

docs.title: plf.dat: Parameters location in fixed packets
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.5.1400,792 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

plf describes the layout of fixed-format telemetry packets: for each SCOS-2000 packet (SPID) it lists which monitoring parameters are extracted and where. Each record places one parameter in one packet by byte offset and bit offset of its first occurrence; the length follows from the parameter's PTC/PFC. Super-commutated parameters, which appear several times in a packet, are described in the same single record by the number of occurrences, the bit distance between them and the time spacing used to time-stamp each sample. A parameter may appear in many packets. Overlapping entries (two parameters from the same bits) and gaps are allowed, but a parameter may have only one record per packet. Offsets count from the end of the SCOS-2000 TM header; with the SCOS-2000 packetiser this is the first byte of the source packet header, because the whole source packet is stored in the packet body. The standard monitoring displays (ANDs, GRDs, SCDs) and the telemetry model use plf to extract parameter values. Internally generated packets (constants packet, MISC packet, synthetic packets) also need plf entries.1

Key: PLF_NAME, PLF_SPID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PLF_NAMEChar(8)MName of the monitoring parameter to be extracted; must match PCF_NAME.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. NCD05011, NIU00043, NIU00044, NIU00045, NIU00046 ICD PDF p. 97 2PLF_SPIDNumber(10)MSCOS-2000 Packet ID of the packet from which the parameter values are extracted; a positive integer matching PID_SPID.Refers to pid.PID_SPID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 80028, 33542, 33543, 50215, 33508 ICD PDF p. 97 3PLF_OFFBYNumber(5)MByte offset of the first occurrence of the parameter, counted from the end of the SCOS-2000 TM header. With the SCOS-2000 telemetry packetiser this coincides with the start of the TM source packet header. Integer starting from 0 (negative values not allowed).Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 16, 18, 22, 20, 26 ICD PDF p. 97 4PLF_OFFBINumber(1)MBit number, within the byte given by PLF_OFFBY, of the first bit of the first occurrence; bit 0 is the leftmost (most significant) bit of the byte. Integer from 0 to 7.Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 0, 4, 6, 2, 1 ICD PDF p. 98 5PLF_NBOCCNumber(4)ONumber of occurrences of the parameter in the packet, from 1 to 9999. Use 1 for parameters that are not super-commutated.Default 1. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 1, 1024, 8, 16, 100 ICD PDF p. 98 6PLF_LGOCCNumber(5)ODistance in bits between the starts of two consecutive occurrences of a super-commutated parameter, from 0 to 32767. Irrelevant when PLF_NBOCC = 1.Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 0, 16, 744, 672, 608 ICD PDF p. 98 7PLF_TIMENumber(9)OTime offset in milliseconds of the first occurrence relative to the packet time, used to adjust the time stamp of the extracted sample (for super-commutated and non-commutated parameters alike). Integer from -4080000 to 4080000. Together with PLF_TDOCC it is used by graphic displays to plot super-commutated samples and to show sample times on scrolling displays and printouts (Note 1, p. 98).Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 0, -875, -1875, -12375, -4875 ICD PDF p. 98 8PLF_TDOCCNumber(9)OTime delay in milliseconds between two consecutive occurrences of a super-commutated parameter, from 1 to 4080000. Irrelevant when PLF_NBOCC = 1. Since ICD 6.1 the default is 1 and 0 is not an allowed value.Default 1. Solar Orbiter: filled in 400,792 of 400,792 rows; e.g. 1, 0, 125 ICD PDF p. 98

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PLF_NAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: Many-to-many link between parameters and fixed packets (section 3.3.2, p. 39).
  • PLF_SPID → pid.PID_SPID: Fixed packet structure identified by SPID.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 44-45) has the same eight fields, with PLF_TDOCC default '0'. ICD 6.0 added the ability to display super-commutated parameters in ANDs (DCR-2422, ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246). ICD 6.1 corrected PLF_TDOCC: its default is 1, not 0, and 0 is not allowed (S2K-40-DCR-847, p. 251). Unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 91-93), 6.9 (p. 95-97) and 7.0 (p. 97-99). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: key PLF_NAME + PLF_SPID, defaults NBOCC '1', LGOCC '0', TIME '0', TDOCC '1'.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 400,792 records placing 107,792 parameters in 9,056 packets. NCD05011 ('OBCHP_PTM_EID', the event identifier at byte 16) appears in 2,322 packets. 725 records are super-commutated (PLF_NBOCC from 8 to 2,046, most often 1,024), e.g. NCA3Z001 in SPID 29540 with 16 occurrences every 744 bits, PLF_TIME -1875 ms and PLF_TDOCC 125 ms. 487 non-super-commutated records give PLF_TDOCC = 0, a value the ICD has disallowed since issue 6.1; it is irrelevant for single occurrences. PLF_TIME is non-zero in 91 records (all negative). 239 records have PLF_OFFBY < 16, mostly in internally generated packets (e.g. SPID 36997 'OBC_HPTM_packet', TM(0,0) APID 34, and SPIDs 66980-66982 'Good/Bad/Idle mini-transfer frame', TM(161,5/4/3) APID 1966) or header fields; saved synthetic parameters use offsets 0 and 13 in SPID 66838. One record (NYM0796V in SPID 66028 'LMS_MLG High Frequency') names a parameter missing from pcf; per ICD section 2.4 (p. 23) the importer would reject it for relational inconsistency. 15,067 raw (PCF_NATUR 'R') parameters have neither a plf nor a vpd entry (1,192 of them have a PCF_PID).

docs.title: ppc.dat: Printout proforma definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.80 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The ppc table lists the monitoring parameters printed in each telemetry printout proforma declared in ppf: one record per parameter in the printout, with its position and the number format used to print its value (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal or the normal engineering/raw form). The number of records per printout must equal PPF_NBPR. As for ppf, the ICD says these files need not be imported into the run-time database and can serve as initialisation files read directly by the printing application, and that printout proforma can currently be defined only with the SCOS-2000 editor. Importing them as specified would need extensions to the underlying data structures, so the table mainly documents the intended structure of a printout definition.1

Key: PPC_NUMBE, PPC_POS

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PPC_NUMBEChar(4)MName of the printout proforma; must match PPF_NUMBE of the corresponding printout. Part of the key.Refers to ppf.PPF_NUMBE. ICD PDF p. 124 2PPC_POSNumber(2)MPosition of the parameter in the printout. Part of the key. ICD PDF p. 125 3PPC_NAMEChar(8)MName of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) printed in the printout.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. ICD PDF p. 125 4PPC_FORMChar(1)OFormat used to print the parameter values. B, O and H apply only to raw values of unsigned integer parameters; N prints the engineering value for calibrated parameters, otherwise raw decimal.
  • B Binary; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
  • O Octal; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
  • D Decimal
  • H Hexadecimal; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
  • N Normal: the engineering value is shown for parameters associated with one or more calibration definitions, otherwise the raw value in decimal
Default N. ICD PDF p. 125

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
Unchanged in field names, types and keys from ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.8 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.58) through ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.117-118), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.121-122) and ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.8 (PDF p.124-125). The only wording change is that the 'N' format refers to 'one or more calibration definitions' instead of 'a calibration curve', following the ICD 6.0 introduction of multiple calibrations per parameter. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

ppc.dat is empty (0 bytes) in both Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB; the database has only a placeholder COL1. pyscos2000 has no ppc model. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.31) requires ppc to be absent.

docs.title: ppf.dat: Printout proforma
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.70 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The ppf table is meant to hold the list and format of telemetry printout proforma, the reports SCOS-2000 can print with selected monitoring parameter values: one record per proforma, giving its name, a header printed on the top line of each page, and the number of parameters. The parameters themselves are listed in ppc. The ICD says ppf and ppc need not be imported into the run-time database and can be used as initialisation files read directly by the relevant application. It also notes that printout proforma can currently be defined only with the relevant SCOS-2000 editor: importing printout definitions as specified here would need extensions and changes to the underlying data structures. The table therefore documents an intended interface more than a supported import path.1

Key: PPF_NUMBE

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PPF_NUMBEChar(4)MName of the printout proforma: alphanumeric string of up to 4 characters that uniquely identifies it. Referenced by ppc.PPC_NUMBE. ICD PDF p. 124 2PPF_HEADChar(32)OHeader printed on the top line of each printed page. ICD PDF p. 124 3PPF_NBPRNumber(2)ONumber of parameters to be printed, integer 1 to 32. Must equal the number of ppc records for this printout. Not marked mandatory in the ICD. ICD PDF p. 124

docs.text: • PPF_NUMBE → ppc.PPC_NUMBE: One printout has PPF_NBPR ppc records.

ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.116-117), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.120-121) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.123-124) name it PPF_NBPR. No change to this table is recorded in the ICD 7.0 change annexes. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Unlike the display tables, ppf/ppc are not listed in the Summary of Displays related data (ICD 7.0 Table 2, PDF p.28) or in the §3.2 summary (PDF p.32).

docs.title: prf.dat: Parameter range sets
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.7.1565 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The prf table defines range sets, i.e. named sets of allowed values or value ranges that SCOS-2000 uses to check the values of command parameters (through CPC_PRFREF) and of sequence formal parameters (through CSP_PRFREF), one record per set; the individual ranges and discrete values are in PRV. A set may be shared by many parameters. Only parameters whose raw value is numerical or a time can be range checked; strings cannot. The record states whether the limits are written as raw or engineering values, the representation type of the limits (ASCII, signed or unsigned integer, real, absolute or relative time) and, for unsigned integers, their radix; these must be compatible with the type or engineering format of every parameter using the set. When a command sequence is loaded on a manual stack only the formal parameter values are checked against their range sets, not every value of the contained commands and sequences, although SCOS-2000 can be configured to check all parameter values at sequence loading time. The unit and the number of ranges are informative, for off-line consistency checks.1

Key: PRF_NUMBR

docs.text:
