  • R Raw values (import default).
  • E Engineering values; allowed only if every parameter using the set is calibrated (CPC_CATEG/CSP_CATEG T or C).
Default R. Solar Orbiter: filled in 565 of 565 rows; e.g. R, E ICD PDF p. 211 4PRF_DSPFMTChar(1)ORepresentation type of the limit values in PRV, whose value formats are given in Appendix A. It must be compatible with the parameters using the set: with their PTC when PRF_INTER=R, and with their DISPFMT when PRF_INTER=E or for time parameters.
  • A ASCII.
  • I Signed integer.
  • U Unsigned integer (import default).
  • R Real.
  • T Absolute time.
  • D Delta/relative time.
Default U. Solar Orbiter: filled in 565 of 565 rows; e.g. U, R, A, I ICD PDF p. 212 5PRF_RADIXChar(1)ORadix of the limit values in PRV; only applicable for unsigned integers (PRF_DSPFMT=U). It may differ from the radix (CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX) of the parameters using the set.
  • D Decimal (import default)
  • H Hexadecimal
  • O Octal
Default D. Solar Orbiter: filled in 549 of 565 rows; e.g. D, H ICD PDF p. 212 6PRF_NRANGENumber(3)ONumber of PRV records defined for this set. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.Solar Orbiter: filled in 564 of 565 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 20, 5, 58 ICD PDF p. 212 7PRF_UNITChar(4)OEngineering unit mnemonic, for consistency checking against the unit (CPC_UNIT/CSP_UNIT) of the parameters using the set. Grey in ICD 7.0: not used by SCOS-2000 processing.Solar Orbiter: filled in 100 of 565 rows; e.g. s, ms, #/nT, B, V ICD PDF p. 213

docs.text:
• PRF_NUMBR → prv.PRV_NUMBR: Allowed values/ranges of the set (one-to-many); PRF_NRANGE should equal their number.
  • PRF_NUMBR → cpc.CPC_PRFREF: Command parameters checked against the set (many-to-one).

  • PRF_UNIT → cpc.CPC_UNIT / csp.CSP_UNIT: Consistency check only.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.7.1, PDF p.102-103) has the same seven fields and defaults (R, U, D) with PRF_NUMBR Number(4). The range set identifier became Char(10) in ICD 6.0 (Annex 1 of ICD 7.0, 'Range Set ID' item, PDF p.247); ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.197-199), ICD 6.9 (PDF p.202-204) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.210-213) are identical in structure. pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same seven columns and key, but gives PRF_DSPFMT the default R instead of the ICD's U.

Notes from the extraction

Default discrepancy: PRF_DSPFMT import default is 'U' in ICD 5.1, 6.9 and 7.0 but 'R' in pyscos2000 (7.2); a file leaving the field empty would be interpreted differently. Solar Orbiter always fills it, so the data are not affected. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 565 range sets (531 in 2020); PRF_INTER R 549 and E 16; PRF_DSPFMT U 457, R 88, I 4 and A 16 (the 16 ASCII sets are exactly the engineering ones, holding lists of allowed alias texts); PRF_RADIX D 529, H 20, empty for the 16 ASCII sets. PRF_NRANGE disagrees with the PRV count for VCTX0001 (declares 104, has 101) and is empty for VNISLP01. Five sets are not referenced by any CPC or CSP record, while CSP_PRFREF 'VSM00001' points to a set that does not exist.

docs.title: prv.dat: Parameter range values
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.7.21,072 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The prv table lists the allowed values and value ranges of each range set declared in PRF, one record per allowed range or discrete value. A record with both a minimum and a maximum defines an inclusive range: a parameter value passes the check if it lies within the limits or equals one of them. A record with only a minimum and an empty maximum defines one allowed discrete value. A set can mix any number of ranges and discrete values, one record per allowed value or range, so that the records of a set together list everything the parameter may take. The limits are written in the representation and type declared by the set (PRF_INTER, PRF_DSPFMT) and, for unsigned integers, in its radix (PRF_RADIX); their maximum length follows from the maximum command size. SCOS-2000 applies these checks when command parameters and sequence formal parameters are entered or loaded, for example on a manual stack; by default only formal parameter values are checked when a sequence is loaded.1

Key: PRV_NUMBR, PRV_MINVAL

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PRV_NUMBRChar(10)MName (PRF_NUMBR) of the range set to which this allowed value or range belongs.Refers to prf.PRF_NUMBR. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,072 of 1,072 rows; e.g. VCD2X05F, VCTX0001, VCDEID15, VCDEID25, VCD2X03F ICD PDF p. 213 2PRV_MINVALCharMLow limit of the range, or the single allowed value if PRV_MAXVAL is empty. Written in a format compatible with PRF_DSPFMT (and PRF_RADIX for unsigned integers). Part of the key. Maximum length depends on the maximum command size.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,072 of 1,072 rows; e.g. 0, 1, 4, 100, 2 ICD PDF p. 213 3PRV_MAXVALCharOHigh limit of the range. Empty means that PRV_MINVAL is a discrete allowed value. Written in a format compatible with PRF_DSPFMT (and PRF_RADIX for unsigned integers).Solar Orbiter: filled in 762 of 1,072 rows; e.g. 255, 100, 30, 10, 65535 ICD PDF p. 213

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • PRV_NUMBR → prf.PRF_NUMBR: Range set owning the value/range; representation and radix come from PRF.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.7.2, PDF p.103-104): PRV_NUMBR Number(4), PRV_MINVAL and PRV_MAXVAL Char(17), key PRV_NUMBR + PRV_MINVAL. ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.199) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.204): PRV_NUMBR Char(10). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.213): limit fields without fixed size, bounded by the maximum command size (S2K-8073, PDF p.261). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same three columns, the same key and PRV_MAXVAL optional.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in columns, keys or optionality (3 columns in prv.dat). Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 1072 records (631 in 2020) for 565 sets, all resolving to PRF. 762 records are ranges and 310 are discrete values; all 310 discrete values belong to the 16 ASCII (engineering text) range sets, so every numeric set is expressed as min/max ranges. Hexadecimal limits are written without prefix (e.g. 0 to 7FFF for set VIP06012). Longest limits: 16 characters (PRV_MINVAL), 10 (PRV_MAXVAL).

docs.title: psm.dat: Parameter sets mapping to commands/sequences
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5.50 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Parameter sets are named collections of command or sequence parameters for which predefined combinations of values, called parameter value sets, can be stored in the database and then applied in the real-time environment to give a value to every contained parameter with one high-level mnemonic (ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5, PDF p.200-201). The psm table is the mapping table that says which parameter sets are used by which commands or sequences: one record per (task, set) pair. It resolves the many-to-many relationship between commands or sequences and parameter sets described in the commanding data overview. One parameter set may be attached to several commands or to several sequences, but never to both a command and a sequence. The ICD explains that even when a command and a sequence have the same parameters with the same names, the PVS_BIT values (bit offset for a command, formal parameter position for a sequence) would necessarily differ when the value sets are built.1

Key: PSM_NAME, PSM_TYPE, PSM_PARSET

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PSM_NAMEChar(8)MName of the task, a command (CCF_CNAME) or a sequence (CSF_NAME), to which the parameter set in PSM_PARSET is attached. Part of the key.Refers to ccf.CCF_CNAME / csf.CSF_NAME. ICD PDF p. 205 2PSM_TYPEChar(1)MType of the task the parameter set is attached to. Part of the key.
  • C The task is a command
  • S The task is a sequence
ICD PDF p. 205 3PSM_PARSETChar(8)MName of the parameter set (PST_NAME) attached to this task. Part of the key.Refers to pst.PST_NAME. ICD PDF p. 205

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PSM_NAME → ccf.CCF_CNAME / csf.CSF_NAME: Selected by PSM_TYPE ('C' or 'S').
  • PSM_PARSET → pst.PST_NAME: A set may not be attached to both a command and a sequence.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
The parameter-set tables appear with the same section numbers (§3.3.3.5.x) in ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.97-99), ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.188-192), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.193-197) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.200-205). psm is unchanged from ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.99) to ICD 7.0 (PDF p.205): three key fields, all mandatory, with PSM_TYPE 'C'/'S'. Unlike cvp, PSM_TYPE allows sequences without a 'not supported' remark. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

The database stores only a placeholder COL1 (no rows), because the file is empty. The file is empty (0 bytes) in the 2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16 Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB. Consistently, CCF_DEFSET is empty in all 5454 ccf rows of the 2025 release and SDF_VALSET is empty in all sdf rows, so Solar Orbiter does not use parameter sets in its MIB. The HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note says the HCSS (Herschel) ingestion ignores PST, PSV, CPS and PVS (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note, §5.2.11, PDF p.14), and the HPSDB note marks all five parameter-set tables 'not supported by CCS, do not use' (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, §5.3.16-5.3.20, PDF p.39-40). pyscos2000 has no psm model. The HCSS note lists PST, PSV, CPS and PVS as ignored but does not mention PSM (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note PDF p.14).

docs.title: pst.dat: Parameter sets
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5.10 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Parameter sets are named collections of command or sequence parameters for which predefined combinations of values, called parameter value sets, can be stored in the database and then applied in the real-time environment to give a value to every contained parameter with one high-level mnemonic (ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5, PDF p.200-201). The pst table declares the parameter sets themselves: one record per set, with a unique name and a description. A parameter set is a named collection of command or sequence parameters. Its named value combinations are declared in psv and filled in pvs, the optional list of member parameters is in cps (used only off-line), and psm says which commands or sequences use the set. A set can be shared by several commands or by several sequences, but not by both a command and a sequence. In the real-time environment a value set is applied by name to give values to all member parameters at once. Commands (CCF_DEFSET) and sequences (CSF_DEFSET) can name a default value set, and sequence elements can take a parameter value from a value set (SDF_VTYPE = 'P', SDF_VALSET).1

Key: PST_NAME

docs.title: psv.dat: Parameter value sets
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5.20 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Parameter sets are named collections of command or sequence parameters for which predefined combinations of values, called parameter value sets, can be stored in the database and then applied in the real-time environment to give a value to every contained parameter with one high-level mnemonic (ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5, PDF p.200-201). The psv table declares the parameter value sets: one record per value set, giving its unique name, the parameter set (pst) it belongs to, and a description. The actual values for each member parameter are in pvs, keyed on the value-set name. Value-set names are the handles used elsewhere in the database. A command can name a default value set (CCF_DEFSET), as can a sequence (CSF_DEFSET), and a sequence element parameter can take its value from a value set (SDF_VTYPE = 'P' with SDF_VALSET). Because the key is the value-set name alone, value-set names must be unique across all parameter sets, not only within one set.1

docs.title: ptv.dat: Commands pre-transmission validation
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.2.45 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The ptv table defines the static pre-transmission validation (PTV) of commands: telemetry-based conditions that must hold before SCOS-2000 releases a command. There is one record per check, each check requiring that a given monitoring parameter equals a given value; all checks defined for the same command are implicitly ANDed, and because the key is the command plus the parameter, a parameter can be used only once per command. A PTV expression belongs to exactly one command: if the same condition is needed for another command it must be defined again (one-to-many relationship from CCF to PTV). The validity of the monitoring parameter is taken into account implicitly, so a check passes only if the parameter is valid and has the required value. Only parameters with a numerical raw representation (no strings or times) that are processed by the telemetry model (parameters located in PLF, or synthetic parameters) may be used. Static PTV can be overridden for an individual command inside a sequence with CSS_STAPTV, and is distinct from the dynamic PTV checks (feasibility, time checks, interlocks) that CSS_DYNPTV controls.1

Key: PTV_CNAME, PTV_PARNAM

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PTV_CNAMEChar(8)MName of the command (CCF_CNAME) to which this validation check applies.Refers to ccf.CCF_CNAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 5 of 5 rows; e.g. ZCD00D09, ZSM00120, ZSM00125, ZSM00130, ZSM00135 ICD PDF p. 160 2PTV_PARNAMChar(8)MName of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) tested by the check. It must have a numerical raw representation (not a string or time) and must be processed by the telemetry model library, i.e. be a TM parameter appearing in PLF or a synthetic parameter of any type.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 5 of 5 rows; e.g. NMAXS005, NCDXS005 ICD PDF p. 160 3PTV_INTERChar(1)ORepresentation in which the expected value PTV_VAL is written.
  • R Raw value (import default); for synthetic parameters the raw value is the output of the OL or hard-coded definition.
  • E Engineering (calibrated) value; only for parameters with a single calibration (PCF_CURTX filled), not for parameters with conditional calibrations defined in CUR.
Default R. Solar Orbiter: filled in 5 of 5 rows; e.g. R ICD PDF p. 160 4PTV_VALChar(17)MValue that the validation parameter must equal for the check to pass. It is written raw unless PTV_INTER=E: raw values in decimal, compatible with the parameter type (PCF_PTC); engineering values in the parameter's engineering representation (ASCII for textually calibrated parameters, PCF_CATEG=S, or the CAF_ENGFMT of the numeric calibration).Solar Orbiter: filled in 5 of 5 rows; e.g. 0 ICD PDF p. 161

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PTV_CNAME → ccf.CCF_CNAME: Command being validated; multiple checks per command are ANDed.
  • PTV_PARNAM → pcf.PCF_NAME: Monitoring parameter tested; must be in plf or synthetic, numeric raw type.
  • PTV_INTER → pcf.PCF_CURTX / cur: Engineering values require a single calibration (PCF_CURTX); not allowed with CUR conditional calibrations.

docs.title: pvs.dat: Parameter value sets definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5.40 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

Parameter sets are named collections of command or sequence parameters for which predefined combinations of values, called parameter value sets, can be stored in the database and then applied in the real-time environment to give a value to every contained parameter with one high-level mnemonic (ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.5, PDF p.200-201). The pvs table holds the contents of the parameter value sets: one record per value in a value set, giving the value-set name (psv), its parameter set (pst), the command or sequence parameter concerned, the parameter's bit offset or position, the representation (raw or engineering) and the value itself. When an operator applies a value set, each listed parameter takes the given value. A record whose value is left empty leaves that parameter's current value unchanged. Because one name can denote a command parameter and a sequence parameter, the ICD requires parameters that share a name and are used in parameter sets to have the same raw and engineering formats (same PTC and display format).1

Key: PVS_ID, PVS_BIT

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1PVS_IDChar(8)MName of the parameter value set (PSV_PVSID) this record belongs to. Part of the key.Refers to psv.PSV_PVSID. ICD PDF p. 202 2PVS_PSIDChar(8)MName of the parameter set (PST_NAME) the value set belongs to.Refers to pst.PST_NAME. ICD PDF p. 202 3PVS_PNAMEChar(8)MName of the command parameter (CDF_PNAME) or sequence parameter (CSP_FPNAME) whose value is given in PVS_VALS. If two sequence parameters, or a command parameter and a sequence parameter, have the same name and are used in parameter sets, they must have the same raw and engineering formats: the same CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC and the same CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT.Refers to cdf.CDF_PNAME / csp.CSP_FPNAME. ICD PDF p. 203 4PVS_INTERChar(1)ORepresentation of the value in PVS_VALS.
  • R Raw representation
  • E Engineering representation; only for parameters associated with a calibration definition (CPC_CATEG/CSP_CATEG = 'T' or 'C')
Default R. ICD PDF p. 203 5PVS_VALSCharOValue for the parameter named in PVS_PNAME, in raw form unless PVS_INTER = 'E'. Raw values follow the parameter type (CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC) and, for unsigned integers, the radix (CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX). Engineering values follow the engineering representation (CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT). No fixed size: the maximum length depends on the maximum allowed command size (§3.3.3.2). May be left Null, in which case applying the value set does not change this parameter's current value. ICD PDF p. 204 6PVS_BITNumber(4)MUnique identification of the parameter within the set: bit offset in the command (CDF_BIT) for command parameters, position (CSP_FPNUM) for sequence parameters. Part of the key.Refers to cdf.CDF_BIT / csp.CSP_FPNUM. ICD PDF p. 204

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• PVS_ID → psv.PSV_PVSID: Owning value set.
  • PVS_PSID → pst.PST_NAME: Owning parameter set.
  • PVS_PNAME → cdf.CDF_PNAME / csp.CSP_FPNAME: Formats constrained by cpc/csp (PTC, RADIX, DISPFMT, CATEG).
  • PVS_BIT → cdf.CDF_BIT / csp.CSP_FPNUM: Occurrence identifier.
  • PVS_ID → sdf.SDF_VALSET: ICD 7.0 describes a 1-to-1 relationship between an sdf entry and a parameter value set (§3.3.3, PDF p.127).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
The parameter-set tables appear with the same section numbers (§3.3.3.5.x) in ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.97-99), ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.188-192), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.193-197) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.200-205). ICD 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci PDF p.98-99) has the same 6 fields, with PVS_VALS Char(17) and PVS_INTER 'E' worded as 'associated to a calibration curve'. ICD 6.2/6.3 updated the PVS_INTER description (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, PDF p.253). ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.191) and ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.196) still print PVS_VALS as Char(17). ICD 7.0 (S2K-8073, for SCOS 5.5.3 and 6.0.0 or later) replaced the fixed size with the maximum command parameter size, for PVS_VALS and other value fields (Annex 2, PDF p.261), giving 'Char' with no length (PDF p.204). Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

The database stores only a placeholder COL1 (no rows), because the file is empty. The file is empty (0 bytes) in the 2025-09-16 and 2020-04-16 Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB. Consistently, CCF_DEFSET is empty in all 5454 ccf rows of the 2025 release and SDF_VALSET is empty in all sdf rows, so Solar Orbiter does not use parameter sets in its MIB. The HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note says the HCSS (Herschel) ingestion ignores PST, PSV, CPS and PVS (hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note, §5.2.11, PDF p.14), and the HPSDB note marks all five parameter-set tables 'not supported by CCS, do not use' (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, §5.3.16-5.3.20, PDF p.39-40). pyscos2000 has no pvs model. Observation by this wiki: PVS_PSID repeats information that can be derived from PVS_ID through psv.PSV_NAME, and the ICD does not say what happens if the two disagree.

A small lookup table (7 rows) of file categories used by Solar Orbiter's file-based uplink, which relies on PUS service 13 'large data transfer' commands such as TC(13,9) 'Accept First Uplink Part' whose application data include a Partition Id and a File Attribute. docs.title: sdf.dat: Command sequence element parameters
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.3.350,014 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The sdf table assigns values to the editable parameters of sequence elements, one record per editable parameter of each command or nested sequence used in a sequence. For each such parameter it identifies the source of the value used when the sequence is loaded: an explicit raw or engineering value written in the record, the value of a formal parameter of the enclosing sequence (so the sequence acts as a template), an entry of a parameter value set, the default of the nested sequence's formal parameter (CSP_DEFVAL), or the default of the command definition (CDF_VALUE, itself possibly inherited from CPC_DEFVAL or extracted from telemetry). It also states whether the value may still be edited after loading. Parameters of commands are located by their bit offset in the command, parameters of nested sequences by the formal parameter number. Only parameters that are editable in the command definition (CDF_ELTYPE=E) may appear; the allowed combinations of CDF_ELTYPE and SDF_FTYPE (E/F valid but not editable in the sequence, E/E valid and editable, F with no SDF entry valid) are checked at import. Since R4.2, commands with group repeaters can be used if all repeater values and repeated parameters are defined, with one SDF entry per repeated instance and SDF_REPPOS mapping shifted offsets back to CDF_BIT. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 these tables are converted on request into XML sequence definitions held in the FARC rather than the run-time MIB, imported as a delta without re-importing the TM/TC database.1

Key: SDF_SQNAME, SDF_ENTRY, SDF_POS, SDF_PNAME

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:

Solar Orbiter: filled in 50,014 of 50,014 rows; e.g. ZIPE70B0, ZIW00112, ZCSD3603, ZIW00060, ZIW00098 ICD PDF p. 180 4SDF_POSNumber(4)MPosition of the parameter: for a command element, the bit offset of the parameter in the command (CDF_BIT); for a nested sequence, the formal parameter number in that sequence (CSP_FPNUM). For commands with group repeaters it is the bit offset after expansion of the groups; if this differs from CDF_BIT, the original CDF_BIT must be given in SDF_REPPOS. Part of the key.Refers to cdf.CDF_BIT / csp.CSP_FPNUM. It is part of the key (the ICD stresses this for commands whose CDF_GRPSIZE is non-zero).Refers to cdf.CDF_PNAME / csp.CSP_FPNAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 50,014 of 50,014 rows; e.g. PCD0C012, PCD8E012, PCD03011, PIW01299, PCD0E012 ICD PDF p. 180 6SDF_FTYPEChar(1)OWhether the parameter value may still be modified after the sequence has been loaded on the stack. If the parameter is mapped to a formal parameter, its value can only be set (through the formal parameter) before loading.
  • F Fixed: the user cannot change the value once the sequence is loaded.
  • E Editable (import default).

  • R Value taken from SDF_VALUE, interpreted as raw.
  • E Value taken from SDF_VALUE, interpreted as engineering; only for calibrated parameters (CPC_CATEG/CSP_CATEG T or C).
  • F Value inherited from the formal parameter of the current sequence named in SDF_VALUE (CSP_FPNAME); not allowed for group repeater parameters (CDF_GRPSIZE>0).
  • P Value taken from the corresponding entry of the parameter value set named in SDF_VALSET.

  • D For a command parameter: value taken from the default of the command definition (CDF_VALUE, or CPC_DEFVAL when CDF_INTER=D, which must then be filled); with CDF_INTER=T the default is again extracted from telemetry after loading.

With VTYPE R or E it is written in the appropriate representation (raw compatible with CPC_PTC/CSP_PTC and CPC_RADIX/CSP_RADIX; engineering compatible with CPC_DISPFMT/CSP_DISPFMT). With VTYPE R, a 'Command ID' parameter takes the name of a fully defaulted command (CCF_CNAME) and a 'Parameter ID' parameter the name of a monitoring parameter with PCF_PID. With VTYPE F it holds the formal parameter name (CSP_FPNAME) to inherit from. docs.text:
• SDF_SQNAME + SDF_ENTRY → css.CSS_SQNAME + css.CSS_ENTRY: Element owning the parameter (must be of type C or S); SDF_ELEMID repeats CSS_ELEMID.
  • SDF_PNAME + SDF_POS → cdf.CDF_PNAME + cdf.CDF_BIT: For command elements; only editable (CDF_ELTYPE=E) parameters; SDF_REPPOS carries the original CDF_BIT when shifted.
  • SDF_PNAME + SDF_POS → csp.CSP_FPNAME + csp.CSP_FPNUM: For nested-sequence elements (formal parameters of the nested sequence).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.3.3, PDF p.87-89) has 9 fields: the key is SDF_SQNAME + SDF_ENTRY + SDF_POS (SDF_PNAME not key) and SDF_VALUE is Char(17). ICD 6.5 added the optional field SDF_REPPOS and changed the SDF_POS description to support commands with group repeaters in sequences (R4.2, SPR-2904; Annex 1 of ICD 7.0, PDF p.255); ICD 6.4 clarified that only editable parameters may appear (PDF p.255) and ICD 6.6 fixed the allowed ELTYPE/FTYPE combinations (S2K-SPR-3400, PDF p.257). ICD 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.168-173) and ICD 6.9 (PDF p.172-176) have 10 fields with SDF_PNAME in the key. ICD 7.0 (PDF p.179-184) makes SDF_VALUE variable-length, bounded by the command size (S2K-8073, PDF p.261). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) has the same ten columns, keys (SDF_SQNAME, SDF_ENTRY, SDF_POS, SDF_PNAME), mandatory fields and default E for SDF_FTYPE.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in columns, order, keys or optionality between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 and the Solar Orbiter sdf.dat (10 columns in all 50014 records of 2025; 30985 in 2020). SDF_REPPOS is filled in every record: for command elements it equals the CDF_BIT of the parameter (differing from SDF_POS in 11896 records, i.e. parameters of expanded repeated groups), for nested-sequence elements it is 0. Value sources: R 25683, F 11575 (formal parameters, all resolving to CSP records of the same sequence), E 10378, D 2328 (always with empty SDF_VALUE, command elements only) and S 50 (nested sequences only); P is never used and SDF_VALSET is always empty. SDF_FTYPE is E in 46251 and F in 3763 records. SDF_VALUE reaches 424 characters (hexadecimal octet-string data), far beyond the 17 characters of earlier ICD issues, which is allowed by the variable size of ICD 7.0.

docs.title: spc.dat: Scrolling displays definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.65 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The spc table lists the monitoring parameters shown in each Scrolling Display (SCD) declared in spf: one record per displayed parameter, with its order in the display. For each parameter it sets how new samples are presented (on a new scrolled line, or by overwriting the old value), whether the Telemetry Desktop setting for invalid values applies, the number format (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal or normal engineering/raw), and the background and foreground colours of the field. The file is expected to be sorted by display name and position, and the number of records per display must equal SPF_NPAR. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model (plf-located or synthetic) are allowed. From SCOS-2000 R5.0 these definitions are converted into XML display files in the FARC.1

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.6 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.56-57) has the same 8 fields with the same values; the key field SPC_POS is not marked mandatory there, and the 'Normal' format refers to a single 'calibration curve' rather than 'one or more calibration definitions'. ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.114-116), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.118-120) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.121-123) mark SPC_POS mandatory. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Notes from the extraction

Column mapping: COL1..COL8 = SPC_NUMBE, SPC_POS, SPC_NAME, SPC_UPDT, SPC_MODE, SPC_FORM, SPC_BACK, SPC_FORE; all 5 lines of the 2025 spc.dat have 8 fields. Solar Orbiter's only SCD, DICSP000, shows 5 SPICE parameters (NIC0P015, NIC0P005, NIC0P020, NIC0P010, NICDF014) at positions 1-5, all present in pcf. SPC_UPDT is empty (scrolling), SPC_MODE 'N' (invalid values always shown), SPC_FORM 'H' for four and 'N' for one, black background '0' and blue foreground '2'. The rows are identical in the 2020-04-16 release; the SWA IDB spc.dat is empty. pyscos2000 has no spc model. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.30) maps all 8 fields with the ICD defaults and plans to restrict SPC_POS to 1-9 with at most 5 records.

docs.title: spf.dat: Scrolling displays
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.51 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The spf table lists the Scrolling Displays (SCDs), one record per display. A scrolling display shows from one to five monitoring parameters; each new sample is either written by scrolling onto a new line or overwrites the previous value, as set per parameter in spc. spf gives only the display identity, its header line, the number of parameters (which must equal the number of spc records for the display) and an update rate that exists only for external applications. The displayed parameters, their order, update mode, format and colours are in spc. Only parameters processed by the telemetry model can be shown, and from SCOS-2000 R5.0 the definitions are converted into XML files in the FARC instead of being imported into the run-time database.1

Key: SPF_NUMBE

ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.5 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.55-56) defines the same four fields, except that SPF_UPUN is given in milliseconds with no range. The unit was questioned in ICD 6.7 (S2K-DCR-5502 item 6, ICD 7.0 Annex 1 PDF p.259), and ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.113-114), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.117-118) and ICD 7.0 (PDF p.120-121) give seconds, range 1-99. Since SCOS-2000 R5.0 (ICD issue 6.4) display definitions are no longer kept in the run-time (POST) MIB database: the ASCII tables are converted on request into XML files stored in the FARC, in a delta fashion that keeps previously imported displays and displays created at run time with the TM Desktop editor (ICD 7.0 §2.5, PDF p.24; §3.3.2.7, PDF p.110; Annex 1, PDF p.254). The XML format is in [AD-5], SCOS-2000 TM Displays and Printout definitions Service ICD (ICD-5001), which is not in the library. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).

Column mapping: COL1..COL4 = SPF_NUMBE, SPF_HEAD, SPF_NPAR, SPF_UPUN; the single line of the 2025 spf.dat has exactly 4 fields. The same record is in the 2020-04-16 release; the SWA IDB spf.dat is empty. pyscos2000 has no spf model. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.30) computes SPF_NPAR itself and ignores SPF_UPUN.

docs.title: tcp.dat: Packet headers characteristics
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.3.1.14 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The tcp table lists the telecommand packet header types known to the database, one record per header type. SCOS-2000 uses a packet header definition to build the first portion of every encoded TC packet: the header is prefixed to the command application data, whose layout is defined separately through the CPC and CDF tables. Each command (CCF record) must name exactly one header through CCF_PKTID, while the same header can be shared by any number of commands. The header itself carries no layout information in this table: its elements (fixed areas and named header parameters such as APID, service type, subtype, acknowledgement flags, packet length and source sequence count) are described in PCDF, and the named header parameters in PCPC, so that TCP and PCPC are linked many-to-many through PCDF. Header parameter values cannot be edited by operators on a manual stack; the command source or command handler sets them (APID, type and subtype from the CCF record, packet length computed from the actual encoded length including repeated groups, sequence counter maintained by the multiplexer per APID). For special command types (CCF_CTYPE R, F, T or N) the PCDF/CDF entries describe a frame data field or throw-event content instead of a packet. The size of the header (sum of its PCDF_LEN values) reduces the room left for command parameters within the maximum command size.1

Key: TCP_ID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1TCP_IDChar(8)MUnique identifier of the TC packet header definition. It is the value that commands quote in CCF_PKTID to select the header to be prepended when the command is encoded, and the value that PCDF records quote in PCDF_TCNAME to attach header elements to this header. Being the table key, a given name may appear only once; names are compared without regard to letter case and should not contain spaces (general rule of ICD section 3.3).Solar Orbiter: filled in 4 of 4 rows; e.g. HPC1_TC, NOM_TC, NOS2KHDR, NO_HDR ICD PDF p. 128 2TCP_DESCChar(24)OFree-text description of the packet header (up to 24 characters). It is informative only and has no effect on encoding.Solar Orbiter: filled in 4 of 4 rows; e.g. HPC_TC_Packet_Header, NIS Throw Events, NOM_DH_TC_Packet_Header, TCP Header for CF/CS ICD PDF p. 128

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• TCP_ID → ccf.CCF_PKTID: One header is referenced by many commands; each command references exactly one header (ICD 7.0 section 3.3.3, PDF p.127-128).
  • TCP_ID → pcdf.PCDF_TCNAME: PCDF holds one record per element of the header (fixed areas and header parameters) with its bit offset and length.
  • TCP_ID → pcpc.PCPC_PNAME (via pcdf.PCDF_PNAME): Many-to-many relationship between headers and header parameters, resolved by PCDF.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
The table is identical in all examined issues: two fields TCP_ID Char(8) mandatory key and TCP_DESC Char(24) optional, in ICD 5.1 (2001, section 3.3.3.1.1, PDF p.60), ICD 6.7 Draft A (2009, PDF p.121), ICD 6.9 (2010, PDF p.125) and ICD 7.0 (2017, PDF p.128). The pyscos2000 schema based on ICD 7.2 also has the same two columns (TCP_ID key and mandatory, TCP_DESC optional).

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy in field names, order or optionality between ICD 7.0, pyscos2000 (7.2) and the Solar Orbiter file (2 tab-separated columns in every line of tcp.dat). The 2025-09-16 Solar Orbiter MIB defines 4 headers (the 2020-04-16 release also has 4): NOM_TC (description 'NOM_DH_TC_Packet_Header', used by 5318 commands; 13 PCDF elements, i.e. 6-octet primary header plus a 4-octet data field header), HPC1_TC ('HPC_TC_Packet_Header', 125 commands; 7 PCDF elements, primary header only with data field header flag 0), NOS2KHDR ('NIS Throw Events', used by the 6 commands with CCF_CTYPE='N') and NO_HDR ('TCP Header for CF/CS', used by the 5 control frames and control segments with CCF_CTYPE 'F' or 'R'). NOS2KHDR and NO_HDR have no PCDF records, so for those commands all content comes from CDF (inference from the data: these special directives and throw events need no packet header, which is consistent with the ICD statement that their PCDF/CDF entries describe the frame data field or the throw-event fields rather than a packet).

docs.title: tpcf.dat: Telemetry packets characteristics
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.4.311,150 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

tpcf stores attributes that belong to a SCOS-2000 TM packet as a whole, i.e. to everything filed under one SCOS-2000 Packet ID (SPID), with at most one record per SPID. The main attribute is the packet mnemonic, a short readable name that monitoring displays show as the source packet of parameter values. Without a mnemonic the displays show 'None'. The table also has an optional packet size. SCOS-2000 neither imports nor uses it, but missions may use it to generate archive (history file) configuration that needs the complete packet list. The ICD recommends a size of 0 for truly variable packets and the exact SCOS-2000 packet size for fixed packets: the SCOS-2000 TM packet header (64 bytes for header versions 0 to 3, 76 bytes for version 4) plus the full source packet length. A size larger than the real packet wastes disk space; a smaller one (but above 64 bytes) slows filing. A tpcf entry is also needed for internally generated packets so that displays show their mnemonic.1

Key: TPCF_SPID

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1TPCF_SPIDNumber(10)MSCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Number (SCOS-2000 Packet ID); unsigned integer that must match PID_SPID of the packet.Refers to pid.PID_SPID. Solar Orbiter: filled in 11,150 of 11,150 rows; e.g. 10000, 1000002, 1000003, 1000006, 10001 ICD PDF p. 93 2TPCF_NAMEChar(12)OAlphanumeric mnemonic of the telemetry packet, shown in the monitoring displays to identify the source packet of parameter values. If none is given, displays show the string 'None'.Solar Orbiter: filled in 11,150 of 11,150 rows; e.g. BAD_PKT, CTFBAD, CTFGOOD, CTFIDLE, DYNUDCS ICD PDF p. 94 3TPCF_SIZENumber(8)OTotal length of the SCOS-2000 telemetry packet in bytes. Not imported into the run-time database and not used by any SCOS-2000 process (grey row); provided for mission-specific tools that generate history-file configuration. Recommended values: 0 for truly variable packets; for fixed packets the exact SCOS-2000 packet size, i.e. the SCOS-2000 TM header (64 bytes for header versions 0-3, 76 bytes for version 4) plus the whole source packet. Too large a value wastes disk space; too small a value (but above the 64-byte header) is filed correctly but more slowly, so the size matters most for frequent packets such as periodic housekeeping and verification reports. The description continues on PDF p. 96.Solar Orbiter: filled in 11,150 of 11,150 rows; e.g. 0, 42, 18, 26, 22 ICD PDF p. 95

docs.text: • TPCF_SPID → pid.PID_SPID: At most one tpcf record per SPID.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 43-44) has the same three fields. ICD 6.1 changed the TPCF_SIZE description to say that the SCOS-2000 header length depends on the header version (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 251), and ICD 6.5 split the long description over two pages (p. 256). Unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 87-89), 6.9 (p. 91-93) and 7.0 (p. 93-96). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: TPCF_SPID mandatory key, TPCF_NAME and TPCF_SIZE optional.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 11,150 records, one per pid SPID (every TPCF_SPID exists in pid and vice versa by count). All mnemonics are filled and unique, up to the full 12 characters (e.g. BAD_PKT, CTFGOOD, DYNUDCS). TPCF_SIZE is 0 for all 2,063 variable (TPSD) packets and for 262 fixed packets; the other 8,825 have sizes from 6 to 4,136 bytes. Most of these are smaller than the 64-byte SCOS-2000 header (7,487 of them are 64 bytes or less) and match the source packet length (e.g. SPID 10002 'YCSV84C0' has size 32 with its last plf parameter at byte 31). Inference: Solar Orbiter fills TPCF_SIZE with the source packet length, not with the header-inclusive SCOS-2000 size the ICD recommends; this is harmless because SCOS-2000 does not use the field.

docs.title: txf.dat: Textual calibrations
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.41,003 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

txf declares the textual calibrations, also called alias sets, which turn the raw value of a status parameter into a text string such as 'ON' or 'OFF'. It has one record per textual calibration. The individual raw-range to text mappings are stored in txp. Parameters use a textual calibration by naming it in PCF_CURTX (single calibration) or CUR_SELECT (conditional calibration), and must then have PCF_CATEG = 'S'. The txf record gives a description, the numeric format of the raw values listed in txp (which must be compatible with the type of the parameters using the calibration) and the number of txp entries. Status parameters are typically checked with status checks in ocp, whose expected values are then written as the calibrated strings when OCF_INTER = 'C' and OCF_CODIN = 'A'. A raw value with no matching text gives an invalid engineering value shown as '****' (PCF_INTER description, p. 50).1

Key: TXF_NUMBR

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1TXF_NUMBRChar(10)MAlphanumeric identifier that uniquely names the textual calibration; it is the value used in PCF_CURTX, CUR_SELECT and TXP_NUMBR.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,003 of 1,003 rows; e.g. AYMODELE, CAAT0001TM, CAAT0003TM, CAAT0005TM, CAAT0007TM ICD PDF p. 69 2TXF_DESCRChar(32)OFree textual description of the textual calibration.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,003 of 1,003 rows; e.g. Memory ID, Failure ID, Mode ID, Odd parity in TMs, APME Mode ICD PDF p. 69 3TXF_RAWFMTChar(1)MFormat of the raw values (TXP_FROM, TXP_TO) given in the txp records of this calibration. It must be compatible with the type of the parameters that use the calibration.
  • I Signed integer
  • U Unsigned integer
  • R Real
Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,003 of 1,003 rows; e.g. U, I ICD PDF p. 69 4TXF_NALIASNumber(3)ONumber of records defined in txp for this textual calibration. Grey row in the ICD: informative, not used by SCOS-2000 processing.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1,003 of 1,003 rows; e.g. 2, 4, 3, 5, 6 ICD PDF p. 69

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• TXF_NUMBR → txp.TXP_NUMBR: Each alias set contains one or more text points (section 3.3.2, p. 39; the overview text calls the point table 'PAS', which is the commanding-side equivalent, while the monitoring points are in txp).
  • TXF_NUMBR → pcf.PCF_CURTX, cur.CUR_SELECT: Used only by status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S'); shareable among parameters.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 33-34) has the same four fields but TXF_NUMBR is Number(4) ('identification number'). It became Char(10) in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247; field-type change also listed for 6.2/6.3, p. 253). Unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 64-65), 6.9 (p. 67-68) and 7.0 (p. 69). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. The ICD's monitoring overview (p. 39) says each textual calibration contains points in 'PAS', but the monitoring alias points are defined in txp (pas is the command-side table); this looks like an editorial slip in the ICD. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 1,003 textual calibrations, raw format U (994) or I (9). TXF_NALIAS is declared Number(3) (at most 999) but four Solar Orbiter calibrations exceed that: PARAMIDTM 'Parameter ID' (19,803 entries, mapping on-board parameter IDs to ground parameter names, used by parameter-ID fields such as NCD0C095), CCDT0004TX 'Event ID list' (1,419), CDMTX000TM (1,192) and CCDT0384TM (1,173). TXF_NALIAS disagrees with the actual txp count for 2 calibrations (CYCT0002TM declares 2 but has 3 points; CYNT0002TM declares 2 but has 1); since the field is not used by SCOS-2000 this is harmless.

docs.title: txp.dat: Textual calibrations definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.2.535,032 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

txp holds the text strings of the textual calibrations declared in txf: one record per raw-value range and string pair. Any raw value of a status parameter that falls within TXP_FROM to TXP_TO, inclusive, is displayed and processed as the string TXP_ALTXT. A single raw value is expressed by giving the same value as lower and upper bound. Raw bounds are written in decimal in the format declared by TXF_RAWFMT. The key is the pair (TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM), so two ranges of one calibration cannot start at the same raw value. The resulting strings are the engineering values used in monitoring displays and, with OCF_INTER = 'C' and OCF_CODIN = 'A', as the expected values of status checks in ocp. A raw value that matches no range is shown as an invalid value '****'.1

Key: TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1TXP_NUMBRChar(10)MIdentifier of the textual calibration this entry belongs to; must match TXF_NUMBR of an existing txf record.Refers to txf.TXF_NUMBR. Solar Orbiter: filled in 35,032 of 35,032 rows; e.g. PARAMIDTM, CCDT0004TX, CDMTX000TM, CCDT0384TM, CTCXZ001TM ICD PDF p. 70 2TXP_FROMChar(14)MLower bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.Solar Orbiter: filled in 35,032 of 35,032 rows; e.g. 1, 0, 2, 3, 4 ICD PDF p. 70 3TXP_TOChar(14)MUpper bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.Solar Orbiter: filled in 35,032 of 35,032 rows; e.g. 1, 0, 2, 3, 4 ICD PDF p. 70 4TXP_ALTXTChar(14)MAlphanumeric string (up to 14 characters) displayed as the engineering value for any raw value in the range TXP_FROM to TXP_TO.Solar Orbiter: filled in 35,032 of 35,032 rows; e.g. Error, DISABLED, INVALID, IDLE, ENABLED ICD PDF p. 70

docs.text: • TXP_NUMBR → txf.TXF_NUMBR: Many entries per textual calibration.

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 34) has the same four fields, all mandatory, with TXP_NUMBR as Number(4); the identifier became Char(10) in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247; also p. 253). Unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 65-66), 6.9 (p. 68-69) and 7.0 (p. 70). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: four mandatory fields, key TXP_NUMBR + TXP_FROM.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 35,032 entries for 1,003 calibrations; every TXP_NUMBR exists in txf; no TXP_ALTXT exceeds 14 characters. Only 31 entries use a true range (TXP_FROM different from TXP_TO), e.g. CDMTX000TM maps 134217793-134256128 to 'MOTOR 1 CLOSE'; all others map single raw values. The largest set, PARAMIDTM, maps each on-board parameter ID to the ground parameter name (e.g. 167776256 -> NCDT00B0, 0 -> DUMMYVAL), turning a textual calibration into a parameter-ID lookup.

docs.title: vdf.dat: Database version
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.1.11 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

The vdf table names and versions the whole database. It is read when the SCOS-2000 run-time database is generated, and if the file holds several records the last one imported sets the internal database version name and description. SCOS-2000 shows the version name to users and uses it as a consistency token, for example to make sure that a saved command stack is loaded against the same database version that produced it. The table also carries domain and version-management information: a domain identifier that binds the entire database to one SCOS-2000 domain (so no other table needs a domain column), plus a release and an issue number used to manage successive database deliveries. For backwards compatibility these three fields are optional: a null domain means the current local domain, and a null release or issue is taken as 0. The importer also compares the domain identifier given as an import option with the one stored in vdf. Unlike most tables, vdf is compulsory: vdf.dat must be present in the import directory and contain at least one record.1

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: #FieldTypeM/ODescription 1VDF_NAMEChar(8)MName of the database version: any alphanumeric string of up to 8 characters. It is the identifier shown by SCOS-2000 applications and used to check that artefacts such as saved stack files were produced with the same database version that is now loaded. When vdf.dat contains several records, the name in the last imported record wins.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 25925PFM ICD PDF p. 38 2VDF_COMMENTChar(32)OFree-text comment associated with the database version (up to 32 characters). Together with VDF_NAME it forms the internal version description taken from the last imported record.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33 ICD PDF p. 38 3VDF_DOMAINIDNumber(5)OIdentifier of the SCOS-2000 domain to which the whole database belongs, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1. Storing it once here avoids a domain column in every table. If it is null, the current local domain identifier is assumed (section 3.3.1.1, p. 37). The importer cross-checks this value against the domain identifier passed to it as an input option.Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 0 ICD PDF p. 38 4VDF_RELEASENumber(5)ODatabase release number, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1, used for database version management. Optional for backwards compatibility; a null value is treated as 0.Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 25925 ICD PDF p. 38 5VDF_ISSUENumber(5)ODatabase issue number within the release, an unsigned integer in the range 0 to 2^16-1, used for database version management. Optional for backwards compatibility; a null value is treated as 0.Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 1 of 1 rows; e.g. 733 ICD PDF p. 38

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (2001) defines vdf with only VDF_NAME (Char(8), mandatory) and VDF_COMMENT (Char(32)) (icd-5-1-tos-gci p. 22). The domain, release and issue fields were added in ICD 6.0 for SCOS-2000 R4.0 ('VDF table modification', ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 249). ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 35-36) and ICD 6.9 (p. 37-38) already show the five-field layout with VDF_DOMAINID, and ICD 6.9 gives VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE the import default '0', as in ICD 7.0 (p. 38). No change to vdf is listed in the ICD 7.0 change annex (Annex 2, p. 261-263). pyscos2000 (based on ICD 7.2) keeps five fields in the same order but names the third one VDF_DOMAIN instead of VDF_DOMAINID; whether ICD 7.2 itself renamed the field is not stated in the available sources.

Notes from the extraction

Field 3 is printed VDF_DOMAINID in ICD 6.7, 6.9 and 7.0 but is called VDF_DOMAIN in pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2 based); the Solar Orbiter SQLite database follows the pyscos2000 name (column VDF_DOMAIN). ICD 7.0 marks no key field for vdf, and pyscos2000 also declares none. The Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16 release has exactly one 5-field record: VDF_NAME '25925PFM', VDF_COMMENT '20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33', VDF_DOMAINID 0, VDF_RELEASE 25925, VDF_ISSUE 733. The 2020-04-16 release has the analogous record '10720PFM' / '20200416-CSW3.0.3p1_MAS6.51' / 0 / 10720 / 651. Inference (not documented in the ICD): Solar Orbiter puts the MIB build number of the release name (MIB__20250916M25925...) into VDF_RELEASE and an encoding of the 'MAS' version (7.33 -> 733) into VDF_ISSUE. The SWA instrument database vdf.dat contains 70 records (a version history from SWA_00.2 to SWA_6.3.4); per the ICD only the last imported record would set the version name, so the record order in the file matters.

docs.title: vpd.dat: Variable packet definition
docs.text:
ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.5.219,863 rows in Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16

vpd defines variable telemetry packets: any packet whose content follows the PUS structure rules, including repeated groups whose repetition count is read from the packet, nested repetitions, and parameters whose identity or type is given by an on-board parameter ID. It is used by the SCOS-2000 Variable Packets Display (VPD) and the related processing together with pcf, and has no relation to plf or to the dpf/gpf/spf display tables. A structure is identified by a TPSD, linked to packets through PID_TPSD, and its records are ordered by VPD_POS; parameter extraction starts PID_DFHSIZE bytes after the start of the source packet. Each parameter begins where the previous one ended, shifted by VPD_OFFSET: positive offsets create gaps, negative ones overlaps. Padding bits before a value are handled through PCF_WIDTH. vpd can also describe fixed packets just to show them in the VPD, one parameter per line with VPD_NEWLINE. Besides extraction, each record carries display attributes: column header, width, justification, new line, what to show and number format. Only packets defined in vpd show their parameters in full mode of the Packet History display. The table must be sorted by VPD_TPSD and VPD_POS.1

Key: VPD_TPSD, VPD_POS

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
#FieldTypeM/ODescription 1VPD_TPSDNumber(10)MTelemetry Packet Structure Definition identifier; unsigned integer matching PID_TPSD of the packet(s) interpreted with this structure.Refers to pid.PID_TPSD. Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,863 of 19,863 rows; e.g. 55083, 80020, 55278, 54137, 54117 ICD PDF p. 100 2VPD_POSNumber(4)MOrdinal position of this parameter within the structure definition, used by database editors to deliver the records in the right order. Grey row in the ICD: the ordering is what matters to SCOS-2000, and the table is expected to be sorted by VPD_TPSD and VPD_POS.Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,863 of 19,863 rows; e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ICD PDF p. 100 3VPD_NAMEChar(8)MName of the parameter appearing at this position of the variable packet; must match PCF_NAME of the monitoring parameter to be processed and displayed.Refers to pcf.PCF_NAME. Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,863 of 19,863 rows; e.g. NCD0C095, NCD05011, NCD0C094, NCD0C0B4, NCD0C0B7 ICD PDF p. 100 4VPD_GRPSIZENumber(3)OSet only for parameters that are repeat counters (the PUS 'N') or for 'dummy' fixed-repetition parameters (see VPD_FIXREP). It gives the number of parameters in the group to be repeated: the group is formed by the next VPD_GRPSIZE records of the table. The VPD application supports nested structures, i.e. a repeat counter may itself be part of a repeated group.Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,863 of 19,863 rows; e.g. 0, 1, 3, 2, 8 ICD PDF p. 101 5VPD_FIXREPNumber(3)OFixed repetition count for arrays of fixed size. A positive value is set on a counter parameter and gives the fixed number of repetitions of the group of VPD_GRPSIZE parameters that follows. Such parameters must be defined in pcf but are not present in the packet: they only declare the fixed array size.
  • 0 No repeat
  • >0 Fixed number of repetitions of the following VPD_GRPSIZE parameters (the parameter itself is not read from the packet)
  • -1 Future extension (italic in the ICD): repeat groups of VPD_GRPSIZE until the end of the packet; probably excludes further nesting
Default 0. Solar Orbiter: filled in 19,863 of 19,863 rows; e.g. 0 ICD PDF p. 101 6VPD_CHOICEChar(1)OWhether the value of this parameter selects the structure of the rest of the packet: if 'Y', the value read is used as a TPSD key to interpret the following entries, and the choice parameter must be the last one of its TPSD group. The row is in italics: per section 3.3.2.5.2 (p. 106), choice structures are not currently supported by the VPD application.

  • N Not a choice field

If 'Y', the value is compared with PCF_PID values to find the SCOS-2000 name of the parameter, e.g. for the parameter-number column of a monitoring report.

When set to 'Y', all parameters of the packet are displayed on separate lines.

In variable packets the value 2 may only be used for parameters with VPD_PIDREF = 'Y' to show the PCF_NAME and PCF_DESCR of the identified parameter; other parameters show only the value, their description being in the column header.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• VPD_TPSD → pid.PID_TPSD: Structure used for packets whose PID_TPSD is not -1.
  • VPD_NAME → pcf.PCF_NAME: Parameter extracted/displayed; PCF_WIDTH (padding) and PCF_PTC (e.g. deduced 11) affect extraction.
  • VPD_PIDREF → pcf.PCF_PID: Values of parameter-ID fields are resolved to parameter names.
  • VPD_CHOICE → vpd.VPD_TPSD: A choice value selects another TPSD for the rest of the packet (not currently supported).

docs.title: History across ICD issues
docs.text:
ICD 5.1 (p. 45-48) already has the 14 fields in the same order; VPD_POS is not marked mandatory there. The ICD 7.0 Annex 1 list of changes for all evolution releases records that the VPD application supports nested repetitions (item 4, p. 244). ICD 6.2/6.3 updated the VPD_FORM description (p. 253). ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 93-98) and 6.9 (p. 97-102) define VPD_FIXREP with values 0 and positive counts only (icd-6-9 p. 99); ICD 7.0 adds '-1' as a future extension (S2K-7750, p. 262). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: key VPD_TPSD + VPD_POS, VPD_NAME and VPD_WIDTH mandatory, defaults GRPSIZE '0', FIXREP '0', CHOICE 'N', PIDREF 'N', JUSTIFY 'L', NEWLINE 'N', DCHAR '0', FORM 'N', OFFSET '0'.

Notes from the extraction

No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. ICD typo: VPD_FIXREP's '-1' option refers to 'VPD_GRPSIZ'. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 19,863 records describing 2,063 structures (one per TPSD-bearing packet), up to 610 positions in one structure. VPD_FIXREP is always 0 and VPD_CHOICE always 'N', consistent with choice structures being unsupported. VPD_DCHAR is always 0. 711 records are repeat counters (VPD_GRPSIZE > 0, up to 130 for NSM00231 'STO Cat RN' in TPSD 80020). 1,449 records are parameter-ID fields (VPD_PIDREF = 'Y', e.g. NCD0C095 'OBCHP_Monitored Par ID'), and 2,886 records place deduced (PTC 11) parameters. VPD_WIDTH is 1 or 0 (1,983 hidden values). VPD_FORM is 'N', 'H' (613) or empty, VPD_JUSTIFY 'L', 'R' (71) or empty, and VPD_NEWLINE 'N' or empty. 389 records use a negative VPD_OFFSET to overlap the previous field, e.g. -32 for NCDD01S1 'CCSDS Sec Header'. VPD_DISDESC values are cut to the 16-character limit, sometimes keeping a trailing blank (e.g. 'OBCHP_Monitored ').

docs.title: Missions
docs.text:
The standards and systems described elsewhere in this wiki - CCSDS packets and frames, the PUS, SCOS-2000 and its Mission Information Base - only become concrete in a mission. This section gathers what the public record says about individual ESA missions: which documents exist, which data could be copied, and what they reveal about how each mission used the standards. Every statement is tied to a document in the library, and every library entry records where the file was copied from and when.

Three missions are documented in depth, because their interface documents (and, for one of them, their real database) are publicly posted:

  • Solar Orbiter - the only mission whose operational MIB is publicly available as data; this wiki analyses two releases with SQL and lets you browse every parameter, packet and command in the MIB explorer. The databases of two of its instruments are also publicly posted, analysed on SWA and STIX, and the instrument-level interface documents are on Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces.
  • Herschel and Planck - a joint project that put SCOS-2000 into the MOC, the central checkout and the instrument EGSE, with a well-documented system database (HPSDB) and MIB tailoring notes.
  • Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express - ESOC's interplanetary mission family, with a shared mission control system and the data delivery, flight dynamics and ground station interface documents that went with it.

A fourth page, Other missions and SCOS-2000 users, collects what the sources say about everything else: the older control systems, INTEGRAL, XMM-Newton, PROBA, the Earth Explorers, Galileo, the Sentinels, BepiColombo, JUICE and the move to EGS-CC.

docs.title: Mission families and SCOS-2000 generations
docs.text:
ESOC builds mission control systems in layers: generic infrastructure (SCOS-2000), a mission family kernel shared by similar missions, and a thin mission-specific layer specified only as a "delta".3132 The families named in the sources are interplanetary (Rosetta, Mars Express, Venus Express, with BepiColombo and Solar Orbiter expected to join), Earth observation (CryoSat, GOCE, Aeolus and later missions such as Swarm), observatory and navigation; the sources name members only for the first two.3132

flowchart TB
  S2K["SCOS-2000 infrastructure (EGOS / MICONYS)"]
  S2K --> IP["Interplanetary family kernel"]
  S2K --> EE["Earth Explorer mission kernel"]
  S2K --> OTHER["Missions on SCOS-2000 without a named family kernel<br/>(e.g. INTEGRAL, Herschel/Planck MCS)"]
  IP --> ROS["Rosetta"]
  IP --> MEX["Mars Express"]
  IP --> VEX["Venus Express"]
  IP -.-> BC["BepiColombo (expected to join, 2007 source)"]
  IP -.-> SO["Solar Orbiter (expected to join, 2007 source)"]
  EE --> CRY["CryoSat"]
  EE --> GOCE["GOCE"]
  EE --> AEO["Aeolus"]
  EE -.-> SW["Swarm (future mission, 2005 source)"]
  S2K ==> CC["EGS-CC (from 2026; Swarm pilot, Ariel first launch)"]

The solid lines are memberships stated in the 2005 and 2007 sources, the dotted lines are missions those sources expected to join; the EGS-CC arrow reflects the 2025 SpaceOps paper.313230 Placing INTEGRAL and the Herschel/Planck MCS outside a named family is this wiki's simplification, because the sources do not assign them to one.

Sharing a control-system kernel is distinct from sharing spacecraft hardware. For hardware, the 2007 Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document retained commonality with BepiColombo, especially for the high-gain antenna and the solar array, said the attitude control system and avionics might also be common, and considered re-using elements from Herschel-Planck, Mars Express or Venus Express.37

docs.title: Where the missions show up in the standards pages
docs.text:
The mission pages are the best place to see standards in use. Some cross-references:

  • Packet structures: Solar Orbiter's APID split into process ID and category (Solar Orbiter), the Herschel test-equipment packet headers with a 3-bit command source in the sequence count (Herschel and Planck), and a decoded Rosetta telecommand with a verified CRC (Rosetta, MEX, VEX); background on Space Packet and PUS packet structures.
  • PUS service selection: the Herschel/Planck table of mandatory, optional and not applicable services and How Solar Orbiter uses PUS; see the PUS message type catalogue.
  • Instrument-level definitions: the Solar Orbiter packet ICD allocates private service ranges to each instrument (for example 200-205 to SWA and 236-240 to STIX); the SWA DPU ICD and the SWA and STIX instrument databases show how one instrument fills its range and how its definitions reappear in the spacecraft MIB - see SWA, STIX and instrument interfaces.3938
  • Data delivery: GDDS for Rosetta/MEX/VEX, EDDS for Solar Orbiter - compare GDDS and mission DDIDs and EDDS.
  • Time correlation: the Rosetta/MEX/VEX coefficient packets and time quality flags, and the Solar Orbiter time stamps - see Time correlation in SCOS-2000.
  • MIB tailoring and heritage: Herschel's HPSDB rules and repatriated CCS tables, the Rosetta/MEX MIB extensions and CryoSat's command parameter types, all visible in the Solar Orbiter release - see Mission tailoring of the MIB and History of the Database Import ICD.

docs.title: Herschel and Planck
docs.text:
Herschel and Planck are two very different ESA science satellites that were developed together: ESA commissioned them jointly under the Horizon 2000 scientific programme, and commonality between the two missions and between their mission phases was a key design driver for cost reasons.1 Herschel is an infrared observatory; Planck measures the Cosmic Microwave Background with receivers cooled to very low temperatures. Both were to fly to Lissajous orbits around the second Lagrange point (L2), separate soon after launch and then operate independently.2

For this wiki the pair matters because it is a well-documented example of a project that put SCOS-2000 everywhere: in the ESOC Mission Operations Centre, in the spacecraft Central Checkout System used for system tests, and in the instrument teams' own electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) and real-time assessment systems.6962 One system database, the Herschel/Planck System Database (HPSDB), collected the MIB data and generated the SCOS-2000 and checkout files for them.627 This page follows the data: the operations requirements that shaped the packets, the packet structures and the space link, the HPSDB and its rules for reading and writing MIB files, how a database release was produced and named, the Herschel science ground segment's tailoring of the MIB, the Planck LFI telemetry chain, and the EGSE history. The SCOS-2000-centred case study, including the April 2000 decision meeting and the HCSS telecommand-history interfaces, is on Herschel/Planck: SCOS-2000 in a science mission ground segment; the bit-level layouts of the interface control documents (packets, frames, the EGSE router, the PIPE protocol and the checkout system's MIB) are on Herschel/Planck interface documents.

What this wiki has, and what it does not have

Every document cited on this page is in the library, with its original URL, the UTC time of copy and a SHA-256 checksum; most were copied on 2026-11-05 from the Herschel Science Archive (SPIRE internal documents), the ESA Cosmos site, arXiv, the NLR report server and the University of Lethbridge SPIRE pages (see Sources and copies). The Herschel/Planck MIB itself was not copied: the HPSDB release zips listed by the Herschel Science Archive refused the download with HTTP 403, so this page contains no data-driven analysis of the Herschel MIB. Where it shows numbers from SQL queries, they come from the Solar Orbiter MIB and are used only for comparison.

A second round of copies on 2026-11-12 added the Packet Structure ICD (issue 6.0) and the Space/Ground ICD (issue 3.2), the EGSE packet router ICD, the EGSE Interface Requirement Specification, the CCS External ICD, the HPSDB Software User Manual (version 2.6), the HPSDB release note issue 9.0 of one Herschel delivery, a 562-page printed overview of the HIFI instrument MIB (issue 139) and Thales Alenia Space's SESP 2015 presentation on the HPSDB's successor (from indico.esa.int). These describe the database and print parts of one instrument MIB, but they are still not the MIB files: no table of the Herschel/Planck database can be queried here.101109148

docs.title: The missions at a glance
docs.text: Item What the sources say Source Programme Joint development of two satellites under ESA's Horizon 2000 scientific programme; commonality between missions and phases is a key driver 1 Orbit Lissajous orbits about L2; the two spacecraft separate soon after launch and operate independently 2 Launch (as planned in 2006) Ariane 5 ECA, then foreseen for February 2008 (the actual date is not stated in the available sources) 2 Attitude control Herschel: highly accurate pointing; Planck: highly stable spinning attitude; many common ACMS units and most of the basic software in common 3 Daily operations Ground contact and real-time control for a few hours per day; the telemetry stored during the previous ~24 h is dumped while the next schedule is uplinked 14 Planck LFI telemetry budget At most 53.5 kbps, because a whole day of packets is stored on board and dumped in the Daily Tele-Communication Period (DTCP) 56 Telemetry/telecommand standard ESA Packet Utilisation Standard (PUS); the operations requirements were derived from ECSS-E-70-41 Draft 5.3 (April 2001). The Packet Structure ICD of 2008 states that, being tailored for Herschel/Planck, it supersedes the PUS, and that the space and ground segments support all and only the structures and services it defines 11479 Packets TC packets at most 248 octets (228 inside a mission timeline command), TM packets at most 1024 octets; only PUS version number 0 is permitted in both headers 8384 Space link X-band uplink and downlink; telemetry at 500 bps, 5 kbps, 150 kbps or 1.5 Mbps; telemetry spacecraft IDs 0x1E6 (Herschel flight model), 0x1E9 (Planck flight model) and 0x1EA (avionics model); one transfer frame length of 1115 octets 91929394 Ground stations Kourou 15 m (LEOP to commissioning), Vilspa 15 m (LEOP), New Norcia 35 m (all phases including routine science) 9798 Database format SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 5.1 (applicable to the spacecraft database); the HCSS note cites issue 5.2; the checkout system read issue 5.1 with the extensions of its own CCS External ICD 1147132 Early name Documents of 2000 call the programme "FIRST/Planck"; from 2001 they say "Herschel/Planck" 6512

docs.title: Who built what
docs.text:
The industrial organisation explains why so many database interfaces existed. Alcatel Alenia Space France (AAS-F) was prime contractor for both satellites and managed the scientific instrument interfaces; Alcatel Alenia Space Italia (AAS-I) was responsible for the service module; a team led by Dutch Space (with Sener and Analyticon) built the Attitude Control and Measurement System (ACMS) of both satellites. Terma (Denmark) developed the ACMS Application Software, Saab Ericsson Space the Basic Software, Terma (the Netherlands) the Herschel/Planck Central Checkout System (HPCCS) and GMV (Spain) the HPSDB.2 By 2007-2008 the prime's documents carry the name Thales Alenia Space: the pages of PS-ICD issue 6.0 bear a Thales Alenia Space copyright line, and the HPSDB release note of April 2008 names "Thales Alenia Space - France" as supplier.79101

  AASF -.-|overall service module responsibility| AASI["AAS-I<br/>service module"]
  AASF -- "responsibility" --> GMV["GMV<br/>HPSDB"]
  AASI -- "subcontract" --> TERMA_NL["Terma NL<br/>HPCCS (central checkout)"]
  AASI -- "subcontract" --> SAAB["Saab Ericsson Space<br/>Basic Software"]
  DS["Dutch Space (+ Sener, Analyticon)<br/>ACMS of both satellites"] -.-|ACMS software| TERMA_DK["Terma DK<br/>ACMS Application Software"]
  ESA -.-|instrument interfaces<br/>managed by AAS-F| PI["Instruments<br/>HIFI, PACS, SPIRE (Herschel)<br/>LFI, HFI (Planck)"]
