Solid arrows are the contract or responsibility relationships the paper states (ESA commissioning, "under AAS-I subcontract", "under AAS-F responsibility"); dotted lines are roles without a stated contract, because the paper does not say who contracted AAS-I, Dutch Space or Terma Denmark.227

docs.title: Operations requirements: the OIRD
docs.text: The Herschel/Planck Operations Interface Requirements Document (SCI-PT-RS-07360, issue 2.2, printed date "31 September 2003", prepared at ESOC by S. J. Dodsworth and S. Matussi) states what the spacecraft and payloads must provide so that ESOC can operate them, and what must be delivered to the MOC to prepare operations.11 Its packet chapter is derived from the PUS (applicable document AD-1, ECSS-E-70/41 Draft 5.3, April 2001); the Space/Ground ICD (SCI-PT-ICD-07418) and the Packet Structure ICD (PS-ICD, cited as SCI-PT-IF-07527) hold the detailed frame and packet layouts.11 Both are now in the library, as SGICD issue 3.2 of 1 December 2004 and PS-ICD issue 6.0 of 25 January 2008 (see below). The PS-ICD's own reference is SCI-PT-ICD-07527; for traceability its requirements name their parent requirements with tags such as [P:SCI-PT-RS-07360#3.1-PACK-14, which points to OIRD requirement PACK-14.907879 Requirements marked "P" apply to spacecraft and payloads, "PO" apply to the spacecraft and may be relevant to payloads, and unmarked ones apply to the spacecraft only.11 The 2001 revision made the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD an applicable document.12

docs.title: Operations concept
docs.text:
Science operations run from an on-board schedule outside ground contact, so the spacecraft and instruments need on-board monitoring and autonomy; packet telemetry is expected to help order the daily dump (status first, then events and command verification reports, then observation data).14 The document insists that operations use the same telemetry and telecommand database as the EGSE, delivered to the operations implementers in time.14 The general concepts it fixes are:1516

  • Telecommand delivery. Every command is a telecommand packet sent via the Command and Data Management System (CDMS), from ground, the mission timeline or an on-board procedure. The APID names the destination; APID plus sequence control identify one command instance; type and subtype give its meaning; the acknowledgement field selects the verification reports (ST[01]).
  • Telemetry collection. Data are polled from units by the CDMS and kept in mass memory until erased by ground command. Packet kinds are housekeeping, science (not processed by the CDMS), telecommand reports, event reports and memory dumps.
  • Packetisation by the CDMS for units that only deliver discrete signals.
  • On-board monitoring by tables, with an event packet at each transition. The document notes this deviates from the PUS, which offers a transition reporting list (ST[12]); events can trigger a telecommand (ST[19]).
  • On-board control procedures (OBCPs) written in a Spacecraft Control Language running in the CDMS (ST[18]; see also ECSS-E-ST-70-01C).
  • Functions as permanently available "black boxes" that can be started, stopped or given instructions (ST[08]).
  • One spacecraft time reference that time-stamps all TM packets, distributed to the instruments at power-on and then updated at agreed intervals (ST[09]).

docs.title: Which PUS services the instruments had to implement
docs.text:
The OIRD table "Applicable PUS Services" fixes the service set for instruments; the PS-ICD defines the capability sets, and a mandatory service may in practice need only its minimum capability set.17

Type Service name (as printed) For instruments Wiki page 1 Telecommand Verification Mandatory ST[01] 2 Device Command Distribution Service Not applicable ST[02] 3 Housekeeping and Diagnostic Data Reporting Mandatory ST[03] 4, 7, 10, 13, 20, 22 Not used Not applicable - 5 Event Reporting Mandatory ST[05] 6 Memory Management Mandatory ST[06] 8 Function Management Optional ST[08] 9 Time Management Service Mandatory ST[09] 11 On-board Operations Scheduling Service Not applicable ST[11] 12 On-board Monitoring Service Not applicable ST[12] 14 Packet Transmission Control Service Mandatory ST[14] 15 On-board Storage and Retrieval Service Not applicable ST[15] 16 On-board Traffic Management Service Not applicable - 17 Test Mandatory ST[17] 18 OBCP Management Optional ST[18] 19 Event/Action Service Not applicable ST[19] 21 Science Data Transfer Mandatory -

Note that the 2001 draft numbering differs from today's PUS-C: service 14 was "Packet Transmission Control", 16 "On-board Traffic Management", 20 was not used for instruments and 21 "Science Data Transfer"; the section headings elsewhere in the OIRD also list service 20 as "Information Distribution CDMS - User" and 22 as "Context Saving".1713 The PS-ICD still used this numbering in issue 6.0 of 2008: its Table 2-1 marks services 4, 7, 10, 13, 20 and 22 as not used, and chapter 5 keeps the headings 16 On-board Traffic Management (for which no specific packet structures are defined), 20 Information Distribution ("not used", its requirements deleted) and 22 Context Saving ("not used", its packet structures "not applicable") next to the defined service 21 Science Data Transfer.86 The differences between PUS generations are explained on PUS-A vs PUS-C, and the PS-ICD service by service on the interface documents page.

docs.title: Packet rules that a database must express
docs.text:
The general packet requirements PACK-0 to PACK-15 translate directly into MIB structures; the right-hand column is this wiki's mapping, not part of the OIRD:18

Rule Requirement (paraphrased) Where it shows in the MIB PACK-0, PACK-13 APIDs are allocated by the ESA project in the PS-ICD (see the APID structure) PID_APID, CCF_APID PACK-1, PACK-2 Different APIDs per subsystem/instrument for TCs; TM uses the same APID as the TCs to that unit where possible pid, ccf PACK-3, PACK-4, PACK-5 A housekeeping parameter's location follows from APID, type/subtype and Structure ID (SID); SIDs unique within an APID; few SIDs per APID pic / pid / plf PACK-6, PACK-7 No sub-commutation; super-commutation only with regular sampling and a known time offset of the first sample PLF_NBOCC, PLF_LGOCC, PLF_TIME, PLF_TDOCC PACK-8 A parameter has the same structure and interpretation in every packet one pcf row per parameter PACK-10, PACK-11, PACK-12 Sampling time implied by APID and SID; the packet time is the start of acquisition; every packet except time and idle packets has a time field PID_TIME, PLF_TIME PACK-14 TCs are validated by the destination at acceptance ST[01] PACK-15 Herschel instrument data packets carry an Observation Identifier (instrument-specific)

Telecommand verification (TCV-0 to TCV-9) asks for a success report for every properly received command, a failure report with reason for every rejected one, execution reports as requested by the acknowledgement field, the command source (ground, mission timeline, OBCP) encoded in the source sequence counter, and execution delays that depend only on the command, so that ground time-outs can be configured.19 Compare the stages and time windows that the MIB's command verification tables define.

docs.title: The Satellite Database requirements
docs.text:
Section 4.2 of the OIRD defines the database that became the HPSDB:20

  • The prime contractor and the instrument teams deliver a Satellite Database (SDB) with all telemetry and telecommand data, command sequences, software parameters and commands; it is a single common database for system engineering, AIV and operations (SDBC-1, SDBC-2).
  • Its content follows the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD (AD-8, issue 5.1) and Annex 2, is internally consistent, consistent with the Flight Dynamics Database and with all on-board software, has no duplications and no irrelevant data, and records every update down to field level (SDBC-4 to SDBC-12).
  • Deliveries: version 0 for the instrument AVM, version 1 at launch minus 36 months, version 2 at L-24 months, version 3 one month before SVT 1 (complete, with flight values), version 4 one month before SVT 2, and a pre-launch update at L-1 month (SDBD-1). Each delivery carries a configuration control file with field-level changes, the spacecraft build standard and the on-board software versions; the database is delivered as ORACLE data files (SDBD-2 to SDBD-5).

Annex A2 adds that the SDB is delivered "according to AD-8" together with a Configuration Control File (version, release date, per-file versions and change tables listing old and new values, date and initials) and a Spacecraft Configuration File (model EQM or PFM, build standard, on-board software versions).21 Annex A4 delegates item names to the Herschel/Planck Naming Convention (H-P-1-ASPI-SP-0141) and names flight procedures FCP_<subsystem>_nnnn, contingency procedures CRP_<subsystem>_nnnn and timelines TDoyFfNn.22

timeline
  title Satellite Database deliveries required by the OIRD (SDBD-1)
  Instrument AVM : Version 0
  L-36 months : Version 1
  L-24 months : Version 2
  SVT 1 minus 1 month : Version 3 (complete, flight values)
  SVT 2 minus 1 month : Version 4
  L-1 month : Pre-launch update

docs.title: The Packet Structure ICD
docs.text: The Packet Structure ICD (PS-ICD, SCI-PT-ICD-07527) complements the ESA packet telemetry and telecommand standards with all mission-specific details of the data exchanged between on-board applications and their ground counterparts, for both spacecraft and all instruments; Appendix 9 adds the protocol of the satellite data bus. It is agreed between the ESA project manager, ESOC and the prime contractor and then controlled by the prime.79 Issue 1 dates from 1 September 2000 and issue 2 from 12 July 2001; requirement identifiers came with issue 3 (2002-2003), issue 4 draft 0 of 25 July 2003 was the first after the document's hand-over to Alcatel Space, and issue 6.0 of 25 January 2008 is the formal release in the library.808182 The full specification is read field by field on Herschel/Planck interface documents; this section keeps what matters for the mission's databases.

docs.title: Headers and limits
docs.text:
Both headers follow the ESA packet standards with mission rules.838485

  • Telecommands are stand-alone packets (sequence flags 0b11) of at most 248 octets, a packet length field whose value (octets in the data field minus 1) is always odd, so that the packet is a whole number of 16-bit words, and a 32-bit data field header with a secondary header flag of 0, PUS version 0, four acknowledgement bits, type, subtype and a spare octet. Commands stored in the mission timeline are encapsulated as variable octet strings in MTL telecommands, inserted with TC(11,4), which leaves 228 octets for the embedded packet.156
  • The 14-bit TC sequence count is split: the 3 most significant bits are a source part that names the generator of the command, the other 11 bits a counter kept by that source for each APID, which the receiver never checks for monotony. A verification report must copy the full sequence control field to identify the command.
  • Telemetry packets are at most 1024 octets, with one source sequence count per APID so the ground can detect losses; only science packets TM(21,x) may use the grouping flags. The 80-bit data field header holds a spare bit, PUS version 0, 4 spare bits, type, subtype, a spare octet and a 48-bit CUC time (4 octets coarse, 2 fine).159 The data field header flag is 0 only in time and idle packets.
Source part Generator of the telecommand 0b000 Ground, highest priority, all sources 0b001 Failure detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR) telecommands of the CDMU 0b010 Mission timeline (maintained by ground, executed by the CDMU) 0b011 On-board control procedures executed by the CDMU 0b100 Ground, low priority, all sources 0b101 FDIR telecommands of the attitude control computer (ACC) 0b110 Other on-board sources of the CDMU 0b111 Other on-board sources of the ACMS

The source part is how the mission met OIRD requirement TCV-6 (see above).8319 Its definition was extended in issue 3.0 of April 2003.80 In a database release of late 2007 the prime switched all telecommands from "ground high priority" to "ground low priority" by default, that is from source 0b000 to 0b100.100

Inference

Reading the release note's priority change as a change of the default source part is this wiki's interpretation: the note does not name the header field, but "ground high priority" and "ground low priority" are the PS-ICD's names for the source values 0b000 and 0b100.

docs.title: APIDs, prime and redundant
docs.text:
Appendix 3 of the PS-ICD allocates the APIDs. The most significant bits form a base APID per instrument or subsystem; the four least significant bits separate packet categories and the prime from the redundant unit, so that part of the packet identification works without decoding the data field header.87

APID (base and offsets) TC TM 0 Standard Distribute CPDU commands Standard spacecraft time source packet 16 (0x010) CDMS, 512 (0x200) ACMS All CDMS / ACMS telecommands Base: all TM except non-essential HK and diagnostics; base + 2: non-essential HK and diagnostics 1024 (0x400) HIFI All HIFI telecommands 1024 prime and 1025 redundant (essential TM); 1026 prime and 1027 redundant (non-essential HK, diagnostics); 1028-1031 science TM(21,x) 1152 (0x480) PACS, 1280 (0x500) SPIRE All PACS / SPIRE telecommands Same pattern, with further offsets for science and (PACS) diagnostic science TM(21,3) 1408 (0x580) HFI, 1536 (0x600) LFI, 1664 (0x680) SCS All telecommands of the unit Same pattern; LFI has no separate redundant APIDs 2016-2046 (0x7E0-0x7FE) SCOE / EGSE reserved SCOE / EGSE reserved 2047 (0x7FF) - Idle packets

Source: Table A-3.1.88 The EGSE range may be used by several groups in parallel during unit-level tests; the HIFI test equipment interfaces used APIDs 2016-2023 inside it, and in system tests the CCS, SCOEs, front ends and instrument EGSEs got fixed APIDs 2016-2044 (see SCOS-2000 as EGSE).8725140 In real time, telemetry of the base APID went to ground on virtual channel 0 and that of base + 2 on VC4.9689

Worked example (real MIB rows): the prime/redundant flag is the last APID bit

The HIFI MIB listing of July 2008 places the parameter HM009190 (HI_Prime_red, "Origin of the periodic HK-packet") of packet HIFI_HK_rev_7 at octet 1, bit 7, and the same flag of HIFI_essential_HK (HM094190) at the same position; its textual calibration 249 maps 0 to HIFI_prime and 1 to HIFI_redundant.116113111 With bit 0 the most significant bit and octet offsets counted from the end of the SCOS-2000 packet header, which is the start of the source packet when the generic packetiser is used (the HCSS clarifications of the import ICD, DCR 308 and DCR 309), and with Structure_ID at octet 16 right after the 16 octets of packet and data field headers, octet 1 bit 7 is the last bit of the 16-bit packet ID, which is the least significant bit of the 11-bit APID.48 The MIB therefore decodes the APID bit that the PS-ICD uses to separate 1024 (prime) from 1025 (redundant), or 1026 from 1027.88 A curve of the Herschel database printed in the release note of April 2008 (curve 170016) names the same values: 1024 HIFI_N, 1025 HIFI_R, and likewise 1152/1153 for PACS and 1280/1281 for SPIRE.108

docs.title: The space link (Space/Ground ICD)
docs.text:
The Space/Ground ICD (SCI-PT-ICD-07418, issue 3.2) fixes the radio link, the ground stations and the transfer frames.90 Both spacecraft use X-band up and down with right-hand circular polarisation (Herschel downlink 8468.5 MHz, Planck 8455.0 MHz).91 Telemetry follows the packet telemetry standard without source packet segmentation, at 500 bps or 5 kbps (PSK on a 45 884 Hz subcarrier), 150 kbps (SP-L) or 1.5 Mbps (GMSK); ranging cannot run with high-rate telemetry.92 Every transfer frame is 1115 octets long and carries a CLCW in its operational control field.9495

Virtual channel Content Downlink priority VC0 Real-time essential spacecraft HK and critical instrument HK 1 (also whenever a time packet is due) VC4 Real-time routine spacecraft and instrument HK 2 VC2 Stored spacecraft and instrument HK 3 VC1 Real-time science 4 VC3 Stored science 5 VC7 Idle frames 6

Source: HP-SGICD-STR-TM-030 to -050; VC5 and VC6 are "not required".96 The frame and segment headers, the CLCW and the MAP identifiers are drawn on the interface documents page; the CCSDS background is on TM synchronization and channel coding and COP-1.

docs.title: The packets as seen by instrument test equipment
docs.text:
Almost two years before the PS-ICD's first formal release (issue 4.0 of 7 November 2003),157 the HIFI team's TEI TMTC packet ICD (SRON-U/HIFI/SP/2001-011, issue 1.0, 19 December 2001) restated the headers for the packets exchanged with HIFI's test equipment interfaces (TEI), citing the PS-ICD issue 2.0 draft 2 as applicable document.23 Its header layouts are the same as those of PS-ICD issue 6.0 above, which is this wiki's comparison of the two documents.248385

Telecommand source packet. The primary header is the usual 48-bit Space Packet header, but the 14-bit sequence count is split into a 3-bit source field (always 0b000 for these test equipment commands) and an 11-bit counter, which each source maintains per APID and which wraps to 0.23 This matches the note to the OIRD's requirement TCV-6, which places the command source in the source sequence counter of the packet header.19

Telemetry source packet. The TM primary header has the 2-bit segmentation flags and a 14-bit source sequence counter; its packet length is always odd. The 80-bit data field header holds a spare bit, a 3-bit PUS version (0), 4 spare bits, type, subtype, a spare octet, and a 48-bit on-board time of 32 bits of coarse seconds and 16 bits of fine sub-seconds; the packet ends with a 16-bit packet error control field.24

The PUS version value 0 is printed in both headers of the TEI ICD, whereas ECSS-E-70-41A (2003) tells users to set the TC and the TM PUS version to 1, noting in footnotes that version 0 was used by the earlier ESA PUS.2326 The TEI ICD predates that issue and follows a PS-ICD draft, so its value 0 matches the earlier ESA PUS convention. The PS-ICD settles the question for the mission: issue 6.0 of 2008 permits only PUS version number 0, in the telecommand and in the telemetry data field header alike, five years after ECSS-E-70-41A had asked for 1.8385 Every TEI accepts a Set OBS-ID command TC(8,4) (function 1, activity 1, a 16-bit structure ID and a 32-bit observation identifier, matching PACK-15) and a connection test TC(17,1), and reports acceptance with TM(1,1) or TM(1,2); the failure report carries an 8-bit code (0 illegal APID, 1 bad length, 2 bad checksum, 3 illegal type, 4 illegal subtype, 5 illegal or inconsistent application data) and an 8-bit parameter.25

docs.title: Why a system database
docs.text:
The HPSDB was procured by AAS-F to keep data consistent between engineering, on-board software, AIT and flight operations, and to support the commonality between the two satellites; GMV developed it.6 It is operated at a central site where final data are stored and consistency is maintained, with several mirror sites; the system EGSE requirement GRQT-0002b asks the Central Checkout System to support an HPSDB mirror site.670 Export files from the HPSDB are used to build the on-board software and to produce the TM/TC definitions in SCOS-2000 format for AIT and operations.6 Looking back in 2015, Thales Alenia Space summarised the two ESA requirements behind it: commonality (between the two spacecraft, and the same data shared by different users), achieved through physical instantiation and category flags, and smooth transition (reuse of validated data from one programme phase to the next, up to operations), achieved through logical instantiation and category flags.148

The data model has four levels:6

  • Element - building blocks such as a star tracker or the ASW elements for common, Herschel and Planck data;
  • Subsystem - for example the ACMS or the Central Data Management Subsystem (ground support equipment is also modelled as a subsystem), built from element data plus subsystem-specific data;
  • Model - for example the Herschel and Planck service modules or the protoflight models, built from subsystems;
  • Generic - data usable by any other definition, such as ON/OFF curves and TM/TC packet headers.

Consistency is enforced by instantiation of "boxes": every box exists at least as a theoretical box (design data, e.g. a default reaction-wheel friction coefficient) and as real boxes (measured data for one unit). Logical instantiation builds subsystems from elements and models from subsystems; physical instantiation creates several real copies of a theoretical box, for example two real star trackers.6

flowchart LR
  G["Generic level<br/>curves, TM/TC headers<br/>(subsystem letter G, position 000)"]
  E["Element level<br/>theoretical boxes"] -- "physical instantiation" --> R["Real boxes<br/>(e.g. STR #1, STR #2)"]
  E -- "logical instantiation" --> S["Subsystem level<br/>e.g. ACMS, CDMS, EGSE"]
  S -- "logical instantiation" --> M["Model level<br/>Herschel SVM, Planck SVM, PFM"]
  G -.-> S
  G -.-> M
  M --> X1["S2K bridge files<br/>(instrument EGSE, ICD 5.1)"]
  M --> X2["CCS bridge files<br/>(HPCCS)"]
  M --> X3["On-board software inputs"]

The diagram combines the levels described in the NLR paper with the export targets and the generic-item naming rules of the HPSDB technical note.628

docs.title: The HPSDB as a tool (GMV user manual 2.6)
docs.text:
GMV's HPSDB Software User Manual (H-P-1-GMV-MA-20487, version 2.6, 15 September 2005) shows the system that the instrument teams, the prime and the AIT sites actually used. Version 1.0 dates from 18 July 2003; version 2.0 (January 2004) added the real data part, version 2.2 (September 2004) the mirror sites, the TM/TC verification and the ON/OFF status of real elements, and version 2.6 the logical instantiation of items and a "where is referenced" tool.117 HPSDB is a web application on Windows 2000 with an Oracle 9i Release 2 database and the Oracle9iAS application server; the central site ran on an HP ProLiant DL380 server and the mirror sites on Dell Precision 650 workstations.118

Data live in three areas, and normal changes pass through them:119123

Operation Effect Who Create New object in the working area Normal users with the right role Checkout Copy of a validated object into the working area, to be modified Normal users Delete Copy into the working area, marked for deletion Normal users Validation Moves the selected boxes from the working to the reference area; replaced copies go to the archive area; deleted objects go straight to the archive The schema manager only Discard Removes the working copy Normal users

Validation refuses an object whose references point outside the reference area or to objects not selected or being deleted. A selection date decides what a user sees: the current date (working copies over reference copies, the only mode with write access), the last validation date (reference area only, read-only) or any past date (the archived reference area of that date).123120 Users have one of nine roles (equipment and subsystem fabricator, engineer or consultant; model engineer or consultant; AIT) and one category flag code: Operations, OB (on-board software), AIT or All; bridge files can be generated for one user category.121122 The category list of the user manual has no flight dynamics entry, unlike the 8-bit flag of the processing note's rule G10 (AIT, operations, software, flight dynamics).31

The central site holds all valid data and traces their evolution; mirror sites (one was required at the Central Checkout System) may modify only real objects. Sites never talk to each other: managers exchange XML transfer and log files by hand, named for example Export_CENTRAL_EL_DPU_02_12_2004_15_33_50.xml.12412570 Two operations write straight into the reference area, outside validation: verification data (which test sequence verified a TM parameter or TC, and when, loaded from a tab-separated file with the same six columns as the CCS "update files", a site taking the place of the host) and the ON periods of real elements; the verification data of an item are reset whenever the item, its curves or its packet structure change.126127134

docs.title: How HPSDB reads and writes MIB files (H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060)
docs.text:
The Alcatel Alenia Space note MIB files processing by HPSDB (H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060, issue 1, dated 07/02/2006; draft 1D1 of 02/02/2006 was sent to ESA to close an action from an instrument database meeting in September 2005) documents how HPSDB ingests and generates two flavours of MIB "bridge files": S2K files for the instrument EGSE, which used MIB ICD issue 5.1 and was "version 2.3eP5 based on SCOS 2000 2.3e", and CCS files for the HPCCS central checkout, which had its own external ICD (H-P-4-TE-ID-8020).27 It lists the constraints that an input file must satisfy so that HPSDB writes back an identical file. Constraints printed in bold cannot be checked by HPSDB and remain the user's responsibility; the others are checked at load time.27

Full round-trip compatibility was not always possible. The note's first example is the packet-to-SPID relation: HPSDB allows several TM packets to map to one SCOS packet (SPID), while the MIB ICD allows any-to-any mappings provided that only one is valid at a time.27 The CCS also had functions that SCOS-2000 then lacked, for example selection of a calibration by condition, event limits and critical telecommands, and SCOS configuration files such as MISCconfig differed between installations.27

The note's twenty general rules (G1-G20) are the clearest public statement of what a system database needs on top of the MIB ICD:28303132

Rule Topic What HPSDB does or requires G1 Object data model Bridge files are extracted per object together with all items of the generic object; MIB files must be wrapped in an object identified by its position, defined in configuration files before loading G2-G5 Naming convention Identifier structure (see below), with special numeric schemes for S2K curves, verification stages and parameter range sets, whose MIB fields were too short for instantiation G6 Enumerated fields Values must be in the ICD set, possibly reduced by the PS-ICD (allowed type/subtype pairs) or by HPSDB (no octal radix) G7 Commutation Packets and structures are lists of parameters, structures and (TC only) fixed areas with offsets, start bits, repetition counters and super-commutation attributes; a flag says whether PLF, VPD or both are generated G8 Default values ICD defaults are forced even where irrelevant; some are replaced by HPSDB defaults (e.g. PID_CHECK, CAF_RADIX, CCA_RADIX) G9 Commonality Discrete and status curves may be shared by TM and TC, so TM and TC curves must not reuse the same identifier G10 Category flag Each item has an 8-bit flag, one bit per user type (AIT, operations, software, flight dynamics); loaded MIB items get "all except FDD" G11 Common fields 64-character mnemonic, short description (32 characters by default), 256-character long description and configuration data (action, user, date, reason, area, source, site, validation and archive dates) G12 TC packet header TC headers are defined generically; TCP, PCPC and PCDF are ignored on input and commands must reference one generic header via CCF_PKTID G13 Reserved characters Because of XML, >, <, ', " and & are forbidden; descriptions use letters, digits, space, +, - and _ G14 Radix No octal (O) for unsigned integers; only D or H G15 Range allocation Value ranges (PID numbers, UDC packet locations, ...) are allocated in the naming convention because SCOS did not support "smooth transition" easily G16 Automatic instantiation Short description gets a position character appended; APID = element offset + position base; PID, UDC and MISC positions get deltas G17 Short description Mandatory in HPSDB; if empty, it is set to the identifier G18 Orphan items Not loaded G19 Sorting Output sorted by the ICD primary key; inputs must be sorted too G20 Derived parameters Expression files must be delivered with the MIB files

The user manual shows the other side of rule G1. A user zips the SCOS-2000 or CCS bridge files together with configuration files that place them in the HPSDB object model: S2K_EL.txt lists the real elements with their theoretical element numbers, S2K_SUB.txt the subsystem with its pseudo position and one line per position (with the ACC and CDMU bus controller flags and the SCOE host and port), S2K_TM.txt is a copy of pid.dat with a naming convention identifier prepended to each row, and S2K_CUR.txt, S2K_CVS.txt and S2K_PRF.txt map SCOS curve, verification stage and range set numbers to generic HPSDB items. Loading creates no box types or generic items, needs the OL expression files for derived parameters, and "is not a SCOS bridge file validator".128129 The manual's example loads three HIFI elements (ICU, FCU and LCU at positions 190, 191 and 194) and two redundant SPIRE real elements of one theoretical element (positions 196 and 197) into subsystem H001001, whose pseudo position is 289.130 The field tables of these files are on the interface documents page.

docs.title: The naming convention, with a real example
docs.text:
HPSDB identifiers are built hierarchically. At element level, the first letter of a character identifier gives the item type and the remaining characters are free. At subsystem or model level, a subsystem letter is put in front (Z for a pseudo subsystem) and a three-digit position is appended (999 for the system pseudo position); numeric identifiers get a two-digit subsystem number in front instead (A = 00 ... Y = 25, 26 for the pseudo subsystem). Generic items use subsystem letter G, subsystem number 07, position 000 and element number 000.28

Curves are NUMBER(6) in HPSDB (three digits of theoretical element number and three free digits) and unique across curve types. Because the S2K MIB fields were too short, an instrument S2K file codes a specific curve as a three-digit number matching the three free digits, and a generic curve as 1xxx, which stands for the HPSDB generic curve G000xxx000; verification stages and parameter range sets use the same trick (1xxxx for 07xxxx000, 1xxx for GRxxx000).29 GMV's user manual of 2005 describes a different mechanism for the generic items, mapping files loaded with the bridge files: in its examples SCOS curves 900, 901 and 905 are read as the generic curves 000900, 000901 and 000905, verification stage 9000 as the generic stage 079000000 and range set 0 as GR000000, and the files limit SCOS curve numbers to 999 and stage and range set numbers to 9999 "for HPSDB compliance".129130 Which of the two mechanisms the Herschel/Planck deliveries used is not stated in the available sources. The HIFI MIB of 2008 indeed numbers its curves with three digits, for example textual curve 249 (HI_Prime_red), numerical curves 293 to 301 and command curves 100 (HRH_switch) and 134 (HIF_mxbias_step_V), as the prime's fax of January 2003 had required (see Mission tailoring of the MIB).113114

Worked example (real identifiers): AESMG002 and AESMG003

The NLR paper gives one pair of real operational identifiers: the ACMS mode telemetry parameters in the Herschel and Planck mode status words start with AESMG, and the Herschel and Planck ASW boxes have numbers 002 and 003, so the same parameter is AESMG002 on Herschel and AESMG003 on Planck.8 Read with the HPSDB rule: a five-character subsystem-level name followed by the three-digit position of the box in which the element is instantiated.28

Inference

That the leading A is the subsystem letter of the ACMS and that E is the item-type letter of the element identifier is this wiki's reading of the G2 rule; neither source spells out the letters of this example. The Herschel release note of 2008 supports the first part: the ACMS is subsystem A105 of the Herschel model, and its position 002 holds the element ACC_A_H_4, while position 001 holds ACC_A_C_4.105 Reading _H_ as Herschel and _C_ as common, and position 002 as the Herschel ASW box of the NLR example, is also this wiki's interpretation; the meaning of E is still not stated in the available sources.

The SPIRE instrument applied the same naming convention to its own MIB in technical note SPIRE-RAL-NOT-001155 (issue 1.2, March 2002). Command names follow SCiiippp, command parameters SPiiippp, monitoring parameters SMiiippp, packets (SPIDs) tttnnnnppp, calibrations tttnnnrrr, alphanumeric displays SAiiippp, graphic displays SGiiippp and scrolling displays SLiiippp, where iii is a theoretical parameter identifier, ttt a system element number (for example 480 for OBS, 490 for the DPU), nnn a running number, rrr a real element number and ppp a position.75 The general rules for project naming conventions are discussed on Mission tailoring of the MIB.

The printed HIFI MIB (issue 139, equivalent to HIFI_ASPI MIB 11.7, 11 July 2008) shows the same structure in a delivered instrument database, and the Herschel release note supplies the positions that the names end with:109105

Real identifier Mnemonic (from the HIFI MIB) Read as Position in model HERSCH_FM9 HM009190 HI_Prime_red (monitoring parameter) H + M + 009 + 190 190 HIFI_ICU_N HM248191 HF_AP_2K_IF_CT (monitoring parameter) H + M + 248 + 191 191 HIFI_FCU_N HP056191 HIF_ch1_mxbias0_V (command parameter) H + P + 056 + 191 191 HIFI_FCU_N HP001197 HIFI_BB_ID (command parameter) H + P + 001 + 197 197 HIFI_OBS_N HD111190 HIFI_ptv_input H + D + 111 + 190 190 HIFI_ICU_N PC004380 DPU_START_AUT_FUN (called a "PACS command parameter" in the HCSS note) P + C + 004 + 380 380 PACS_DPU_N

The mnemonics come from the HIFI MIB annex and the HCSS note.111112116110115155 The EGSE Interface Requirement Specification confirms the letters for EGSE items: remote commands are YC, their parameters YP and remote monitoring parameters YM, followed by a three-character function and the item's position (for example 940 for the CCS).141142 In 2015 Thales Alenia Space listed the item letters of its successor database as A TM packet, C curve, D synthetic parameter, G group, K constant and M TM parameter.149

Inference

The split of each name into subsystem letter, item-type letter, three free characters and a three-digit position is this wiki's reading of rule G2 applied to the printed names; the HIFI documents do not explain their identifiers. That D marks derived (synthetic) parameters in the HIFI MIB is inferred from the 2015 letter list, which was written for a later database, and from names such as HIFI_ptv_input. For PC004380 the reading gives a command (C), while the HCSS note calls it a command parameter. Two library sources favour the command reading without naming PC004380: the EGSE IRS uses C for remote commands and P for their parameters, and the user manual's verification-file example lists PC001428 with type c (telecommand).142126 The short description DPU_START_AUT_FUN also fits a command, but no source settles it.

docs.title: Table by table: examples of HPSDB processing
docs.text:
Chapter 5 of the note goes through every MIB table field by field, stating the input processing, the HPSDB field, the output processing and the constraint.33 Some examples show how much a system database rewrites:

  • VDF is not loaded; on output HPSDB computes the version name from the selected date (by default the last validation date) and creates several records.34
  • PCF holds all kinds of parameter in one table - TC, TC software, TC header, TM, TM software, dynamic and static UDC, saved synthetic, MISC and (CCS only) system parameters.34
  • PID: HPSDB splits the MIB table into a TM packet definition and a SCOS packet definition, allows only many-to-one links from TM packets to SPIDs (AIT wanted one-to-one), forces PID_TPSD to the SPID or -1, PID_TIME and PID_VALID to Y, and requires one PID_DFHSIZE (default 16) per SPID.35
  • PIC is never loaded: to support smooth transition it is defined once in the generic part of HPSDB, every Herschel/Planck SCOS and CCS user had to implement the same table, and it is regenerated from generic data on output.35
  • Parameter sets (PST, PSV, CPS, PVS, PSM): "Not supported by CCS", constraint "do not use", although HPSDB can load them.36
  • Specific CCS data: the note also processes tables that existed only in the CCS ICD - conditional calibration CUR, groups GRP, GRPA, GRPK, SCOE definitions SCO, TC and TM distribution TCD and TMD, and logarithmic curves LGF.37 That ICD, Terma's CCS External ICD H-P-4-TE-ID-8020 (issue 1.8, 18 January 2006), declares the import ICD issue 5.1 fully applicable to the checkout system except for its listed changes; they are analysed on Mission tailoring of the MIB.131132

docs.title: From CCS-only tables to the standard MIB
docs.text:
Several of those CCS-only features came back into SCOS-2000. The change annex of MIB ICD issue 7.0 lists, for ICD version 6.0, the Herschel & Planck Check Out System functionalities repatriation: curve selection (several calibrations per parameter selected by another parameter's value), delta limits, enable/inhibit of parameters, packets and named groups, character curve identifiers (from NUM(4) to CHAR(10)), wider verification stage identifiers (NUM(5) to NUM(8)), character range-set identifiers, the logarithmic curve LGF for platinum thermistors, editable string parameters and automatic length fields for variable strings.38 The cur, grp, grpa, grpk and lgf tables of the ICD history are this heritage; SCO, TCD and TMD do not appear in the ICD 7.0 text.3839

The features are in active use on a later mission. In the September 2025 Solar Orbiter release, 907 parameters have conditional calibrations (1 974 cur rows), 105 monitoring checks are delta checks (OCP_TYPE = D), and 2 monitoring groups with 4 packet-group rows exist, while lgf is empty.4241

SQL used (Herschel/Planck heritage features in the Solar Orbiter MIB) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL)
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT CUR_PNAME) FROM cur;   -- 1974 | 907
SELECT OCP_TYPE, count(*) FROM ocp GROUP BY 1;         -- C 15, D 105, H 4153, S 3096
SELECT count(*) FROM grp;  SELECT count(*) FROM grpa;  SELECT count(*) FROM grpk;  -- 2, 0, 4
SELECT count(*) FROM lgf;                              -- 0

docs.title: A real delivery: HPSDB release note 9.0
docs.text:
The release note H-P-2-ASP-LI-1441 issue 9.0 (7 April 2008, written by the Thales Alenia Space data base manager and approved by the deputy project manager) documents one delivery of the Herschel database. It went from the central site, running HPSDB 3.3.1.30, to ASED in Friedrichshafen for the Herschel IRR, as the theoretical model HERSCH_FM9 in CCS format with the "AIT User" filter, and was sent by e-mail on 9 April 2008.99101107 Its inputs came from every level of the data model: generic data, the bus profile and the OBCPs at element level, HIFI, SPIRE, PACS and the cryostat at subsystem level, and the service module and system data at model level.101

flowchart LR
  M["Theoretical model HERSCH_FM9<br/>(position 999)"]
  M --> A["109 A105 ACMS 3.7"]
  M --> D["159 D108 CDMS 3.4"]
  M --> H["289 H004 HIFI FM v11_6<br/>190 ICU, 191 FCU, 192 HRS,<br/>193 WBS, 194 LCU, 197 OBS"]
  M --> K["319 K002 Cryostat"]
  M --> P["429 P002 PACS FM 8.17<br/>380 DPU ... 420 DMC"]
  M --> R["479 R101 TTC_HER"]
  M --> S["559 S002 SPIRE FM 2.2.H1 PR<br/>500 OBS ... 525 TCV"]
  M --> W["584 W101 EPS_H"]
  M --> T["899 T101 TCS_HER"]
  M --> Y["989 Y104 EGSE<br/>940 CCS, 946 TMTCDFE, 962-966 instrument EGSEs"]

The tree redraws Figures 1 to 11 of the note.104105 The output complied with the CCS External ICD issue 1.8 and the naming convention H-P-ASPI-SP-0141 (issue printed as "02/02") and carried an MD5 checksum. The delivery was one zip file holding eight files: the release note itself, six of its reference documents and the zip generated by HPSDB, whose name follows a fixed convention:106

Part of <Area>_<Box>_<Object>_<MIB type>_<Date>[_<M>].zip Values Area R reference area, A archive area (both configured), W working area (not configured) Box TE theoretical element, TR real element, TS theoretical subsystem, TR real subsystem (as printed), TM theoretical model, RM real model Object Unique identifier of the database object MIB type C CCS MIB files, S S2K MIB files, M MCS MIB files Date Generation date as YMMDDHHMN (one digit for the year) M Optional; marks manual updates

So R_TM_HERSCH_FM9_C_804071709.zip is the reference-area theoretical model HERSCH_FM9 in CCS format, generated on 7 April 2008 at 17:09.101106 The note's change record (issues 1.0 of 10 October 2007 to 9.0) reads like the configuration log of the last year before launch: instrument EGSE data loaded only for HIFI, PACS and the EGSE; new CDMU and ACMS on-board software versions; OBCP deliveries 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11; HIFI 11.3 and 11.6, SPIRE 2.2 G7 and 2.2 H1 PR; SCO.DAT and TCD.DAT changed for the flight-model cryo SCOE; a changed TC sub-schedule; and all telecommands moved to ground low priority by default.100 Open non-conformances of the instrument EGSE delivery included files not compatible with Windows, "extra spaces on cpc.dat" and a missing tpcf.dat.102 The note's TC routing table sends APID 0 and the APIDs of the CDMS, the ACMS and the three instruments (16, 512, 1024, 1152 and 1280) to the TM/TC front end, and ten EGSE APIDs between 2017 and 2044 to their own equipment (2020 is the front end's own).103

docs.title: The HPSDB after Herschel and Planck
docs.text: At SESP 2015 Thales Alenia Space presented the System Reference Data Base (SRDB), an adaptation of HPSDB for the MTG programme. The concept was declared validated by Herschel/Planck, with one major change for MTG: an object may be attached to a former version of another object, whereas HPSDB could attach only the most recent version. New requirements such as resources, an owner flag and lists of aliases were added.148154 The slides restate the HPSDB ideas with small examples: objects and items, pseudo-items with category flags (each user category sees a consistent view of an object), physical instantiation with per-unit modification, logical instantiation of elements at positions in a subsystem, a generic object, the working, reference and archive areas, and object versioning with automatic or forced attachment.150151152 For the EGS-CC the plan was to map the high-level data model onto the EGS-CC product structure and the items and pseudo-items onto its other packages; in 2015 this was "still to be done".153154

docs.title: The HPSDB MIB releases at the Herschel Science Archive
docs.text:
The Herschel Science Archive keeps a legacy operations area for the spacecraft database. Its description page (not in this wiki's library) presents the Herschel-Planck Spacecraft Database as ASCII tables mirroring the SCOS-2000 relational database that define the telecommand and telemetry packets of the spacecraft and instruments.43 According to this wiki's source survey of 2026-11-05, the page says the MIB reached version 13 and that changes were added as new structure-ID versions so that version 13 can reprocess all mission telemetry; it gives as format references the Database Import ICD EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 issue 6.6 (2008-08-25) and the HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note HSC/DOC/0300 issue 1.9 (2007-09-14).43

The data directory lists 15 zips: MOC issues 2 to 13 from July 2009 to October 2011, about 9.5 to 12 MB each with issue 7 present three times, and one earlier and smaller zip from May 2009 (HPSDB_R_TM_HERSCH_FM1_M_903062241, 1.8 MB); the newest is HPSDB_MOC_HERSCH_CCS_issueMOC13_201110111030.zip.44

Inference

Read with the file naming convention of the 2008 release note (above), the oldest name decodes, after an HPSDB_ prefix, as R reference area, TM theoretical model, object HERSCH_FM1, M MCS MIB files (the format for the mission control system, where the 2008 note's delivery was C, CCS files), generated on 6 March 2009 at 22:41.106 The MOC issues follow a pattern that the release note does not describe: mission, the word CCS, an issue label issueMOC13 and a 12-digit timestamp, here 2011-10-11 10:30. Whether CCS there means the CCS file format, and who produced the MOC issues, is not stated in the available sources.44

Not verified by this wiki

These release facts come from directory listings recorded during the source survey, not from library copies. The zip downloads were refused (HTTP 403), so the table list, row counts and ICD compliance of the Herschel/Planck MIB are not stated in the available sources. Neither issue 6.6 of the ICD nor issue 1.9 of the HCSS note is in the library; the library has ICD issues 5.1, 6.7 draft A, 6.9 and 7.0 and HCSS note issue 1.5.

docs.title: The HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note
docs.text:
The Herschel Common Science System (HCSS) is the common software of the Herschel science ground segment. It uses MIB data to build instrument-related commands and to interpret downlinked data for clients such as Quick Look Assessment (QLA) and Interactive Analysis (IA); the MIB itself is produced by an external MIB editor and handed over as ASCII files that the HCSS MIB ingestion software validates.45 Note HSC/DOC/0300 defines that interface. The library copy is issue 1.5 (21 December 2004, prepared by H. Siddiqui, approved by the Herschel Science Centre and the PACS, HIFI and SPIRE teams); its change record runs from issue 0.1 (14 January 2003) and issue 1.5 moved the applicable ICD to 5.2 and the naming convention to 2.1.46 The note says that the ICD and the naming convention "are however found to be ambiguous in places" and therefore clarifies them, tailors them for Herschel and lists the checks.45

Clarifications of the ICD include: one line per record with OS line endings and exactly N-1 tabs for N fields (trailing grey fields may be omitted); mandatory numeric fields must not be blank; non-mandatory fields without default are empty (0, 0.0 or empty string); an out-of-limits condition is raised only strictly below the low or above the high limit; PLF_OFFBY/PLF_OFFBI count from the end of the SCOS-2000 packet header, which equals the start of the source packet when the generic packetiser is used; bit 0 of PLF_OFFBI is the most significant bit; and decimal numbers use a point.48 Three of these came with ESOC Document Change Requests: DCR 286 (an optional field may be left empty but its separator must be present), DCR 309 (the PLF_OFFBY reference point) and DCR 308 (bit 0 of PLF_OFFBI is the most significant); the note reproduces their text with the e-mail exchange between the Herschel Science Centre and the SCOS-2000 team of 5 December 2002. The note cites no DCR for the decimal-point rule.4849

Herschel constraints for the final interface include:505152

  • all ICD tables in one directory, synthetic parameter definitions in synthetic/, plus an extra two-column command durations table used by the HCSS Common Uplink System (CUS);
  • VDF ignored, constant parameters (PCF_NATUR = C) ignored;
  • a packet is identified by type, subtype, APID and SID, and a unique SPID is assumed for every packet type;
  • a PID_PI1_VAL greater than 0 is not allowed where PIC_PI1_OFF = -1;
  • every non-Z command needs at least four PCDF rows (version, type, data field header flag and APID), which contradicts the ICD statement that PCDF_TCNAME is unique;
  • CDF_CNAME plus CDF_PNAME unique (repeated groups instead of repeated names);
  • command sequences (CSF, CSS, SDF, CSP) and parameter sets (PST, PSV, CPS, PVS) ignored;
  • TXP_FROM not above TXP_TO, and no overlapping textual calibration ranges;
  • short descriptions restricted to [a-zA-Z0-9_]+, and the first character of the name plus the description unique for commands, command parameters and parameters, as is APID plus PID_DESCR.

Section 7 lists the checks, numbered 7.0.1 to 7.0.34 (7.0.6 removed), with their actions, from file names (7.0.1) to consistency of CDF_VALUE with de-calibration curves (7.0.32), CPC_RADIX (7.0.33) and a PID_INTER that must be null for every packet other than the periodic housekeeping report type 3, subtype 25 (7.0.34).53 Check 7.0.27 is worded as an error when TXP_TO is greater than TXP_FROM, the reverse of constraint 5.2.12 (the check itself cites 5.2.13); this wiki reads the constraint, not the check wording, as the intended rule.

Applying some HCSS checks to the Solar Orbiter MIB (illustrative)

The HCSS rules were Herschel-specific, so a later mission is not expected to satisfy them; running a few of them on the September 2025 Solar Orbiter release shows which are generic data-quality checks and which are project choices.42

HCSS check Solar Orbiter 2025 result 7.0.18, 7.0.20, 7.0.21: PCF_NAME, CPC_PNAME (CPC_NAME in the database), CCF_CNAME unique No duplicates 7.0.14: every PLF_SPID exists in PID Yes 5.2.6 / 7.0.12: no PID_PI1_VAL > 0 where the applicable PIC_PI1_OFF is -1 No violation (APID-specific pic rows taken first) 7.0.15: status parameters (PCF_CATEG = S) have a textual calibration 5 of 26 538 do not (for example NIM01028) 7.0.27/7.0.28: TXP_FROM ≤ TXP_TO, no overlaps 0 inverted ranges; 1 overlap, a duplicated row of calibration CYCT0002TM 5.3.1: short descriptions match [a-zA-Z0-9_]+ 68 789 of 126 745 parameter descriptions contain other characters (52 620 contain a space) SQL used (HCSS-style checks) 
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1);
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT PLF_SPID FROM plf WHERE PLF_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM pid));
SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf WHERE PCF_CATEG = 'S' AND coalesce(PCF_CURTX, '') = '';
SELECT count(*) FROM txp WHERE TXP_FROM + 0 > TXP_TO + 0;
SELECT a.*, b.* FROM txp a JOIN txp b ON a.TXP_NUMBR = b.TXP_NUMBR AND a.rowid < b.rowid
   AND a.TXP_FROM + 0 <= b.TXP_TO + 0 AND b.TXP_FROM + 0 <= a.TXP_TO + 0;
-- descriptions with a character outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _ (trim leaves a non-empty rest)
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf
 WHERE trim(PCF_DESCR, 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_') <> '';   -- 68789
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_DESCR LIKE '% %';   -- 52620
-- PIC rule: per pid row, use the APID-specific pic row if present, else the generic one
WITH eff AS (SELECT p.PID_PI1_VAL v, coalesce(
    (SELECT PIC_PI1_OFF FROM pic c WHERE c.PIC_TYPE = p.PID_TYPE AND c.PIC_STYPE = p.PID_STYPE AND c.PIC_APID = p.PID_APID),
    (SELECT PIC_PI1_OFF FROM pic c WHERE c.PIC_TYPE = p.PID_TYPE AND c.PIC_STYPE = p.PID_STYPE AND coalesce(c.PIC_APID, '') = '')) off
  FROM pid p)
SELECT count(*) FROM eff WHERE v + 0 > 0 AND off + 0 = -1;   -- 0

docs.title: The SPID uniqueness discussion (2002)
docs.text:
Constraint 5.2.5 assumed one SPID per packet type, but the PACS MIB of 2002 gave every TC verification packet SPID 10006, because the SCOS-2000 version of the time did not allow a range of SPIDs for packet type 1. The PACS team argued that this broke the ICD (a SPID must define the packet structure uniquely, and a parameter may have only one location per packet) and that SCOS-2000 abused PCF_VALID to select the location.54 ESOC's answer of 23 September 2002 confirmed the limitation - the verifier only "listens" to a predefined list of SPIDs for report-based verification - and added that Rosetta had implemented any SPID for service 1 packets and Cryosat a range of SPIDs, with integration of the useful Rosetta and Cryosat changes planned for SCOS-2000 R3.1 (reading all service-1 SPIDs from pid.dat).54

The restriction has left no trace in the Solar Orbiter MIB of 2025: its 1 809 service-1 packet definitions on 31 APIDs (29 for each subtype) all have different SPIDs, one for each acceptance or completion success report and one for each failure code of TM(1,2) and TM(1,8), selected by a 16-bit identification field at offset 20.42 See command verification in the MIB for how those SPIDs are used today.

SQL used (service 1 SPIDs in the Solar Orbiter MIB) 
SELECT PID_STYPE, count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_SPID), count(DISTINCT PID_APID)
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' GROUP BY 1;   -- 1: 29/29/29, 2: 274/274/29, 7: 29/29/29, 8: 1477/1477/29
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_SPID), count(DISTINCT PID_APID)
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1';               -- 1809 | 1809 | 31
SELECT * FROM pic WHERE PIC_TYPE = '1';       -- subtypes 2 and 8: PI1 at offset 20, width 16

docs.title: The ACMS operations database (NLR-TP-2007-240)
docs.text:
The NLR report Turning requirements into operations - Herschel/Planck ACMS Database Experience (April 2007, based on SpaceOps 2006 paper AIAA-2006-590) is a first-hand account of how a subsystem team produced MIB data for both satellites.1 The relevant PUS services for ACMS operations were service 3 (generated by the basic software from a datapool of ASW and BSW parameters), service 5 and service 8 (most ACMS-specific commands).4 The ASW held an on-board database (OBDB) of more than 3 000 parameters. Because service 3 can only report datapool parameters, every parameter of interest had to be in the datapool; a later interface let the ASW define its own 16/32/64-bit datapool entries and identifiers (DIDs).4

A dedicated database was not planned at first. It became necessary in phase B because the Word telemetry document could not be kept consistent by hand, the interface was larger than for other Dutch Space subsystems, SCOS-2000 in the ACMS test equipment needed every TM/TC detail including operational identifiers, and the HPSDB was not yet mature enough to rely on.5 The team built it in the DOORS requirements tool, with formal modules for parameters, parameter types (with their PTC/PFC), units (with HPSDB and SCOS-2000 representations of at most four characters), enumerations, conversions, command characteristics, TC and TM packet structures, packet identification criteria, packet identifiers, alphanumeric displays, HPSDB boxes and a change log.8 The off-the-shelf SCOS-2000 MS Access database was rejected because it served one mission only, had no object-level configuration control and could not link ASW data to the ASW specification.7

Each object carries spacecraft (Herschel, Planck or common), software (ASW or BSW) and first/last version attributes, so that version-specific SCOS-2000 and HPSDB files are generated from one CSV export; exports are kept under CVS instead of DOORS baselines, and a ccsdiff script compares the .dat files generated by HPSDB with those used in ACMS AIT. GMV provided the tool that converts the ACMS XML into HPSDB XML.9 The report's five recommendations - integrate the database with specifications and ICDs, use database identifiers in tests, keep TM/TC identifiers independent between requirements, software, test and operations but traceable, version every object, and use inheritance and instantiation - end with a call to standardise the database design for all space programmes.10

Inference

Relating that call to the standardised monitoring and control data definitions of ECSS-E-ST-70-31C and to the EGS-CC tailoring data model (see Ancillary systems and EGS-CC) is this wiki's reading; the NLR report does not name either.

flowchart LR
  DOORS[("ACMS Operations Database<br/>(DOORS)")] -- "CSV/XML export<br/>per version" --> GEN["generation scripts"]
  GEN --> S2K["SCOS-2000 / HPCCS .dat files<br/>(ACMS AIT)"]
  GEN --> ASW["ASW datapool + OBDB<br/>(Terma)"]
  GEN --> TCL["Tcl code for test scripts"]
  GEN --> AX["ACMS XML"] --> GMV["GMV tool"] --> HP[("HPSDB")]
  HP -- "HPSDB export" --> S2K2["SCOS-2000 .dat files<br/>generated by HPSDB"]
  S2K2 -- "ccsdiff" --- S2K

docs.title: Planck LFI: SCOS-2000 inside an instrument ground segment
docs.text: The paper Level 1 on-ground telemetry handling in Planck LFI (Zacchei et al., JINST 4 T12019, 2009; arXiv:1001.4730) describes the first processing level of the Low Frequency Instrument's Data Processing Centre (DPC). The Planck science ground segment consists of the LFI and HFI DPCs, the MOC and the Planck Science Office; Level 1 takes raw telemetry compliant with the ESA packet telemetry standard and the PUS and produces Time Ordered Information (TOI) per housekeeping and science parameter.55

docs.title: What the instrument sends
docs.text:
LFI has 22 radiometers behind 11 feed horns at 30, 44 and 70 GHz; each radiometer gives two outputs, so there are 44 science channels. A 14-bit ADC in the Data Acquisition Electronics digitises each output, and the Radiometer Electronics Box Assembly (REBA) runs the on-board software, builds the HK and science packets and executes telecommands.56 To stay within 53.5 kbps the REBA offers seven processing types: PType 0 raw samples, 1 co-added samples, 2 and 3 mixing with gain modulation factors and requantisation to 16-bit integers, and 4 to 6 lossless adaptive arithmetic compression of types 0, 2 and 3. Nominally all 44 detectors use PType 5, and every 15 minutes one detector is additionally processed in PType 1 for calibration.5657

Packets follow the ESA packet telemetry and telecommand standards, the CCSDS packet telemetry recommendations and the PUS: a primary header (type, APID, sequence counter modulo 16384, length), a fixed secondary header (service type, subtype and a 48-bit CUC on-board time), a Structure ID, a data segment and a 16-bit CRC; science packets add a tertiary header with detector, phase-switch status, processing type, REBA parameters and number of samples.58 The four fields APID, type, subtype and SID identify the structure of a packet for the ground software, and the mission defined custom services for science telemetry.58

Part Content Source Primary header Packet type, APID, sequence count (modulo 16384), packet length 58 Secondary header Service type and subtype; on-board time as 48-bit CUC 58 SID Structure identifier; with APID, type and subtype it selects the layout 58 Tertiary header (science only) Detector ID, phase switch status, processing type, REBA parameters, number of samples 59 Data segment Science: up to 980 bytes; HK: parameter fields per the PUS parameter types 5960 CRC 16 bits, specified in the PUS 58

Housekeeping is periodic (essential every 32 s, for low-gain-antenna periods; fast every 1 s, with some packets super-commutated into four identical sub-fields so that a packet comes every 4 s; slow every 64 s) or non-periodic (command responses, events and alarms).60 The paper notes that the MIB's PLF table gives, besides the offset, the number of occurrences of a parameter in super-commutated packets, the field PLF_NBOCC; that the sub-field spacing goes into PLF_LGOCC follows from the ICD field definitions rather than from the paper.6240

docs.title: The Level 1 architecture
docs.text:
Level 1 has three subsystems: a Real-Time Assessment system (RTA) based on SCOS-2000; a Telemetry Handler (TMH) built largely by the ISDC team in Geneva by reusing software from the INTEGRAL ground segment; and a Telemetry Quick-Look system (TQL) built on ROOT.61 SCOS-2000 receives the telemetry, maintains a local raw packet archive, checks for missing, damaged or duplicated packets, displays calibrated HK, sends telecommands and raises out-of-limits alarms; it could not process the compressed science telemetry, which is why it served mainly as EGSE and HK monitor.62

Configuring SCOS-2000 for LFI meant writing the MIB: the paper names PID (APID, type, subtype and SID as the packet's "primary key"), PCF (parameter ID, description, type and calibration reference) and PLF (parameter offset and number of occurrences for super-commutated packets), plus out-of-limits values with validity criteria for different test conditions (e.g. warm or cryogenic), conditional calibrations and displays.62 The TMH then reads the same MIB files to extract and calibrate HK parameters, so one database serves both the SCOS-2000 displays and the scientific pipeline.63

flowchart LR
  REBA["LFI REBA<br/>HK + science packets"] --> S2K["SCOS-2000 (EGSE / RTA)<br/>PDS, HFA, displays, OOL"]
  S2K -- "FDIF client task (SCOS 2.3e)" --> TMH
  REBA -.->|integration tests - HPCCS| HPCCS["HPCCS"]
  HPCCS -- "PIPE protocol" --> GW["LFIGateway"]
  GW --> TMH["TMH pipeline<br/>Data Receive -> TMU -> TM2TOI"]
  GW --> HPCCS2["LFI HPCCS client"]
  TMH --> TQL["TQL quick-look<br/>(ROOT)"]
  TMH --> TOI[("TOI archive<br/>FITS, 1-hour chunks")]
  MIB[("MIB ASCII tables")] --> S2K
  MIB --> TMH

The tailoring followed the SCOS-2000 releases. For instrument-only tests the EGSE ran SCOS 2.3e; its telemetry receiver was modified to replay simulated LFI data, and a task using the Flight Dynamics Interface (FDIF) let the TMH register as a SCOS client and receive live packets. From the Planck integration tests onward the EGSE was the HPCCS, which talks to external equipment through the Packet Interface Protocol for EGSE (PIPE); a new LFIGateway relayed telemetry from the HPCCS operated by the spacecraft team to the LFI team's own HPCCS and TMH/TQL.62 The PIPE format is defined in the prime's EGSE Interface Requirement Specification (H-P-1-ASPI-IS-0121, issue 4.1, 14 December 2004): every message starts with a 10-byte header (message ID, virtual channel ID, remaining length, a 4-byte request ID and the synchronisation word 0xFADE) followed by a body, which for spacecraft telecommands and telemetry is the TC packet or the TM source packet, embedded unchanged,158 and the CCS distributes telemetry to the instrument stations on their own LAN with message ID 0x20; the LFI EGSE was the station with APID 2041.135137138140 The protocol is described on SCOS-2000 as EGSE and field by field on the interface documents page.

The TMH pipeline has three parts: Data Receive stores raw packets in a FITS archive and forwards them to TQL; the TeleMetry Unscrambler (TMU) groups HK packets by APID, type, subtype and SID and science packets by detector and processing type, into hour-long FITS files of an intermediate archive; and TM2TOI produces the final TOI archive, one FITS file per HK parameter, with raw and calibrated values and quality flags.63 Science samples are then decompressed, dequantised, demixed and converted from ADU to volts using parameters from the tertiary header and from HK telemetry, and each sample's time is rebuilt from the packet time, the sample index and the sampling frequency.64

docs.title: Instrument EGSE: from the 2000 decision to SCOS EGSE 2.3e P5
docs.text:
The decision. At an ESOC meeting on 19 April 2000 with all FIRST/Planck instrument teams, ESA confirmed SCOS-2000 as the baseline for MOC operations and stated that it would support the product for flight operations and EGSE; the minutes record that "All PI groups unanimously stated their intention to use SCOS 200 as a basis for EGSE and RTA" (sic).6566 The PROBA experience (SCOS 2 with an ORACLE database, a Delphi router and Tcl/Tk procedures) was presented as the model, and the database question was left to the prime contractor, with ORACLE, MS Access (the Integral tool) or custom solutions as options.65 The SCOS-2000 presentation of 18 April 2000 proposed reusing PROBA's router and Tcl/Tk procedure tool with MS Access database editors from Integral.67 The full story is on Herschel/Planck: SCOS-2000 in a science mission ground segment and SCOS-2000 as EGSE.

The building blocks. The Herschel EGSE integration plan (SRON-U/HIFI/PL/2001-1, issue 1, 6 November 2001) lists who delivered each block of the common instrument-level test EGSE (EGSE-ILT) of HIFI, PACS and SPIRE: SCOS-2000, the OBSM and the MIB editor from ESA, the SCOS gateway from ESTEC, the test-equipment interface and TM/TC router from HIFI, test control from PACS and the CDMS simulator from SPIRE; each of the router, test-equipment interface, CDMS-simulator and test-control tests loads a test MIB into SCOS-2000 as its second step, right after connecting the subsystems.68

The router. The HIFI team's Herschel EGSE Packet Router ICD (SRON-G/HIFI/ICD/2001-001, issue 1.1, 23 October 2001), agreed by the EGSE and ICC managers of the three instruments and the HSC, specifies the Java router that linked SCOS-2000, the test equipment interfaces, the HCSS telemetry ingester and the CDMS simulator during instrument level tests. Clients open a TCP connection, name themselves and subscribe to packet addresses: the APID for telemetry, 4096 plus the APID for telecommands. Every message has a 5-octet header (a message type from 1 to 12 and a 4-octet content length), and the same interface was to deliver raw telemetry to the HCSS in later phases.143144146147 The router has no security, handshake or flow control of its own; details are on SCOS-2000 as EGSE.145

The kernel. ESA's EGSE based on SCOS 2000 - The EGSE & Mission Control System (TOS-EMG/01-1029, issue 4.0, 2004-03-09) is the user manual of the "SCOS EGSE Release 2.3e P5" delivered to the Herschel/Planck instrument developers. It explains that the EMCS follows the PROBA approach with SCOS-2000 in place of SCOS 2, adds a Test and Operations Procedure Environment (TOPE) in Tcl/Tk pending the ECSS PLUTO language (ECSS-E-ST-70-32C), and introduces a Space System Model in which every addressable system element has a 16-bit identifier: 0x0000-0x07FF are on-board application processes (the APIDs), 0x0800 is the spacecraft identifier entry in the MIB, and higher ranges are reserved for SCOS tasks, front ends and EGSE routers.7172 Its change log records Herschel-specific additions such as the Herschel/Planck TC history/OOL server, a configurable mission epoch and a time-tagging mode for the Herschel instrument OBT scenario.73 For Herschel, SRON developed a Linux-based EGSE router instead of the Windows router used on PROBA.74

The system level. Alcatel's EGSE General Requirements Specification (H-P-1-ASPI-SP-0045, issue 03, 10/06/02) records the baseline that instrument EGSEs and the ESOC flight control system are both based on SCOS-2000, so that instrument station software, test procedures and OBCPs move from instrument tests through system tests to commissioning with minimal change. It requires a Central Checkout System (with a one-server "CCS lite" for PLM and instrument EGSE) with standard interfaces for on-line and off-line data distribution to instrument EGSE, pre-transmission checks against the Satellite Database, and support of an HPSDB mirror site.6970 Its companion, the EGSE Interface Requirement Specification, defines the PIPE protocol on two LANs (SCOE/DFE and instrument stations), fixes the APIDs, host names and naming-convention positions of every EGSE item, and asks each SCOE subcontractor to supply its remote command and monitoring definitions in a format that can be loaded into the HPSDB.136140141139 Terma's CCS External ICD lists the checkout system's four external interfaces: the two PIPE LANs, a web station, and the HPSDB, which sends bridge files (the MIB) and receives update files naming every telecommand and parameter that a test sequence has validated.133134 ESA's 2003 list of SCOS-2000 clients counts both the Herschel/Planck CCS (on Red Hat 7.2) and the Herschel/Planck instrument EGSE (on SUSE 7.3), next to the Herschel/Planck MCS.76 An ESA Bulletin article of 2007 notes that common tools for spacecraft checkout and operations preparation, promoting a seamless transition from manufacture to operations, "was exploited recently by Herschel and Planck".77
