docs.text: Item Value Source CCSDS spacecraft identifier 0x28A (650), the same for TM and TC, for the flight model, the ETB and the OBC-DM 1821 Packet standard ECSS-E-70-41A (PUS-A, 2003), applicable document AD1 12 TC packet data field at most 242 octets: 4 data field header + 236 application data + 2 packet error control 14 TM source packet at most 4112 octets; data field at most 4106 octets (10 header + 4096 source data) 1920 TM transfer frame fixed length of 1115 octets (8920 bits), CLCW in every frame, 4-octet frame secondary header 21 TC transfer frame at most 256 octets; two virtual channels (VC1, VC2) addressing the two on-board decoders 18 Packet time stamp CUC with 4 octets of coarse and 2 octets of fine time 20 MCS mission identifier 650 in the SCOS-2000 packet header 41 Ground station IDs in the archive 21 Kourou, 22 Perth, 23 New Norcia, 24 Cebreros, 25 Malargüe, 30 Maspalomas; 201 reference test station (ESOC), 202 NDIU Lite, 203 NDIU IFMS 41 Latest MIB release copied MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (VDF 25925PFM, comment 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33) 64 Instrument to platform data link SpaceWire (ECSS-E-50-12), two independent links per instrument routed separately, SpaceWire time codes received by every instrument (EID-A, 2007) 75 Instrument databases copied SWA 6.3.4 and 6.5.0 (IRAP), STIX 2.26.38 6791

docs.title: Who does what: the ground segment
docs.text:
The documents name three groups of actors. The Operational Ground Segment (OGS) at ESOC runs the MCS, its long-term archive (LTA) and the Data Dissemination System (DDS). The Science Ground Segment (SGS) with the SOC at ESAC plans science operations. The instrument teams, led by Principal Investigators (PIs), design their instrument operations and need their data back.301 The DDS gives the SGS and the PIs controlled access to the archive, while a second, push-based path forwards every archived packet to the SGS as RAPID files.31 In the other direction, the SOC turns the MOC's planning products into a planning skeleton for the instrument teams, the E-FECS, and collects their Instrument Operations Requests (IORs), which it forwards to the MOC as Payload Operations Requests (PORs).21

The split goes back to the instrument requirements of 2007. Issue 1 of the Experiment Interface Document Part A (EID-A) already placed the MOC and the communications infrastructure under ESA/ESOC, archived housekeeping and raw payload data at the MOC, and had the SOC generate the payload operations requests that the MOC implements and distribute the data to the PIs. It listed the MOC tasks relevant to science: overall mission planning, supplying each PI in near real time with the raw data of their instrument plus spacecraft housekeeping and auxiliary data, giving the SOC a subset, checking a set of payload parameters for out-of-limit values in near real time, and notifying payload anomalies.72 Its baseline ground station was New Norcia, with Cebreros as backup;73 the DDID of 2019 lists six ESA stations (see the table above).41

flowchart LR
  SC["Solar Orbiter<br/>OBC, SSMM, 10 instruments, STR"] -- "TM frames<br/>1115 octets" --> GS["ESA ground stations<br/>(IDs 21-25, 30)"]
  GS -- "TC frames / CLTUs" --> SC
  GS <--> MCS["MOC at ESOC<br/>SCOS-2000 based MCS"]
  MCS --> LTA[("MCS long-term archive<br/>PARC, DARC, FARC")]
  LTA --> DDS["DDS = EDDS<br/>(relay LAN)"]
  LTA -- "RAPID files via GFTS<br/>(nominal OGS to SGS path)" --> SGS["SGS / SOC at ESAC"]
  DDS -- "batch and stream requests<br/>HTTPS, SFTP" --> SGS
  DDS --> PI["Instrument teams / PIs"]
  MCS -- "FECS, PTEL<br/>(MOC planning inputs)" --> SGS
  SGS -- "E-FECS via GFTS" --> PI
  PI -- "IORs" --> SGS
  SGS -- "PORs" --> MCS

The diagram combines the data flows of the DDID and the planning relationships of the E-FECS ICD.31362 The data flows are covered on the EDDS, mission archives and GDDS and DDIDs pages; the ground station gateway is on NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface.

docs.title: The space-ground interface: SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079
docs.text:
What it is. SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7 is the Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure Interface Control Document, written by the prime contractor Airbus Defence and Space Ltd (copyright 2014) in response to ESA's Statement of Work and Operations Interface Requirements Document (OIRD), on the basis of ESA's Solar Orbiter Generic Frame and Packet Structure (SO-ESC-RS-05002).1012 It is the baseline definition of all application-level data structures exchanged between the on-board computer, the solid-state mass memory, the 10 payload instruments and the star trackers, and of the same structures in their ground peer entities.10 It was exported from the PUS module of the prime's DOORS requirements database, which is why the text carries object identifiers such as PUS-31.11 Its 396 pages cover the TC and TM packet and frame layers (chapters 3 and 4), every tailored PUS service (chapter 5) and annexes on time and idle packets, the CRC, APID and source/destination allocation, failure and event identifiers, housekeeping structure identifiers and the on-board parameter identifier.13

Its rules on PUS are strict: changing the definition of a standard service, or using it in a non-standard way, is forbidden; any user-specific packet must be defined as a private service in a range assigned to the user, and private services are documented in each unit's own TM/TC ICD rather than here.10 The services themselves are analysed on How Solar Orbiter uses PUS.

docs.title: Application process identifiers
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter gives structure to the 11-bit APID: its 7 most significant bits are a process ID (PID) that names the on-board application, and its 4 least significant bits are a packet category (CAT). For telecommands the category is always 12; for telemetry it says what kind of packet the process is emitting.1419

CAT TM meaning (Annex 8) 0 Time packet, service 9 only 1 TC verification, service 1 only 2 High Priority TM (HPTM) housekeeping, platform only 3 Table generation: variable-length tabular reports 4 Routine, cyclic HK, TM(3,25) of the default service 3 5 Functional cyclic: private TM(3,25) produced on ground request 6 Functional non-cyclic: private report packets on ground request 7 Events: service 5 and TM(17,2) 8 Diagnostic: TM(3,26) or private diagnostic packets 9 Memory dump, service 6 only 10 File transfer, service 13 only 11 Context, service 22 only 12 Private science (service 21) for TM; all telecommands 13 / 14 / 15 Spare / reserved for OCC and EGSE / idle packets

The category table and the process ID table are Figures 13.1-1 and 13.1-2 of the ICD.26 The process IDs are allocated as follows: 0 time; 2 the OBC hardware (CPDU high-priority commands, HPTM); 10 to 16 the Central Software (CSW) applications - 10 data management, 11 AOCS, 12 payload, 13 platform, 14 system control, 15 OBCP, 16 thermal; 30 to 32 the SSMM; 40 and 41 star trackers A and B; 49 payload broadcast; then instrument ranges EPD 50-56 and 100, EUI 57-62, MAG 63-66, METIS 67-71, PHI 72-74, RPW 75-81, SOLOHI 82-84, SPICE 85-89 and 101-104, STIX 90-94, SWA 95-99; 112 to 127 EGSE.26 For example the AOCS application (PID 11) sends its events on APID 11 × 16 + 7 = 183, and every command for it goes to APID 11 × 16 + 12 = 188; both appear in the real MIB (see the APID catalogue).64

docs.title: Telecommand path
docs.text:
A TC packet carries the PUS-A data field header with PUS version 1, the acknowledgement flags (only acceptance and completion are used), service type, subtype and an 8-bit source ID. The sequence count is kept per APID and source ID but is not checked on board, and the packet is protected by a 16-bit CRC.141564 The bit-level layout and the way SCOS-2000 builds it from the MIB are on PUS packet structures. Reserved ground source IDs distinguish the mission timeline (110), TC sequences (111), recovery actions (112), the back-up mission timeline (113) and direct commands (120); the CSW uses 11 (AOCS), 14 (system control) and 15 (OBCP) for commands it generates itself.27

Packets travel in TC segments whose header carries 2 sequence flags, always 0b11 because Solar Orbiter never segments packets, and a 6-bit MAP ID: 0 for CPDU commands, TC(2,3), and 1 for all other commands.16 To raise the uplink throughput, several complete packets are aggregated in one segment; each packet's start is found from the length of the previous one.17 In the MIB, the MAP ID 0 path is used by the 125 HPC-1 commands: they have the header HPC1_TC without a secondary header, go to APID 44 (process 2, category 12) and are flagged high priority (CCF_HIPRI = Y) with CCF_MAPID = 0, the field that SCOS-2000 uses to force the MAP ID of high-priority commands. The TC(2,3) commands, which the ICD's MAP ID text names as the CPDU commands, are in the MIB ordinary PUS commands to the CSW on APID 172, mostly named "HPC-3 ..." (see service 2).6466

The CPDU (Command Pulse Distribution Unit) inside the OBC can switch vital units on and off without the CSW. Commands sent to it from the ground are HPC-1 commands; the reconfiguration module can use the same lines (HPC-2), and the CSW can write CPDU registers to produce the same pulses (HPC-3).16 The segment is the data field of a TC transfer frame (CCSDS 232.0) with version 0b00, the usual bypass and control command flags giving AD, BD and BC frames under COP-1, spacecraft ID 650 and a maximum length of 256 octets, so that only the low 8 bits of the 10-bit frame length field are ever used.18 The frames are then encoded into CLTUs (see TC synchronization and channel coding); the ICD lists ECSS-E-ST-50-04C as a reference for this layer.12

flowchart LR
  P["TC packet<br/>APID = PID x 16 + 12<br/>data field max 242 octets"] --> S["TC segment<br/>flags 11, MAP 0 or 1<br/>(aggregated packets)"]
  S --> F["TC frame<br/>SCID 650, VC 1 or 2<br/>max 256 octets"]
  F --> C["CLTU<br/>(ground station)"]
  C --> D["On-board decoder 1 or 2"]
  D -- "MAP 1" --> CSW["CSW / destination APID"]
  D -- "MAP 0" --> CPDU["CPDU<br/>HPC-1 pulse commands"]

docs.title: Telemetry path
docs.text:
All on-board TM uses packet version 0b000; the data field header flag is 1 except in the standard time packet. APID 0 is reserved for the time packet and APID 2047 (all ones) for idle packets.19 The grouping flags may mark the first, continuation and last packets of a multi-packet answer (memory dumps, report of service definitions) but each packet stays a self-standing PUS packet; the source sequence count is kept per APID and destination ID and the ground must alarm on every discontinuity.19 The 10-octet data field header holds the PUS version (1), service type and subtype, the destination ID and a 6-octet CUC time; its exact octet layout is a figure without text in the ICD and is reconstructed on PUS packet structures.20 The destination ID is the command's source ID copied back for solicited TM, the receiving process for packets meant for another on-board process, and 0b00000000 (ground) otherwise, always for categories 2, 3, 4, 8 and 9; the time packet has no data field header and therefore no destination ID.28

Packets are carried in TM transfer frames of exactly 1115 octets (CCSDS 132.0): version 0b00, spacecraft ID 650, an operational control field with a CLCW in every frame, a frame secondary header in every frame, a synchronisation flag of 0 with packet order flag 0 and segment length identifier 0b11, and a first header pointer of all ones when no packet starts in the frame, or 0b11111111110 in idle frames on VC7. A frame error control word is present in every frame.21 Packets longer than the 1099-octet frame data field are spread over several frames.19

Priority Virtual channel Content Sent when ready and none available on 1 VC4 Real-time high-priority TM - 2 VC0 Real-time TM, and the time packet when due VC4 3 VC5 Critical event log (playback) VC4, VC0 4 VC1 Playback from the OBC mass memory VC4, VC0, VC5 5 VC2 Playback from the SSMM VC4, VC0, VC5, VC1 6 VC3 Playback from the SSMM VC4, VC0, VC5, VC1, VC2 7 VC7 Idle frames only all of the above

The priority scheme is from §4.3 of the ICD. The ICD lists VC5 before VC0, but its conditions ("when ready and no VC4 or VC0 available" for VC5, "no VC4 available" for VC0) put VC0 above VC5, which is the order used in the table. Only VC2 and VC3 may carry compressed packets; VC0, VC1, VC4 and VC5 never do.22 On the ground, the MCS stream identifiers 1000 to 1003 correspond to the on-line VC0 (real-time non-science), VC1 (playback non-science), VC2 (science) and VC3 (file transfer), which suggests how the VCs are used in flight.41

docs.title: Time, idle packets and the CRC
docs.text:
The standard spacecraft time packet has APID 0, no data field header and 8 octets of data. Its time refers to the leading edge of the first bit of the attached synchronisation marker of the VC0 frame whose virtual channel frame count is 0; ground uses it to correlate on-board time with UTC.23 See Time correlation in SCOS-2000 and CCSDS time codes.

Idle packets have APID 2047, no data field header and random filler data.24 The packet error control uses the CCITT polynomial \(x^{16}+x^{12}+x^5+1\) with the register preset to all ones, computed over the whole packet except the CRC itself. The ICD gives test vectors, for example 00 00 gives 0x1D0F and AB CD EF 01 gives 0x04A2 (real values from the source).25

docs.title: Data delivery: the DDID and the EDDS
docs.text: What it is. The Solar Orbiter Data Delivery Interface Control Document (DDID), SOL-ESC-IF-05011 issue 1 revision 2 of 26 June 2019, prepared by the Solar Orbiter data systems manager's team in ESA's operations directorate (OPS-GDS), is the mission-specific complement to the generic EDDS External User ICD (EGOS-GEN-EDDS-ICD-1001); the two are meant to be read together.29 It specifies the request and delivery mechanisms and the data products of the Solar Orbiter DDS, which is an instance of the generic EGOS Data Dissemination System, for all mission phases.29

docs.title: Services and access control
docs.text:
The DDS offers an HTTPS web interface and an EDDS client application for requesting TM packets and parameters, TC history, spacecraft and MCS events, auxiliary files and catalogue information. Requests are XML documents, either batch requests that return a complete data set as a file, or stream requests for near-real-time data; they can be saved, scheduled, or dropped as XML files on the server via SFTP. Responses are pushed to the user's SFTP server or kept for download.3137 Users can also subscribe to auxiliary files as they arrive in the file archive.31 The DDS server runs in cold redundancy - only one of the prime and backup servers is up at a time, and a switch-over needs the user to point the client at the other machine - with an availability requirement of at least 95% over a month.3335

Each account can be restricted by APID, SPID, parameter name, file name or file type, by data volume over a period, by a relative time range (for example only the last 12 months) and by an access period; accounts may create sub-users within their own rights.323851 During cruise, most users were expected to fetch only their own payload data plus some housekeeping, while near the Sun the SGS would retrieve the full data set and redistribute it.38

docs.title: Where the data come from
docs.text:
The DDS reads the MCS long-term archive: packets, events and TC data from the packet archive (PARC), auxiliary files and TM files from the file archive (FARC), and parameters from the parameter archive (DARC). Spacecraft TM is available as soon as it is stored, normally within seconds of reception at the ground station.36 See Mission archives: PARC, DARC and FARC.

Data type Archive Notes TM, TC and event packets, packet statistics PARC includes MCS-generated packets such as time correlation packets TM parameters, parameter statistics DARC Command history, TM gap and other reports PARC Auxiliary files, TM files, archive catalogues FARC

The table condenses §6.2 of the DDID.37 Among the auxiliary file types is the MIB itself (archive file type MIB), alongside flight dynamics products (attitude, orbit, events, one-way light time, HGA blockage) and planning files.49

docs.title: The SCOS-2000 packet as delivered
docs.text:
Raw packet requests return the SCOS-2000 packet (also called the TDEV packet): a common header, a TM-, TC- or event-specific header, then the packet data. For spacecraft TM the packet data is the complete, unstripped source packet starting with the CCSDS version number; all DDS data are big-endian and times are 4 octets of seconds since 1 January 1970 (leap seconds not counted) plus 4 octets of microseconds.3940 The EDDS request and data formats page covers the generic formats; the Solar Orbiter values are these:

The field list and values are from §7.1.1 of the DDID.41 Two fields tie every archived packet to a MIB release: the filing key is the SPID and DB Rel / DB Iss record the VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE of the vdf table in force when the packet was archived.41 For the September 2025 MIB those are 25925 and 733.64

The TM header and the RouteID codes are from §7.1.2.42 The TC header instead holds the uplink, execution and last-update times, MCS request identifiers, the PUS APID, sequence count, type, subtype and acknowledgement flags, an uplink flag that records whether the command passed pre-transmission verification (PTV), and the command source; its "command details" body is produced by overlaying a C++ class on 32-bit aligned memory, so fields are padded to 32-bit boundaries.4344 The MCS also archives, for each command, a second TC packet with SPID 200 holding its static PTV and verification details from the MIB; external users ignore it. Released commands are filed with SPID 100.4041

Inference

The common header adds up to 480 bits (60 octets) and the TM header to 128 bits (16 octets), 76 octets in all. The SCOS-2000 ICD gives 76 octets as the TM packet header size of SCOS-2000 packet header version 4,65 while the DDID states version 5 for Solar Orbiter. The equality of the sizes is this wiki's arithmetic; whether version 5 has the same size is not stated in the available sources.

When frames are missing while the MCS assembles a long packet, it files the part built so far as a "bad" source packet (data unit type 1, qualifier 1) and the following frames as individual good frames, so users can still recover the data.45

docs.title: Internal packets and time correlation
docs.text:
The archive also contains MCS-internal packets on APID 1966, which external users filter out, except the time correlation packets:4647

SPID Type, subtype Content 66810 - File transfer model meta-data 66980 / 66981 / 66982 - Good / bad / idle mini transfer frame 66983, 66985, 66999 - Bad TM packets, missing packet detection, TM packet with no assigned SPID 66830, 66831, 66832 - Dynamic UDCs, TC Spacon and MISC configuration packets 66840 (164,1) Time correlation report 66841 (164,2) Time couple (OBT of a time packet with its ground times) 66842 (164,3) Time correlation coefficients 66850 - Releaser TM packet including ground station response

The real MIB defines all 14 of these on APID 1966 with private types 160, 161, 162, 164 and 165 (type 164 for the three time correlation packets), plus four packets the DDID does not list: three "MATIS" packets of type 166 (SPIDs 101-103) and "Saved Synthetics" (SPID 66838, type 251) - 18 in all (see explorer: APID 1966).64

docs.title: TM files, the command history and RAPID files
docs.text:
Telemetry downlinked through Solar Orbiter's service 13 file transfer arrives as TM files: plain concatenations of TM packets, stored in the FARC as file type "DLPP Files" and named <PS_ID>_<file_reconstruction_timestamp>, for example 13_2014.336.13.54.07.057. Their transaction history is recorded in event packets with SPID 4000 (transaction ID, packet store ID, status, FDUs received and expected, retransmissions, times, file name, injection kind and time).50 The command history report carries additional "Science Kernel" custom fields (in the XML response, CustomField elements with name, type and value), among them the service 13 file ID and file attribute (PLAIN, OBCP, TC_DELAYED, TC_IMMEDIATE or PAYLOAD_CONTEXT) of commands uplinked inside files.48

The nominal OGS-to-SGS path is not the DDS but RAPID (Raw Archive Packet Interceptor Dumper) files: the MCS writes every SCOS-2000 packet it archives into one of three open files (TM, TC, events), closes them every 50 seconds and lets the Generic File Transfer System (GFTS) forward them to the SGS: one GFTS instance moves them from the MCS long-term archive across the operational LAN (OPSLAN) firewall to the DDS server on the relay LAN, and a second one across the ESOC corporate firewall and the SGS firewall. Packets appear in reception order, so re-dumped or recalled data arrive out of generation order, and a TC packet is re-sent whole every time its verification status changes. Two weeks of RAPID files are kept for recovery.5234 Files are named PARC_<Type>_<FirstPacketTime>__<LastPacketTime>.53

RAPID record field Octets Meaning ID 8 Record structure version, 1 ST, ET 8 + 8 First and last time of a delete range (not used) AT 8 Action time: microseconds since 1970 when the packet was inserted or updated DS 8 Size of the packet field TYPE 4 0 insert, 1 update (a TC packet), 2 delete (ignored) SM 4 Sync marker 0x1ACFFC1D NS, FS, FIL 4 + 4 + 0 Unused, filter size (0), filter (absent) PACKET DS The SCOS-2000 packet

Each record is preceded by a 32-bit length.53 The sync marker has the same value as the CCSDS attached sync marker of TM frames (see TM coding).

docs.title: The EDDS/DDID training presentation
docs.text: EDDS / DDID - Presentation & Demo is an 80-slide ESA training deck first given on 28 September 2017 by the BepiColombo mission data systems manager and the EDDS technical officer, updated for Solar Orbiter in January 2019; its file name gives the reference SOL-ESC-PRS-22100 issue 1 revision 0 of 2019-01-30, which is not printed on the slides.54 It explains to external users how the DDID complements the EDDS External User ICD (then issue 15.0 of February 2018), that EDDS gives controlled access to mission data for users without MCS access by reading PARC, DARC, FARC and the file system, and that it keeps the interfaces of its predecessors GDDS and TDRS.5556 The deck still gives the DDID reference as BC-ESC-IF-05011, issue 1.0 of 2013-09-10, with issue 1.2 expected in mid-2019; the issue in the library is SOL-ESC-IF-05011 issue 1 revision 2 of 26 June 2019.5529 It also stresses what EDDS is not: a data warehouse or an analysis tool.57 See TDRS and GDDS.

docs.title: Planning: the E-FECS ICD
docs.text:
What it is. SOL-SGS-ICD-0006 issue 3.0 (5 October 2021), issued at ESAC, defines the E-FECS (Enhanced Flight Events and Communication Skeleton), the XML "planning skeleton" through which the SOC tells the instrument teams the global planning constraints before they prepare their IORs in short-term planning (STP).21 The MOC provides the FECS (from its flight control team) and the PTEL (from flight dynamics); after long-term planning (LTP) the SOC produces the E-FECS, mostly by adding windows to those inputs. It is used in cruise and in the nominal and extended mission phases.2

flowchart LR
  MOC["MOC<br/>FECS (FCT) + PTEL (FD)"] --> LTP["SOC long-term planning<br/>(~6 months)"]
  LTP --> EF["E-FECS<br/>EFECS_Mnn_Vvv.xml<br/>delivered at T-20 weeks"]
  EF --> IT["Instrument teams<br/>short-term planning (~1 week)"]
  IT -- "IORs" --> SOC["SOC"]
  SOC -- "PORs" --> MOC2["MOC<br/>commanding"]

The flow follows §1 and §3 of the ICD.238 Several of its rules touch TM/TC directly:

  • Time format. Every event time uses the CCSDS ASCII time code B day-of-year form YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ssZ, with no sub-seconds and a mandatory Z; because the legacy planning systems ignore leap seconds, a window containing one may last a second longer.4 See CCSDS time codes.
  • Passes. Any low-latency data written to SpaceWire before the start of a PASS event is downlinked in that pass (special cases aside). Pass events carry the station, the frame-level downlink rate, the modulation, whether ranging is on, and a "MIB code" for the transponder configuration.5 The transponder's parameters and commands in the MIB are described on RF and ranging.
  • Routing maintenance. During ENG_WIN windows TM and TC routing to and from the instruments is suspended or not guaranteed because of SSMM/SpaceWire maintenance, so no planned instrument TCs may be submitted.6
  • TAC windows. For turn-around calibrations the SOC re-routes all of an instrument's science APIDs (other than low-latency data) to a small shared store for prompt downlink; instrument teams wait 15 seconds after the window starts for the routing commands to complete.7
  • Packet store resizing. Resizing SSMM packet stores loses data unless the stores are empty, and needs a short window without SSMM memory operations; how to plan this was still an open issue.9

E-FECS files are delivered through GFTS at about T-20 weeks for each six-month period and are named EFECS_M[nn]_V[vv].xml, with B instead of V for a backup plan.8

docs.title: On-board inter-instrument communication
docs.text:
What it is. SOL-SGS-TN-0007 issue 2.0 (7 October 2016), issued at ESAC for the Science Ground Segment, records how the instrument teams agreed to exchange real-time information on board so that they can react autonomously to solar events, for example by triggering coordinated burst modes.58 Instruments never talk to each other directly. Each sends an inter-instrument communication (IIC) housekeeping packet TM(3,25) to the OBC, with category 5, its own process ID (different from the one used for its other HK) and a structure ID; the OBC copies the parameters into its data pool within a nominal 250 ms.59 Up to 8 times a second the OBC assembles a TC(20,128) carrying 36 octets of platform data and up to 200 octets of instrument data and distributes it; TC(20,1) and TC(20,2) start and stop distribution per instrument, with a period from one CSW cycle (125 ms) to 65 535 cycles (about 8191 s; 0 requests a one-shot distribution). The nominal maximum end-to-end delay is 500 ms. The same TC(20,128) also acts as the OBC heartbeat that lets instruments go safe if the spacecraft enters Survival Mode.5960

sequenceDiagram
  participant SWA as SWA (PID 95)
  participant OBC as OBC CSW data pool
  participant RPW as RPW
  participant MAG as MAG
  SWA->>OBC: TM(3,25), CAT 5, SID 255, every 4 s<br/>heartbeat, PAS density, velocity
  MAG->>OBC: TM(3,25), CAT 5, 8 Hz
  Note over OBC: parameters extracted within 250 ms
  OBC->>RPW: TC(20,128), 236 octets, 1 Hz
  OBC->>SWA: TC(20,128), 8 Hz
  OBC->>MAG: TC(20,128), 1 Hz
  Note over RPW,MAG: RPW derives its shock trigger from SWA density and velocity

The cadences in the diagram are the agreed ones: MAG generates at 8 Hz, SWA at 0.25 Hz and the other participants at 1 Hz (SPICE does not participate); all instruments receive TC(20,128) at 1 Hz except SWA at 8 Hz.61 Each instrument's IIC data starts with a 4-octet heartbeat copied from the OBT coarse time.61 The 236-octet TC(20,128) data field is split into fixed allocations, spares included:63

Octets Owner Size 1-36 Spacecraft (thruster and solar array flags, AOCS mode, roll, wheel speeds) 36 37-66 EPD 30 67-89 EUI 23 90-109 MAG 20 110-129 METIS 20 130-143 PHI 14 144-176 RPW 33 177-190 SOLOHI 14 191-206 STIX 16 207-222 SWA 16 223-236 SPICE (all spare) 14

The platform content is described in chapter 4 of the note, with several fields still marked TBC.62 The instrument side of the SWA contribution - a TM(3,25) with SID 255 every 4 seconds carrying the heartbeat, the PAS proton density and the three velocity components - is defined again in §9 of the SWA DPU Communications ICD.86 The SWA IIC packet can be followed field by field in the real SWA database on Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database, and the service 20 usage on How Solar Orbiter uses PUS.

docs.title: Instrument interfaces and instrument databases
docs.text:
The library holds two layers of instrument documents - ESA's requirements on all instruments (the EID-A) and one instrument's own interface control document (the SWA DPU ICD), which the SWA instrument database follows - plus the databases of two instruments.708287

flowchart TB
  MRD["Mission Requirements Document<br/>SOL-EST-RS-0049"] --> EIDA["EID-A, SOL-EST-IF-0050<br/>ESA requirements on every instrument<br/>(issue 1, 2007)"]
  EIDA --> EIDB["EID-B<br/>each PI's binding response"]
  EIDA --> DPU["SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003<br/>SWA DPU Communications ICD<br/>(issue 8.2, 2019)"]
  PKT["SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7<br/>TM-TC and packet structure ICD"] --> DPU
  DPU --> IDB["SWA instrument database<br/>(Planetek; versions follow ICD issues)"]
  IDB -.-> MIB["Spacecraft MIB release<br/>(same SWA definitions)"]
  STIX["STIX instrument database 2.26.38"] -.-> MIB

The solid arrows are stated in the documents: the EID-A places itself under the Mission Requirements Document and next to EID-B, the DPU ICD lists the EID-A (as SOL-EST-RCD-0050 issue 5) as an applicable document and the packet structure ICD issue 7 as a reference, and the IDB release notes align IDB versions with DPU ICD issues.708287 The dotted arrows are this wiki's inference from comparing the databases (see the Inference notes on the SWA and STIX pages).

docs.title: EID-A: what ESA asked of the instruments in 2007
docs.text:
What it is. The Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document - Part A, SOL-EST-IF-0050 issue 1 revision 0 of 9 October 2007, was prepared at ESTEC by the Solar Orbiter team. The EID is first released with the instrument Announcement of Opportunity; Part A states the technical and programmatic requirements that every PI must meet, Part B is each PI's response and becomes the sole binding agreement between the project office and that PI, and both are placed under configuration control once signed.70 The copy in the library was taken from the host explorers.larc.nasa.gov.91 It was written before the payload was selected: its resource table lists potential instruments named VIM, EUS, COR, HI/WFC and DPD next to SWA, RPW, MAG, EPD, EUI and STIX, and it allocates the payload 180 kg, 180 W and 100 kbps in all, against maximum data rates of, for example, 14 000 bps for SWA and 200 bps for STIX.71

Its TM/TC-relevant requirements are few but basic:

Topic EID-A issue 1 requirement Where it ended up Data handling the spacecraft Data Management System provides instrument command and control, command timeline management, packetised science data acquisition, mass memory storage and transmission, and health monitoring of instruments that are off; the bus is SpaceWire (ECSS-E-50-12) and each instrument uses a dual cold-redundant SpaceWire interface for TM and TC packets74 the SWA DPU talks to the OBC over SpaceWire, with TC, TM and time-code services in its EXOS layer84 Links and time SpaceWire link interface compliant up to the packet and network levels; two independent lines per instrument, addressed and routed separately; every instrument shall receive SpaceWire time codes; digital telemetry "TBW"75 in the SWA DPU, time-code management is implemented in the DPM FPGA and reported through EXOS84 Fault handling no automatic reconfiguration after a failure; go to a safe mode, send TM records of the fault to the DMS, recover only by ground telecommand76 the inter-instrument TC(20,128) doubles as the OBC heartbeat that lets instruments go safe when the spacecraft enters Survival Mode59 On-board software ECSS-E-40; boot software in PROM with access to all functions; an event report before any forced processor reset and on overload, arithmetic overflow, illegal instruction, data bus error, EDAC-detected memory corruption and checksum error; a single telecommand to enable software, after checking the upload; all ground communication with software functions through dedicated TC and TM source packets77 the SWA DPU boot software resides in PROM and cannot be patched84 EGSE the instrument station exchanges TM with the Central Checkout Equipment over a TCP/IP LAN at source packet level, using an EGSE protocol to be defined by the contractor; the CCE commands the instrument and monitors its housekeeping78 see SCOS-2000 as EGSE

The PUS is not mentioned in issue 1, and its operations chapter is mostly placeholders: mission operations, inputs to the satellite database, on-board software maintenance, inputs to the planning system and command request handling are all "TBW".79 In the library, the PUS tailoring is covered by the later packet structure ICD and planning by the E-FECS ICD; how instrument definitions enter the satellite database is visible only in the data. The DPU ICD cites issue 5 of the EID-A, which is not in the library.82

docs.title: The SWA DPU Communications ICD
docs.text: What it is. SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003 issue 8.2 (7 August 2019) is the communications interface control document of the SWA Data Processing Unit, written by the Italian DPU team under an ASI contract in the format of Annex E of ECSS-E-ST-40C. Over 403 pages it gives the DPU software architecture, the APID allocation of every SWA telemetry type, the format and error codes of every telecommand the DPU accepts (PUS services 3, 5, 6, 9, 17, 20, 21 and the private services 200 to 204), the housekeeping, asynchronous, inter-instrument and science packets, the internal protocols with the four sensors, and the code tables for events and for the failure reports TM(1,2) ("TARF") and TM(1,8) ("TECF").808185 It references ECSS-E-70-41A (PUS-A) and SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7, the packet structure ICD described above.82 Its change record runs from issue 1 (27 June 2014) to 8.2, and the SWA IDB release notes follow most of its issues; the comparison of the ICD, the IDB and the MIB is on Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database, and the document itself is presented on Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces.8387

-- run on swa-idb.sqlite, swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite and stix-idb-2.26.38.sqlite
ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m;

docs.title: The MIB releases
docs.text:
The SWA/PAS team's server at IRAP hosts the Solar Orbiter MIB as a directory of 111 dated releases (April 2020 to September 2025), each a zip named like MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL.zip, plus latest/ and previous/ sets, SWA instrument database versions and the ICD.69 This wiki copied two releases and two SWA databases from there, and the STIX database from a separate server:

docs.title: Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces: SWA DPU ICD and EID-A
docs.text:
A science instrument reaches the ground through a chain of interface documents. ESA's Experiment Interface Document (EID) Part A states what every Solar Orbiter instrument must comply with, and each Principal Investigator answers with a Part B.2 The spacecraft prime contractor's TM/TC and packet structure ICD, SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079, fixes the packet formats, APIDs and PUS services on board (see Solar Orbiter).53 Each instrument then documents its own packets and commands: for SWA (the "Solar Wind Analyzer" in the EID-A acronym list) this is the DPU Communications Interface Control Document SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003, and the same content is delivered in machine form as the SWA instrument database (IDB), which ends up in the spacecraft MIB.151648 This page covers the three round-2 sources of that chain - EID-A issue 1.0, the SWA ICD issue 8.2 and the SWA IDB v6.5.0 with its release notes - and checks the ICD against the data. The database itself is analysed on Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database; the STIX equivalent is STIX instrument database.

flowchart LR
  ICD["SWA DPU Communications ICD<br/>SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003 issue 8.2"]
  EIDA["EID-A<br/>SOL-EST-IF-0050<br/>ESA requirements on all PIs"] --> EIDB["EID-B<br/>per instrument (PI response)"]
  TN["SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079<br/>spacecraft TM/TC and packet ICD"] --> ICD
  EIDA -.->|"AD[2], issue 5"| ICD
  ICD --> IDB["SWA IDB (Planetek)<br/>v2.0.0 ... v6.5.0"]
  IDB -.-> MIB["Solar Orbiter MIB<br/>(SCOS-2000 at ESOC)"]
  TN7["SOL-SGS-TN-0007<br/>inter-instrument communication"] -.-> ICD

The solid arrows show which document each one cites: the SWA ICD lists the EID-A (issue 5) as applicable and the packet ICD issue 7 and ECSS-E-70-41A as references, and the IDB release notes tie many IDB versions to ICD issues.1847 The EID-B is named by the EID-A but is not in the library.2 The dotted arrows are this wiki's reading: the SWA ICD does not list SOL-SGS-TN-0007, but its S20 packet implements the note's SWA allocation (the note's SWA table in turn names SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003 "Issue 2_draft" as its reference), and the route from IDB to MIB is not documented (see the Inference at the end of the page).1862

The three sources

Library item Document Origin 12-3-solarorbiter-eid-a-issue-1-0-2007-10-09 Solar Orbiter Experiment Interface Document - Part A, SOL-EST-IF-0050, issue 1 revision 0, 9 October 2007, 200 pages copied 2026-11-12 from explorers.larc.nasa.gov so-swa-dpu-cd-ic-003-...-issue8-2 SWA DPU Communications Interface Control Document, SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003, issue 8.2, 07/08/2019, 403 pages copied 2026-11-12 from solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/documents/ICD/ swa-idb-v6-5-0 SWA IDB v6.5.0: 56 .dat files and IDB_relNotes.txt copied 2026-11-12 from solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/MIB/SWA_IDB_v6.5.0.zip (115 876 bytes)

Titles, issues and dates are from the documents' cover pages; hosts, sizes and copy dates from this wiki's source registry.11652

docs.title: The Experiment Interface Document, Part A (2007)
What the document is
docs.text:
The EID-A was to be released with the instrument Announcement of Opportunity; its background section notes that ESA's Science Programme Committee was to decide in November 2007 whether and how to proceed with the mission.2 It exists to make the PIs design, build and verify their instruments within the spacecraft's constraints and the prime contractor build a spacecraft into which they can be integrated. Part A holds the technical and programmatic requirements common to all PIs; Part B, written by each PI, becomes the only binding agreement between the ESA project office and that PI, and both parts become applicable documents to the prime contractor.2 Once signed they are under configuration control: changes go through an Engineering Change Request, deviations through a Request for Waiver, each numbered for example ECR/XYZ/0100, and the receiving party's board must decide within 4 weeks.12 The copy in the library is issue 1.0, signed on 9 October 2007; the SWA ICD lists the EID-A as applicable document AD[2] under the reference SOL-EST-RCD-0050 at issue 5, which is not in the library.118

The 2007 instrument list shows how early this issue is: its resource table (Table 3) lists eleven potential instruments with mass, power and data rate, among them SWA (then "Solar Wind Plasma Analyzer", 16.5 kg nominal, 14 W, 14 000 bit/s) and STIX (4.4 kg, 4 W, 200 bit/s), against a payload allocation of 180 kg, 180 W and 100 kbit/s that the listed total of 106 100 bit/s exceeds.4 The flown payload named in the packet ICD (EPD, MAG, RPW, SWA, SPICE, PHI, EUI, METIS, STIX, SoloHI) differs from that 2007 list.54

docs.title: Data handling requirements
docs.text:
The data handling chapter is short. The on-board data handling system - the Data Management System (DMS), combining the functions of a Command and Data Management Unit and the attitude control computer - is the instruments' gateway to ground and provides instrument command and control, command timeline management, packetized science data acquisition, mass-memory storage and transmission, and health and safety monitoring while instruments are off.5 The bus architecture is SpaceWire to ECSS-E-50-12, and each instrument must use a dual cold-redundant SpaceWire interface "for transmission of TM and reception of TC packets".5 The detailed requirements are:8

Clause Requirement 4.8.2.1 A SpaceWire link interface (cables and connectors, LVDS drivers, codec, FIFO) compliant up to the packet and network levels of the SpaceWire standard 4.8.2.1 (1) Instruments receive SpaceWire time codes according to ECSS-E-50-12 4.8.2.3 (2) Two independent SpaceWire lines per instrument, addressed and routed separately to the spacecraft data handling system 4.8.2.2, 4.8.2.4 Monitoring and synchronisation interfaces "TBD"; digital telemetry "TBW"

A SpaceWire Remote Terminal Controller ASIC under ESA development could implement the remote terminal, but it is a PI-provided item (targets: about 50 MIPS, under 500 mW and 100 g).5

docs.title: Software and fault-handling requirements that shape TM/TC
docs.text:
The requirements of section 4.9.1 that most directly shape telemetry and telecommands are:9

  • all on-board software complies with ECSS-E-40, with separate memory areas for code, fixed constants and variable parameters, a minimum boot software in PROM from which every function, including EEPROM updates, is reachable, and modules that can be changed without moving others;
  • software resource usage (memory, CPU, I/O) should be telemetered, uploaded software must be checkable before it is enabled, and enabling should take a single telecommand;
  • any communication between ground and an on-board software function uses telecommand and telemetry source packets designed for the purpose;
  • an event report is generated before a forced processor reset, and on processor overload, unexpected arithmetic overflow, illegal instruction, data bus error, memory corruption detected by EDAC, and checksum error.

Fault tolerance relies on redundancy; after a failure an instrument must not reconfigure itself to continue but go to a safe mode, send telemetry records of the fault to the DMS and wait for a ground telecommand to recover; and instrument computers must reset and resume from a defined mode after power cycling.67 The SWA ICD's safe mode, boot software and event list (below) can be compared with these clauses.

docs.title: Operations, database and ground equipment
docs.text: The operational chapter assigns the MOC and communications to ESA/ESOC, archiving at the MOC, and the SOC to produce payload operations requests and distribute data to the PIs; the MOC supplies raw instrument data with housekeeping and auxiliary data and performs near-real-time out-of-limit checks on a set of payload parameters.310 The PI defines the instrument modes, supplies a user manual, inputs to the database and to the Flight Operations Plan, and maintains the software to end of mission.1011 Most operational subsections are still empty: "Inputs to Satellite Database", on-board software maintenance, command request handling and the mission products are all "TBW" in issue 1.0.10 On-board software is delivered with each model, either resident in non-volatile memory or loadable through the spacecraft telecommand uplink.13 The instrument EGSE must integrate into the system EGSE; its Instrument Station talks to the Central Checkout Equipment (CCE) over a TCP/IP LAN, exchanging telemetry "at Source Packet level", and the CCE commands the instrument and monitors its housekeeping.13

docs.title: What EID-A issue 1.0 does not specify
docs.text: The document's normative references are the mission requirements document, engineering standards of the ECSS-E-10, -20 and -30 series, SpaceWire (ECSS-E-50-12), software (ECSS-E-40), product assurance standards (ECSS-Q, ESA PSS) and a materials handbook; the PUS (ECSS-E-70-41) is not among them, and the document does not mention it anywhere.14 Issue 1.0 therefore says nothing about packet structure, APIDs, PUS services, time formats, verification or the database format: those come from the spacecraft packet ICD, whose PUS services, Annex 8 APID scheme and Annex 9 failure and event IDs the SWA ICD and IDB follow (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS).5458 Whether the later issue 5 cited by SWA adds such requirements is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Purpose and history
docs.text:
The ICD gives the communication interface of the SWA Data Processing Unit (DPU) using the method of Annex E to ECSS-E-ST-40C, as deliverable EN-019 of the Italian Space Agency (ASI) contract 2013-055-1.0 (as printed in §1.1-1.2); it was prepared, checked and approved by the DPU team and its distribution list includes ASI, MSSL, IAPS, TSD, SITAEL, Leonardo and Planetek.1716 Its change record runs from issue 1 (27/06/2014) to 8.2 (07/08/2019):16

Issue Date Main changes 1 27/06/2014 first issue 2 31/07/2015 ICDR RIDs: science TM (S21), inter-process contribution (S20), HK for OBC FDIR, TC handling policy 3 11/12/2015 HK optimisation, SIDs 1, 2, 3, 11-15, safe state TCs, event/TARF/TECF auxiliary data sections 4 - 4.7 08/06/2016 - 2017 (4.6: 21/04/2017) burst and engineering modes, time offset TC(200,163), IIC test TM and TC (4.2), memory IDs, service 12 monitoring remapped to service 200 (4.4), boot report renamed FSW start-up report, debug TM(200,248), 3-bit DPU state with a transition state 5.0 - 6.2 2017 - 31/07/2018 event and recovery codes, monitoring ID lists, unused TECF codes deleted (6.1), per-APID SSID table, parameter data aligned to length 7.0 - 7.1 08/03/2019 - 13/03/2019 macro state in HK, ExOS low-level error codes, TC(203,160) 8.0 - 8.2 30/04/2019 - 07/08/2019 EAS engineering SIDs, PAS engineering PIDs, "minor editorial fixing"

The applicable documents are the ASI contract annex, the EID-A (issue 5), the SWA science operations requirements and the DPU flight software requirements and design documents; the reference documents are ECSS-E-70-41A (PUS), ECSS-E-ST-40C, the packet ICD SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7, the SpaceWire application protocol SOL.S.ASTR.RS.00038, and the HIS, EAS and PAS sensor documents from their teams.18 All open points (TBC, TBD, TBW) are closed in issue 8.2.46

docs.title: SWA and its DPU
docs.text:
SWA has four units: two Electron Analyser Systems (EAS1, EAS2) for electron velocity distributions and moments, a Proton Alpha Sensor (PAS) for the major solar wind ions, and a Heavy Ion Sensor (HIS) for charge states of oxygen and iron and minor ions; all are connected to the DPU by SpaceWire at 10 Mbit/s.19 The DPU provides power, control, temporary storage, communication and computation; its hardware is a rigid-flex backplane with six SpaceWire splitters, two Data Processing Modules (each a communication and science processing board plus a CPU board) and two Power Conditioning and Distribution Modules.19 Its software provides TC reception, science and HK telemetry, sensor control (all sensors are switched by the DPU except HIS, powered by a dedicated spacecraft line, although Table 7 also lists DPU commands TC(200,153)/(200,154) to switch HIS on and off), buffering of 5 minutes of high-resolution EAS and PAS data for triggered transmission, moment calculation and compression, time synchronisation, and inter-instrument exchange through PUS service 20.20

flowchart TB
  subgraph ASW["Application Software layer"]
    PCMSW["PCMSW: TC validation and execution, DPU states, FDIR,<br/>time management, EAS1/EAS2/PAS/HIS managers"]
    SDPSW["SDPSW: moments, lossless compression (CCSDS 121)"]
  end
  subgraph ASSW["Application Service layer"]
    PUS["PUS and mission services library"]
  end
  subgraph MSSW["Machine Services layer"]
    RTOS["VxWorks kernel"]
    EXOS["ExOS: SpaceWire links, time codes, HK, memory, CRC"]
    BSP["BSP drivers"]
  end
  BOOT["Boot SW in PROM<br/>memory tests, MRAM patching, loads ASW"] --> ASW
  ASW --> ASSW --> MSSW

The layers and components are those of the ICD's sections 4 and 4.1; everything runs on a LEON2 CPU.2021 The boot software checks the memories and EDAC, initialises SpaceWire, copies the software from MRAM to RAM and starts it; it cannot be patched.21 Compression is lossless and CCSDS 121 compliant; moments of order 0 to 2 (and 3 for EAS) are computed, and in normal mode compression runs in the deterministic time slots while triggered-mode work runs as a separate low-priority task.21

docs.title: Packet formats
docs.text:
The ICD refers to the packet ICD for the packet formats and to the SpaceWire application protocol for the transport, and draws each packet as a grid of 16-bit words.22 Every telecommand starts with the same five words - version, type, data field header flag, PID 95 and category; sequence flags and count; packet length; secondary header flag, PUS version 1, ack flags and service type; subtype and source ID - and ends with the packet error control word.23 The SWA IDB's TC header NOM_TC gives the exact bit positions:48

The ICD names the fields VN, TY, DF, PID, PKT, SF, PSC, PL, SHF, PVN, ACK, ST, SS, SI and PEC; the IDB fixes the source ID to 0x78 (120), the value the packet ICD reserves for ground direct commands, and asks for acceptance and completion reports (CCF_ACK = 9) on all 201 commands.234857 The IDB treats PID and PKT as one 11-bit APID element, 95 x 16 + 12 = 1532.4853

Telemetry uses a 10-octet data field header drawn as secondary header flag, PUS version 001, four spare bits and the service type; subtype and destination ID; and three words of on-board time (OBRT).3940 The field widths follow from the printed values (3-bit 001, 4-bit 0000) in a 16-bit word, and agree with the 10-octet data field header and the 6-octet CUC time (4 octets coarse, 2 fine) of the packet ICD and with the 16-octet header length (PID_DFHSIZE = 16) of every SWA packet in the IDB.5648

docs.title: APIDs: the ICD table and the database
docs.text:
The ICD's Table 1 assigns each kind of telemetry a PID and packet category; the IDB places the packets as follows:2248

ICD Table 1 content ICD PID / CAT (APID) SWA IDB v6.5.0 HK for S20, TM(3,25) SID 255 (PAS quick-look moments) 95 / 5 (1525) 1525: SWA_TM_II_INFO Low-latency TM(21,3)/(21,6): EAS quick-look strahl, PAS moments 215 and calibration 214, HIS 132-134 95 / 12 (1532) 1532: 9 packets HK normal TM(3,25): DPU 11 and 16, EAS 1 and 2, HIS 100 and 101, PAS 3 96 / 4 (1540) 1540: these 7 plus boot-software HK SID 20 HK diagnostic TM(3,26): DPU 4-10, 12, 13 96 / 8 (1544) 1544: 9 packets Science normal: EAS 3D, partial moments, engineering; PAS distributions and engineering; HIS 96 / 12 (1548) 1548: 45 packets Optional burst and trigger data 97 / 12 (1564) 1564: 25 packets HK ground monitoring TM(3,25) 98 / 4 (1572) 1572: SID 15 and SWA_TM_HIS_ALIVE (SID 102) Science core burst 98 / 12 (1580) 1580: 13 packets TM(1,1), (1,2), (1,7), (1,8) 99 / 1 (1585) 1585: 175 packets HK for OBC action TM(3,25) 99 / 4 (1588) 1588: SID 14 Events TM(5,1)-(5,4) 99 / 7 (1591) 1591: 248 events and TM(17,2) Memory dump (6,6) and checksum (6,10), TM(17,2), TM(200,249)-(200,253), TM(201/202/203,200) 99 / 9 (1593) dumps on 1545 (96 / 9); private reports on 1542 (96 / 6) and again, with other SPIDs, on 1593 EAS engineering low-latency, modes 3 and 4 99 / 12 (1596) 1596: 4 packets

The differences in the last rows bring the database closer to Annex 8 of the packet ICD, which reserves category 7 for service 5 and TM(17,2), category 9 for service 6 dumps and category 6 for private report packets produced on ground request.54 The release notes record the steps: TM(17,2) "CAT set to 7" in IDB 2.3.0, "Fixed some APID according to ICD v8.3" in 6.3.3, and in 6.3.3_wa nine report packets re-added "with APID = 1593 (as in v6.2.1)".47 An ICD issue 8.3 is not in the library. The 2021 IDB already has the dumps on 1545 and the reports on 1542 and 1593; their earlier placement in the April 2020 MIB is traced on SWA.49

SQL used (APIDs and header) 
-- swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite
SELECT PID_APID, count(*), group_concat(DISTINCT PID_TYPE || '/' || PID_STYPE)
  FROM pid GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CAST(PID_APID AS INT);
SELECT PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_TYPE || '/' || PID_STYPE, PID_DESCR
  FROM pid WHERE PID_APID IN ('1542', '1593') ORDER BY 1, 3;
SELECT * FROM pcdf;  SELECT CCF_ACK, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;

docs.title: Telecommands by manager
docs.text:
The flight software routes each TC to a manager; the ICD lists them in Tables 2 to 8, and the IDB v6.5.0 defines 201 commands, all on APID 1532:23303334353648

Manager (ICD table) Service type Subtypes in the ICD IDB commands PUS manager (Table 2) 3, 5, 6, 9, 17, 21 3: 5, 6, 129; 5: 5, 6; 6: 2, 5, 9, 129; 9: 129; 17: 1; 21: 1, 2 13 PUS manager, on-board monitoring (Table 2) 200 170-176 7 PUS manager, inter-instrument data 20 128 (received from the OBC) - DPU manager (Table 3) 200 128-149, 151, 152, 200-203 28 Sensor manager (Table 4) 200 160-165 7 (two variants of 162) HIS manager (Table 7) 200 153-155 4 (with 156) EAS1 / EAS2 managers (Table 5) 201 / 202 129-173 except 151 and 163 44 / 44 (with 174) PAS manager (Table 6) 203 128-160 33 HIS internal (Table 8) 204 (also HIS's own TC(6,2), (6,5), (6,9), (9,129), (20,128)) 27 subtypes from 128 to 181 21 (not 134, 139, 140, 142, 151, 177)

This confirms what the database alone only suggested (see SWA): type 200 belongs to the DPU and its general functions, 201 to EAS1, 202 to EAS2, 203 to PAS and 204 to HIS, all inside the range 200-205 that the packet ICD reserves for SWA.34353655 The IDB adds three commands the ICD does not have - TC(201,174) and TC(202,174) "set EAS summation" and a second TC(200,162) - and still contains TC(200,156) "DPU stop the HIS macro execution", whose removal issue 4.3 records.484716

docs.title: PUS manager: services 3, 5, 6, 9, 17, 21
docs.text:
• Service 3. TC(3,5)/(3,6) enable or disable one HK packet by its SID (1-15; types HK or DIAG), TC(3,129) changes its period in 125 ms time slices, which must be a multiple of 8 (one second); bad SIDs and rates fail execution with codes 0xA8D9 and 0xA8DA.24
  • Service 5. TC(5,5)/(5,6) enable or disable a list of event IDs, given in decimal from 43500 (EvntOk) to 43564 (DPUSwWarning), for example 43526 RpwTriggerOccurred, 43547 dpuSafeState, 43550 thrustFire.25
  • Service 6. Load, dump and check by absolute address, and abort dump TC(6,129). Memory IDs are 0x8000 RAM (start 0x40000000, 8 MiB), 0x8001/0x8003 MRAM 1 and 2 (0x10000000, 2 MiB), 0x8002 PROM (0x00000000, 128 KiB) and 0x8040-0x8080 HIS memories; dumps are sent as TM(6,6) of at most 1 024 octets at 1 Hz, using the grouping flags when several packets are needed.2639 The packet ICD allocates memory IDs 0x80--/0x81-- to SWA.60
  • Service 9. TC(9,129) "accept time synchronisation" carries the spacecraft SCET coarse and fine time; an internal error gives 0xA868.27 The 2025 spacecraft MIB no longer has this command (ZIA58057), although IDB v6.5.0 does.5048
  • Service 17 and 21. Connection test TC(17,1) answered by TM(17,2); TC(21,1)/(21,2) start and stop all science packets.29

docs.title: On-board monitoring on service 200
docs.text:
Issue 4.4 moved the parameter monitoring from service 12 to the private service 200 "according on FDIR agreement".16 Seven TCs manage a list of monitoring items: enable and disable items or the whole function (TC(200,170)/(200,171), up to 215 items per TC, N = 0 meaning the service level), configure items (TC(200,172), up to 7 per TC, only while the item is disabled), report the configuration as TM(200,249) (TC(200,173)), and enable, disable or reset the counters of the error-event handler (TC(200,174)-(200,176)).28 One configuration entry holds:28

Field Meaning monId, monStatus item identifier (69 named items 0-68, for example 0 EAS2POWER_MI, 8 TC20MISSING, 9 TIMECODEMISSING, 10 THFIREFLAG_MI, then spares) and enable flag parType, filter parameter type (for example 0 = PAR_WORD, unsigned 16 bits) and the filter value used to confirm a failure parId 32-bit parameter identifier, for example 0x00030013 HK_I_PLUS_28V_PRI, 0x00060000 MissingTc20 two validityParId 32-bit identifiers of validity parameters (0x000A0000 EAS1 HK valid ... 0x000A0007) lowThreshold, highThreshold limits lowEventId, highEventId error event raised below or above the limit for more than filter samples, from a list such as 3 ReqSWASafeEvnt, 4 RequestSWAOffEvnt, 16 MissingTc20Evnt, 18 ThFireTc20Evnt, 24 HisAlivenessEvnt, or 0xFF none

Having been moved from service 12, this is the instrument-level counterpart of PUS ST[12] on-board monitoring; the error-event handler resembles, in this wiki's reading, an event-to-action list as in ST[19].16 The items TC20MISSING, THFIREFLAG_MI and SASTEERING_MI watch the OBC's TC(20,128), which SOL-SGS-TN-0007 defines both as a heartbeat letting instruments go safe if the spacecraft enters survival mode and as the carrier of the platform's thruster-firing and solar-array-steering flags.2861

Inference

The ICD does not state whether the event IDs 0-26 of the error-event handler trigger the macros of section 12 (for example DPUSafeM) or the OBC-side requests of SID 14. The names (ReqSWASafeEvnt, RequestSWAOffEvnt) suggest requests to the spacecraft, which SID 14 below implements with OBCP flags; this link is this wiki's reading.

docs.title: DPU manager: states, configuration and macros
docs.text:
The DPU manager runs the instrument's state machine. Each mode command starts a DPU "CCSDS macro" - DPUDiagM, DPUStbyM, DPUOps or DPUSafeM - and fails acceptance with 0xA7FF when the current state does not allow it or 0xA805 while a safe transition is running.30313243

stateDiagram-v2
  BOOT : Boot SW in PROM
  BOOT --> BOOT : TC(200,200) stay in boot
  BOOT --> ASW : TC(200,201) leave boot, load ASW
  state ASW {
    STBY : Stand-by (3)
    DIAG : Diagnostic (0)
    OPS : Operational (1)
    SAFE : Safe (2)
    STBY --> DIAG : TC(200,128)
    STBY --> OPS : TC(200,130)
    DIAG --> STBY : TC(200,129)
    OPS --> STBY : TC(200,129)
    SAFE --> STBY : TC(200,129)
    STBY --> SAFE : TC(200,152)
    DIAG --> SAFE : TC(200,152)
    OPS --> SAFE : TC(200,152)
  }
  ASW --> BOOT : TC(200,151) reset

The preconditions are the ICD's: diagnostic and operational only from stand-by, safe only from operational, stand-by or diagnostic; stand-by has no stated precondition (its only acceptance failure is a safe transition in progress), and the reset reboots the software by stopping the watchdog refresh.3132 The numbers are the 3-bit DPU currentStatus of SID 11, which also has value 4 for a transition in progress.37 The state the ASW starts in is not stated in the available sources. TC(200,202) selects which flight software copy the boot software loads next (0 nominal, 1 patchable).32

The other DPU manager commands manage configuration parameters (modify, report as TM(200,250), accept into flash, discard, apply to MRAM, re-initialise the science processing), macros (modify, report as TM(200,251), accept, discard), science compression, RPW trigger handling (freezing the rolling buffers), the "book keeping" algorithm, IIC test generation, the boot report TM(200,252), the error log TM(200,253) and a debug register access answered by TM(200,248).3039 Section 12 lists the macros: 23 sensor macros (EAS power, run, idle, pre-amplifier, dump; PAS power, configuration and cyclograms), 12 HIS macros and 6 DPU macros - DPUTFFMacro (16), DPUOps (17), DPUStbyM (18), DPUSafeM (19), DPUDiagM (20) and DPUSASteer (21). A macro holds at most 16 TCs of at most 64 octets each, drawn from a list of TC instances (for example 0x0E SetE1Off, an instance of TC(201,132), or 0x26 DisTcProc, TC(200,165) with value 7), and its content can be modified with service 6.43 The step list is not fully consistent with the TC tables: it maps PasPwrOffFast (0x14) to TC(200,154), which Table 7 names "Switch off HIS", and maps both SetPas (0x13) and PasPwrOff (0x1C) to TC(203,138), which Table 6 names "PAS FastPower OFF"; which mapping is intended is not stated in the available sources.433536

docs.title: Sensor, EAS, PAS and HIS managers
docs.text: The sensor manager puts all sensors into burst mode at the next 4-second boundary (TC(200,160), durations in 0.125 s steps), puts both EAS into science mode, sets the product cadence (TC(200,162): EAS 10 s, 100 s or 400 s; PAS and HIS nominal or low), shifts science timing against the SCET by -299 to +299 (TC(200,163)), stops macros, and enables or disables commanding of individual sensors (TC(200,165)).33 The EAS managers hold 43 commands each, mostly register, table and high-voltage settings (dither, notch, deflection and hemisphere tables, MCP high voltage, eight engineering modes 2-9, strahl selection, pre-amplifiers); the PAS manager's 33 commands cover calibration and engineering modes, high-voltage ramps, sequence and configuration tables, start and stop science and stand-by.3435 HIS commands TC(204,x) are passed through: the DPU routes them unchanged and HIS validates them itself.3642

docs.title: Verification: TARF and TECF codes
docs.text:
Each TC description lists its TARF (acceptance failure, reported in TM(1,2)) and TECF (execution failure, TM(1,8)) error codes; sections 14 and 15 tabulate them with the auxiliary data each failure report carries.45 The IDB defines one packet per code; for the TARF codes:48

ICD TARF Code IDB TM(1,2) TcApidError, TcLenError, TcPecError (with received and computed checksum), NotValidSrvType, NotValidSrvSubtype, TcSfError 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 SPIDs 58001-58006, codes 0-4 and 6 TcTyError, TcVnError, TcDfError, TcPkcError, TcShfError, TcPusVerError 0xA7F8-0xA7FD 58007-58011 and 58013 (58012 is TM(1,7)) TcNotPlausible, DpuNotPlausibleTcError both 0xA7FF in the ICD 0xA7FE and 0xA7FF Eas1/Eas2/Pas/HisNotPlausibleTcError, TcReceivedWhileNotSynch, DpuSafeOnGoing 0xA800-0xA805 58016-58020, 58190

The low codes are the standard failure IDs of the packet ICD (0 illegal APID to 6 illegal segment sequence flag) and the others lie in SWA's block 43000-43999 (0xA7F8 = 43000).58 The ICD gives TcNotPlausible the same code as DpuNotPlausibleTcError; the IDB resolves the clash with 0xA7FE.4548 The 153 TM(1,8) packets run up to 0xA901 SafeEntMacroErr.48 On the ground every SWA command uses the same two verification stages, acceptance 58901 and completion 58907, both report-based with a 20-second interval (see Command verification in the MIB).48

docs.title: Housekeeping and diagnostic telemetry
docs.text:
Table 9 lists 19 cyclic packets: SIDs 1-3 sensor HK (EAS1, EAS2, PAS), 4-10 and 12-13 DPU diagnostics (TC counters, validity, hardware diagnostics, maximum manager durations, FDIR status and monitoring values, derived parameters, TM and error counters), 11 DPU HK, 14 OBC FDIR, 15 ground monitoring, 16 IIC test, 100 and 101 HIS boot and HK, and 20 boot-software HK.37 The ICD gives offsets from the start of the source data; the IDB's plf offsets are 16 octets larger because they count from the packet start.3748 Octet 4 of SID 11 (IDB octet 20, container NIAG0703) holds the DPU manager state:3748

The IDB's textual calibration of NIAD0703, CIAT0017TM, covers only 0 DIAG, 1 OPS, 2 SAFE and 3 STBY: it has no text for the raw value 4 (transition, added in ICD issue 4.4).4816

SID 14 (APID 1588, category 4 on PID 99) is the packet the spacecraft watches for SWA FDIR.2238 Its first data octets carry a 2-bit DPU mode and boot flag, then four request flags; the ICD defines the action for each: run OBCP 1 REC_SWA1 (switch SWA off by its LCL), OBCP 2 REC_SWA2 (SWA safe), OBCP 3 REC_SWA3 (safe, then off) or OBCP 4 REC_SWA4 (reset SWA); a 16-bit "OBCP #5 request" word asks for HIS to be switched off.38

The rest of SID 14 holds the DC-DC current, the two thermistors (A checked by the OBC, B not), the HIS switch-off request and two DPU power-good flags; the IDB packet YIA58211 is 34 octets with exactly these fields.3848 Browse it as packet 58211. SID 16 echoes samples of the received TC(20,128) - reception time, MAG heartbeat and field components - to test the inter-instrument link.38

SQL used (HK layouts) 
SELECT l.PLF_OFFBY, l.PLF_OFFBI, c.PCF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, c.PCF_PTC || '/' || c.PCF_PFC, c.PCF_CURTX
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID IN ('58200', '58211') ORDER BY l.PLF_SPID, CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
SELECT g.COL2, g.COL3, c.PCF_DESCR, c.PCF_CURTX FROM pcf_glob_det g
  JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = g.COL2 WHERE g.COL1 IN ('NIAG0703', 'NIAG2100', 'NIAG2103');
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR = 'CIAT0017TM';

docs.title: Asynchronous reports, events and the S20 contribution
docs.text:
Reports produced on request are TM(200,248) debug data, (200,249) monitoring configuration, (200,250) configuration parameters (a count followed by identifier, length and data per parameter, for example 0x0002 RebootCnt), (200,251) macro content, (200,252) FSW start-up report, (200,253) error log, and (201,200), (202,200), (203,200) EAS1, EAS2 and PAS parameter dumps; the ICD gives all of them PID 99 and category 9.3922 Section 13 lists the events with their auxiliary data, codes from 0xA9ED (TcAcqError) upwards.44 In the IDB the SWA event IDs run from 43501 to 43999 (0xA9ED-0xABDF) in all four severities: SWA numbers its events inside its 43000-43999 block (Table 14.3-1 allocates these ranges for both failure and event IDs) rather than by the severity ranges that the packet ICD defines for the central software (and makes optional for others).4859

Every 4 seconds the DPU sends the TM(3,25) with PID 95, category 5 and SID 255 for distribution to other instruments: the heartbeat (coarse OBRT), the PAS proton density and the three solar wind velocity components, then spares, with a packet length field of 0x1A.40 The bit layout and its agreement with SOL-SGS-TN-0007 and the IDB are on SWA.62

docs.title: Science telemetry and sensor protocols
docs.text:
Science products use service 21. An EAS 3D product, generated every 100 s in normal mode, is one TM(21,3) with SID, SID counter, SCET, the EAS mode, validity flags for the whole set, each of the 16 elevations and each energy, and the compression information, followed by TM(21,6) packets (grouping flags first, continuation, last) carrying up to 2 045 words of compressed data.41 PIDs 96, 97 and 98 distinguish normal science, optional burst or RPW-frozen data and core burst; HIS science packets are passed through unchanged.41 The IDB has 96 such packets (54 TM(21,3) and 42 TM(21,6) on the science APIDs 1532, 1548, 1564, 1580 and 1596).48 Table 10 of the ICD lists the six HIS science products (pulse-height analysis, alpha and heavy matrix rates, alpha and heavy velocity distributions, rates) as TM(21,5), whereas the IDB defines no TM(21,5) packet and carries HIS science as TM(21,3) and TM(21,6) with SSIDs 128-134 and 191 (for example SPID 58808 SWA_TM_SCI_HIS_PHA_NORM, TM(21,6) on APID 1548).4148

Inside SWA the DPU talks to EAS and PAS with a simple register protocol over SpaceWire, not with PUS packets. Each EAS command starts with a header octet:42

followed by a 16-bit address, a 16-bit length and data in 24-bit units, the EAS internal bus width.42 A command that could damage the instrument is sent as an enable packet followed immediately by a go packet with identical address and data; any other packet in between clears the enable and the go is rejected.42 HIS, in contrast, speaks CCSDS: the DPU forwards TCs to it and its TM to the spacecraft, and on receiving a HIS TM(5,3) it forwards the packet and powers HIS off at once.42

docs.title: The SWA IDB v6.5.0 and its release notes
What was copied
docs.text: The zip holds 56 .dat files (32 non-empty) dated 2025-06-17 10:56, an empty synthetic/ folder dated 2015-10-02 and IDB_relNotes.txt dated 2025-06-17 11:01; unlike the 2021 ASCII.zip it has no __MACOSX entries.48 The files use CR LF line ends and the same issue-5.1 field counts (19 for pcf, 13 for cpc).48 It is browsable as the swa65 explorer, for example APID 1593.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
The notes, written at Planetek Italia, list the IDB versions from 2.0.0 (08/03/2016, "released with EGSE SW spacePTS v2.0") to 6.5.0 (17/06/2025).47 Many entries name the ICD issue they implement, often within days of it:4716

IDB version Date ICD issue (date) 2.1.0, 2.2.0 10/06/2016, 16/06/2016 4 (08/06/2016) 2.3.0 19/07/2016 4.1 (25/07/2016 in the ICD record) 2.4.4 31/08/2016 4.2 (30/08/2016) 2.6.0 04/11/2016 4.3 (21/10/2016) 3.0.0 14/03/2017 4.4 (10/03/2017) 3.1.0 30/03/2017 4.5 (30/03/2017) 4.0.0 26/06/2017 5.0 5.0.0 22/12/2017 6.0 (27/11/2017) 5.2.0, 5.3.0 23/05/2018, 14/11/2018 6.1 (21/02/2018), 6.2 (31/07/2018) 5.4.0, 5.4.1 11/03/2019, 13/03/2019 7.0 (08/03/2019), 7.1 (13/03/2019) 6.0.0, 6.2.0 30/04/2019, 17/06/2019 8.0 (30/04/2019), 8.1 (17/06/2019) 6.3.3 11/10/2021 8.2 for three packets, 8.3 for APIDs

The other entries record database work - remarks from MSSL and from review lists, HIS updates from the HIS team's spreadsheets, calibration and limit changes, errors found with a tool called PDIT, and an "AIRBUS issue" fixed in 4.0.3.47 After the 2021 versions come 6.4.0-6.4.5 (2022-2023: a textual calibration, mcf and ocf, the cadence command TC(200,162), ocp), 6.4.6 (11/06/2025: commands ZIA58951 and ZIA58952, textual calibration CIAT0066TM) and 6.5.0 (17/06/2025: SPIDs 58730-58733).47

docs.title: From the 2021 set to v6.5.0, and to the 2025 MIB
docs.text:
Comparing the copied 2021 ASCII.zip (last version 6.3.4) with v6.5.0 confirms the notes:4849

Change Data Release note 4 packets added TM(1,8) on APID 1585: 58730 SWA_EAS1_BAD_SUM, 58731 SWA_EAS2_BAD_SUM, 58732 SWA_EAS1_OFF_ENT_ERR, 58733 SWA_EAS2_OFF_ENT_ERR (failure IDs 43149-43152) 6.5.0 3 commands added ZIA58950 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE TC(200,162) with 9 parameters (beside the 5-parameter ZIA58728) and its new command text tables CIAT0070TC-CIAT0075TC; ZIA58951/ZIA58952 set EAS1/EAS2 summation TC(201/202,174) 6.4.2-6.4.5 (cadence TC), 6.4.6 text of failure IDs 43149/43150 Eas1FOffEntErr/Eas2FOffEntErr become Eas1BadSum/Eas2BadSum in CIAT0066TM 6.4.6 limits NIA05128-NIA05131 switch their ocf from raw to calibrated values; 7 parameters get new hard limits; the 90-450 check moves from NIA05131 to NIA05130 (whose raw 6000-6500 range goes), leaving NIA05131 with an ocf record but no ocp row 6.4.1 ("MCF and OCF Updated"), 6.4.4 (ocp for NIA05131); no note names the other ocp changes calibrations CIAP0002TM, CIAP0003TM, CIAP0005TM polynomials; command text table CIAT0068TC (used by ZIA58728); the unused command text table CIAT0069TC (SENS_EN) is removed 6.4.1 (MCF), 6.4.0; no note for CIAT0069TC unchanged all 2 885 parameters (description, type, calibration, unit), the 70 vdf names -

The four new failure IDs, 0xA88D-0xA890, are among the codes that ICD issue 6.1 lists as "not used" and deletes, and that IDB 5.1.0 removed as TM(1,8) packets in 2018: the values have been reused for the new summation errors.164748 Against the 2025 spacecraft MIB, v6.5.0 is almost a match: all 613 packets, all 6 535 plf entries, all 2 885 parameters (description, type, calibration) and all 1 054 pas values are present and equal, and the 80 polynomials differ only in number formatting. The exceptions are the time command ZIA58057 and the unused textual calibration CAAT0008TM (absent from the MIB); 243 parameter units (237 of them units that only the IDB gives, such as V or mA); 13 of the 538 command parameters, Boolean (PTC 1) in the IDB but enumerated (PTC 2, PFC 1) in the MIB (nine of them already so in the April 2020 release, which lacks the other four, the sensor flags PIA60091-PIA60094 of ZIA58950); the variable layouts of two compressed EAS burst packets, 58726 and 58889, where the MIB inserts 10 bit-field entries (NIAD4626-NIAD4635, overlapping their container words through offsets of -8) so that 36 of the IDB's 481 vpd entries move (the notes of 6.3.2 and 6.3.3 record fixes to exactly these packets); applicability criteria that the MIB adds to four of the 325 limit checks; and the verification of ZIA58950, which the MIB maps to stages 11 and 17 (report-based, 20 s, used by some 2 200 other, mostly platform, commands) instead of SWA's 58901 and 58907.48505147 Browse ZIA58951 and packet 58730.

The version record was not updated

The vdf of v6.5.0 holds the same 70 names as the 2021 set, ending at 6.3.x, with no record for 6.4.0-6.5.0; and its order differs, the last record being SWA_6.3.3_wa instead of SWA_6.3.4.4849 SCOS-2000 takes the database version name from the last vdf record imported, and VDF_NAME holds 8 characters, an over-long field being truncated with a warning.6364 This wiki's deduction from those rules: an import of v6.5.0 that reads the file in order would name the database after SWA_6.3.3_wa, truncated to SWA_6.3., not after 6.5.0 (see also SWA).

SQL used (v6.5.0 against the 2021 set and the 2025 MIB) 
-- swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite
ATTACH 'file:swa-idb.sqlite?mode=ro' AS a;
ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m;
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR
  FROM main.pid WHERE PID_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM a.pid);          -- 58730-58733
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM a.ccf);
SELECT rowid, VDF_NAME FROM main.vdf ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 3;          -- ... SWA_6.3.3_wa
SELECT x.TXP_FROM, y.TXP_ALTXT, x.TXP_ALTXT FROM main.txp x JOIN a.txp y
    ON x.TXP_NUMBR = y.TXP_NUMBR AND x.TXP_FROM = y.TXP_FROM WHERE x.TXP_ALTXT <> y.TXP_ALTXT;
SELECT count(*), sum(PID_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM m.pid)) FROM main.pid;     -- 613 | 613
SELECT count(*) FROM main.plf x JOIN m.plf y ON x.PLF_NAME = y.PLF_NAME AND x.PLF_SPID = y.PLF_SPID
   AND x.PLF_OFFBY = y.PLF_OFFBY AND x.PLF_OFFBI = y.PLF_OFFBI;              -- 6535
SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM m.ccf);  -- ZIA58057
SELECT a.VPD_TPSD, count(*) FROM main.vpd a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM m.vpd b
 WHERE a.VPD_TPSD = b.VPD_TPSD AND a.VPD_POS = b.VPD_POS AND a.VPD_NAME = b.VPD_NAME
   AND a.VPD_GRPSIZE = b.VPD_GRPSIZE AND a.VPD_OFFSET = b.VPD_OFFSET) GROUP BY 1;  -- 58726, 58889
SELECT x.OCP_NAME, y.OCP_RLCHK, y.OCP_VALPAR FROM main.ocp x JOIN m.ocp y
    ON y.OCP_NAME = x.OCP_NAME AND y.OCP_POS = x.OCP_POS
 WHERE ifnull(y.OCP_RLCHK, '') <> ifnull(x.OCP_RLCHK, '');                       -- 4 rows
SELECT PID_PI1_VAL, printf('0x%X', CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT)), PID_DESCR
  FROM main.pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' AND PID_STYPE = '2' ORDER BY CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT);
SELECT x.CPC_NAME, x.CPC_PTC || '/' || x.CPC_PFC, y.CPC_PTC || '/' || y.CPC_PFC FROM main.cpc x
  JOIN m.cpc y ON y.CPC_NAME = x.CPC_NAME WHERE x.CPC_PTC <> y.CPC_PTC;          -- 13 rows, 1/0 -> 2/1
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf x JOIN m.pcf y ON y.PCF_NAME = x.PCF_NAME
 WHERE ifnull(x.PCF_UNIT, '') <> ifnull(y.PCF_UNIT, '');                       -- 243
SELECT * FROM m.cvp WHERE CVP_TASK = 'ZIA58950';                               -- stages 11, 17
SELECT x.OCF_NAME, y.OCF_INTER, x.OCF_INTER FROM main.ocf x JOIN a.ocf y ON y.OCF_NAME = x.OCF_NAME
 WHERE x.OCF_INTER <> y.OCF_INTER;                                             -- NIA05128-NIA05131

docs.title: How the pieces fit
docs.text:
Question EID-A 1.0 SWA ICD 8.2 SWA IDB / MIB Physical link dual SpaceWire, time codes SpaceWire to OBDH and to each sensor - Packet format "TM and TC packets" PUS-A style headers per the packet ICD NOM_TC, PID_DFHSIZE 16 APIDs - Table 1 15 APIDs, partly moved to Annex 8 categories Commands single TC to enable software Tables 2-8, 7 managers 201 commands, CCF_ACK 9 Faults safe mode, event reports events, TARF/TECF, monitoring on service 200, SID 14 OBCP requests TM(1,2)/(1,8) per code, ocp limits Database "Inputs to Satellite Database: TBW" - IDB versions tied to ICD issues

The table summarises the sections above.8910222348

Inference

The documents show a division of labour: ESA's EID-A sets the physical interface and the behaviour (safe mode, event reports), the prime contractor's packet ICD sets the PUS layer, the instrument team's ICD maps the instrument onto it, and Planetek's IDB transcribes the ICD into MIB tables that the spacecraft MIB absorbs. The release notes' habit of citing ICD issues, and the near-identity of IDB v6.5.0 and the 2025 MIB, support this; the formal delivery route from IDB to MIB is not described in the available sources.
