docs.title: The Solar Orbiter MIB
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter Mission Information Base is the set of ASCII tables that tells the SCOS-2000 mission control system how to recognise every telemetry packet of the spacecraft, how to extract and calibrate every parameter, how to check limits, and how to encode, verify and sequence every telecommand. It follows the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001), whose issue 7.0 is published next to the MIB as the "MOC-applicable" issue.12 Because more than a hundred operational releases were posted publicly, it is the only flight MIB this wiki can analyse row by row.

Every number on this page comes from this wiki's own SQL queries on two releases:

  • 2025-09-16, MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL, the newest release (library page), and
  • 2020-04-16, MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL, the oldest (library page).

Both were loaded into read-only SQLite databases with one table per .dat file, using the ICD 7.2 column names where known. The queries are shown in collapsed "SQL used" blocks. The tables themselves are explained on the MIB data model and the per-table pages such as pcf; every parameter, packet and command can be opened in the MIB explorer.

docs.title: Where the releases come from
docs.text:
The SWA/PAS team's server at IRAP lists 111 dated release zips, from April 2020 to September 2025, in MIB/MIBs/, each also unpacked as a folder, plus latest/ and previous/ sets; the listing carries no description or terms of use.7 This wiki copied the first and last releases on 2026-11-05:

Release Zip size Copied (UTC) SHA-256 MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL 6 187 063 bytes 2026-11-05 14:24:03 c8ef0ea254d48b763333993b8710b6fc3d1db519e2d6c9629122c0f81cb13690 MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL 4 735 907 bytes 2026-11-05 14:26:42 a524903135d0a62c8aec3f83f58483b4f996e6c0fe966eb12c7e18cda2fb0ec7

The original URLs are https://solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/MIB/MIBs/<release>.zip.8 The instrument databases of two instruments are also publicly posted in the same table format: SWA on the same server (this wiki copied versions 6.3.4 and 6.5.0) and STIX on a separate server (version 2.26.38).37 They are analysed on Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database and Solar Orbiter STIX instrument database; how their definitions sit inside the spacecraft release is summarised in Instrument databases inside the release.

docs.title: Decoding the release name
docs.text:
The vdf table of each release has a single record. The ICD defines VDF_NAME (Char(8)) as the database version name, VDF_COMMENT as a free comment and VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE as release and issue numbers; the name is shown on displays and checked, for example, when a saved command stack is reloaded.9

Field 2020-04-16 2025-09-16 VDF_NAME 10720PFM 25925PFM VDF_COMMENT 20200416-CSW3.0.3p1_MAS6.51 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33 VDF_DOMAINID 0 0 VDF_RELEASE 10720 25925 VDF_ISSUE 651 733

These values are in the archive too: the SCOS-2000 packet header that the MCS files with every packet has DB Rel and DB Iss fields recording the VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE in force when the packet was archived.1011

MIB__ 20250916 M 259 25 PFM S001 _SOL
      |        | |   |  |   |    '-- mission (Solar Orbiter)
      |        | |   |  |   '------- not explained in the available sources
      |        | |   |  '----------- VDF_NAME suffix (meaning not stated)
      |        | |   '-------------- two-digit year (25)
      |        | '------------------ day of year (259 = 16 September 2025)
      |        '-------------------- literal "M"
      '----------------------------- release date YYYYMMDD

Inference

The decoding above is this wiki's reading of the two releases, not a documented convention. The three digits after M equal the day of year of the date (259 for 2025-09-16, 107 for 2020-04-16), which the project's survey also observed on the IRAP listing;7 the next two digits equal the two-digit year; and the five digits together are VDF_RELEASE (25925, 10720) and the first five characters of VDF_NAME. The comment names a Central Software (CSW) version - CSW being the OBC software of the ICD13 - and a "MAS" version whose number matches VDF_ISSUE (7.33 / 733, 6.51 / 651). The meanings of PFM, S001 and MAS are not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Files and row counts
docs.text:
The 2025 release contains 59 .dat files - the 53 ICD tables, three mission files (ASW_sw_para, pcf_glob_det, dup) and three more mission files s13a, s13p and s13t dated June 2021 - and a synthetic/ directory with 1 582 OL expression files; the 2020 release has the first 56 files and 390 synthetic files.1112 The ICD names each ASCII file after its table in lower case with the extension .dat, and each dynamic synthetic parameter is an extension-less file named after the parameter.14 Records are TAB-separated, one per line, as the ICD specifies; the pcf file uses all 23 fields of ICD 7.0, whose importer accepts 19 to 23.11315

Family Table 2020-04-16 2025-09-16 Change Parameters pcf 102 104 126 745 +24.1% Packets pid / tpcf 9 027 11 150 +23.5% pic 228 256 +12.3% plf 326 492 400 792 +22.8% vpd 18 770 19 863 +5.8% Calibration cur 1 586 1 974 +24.5% caf / cap 676 / 7 753 679 / 7 830 +0.4% / +1.0% txf / txp 955 / 31 904 1 003 / 35 032 +5.0% / +9.8% mcf / lgf 226 / 0 229 / 0 +1.3% Checks ocf / ocp 3 304 / 4 686 5 338 / 7 369 +61.6% / +57.3% Synthetics synthetic/ files 390 1 582 x4.1 Commands ccf 5 238 5 454 +4.1% cdf / cpc 44 944 / 6 947 47 609 / 7 155 +5.9% / +3.0% prf / prv 531 / 631 565 / 1 072 +6.4% / +69.9% paf / pas 605 / 9 741 624 / 11 834 +3.1% / +21.5% cca / ccs 100 / 1 233 99 / 1 226 -1.0% / -0.6% ptv 0 5 new TC headers tcp / pcpc / pcdf 4 / 6 / 20 4 / 7 / 20 Verification cvs / cve / cvp 206 / 171 / 10 277 206 / 171 / 10 697 +4.1% (cvp) Sequences csf 2 701 3 404 +26.0% css / sdf / csp 9 089 / 30 985 / 5 598 13 879 / 50 014 / 10 981 +52.7% / +61.4% / +96.2% Displays dpf / dpc, spf / spc 33 / 626, 1 / 5 33 / 626, 1 / 5 unchanged Groups grp / grpk 1 / 4 2 / 4 Routing dst 1 1 Mission files ASW_sw_para / pcf_glob_det / dup 85 430 / 52 417 / 36 105 222 / 56 631 / 69 +23.2% / +8.0% / +91.7% Version vdf 1 1

The tables lgf, gpf/gpc, ppf/ppc, grpa, the parameter-set tables pst, psv, cps, pvs and psm are empty in both releases.1112

The numbers show where the work went in five years of flight: telemetry decoding grew by about a quarter, ground monitoring checks by 60%, the number of sequences by a quarter and their content (elements, element values, formal parameters) by half to almost double, while the command catalogue itself grew only 4%.

SQL used (versions and row counts) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite and solo-2020-04-16.sqlite
SELECT * FROM vdf;
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf;      -- repeated for every table
SELECT count(*) FROM synthetic;

docs.title: Nature, type and calibration category
docs.text:
Of the 126 745 monitoring parameters of 2025, 125 161 are raw telemetry (PCF_NATUR = R), 1 582 are dynamic OL synthetics (D) and 2 are saved synthetics (S); the ICD defines these natures, plus P (SPEL), H (hard-coded) and C (constant), which Solar Orbiter does not use.1116 By calibration category, 100 087 are numerical (N), 26 538 status (S, textual calibration) and 120 text strings (T), the categories defined for PCF_CATEG.1117 The most common types are PTC 3 unsigned integers (50 341), PTC 5 reals (29 718) and PTC 2 enumerations (29 443); see MIB parameter types for the full breakdown.11

107 791 parameters are placed in fixed packets by plf and 2 720 in variable packets by vpd. 15 067 raw parameters appear in neither; 11 945 of those are listed in the mission-specific ASW_sw_para file and 10 786 are "detail" entries of pcf_glob_det (see mission-specific files).11

docs.title: Subsystems
docs.text:
PCF_SUBSYS is defined by the ICD only as the name of the group to which the parameter belongs, a future filtering aid.19 Solar Orbiter fills it with numbers for software subsystems and instruments and with unit names for platform equipment. Counting, for each value, the APIDs of the packets in which its parameters are placed shows what each number stands for:1123

PCF_SUBSYS 2020 2025 Packets mostly on process ID (APID ÷ 16) Reading 2 28 842 29 152 11, and ground APIDs 1953-1983 AOCS 1 20 579 22 607 10, 14, 13, 16, ground APIDs Data management (DMS) and OBC software (blank) 3 329 18 610 124, 13, 14 on-board monitoring definitions, RIU, ground 6 16 155 16 934 16, 13 thermal control and platform 4 2 955 7 560 30-33 and ground APIDs SSMM 101 3 713 3 723 63-66 MAG 8 3 549 3 569 14 system control 102 2 887 3 400 57-60 EUI 106 3 067 3 067 75-81 RPW 109 2 886 2 881 95-99 SWA PCDU_A, PCDU_B 1 687, 1 675 2 224, 1 675 13, 14 PCDU A and B (EPS units managed by the platform application) 107 1 725 1 740 82-84 SOLOHI 7 1 385 1 467 14, 12 payload application 108 1 032 1 033 85-89 SPICE 5 858 860 11, 40, 41 star trackers 104 767 824 72-74 PHI 103 685 685 50-55, 100 EPD 105 665 683 90, 94 STIX RIU 414 638 13 RIU (gives access to FSS, CPS, I-boom and thermistors) 110 577 620 67-69 METIS others 2 793 25 equipment names (OBC, APMH_A/B, APMM_A/B, DEU_A/B, SADE_A/B, eight IMU_xx, RW_1-RW_4, DST_1/2, EGSE_GEN, Z_STD_DE) and the numbers 250 and 3

Inference

The "Reading" column is deduced by matching the process IDs of the packets to the Annex 8 process allocation of the Solar Orbiter packet structure ICD (10 DMS, 11 AOCS, 12 payload, 13 platform, 14 system control, 16 thermal; 30-32 SSMM; 40/41 star trackers; instruments 50-104).25 The MIB itself does not name the subsystem numbers. Instrument subsystems 101-110 are not in alphabetical order (MAG, EUI, EPD, PHI, STIX, RPW, SOLOHI, SPICE, SWA, METIS).

Two of the readings are supported by the instrument teams' own databases: the SWA database gives PCF_SUBSYS = 109 to all its parameters except four fillers, and the STIX database gives 105 to 673 of its 681 parameters and uses 105 as the domain identifier of its vdf record.3435

docs.title: Name prefixes
docs.text:
Parameter names have at most 8 characters (126 502 have 8, 243 have 7); 126 740 of them begin with N (the remaining five are four ZZP... fillers and one DUM... "ALWAYS_VALID").11 Commands begin with Z (5 441 of 5 454), sequences with A (all 3 404), packet mnemonics in tpcf with Y (11 131 of 11 150), calibrations almost always with C (all numerical and polynomial ones; all textual ones but AYMODELE and PARAMIDTM) and command parameters mostly with P or R.11 The second and third letters group the parameters:

Prefix 2020 2025 Examples and owner NCA 29 132 29 563 AOCS (MeasTaccwrtIRFSC) NCF 14 946 15 228 platform application NCD 11 353 13 414 data management (OBCHP_PTM_TC_Packet_ID) NSM 2 955 7 568 SSMM NCX 6 458 6 490 SGM group contents in TM(132,2) reports on ground APID 1955 NPW 3 410 3 962 PCDU NCS 3 851 3 928 system control NXF, NXT, NXA, NXL, NXS 0 13 713 on-board monitoring definitions per CSW process (new) NIM 3 737 3 747 MAG NTC 2 936 3 667 thermal control NRU 2 462 3 356 RIU NIU 2 887 3 400 EUI NIW 3 067 3 067 RPW NIA 2 887 2 882 SWA NIH 1 725 1 748 SOLOHI NCL 1 395 1 479 payload application NIC 1 032 1 033 SPICE NST 862 862 star trackers NIP 767 820 PHI NMU 808 808 IMUs NID 690 690 EPD NIX 666 687 STIX NIT 577 620 METIS NAH, NAM 535, 526 535, 526 APME-H (HGA) and APME-M (MGA) units NDM, NDS 414, 306 414, 309 DEU and DST units NYG, NYN, NYC, NYM, NYP 197, 0, 0, 0, 118 198, 172, 158, 156, 118 ground and EGSE (ERT sec, LMS_NNO, LMS_CEB, LMS_MLG, PSS)

Inference

Solar Orbiter's naming convention is not documented in the library sources. The pattern is consistent with: first letter = object kind (N monitoring parameter, Z command, A sequence, Y packet, C calibration, P command parameter); second letter = owner family (C central software, I instrument, S SSMM/STR/SADE, P PCDU, R RIU and wheels, A antenna mechanisms, D DEU/transponder, M IMU, T thermal, X derived monitoring definitions, Y ground); third letter = application or instrument. The instrument letters are M MAG, U EUI, D EPD, P PHI, X STIX, W RPW, H SOLOHI, C SPICE, A SWA and T METIS, the same letters as in the commands (ZIA... goes to the SWA APID 1532, ZIT... to METIS APID 1084). Other ESA projects used different conventions, for example SPIRE's SM/SC prefixes.33

The instrument databases support the instrument letters for two cases: every SWA database parameter but four ZZPAD fillers is named NIA... and every SWA command ZIA..., and every STIX parameter but four fillers is NIX... and every STIX command ZIX....3435

SQL used (parameters) 
SELECT PCF_NATUR, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PCF_CATEG, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT PCF_PTC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf WHERE PCF_NATUR = 'R'
   AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PLF_NAME FROM plf)
   AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT VPD_NAME FROM vpd);          -- 15067
-- subsystem counts in both releases
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
SELECT a.s, n25, coalesce(n20, 0)
  FROM (SELECT PCF_SUBSYS s, count(*) n25 FROM main.pcf GROUP BY 1) a
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT PCF_SUBSYS s2, count(*) n20 FROM o.pcf GROUP BY 1) b ON a.s = b.s2
 ORDER BY n25 DESC;
-- which on-board process the parameters of each subsystem are packed by
SELECT c.PCF_SUBSYS, CAST(p.PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 AS proc, count(*)
  FROM pcf c JOIN plf l ON l.PLF_NAME = c.PCF_NAME JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = l.PLF_SPID
 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;
-- name prefixes
SELECT substr(PCF_NAME, 1, 3), count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT length(PCF_NAME), count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1;                -- 7: 243, 8: 126502
SELECT substr(CCF_CNAME, 1, 1), count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;

docs.title: APIDs and packets
docs.text:
The 2025 release defines 11 150 packets (SPIDs) on 293 distinct APIDs, with 193 distinct type/subtype pairs across 66 service types; the 2020 release had 9 027 packets on 268 APIDs.1112 The packetiser recognises a packet by its APID, type, subtype and up to two extra identification fields located by pic, and looks up the SPID in pid; APIDs 0 to 2047 are for spacecraft packets and 2048 and above for packets generated on the ground.2324 Solar Orbiter's APID is a 7-bit process ID followed by a 4-bit packet category (see the mission page), so every APID can be decoded:25

Component (process IDs) APIDs 2020 APIDs 2025 Packets 2020 Packets 2025 OBC Central Software (10-16) 44 44 3 143 3 358 EGSE process range 112-127 (ground-defined APIDs 1937-1996, plus the idle-packet APID 2047) 31 45 1 854 2 438 EUI (57-62) 14 18 783 2 055 SWA (95-99) 13 15 600 613 SPICE (85-89, 101-104) 21 21 451 451 EPD (50-56, 100) 20 20 319 319 RPW (75-81) 28 28 287 287 SOLOHI (82-84) 21 21 284 284 SSMM (30-32, plus APID 533 "SSMM FDIR TM" on process 33, a spare in Annex 8) 19 19 244 260 METIS (67-71) 11 11 259 260 STIX (90-94) 9 9 246 246 Star trackers (40, 41) 12 12 244 244 MAG (63-66) 11 11 196 207 PHI (72-74) 11 10 112 117 OBC hardware, time, frames (0, 2) 3 3 5 5 Non-spacecraft APIDs 2048-2065 0 6 0 6

The SWA row can be checked against the instrument's own interface document: the 13 SWA APIDs of the 2020 release are exactly the 13 process ID and category pairs of Table 1 of the SWA DPU Communications ICD issue 8.2 (2019), and the two added by 2025, 1542 and 1545, date from SWA database 6.3.3 (October 2021), whose release note cites an ICD issue 8.3 that is not in the library.38361211

By packet category (for on-board APIDs below 1792), events dominate: category 7 holds 5 694 packet definitions on 27 APIDs, category 1 (verification) 1 804 on 31 APIDs, category 12 (science) 334 on 45 APIDs, category 9 (dumps) 259 and category 4 (routine HK) 162 on 37 APIDs.11 The many event and verification definitions are a consequence of the PID key: each event identifier or failure code gets its own SPID, so one report type becomes hundreds of packets (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS).

docs.title: Special APIDs
docs.text:
APID Packets What it is 0 1 TM(9,2) "Time Report", the time packet (explorer) 1 3 good, bad and idle complete transfer frames (frame-level pseudo-packets) 34 1 OBC_HPTM_packet, process 2 category 2 1966 18 MCS-internal packets, types 160-166, 251 (explorer) 1953-1996 (except 1966) 2 403 ground "virtual" APIDs carrying re-identified copies of dumps, events and monitoring reports 2047 1 idle packet 2048-2065 6 LMS_NNO, LMS_CEB, LMS_MLG low/high frequency packets, no data field header

The time, idle, frame and internal packets match the DDID and the packet structure ICD.292711 The 2048-2065 range is the one the ICD reserves for packets not generated by the spacecraft.23 The station codes NNO, CEB and MLG match the New Norcia, Cebreros and Malargüe stations of the DDID's ground station list, but what "LMS" means is not stated in the available sources.30

The virtual APIDs 1953 to 1996 are the most interesting. Their PIC rules add a second identification field: for example events TM(5,1) on APID 1975 are split by an 8-bit field at octet 18, giving 12 packets "LEOP_AS_Step_1_Executed" to "Step_12"; TM(12,9) monitoring list reports on APIDs 1986-1990 are split into parts #1 to #3 by an 8-bit field at octet 19 and a second 8-bit field deep inside the packet (octet 883 to 2755 depending on the APID); TM(6,6) dumps on 1961, 1965, 1976 and 1977 by a 32-bit field at octet 18.11 The mission file dup.dat lists 69 (SPID, APID) pairs whose SPIDs are ordinary packets of real APIDs - for instance SPID 10153 (event 2753 on APID 231) is paired with APID 1975.11

Inference

dup.dat appears to tell a mission-specific ground process to duplicate selected packets onto a virtual APID, where the PIC and PID tables then decode them with a finer identification than the spacecraft's APID allows. This explains why APID 1975 holds 12 variants of one LEOP event and why APIDs 1986-1990 and 1992-1996 hold per-application monitoring list and functional monitoring status reports (1991 carries star tracker 2 mode transition events). Neither dup.dat nor this mechanism is described in the ICD or the DDID.

docs.title: Packet sizes
docs.text:
The ICD defines TPCF_SIZE as the total size of the SCOS-2000 packet, recommending the source packet length plus the SCOS-2000 header (64 or 76 octets depending on the header version), and 0 for truly variable packets.21 The time packet has TPCF_SIZE = 14, exactly 6 octets of primary header plus the 8 data octets of Annex 4,1128 and the SWA inter-instrument packet has 33, its source packet length (see the SWA page).

Inference

These values suggest that Solar Orbiter fills TPCF_SIZE with the source packet length rather than with the SCOS-2000 packet size that the ICD recommends. The field is not used by SCOS-2000 itself, and the mission's convention is not stated in the available sources.

Across the release, 2 325 packets have size 0, 7 487 are at most 64 octets, 329 between 65 and 256, 936 between 257 and 1 024, 67 between 1 025 and 4 112, and 6 above:11

SPID APID Packet TPCF_SIZE plf entries 64902-64907 1940 TM(3,25) "PSS HK Packet 2" to "7" 4 136 31 each 65037 1955 TM(132,2) "SGM-R Grp 18 AOCS_PROFILE_SSE p1" 4 112 983 65866 1955 TM(132,2) "SA Nominal Steering Profile part 1" 4 112 1 026 65909 1986 TM(12,9) "AOCS - Monitoring List Report #1" 4 099 1 275 80028 483 TM(142,7) "SSMM Router Configuration Report" 1 084 3 816 (the most of any packet)

Six EGSE packets on APID 1940 (process 121, in the EGSE range) are larger than the 4 112-octet maximum that the ICD sets for on-board TM; the largest spacecraft packets reach that maximum exactly.2711 See SSMM router report and AOCS monitoring list in the explorer.

SQL used (APIDs and packets) 
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT PID_APID), count(DISTINCT PID_TYPE || '/' || PID_STYPE),
       count(DISTINCT PID_TYPE) FROM pid;                         -- 11150 | 293 | 193 | 66
-- decode APID = process ID * 16 + category
SELECT CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 AS proc, count(DISTINCT PID_APID), count(*)
  FROM pid GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
SELECT CAST(PID_APID AS INT) & 15 AS cat, count(DISTINCT PID_APID), count(*)
  FROM pid WHERE CAST(PID_APID AS INT) < 1792 GROUP BY 1;
SELECT * FROM pic ORDER BY CAST(PIC_TYPE AS INT), CAST(PIC_STYPE AS INT), PIC_APID;
SELECT d.COL1, d.COL2, p.PID_APID, p.PID_TYPE, p.PID_STYPE, p.PID_PI1_VAL, p.PID_DESCR
  FROM dup d LEFT JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = d.COL1;
-- sizes
SELECT t.TPCF_SPID, t.TPCF_SIZE, p.PID_APID, p.PID_TYPE, p.PID_STYPE, p.PID_DESCR,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM plf WHERE PLF_SPID = t.TPCF_SPID)
  FROM tpcf t JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = t.TPCF_SPID
 ORDER BY CAST(TPCF_SIZE AS INT) DESC LIMIT 15;
SELECT PLF_SPID, count(*) n FROM plf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 3;

docs.title: Calibrations and checks
Synthetic parameters
docs.text:
The synthetic directory holds one OL file per dynamic synthetic parameter, read by the importer from the directory configured for OL expressions.20 The 2025 release has 1 582 files, one for each D parameter, against 390 in 2020: 1 195 were added, 3 removed and 75 changed.1112 The expressions average 482 characters; the longest, for NYGSX003 "Spacecraft Downlink Acti...", has 3 995. Their outputs are mostly Booleans (PTC 1, 1 097), enumerations (PTC 2, 208), reals (119) and unsigned integers (85).11

Most of the growth is in the NX* family: 996 synthetics (283 NXF, 266 NXA, 223 NXT, 158 NXL, 66 NXS), all but one of which (NXAD4423 "PAS_MODE_CHECK") are "consistency" flags. The comment at the top of, for example, NXFF001D "PID13_F001_CONSISTENCY" says that it checks whether the monitors reported in the generic service 142 packet of process 13 were parsed in the intended order, returning 1 when the parsed and intended monitoring IDs match.11 Simpler examples are the NCSSZ... validity formulas, which return 1 when either of two power-status parameters of an instrument reads "ON".11 The OL language is described on Synthetic parameters and the OL language.

SQL used (synthetics) 
SELECT count(*), avg(length(SOURCE)), max(length(SOURCE)) FROM synthetic;
SELECT substr(NAME, 1, 3), count(*) FROM synthetic GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT p.PCF_PTC, count(*) FROM synthetic s JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = s.NAME GROUP BY 1;
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
SELECT count(*) FROM main.synthetic WHERE NAME NOT IN (SELECT NAME FROM o.synthetic);  -- 1195
SELECT count(*) FROM main.synthetic s JOIN o.synthetic t ON s.NAME = t.NAME
 WHERE s.SOURCE <> t.SOURCE;                                                         -- 75

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
The 5 454 commands of 2025 use four header layouts: NOM_TC for 5 318 normal PUS commands, HPC1_TC for 125 CPDU commands without secondary header, NO_HDR for 5 on-board control directives - the COP-1 control frames UNLOCK and SETVR (CCF_CTYPE = F) and the control segments RESET, REIN_TTR and TC_ONLY (CCF_CTYPE = R) - and NOS2KHDR for 6 ground link and session control commands of type 251 ("GENERIC OPEN TC LINK", "OPEN SESSION", ...); the layouts are dissected on PUS packet structures.114 Each command's APID decodes like the TM APIDs, always with category 12:26

APID Process Destination Commands 2020 2025 Name prefix 172 10 CSW data management (incl. hardware commands via service 2) 1 935 1 971 ZCS, ZCD, ZPW, ZRU, ZMU, ... 236 14 CSW system control 946 966 ZCS 188 11 CSW AOCS 424 454 ZCA 1532 95 SWA 198 200 ZIA 1164 72 PHI 186 199 ZIP 492, 508, 524 30-32 SSMM, SSMM A, SSMM B 125 210 ZSM 44 2 CPDU (HPC-1, MAP ID 0) 125 125 ZBC 1020 63 MAG 113 126 ZIM 1084 67 METIS 125 126 ZIT 924 57 EUI 121 122 ZIU 220 13 CSW platform 113 118 ZCF 1324 82 SOLOHI 102 102 ZIH 1452 90 STIX 99 98 ZIX 652, 668 40, 41 star trackers 1 and 2 98 98 ZST 1372 85 SPICE 92 91 ZIC 268 16 CSW thermal 74 84 ZTC 204 12 CSW payload 76 78 ZCL 812, 876, 796 50, 54, 49 EPD; payload broadcast 123 123 ZID 1212-1308 75-81 RPW (7 APIDs) 138 138 ZIW 1948 121 EGSE "PSS" 14 14 ZYP 1964 122 ground link and session control (service 251, NOS2KHDR) 6 6 EGENRTCC, ESESIONO, ... (none) - frame-level directives 5 5 UNLOCK, SETVR, RESET, ...

CCF_SUBSYS, the "identifier of the subsystem which the command belongs to",22 uses the same numbers as PCF_SUBSYS: 1 (1 971 commands), 8 (976), 2 (447), 4 (210), the instruments 101-110, 5 (98, the star tracker commands), 6 (199) and 7 (78); 150 commands have no subsystem.11 Command sequences (3 404) all start with A; the second letter groups them (AI instrument 1 474, AD data management 875, AA AOCS 331, AT thermal 304, ...). The largest is AIPF981A "PHI copy cal data" with 312 elements, followed by ASYF100K "TM MODE Any to SAFE" with 310.11 Sequences and their tables are on Command sequences and parameter sets.

SQL used (commands and sequences) 
SELECT CCF_PKTID, CCF_CTYPE, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2;
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
SELECT CCF_APID, CAST(CCF_APID AS INT) >> 4, count(*),
       (SELECT count(*) FROM o.ccf b WHERE b.CCF_APID = a.CCF_APID)
  FROM main.ccf a GROUP BY CCF_APID ORDER BY CAST(CCF_APID AS INT);

SELECT CSF_NAME, CSF_DESC, CSF_ELEMS FROM csf ORDER BY CAST(CSF_ELEMS AS INT) DESC LIMIT 5;

docs.title: Mission-specific files
docs.text:
Six files of the release are not ICD tables.11 Their columns have no names in the release, so the descriptions below are read from the data.

File Rows 2025 Content observed ASW_sw_para.dat 105 222 a name and an on-board software symbol (always filled); the names are 77 565 monitoring parameters (e.g. NIA00102), 7 665 packet mnemonics, 3 676 command parameters, 2 221 commands and 14 095 names found in no MIB table (13 727 starting with B, e.g. BCAY0000 - SSEA_SEGMENTS_END_TIME_C); third column mostly empty, a, or a comment such as "padding field of sSE segments" pcf_glob_det.dat 56 631 a "global" parameter, a "detail" parameter and a number: e.g. NAH0Z000 "APMHA_TM_1 [000]" with details NAHD0000 "APMHA_Mode" (0), NAHD0001 "APMHA_Mode trans" (3), ...; 8 704 globals, all names present in pcf dup.dat 69 (SPID, virtual APID) pairs, see Special APIDs s13a.dat 7 file attributes: PLAIN, OBCP, DEL "DELAYED TC", IMM "IMMEDIATE TC", PAYLOAD "PAYLOAD CONTEXT", INVALID, OTHER s13p.dat 11 memory partitions with numbers 161-195: TCFA "OMM TC Files (A)", OBCA "OMM OBCPs (A)", SYSA "OMM System Files (A)", ..., CSWA "SGM-EEPROM CSW TC Files (A)" s13t.dat 12 file types: OBCP, SCOS0-SCOS3 "SCOS stack file", CSF0-CSF3 (mixed, plain, time-tagged and backup-MTL TC sequences), PLAIN, ALL, UNKNOWN

Inference

ASW_sw_para most likely maps MIB names (and other on-board items) to the application software's symbol table, which would explain why 11 945 parameters that sit in no packet are still defined: they are data-pool variables reachable by dump or parameter-management services. pcf_glob_det appears to relate a whole word to the bit-field parameters inside it, the number being a bit position. The s13* files describe service 13 file uploads: the attribute names match the s13ObFileAttribute values that the DDID lists for commands uplinked as files (PLAIN, OBCP, TC_DELAYED, TC_IMMEDIATE, PAYLOAD_CONTEXT),31 the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 6 match the service 13 file attributes OBCP, delayed TC sequence, immediate TC sequence and "Other" of the packet structure ICD,32 and the CSF types match SCOS-2000 sequence files. None of these files is described in the ICD or the DDID.

SQL used (mission-specific files) 
SELECT * FROM asw_sw_para LIMIT 5;
SELECT COL3, count(*) FROM asw_sw_para GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5;
SELECT sum(COL1 IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf)), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT TPCF_NAME FROM tpcf)),
       sum(COL1 IN (SELECT CPC_NAME FROM cpc)), sum(COL1 IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM ccf)),
       count(*) FROM asw_sw_para;                     -- 77565 | 7665 | 3676 | 2221 | 105222
SELECT a.COL1, a.COL2, a.COL3, p.PCF_DESCR, q.PCF_DESCR
  FROM pcf_glob_det a JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = a.COL1 JOIN pcf q ON q.PCF_NAME = a.COL2 LIMIT 6;
SELECT count(DISTINCT COL1), count(DISTINCT COL2) FROM pcf_glob_det;
SELECT * FROM s13a; SELECT * FROM s13p; SELECT * FROM s13t;
WITH o AS (SELECT PCF_NAME n FROM pcf WHERE PCF_NATUR = 'R'
             AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PLF_NAME FROM plf)
             AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT VPD_NAME FROM vpd))
SELECT count(*), sum(n IN (SELECT COL1 FROM asw_sw_para)),
       sum(n IN (SELECT COL2 FROM pcf_glob_det)) FROM o;          -- 15067 | 11945 | 10786

docs.title: From 2020 to 2025: what changed
docs.text:
Comparing names and keys between the two releases:1112

Object (key) Added Removed Changed Net Parameters (PCF_NAME) 24 801 160 407 descriptions, 506 type/calibration/unit definitions +24 641 Packets (PID_SPID) 2 135 12 568 key or description changes +2 123 APIDs 26 1 +25 Commands (CCF_CNAME) 239 23 260 description/APID/type/parameter-count changes +216 Sequences (CSF_NAME) 790 87 +703 Synthetic files 1 195 3 75 expressions +1 192 
flowchart LR
  A["April 2020<br/>MIB 10720PFM<br/>CSW 3.0.3p1, MAS 6.51<br/>102 104 parameters<br/>9 027 packets, 268 APIDs<br/>5 238 commands"] --> B["September 2025<br/>MIB 25925PFM<br/>CSW 3.1.2, MAS 7.33<br/>126 745 parameters<br/>11 150 packets, 293 APIDs<br/>5 454 commands"]

Where the growth went:

  • On-board monitoring decoded on ground. 13 713 new NX* parameters and 996 consistency synthetics decode the TM(12,9) monitoring list reports and TM(142,11) functional monitoring status reports of each CSW application, placed on ten new virtual APIDs, 1986-1990 and 1992-1996 (AOCS, payload, platform, system and thermal).11
  • SSMM. 4 616 new NSM parameters, mostly in the SSMM router configuration report and in dumps of SSMM memory controller registers on new APIDs 1980-1983.11
  • EUI events. Two new event APIDs (951 and 967) with 620 event packets each, plus new report APIDs 934 and 950 (category 6); packets of type 5 make up 1 496 of the 2 135 new packets.11
  • Dumps and SGM. 416 new TM(131,x) and 94 new TM(141,x) packets (snapshot, OBDB and direct read reports).11
  • SWA reports. New APIDs 1542 and 1545, to which the 2025 release moves (with their SPIDs) nine SWA parameter and debug reports and 54 memory dump and check packets that the 2020 release had on APID 1593; nine new report packets of the same names replace them on 1593. The SWA database release notes date the move to version 6.3.3 (11/10/2021) and the nine copies on APID 1593 to 6.3.3_wa (04/11/2021) (see the SWA page).111236
  • Ground packets. Six non-spacecraft LMS_ packets on APIDs 2048-2065 and their 486 NYN/NYC/NYM parameters.11
  • Commands. 88 new SSMM commands, 44 new data management, 30 AOCS and 22 system control commands.11

What disappeared is small but telling. Among the 12 removed packets, APID 1163 (PHI context data, TM(22,2)) is gone, and so are two SADE recovery events, two PHI events, an SGM error event, two thermal snapshot events, an SGM group report on APID 1955, an SSMM direct read report and two EUI reports.11 Among the 23 removed commands are the four TC(9,128) "Set OBT" variants and every TC(9,129) "Accept time update" command of the instruments and the SSMM (EPD, MAG, METIS, PHI, EUI, STIX, SPICE, SWA, SSMM, SSMM A and B).11 The instrument-side definitions kept the command: the SWA DPU ICD lists TC(9,129) "Accept Time update" among the PUS services the DPU handles, and the SWA database 6.5.0 of June 2025 and the STIX database 2.26.38 still define ZIA58057 and ZIX09129, so the removal was made on the spacecraft database side.393435 The time services are discussed on How Solar Orbiter uses PUS.

SQL used (2020-2025 differences) 
-- run on solo-2025-09-16.sqlite
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf WHERE PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM o.pcf);   -- 24801
SELECT count(*) FROM o.pcf WHERE PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM main.pcf);   -- 160
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pid WHERE PID_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM o.pid);   -- 2135
SELECT count(*) FROM o.pid WHERE PID_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM main.pid);   -- 12
SELECT count(*) FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM o.ccf); -- 239
SELECT count(*) FROM o.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf); -- 23
SELECT count(*) FROM main.csf WHERE CSF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT CSF_NAME FROM o.csf);   -- 790
SELECT count(*) FROM o.csf WHERE CSF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT CSF_NAME FROM main.csf);   -- 87
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf a JOIN o.pcf b ON a.PCF_NAME = b.PCF_NAME
 WHERE a.PCF_DESCR <> b.PCF_DESCR;                                               -- 407
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf a JOIN o.pcf b ON a.PCF_NAME = b.PCF_NAME
 WHERE a.PCF_PTC <> b.PCF_PTC OR a.PCF_PFC <> b.PCF_PFC OR a.PCF_CURTX <> b.PCF_CURTX
    OR a.PCF_CATEG <> b.PCF_CATEG OR a.PCF_UNIT <> b.PCF_UNIT;                    -- 506
SELECT substr(PCF_NAME, 1, 3), count(*) FROM main.pcf
 WHERE PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM o.pcf) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT PID_APID, count(*), min(PID_DESCR) FROM main.pid
 WHERE PID_APID NOT IN (SELECT PID_APID FROM o.pid) GROUP BY 1;

docs.title: Instrument databases inside the release
docs.text:
The SWA and STIX instrument databases are publicly posted in the same table format, so their definitions can be compared row by row with the September 2025 release. Both are almost entirely contained in it:343511

Comparison with the 2025 release SWA database 6.5.0 (2025-06-17) STIX database 2.26.38 (files of 2024-02-02) Parameters present, with the same description, PTC/PFC and calibration 2 885 of 2 885 681 of 681 ... of which with a different unit 243 10 ... of which the release flags for DARC (PCF_DARC = 1), a field the databases lack 335 300 Packets with the same APID, type, subtype, identification value and description 613 of 613 246 of 246 Fixed layout entries (plf) with the same SPID and offsets 6 535 of 6 535 926 of 927 Commands present 200 of 201 99 of 100 Command elements (cdf) identical 1 147 of 1 184 1 373 of 1 377 Polynomial calibrations numerically equal 80 of 80 7 of 7 Limit checks (ocp) with the same limits 325 of 325 32 of 32 Synthetic parameters none in the database 3 of 3, identical OL source

What the spacecraft release adds or changes is small and mission-level: the DARC flags; for SWA, applicability conditions on four limit checks, the spacecraft verification stages 11 and 17 for the cadence command ZIA58950 and the synthetic NIASX001 "PAS_IN_SCIENCE"; for STIX, ten NIX?Z40x parameters and the command ZIXX0128 "STIX Information Distribution Aligned"; and for both, the removal of the TC(9,129) command.343511 Every SWA packet and command of the release is in the 6.5.0 database, and every STIX packet is in 2.26.38.343511 The details are on the SWA page and the STIX page.

Inference

The comparison indicates that the spacecraft MIB is assembled by importing each instrument team's database and adding mission-level fields and decisions on top. How and by whom this is done is not stated in the available sources; the 2007 Experiment Interface Document Part A leaves its section on instrument inputs to the satellite database to be written (TBW).40 The other eight instruments' databases are not in the library.

SQL used (instrument databases against the 2025 release) 
-- run on swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite and on stix-idb-2.26.38.sqlite
ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m;
SELECT count(*), sum(ifnull(a.PCF_UNIT, '') <> ifnull(b.PCF_UNIT, '')) FROM main.pcf a JOIN m.pcf b USING (PCF_NAME)
 WHERE a.PCF_DESCR = b.PCF_DESCR AND a.PCF_PTC = b.PCF_PTC AND a.PCF_PFC = b.PCF_PFC
   AND a.PCF_CURTX IS b.PCF_CURTX;                                          -- 2885 | 243; 681 | 10
SELECT count(*) FROM m.pcf WHERE PCF_DARC = '1' AND PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM main.pcf);  -- 335; 300
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pid a JOIN m.pid b USING (PID_SPID)
 WHERE a.PID_APID = b.PID_APID AND a.PID_TYPE = b.PID_TYPE AND a.PID_STYPE = b.PID_STYPE
   AND a.PID_DESCR = b.PID_DESCR AND a.PID_PI1_VAL IS b.PID_PI1_VAL;         -- 613; 246
SELECT count(*) FROM main.plf a JOIN m.plf b ON a.PLF_NAME = b.PLF_NAME AND a.PLF_SPID = b.PLF_SPID
   AND a.PLF_OFFBY = b.PLF_OFFBY AND a.PLF_OFFBI = b.PLF_OFFBI;              -- 6535; 926
SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM m.ccf);   -- ZIA58057; ZIX09129
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM main.cdf INTERSECT SELECT * FROM m.cdf);          -- 1147; 1373
SELECT count(*) FROM main.mcf a JOIN m.mcf b USING (MCF_IDENT)
 WHERE CAST(a.MCF_POL1 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL1 AS REAL) AND CAST(a.MCF_POL2 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL2 AS REAL)
   AND CAST(a.MCF_POL3 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL3 AS REAL) AND CAST(a.MCF_POL4 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL4 AS REAL)
   AND CAST(a.MCF_POL5 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL5 AS REAL);                          -- 80; 7
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT OCP_NAME, OCP_POS, OCP_TYPE, OCP_LVALU, OCP_HVALU FROM main.ocp
            INTERSECT SELECT OCP_NAME, OCP_POS, OCP_TYPE, OCP_LVALU, OCP_HVALU FROM m.ocp);  -- 325; 32
SELECT count(*) FROM main.synthetic a JOIN m.synthetic b USING (NAME) WHERE a.SOURCE = b.SOURCE;  -- 0; 3
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR FROM m.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME LIKE 'ZIX%'
   AND CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf);                  -- ZIXX0128 (STIX run)

docs.title: Quality notes
docs.text:
• Referential integrity is good. All 400 792 plf records point to an existing packet, and all but one (NYM0796V in SPID 66028) to an existing parameter; every pcf_glob_det name and every dup SPID exists.11
  • Field limits are exceeded in places. 2 876 command descriptions exceed the ICD's Char(24) CCF_DESCR, and the pcdf element type O used for the source ID is not in the ICD's list; both are discussed on The MIB and Mission tailoring of the MIB.11
  • MAP IDs are set only where they matter. The 125 HPC-1 commands are high priority (CCF_HIPRI = Y) with CCF_MAPID = 0, as SCOS-2000 expects for commands whose MAP ID is forced; 128 ordinary commands carry CCF_MAPID = 1 and 77 EPD "SIS" commands the value 54, although the field is meant for high-priority commands and the packet structure ICD defines only MAP IDs 0 and 1.1156
  • Spare and test content stays. Test commands of maximum length, PSS EGSE packets and the DUM "ALWAYS_VALID" parameter are kept in the flight database.11

SELECT count(*), sum(PLF_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM pid)),
       sum(PLF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf)) FROM plf;     -- 400792 | 400792 | 400791
SELECT PLF_NAME, PLF_SPID FROM plf WHERE PLF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM pcf);
SELECT sum(length(CCF_DESCR) > 24), max(length(CCF_DESCR)) FROM ccf;           -- 2876 | 40
SELECT PCDF_TCNAME, PCDF_DESC, PCDF_TYPE FROM pcdf WHERE PCDF_TYPE = 'O';
SELECT CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID, CCF_PKTID, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;

docs.title: How Solar Orbiter uses PUS
docs.text: The Packet Utilization Standard (PUS) defines services - families of requests and reports identified by a service type and subtype - that a mission picks and tailors. Solar Orbiter's tailoring is written down in its space-ground packet structure ICD, SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079,1 and implemented, packet by packet, in its SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base. This page reads the two side by side: the pid table gives every telemetry (TM) packet definition with its type and subtype, and the ccf table every telecommand (TC). All counts are from this wiki's queries on the September 2025 release (and, where stated, the April 2020 release), shown in the "SQL used" blocks.3738

docs.title: Which PUS: A or C?
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter uses PUS-A, ECSS-E-70-41A of 30 January 2003. The question can be settled from both the documents and the MIB:

Evidence What it shows The packet structure ICD's applicable document AD1 is ECSS-E-70-41A, and all application-level structures are "according to" it the standard is PUS-A34 TC and TM data field headers carry PUS version 1 (0b001) PUS-A requires version 1; PUS-C requires version 2562125 The MIB TC header NOM_TC has a fixed 1-bit "Secondary Header Flag" = 0 at bit 48 and a fixed 3-bit "PUS Version" = 1 at bit 49 the PUS-A TC data field header layout, not PUS-C's 4-bit version field3722 The TC source ID is 8 bits (DFH_SRC at bit 72) and the TM destination ID 8 bits PUS-A field sizes; PUS-C uses 16-bit source and destination IDs37726 PID_DFHSIZE = 16 for 11 138 of the 11 150 packets: 6 octets of primary header + 10 octets of data field header the ICD's 10-octet TM data field header with optional PUS-A fields376 Services 4, 7 and 10 are not used; 16 and 20-22 have Solar Orbiter's own meanings consistent with PUS-A's service list, where 7, 10 and 16 are "not used" and 20-22 do not exist224

The header is taken from the MIB's pcdf table and agrees with the ICD.375 The packet layouts, including the TM header reconstruction, are on PUS packet structures; the differences between the issues are on PUS-A vs PUS-C.

The ICD forbids non-standard use of standard services and requires user-specific packets to be private services; services are marked mandatory, optional or reserved for a user, and for optional ones the minimum capability sets of ECSS-E-70-41A apply.41 PUS-A itself reserves service types 0-127 for the standard and leaves 128-255 to missions, and within a standard service leaves subtypes 128-255 to missions.23 Solar Orbiter uses both freedoms heavily, as the counts below show.

docs.title: How the MIB sees a PUS packet
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 identifies a TM packet by APID, type and subtype plus up to two extra identification fields whose position and width are given per type/subtype (and optionally per APID) in pic; each distinct key gets its own SPID.2930 The Solar Orbiter PIC rules for the standard reports are:37

Report 1st field (octet, bits) Meaning of the field TM(1,2), TM(1,8) 20, 16 failure code, after the 4 octets of TC packet ID and sequence control TM(3,25), TM(3,26) 16, 8 structure ID (SID) TM(5,1) to TM(5,4) 16, 16 event ID; on virtual APIDs a 2nd field at octet 18 (19 for TM(5,1) on APID 1974) TM(6,6) 16, 16 memory ID; on virtual APIDs a 2nd 32-bit field at octet 18 TM(21,3), TM(21,5), TM(21,6) 16, 8 science structure ID (SSID) TM(12,9) on APIDs 1986-1990 19, 8 with a 2nd 8-bit field deep inside the packet

Octet 16 is the first octet after the 6-octet primary header and the 10-octet data field header. The consequence is that one PUS report type becomes many database packets: every event ID and every failure code has its own SPID, with its own parameter layout. That is why services 1 and 5 account for 8 965 of the 11 150 packet definitions.37

On the TC side, each command's CCF_ACK sets the acknowledgement flags. The ICD allows only 0000, 0001 (acceptance), 1000 (completion) and 1001 (both);8 the MIB uses 9 (1001) for 5 225 commands, 1 for 78 and 0 for 21 (130 have no value: commands without a PUS header).37 Verification is covered on Command verification in the MIB.

SQL used (PUS version and identification) 
-- solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL)
SELECT * FROM pcdf WHERE PCDF_TCNAME = 'NOM_TC' ORDER BY CAST(PCDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT PID_DFHSIZE, PID_TIME, count(*) FROM pid GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT * FROM pic ORDER BY CAST(PIC_TYPE AS INT), CAST(PIC_STYPE AS INT);
SELECT CCF_ACK, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;

The service names are those of the ICD's Table 5.1-1;1 the PUS-C correspondences follow PUS-C's Table 4-1;27 the counts are TM packet definitions (SPIDs) and commands with the nominal PUS header NOM_TC.3738 The individual message types are catalogued on PUS message types.

SQL used (services per release) 
-- run on solo-2025-09-16.sqlite
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
WITH t AS (
  SELECT CAST(PID_TYPE AS INT) t, 'TM25' k FROM main.pid
  UNION ALL SELECT CAST(PID_TYPE AS INT), 'TM20' FROM o.pid

  FROM pid GROUP BY t, s ORDER BY t, s;

  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_PKTID = 'NOM_TC' GROUP BY t, s ORDER BY t, s;

docs.title: Service 1: TC verification
docs.text: Every on-board unit implements acceptance success and failure (1,1 and 1,2) and execution success and failure (1,7 and 1,8); start and progress reports are not used.18 The CSW applies static acceptance checks to every TC independently of the acknowledgement flags: header constants, a packet length between 5 and 241, the length against the received octets, the CRC, the process ID and the category 12.8 In the MIB, service 1 reports sit on 31 category-1 APIDs: 29 of them have exactly one 1,1 and one 1,7 packet, while the 274 failure-code packets of type 1,2 and 1 477 of type 1,8 are spread over all 31 (SOLOHI's APIDs 1329 and 1345 have failure reports only).37 Failure codes follow Annex 9: standard codes 0 to 7 (illegal APID, length, CRC, type, subtype, application data, segment flags, MAP ID), then ranges per user - SSMM 1000-1999, star trackers 2000-2999, OBCPs 4000-9999, CSW 10000-39999, EPD 40000s, MAG 41000s, RPW 42000s, SWA 43000s, SPICE 44000s, PHI 45000s, EUI 46000s, METIS 47000s, STIX 48000s, SoloHi 49000s.9 The units' codes in the MIB agree: SSMM failure codes run from 1000 to 1090, star tracker codes 2500-2655, EPD 40000-40717, MAG 41100-41822, RPW 42000-42005, SWA 43000-43265, SPICE 44000-44099, PHI 45011-45827, EUI 46700-46800, METIS 47000-47719, STIX 48000-48463 and SOLOHI 49000-49004.37 The CSW (processes 10-16) is the exception: besides codes in its 10000-39999 range it defines codes 256-277 for its own acceptance checks (for example 256 "Illegal CCSDS packet version number") and 175 distinct codes between 509 and 4881, which Annex 9 assigns to the reserved standard range, to spares, to the SSMM, to the star trackers and to OBCPs.379

docs.title: Service 2: device command distribution
docs.text: TC(2,3) carries CPDU commands, TC(2,128) MIL-STD-1553 commands with the TM(2,129) answer, and TC(2,130) a SpaceWire packet.1 Service 2 is by far the largest TC service: 1 257 TC(2,128) bus commands (for example "DEU A Arm Pinpuller") and 105 TC(2,3) CPDU commands, all to the data management APID 172, plus one TC(2,130).37 Apart from the generic "Distribute CPDU commands", the MIB names the TC(2,3) commands "HPC-3 ..." (for example "HPC-3 IMU 1 Channel 1 On"), the pulses that the CSW produces by writing CPDU registers. The ground-to-CPDU HPC-1 commands are a separate set: 125 commands to APID 44 (process 2) with the HPC1_TC header, no secondary header and CCF_MAPID = 0, none of which shares a description with a TC(2,3) command.3712 See ST[02] Device access.

docs.title: Service 3: housekeeping and diagnostic reporting
docs.text:
The routine HK report TM(3,25) is mandatory for all units; the CSW also implements the PUS-A definition, clearing, enabling, disabling and reporting subtypes 1-12, a diagnostic report TM(3,26), and private subtypes 128-139 (report definitions in summary form, update periods, collection intervals, one-shot request, adding parameters to a definition, snapshot anomaly report).1 The MIB has 288 TM(3,25) definitions on 62 APIDs and 89 TM(3,26) on 14 APIDs, and 345 service 3 commands.37

Structure IDs follow a pattern per category. For the CSW, Annex 10 allocates SIDs 1-127 to TM(3,25) and 128-255 to TM(3,26), in blocks (1-10 general status, 11-30 mode, 31-60 equipment, 61-90 specific requests, 101-104 ESOC, 105-127 ancillary data; 128-137, 138-157, ... for diagnostics).11 In the MIB the data management application, for instance, reports 15 SIDs between 1 and 16 on its HPTM APID 162 (category 2), the same reports as SIDs 77-92 on its routine HK APID 164 (category 4), SIDs 153-156 on its functional cyclic APID 165 (category 5) and diagnostic SIDs 193-194 on APID 168 (category 8); the AOCS follows the same pattern (HPTM SIDs between 1 and 21, routine 77-97, functional cyclic 153-159 and 191-192, diagnostic 193-223, 228-229 and 251-255). Every one of the 68 CSW HPTM TM(3,25) definitions has a routine HK counterpart on the APID two higher with a SID 76 higher, and in 67 cases the two share the same description.37

Inference

The MIB's CSW SIDs do not follow the Annex 10 blocks: the routine HK SIDs 77-102 run across the "specific data request" (61-90), spare (91-100) and ESOC (101-104) blocks, and the category 5 TM(3,25) SIDs 153-159 and 188-192 fall in the range that Annex 10 reserves for TM(3,26). The offset of 76 between HPTM and routine HK SIDs is this wiki's observation from the data; the rule behind it is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: Service 5: event reporting
docs.text: Events are the largest TM service: 7 156 definitions on 50 APIDs - 1 374 normal/progress (5,1), 1 159 low severity (5,2), 2 911 medium severity (5,3) and 1 698 high severity (5,4) reports, plus the CSW's private event log subtypes 130, 132 and 134.371 Annex 9 encodes the severity in the two most significant bits of the 16-bit event ID (5,1 from 0x0000, 5,2 from 0x4000, 5,3 from 0x8000, 5,4 from 0xC000) and splits each quarter into boot software, general and specific application, unexpected error, monitoring, OBCP and ESOC ranges.10 All 2 308 CSW event definitions (processes 10-16) obey the severity rule; the instruments' events follow it less consistently (5 499 of all 7 142 events of subtypes 1-4 obey it).37 The busiest event APIDs are the thermal control events (APID 263, 699 definitions), the three EUI event APIDs (620 each) and the AOCS events (APID 183, 436).37

docs.title: Service 6: memory management
docs.text: Load (6,2), dump (6,⅚,6) and check (6,9/6,10) by absolute address are mandatory for all units; private subtypes add pre-loaded RAM patches, abort dump, enabling and disabling the SSMM EEPROM patch, and load with mask.1 The MIB has 289 TM(6,6) dump and 20 TM(6,10) check report definitions and 221 commands; dumps are identified by a 16-bit memory ID at octet 16.37

docs.title: Service 8: function management
docs.text: The CSW's TC(8,1) "Perform Function" is used by 64 commands (for example "1553 Failure Recovery"); private subtypes 140-144 enable or disable functions and their auto-reset and report their status in TM(8,145).371

docs.title: Service 9: time management
docs.text:
The OBC keeps the on-board time as CUC with 4 octets of seconds and 2 of sub-seconds from a zero reference of 1 January 2000; TM(9,2) reports it (without data field header, on APID 0), TC(9,1) changes its rate, TC(9,128) sets the OBT, and TC(9,130)/(9,131) start and stop time synchronisation of a user, which makes the CSW send TC(9,129) "accept time update" packets to that user.1314 The 2020 MIB defined 19 service 9 commands, including four TC(9,128) variants and eleven TC(9,129) commands addressed to the SSMM and the instruments; the 2025 release keeps only TC(9,1), two TC(9,130) and one TC(9,131).3837

Inference

Since the ICD says that TC(9,129) is generated by the CSW, not sent from the ground, its removal from the ground command database is consistent with its definition; why the TC(9,128) "Set OBT" commands were also removed is not stated in the available sources.

Time correlation itself is done on ground with the MCS packets TM(164,1) to TM(164,3) on APID 1966, described on Solar Orbiter and Time correlation in SCOS-2000.31

docs.title: Service 11: on-board operations scheduling
docs.text: The CSW implements the PUS-A time-based schedule almost completely: enable, disable and reset release, insert, delete (also over a time period), time-shift, detailed and summary reports (9-17) and schedule status 18/19.1 The MIB adds a private TC(11,132) "Insert Backup MTL Telecommands" (two commands to APID 172), which Table 5.1-1 of the ICD does not list.371 The insert command ZCD00B04 (explorer) is dissected on PUS packet structures and in the TC worked example.

docs.title: Service 12: on-board monitoring
docs.text: Enable, disable, change maximum report delay, clear, add, delete, modify and report the monitoring list, and report the out-of-limit list, with the check transition report TM(12,12).1 The 254 commands are dominated by TC(12,5) "add parameter" (114 variants by parameter type) and TC(12,7) "modify checking information" (83).37 The 32 TM definitions include 19 TM(12,9) monitoring list reports, 13 of them on the virtual APIDs 1986-1990 that the ground uses to decode each CSW application's list (see The Solar Orbiter MIB).37 Ground and on-board checks are compared on Monitoring checks.

docs.title: Service 13: large data transfer
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's service 13 uplinks files from the ground to the CSW (first, intermediate and last parts, abort, acknowledgement, unsuccessful part and abort reports, TC(13,9) to TM(13,16)) and downlinks files from the SSMM with a private protocol of file transfer sessions and "low-level file transfer" (LLFT) subtypes 128-153.115 Each uplinked file has an attribute: 1 OBCP, 2 TC sequence for delayed execution, 3 TC sequence for immediate execution, 6 other and 7 internal, with 4 and 5 unused.15 The MIB has 28 service 13 commands on APIDs 172 and 492 (SSMM) and 9 report definitions.37 Downlinked files reach users as "DLPP" TM files in the file archive.32 The MIB's mission file s13a.dat lists the attribute values 0 PLAIN, 1 OBCP, 2 DELAYED TC, 3 IMMEDIATE TC, 4 PAYLOAD CONTEXT, 5 INVALID and 6 OTHER, so it gives meanings to 0, 4 and 5, which the ICD leaves undefined or marks unused, and has no entry for the ICD's 7.3715 Service 13 is a PUS-A large data transfer, not the PUS-C ST[13] or ST[23].

docs.title: Service 14: packet forwarding control
docs.text: Twelve commands enable and disable the forwarding of TM source packets, housekeeping, diagnostic and event packets, and report the forwarding status (TM(14,8), (14,12), (14,129), (14,131)).137

docs.title: Service 15: on-board storage and retrieval
docs.text: The CSW and the SSMM both implement service 15, with the SSMM adding creation, resizing, deletion, renaming, listing and copying of packet stores, cyclic/non-cyclic modes, default virtual channel and priority, and the CSW adding SID-based storage selection and the storage routing table - subtypes 128 to 156.1 All 47 commands go to APIDs 172 and 492.37 The E-FECS notes that resizing SSMM packet stores loses data unless the stores are empty.36 See ST[15].

docs.title: Service 16: on-board traffic management
docs.text: A Solar Orbiter service in a type number that PUS-A marks "not used": five commands set the MIL-STD-1553 bus configuration and switch buses or remote-terminal channels between nominal and redundant; the ICD says they are not meant for nominal flight operations but for investigation or recovery after bus FDIR.162437

docs.title: Service 17: test
docs.text: TC(17,1) and the TM(17,2) connection test report are mandatory for all units; the CSW adds TC(17,3) to request a connection test of another unit, and TC(17,128) is a test command of maximum length.1 18 units have a TC(17,1) in the MIB and 17 have a TM(17,2).37

docs.title: Service 18: on-board control procedures
docs.text: Suspend, resume, communicate parameters, report the OBCP list and private load-and-start, stop-and-delete and OBCP HK subtypes; TM(18,144) carries OBCP telemetry.1 The 38 TC(18,140) "Load and start OBCP" variants account for most of the 46 commands, which grew from 32 in 2020.3738 How the ICD's OBCP description lines up with the OBCP standard is on ECSS-E-ST-70-01C.

docs.title: Service 19: event-action
docs.text: Add, delete and clear event detection entries, enable and disable actions, and report the list or a single entry (TC(19,130)/TM(19,131)).1 The 48 commands are on three APIDs, with 25 TC(19,1) "Add Event" variants.37

docs.title: Service 20: information distribution
docs.text:
Not PUS-C's parameter management: Solar Orbiter's service 20 distributes inter-instrument data and the OBC heartbeat. TC(20,1) and TC(20,2) start and stop distribution to a user, and the single TC(20,128) carries all the data.1734 The MIB has the CSW's TC(20,1) per instrument (ten "Start Information Distribution ..." commands to APID 172, plus a generic "... for User" one) and one TC(20,2), and five TC(20,128) definitions on APID 796 - process 49, "payload broadcast" in Annex 8 - for EPD, MAG, PHI and STIX.3720 The instruments' contributions arrive as category 5 TM(3,25) packets, compared with the 2016 agreement below.

Instrument IIC packet in SOL-SGS-TN-0007 (2016) Category 5 TM(3,25) in the 2025 MIB EPD PID 100, SID 100 APID 1605 (PID 100), SID 100 EUI PID 57, SID 10 APID 933 (PID 58), SID 10 "EUI_HK_IIM" MAG PID 65, SID 20 APID 1045 (PID 65), SID 20 METIS PID 69, SID 20 APID 1109 (PID 69), SID 20 "SID 20 - IIC" PHI PID 74, SID 6 APID 1189 (PID 74), SIDs 2 "heartbeat" and 8 RPW PID 81, SID 6 APID 1269 (PID 79), SID 6 "shared with other SolO instruments" SOLOHI PID 84, SID 5 APID 1349 (PID 84), SID 80 "OBC InterInstrument Packet" STIX PID 94, SID 4 APID 1509 (PID 94), SID 4 SWA PID 95, SID 255 APID 1525 (PID 95), SID 255 "SWA_TM_II_INFO" SPICE PID 88, SID 7 (not participating) APID 1653 (PID 103), SID 7 "SPICE Heartbeat HK Report"

The 2016 values are from the note's packet tables;35 the 2025 values are this wiki's query.37 The parameters of these packets match the field lists of the note - for example EUI's FlareCloseToHRI and OffLimb flags, RPW's RPW_S20_SBM1_FLAG, PHI's mean and RMS jitter, SOLOHI's power-off request and door-armed flags, SWA's density and velocity - so they are the IIC packets even where the numbers differ.3735 Five instruments match exactly; EUI, RPW and SPICE use other process IDs and PHI and SOLOHI other SIDs. A twelfth category 5 TM(3,25), SOLOHI's APID 1317 SID 17 "OBC HK Combo Status Packet (Diagnostic)", has no counterpart in the note.37

Inference

The differing process IDs and SIDs suggest that the IIC agreements were revised after issue 2.0 of the note; neither the revision nor its reason is in the available sources.

docs.title: Service 21: science data transfer
docs.text: A Solar Orbiter service for moving instrument science to the SSMM: TC(21,1) and TC(21,2) start and stop the transfer, TC(21,128) resets the output buffer, and the data come in TM(21,3) (fixed length with SSID), TM(21,4) (fixed, no SSID), TM(21,5) (variable stream with SSID) or TM(21,6) (variable with structure and SSID).18 The MIB has 105 TM(21,3), 72 TM(21,5) and 151 TM(21,6) definitions on 45 science APIDs (category 12), and 6 TM(21,7) definitions for SPICE, a subtype that the ICD does not define.37

docs.title: Service 22: context saving
docs.text: Instruments save their operational context as a file in the OBC mass memory (OMM), where the ground can also reach it with service 133, and get it back on request: the ground asks the CSW to save a context (22,5), the CSW requests it from the instrument (22,1), which answers with a context report (22,2) within 5 seconds; on a retrieval request (22,4) the CSW sends the context back in up to 18 TC(22,3) segments.19 Only STIX's context report remains in 2025; PHI's TM(22,2) on APID 1163 was removed after 2020.3738

docs.title: Mission-specific services 128-255
docs.text:
The ICD assigns private service ranges per user.1 The MIB shows which are actually populated:

Types Owner (ICD) TM defs TC defs Examples from the MIB 128-129 EPD 9 92 TC(128,1) "Trigger trans", 129,224 "Command Echo ASW", SIS macro commands 130 CSW TM extraction 1 3 define, delete, report TM extraction descriptors 131 CSW device management / private function management 693 875 875 TC(131,1) uploads such as "AGP Segment 0 Part 1 Upload"; PCDU snapshots and OBDB dumps 132 CSW SGM management 71 246 SGM group read/write; 239 TC(132,3) e.g. "BUMTL set CRCs and file selection in SGM" 133 CSW file management 2 6 copy, delete, modify, report file; verify checksum 134 CSW TC sequencer 0 13 start/abort sequence, "Execute Loss-of-UL FDIR TC File" 139 CSW data-pool (parameter) management 26 234 217 TC(139,1) "change value" variants, e.g. "Set value of (1-byte integer) parameters"; TM(139,3) 140-141 SSMM mode transition, direct commanding 95 95 SSMM BIT/INIT/OPERA modes; 67 direct register reads 142 CSW functional monitoring / SSMM redundancy 18 59 add/delete/protect FMON; router configuration report 143-145 SSMM memory arrays, reboot, BIT reports 4 13 test/configure/scrub memory modules 150-157 star trackers 18 70 "STR1 AAD Mode"; TM(156,x) attitude data 160-166 (ground: MCS-internal packets on APID 1966) 17 0 time correlation TM(164,1-3), mini frames, MATIS 170 (EGSE "PSS", APID 1948) 0 5 "PSS Set HK Parameter OFF" 180-184 RPW 7 93 DPU_BOOT_DAS, LFR calibration commands 200-205 SWA 18 188 SWA_TC_EAS1_CLEAR_RAM, parameter reports 206-218 EUI 18 110 EUI_ChangeModeBasic, table dumps 226-230 MAG 2 117 "Activate FIB", EEPROM table of contents 231-235 PHI 28 161 acquireFPAImages, file system 236-240 STIX 14 85 ASIC readouts, TM corridor limits 241-245 METIS 3 80 HVU configuration, acquisition 246-250 SoloHI 7 98 CCFREEHEADERS; TM(247,x), TM(248,1) 251 (ground: link and session control, saved synthetics) 1 6 (NOS2KHDR) GENERIC OPEN TC LINK on APID 1964 252-255 SPICE (ICD range 251-255) 2 82 only type 255 is used, e.g. CLR_LATCHED

The owners are those of Table 5.1-1;1 types 160-166 are the MCS packets of the DDID;33 the counts are from the 2025 MIB.37 The CSW's private services carry much of the operational load: TC(131,1) alone accounts for 875 commands.

Inference

Several Solar Orbiter private services do jobs that PUS-C later standardised: 139 data-pool management resembles PUS-C ST[20], 133 file management ST[23], 134 TC sequencer ST[21], and 142 functional monitoring the functional monitoring subservice of PUS-C ST[12].28 The similarity is functional; the packet layouts are Solar Orbiter's own and are not claimed to match PUS-C. Type 251 is used both by ground packets (on APIDs 1964 and 1966, process 122 in the EGSE range) and, according to the ICD, by SPICE; since SPICE's process IDs are 85-89 and 101-104, the two uses do not collide in practice (and SPICE's MIB entries use only type 255).

SQL used (private services and IIC packets) 
SELECT CAST(CCF_TYPE AS INT) t, count(*), count(DISTINCT CCF_STYPE), group_concat(DISTINCT CCF_APID),
       min(CCF_DESCR)
  FROM ccf WHERE CCF_PKTID = 'NOM_TC' AND CAST(CCF_TYPE AS INT) > 22 GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;
SELECT CAST(PID_TYPE AS INT) t, count(*) FROM pid WHERE CAST(PID_TYPE AS INT) > 22
 GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;
-- category 5 TM(3,25) = candidate inter-instrument communication packets
SELECT PID_APID, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 AS pid, PID_PI1_VAL AS sid, PID_DESCR
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '3' AND PID_STYPE = '25' AND (CAST(PID_APID AS INT) & 15) = 5;
SELECT l.PLF_OFFBY, p.PCF_NAME, p.PCF_DESCR FROM plf l JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID IN ('51010', '55082', '56358', '53008') ORDER BY l.PLF_SPID, CAST(l.PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_APID, CCF_STYPE FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '20';
-- failure codes per process, outside the standard 0-500 range
SELECT CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 p, min(CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT)), max(CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT))
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' AND PID_STYPE IN ('2', '8') AND CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) > 500
 GROUP BY p;
-- HPTM (category 2) and routine HK (category 4) twins
SELECT count(*) FROM pid a JOIN pid b ON CAST(b.PID_APID AS INT) = CAST(a.PID_APID AS INT) + 2
   AND CAST(b.PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) = CAST(a.PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) + 76 AND b.PID_TYPE = '3' AND b.PID_STYPE = '25'
 WHERE a.PID_TYPE = '3' AND a.PID_STYPE = '25' AND CAST(a.PID_APID AS INT) & 15 = 2;   -- 68
-- event severity encoded in the two top bits of the event ID
SELECT PID_STYPE, count(*), sum((CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) >> 14) = CAST(PID_STYPE AS INT) - 1)
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '5' AND PID_STYPE IN ('1','2','3','4')
   AND (CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4) BETWEEN 10 AND 16 GROUP BY 1;
-- removed time commands
ATTACH 'solo-2020-04-16.sqlite' AS o;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_APID, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_DESCR FROM o.ccf
 WHERE CCF_TYPE = '9' AND CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf);

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  subgraph STD["Standard PUS-A service types used (15)"]
    S1["1 verification<br/>1 809 TM"] --- S5["5 events<br/>7 156 TM"]
    S2["2 device<br/>1 363 TC"] --- S3["3 HK<br/>397 TM / 345 TC"]
    S6["6 memory"] --- S12["12 monitoring"]
    S11["11 scheduling"] --- S15["15 storage"]
    OTH["8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19"]
  end
  subgraph SOLO["Solar Orbiter services in the standard range"]
    S16["16 traffic management"] --- S20["20 information distribution"]
    S21["21 science data transfer"] --- S22["22 context saving"]
  end
  subgraph PRIV["Private types 128-255 (70 types)"]
    CSW["CSW 130-134, 139, 142"] --- SSMM["SSMM 140-145"]
    INS["instruments 128-129, 180-255"] --- GND["ground 160-166, 170, 251"]
  end

Of the 90 service types that occur in TM definitions or nominal commands, one is type 0 (packets without data field header), 15 are PUS-A standard services, 4 are Solar Orbiter services numbered in the standard range (16, 20, 21, 22) and 70 are private; services 4, 7 and 10 are absent, exactly as the ICD says.372
