docs.title: Solar Orbiter STIX instrument database
docs.text:
STIX is one of the ten Solar Orbiter instruments named in the spacecraft packet ICD; the Experiment Interface Document expands the acronym as "Spectrometer Telescope Imaging X-rays".16 On board it is the application owning process IDs 90 to 94 and the private services 236 to 240 of the spacecraft packet ICD.68 Its instrument database (IDB) - the instrument's packets, parameters, calibrations and commands written as SCOS-2000 MIB tables - is published on a server at FHNW (pub099.cs.technik.fhnw.ch), from which this wiki copied release 2.26.38.2 An instrument database uses the same tables as the spacecraft Solar Orbiter MIB; this page analyses every non-empty table of the copy and checks, row by row, how much of it is in the two copied spacecraft MIB releases. The same data can be browsed in the STIX explorer. The companion page for the SWA instrument is Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database; the documents that define what an instrument must provide are on Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces.

What was copied

Item Value Library item stix-idb-v2-26-38-raw Original URL https://pub099.cs.technik.fhnw.ch/data/idb/v2.26.38.raw.zip Copied 2026-11-12 17:45:36 UTC Size, SHA-256 70 526 bytes, 4b627929a521831bcba45c66b24dcec07fdb177ffb008e22442c88dc5261fabf Contents folder v2.26.38/STIX-IDB-2.26.38/idb/ with 56 .dat files (26 non-empty) and a synthetic/ folder with 3 files; 62 zip entries, all dated 2024-02-02 12:59 or 13:00 Version record STX_226, comment PFM_applicable, domain 105, release 2, issue 26 Explorer key stix, for example packet 54103

The URL, time, size and hash come from this wiki's source registry;2 the contents, dates and the version record were read from the zip directory and the files.3 The .dat files are TAB-separated with Windows (CR LF) line ends, like the copied SWA databases and unlike the Unix format the ICD specifies.321

docs.title: Version: one vdf record
docs.text:
The vdf table names the database version. The ICD defines VDF_NAME as up to 8 characters, a 32-character comment, and a domain identifier, release and issue number, all three optional; when several records exist, the last one imported names the database, and the importer cross-checks the domain identifier against its own domain option.22 The STIX IDB has exactly one record:3

Field Value Remark VDF_NAME STX_226 7 characters: release 2, issue 26 VDF_COMMENT PFM_applicable the spacecraft MIB release names also carry PFM VDF_DOMAINID 105 same number as the PCF_SUBSYS of 673 of the 681 parameters VDF_RELEASE / VDF_ISSUE 2 / 26

The third number of the release name, 38, appears only in the folder and zip names; it is not stated in the available sources what it counts. The two spacecraft MIB releases copied by this wiki use domain 0 in their vdf (25925PFM and 10720PFM).45 Unlike the SWA IDB, which keeps its 70-version history in vdf (see SWA), the STIX file carries no history.

docs.title: What the IDB contains
docs.text:
Family Table STIX IDB Same key in 2025 MIB Version vdf 1 - Parameters pcf 681 681 Packets pid / tpcf / pic 246 / 246 / 29 246 / 246 (177 with the same size) / - Packet layout plf / vpd 927 / 774 926 / 452 identical Numerical calibration caf / cap 14 / 75 14 / 75 Textual calibration txf / txp 81 / 379 80 (73 identical) / 377 identical Polynomial calibration mcf 7 7 Monitoring checks ocf / ocp 14 / 32 14 / 32 identical Synthetic parameters synthetic/ files 3 3, identical source Commands ccf / cdf / cpc 100 / 1 377 / 669 99 / 1 373 identical / 669 Command text calibration paf / pas 43 / 149 43 (40 identical) / 149 identical TC header tcp / pcpc / pcdf 1 / 6 / 13 - Verification cvs / cvp 4 / 200 4 / 198 Mission files sw_para / pcf_glob_det 1 468 / 213 1 464 in ASW_sw_para / 213 Empty sequences, parameter sets, cur, lgf, cve, cca/ccs, prf/prv, ptv, dst, all displays and groups, ssy 0 -

The counts are from this wiki's queries; "same key" counts rows of the 2025 release with the same name or SPID, "identical" counts rows equal in every compared field.34 The STIX database has no displays, groups, command sequences, parameter sets or range checks: it defines the instrument's data and commands only.

docs.title: Which ICD issue the files follow
docs.text:
Counting TAB-separated fields per record, pcf has 19 fields, cpc 13, ccf 21, pic 6, cvs 6 and caf 7.3 Nineteen pcf and thirteen cpc fields are the layouts of the Database Import ICD issue 5.1,24 which issue 7.0 still accepts because fields 20 to 23 of pcf are optional.23 The optional PIC_APID, CVS_UNCERTAINTY and CAF_INTER fields of issue 7.0 are therefore absent.252627 The SWA databases show the same field counts (see SWA). See History of the Database Import ICD.

SQL used (contents and version) 

-- stix-idb-2.26.38.sqlite
SELECT * FROM vdf;                         -- STX_226 | PFM_applicable | 105 | 2 | 26
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf;                  -- repeated for every table
SELECT PCF_SUBSYS, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1;   -- 105: 673, empty: 8
-- run with ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m
SELECT count(*), sum(PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM m.pcf)) FROM main.pcf;   -- 681 | 681
Field counts were taken from the .dat files inside the zip with a TAB count per line.

docs.title: APIDs and packet categories
docs.text:
On Solar Orbiter the 11-bit APID is the 7-bit process ID followed by a 4-bit packet category, so APID = PID x 16 + CAT.96 The IDB uses nine telemetry APIDs:3

APID PID / CAT Category meaning (Annex 8) Packets PUS types 1441 90 / 1 TC verification 106 TM(1,1), (1,2), (1,7), (1,8) 1444 90 / 4 routine housekeeping 2 TM(3,25) SIDs 1 and 2 1447 90 / 7 event generation 84 TM(5,1)-(5,4), TM(17,2) 1448 90 / 8 diagnostic 14 private services 236-239 1449 90 / 9 dump 20 TM(6,6), TM(6,10) 1451 90 / 11 context 1 TM(22,2) 1468 91 / 12 private science 10 TM(21,6) X-ray and spectrogram 1500 93 / 12 private science 8 TM(21,6) quick-look and calibration 1509 94 / 5 functional cyclic 1 TM(3,25) SID 4 (inter-instrument data)

Every packet sits in a category that Annex 8 of the packet ICD allows for its service: 1 for service 1, 4 for routine TM(3,25), 5 for inter-instrument TM(3,25), 7 for events and TM(17,2), 8 for the private reports ("private diagnostic packets produced upon Ground request"), 9 for dumps, 11 for service 22 and 12 for science.67 Annex 8 also offers category 6 for private fixed-length report packets produced on ground request; STIX does not use it, while SWA moved its private reports there (see Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces).63 Process ID 92 is not used; telecommands go to APID 1452 (PID 90, CAT 12) and one command to APID 796, process 49, the OBC "payload broadcast" process (see Commands).36 All 246 packets have PID_DFHSIZE = 16 (the 6-octet packet header plus the 10-octet data field header of Solar Orbiter telemetry), a packet time field (PID_TIME = Y), no CRC check (PID_CHECK = 0) and no SCOS-2000 event generation (PID_EVENT = N); 45 are variable packets with a vpd structure.33011

SQL used (APIDs) 
SELECT PID_APID, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4 AS pid, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) & 15 AS cat,
       count(*), group_concat(DISTINCT PID_TYPE || '/' || PID_STYPE)
  FROM pid GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CAST(PID_APID AS INT);
SELECT PID_DFHSIZE, PID_TIME, PID_CHECK, PID_TPSD <> '-1', count(*) FROM pid GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4;

docs.title: Packet catalogue by PUS type and subtype
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 identifies a packet by APID, type, subtype and up to two extra fields whose position the pic table gives per type and subtype; each combination has one pid row and one SPID.2530 The STIX pic rows place the first identification field at octet 20 (16 bits, the failure code) for TM(1,2) and TM(1,8), at octet 16 (8 bits, the SID or SSID) for TM(3,25) and TM(21,6), and at octet 16 (16 bits) for events and memory dumps; octet 16 is the first octet after the headers.3 The 246 SPIDs run from 54001 to 54365:3

Type, subtype Packets Identification field What the packets are TM(1,1) / TM(1,7) 1 / 1 - acceptance success, completion success TM(1,2) 12 failure ID acceptance failures: the 8 standard IDs 0-7 and 48000, 48001, 48003, 48023 TM(1,8) 92 failure ID completion failures 48005 to 48463 TM(3,25) 3 SID SID 1 and 2 housekeeping (APID 1444), SID 4 inter-instrument data (APID 1509) TM(5,1) / (5,2) / (5,3) / (5,4) 25 / 29 / 26 / 3 event ID information, warning, error and high-severity events TM(6,6) / TM(6,10) 19 / 1 memory ID (TM(6,6) only) memory dumps per memory, memory check TM(17,2) 1 - connection test report TM(21,6) 18 SSID science data, see below TM(22,2) 1 - context report TM(236,16), (236,19) 2 - subsystem configuration report, FDIR parameter report TM(237,12), (237,20) 2 - start-up software (SuSW) and application software (ASW) parameter reports TM(238,3), (238,7) 2 - archive memory user data selections, filesystem check report TM(239,3), (239,6), (239,8), (239,10), (239,12), (239,14), (239,18), (239,21) 8 - ASIC temperature, on-demand ASIC ADC readout, ASIC baseline, channel dark current, threshold scan, ASIC ADC read, ASIC register read, stored attenuator data

The private service types 236-239 are all within the range 236-240 that the packet ICD reserves for STIX; service 240 is not used.83 The pic table also defines TM(239,16), for which no packet exists.3 Each failure code and each event ID is its own packet, which is why service 1 (106 packets) and service 5 (83) make up 189 of the 246 definitions; the general mechanism is explained on How Solar Orbiter uses PUS.

docs.title: Failure codes and event IDs against the mission allocation
docs.text:
Annex 9 of the packet ICD reserves failure IDs 0 to 500 for standard codes (0 illegal APID, 1 incomplete or invalid length, 2 wrong CRC, 3 illegal type, 4 illegal subtype, 5 illegal or inconsistent data, 6 illegal segment sequence flag, 7 illegal MAP ID) and gives STIX the block 48000 to 48999.13 STIX follows this: its TM(1,2) packets use the eight standard codes and its own codes start at 48000 (for example 48018 "Invalid HK data report period in TC(3,129)", 48035 "No Timecode within 2s after TC(9,129)").3 One description differs from the allocation: STIX's code 7 reads "Illegal segment sequence flag", the meaning the annex gives to code 6, where the annex assigns 7 to an illegal MAP ID.313

For events the annex splits the 16-bit event ID by severity, the first two bits giving the report subtype (0x0000-0x3FFF for TM(5,1), 0x4000 for (5,2), 0x8000 for (5,3), 0xC000 for (5,4)), and each quarter into boot software, general application, specific application, "unexpected SW and HW errors", monitoring, OBCP and ESOC ranges; the annex makes this applicable to the central software and optional for other software.14 All 83 STIX event IDs respect both the severity bits and the ranges:3

Subtype IDs Boot SW General application Unexpected SW/HW errors Monitoring TM(5,1) 0x0001-0x14A3 4 6 14 1 (0x14A3 "FDIR protection enabled") TM(5,2) 0x4001-0x5446 2 - 27 - TM(5,3) 0x8001-0x9450 2 3 21 - TM(5,4) 0xC001-0xD421 1 - 2 -

The three high-severity events are requests to the spacecraft: execute a nominal sequence (0xC001), power down immediately (0xD420) and power cycle after an SDRAM initialisation time-out (0xD421).3

SQL used (catalogue, failure and event IDs) 
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, count(*) FROM pid GROUP BY 1, 2
 ORDER BY CAST(PID_TYPE AS INT), CAST(PID_STYPE AS INT);
SELECT * FROM pic ORDER BY CAST(PIC_TYPE AS INT), CAST(PIC_STYPE AS INT);
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' ORDER BY 2;
SELECT PID_STYPE, CASE
         WHEN (v & 16383) BETWEEN 1 AND 31 THEN 'boot'
         WHEN (v & 16383) BETWEEN 32 AND 1055 THEN 'general'
         WHEN (v & 16383) BETWEEN 5152 AND 5279 THEN 'unexpected'
         WHEN (v & 16383) BETWEEN 5280 AND 13471 THEN 'monitoring' END, count(*)
  FROM (SELECT PID_STYPE, CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT) v FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '5')
 GROUP BY 1, 2;

docs.title: Housekeeping and the inter-instrument packet
docs.text:
SID 1 (SPID 54101) and SID 2 (SPID 54102) carry the instrument housekeeping: software running (ASW or SuSW), instrument mode, DPU temperatures, currents and voltages, CPU load, SpaceWire counters and FDIR status (with per-channel FDIR masks and TC/TM counters in SID 1); SID 2 adds detector quadrant temperatures, high-voltage and attenuator status, aspect-system photodiode voltages and filesystem statistics.3 SID 2 also reports NIXD0077 "TC(20,128) seq cnt" (octet 88), which follows the packet ICD's recommendation that payloads report the sequence count of the last TC(20,128) they received.317 Their plf layouts end at octet 59 (last parameter, 16 bits, at octet 57) and octet 109 (32 bits at octet 105), but their tpcf sizes are 46 and 105; the 2025 spacecraft MIB has 59 and 109.34 The ICD defines TPCF_SIZE as the total SCOS-2000 packet length (recommended to include the 64- or 76-byte SCOS-2000 packet header), not imported into the run-time database nor used by any SCOS-2000 process, so the mismatch does not affect telemetry processing; if a mission uses the field to configure its history files, a size smaller than the real packet still files correctly, only more slowly.31

SID 4 is the STIX contribution to on-board inter-instrument communication. The note SOL-SGS-TN-0007 asks STIX for a TM(3,25) with PID 94, CAT 5 and SID 4 at 1 Hz, carrying 16 octets for distribution: a 4-octet heartbeat copied from the OBT coarse time, thermal and non-thermal flare indices and a location status in one octet, signed Z and Y flare locations in arcminutes, a 4-octet flare duration, a 4-octet attenuator motion flag and a spare octet.19 The IDB packet YIX54103 (SPID 54103, APID 1509, 33 octets) implements exactly this layout:3

The octet offsets, bit offsets and types are the plf and pcf entries; octet 21 is also defined as the 8-bit container NIXG0021.3 In the SCOS-2000 code table PTC 4 PFC 4 is an 8-bit signed integer and PTC 3 PFC 14 a 32-bit unsigned integer.33 The OBC copies these 16 octets into octets 191 to 206 of the TC(20,128) it distributes to the instruments.20

The packet changed between the copied releases. In the April 2020 spacecraft MIB the flare octet held the location status at bit 1, the non-thermal index at bit 3 and a 3-bit thermal index at bit 5 (NIXD0059-NIXD0061), the attenuator flag was a single bit at octet 28 and a 32-bit filler followed at octet 29; the IDB moves the thermal index to bits 0-2, the location status to bits 5-6, makes the motion flag a 32-bit word, and introduces the new names NIXD0505-NIXD0507 and NIXG0021, so it now matches the TN-0007 byte table.5319 The old names stay in the IDB: NIXG0020 and NIXD0059-NIXD0061 (now described as "QL") are the flare fields of the quick-look packet 54122 "Flare flag and location".3 The 2025 MIB keeps the IDB layout but omits the final ZZPAD008 entry; the packet size stays 33 octets in all three databases.45 Browse it as packet 54103.

docs.title: Memory dumps and memory IDs
docs.text: Each of the 19 TM(6,6) packets is identified by its memory ID: 0xD000-0xD004 and 0xD011/0xD012/0xD021/0xD022 for the main unit's EEPROM, SRAM, SDRAM, two flash memories and four application-software image slots, the same values with 0xD1 for the redundant unit, and 0xDF00 for full memory access.3 The packet ICD allocates the memory IDs 0xD0-- and 0xD1-- to STIX, and its basic rules, for cross-access between redundant units, give unit B the unit A ID plus 256 (most significant byte 1), which is the main/redundant pattern seen here.15 The same 19 values form the textual calibration CIXT0014TM "Memory ID".3

docs.title: Science packets
docs.text:
All STIX science travels as TM(21,6), the variable-length science packet with a structure identifier (SSID) in its first octet followed by fixed parameters and counted repeating blocks.16 The 18 SSIDs split over two APIDs:3

APID SSIDs Products 1468 (PID 91) 10-14, 20-24 X-ray levels L0 to L3 and spectrogram, each "auto" (10-14) and "user" requested (20-24) 1500 (PID 93) 30-34, 41-43 quick-look summed light curves, background monitor, detector-specific spectra, variance, flare flag and location, background spectrum for calibration, aspect, TM management status and flare list

These packets are defined in vpd, which lists the parameters in order and lets a parameter repeat the next VPD_GRPSIZE entries a number of times equal to its own value; groups may be nested, and VPD_OFFSET moves a parameter's start relative to the end of the previous one, a negative offset making two parameters overlap.32 STIX uses both features. The quick-look light-curve packet (SPID 54118) starts with SSID, SCET coarse and fine time, integration duration and detector mask, then the 16-bit NIXG0404 "SSID global 3" immediately followed by NIXD0407 "Pixel mask 1" with offset -12, so the 12-bit mask is read from the last 12 bits (bits 4 to 15) of the word just read; later, "Number of energies" (NIX00270) repeats a 2-entry group whose first entry, "Num of data pnts LC", itself repeats the compressed light-curve values.3

flowchart TD
  A["NIX00270 Number of energies<br/>GRPSIZE 2"] --> B["NIX00271 Num of data pnts LC<br/>GRPSIZE 1"]
  B --> C["NIX00272 Compressed light curves<br/>(repeated NIX00271 times)"]
  A -. "repeated NIX00270 times" .-> B
  D["NIX00273 Num of data pnts TRIG<br/>GRPSIZE 1"] --> E["NIX00274 Compressed triggers"]
  F["NIX00275 Num of data pnts RCR<br/>GRPSIZE 1"] --> G["NIX00276 RCR"]

The diagram shows positions 18-24 of SPID 54118 as defined in vpd.3 Of the 45 variable packets, 38 have TPCF_SIZE 0 and 7 have 19, although the ICD recommends 0 for truly variable packets; three fixed packets (54127, 54138, 54292) also have size 0.331

SQL used (housekeeping, IIC, dumps, science) 
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, l.PLF_OFFBY, l.PLF_OFFBI, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC, c.PCF_CURTX
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME
 WHERE l.PLF_SPID = '54103' ORDER BY CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS INT), CAST(PLF_OFFBI AS INT);
-- same query on solo-2020-04-16.sqlite and solo-2025-09-16.sqlite for the comparison
SELECT PID_SPID, printf('0x%04X', CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT)), PID_DESCR
  FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '6' ORDER BY CAST(PID_PI1_VAL AS INT);
SELECT PID_APID, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '21';
SELECT v.*, p.PCF_DESCR FROM vpd v JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = v.VPD_NAME
 WHERE VPD_TPSD = '54118' ORDER BY CAST(VPD_POS AS INT);
SELECT p.PID_TPSD <> '-1', t.TPCF_SIZE, count(*) FROM tpcf t JOIN pid p ON p.PID_SPID = t.TPCF_SPID
 GROUP BY 1, 2;

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
The 681 parameters are named by the Solar Orbiter convention: N for a monitoring parameter, a second letter I for instrument and X for STIX, as on the spacecraft MIB's name prefix table.4 Within the IDB:3

Prefix Count Meaning in the data NIX0 397 ordinary parameters (counters, temperatures, science fields) NIXD 214 "detail" fields: bits or bit groups of a larger word NIXG 63 "global" container words NIXS 3 synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR = D) ZZPA 4 fillers ZZPAD008, ZZPAD016, ZZPAD024, ZZPAD032

The mission file pcf_glob_det relates 62 global words to 213 details in three columns. In every one of the 92 rows where both parameters appear in the same fixed packet, the third column equals the detail's bit position measured from the start of its global word, (detail octet - global octet) x 8 + detail bit - global bit; for example NIXG0001 holds NIXD0304 "EDAC reason for reboot" at bit 0, NIXD0302 "WDT reason for reboot" at bit 2 and NIXD0303 "Currently running IDPU" at bit 7.3 Only NIXD0064 is not a detail, and only NIXG0064 is not a global; both belong to the 1-bit attenuator flag of the 2020 layout.35

PTC / PFC Type (SCOS-2000 table) Parameters 3 / 4, 3 / 12, 3 / 14 8-, 16-, 32-bit unsigned 162, 134, 101 3 / 8, 3 / 2, 3 / 6, 3 / 13, 3 / 1, 3 / 0, 3 / 10 12-, 6-, 10-, 24-, 5-, 4-, 14-bit unsigned 40, 33, 24, 20, 13, 2, 1 2 / 1 to 2 / 32 enumerated, 1 to 32 bits 124 1 / 0 Boolean, 1 bit 18 4 / 4 8-bit signed 4 7 / 6, 7 / 12 fixed 6- and 12-octet strings 3, 1 9 / 17 absolute time, CUC 6 octets 1

The type names are those of the ICD's Appendix A.333 576 parameters are numerical and 105 status (PCF_CATEG), 678 are raw telemetry and 3 synthetic; 157 have a calibration, 23 have the unit V, 20 degC, 6 mA; none uses a validity parameter (PCF_VALID is empty everywhere).3 Seventeen parameters appear in no packet: the three synthetics, three fillers, the unused globals NIXG0013 and NIXG0064, and nine others such as NIX00060 "Flare Message" and NIX00309 "Flare strength".3

Explore, for example, NIXD0058 HK_DET_C or NIX00059 heartbeat.

SQL used (parameters) 
SELECT substr(PCF_NAME, 1, 4), count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
SELECT PCF_CATEG, PCF_NATUR, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1, 2;
-- bit offset check of pcf_glob_det (92 of 92 rows match)
SELECT count(*), sum(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM plf a JOIN plf b ON a.PLF_SPID = b.PLF_SPID
         WHERE a.PLF_NAME = g.COL1 AND b.PLF_NAME = g.COL2
           AND (CAST(b.PLF_OFFBY AS INT) - CAST(a.PLF_OFFBY AS INT)) * 8
               + CAST(b.PLF_OFFBI AS INT) - CAST(a.PLF_OFFBI AS INT) = CAST(g.COL3 AS INT)))
  FROM pcf_glob_det g
 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM plf a JOIN plf b ON a.PLF_SPID = b.PLF_SPID
                WHERE a.PLF_NAME = g.COL1 AND b.PLF_NAME = g.COL2);
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR FROM pcf
 WHERE PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PLF_NAME FROM plf) AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT VPD_NAME FROM vpd);

docs.title: Calibrations
docs.text:
Kind Tables Definitions Parameters using them Examples Numerical (interpolated curves) caf / cap 14 / 75 points 42 CIXP0024TM "Temperature Sensors" (degC, used by 20 parameters), CIXP0025TM "PSU DPU 1V5 Current" (mA) Polynomial mcf 7 10 CIX00035TM HK_DPU_1V5_V with A1 = 0.000735043, CIX00040TM "Scaling by 15.2588", CIX00041TM "CPU scaling" (A1 = 4) Textual, STIX-specific txf / txp 45 CIXT... 68 CIXT0023TM instrument mode, CIXT0120TM SSID names Textual, generic txf / txp 36 CAAT... 37 CAAT0001TM Off_On, CAAT0021TM Still_Moving, CAAT0033TM False_True

The figures are from the IDB.3 The 36 CAAT textual calibrations are not STIX-specific: the 2025 spacecraft MIB has 36 of them and uses them for parameters of many subsystems (1 096 NRU parameters alone); the IDB has the same set except that it contains CAAT0008TM, which no STIX parameter uses and the 2025 MIB lacks, and lacks CAAT1008TM "OBCP_boolean".34 How the ICD defines these tables is on Calibration in the MIB.

The textual calibrations give the instrument's state model:3

Calibration Values CIXT0023TM instrument mode 0 LIKELY_BOOT, 1 BOOT, 2 SAFE, 3 MAINTENANCE, 4 CONFIGURATION, 5 NOMINAL CIXT0024TM mode transition reason 0 TC_TRANSITION, 1 AUTO_NOMINAL, 2 AUTO_FAILURE CIXT0021TM software running 0 ASW, 1 SuSW CIXT0057TM StartASW state machine 0 INIT, 1 BOOTVALID, 2 BOOTINVALID, 3 AUTOLOAD, 4 AUTOEXECUTE, 5 IDLE, 6 LOAD, 7 EXE, 8 SAVE, 9 EXECUTEASW CIXT0208TM system ID 1 IDPU, 2 DETECTORS, 3 ASPECT SYSTEM, 4 ATTENUATOR, 5 PSU

The available sources list these modes, reasons and states but not the transitions allowed between them.

docs.title: Monitoring checks and the three synthetic parameters
docs.text:
Fourteen housekeeping parameters - DPU, SpaceWire, detector and attenuator currents and the DPU, reference, SpaceWire link, high and attenuator voltages - have monitoring checks, all on raw values (OCF_INTER = U, OCF_CODIN = I) and all to be confirmed by one sample (OCF_NBCHCK = 1).3 An ocp check applies only when its applicability parameter (OCP_RLCHK) is valid and equals OCP_VALPAR; checks are tried in order and the search stops at the first applicable check or soft/hard pair, unless the system is configured to apply all of them.34 STIX uses this to change limits with the instrument configuration, and the three synthetic parameters exist only to provide those applicability values. Each is a dynamic OL parameter (PCF_NATUR = D), whose source is an ASCII file named after the parameter in the synthetic/ folder, evaluated by SCOS-2000 when a contributing parameter changes.353

Synthetic Description Returns (from CIXTS00xTM) Computed from NIXS0001 DPU_SPW_C criter 0 ASW_SpW_Off, 1 ASW_Single_SpW, 2 ASW_Both_SpW, 3 SuSW_Limits 3 if NIXD0021 (software running) is 1 (SuSW), else the sum of the two SpaceWire power flags NIXD0080 + NIXD0081 NIXS0002 DPU_DET_C criter 0 NOT_POWERED, 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q 0 in SuSW, else the number of powered detector quadrants NIXD0082-NIXD0085 NIXS0003 ATT_C criteria 0, 1 or 2 motors 0 in SuSW, else the number of moving attenuator motors NIXD0088 + NIXD0089

The OL files use if ... then ... else ... endif, return(...), local variables (VAR_spw := NIXD0081.raw+NIXD0080.raw;) and the .raw view of parameters.3 All three return 8-bit enumerated values with a textual calibration.3 See Synthetic parameters and the OL language.

The limits of the detector current NIXD0058 (HK_DET_C, mA) then follow the number of powered quadrants:3

OCP_POS Type Raw low Raw high Applies when 1 soft 0 80 NIXS0002 = 0 (not powered) 2 soft 0 188 NIXS0002 = 1 3 soft 19 310 NIXS0002 = 2 4 soft 39 433 NIXS0002 = 3 5 soft 59 555 NIXS0002 = 4 6 hard 0 546 always (no applicability parameter) 
flowchart LR
  Q["NIXD0082..85<br/>quadrant power flags"] --> S["NIXS0002<br/>(OL: count of powered quadrants)"]
  W["NIXD0021<br/>SW running"] --> S
  S -->|"OCP_RLCHK = NIXS0002<br/>OCP_VALPAR = 0..4"| L["ocp soft limit set<br/>for NIXD0058"]
  T["NIXD0058 HK_DET_C<br/>(SID 2)"] --> L
  L --> O["OOL status"]

The same pattern selects the SpaceWire current limits of NIXD0030 by NIXS0001 (positions 1-4) and the attenuator current limits of NIXD0075 by NIXS0003, while the DPU 1.5 V current NIXD0029 switches its limits directly on NIXD0021 (ASW or SuSW) and the SpaceWire link voltages NIXD0031/NIXD0032 on the link power flags.3

Inference

By the ICD's stop-at-first rule, the hard check at position 6 of NIXD0058 is reached only when none of the five soft checks applies, which happens only if NIXS0002 is invalid or outside 0-4, because a soft check followed by a soft check with a different criterion is not a soft/hard pair.34 The same holds for the trailing hard checks of NIXD0029 and NIXD0030. For NIXD0075 the order is soft (0 motors), soft (1 motor), hard (no criterion), soft (2 motors): with two motors moving, the search would stop at the hard check and the 2-motor soft limits (raw 28-870) would never be used. Whether ESOC configures SCOS-2000 to apply all applicable checks (the global option the ICD mentions) is not stated in the available sources. Note also that for four quadrants the hard high limit of NIXD0058 (546) is below the soft one (555).

SQL used (checks and synthetics) 
SELECT o.*, p.PCF_DESCR, p.PCF_UNIT FROM ocf o JOIN pcf p ON p.PCF_NAME = o.OCF_NAME;
SELECT * FROM ocp ORDER BY OCP_NAME, CAST(OCP_POS AS INT);
SELECT * FROM synthetic;                       -- the three OL sources
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR LIKE 'CIXTS%';

docs.title: The TC packet header
docs.text:
The IDB defines one TC header, NOM_TC "STANDARD TC PKT", whose 13 pcdf elements give the packet header and the 4-octet PUS data field header bit by bit:3

The element types F, A, P, K, T and S mean a fixed value, the command's APID, a value set by the command subsystem, and the acknowledgement flags, type and subtype taken from ccf.36 The layout is the spacecraft ICD's: 3-bit version 0, type 1, header flag 1, a 14-bit count and stand-alone sequence flags 0b11, a non-CCSDS secondary header with PUS version 1, and acknowledgement bits for acceptance (least significant) and completion (most significant).910 CCF_ACK = 9 = 0b1001 asks for both reports for every STIX command.337 The STIX header fixes the source ID to 0, whereas the packet ICD reserves ground source IDs 110-113, 120 (direct commands) and the spares 121-122, and the SWA IDB fixes 120; the 2025 spacecraft MIB's own NOM_TC uses an element of type O for it, a type that the ICD issue 7.0 list (F, A, T, S, K, P) does not define.312436

docs.title: Commands by service
docs.text:
Service Commands Subtypes Examples 3 housekeeping 3 5, 6, 129 enable/disable HK report, update HK period 6 memory management 4 2 (two variants), 5, 9 ZIX0602A/ZIX0602B load memory, dump, check 9 time 1 129 ZIX09129 accept time synchronisation (one 9/17 time parameter) 17 test 1 1 connection test 20 information distribution 1 128 ZIX20128 on APID 796 21 science transfer 3 1, 2, 128 enable/disable transfer to the SSMM (32-bit SSID mask), reset output buffer 22 context 2 1, 3 request context, accept context 236 instrument management 25 1-15, 17, 18, 20 mode transition, warm reset, ASW image load/execute/save, subsystem power, eight configuration variants of TC(236,6), FDIR 237 parameters and data processing 41 1-11, 13-19 SuSW/ASW parameter load and report, calibration accumulation, 24 look-up-table uploads TC(237,7), QL, rate-control and compression parameters 238 archive memory 7 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 select data for download, free data, filesystem check, aspect burst data 239 detectors 12 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20 ASIC reset, temperature, baseline, dark current, threshold scan, test pulses, register read/write

The names given to services 236-239 in the first column summarise the IDB command descriptions; the packet ICD calls 236-240 only "STIX Private Services".38 All 100 commands are named ZIX + five characters and belong to subsystem 105; none is flagged critical (CCF_CRITICAL is N for 96 and empty for 4).3 Ninety-nine go to APID 1452; ZIX20128 alone goes to APID 796, PID 49 with category 12, which the packet ICD names the OBC payload broadcast process and the process addressed by TC(20,128).3617 Its 11 elements describe the whole 236-octet data field that the OBC sends, in TN-0007 order: platform data (36 octets), EPD (30), EUI (23), MAG (20), METIS (20), PHI (14), RPW (33), SoloHI (14), STIX (16, at bit 1520), SWA (16) and SPICE (14).320 Like every STIX command, ZIX20128 has CCF_ACK 9 and the fixed source ID 0 of NOM_TC, whereas the packet ICD describes the on-board TC(20,128) with Ack = 0 (no TM(1,1) or TM(1,7) from the payloads) and source ID 14 (system control); the 2025 MIB also keeps CCF_ACK 9.3174

The 669 command parameters (all PIX...) are 585 unsigned integers (PTC 3), 71 enumerated, 11 fixed octet strings, one signed integer and one CUC time; 24 have a textual calibration through paf/pas and the rest are numerical without calibration; there are no range checks.3 For TC(236,1) "Mode transition", PIX00080 "Operation mode" offers BOOT (1), SAFE (2), MAINTENANCE (3), CONFIGURATION (4), NOMINAL (5) and ILLEGAL_MODE (6), and PIX00081 MANUAL_NOMINAL (0) or AUTO_NOMINAL (1); the largest commands are the QL and compression parameter updates TC(237,9) and TC(237,11), with 112 and 106 elements.3

Worked example: TC(236,1) to NOMINAL, manual (illustrative bytes)

Using the IDB definitions - APID 1452, NOM_TC, CCF_ACK 9, sequence count 0 chosen for the example, application data PIX00080 = 5 and PIX00081 = 0 - the packet is 1D AC C0 00 00 07 19 EC 01 00 05 00 92 D3: 0x1DAC = version 0, TC, header flag, APID 1452; 0xC000 = stand-alone, count 0; length 7 (8 octets of data field minus one); 0x19 = PUS version 1 with ack 0b1001; type 236 (0xEC), subtype 1, source ID 0; mode 5, transition 0; and the CRC-16 0x92D3, computed with the spacecraft ICD's CCITT algorithm (which gives 0x1D0F for 00 00, as the ICD's test vector).318 These bytes are constructed for explanation, not taken from a real command history. Browse the command as ZIX36001.

docs.title: Verification stages
docs.text:
Four cvs stages, all report-based (CVS_SOURCE = R) and opening immediately (CVS_START 0), cover all 100 commands through 200 cvp rows - one acceptance and one completion stage each:3

CVS_ID Stage CVS_INTERVAL Used by 54001 acceptance 20 s all 100 commands 54002 completion 60 s 82 commands 54003 completion 1 800 s ZIX36003 load ASW image to RAM, ZIX36014 execute ASW image 54004 completion 9 999 s 16 long operations: memory loads, mode transition, self-test, ASW save, RAM test, calibration accumulation, LUT apply, TM corridor limit, freeing archive data, threshold scan, test pulses, ASIC register read/write

CVS_START and CVS_INTERVAL are in seconds, the interval being the sampling interval from which SCOS-2000 computes the verification window; CVS_SPID is filled although the ICD allows it only for parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE = V) and calls it irrelevant for report-based ones.263 See Command verification in the MIB and stage 54004 in the explorer.

SQL used (commands) 
SELECT * FROM tcp; SELECT * FROM pcpc; SELECT * FROM pcdf;
SELECT CCF_TYPE, count(*), group_concat(DISTINCT CCF_STYPE) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT CCF_APID, CCF_ACK, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1, 2;
SELECT d.*, p.CPC_DESCR, p.CPC_PTC, p.CPC_PFC, p.CPC_PAFREF FROM cdf d
  LEFT JOIN cpc p ON p.CPC_NAME = d.CDF_PNAME
 WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('ZIX36001', 'ZIX20128') ORDER BY CDF_CNAME, CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CIXT0080TC', 'CIXT0081TC');
SELECT * FROM cvs; SELECT CVP_CVSID, count(*) FROM cvp GROUP BY 1;

docs.title: Mission-specific files
docs.text: Two files are not ICD tables. pcf_glob_det is described above. sw_para has 1 468 rows of three columns: a name, an always empty second column and a description. 653 names are monitoring parameters, 485 command parameters (PIX), 226 packet mnemonics (YIX, the TPCF_NAME values) and 100 commands; four rows hold 8-character text fragments ("(1...inv", "0...not", "The auto", "This rep") rather than names.3 The spacecraft release has the file as ASW_sw_para, with the same three columns; 1 464 of the 1 468 STIX names are in it (all but the four fragments).4 Twenty-four NIX parameters are not listed in sw_para.3

docs.title: How the IDB relates to the spacecraft MIB
docs.text:
Comparing names and definitions with the two copied spacecraft releases:345

Object STIX IDB In 2020 MIB In 2025 MIB Notes on 2025 Parameters (PCF_NAME) 681 669 681 description, PTC/PFC, category, nature, calibration and subsystem identical for all 681; 10 units differ (IDB has S, % or V, MIB none); PCF_DARC = 1 added for 300 Packets (PID_SPID) 246 246 246 APID, type, subtype, identification value, description and PID_TPSD identical; TPCF_SIZE differs for 69 (for example SID 1 46 → 59, TM(1,1) 22 → 20, seven variable science packets 19 → 0), while the 2020 sizes equal the IDB's Fixed layout (plf) 927 915 identical 926 identical only ZZPAD008 of SPID 54103 missing Variable layout (vpd) 774 709 identical 452 identical 13 science packets have one extra entry each in 2025, which shifts the VPD_POS of every later entry Commands (CCF_CNAME) 100 100 99 ZIX09129 absent; ZIXX0128 added Command elements (cdf) 1 377 1 370 identical 1 373 identical ZIX20128 reordered Checks, calibrations, synthetics, verification 14 / 32, 14 + 7 + 81, 3, 4 / 200 32 ocp identical, synthetics identical ocp identical, 80 txf, synthetics identical, 198 cvp pcf_glob_det 213 202 identical (of 204 NIX rows) 213 identical 2025 has 5 more rows

The STIX names all carry over, which answers the question whether the instrument's parameters are in the spacecraft MIB: every one of the 681 is there with the same type and calibration.4 The differences are few and specific:

  • New in the IDB since April 2020: twelve parameters - the IIC flare octet NIXG0021 with NIXD0505-NIXD0507, the rotating-buffer fill level and file statistics NIXD0501-NIXD0504 in SID 2, NIXD0500 "SpW failure source", NIXD0448 "Bit reduction", NIXD0449 "Flare in progress" and NIX00490 "Averaging value Asp TC" - and the reworked SID 4 layout described above; the 2020 parameter NIX00441 "Delta time in 0.1 sec" is gone.35
  • Changed after the IDB, in 2025: the 1-bit NIXD0448 "Bit reduction", which the IDB places only in the calibration background packet 54124 (offset -13 after the 16-bit NIXG0404 "SSID global 3" word, that is bit 3 of the word), is inserted the same way into 13 more science packets (54110-54118, 54120, 54121, 54142, 54143); the following pixel mask NIXD0407 changes its offset from -12 to 0 and so keeps its position; ten parameters NIXDZ401-NIXDZ405 "Pixel mask n detail" and NIXGZ401-NIXGZ405 "SSID global 3.n" are added to pcf and pcf_glob_det but used in no packet.43
  • TC(20,128): the 2025 ZIX20128 places SPICE after SoloHI at bit 1520 and STIX and SWA after it, an order that differs from TN-0007, while a new ZIXX0128 "STIX Information Distribution Aligned", described as duplicated from ZIX20128, keeps the IDB and TN-0007 order (STIX at 1520, SWA at 1648, SPICE at 1776).4320
  • Removed by 2025: ZIX09129, TC(9,129) accept time synchronisation, as for the other instruments' TC(9,129) commands (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS).4
timeline
  title STIX definitions in the copied databases
  2020-04-16 : Spacecraft MIB 10720PFM - 669 of the IDB's 681 parameters, 246 STIX packets, 100 commands
  2024-02-02 : STIX IDB 2.26.38 (STX_226, PFM_applicable) - 681 parameters, new IIC flare octet
  2025-09-16 : Spacecraft MIB 25925PFM - all 681 IDB parameters plus 10 NIX?Z40x, 99 IDB commands plus ZIXX0128

Inference

The pattern - every IDB parameter and packet in the 2025 spacecraft MIB with identical definitions (apart from 10 units and 69 tpcf sizes), 2020 differences that the IDB resolves towards TN-0007, and 2025 additions (DARC flags, the bit-reduction field, the aligned TC(20,128), corrected record counts) absent from the IDB - suggests that the spacecraft MIB imports the STIX team's database and that ESA or the STIX team applied later changes on the MIB side. The 2.26.38 copy may also not be the latest IDB; the import process is not described in the available sources. The parallel analysis for SWA reaches the same conclusion (see SWA).

SQL used (comparison with the spacecraft MIB) 
-- run on stix-idb-2.26.38.sqlite
ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m;
ATTACH 'file:solo-2020-04-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS o;
SELECT count(*), sum(PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM m.pcf)),
       sum(PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM o.pcf)) FROM main.pcf;         -- 681 | 681 | 669
SELECT count(*), sum(a.PCF_DESCR = b.PCF_DESCR), sum(a.PCF_PTC = b.PCF_PTC AND a.PCF_PFC = b.PCF_PFC),
       sum(ifnull(a.PCF_UNIT, '') = ifnull(b.PCF_UNIT, ''))
  FROM main.pcf a JOIN m.pcf b ON a.PCF_NAME = b.PCF_NAME;                 -- 681 | 681 | 681 | 671
SELECT count(*) FROM main.plf a JOIN m.plf b ON a.PLF_NAME = b.PLF_NAME AND a.PLF_SPID = b.PLF_SPID
   AND a.PLF_OFFBY = b.PLF_OFFBY AND a.PLF_OFFBI = b.PLF_OFFBI;            -- 926
SELECT count(*) FROM main.vpd a JOIN m.vpd b ON a.VPD_TPSD = b.VPD_TPSD AND a.VPD_POS = b.VPD_POS
   AND a.VPD_NAME = b.VPD_NAME AND a.VPD_GRPSIZE = b.VPD_GRPSIZE AND a.VPD_OFFSET = b.VPD_OFFSET;  -- 452
SELECT VPD_TPSD, count(*) FROM m.vpd WHERE VPD_NAME = 'NIXD0448' GROUP BY 1;   -- 14 packets
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR FROM m.pcf WHERE PCF_NAME LIKE 'NIX%'
   AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM main.pcf);                     -- NIXDZ40x, NIXGZ40x
SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM m.ccf);   -- ZIX09129
SELECT count(*), sum(a.TPCF_SIZE <> b.TPCF_SIZE) FROM main.tpcf a JOIN m.tpcf b
    ON a.TPCF_SPID = b.TPCF_SPID;                                           -- 246 | 69 (0 against o.tpcf)
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf_glob_det a JOIN o.pcf_glob_det b
    ON a.COL1 = b.COL1 AND a.COL2 = b.COL2 AND a.COL3 = b.COL3;             -- 202
SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_BIT, CDF_ELLEN, CDF_PNAME FROM m.cdf
 WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('ZIX20128', 'ZIXX0128') ORDER BY 1, CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);

docs.title: Quality notes
docs.text:
The following inconsistencies are visible in the data (this wiki's queries):3

  • CIXP0024TM declares 13 curve points (CAF_NCURVE) but has 14 cap rows, and six textual calibrations (CIXT0025TM, CIXT0340TM, CIXT0359TM, CIXT0401TM, CIXT1168TM, CIXTS001TM) declare a TXF_NALIAS different from their txp row count, as do two command text calibrations with PAF_NALIAS (CIXT0032TC declares 11 and has 8 pas rows, CIXT0080TC declares 5 and has 6); the ICD defines all three fields as the number of rows in the companion table.272829
  • Six commands have a CCF_NPARS different from their number of cdf elements: ZIX20128 (declares 0, has 11), ZIX37009 (115, 112), ZIX37010 (7, 66), ZIX37011 (116, 106), ZIX38006 (2, 3) and ZIX39015 (7, 10); ZIX17001 leaves the field empty and has no elements. The ICD offers the field for exactly this consistency check.38
  • SPID 54292 "Error - SDRAM init pattern memory test" has the TPCF_NAME YIX54929, not the YIX54292 the naming pattern of the other 245 packets would give.
  • The 2025 spacecraft MIB has every one of these counts consistent: CIXP0024TM declares 14 points, the six TXF_NALIAS and two PAF_NALIAS values equal their row counts, and the six commands' CCF_NPARS equal their cdf elements (ZIX17001 has 0). It keeps YIX54929.4
  • The tpcf sizes of variable packets mix 0 and 19 (see above), the sizes of HK SID 1 (46) and SID 2 (105) are shorter than their plf layouts (59 and 109 octets), and pic defines a TM(239,16) with no packet.31

docs.title: Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database
docs.text:
SWA, the Solar Wind Analyser, is one of the ten Solar Orbiter instruments. Its Data Processing Unit (DPU) interface document describes a suite of four sensors - two Electron Analyser Systems (EAS1 and EAS2), a Proton Alpha Sensor (PAS) and a Heavy Ion Sensor (HIS) - each connected to the DPU by a 10 Mb/s SpaceWire link.1210 The 2007 Experiment Interface Document lists the same instrument as the "Solar Wind Plasma Analyzer"27, and planning documents refer to the sensors individually, for example the light-sensitive "SWA-EAS".2 The SWA/PAS team at IRAP (the DPU ICD cites IRAP documents for the PAS unit and its interface to the DPU)11 hosts the server from which this wiki copied the Solar Orbiter MIB, and the same server carries the SWA instrument database (IDB): the instrument's packets, parameters, calibrations and commands written as SCOS-2000 MIB tables, with release notes from Planetek Italia.37

This page analyses two copied IDB versions - 6.3.4 (the file ASCII.zip) and 6.5.0 - reads the release notes against the data and against the SWA DPU Communications ICD, and checks, by name and by content, how much of each version is in the spacecraft database. The interface documents themselves are presented on Solar Orbiter instrument interfaces; the STIX instrument database is analysed the same way on Solar Orbiter STIX instrument database.

What was copied

Item SWA IDB 6.3.4 (ASCII.zip) SWA IDB 6.5.0 Library item swa-idb-ascii swa-idb-v6-5-0 Original URL https://solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/MIB/ASCII.zip https://solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/MIB/SWA_IDB_v6.5.0.zip Copied (UTC) 2026-11-05 14:26:47 2026-11-12 17:52:24 Size 142 018 bytes 115 876 bytes SHA-256 aad3e32da477e39cc47d7872a2538eacb37c0559f45a3dc6ec1a6c6fa501dbdb 9f63f211dc1890df42d754c40dedb394af80f032a68b05c677e3b8ba1d9f5eaa Contents folder ASCII/ with 56 .dat files (32 non-empty) dated 2021-12-03 and an empty synthetic/ folder; 59 __MACOSX resource entries (56 dated 2021-12-03, the two folder entries 2021-12-13, one 2015-10-02) folder SWA_IDB_v6.5.0/ASCII/ with 56 .dat files (32 non-empty) dated 2025-06-17, an empty synthetic/ folder dated 2015-10-02, and the release notes IDB_relNotes.txt (2025-06-17); no __MACOSX entries Last vdf record (file order) SWA_6.3.4, "Released on 29/11/2021" SWA_6.3.3_wa, "Released on 04/11/2021" Explorer swa swa65

The URLs, times, sizes and hashes are from this wiki's source registry;34 the contents and dates are from the zip directories and the files themselves.56 The __MACOSX entries of the older zip show it was made on a Macintosh. In both versions the .dat files use Windows (CR LF) line ends, unlike the spacecraft MIB files and the Unix format that the ICD specifies.56831

docs.title: The instrument behind the database
docs.text:
The DPU is, in the words of its ICD, the "heart" of SWA: it provides power, control, temporary storage, communication and computing for the suite. Its hardware is a backplane with six SpaceWire splitters, two Data Processing Modules (each a communication and science data processing board plus a CPU board) and two Power Conditioning and Distribution Modules (PCDM), which also receive the spacecraft's high-power pulse commands and collect housekeeping.12 The application software receives telecommands, sends housekeeping, event and (when enabled) science telemetry, commands and powers the sensor heads (except HIS, which the spacecraft powers on a dedicated line), keeps five minutes of high-resolution EAS1, EAS2 and PAS data for transmission when an event trigger arrives, computes moments and compresses data, maintains time synchronisation, and exchanges data with the other instruments through PUS service 20.13

flowchart LR
  OBC["Spacecraft OBC and SSMM"] <-- "SpaceWire: TC and TM packets, time codes" --> DPU
  subgraph SWA["SWA instrument"]
    DPU["DPU<br/>2 DPM + 2 PCDM, LEON2<br/>VxWorks, EXOS, PUS library<br/>PCMSW + SDPSW"]
    DPU <-- "SpaceWire 10 Mb/s" --> E1["EAS1"]
    DPU <-- "SpaceWire 10 Mb/s" --> E2["EAS2"]
    DPU <-- "SpaceWire 10 Mb/s" --> P["PAS"]
    DPU <-- "SpaceWire 10 Mb/s" --> H["HIS"]
  end

The diagram follows §3 and §4 of the DPU ICD.1213 The software has three layers: the application software (the process control and TM/TC software PCMSW, and the science data processing software SDPSW), an application service layer with the PUS library, and a machine services layer with the VxWorks real-time kernel, the extended operating system EXOS and the board support package, all on a LEON2 processor. A boot software in PROM, which cannot be patched, tests the memories and loads the application from MRAM. The SDPSW compresses distributions losslessly with a CCSDS 121 compliant algorithm and computes the moments of order 0 (number density), 1 (number flux density vector), 2 (moment flux density tensor, as the ICD calls it) and, for EAS only, 3 (energy flux density vector).13

docs.title: Which software component owns which service
docs.text:
The DPU ICD groups the telecommands by the software component that handles them. This explains the private service types that the IDB uses:151617192021

Component (ICD table) Service types Examples PUS manager (Table 2) standard 3, 5, 6, 9, 17, 20, 21; private 200 subtypes 170-173 for parameter monitoring and 174-176 for the error/event handler TC(3,5) enable HK, TC(6,5) dump memory, TC(9,129) accept time update, TC(20,128) inter-instrument data, TC(200,170) enable monitoring DPU manager (Table 3) 200 TC(200,128) enter diagnostic mode, TC(200,133) modify configuration parameters, TC(200,136) enable/disable IIC test Sensor manager (Table 4) 200, subtypes 160-165 TC(200,160) all sensors to burst mode, TC(200,162) cadence mode, TC(200,163) time offset EAS1 / EAS2 managers (Table 5) 201 / 202 TC(201/202,131) switch on EAS, TC(201/202,164-171) engineering modes 2-9 PAS manager (Table 6) 203 TC(203,128) calibration mode, TC(203,157) start science HIS manager (Table 7) 200, subtypes 153-155 switch HIS on and off, start a HIS macro HIS internal TCs (Table 8) 204 TC(204,135) HIS high voltage, TC(204,180) emergency HV ramp-down

The spacecraft packet ICD reserves services 200 to 205 for SWA's private services, so all of these stay within the allocation.36 The ICD's TC and TM data field headers are the spacecraft ones (PUS version 1, 8-bit source or destination ID, 48-bit CUC time):14

Together with the 6-octet primary header this is the 16-octet header that every IDB packet declares (PID_DFHSIZE = 16).146 The header layout is discussed for the whole spacecraft on PUS packet structures.

docs.title: Versions: the vdf table as a release history
docs.text:
The ICD's vdf table normally holds a single record naming the database version; if several are present, the last one imported sets the name.29 The SWA IDB instead keeps all the versions it has been through, each with a release date in the comment and the major and minor numbers in VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE. Version 6.3.4 has 70 records:5

Versions Records Dates (from VDF_COMMENT) SWA_00.2, SWA_00.3 2 "Received from MSSL", "SWA Mandatory test" SWA_1.0 1 02/10/2015 SWA_2.0.0 to SWA_2.7.4 27 08/03/2016 to 07/03/2017 SWA_3.0.0 to SWA_3.4.0 12 14/03/2017 to 26/05/2017 SWA_4.0.0 to SWA_4.2.1 9 26/06/2017 to 28/11/2017 SWA_5.0.0 to SWA_5.4.1 7 22/12/2017 to 13/03/2019 SWA_6.0.0 to SWA_6.3.4 12 30/04/2019 to 29/11/2021, including 6.3.4_beta (30/11/2021) and 6.3.3_wa

MSSL, the source of the first version, is the Mullard Space Science Laboratory in the DPU ICD's acronym list.10 The records are not in chronological order inside each minor version (for example SWA_2.3.2 precedes SWA_2.3.1 and SWA_2.3.0), and SWA_6.3.4_beta, dated a day after SWA_6.3.4, is filed before SWA_6.3.0; by the ICD rule the effective name is the last record, SWA_6.3.4.529 67 of the 70 names are longer than the Char(8) of VDF_NAME, the longest having 14 characters; the ICD's importer truncates an over-long field and issues a warning.52931

Version 6.5.0 does not record itself. Its vdf file holds the same 70 records with the same names and comments, but SWA_6.3.4 has moved up next to SWA_6.3.4_beta, before SWA_6.3.0, so the last record is now SWA_6.3.3_wa; none of the eight versions 6.4.0 to 6.5.0 has a record.6

Inference

Imported by the ICD rule, the 6.5.0 files would name the database after SWA_6.3.3_wa (and, truncated to 8 characters, SWA_6.3.), not 6.5.0. The folder name and the release notes are then the only places where the version appears. Whether the instrument team or the MOC renames the database on import is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: The release notes
docs.text:
IDB_relNotes.txt, inside the 6.5.0 zip, is headed "SWA IDB RELEASE NOTES", names Planetek Italia srl and one author, and carries a header date of 13/06/2016. It has 75 entries, from 2.0.0 (08/03/2016, "IDB version released with EGSE SW spacePTS v2.0") to 6.5.0 (17/06/2025), each with the version, date, change description and author.7 The IRAP directory also lists other SWA IDB versions (SWA_IDB_v5.1, v6.0.1, v6.3.3_wa, v6.3.4_beta2, v6.4.6), which were not copied.40

Inference

The DPU ICD lists Planetek ("PK") among its acronyms, has a Planetek address in its distribution list and carries the Planetek Italia logo in its page header next to those of TSD Space, Leonardo and SITAEL.10 This suggests that the IDB maintainer is part of the DPU team, but neither the ICD nor the release notes says so.

Compared with the vdf records, the notes have no entries for the three earliest versions (00.2, 00.3 and 1.0), the vdf has none for 6.4.0 to 6.5.0, and three dates differ: 2.1.0 (notes 10/06/2016, vdf 09/06/2016), 5.1.0 (21/02/2018 against 12/02/2018) and 6.3.4_beta (03/12/2021 against 30/11/2021).76

The notes tie most major steps to an issue of the SWA DPU Communications ICD (SO-SWA-DPU_CD-IC-003), whose own change record gives the issue dates:726

IDB version (date) Aligned with DPU ICD issue ICD issue date 2.1.0 (10/06/2016), 2.2.0 (16/06/2016) 4 08/06/2016 2.3.0 (19/07/2016) 4.1 25/07/2016 2.4.4 (31/08/2016) 4.2 30/08/2016 2.6.0 (04/11/2016) 4.3 21/10/2016 3.0.0 (14/03/2017) 4.4 10/03/2017 3.1.0 (30/03/2017) 4.5 30/03/2017 4.0.0 (26/06/2017) 5.0 not dated in the change record 5.0.0 (22/12/2017) 6.0 27/11/2017 5.2.0 (23/05/2018) 6.1 21/02/2018 5.3.0 (14/11/2018) 6.2 31/07/2018 5.4.0 (11/03/2019), 5.4.1 (13/03/2019) 7.0, 7.1 08/03/2019, 13/03/2019 6.0.0 (30/04/2019) 8.0 30/04/2019 6.2.0 (17/06/2019) 8.1 17/06/2019 6.3.3 (11/10/2021) "ICD v8.2" for three packets, "ICD v8.3" for APIDs 8.2: 07/08/2019; 8.3: not in the library

The IDB 2.3.0 entry claims alignment with ICD issue 4.1 six days before the date that the ICD gives that issue. Issue 8.2, the copy in the library, changed only editorial matters.726 Other entries record remarks from MSSL and from Airbus, fixes found with a tool named "PDIT v1.0", HIS definitions taken from a HIS spreadsheet and the HIS telemetry ICD, calibration updates and individual packet and command fixes.7

docs.title: What changed from 6.3.4 to 6.5.0
docs.text:
The eight release-note entries after 6.3.4 can be checked against the two copied versions row by row:756

Release note (date) What the data show, 6.3.4 to 6.5.0 6.4.0 (14/02/2022) "CIAT0068TC Updated" the command calibration CIAT0068TC (SENS_RATE_2, PAS and HIS rates of ZIA58728) gains the value 0 NOTHING beside 1 NOMINAL_CADENCE and 2 LOW_CADENCE; the notes record that 6.3.3 had added it and 6.3.4_beta reverted it 6.4.1 (04/05/2022) "MCF and OCF Updated" three polynomial curves change slope: CIAP0002TM (PCDM_EAS2) 0.149066 to 0.19062938, CIAP0003TM (PCDM_EAS1) 0.151137 to 0.19062938, CIAP0005TM (PCDM_PAS) 0.283553 to 0.45487188, used by the mA currents NIA00832, NIA00833, NIA00835; four ocf records NIA05128-NIA05131 switch from raw integer limits (U/I) to calibrated real limits (C/R) 6.4.2, 6.4.3 (03-04/2023) "Updated TC(200,162) SELECT CADENCE TC" see 6.4.5 6.4.4 (05/05/2023) "Updated OCP table with NIA05131" nine ocp rows differ: eight limit ranges change (for example the high-voltage monitors NIA05122/NIA05126 from 0-40 to 1900-2200, and NIA05130 from 6000-6500 to the 90-450 that 6.3.4 had on NIA05131), and NIA05131 keeps its ocf record but has no ocp row. With only two versions copied, which of 6.4.1 and 6.4.4 made each limit change cannot be told 6.4.5 (05/06/2023) "ZIA58728 moved to ZIA58950", "ZIA58728 restored to v6.4.1" both commands exist: ZIA58728 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE_MODE unchanged and the new ZIA58950 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE, both TC(200,162); six new command parameters and six new command calibrations (CIAT0070TC to CIAT0075TC); CIAT0069TC (SENS_EN) removed 6.4.6 (11/06/2025) "Add ZIA58951 and ZIA58952", "Update CIAT0066TM in txp file" ZIA58951/ZIA58952 SWA_TC_SET_EAS1/2_SUMMATION, TC(201,174)/TC(202,174), one 16-bit parameter PIA60860; failure codes 43149 and 43150 of the textual calibration CIAT0066TM renamed from Eas1FOffEntErr/Eas2FOffEntErr to Eas1BadSum/Eas2BadSum 6.5.0 (17/06/2025) "Add SPIDs 58730, 58731, 58732, 58733 in PID table" four TM(1,8) failure reports on APID 1585 with 7 plf entries each (28 plf rows)

Nothing else differs: pcf, pcf_glob_det, txf, vpd, pic and the TC header tables are identical, and the remaining row-count changes (cdf +11, cpc +7, cvp +6, sw_para +1) are the entries of the three new commands.56 The ocf change matters: the ICD defines OCF_INTER = C as limits expressed in engineering (calibrated) values and OCF_CODIN = R as real values, so the new ranges are in calibrated units.32

Inference

The copy called 6.3.4 on this page appears to hold the 6.3.4_beta state. Its CIAT0068TC lacks the value 0 NOTHING, which the notes say 6.3.3 added and only 6.3.4_beta removed (the 6.3.4 entry itself reverts only PIA60352 and PIA60357), and its .dat files are dated 2021-12-03, the date that the notes give 6.3.4_beta.75 Because the SWA_6.3.4_beta record is filed before SWA_6.3.0, the ICD rule still names the database SWA_6.3.4.

SQL used (versions and the 6.3.4 to 6.5.0 differences) 

-- swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite, with the 6.3.4 copy attached
ATTACH 'file:swa-idb.sqlite?mode=ro' AS o;
SELECT rowid, VDF_NAME, VDF_COMMENT FROM main.vdf ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 8;   -- last: SWA_6.3.3_wa
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR
  FROM main.pid WHERE PID_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM o.pid);            -- 58730-58733
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_DESCR, CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_NPARS
  FROM main.ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM o.ccf);           -- ZIA58950-58952
SELECT * FROM main.ocf EXCEPT SELECT * FROM o.ocf;
SELECT * FROM main.ocp EXCEPT SELECT * FROM o.ocp;  SELECT * FROM o.ocp EXCEPT SELECT * FROM main.ocp;
SELECT * FROM main.txp EXCEPT SELECT * FROM o.txp;
SELECT * FROM main.paf EXCEPT SELECT * FROM o.paf;  SELECT * FROM o.paf EXCEPT SELECT * FROM main.paf;
SELECT a.MCF_IDENT, b.MCF_POL2, a.MCF_POL2 FROM main.mcf a JOIN o.mcf b USING (MCF_IDENT)
 WHERE a.MCF_POL2 IS NOT b.MCF_POL2;
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf a JOIN o.pcf b USING (PCF_NAME)
 WHERE a.PCF_DESCR IS NOT b.PCF_DESCR OR a.PCF_PTC IS NOT b.PCF_PTC OR a.PCF_PFC IS NOT b.PCF_PFC
    OR a.PCF_CURTX IS NOT b.PCF_CURTX OR a.PCF_UNIT IS NOT b.PCF_UNIT;           -- 0
The release-note entries were compared with the vdf records by a script that parses the version and date of each entry.

docs.title: What the IDB contains
docs.text:
Family Table IDB 6.3.4 IDB 6.5.0 SWA share of the 2025 spacecraft MIB Version vdf 70 70 1 (spacecraft) Parameters pcf 2 885 2 885 2 882 NIA parameters Packets pid / tpcf 609 / 609 613 / 613 613 on SWA APIDs pic 24 24 - plf / vpd 6 507 / 481 6 535 / 481 - Calibration caf / cap 1 / 8 1 / 8 - txf / txp 128 / 1 460 128 / 1 460 - mcf 80 80 - Checks ocf / ocp 206 / 326 206 / 325 - Commands ccf / cdf / cpc 198 / 1 173 / 531 201 / 1 184 / 538 200 commands on APID 1532 cca / ccs, paf / pas 3 / 15, 75 / 1 041 3 / 15, 80 / 1 054 - TC header tcp / pcpc / pcdf 1 / 6 / 13 1 / 6 / 13 - Verification cvs / cvp 2 / 396 2 / 402 - Groups, displays grp / grpk / dpf / dpc 2 / 4 / 1 / 1 2 / 4 / 1 / 1 - Mission files sw_para / pcf_glob_det 2 841 / 855 2 842 / 855 - Empty sequences, cur, lgf, cve, prf/prv, ptv, dst, graphic and scrolling displays, parameter sets, ssy, synthetics 0 0 -

The counts are from this wiki's queries.568 Three files differ from the spacecraft release: sw_para.dat replaces ASW_sw_para.dat, an empty ssy.dat (not an ICD table) is present, and the s13* and dup files are absent.58 The test-like entries are telling: the only display DQQA1234 is described as "This is a test", and the group GRPPAR as "Example for Parameters".5

docs.title: Which ICD issue the files follow
docs.text:
Counting TAB-separated fields per record, the IDB's pcf has 19 fields, cpc 13 and ccf 21 in both versions, against 23, 15 and 21 in the 2025 spacecraft MIB.568 Nineteen pcf fields and thirteen cpc fields are the issue 5.1 layouts,33 which the 7.0 importer still accepts for pcf (fields 20-23 are optional for backward compatibility).30 The effect is visible in the merged data: the spacecraft MIB sets PCF_DARC = 1 for 335 of the 2 885 SWA parameters, a field the IDB does not have.8 The STIX instrument database uses the same field counts (see STIX); see also History of the Database Import ICD.

SQL used (contents) 

-- swa-idb.sqlite (6.3.4) and swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite (6.5.0)
SELECT rowid, * FROM vdf;
SELECT sum(length(VDF_NAME) > 8), max(length(VDF_NAME)) FROM vdf;      -- 67 | 14
SELECT count(*) FROM pcf;                                             -- repeated per table
SELECT * FROM dpf; SELECT * FROM grp;
Field counts were taken from the .dat files with a TAB field count per line.

docs.title: APIDs and packets
docs.text:
Annex 8 of the packet structure ICD gives SWA the process IDs 95 to 99; the APID is the process ID times 16 plus the packet category.35 Both IDB versions use 15 APIDs; the DPU ICD's Table 1 assigns the SWA telemetry to 13 process ID and category pairs:5614

APID PID / CAT Category meaning 6.3.4 6.5.0 Types in the IDB DPU ICD issue 8.2, Table 1 1525 95 / 5 functional cyclic 1 1 TM(3,25) SID 255 SWA_TM_II_INFO HK for service 20 (PAS quick-look moments), SID 255 1532 95 / 12 science (and TC APID) 9 9 TM(21,3), TM(21,6) low-latency data: EAS quick-look SIDs 8, 9, 38, 39; PAS moments 215; PAS calibration 214; HIS 132-134 1540 96 / 4 routine HK 8 8 TM(3,25): DPU, EAS1, EAS2, PAS, HIS, boot SW, IIC data normal HK: DPU 11, 16; EAS 1, 2; HIS 100, 101; PAS 3 1542 96 / 6 functional non-cyclic 9 9 private 200-203 reports not listed 1544 96 / 8 diagnostic 9 9 TM(3,26) diagnostic HK: DPU 4-10, 12, 13 1545 96 / 9 dump 54 54 TM(6,6), TM(6,10) not listed 1548 96 / 12 science 45 45 TM(21,3), TM(21,6) normal science: EAS engineering, 3D and partial moments; PAS distributions and engineering; HIS normal mode 1564 97 / 12 science 25 25 TM(21,3), TM(21,6) optional burst and trigger data 1572 98 / 4 routine HK 2 2 SWA_TM_GROUND_MONITORING, SWA_TM_HIS_ALIVE ground monitoring HK 1580 98 / 12 science 13 13 TM(21,3), TM(21,6) core burst: EAS 4, PAS 208-213, HIS 128-131, 191 1585 99 / 1 verification 171 175 TM(1,1), (1,2), (1,7), (1,8) TARS (1,1), TARF (1,2), TECS (1,7), TECF (1,8) 1588 99 / 4 routine HK 1 1 SWA_TM_OBC_FDIR_HK HK for OBC action 1591 99 / 7 events 249 249 TM(5,1)-(5,4), TM(17,2) events TM(5,1)-(5,4) 1593 99 / 9 dump 9 9 private 200-203 reports memory dump and checksum, TM(17,2), reports (200,249)-(200,253) and (201/202/203,200) 1596 99 / 12 science 4 4 TM(21,3) EAS engineering product (low latency), engineering modes 3 and 4

The category meanings are those of Annex 8.35 Every packet has PID_DFHSIZE = 16 with a time field and no CRC check, like the spacecraft packets, and 88 are variable packets with a VPD structure.56 Events and verification reports dominate: 199 low-severity TM(5,2) and 149 (6.3.4) or 153 (6.5.0) TM(1,8) failure definitions, because each event ID and failure code is a separate packet (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS).56

Two differences between the IDB and ICD issue 8.2 are documented in the release notes:

  • TM(17,2). The ICD lists the connection test report in the category 9 group of APID 1593, while the IDB has it (SWA_TM_CT_REP, SPID 58061) on the event APID 1591; IDB 2.3.0 (July 2016) had already set its category to 7, the category that the spacecraft packet ICD assigns to service 5 and TM(17,2).147356
  • The 1542 and 1545 APIDs. ICD 8.2 puts the memory dumps and the private reports on 99/9 (APID 1593). IDB 6.3.3 (11/10/2021) "fixed some APID according to ICD v8.3", moving them to 1542 and 1545, and 6.3.3_wa (04/11/2021) added nine report packets, SPIDs 58191-58199, back on APID 1593 "as in v6.2.1", which is why the IDB carries each private report twice.75 Issue 8.3 is not in the library.

The housekeeping structure IDs are: TM(3,25) SIDs 1 EAS1, 2 EAS2, 3 PAS, 11 DPU, 14 OBC FDIR, 15 ground monitoring, 16 IIC data, 20 boot software, 100 HIS boot, 101 HIS, 102 HIS alive and 255 inter-instrument information; TM(3,26) SIDs 4-10, 12 and 13 for DPU counters, validity, hardware diagnostics, FDIR and derived parameters.5 The DPU ICD's Table 9 lists the same SIDs 1 to 16, 20, 100 and 101 with their identifiers (for example DpuHkSsid for SID 11 and IIC_TEST_HK for SID 16) and marks 4-10, 12 and 13 as diagnostic; SIDs 102 and 255 are not in that table.23

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
All 2 885 parameters are raw telemetry; 2 881 are named NIA... with PCF_SUBSYS = 109, and four ZZPAD008 to ZZPAD032 are 8-, 16-, 24- and 32-bit fillers.5 By name, 1 697 are NIA0..., 855 NIAD..., 286 NIAG... and 43 NIA1...; by description, 384 start with HIS, 218 with EAS1, 217 with EAS2, 72 with PAS and 33 with DPU.5 Types: 1 155 are 16-bit unsigned (PTC 3, PFC 12), 667 Booleans, 499 8-bit, 263 32-bit and 100 24-bit unsigned integers; 2 365 have a numerical and 520 a status category.5 The 855 NIAD parameters are exactly the "detail" side of the 855 rows of pcf_glob_det, which relate them to 166 container words.5 1 055 parameters appear in no plf or vpd entry; 206 have ground monitoring checks (158 hard, 168 soft limits in ocp in 6.3.4).5 The pcf table of 6.5.0 is identical to that of 6.3.4, row for row.6

The sw_para file lists 2 841 names - 1 758 monitoring parameters, 471 packet mnemonics (YIA...), 428 command parameters and 184 commands - with an empty second column, where the spacecraft release's ASW_sw_para gives an on-board software symbol; the third column holds the letter a in 2 463 rows and otherwise a field name or a comment (for example SWA_TC_HIS_MODE: change mode). All 2 841 names are also in ASW_sw_para.58 Version 6.5.0 adds one row, ZIA58950.6

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
The 6.3.4 IDB has 198 commands, all named ZIA58... and all with CCF_ACK = 9 (acceptance and completion reports): 45 of type 200, 43 each of types 201 and 202, 33 of 203, 21 of 204, and 13 standard ones - memory management (4), housekeeping (3), event enable/disable (2), science transfer enable/disable (2), time (1, TC(9,129)) and connection test (1).5 Version 6.5.0 has 201: one more of type 200 and one more each of 201 and 202.6 The DPU ICD's HIS internal table lists 27 type-204 commands; the IDB has 21 of those subtypes, and the release notes record six HIS commands removed in IDB 4.2.0 (August 2017).2167

The single TC header NOM_TC has the same layout as the spacecraft one, but the 8-bit source ID is a fixed value 0x78 (120) - the ground source ID that the packet structure ICD reserves for direct commands - where the 2025 spacecraft MIB uses the element type O.5378 Two verification stages are defined: 58901 (acceptance) and 58907 (completion), both report-based (CVS_SOURCE = R) with a start offset of 0 and an interval of 20 seconds; every command uses both, which makes the 396 (6.3.4) and 402 (6.5.0) cvp rows.56 See Command verification in the MIB.

docs.title: Worked example: the cadence command, from ICD to IDB
docs.text:
TC(200,162) "Sensor Cadence Mode" changes how often each sensor generates its science products. ICD issue 8.2 defines one 16-bit application data word: 8 spare bits, then a 2-bit rate for EAS1, EAS2, PAS and HIS. For EAS the values are 0b00 10 s (high cadence), 0b01 100 s (nominal) and 0b10 400 s (low); for PAS and HIS only nominal and low are defined.18 The IDB command ZIA58728 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE_MODE encodes exactly this layout:6

The command added in 6.4.5, ZIA58950 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE, keeps the same type, subtype and rate positions but uses four of the spare bits as per-sensor "ignore" flags, and it gives PAS four rates:6

The element positions (CDF_BIT) and lengths above are the IDB's cdf rows; the value names are its pas rows.6 Neither the ignore flags nor the high and medium PAS cadences appear in ICD issue 8.2, so they come from a later definition that is not in the library.18 The same is true of the EAS summation commands TC(201,174) and TC(202,174): the EAS manager table of issue 8.2 ends at subtype 173.196 Browse the two commands as ZIA58728 and ZIA58950.

docs.title: Four failure codes that came back
docs.text:
TM(1,8) reports a telecommand's execution failure; each failure code is its own packet in the IDB, identified by the 16-bit failure ID at octet 20 (PIC rule for TM(1,8)). The four packets added in 6.5.0 have this layout (28 octets, TPCF_SIZE 28):6

SPID Failure ID Hex Packet name CIAT0066TM text 58730 43149 0xA88D SWA_EAS1_BAD_SUM Eas1BadSum 58731 43150 0xA88E SWA_EAS2_BAD_SUM Eas2BadSum 58732 43151 0xA88F SWA_EAS1_OFF_ENT_ERR Eas1FOffEntMEr 58733 43152 0xA890 SWA_EAS2_OFF_ENT_ERR Eas2FOffEntMEr

These four codes have a history. DPU ICD issue 6.1 (21/02/2018) deleted eighteen "not used" execution failure codes, among them 0xA88D to 0xA890, and IDB 5.1.0 of the same date removed the corresponding TM(1,8) packets; the TECF table of issue 8.2 accordingly jumps from 0xA88C to the next code.26257 IDB 6.5.0 brings the four values back as SPIDs 58730-58733, two of them with new names (BAD_SUM); the notes do not say whether this is related to the EAS summation commands added in 6.4.6.76 See APID 1585 in the 6.5.0 explorer.

SQL used (APIDs, parameters, commands) 
SELECT PID_APID, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) >> 4, CAST(PID_APID AS INT) & 15, count(*),
       group_concat(DISTINCT PID_TYPE || '/' || PID_STYPE)
  FROM pid GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CAST(PID_APID AS INT);
SELECT PID_APID, PID_STYPE, PID_PI1_VAL, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '3';
SELECT substr(PCF_NAME, 1, 4), count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT PCF_PTC, PCF_PFC, count(*) FROM pcf GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
SELECT CCF_TYPE, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT CCF_ACK, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT * FROM tcp; SELECT * FROM pcdf; SELECT * FROM cvs;
-- 6.5.0: cadence commands and the new TM(1,8) packets
SELECT CDF_CNAME, CDF_ELTYPE, CDF_ELLEN, CDF_BIT, CDF_PNAME, CDF_VALUE, c.CPC_DESCR
  FROM cdf LEFT JOIN cpc c ON c.CPC_NAME = CDF_PNAME
 WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('ZIA58728', 'ZIA58950') ORDER BY 1, CAST(CDF_BIT AS INT);
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CIAT0045TC', 'CIAT0068TC', 'CIAT0070TC', 'CIAT0071TC', 'CIAT0075TC');
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, l.PLF_OFFBY, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME WHERE l.PLF_SPID = '58730'
 ORDER BY CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
SELECT CCF_STYPE FROM ccf WHERE CCF_TYPE = '204' ORDER BY CAST(CCF_STYPE AS INT);   -- 21 subtypes

docs.title: The IIC packet in the database
docs.text:
The inter-instrument communication note SOL-SGS-TN-0007 specifies SWA's contribution as a TM(3,25) with process ID 95, category 5 and SID 255, generated every 4 seconds, carrying 16 octets for distribution: a 4-octet heartbeat copied from the OBT coarse time, the PAS proton density (2 octets), the three solar wind velocity components (2 octets each) and 4 spare octets.1 Section 9 of the DPU ICD defines the same packet from the instrument side: generated once every 4 seconds, packet length field 0x1A, the heartbeat being the coarse time field of the on-board time, the density the order-0 PAS moment and Vx, Vy, Vz the order-1 PAS moments, all 16-bit values.24 The IDB's packet SWA_TM_II_INFO (SPID 58907) on APID 1525 implements exactly that:5

The offsets and types are the plf and pcf entries of the IDB; the packet's TPCF_SIZE of 33 octets is 16 octets of headers, 1 octet of SID and the 16 octets of distributed data.5 The ICD's length field agrees: a packet data length of 0x1A = 26 means 27 octets after the 6-octet primary header, 33 in all. The types follow the SCOS-2000 code table, in which PTC 3 PFC 12 is a 16-bit and PFC 14 a 32-bit unsigned integer.34 The SID is not placed in the OBC data pool, and the OBC copies the 16 octets into octets 207 to 222 of the TC(20,128) it distributes to all instruments - to SWA itself at 8 Hz.3839 The same packet exists with the same SPID and layout in the 2025 spacecraft MIB; browse it as SPID 58907 in the SWA explorer or NIA01553 in the spacecraft MIB.8

docs.title: How the IDB relates to the spacecraft MIB
docs.text:
Comparing names and definitions with the two copied spacecraft releases:5689

Object IDB 6.3.4 IDB 6.5.0 Also in 2020 MIB (from 6.3.4) Also in 2025 MIB (from 6.5.0) Notes on 2025 Parameters (PCF_NAME) 2 885 2 885 2 885 2 885 description, PTC, PFC and calibration identical; 243 have a different unit, 237 of them a unit only in the IDB Packets (PID_SPID) 609 613 600 613 APID, type, subtype, identification value and description identical for all 613 Fixed layout (plf) 6 507 6 535 - 6 535 identical name, SPID and offsets Commands (CCF_CNAME) 198 201 198 200 ZIA58057 TC(9,129) absent; 7 commands have a different parameter count Command elements (cdf) 1 173 1 184 - 1 147 identical Polynomial calibrations (mcf) 80 80 - 80 numerically equal 6.3.4: 77 Checks (ocp) 326 325 - 325 with the same limits 6.3.4: 317; 4 checks get an applicability condition in 2025 Textual calibrations (txp) 1 460 1 460 - 1 458 identical pcf_glob_det, sw_para rows 855, 2 841 855, 2 842 - all 855; 2 841 names in ASW_sw_para the new ZIA58950 is not in ASW_sw_para

The spacecraft MIB has the SWA definitions, with the subsystem number 109 and the NIA / ZIA prefixes, but none of the IDB's version history.8 Version 6.5.0 is much closer to the 2025 release than 6.3.4: every SWA packet and every SWA command of the 2025 MIB is in 6.5.0, and the polynomial curves, limits and failure-code texts changed in 6.4.x and 6.5.0 are the values found in the 2025 MIB.568

timeline
  title SWA definitions in the copied databases
  2020-04-16 : Spacecraft MIB 10720PFM - 2 887 NIA parameters, 600 SWA packets, 198 SWA commands
  2021-11-29 : SWA IDB 6.3.4 (files dated 2021-12-03) - 609 packets incl. 9 debug and parameter reports on APID 1593
  2025-06-17 : SWA IDB 6.5.0 - 613 packets, 201 commands
  2025-09-16 : Spacecraft MIB 25925PFM - 2 882 NIA parameters, 613 SWA packets, 200 SWA commands

The differences place 6.3.4 between the two spacecraft releases and 6.5.0 just before the September 2025 one:

  • Changed after April 2020, as in the IDB: the 63 packets that the 2020 MIB had on APID 1593 (category 9) - nine private reports of types 200-203 and 54 TM(6,6)/TM(6,10) dumps and checks - sit in both IDB versions (and in 2025), with the same SPIDs, on the new APIDs 1542 (category 6) and 1545 (category 9), and APID 1593 holds nine new packets with the same names and new SPIDs 58191-58199: SWA_TM_DEBUG_CMD_REPORT, SWA_TM_MON_CONF_REPORT, SWA_TM_PARAM_REPORT, SWA_TM_MACRO_REPORT, SWA_TM_FSW_STARTUP_REPORT, SWA_TM_ERROR_LOG_REPORT and the EAS1, EAS2 and PAS parameter reports (types 200-203). The release notes date the move to 6.3.3 and the copies to 6.3.3_wa (see APIDs and packets).5987
  • Added after 6.3.4, in 6.5.0 and in 2025: the four failure reports TM(1,8) on APID 1585 (SWA_EAS1_BAD_SUM, SWA_EAS2_BAD_SUM, SWA_EAS1_OFF_ENT_ERR, SWA_EAS2_OFF_ENT_ERR) and the three commands ZIA58950 SWA_TC_SENS_CADENCE TC(200,162) (explorer), ZIA58951 and ZIA58952 for the EAS1 and EAS2 summation.689
  • Changed on the spacecraft side only: in 2025, ZIA58950 is verified with the spacecraft stages 11 and 17 instead of the IDB's 58901 and 58907 (both pairs are report-based acceptance and completion stages with a 20-second interval). Four limit checks get an applicability condition - the ICD's OCP_RLCHK/OCP_VALPAR pair, which enables a check only when another parameter has a given value: NIA05120 EAS1_3_3_VD_V_MON when NIAD4410 EAS1_STATE is 2 (RUNNING), NIA05124 EAS2_3_3_VD_V_MON when NIAD4420 EAS2_MODE is 2 (BWOSCIENCE), NIA05130 HK_I_P28V_PRI when NIAD4422 PAS_STATE is 2 (RUNNING), and NIA05128 V-MON-C when the synthetic NXAD4423 PAS_MODE_CHECK is 0. NIA05128 also needs 3 consecutive violating samples instead of 1 (OCF_NBCHCK), and the ocf record of NIA05131, which has no checks in 6.5.0, is dropped.6832
  • Only in the spacecraft MIBs: the dynamic synthetic parameter NIASX001 "PAS_IN_SCIENCE", present in both 2020 and 2025 (the IDB has no synthetics), and five NIAD416x SpaceWire-link parameters of the 2020 release that neither IDB version nor the 2025 release has.985
  • In both IDBs but removed by 2025: ZIA58057 SWA_TC_ACC_TIME, the TC(9,129) "accept time" command, which the 2025 MIB dropped together with the other instruments' TC(9,129) commands (see How Solar Orbiter uses PUS). The DPU ICD still lists TC(9,129) "Accept Time update" as a PUS manager command, and IDB 6.5.0 still defines it, so the removal is a spacecraft-database decision.152268

Inference

The pattern - every 6.5.0 parameter, packet and layout present in the 2025 spacecraft MIB three months later with the same names, numbers and values, all commands but one, and mission-level additions (DARC flags, applicability conditions, spacecraft verification stages, the dropped TC(9,129)) only on the spacecraft side - indicates that the spacecraft MIB imports the SWA definitions from the instrument team's database and that ESA or the spacecraft team adds mission-level fields and decisions. The merging process itself is not described in the available sources: the 2007 Experiment Interface Document Part A leaves its section "Inputs to Satellite Database" to be written (TBW).28 The STIX database shows the same pattern (see STIX).

SQL used (comparison with the spacecraft MIB) 
-- run on swa-idb.sqlite (6.3.4); repeat on swa-idb-v6.5.0.sqlite
ATTACH 'file:solo-2025-09-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS m;
ATTACH 'file:solo-2020-04-16.sqlite?mode=ro' AS o;
SELECT count(*), sum(PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM m.pcf)),
       sum(PCF_NAME IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM o.pcf)) FROM main.pcf;          -- 2885 | 2885 | 2885
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pcf a JOIN m.pcf b ON a.PCF_NAME = b.PCF_NAME
 WHERE a.PCF_DESCR = b.PCF_DESCR AND a.PCF_PTC = b.PCF_PTC AND a.PCF_PFC = b.PCF_PFC;   -- 2885
SELECT sum(a.PCF_UNIT <> b.PCF_UNIT) FROM main.pcf a JOIN m.pcf b ON a.PCF_NAME = b.PCF_NAME;  -- 243
SELECT count(*), sum(PID_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM m.pid)),
       sum(PID_SPID IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM o.pid)) FROM main.pid;          -- 609 | 609 | 600 (6.3.4)
SELECT count(*) FROM main.pid a JOIN m.pid b USING (PID_SPID)
 WHERE a.PID_APID = b.PID_APID AND a.PID_TYPE = b.PID_TYPE AND a.PID_STYPE = b.PID_STYPE
   AND a.PID_DESCR = b.PID_DESCR AND a.PID_PI1_VAL IS b.PID_PI1_VAL;         -- 613 (6.5.0)
SELECT count(*) FROM main.plf a JOIN m.plf b ON a.PLF_NAME = b.PLF_NAME AND a.PLF_SPID = b.PLF_SPID
   AND a.PLF_OFFBY = b.PLF_OFFBY AND a.PLF_OFFBI = b.PLF_OFFBI;              -- 6507 / 6535
SELECT count(*), sum(CCF_CNAME IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM m.ccf)),
       sum(CCF_CNAME IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM o.ccf)) FROM main.ccf;        -- 198 | 197 | 198 (6.3.4)
SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM m.ccf WHERE CCF_APID = '1532'
   AND CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CCF_CNAME FROM main.ccf);                    -- none for 6.5.0
SELECT count(*) FROM main.mcf a JOIN m.mcf b USING (MCF_IDENT)
 WHERE CAST(a.MCF_POL1 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL1 AS REAL) AND CAST(a.MCF_POL2 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL2 AS REAL)
   AND CAST(a.MCF_POL3 AS REAL) = CAST(b.MCF_POL3 AS REAL);                 -- 77 / 80
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT OCP_NAME, OCP_POS, OCP_TYPE, OCP_LVALU, OCP_HVALU FROM main.ocp
            INTERSECT SELECT OCP_NAME, OCP_POS, OCP_TYPE, OCP_LVALU, OCP_HVALU FROM m.ocp);  -- 317 / 325
SELECT * FROM main.ocp EXCEPT SELECT * FROM m.ocp;                          -- 4 rows without VALPAR
SELECT * FROM main.ocf EXCEPT SELECT * FROM m.ocf;                          -- NIA05128, NIA05131
SELECT * FROM m.cvp WHERE CVP_TASK = 'ZIA58950';                            -- stages 11, 17
SELECT COL1 FROM main.sw_para WHERE COL1 NOT IN (SELECT COL1 FROM m.asw_sw_para);   -- ZIA58950 (6.5.0)
SELECT PID_SPID, PID_APID, PID_DESCR FROM main.pid WHERE PID_SPID NOT IN (SELECT PID_SPID FROM o.pid);
SELECT a.PID_APID, b.PID_APID, count(*) FROM main.pid a JOIN o.pid b ON b.PID_SPID = a.PID_SPID
 WHERE a.PID_APID <> b.PID_APID GROUP BY 1, 2;                         -- 1542|1593|9, 1545|1593|54
SELECT PCF_NAME, PCF_DESCR FROM o.pcf WHERE PCF_NAME LIKE 'NIA%'
   AND PCF_NAME NOT IN (SELECT PCF_NAME FROM main.pcf);                -- NIAD4161-4165, NIASX001
SELECT l.PLF_NAME, c.PCF_DESCR, l.PLF_OFFBY, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC
  FROM plf l JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = l.PLF_NAME WHERE l.PLF_SPID = '58907'
 ORDER BY CAST(PLF_OFFBY AS INT);
