docs.title: 1. Command definition in the MIB
docs.text:
In the SCOS-2000 database the central entity is the command definition in the ccf table. A command has PTV expressions (ptv, one-to-many and ANDed together) and verification stages (cvs, shared by many commands through the mapping table cvp). It also has parameter sets (pst via psm) and parameters (cpc, placed in the application data field by cdf). Each command parameter may reference one numerical (de-)calibration (cca/ccs), one textual calibration or alias set (paf/pas) and one range set (prf/prv). Each command also references one packet header (tcp), whose fields are described by pcpc and placed by pcdf.1

erDiagram
  TCP ||--o{ PCDF : "header elements"
  PCPC |o--o{ PCDF : "header parameter (none for fixed areas)"
  TCP ||--o{ CCF : "packet header of"
  CCF ||--o{ CDF : "elements"
  CPC |o--o{ CDF : "parameter instance (none for fixed areas)"
  CCF ||--o{ PTV : "static PTV"
  CCF ||--o{ CVP : "verification profile"
  CVS ||--o{ CVP : "stage"
  CVS ||--o{ CVE : "parameter criteria"
  CCF ||--o{ PSM : "parameter sets"
  CPC }o--o| CCA : "numerical calibration"
  CPC }o--o| PAF : "textual calibration"
  CPC }o--o| PRF : "range set"
  CCA ||--o{ CCS : "points"
  PAF ||--o{ PAS : "aliases"
  PRF ||--o{ PRV : "ranges or values"

Relationships as described in ICD issue 7.0 §3.3.3; fixed areas carry no parameter name in PCDF or CDF. Diagram by this wiki.1210

docs.title: The packet header template
docs.text:
The PCDF rows say, bit by bit, where each header element sits and where its value comes from. The type is F for a fixed value, A, T, S or K for the APID, service type, subtype or acknowledgement flags taken from the CCF, and P for values that the command subsystem sets itself, such as the packet length and the source sequence counter.2 Operators cannot edit header parameters on the manual stack. The multiplexer maintains the source sequence counter per APID.2 The Solar Orbiter MIB defines four headers: NOM_TC for normal PUS commands (5,318 commands), HPC1_TC for CPDU high-priority commands (125), NO_HDR for frame-level control commands (5) and NOS2KHDR for NIS throw events (6).96 HPC1_TC is only the 6-octet primary header with the data field header flag fixed to 0, and its 125 commands have no service type or subtype. This matches the PUS rule that CPDU command packets have no secondary header.9636 The NOM_TC template reads:96

Inference

The Solar Orbiter MIB gives the Source ID element the PCDF type O, which is not among the types listed in ICD issue 7.0 (F, A, T, S, K, P).296 What SCOS-2000 does with type O is not stated in the available sources. A mission-specific or later-release extension seems likely.

docs.title: Commands and their parameters
docs.text:
The CCF row gives the name, description, header (CCF_PKTID), type, subtype and APID, and the number of elements. It also gives whether the command can be loaded stand-alone (CCF_EXEC) and which sources may plan it (CCF_PLAN).5 The default interlock scope and stage (CCF_ILSCOPE, CCF_ILSTAGE) and the subsystem follow.6 Then come the high-priority flag and fixed MAP ID for CPDU-type commands (CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID), a redundant APID, the default acknowledgement flags (CCF_ACK, 0 to 15) and the default on-board sub-schedule.78 CCF_CTYPE marks the special cases. R is a control segment (reset MAP) and F a control frame (BC frame: Unlock or Set V(R)); for both, PCDF/CDF describe the frame data field instead of a packet. S is a packet without CRC, and T and N are SLE and NIS throw events that are never uplinked.4

Each command element in CDF is a fixed area (A), a fixed parameter (F) or an editable parameter (E), at a bit offset from the start of the application data field. SCOS-2000 uses that offset only to sort the elements, which it then encodes one after the other without gaps.10 The value of an editable parameter can come from the parameter default (D), from a raw (R) or engineering (E) value given in CDF, or from a live telemetry parameter (T, a dynamic default).11 Unlike monitoring calibrations, command calibrations work in both directions: engineering to raw for encoding, raw to engineering for display. They must be one-to-one, and in ccs the engineering value is in CCS_XVALS and the raw value in CCS_YVALS.22 A range set accepts a value that lies within, or equals, the limits of any of its PRV rows, and a PRV row with no maximum is a single allowed value.23

Real example: ZCSD3905 SADE PY Motor Move

Element CDF Definition (from the MIB) Header NOM_TC, TC(131,1), APID 236, CCF_ACK = 9 service 131 lies in the mission-specific range 128 to 25540 Fixed area bits 0–15, value 3905 described as "Identification number of" (the 24-character description is cut short in the MIB) PCSB002A SADE Unit ID bits 16–23, editable PTC 2 / PFC 8; aliases (CCDT0024TC): SADE_A = 0, SADE_B = 1, SADE_INUSE = 2, SADE_NOT_INUSE = 3 PCSB00CD SADE Delta Position bits 24–55, editable PTC 3 / PFC 14 (32-bit unsigned59), unit deg; calibration CSDP0005TC, 3 points: 0 deg ↔ 0, 0.0727 deg ↔ 512, 305040.290909091 deg ↔ 2147483648 PCSB00CC SADE Motion Direction bits 56–63, editable aliases (CCDT0287TX): CLOCKWISE = 0, ANTI_CLOCKWISE = 1 Verification CVP stage 14001 (acceptance, report-based) and 14007 (completion, report-based), each with CVS_START 0 s and CVS_INTERVAL 20 s

Explorer: ZCSD3905.97

Across the release there are 5,454 commands and 7,155 command parameters. 327 parameters reference a numerical calibration, 1,624 an alias set and 694 a range set, using 99 CCA curves, 624 alias sets and 565 range sets.97 The parameter-set tables (PST, PSV, CPS, PVS, PSM) are empty in this release.97 One curiosity: the range set VCD00353 used by the housekeeping SID parameter PCD03011 is described as "Integer between 1 and 19" but allows 1 to 192.97

Inference

PRF_DESCR is limited to 24 characters,23 and "Integer between 1 and 192" has 25. The description of VCD00353 was therefore most likely truncated on import, and the PRV values (1 to 192) are authoritative.

docs.title: 2. Command sequences
docs.text:
A command sequence (csf) is an ordered list of elements (css), each a command, a nested sequence or a comment. Elements carry their own parameter values (sdf), and the sequence may declare formal parameters (csp) that act as placeholders filled in at load time. Nested sequences are expanded like macros when loaded, and a sequence must never contain itself. Since R5.0 the sequences are kept as XML in the FARC, and the ASCII tables remain for backward compatibility.13 Each element can say how its release time is computed: relative to the previous command (R), or relative to the sequence start (A), as a delta hh.mm.ss. It can also say whether it needs a separate manual dispatch ("ARM&GO", CSS_MANDISP), whether it is grouped (released as an uninterrupted batch) or blocked (aggregated into one segment), and how its interlock, PTV and CEV are set.15 The sequence-level flag CSF_IFTT says whether the sequence contains execution time-tagged commands. B lets the user choose at load time between on-board time-tagged and ground time-tagged release.14

Real example: AACC309A STR A time update v06

Entry Element Release Parameters 1 ZST15401 STR1 Select ASP Channel, TC(154,1), APID 652 A, 00.00.00, manual dispatch PST05054 ← formal parameter XC309A01 "ASP CHANNEL" (textual; SDF_VTYPE = F)16 2 ZCD00982 Start Time Synchronisation to User, TC(9,130), APID 172 R, 00.00.01, manual dispatch, so counted from its own dispatch time PCD09821 = STAR_TRACKER_A (engineering), PCD09822 = 0 (raw)

CSF_IFTT = B, one formal parameter, two elements. Explorer: AACC309A.98

Solar Orbiter's release has 3,404 sequences with 13,879 elements, 50,014 element parameter values and 10,981 formal parameters. 3,354 sequences have CSF_IFTT = B, and the rest N.98 See Command sequences and parameter sets.

MIB sequences are one way of grouping commands. ECSS standardises two others: a language for checkout and operations procedures (PLUTO, ECSS-E-ST-70-32), and on-board control procedures that run on the spacecraft itself (OBCPs, ECSS-E-ST-70-01), which the PUS controls through ST[18].111 See PLUTO, OBCPs and, for how missions prepare their databases and procedures, operations preparation.

docs.title: 3. The command stack and the release chain
docs.text:
SCOS-2000's commanding functions include the manual stack, where commands are loaded with their parameters (with de-calibration) and execution time-tags. The stack also supports release dependencies, grouping, blocking, delta release times, interlocking, a master manual mode and a wait mode, static and dynamic PTV, and sequences with formal parameters. Next to it sit an autostack with restricted functions and no editing, and a multiplexer that lets several sources command in parallel. The command releaser interfaces to the external destination, the NCTRS. An on-board queue model tracks time-tagged commands, and a command verifier performs multi-stage verification and disables status consistency checks on the affected parameters.26 The command history records, for each command, the sequence that loaded it and the type of command source, its release and execution times, the transmission mode (AD or BD), the PTV and CAV/CEV check states, the interlock, the AD frame count, and the status of each verification stage. These are the columns of the TC history printout of the Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express control systems, whose data delivery interface document is public.29

Interlocks stop further commanding until a command reaches a given stage. The scope can be global (G), local to the command source (L), local to the subsystem (S), global for the subsystem (B), local or subsystem only on verification failure (F, T), or none (N). The stage waited on can be ground station reception (R), uplink (U), on-board reception (O, treated as U in BD mode), application acceptance (A) or completion (C).6 Every Solar Orbiter command in the release defaults to no interlock (CCF_ILSCOPE = N). 5,443 commands name the completion stage C as their default interlock stage. The 5 frame-level NO_HDR commands carry the undocumented value N, and the 6 NIS throw events leave the field empty.99101

docs.title: Routing
docs.text: The releaser sends spacecraft commands to the NCTRS unless the optional dst table routes their APID elsewhere. The other choice is EGSE, as EGSE.SCOE for non-spacecraft commands or EGSE.TC.<address> for a TC front end.9 Solar Orbiter's release has a single DST row, which sends APID 1372 to EGSE.TC.0x8800, the very example given in the ICD.999 The NCTRS links the MCS to the ground station network and uses SLE for non-ESA stations.27 Outside ESA, DLR's GECCOS (derived from SCOS-2000) speaks the same bespoke NCTRS protocol, which is translated to standard SLE.28 See NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface.

docs.title: 4. Pre-transmission validation
docs.text:
Before release, SCOS-2000 runs static PTV. Each ptv row requires a monitoring parameter (numerical, processed by the TM model) to equal a raw or engineering value. All rows of a command are ANDed together, and an invalid parameter fails the check.12 Dynamic PTV covers feasibility checks, time checks and interlocks, and both kinds can be overridden per sequence element (CSS_DYNPTV, CSS_STAPTV).17 In the Solar Orbiter archive the SCOS-2000 TC packet header records an uplink flag, which is 1 if the command passed PTV and is to be released and 0 if it failed.32

Solar Orbiter uses static PTV sparingly. The release has five PTV rows. ZCD00D09 "Accept First Uplink Part" (TC(13,9)) requires the synthetic parameter NCDXS005 "Nb Immediate TCF" to be 0. Four SSMM file-transfer commands, among them ZSM00120 "SSMM Abort LLFT" (TC(13,145)), require NMAXS005 "SSMM FTS COMMANDING PTV" to be 0. Both parameters are dynamic OL synthetic parameters.100

docs.title: 5. The PUS TC secondary header
docs.text:
A telecommand packet carries a request from a ground application process to an on-board one.34 Apart from CPDU command packets, every PUS telecommand has a secondary header.36

PUS-C (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C, 2016)PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A, 2003), used by Solar Orbiter

Field Bits Values Meaning TC packet PUS version number 4 2 Version 0 = ESA PUS, 1 = ECSS-E-70-41A.36 Acknowledgement flags 4 bit 3 acceptance, bit 2 start, bit 1 progress, bit 0 completion Which successful stages to report. PUS numbers bits from the most significant (bit 0), so acceptance is the least significant bit of the field.3733 Message type ID 8 + 8 service type, message subtype Identifies the request.37 Source ID 16 Identifies the issuing application process; with the sequence count it identifies the packet uniquely.3735 Spare optional Pads the header to whole words.37

After the application data and optional spare comes the 16-bit packet error control field. For telecommands it is mandatory, and the mission chooses the ISO checksum or the CRC.38

PUS-A has a 1-bit CCSDS secondary header flag (0 = non-CCSDS header), a 3-bit PUS version (1), a 4-bit Ack field, 8-bit type and subtype, an optional source ID of mission-defined length, and optional spare bits. Failure reports are generated by default, so the Ack bits request only the success acknowledgements. Service types 0 to 127 are reserved for the standard and 128 to 255 are mission-specific. The PEC is a checksum or CRC fixed for the mission.40

Solar Orbiter sets the version to 1 and uses only the acceptance bit and the completion bit; the start and progress bits must be zero.49 Its CRC uses the generator polynomial \(X^{16}+X^{12}+X^5+1\) with an all-ones preset, computed over the whole packet except the CRC itself.50 Ground source IDs include 110 for the mission timeline, 111 for TC sequences, 112 for event-action recovery commands, 113 for the back-up timeline and 120 for direct commands.51 In the MIB, 5,225 commands have CCF_ACK = 9 (0b1001, acceptance and completion), 78 have 1 (acceptance only), 21 have 0, and 130 have none.99

The ICD notes that SCOS-2000 matches each TM(1,x) report to its command by the 4 octets that echo the TC packet ID and sequence control, which must sit at the same position in every type-1 packet. Clearing an Ack bit at load time disables the corresponding report-based stage, but it cannot add a stage that the CVP table does not define.2421

docs.title: 6. The Space Packet primary header for telecommands
docs.text:
The primary header has the same layout as on the downlink. Here the packet type is 1, the APID names the destination application process, and the 14-bit field holds a sequence count or a packet name. With the source ID this identifies the packet.4735 Solar Orbiter splits the APID into a 7-bit process ID and a 4-bit category, which is fixed to 12 for telecommands. It sets the sequence flags to 0b11, and it keeps the sequence count per APID and source ID for ground traceability only: the application accepts commands whatever the counter.48 The packet data field is at most 242 octets: 4 octets of data field header, 236 octets of application data and the 2-octet CRC.48

Two limits that agree

SCOS-2000 limits a command to CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE octets, 248 by default. The space for parameters is then reduced by the header, the CRC and any time-tag wrapper (the TC(11,4) insert command).3 For Solar Orbiter, 6 octets of primary header plus the 242-octet maximum data field also give 248 octets. The match is this wiki's observation; the Solar Orbiter configuration value of the MISC variable is not stated in the available sources.

docs.title: 7. The TC transfer frame and segment
docs.text:
The TC Space Data Link Protocol carries packets in variable-length frames of up to 1,024 octets. A frame has a 5-octet primary header, a data field of up to 1,019 octets (1,017 with an FECF) and an optional 2-octet frame error control field.60

Field Bits Values Meaning Transfer frame version number 2 0b00 TC version 1.61 Bypass flag 1 0 Type-A, 1 Type-B Whether the FARM applies its frame acceptance checks.62 Control command flag 1 0 Type-D, 1 Type-C Whether the data field holds a frame data unit or a control command.62 Reserved spare 2 0b00 Reserved.63 Spacecraft ID 10 CCSDS-assigned Static for all mission phases.63 Virtual channel ID 6 No numbering constraint.64 Frame length 10 C = octets - 1 Hence the 1,024-octet maximum.64 Frame sequence number 8 N(S) Lets the FARM check that Type-A frames are in sequence; kept per VC; all zeros in Type-B frames.64 Bypass Control Frame type Use 0 0 AD Data under the sequence-controlled (AD) service of the COP 0 1 Reserved 1 0 BD Data under the expedited (BD) service, acceptance checks bypassed 1 1 BC COP control commands (Unlock, Set V(R))

Source: CCSDS 232.0-B-4 table 4-1.62

The segment header is one octet: 2 sequence flags and a 6-bit multiplexer access point (MAP) ID. It is needed on a VC that has more than one MAP or that carries service data units too large for one frame. If it is used on a VC it must be used in every data frame of that VC, but it is never present in control-command frames. Sequence flags 0b11 mean an unsegmented service data unit or several whole packets.65

The two control commands are Unlock, a single all-zeros octet, and Set V(R), three octets 0x82 0x00 followed by the new V(R).66 The receiving end applies frame validation checks to every frame, Type-A or Type-B. It checks the expected version number and MCID, header values consistent with the spacecraft's implemented features, a frame length that matches the octets received, and, if present, the FECF CRC. A frame that fails any check is discarded.68 The FECF uses the same CRC-16 as TM frames.67

docs.title: What Solar Orbiter does
docs.text:
Item Solar Orbiter value SCID 0x28A = 650 (same for the flight model, ETB and OBC-DM)54 VCIDs 1 and 2, one per on-board TC decoder, used consistently in the CLCWs54 Maximum frame length 256 octets, so bits 22–23 of the header are always 0b0054 Frame sequence number V(S) in AD frames, zero in BC and BD frames55 Segment always present, no segmentation (flags 0b11)52 MAP IDs 0 = CPDU (TC(2,3) high-priority commands), 1 = normal commanding; not used to select the active processor52 Aggregation several complete packets per segment, to raise uplink throughput53

SCOS-2000 supports this blocking at segment level: several packets aggregated into one segment and sent as one frame and one CLTU.25 In the MIB, the 125 HPC1_TC commands are high-priority with MAP ID 0, matching the CPDU MAP ID of the Solar Orbiter packet ICD.9952 CCF_MAPID is also filled for 205 non-high-priority NOM_TC commands: 1 for 128 commands to APIDs 796, 812 and 1020, and 54 for 77 commands to APID 876. The SCOS-2000 ICD says the field is irrelevant unless CCF_HIPRI = Y.997 The MIB also defines the BC-frame commands UNLOCK (one fixed octet 0) and SETVR (a fixed 16-bit 8200 followed by the 8-bit VR parameter), both with CCF_CTYPE = F. It defines three control segments with CCF_CTYPE = R: RESET, REIN_TTR and TC_ONLY.101 The ICD strongly recommends a global interlock on at least the uplink stage for BC frames.4 Solar Orbiter's BC-frame commands carry no default interlock, CCF_ILSCOPE = N.101

A 256-octet frame holds exactly one maximum-size Solar Orbiter packet: 5 octets of frame header, 1 octet of segment header, 248 octets of packet and 2 octets of FECF add up to 256. The text of §3.4 only says the frame length runs to the FECF "if present", but the ICD's telecommand overview drawing (figure 3.1-1, a picture that is not in the extracted text, read in the PDF) ends every TC frame with a 2-octet frame error control field (CRC).5448104 The ECSS adoption notice of CCSDS 232.0-B-4 also makes the FECF mandatory.105 The telecommand worked example discusses the frame drawing in detail.

docs.title: 8. COP-1: FOP-1 on the ground, FARM-1 on board
docs.text:
COP-1 is a closed-loop, go-back-n ARQ procedure. The FOP-1 at the sending end sends the frames of one VC. The FARM-1 at the receiving end accepts Type-A frames only in strict sequence and reports its state in the CLCW.70 The AD service guarantees, with high probability, that no frame data unit is lost, duplicated or delivered out of order on that VC. It uses Type-AD frames for data and Type-BC frames for the Unlock and Set V(R) control commands. The BD service sends Type-BD frames that bypass acceptance and are only counted.71

FOP-1 states after CCSDS 232.1-B-2 §5.1.2. The complete behaviour is in the FOP-1 state table (events E1 to E46). The transitions shown here are simplified by this wiki.7475

FOP-1 keeps, per VC, V(S), a one-entry wait queue, a sent queue, the expected acknowledgement NN(R), the timer value T1_Initial, the transmission limit and count, the sliding window width K, the timeout type and the suspend state.73 It is controlled by four "Initiate AD Service" directives, one "Terminate AD Service", one "Resume AD Service" and five "FOP-1 Setup" directives, among them "Set V(S) to V*(S)".72

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  O: S1 Open
  W: S2 Wait
  L: S3 Lockout
  O --> W: no buffer for an accepted Type-A FDU
  W --> O: buffer released
  O --> L: N(S) outside the sliding window
  W --> L: N(S) outside the sliding window
  L --> O: Unlock control command

FARM-1 states after CCSDS 232.1-B-2 §6.1.2; simplified by this wiki.76

FARM-1's sliding window has a total width W that is fixed for the mission. When retransmission of Type-AD frames is allowed, W is even, between 2 and 254, and is split into a positive part PW and a negative part NW of W/2 each. Corrigendum 1 adds a mode without retransmission in which W can be any integer from 1 to 256. In the first mode, a frame with N(S) = V(R) is accepted, and V(R) is incremented. A frame in the positive window is discarded and the Retransmit flag is set. A frame in the negative window is simply discarded. A frame outside both windows sends the FARM into Lockout.77

The CLCW (32 bits, in the OCF of TM frames) carries the control word type 0, version 0b00, a mission-specific status field, COP in effect 0b01, the TC VCID it reports on, two spare bits, the No RF Available, No Bit Lock, Lockout, Wait and Retransmit flags, the two low bits of the FARM-B counter, a spare bit, and the 8-bit report value N(R).69 Its bit layout is drawn on Downlink, section 5. Solar Orbiter inserts a CLCW in every TM frame and uses its TC VCIDs consistently with the TC frames.56 Its OBC also reports the CLCW fields as housekeeping parameters, with descriptions such as PDEC_CLCW.A.LkOt, .Wait, .ReTx and .RepValue.102

docs.title: 9. The CLTU: BCH coding, start and tail sequences
docs.text:
The communications link transmission unit (CLTU) delimits and synchronises the coded frames. With BCH coding it is a 16-bit start sequence, a series of 64-bit BCH codewords and a 64-bit tail sequence.79

Part Value Purpose Start sequence 0xEB90 (1110101110010000) Marks the start of the encoded data; also resolves bit-sense ambiguity.8078 BCH codewords 56 information bits + 7 complemented parity bits + 1 filler bit (0) (63,56) modified BCH code, \(g(x) = x^7 + x^6 + x^2 + 1\); the complemented parity helps bit synchronisation and detects bit slips.82 Fill alternating 0/1, starting with 0 Completes the last codeword.83 Tail sequence 0xC5C5C5C5C5C5C579 A deliberately non-correctable pattern that stops decoding.81

With BCH coding, randomization of the frames before encoding is required unless the designer verifies that the system works without it. The randomizer sequence comes from \(h(x) = x^8 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1\) and repeats every 255 bits. With the LDPC option (64-bit start sequence 0x034776C7272895B0, (128,64) or (512,256) codewords) randomization is always applied.8580 The decoder on board moves between three states: inactive (no bit lock), search (bit-by-bit search for the start sequence) and decode. It returns to search when a codeword cannot be corrected, which is what the tail sequence provokes on purpose.84

  S2 --> S3: E3 start sequence found
  S3 --> S2: E4 codeword rejection (e.g. tail sequence)

Full detail: TC synchronization and channel coding: the CLTU.

docs.title: 10. The physical layer operations procedure
docs.text: A PLOP defines the sequence of carrier modulation modes in a pass. CMM-1 is the unmodulated carrier, CMM-2 the carrier modulated with the acquisition sequence (alternating bits, preferably at least 16 octets), CMM-3 the carrier with a CLTU, and CMM-4 the carrier with the idle sequence.8788 PLOP-1 turns the modulation off after every CLTU, forcing the receiver back to inactive. PLOP-2 keeps the channel active and separates CLTUs by the tail sequence (and optional idle), leaving the receiver in search. At least one octet of idle sequence between CLTUs is recommended, to avoid a rare false start inside a tail. Missions whose planning began after September 2010 must use PLOP-2.8689

docs.title: 11. SLE FCLTU: from the control centre to the antenna
docs.text:
The Forward CLTU service lets the user send CLTUs to the spacecraft through a forward space link channel. The provider radiates them in the order received, bit for bit, without interpreting them. It can only check constraints such as the maximum length, and it works only in online delivery mode, with one service instance per physical channel.90 Its operations are:92

Operation Invoker Purpose CLTU-BIND / CLTU-UNBIND user Establish or release the association CLTU-START / CLTU-STOP user Prepare for, or stop, transfer and radiation CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA user Hand over one CLTU, confirmed CLTU-ASYNC-NOTIFY provider Report events such as radiated, expired or production interrupted CLTU-SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT / CLTU-STATUS-REPORT user / provider Periodic or immediate status CLTU-GET-PARAMETER user Read a service parameter CLTU-THROW-EVENT user Ask complex management to act, for example on production settings CLTU-PEER-ABORT either Abort the association

Each CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA invocation carries a monotonically increasing CLTU identification, an earliest and a latest radiation time (either may be null), a delay time (the minimum gap in microseconds before the next CLTU, interpreted according to the PLOP in effect), and whether a radiation report is wanted.9394 If radiation has not started by the latest radiation time, the provider notifies "sldu expired", discards the buffered CLTUs and blocks further transfers until the user stops and restarts the service. A "production interrupted" event has a similar blocking effect.95 The provider also reads the CLCWs from the return link to decide whether the physical channel is available, unless management configures it to ignore them.91 The same function generates the acquisition and idle sequences of the PLOP.91

Inference

Because the FCLTU provider radiates CLTUs unchanged, everything above the physical layer (packet, segment, frame, FOP-1, BCH encoding) must happen on the control-centre side before CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA. Which ESOC component (SCOS-2000 or the NCTRS) runs FOP-1 and builds the CLTU is not stated in the available sources. The SCOS-2000 ICD does say that commands can be blocked into one segment and sent "as a single frame/CLTU".9025

SLE also defines forward services at higher levels. With the Forward Space Packet service the user hands over only packets, and the provider builds the frames, runs COP-1 (using the CLCWs of the ROCF service) and generates the CLTUs, so that several users can command one spacecraft without coordinating with each other.106 The library's copy of that book is stamped historical; see FSP for a side-by-side comparison with FCLTU.107 Which service instances run in a pass, and with which production parameters, is agreed through SLE service management.

The radiated CLTU modulates the uplink carrier, the subject of the CCSDS radio frequency and modulation book 401.0 and of ECSS-E-ST-50-05C.109110 The Solar Orbiter MIB lists the telecommand bit rates that its deep-space transponder can be set to: 7.8125, 15.625, 250, 1000, 2000 and 4000 bit/s.108 See radio frequency, modulation and ranging.

docs.title: 12. Closing the loop: ST[01] reports and MIB verification
On board: ST[01] request verification
docs.text:
PUS-C's request verification service has three subservices. Routing and reporting checks that a request can be routed and is not corrupted, and reports failures as TM[1,10]. Acceptance and reporting checks the request before it is handed to the service, for example its integrity and the availability of the service, and reports TM[1,1] or TM[1,2]. Execution reporting issues the start, progress and completion reports on behalf of the executing service.4243 Failures are always reported. Successes are reported only when the corresponding acknowledgement flag was set.4445

Report Meaning Solar Orbiter TM[1,1] / TM[1,2] successful / failed acceptance both mandatory57 TM[1,3] / TM[1,4] successful / failed start of execution not used (Ack bit 2 = 0)49 TM[1,5] / TM[1,6] successful / failed progress of execution not used (Ack bit 1 = 0)49 TM[1,7] / TM[1,8] successful / failed completion of execution both mandatory57 TM[1,10] failed routing defined only in PUS-C; PUS-A lists subtypes 1 to 84341

Each report starts with the request ID: the packet ID and the packet sequence control of the telecommand. That is not unique by itself; the source is given by the destination ID of the report.46 Failure reports add a failure code and optional data.46 In the Solar Orbiter MIB, the PIC extracts the 16-bit failure code of TM(1,2) and TM(1,8) at octet 20, just after the request ID. Combined with the APID, this gives a separate SPID per failure code: 274 SPIDs for TM(1,2) and 1,477 for TM(1,8).103 The SCOS-2000 verifier itself ignores the failure code and uses only the subtype.24

docs.title: On the ground: the verification stages
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 tracks each released command through a chain of stages. The ground-side uplink verification stages are release to the NCTRS, ground station reception, uplink (radiation) and on-board reception, the last only in AD mode. Execution verification follows as acceptance (CAV) and completion (CEV).29 A stage is pending, passed, failed, timed out, unverified, unknown or idle, among other states.30 In the EGSE version the ground acknowledgements are explicit: the front end returns a GS_Ack on reception, a UL_Ack when a BD-mode command has been sent, and an ONB_Ack when the spacecraft confirms an AD-mode command.31

sequenceDiagram
  participant MS as Manual stack
  participant RL as Releaser
  participant NC as NCTRS
  participant GS as Ground station (FCLTU)
  participant SC as Spacecraft
  participant VR as SCOS-2000 verifier
  MS->>RL: load, edit, PTV OK, release
  RL->>NC: TC (stage R: release)
  NC->>GS: CLTU
  GS-->>VR: station response, received (stage G)
  GS->>SC: radiate
  GS-->>VR: station response, uplinked (stage T)
  SC-->>GS: CLCW in the TM frames (AD mode)
  GS-->>VR: on-board reception (stage O, AD only)
  SC-->>VR: TM[1,1] acceptance (stage A)
  SC-->>VR: TM[1,7] completion, or parameter check (stage C)
  VR->>MS: stage status, release interlocked commands

Stage letters from the Rosetta / Mars Express / Venus Express command history description. The station responses follow the EMCS acknowledgement policy and the Solar Orbiter DDID, which updates the uplink time from the station's radiation response. The message flow is simplified by this wiki: responses that pass through the NCTRS are drawn as going straight to the verifier.293132

The MIB defines the execution stages. Each cvs row has an ID and a stage type: A acceptance, S start, 0 to 9 progress steps, C completion. Its source is either R for a TM report or V for a check of monitoring parameter values. The row also gives the delay after release (or after execution for time-tagged commands) at which the window opens (CVS_START) and the length of the sampling interval from which the overall verification window is computed (CVS_INTERVAL). It can also give a SPID that closes a parameter-based stage (a future extension) and a specific verification window (CVS_UNCERTAINTY).19 Report-based progress stages can only be step 0.19 Parameter-based stages are made of cve rows. Each requires a valid parameter to equal a value within a tolerance, all rows of a stage are ANDed together, and each row can also suspend status-consistency checking of the parameter during the window.20 cvp attaches at most one stage of each type to a command.21

Two real verification profiles

Command Ack Stages (from CVP and CVS) ZCD00305 Enable HK Para Rpt Gen, TC(3,5), APID 172 9 14001 A, report, CVS_START 0 s, CVS_INTERVAL 20 s; 14007 C, report, 0 s, 20 s ZPW04604 PCDU A BDR1_C1 SwitchON, TC(2,128), APID 172 1 11 A, report, 0 s, 20 s; 32 C, parameter: NPWD0753 "IFA_BDR1_Conv1_ST" = raw 1 (ON), tolerance 0, CVS_INTERVAL 60 s, CVE_CHECK = B (used both for verification and to drive status-consistency checking)

The second command requests only the acceptance report (Ack = 1). Its completion is proved by telemetry instead: the converter status must read ON within the stage's verification window, which is computed from the 60 s interval.10320

The release defines 206 stages: 16 report-based acceptance stages, 23 report-based completion stages and 167 parameter-based completion stages, with 171 CVE criteria and 10,697 CVP links. 62 commands have no verification stage at all.103 The most shared stages are 11 (acceptance, 2,263 commands) and 17 (completion, 2,185 commands), followed by 14001 and 14007 (1,524 each).103

SQL used

Run with sqlite3 -readonly against solo-2025-09-16.sqlite (release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL). All columns are text. The tables cvs, cve and cvp carry their ICD column names (CVS_ID ... CVS_UNCERTAINTY, CVE_CVSID ... CVE_CHECK, CVP_TASK, CVP_TYPE, CVP_CVSID) in the current build of the database.

-- headers and command population
SELECT * FROM tcp;  SELECT * FROM pcpc;
SELECT * FROM pcdf ORDER BY PCDF_TCNAME, cast(PCDF_BIT AS int);
SELECT CCF_PKTID, CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1,2,3;
SELECT CCF_MAPID, CCF_APID, count(*) FROM ccf
 WHERE CCF_PKTID = 'NOM_TC' AND CCF_MAPID <> '' GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT CCF_CNAME, CCF_PKTID, CCF_CTYPE, CCF_ILSTAGE FROM ccf WHERE CCF_ILSTAGE IN ('N','');
SELECT CCF_ACK, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;

SELECT CCF_CTYPE, count(*) FROM ccf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT * FROM ccf WHERE CCF_PKTID IN ('NO_HDR','NOS2KHDR');
SELECT * FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME IN ('UNLOCK','SETVR') ORDER BY CDF_CNAME, cast(CDF_BIT AS int);
SELECT * FROM dst;  SELECT * FROM ptv;
SELECT count(*), sum(CPC_CCAREF<>''), sum(CPC_PAFREF<>''), sum(CPC_PRFREF<>'') FROM cpc;

-- example command
SELECT * FROM ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME = 'ZCSD3905';
SELECT * FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME = 'ZCSD3905' ORDER BY cast(CDF_BIT AS int);
SELECT * FROM cpc WHERE CPC_NAME IN (SELECT CDF_PNAME FROM cdf WHERE CDF_CNAME = 'ZCSD3905');
SELECT * FROM ccs WHERE CCS_NUMBR = 'CSDP0005TC';
SELECT * FROM pas WHERE PAS_NUMBR IN ('CCDT0024TC','CCDT0287TX');
SELECT * FROM prf WHERE PRF_NUMBR = 'VCD00353'; SELECT * FROM prv WHERE PRV_NUMBR = 'VCD00353';

-- sequences
SELECT CSF_IFTT, count(*) FROM csf GROUP BY 1;
SELECT * FROM css WHERE CSS_SQNAME = 'AACC309A' ORDER BY cast(CSS_ENTRY AS int);
SELECT * FROM sdf WHERE SDF_SQNAME = 'AACC309A';
SELECT * FROM csp WHERE CSP_SQNAME = 'AACC309A';

-- verification
SELECT CVS_TYPE, CVS_SOURCE, count(*) FROM cvs GROUP BY 1,2;
SELECT CVP_CVSID, count(*) n FROM cvp GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 4;
SELECT p.CVP_CVSID, s.* FROM cvp p JOIN cvs s ON s.CVS_ID = p.CVP_CVSID
 WHERE p.CVP_TASK IN ('ZCD00305','ZPW04604');
SELECT * FROM cve WHERE CVE_CVSID = '32';
SELECT count(*) FROM ccf WHERE CCF_CNAME NOT IN (SELECT CVP_TASK FROM cvp);
SELECT * FROM txp WHERE TXP_NUMBR IN ('CDST0003TM', 'CDST0001TM');   -- transponder options
SELECT cast(PID_STYPE AS int), count(*) FROM pid WHERE PID_TYPE = '1' GROUP BY 1;

docs.title: Worked example: ZCD00305 from packet to CLTU
docs.text:
The command ZCD00305 "Enable HK Para Rpt Gen" is TC(3,5) to APID 172, with NOM_TC header and Ack 9. It has one editable element, PCD03011 "HK SID" (PTC 3 / PFC 4, 8-bit unsigned, range set VCD00353: 1 to 192).9759 On board it asks the housekeeping service to enable periodic generation of the report with the given SID. Solar Orbiter lists TC(3,5) as "Enable Housekeeping Parameter Report Generation".3958 The values below are illustrative: SID 1, source ID 120 (direct commands), sequence count 1, VC 1, MAP ID 1, N(S) = 0x2A and no randomization; the TC FECF is included, as the ICD's figure 3.1-1 shows.104 The CRCs and BCH parity were computed by this wiki with the algorithms cited. The bytes are not taken from a real uplink.

Layer Octets (hex) Decoding Packet primary header 18 AC C0 01 00 06 version 0, type 1, DFH 1, APID 172 (0b00010101100: PID 10, category 12); flags 0b11, count 1; length 6 = 7 octets of data field minus one Data field header 19 03 05 78 secondary header flag 0, PUS version 1, Ack 0b1001; type 3; subtype 5; source ID 120 Application data 01 SID 1, within range 1 to 192 Packet error control 7E 79 CRC-16, preset all ones, \(X^{16}+X^{12}+X^5+1\), over the 11 preceding octets Frame primary header 02 8A 04 14 2A TFVN 0, bypass 0, control 0 (AD frame); SCID 650; VCID 1; length 20 (21 octets); N(S) 42 Segment header C1 flags 0b11, MAP ID 1 (normal commanding) Frame error control C1 39 CRC-16 over the 19 preceding frame octets CLTU EB 90 · 02 8A 04 14 2A C1 18 6C · AC C0 01 00 06 19 03 DA · 05 78 01 7E 79 C1 39 0C · C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 79 start sequence; 3 BCH codewords (7 information octets, then parity/filler octet); tail sequence. The 21-octet frame fills exactly three codewords, so no fill is needed. 34 octets in total

The packet is 13 octets, the frame 21 octets and the CLTU 34 octets. Under PLOP-2 the CLTU would be preceded by the acquisition sequence at the start of the pass and followed by at least one octet of idle sequence.89 Once on board, the FARM accepts the frame if V(R) = 42 and moves V(R) to 43, which the next CLCW reports as N(R) = 43.7769 The application then sends TM(1,1) and, after enabling the report, TM(1,7). SCOS-2000 closes stages 14001 and 14007 when these arrive within their verification windows, which are computed from the 20 s CVS_INTERVAL.10319

docs.title: Worked example: building a real Solar Orbiter telecommand
docs.text:
This page builds one real Solar Orbiter telecommand from its definition in the public Mission Information Base (MIB) down to the bits that leave the ground station antenna. The command definition, its parameter, the textual de-calibration, the packet header template and the verification stages are real rows of the release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (database 25925PFM, comment 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33).1 Their meaning comes from the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 7.0.2 The Solar Orbiter packet and frame rules come from the Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure ICD (SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7).3 The CCSDS and ECSS standards supply the coding rules. Every byte shown is computed on this page.

What is real and what is illustrative

Real (from the sources cited): command name, APID, type, subtype, acknowledgement flags, parameter type, alias table, packet header template, verification stages, the Solar Orbiter spacecraft ID (650), the MAP ID convention and the frame and packet length limits. Illustrative (chosen by this wiki and labelled as such): the packet sequence count (42), the source ID (120), the virtual channel (1), the frame sequence number (5) and the choice between AD and BD service. The CRCs, BCH parity octets and randomized octets are computed from those values with the algorithms of the standards.

We enable the METIS housekeeping report with SID 108, so this page is the uplink twin of Worked example: decoding a real Solar Orbiter telemetry packet, which decodes exactly that report. The general uplink chain is described on Uplink: from operator command to on-board execution.

docs.title: The command we picked
docs.text:
We wanted a command with a single parameter that is harmless by design: it changes what telemetry is generated, not the state of the spacecraft. TC(3,5) "Enable housekeeping parameter report generation" fits. In the Solar Orbiter ICD it carries a single 1-octet SID and starts the generation of one defined housekeeping report.17 The METIS version is:77

Property Value Command ZIT00305 "Enable HK Par. Rep. Gen" Detailed description TC(3,5) - ENABLE HK PARAMETER REPORT Generation PUS service type / subtype 3 / 5 APID 1084 (0x43C) = Process ID 67, packet category 12 Parameter PIT00301 "HK_SID", 8 bits, textual de-calibration CITT1120TC Packet header template NOM_TC Acknowledgement flags 9 = 0b1001 (acceptance and completion reports) Verification stages 59001 (acceptance), 59003 (completion), both report based

Solar Orbiter allocates Process IDs 67 to 71 to METIS, and every telecommand APID has packet category 12.186 All 126 METIS commands go to APID 1084, while the SID 108 report is generated on APID 1092 (Process ID 68).7783 The command definition, its parameter and its verification stages are identical in the April 2020 release MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL. Two things around them differ: the alias set has grown from 17 entries in 2020 to 18 in 2025 (HK_SID_110 was added), and in the 2020 NOM_TC header template the source ID is a fixed area of value 0 instead of a header parameter (see step 3).86

flowchart TD
    A["MIB: CCF + CDF + CPC + PAF/PAS<br/>ZIT00305, SID = HK_SID_108"] --> B["SCOS-2000 encoding<br/>TCP/PCDF header NOM_TC + application data + CRC"]
    B --> C["PUS-A TC packet<br/>13 octets, APID 1084"]
    C --> D["TC segment<br/>header 0xC1: no segmentation, MAP 1"]
    D --> E["TC transfer frame<br/>SCID 650, VC 1, AD or BD, FECF"]
    E --> F["CLTU<br/>EB90 + 3 BCH codewords + tail"]
    F --> G["NCTRS/NIS, ground station<br/>(SLE FCLTU)"]
    G --> H["Spacecraft TC decoder:<br/>FARM-1, MAP 1 to the central software"]
    H --> I["METIS (APID 1084) executes TC(3,5)"]
    I --> J["TM(1,1) acceptance, TM(1,7) completion<br/>then TM(3,25) SID 108 on APID 1092"]

Layering from the Solar Orbiter ICD (§3) and the CCSDS TC standards;52541 the routing default from the ICD's DST table description.57

docs.title: Step 1: the command definition (CCF)
docs.text:
The CCF holds one record per command.53 The record of ZIT00305, field by field:77

# Field Value Meaning (ICD §3.3.3.2.1) 1 CCF_CNAME ZIT00305 unique command name 2 CCF_DESCR Enable HK Par. Rep. Gen short description (24 characters) 3 CCF_DESCR2 TC(3,5) - ENABLE HK PARAMETER REPORT Generation detailed description 4 CCF_CTYPE (empty) a normal packet command; R, F, S, T and N would mark control segments, BC frames, packets without CRC, SLE and NIS throw events 5 CCF_CRITICAL N not critical (hazardous) 6 CCF_PKTID NOM_TC packet header template from the TCP table 7-9 CCF_TYPE, CCF_STYPE, CCF_APID 3, 5, 1084 copied into the header fields of PCDF type T, S and A 10 CCF_NPARS 1 one CDF element 11 CCF_PLAN N not plannable by any source 12 CCF_EXEC Y may be loaded stand-alone on a manual stack 13 CCF_ILSCOPE N no interlock by default 14 CCF_ILSTAGE C stage an interlock would wait for: completion 15 CCF_SUBSYS 110 on-board subsystem identifier 16-17 CCF_HIPRI, CCF_MAPID N, (empty) not a high-priority command; no forced MAP ID 18 CCF_DEFSET (empty) no default parameter value set 19 CCF_RAPID (empty) no redundant APID 20 CCF_ACK 9 default value of the 4-bit Ack field, modifiable at load time 21 CCF_SUBSCHEDID 110 default on-board sub-schedule if loaded time-tagged

Field meanings from the ICD.53545556 The interlock stage only matters when an interlock is set; with CCF_ILSCOPE = N there is none.55 CCF_CRITICAL = N is not unusual: in this release 5448 of the 5454 commands have N and the other 6 leave the field empty, so no command is flagged critical in the MIB.85 The ICD leaves the extra protection of critical commands to each mission.53

There is no PTV row for ZIT00305, so no static pre-transmission validation applies, and no PSM row, so no parameter set.78 The DST table has a single row, for APID 1372. APID 1084 is therefore routed to the default destination, the NCTRS.8557

docs.title: Step 2: the application data (CDF, CPC and the alias set)
docs.text:
The CDF lists the elements of the application data field, in the order of CDF_BIT. SCOS-2000 encodes them with no gaps, so even padding bits must be declared.60 ZIT00305 has a single element:78

CDF_ELTYPE CDF_ELLEN CDF_BIT CDF_GRPSIZE CDF_PNAME CDF_INTER CDF_VALUE CDF_TMID E (editable) 8 0 0 PIT00301 R (empty) (empty)

CDF_BIT counts from the end of the packet header, data field header included, so bit 0 is the first bit after the 10-octet NOM_TC header. CDF_ELLEN is informative for parameters: the length really comes from the parameter's PTC/PFC.61 An editable element with an empty CDF_VALUE and no dynamic default has no default at all: the operator must type a value before the command can be loaded.62

The parameter itself is defined in the CPC:78

Field Value Meaning (ICD §3.3.3.2.2) CPC_PNAME, CPC_DESCR PIT00301, HK_SID name and description CPC_PTC / CPC_PFC 2 / 8 enumerated, 8 bits CPC_DISPFMT A engineering values are entered and shown as ASCII text CPC_RADIX (empty → default D) raw values displayed in decimal CPC_CATEG T textual (de-)calibration, so CPC_PAFREF is mandatory CPC_PRFREF (empty) no range check set CPC_CCAREF (empty) no numerical (de-)calibration CPC_PAFREF CITT1120TC alias set in PAF/PAS CPC_INTER, CPC_DEFVAL R, (empty) no parameter-level default

Meanings from the ICD and Appendix A.585973 The Solar Orbiter ICD calls the SID an unsigned integer of 1 byte; an 8-bit enumerated value encodes the same way.1773

docs.title: The textual de-calibration CITT1120TC
docs.text:
Commanding calibrations work in both directions, from engineering to raw for encoding and from raw to engineering for display, and must be one-to-one.66 The PAF row CITT1120TC ("HK SID", raw format U) has 18 aliases in the PAS:79

PAS_ALTXT PAS_ALVAL PAS_ALTXT PAS_ALVAL SID_1_BOOT 1 HK_SID_107 107 IIC_SID_20 20 HK_SID_108 108 HK_SID_101 101 HK_SID_109 109 HK_SID_102 102 HK_SID_110 110 HK_SID_103 103 TASKs_Status 112 HK_SID_104 104 HK_SPARE_1 ... HK_SPARE_4 113 ... 116 HK_SID_105 105 IIC_COPY 120 HK_SID_106 106

The operator picks HK_SID_108, SCOS-2000 looks up PAS_ALVAL and encodes the raw value 108 = 0x6C.6779 The alias set mirrors the telemetry textual calibration CITT1120TM used for the SID field of the METIS reports, entry for entry.79

Six METIS commands share PIT00301: TC(3,1) define, TC(3,3) clear, TC(3,5) enable, TC(3,6) disable, TC(3,9) report and TC(3,130) collection interval.78

docs.title: Range checks and numerical de-calibrations: not used here
docs.text:
PIT00301 has neither a range set (PRF/PRV) nor a numerical curve (CCA/CCS).78 For contrast, the platform command ZCD00305, the same TC(3,5) for the central software's data management application on APID 172 (Process ID 10), uses an 8-bit unsigned SID parameter (PCD03011, PTC 3 / PFC 4) with range set VCD00353.807318 That range set has one raw range, 1 to 192, although its description reads "Integer between 1 and 19".80 SCOS-2000 accepts a value equal to either bound.68

Inference

The mismatch between the VCD00353 description ("1 and 19") and its values (1 to 192) is most likely a truncation: PRF_DESCR holds at most 24 characters, and "Integer between 1 and 192" has 25.72 The April 2020 release has the same description and range.86 The MIB itself does not say which is intended; the PRV values are what SCOS-2000 checks. The uplink walk-through reaches the same reading.

docs.title: Step 3: the packet header template (TCP, PCPC, PCDF)
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 builds the packet header from a template. The TCP names the templates, the PCPC names the header parameters and the PCDF lays the elements out by bit offset from the start of the packet.50 The Solar Orbiter MIB defines four templates: HPC1_TC (high-priority CPDU commands, no data field header), NOM_TC (normal commands), NO_HDR (control frames and segments) and NOS2KHDR (NIS throw events).81 5318 commands use NOM_TC, 125 use HPC1_TC, 6 use NOS2KHDR and 5 use NO_HDR.85

The 13 PCDF elements of NOM_TC:81

PCDF_BIT PCDF_LEN PCDF_DESC PCDF_TYPE PCDF_PNAME PCDF_VALUE (hex) Filled by 0 3 Version Number F 0 fixed 3 1 Type F 1 fixed: telecommand 4 1 DataFieldHeaderFlag F 1 fixed 5 11 APID A PH_APID 0 CCF_APID 16 2 Sequence Flag F 3 fixed: 0b11 18 14 Sequence Count P PH_SSC 0 command system 32 16 Packet Length P PH_LEN 0 command system 48 1 Secondary Header Flag F 0 fixed 49 3 PUS Version F 1 fixed: PUS version 1 52 4 Ack K DFH_ACK 0 CCF_ACK 56 8 Service Type T DFH_TYPE 0 CCF_TYPE 64 8 Service Subtype S DFH_STPE 0 CCF_STYPE 72 8 Source ID O DFH_SRC 0 see below

Rows from the MIB (all with radix H; all PCPC parameters are unsigned, code U);81 type letters from the ICD: F fixed, A APID, T type, S subtype, K acknowledgement flags, P set automatically by the command subsystem.51 The packet length counts the actual length, repeated groups included, and the multiplexer keeps a sequence counter per APID. Operators cannot edit header parameters on a manual stack.51

Inference

Open point, PCDF_TYPE = O. The Source ID element uses type O, which is not among the six types listed in ICD issue 7.0, nor in the other ICD issues in this wiki's library. Its exact semantics are not stated in the available sources. Since the PCDF value is 0 and the Solar Orbiter ICD reserves values 110 to 113 and 120 to 122 for ground sources, it is presumably a mission-specific type through which the command source inserts its own identifier. This is an inference.1951 The April 2020 release supports this reading: there the same element is a fixed area (PCDF_TYPE = F, value 0, no PCDF_PNAME), the PCPC has only six parameters (no DFH_SRC) and the template is described as "Normal Header", so every NOM_TC command encoded with that release carried source ID 0.86

The NOM_TC template matches the Solar Orbiter ICD's description of the TC packet: version 000, type 1, data field header flag 1 (all commands except CPDU commands), sequence flags 11 ("stand-alone"), then a 4-octet data field header with the CCSDS secondary header flag 0, PUS version 1, the Ack field, type, subtype and an 8-bit source ID.67919 It is the PUS-A layout of ECSS-E-70-41A §5.3.3 with the optional source ID present and no spare.21

Solar Orbiter (PUS-A, version 1)PUS-C (version 2), for comparison

Layout from the MIB PCDF and the Solar Orbiter ICD.819

Bits Content 4 TC packet PUS version number, set to 2 4 acknowledgement flags (same bit meanings) 8 + 8 message type: service type ID, message subtype ID 16 source ID optional spare

The PUS-C header is 5 octets instead of Solar Orbiter's 4, because the version field grows to 4 bits and the source ID to 16 bits.23 See PUS packet structures and PUS-A vs PUS-C.

docs.title: The Ack field
docs.text: In PUS-A the four Ack bits ask for success reports: bit 3 (the least significant) for acceptance, bit 2 for start of execution, bit 1 for progress and bit 0 (the most significant) for completion; failure reports are always generated.21 Solar Orbiter restricts the field to 0000, 0001, 1000 and 1001; the start and progress bits must be zero.915 CCF_ACK = 9 is 0b1001: acceptance and completion. 5225 of the 5454 commands in the release use 9.85 The flags can be changed when a command is loaded, and unsetting a flag also disables the matching report-based verification stage.5665

docs.title: Step 4: assemble the packet
docs.text:
Putting the pieces together, with an illustrative sequence count of 42 and source ID 120:

Octets Field Bits Value Origin 0-1 version, type, DFH flag, APID 000 1 1 10000111100 0x1C3C PCDF fixed values + CCF_APID 1084 2-3 sequence flags, sequence count 11 00000000101010 0xC02A fixed 11 + count 42 (illustrative) 4-5 packet length 6 0x0006 7 octets in the data field, minus one 6 sec. header flag, PUS version, Ack 0 001 1001 0x19 fixed + CCF_ACK 9 7 service type 3 0x03 CCF_TYPE 8 service subtype 5 0x05 CCF_STYPE 9 source ID 120 0x78 "direct commands" ground source (illustrative choice) 10 SID (PIT00301) 108 0x6C HK_SID_108 via CITT1120TC 11-12 packet error control CRC-16 0x4F50 computed over octets 0-10 
1C 3C C0 2A 00 06 19 03 05 78 6C 4F 50        (13 octets)

Header field rules from CCSDS 133.0-B-2 and the Solar Orbiter ICD;24678 values from the MIB rows above.778179

How the remaining fields are set:

  • Sequence count. The Solar Orbiter ICD wants it kept per APID and source ID, for tracing the command through the ground system; the receiving application does not check it.7 In SCOS-2000 the multiplexer maintains it per APID.51
  • Packet length. C = (octets in the data field) − 1 = (4 + 1 + 2) − 1 = 6. The Solar Orbiter static acceptance checks require 5 ≤ C ≤ 241 and compare C with the number of received octets.815
  • Packet error control. A CRC with generator \(G(x) = x^{16} + x^{12} + x^5 + 1\), shift register preset to all ones, computed over the whole packet except the last 16 bits.1022 The SCOS-2000 releaser appends it to every command unless CCF_CTYPE = S.54 This wiki's implementation reproduces the Solar Orbiter ICD's test vectors (00 00 → 1D0F, AB CD EF 01 → 04A2, 14 56 F8 9A 00 01 → 7FD5) before being applied here.10

The size limits fit together. The Solar Orbiter ICD limits a TC packet data field to 242 octets (4 header + 236 application data + 2 error control), which makes the largest packet 248 octets.8 Its overview drawing (figure 3.1-1) stacks the layers: a TC frame of at most 256 octets is a 5-octet frame header, a frame data field of at most 249 octets (a 1-octet segment header plus up to 248 octets of packets) and a 2-octet frame error control field.511 SCOS-2000's default maximum command size (CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) is also 248 octets.52

Inference

The sources do not say that SCOS-2000's 248-octet default and the Solar Orbiter 248-octet packet limit were chosen to match. They are simply equal.

docs.title: Step 5: how the command will be verified (CVP, CVS, CVE)
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 verification is either report based (PUS service 1 reports) or parameter based (checks on telemetry values). The CVP attaches stages to a command, the CVS defines each stage and the CVE holds the criteria of parameter-based stages.63 ZIT00305 has two stages:82

CVS_ID CVS_TYPE CVS_SOURCE CVS_START CVS_INTERVAL CVS_SPID CVS_UNCERTAINTY 59001 A acceptance R report 0 s 16 s (empty) (empty → −1, standard window) 59003 C completion R report 0 s 32 s (empty) (empty → −1, standard window)

Values from the MIB, columns in ICD field order;82 meanings from the ICD.6465 CVS_START is the delay after release before the window opens, CVS_INTERVAL the sampling interval used to compute the window, and an empty CVS_UNCERTAINTY keeps the default window of the TC Spacon.64 Report-based stages need no CVE rows, and there are none for these two stages.82 Stage 59001 is attached to all 126 METIS commands on APID 1084 and stage 59003 to 125 of them; the exception, ZIT00605 (TC(6,5) dump memory), uses completion stage 59004 with a 4561 s interval instead.82

The acceptance and completion stages are passed by METIS service 1 reports on APID 1073 (Process ID 67, category 1, reserved for TC verification):8318

  • TM(1,1) acceptance success, SPID 59001, and TM(1,7) completion success, SPID 59003. Both carry the 2-octet TC packet ID and the 2-octet packet sequence control of the command, which the MIB places at octets 16 and 18 (NIT82001, NIT82002).8316
  • For our command these four octets would be 1C 3C C0 2A. The SCOS-2000 verifier extracts them from every service 1 report to find the command instance.74
  • Failures arrive as TM(1,2) or TM(1,8) with a 2-octet failure ID after the echo. The PIC identifies service 1 subtypes 2 and 8 by a 16-bit PI1 at octet 20, so each failure ID gets its own SPID (for example TM(1,2) failure ID 2, "PEC_ERROR", is SPID 59007).8320 The verifier itself uses only the subtype, not the failure code.74

Inference

The verification stage IDs 59001 and 59003 are equal to the SPIDs of the METIS TM(1,1) and TM(1,7) packets. This looks like a naming convention of the Solar Orbiter MIB; the ICD does not require it, and CVS_SPID is empty for these stages.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Op as Operator (manual stack)
    participant S2K as SCOS-2000 releaser / verifier
    participant GS as NCTRS, NIS, ground station
    participant SC as Spacecraft TC decoder
    participant MET as METIS (APID 1084)
    Op->>S2K: load ZIT00305, HK_SID = HK_SID_108
    S2K->>GS: release (packet in frame/CLTU)
    GS-->>S2K: ground reception (R), uplinked (U)
    GS->>SC: CLTU radiated
    SC-->>S2K: CLCW in every TM frame: FARM-1 state, V(R)
    SC->>MET: TC(3,5) via MAP 1
    MET-->>S2K: TM(1,1) on APID 1073, echo 1C3C C02A (stage 59001)
    MET-->>S2K: TM(1,7) on APID 1073, echo 1C3C C02A (stage 59003)
    MET-->>S2K: TM(3,25) SID 108 on APID 1092 from now on

The ground stages R, U and O are the interlock stages named in the ICD (reception at the ground station, uplink, on-board reception); in BD mode O is treated as U.55 Stages A and C come from the CVS rows above.82 The CLCW that every Solar Orbiter TM frame carries reports the FARM-1 state of the TC virtual channel, including V(R), the sequence number of the next Type-AD frame it expects.1436

Inference

The ICD does not say how SCOS-2000 detects stage O. For an AD frame, a V(R) that has moved past the frame's N(S) shows that FARM-1 accepted it, which is presumably what closes the stage; the diagram does not claim more than that the CLCW carries this information.

Inference

That the enabled SID 108 report then appears on APID 1092, although the command went to APID 1084, is deduced from the MIB: the alias HK_SID_108 of the command and the SID value 108 of SPID 59208 are the same, and METIS defines SID 108 only on APID 1092.7983 The MIB does not link commands to the packets they enable. ICD Appendix C also warns that SCOS-2000 needs the packet definition in the database before the report is enabled on board.76

docs.title: Step 6: the TC segment and the transfer frame
The segment header
docs.text:
Solar Orbiter puts every TC packet in a TC segment. The 1-octet segment header has 2 sequence flags, always 11 because packets are never segmented, and a 6-bit MAP ID: 0 for CPDU commands, 1 for all normal commands.11 The segment data field may hold several complete packets (aggregation), each found from the length of the one before; SCOS-2000 supports this blocking, but high-priority commands cannot be aggregated.127555 Our segment holds one packet:

Field layout from CCSDS 232.0-B-4 §4.1.3.2.2 and table 4-2,28 values from the Solar Orbiter ICD.11

docs.title: The frame header
docs.text:
The TC transfer frame adds a 5-octet primary header and a 2-octet frame error control field (FECF).2526

Field Bits Solar Orbiter rule Our frame Version number 0-1 00 00 Bypass flag 2 0 = Type-A, FARM acceptance checks; 1 = Type-B, checks bypassed AD: 0, BD: 1 Control command flag 3 0 = data, 1 = control command 0 Spare 4-5 00 00 Spacecraft ID 6-15 0x28A (650), also used by the ETB and OBC-DM 650 Virtual channel ID 16-21 one VC per on-board TC decoder; the ICD lists 000001 and 000010 1 (illustrative) Frame length 22-31 total octets − 1; Solar Orbiter frames are at most 256 octets, so bits 22-23 are 00 20 Frame sequence number 32-39 AD: the FOP-1 counter V(S); BD and BC: 0x00 AD: 5 (illustrative), BD: 0

Rules from the Solar Orbiter ICD §3.4 and CCSDS 232.0-B-4 §4.1.2.132627 The ICD's VC wording is not fully consistent: it calls the "suggested values" zero and one but encodes the two decoders as 000001 and 000010.13 The frame is 5 + 1 + 13 + 2 = 21 octets, so the length field holds 20.

The FECF is present. The text of the Solar Orbiter ICD §3.4 only counts the frame length "to the last bit of the FRAME ERROR CONTROL FIELD (if present)", but its drawings settle the question: figure 3.1-1 shows a 2-octet TC frame error control field (CRC) at the end of every TC frame, and the frame drawing of §3.4 lists a 16-bit frame error control field after the data field, with at most 251 octets for the two together.513 This matches the ICD's TC coding reference, ECSS-E-ST-50-04C, in which all TC frames carry the FECF, and the current ECSS adoption notice of CCSDS 232.0-B-4, which makes it mandatory.43331

The FECF uses the same CRC as the packet error control (generator \(x^{16} + x^{12} + x^5 + 1\), preset to all ones), computed over the 19 preceding octets.30 This wiki's implementation reproduces the FECFs of the CCSDS 230.1-G-3 examples (4C A9 for the Unlock frame, BB 22 for the BD example, 9F 71 for the AD example).47

Type-AD (sequence-controlled)Type-BD (expedited) 
02 8A 04 14 05 | C1 | 1C 3C C0 2A 00 06 19 03 05 78 6C 4F 50 | 03 FF
header           seg  TC packet                                 FECF

Bypass 0, N(S) = 5 (illustrative). The FARM-1 passes the frame on only if N(S) equals V(R), the sequence number it expects next; the outcome is reported in the CLCW carried by every Solar Orbiter TM frame.273614

22 8A 04 14 00 | C1 | 1C 3C C0 2A 00 06 19 03 05 78 6C 4F 50 | 56 0B
header           seg  TC packet                                 FECF

Bypass 1 and N(S) = 0, as the Solar Orbiter ICD requires for BD frames. The FARM acceptance checks are bypassed; the frame validation checks still apply.1327

The MIB also defines the COP-1 control frames that prepare AD mode: UNLOCK (control command flag set, one fixed octet 0x00) and SETVR (fixed area 0x8200 followed by an editable 8-bit V(R)), both with CCF_CTYPE = F and the empty header template NO_HDR.84 Their structure is the CCSDS Unlock and Set V(R) control commands.29

docs.title: Step 7: the CLTU
docs.text:
The frame is wrapped in a Communications Link Transmission Unit for the physical layer: a 16-bit start sequence, BCH codewords and a 64-bit tail sequence.41 Each BCH codeword carries 56 information bits followed by 7 complemented parity bits and a filler bit 0, using the (63,56) modified BCH code with \(g(x) = x^7 + x^6 + x^2 + 1\).3738 If the frame does not fill the last codeword, fill octets 0x55 (alternating bits starting with 0) are appended.39

Our 21-octet frame is exactly three 7-octet blocks, so no fill is needed and the CLTU is 2 + 3 × 8 + 8 = 34 octets. ECSS-E-ST-50-04 puts exactly one frame in each CLTU.32

Start sequence 0xEB90 and tail 0xC5C5C5C5C5C5C579 from CCSDS 231.0-B-4 §5.2;4243 codewords computed by this wiki with the BCH encoder of §3.3 and, in the randomized tabs, the pseudo-randomizer of §6 applied to the frame before encoding.384546 Both algorithms were first checked against the unrandomized and randomized CLTUs of CCSDS 230.1-G-3 annex F, examples 1, 12 and 15.47

Inference

Randomization. Whether Solar Orbiter randomizes its TC frames is not stated in the available sources. With BCH coding, CCSDS requires the randomizer unless the system designer verifies that the link works without it, so in practice it is optional and fixed per physical channel by management. In ECSS-E-ST-50-04, which the Solar Orbiter ICD lists as its TC coding reference, randomization is always used; the ECSS handbook adds that some European on-board hardware cannot handle it.44344 Both forms are therefore shown.

On board, the decoder looks for the start sequence, decodes each codeword (ECSS-E-ST-50-04 always uses single-error-correction mode, which is why the FECF is needed), removes the randomization after decoding, and stops at the tail sequence, which is built to be uncorrectable.4033354643 Acquisition and idle sequences around the CLTU depend on the physical layer operations procedure (PLOP) and are not shown.47 Details: TC synchronization and channel coding: the CLTU.

docs.title: Step 8: from SCOS-2000 to the antenna
docs.text:
With no DST entry for APID 1084, SCOS-2000 releases the command to the NCTRS, the default destination for spacecraft commands.5785 Towards the ground station, the CCSDS SLE forward CLTU service is the standard service "that enables a mission to send CLTUs to a spacecraft".48 (The alternative Forward Space Packet service, whose book the library holds as a historical copy, takes packets instead and leaves the frames and CLTUs to the provider.)6970 Which ground component encodes the frame and the CLTU for Solar Orbiter is not stated in the sources used for this page; see NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface. The CLTU then modulates the uplink carrier at one of the telecommand bit rates of the spacecraft transponder (7.8125 to 4000 bit/s in the MIB's calibration of the transponder's TC bit rate parameter);71 see radio frequency, modulation and ranging. The ICD notes that a CLTU has a mission-specific maximum size, which constrains CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE.52

The released command is archived too. The Solar Orbiter data delivery ICD says the archive keeps a TC packet per released command (SPID 100) with its verification status and the full packet sent to the spacecraft, plus a separate packet (SPID 200) with the static PTV and verification details from the MIB.49

docs.title: Worked example: decoding a real Solar Orbiter telemetry packet
docs.text:
This page follows one real housekeeping packet of the Solar Orbiter spacecraft through the ground system, byte by byte. The packet definition, every parameter, every calibration curve and every limit come from the public Solar Orbiter Mission Information Base (MIB), release MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (database 25925PFM, comment 20250916-CSW3.1.2_MAS7.33).1 The meaning of each MIB field comes from the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 7.0, which the public Solar Orbiter document site (hosted at IRAP) files among its MOC documents as the "MOC-applicable MIB" ICD.2 The packet structure comes from the Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure ICD (SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 issue 7).3 The bytes at the end are a constructed example: no real downlinked telemetry is used on this page.

What is real and what is illustrative

Real (from the sources cited): the APID, type, subtype, SID, SPID, packet layout, parameter names and types, calibration points, polynomial coefficients, textual aliases, limit values, and the header conventions of Solar Orbiter. Illustrative (constructed by this wiki): the source sequence count, the on-board time and the raw parameter values in the byte string of step 6. They were chosen to look plausible and to exercise every calibration type. They are not spacecraft data.

The companion page Worked example: building a real Solar Orbiter telecommand builds the command that switches this very report on. The general flow is explained on Downlink: from on-board parameter to operator display.

docs.title: The packet we picked
docs.text:
We want a fixed-layout PUS housekeeping report (service type 3, subtype 25) that is small enough to decode completely and that still uses every kind of monitoring calibration the MIB offers. The MIB holds 288 TM(3,25) packet definitions on 62 APIDs.58 Filtering them by size and by the calibration tables their parameters reference leaves only two packets of 5 to 45 parameters that combine numerical curves, polynomials, textual calibrations and a limit check (SPIDs 59208 and 54101, the latter with 44 parameters; query in the SQL box below). The best fit is the METIS instrument's "HK SID 108 - HVU - LED" report:59

Property Value Source table SCOS-2000 packet ID (SPID) 59208 PID PID_SPID Description TM(3,25) - HK SID 108 - HVU - LED PID_DESCR APID 1092 (0x444) PID_APID PUS service type / subtype 3 / 25 (housekeeping parameter report) PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE First extra identifier (PI1) 108 (the structure ID, SID) PID_PI1_VAL Packet mnemonic YIT59208 TPCF TPCF_NAME Packet size 37 octets TPCF_SIZE Parameters 11, all at fixed positions PLF Calibrations used 2 textual, 3 two-point numerical, 1 175-point numerical, 1 polynomial TXF, CAF, MCF Limit checks soft and hard limits on the HVU temperature OCF, OCP

Values from the 2025 release.59616364 The same layout (the same eleven parameters at the same offsets), the same numerical curves, polynomial and limits are already present in the April 2020 release MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL, with two differences: in 2020 SAFE_Param (NIT0E072) is an uncalibrated 16-bit unsigned integer (PTC 3 / PFC 12, category N, no CITT1072TM), and the SID alias set CITT1120TM has 17 entries (no HK_SID_110).66

APID 1092 splits into a 7-bit Process ID of 68 and a 4-bit packet category of 4 (1092 = 68 × 16 + 4). The Solar Orbiter ICD allocates Process IDs 67 to 71 to the METIS payload instrument and reserves category 4 for routine, cyclic TM(3,25) housekeeping.18 The same APID carries 16 different TM(3,25) packets in the MIB, told apart only by their SID (1, 102 to 110, 112 to 116 and 120).59 That is why the SID matters so much in the identification step below.

Inference

The parameter descriptions use the abbreviations HVU, MCP and LED (for example HVU_mcp_V, LED_curr_set). The MIB does not expand them. They plausibly refer to a high-voltage unit, a micro-channel plate and a light-emitting diode used for calibration, but this is not stated in the available sources. Nothing on this page depends on that reading.
