docs.title: EDDS request and data formats
docs.text:
This page is the format reference for the EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS). It covers what a client sends (XML requests), what it gets back (acknowledgements, identifiers, response files) and the binary records inside those files. The generic definitions come from the EDDS External User Interface Control Document (EUICD), mainly issue 24.0 of January 2025. That document says its XML schema files are the primary reference and the text follows them.1 The mission layer comes from the Solar Orbiter Data Delivery Interface Control Document (DDID) SOL-ESC-IF-05011 issue 1.2. The DDID explains which archive answers each request, which SCOS-2000 headers wrap each packet, and how RAPID files carry the whole packet archive to the Science Ground Segment.2

Three real byte sequences are decoded below. One is a raw PARC telemetry packet shown in an ESOC presentation, and two are the GDDS binary examples printed in the EUICD. Every decoding step is marked as this wiki's own work.

docs.title: Overview: one request, many shapes of answer
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  R["RequestMessagePart (XML)<br/>ContextPart + BatchRequest"] --> V{"schema and<br/>privilege checks"}
  V --> P["data provider<br/>PARC / DARC / FARC / SMON / ..."]
  P --> F["formatter<br/>EDDS raw, GDDS binary, SFDU,<br/>Protocol Buffers, XML, ASCII, TDRS"]
  F --> X["optional XSLT transform"]
  X --> S["split into chunks<br/>(splittable formats)"]
  S --> PP["post-processing<br/>ZIP / TAR / TAR.GZ, AES, XFDU"]
  PP --> D["delivery<br/>EDDS server or file server push"]
  V -.-> A["AcknowledgementPart (XML)<br/>updated at every stage"]

The figure is this wiki's summary of the processing order given in the SDD.3 The request type decides which formats are allowed. The EUICD's format table, condensed (✓* marks formats that can be split into several response files):4

Request family EDDS raw Binary (Protocol Buffers or files) XML ASCII Others Packet TM, TC (PARC) ✓* – – – GDDS_BINARY*, SFDU Packet EV (PARC) ✓* – – – – Packet TM, TC, EV raw (PARC) – ✓* ✓* – – TM report, TC report, event record report – ✓* ✓* ✓* RawSourceBinary* (TM report) OOL record report – ✓* ✓* – – TM gap report – ✓ ✓ – – Packet statistics – – ✓ – – Parameter TM (DARC, SMON) – ✓* ✓* – TDRS Parameter definition – ✓* ✓* – – Parameter statistics, preview – – ✓* ✓* – FARC file, file-system file – ✓ (as received, in TAR) – – – FARC and file-system catalogues – – ✓ ✓ – Acknowledgement – – ✓ – –

Splitting is configured by the EDDS administrator. Each chunk keeps a valid header and tail of its format.4 The column positions of Table 13 do not survive text extraction well. This wiki placed the marks using the per-type format enumerations of EUICD Appendix H (for example ParamStatisticsFormat is XML or ASCII, and ParamDefinitionFormat is XML or BINARY).5

docs.title: Request types
docs.text:
Every request names one data-access type. The enumeration DataAccessDataElement (EUICD Appendix D.24) is also the "subtype" field of the request ID.67

Data source Request types DARC Param, ParamStatistics, ParamDefinition, ParamPreview SMON SmonParam PARC PktTm, PktTc, PktEv, PktTmRaw, PktTcRaw, PktEvRaw, PktTmStatistics, PktTcStatistics, PktEvStatistics, PktTmReport, PktTcReport, PktTmGapReport, EventRecordReport, OolRecordReport FARC ArchiveCatalogue, ArchiveFile, ArchiveSubscription File system FileSystemFileCatalogue, FileSystemFolderCatalogue, FileSystemFile, FileSystemSubscription EDDS EddsUsageReport Streams ParamStream, PktTmStream, PktTcStream, PktEvStream, OolStream EGS-CC EgsccActivityReport, EgsccLogMessageReport (and the Egscc... packet and parameter types of Table 12)

The DataSource enumeration names the back ends: FARC, DARC, PARC, EDDS, SMON, FileSystem and DataProvisionService.8 The types that return XML are paired with response types. Param returns ParamResponse, PktTmRaw returns PktRawResponse, PktTcReport returns PktTcReportResponse, ArchiveCatalogue returns CatalogueResponse, and so on. The packet types PktTm, PktTc and PktEv and the file types return binary files.9

docs.title: Element tree
docs.text:
The top element of a batch request is RequestMessagePart in the namespace http://edds.egos.esa/model. The tree below follows the "children" lists of the schema appendices.10111213

flowchart TD
  RMP["RequestMessagePart"] --> CP["ContextPart<br/>MissionId, DomainId, PrivacyTag"]
  RMP --> BR["BatchRequest"]
  BR --> C["Comment"]
  BR --> SCH["Schedule<br/>ScheduleOnce, ScheduleRepeating<br/>or ScheduleWithExpiry"]
  BR --> U["User<br/>UserName, Role"]
  BR --> DR["DataRequest<br/>(exactly one request type)"]
  BR --> AD["AckDelivery<br/>EmailDelivery"]
  DR --> PT["PktTm (example)"]
  PT --> RPP["RequestPostProcessing<br/>DataCompression, DataEncrypting"]
  PT --> DEL["Delivery<br/>ServerDelivery or FileServerDelivery"]
  PT --> TF["TmPacketFilter"]
  PT --> PF["PacketFormat"]
  TF --> PNL["PacketNameList"]
  TF --> TR["TimeRange"]
  TF --> TFI["TimeFiltering"]
  TF --> TFL["TmFilterList → PktTmFilterKeyword"]
  TF --> DS["Dataspace, BriefReportFlag, IncludeRawData"]

The common building blocks are listed below.

Element Content Values and rules ContextPart MissionId, DomainId, PrivacyTag PrivacyTag is PRIVATE, ROLE, MISSION or PUBLIC1415 User UserName, Role The role picks the privileges and the quota sets16 ScheduleOnce Immediate or Once (AbsoluteTime, AbsoluteDOYTime or RelativeTime) Relative times use the XSD duration type17 ScheduleRepeating RepeatingSchedule: StartTime, Repetition (CronExpression or Step), EndTime (FinalDate, FinalDOYDate, Delta or NumberOfRepetition) The Archiver creates one request, and one job ID, per execution1718 ScheduleWithExpiry As ScheduleOnce plus RequestExpiryDate – 17 RequestPostProcessing DataCompression, DataEncrypting ZIP, TAR, TARGZ, NONE; NONE, AES (implementation mission-specific)19 ServerDelivery FileName, NamePrefixSuffix, TimeFormat, CustomTimeFormat TimeFormat is CCSDS, DOY or CUSTOM. File names may not contain a slash, backslash, backtick, question mark, angle bracket, vertical bar, colon, tab or line break.20 FileServerDelivery TargetLocations (Target, FileServerUsername, FileServerPassword, TargetFolder), naming fields, KeepFileAfterDelivery Pushes the result to the user's (S)FTP server20 AckDelivery EmailDelivery (EmailList, Default) Acknowledgement by e-mail20 TimeRange StartTime, StartDOYTime, RelativeStartTime, EndTime, EndDOYTime, Duration, ConsolidationTime Used by all packet and parameter filters21 TimeFiltering GENERATION_TIME or STORAGE_TIME On-board time (primary key) or archive reception time (secondary key)22

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Packet filters combine a time range with keyword lists. The keywords below are the children of the filter-keyword types.23

Filter Keywords PktTmFilterKeyword Apid, Pid, Category, GenerationTime, GenerationDOYTime, ReceptionTime, ReceptionDOYTime, TimeQuality, VirtualChannel, DataStream, DataBaseVersion, GroundStation, SourceSequenceCounter, SpacecraftId, MaximumDataVolume PktTcFilterKeyword ExecutionTime, ReleaseTime (and DOY forms), Type, SubType, Name, DataStream, DataBaseVersion, SourceSequenceCounter, SequenceName, CommandSource, the four acknowledgement flags, CommandSubSystem, CommandSubschedule, MaximumDataVolume, GroundStationId, Description, Apid, UplinkMode, OverallVerificationStatus, and one status keyword per verification stage (release, ground station, uplink, on-board reception, acceptance, execution start, steps 1 and 2, completion; real-time and playback) PktEvFilterKeyword GenerationTime, GenerationDOYTime, Id, MessageText, Category, Severity, ApplicationId, ApplicationName, Workstation, MaximumDataVolume ParamTmFilter DarcDataSpace, ParamNameList, TimeRange, TimeFiltering, DeliveryRange, OnChange, ParamFilterList, SuperCommutationFlag, MaxDecimalPlaces, the TDRS options TdrsUseDOY, TdrsStatsOnly and TdrsDataOnly, and RepresentationSelection (ENG, RAW or ALL)

Packet names (APID, PI1, PI2, SPID, type, subtype) are written in the SpidsSpecifier syntax: a comma-separated list of values or numeric ranges such as 100-200.24 The CommandSource enumeration lists the SCOS-2000 command sources: MANUAL_STACK, AUTO_STACK, EXT_SOURCE, TC_SPACON, OBQM_DISP, SMF_SOURCE, NAVPRS_STACK, MKMF_STACK, PKMF_STACK and SKMF_STACK. UplinkMode is A (AD transmission mode) or B (BD).2526 These AD and BD modes are the COP-1 service types.

The APID filter is not native to the PARC Manager, which can only query by SPID. The EDDS expands APID, type, subtype, PI1 and PI2 filters into a SPID list using the mission's pid.dat.27 The SRS asks that the APID filter cover "all fields of the APID (e.g. PID and PCAT)".28 This refers to the split of the 11-bit APID into a 7-bit process ID and a 4-bit packet category, as Solar Orbiter's packet ICD defines it, for example.29 The EUICD's TM header fields "PID" and "Category" are both "calculated from the APID".51

docs.title: An illustrative request
docs.text:
The EUICD contains no complete XML request instance. Its Appendix O gives Java code that builds a DARC parameter request object by object.30 The listing below is that object tree written out as XML by this wiki. It is illustrative: the parameter names come from the Solar Orbiter MIB, but the element order, the namespace prefix and the mandatory-element rules have not been checked against the XSD.

<RequestMessagePart xmlns="http://edds.egos.esa/model">
  <ContextPart>
    <MissionId>SOLO</MissionId>            <!-- mission name as configured in EDDS -->
    <DomainId>0</DomainId>
    <PrivacyTag>PRIVATE</PrivacyTag>
  </ContextPart>
  <BatchRequest>
    <Comment>IMU temperature, one day</Comment>
    <Schedule><Immediate/></Schedule>      <!-- ScheduleOnce/Immediate -->
    <User><UserName>investigator1</UserName><Role>PI_ROLE</Role></User>
    <DataRequest>
      <Param>
        <RequestPostProcessing>
          <DataCompression>TARGZ</DataCompression>
          <DataEncrypting>NONE</DataEncrypting>
        </RequestPostProcessing>
        <Delivery><ServerDelivery><FileName>imu_temp</FileName></ServerDelivery></Delivery>
        <ParamTmFilter>
          <DarcDataSpace>DEFAULT</DarcDataSpace>
          <ParamNameList>
            <ParamNameListElement>NMUD1113</ParamNameListElement>
          </ParamNameList>
          <TimeRange>
            <StartTime>2025-09-01T00:00:00Z</StartTime>
            <EndTime>2025-09-02T00:00:00Z</EndTime>
          </TimeRange>
          <TimeFiltering>GENERATION_TIME</TimeFiltering>
          <DeliveryRange><None/></DeliveryRange>
        </ParamTmFilter>
        <ParamTmFormat><Format>DARC_Binary</Format></ParamTmFormat>
        <DataSource>DARC</DataSource>
      </Param>
    </DataRequest>
    <AckDelivery><EmailDelivery><Default/></EmailDelivery></AckDelivery>
  </BatchRequest>
</RequestMessagePart>

NMUD1113 is the "IMU11 SIA temperature" parameter. The Param format choices are XML, TDRS, Binary (EGS-CC binary) and DARC_Binary.31 For speed, the EUICD's own example code recommends binary output.30

docs.title: Stream requests
docs.text: A stream request has the same shape. StreamRequestMessagePart holds a ContextPart and a StreamRequest. The StreamRequest holds Comment, Schedule, User and a StreamDataRequest, which contains one of ParamStream, PktTmStream, PktTcStream, PktEvStream or OolStream. The packet and OOL streams each have a DataSource and a Filter; ParamStream has a ParamNameList and a ParamTmStreamFilter.32

docs.title: GDDS requests through the Request Submitter
docs.text:
The Request Submitter accepts requests in the older GDDS XML format. It first validates a file against the EDDS schema, then against the GDDS schema. GDDS files are converted with the XSLT GDDS2EDDS.xsl and submitted under the Submitter's own user account.3334 The mapping has limits:34

GDDS element EDDS mapping schedule/firstStartTime, schedule/interval Execution time of the first request; days between requests. GDDS has no end date, so 10 requests are always created. general/comment Request comment. Extra lines Mission: and Domain: select a mission and domain other than the default. general/userInfo with destInfo/FTP Credentials, file name and directory for file-server delivery; otherwise EDDS server delivery general/formatInfo/compression EDDS compression option (SFDUrequired and missionFormat are not used) item with dataType TLM TM packet request. dataSource is the APID; the filter needs a lower and an upper SourcePktsGenTime bound. item with dataType CMH, dataSource CMDH Raw TC packets (bounds on ExecutionTime) item with dataType CMH, dataSource CMDPB / CMDPF TC brief or full report item with dataType AUX Archive file (Name, and Release plus Issue mapped to a version)

GDDS filters are recursive binary trees of bin and leaf nodes with operations such as OP_AND, OP_GTE and OP_LTE. The EDDS accepts them only in a simple form, with no OR inside an AND. If such an "illegal" expression occurs, the whole subtree is ignored.34

docs.title: Request and response IDs
docs.text:
Request IDs are created by the Archiver when the request is stored.7

Form Used for Example (illustrative) [RequestType].[Username].[yyyy.DDD.hh.mm.ss.SSS] AccountRequest (LDAP changes) AccountRequest.investigator1.2025.255.10.00.00.000 [RequestType].[Subtype].[Mission].[Domain].[yyyy.DDD.hh.mm.ss.SSS].[RandomStr] Everything else BatchRequest.Param.SOLO.0.2025.255.10.00.00.000.Ab3x

RequestType is one of BatchRequest, StreamRequest, Cancel, DeleteData, DeleteRequest or AccountRequest. The time is the creation time in day-of-year form, GMT. RandomStr is four random characters. Response files are named <request id without random part>@<creation time>.<counter>.<extension>, with the counter starting at 1 for split responses.7 The Delivery Manager recovers the request ID from the file name to look up the delivery method.35 Stream Client recordings use TmRecording_, TcRecording_, OolRecording_, EvRecording_ or ParamRecording_, followed by day, month, year, hour, minute, second and millisecond, separated by underscores.36

docs.title: The AcknowledgementPart
docs.text:
There is exactly one acknowledgement per request. It is created by the Archiver and updated at every stage.37 Its children are:38

Group Elements Identity ContextPart, RequestId, User, Priority Status State, Retries, Reason (for retries), Error, ProblemRecords (records that could not be retrieved) Times (each also in DOY form) ReportCreationDate, SubmissionTime, ScheduledTime, StartTime, CompletionTime, ExpiryTime Progress Percentage, RetrievedSamples, FilteredSamples Output ResponseFiles (each a ResponseFileEntry: FileName, Size, Status, Error, Checksum, a CRC32 of the completed file), Delivery, AckDelivery Resume support FilterTimeWindow (the time-range filter converted to an absolute window), LastSampleReference (the last record stored, for resumable requests)

State takes the values of the request life cycle: SUBMITTED, QUEUED, CANCELED, SUSPENDED, COMPLETED_NO_RESULTS, SERVER_COMPLETED, DELIVERED, DELIVERED_RESP_DELETED, DELIVERED_PARTIAL_RESULTS, and the errors ERROR_LOCALLY_DELIVERED, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, ERROR_INVALID_REQUEST, ERROR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ERROR_SERVER_NOT_AVAILABLE, ERROR_DELIVERY and ERROR_UNKNOWN.39 The SUM adds ACTIVE; the state diagram is on the EDDS page.40

docs.title: Response packaging
docs.text:
• Compression. ZIP archives compressed files. TAR bundles files without compression (USTAR format). TARGZ compresses the tar file with gzip.4142
  • Encryption. AES, enabled per mission. The SDD's delivery manager notes that a key file can be one of the response files.1935
  • XFDU. An optional post-processing step wraps the response in a CCSDS XML Formatted Data Unit (CCSDS 661.0-B-1). The SDD's XFDU formatter adds each data file in Base64, with metadata and a checksum that the XFDU library itself does not compute.4344 The SRS asks that each EDDS data-object ID map one-to-one to an XFDU data-object ID, and that a CCSDS Submission Information Package layer could later be added on top.45
  • XML transforms. Every XML-capable request can be passed through a mission stylesheet. getTransformations() lists the stylesheets available.46
  • ASCII. Similar to the XML without markup. The TC report imitates the SCOS-2000 Command History display, with one column per check and verification stage. Examples are S and D (static and dynamic PTV checks), C (CEV), IL (interlock), R, G, T, O and A (release, ground station, uplink, on-board reception, acceptance), and SS, 1122 and CC (execution start, steps and completion). Stage values include F, U, X, P, T, S, I, A, C, V, N and E.47 See command verification for the stages.
  • TDRS spreadsheet. Tab-separated parameter values in the format of the TDRS ICD, produced by Param.xsl or by a faster native formatter. The TDRS retrieval ID, execution ID and expiration day are filled with dummy values, except that the native formatter puts the EDDS request ID in the retrieval ID.48

docs.title: EDDS raw binary
docs.text:
The "EDDS raw" (EDDS binary) format is self-describing. A mission chooses which header fields accompany each packet.49

Part Occurs EDDS raw header once EDDS header fields (1), data element (1) per packet … EDDS header fields (N), data element (N)

The EDDS raw header is N (1 octet), the number of header fields defined, followed by one octet per field giving its size. For a string field, the size octet only says whether the field is included, because string lengths are known only at run time. Strings are written as a length followed by the characters, both in hexadecimal.5051

The sequence count lets a client detect missing elements. The TC and EV elements have the same three parts. For them, the EUICD calls the count and length fields "Unsigned Integer" without giving their sizes.51

docs.title: Header fields available per packet type
docs.text:
# TM header field (EUICD Table 16) # TC header field (Table 18) 1 Source sequence counter 1 PUS service type 2 APID 2 Source type 3 PID (from the APID) 3 PUS service subtype 4 Category (from the APID) 4 APID 5 P1 value (mission-specific) 5 PID 6 P2 value 6 Category 7 SCOS-2000 data stream 7 Virtual channel ID 8 Generation time (CUC, time-correlated) 8 Verification status (mission-specific) 9 Reception time (CUC, extraction from frame) 9 Uplink time (CUC) 10 Packet length (for GDDS compatibility) 10 Execution time (CUC) 11 SPID 11 Last update time 12 Ground station 12 Release time 13 Virtual channel 13 Sequence name (top-level parent) 14 Data unit type 14 Sub-schedule 15 PUS service type 15 Subsystem 16 PUS service subtype 16 Command source (workstation) 17 SLE service ID (8 bits, for GDDS compatibility) 17 Command acknowledgement (4-bit PUS ack) 18 Time quality: 0 good, 1 inaccurate, 2 bad 18 Verification stages supported (R, GTO, AC) 19 Quality flag / time-stamp type: 0 packet reception, 1 frame transmission, 2 packet generation 19 Data stream 20 Database version 20 Domain 21 Domain 21 Database version 22 PUS source sequence count 23–27 CUV; CAV VC0; CEV VC0; CAV VC1; CEV VC1 28 Packet length 29 Command name

The table is from EUICD §6.1.2.1–§6.1.2.2.51 EV packets can carry event type, event ID, source, category, generation time and domain.52 The EGS-CC variants add fields such as the live flag, packet instance ID, earth-received time, route, data partition and storage time.51 Header layouts are configured per mission in XML files (RawTmPktHeader, RawTcPktHeader) that name each field and its length.53

EDDS raw is hexadecimal text

Despite the word "binary", the EUICD speaks of data "stored in a raw (ASCII hexadecimal) file".49 The Solar Orbiter DDID and the ESOC presentation describe EDDS raw as an ASCII string of the hexadecimal packet data, including the EDDS raw header.5455

docs.title: GDDS binary
docs.text:
GDDS_BINARY reproduces the response format of the older GDDS FTP service.56 Unlike EDDS raw, it is real binary: a fixed header followed by the source packet without any SCOS-2000 header.54 The EUICD explains it by analogy with EDDS raw. The GDDS TM header fields correspond to EDDS fields 8, 10, 12, 13, 17 and 18, and the TC header fields to EDDS fields 9, 10, 23 to 29 and 13. Its examples show the header fields followed directly by the packet.57

The EUICD says the 8-octet times hold seconds since 1970 in the first four octets and microseconds in the last four.57 The Solar Orbiter DDID adds that the seconds count ignores leap seconds.54

docs.title: Worked example: the EUICD's two GDDS telecommands
docs.text:
The EUICD prints two TC records (real bytes from the source).57 This wiki decodes them below. The interpretation of the PUS fields uses the PUS-A TC layout of ECSS-E-70-41A.5859

Field Record 1 bytes Decoded by this wiki Uplink time 4FB6 5AD2 000E 9A94 1337350866 s and 957076 µs = 2012-05-18T14:21:06.957076Z Execution time 4FB6 5BE4 0006 9398 1337351140 s and 431000 µs = 2012-05-18T14:25:40.431Z CUV, CAV VC0, CEV VC0, CAV VC1, CEV VC1 0004 1000 0000 1000 0000 Stage codes; their meaning is not stated in the available sources Packet length 0000 000D 13 octets Command ID 5A41 4330 3330 3036 ASCII ZAC03006 Parent sequence ID 0000 0000 0000 0000 none TC packet 18BC C1F1 0006 1903 0600 0084 C0 See below

The 13-octet packet starts with a Space Packet primary header. 0x18BC gives version 0, type 1 (TC), secondary header flag 1 and APID 0x0BC = 188. 0xC1F1 gives sequence flags 0b11 (stand-alone) and sequence count 497. The length field 0x0006 means a 7-octet data field, and 6 + 7 = 13 agrees with the GDDS length field. The data field header 0x19 03 06 reads as: CCSDS secondary header flag 0, PUS version 1, ack 0b1001 (acceptance and completion), service 3, subtype 6.58

Record 2 is a 33-octet ZMT11004 packet (18FC C012 001A 190B 0400 0007 …): APID 252, sequence count 18, length field 26 (27-octet data field), data field header 0x19 0B 04, which is service 11, subtype 4. After the three octets 00 00 07 come the six octets 4FB6 5BE4 6E56, then the complete record 1 packet (18BC C1F1 0006 1903 0600 0084 C0), and finally the two octets B539. Its uplink and execution times are both 4FB6 5AD2 000E 9A95, one microsecond after record 1's uplink time.57

Inference

Record 2 looks like a PUS-A TC(11,4) "Insert Telecommands in Command Schedule" request.59 It would load record 1's command into the on-board schedule. The six octets before the embedded packet would then be its release time: 0x4FB65BE4 equals record 1's execution time in seconds, and 0x6E56/65536 = 0.431 s equals record 1's 431000 µs. The first 00 after the subtype may be an optional PUS-A source ID, and the final B539 probably the packet error control, but neither they nor the octets 00 07 before the time are explained in the available sources. Record 1's own data field (19 03 06 00 00 84 C0) would then be header, source ID, one octet of application data and a 2-octet error control field.

docs.title: Worked example: the GDDS TM records
docs.text:
The two TM records in the same EUICD section have generation times 4E94 46BE A7B8 D000 and 4E94 46BE 6334 3000, packet length 0x50 (80 octets), and zero ground station, virtual channel, SLE service and time quality.57 0x4E9446BE is 2011-10-11T13:38:06Z.

Inference

The second words (0xA7B8D000 = 2813906944 and 0x63343000 = 1664364544) are larger than 106, so they cannot be microseconds as the EUICD states. The 80-octet payloads also do not decode as CCSDS packets: read that way, their length field would be 0xFFFF. The first payload ends in the ASCII text UPDATE %. Read instead as the 16-octet SCOS-2000 TM-specific header in little-endian order (see below), the first 16 octets of each payload give validity 0, TPSD -1, route ID 0, APID 200, SSC 1 (2 in the second record) and type and subtype 200, which suggests an internal SCOS-2000 packet body rather than a spacecraft source packet. This is speculation. The TM example is best read as a layout illustration only.

docs.title: Protocol Buffers binary
docs.text:
The "Binary" format of most report and parameter types is Google Protocol Buffers. A file starts with an ASCII header line of the form # Key1: Value1; ... ; KeyN: ValueN, with the keys Type and Version. The header line is followed by length-prefixed ("framed") messages, each prefixed by its size as a varint.60 The .proto files ship in the edds-ws-common project. The EDDS uses the Protocol Buffers implementation of the ActiveMQ library, whose output is compatible with Google's implementation.61

Message Used by Main fields DarcParameterBinary Parameter TM (DARC; also HARC "DARC_Binary") param_name, gen_time, storage_time, value, validity (VALID, INVALID, UNKNOWN, EXPIRED), type (BIT, UTINYINT … DOUBLE, STRING, DATETIME, …), and fields absent in DARC 2.2.2 and earlier: parentGenTime, parentId (the SPID), typed raw values ParamDefinitions / ParamDefinitionRecord Parameter definitions name, description, unit, type, active SMONParameterBinary SMON parameters name, calibration ID, packet instances (reception and generation time, sample offset, sequence counter), representation samples with validity and behaviour states PacketRawBinary Packet TM/TC/EV raw packet (hex string of the SCOS-2000 packet), packet_id PacketTMBinary Packet TM report APID, PID, category, SPID, type, subtype, generation and reception time, ground station, VC, data unit type, PI1, PI2, packet length, mnemonic, body, decoded parameters (name, unit, radix, bit and byte offset, value) PacketTCBinary Packet TC report command name, source, sequence, release, uplink and execution times, PUS type and subtype, APID, SSC, PTV and CEV check states, group and block flags, interlocks, every verification-stage state (real-time and playback), time-tag status, parameters, mission-specific fields, body PacketTMGapBinary TM gap report gap start and end, data partition, APID, SSC before and after, packets missing OOLReportBinary OOL record report record type (LIMIT, STATE, STATUS_CONSISTENCY, SOFT_HARD_LIMIT, DELTA, …), parameter state, value, limits, delta and violation data EventRecordReportBinary Event record report ID, domain, generation time, application, severity, type, workstation, message

The fields are from EUICD §6.7.3.3.62 The OOL states correspond to the SCOS-2000 monitoring checks defined in the MIB. The PTV and CEV check states of the TC report correspond to the MIB's verification definitions.

RawSourceBinary, available for TM report requests, is the simplest format. It is a plain concatenation of CCSDS TM source packets with no extra header, made from the raw packet bodies of the report.6364

docs.title: Worked example: a real Packet TM Raw file
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter EDDS presentation shows the first bytes of a "Pkt TM Raw" response in binary format (real bytes from the source).65 It starts with the ASCII header # Type: Packet TM Raw PARC data; Version: 1.0; followed by:

Bytes (hex) Decoded by this wiki 0A Line feed ending the header line DD 02 Varint frame length: 0x5D + 2 × 128 = 349 octets of message 0A Field 1 (packet), wire type 2 (length-delimited) D8 02 Length 0x58 + 2 × 128 = 344 30 30 30 30 … 344 ASCII hex characters ("0000…"), that is a 172-octet SCOS-2000 packet 10 01 Field 2 (packet_id), wire type 0 (varint), value 1. 1 + 2 + 344 + 2 = 349 octets, the frame length

Inference

EUICD §6.7.3.1 says the header line ends with a "single line feed character (byte value A0 in HEX)".60 The real file has 0x0A, which is the ASCII line feed, so "A0" in the EUICD is probably a transposition. The same section lists only Parameter and SMON Parameter as Type values, while the sample's header says Packet TM Raw PARC data. The slide shows the framing bytes twice, and one copy reads D8 82 instead of D8 02; only D8 02 gives a length that matches the 344 hex digits that follow. The presentation also shows the same packet in the XML format, as the <Packet> element of a PktRawResponse. The 344 hex digits are identical.

The 172-octet packet itself is decoded field by field in the SCOS-2000 packet section below.

docs.title: SCOS-2000 packets inside the PARC
docs.text: "Raw" PARC requests return the packet exactly as the packet archive stores it. That is a SCOS-2000 packet (also called a TDEV packet): a common header, a type-specific header for TM, TC or EV, and the packet data.67 For spacecraft TM, the packet data is the complete, unstripped source packet. Internal MCS "telemetry" (filed on a separate data stream) and occasionally whole frames can also appear. For TC, the packet data holds the MCS command details and the uplinked packet.67 The DDID takes its definitions from the SCOS-2000 Packet Management ADD, which is not in the library.68

docs.title: Common header (60 octets)
docs.text:
The field meanings, condensed from DDID §7.1.1:68

Field Bits Meaning and Solar Orbiter values FT (filing time) 32 + 32 The primary key, which the EDDS calls generation time. For TM it is the correlated on-board time when time-stamp = 2 and time quality = 0. For TC it is the release time. CT (creation time) 32 + 32 When the SCOS-2000 packet was created, roughly its reception and storage. For TC, the (estimated) execution time. S/C ID 16 650 for Solar Orbiter G/S ID 16 21 Kourou, 22 Perth, 23 New Norcia, 24 Cebreros, 25 Malargüe, 30 Maspalomas, 201 Reference Test Station (ESOC), 202 NDIU Lite, 203 NDIU IFMS Type, Version 4, 4 Type 1 TM, 2 TC, 3 event; version 5 Time-stamp 2 0 = time-stamped at SCOS-2000 reception (PR), 1 = frame transmission time, i.e. earth reception time minus propagation delay (FT), 2 = correlated SCET (PG) Stream ID 16 1000 to 1003 = VC0 real-time non-science, VC1 playback non-science, VC2 science, VC3 file transfer (online); 2000 to 2003 the offline equivalents; 1 for TC; 1000 and 1001 for events; 65535 internal packets to be ignored Filing key 32 The SCOS-2000 SPID, linking to the MIB pid table. TCs use SPIDs 100 and 200. Mission, context, domain IDs 16 each 650, 0, 0 for Solar Orbiter; not for external use DB release, DB issue 16 each VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE of the MIB used for archiving

The DDID lists the offline VC1 playback stream twice, as 2001 and 2002, and then VC2 science as 2003. The table above reproduces the entries as printed.68

docs.title: TM-specific header (16 octets)
docs.text:
The TPSD is the MIB's PID_TPSD. It is -1 for fixed-structure packets and the vpd structure number for variable ones.6970 The low octet of the route ID classifies the data unit:69

Data unit type (high nibble) Qualifier (low nibble) 0 TM transfer frame 0 good, 1 bad, 2 idle 1 TM source packet 0 good, 1 bad, 2 idle, 3 unknown, 4 service 9 time packet 2 internal MCS TM packet 0 CLCW, 1 user-defined constants, 2 status consistency check, 3 dynamic MISC, 4 on-line MIB changes, 5 SPPG, 6 SPID validity, 7 TPKT configuration, 8 external source

When frames are missing in the middle of a large science packet, the MCS files the partial packet as data unit 1, qualifier 1 (bad). It then files the remaining frames one per SCOS-2000 packet as data unit 0, qualifier 0, until it finds the next packet header. The MCS cannot detect frames missing at the start of the next packet, so the DDID tells users to separate packets by time stamp.71

docs.title: TC-specific header (44 octets)
docs.text: The TC packet data hold the "command details". These are the static MIB information (mnemonic, parameters, verification definitions) and dynamic status, so that the TC history stays readable even after the runtime MIB has changed. The layout is defined in a separate ICD, and the DDID warns that it changes during development.72 It is written by overlaying a C++ object on a 32-bit platform, so fields are 32-bit aligned with padding: an 8-bit field at offset 100 followed by a 32-bit field puts the second at 104.72 For decoding, the EDDS needs an XML description of this structure per mission (TCPacketStructure.xsd).53 The MCS also archives a second TC packet per command, with SPID 200, which holds the PTV/CEV details. External users should ignore it.67 There is no event-specific header: event information goes straight into the packet data.71

docs.title: Worked example: decoding the raw PARC packet
docs.text:
The 172-octet packet from the presentation (real bytes, decoded by this wiki using the DDID field list) is shown below.656869

Offset Bytes Field Value 0 0000 00 00 C-Tree, access flag, spare/sim 0, 0, 0 4 69 73 27 56 FT seconds 0x56277369 = 1445426025 → 2015-10-21T11:13:45Z 8 B9 40 08 00 FT microseconds 540857 12 6F 73 27 56 CT seconds 1445426031 (6 s after FT) 16 C5 7C 09 00 CT microseconds 621765 20 01 00 00 00 Create ID 1 24 30 03 S/C ID 816 26 CB 00 G/S ID 203 (NDIU IFMS in the DDID list) 28 AC 00 00 00 Size 172 = whole packet 32 15 Type, version 1 (TM), 5 33 26 Flags, time-stamp, time quality bit assignment not confirmed 34 E8 03 Stream ID 1000 (VC0 real-time, online) 36 9C 11 00 00 Seq counter 4508 40 A8 DE 00 00 Filing key (SPID) 57000 44–47 0000 0000 Retrieval keys 0 48 30 03 Mission ID 816 50–53 0000 0000 Context, domain 0, 0 54 06 00 01 00 DB release, issue 6, 1 58 00 00 Spare 60 00 00 30 00 Validity not used 64 FF FF FF FF TPSD -1 (fixed packet) 68 10 FF Route ID LSB 0x10: data unit 1 (source packet), qualifier 0 (good) 70 F4 05 PUS APID 1524 72 64 0F PUS SSC 3940 74 03 19 Service, subtype 3, 25 76 0D F4 CF 64 00 59 … Source packet (96 octets) see below

The source packet starts at octet 76 in big-endian CCSDS order. 0x0DF4 gives version 0, type 0 (TM), secondary header flag 1, APID 0x5F4 = 1524. 0xCF64 gives sequence flags 0b11 and count 3940. The length field 0x0059 = 89 gives a 96-octet packet, and 60 + 16 + 96 = 172 equals the Size field. Octets 6–8 of the source packet, 10 03 19, give service 3 subtype 25, a housekeeping report.

Inference

  • The multi-octet SCOS-2000 header fields are little-endian in this sample. Only that reading gives a plausible date, microseconds below 106, a Size of 172 and an APID and SSC that match the source packet. The CCSDS source packet itself is big-endian. The DDID says the Solar Orbiter EDDS is configured so that "all data" is big-endian, but it does not say whether that covers the archived SCOS-2000 header.54
  • The sample is probably not Solar Orbiter data. S/C ID and mission ID are 816, not
  • In the 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB, SPID 57000 is "SPICE Real Time and FDIR HK Report" on APID 1364, and APID 1524 does not occur in either the April 2020 or the September 2025 release. The presentation is dated September 2017, its first presenter was BepiColombo's mission data systems manager, it was updated for Solar Orbiter only in January 2019, and the time stamps date from October 2015.6673
  • The type and version octet 0x15 decodes as type 1, version 5 if the first-listed field takes the high nibble. The same rule applied to octet 33 (0x26) would give filing 1, dist 0, time-stamp 1, time quality 2, which this wiki cannot confirm.

docs.title: What the Solar Orbiter DDS delivers and from where
docs.text:
Data type Source on the MCS long-term archive DDID section TM packets (including MCS-generated packets such as time correlation) LTA PARC 7 and 8.1 TC packets LTA PARC 7 and 8.1 Event packets LTA PARC 7, 8.1, 8.4.2.2 TM, TC and event statistics LTA PARC SUM 5.2.3 TM parameters and parameter statistics LTA DARC 8.2 Command history report, TM gap report, TM/TC/event reports LTA PARC 8.3 Auxiliary files, TM files, archive catalogues LTA FARC 8.4

The table follows DDID §6.2.74 Telemetry packets downlinked through the Solar Orbiter service 13 file protocol are delivered as TM files rather than as packets. See ST[13] large packet transfer.74 For Solar Orbiter, the formats are configured as follows:54

  • EDDS raw with no extra header fields (N = 0). Each element is therefore 00, then the EDDS sequence count, the data length and the source packet, without any SCOS-2000 header. This is exactly the layout above with an empty field list.
  • GDDS binary: the binary header followed by the source packet. The SLE service ID field is "not believed relevant to the end user".
  • Packet raw (Protocol Buffers or XML): the hex string includes the SCOS-2000 headers.
  • Byte order: big-endian. Times: 4-octet seconds since 1970 (leap seconds not counted) plus 4-octet microseconds.

The DDID refers to EUICD sections by the numbering of EUICD issue 15, the issue current when the DDID was revised (the 2019 presentation names issue 15.0 as the EUICD that the DDID complements).76 Its "6.7.3.3.6" (binary TC report), "6.7.3.3.8" (TM gap report), "6.7.3.3.9" (OOL report) and "Table 5" (EDDS file header) match issue 15. In issue 24.0 these are §6.7.3.3.7, §6.7.3.3.11, §6.7.3.3.12 and Table 15.756279

docs.title: MCS-internal packets and the MIB
docs.text:
Besides spacecraft packets, the Solar Orbiter TM archive holds packets generated by the MCS itself, on APID 1966. Users should filter them out by APID or by SPID, except for the time correlation packets.77 The DDID lists 14 SPIDs. This wiki's queries show that the April 2020 MIB defines exactly those 14 SPIDs on APID 1966. The September 2025 release defines 18: it adds three MATIS packets and "Saved Synthetics".73

SPID PUS type, subtype Description in the 2025 MIB In DDID list In 2020 MIB 101, 102, 103 166, 1–3 MATIS basic HKTM OK, RX lock expected, SSMM FTS commanding – – 66810 160, 1 File Transfer Model, modelled transfer packet ✓ ✓ 66830 160, 3 Dynamic UDCs ✓ ✓ 66831 160, 6 TC Spacon packet (TC configuration) ✓ ✓ 66832 160, 5 MISC config variables packet ✓ ✓ 66838 251, 2 Saved Synthetics – – 66840 164, 1 Time Correlation Report ✓ ✓ 66841 164, 2 TCO Time_Couples OBT ✓ ✓ 66842 164, 3 TCO_Coefficients OBT ✓ ✓ 66850 165, 1 TM packet used by the Releaser G/S response ✓ ✓ 66980, 66981, 66982 161, 5 / 4 / 3 Good, bad, idle mini-transfer frame ✓ ✓ 66983 162, 1 Bad telemetry packets ✓ ✓ 66985 160, 2 Missing packets detection (variable packet, TPSD 66985) ✓ ✓ 66999 162, 2 TM packet with no assigned SPID ✓ ✓

The APID 1966 explorer page lists them all. The DDID gives the time correlation packets as type 164 with subtypes 1, 2 and 3, which agrees with the MIB.77 The spacecraft's own time packets have APID 0.77 In the MIB that is SPID 9999, TM(9,2) "Time Report", a 14-octet packet with parameters at octets 6, 7 and 8 (the last is NCD09023 "OBCHP_OBT").73 See ST[09] time management.

The time correlation coefficient packet (SPID 66842, 66 octets) is what an external user needs to turn on-board time into UTC. Its parameters, from the MIB:73

Octet Parameter Description PTC/PFC 16 NYG02023 TCO VALIDITY 2 ¾ 17 NYG02024 TCO ACCURACY 2 ¾ 18 NYG02026 TCO GRADIENT 2 5/2 26 NYG02027 TCO OFFSET 2 5/2 34 NYG02028 TCO OBT_N 2 5/2 42 NYG02029 TCO UTC_N 2 5/2 50 NYG02031 TCO STD 2 5/2 58 NYG02032 TCO STE 2 5/2

The parameter types are explained under PTC/PFC in SCOS-2000, and the octet positions are the PLF_OFFBY values. The eight values fill the packet exactly: the last 8-octet value starts at octet 58 and the packet is 66 octets long.73 The DDID points to the BepiColombo/Solar Orbiter packetiser ICD for the packet content, and the time correlation page explains gradient and offset.78

SQL used

Run against solo-2025-09-16.sqlite and solo-2020-04-16.sqlite on 2026-11-12. All columns are text.

-- MCS-internal packets
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR, PID_TPSD, PID_DFHSIZE
FROM pid WHERE CAST(PID_APID AS int) = 1966 ORDER BY CAST(PID_SPID AS int);
-- 18 rows in 2025, 14 rows in 2020

-- time packet, idle packet and packet sizes
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR, PID_DFHSIZE
FROM pid WHERE PID_SPID IN ('9999', '66986');
SELECT * FROM tpcf WHERE TPCF_SPID IN ('9999', '66840', '66841', '66842');
-- 9999 YCD00902 14 | 66840 TCORRREP 173 | 66841 OBTCOUPL 105 | 66842 OBTCOEFF 66

-- parameters of the time and time-correlation packets
SELECT p.PLF_SPID, p.PLF_NAME, p.PLF_OFFBY, p.PLF_OFFBI, c.PCF_DESCR, c.PCF_PTC, c.PCF_PFC
FROM plf p LEFT JOIN pcf c ON c.PCF_NAME = p.PLF_NAME
WHERE CAST(p.PLF_SPID AS int) IN (66840, 66841, 66842, 9999)
ORDER BY CAST(p.PLF_SPID AS int), CAST(p.PLF_OFFBY AS int);

-- the SPID of the presentation sample
SELECT PID_TYPE, PID_STYPE, PID_APID, PID_SPID, PID_DESCR FROM pid WHERE PID_SPID = '57000';
-- 3 | 25 | 1364 | 57000 | SPICE Real Time and FDIR HK Report

docs.title: Command history report fields
docs.text: Solar Orbiter's TC report carries extra "Science Kernel" fields. In XML they are CustomField elements (name, type, value), and in Protocol Buffers they are mission-specific fields. The fields are isForcedSubScheduleId, CevCheckStatePB (CEV check state for the playback stream), uniqueID (traceability to a command request file), s13ObFileId and s13ObFileAttribute (PLAIN, OBCP, TC_DELAYED, TC_IMMEDIATE or PAYLOAD_CONTEXT). The last two flag commands uplinked inside service 13 files.79

docs.title: Files: auxiliary files and TM files
docs.text:
The FARC file types available to users include the MIB itself (type MIB), attitude and pointing timelines, event files, short- and long-term orbit files, one-way light time, station visibility predictions, HGA blockage, solar aspect predictions, command request files (CRFG), user events and ground-station scheduling events.80

TM files downlinked through service 13 are stored in the FARC under data, as file type DLPP Files. Each is a plain concatenation of TM packets, named <packet store ID>_<reconstruction time>, for example 13_2014.336.13.54.07.057.81 Their transaction history comes as event packets with SPID 4000:82

Field Octets Transaction ID, packet store ID, status, FDUs received, FDUs expected, retransmissions 4 each Start time, last packet time, end time 4 each Size of file name field 4 File name as given by the previous field Injection kind (0 automatic, 1 manual), injection time 4 each

Status takes 11 values: 0 unknown, 1 active, 2 completed, 3 incomplete, 4 injected, 5 pending abort, 6 cancelled, 7 aborted, 8 pending injection, 9 injection error, 10 cleaned.82

docs.title: RAPID files
docs.text:
The nominal route from the operations ground segment to the Science Ground Segment is not the EDDS. It is a stream of RAPID (Raw Archive Packet Interceptor Dumper) files forwarded by the Generic File Transfer System (GFTS).8384 The MCS writes every SCOS-2000 packet it archives into one of three open RAPID files, one each for TM, TC and EV. It closes them after a configurable time: 50 s on the long-term archive for Solar Orbiter. GFTS then moves them across the OPS LAN firewall to the relay server, and from there to the SGS, with up to 5 parallel transfers to clear a backlog. Two weeks of RAPID files are kept for recovery.8385

File names follow PARC_<Type>_<FirstPacketTime>__<LastPacketTime>, with times as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmmmm. Type is TM, TC or EV. The times are the reception time for TM, the last update time for TC, and the creation time for events, for example PARC_TM_2019-04-04T12:30:00.000000__2019-04-04T12:32:50.000000.86 A file is a sequence of records, each preceded by a 32-bit length. Each record has a fixed metadata part, then the SCOS-2000 packet.87 ST, ET and AT are 8-octet fields of type "Time". The DDID's §7 defines its time fields as 4-octet seconds since 1970 plus 4-octet microseconds; it does not say whether the RAPID record uses the same encoding.8754

The action field matters for TCs. A TC packet is rewritten whenever its verification status changes, and the new copy arrives in a later RAPID file with action "update". An ingestion tool must overwrite the earlier copy, identified by its release time. TM and EV packets are never updated, but recalls can store the same packet twice with a new reception time. Packets also arrive in reception order, not generation order.88

Inference

The sync marker 0x1ACFFC1D is the same 32-bit value as the CCSDS attached sync marker of TM transfer frames for uncoded, convolutional or Reed-Solomon coded data.92 The DDID gives no reason for the choice.

docs.title: Gaps in the available sources
docs.text:
• The SCOS-2000 Packet Management ADD (EGOS-MDS-S2K-ADD-0024), the Command Source Handler ICD (TC command details) and the RAPID ICD (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-1005) are cited by the DDID but are not in the library.89
  • The full XSD files are attached to the DDID PDF as a ZIP (EDDS 2.3 schemas, according to the DDID; the 2019 presentation names an EDDS_2.1_wsdl_schema_definitions.zip). Text extraction does not recover them, so this page relies on the EUICD's schema appendices.9091
  • The meanings of the GDDS stage codes (CUV, CAV, CEV values), of the SLE service ID values and of the OOL packet versions 5 to 7 are not stated in the available sources.

  2. Solar Orbiter DDID SOL-ESC-IF-05011 issue 1.2, title page and §1.1 Objective, PDF pp. 1 and 7. ↩
