docs.title: The design (TC History Ingestion TN)
docs.text:
The HCSS needed to know what was actually sent. Requirement HCSS-UR-3.1-1111 asks that the HCSS associate each telecommand in the TC history with the instrument or spacecraft request in the observation schedule, and use case UCF-759 asks that failed, missing and additional commands be flagged.82 The TC History Ingestion Technical Note (SPIRE-ICS-DOC-002314, issue 0.2, 18 March 2003; issue 0.1 of 7 September 2001, updated when the code went into the HCSS) describes the process for the instrument level test phase, version 0.1.x of the HCSS, over a TCP/IP interface to SCOS-2000 that a CORBA interface was to replace.798081 Among its references is the SCOS-2000 Command History Data Provision Services ICD (S2K-MCS-ICD-0008-TOS-GCI, issue 1.2, August 2000).81

The assumptions show how SCOS-2000 data meet the science schedule:82

  • the TC history file (THF) is an ASCII file produced by SCOS-2000 and contains values only for editable command parameters;
  • commands in the HCSS schedule carry a 32-bit sequence identifier (TCID); manual commands have a null or default TCID;
  • the uplinked schedule also sets observation and building block identifiers (OBSID, BBID), which relate manual commands to observations;
  • TC history times are UT, schedule times TAI, and in instrument level tests only relative times are used, so time conversion is needed;
  • on-board generated event-driven TCs are out of scope; telecommands are the lowest level of command generation and become persistent when the schedule is exported to the MOC.

The process has two components linked by their own TCP/IP connection: a THF server, which asks SCOS-2000 for the history of a time window, receives the file name and fetches the file from the directory where SCOS-2000 wrote it; and a TC history ingestor, which validates the file (first line, time window), creates one TCHistory object per command, links it to its TC in the database by TCID, flags missing histories and missing TCs, updates the success flags of observations and block executions, commits, and waits for the next period.83

sequenceDiagram
  participant I as TC history ingestor (HCSS)
  participant F as THF server
  participant S as SCOS-2000
  participant D as HCSS database
  loop every configured period
    I->>F: request TC history for a time window
    F->>S: connect, ask for the window
    S-->>F: file name of the THF written to its directory
    F->>F: read the THF from the shared directory
    F-->>I: THF
    I->>I: validate first line and time window
    I->>D: create TCHistory objects, link by TCID
    I->>D: flag missing TCs and histories, update BB and observation success
    I->>D: commit once per file
  end

The design decisions, in short:868788

Decision Content Interface TCP/IP to SCOS-2000 for now, CORBA later; the THF server must run on the SCOS-2000 host or see its directory Availability On a lost or failed connection, wait and retry, logging each event Missing TCs A history with a TCID unknown to the database is logged and stored anyway (an error condition, so that no data are lost) Manual commands TCID 0; the observation and building block are guessed from the time stamp; the history is stored without association Success A failed TC is logged; a building block is marked uplinked when all its TCs succeeded, an observation executed when all its TCs succeeded Size and rate A THF holds 0 to many TCs, typically a day; one THF per day is foreseen; one commit per file

The software lives in the Java package nl.esa.herschel.tchingest (api, bin, doc, server, test, util). The FileIngestion interface (getFile, checkFile, processFile, initStore, commitData) is shared by the TC history and out-of-limits ingestion, with abstract classes for file details, ingestion (including roll-back on abort) and the file server.8485

docs.title: Operating it (TCH/OOL user manual)
docs.text:
The User Manual for Telecommand History and Out-of-Limits ingestion (SPIRE-ICS-DOC-001852, issue 2.3, 13 November 2008) covers both ingestors. Its change record shows the history: a combined version in October 2003, integrated system test (IST) support in April 2004, a command-line retrieval mode in May 2004, time-out and delete properties in February 2007, and support for "DDS OOL files" in November 2008.8990 Each ingestion has a file retriever that asks SCOS-2000 for a THF or an out-of-limits file (ORF) and receives its name, a file server used during instrument level tests (ILT mode) to serve files periodically over TCP/IP, and an ingestor that works either from the server (ILT mode) or from files named on the command line (IST mode). The OOL ingestor also reads DDS files from the MOC in the routine phase.91 Every ingestor validates the file and the time window, creates objects, skips objects already in the database, makes the others persistent, links them where possible and commits. The TC history ingestor checks the header line, links histories to TCs, updates success flags and looks for gaps in TC IDs; the OOL ingestor attaches each OOLPacket to the building block closest in time.92

The configuration properties and their defaults:939495

Property Meaning Default hcss.tchool.database HCSS database for both ingestors Site-specific, must be overridden hcss.tchool.tch.server, hcss.tchool.ool.server Hosts of the THF and ORF servers 127.0.0.1 hcss.tchool.tch.port, hcss.tchool.ool.port Ports of the THF and ORF servers 3187, 3188 hcss.tchool.attemptwaittime Wait before reconnecting to a file server 60000 ms hcss.tchool.maxattempts Reconnection attempts per file 5 hcss.tchool.fileperiod Interval between file requests 60000 ms hcss.tchool.s2kserver, hcss.tchool.s2kport SCOS-2000 host and port 127.0.0.1, 2209 hcss.tchool.s2kdirectory Directory where SCOS-2000 writes files (input only) /spired/HPR hcss.tchool.s2ktimezone Time zone of SCOS-2000 UTC hcss.tchool.delete Delete extracted files after sending true hcss.tchool.timeout Connection time-out (SCOS connection) 2000 ms hcss.tchool.dateformat Format of the start times yyyy/MM/dd-HH:mm:ss (the THF/ORF format is yyyy.DDD.HH.mm.ss) hcss.tchool.tch.starttime, hcss.tchool.ool.starttime Start of the first request 2003/10/20-15:00:00 hcss.tchool.timetolerance Two times are equal within this margin 1000 ms

In ILT mode the operator starts thfserver and orfserver on (or with visibility of) the SCOS-2000 machine and then the ingestors; in IST mode tchoolretrieve [TC | OL] (or its GUI) extracts the files, which are copied to the database machine and passed to tchingest or oolingest. The OOL ingestor treats a file whose name ends in .OOL or .TLM as DDS format, otherwise as SCOS format.96 Appendix A lists 26 error messages, mostly missing or invalid configuration, connection failures, database exceptions and malformed THF records (missing header, wrong time format, command data, bit pattern or parameter data records of wrong length). Appendix B lists warnings such as "already in database", unknown TC, first TC outside the time tolerance, unassociated histories, unsuccessful TCs and missing histories.9798

The THF format

The record names in these error messages (header, command data, bit pattern and parameter data records) are those of the THF's own ICD, the TC History ICD (SPIRE-ICS-DOC-000900, issue 1.0, 30 October 2002, prepared by M. J. Graham), which is now in the library: an ASCII file named THF_yymmdd_cccc.DAT, made of a header record and fixed-length records that end with a new-line but have no field delimiters, each command record (C) followed by a bit pattern record (B) and zero or more parameter records (P); the bit pattern is not applicable to ILT, where it is available through SCOS-2000.154155156 The record layouts are on the interface documents page. The format of the out-of-limits files (ORF) is still not stated in the available sources.9791

docs.title: SPIRE database management and configuration control
docs.text:
SPIRE's note on database management and CUS configuration control (SPIRE-RAL-NOT-002829, issue 1.0, 19 February 2007) shows the HCSS side of a test campaign. It applies to all SPIRE test environments: ILT, AVM, IST and the HSC.99100 The HCSS stored its data in a Versant object database (version 7.0.1.1 or later) with a Java 1.5 runtime.101 Creating a test database takes these steps:102104

Step What it does Allocate and initialise Create the database and its instrument model registries (HIFI, PACS, SPIRE) Public access and index Allow access; index TM source packets by time First configuration Create mission configuration config1; every later change to definitions or calibration tables needs a new configuration Ingest the MIB Point hcss.mib.datadir at the MIB directory and run the ingestion with a label; semantic problems are written to mibchecker.log, serious ones stop the ingestion, minor ones do not (example label SPIRE_MIB_2.2.G1) Load into the CUS Load the labelled MIB into the Common Uplink System GUI Calibration tables and CUS definitions Upload calibration tables and the building blocks, procedures and modes from CVS Observation identifiers Set the initial OBSID (in hexadecimal) for the database Instrument model Bind MIB and CUS definitions to the configuration; list the models (for example SPIRE PFM5)

The ingestion settings name the files that complement the MIB: the table definitions, a CUS script, a command list and the command durations file required by the HCSS note.10370 The configuration control rationale is to know, later, "which version of which script was used to produce a particular set of SPIRE telemetry data". Definitions live in the ESA CVS repository, one folder per campaign (CUS and TestControl for ILT, CUS and CCS templates for IST); a single FM folder was to replace them because separate folders proved hard to maintain. Verified definitions are committed and tagged LABEL_CONFIGN (for example AVM_TEST_CONFIG6). Once a test starts, changes are tracked only by the database's automatic versions (CVS 1.2 becomes 1.2.1 when ingested) and checked back into CVS (1.3) after the test, because managing hundreds of definitions by check-in and check-out "can become highly unstable". A new mission configuration freezes a snapshot. Test control scripts and CCS templates have no database versioning, so their working folders are themselves CVS checkouts.105106 A calibration table TestSetup.txt with keys configuration, env (moc, ilt, hsc, ist, par), test_type (ft, pr), instrument (prime, redundant), condition (warm, cool, cold) and dbg_level lets the same CUS definitions run in every environment.107108

docs.title: The ACMS database experience (NLR)
docs.text:
Authors from NLR, Dutch Space, Alcatel Alenia Space (France and Italy) and ESTEC reported the database experience of the attitude control and measurement system (ACMS), developed under Dutch Space responsibility, at SpaceOps 2006 (AIAA-2006-590; NLR report NLR-TP-2007-240, April 2007). The ACMS Test Equipment used the SCOS-2000-based Central Checkout System, ensuring "commonality between tools and data used during subsystem and system level testing and the operational phase".109 The team built its own ACMS operations database in the DOORS requirements tool because the TM definition document could no longer be kept consistent by hand, the TM/TC interface was more complex and extensive than for other ACMS subsystems that Dutch Space had developed, SCOS-2000 in the test equipment needed every TM/TC detail including operational identifiers, and the HPSDB was not mature enough at the time. Dutch Space then supplied its data to the HPSDB as HPSDB-compatible XML.111112

The SCOS-2000 MS Access database "did not fit": it supports one mission only (not the commonality of two satellites with common data), has no configuration control at object level, and cannot relate application software TM/TC to the software specification.112 The DOORS database has modules that mirror the MIB: command characteristics (ccf), TC packet structures (cdf), parameters (pcf, cpc), conversions (caf, cap, cca, ccs, mcf), enumerations (txf, txp, paf, pas), packet identification criteria (pic), packet identifiers (pid, tpcf), TM packet structures (plf), alphanumeric displays, HPSDB boxes and a change log.113114 Operational identifiers are built from HPSDB box numbers: the ACMS mode parameters are AESMG002 on Herschel and AESMG003 on Planck.114 Every object carries its spacecraft (Herschel, Planck or common), software (ASW or BSW) and a VersionFrom/VersionTo range, from which specific SCOS-2000 or HPSDB files are generated; exports, not DOORS baselines, are kept under CVS, and the HPSDB-generated *.dat files are compared with those used in ACMS AIT by a ccsdiff script.115116

The paper's recommendations: integrate the database with specifications and ICDs, make test specifications use database identifiers, keep requirement, software, test and operational identifiers independent but traceable, version every object, and use inheritance and instantiation to avoid duplication. It closes with a plea to standardise "a database design/interface for definition of operations and test related information", for all programmes.117 ESA's 2007 Bulletin likewise notes that common tools for checkout and operations preparation promote a seamless transition from manufacture to operations, as "exploited recently by Herschel and Planck".118

docs.title: The Herschel MIB in the archive
docs.text:
The Herschel MIB itself is not in this wiki's library. ESA's Herschel Science Archive has a page for the Herschel-Planck Spacecraft Database and a data/ folder with fifteen zip files: MOC issues 2 to 13 (July 2009 to October 2011, issue 7 three times) and an earlier, smaller zip from May 2009. According to that page the database reached version 13, with changes added as new SID versions so that version 13 can reprocess all mission telemetry, and its format references are the Database Import ICD issue 6.6 (2008-08-25) and the HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note issue 1.9 (2007-09-14), later than the issue 1.5 described above.124 Read with the file naming convention printed in the 2008 release note, the oldest of these names (HPSDB_R_TM_HERSCH_FM1_M_903062241) would be a reference-area theoretical model HERSCH_FM1 in MCS format, generated on 6 March 2009; the MOC issues use another pattern. This decoding is this wiki's reading, not stated by any source; it is explained on the mission page.151124

Not verified by this page

This wiki's page plan (tools/plan.json) records that the archive currently answers HTTP 403 when the zip files are requested, so no Herschel release could be copied or analysed, and the MIB explorer covers only Solar Orbiter. This page did not access the network and could not re-check either the listing or the refusal.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
• One database, many consumers. The OIRD demanded a single satellite database for engineering, AIV and operations. In practice the instrument EGSE, the HPSDB, the CCS, the MOC and the HCSS each read the SCOS-2000 tables with their own rules, and each documented them: the naming convention, the Alcatel limits, the HPSDB constraints and the HCSS tailoring note.364764
  • The ICD needed interpreting. The HCSS questions of 2002 produced ESOC change requests on separators, PLF offsets and bit numbering, and exposed the SPID limitation of the verifier.7778 The history of the import ICD follows how such points entered later issues.
  • Mission-level conventions are local. Leading characters, identifier lengths and description character sets were set by one programme for its own smooth transition. A modern MIB such as Solar Orbiter's follows different conventions (see mission tailoring of the MIB).123
  • Configuration control was explicit. The one delivery documented in the library travelled as a zip with a release note listing its inputs, change records, open non-conformances and an MD5 checksum, and test results flowed back as update files naming each validated command and parameter.151148135
  • The model outlived the missions. In 2015 the prime presented the HPSDB, adapted as a System Reference Data Base for a later programme, as a validated concept and planned to map it onto the EGS-CC data model.158159160

docs.title: Herschel/Planck interface documents: packets, ground links and the CCS
docs.text:
Herschel and Planck shared one prime contractor, one set of packet rules for both spacecraft and their instruments, and one mission operations centre at ESOC.1213 This page reads the set of Herschel/Planck interface control documents that the library now holds, from the on-board packet layer to the operator's workstation at ESOC. The central document is the Packet Structure Interface Control Document (PS-ICD, SCI-PT-ICD-07527), which fixes every telemetry and telecommand packet, service, application process identifier and parameter type of both spacecraft, and also the MIL-STD-1553B data bus protocol between the central computer and the instruments.1276 Around it sit the Space/Ground ICD for the radio link and the transfer frames, the documents of the test systems (the instrument teams' EGSE router, the PIPE protocol, the Central Checkout System and the Herschel/Planck System Database), the HIFI instrument's telecommand and database documents, and the ground segment interface documents that carried telemetry and command history to the science centres.91144209

The programme-level story (the decision of 2000 to build on SCOS-2000, the HPSDB naming convention, the HCSS tailoring of the MIB) is told on Herschel/Planck: SCOS-2000 in a science mission ground segment, and the missions themselves on Herschel and Planck. This page goes one level down, into the bits, bytes and message flows. Where the documents disagree with each other, the page says so; a summary of the discrepancies is at the end.

At a glance

  • Packets: TC packets of at most 248 octets (228 when stored in the mission timeline), TM packets of at most 1024 octets, PUS version number 0, a 3-bit command source field inside the TC sequence count, and a 16-bit CRC on every packet.1719
  • APIDs: one base APID per user; its four least significant bits separate essential housekeeping, routine housekeeping and science, and prime from redundant units.67
  • Link: X-band up and down, 1115-octet transfer frames, Reed-Solomon (255,223) with interleave 5 plus convolutional coding, six virtual channels in use, COP-1 with AD and BD.10495100
  • Bus: a 1 s frame of 64 subframes of 24 message slots; TM packets are pulled by the bus controller with a request/confirmation handshake.83
  • Test systems: a TCP router keyed on APID for instrument tests, the PIPE protocol (10-byte header, sync word 0xFADE) between the CCS and every SCOE, and MIB extensions (cur, grp, lgf, delta limits) that later entered the standard SCOS-2000 import ICD.137148177247

docs.title: Status and history
docs.text:
The PS-ICD complements the ESA Packet Telemetry and Packet Telecommand standards (PSS-04-106 and PSS-04-107) with "all the mission specific details" of the data transfer between ground and on-board applications. Being tailored for Herschel/Planck, it states that it supersedes the Packet Utilisation Standard ECSS-E-70-41A, which it lists only as a reference document. Requirement 1000-GEN makes it exhaustive: the space and ground segment shall support all and only the structures and services it defines.12 The document is agreed by the ESA project manager, the ESOC representative and the prime contractor, and then controlled by the prime contractor.12 Requirements carry identifiers (for example 3000-TC, 5050-TCV) and point to their parent requirement in the Operations Interface Requirements Document (OIRD, SCI-PT-RS-07360) with tags such as [P:SCI-PT-RS-07360#3.1-PACK-14.12

docs.title: Operations scenario
docs.text: The PS-ICD's scenario explains why its services look the way they do. Most telecommands are stored on board and released at a defined time by the on-board scheduling service, from a Mission Timeline (MTL): a linear sequence of time-tagged commands, loaded during each daily communication period, that controls the satellites for up to 48 hours. Function management and on-board control procedures (OBCPs) handle longer activities, and OBCPs "shall be kept simple".1315 Every telecommand is verified by a TC verification report at acceptance (1010-GEN); progress and completion may be reported by verification packets or by housekeeping.13 The Command and Data Management System (CDMS) routes all packets and is the controller of the on-board serial data bus.14

docs.title: Telecommand packet
docs.text:
All telecommand packets follow PSS-04-107 with the following mission rules (3000-TC, 3010-TC):17

The packet ends with a 16-bit Packet Error Control field (see the CRC).17

Field Bits Values Meaning Version 3 0b000 Required for all commands Type 1 1 Telecommand Data field header flag 1 1 Only TC(2,3), the Standard Distribute CPDU command, has no data field header, so its type and subtype are not in the packet APID 11 Appendix 3 Application or unit addressed Sequence flags 2 0b11 All telecommands are stand-alone packets Source part 3 see below Generator of the command Sequence part 11 0 to 2047 Incremented by the source for each command to that APID; wraps to 0; never checked for monotony by the receiver Packet length 16 odd, ≤ 241 Data field length minus one; the data field is a whole number of 16-bit words CCSDS secondary header flag 1 0 "Non-CCSDS defined" secondary header PUS version 3 0 Only version 0 allowed Ack 4 bit 3 to bit 0 Requests for success reports; failure reports are always generated Type, subtype 8 + 8 Appendix 2 Unique across all application processes Spare 8 0 Pads the header to two words

The 3-bit source part is the mission's way to trace who released a command, which matters because one instrument can receive commands from ground, the timeline, OBCPs and FDIR:17

Source Meaning 000 Ground, highest priority, all sources 001 FDIR telecommands of the CDMU 010 Mission Time Line (maintained by ground, executed by the CDMU) 011 On-board control procedures (executed by the CDMU) 100 Ground, low priority, all sources 101 FDIR telecommands of the ACC 110 CDMU, other on-board sources 111 ACMS, other on-board sources

When an acknowledgement is requested, the verification report must copy the full sequence control word as the identifier of the command.17 The Ack bits use the CCSDS numbering, so the acceptance request is the last bit of the field (---1). Ground sets it nominally; when it is cleared, the application still performs the acceptance checks but does not send the TM(1,1) success report.18

Length limits. The packet data field holds at most 242 octets, so a TC packet is at most 248 octets. Because almost all commands are executed from the MTL, they are wrapped as a variable octet string inside TC(11,4), which leaves 228 octets for the embedded packet and 216 octets for its application data.1743 Commands stored as event/action actions are limited to 232 octets (220 of application data), and an OBCP load segment carries at most 232 octets of code.5755

docs.title: Telemetry packet
docs.text:
Telemetry packets follow PSS-04-106 (4000-TM, 4010-TM); for the version number the PS-ICD declares itself consistent with CCSDS 102.0-B-4 and superseding PSS-04-106:1920

Field Bits Values Meaning Grouping flags 2 0b11 No segmentation; only science packets TM(21,x) may mark groups: 01 first, 00 continuation, 10 last; neither the on-board system nor the ESA ground system supports groups, so users handle them Source sequence count 14 0 to 16383 One counter per APID, so the ground can detect missing packets Packet length 16 odd, ≤ 1017 Data field at most 1018 octets, packet at most 1024 octets Spare (first bit) 1 0 Symmetry with the TC header PUS version 3 0 Only version 0 allowed Time 48 CUC Local on-board time; its relation to data generation is fixed per type and subtype of each application Packet Error Control 16 CRC Present for the whole mission for all applications

Sources: §4.1.1920

PUS version 0

ECSS-E-70-41A (2003) tells its users to set the TC and TM PUS version number to 1.245 The PS-ICD keeps version 0, the value of the earlier ESA PUS, in both headers.1720 See PUS-A vs PUS-C and PUS packet structures.

docs.title: On-board verification of telemetry
docs.text: Some TM packets are consumed on board, for example by the event/action service, so the CDMU and the ACC check them before use. Requirement 4020-TM lists the checks with failure codes that match the TC acceptance codes: 2 for the packet error control, 1 for the length, 0 for an illegal APID, 3 for the type and 4 for the subtype; science packets of service 21 are exempt. A failed packet produces a type 5 event with the code and at least 4 octets of the faulty packet, its data are not used on board, and the packet goes to ground on its usual virtual channel, or on VC4 if its APID, type or subtype cannot be identified.21

docs.title: Conventions and field alignment
docs.text:
Bit 0 is the first transmitted bit and the most significant bit of an unsigned field; for a signed field, bit 0 is the sign.61 The alignment rules of Appendix 1 shape every layout on this page:61

  1. A parameter of 16 bits or more is word aligned (its LSB on a word boundary).
  2. A parameter shorter than 16 bits never crosses a word boundary.
  3. Short parameters are right-adjusted in their 16-bit word, with padding in the most significant bits.
  4. Several short parameters in one word are right-adjusted together.

A consequence appears in the housekeeping report: 8-bit parameters are grouped by pairs in a word, so an odd sequence of them gets a spare octet before its last member.31 Type and subtype numbers are written as two numbers, TC(1,1) or TM(1,2), and the numbering of types is chosen to pair TCs with their reports, so it is not contiguous.62

docs.title: Parameter types
docs.text:
Appendix 6 defines the only parameter types allowed in packets. The parameter code is a pair (PTC, PFC) of two 8-bit numbers (the 8-bit widths date from issue 3).724 Compare the PUS parameter types and MIB parameter types.

PTC Type PFC values and lengths Notes 1 Boolean PFC 0: 1 bit 0 false, 1 true 2 Enumerated PFC 1-8, 12, 16, 32: that many bits Discrete, unordered values such as error codes 3 Unsigned integer PFC 0-11: 4 to 15 bits; 12: 2 octets; 13: 3 octets; 14: 4 octets 4 Signed integer Same lengths as PTC 3 5 Real PFC 1: 32-bit IEEE 754 single; PFC 2: 64-bit IEEE double PFC 1 is also the internal format of the DSP21020; PFC 3 (MIL-STD-1750A) removed in issue 6.0 6 Bit string PFC 1, 2, 4, 8 bits 7 Octet string PFC 0 variable (with length), PFC > 0 fixed Cannot be edited by the operator; a TC or TM packet carried as a variable octet string uses its own packet length instead of a length field 8 Character string PFC 0 variable, PFC > 0 fixed On board only for the PROM software version identifier; SCOE/EGSE may use it freely 9 Absolute time PFC 17: 6 octets, 4 coarse + 2 fine CUC without P-field, synchronised to TAI 10 Relative time – Not used 11 Deduced PFC 0 Type taken from a preceding field; used for OBCP parameters in TM(18,13), which are 32 bits except 64 bits for double reals

Sources: Appendix 6 §A6-2 to A6-3.10.727311

A unit that cannot provide a time synchronised with the Central Time Reference (CTR) sets the most significant bit of its time field to 1; the rest of the field then has a user-specific meaning.73

docs.title: Packet error control
docs.text:
The 16-bit packet check sequence is a CRC with generator \(G(x) = x^{16} + x^{12} + x^5 + 1\) (CCITT V.41), encoder and decoder preset to all ones, computed over the whole packet except the last 16 bits. The same algorithm checks memory blocks in service 6. For blocks shorter than 32768 bits it detects all odd numbers of bit errors, all double errors and all single bursts of up to 16 bits.70 Appendix 4 gives test vectors (hexadecimal, real values from the source):71

Data Packet check sequence 00 00 1D 0F 00 00 00 CC 9C AB CD EF 01 04 A2 14 56 F8 9A 00 01 7F D5

Checked by this wiki

A bit-wise implementation of this CRC (polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) reproduces all four vectors. The check is this wiki's, run with Python on 2026-11-12; the worked example further down uses the same implementation.

docs.title: APID assignment
docs.text:
Appendix 3 gives every user a base APID in the most significant bits and uses the four least significant bits to tell packet categories and prime or redundant units apart, so part of the packet identification needs no decoding of the data field header. The project office manages the allocation, and one range is reserved for test equipment.67

APID (dec) Hex TC packets TM packets 0 0x000 Standard Distribute CPDU commands Standard spacecraft time packet 16 (BA) 0x010 All CDMS commands All CDMS TM except routine HK and diagnostic reports 18 (BA+2) 0x012 – CDMS routine (non-essential) HK and diagnostic reports 512 / 514 0x200 / 0x202 All ACMS commands (512) As for the CDMS 1024 / 1025 0x400 / 0x401 All HIFI commands (1024) HIFI prime / redundant, except routine HK, diagnostics and science 1026 / 1027 0x402 / 0x403 – HIFI prime / redundant routine HK and diagnostics 1028-1031 0x404-0x407 – HIFI science TM(21,x), prime and redundant 1152-1155 0x480-0x483 All PACS commands (1152) As for HIFI (prime, redundant, HK, HK) 1158 / 1159 0x486 / 0x487 – PACS diagnostic science TM(21,3), prime / redundant 1160, 1162 / 1161, 1163 0x488, 0x48A / 0x489, 0x48B – PACS science, prime / redundant 1280-1283 0x500-0x503 All SPIRE commands (1280) As for HIFI 1284, 1286, 1288 / 1285, 1287, 1289 0x504... / 0x505... – SPIRE science, prime / redundant 1408-1411 0x580-0x583 All HFI commands (1408) As for HIFI 1412, 1414 / 1413, 1415 0x584, 0x586 / 0x585, 0x587 – HFI science, prime / redundant 1536 / 1538 / 1540 0x600 / 0x602 / 0x604 All LFI commands (1536) LFI (prime and redundant share APIDs): other TM / routine HK / science 1664-1667 0x680-0x683 All SCS commands (1664) Sorption cooler prime, redundant, HK, HK 2016-2046 0x7E0-0x7FE SCOE / EGSE reserved SCOE / EGSE reserved 2047 0x7FF – Idle packets

Source: Table A-3.1.68

Table A-3.2 then maps each TM packet type to an APID offset and a real-time virtual channel: time packets on VC0 from APID 0; all service reports, events and the essential housekeeping report TM(3,25) on the base APID and VC0 (base + 1 for a redundant instrument); the routine TM(3,25) and the diagnostic report TM(3,26) on base + 2 and VC4 (base + 3 when redundant); science TM(21,1) to TM(21,4) on the APIDs of Table A-3.1 and VC1. Stored packets are dumped on the VC of their packet store, with VC3 recommended for science stores and VC2 for the others; idle and time packets are never stored.69 Issue 3 introduced the rule that essential housekeeping gets "Base-APID + 0" and the highest priority.4

Cross-check in other documents (real values)

The HIFI telecommand ICD states that the HIFI on-board software can only have APID 1024.201 The HPMCS template client filters on APID 0x604, commented as "LFI scientific packets", which is the LFI science APID of Table A-3.1.239 The 2008 HPSDB release note lists a calibration curve that maps the APIDs 16, 512, 1024/1025, 1152/1153 and 1280/1281 to CDMS, ACMS and the nominal and redundant sides of HIFI, PACS and SPIRE.198

docs.title: Time packet and idle packet
docs.text:
The Standard Spacecraft Time Source Packet carries spacecraft elapsed time to ground for correlation with UTC. It has no data field header, APID 0 and an 8-octet data field (packet length field 7). Its time refers to the leading edge of the first bit of the attached sync marker of the VC0 transfer frame whose VC frame count is 0 modulo 64. Its sequence count wraps from \(2^{14}-1\) to 0 and must never "short-cycle".74

The P-field value 0b00101110 reads, in the CCSDS rules, as no extension, time code identification 010 (agency-defined epoch, level 2), \(3 + 1 = 4\) octets of seconds and 2 octets of fraction.74246 The same P-field byte reappears in the time broadcast on the on-board bus (see below), and the EGSE interface specification gives the EGSE CUC time a TAI epoch of 1958 January 1.85150 See Time code formats and Time correlation in SCOS-2000.

The idle packet fills a frame when not enough source packets are available: APID 0x7FF, no data field header, sequence flags 11, sequence count fixed at 0x0000, free length and a pseudo-random data field.75

docs.title: The services
docs.text:
Table 2-1 lists the services and where they are implemented. No other services are foreseen for the missions, and each unit implements only an agreed subset, recorded in its user manual and in Table A-2.1.16

Service Name in the PS-ICD CDMS ACMS Instruments Page 1 Telecommand Verification Yes Yes Yes ST[01] 2 Device Command Distribution Yes Yes No ST[02] 3 Housekeeping and Diagnostic Data Reporting Yes Yes Yes ST[03] 5 Event Reporting Yes Yes Yes ST[05] 6 Memory Management Yes Yes Yes ST[06] 8 Function Management Yes Yes Optional ST[08] 9 Time Management Yes Yes Yes ST[09] 11 On-board Operations Scheduling Yes No No ST[11] 12 On-board Monitoring Yes Optional Optional ST[12] 14 Packet Transmission Control Yes Yes Yes ST[14] 15 On-board Storage and Retrieval Yes No No ST[15] 16 On-board Traffic Management Yes No No – 17 Test Yes Yes Yes ST[17] 18 On-board Control Procedure Yes No Optional ST[18] 19 Event/Action Yes Optional No ST[19] 21 Science Data Transfer No No Yes – 4, 7, 10, 13, 20, 22 Not used – – – –

Services 20 (information distribution) and 22 (context saving) are kept as headings marked "not used": the requirements of service 20 are all deleted, and context saving was deleted as a service in issue 3.16594 The rest of this section lists, service by service, the rules that are specific to Herschel/Planck.

docs.title: Service 1: telecommand verification
docs.text:
• The report carries the APID of the application that generates it (5020-TCV).22
  • An acceptance success report TM(1,1) is sent within 2 seconds of reception (5050-TCV).22
  • TM(1,1), TM(1,3) and TM(1,7) carry the TC packet ID (2 octets) and sequence control (2 octets); TM(1,5) adds a 2-octet step number; TM(1,2) and TM(1,8) add a 2-octet failure code and optional parameters.2324
  • Standard acceptance failure codes: 0 illegal APID, 1 incomplete or invalid length, 2 incorrect checksum, 3 illegal type, 4 illegal subtype, 5 illegal or inconsistent application data; 16 to 65535 are application-specific and need ESA and prime approval. The parameter field is a whole number of words, at least 4 octets; for a header error the complete header, for a CRC error the complete CRC is reported.24
  • TM(1,9) Telecommand Contents Report is mandatory for the CDMU and ACC: every command released by an on-board source (timeline, OBCP, FDIR) is copied into a TM(1,9) and stored in the solid state mass memory, because the ground cannot otherwise know what was executed.2225

docs.title: Service 2: device commands
docs.text: TC(2,1) carries 1 to 8 pulse command addresses, TC(2,2) 1 to 8 register address/data pairs.26 The CPDU command TC(2,3) carries pairs of an 8-bit output line identifier and an octet with 5 spare bits and a 3-bit duration \(D\); the pulse lasts \(13\ \text{ms} \times 2^{D}\), from 13 ms (\(D=0\)) to 1664 ms (\(D=7\)). The "Standard" version, without data field header, is executed directly by the TC decoder with 1 to 120 pulse instructions; the "Mission specific" version goes through the on-board software and carries 1 to 8.27

docs.title: Service 3: housekeeping and diagnostics
docs.text:
Each unit sends one nominal HK packet at a default period, plus essential HK packets on the base APID sized for the worst link conditions.28 All periods are powers of two of the unit's basic sampling period: the packet period is \(2^{n}\) times it (\(n \ge 0\)), and a super-commutated parameter appears \(2^{k}\) times consecutively at the end of the report and is sampled correspondingly faster, which gives it a reporting period shorter than the basic sampling period.28 A Structure Identifier (SID) implicitly defines all sampling and structure of a packet.28

TC(3,1) and TC(3,2) define a report with an HK packet ID (16 bits), SID (16), sampling interval (16), segment ID (8), N (8) and N parameter IDs (16 bits each). Long definitions are split into segments 1 to K (at most 254) and closed by a segment 0xFF with N = 0; a single-packet definition uses segment 0. One TC carries at most 114 parameter IDs. For the CDMS and ACMS a dedicated USD-ID turns a "parameter" into a RAM area (start address MSB, LSB, length), at most 28 per TC.2930 Redefinition requires the old entry to be cleared, keeps the APID and real-time VC implied by the HK packet ID, and disables the packet meanwhile; TC(3,3) and TC(3,4) clear definitions and disable generation as TC(14,2) would; TC(3,9) and TC(3,11) ask for TM(3,10) and TM(3,12).2830 The reports TM(3,25) and TM(3,26) contain a 16-bit SID, the parameters and an optional spare octet for word alignment.31

docs.title: Service 5: event reporting
docs.text:
Three subtypes route events by severity: TM(5,1) for information and warnings, TM(5,2) exception reports when an on-board recovery procedure exists (the CDMS may modify the MTL or start an OBCP), and TM(5,4) error/alarm reports when only ground can intervene.32

An optional variable Parameters B field follows. The design goal is that the event ID alone determines the layout.33 Routine, especially cyclic, software functions shall not need TC verification reports, and events that only show normal software progress need ESA and prime approval.32

docs.title: Service 6: memory management
docs.text: The service is a last resort, used only when a memory location cannot be reached by nominal means. Addresses count in Smallest Addressable Units (SAU) of 8, 16, 32 or 48 bits, defined per unit; the memory ID and start address together give the absolute address, and their combination may extend the 16-bit address for the CDMS and ACMS.34 TC(6,2) loads (memory ID 16, start address 16, spare 8, N 8, data, optional pad octet, CRC 16 over the unpadded data), with at most 228 octets of data; the unit writes, reads back and compares before reporting TM(1,7) or TM(1,8). TC(6,5) and TC(6,9) dump and check (memory ID, start, N), TC(6,11) aborts a dump, and TM(6,6) and TM(6,10) return data (at most 1016 octets per packet) or a CRC; a star-tracker dump has its own data layout.3536

docs.title: Service 8: function management
docs.text: TC(8,1) starts a function (FID 8 bits, spare 8, SID 16, parameters), TC(8,2) stops it, TC(8,4) performs an activity (FID, activity ID, SID, parameters), TC(8,5) asks for the TM(8,6) status report.37 Starting an active function or stopping a stopped one is rejected with TM(1,2), and an activity on a stopped function is rejected too. The split between TC(8,1) and TC(8,4) supports an "Arm-Fire" pattern, and critical functions should terminate by themselves.3738 The design goal again is one fixed parameter set per FID and activity, so the SID can be "don't care".38 Table A-2.1 also lists TM(8,7) SREM data, TM(8,8) VMC data and TM(8,9) mass memory dump reports, each for a single user.64

docs.title: Service 9: time management
docs.text:
The CDMS holds the Central Time Reference (CTR). It synchronises a user by sending it TC(9,4) Enable Time Synchronisation and TC(9,5) Time Code (48 bits); the user sets its clock at the next synchronisation signal on the bus. Ground triggers the procedure with TC(9,3) Synchronise User (5 spare bits and the user's 11-bit APID). It verifies a user with TC(9,6), on which the CDMS sends TC(9,7) to the user; at the next sync signal the CDMS reports TM(9,8) (the CTR) and the user TM(9,9) (its own clock). Ground resets the CTR itself with TC(9,10), which carries the old time at which to switch and the new time.3940 Neither the clocks nor the time-tagging may ever stop (5490-OBTM).39

sequenceDiagram
    participant G as Ground
    participant C as CDMS (CTR)
    participant U as User application
    G->>C: TC(9,3) Synchronise User (APID)
    C->>U: TC(9,4) Enable Time Synchronisation
    C->>U: TC(9,5) Time Code (48-bit CUC)
    C-->>U: next sync signal on the bus
    Note over U: local clock set to the Time Code value
    G->>C: TC(9,6) Verify User Time (APID)
    C->>U: TC(9,7) Enable Time Verification
    C-->>U: next sync signal
    C->>G: TM(9,8) Central Time Reference
    U->>G: TM(9,9) Time Verification Report

The diagram follows §5.9. Table A-2.1 sets the procedure per user: TC(9,4) alone for the ACMS and HFI, TC(9,4) and TC(9,5) for LFI and the sorption cooler (SCS), and neither for HIFI, PACS and SPIRE, for which §5.9.1.1 says that TC(9,3) is rejected. All except the CDMS answer TC(9,7) with TM(9,9).394064

docs.title: Service 11: the mission timeline
docs.text:
The MTL supports subschedules: groups of commands for one activity (an attitude manoeuvre, an instrument observation) that can be enabled, disabled or deleted without touching the rest. Subschedule ID 0 addresses the whole timeline in every service 11 command except TC(11,4), so real subschedules use 1 to 4095; IDs up to a compile-time PermSubSchMaxId are permanent, higher ones transient. An error on one release does not stop the timeline.41

  • TC(11,1) and TC(11,2) enable or disable release by N subschedule IDs and M APIDs; N = 0 means "not by subschedule", N = 1 with ID 0 means all subschedules. Each change is reported with a TM(5,1).4211
  • TC(11,3) resets the schedule.42
  • TC(11,4) inserts one command: a 48-bit absolute time tag, a 16-bit subschedule ID and the TC packet as a variable octet string, whose source field must be 010.43
  • TC(11,5) deletes a sequence identified by subschedule, APID, time tag and sequence control, plus a count; TC(11,6) deletes between two time tags.44
  • TC(11,9)/(11,11) give the detailed report TM(11,10), TC(11,12)/(11,14) the summary TM(11,13), and TC(11,18) the status report TM(11,19).65

The OBCP note shows the subschedules in use: its datapool list gives every instrument a command subschedule, and SPIRE, LFI and the sorption cooler electronics also a "meta" subschedule (SPIRE defaults 370 and 100). A SPIRE recovery OBCP disables both SPIRE subschedules with TC(11,2) (N = 2, M = 0).128130

docs.title: Service 12: on-board monitoring
docs.text: The CDMS keeps a monitoring list of check definitions per parameter, and reports every checking status transition, both out of and back into range. The default number of consecutive samples for a transition is 3, and the basic monitoring period is a negative power of two of the basic sampling period.45 TC(12,5) adds or modifies entries with, for each one: parameter ID, monitoring ID, monitoring status, monitoring interval (1 to 65535), repetition number, a 16-bit check value, a 16-bit mask, a check type and two event IDs.46 The parameter is right-aligned and ANDed with the mask before comparison. The check types are bit values: 1 equal, 2 greater, 4 less, 8 not equal, 16 greater or equal, 32 less or equal, each with an expected result of FALSE. A transition to OUT_OF_RANGE generates TM(5,2) with Event-ID-1, the return generates TM(5,1) with Event-ID-2, and monitoring event IDs are above 32767.4748 Compare the ground-side monitoring checks in the MIB.

docs.title: Services 14 to 17
docs.text:
• Service 14 enables and disables TM packets by type, subtype and packet ID (TC(14,1)/(14,2), report TM(14,4)). It is for contingencies only, since packets start and stop with their modes; the CDMS also uses it to choose real-time downlink or mass-memory storage (TC(14,5), TC(14,6), TM(14,7)), also autonomously when a mode change reduces the bandwidth.50
  • Service 15 controls packet stores in the solid state mass memory (SSMM): enable or disable storage, edit the storage selection by APID, type and subtype, dump by packet or by time, delete up to a time, and report catalogues with pointers and coarse times. Stores and their virtual channels are allocated with a CDMS service 8 function.515269
  • Service 16 has no packets; the CDMS reports routing anomalies with events.53
  • Service 17: TC(17,1) without data, answered by TM(1,1) and the empty TM(17,2).53

docs.title: Service 18: on-board control procedures
docs.text: OBCPs run in the CDMS, the ACC and possibly instrument computers; each has a procedure ID from 1 to 65535 (0 in TC(18,4) stops all). TC(18,1) loads code in segments (ID, segment 1 to 254 then 0xFF, N ≤ 232, code); the loaded procedure is "stopped". Further commands delete, start, stop, suspend, resume, pass parameters, list, report status (TM(18,13), with procedure status 0 stopped, 1 running, 2 suspended) and dump (TC(18,14), TM(18,15)). Commands released by an OBCP get a fresh sequence count and CRC at release, and TM(1,9) reports these final values.545556 See ECSS-E-ST-70-01C on-board control procedures.

docs.title: Service 19: event/action
docs.text: The CDMS (optionally the ACMS) holds a detection list of {APID, event ID, action TC, enabled}. When a TM(5,1), (5,2) or (5,4) matches an enabled entry, the stored TC is sent. TC(19,1) adds an entry with its action disabled; replacing an entry needs its action to be disabled first. TC(19,4) and TC(19,5) enable and disable actions, TC(19,6) asks for TM(19,7) with one TC per packet. Editing the list is classified as hazardous.5758

docs.title: Service 21: science data
docs.text: TM(21,1) nominal science, (21,2) science type B, (21,3) diagnostic science and (21,4) auxiliary science share one layout: a 16-bit SID and the parameters, whose structure follows from APID, subtype and SID in the instrument user manual. Several subtypes avoid giving an instrument too many APIDs.60

docs.title: Who implements what
docs.text:
Table A-2.1 crosses every TC and TM with its users (CDMS, ACMS, HIFI, PACS, SPIRE, HFI, LFI, SCS). All eight implement TM(1,1), (1,2), (1,7), (1,8), the essential and routine TM(3,25), the three event reports, memory load, dump and check, TC(14,1) to TC(14,3) with TM(14,4), and the connection test.636466 The other columns read as follows:63646566

  • CDMS only: the Standard Distribute CPDU command, TM(8,7) to TM(8,9), TC(9,3), TC(9,6), TC(9,10) and TM(9,8), TC(14,5), TC(14,6) and TM(14,7), all of services 11, 12, 15 and 19, and the OBCP dump TC(18,14) and TM(18,15).
  • CDMS and ACMS: TM(1,9), service 2 (except the Standard CPDU command), the definition and report packets TC(3,1) to TM(3,12), and TC(6,11).
  • Execution reports: TM(1,3) by the CDMS, ACMS, PACS and SPIRE; TM(1,5) by the CDMS, ACMS and SPIRE.
  • Function management: TC(8,4) by all except the SCS; TC(8,1) and TC(8,2) by the CDMS, ACMS, HIFI, SPIRE, LFI and SCS; TC(8,5) by the CDMS, ACMS, SPIRE and LFI; TM(8,6) by the CDMS, ACMS, HIFI, SPIRE and LFI.
  • OBCPs: the CDMS and PACS implement TC(18,1) to TM(18,13).
  • Science: TM(21,1) and TM(21,3) by HIFI, PACS, SPIRE, HFI and LFI; TM(21,2) by PACS, SPIRE, HFI and LFI; TM(21,4) by SPIRE and HFI.

The column assignment was read on the PDF pages, since the text extraction of Table A-2.1 loses the column positions.

docs.title: The satellite data bus (Appendix 9)
docs.text:
Appendix 9 is a self-contained specification of the physical, data link and transfer layers of the MIL-STD-1553B bus between the CDMS and its remote terminals (RTs), with its own numbering.76 Transformer-coupled stubs and a 75 Ω TSP cable are used; the CDMS, a redundant unit, is the bus controller (BC); RT-to-RT transfers are not foreseen; broadcast is allowed; message repetition on error is allowed.7778

Timing. The Satellite Data Bus Protocol is cyclic and synchronised with the central on-board time: a 1-second frame of 64 subframes, each of 24 message slots. Subframes 1, 17, 33 and 49 are reserved for telecommands (33 also carries the time), the other 60 for telemetry; a TM packet must fit in one subframe. Slot 1 (150 µs) carries the synchronisation mode command (without data word in subframe 1, with data word elsewhere), slots 2 to 4 command and acquisition, slots 5 to 20 (750 µs each) data transfer, 21 to 23 packet control such as polling, and slot 24 is a regulation slot.8384 The performance requirements are: at least 350 kbps of packet throughput for all users, 50 TM and 12 TC packets per second, one time synchronisation per second, timing accuracy better than 100 µs and every user served at least twice a second.82 The BC switches between predefined bus profiles on ground command without interrupting service.84

Subaddress Transmit (RT to BC) Receive (BC to RT) 0, 31 Mode commands Mode commands 1 Unit status data Unit control (low-level commands) 8 Internal time Time messages (broadcast) 10 TM packet transfer request TM packet transfer confirmation 11 to 26 TM data (11 carries the most significant bytes) 11 to 14: TC data 27 TC packet transfer confirmation TC packet transfer descriptor 28 Low-level command status Low-level command 30 Data wrap read (test, mandatory) Data wrap write (test, mandatory)

Source: Table 3.2.3-1, abridged (SA 2 to 7, 9, 15 to 26 receive and 29 are generic data or unused).79

Inference

Sixteen transmit subaddresses (11 to 26) of 32 16-bit words each hold \(16 \times 64 = 1024\) octets, exactly the maximum TM packet, and four receive subaddresses (11 to 14) hold 256 octets, enough for a 248-octet TC packet. The PS-ICD does not state this reasoning; it is this wiki's arithmetic from the subaddress table and the packet limits.7982

Telecommand delivery. In one subframe the BC writes the packet from SA 11R onwards and then a two-word Packet Transfer Descriptor to SA 27R; at the next sync the RT checks the reserved bits and the 8-bit packet count, stores a new packet, and copies the descriptor to SA 27T as its confirmation, which the BC reads no earlier than three subframes later.86

Telemetry retrieval. The RT announces a packet in its two-word TM Packet Transfer Request at SA 10T; the BC polls it at least one subframe ahead, reads the packet from SA 11T to 26T and returns a TM Packet Transfer Confirmation to SA 10R in the same subframe, with the flow control set to 11. A transmission error discards the packet and leads to one retry. In burst mode one RT sends fixed 1024-octet science packets in consecutive subframes, without retry.878889

Time distribution. In subframe 33 the BC broadcasts (RT address 31, SA 8, 4 data words) the time valid at the start of the next frame: a reserved octet, the P-field 0b00101110, 4 octets of coarse and 2 of fine time; RTs copy it to SA 8T at the next frame sync.85

Bus FDIR. The BC collects the message error, busy, subsystem and terminal flags of RT status words, transmission errors, no-response time-outs and loop-back failures. Bus medium A is the default; on a no-response, transmission or loop-back error the BC tests medium B with dedicated messages and switches all traffic to B only if B works; it never switches back automatically. Ground commands select the medium and enable or disable the automatic reconfiguration.8081

flowchart TD
  A["1 s frame on medium A:<br/>update error flags"] --> B{"MIL-bus error?<br/>(no response, transmission,<br/>loop-back)"}
  B -- no --> A
  B -- yes --> C["Test command on medium B"]
  C -- "not OK" --> S["Stay on medium A<br/>(a switch would not help)"]
  C -- OK --> D["Test command on medium A"]
  D -- "OK (error gone)" --> S
  D -- "not OK" --> E["Switch all traffic to medium B<br/>(no automatic return)"]

The flowchart redraws Figure 3.5.2.4-1.81 The OBCP note names three levels of this FDIR (DLL, TFL TC and TFL TM) whose events start instrument OBCPs (see below).121

docs.title: The Space/Ground ICD
docs.text: The SGICD defines the interface between the spacecraft and the ground stations and is the source for all link budget data. It is controlled by the ESA project manager.91

docs.title: Radio frequency and modulation
docs.text:
Item Herschel Planck Downlink frequency (X-band, 8450-8500 MHz) 8468.5 MHz 8455.0 MHz Uplink frequency (X-band, 7190-7235 MHz) 7207.8483 MHz 7196.3580 MHz Uplink/downlink frequency ratio 749/880 749/880 Spacecraft ID (TM and TC) 0x1E6 (486) 0x1E9 (489)

The avionics model has spacecraft ID 0x1EA (490).92106 Both links are right-hand circular.92 The telemetry modes are:9394

Mode Information rate Modulation Subcarrier Transmitted symbol rate Low-1 500 bps (500.0065) PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM 45 884 Hz sine 1147.1 sps Low-2 5 kbps (5000.0645) PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM 45 884 Hz sine 11 471 sps Medium 150 kbps (150 001.95) PCM(SP-L)/PM – 344 130 sps High 1.5 Mbps (1 500 019.35) GMSK, BT = 0.25 – 3 441 300 sps

Telecommands use PCM(NRZ-L)/PSK/PM on a 16 kHz sine subcarrier at 125 bps or 4 kbps; the ranging tone is 698 260 Hz.97 Ranging cannot run together with high-rate telemetry; during high-rate passes only Doppler tracking is used.93 The concatenated code is Reed-Solomon (255,223) with interleave depth 5 and a rate ½, constraint length 7 convolutional code; the sync marker 0x1ACFFC1D starts each code block, and a pseudo randomiser is used.9596 After XMM's in-orbit TC rejections, the document adds a requirement on the selection of the active decoder input (probability of rejection below \(10^{-3}\)) and on commands with a transition density of only 3 %.99 The uplink sweep covers ±130 kHz at 500 Hz/s.98 COP-1 is supported with the AD and BD services in parallel.100 See Radio frequency, modulation and ranging, TM synchronization and channel coding and COP-1.

Checked by this wiki

The odd information rates follow from the code. An RS codeblock of interleave 5 holds \(5 \times 223 = 1115\) data octets (the frame length below) in \(5 \times 255 = 1275\) octets, plus the 4-octet sync marker: \(573.55 \times 1115 / 1279 = 500.0065\) bps, and the subcarrier is 40 times the Low-1 symbol rate (\(45\,884 / 1147.1 = 40\)). This is this wiki's arithmetic on the values of §2.1.5.94

docs.text:
Station Location Uplink EIRP (nominal) G/T at 10° Phases Kourou 15 m 5.25° N, 52.80° W 81 dBW (300 W) 38.0 dB/K LEOP, transfer to L2, commissioning Vilspa 15 m 40° 26′ 48″ N, 3° 57′ 05″ W 81 dBW (300 W) 35.7 dB/K LEOP New Norcia 35 m 30.97° S, 116.21° E 97 dBW (2 kW), 107 dBW (20 kW for emergencies) 50.1 dB/K All phases including routine science

Sources: §4.2 and §4.3.2.101102 All three use IFMS receivers and the TMTCS, a TCDS decoder and a 5 µs UTC synchronisation. Link budgets need a nominal margin above 3 dB and worst-case RSS and mean minus 3σ margins above 0 dB; 2.7 dB Eb/N0 gives a frame loss probability of \(10^{-5}\).101102 New Norcia passes start at medium rate, range for some minutes, switch to high rate and end the same way in reverse.103

docs.title: Telemetry transfer frame
docs.text:
Frames follow PSS-04-106 with a single length of 1115 octets (8920 bits): a 6-octet primary header, a 4-octet secondary header, 1099 octets of data, a 4-octet operational control field and a 2-octet frame error control field.104105

VC Content Downlink priority 0 Real-time essential spacecraft HK and critical instrument HK 1 (also when a time packet is due) 4 Real-time routine spacecraft and instrument HK 2 2 Stored spacecraft and instrument HK 3 1 Real-time science 4 3 Stored science 5 7 Idle frames 6, only when nothing else is ready 5, 6 Not required –

Sources: HP-SGICD-STR-TM-030 to -050.107 Any combination of VCs can be sent at any rate, partial frames are completed with idle packets before VC7 starts, and both frame counters must not be reset before 255 unless unavoidable (and then documented).107108 This is the ground-side picture of the APID categories of the PS-ICD: essential HK on the base APID goes to VC0, routine HK on base + 2 to VC4.69

Every frame carries a CLCW in the operational control field:109

The CLCW insertion scheme 2 of PSS-04-107 is used: the nominal decoder's CLCW goes in frames with even master channel frame count, the redundant decoder's in odd ones.109

docs.title: Telecommand segment and frame
docs.text:
Telecommand packets (except the CPDU commands) go into segments of PSS-04-107 with a 1-octet header: sequence flags 11 (no segmentation) and a 6-bit MAP identifier. Several complete packets may be aggregated in one segment; the next packet starts at the previous start plus its packet length field plus 7.110111

MAP ID Destination 0 The CPDU connected to the current decoder 1 The active processor 2 The non-active processor 5 CROME reinitialise 6 Set TC-only mode in the reconfiguration module of the current decoder

Source: HP-SGICD-STR-TC-025.111

The two VC IDs address the two on-board decoders and must match the CLCWs. Because frames are at most 256 octets, the two upper bits of the 10-bit length are always 00.112113 A 256-octet frame leaves 249 octets after the 5-octet header and 2-octet error control: one segment header plus one 248-octet packet. This is this wiki's arithmetic on the values of §6.2 and §6.3.11317 See TC Space Data Link Protocol and Space link identifiers.

docs.title: Payload management and OBCPs
docs.text:
Technical note H-P-1-ASP-TN-1072 specifies the OBCPs that the CDMS software runs for the instruments, and the Event/Action Table (EAT) entries that link instrument events to them. OBCPs that ground may need for nominal operations are outside its scope.119

Each EAT entry has three configuration fields beyond the service 19 content:120

Field Value for instrument internal FDIR Value for spacecraft 1553 bus FDIR Action Handling ID 01b: disabled in Autonomous Fail Safe (AFS), enabled in Autonomous Fail Operational (AFO) 11b: enabled in AFS and AFO Parameter Passing Status 1 when Parameters A of the event is passed to the started TC, usually 0 Same Action Status 1, enabled by default Same

Because a redundant instrument side reports on its own APID, each failure case needs two EAT entries.120 The spacecraft-level FDIR that affects instruments covers the 1553 bus (events from the CDMU basic software; the OBCP to start is defined in the EAT and is therefore configurable in the HPSDB and in flight), the science data monitoring and the class B heater loops.121 The bus TFL TM FDIR is configured by SDB_FDIR_TFL_TM_PERIOD_<Instrument>_VALUE = 90 s and SDB_FDIR_TFL_TM_MIN_<Instrument>_VALUE = 1, so it triggers when no more than one TM packet arrived from an instrument in 90 seconds; the alternative science data monitoring uses the service 12 monitoring table (MOT) and can be retuned in flight.121

docs.title: Spacecraft modes
docs.text:
There are five spacecraft modes. Transitions are commanded by ground (directly, by MTL or, unlikely, by OBCP) or taken autonomously on separation or after level 3 or 4 alarms of the CDMS or ACMS.122

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Launch
    Launch --> SAM: separation detected
    SAM --> NOM: TC
    SAM --> EAM: TC
    EAM --> NOM: TC
    NOM --> SAM: TC or ACMS level 3/4 (AIR)
    EAM --> SAM: TC or ACMS level 3/4 (AIR)
    NOM --> EAM: TC or CDMS level 3a/3b
    NOM --> SM: TC or CDMS level 4
    EAM --> SM: TC or CDMS level 4
    SM --> SAM: TC

The diagram is a reading of Table 3.1.2-1 of the note, which also lists re-entries into SAM and EAM after CDMS level 3a/3b alarms; abbreviations: SAM Sun Acquisition Mode, EAM Earth Acquisition Mode, NOM Nominal Mode, SM Survival Mode. The table marks a transition from SAM to SM as illegal, while the text speaks of transitions to SM "from any mode".122123124 Since the instruments need the same reaction to every transition into SAM or EAM, one "mother" OBCP per spacecraft is enough, DB_H_PL_SC_MODE_OBCP or DB_P_PL_SC_MODE_OBCP (ID 0x0001, time-out 30 s, to be confirmed). On Herschel it starts the SPIRE and HIFI standby OBCPs and the PACS safe OBCP with TC(18,3) and no parameters; on Planck it does nothing, because HFI, LFI and the sorption cooler electronics (SCE) ask for no action. A survival mode OBCP stays a placeholder, since autonomous survival mode switches the instruments off and stops the MTL.124125126

docs.title: An instrument OBCP in detail
docs.text:
SPIRE's internal FDIR raises four TM(5,2) events: 0xC000 (DRCU power or temperature anomaly), 0xC010 (DPU power anomaly, switch SPIRE off), 0xC100 (operations anomaly, disable SPIRE commands) and 0xC110 (resume at the next subschedule), on APID 0x0500 or 0x0501.127 The OBCP DB_OBCP_H_SPIRE_DRCU_OFF (ID 0x1102, time-out 600 s, to be confirmed) shows the pattern that the note applies everywhere:128129

  1. Stop any conflicting OBCP (here the resume OBCP 0x1107) with TC(18,4).
  2. Disable, with TC(19,5), the EAT entries of the triggering event and of the event that would undo the recovery (0xC000 and 0xC110 on both APIDs).
  3. Disable the SPIRE command and meta subschedules with TC(11,2).
  4. Switch off the nominal and redundant power lines with the PCDU function TC(8,4,112,3) (unit codes 0x0033 and 0x0034, LCL 51 and 52).
  5. Report a TM(5,4) with event ID 0x1000 "SPIRE DRCU Switched OFF".
  6. Re-enable the EAT entries that triggered it with TC(19,4).

OBCP parameters such as the subschedule IDs live in CDMS datapool words DID_OBCP_32_OFFSET_nnn; the same identifier carries different parameters on the two spacecraft, for example offset 000 is SPIRE_SUBS_ID_CMD on Herschel and HFI_SUBS_ID_CMD on Planck.130 The note leaves open which acknowledgements OBCP-generated commands should request, whether TM(1,9) is wanted for each, and suggests at most one TC per second per OBCP.131

docs.title: The CDMU front end during payload module tests
docs.text:
For the payload module tests the chain was instrument EGSE, CCS, PLM SCOE / CDMU DFE, warm units. Because the CDMU DFE does not simulate the CDMU completely, TN-0591 lists what it does.115

Service TC TM Comment 1 n/a Yes (1,1), (1,2) 6 No Like service 1 The CCS receives memory TM and routes it to the instrument EGSE 9 Yes (9,3), (9,4), (9,5) No TC(9,6), (9,7), (9,9) not supplied 17 Yes Yes 11, 18, 19 No No Covered by CCS TCL test sequences (time-tagged TCs come from a CCS sequence) 5, 20, 21 No No The CCS receives the TM (and, for 20 and 21, routes it to the instrument EGSE) Others No No Service 3 TCs may be sent for instrument packets, not for the DFE's own

Source: §3.1 and §3.2.116117 Every TM received by the DFE is wrapped in a PIPE message and sent to the CCS and to the instrument EGSEs on the CCS LAN.117

docs.title: The EGSE packet router (instrument level tests)
docs.text:
During instrument level tests (ILT) a SCOS-2000 system, the test equipment interface computers, the HCSS telemetry ingester and a CDMS simulator exchanged PS-ICD packets through a router, a software package that runs on any platform supporting Java. Every client opens one TCP connection; forwarding is based on the packet address, and the same interface later served the HCSS ingestion of raw telemetry.133134

Integers are most significant octet first; a message is 5 octets longer than its content.137 For a USER_DATA message, contentLength is the packet length field plus 7. The packet address is the APID for telemetry and \(4096 +\) APID for telecommands, which is the packet ID with version and header flag masked out. Address 8192 is reserved as a special value: it acts as a wild card in block entries and marks empty replies.138139140

Type Mnemonic Sent by Purpose 1 USER_DATA Client or router A PS-ICD packet 2 / 3 ADD_CLIENT / DEL_CLIENT Client Subscribe to / unsubscribe from a packet address 4 / 5 ASK_CLIENT / SHOW_CLIENT Client / router List subscriptions (with IP address and port for debugging) 6 NAME_CLIENT Client First message; unique client name 7 / 8 ADD_BLOCK / DEL_BLOCK Client Block a route (source name, destination name, address) 9 / 10 ASK_BLOCK / SHOW_BLOCK Client / router List blocks 11 / 12 ASK_TRAFFIC / SHOW_TRAFFIC Client / router Packet counts per address, source and destination

Source: Table 2.137 The router forwards a USER_DATA copy to every client that subscribed to the address unless an ADD_BLOCK matches; a block entry matches when each of source name, destination name and address equals the message or is empty (or 8192). List replies count down with messageSequenceNumber to 0.139140 There is no handshake, flow control or security: TCP provides integrity, and the network must be isolated. After any crash clients simply reconnect with the same name and repeat their requests; packets in transit are lost. The LAN should have 5 Mbit/s free (TBC), and each client is limited to 500 kbit/s averaged over a second (TBC). The router ICD cites the ground segment IRD in its issue 1 revision 3 of November 2000 and warns that its performance requirements FSG-IR-4.2-40 and -50 may not be met when platform and network lack free capacity; in IRD issue 2.6 the requirements with these numbers are the 5-second latency and the 700 kbps data rate of the ILT telemetry interface.135136141133219

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Client A (TM source)
    participant R as Router
    participant B as Client B (viewer)
    A->>R: NAME_CLIENT "A"
    loop regular intervals
        A->>R: USER_DATA (TM, APID 77)
    end
    B->>R: NAME_CLIENT "B"
    B->>R: ADD_CLIENT address 77
    R->>B: USER_DATA copies (TM, APID 77)
    B->>R: DEL_CLIENT address 77
    Note over R: forwarding to B stops

The sequence redraws the example of Appendix A.142

docs.title: PIPE: the CCS protocol for SCOEs and instrument stations
docs.text:
The EGSE Interface Requirement Specification defines how the Central Checkout System (CCS), the special check-out equipment (SCOEs), the TM/TC front end (DFE) and the instrument stations (IS) exchange data on 100 Mbit/s Ethernet with TCP/IP, on separate SCOE/DFE and IS LANs.144146 The PIPE protocol carries packets unchanged behind a header and adds remote commanding (RC) and remote monitoring (RM) of the test equipment itself, with acknowledgements, TC echo and a keep-alive.145 The CCS is the client and every SCOE, DFE or IS a server that accepts connections automatically, one socket per connection. The CCS expects a message at least every 60 seconds; an inconsistent length or synchronisation word in the header, or a message that cannot be read in 5 seconds, drops the connection with an alarm, while an unknown message ID or illegal VCID only raises an alarm.147

Bytes are big-endian. The body is a TM or TC source packet of at most 1024 or 248 bytes.148149

Message ID Kind (Type, subtype) Direction 0x80 TC: spacecraft telecommand – CCS → DFE 0x44 RC: SCOE remote command (8,4) CCS → SCOE/DFE/IS 0x20 TM: on-board telemetry, and its distribution – DFE → CCS, CCS → SCOE/DFE/IS 0x10 RM: SCOE periodic / asynchronous telemetry (3,25) / (5,1) SCOE/DFE/IS → CCS 0x11 RM: alive packet (0,0) SCOE/DFE/IS → CCS 0x50 / 0x51 ACKRC: RC acceptance success / failure (1,1) / (1,2) SCOE/DFE/IS → CCS 0x55 / 0x56 ACKTC: TC acceptance success / failure (1,1) / (1,2) DFE → CCS 0xA0 TC echo – DFE → CCS, CCS → IS 0x57 TC report: success / transmission failure (5,1) / (5,4) DFE → CCS

Source: Table 11.153 RM packets are TM source packets in PS-ICD format whose APID identifies the SCOE, with a CUC time and an unused error control field; RC packets are TC(8,4) packets with Ack 0001, a function ID, activity ID, SID and parameters, and an error control field forced to 0 and not used.150151

Telecommand flow. The CCS sends one TC (0x80) and waits up to 5 seconds for the DFE's ACKTC. The DFE checks the length and CRC, its own on-line and remote state, the dangerous command list, its buffer and whether the NDIU is in charge, and answers 0x55 (queued) or 0x56; while its buffer is full it withholds the ACKTC, which throttles the CCS. It then encodes a CLTU, decodes it back and sends the result as a TC echo, and finally a TC report (0x57): in AD mode after the CLCW check (on-board acceptance), in BD mode after its own acceptance. The TC report is a guaranteed one-to-one final confirmation for every TC, even after a failed ACKTC.154157158

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as CCS
    participant D as TM/TC DFE
    participant S as Spacecraft
    C->>D: 0x80 TC, RqId=2
    D->>C: 0x55 ACKTC success, RqId=2 (under 5 s)
    D->>S: CLTU (AD mode)
    D->>C: 0xA0 TC echo, RqId=0
    S-->>D: TM frames with CLCW
    D->>C: 0x57 TC report, RqId=2
    C->>D: 0x80 TC, RqId=3

The diagram condenses Figure 9; the TC report is asynchronous to the echo.154

ACKTC failure code Meaning ACKRC failure code Meaning 0 Not authorised, local mode 0 Not authorised, local mode 1 Not authorised, NDIU in charge 1 Not authorised, off-line 2 Not authorised, off-line 2 TC input buffer full 3 TC in the dangerous list 3 Illegal APID 4 TC input buffer full 4 Illegal data field header 5 Illegal or inconsistent length 5 Illegal packet length 6 Time-out on reception 6 Time-out on reception 7 Port disconnected while reading 7 Port disconnected while reading 8 Incorrect checksum 8 RC unknown 9 TC encoder not ready

Sources: §4.7.2 and §4.8.2.156157

The TC report's source data is an event layout (event ID, SID, 8 octets of Parameters A and event counter, all but the ID forced to 0) followed by the request ID (4 octets), result code, priority, protocol (AD or BD), VCID, MAP ID, number of retransmissions (1 octet each), an 8-octet CUC time of final confirmation and the 6-octet header of the original TC.159 Periodic RM packets (1 per second for the power and PLM SCOEs, 1 per 10 s otherwise) begin with a SID and common parameters: SCOE mode (local or remote), software activity, configuration, on-line status, self-test status and SCOE set (AVM, Herschel or Planck).155 The alive packet is a TM(0,0) with no data, never archived.160 Time on all EGSE items is synchronised by NTP, with the CCS as server.162 The DFE to CCS TM interface must support 150 kbps and the TC interface 4 kbps, plus overhead.163

The EGSE items have their own APIDs inside the PS-ICD's reserved range, and their own positions in the naming convention, with subsystem letter Y (number 25):161164

EGSE item APID Naming position CCS (master test processor) 2016 (0x7E0) 940-941 CDMU SCOE 2017 (0x7E1) 948-949 ACMS SCOE 2018 (0x7E2) 920-939 TT&C SCOE 2019 (0x7E3) 950-951 TM/TC DFE 2020 (0x7E4) 946-947 BATSIM / LPS-SAS 2023 / 2024 956-957 / 952-955 PLM SCOE 2025 (0x7E9) 942-943 Herschel cryo SCOE / cryo COTE 2026 (0x7EA) 958-961 CDMU DFE / 1553 bus monitor 2028 / 2029 944-945 / – HFI, LFI EGSE 2040, 2041 (0x7F8, 0x7F9) 968-971 HIFI, PACS, SPIRE EGSE 2042, 2043, 2044 (0x7FA-0x7FC) 962-967

Identifiers may use only digits, the upper-case letters except I, O and Q, and the underscore.164

Worked example (illustrative values, real layouts): one HIFI command on three interfaces

The HIFI command HIFI_Set_OBS_ID is TC(8,4) with function ID 1, activity ID 0, SID 0, a 32-bit HIFI_BB_ID and a 32-bit HIFI_OBS_ID, 24 octets in total.200204 With the values BB_ID = 1, OBS_ID = 0x12345678, sequence count 5 from ground and acknowledgement of acceptance and completion (all chosen for illustration), the packet is:

1C 00   version 000, type 1, DFH 1, APID 0x400 (1024)
C0 05   sequence flags 11, source 000 (ground), count 5
00 11   packet length 17 (24 octets - 7)
09      sec. hdr flag 0, PUS version 0, Ack 1001 (completion + acceptance)
08 04   type 8, subtype 4
00      spare
01 00   function ID 1, activity ID 0
00 00   SID 0
00 00 00 01   HIFI_BB_ID
12 34 56 78   HIFI_OBS_ID
EA 2C   CRC-16 (computed by this wiki with the Appendix 4 algorithm)

In the ILT router it travels as a USER_DATA message 01 00 00 00 18 + packet, to packet address \(4096 + 1024 = 5120\).137138 Sent by the CCS to the DFE it is a PIPE message 80 00 00 1E <request ID> FA DE + packet, since the remaining length is \(24 + 6 = 30\).148

docs.title: The CCS external interfaces and its MIB
docs.text:
The Terma CCS External ICD names four external interfaces: the SCOE/DFE LAN and the instrument station LAN (both PIPE), a World Wide Web station, and two HPSDB file interfaces, bridge files (the MIB, HPSDB to CCS) and update files (CCS to HPSDB). TM dumps from the DFE are handled through a separate packet analysis tools note.167

An update file is tab-separated ASCII, one line per object validated by a test sequence: <datetime> <type> <name> <test sequence name> <issue> <host>, with the SCOS time format YYYY.DDD.HH.MM.SS.mmm and type c (telecommand) or p (parameter). The MIB issue comes from vdf.dat.168 The HPSDB manual's data verification file has the same six columns (with a site instead of a host) and records the test that verified each item.188

The bridge files follow the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 5.1 with explicit exceptions:166177

Change Tables Content Danger actions – No MIB change; a parameter beyond its danger limits starts the test sequence danger_<parname> Delta limits ocp New OCP_TYPE 'D' with the delta in OCP_LVALU; the type list is S soft, H hard, D delta, C status consistency (needs PCF_USCON = 'Y'), E event only Calibration selection pcf, new cur PCF_CURTX null when a selection exists; cur lists, per parameter and position, an integer selector parameter, its raw value and the calibration to apply; the first match wins Groups new grp, grpa, grpk Groups of parameters ('PA') or packets ('PK', by SPID) System parameters pcf, pid Names starting YZ reserved (Y = EGSE subsystem, Z = system parameters); SPIDs 100 to 999 reserved for EGSE use Equipment and routing new sco, tcd, tmd Equipment name, host and port; TC distribution by APID; TM distribution by SPID Extrapolation caf CAF_INTER 'P' extrapolate or 'F' invalid; PCF_INTER ignored by the HPCCS ECP 1 calibration and range tables Curve and range set IDs from Number(4) to Char(10); CVS_ID from Number(5) to Number(10) ECP 3 new lgf Logarithmic calibration \(Y = 1/(A_0 + A_1 \ln X + \dots + A_4 \ln^4 X)\) ECP 9-12 ccf, csf Default on-board subschedule ID per command and per sequence

Sources: §8 to §9.13.169170171172173174175176 These are the functions that ESA later "repatriated" into SCOS-2000; the history of the import ICD records them for issue 6.0, and the standard tables cur, grp, grpa, grpk and lgf descend from them.247

Two small differences from the standard ICD

ICD 7.0 attributes the default sub-schedule ID in ccf and csf to functions repatriated from Cryosat, while the CCS ICD already shows CCF_SUBSCHEDID and CSF_SUBSCHEDID for the Herschel/Planck CCS in January 2006; ICD 7.0 also puts minimum and maximum delta limits in OCP_LVALU and OCP_HVALU, where the CCS ICD used a single value.248176249170

The same features in the Solar Orbiter MIB (real data)

The Solar Orbiter release of 16 September 2025 uses most of them (queries below). Its ocp has 105 delta checks ('D') and 15 status consistency checks ('C'), the latter on parameters such as NCDT02A0 whose PCF_USCON is 'Y'. Its cur has 1974 rows for 907 parameters, none of which has a PCF_CURTX, as the CCS ICD required. A typical case is NCAB0EP0 ("CPS A TLV LCL Cur"): when the PCDU model parameter NPWZ0000 is 10 ("EM" in textual calibration AYMODELE) the curve CPWP3005TM applies, when it is 11 ("FM") CPWP8005TM. grp holds two groups: GRPPAR ("Example for Parameters") has no members because grpa is empty, and GRPHK groups four SWA housekeeping SPIDs (58200 to 58202 on APID 1540 and 58907 on APID 1525). CCF_SUBSCHEDID is filled for 5304 of 5454 commands, with 17 values from 1 to 110. lgf is empty, all CAF_INTER values are empty, and only three SPIDs fall in 100-999: 101 to 103, MATIS packets of type 166 on APID 1966.250

Inference

That Solar Orbiter's low SPIDs 101-103 for MATIS packets echo the Herschel/Planck rule that reserved SPIDs 100-999 for EGSE use is a reading by this wiki; the Solar Orbiter MIB does not say why these SPIDs were chosen.172250

docs.title: The HPSDB: user manual and a real delivery
docs.text:
The Herschel/Planck System Database (HPSDB), built by GMV on Oracle 9i under Windows 2000, is a web application with a central site and several mirror sites. Only real objects may be modified at a mirror site, and changes travel as XML transfer and log files that the managers copy by hand, because the sites do not talk to each other.179182

Objects are boxes (elements, subsystems, models and one generic box) that contain items (TM packets, TC packets, parameters, curves and so on). Boxes and items are either theoretical or real (instantiated), and items defined in an element are visible through the subsystem and model that contain it.181 Data live in three areas:180

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Working: create
    Reference --> Working: checkout (copy to edit)
    Reference --> Working: delete (copy marked for deletion)
    Working --> Reference: validation by the manager
    Reference --> Archive: replaced or deleted by a validation
    Working --> [*]: discard

The diagram follows §3.1.1; only the manager validates, and validation refuses an object whose referenced objects are neither in the reference area nor selected for the same validation, or are deleted by it.180187 Bridge file loading imports SCOS-2000 or CCS MIB files from a zip file together with configuration files that map them to the naming convention:183184

Configuration file Content S2K_EL.txt Real element identifier, theoretical element number, SW or HW, description, product tree identifier S2K_SUB.txt Subsystem identifier, pseudo position and element number; then one line per position with ACC and CDMU bus controller flags, element, SCOE host and port S2K_TM.txt A copy of pid.dat with a naming convention identifier prepended S2K_CUR.txt, S2K_CVS.txt, S2K_PRF.txt Mapping of SCOS curve, verification stage and range set numbers to HPSDB generic items

The manual's example uses the HIFI positions: ICU________001 at position 190, FCU________002 at 191, LCU________005 at 194, in subsystem H001001, and S2K_TM.txt lines with identifiers 289TMPKA000289 to 289TMPKA002289 for packets of APIDs 1024 and 1026.185 Bridge files can be generated for the SCOS or CCS format from any box; verification data and real-element ON/OFF periods are written directly into the reference area.186188189

The release note H-P-2-ASP-LI-1441 issue 9.0 documents one such generation: theoretical model HERSCH_FM9 from central site HPSDB 3.3.1.30 to ASED in Friedrichshafen, in CCS format with the AIT user filter, for the Herschel IRR, as R_TM_HERSCH_FM9_C_804071709.zip with an MD5 checksum.
