docs.title: TDRS: Telemetry Data Retrieval Service
docs.text:
The TDRS is the SCOS-2000 add-on that let authorised users outside the operations room retrieve telemetry parameter values from a mission's archive over the web. A user described a retrieval in a small text file or a web form: which parameters, which time windows, raw or calibrated values, which filters. The TDRS read the packets from the SCOS-2000 history files and extracted and optionally calibrated the parameters. It returned the result as MVDA binary files or as tab-separated spreadsheet files, by web download, e-mail or FTP.129 Venus Express, for example, used it for parameter access, and its functions were later absorbed into the EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS).21

The main source is the "SCOS-2000 TDRS-External Interfaces Control Document" (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0017, issue 5.1, 22 August 2008). It was prepared by the TDRS team at LogicaCMG and approved by ESOC.3 It defines the retrieval request file, the result files and the user log. It also defines the internal interfaces between the web server and the three TDRS subsystems.45

System or Services?

The EDDS SRS and the Venus Express paper call it the "Telemetry Data Retrieval System".62 Its requirements document is titled "SCOS-2000 TM Data Retrieval Services Software Requirements Document" (S2K-MCS-SRD-0004-TOS-GIC). A 2005 ESOC talk lists it as "Telemetry Data Retrieval Services (TDRS)".78 This wiki keeps the abbreviation TDRS for all three names.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Aspect TDRS Data TM parameter samples extracted from fixed-length packets in the SCOS-2000 history file archive12 Users Authorised users on the ESOC Intranet and the public Internet, through a web browser and e-mail1 Input Retrieval request file (.req), written by hand or generated by the web forms4 Retrieval types FAST (raw values), FAST_ENG (raw and calibrated), COMPLETE (also validity and out-of-limit state)9 Outputs MVDA (Header.dat, TimeNNNN.dat, DataNNNN.dat), spreadsheet (.fst, .fen, .cmp), column-organised spreadsheet (.col), user log (.log)10 Architecture Web server → PCGI (CGI programs) → PRQM (CORBA and files) → PSRV (TCP/IP) → SCOS-2000111213 Security SSL certificates at the web interface; limits on parallel requests, archive requests and result size14 Documented releases ICD issues 1.0 (Feb 2000) to 5.1 (Aug 2008), covering SCOS-2000 release 3.1 and TDRS releases 2.0.1, 2.1 and 3.115 Successor EDDS parameter retrieval with the "TDRS spreadsheet" output format1617

docs.title: Role in the ground segment
docs.text:
The EDDS requirements describe TDRS as one of three SCOS-2000 subsystems that gave local and remote users access to MCS data, next to WebRM and GDDS.1

  • TDRS handled telemetry only. It provided a retrieval interface that extracts TM parameter values from the history-file archive and presents them as MVDA or spreadsheet files. The parameters come from fixed-length TM packets.1
  • The user interface and web handling were kept separate from the retrieval itself. The SRS says this division let security and performance responsibilities be distributed.1

The Venus Express paper describes the same service from the user side. TDRS retrieves the telemetry packets that contain the requested parameters, extracts the parameters, and optionally calibrates them and evaluates their validity and out-of-limit status. It cannot read variable-length packets.2 The spreadsheet files hold a raw value and a time stamp for each occurrence of each requested parameter. A complete retrieval adds validity and out-of-limit status.2

On Venus Express the two external doors were therefore split by data type. Packets and auxiliary files came through the DDS (based on the GDDS), and parameters came through the TDRS.18

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The ICD describes TDRS as a chain of three subsystems behind a standard web server. A persistence layer, PERS, centralises writing and parsing of request files.1119

flowchart LR
  B["Web browser<br/>(SSL client certificate)"] -->|"HTTP: forms, HTML pages"| W["Web server"]
  W -->|"CGI calls"| PCGI["PCGI<br/>CGI executables<br/>(user interface)"]
  PCGI -->|"CORBA: interface PRQM"| PRQM["PRQM<br/>request manager"]
  PCGI -->|".req files (via PERS)"| PRQM
  PRQM -->|"TCP/IP: PSRVretrRequest"| PSRV["PSRV server<br/>forks PSRVfastChild /<br/>PSRVcompleteChild"]
  PSRV -->|"TCP/IP: PSRVextractData, PSRVstatus"| PRQM
  PSRV -->|"history files, MIB"| S2K[("SCOS-2000<br/>archive + database")]
  PRQM -->|"result and log files"| W
Subsystem Responsibility Integrity check it performs How it reports errors PCGI Web user interface: CGI executables that build HTML pages Values received from HTML forms An error HTML page PRQM Request management: validation, scheduling, collecting results, writing files Received CORBA requests A PRQMvalidationInfo structure PERS Common persistence layer for request files Contents of request files An error flag per operation PSRV Retrieval back end inside SCOS-2000: extraction, calibration, checks Received TCP/IP data A PSRVstatus structure

The table follows ICD §5.6 and §5.8.14 The expansions of PCGI, PRQM, PSRV and PERS are not stated in the available sources.

All TDRS files are stored only on the web-server machine: temporary and regular request files, log files and result files. PSRV writes only the usual SCOS-2000 trace file.14 The system can limit the number of parallel retrieval requests, the number of archive requests and the size of result files.20 Each interface synchronises differently. The web browser blocks until the CGI program returns. CORBA calls block until the operation completes. PRQM and PSRV can be started in either order and handshake through command codes.20

The files are "Unix ASCII or binary Solaris format". The ICD states that binary MVDA files will not be transferred from Solaris to Linux, because MVDA is deprecated for future TDRS installations.20

docs.title: The web interface (PCGI)
docs.text:
The ICD describes the user interface as "a big state machine". The states are HTML pages, and the transitions are runs of PCGI executables.21

HTML page Purpose Produced by Welcome, Home Entry after login; top-level menu PCGIhome Request Specification, Submit Request Enter and submit a retrieval PCGIReqFormHdlr (actions: more windows, more repeated windows, more parameters, next, reset) Request Submitted Confirmation PCGIretrRequestEngine Request Status, Request Cancelled Status of running and finished requests; cancel PCGIstatusRequestEngine, PCGIcancelRequestEngine Resubmit Request, Request Resubmitted Resubmit a request stored on the client's disk PCGIresubmitRequestEngine Load / Save Request Requests stored on the server PCGIloadRequestEngine, PCGIsaveRequestEngine Parameter List Parameter chooser PCGIparamIterator Error General errors any

The pages and programs are listed in ICD §13.1–§13.2.11 The main state machine, as drawn in ICD §13.3 (simplified by this wiki):21

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Home: network login, PCGIhome
    Home --> EditRequest: PCGIReqFormHdlr(get_general)
    EditRequest --> EditRequest: more params / windows, parameter list, load, save, reset
    EditRequest --> SubmitRequest: PCGIReqFormHdlr(general, ActionNext)
    SubmitRequest --> RequestSubmitted: PCGIretrRequestEngine(status OK)
    SubmitRequest --> SubmitRequest: PCGIretrRequestEngine(status error)
    RequestSubmitted --> EditRequest: PCGIReqFormHdlr(get_general)
    Home --> RequestStatus: PCGIstatusRequestEngine
    RequestStatus --> RequestCancelled: PCGIcancelRequestEngine
    Home --> Resubmit: PCGIReqFormHdlr(get_resubmit)
    Resubmit --> Resubmitted: PCGIresubmitRequestEngine
    RequestCancelled --> Home: PCGIhome
    Resubmitted --> Home: PCGIhome
    RequestSubmitted --> Home: PCGIhome
    EditRequest --> Error
    SubmitRequest --> Error

docs.title: PCGI to PRQM: the CORBA interface
docs.text:
PRQM exposes a single CORBA interface, PRQM. The request details travel in a request file; the CORBA call carries only key information.12

Operation Purpose newRequest(PRQMrequestInfo, ignorevaliddatefail) Issue a retrieval. PRQMrequestInfo holds the user ID, the path of the request file and the execution time (seconds since 1970). The flag says whether to ignore a validation failure. getStatus(userid) Status of all requests of a user cancelRequest(userid, exeid) Cancel a request getDBInfo() List the available MIB databases with their validity begin and end times getParameterCount(), getParameters(from, to) Size of the parameter list and a slice of names and descriptions (to = 0 returns all)

The result of newRequest is a PRQMvalidationInfo. It holds isok (validated and scheduled), ismaxreg (maximum number of requests exceeded), info (for example syntax errors) and the new execution ID. A PRQMstatusInfo gives the execution ID, state, execution time, description, and links to the request, result, header, timer and log files, with a flag for MVDA output.22

docs.title: PRQM to PSRV: the retrieval protocol
docs.text:
PRQM and PSRV talk over TCP/IP. A retrieval is sent in two phases. The PSRV server receives the direct attributes of the request and then starts a child process of the right kind, a fast child or a complete child. The child opens its own TCP/IP connection back to PRQM and receives the parameter details on it.13

sequenceDiagram
    participant Q as PRQM server
    participant S as PSRV server
    participant C as PSRV child
    Q->>S: PSRV_IF_INITREQUEST
    Q->>S: PSRVretrRequest (retrieval type, retrieval ID, DB version, PRQM ID, user ID)
    S->>C: start PSRVfastChild or PSRVcompleteChild
    C->>Q: connect (new TCP/IP connection)
    Q->>C: PSRVretrParam (data streams, parameters, time windows, retrieval mode)
    loop every PSRV_PING_RATE samples
        C->>Q: PSRV_IF_DATA + PSRVextractData (x N)
        C->>Q: PSRV_IF_PING
        Q-->>C: -1 (synchronisation reply)
    end
    C->>Q: PSRV_IF_CHILDSTATUS + PSRVstatus
    C->>Q: PSRV_IF_CHILDDONE

The diagram combines ICD §15.1 and §15.2.1323 The data types on this interface mirror the request file.

Type Content PSRVclientCommand PSRV_IF_INITREQUEST (new retrieval follows), PSRV_IF_CANCEL (request ID follows) PSRVretrType FAST (raw values only), FAST_ENG (raw, calibrated and units), COMPLETE (also validity and status), GETPARAMS (names and descriptions only) PSRVretrParam data streams, parameter list, extraction time windows, retrieval mode (0 packet by packet, 1 interval by interval) and its interval PSRVparam name, SPID (0 = all), retrieval filter, occurrence start and interval for supercommutated parameters, sampling (every Nth packet, -1 none), sampling interval, only-when-valid, only-when-not-nominal, minimum and maximum threshold PSRVretrievalFilter VALUE_AFTER, VALUE_BEFORE, VALUE_BEFORE_AFTER, ON_OCCURRENCE, NO_FILTERING PSRVcmd NO_CMD, EXECUTE_CMD, EXECUTE_IF_VALID_CMD, VALIDATE_CMD PSRVtimeWindow and subclasses sorted start and stop time lists; repeated and irregular windows are expanded into these lists PSRVserverCommand VALIDATION, IF_DATA, IF_CHILDSTATUS, IF_CHILDDONE, IF_PARAMETERS; also states computed on the PRQM side such as IF_CHILDDEAD and IF_SERVERDEAD PSRVextractData name, sample time, source value (raw, or the synthetic value of a derived parameter), value format, validity, OOL state; optional engineering value, its validity and unit PSRVdataFormat S8, U8, S16, U16, S32, U32, S64, U64, FLOAT, DOUBLE, QUADRUPLE (Sun formats), ASCII, RIEEE (32-bit IEEE), RMIL (32-bit MIL-STD-1750A), UNDEFINED PSRVool UNDEF, NOMINAL, LOW_LOW (low alarm), LOW (low warning), HIGH, HIGH_HIGH, SCC_FAIL PSRVstatus log time, error code, text, retrieval ID (-1 = general message) PSRVerrorCode 27 codes, from PSRV_OK through PSRV_PARAM_NOTFOUND, PSRV_CANNOT_LOADDB, PSRV_NO_CALIBRATION and PSRV_STORE_FULL to PSRV_MAX_REQUESTS

The table summarises ICD §15.1.1–§15.2.4.1323 Values travel as strings, whatever their internal format.23 The ICD itself marks PSRV_IF_SERVERSTATUS and PSRV_IF_NETPROBLEM as "seems not to be used".23

docs.title: The retrieval request file (.req)
docs.text:
A retrieval request file completely describes one retrieval: parameters, time intervals, database version, filter options and output format. The TDRS syntax-checks it and rejects it on any error. Missions may extend the format if their TDRS installation supports the extensions.9

Syntax. The file is ASCII. Each field is a name, a colon and a value, and fields are separated by carriage returns. Names are case-insensitive. A # starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. Optional fields may be omitted. Text with spaces goes in double quotes.9 Internally, the request is stored under a unique name <retrieval ID>_<execution ID>_<user ID>_<expiration day>.req. The ICD's example is 0_1_SMITH_038.req, where 038 is the expiration date.924

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
# Field Type Values and rules M/O 1 RetrievalDesc Char Free description in quotes O 2 RetrievalType Number 0 FAST, 1 FAST_ENG, 2 COMPLETE M 3 OutputFormat Number 0 MVDA, 1 SPREADSHEET, 2 COLUMNMODE_SPREADSHEET (default) O 4 DataOrStatistics Number Column mode only: 0 DATA, 1 STATISTICS, 2 DATA_AND_STATISTICS (default) O 5 TimeFormat Number 0 ASD yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss[.mmm] (default), 1 CCSDS ASCII A yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.mmm, 2 both. Ignored for MVDA. O 6 Dbversion Char Name of the MIB database version to use M 7–8 EmailAddr, AttachSize Char, Number Results by e-mail; attachment limit in kbytes (0 = no attachment; the server limit always wins) O 9–12 FTPaddr, FTPuser, FTPpassword, FTPdirName Char Automatic FTP transfer of the results; an anonymous account is recommended O (M if FTPaddr) 13 Log Number 0 off, 1 on (default) O 14 Datastream Number 1–65535, repeatable, at most 4 M 15 TimeWindow Number 0 SINGLE, 1 REPEATED, 2 IRREGULAR M 16–17 StartTime, StopTime Char(21) Single window. StopTime is absolute, or relative [+][ddd.]hh.mm.ss.mmm, and not before the start. M 18–21 OverallStartTime, OverallStopTime, WinLength, RepeatPer Char Repeated windows: WinLength and RepeatPer are [ddd.]hh.mm.ss, with RepeatPer > WinLength M 22–23 StartTime, StopTime Char(21) Irregular windows, repeatable. Each start must be after the previous stop. M 24 ParamName Char(8) Parameter name; starts a per-parameter block M 25 SPID Number(10) Use only samples from this packet, 1 to 231−1. Default: all packets. Ignored for synthetic parameters. O 26 RetrievalFilter Number 0 VALUE_AFTER, 1 VALUE_BEFORE, 2 VALUE_BEFORE_AFTER, 3 ON_OCCURRENCE, 4 NO_FILTERING (default) O 27–28 OccurrenceStart, OccurrenceInterval Number With ON_OCCURRENCE: first occurrence (1–65535) and number of occurrences (0–65535) M 29 SamplingN Number Use every Nth packet (1–65535); COMPLETE only O 30 OnlyWhenValidityOK Number 1 = use the sample only if the parameter is valid O 31 OnlyWhenNotNominal Number 1 = use the sample only if its OOL state is not nominal (see note) O 32–33 MinThresholdValue, MaxThresholdValue Number/Char Keep values ≥ min and/or ≤ max. FAST compares the raw view, the others the default view. O 34 RetrievalMode Number 0 packet per packet, 1 interval per interval – 35 IntervalRetrievalTime Char(12) Step time for interval mode –

The field list is ICD §8.6.9

Inference: inconsistencies in the ICD

  • Field 31 is described as "use the sample only when the parameter has no OOL nominal state", while PSRV describes the same flag as "only when OOL is not nominal". Both readings say the filter keeps out-of-limit samples.913
  • Fields 19 and 23 refer to the format "of the StopTime in field 12". Field 12 is FTPdirName, so field 17 is meant.9
  • OccurrenceInterval is defined as the number of occurrences to extract, yet the same entry says that OccurrenceStart = 1 with OccurrenceInterval = 1 retrieves all samples in the packet.9
  • The ON_OCCURRENCE rule says that for a non-supercommutated parameter with OccurrenceStart ≠ 1 nothing is extracted. OccurrenceStart = 1 with OccurrenceInterval = 0 switches supercommutation off.9

docs.title: Retrieval types
docs.text:
Type What PSRV returns Spreadsheet extension FAST Raw values only .fst (or MVDA) FAST_ENG Raw values, calibrated (engineering) values and units .fen COMPLETE Everything: raw and calibrated values, units, validity and status (OOL) information .cmp

The table combines ICD §8.6, §10.4 and §15.1.2.1.92813 The calibration is the one defined for the parameter in the database version named in the request: see calibration in the MIB. The OOL states are those of the monitoring checks.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
ICD Appendix B fixes how the two threshold fields combine.25

Thresholds given Textual value Numerical value Only minimum Must match exactly Keep values ≥ min Only maximum Not allowed (validation error) Keep values ≤ max Both, min < max Not allowed Keep min ≤ value ≤ max Both, min = max Not allowed Keep only that value Both, min > max Not allowed Not allowed

docs.title: An illustrative request
docs.text:
The ICD's own example asks for three invented parameters over three irregular windows.9 The file below is illustrative. It was written by this wiki using real parameter names from the September 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB, but Solar Orbiter was never served by TDRS.

RetrievalDesc:"IMU temperature and one PCDU snapshot channel"
RetrievalType:2              # COMPLETE: raw, engineering, validity, OOL
OutputFormat:1               # SPREADSHEET -> .cmp file
TimeFormat:1                 # CCSDS ASCII A
Dbversion:25925PFM           # database name; see note below
Log:1
Datastream:1000
TimeWindow:1                 # REPEATED: 10 minutes every hour
OverallStartTime:2025.244.00.00.00
OverallStopTime:2025.245.00.00.00
WinLength:00.10.00
RepeatPer:01.00.00
# temperature, only from one of its two packets
ParamName:NMUD1113
SPID:29534
OnlyWhenValidityOK:1
# supercommutated current: occurrences 1 and 2 of 1024
ParamName:NPWX2502
SPID:66686
RetrievalFilter:3
OccurrenceStart:1
OccurrenceInterval:2
RetrievalMode:0

NMUD1113 ("IMU11 SIA temperature", degC) is placed in two fixed TM(3,25) packets, SPIDs 29517 and 29534. NPWX2502 ("LCL1_01 RWAB-1 SnapS", A) occurs 1,024 times in SPID 66686, a TM(131,2) PCDU snapshot packet.26

Inference

The ICD only says Dbversion is the "name of the database version". Using the MIB's VDF_NAME (25925PFM for this release) is this wiki's assumption. TDRS could list the available databases and their validity periods with the CORBA call getDBInfo.1226

docs.title: Result files
docs.text:
All TDRS output files except fast MVDA files carry the retrieval ID, execution ID, user ID and an expiration day (ddd) in their names. The expiration day is computed from the request and a configurable expiration period.24

File Content Produced for xxxxxx.req The retrieval request input, kept by TDRS Header.dat, TimeNNNN.dat, DataNNNN.dat MVDA header, time and value files FAST with MVDA output Res<ids>.fst, .fen, .cmp Spreadsheet fast, fast with engineering values, complete Res<ids>.col Column-organised spreadsheet column mode <ids>.log User log when Log is on

The file table is ICD §4.3; the .log name is from §12.4.1031

docs.title: MVDA files
docs.text:
A fast retrieval without engineering values produces exactly the output of MVDA (the SRS expands it as Mission Visual Data Analysis). That output is one ASCII header file, and one binary data file and one binary time file per parameter.276 Header lines are space-separated, one per parameter. The ICD notes that one line per time window for repeated or irregular windows is a future extension.27

# Header field Content 1 Param. Id. Parameter name 2–3 Start Time, Stop Time yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.mmmmmm 4 Data pointer The number used in the names of the data and time files 5 Nsamples Samples retrieved 6 DataFormat S8, U8, U16, S16, U32, S32, U64, S64, F, D, Q (Sun float, double, quadruple), A##### (ASCII, \0-separated), RIEEE, RMIL. The ICD describes S32 as "signed integers of 16 bit", evidently a slip. 7 Eng 0 = no engineering values, 1 = included

Each time file holds 8 octets per sample: 4 octets of seconds since 1970 and 4 octets of microseconds. A data file holds one value per sample in the declared format. In the ICD's U32 example the sizes are 4 × Nsamples and 8 × Nsamples.27

docs.title: Spreadsheet files (.fst, .fen, .cmp)
docs.text:
One ASCII file per request, with a header line of column names, then one tab-separated row per sample. It is meant for import into MS Excel, and missions may append columns.28

# Column Content Filled for 1 Time1 ASD time yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss.mmmmmm all (one of the two time columns) 2 Time2 CCSDS ASCII A yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.mmmmmm all (one of the two) 3 Parameter Name all 4 Raw Raw value as text. For a synthetic parameter this is the source value, and may be text. all 5 RawValidity Validity text as in the SCOS-2000 telemetry desktop COMPLETE 6 EngineeringUnit Unit from the MCS database FAST_ENG, COMPLETE 7 Engineering Calibrated value (number or text) FAST_ENG, COMPLETE 8 EngValidity Validity of the engineering value COMPLETE 9 OOL NOM, LL, L, H, HH, SCC_UNIT, SCC_F, UDEF, delta states (MIN_D_LOW, MIN_D_HIGH, MAX_D_LOW, …), D_EQUAL, VIOL COMPLETE

The columns are ICD §10.6.28 VIOL marks a parameter that is outside its limits but whose number of violations has not reached the maximum number of violations (see monitoring checks). The ICD's delta list names MIN_D_HIGH twice; the second entry, described as "high limit OOL for positive delta", is presumably MAX_D_HIGH.28 Rows for a parameter without calibration leave the engineering columns empty.28

docs.title: Column-organised files (.col)
docs.text:
The column mode is designed to be more readable than the plain spreadsheet. It has one common column of labels and one column per parameter.29

  1. Retrieval header data: retrieval start and stop, retrieval ID, execution ID, user, expiration day and count of samples.
  2. Per-parameter header rows: name, description, view (RAW or CAL), unit, first and last sample time. With statistics requested, also the minimum and its time, maximum and its time, average, standard deviation, sample count, and the minimum and maximum thresholds used.
  3. Data rows: one per distinct sample time, with each parameter's value in its column, or empty if that parameter has no sample at that time. FAST reports raw values; FAST_ENG and COMPLETE report engineering values.

The ICD example shows three gyro parameters over 16 s, with each parameter's statistics and five data rows.29 The naming paragraph of this chapter repeats the .cmp example of the spreadsheet chapter, although the extension is .col.29

docs.title: Value formats
docs.text:
Values in the spreadsheet files are text, with one format per SCOS-2000 internal type.30

Data type Internal encoding Text format Unsigned integer, natural 32-bit signed integer Integer up to 231−1, no sign Integer 32-bit signed integer Minus sign only for negative values Boolean 32-bit signed integer 1, 0, TRUE or FALSE Logical 32-bit signed integer Up to 8 binary digits followed by b or B, e.g. 10101b Real Double precision Fixed or scientific notation, e.g. 3.5e-2 String Character string In double quotes Absolute time TDSsunTime ASD yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss[mmm], ASCII A yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.[uuuuuu] or ASCII B yyyy-dddThh:mm:ss.[uuuuuu] Delta time TDSsunTime ddd.hh.mm.ss[mmm], at most 365.23.59.59.999

These text forms relate to the MIB's parameter types. The CCSDS ASCII time codes are on the time codes page.

docs.title: The user log
docs.text:
The log is ASCII with name: value fields, several to a line, separated by commas.31 It records:

  • the execution start time, the total duration and the retrieval type;
  • per parameter: the sample count, the time of the first retrieval and the duration;
  • log entries, each with a time stamp, a severity (Warning or Error) and a message.

The ICD's example warns that a requested parameter does not exist and that an occurrence start does not match, and ends with "Result data size exceeds limit".31

docs.title: WebRM
docs.text:
WebRM (Web Remote Monitoring) was the live counterpart of TDRS. It let users monitor a spacecraft without physical access to the MCS, over the Intranet or the public Internet.1 It had two parts.

  1. External interface servers. Injection servers sent data to the SCOS-2000 kernel. Provision servers collected monitoring data and distributed it to all active clients. Both used CORBA and were built for SCOS-2000.
  2. The WebRM client. A Java application (Java 2, JRE 1.4) with displays that look like the SCOS-2000 ones. It supported monitoring only, although the CORBA interfaces also allowed injection.

A 2005 ESOC talk groups "Telemetry Data Retrieval Services (TDRS) and WebRM" as web interfaces that give external users, such as payload owners, live telemetry and command verification, telemetry retrieval and statistics.8 No WebRM interface document is in the library. Its requirements baseline (WEB-RM User & Software Requirements Baseline, issue 1.4, 2003) is cited by the EDDS SRS.32

docs.title: How TDRS fed the EDDS
docs.text:
The EDDS requirements were built from TDRS, WebRM and GDDS.1 For TDRS the trail is visible in three places.

  1. Requirements. The SRS cites the TDRS requirements document as [RD-3] and the TDRS ICD (issue 4.3) as [RD-11]. Twenty-nine EDDS requirements cite [RD-3] in their "Source:" field. Among them is the list of TM packet filter attributes (type, subtype, APID, PI1, PI2, VC, domain, on-board or reception time, every Nth packet, maximum data volume, quality flag, database version, ground station, SPID, SSC, spacecraft ID).3233 This wiki counted the "Source:" fields. A further 25 requirements cite [RD-4] with SR-TMDR- identifiers; the SRS lists [RD-4] as the GDDS requirements document, so whether these also trace to TM data retrieval requirements is unclear (see the EDDS page).33
  2. Backward compatibility. SRS Appendix B lists exactly one TDRS item. The EDDS lets a mission define an XSLT that turns TM parameter data into the TDRS spreadsheet format (requirement EDDS-SR-00640).16 A related requirement says the spreadsheet format shall be tab-delimited ASCII following the TDRS ICD.34
  3. Implementation. EDDS ships Param.xsl, which converts the XML parameter response into a TDRS-like spreadsheet, and a native TDRS output format for large volumes. The TDRS retrieval ID, execution ID and expiration day columns are mandatory in the TDRS ICD but have no EDDS equivalent, so they are filled with 0. The native formatter writes the EDDS request ID as the retrieval ID.17 EUICD issue 24.0 cites TDRS ICD issue 5.1 for the format.35

Inference: concept mapping

TDRS concept Closest EDDS concept .req retrieval request file XML RequestMessagePart with a Param or SmonParam request (formats) FAST / FAST_ENG / COMPLETE Representation selection RAW/ENG (DARC) or RAW/ENG/ALL (SMON), with OOL data from SMON Single / repeated / irregular windows TimeRange plus a ScheduleRepeating with a cron expression Retrieval filters, sampling ParamTmFilter with OnChange, DeliveryRange and ParamFilterList (semantics not detailed in the EUICD) E-mail / FTP results AckDelivery / FileServerDelivery Retrieval ID, execution ID Request ID and job IDs Expiration day Response retention set by the mission administrator User log Acknowledgement and historical log

The EDDS element names are from the EUICD schema appendices.36 The pairing is this wiki's reading; no source gives such a table.

docs.title: Why the MIB matters to a TDRS retrieval
docs.text:
A retrieval names parameters and packets, so TDRS depends on the MIB: parameter names from pcf, packet positions from plf, SPIDs from pid and calibrations from the calibration tables. The September 2025 Solar Orbiter MIB shows how the TDRS limits would apply to a modern mission.26

Check Solar Orbiter MIB (Sep 2025) TDRS rule Parameter names 126,745 parameters; the longest name has 8 characters (126,502 have exactly 8) ParamName is Char(8)9 Fixed versus variable packets 9,087 packet definitions with PID_TPSD = −1 (fixed) and 2,063 variable Only fixed-length packets are processed12 Parameters reachable 107,792 distinct parameters placed by plf, all of them in fixed packets; 2,305 others defined only in variable-packet structures (vpd) The 2,305 would be out of reach Supercommutation 725 plf placements in 257 packets with more than one occurrence ON_OCCURRENCE with OccurrenceStart and OccurrenceInterval Synthetic parameters 1,582 parameters with PCF_NATUR = D (dynamic OL synthetic) and 2 with S (saved synthetic) SPID is ignored for synthetic parameters937

PID_TPSD = −1 marks packets not processed through the variable-packet tables.38

Inference

Treating "fixed-length packets" in the TDRS descriptions as SCOS-2000 packets with PID_TPSD = −1 is this wiki's interpretation. The counts themselves are query results.

SQL used

Run against solo-2025-09-16.sqlite on 2026-11-12.

SELECT count(*), max(length(PCF_NAME)), sum(length(PCF_NAME) = 8) FROM pcf;
-- 126745 | 8 | 126502
SELECT count(*) FROM pid WHERE CAST(PID_TPSD AS int) = -1;   -- 9087
SELECT count(*) FROM pid WHERE CAST(PID_TPSD AS int) <> -1;  -- 2063
SELECT count(DISTINCT PLF_NAME) FROM plf;                    -- 107792
SELECT count(DISTINCT p.PLF_NAME) FROM plf p JOIN pid d ON d.PID_SPID = p.PLF_SPID
 WHERE CAST(d.PID_TPSD AS int) <> -1;                        -- 0

docs.title: Venus Express: the ground segment around TDRS
docs.text:
The Venus Express data-handling paper (ESA SP-1295) shows where TDRS sat in a real planetary mission. The control concept was inherited from Rosetta and Mars Express: a single control centre at ESOC and the deep-space antennas at New Norcia and Cebreros. The data systems were a "delta development" of the systems built jointly for Rosetta and Mars Express.39 See Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express.

Component Role in the paper VMCS (Venus Express Mission Control System) SCOS-2000 based. Real-time housekeeping processing, command verification, out-of-limit detection, OBT-to-UTC time-stamping better than 2 ms, calibration, command history, operational database and on-board software maintenance. The paper describes the TDRS as part of it. VDDS (Venus Express Data Disposition System) Based on the GDDS: remote near-real-time and offline access, daily raw data media production, DVDs for the science operations centre MPS (Mission Planning System) Offline, mission-specific planning from PI, VSOC and ESOC inputs; produces command and station schedules FOP system Offline preparation of flight operations procedures and command sequences for import into the operational database NCTRS Receives telemetry from the stations (time-stamped with earth reception time) and forwards telecommands; also collects tracking data for flight dynamics and PIs

The components are described in §2.1–§2.2 of the paper.3940 The paper expands NCTRS as "Network Controller and Telemetry Receiver System". The 2005 ESOC talk says "Network Control and TM/TC Router System"; see NCTRS and NIS.408

flowchart LR
  SC["Venus Express"] --> GS["Cebreros / New Norcia"]
  GS --> N["NCTRS"]
  N --> V["VMCS (SCOS-2000)<br/>OPS LAN, no remote access"]
  V --> T["TDRS<br/>parameters"]
  V --> D["VDDS (GDDS)<br/>packets, auxiliary files,<br/>catalogues, DVDs"]
  T --> PI["Instrument teams (PIs)"]
  D --> PI
  D --> VSOC["VSOC (ESTEC)"]
  PI --> PSA["Planetary Science Archive<br/>(PDS standard)"]
  VSOC --> PSA
  VSOC -->|"ADCS: orbit, attitude, time correlation to SPICE"| PI

The figure is this wiki's summary of §2.3, §3 and §4 of the paper.184142

The paper defines the processing levels of the data flow.43

Level Content Produced by 0 Raw telemetry as received at the station spacecraft 1 Cleaned, merged, time-ordered data in frame format NCTRS and telemetry receiver 1a Level 1 separated by instrument, as requested through the DDS not stated 1b Sorted by data type and mode, in scientifically useful form, uncalibrated instrument team 2 Calibrated, in scientific units instrument team 3 Higher-level products instrument teams and others

Other points from the paper:

  • The VMCS is reachable only by operations staff. External access goes through the VDDS and the TDRS, which bridge the external world and the protected operational LAN.18
  • VDDS requests are expressed in a recursive XML query language. They come from standing orders, the web interface or FTP-submitted files, and are delivered online, by FTP or on DVD. Online previews embed the data as a byte stream in an XML response.44
  • The DVDs use the CCSDS Standard Formatted Data Unit concept, so that the science community can find and decode data without prior knowledge of the file structure. ESOC keeps all Level 1 data for 10 years after the end of the mission.18
  • Science archiving follows the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) standard in ESA's Planetary Science Archive. Data collection phases of 3 months are followed by 6 months of archive preparation, with peer review for the first and last deliveries. The first data were released in May 2007.41
  • The Auxiliary Data Conversion System, a set of Perl scripts, polls the ESOC DDS several times a day for orbit, attitude and time correlation data. It converts them into SPICE kernels, including SCLK clock kernels from the time correlation packages.42 See time correlation in SCOS-2000.

docs.title: Mission families: the setting
docs.text: The 2005 ESOC talk explains why generic tools such as TDRS existed. ESOC's strategy was to reuse software, procedures and operations concepts across missions. Mission control requirements were written as a "delta" against SCOS-2000, and missions with similar profiles shared a "family kernel" on top of SCOS-2000.45 The families named are Earth Explorer (low orbit, short passes), planetary (long propagation delay, on-board autonomy) and observatory (long visibility, proposal-based observations). For the Earth Explorer family, the talk counts the requirements at definition phase per mission: Cryosat 406 kernel and 35 mission-specific, GOCE 129 and 62, Aeolus 57 and 115.46 TDRS and WebRM appear in that talk as part of the shared infrastructure next to SCOS-2000, NCTRS and GDDS.8

docs.title: Gaps in the available sources
docs.text:
• The TDRS SRD, the TDRS Architectural Design Document and the TDRS Operator User Manual (issue 2.0, July 2000) are cited but not in the library.747
  • The meaning of the abbreviations PCGI, PRQM, PSRV, PERS and ASD, and the "PAS application" that stores request files, are not stated in the available sources.9
  • The MVDA retrieval and programmer's guides, and the WebRM interface documents, are not available.7
  • When TDRS was retired is not stated in the available sources. Issue 18.0 of the EDDS SRS (2018) still refers to it in the present tense.1

docs.title: Time correlation in SCOS-2000
docs.text:
A spacecraft keeps its own clock, the on-board time (OBT). The ground keeps UTC. The two are different clocks with different epochs, rates and drifts, and the spacecraft cannot simply be told "the time": every packet it sends is stamped with OBT, and every time-tagged command it executes waits for an OBT. Time correlation is the ground function that measures the relation between the two clocks and converts between them. In SCOS-2000 it is needed mainly by the telemetry packetiser, to time-stamp packets in UTC, and by the releaser, to encode time-tagged commands in OBT.4

This page explains the mechanism end to end: what the spacecraft sends, which delays the ground removes, how pairs of times become coefficients, how the coefficients are monitored, and how the SCOS-2000 software (the "TCO" subsystem) is built. It then shows what three generations of ESA missions did with it: Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express, and Solar Orbiter, whose MIB still defines the internal time correlation packets. The on-board side of the story (the ST[09] time management service) and the time code formats (CCSDS 301.0-B-4) have their own pages.

docs.title: The documents
docs.text:
The main source is the SCOS-2000 Time Correlation Technical Note, EGOS-MCS-S2K-TN-1030, version 1.0, dated 2018-10-31 and prepared by the SCOS-2000 GIMUS team. Its change log says it was created for S2K-7699: chapters 1 to 3 are mostly new, chapter 4 is taken from the EUD4S2K software user manual, section 5.2 from a Gaia time correlation document, and the rest refers to the TM Packetiser and Packet Displays ADD (EGOS-MCS-S2K-ADD-0017).12 Read with the body numbering, chapter 4 is "Time Correlation Mechanisms" and section 5.2 "Time Correlation Packets"; with the (different) numbering of the table of contents they would be the packetiser chapter and "Methods of Time Correlation", so the attribution is not fully certain (see the note below). Neither the EUD4S2K manual nor ADD-0017 is in this wiki's library.

Section numbers in TN-1030

The table of contents of TN-1030 numbers its chapters one lower than the headings in the body (for example "3 Time Correlation Mechanisms" in the contents is "4 TIME CORRELATION MECHANISMS" in the text).3 This page cites the numbers printed in the body.

Other sources fill in context: the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD issue 7.0 (how parameters are correlated), the Rosetta/Mars Express/Venus Express Data Delivery Interface Document (the earlier, manual time correlation of those missions), the Solar Orbiter Data Delivery ICD, the Solar Orbiter packet structure ICD, and the public Solar Orbiter MIB.

docs.title: Why the ground needs it
docs.text:
The standards ask for it at every level:

  • ECSS-E-ST-50C requires the space link to provide a time correlation capability that lets the on-board time be correlated with the time kept on the ground.31
  • ECSS-E-ST-70-11C (§5.4 "Datation and synchronization") requires the space segment to provide timing information so that the ground can maintain the OBT-to-UTC correlation better than a mission constant <TIME_CORREL_ACCUR> over a period <TIME_CORREL_PERIOD>; to let the ground set the OBT by telecommand; to keep the OBT monotonic and free of wrap-around for the mission lifetime; to limit the on-board time system's contribution to <ONBOARD_STABILITY> ms per day; and to document every on-board delay that contributes to the correlation. For GNSS-disciplined clocks it adds an on-board GNSS/OBT correlation reported in housekeeping telemetry.2930
  • The PUS time management service supplies the raw material: time reports that sample the spacecraft time reference at a precisely defined instant, so that the ground "can perform a correlation" between spacecraft time and UTC.25

SCOS-2000 itself treated time correlation as mission-specific code until release 5.2; from R5.2 a generic implementation supporting both free-running and synchronised clocks is part of the kernel.34 Earlier still, Earth Explorer missions contributed pieces: GOCE is listed as having contributed a "Time Correlator" to the Earth Explorer mission family kernel built on top of SCOS-2000.35

docs.title: Two clocks and their time codes
docs.text:
On-board time. The OBT is usually a binary counter of seconds and sub-seconds, encoded in the CCSDS Unsegmented time Code (CUC): a T-field of coarse octets (seconds) and fine octets (binary fractions), with an optional P-field that says how many of each there are and whether the epoch is the CCSDS epoch of 1958 January 1 TAI (level 1, code 0b001) or an agency-defined epoch (level 2, code 0b010).23 A clock synchronised to an external reference may instead use the CCSDS Day Segmented code (CDS: day count, milliseconds of day, optional sub-milliseconds), which is UTC-based and therefore subject to leap seconds.24 PUS reflects this split: CUC suits spacecraft time measurement, while CDS is typically used for an on-board time already synchronised with a ground reference such as TAI or UTC.25

Ground time. Inside SCOS-2000, times are held in the Unix-like TDSsunTime structure (4 octets of seconds and 4 of microseconds) or TDSsunTime_pico (plus 4 octets of picoseconds), counted from an epoch given by the MISC variable TCO_ESA_EPOCH; if that variable cannot be read, a DEFAULT_ESA_EPOCH hard-coded in the software is used.1011

Which telemetry is correlated. In the MIB, each absolute-time parameter (PTC 9) carries two fields in pcf: PCF_CORR (Y, the default, applies the time correlation when the raw value is interpreted; N extracts the time as is) and PCF_OBTID, which selects one of the mission's on-board clocks. A mission with N clocks numbers them 1 to N; when PCF_OBTID is empty the MISCconfig variable TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID applies, and an uncorrelated parameter without an OBT ID takes its epoch from TCO_ESA_EPOCH. Relative times (PTC 10) must set PCF_CORR = N.32 SCOS-2000 supports CUC formats with 1 to 4 coarse and 0 to 3 fine octets (PFC 3 to 18), CDS without and with microseconds (PFC 1 and 2; the PFC 2 row adds that CDS is supported only for command parameters, not monitoring parameters), and an 8-octet Unix time (PFC 30); the self-describing form with a P-field (PFC 0) is not supported.33

The Solar Orbiter MIB shows how this is used in practice. Of its 126,745 monitoring parameters, 3,796 are absolute times. The 3,793 on-board times in CUC form (2,116 with 4 coarse octets, PFC 15, and 1,677 with 4 coarse and 2 fine octets, PFC 17) all leave PCF_CORR empty and therefore take the default Y. The three exceptions explicitly set N: two Unix-format times (PFC 30), "Period From" and "Period To" of the ground-generated time correlation report, and one CDS time with microseconds, "GS Acceptance Time" of the ground station response packet, which the ICD's remark on PFC 2 would not allow for a monitoring parameter. No parameter sets PCF_OBTID, so the mission uses a single default clock.5133

docs.title: The measurement: what the spacecraft sends
docs.text:
The spacecraft samples its clock when a particular telemetry frame starts to leave. In TN-1030's words the trigger is the transmission of a frame whose frame counter is a multiple of N, where N is a power of 2 between 1 and 256; the sampled time is "latched" and sent to the ground in a time packet carried by a later frame.6 The ground, knowing N, can work out which frame triggered the sample.

PUS defines the same rule precisely. The time reporting subservice samples the spacecraft time reference for each virtual channel 0 frame whose frame count modulo the time report generation rate is zero, and it samples at the leading edge of the first bit of that frame's attached synchronisation marker. The rate is one of 1, 2, 4, ... 256 and can be changed by TC[9,1].2627 Time reports are spacecraft time packets: APID 0, no secondary header, message type TM[9,2] (CUC) or TM[9,3] (CDS).28

Solar Orbiter's time packet

Solar Orbiter's packet structure ICD defines the Standard Spacecraft Time Source Packet as an APID 0 packet with no data field header and 8 data octets: an S-field whose bits 4 to 7 give the generation frequency, a P-field fixed at 0b00101110 (CUC, agency-defined epoch, 4 coarse and 2 fine octets; the ICD states the octet counts, and the epoch code 0b010 is decoded here with CCSDS 301.0-B-423) and a 6-octet T-field holding the spacecraft elapsed time. The T-field relates to the leading edge of the first ASM bit of the VC 0 frame with frame count 0.36 The MIB defines it as SPID 9999 "Time Report" (type 9, subtype 2, APID 0) with the parameters NCD09021 (S-field, offset 6), NCD09022 (P-field, offset 7) and NCD09023 "OBCHP_OBT" (PTC 9, PFC 17, offset 8).51 The decoding is worked through on the ST[09] page.

docs.title: The delays: from Earth reception back to the latch
docs.text:
The frame that triggered the sample reaches the ground station some time later and is stamped there with its Earth Reception Time (ERT). The ERT arrives at the MCS in the header with which the network interface (NCTRS/NIS) delivers the frame.6 Between the on-board trigger and the ERT stamp lie four delays, defined in TN-1030 §6.1:13

# Instant or interval Definition a Frame Transmission Time (FTT) When the Transfer Frame Generator (TFG) on board starts transmitting the frame; for time correlation frames the TFG signals this instant to request the OBT sample b OBT Latching Time (OLT) When the OBT corresponding to that FTT is sampled and stored in the on-board register c Frame Radiation Time When the leading edge of the first bit of the ASM preceding the frame is at the phase centre of the on-board antenna d Frame Reception Time When the same edge is at the phase centre of the ground antenna (definition taken from SLE) e Earth Reception Time (ERT) The UTC time stamp that the ground station equipment gives the frame; for SLE service providers it must equal the frame reception time f On-board frame radiation delay From the latch request to the start of radiation: frame radiation time minus FTT g OBT latching delay From the latch request to the actual latch: OLT minus FTT h Propagation delay One-way light time (OWLT) from on-board antenna to ground antenna i Ground delay ERT minus frame reception time; zero by definition for SLE providers, which correct the time stamp themselves j UTC Time of Transmission (UTT) The UTC corresponding to a given OBT; the name assumes a zero latching delay and is, TN-1030 notes, misleading but common 
sequenceDiagram
    participant TFG as On-board TFG and clock
    participant ANT as On-board antenna
    participant GS as Ground antenna and station
    participant MCS as SCOS-2000 packetiser
    Note over TFG: FTT: frame k starts (k mod N = 0), latch requested
    Note over TFG: OLT = FTT + OBT latching delay (OBT sampled)
    TFG->>ANT: on-board frame radiation delay
    ANT->>GS: propagation delay (OWLT)
    Note over GS: frame reception time, then ERT stamp after the ground delay
    GS->>MCS: frame k with ERT (via NCTRS/NIS)
    TFG->>GS: a later frame carries the time packet with the latched OBT
    GS->>MCS: time packet
    Note over MCS: match packet to frame k, compute OLT, build a time couple

The arithmetic is simple:613

\[ \mathrm{FTT} = \mathrm{ERT} - \text{ground delay} - \text{propagation delay} - \text{on-board frame radiation delay} \] \[ \mathrm{OLT} = \mathrm{FTT} + \text{OBT latching delay} \]

The pair (OBT from the time packet, OLT in UTC) describes one physical event, the latching of the clock, seen by two clocks. It is called a time couple, and SCOS-2000 stores each one in a telemetry packet of its own.6 Where the delays come from is mission configuration: the propagationDelay API returns a light-time delay, an on-board delay and a station delay for a given UTC and an optional auxiliary identifier (for example a ground station), and its default implementation simply returns a value set with setPropagationDelay.9 For Rosetta and Mars Express, Flight Dynamics supplied the propagation delay routine, to be embedded in the R(ME)MCS time correlation component, computing the downlink delay as a function of UTC at reception from per-station One-Way Light Time (OWLT) files.46

docs.title: Matching the time packet to its frame
docs.text:
Because the time packet arrives after the frame it refers to, the packetiser remembers the frame time of every candidate frame and opens an interval in which a time packet is expected. A packet outside the interval is ignored and no couple is made.6 Formally, the candidate FTT must satisfy16

\[ \mathrm{FTT}_{report} - \mathit{FarLimit} \le \mathrm{FTT}_{obt} \le \mathrm{FTT}_{report} - \mathit{CloseLimit} \]

where \(\mathrm{FTT}_{report}\) is the FTT of the frame carrying the time report and the two limits are the MISCdynamic variables TCO_FAR_FTT_PLAUSIBILITY_LIMIT and TCO_CLOSE_FTT_PLAUSIBILITY_LIMIT. Whether the check is applied at all is a MISC variable set per OBT from the Time Correlation application.16

A time couple (illustrative numbers)

Quantity Value ERT of the triggering VC 0 frame 12:10:00.250 000 UTC Ground delay 0.000 120 s Propagation delay 480.000 000 s On-board frame radiation delay 0.000 050 s OBT latching delay 0.000 010 s FTT 12:02:00.249 830 UTC OLT 12:02:00.249 840 UTC OBT in the time packet 811 339 200.500 000 s

The formulas are TN-1030's; the numbers are invented by this wiki.13

docs.title: From couples to coefficients
docs.text:
SCOS-2000 fits a straight line through the couples. Two algorithms exist and can be switched at run time:714

Clock Algorithm (TN-1030 name) Couples needed Coefficients Free-running Least squares ("free running clock") A buffer of recent couples Gradient and offset of the best-fit line Synchronised to an external source such as GPS Difference ("synchronised on-board clock") The last couple Offset only; gradient fixed to 1

To keep resolution, the conversion is written relative to the last couple used in the calculation, \((\mathrm{OBT}_N, \mathrm{UTC}_N)\):712

\[ \mathrm{UTC}(\mathrm{OBT}) = \mathrm{UTC}_N + \mathit{Gradient}\,(\mathrm{OBT} - \mathrm{OBT}_N) + \mathit{Display\ Offset} \]

The older absolute form \(\mathrm{UTC} = \mathit{Gradient}\cdot\mathrm{OBT} + \mathit{Offset}\) is kept in the coefficient packet but marked obsolete; the two offsets are related by \(\mathit{Offset} = \mathrm{UTC}_N - \mathit{Gradient}\cdot\mathrm{OBT}_N + \mathit{Display\ Offset}\). TN-1030 Figure 4 shows the two coordinate systems.712

Inference: sign conventions

TN-1030 prints the relative relation with a plus sign before the gradient term in the description of the Gradient field, and with a minus sign in the description of the Display Offset field; the difference algorithm is printed as \(\mathrm{UTC}_N + \mathrm{OBT} - \mathrm{OBT}_N - \mathit{Offset}\).712 Only the plus form is consistent with a gradient near 1, so this page uses it. The sign of the offset in the difference algorithm cannot be settled from the available sources.

A least-squares correlation (illustrative numbers)

Four couples taken every 15 minutes; OBT is shown relative to 811 339 200 s, UTC relative to 12:00:00 on the day of the pass:

Couple OBT − 811 339 200 (s) OLT (s after 12:00:00) 1 0 0.250 010 2 900 900.250 210 3 1 800 1 800.250 455 4 2 700 2 700.250 675

An ordinary least-squares fit gives Gradient = 1.000 000 249 (the on-board clock runs about 0.25 ppm slow against UTC) and, relative to couple 4 (\(\mathrm{OBT}_N\) = 2 700, \(\mathrm{UTC}_N\) = 2 700.250 675), a Display Offset of −0.000 001 5 s. The residuals are 8.5, −15.5, 5.5 and 1.5 µs. One hour later a couple with OBT 6 300 and OLT 6 300.251 875 is received; the coefficients predict 6 300.251 570, so its deviation is +0.000 305 s. The numbers are constructed by this wiki to illustrate TN-1030's equations.7

docs.title: Monitoring the correlation: deviation, accuracy, validity
docs.text:
Every new couple tests the coefficients in force. The deviation is the UTC of the couple (its OLT) minus the UTC obtained by converting the couple's OBT with the current coefficients. Two configurable limits, the tighter accuracy limit and the looser validity limit, classify it:64

Condition Status deviation ≤ accuracy valid and accurate accuracy ≤ deviation ≤ validity valid but inaccurate validity ≤ deviation invalid (and inaccurate)

In the engine the limits are the MISCdynamic variables TCO_ACCURACY_INTERVAL and TCO_VALIDITY_INTERVAL; in the coefficient packet "inaccurate" means the user-controlled soft threshold was exceeded and "invalid" the hard one.1612 The validity limit is meant to catch coefficients that no longer apply at all, for example after a jump of the on-board clock.14

stateDiagram-v2
    VA: Valid, accurate
    VI: Valid, inaccurate
    II: Invalid, inaccurate
    VA --> VI: (1) couple deviation above accuracy limit
    VA --> II: (2) deviation above validity limit, or reset
    VI --> II: (3) deviation above validity limit, or reset
    II --> VA: (4) correlation performed, new coefficients committed
    VI --> VA: (5) correlation performed, new coefficients committed

The diagram is TN-1030 Figure 6.14 A status change is filed by setCorrelationStatus, which also raises an alarm or an information message depending on the direction of the transition.16

Synchronisation status. For a clock disciplined by an external source, the expected offset between OBT and UTC is known: GPS time, for instance, ignores leap seconds, so it differs from UTC by a known number of seconds. If the computed offset is within the accuracy limit of the expected value, the coefficients are synchronised; otherwise unsynchronised. Unlike accuracy and validity, synchronisation is assessed only when new coefficients are generated, not on each couple. Coefficients can therefore be valid and accurate yet desynchronised: usable for conversion, while the clock has lost its time source.614 The server's checkSynchronised computes the expected TAI/UTC difference (TCO_TAI_UTC_DIFFERENCE) minus the current correction and compares its absolute value with the accuracy interval.20

stateDiagram-v2
    S: Synchronised
    U: Unsynchronised
    S --> U: new correlation, abs(offset - expected) above accuracy
    U --> S: new correlation, abs(offset - expected) below accuracy

docs.title: Automatic and manual operation
docs.text:
Manual mode. The operator asks for a calculation. In the simplest case it uses the live buffer, as the automatic mode does, but the result is an intermediate set of coefficients that become active, and whose packet is archived, only when confirmed (confirmTCOparameters). The operator may instead give an end time (the configured number of couples before it is used) or an end and a start time (all couples in the archive between them); such calculations use a dedicated buffer so that the live one is untouched, and in difference mode only the last couple before the end time matters. When confirming, the operator can set the validity time, which becomes the filing time of the coefficient packet; in automatic mode it is "now". Validity and accuracy are always checked in manual mode.1916

Automatic mode (TCO_AUTO_UPDATE) adds two rules, applied only while the MISCdynamic flag TCO_SUSPEND_VALIDITY_CHECK is false:16

  1. Auto-update. If the deviation is above the accuracy interval but not above the validity interval, the engine asks the TCO server to recompute the coefficients from the latest couples and to store a new coefficient packet.
  2. Auto-reset. If the deviation exceeds the validity interval for N consecutive couples (TCO_AUTORESET_INVALID_DEVIATIONS), the couples are still evaluated but kept out of the buffer, treated as rogues; after the N-th, the server resets the correlation (resetTCOparameters): the status becomes invalid, the buffer is emptied, the validity check is suspended, and as soon as two new couples are in the buffer the coefficients are recomputed automatically.
flowchart TD
    A[Time packet passes plausibility check] --> B[createTimeCouple: couple stored by TCO server]
    B --> C[Convert couple OBT with current coefficients]
    C --> D{deviation vs limits}
    D -- "below accuracy" --> E[valid and accurate, no action]
    D -- "accuracy to validity" --> F[status change filed; auto mode: recalculate and commit]
    D -- "above validity" --> G[count consecutive invalid couples]
    G -- "fewer than N" --> H[couple not buffered, treated as rogue]
    G -- "N reached" --> I[reset: invalid, buffer emptied, checks suspended]
    I --> J[two new couples buffered, recalculate, resume checks]

Inference: three statements of the update trigger

Sections 4 and 6.2 of TN-1030, and the summary paragraph that closes §6.3.2, say the automatic recalculation happens whenever the deviation exceeds half the accuracy limit, and the sequence diagram (Figure 9) is annotated "If ½ accuracy limit is exceeded"; step (6) of the engine description in §6.3.2 uses the accuracy interval itself; and the overview in §3.1 speaks of the deviation exceeding the thresholds "for the validity".46141617 The available sources do not say which threshold the released software applies, or whether it is configurable. This page follows step (6), the most detailed statement.

The MISC variables named in TN-1030 are listed below. TN-1030 notes that each is duplicated per on-board clock, the server using the suffix _n for the n-th OBT.1620

Variable Kind (as printed) Role TCO_ESA_EPOCH MISC Epoch of the Unix-like time fields; fallback DEFAULT_ESA_EPOCH in code TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID MISCconfig Clock used when PCF_OBTID is empty (from the ICD) TCO_FAR_FTT_PLAUSIBILITY_LIMIT, TCO_CLOSE_FTT_PLAUSIBILITY_LIMIT MISCdynamic Window in which a time packet is matched to its frame TCO_ACCURACY_INTERVAL, TCO_VALIDITY_INTERVAL MISCdynamic Soft and hard limits on the deviation TCO_AUTO_UPDATE MISCconfig Enables automatic update and reset TCO_SUSPEND_VALIDITY_CHECK MISCdynamic Set during a reset until two new couples are buffered TCO_AUTORESET_INVALID_DEVIATIONS (not stated) Consecutive invalid couples that trigger a reset TCO_TAI_UTC_DIFFERENCE (not stated) Expected offset used for the synchronisation check

TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID comes from the import ICD;32 the others from TN-1030.101620

docs.title: Software architecture
docs.text:
The time correlation function has three parts: an engine inside the telemetry packetiser, a client library used by every application that converts times, and a TCO server that owns the calculations and the time correlation packets. There is no access to the server other than through the client library; the operators' Time Correlation application also goes through the library.5

flowchart LR
    subgraph PKT[Telemetry packetiser]
        TF[TPKTMtfDataProcessor<br/>frames] --> ENG[TPKTMtcoEngine]
        SP[TPKTMsrcPktDataProcessor<br/>source packets] --> ENG
        CFG[TPKTMtcoConfig<br/>rules and clocks] -.-> ENG
    end
    subgraph LIB[TCO client library]
        FN[TCOfunction / TCOconcreteInstance] --> CC[TCOclientCache<br/>one per OBT]
    end
    subgraph SRV[TCO server process]
        IF[TCOserverInterface CORBA] --> IMPL[TCOserverImpl<br/>one per OBT]
        IMPL --> CALC[TCOdifferenceCalculation /<br/>TCOleastSquaresCalculation]
        IMPL --> TM[TCOtmPktIF to the CPD]
    end
    ENG --> FN
    APP[Time Correlation application,<br/>other SCOS-2000 tasks] --> FN
    CC -->|cache miss, calculations| IF
    TM --> ARC[(Packet archive PARC)]

The diagram condenses TN-1030 Figures 8, 10, 11 and 12.151819

docs.title: The TCO engine in the packetiser
docs.text:
The engine has two jobs: detect the frames whose transmission triggers an on-board sample, and turn the subsequent time packets into couples. The engine class is assisted by a rule class and a clock class, and a configuration class ties them together; a mission normally replaces only the configuration class:15

Class Purpose TPKTMtcoTimePktRule Rule recognising trigger frames: virtual channel IDs, data stream types and sampling frequency (TN-1030's example: real-time VC 0 data with VCFC % 32 = 0). Can be subclassed TPKTMtcoObt Describes an on-board clock: its time format and where its time lies in the time packet. Can be subclassed, for example when each clock has its own time packet TPKTMtcoConfig Singleton that creates rules and clocks and maps them: each clock has exactly one rule, a rule may serve several clocks TPKTMtcoEngine Singleton that applies the rules to every frame (processTF) and every time packet (processSrcPkt)

For each time packet that matches a rule, the engine performs seven steps for every clock mapped to the rule: (1) plausibility check of the candidate FTT; (2) if it fails, nothing else happens; (3) extract the OBT in the configured format (CUC or CDS) and call createTimeCouple, the server storing the couple packet; (4) convert the OBT with obtUtt locally, without the server; (5) compare with the OLT and file any status change; (6) apply the auto-update rule; (7) apply the auto-reset rule.16 Figure 9 of TN-1030 shows the calls crossing from the engine through TCOconcreteInstance and TCOclientCache to the CORBA TCOserverInterface and TCOserverImpl, which sends packets to PDSpktSource.17

An engine can also be created in offline mode: frame detection and couple creation work, but everything that depends on the current coefficients (counting deviations, automatic reset) is disabled. TN-1030 expects it to be used on historical telemetry, for example to regenerate more accurate couples with better propagation delays.15

docs.title: The client library
docs.text:
TCOfunction is the abstract interface for conversions; TCOconcreteInstance is the SCOS-2000 implementation, a singleton used by the classes that take part in correlation, while ordinary users of conversions hold a TCOfunction obtained through TCOfactory::createTCO. A mission with a different strategy writes its own TCOfunction subclass and makes the factory return it.18 TCOconfig creates one TCOobt per on-board clock (format and location of the OBT in time packets), each with a TCOtimeFormat; the library provides TCOtimeFormatCUC (parameterised by the PFC) and TCOtimeFormatCDS, and missions may add formats.418 For each monitored clock the instance creates a TCOclientCache, which keeps the last and the last "next valid" coefficients with their validity intervals, so that a conversion for a time inside the interval of the last coefficients is answered without asking the server, a measure TN-1030 calls necessary for performance.18

The public operations, all keyed by the OBT identifier obtId, are:918

Operation What it does instance(), destroyInstance(), isTcoServerAvailable() Singleton handling; server availability obtUtt OBT to ground time with the current coefficients; false if none are set obtUttAccuracy Same, optionally for a reference UTC (refUtt), returning the accuracy flag of the coefficients used obtUttValid Uses the OBT to find the applicable coefficients; if they are invalid, uses the next valid ones and returns false uttObt UTC to OBT (listed in the class diagrams) propagationDelay, setPropagationDelay Delay model; the default returns the value set createTimeCouple Creates a couple packet from OBT, FTT, ERT, filing time, light time, on-board and station delays, auxiliary ID and deviation; updateBuffer controls use in the live buffer setCorrelationStatus Files validity, accuracy and synchronisation status with a message severity calculateTCOparameters, confirmTCOparameters, resetTCOcalculation Calculation life cycle, optionally with time limits or a validity time checkTAIsynchronised Synchronisation status of the current coefficients getTCOcoefficients, setTcoCoefficients, injectTCOcoefficients, deleteTimeCouple(s), updateTCOtimes Listed in the class diagram of the client side

docs.title: The TCO server
docs.text:
The server is a resident process with a CORBA interface (TCOserverInterface); like the client, it creates one TCOserverImpl per on-board clock and delegates to it.19 It produces and distributes the couple packets, calculates and confirms current or historical coefficients, deletes coefficients that are no longer valid, injects coefficients and retrieves them, and it converts times for historical data, which needs coefficients from the archive.19 Notable operations of TCOserverImpl:20

  • initialiseTCOparameters(cacheInit) restores at start-up the current and last valid coefficients and their status, from the cache and history files or from MISCconfig variables.
  • obtUttReference finds, through TCOtmPktIF, the coefficients valid at a reference UTC, searching by filing or creation time, backwards only if the earliest known coefficients precede the current time; it converts even with invalid coefficients (returning false) and returns zero when none are found. obtUttValid looks forward for the next valid coefficients instead.
  • calculateTCOparameters computes new coefficients from the buffer filled by createTimeCouple, marks them valid and accurate, and stores them in MISCconfig variables and a local cache; confirmTCOparameters activates manually calculated ones and archives their packet.
  • createTimeCouple(..., inPast) with a filing time in the past creates the packet without touching the live buffer, for reprocessing.
  • deleteTimeCouple(from, to) asks the PARC to delete couple packets; findEarliestTime returns the earliest valid OBT and UTC coefficients retrievable from PARC.

Historical look-ups are keyed on OBT, which fails when the OBT is reset (for instance in simulations) and many coefficient packets cover similar OBT ranges. The server therefore deletes, whenever it creates a coefficient packet, all archived coefficient packets relating to an OBT within the period in which the previous coefficients were valid.19 TCOtmPktIF talks to the CPD, the Client Packet Distributor,22 using filters built from SPIDs held in MISCconfig variables; TCOcalculation is the abstract calculator with the two specialisations for the difference and least-squares methods.21

docs.title: Time-stamping telemetry
docs.text:
Every frame and source packet that SCOS-2000 files or distributes has a time stamp that is the prime filing key of the archive. The packetiser offers three policies, one of which the mission selects:8

  1. the time when the SCOS-2000 packet is filed (useful when replaying old frames in tests);
  2. the FTT of the frame that carried the packet header, computed from the ERT minus the ground, propagation and on-board processing delays;
  3. the on-board generation time, converted from the OBT in the packet with the TCO API.

The Solar Orbiter DDID shows the result in the SCOS-2000 packet header: a 2-bit Timestamp field (0 = packet reception "PR", 1 = frame transmission "FT", 2 = correlated SCET "PG") and a 2-bit Time Quality field (0 good, 1 inaccurate, 2 bad), meaningful when Timestamp = 2. The filing time (the EDDS "generation time") is then the correlated on-board generation time; reception time stamping is used only when the user explicitly selects it, for example to bypass time correlation.37 Superseded TCO coefficient packets are filed on the internal stream 65535, which external users should ignore.37

The Rosetta/Mars Express/Venus Express DDID gives the time quality algorithm of that generation:43

Time quality Condition Time stamp 0 good OBT valid (top bit of the OBT not set) OBT converted with the applicable correlation 1 inaccurate OBT invalid, packet received on VC 0 ERT of the VC 0 frame minus propagation, on-board and ground delays 2 bad OBT invalid, packet received on VC 1 ERT of the VC 1 frame minus the same delays

A plausibility check followed: a correlated VC 0 time stamp may be no more than a configurable number of seconds (usually 2) ahead of, nor (usually 15) behind, the corrected reception time of its frame; for VC 1 (playback) only the "ahead" check applies. With autocorrection enabled a failure sets the quality to bad and replaces the time stamp with the corrected frame time; otherwise only a warning is logged.43 Because stored data are dumped later, a packet is time-stamped with the correlation valid for its OBT, not with the current one.41

docs.title: The time correlation packets
docs.text: The TCO subsystem keeps its products as SCOS-2000 telemetry packets, so they are archived, distributed and retrievable like any other telemetry.10

docs.title: Time couple packet (TN-1030 Table 1)
docs.text:
The "Position" column of TN-1030 gives octet offsets; the fields total 88 octets.11

Field Bits Octet Meaning OBT 64 0 On-board time as TDSsunTime, used internally by the MCS OLT 96 8 OBT latching time (TDSsunTime_pico): the UTC paired with the OBT, the "points" of the least-squares fit FTT 96 20 Frame transmission time ERT 96 32 Earth reception time; equals the frame reception time for SLE providers Light time delay 64 44 One-way light time, IEEE double, seconds On-board frame radiation delay 64 52 FTT to frame radiation, seconds OBT latching delay 64 60 FTT to OLT, seconds Ground station delay 64 68 Station processing delay, seconds Ground station ID 32 76 Integer Deviation 64 80 OLT minus the UTC computed from the OBT with the current coefficients

docs.title: Time correlation (coefficient) packet (TN-1030 Table 2)
docs.text:
Field Bits Octet Values and meaning Version 8 0 Structure version, 1 in the original implementation Algorithm 32 1 1 = DIFFERENCE (synchronised clock), 2 = LEAST SQUARE (free-running clock) Synchronisation check 8 5 1 = synchronisation status checked, 0 = not Validity 8 6 0 = INVALID, 1 = VALID (hard threshold) Accuracy 8 7 0 = INACCURATE, 1 = ACCURATE (soft threshold) Synchronisation 8 8 0 = DESYNCHRONISED, 1 = SYNCHRONISED Spare 24 9 Padding Gradient 64 12 UTC seconds per OBT second; 1 for the difference algorithm Offset 64 20 Offset of the absolute form; obsolete OBT_N 64 28 OBT seconds since the epoch of the last couple used UTC_N 64 36 UTC seconds since the epoch of the last couple used Display offset 64 44 Offset of the relative form

All rows are from TN-1030 Table 2.12 The 32-bit Algorithm field starting at octet 1 means the doubles are not 8-octet aligned relative to the start of the data (they start at octets 12, 20, ...); this is as printed.

docs.title: Testing without a spacecraft
docs.text:
TN-1030 explains how to exercise the chain without real data: in the TM-TC Test Tool's simulation tab, the TM Packet Injector can add packets by SPID, and three SPIDs matter, time report 1000005, time couple 1000098 and time coefficients 1000099.4

Inference

These SPIDs are those of TN-1030's test or reference configuration. A mission chooses its own: Solar Orbiter uses 9999 for the time report and 66840 to 66842 for the ground products (next section).451 The server reads the SPIDs from MISCconfig variables.21

docs.title: Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express: manual correlation
docs.text:
The common DDID of the three planetary missions documents the time correlation of the generation before TN-1030, which was part of the mission control systems rather than the kernel.4134

  • Sampling. Following the ESA Packet Telemetry Standard, the spacecraft elapsed time clock is sampled at the first ASM bit of the VC 0 frame with frame count 0 and sent in the standard spacecraft time source packet before 255 more VC 0 frames have been counted; intervals of 128 down to 1 frame may be chosen instead. The ground stamps the reception of the same bit with a CDS-coded UTC and extracts the CUC time sample. On Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express the rate is selectable among every 256, 128, 64, 32 or 16 VC 0 frames.41
  • Delays. The packetiser takes the ERT of each "zeroth" VC 0 frame and removes three corrections: the station delay (a fixed, measured part per station plus a bit-rate-dependent part common to all stations), the propagation delay from the Flight Dynamics OWLT file, and the on-board processing delay (fixed plus bit-rate-dependent). With the next time source packet it creates a "Time Telemetry" packet (type 190, subtype 0, APID 0) holding the spacecraft time and its generation UTC.41
  • Coefficients. The Flight Control Team triggered each correlation manually, choosing the time range of Time Telemetry packets for a least-squares fit, then accepted or rejected the result and gave a validity start time. A correlation stayed valid until the next coefficient packet. The gradient was nominally 1, and the DDID warns users to treat any packet with a gradient substantially different from 1 with caution.41

The Time Correlation Coefficient Packet was an MCS-generated packet (APID 1966, type 190, subtype 40), not a spacecraft packet, stored big-endian after the SCOS-2000 TM header.4542

The generation time is CUC without P-field, 4 coarse and 2 fine octets; in the DDS header of a delivered coefficient packet, the SCET field holds the time from which the correlation became valid, and the ground station ID of these packets is 0 because the couples can come from several stations.4244 Flight Dynamics extracted these "Time Coefficient History packets", with the telemetry, from the MCS data archive system (DAS) using its own SCOS-2000/ORATOS Data Access (SoDA) software.47 The mission papers state the achieved result: the Mars Express and Venus Express control systems time-stamp telemetry by converting OBT to UTC with an accuracy of better than 2 ms.4849 Downstream, the Venus Express science operations centre converted the time correlation packets into SPICE spacecraft clock (SCLK) kernels for the instrument teams.50

docs.title: Solar Orbiter: the kernel implementation on a current mission
docs.text:
The Solar Orbiter DDID tells external users that the MCS files internal packets on APID 1966 that they should normally ignore, with one exception, the time correlation packets, which are available from the data dissemination system (EDDS):38

SPID PUS type, subtype Name in the DDID Name in the MIB 66840 164, 1 Time Correlation Report packet Time Correlation Report 66841 164, 2 Time Couple packet TCO Time_Couples OBT 66842 164, 3 Time Correlation Coefficient packet TCO_Coefficients OBT

The DDID defers the content of all three to the Solar Orbiter/BepiColombo Packetiser ICD (BC-ESC-IF-22002, chapter 3.6.2) and, for the report, to the BepiColombo MCS SDD; its own appendix on time correlation was removed in issue 1 revision 2 in favour of the BepiColombo "Time Correlation Approach and Accuracy" note (BC-ESC-TN-05004).3839 None of these is public, but the MIB defines the packets, so their layouts can be read from plf and pcf:51

SPID 66841 field Octet PTC/PFC TN-1030 Table 1 counterpart (octet + 16) SCET or OBT TDSsunTime 16 ⅞ (8 octets) OBT (0 + 16) OBT Latching Time 24 7/12 (12 octets) OLT (8 + 16) Frame Transmission Time 36 7/12 FTT (20 + 16) Earth Reception Time 48 7/12 ERT (32 + 16) Light Time Delay (unit "nsec") 60 5/2 (double) light time delay (44 + 16) OB Frame Rad Delay 68 5/2 radiation delay (52 + 16) Ground Stat Delay 76 5/2 ground station delay (68 + 16 = 84) Groundstation ID 84 3/14 (32 bits) ground station ID (76 + 16 = 92) TC Deviation 88 5/2 deviation (80 + 16 = 96) Frame Counter RefFrame, Frame Counter OBTFrm 96, 97 ¾ each none OBT Size 98 ¾ none Raw OBT 99 9/17 none SPID 66842 field Octet PTC/PFC TCO VALIDITY, TCO ACCURACY 16, 17 ¾ each TCO GRADIENT, TCO OFFSET 18, 26 5/2 each TCO OBT_N, TCO UTC_N 34, 42 5/2 each TCO STD, TCO STE (standard deviation and error) 50, 58 5/2 each

The tpcf sizes are 105 octets (couple), 66 (coefficients) and 173 (report), consistent with the last field of each packet.51 The report packet holds the period covered (two Unix-format times), the numbers of packets and bad packets received, the bit rate and encoding scheme, the time generation rate, offset and gradient (each with an "HL" flag octet), standard deviation and error, the deviation, and a 70-character dump file path.51

Inference: one lineage, two dialects

The Solar Orbiter couple packet is TN-1030's layout shifted by 16 octets but without the OBT latching delay field, so from the ground station delay onwards its offsets are 8 octets smaller, and it appends the two frame counters, the OBT size and the raw 6-octet OBT. The coefficient packet does not follow TN-1030 Table 2 at all (no version, algorithm or synchronisation fields; standard deviation and error added); it is closer to the Rosetta-era packet (gradient, offset, standard deviation). The constant 16-octet shift matches PID_DFHSIZE = 16 of these packets, suggesting the MIB counts a 16-octet header before the data, as for a PUS packet; but the releaser's ground station response packet (SPID 66850, same APID and the same PID_DFHSIZE) has offsets starting at 0, so the MIB is not consistent on this point (see NCTRS, NIS). The "nsec" unit of the light time delay contradicts TN-1030's seconds. All of this is deduced from the MIB and is not stated by any public document.511112

Both MIB releases (2020-04-16 and 2025-09-16) define the three packets with the same parameter counts and sizes.5152 The DDID also explains where the data end up for the science ground segment: time packets and coefficient packets are ordinary telemetry in the RAPID files forwarded to it.40

docs.title: Accuracy: what the sources say
docs.text:
TN-1030 gives no numbers: accuracy and validity limits are configuration. The error sources are nevertheless visible in the equations. Every delay subtracted from the ERT, the time-tagging accuracy of the station, the latching delay and the on-board sampling accuracy all add to the deviation, and PUS asks the mission to declare the sampling accuracy and the accuracy of the time difference between the reference frame's transmission and the sampled time.1326 ECSS-E-ST-70-11C asks for a correlation better than <TIME_CORREL_ACCUR> over <TIME_CORREL_PERIOD>, with an on-board contribution below <ONBOARD_STABILITY> ms per day, all mission constants.2930 For Mars Express and Venus Express the published figure is better than 2 ms.4849

Inference: the error budget

The propagation delay dominates in size (minutes for interplanetary missions) but is predicted precisely by Flight Dynamics, so its error is small; ground and on-board delays are small but must be calibrated per station and per bit rate, as the Rosetta-era corrections show.41 The least-squares fit averages random errors over the buffer, while the difference algorithm takes each couple at face value. This qualitative reading is the wiki's, not TN-1030's.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
• TN-1030 does not say whether the Table 1 and Table 2 layouts (taken, per its change log, from a Gaia document) are the kernel default or Gaia-specific, and it gives neither the size of the couple buffer nor the configuration of the least-squares window.
  • The update threshold (accuracy limit or half of it) is stated inconsistently (see above).
  • The signs in the relative and difference formulas are printed inconsistently.
  • The Solar Orbiter packets' exact semantics depend on the non-public Packetiser ICD BC-ESC-IF-22002 and the BepiColombo time correlation note BC-ESC-TN-05004.
